Adding ACAG to the clinical reference model increased the cross-validated area under the curve from 0.803 to 0.829; the extended-model calibration slope was 0.823. Among participants without a detected event, the last readable echocardiogram occurred a median of 323 days after discharge. Admission ACAG was associated with subsequent TRV elevation and provided modest additional discrimination in this cohort. Its availability in routine admission testing makes it a candidate for further evaluation in post-exacerbation risk assessment, with prospective external validation needed before clinical application.

Title: Development and Validation of an Early Postoperative Risk Stratification Model for Hydrocephalus Following Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hydrocephalus is a common complication after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). This study aimed to identify perioperative risk factors and develop an early postoperative risk stratification model to support postoperative monitoring rather than purely preoperative prediction.
METHODS: Employing a retrospective case-control design, clinical data from 331 patients with aSAH treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan Medical University between August 1, 2018, and December 31, 2024, were collected and analyzed. The primary endpoint was postoperative hydrocephalus occurring within 3 weeks after aneurysm treatment, diagnosed according to combined radiological and clinical criteria. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was employed to screen risk factors. Multiple machine-learning models were compared, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis was used for individualized model interpretation.
RESULTS: The admission Glasgow Coma Scale score, intraoperative external ventricular drainage/lateral ventricular drainage, and intraventricular hemorrhage were identified as key variables associated with postoperative hydrocephalus. The logistic regression model emerged as the optimal model; locked test set area under the curve (95% CI): 0.891 (0.739-1.000); accuracy: 0.720 (0.688-0.775); sensitivity: 0.899 (0.823-0.987); specificity: 0.683 (0.635-0.740).
CONCLUSION: The logistic regression model with SHAP-based interpretation may support early postoperative risk stratification for hydrocephalus after aSAH. Given its modest positive predictive value, the model should be used to triage patients for intensified monitoring and timely reassessment.

Title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).
CONCLUSION: LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

Title: Dexamethasone implant in vitreoretinal surgery for diabetic retinal detachment: A retrospective comparative study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effect of simultaneous intraoperative dexamethasone implant on visual and anatomical outcomes in eyes undergoing pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with silicone oil for diabetic retinal detachment (DRD).
DESIGN: Retrospective comparative case series.
METHODS SETTING: Tertiary eye care center.
STUDY POPULATION: Sixty eyes of 60 patients with DRD.
INTERVENTION/OBSERVATION PROCEDURES: Medical records of 60 eyes of 60 patients undergoing PPV with silicone oil for diabetic tractional retinal detachment or combined tractional-rhegmatogenous retinal detachment were retrospectively reviewed. Thirty eyes underwent standard PPV with silicone oil tamponade, while 30 eyes underwent PPV with simultaneous intraoperative dexamethasone implant. Silicone oil removal was performed at 2-3 months. All patients were followed for at least 6 months.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The main outcome measures were best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT). Secondary outcomes included postoperative macular edema (ME), epiretinal membrane (ERM) formation, need for rescue dexamethasone therapy, anatomical success, and requirement for secondary internal limiting membrane peeling.
RESULTS: At 6 months, BCVA was 0.62 ± 0.14 logMAR in Group A versus 0.48 ± 0.12 logMAR in Group B ( P < 0.01). Mean CMT was 314 ± 35 μm versus 272 ± 28 μm, respectively ( P < 0.05). ME occurred in 30% of eyes in Group A versus 10% in Group B. Rescue dexamethasone was required in 16.7% of Group A and none in Group B. ERM formation was observed in 23.3% versus 6.7% ( P = 0.07), and secondary ILM peeling was required in 10% versus 0% in Groups A and B, respectively. Retinal reattachment rates at 6 months were comparable (93.3% vs 96.7%).
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative dexamethasone implantation may improve postoperative visual and anatomical outcomes and warrant further evaluation in prospective randomized studies.

Title: Ocular involvement in Takayasu arteritis - A case series from a tertiary eye center in South India.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To analyze the clinical profile of patients with Takayasu arteritis (TAK) from a South Indian patient population who presented to a tertiary referral eye center.
METHODS: Retrospective case series between 2016 and 2025.
RESULTS: Of the 13 cases of TAK, 11 were females and 2 were males (female: male = 11:2). The mean age was 31.92 ± 7.04 years. Nine cases initially presented to an ophthalmologist. The most common presenting symptoms were eye pain (eight cases) and diminution of vision (seven cases), of whom two had sudden vision loss. Ocular involvement included ocular ischemia with retinal vessel spasm and constriction (three cases), Takayasu retinopathy (three cases), and central retinal artery occlusion (one case). Optic disc pallor, dilated conjunctival and episcleral vessels, scleritis, hypertensive retinopathy, and atypical Tolosa Hunt syndrome were other presentations. Presumed ocular tuberculosis in two cases led to an incidental diagnosis of TAK. Based on the imaging findings, six cases had type I TAK, five cases had type V TAK, and one case each had type IV and type IIa TAK. Treatment included systemic corticosteroids and conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (methotrexate and mycophenolate mofetil) and tocilizumab. Good visual outcome on early treatment was seen in our series.
CONCLUSION: TAK is an important and underrecognized cause of ocular inflammation and ischemia in young patients. Our series highlights that ocular involvement can precede systemic diagnosis. Early diagnosis and treatment results in a good visual outcome.

Title: Thirty-year follow-up of retinal vasculitis at a tertiary eye care center in India.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the clinical course of patients with retinal vasculitis over a three-decade follow-up.
METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients with a minimum follow-up of 30 years at a tertiary eye care institute in India.
RESULTS: A total of 37 patients were included. The mean follow-up duration was 34.3 ± 2.9 years (range: 30-44 years). The mean age of the patients at presentation was 31.05 ± 15.6 years, and 97% of them were male. In 54% of the patients, the involvement was bilateral. Five patients who initially presented with unilateral involvement subsequently developed involvement in the other eye. Presumed tuberculosis was diagnosed in five patients. None of the remaining patients developed ocular or extraocular manifestations of tuberculosis during the 30-year follow-up. Common investigations done for all patients were antinuclear antibody, Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test, Mantoux test, chest radiography, and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels. The use of immunosuppressives was low (2), as was the use of intravitreal anti-Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) (1). The primary modalities of treatment were oral corticosteroids and photocoagulation. The most common complications were glaucoma (35, 56.5%), vitreous hemorrhage (30, 48.4%), and optic neuropathy (10, 16.1%). Recurrence of inflammation was seen in 30.6% of eyes in three decades of follow-up. Nineteen eyes required vitrectomy, and five eyes underwent scleral buckling for retinal detachment. The mean visual acuity in logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution at presentation was 0.8, and at the final visit, after 30 years of follow-up was 0.66. It was observed that 41.9% of eyes had visual improvement, 24.2% of eyes remained visually stable, and vision deteriorated in 33.9% of eyes.
CONCLUSION: Retinal vasculitis has a chronic and unpredictable course, warranting long-term follow-up to detect late bilateral involvement and recurrence. While recurrence becomes less frequent over time, it may still occur after many years. Most patients continue to have idiopathic disease without subsequent identification of a systemic cause.

Title: Risk Factors for Cardiovascular Mortality in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, but the relative contributions of OSA-specific parameters versus classical cardiometabolic risk factors remain poorly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,368 consecutive adults referred for diagnostic polysomnography at a tertiary sleep center and followed for up to 20 years. The primary outcome was cause-specific cardiovascular mortality ascertained by national death registry linkage. Analyses integrated cause-specific Cox regression, Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, and a random survival forest (RSF) competing-risk model (1000 trees; 70/30 train-test split). Gower-distance-based hierarchical clustering of RSF-predicted cumulative incidence identified patient phenotypes.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 8.6 years (interquartile range 6.7-12.5), 335 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Heart failure (30.4%), chronic ischemic heart disease (14.0%), and acute myocardial infarction (11.6%) were the leading causes. Independent predictors were age (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.10, per year), male sex (1.68, 1.29-2.18), active smoking (1.68, 1.30-2.15), hypertension (1.73, 1.29-2.33), atrial fibrillation (2.16, 1.56-2.98), prior myocardial infarction (1.71, 1.25-2.35), and diabetes (1.37, 1.06-1.76). Nocturnal desaturation lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Among patients with an apnea-hypopnea index ≥15 events/h, a good continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) response was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (0.72, 0.55-0.96). The RSF C-index was 0.80. Six phenotypes showed cardiovascular mortality of 2.9% to 14.4%.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular mortality in OSA was driven predominantly by classical cardiometabolic risk factors rather than by nocturnal hypoxemic burden or CPAP response. Comorbidity-targeted prevention should be prioritized, and phenotype-aware stratification may identify subgroups warranting intensified cardiovascular surveillance.

Title: Anterior Versus Posterior Circulation Acute Ischemic Stroke and 3-Month Cognitive Profiles: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is common, but its pattern may differ between vascular territories. This single-center cohort included adults with first-ever, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed acute ischemic stroke admitted between May 2022 and June 2024. Infarcts were classified as anterior or posterior circulation, and cognition was assessed in person at 3 months using the Beijing version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). The primary PSCI definition was an education-adjusted MoCA score <26, with a sensitivity analysis using <22. Of 173 enrolled patients, 167 completed follow-up (91 anterior and 76 posterior circulation infarctions). PSCI occurred in 50/91 (54.9%) and 27/76 (35.5%) patients, respectively (p = 0.012). The unadjusted odds ratio was 2.21 (95% confidence interval, 1.18-4.14), and the adjusted odds ratio was 2.18 (95% confidence interval, 1.06-4.49; p = 0.035). With the <22 cutoff, the corresponding prevalences were 31.9% and 15.8%, and the adjusted odds ratio was 2.43 (95% confidence interval, 1.06-5.54; p = 0.035). After false-discovery-rate correction, differences in visuospatial/executive, naming, delayed-recall, language, abstraction, and orientation performance remained, whereas attention did not differ. Cognitive outcomes differed between vascular-territory groups despite similar global disability scores; these group-level associations do not establish a causal effect of territory or a domain-specific diagnosis.

Title: Associations of International Normalized Ratio and Hematocrit With Stroke Status and Machine Learning Mortality Prediction in Critical Care Databases.
Abstract: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability. This retrospective cohort study evaluated associations of international normalized ratio (INR) and hematocrit (Hct) with stroke status in 29,831 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Stroke status was identified using predefined International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revision codes. INR and Hct were defined using the first measurements within 24 h after ICU admission. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, quartile analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Primary analyses used complete-case cohorts, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. A post hoc exploratory secondary analysis among patients with stroke used Cox regression to identify six prognostic variables for machine learning-based prediction of ICU mortality. Stroke proportions decreased across increasing INR quartiles and increased across increasing Hct quartiles. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in INR was associated with lower stroke odds, with odds ratios (ORs) of 0.105-0.395 across cohorts, whereas each 1-percentage-point increase in Hct was associated with higher stroke odds (ORs, 1.076-1.103). RCS analyses supported overall associations but not consistent nonlinearity after full adjustment. Multiple-imputation results were directionally consistent. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.669-0.766), 0.670 (95% CI, 0.603-0.737), and 0.630 (95% CI, 0.557-0.703) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. INR was inversely associated and Hct positively associated with stroke status. These observational associations require cautious interpretation; the exploratory ICU mortality analysis provides a complementary prognostic perspective among patients with stroke.

Title: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Bone Mineral Density in Cohorts from Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine.
Journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
Abstract: A somatic mutation causing clonal expansion in hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), but not resulting in hematologic malignancy, is termed clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP). CHIP is associated with non-hematologic disorders, including accelerated atherosclerosis, heart failure, ischemic stroke, gout, liver disease, and kidney disease. Because osteoclasts are derived from the macrophage-monocyte lineage of HSCs, changes in the bone marrow niche due to CHIP may drive changes in BMD. To investigate whether CHIP may be related to BMD, we used CHIP mutation calls from the Trans-omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) whole genome sequencing data and DXA derived BMD from multiple cohorts. Data from the the Amish cohort, Cardiovascular Health Study, the Framingham Heart Study, San Antonio Family Study, and the Women's Health Initiative were combined for analysis. Multiple linear regression was used to determine the association between CHIP mutation status and BMD, adjusting for cohort, age, age,2 sex, and, for family-based cohorts, empiric kinship estimated from genotype data. CHIP mutation status was analyzed both as a binary variable (any CHIP mutation) and as an ordinal variable (no CHIP mutation, 1 CHIP mutation in any gene, two or more CHIP mutations in a single gene, two or more CHIP mutations in different genes). A total of 3368 samples had both CHIP and BMD data, and 10.9% of samples contained any CHIP mutation. The presence of any CHIP mutations was not associated with either femoral neck or lumbar spine BMD; however, the presence of two or more CHIP mutations in different genes was positively associated with LSBMD (beta = 0.36, p = .015). We found no overall association between the presence of CHIP mutations and BMD in a large, diverse sample of genomes. Our findings of greater BMD in persons harboring multiple CHIP mutations confirm mouse models demonstrating that Dnmt3a and Tet2 mutations independently cause increased BMD.

Title: Potassium-biofortified tomato as a food matrix: compositional evidence, dietary exposure and requirements for cardiovascular evaluation.
Abstract: No eligible human trial has tested potassium-biofortified tomato, and the searched literature identified no non-stressed commercial cultivar with a reproducible 600 mg K per 100 g fresh-weight specification. The central evidence gap is the absence of a validated path from fruit potassium concentration to realistic dietary exposure and product-specific human testing. This critical narrative review mapped agronomic, breeding, analytical and cardiovascular evidence relevant to edible tomato (Solanum lycopersicum). Searches covered January 2010 to October 2025 and were updated through 27 July 2026. Direct fruit-composition studies showed genotype- and environment-dependent potassium concentrations, but few isolated potassium as the intervention and reported reproducible fresh-weight values. At 100 g day-1, modelled tomatoes containing 400 or 600 mg K per 100 g supply 400 or 600 mg K, equivalent to 11.4% or 17.1% of the EFSA adult Adequate Intake of 3500 mg day-1; the increments above a 200 mg per 100 g reference are 200 or 400 mg day-1. Historical country-level means reported by EPIC range from 5.9 to 112.5 g day-1; they anchor plausible serving scenarios but do not represent current European consumption monitoring. Potassium interventions reduce blood pressure modestly on average, but their effects cannot be transferred to tomato. Evidence from other food matrices and multimodal clinical regimens is hypothesis-generating only. The evidence supports a staged research pathway: multi-season compositional validation, representative multi-element batch release and processing mass balance, followed by tomato-specific kinetic studies and risk-stratified randomised trials. Potassium-biofortified tomato remains a testable food-development concept, not an established cardiovascular intervention.

Title: Effect of glucagon-like-peptide-1 receptor agonists on major cardiovascular outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
Abstract: Glucagon-like-peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are an antihyperglycemic group of drugs that have emerged as potentially preventing the risk of cardiovascular events. This meta-analysis assesses the effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists on cardiovascular outcomes. A detailed search of existing literature was based on MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov. The search included all the studies from inception to February 2026. Statistical analyses were performed using the RevMan software, and a random-effects model was used to conduct the meta-analysis. Data were represented via forest plots, and dichotomous outcomes were evaluated using the Mantel-Haenszel method. This meta-analysis includes 12 randomized control trials (RCTs) with 82,669 patients. The analysis showed that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce risk of cardiac death [relative risk (RR): 0.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.96, p=0.003, I²=0%], all-cause mortality (RR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.93, p<0.00001, I²=0%), stroke (RR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.77-0.94, p=0.001, I²=0%), non-fatal stroke (RR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.79-0.96, p=0.005, I²=0%) and revascularization (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95, p=0.007, I²=59%). There was no statistically significant reduction in myocardial infarction (MI) (RR: 0.92, 95% CI: 0.84-1.01, p=0.09, I²=42%), fatal MI (RR: 1.15, 95% CI: 0.80-1.66, p=0.44, I²=0%), non-fatal MI (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.82-1.01, p=0.09, I²=51%), fatal stroke (RR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.55-1.00, p=0.05, I²=0%), heart failure hospitalization (RR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.85-1.03, p=0.20, I²=17%), or hospitalization for unstable angina (RR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, p=0.71, I²=0%). This meta-analysis demonstrates that GLP-1 receptor agonists have a significant impact on cardiovascular death. More thorough RCTs with longer follow-up periods are required to completely understand the possible cardiovascular advantages of GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Title: [Effect of postoperative nutritional supplementation on the reduction of clinical complications in geriatric patients with hip fracture: a retrospective study in a hospital setting].
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The high incidence of hip fractures among the elderly population in Spain, with an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 cases annually, represents a serious public health issue due to high mortality rates and associated complications, particularly in malnourished patients. The objective of this paper was to assess the effectiveness of nutritional supplementation as part of postoperative treatment in elderly patients with hip fractures.
METHODS: A study was conducted at the University Hospital of León with a sample of 497 patients aged between seventy-five and one hundred five years. Clinical records were used to collect data on functional status prior to the fracture, nutritional support, and clinical outcomes. Statistical analysis was performed to identify associations between nutritional supplementation and the occurrence of postoperative complications.
RESULTS: Protein supplements were prescribed more frequently to patients who were completely dependent (27.1 %) and to those who required a great deal of assistance to walk or were unable to walk (25.5 %), with statistically significant associations (P=0.001 and P=0.005, respectively). Furthermore, their prescription was significantly associated with complications during hospitalisation, such as the need for a blood transfusion (P<0.001), respiratory failure (P<0.001), heart failure (P<0.001) and malnutrition (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The prescription of nutritional supplements on discharge was more common among patients with greater functional dependence and who had experienced complications during their hospital stay. No significant differences were observed by gender. These results reinforce the importance of an individualised nutritional assessment in older people with hip fractures.

Title: Remnant cholesterol predicts progression from prehypertension to incident hypertension: Evidence from a prospective cohort study and Mendelian randomization analysis.
Abstract: ObjectiveRemnant cholesterol (RC), a marker of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnants, has emerged as an important contributor to residual cardiometabolic risk. However, whether RC contributes to the transition from prehypertension to clinical hypertension remains unclear. We investigated the association between RC and incident hypertension among adults with prehypertension and further assessed genetic evidence using Mendelian randomization (MR).MethodsThis prospective cohort study included 2,858 adults with prehypertension from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, followed from 2011 to 2015. RC was calculated as total cholesterol minus low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. Two-sample MR, including inverse-variance weighted and Bayesian weighted MR methods, was used to evaluate the genetic association between RC and hypertension-related traits.ResultsDuring 4 years of follow-up, 891 participants developed incident hypertension. Higher RC was independently associated with increased odds of incident hypertension. In the fully adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL increase in RC was associated with a 2% higher odds of hypertension. Compared with participants in the lowest RC quartile, those in the highest quartile had 67% higher odds of incident hypertension, corresponding to an absolute increase of 11.86% in cumulative hypertension incidence during follow-up. Compared with the lowest RC quartile, the highest quartile showed a significantly higher risk of incident hypertension. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a linear dose-response association, with no evidence of nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses suggested stronger associations among older adults, non-smokers, individuals with normal body weight, and participants without depressive symptoms. MR analyses further supported a positive genetic association between elevated RC and hypertension-related traits.ConclusionsAmong adults with prehypertension, elevated RC was independently and linearly associated with higher risk of progression to incident hypertension. Genetic evidence further supported a potential role of RC in hypertension-related traits. These findings suggest that RC, which can be readily calculated from routine lipid profiles, may complement existing approaches for hypertension risk assessment and targeted blood pressure monitoring among individuals with prehypertension.

Title: Prediction and Risk Stratification for 30-Day Mortality in Stable Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Recalibration of the Multimarker Calculator and Evaluation of the AHA/ACC Classification.
Journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in haemodynamically stable acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains challenging. The multimarker calculator (MMC) provides individualized 30-day mortality estimates, whereas the 2026 AHA/ACC Acute PE Clinical Categories (AHA/ACC classification) provide a phenotype-based framework incorporating clinical severity, right ventricular dysfunction, cardiac biomarker elevation, and respiratory compromise. We evaluated these approaches and recalibrated the original MMC in a Chinese multicentre cohort.
METHODS: We included adults with haemodynamically stable acute PE from the prospective, multicentre China pUlmonary thromboembolism REgistry Study (2012-2021). The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The MMC, 2019 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) model, and AHA/ACC classification were assessed using discrimination, decision-curve analysis, risk classification, and subgroup analyses. Logistic recalibration updated the original MMC linear predictor. The AHA/ACC classification was evaluated using 7-, 4-, and simplified phenotype-based 3-category schemes.
RESULTS: Among 11,568 patients, 331 died within 30 days (2.9%). The MMC and 7-category AHA/ACC classification showed better discrimination than the ESC model (AUC, 0.704 and 0.680 vs. 0.606). The original MMC overestimated intermediate-high-risk mortality (mean predicted risk, 16.2%; observed risk, 9.4%). Recalibration improved calibration and identified a smaller intermediate-high-risk subgroup comprising 2.2% of patients, with 13.2% observed mortality. In the 3-category AHA/ACC classification, mortality increased stepwise across category B, partial phenotype involvement, and dual cardiopulmonary phenotype involvement (0.7%, 2.7%, and 6.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: The recalibrated MMC may be useful for individualized 30-day mortality risk estimation, whereas the AHA/ACC classification may offer a simple framework for phenotype-based risk grouping.

Title: Prediction of All-Cause Mortality, Cardiovascular Mortality, and Angiographic Coronary Disease From LVEF Reserve: Findings From the Multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular ejection fraction reserve (LVEF-R), defined as stress EF minus rest EF, is a marker for high-risk coronary artery disease in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging, but its prognostic and diagnostic significance in large real-world populations remains incompletely defined. We aimed to analyze the association of LVEF-R with mortality and high-risk obstructive coronary artery disease in a large multicenter cohort.
METHODS: We analyzed 34 976 patients from 13 sites who underwent gated rest and vasodilator stress positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging from the Registry of Flow and Perfusion Imaging for Artificial Intelligence with PET. Associations between LVEF-R and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models. In a subset with invasive coronary angiography (n=6843), the relationship between LVEF-R and angiographic disease was evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 9392 (26.9%) patients had an LVEF-R<0%. Over a median follow-up of 4.1 years, lower LVEF-R demonstrated a graded association with higher mortality. Compared with LVEF-R>5%, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.20 for LVEF-R 0% to 5% ([95% CI, 1.13-1.28]; P<0.001), 1.32 for -5% to 0% ([95% CI, 1.23-1.42]; P<0.001), and 1.38 for ≤-5% ([95% CI, 1.24-1.52]; P<0.001). A negative LVEF-R was also associated with high-risk coronary artery disease, including left main and 3-vessel disease.
CONCLUSIONS: LVEF-R is an independent predictor of mortality, with a graded association between impaired reserve and adverse outcomes. A negative LVEF-R identifies patients with a higher likelihood of multivessel or left-main coronary artery disease, supporting its role as a clinically relevant marker of high-risk disease.

Title: Glutaminolysis Shapes Cardiac Resilience to Stress via Mitochondrial Glutathione.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac reserve is a strong predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable the heart to mount an adaptive response to stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to dissect the specific role of glutaminolysis, a key anaplerotic and redox-supporting pathway, in regulating cardiac reserve.
METHODS: Cardiac reserve was assessed by echocardiography under β-adrenergic stimulation in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase and in wild-type controls. Stable isotope tracing with [U-13C] glutamine was performed in Langendorff-perfused hearts. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of acute glutamine supplementation in healthy volunteers was conducted to evaluate translational relevance (ChiCTR2400082676).
RESULTS: During acute stress, such as exercise or β-adrenergic stimulation, glutaminolysis was rapidly mobilized to supply mitochondrial glutathione, preserving mitochondrial redox homeostasis and sustaining cardiac contractile reserve. Mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase exhibited marked impairments in both contractile reserve and exercise capacity, accompanied by a failure to elevate mitochondrial glutathione and consequent mitochondrial oxidative stress. Chronic exercise training upregulated cardiac glutaminase expression and expanded the mitochondrial glutathione pool, linking this adaptive mechanism to training-induced improvements in cardiac reserve. In humans, acute oral glutamine supplementation enhanced cardiac reserve, as assessed by exercise stress echocardiography, in a placebo-controlled crossover design.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a novel metabolic paradigm in which glutaminolysis functions as a dynamic pathway supporting mitochondrial health and cardiac resilience, and highlight glutamine supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance cardiac reserve.

Title: Outcomes of Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators in Patients Being Considered for Heart Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillators (S-ICD) are an alternative to transvenous devices (TV-ICD) in patients not requiring bradycardia pacing, resynchronization (CRT) or anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP). At our center, S-ICDs are often preferred in patients being considered for heart transplantation (HTx) without pacing/CRT/ATP needs, as their removal post-HTx avoids retained transvenous leads which can preclude MRI surveillance for graft rejection. We assessed outcomes of S-ICDs in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 201 S-ICD implants at our center; July 2016 - March 2025.
RESULTS: We identified 33 patients (22 male; age 46 ± 13 years) who, at time of S-ICD implant, had been referred for HTx evaluation or were referred at any time thereafter. Etiologies were nonischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 18), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (n = 5), ischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 4), congenital heart disease (n = 4), and myocarditis (n = 2). Median follow-up was 296 days [IQR = 72-798]. Two patients died, both non-arrhythmic. Four patients received appropriate S-ICD therapies and three had inappropriate shocks due to P- or T-wave oversensing (TWOS) (n = 2), or a rapidly conducted atrial arrhythmia (n = 1). Three patients, all with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, received transvenous device upgrades: one to CRT-P for disease progression, one to TV-ICD for ATP-terminable ventricular tachycardia and one to TV-ICD due to inappropriate shocks from TWOS. Thirteen patients underwent HTx at median 257 days [IQR = 130-453] post S-ICD; three of whom were bridged with HeartMate 3 LVADs. One LVAD patient needed S-ICD deactivation due to electromagnetic interference. There were no retained device components following HTx and S-ICD extraction.
CONCLUSION: In selected pre-HTx patients, S-ICDs offer arrhythmic protection while avoiding retained leads post-HTx.

Title: Renal Function and 4-Year Outcomes in Edoxaban-Treated Patients: A Sub-Analysis From the ETNA-AF Europe Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants, like edoxaban, are essential in managing atrial fibrillation (AF). The impact of renal function on edoxaban dosages in real-world settings remains unclear. This 4-year ETNA-AF-Europe study follow-up analysis investigated how chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages affect the safety and effectiveness of usual edoxaban doses.
METHODS: ETNA-AF-Europe (NCT02944019) was an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2022 across 776 centres in 10 European countries. Hazard ratios (HR) and annualized event rates were calculated for all-cause death, cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and bleeding events for the overall population and participants stratified by dose (30/60 mg) and CKD stages at baseline.
RESULTS: Of the 13,164 participants in the full analysis set, 9114 participants with CKD (Stage 1, n = 2064; Stage 2, n = 4855; Stage 3, n = 1985; Stage 4, n = 135; missing, n = 75) received label-recommended edoxaban doses. Compared with CKD Stage 1, higher CKD stages were associated with increased risks for stroke (Stage 3: HR [95% CI]: 1.889 [1.240-2.878], p = 0.003) and CV death (HR [95% CI]; Stage 4: 14.450 [8.270-25.247], Stage 3: 4.672 [3.312-6.969], Stage 2: 2.066 [1.394-3.062], all p < 0.001). All-cause death followed a similar trend. After adjusting for age, sex, body weight, CHA2DS2-VASc and modified HAS-BLED scores, most bleeding and effectiveness outcomes showed no nominally significant differences across CKD stages.
CONCLUSIONS: Edoxaban in patients with AF is effective and well tolerated across CKD stages and appropriate label dosing can offset the risk from renal impairment.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Early Outcomes of Harmony Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Implantation in the Middle East: A Single-Center Experience From Saudi Arabia.
Journal: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Significant pulmonary regurgitation (PR) is a common late complication after repair of right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) lesions, potentially leading to right ventricular failure. The Harmony transcatheter pulmonary valve (TPV) was developed for large, native, or patched RVOTs. Although multicenter studies have shown favorable results, regional single-center data, particularly from the Middle East, are scarce. This study reports our initial single-center experience with Harmony TPV implantation, focusing on procedural success, safety, and 1-year outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 10 consecutive patients who underwent Harmony TPV implantation at our institution. Data were collected on baseline characteristics, procedural details, and outcomes. Procedural success, complications, and hemodynamic performance were assessed.
RESULTS: The median age of our population was 15.5 years, and 70% of patients were male. The most common underlying diagnosis was post-tetralogy of Fallot repair (50%). All patients had severe PR at baseline. Technical success was achieved in all patients. There was no mortality. Minor periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients, including minor femoral vein avulsion, fever, ecchymosis, and frequent premature ventricular contractions, all managed conservatively. At 1-year follow-up, freedom from death, moderate/severe PR, mean RVOT gradient >40 mm Hg, or reintervention was 100%. No endocarditis, valve thrombosis, or stent fracture was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This single-center experience from the Middle East demonstrates that Harmony TPV implantation is a feasible and safe procedure with excellent early clinical and echocardiographic outcomes. These findings are consistent with previously published international series and support the adoption of this technology in specialized centers for managing severe PR in patients with complex RVOT anatomy.

Title: Results from a Phase II Single Arm Trial Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Anhydrous Enol-Oxaloacetate on Improving Cognitive Complaints in Breast Cancer Survivors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) affects a substantial proportion of breast cancer survivors (BCS) and effective pharmacologic interventions are lacking. Oxaloacetate (OAA), a naturally occurring metabolic intermediate with glutamate-scavenging, anti-inflammatory, and mitochondrial bioenergetic properties, was evaluated for its safety and preliminary efficacy in improving cognitive complaints in BCS with moderate to severe CRCI.
METHODS: We conducted a single-arm, phase II trial enrolling early-stage BCS who were 12 months to 5 years post-primary treatment and reported significant cognitive complaints on the PROMIS Cognitive Function questionnaire. Participants received oxaloacetate 500 mg orally twice daily for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was improvement in perceived cognitive impairment, measured by the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Cognitive Function Perceived Cognitive Impairment (FACT-Cog PCI) score. Secondary outcomes included fatigue, insomnia, psychological symptoms, physical and mental health-related quality of life, neuropsychological test performance, and safety. Simon's two-stage design with subsequent sequential monitoring was used.
RESULTS: Eighteen participants were enrolled; sixteen completed the intervention. All evaluable participants demonstrated clinically and statistically significant improvement in perceived cognitive impairment (mean FACT-Cog PCI change +26.4 points; p<0.0001), with improvement from the impaired to the normative range. Statistically significant improvements were also observed in total fatigue (p<.0001), mental fatigue (p<.0001), and physical function (p=.0003), with a trend toward improvement in insomnia (p=.09). Neuropsychological testing showed improvements in executive function and processing speed. Oxaloacetate was generally well-tolerated; gastrointestinal symptoms were the most common adverse events, leading to treatment discontinuation in two participants. There were no serious adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: Oxaloacetate treatment led to significant improvements in perceived cognitive impairment, fatigue, and physical functioning among BCS with CRCI, with acceptable tolerability. These findings support further investigation in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial to confirm efficacy.

Title: Comparison of Cumulative Dissipated Energy Between Two Phacoemulsification Systems Using a Modified Flip-and-Chop Technique With Multidirectional Jerking Movement From a Phacoemulsification Handpiece.
Abstract: Introduction The four-dimensional Unity phacoemulsification tip is designed to optimize tip motion and reduce time and energy consumption in cataract surgery. This study highlights a modified flip-and-chop technique with an added multidirectional jerking motion to the phacoemulsification handpiece intraocularly (referred to as the "five-dimensional flip-and-chop") and compares the cumulative dissipated energy (CDE) between the four-dimensional Unity system (Alcon Inc., Geneva, Switzerland) and the torsional Centurion system (Alcon Inc., Geneva, Switzerland) under this technique. Methods This is a retrospective, sequential, non-randomized comparison of 40 consecutive cases of Centurion to 40 consecutive cases of Unity performed by a single surgeon at a single ambulatory surgical suite. The initial cataract density between the groups was compared using optical coherence tomography (OCT) image quality (IQ) values from a single Maestro 2 device (Topcon, Tokyo, Japan). Results The two groups had comparable mean ages, sex distributions, and IQs. The mean CDE was significantly lower in the Unity group (5.39; SD=2.8) than in the Centurion group (8.23; SD=5.9), with p=0.0075. Conclusion Utilizing the modified "five-dimensional flip-and-chop" technique, the four-dimensional Unity system produced significantly lower CDE than the torsional Centurion system. The addition of this technique to the phacoemulsification handpiece may further improve the efficiency of phacoemulsification.

Title: Clinical outcomes of COPD associated with cigarette smoke, biomass smoke, and combined exposure: A retrospective observational study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) related to combined exposure to cigarette and biomass smoke is insufficiently characterized. The aim of this study was to compare exacerbations and chronic respiratory failure (CRF) across smoking-associated, biomass-associated, and combined exposure COPD.
METHODS: In this retrospective, multicenter, observational study, 319 patients with stable COPD were classified into three groups based on exposure history: smoking-associated (n=159), biomass-associated (n=80), and combined cigarette and biomass exposure (n=80). Smoking and biomass exposure histories were retrospectively obtained from medical records. Cigarette exposure was quantified in pack-years, biomass exposure was assessed according to the documented type and duration of household fuel use, and patients with both exposures were classified as the combined-exposure group. Exacerbation frequency, CRF, and pulmonary function tests were evaluated. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, cardiac diseases, sarcopenia, and lung cancer were used to assess the associations of exposure group with annual exacerbation frequency and CRF.
RESULTS: Patients with combined exposure were younger (59.22 ± 10.82 years) compared with those in the smoking-associated (61.37 ± 11.04 years) and biomass-associated groups (63.45 ± 11.92 years, p=0.015). The combined exposure group had lower FEV1 (% predicted: 48.27 ± 10.14 vs 55.28 ± 17.61 and 55.62 ± 11.29; p=0.003) and higher dyspnea scores (mMRC: 2.18 vs 1.39 and 1.88; p<0.001). Exacerbation burden was significantly greater in the combined exposure group, including higher annual exacerbation rates (2.18 ± 0.82 vs 2.08 ± 0.22 and 1.88 ± 0.32; p=0.041) and severe exacerbations (1.78 ± 0.35 vs 1.39 ± 0.18 and 1.20 ± 0.19; p<0.001). CRF was more frequent in the combined-exposure group (26.2% vs 17.0% and 11.2%; p=0.028). In adjusted analyses, combined exposure was independently associated with increased risk of severe exacerbations compared with cigarette smoking alone (AOR=1.89; 95% CI: 1.22-2.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Findings of this study suggest that combined exposure to cigarette and biomass smoke is potentially associated with earlier COPD presentation, increased exacerbation frequency and lower FEV1.

Title: Comparative efficacy and safety of de-escalation, abbreviation, and standard potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based dual antiplatelet therapy strategies after acute coronary syndrome: a network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is the default antiplatelet strategy after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), though de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT and abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy are increasingly adopted to mitigate bleeding risk. However, their relative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Network meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials were performed to compare three guideline-endorsed strategies: (i) short-term potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based DAPT de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT, (ii) abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy, and (iii) standard 12-month potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based DAPT. The primary efficacy endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary efficacy endpoints included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, and stroke. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. The key net clinical endpoint was net adverse clinical events (NACE). PROSPERO (CRD420251144892) Seven randomized controlled trials involving 20 673 patients were included. Both the de-escalation and abbreviation strategies significantly reduced major bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.25-0.74, P = 0.002; and RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.33-0.58, P < 0.001, respectively) and NACE (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.70, P < 0.001; and RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.61-0.84, P < 0.001, respectively) without increasing MACE or other ischaemic outcomes. Indirect comparison indicated that de-escalation vs. abbreviation strategies demonstrated comparable MACE, NACE, and bleeding outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Following ACS, both de-escalation to clopidogrel-based DAPT and abbreviated DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy effectively reduce bleeding risk without compromising ischaemic protection. Given that the only available comparison between the two simplified strategies was indirect and showed comparable MACE and NACE outcomes, further research is warranted to determine the optimal individualized approach.

Title: Perioperative Blood Management in General Surgery: Recent Advances, Current Limitations, and the Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Patient blood management (PBM) is a patient-centered approach to blood use that aligns with modern medical practice. It is based on multidisciplinary collaboration and evidence-based medicine. Its aim is to improve clinical outcomes by correcting preoperative anemia, reducing perioperative blood loss, standardizing transfusion practices, and optimizing the management of coagulation function. Patients undergoing general surgery, particularly complex liver surgery or gastrointestinal cancer surgery, often face preoperative anemia, intraoperative bleeding, increased transfusion requirements, and postoperative coagulation abnormalities. These factors make perioperative blood management more complex. This narrative review searched PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) for relevant studies published over the past 10 years. It summarizes recent advances, current limitations, and challenges in the clinical translation of perioperative blood management in general surgery. This review focuses on the assessment and management of preoperative anemia, bleeding control and hemostatic strategies, transfusion management, coagulation monitoring, and thrombotic risk management. It also discusses recent advances and current limitations in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for risk prediction, clinical decision support, and individualized management. Current evidence suggests that PBM may help optimize perioperative care in general surgery. AI/ML may also support clinical decision-making by predicting bleeding risk, estimating transfusion requirements, and stratifying thrombotic risk. However, studies specifically focusing on general surgery patients remain limited. Most available evidence comes from cardiac surgery, orthopedics, or other surgical populations. In addition, current prediction models still have several limitations, including insufficient external validation, a lack of prospective evaluation, and limited interpretability. Therefore, these models should currently be used only as tools to support clinical judgment. Therefore, future studies should include more multicenter prospective research in general surgery populations. AI/ML-assisted decision support should also be further explored within standardized PBM pathways to improve the precision and standardization of perioperative blood management in general surgery.

Title: Recent advances in loco-ablative therapies for liver cancers.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most pervasive form of liver cancer worldwide, with its incidence rising due to lifestyle trends. The majority of HCC cases cannot be treated surgically; hence, loco-ablative therapies are required. Classically, radiofrequency ablation (RFA) has been the loco-ablative therapy most often selected for nonresectable HCC. However, due to technological advances and a better understanding of HCC's pathophysiology, new loco-ablative therapies have been developed for HCC. These novel techniques offer an alternative to surgery and RFA depending on each patient's clinical presentation, such as the number and size of nodules. Moreover, they present different benefits and potential clinical complications; therefore, knowledge of available techniques is important to allow clinicians to select the most suitable therapy for their patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review was carried out to summarize the existing loco-ablative therapies for HCC, as well as to investigate emerging loco-ablative therapies for HCC. The benefits, drawbacks, indication for, and mechanism of each technique are outlined.
CONCLUSIONS: The frontier of locoregional HCC treatment is shifting toward histotripsy and combinations of existing locoregional therapies with immunotherapy. The importance of a multidisciplinary team is highlighted. Nonetheless, there remains a role for surgical resection of HCC and classical locoregional therapies such as RFA, as there is a lack of large-scale randomised controlled trials investigating the role of novel locoregional techniques for treating HCC patients.

Title: Association and Discriminative Performance of a Bilirubin-D-Dimer-Albumin Index for LVEF <45% in Patients with Heart Failure: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate identification of reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is important for risk stratification and management of patients with heart failure (HF). Because HF involves multiple interrelated pathophysiological processes, a combination of biomarkers may provide information beyond that offered by individual markers. This study evaluated the association and discriminatory performance of the bilirubin-D-dimer-albumin (BDA) Index for identifying LVEF <45% and compared its performance with that of NT-proBNP.
METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective study, 338 patients with HF were categorized according to echocardiographic LVEF as <45% (n=149) or ≥45% (n=189). The BDA Index was calculated as ln(total bilirubin [µmol/L]) × ln(D-dimer [ng/mL]) / albumin [g/L]. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and DeLong's test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between the BDA Index and LVEF <45%, with internal validation performed using 1000 bootstrap samples and 10-fold cross-validation. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was used to assess the potential clinical utility of the model.
RESULTS: The BDA Index was significantly higher in patients with LVEF <45% (P<0.001). Its AUC was 0.902 (95% CI, 0.870-0.934), compared with 0.773 (95% CI, 0.723-0.823) for NT-proBNP (DeLong's test, P<0.001). At the Youden-derived cutoff of 0.435, sensitivity and specificity were 87.9% and 78.3%, respectively. After multivariable adjustment, each 0.1-unit increase in the BDA Index was associated with LVEF <45% (OR, 4.65; 95% CI, 2.94-7.36; P<0.001). Adding the BDA Index significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ2=73.44, df=1, P<0.001) and increased the AUC from 0.873 to 0.934. Internal validation yielded an optimism-adjusted AUC of 0.908, while 10-fold cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.901. DCA showed greater estimated net benefit for the model incorporating the BDA Index across threshold probabilities of 5%-80%.
CONCLUSION: In this single-centre retrospective cohort, the BDA Index showed good discriminatory performance for identifying LVEF <45% and provided additional information beyond NT-proBNP and other clinical and laboratory variables. Prospective multicentre studies with independent external validation are needed to assess its reproducibility, calibration, and potential clinical utility.

Title: Low-Dose Epidural Hydromorphone as an Adjunct to Ropivacaine for Intraoperative Visceral Traction Pain During Elective Cesarean Delivery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Visceral traction during cesarean delivery may cause pain, nausea, and autonomic activation despite an adequate neuraxial block. We evaluated whether adding 0.3 mg epidural hydromorphone to ropivacaine altered patient-reported pain and clinically relevant traction responses across predefined perioperative phases.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 96 women undergoing elective cesarean delivery were randomized 1:1 to epidural hydromorphone or saline. The registered primary outcome domains were visual analog scale (VAS) pain score and heart rate variability (HRV) across five time points. Other prespecified clinical measures included clinician-rated traction response, maternal adverse events, and neonatal outcomes. The protocol-specified repeated-measures analysis was used for longitudinal pain; abdominal exploration (T2) was selected after registration as the focal phase for detailed reporting.
RESULTS: All 96 women completed the trial. The longitudinal pain analysis showed a group-by-time interaction (Greenhouse-Geisser corrected p=0.008; participant-level randomization-based permutation p=0.009). At the post-registration focal comparison during abdominal exploration, median (IQR) VAS was 1.65 (0.70-2.60) with hydromorphone and 1.90 (0.78-3.92) with saline (nominal Mann-Whitney p=0.039). Clinician-rated traction grade favored hydromorphone (trend p=0.003). Nausea or vomiting occurred in 3/48 (6.2%) versus 12/48 (25.0%) women (risk ratio 0.25, 95% CI 0.08-0.83; p=0.022). For the registered HRV domain, the interaction for ln(LF/HF), selected after registration as the principal reported metric, was not significant (p=0.442). No maternal respiratory depression occurred, and neonatal outcomes showed no material between-group differences.
CONCLUSION: Low-dose epidural hydromorphone added to ropivacaine was associated with a different longitudinal pain profile and fewer episodes of intraoperative nausea or vomiting during elective cesarean delivery. Post hoc pain-distribution and exploratory physiological findings require prospective confirmation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400094749; registered December 26, 2024, before enrollment.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Case Reports; Clinical Trial

Title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
Abstract:
AIMS: The expected clinical and functional trajectory after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with left ventricular dysfunction remains uncertain. Recent trials have highlighted substantial heterogeneity in both clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement, underscoring the need for improved post-PCI prognostic risk stratification in this high-risk population. This study aimed to develop machine learning models predicting clinical outcomes and LVEF improvement after PCI in patients with reduced LVEF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective single-centre study included adults undergoing PCI between 2004 and 2025 with baseline LVEF <45%. Two CatBoost models were developed using 53 routinely available pre- and intra-procedural predictors. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or coronary artery bypass grafting. The secondary endpoint was an absolute LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and enrichment analysis. The dataset included 3336 procedures from 2793 patients (median LVEF 35%). For the primary endpoint (n = 2152; event rate 37.5%), the model achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83) and a PR-AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.63-0.77), with event rates of 83.7% in the highest-risk decile and 9.3% in the lowest-risk decile. For LVEF improvement (n = 2551; 34.7% improved), performance was moderate (AUC 0.73), with enrichment to 76.9% in the highest-probability decile.
CONCLUSION: Machine learning models using routinely available patient and procedural data enabled meaningful prognostic stratification in patients with left ventricular dysfunction undergoing PCI, supporting individualized estimation of clinical and functional trajectories after revascularization.

Title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).
METHODS: This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM.
RESULTS: Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage (p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6-46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages (p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase.
CONCLUSION: Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

Title: Cumulative exposure and trajectories of cardiovascular health in relation to hepatic steatosis risk in children: a 6-year longitudinal study.
Under-recognition of metabolic syndrome in North West London (2000-2023): a 23-year retrospective analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Despite the rising prevalence of obesity, hypertension, dyslipidaemia and glucose dysregulation, MetS remains inconsistently recognised and coded within electronic health records (EHRs). We aimed to determine the extent of under-recognition of MetS within North West London (NWL) over a 23-year period.
METHODS: The Discover-NOW London Secure Data Environment dataset was retrospectively analysed between 1 January 2000 and 31 July 2023. Adults aged ≥18 years were identified as having MetS if coded within EHRs or if they met ≥3 of 5 American Heart Association (AHA) 2005 diagnostic criteria. An Extended AHA definition incorporating BMI and HbA1c was also applied to reflect routine clinical practice.
RESULTS: Among 2 096 480 adults registered in NWL during the study period, 975 individuals (0.04%) had a clinician-coded diagnosis of MetS. In contrast, 594 325 individuals (21.2%) met AHA-defined criteria and 875 993 (31.3%) met Extended AHA-defined criteria. Women, individuals of Black or Black British ethnicity, and those from more deprived areas were under-represented in the coded cohort relative to algorithm-defined cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Metabolic syndrome is substantially under-recorded within routine clinical coding in NWL. Recognition of the true prevalence of MetS within healthcare datasets may support improved risk stratification, enable population-level surveillance, and facilitate evaluation of MetS-related morbidity and healthcare utilisation.

Title: Stroke After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Contemporary Valves: Insights From the OCEAN-TAVI Registry.
Journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a serious complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), even with contemporary devices. The objective of the study was to evaluate the incidence, predictors, and prognosis of in-hospital stroke in patients undergoing TAVR with contemporary valve platforms.
METHODS: We analyzed 5123 patients from the multicenter OCEAN-TAVI registry who underwent TAVR with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA, Evolut FX, or Navitor between May 2022 and December 2024. Stroke incidence across valve types was compared using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Predictors were assessed using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: In-hospital stroke occurred in 2.5% of patients. After IPTW adjustment, stroke incidence differed among valve types: 1.7% of patients treated with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR), 4.5% with Evolut FX, and 2.4% with Navitor (p = 0.044). Disabling stroke was more frequent with Evolut FX (2.5%) compared with S3UR (0.4%) and Navitor (0.7%; p < 0.001). Self-expanding valve use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.64, 95% CI 1.67-4.16 for Evolut FX; aOR 2.37, 95% CI 1.35-4.18 for Navitor; both vs. S3UR), prior stroke (aOR 1.83, 95% CI 1.19-2.73), reduced renal function, and nontransfemoral access (aOR 2.11, 95% CI 1.29-3.45) were independently associated with in-hospital stroke. One-year survival was significantly lower among patients with stroke than among those without stroke (73.0% vs. 90.3%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital stroke remains an important complication after contemporary TAVR and is associated with worse clinical outcomes. Differences in stroke incidence across valve types were observed, highlighting the need for improved risk assessment.

Title: Clinical impact of deep-vein thrombosis screening in recipients of lung transplants: A contemporary single-center study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) events are common after lung transplantation and can have a significant impact on morbidity and mortality. Our objective was to assess the impact of a deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) screening program on VTE incidence and clinical outcomes in recipients of lung transplants.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of all adults who received lung transplants (≥18 years) at our center between May 2020 and June 2024, excluding multiorgan transplants. Patients were divided into prescreening (May 2020 to June 2022) and screening (June 2022 to June 2024) groups. We evaluated VTE incidence, graft function, bleeding complications, and survival.
RESULTS: There were a total of 287 patients in the study, 130 in the prescreening group and 157 in the screening group. DVT incidence was significantly greater in the screening group compared with the prescreening group (54.1% vs 20.7%; P < .001). There was no difference in the incidence of pulmonary embolus, graft function by percent expiratory volume in 1 second predicted out to 1 year, overall survival out to 1 year, nor bleeding complications between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: DVT screening in recipients of lung transplants detects clinically insignificant DVTs and may introduce potential harm from overtreatment. The use of DVT-screening programs in recipients of lung transplants should be reconsidered.

Title: The GLIDE Score: One-Year Outcomes Following Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The GLIDE score is a 5-point imaging-based tool to predict residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). Lower residual TR is associated with better prognosis, but long-term associations between GLIDE score and outcomes are uncertain.
METHODS: We performed an analysis of a multinational registry of patients undergoing T-TEER for severe or greater TR from January 2017 to November 2022. GLIDE scores were assessed using preprocedural transesophageal echocardiography. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year, and the secondary endpoints included TR grade of moderate or less at 1 year.
RESULTS: In 336 patients (81 [interquartile range 77-84] years; 44.6% male, TRI-SCORE 5 [interquartile range 4-6]), survival and HFH follow-up at 1 year was available in 90.5%. One-year mortality was 15.8%. The GLIDE score was significantly associated with the combined primary endpoint (hazard ratio: 1.20; 95% CI 1.03-1.40; p = 0.019), even after adjustment for TRI-SCORE. Freedom from death or HFH was significantly higher among patients with GLIDE scores ≤1 compared to those ≥2 (p = 0.032). Of the 251 1-year survivors, follow-up echocardiography was available in 170 (68%). The GLIDE score predicted 1-year TR severity (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.73; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with moderate or less residual TR achieved in 80.6%, 54.9%, and 18.8% of patients with GLIDE scores of 0-1, 2-3, and ≥4, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The GLIDE score is associated with 1-year survival and HFH after T-TEER as well as ≤ moderate TR.

Title: Endoscopic versus open vein harvesting technique and 2-year saphenous vein graft patency: A subanalysis of the Newton-CABG CardioLink-5 randomized trial.
Machine Perfusion in Split Liver Transplantation: A Scoping Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Split liver transplantation (SLT) maximizes donor organ utilization but faces challenges with ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI). Machine perfusion techniques, including hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE), dual HOPE (DHOPE), and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP), may enhance graft viability and expand the donor pool. This scoping review maps existing clinical and experimental evidence on machine perfusion in SLT, examining benefits, feasibility, outcomes, and knowledge gaps.
METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute manual guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through September 3, 2025, plus gray literature (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, Google Scholar). Studies exploring machine perfusion techniques in liver splitting of human or animal grafts, with or without transplantation, were included.
RESULTS: After screening 958 records, 38 studies were included (29 primary studies, 9 reviews). Among primary studies, 84 clinical transplant cases using machine perfusion were identified (including 2 cases with unspecified perfusion modality); however, this number may not represent unique patients because of possible overlap between same-center cohorts. HOPE (7 studies, 40 cases) was supported by preliminary comparative data suggesting reduced IRI versus static cold storage, with 1 cohort study showing lower postreperfusion syndrome rates (13.3% versus 47.1%, P = 0.04) and reduced IRI scores (3 versus 4, P = 0.03). NMP (16 studies, 34 cases) enabled extended preservation up to 25 h with 100% short-term graft survival in case series. DHOPE (4 studies, 8 cases) reported feasibility for complex full-left/full-right splitting. Evidence was limited by small sample sizes (median n = 2, range 1-26), short follow-up (maximum 18 mo, median 6 mo), absence of randomized trials, and potential publication bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Machine perfusion remains an investigational strategy in SLT. Preliminary evidence suggests HOPE may reduce IRI and NMP may provide logistical advantages through extended preservation. However, evidence derives entirely from small observational studies without randomization. Multicenter prospective studies with standardized protocols, longer follow-ups, and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed.

Title: Effects of exercise-related interventions on blood pressure and related variables among individuals with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to global cardiovascular disease burden and premature mortality. Although pharmacological treatment is effective, long-term Blood Pressure (BP) control remains suboptimal for many patients, highlighting the importance of non-pharmacological strategies such as physical exercise. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of exercise training interventions for improving BP outcomes among adults with hypertension. While a limited number of included randomized controlled trials involved participants with prehypertension, the review primary focus was hypertension management.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across five electronic databases (Scopus, AMED, MEDLINE, PUBMED, and CINAHL) to identify relevant clinical trials. A small number of trials involving participants with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension were retained where they met the predefined eligibility criteria and contributed to the overall evidence regarding elevated BP management. Methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the PEDro scale. Data were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis, and pooled effects were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical heterogeneity was evaluated using the I2 statistic. Meta-analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5. Structured Narrative synthesis was performed where meta-analysis was not feasible.
RESULTS: A total of 26 studies that recruited 1,576 participants met the inclusion criteria and were included in the review. Majority of the studies were of moderate-to-good methodological quality (∼70%). Aerobic training consistently produced statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in both SBP (SMD: -0.97; 95% CI -1.46 to -0.47; p = 0.0001) and DBP (SMD: -1.55; 95% CI -2.19 to -0.90; p < 0.00001). Combined aerobic and resistance training also resulted in significant reductions in SBP (SMD: -1.11; 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.11; p = 0.03) and DBP (SMD: -1.25; 95% CI: -2.24 to -0.27; p = 0.01), suggesting potential additive or complementary effects of multimodal exercise interventions. Resistance training alone demonstrated a significant and large reduction in DBP but showed inconsistent and non-significant effects on SBP. In addition to blood pressure reduction, several studies reported improvements in secondary outcomes, including cardiorespiratory fitness, heart rate variability, body composition, inflammatory markers, physical performance, and quality of life. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed across most pooled analyses, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests that aerobic exercise, either alone or combined with resistance training, is associated with some beneficial reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure among individuals with hypertension.

Title: A Comparative Review of Performance and Concurrent Cardiac Rhythm Assessment Across Home Sleep Apnea Testing Devices.
Abstract: Home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) is now widely used in place of in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) for the evaluation of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), but published performance varies across FDA-cleared devices. This narrative review aimed to summarize the published performance of FDA-cleared Type III HSAT devices currently marketed in the United States and compare their labeled capabilities for assessing SDB over multiple nights and concurrently evaluating cardiac rhythm and atrial fibrillation (AF) burden. A search of the FDA 510(k) database identified 68 devices with MNR as the primary product code that were cleared after August 1, 2016, or were cleared earlier but released for sale after that date. There were 13 devices that met these criteria and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) criteria for a Type III HSAT. For each device, sensitivity and specificity against PSG, scored under American Academy of Sleep Medicine Rule 1B (4% oxygen desaturation), were obtained from the FDA 510(k) Summary or a peer-reviewed validation study. Balanced accuracy (the mean of sensitivity and specificity) was calculated at apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds of 5, 15, and 30 events per hour. Five devices were excluded from the comparison and are reported for information only because their performance data were not reported using a methodology consistent with that of the other devices: they used a different scoring rule or severity threshold, reported central apnea detection only, or relied on a less credible source for the reported data. Among the remaining eight devices, reported sample sizes ranged from 30 to 476 subjects. All eight reported performance at AHI ≥ 15, five at AHI ≥ 5, and three at AHI ≥ 30. At AHI ≥ 15, balanced accuracy was highest for AcuPebble Ox200 (Acurable Limited, London, UK) (96.5), followed by WatchPAT SW (Itamar Medical, Caesarea, Israel) (94.0) and RX-1 Sleep (Rhythm Express, St. Paul, MN) (92.2). RX-1 Sleep reported the highest balanced accuracy at AHI ≥ 5 (90.9) and AHI ≥ 30 (92.9). These comparisons are indirect and descriptive: each device was validated against PSG in a separate cohort, none was evaluated against another device in the same patients, and between-device differences were not statistically tested. Prospective head-to-head studies against a common reference standard would be needed to confirm differences in relative performance. Among the devices compared, RX-1 Sleep system provides an aid for concurrent assessment of SDB and AF burden in a single test. Other devices can flag or record rhythm information but cannot quantify AF burden. Together with its published performance and multi-night testing capability, this may offer clinical benefit given the severity-dependent association between SDB and AF burden and the elevated cardiovascular risk observed when the two conditions coexist.

Title: Saphenous vein grafts from thigh versus calf: Comparison of angiographic patency and clinical outcomes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study compared angiographic patency and clinical outcomes between patients who received saphenous vein (SV) grafts from the upper leg (UL) and those who received grafts from the lower leg (LL) for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: A total of 1630 patients who received primary isolated off-pump CABG using the SV harvested via the no-touch technique from the UL (UL group, n = 203) or the LL (LL group, n = 1427) were enrolled in this study. Propensity score matching was performed, and 202 pairs were matched. Early, 1-year, and 5-year graft angiograms were obtained for 99.5%, 85.7%, and 31.2% of the cohort, respectively. The median follow-up duration was 85.8 months. The primary outcome was midterm angiographic patency, and the secondary outcomes were midterm clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: There was no significant difference in baseline characteristics between the matched groups.
