DCM etiology was idiopathic in 42%, genetic in 22%, and myocarditis-associated in 36%. There was no procedural mortality. Overall survival was 90% and 72% achieved transplant-free functional recovery. Following PAB, magnetic resonance imaging-derived LVEF improved from 19% ± 7% to 56% ± 11%, and LVEDD z-scores decreased from +6.3 to +1 (P < .001). In 33 patients, recovery was sustained over a median follow-up of 7 years, including 15 patients with stable LV function for over 10 years.
CONCLUSIONS: In infants and young children with severe LV-DCM, PAB is associated with high long-term survival, sustained transplant-free recovery, and durable reverse cardiac remodeling.

Title: Combined Transarterial Embolization and Percutaneous CT-Guided Cryoablation of Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
Abstract: Purpose The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and oncological outcomes of combined transarterial embolization followed by percutaneous CT-guided cryoablation for renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Material and methods This retrospective single-center study included 24 patients with 24 biopsy-proven RCC who underwent transarterial embolization followed by percutaneous CT-guided cryoablation between May 2019 and August 2025. Procedural parameters, tumor characteristics, and oncological outcomes, as well as overall survival (OS), were assessed and analyzed. Results The mean tumor diameter was 3.9 ± 1.4 cm, and the mean ablation time was 26 ± 4.9 minutes. No major peri-procedural complications were observed. Early post-procedural imaging demonstrated initial complete ablation in 23 out of 24 tumors, equating to a rate of 95.8%. The rate of local tumor progression was 8.3% (2/24) and the rate of distant progression was 12.5% (3/24), which all occurred in patients without pre-existing metastatic disease. None of the patients with pre-existing metastatic disease developed local or distant disease progression during follow-up. The mean OS was 3.1 years (95% CI: 2.4-3.7) with a one- and two-year OS rate of 95% and 69.1%, respectively. Conclusion Combined transarterial embolization followed by percutaneous CT-guided cryoablation appears to be a safe and feasible treatment approach for selected patients with RCC, particularly those with limited surgical options.

Title: Descending aortic translocation for aerodigestive vascular compression.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with complex vascular ring anomalies can present with symptoms of esophageal and airway compression, occasionally persisting despite relief of the vascular ring, due to residual compression from the aorta. We report our early experience with descending aortic translocation to address aerodigestive vascular compression.
METHODS: This is a retrospective single-center review of patients undergoing descending aortic translocation. The operation involves dividing the distal aortic arch on cardiopulmonary bypass, relocating the descending aorta beneath the carina and right pulmonary artery, and anastomosis to the posterior aspect of the ascending aorta, thereby entirely relieving compression on the aerodigestive tract. Concomitant esophageal mobilization and tracheopexies are performed as needed.
RESULTS: From 2020 to 2023, 15 patients underwent descending aortic translocation. Anatomic variants included hairpin aorta (n = 2), circumflex aorta (n = 4), midline descending aorta (n = 7), and bowstring aorta (n = 2). Median age was 2 years. Preoperatively, most patients (80%) had mixed esophageal and airway symptoms and had undergone at least 1 prior operation (60%). Intraoperative bronchoscopy revealed improved airway patency for all patients. Postoperatively, 93% of patients had relief of respiratory symptoms, and 79% of patients had improved dysphagia. Postoperative complications included neurologic event (n = 1) with full resolution, right pulmonary artery compression requiring stenting (n = 1), and need for reoperation (n = 2).
CONCLUSIONS: Descending aortic translocation is a novel approach that can provide symptomatic relief of aerodigestive compression related to complex aortic anomalies. For patients with persistent symptoms after initial vascular ring repair, ongoing aortic compression may need to be addressed, thus also raising the question of whether descending aortic translocation should be considered as a first-line therapy.

Title: Five-year outcomes of chordal replacement therapy for primary mitral regurgitation: The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study is a prospective, first-in-human early feasibility study evaluating the technical feasibility, the long-term safety, and device durability of a novel chordal replacement system for the treatment of primary degenerative mitral regurgitation.
METHODS: Five patients with symptomatic severe primary degenerative mitral regurgitation attributable to isolated central posterior leaflet prolapse or flail underwent surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system through a left atrial approach under cardiopulmonary bypass combined with ring annuloplasty. Clinical and transthoracic echocardiographic follow-up was prospectively performed at discharge and through 60 months.
RESULTS: Technical device success was achieved in all patients. Mitral regurgitation was reduced to none or trace immediately after implantation and remained stable throughout the 5-year follow-up. No device-related major adverse events, structural device failure, implant dislodgement, chordal rupture, reoperation, or rehospitalization occurred. Reverse cardiac remodeling was observed, including reduction in left ventricular end-diastolic diameter and left atrial volume, whereas left ventricular function remained preserved during long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system was simple to perform and demonstrated excellent long-term technical durability and sustained clinical performance over 5 years. These findings support further clinical evaluation of this technology and the ongoing development of a fully transcatheter transseptal delivery platform.

Title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype is associated with postmyectomy change in diastolic function measured by artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diastolic dysfunction may persist after septal myectomy for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, contributing to residual or recurrent symptoms. To better understand postoperative diastolic function, we assessed the association between preoperative obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotypic characteristics and change in artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram determined diastolic function, previously shown to quantify diastolic function.
METHODS: We analyzed 166 consecutive patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergoing septal myectomy with prospective artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram diastolic function data. Participants were classified as improved diastolic function (improved grade or persistently normal filling pressure) or persistent diastolic dysfunction (worsened grade or persistently high filling pressure).
RESULTS: The study population was 41% female with a median age of 59 years. There was no significant difference in baseline clinical characteristics between patients with improved diastolic function or persistent artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram diastolic dysfunction. Patients with worsened postoperative diastolic dysfunction by artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram had a greater left atrial volume index (P < .01), a greater left ventricular mass index (P < .01), a higher medial E/e' ratio (P < .01), and increased posterior wall thickness (P < .01) compared with those with improved or normal filling pressure grades by artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram. All-cause mortality was low with no significant difference between artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram diastolic function groups (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.14-2.06).
CONCLUSIONS: Change in artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram diastolic function is associated with echocardiographic predictors of diastolic dysfunction in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients undergoing septal myectomy. Patients with an advanced obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype preoperatively may be less likely to experience improvement in diastolic function after septal myectomy based on artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram diastolic grade changes.

Title: Coronary sinus lactate at reperfusion: A predictor of atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study explored the association of coronary sinus (CS) lactate levels with POAF after CABG.
METHODS: This was a single-center prospective cohort study of patients without a history of atrial fibrillation undergoing isolated CABG (December 2024 to February 2026). CS lactate was sampled before initiation of cardiopulmonary bypass (pre-CPB), before cross-clamp removal (pre-XC), and after cross-clamp removal (post-XC). POAF was defined as electrocardiogram-documented atrial fibrillation treated with amiodarone during the index hospitalization. Restricted cubic splines were used to define a binary cutoff of post-XC CS lactate at >3 mmol/L. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between CS lactate elevation and POAF.
RESULTS: Of the 94 patients included, POAF occurred in 24 patients (26%). Patients with POAF were older and more commonly male but had similar median CPB time and XC duration. Patients with a post-XC lactate >3 mmol/L (n = 13/94, 14%) had significantly greater rates of POAF compared with those without lactate elevation (62% vs 20%, P = .001). After risk adjustment, post-XC lactate >3 mmol/L was associated with a 11.7-fold increase in odds of POAF (P = .010). Increasing age was also linked to greater likelihood of POAF. There was no significant association of POAF with CPB time, XC duration, pre-CPB CS lactate, or pre-XC CS lactate.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated CS lactate after cardiac reperfusion was associated with increased likelihood of POAF. Our findings suggest that CS lactate may be used to guide POAF prophylaxis.

Title: Postoperative changes in QRS duration and long-term mortality after septal myectomy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether change in QRS duration (ΔQRS), defined as postoperative QRS duration minus preoperative QRS duration, after septal myectomy for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) has prognostic significance for all-cause mortality.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of patients with oHCM who underwent transaortic septal myectomy between July 23, 2009, and July 30, 2020, with available preoperative and early postoperative (days 4-7) electrocardiography (ECG) data. Patients with a preoperative or postoperative permanent pacemaker were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox models were adjusted for age, sex, operative time, major concomitant surgery, and preoperative right bundle branch block. ECG analyses examined preoperative QRS duration, ΔQRS (postoperative minus preoperative QRS), and, in exploratory models, postoperative left bundle branch block (LBBB) and absolute postoperative QRS duration.
RESULTS: Among 1143 patients (1141 in complete-case multivariable analyses), the mean preoperative QRS duration was 129.5 ± 25.4 ms and increased modestly postoperatively (133.5 ± 26.0 ms); the mean ΔQRS was 4.0 ± 12.8 ms. A total of 122 deaths occurred during follow-up. Preoperative QRS duration was not associated with mortality (hazard ration [HR] per 10 ms, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94-1.09; P = .78). In contrast, greater ΔQRS was independently associated with higher mortality (HR per 10 ms, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.01-1.34; P = .037), including after adjustment for preoperative QRS duration. Threshold analyses demonstrated increased risk with ΔQRS ≥0 ms (HR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.17-3.03; P = .009) and ΔQRS ≥10 ms (HR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68; P = .001). Absolute postoperative QRS duration ≥150 ms was not associated with mortality (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.76-1.71; P = .52). In exploratory comparison models, ΔQRS showed a stronger and more consistent association with mortality compared to postoperative LBBB or absolute postoperative QRS duration.
CONCLUSIONS: ΔQRS following transaortic septal myectomy for oHCM was independently associated with all-cause mortality. In exploratory comparison models, ΔQRS showed a stronger and more consistent association with mortality compared to postoperative LBBB or absolute postoperative QRS duration. ΔQRS may represent a simple, clinically available marker to enhance postoperative risk stratification following septal myectomy for oHCM.

Title: Health economic and hospital resource use in isolated mitral valve repair in more than 8000 patients: Robotic versus nonrobotic approaches.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the health economics and hospital resource use in isolated mitral valve repair (MVr) in patients undergoing robotic versus nonrobotic surgical approaches.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Premier Healthcare Database for patients who underwent isolated MVr surgery from 2019 to 2024. Hospital chargemaster data was text mined for "robotic," and patient and procedure characteristic and outcomes were stratified by robotic versus traditional surgical approaches. Differences in outcomes (MVr hospitalization cost, intensive care unit [ICU] days, length of stay, operating room time, prolonged ventilation, and 30-day cardiovascular [CV] readmissions) were estimated using generalized linear modeling with adjustment for patient, procedure, and hospital characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 8025 patients received an isolated MVr (mean age 57.8 ± 17.7 years, 39.4% female). Overall, 780 (9.7%) of the procedures were performed robotically, with robotic use generally increasing each year from 7.7% in 2019 to 14.7% in 2024. Compared with traditional (nonrobotic) surgery, robotic cases cost 12% more ($57,678 robotic vs $51,530 nonrobotic, P < .0001). However, patients who underwent robotic surgery spent 14% less time in the ICU (2.4 vs 2.8 days, P < .0001) and 16% less time in the hospital overall (5.7 vs 6.8 days, P < .0001). Robot use was also associated with lower 30-day CV readmission rates (3.1% vs 4.9%, P = .0215). There was no statistical difference in operating room time or prolonged ventilation use.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic use in isolated MVr procedures has increased ∼7% over the last 5 years. This signals ongoing physician and hospital adoption of robotic use in MVr. The use of innovative robotic interventions comes at an increased cost to the hospital but may be associated with procedural efficiencies, including shorter ICU days and shorter overall hospital stays, as well as lower 30-day CV readmission rates, which may have important clinical and economic benefits for patients and health care systems.

Title: Development and multicenter validation of a machine learning model for predicting in-hospital postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly surgical patients: the critical role of intraoperative hemodynamic disturbances and blood transfusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is a rare but life-threatening complication in elderly surgical patients. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for predicting IHCA and to identify key perioperative risk factors.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients aged ≥65 years who underwent non-cardiac surgery at six tertiary hospitals between January 2020 and January 2025. Clinical, laboratory, and perioperative variables were collected. Five machine learning algorithms, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), were developed and compared. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, cross-validation, and external validation. SHAP analysis was applied to interpret the optimal model.
RESULTS: Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.967 and 0.960 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. It also achieved the lowest Brier score and the highest clinical net benefit. External validation confirmed excellent discrimination (AUC=0.971) and calibration. SHAP analysis identified advanced age, intraoperative tachycardia, intraoperative hypotension, intraoperative blood transfusion, intraoperative hypoxemia, elevated postoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide, lactate, and D-dimer levels as the most important predictors of IHCA.
CONCLUSION: An interpretable XGBoost-based model demonstrated excellent performance for predicting postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly patients. The identified risk factors reflected perioperative vulnerability, intraoperative hemodynamic instability, and postoperative physiological deterioration.

Title: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected pulmonary embolism.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize pleuroparenchymal abnormalities identified on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in cancer patients investigated for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) and to compare imaging findings between patients with and without confirmed PE.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 113 consecutive cancer patients who underwent CTPA for suspected acute PE between January 2022 and January 2026. Radiology reports and electronic medical records were reviewed for demographic data, malignancy type and stage, PE-related imaging characteristics, and pleural and pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities. Imaging findings were compared between PE-positive and PE-negative groups. An exploratory multivariable model with a restricted set of imaging predictors was constructed to limit overfitting, with correction for multiple comparisons and bootstrap-based internal validation. Exploratory subgroup analyses by malignancy type and disease burden were also performed.
RESULTS: PE was confirmed in 32 patients (28.3%). The median age was 59 years (IQR, 51-65), and 42.5% were female. The highest PE prevalence was observed in gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and thoracic malignancies. At nominal testing, infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity was more frequent in PE-positive patients (12.5% vs. 1.2%; OR, 11.43; p = 0.022), whereas ground-glass opacity (15.6% vs. 35.8%; OR, 0.33; p = 0.041) and interstitial/septal change (3.1% vs. 25.9%; OR, 0.09; p = 0.007) were less frequent. None remained statistically significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q = 0.133, 0.166, and 0.082, respectively). The parsimonious model had an apparent AUROC of 0.707 and an optimism-adjusted AUROC of 0.699, with acceptable grouped calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.522). No exploratory cancer-subgroup comparison met q < 0.05.
CONCLUSIONS: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities are highly prevalent in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE; however, most findings are nonspecific. Infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity generated the strongest exploratory PE-associated signal, but no individual imaging comparison survived multiplicity correction and model estimates remained imprecise. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

Title: A Novel Insight Into Luspatercept: Therapeutic Implications in Myelodysplastic Syndrome Patients With Elevated Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure.
Abstract: Luspatercept enhances late-stage erythroid maturation by sequestering transforming growth factor-β superfamily ligands and attenuating pathological signaling, with a mechanism highly analogous to that of sotatercept, a breakthrough therapeutic agent for pulmonary hypertension (PH). Despite this solid mechanistic basis, the potential vascular and prognostic effects of luspatercept in PH patients remain largely uncharacterized. This retrospective proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate the impact of luspatercept on pulmonary artery pressure and surrogate prognostic markers, and to explore its novel therapeutic potential in patients with increased pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP). We retrospectively analyzed serial echocardiographic parameters among patients with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) who received luspatercept treatment, focusing on individuals with elevated baseline PASP. Dynamic changes in cardiopulmonary indicators and laboratory biomarkers were comprehensively compared before and after intervention. A total of five MDS patients with elevated baseline PASP were enrolled in the final analysis. Although formal statistical comparisons failed to reach significance, which was largely attributable to the limited sample size, consistent clinically beneficial improvements were observed after luspatercept treatment. The median PASP decreased from 62.0 (IQR 14) mmHg at baseline to 33.0 (IQR 18.5) mmHg following treatment. Parallel reductions in N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and uric acid levels were identified, accompanied by a mild yet favorable elevation in hemoglobin concentration. In this small cohort of MDS patients with elevated PASP, luspatercept treatment was associated with decreased pulmonary artery pressure, reduced NT-proBNP and uric acid levels, and improved hemoglobin levels. These preliminary findings suggest novel pleiotropic benefits of luspatercept in improving pulmonary arterial pressure, cardiac function, and anemia status, providing a compelling rationale for further prospective clinical studies to verify its therapeutic value in PH populations.

Title: Chamber-specific long-term prognosis of intracardiac thrombus: a 21-year propensity-matched cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of intracardiac thrombus varies by cardiac chamber, yet large-scale comparative long-term outcome data across all four chambers remain limited.
METHODS: In this retrospective propensity-matched cohort study using the Chang Gung Research Database (2001-2022), we identified 1,541 patients in the final propensity-matched analytic cohorts with echocardiographically confirmed single-chamber intracardiac thrombus [left atrial (LA) n = 619, left ventricular (LV) n = 774, right atrial (RA) n = 125, right ventricular (RV) n = 23]. Patients were 1:4 matched with controls without thrombus for demographics, comorbidities, and medications. Primary outcomes included ischemic stroke/systemic embolism, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiac death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of the above). Follow-up continued until the first event, death, or December 31, 2022.
FINDINGS: Compared with matched controls, LA thrombus was associated with increased risks of ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (hazard ratio, HR = 1.85), heart failure (HR = 1.30), cardiac death (HR = 2.02), and MACE (HR = 1.61). LV thrombus was associated with increased risks of ischemic stroke/systemic embolism (HR = 1.38), myocardial infarction (HR = 1.58), heart failure (HR = 1.40), cardiac death (HR = 1.32), and MACE (HR = 1.36). RA thrombus was associated with pulmonary embolism (HR = 4.63), heart failure (HR = 1.70), and MACE (HR = 1.63), whereas cardiac death was not significantly increased (HR = 1.96). RV thrombus was rare and showed no significant associations with any outcome. Left atrial appendage thrombus did not confer additional risk compared with non-appendage LA thrombus.
CONCLUSIONS: The prognostic impact of intracardiac thrombus is strongly location-dependent. LV and LA thrombi carried the broadest cardiovascular risks, RA thrombus was disproportionately linked to pulmonary embolism and mortality, and RV thrombus had limited long-term impact. These findings support chamber-specific risk stratification and management strategies for patients with echocardiography-detected intracardiac thrombus.

Title: Prognostic Value of Conventional Echocardiographic Parameters of Right Ventricular Dysfunction in a Real-World Cohort of Patients With Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a known marker of adverse outcomes in acute pulmonary embolism (PE). However, the prognostic utility of individual echocardiographic parameters in clinically heterogeneous patient populations remains a matter of debate. This study aimed to evaluate the association of baseline echocardiographic parameters of RV dysfunction with the Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (PESI) score and in-hospital mortality.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 32 consecutive patients with computed tomography-confirmed acute PE. A comprehensive transthoracic echocardiogram was performed within 12 hours of admission. Parameters including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), RV fractional area change (RV FAC), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S'), and RV myocardial performance index (MPI) were measured. The PESI score was calculated for all patients. No a priori power calculation was performed, and analyses were exploratory; significance was judged against a Bonferroni-corrected threshold for the systolic parameters tested.
RESULTS: The mean age was 55.4 ± 18.0 years, and the mean PESI score was 115.2 ± 40.5, indicating a high-risk cohort (59.4% in PESI classes IV-V). In-hospital mortality was 12.5%. Baseline TAPSE, S', and RV FAC showed no significant correlation with the continuous PESI score (p = 0.084, p = 0.235, and p = 0.637, respectively) and no significant association with in-hospital mortality (p > 0.05 for all). Abnormal RV FAC (<35%) was associated with PESI class distribution (χ²(4) = 11.08, p = 0.026, Cramér's V = 0.59) but did not retain significance after correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, prospective cohort of patients with acute PE and a high burden of comorbidities, conventional echocardiographic parameters of RV systolic function, including TAPSE and S', were not significantly associated with the PESI score or in-hospital mortality, and the single positive association (RV FAC with PESI class) did not survive correction for multiple testing. Given the limited sample and few events, these exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating and are consistent with an adjunctive - rather than stand-alone - role for echocardiographic RV assessment in risk stratification.

Title: Patient selection strategies for deep inspiration breath-hold in left-sided breast cancer: a review of current evidence and future directions.
Abstract: With accumulating evidence confirming that postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy improves survival outcomes in patients with left-sided breast cancer, the long-term cardiotoxicity risks associated with radiotherapy have attracted widespread attention. The deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH) technique increases the distance between the heart and the breast target, effectively reducing radiation dose to the heart and coronary arteries. However, the resource-intensive nature of DIBH and substantial heterogeneity in therapeutic benefits among patients pose a major clinical challenge: how to accurately and efficiently identify patients suitable for DIBH. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding DIBH patient selection, and integrates available strategies with clinical workflows to construct a three-tiered decision-making framework encompassing feasibility assessment, indication evaluation, and clinical benefit assessment. Given the existing gaps in high-level prospective clinical evidence, three primary research directions are proposed: (1) conducting large-scale multi-center prospective cohort studies to validate the generalizability and clinical practicality of selection strategies; (2) developing an individualized normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model integrating multi-dimensional risk factors to guide precise decision-making; and (3) implementing prospective clinical trials of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted selection platforms to accelerate the clinical translation of intelligent selection tools. This review synthesizes current evidence on DIBH patient selection, constructs a hierarchical decision framework to provide a reference for clinical practice, and delineates directions for future research.

Title: Short-term superiority in proteinuria control with exploratory longitudinal trajectories: finerenone-dapagliflozin combination in non-diabetic kidney disease.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Finerenone and dapagliflozin have demonstrated renal protective effects in diabetic kidney disease, but real-world evidence on their combination in non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD) remains scarce. We assessed whether their combination improves short-term proteinuria control versus monotherapy, with long-term trajectories explored as hypothesis-generating outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 327 NDKD patients admitted to Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (January 2022-March 2026). Patients were divided into three groups: finerenone monotherapy, dapagliflozin monotherapy, or combination therapy. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Short-term (3 months) efficacy, safety, and exploratory cost analysis were compared. Longitudinal data were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE), with the primary inferential window at 3-6 months and a sensitivity analysis at 3-24 months. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of treatment failure in the full unmatched cohort. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed in membranous nephropathy and hypertension.
RESULTS: After PSM, at 3 months, combination therapy achieved a higher overall remission rate than dapagliflozin monotherapy (69.57% vs. 39.13%, OR = 3.56, 95% CI: 1.50-8.40, P = 0.003), but not versus finerenone monotherapy (68.29% vs. 51.22%, OR = 2.05, 95% CI: 0.84-5.05, P = 0.115). In the primary 3-6 months GEE analysis, time effects were significant for clinical remission rates and proteinuria; Sensitivity GEE analysis (3-24 months) was consistent. Descriptive analyses from 3 to 24 months showed numerical improvement trends across groups, but these are exploratory. Adverse event rates were low, but the analysis was underpowered to exclude increased hyperkalemia risk. In exploratory cost analysis, the ICER was 22.99 RMB per 1% increase in remission rate versus finerenone and 20.79 RMB versus dapagliflozin; probabilistic sensitivity analysis was broadly consistent with the base case, without judgment of economic superiority. Dapagliflozin monotherapy was independently associated with treatment failure (OR = 2.163, 95% CI: 1.073-4.362, P = 0.031) in the full unmatched cohort. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential benefit in membranous nephropathy and hypertension.
CONCLUSION: Finerenone combined with dapagliflozin provides higher observed short-term (3 months) efficacy in NDKD, with low observed adverse event rates. Long-term outcomes require validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Relationships among heart rate variability, sleep disturbances, and fatigue in patients undergoing interventional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatigue and sleep disturbances are commonly experienced by patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the potential association between these conditions and autonomic nervous system reflected by heart rate variability (HRV) is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the differences in HRV parameters among HCC patients with different degrees of fatigue and sleep disturbances, as well as the relationship between HRV parameters and fatigue and sleep disturbances.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, a total of 66 patients with HCC hospitalized for interventional therapy were enrolled. Patients completed questionnaires during hospitalization, including the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Fatigue Scale-14 (FS-14), and underwent a 5-minute resting electrocardiogram (ECG) for HRV analysis. Group comparisons and logistic regression models adjusted for age were used to examine the associations between HRV parameters and symptom severity, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: Acceleration capacity (AC) was significantly higher and low frequency (LF) was significantly lower in the high PSQI group compared to the low PSQI group (AC: p = 0.036; LF: p = 0.041); Compared to the low FS-14 group, the high FS-14 group had significantly higher mean heart rate (MeanHR) and AC, while most other HRV indices were significantly lower (MeanHR: p = 0.029; AC: p = 0.009). The results of the adjusted logistic regression model indicated that increased AC showed a marginal trend toward an association with poor sleep quality (p = 0.071), while MeanHR remained significantly associated with severe fatigue (OR = 1.098, p = 0.004). After FDR correction, the differences in eight HRV parameters between fatigue groups remained significant (all q < 0.05), whereas the differences between sleep-quality groups did not survive correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that alterations in HRV parameters, particularly mean heart rate (MeanHR) and acceleration capacity (AC), are associated with the severity of fatigue and sleep disturbances in HCC patients. Given the exploratory cross-sectional design, these metrics should be regarded as candidate non-invasive physiological correlates of autonomic dysfunction and symptom burden. Their clinical relevance requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Blood-based biomarkers and major adverse cardiac events after percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review with narrative synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) remain common after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite advances in stent technology and secondary-prevention pharmacotherapy. Blood-based biomarkers have been proposed as tools for individualised risk stratification, but reported prognostic associations vary widely across studies.
OBJECTIVES: This review addressed two prespecified and analytically separate questions. The primary (prognostic) question was: among adults undergoing PCI, are elevated concentrations of blood-based biomarkers associated with subsequent MACE and mortality? The secondary (treatment-effect) question was: among adults undergoing PCI, do specified pharmacotherapeutic strategies reduce MACE? The two questions were addressed using separate eligibility criteria, separate effect measures, separate risk-of-bias instruments and separate syntheses; prognostic associations and treatment effects were not pooled together.
METHODS: MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase (via Ovid), Web of Science Core Collection and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from 1 January 2010 to 28 February 2025, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO ICTRP, OpenGrey and backward and forward citation searching. Records were restricted to English-language reports. Eligible studies for the primary question enrolled adults (≥18 years) undergoing PCI, measured a blood-based biomarker at a defined time point relative to the index procedure, and reported MACE or mortality with an extractable adjusted or unadjusted effect estimate. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS for prognostic factor studies, supported by ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2.0 and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate to design. Random-effects meta-analysis was to use the restricted maximum likelihood estimator for between-study variance with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, with DerSimonian-Laird estimates as a sensitivity analysis. No analyte met the minimum study count required to trigger pooling (Section 3.5), so no meta-analysis was performed. Pooling was restricted to biomarker-outcome pairs with at least three methodologically comparable primary studies. Prediction intervals accompany every pooled estimate derived from five or more studies. Certainty of evidence was rated using a GRADE framework adapted for prognostic factor reviews.
RESULTS: Forty-two studies were included, comprising 41 primary reports and one systematic review retained for cross-referencing only, together contributing 37,524 participants to the prognostic synthesis. The evidence base was dispersed across 42 distinct analytes: 38 were evaluated in a single study and four in two studies, so no analyte reached the minimum of three studies prespecified for quantitative pooling. Meta-analysis was therefore not undertaken, and the evidence is reported as a structured narrative synthesis. Elevated concentrations of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, C-reactive protein and its high-sensitivity assay, interleukin-6, the systemic immune-inflammation index and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were each reported as associated with increased risk of MACE, consistently in direction but on the basis of one or two studies per analyte. Evidence for microRNA-497-5p and other emerging analytes rested on single small studies and is reported as preliminary. Thirteen studies were rated at high overall risk of bias, seventeen at moderate and twelve at low. Certainty was very low for the 38 single-study analytes and low for the remainder. Treatment-effect evidence identified under the secondary question is reported separately and was not combined with the prognostic synthesis.
CONCLUSIONS: Blood-based biomarkers show consistent directional associations with MACE after PCI, but the evidence is too dispersed for quantitative synthesis: no analyte was evaluated in more than two of the included studies. Heterogeneity in assay platform, sampling time, cut-off derivation and endpoint definition compounds this dispersion. These findings support further evaluation of a small number of candidate markers in adequately powered cohorts with standardised measurement, not the incorporation of any biomarker into routine post-PCI decision-making. No included study randomised patients on the basis of a biomarker result, so no biomarker-guided treatment recommendation can be made.

Title: A mobile health-assisted cardiovascular follow-up after pregnancy complications (MumCare): protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes is associated with increased risk of long-term maternal cardiovascular (CV) disease. Despite recommendations for preventive strategies, few women receive CV follow-up postpartum. We have developed a personalized digital mobile Health companion, the MumCare (Mum's cardiovascular health for life) application, aiming at improving control of modifiable risk factors for CV disease and to bridge hospital and community health services. This paper describes the protocol for a MumCare randomized controlled trial in Norway.
METHODS: Study participation is offered to women at Oslo University Hospital with a diagnosis of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes. Following informed consent (either during pregnancy or within 4 weeks postpartum), a block randomization process assigns participants to one of two groups (access to the Mum Care app or not). The app provides educational material, allows women to track modifiable risk factors, and prompts feedback to registered blood pressures. It also prompts the women to book the nationally recommended follow-up at their general practitioner's at 3-4 and 12 months postpartum. The primary study objective is to assess the effect of MumCare application access on 1-year follow-up rate with a general practitioner. Secondary objectives are to assess group differences at 14 months postpartum regarding: 1) satisfaction with the postpartum mHealth-assisted technology, 2) self-management evaluation, general self-efficacy; and at 14-18 months: 3) modifiable risk factors for CV disease (including hypertension, dyslipidemia, blood sugar control, smoking, weight and physical activity), CV non-invasive hemodynamics and CV-related biomarkers.
DISCUSSION: This randomized controlled trial tests the effect of a mobile Health-assisted follow-up of modifiable risk factors after pregnancy complications associated with premature CV disease in women. A study limitation is a risk of underrepresentation of recently immigrated women due to the restricted language options offered in the app.

Title: Gut microbial immunometabolic pathways associated with cardiac arrest risk: genetic evidence and exploratory fecal microbiome profiling.
Journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest remains difficult to predict, and upstream biological determinants are poorly defined. Gut microbiota can influence host metabolism, immunity and inflammation, but their relevance to cardiac arrest risk remains unclear.
METHODS: We performed bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization to prioritize associations between gut microbial traits and cardiac arrest. Two-step mediation analyses were then used to assess whether circulating metabolites, immune cell phenotypes and inflammatory proteins could represent candidate intermediary pathways. An independent exploratory fecal 16S rRNA cohort of patients with cardiac arrest and healthy controls was analysed to provide descriptive post-arrest microbiome context.
RESULTS: Mendelian randomization prioritized 14 candidate gut microbial taxa or microbial metabolic pathways associated with cardiac arrest risk. Mediation analyses identified 55 candidate mediation pathways involving 41 candidate mediators, including 10 pathways with comparatively stronger statistical support based on the joint-significance criterion and the Sobel test. Metabolite-related signals accounted for most candidate mediation pathways, with additional contributions from immune cell phenotypes and inflammatory factors. In the exploratory 16S cohort, diversity and ordination patterns did not show robust group separation, whereas descriptive compositional summaries showed partial taxonomic overlap with signals highlighted by the genetic analyses; these observations were not considered directional or causal validation.
CONCLUSION: These findings prioritize an immunometabolic framework linking gut microbial variation to cardiac arrest risk, with metabolic mediation representing the predominant candidate layer for follow-up study. The exploratory clinical 16S results provide descriptive post-arrest context rather than independent validation, and the genetic findings should be interpreted as candidate associations requiring larger prospective and experimental confirmation.

Title: Adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy for post-stroke cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) on cognitive, neurological, and functional outcomes in patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), and explore potential sources of heterogeneity.
METHODS: Eight databases were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating adjunctive HBOT in patients with PSCI were included. The primary outcome was the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); secondary outcomes included the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), Modified Barthel Index (MBI), and Barthel Index (BI). Random-effects meta-analyses, prespecified subgroup analyses, and meta-regression were performed. Sensitivity analyses, funnel plots, Egger's tests, and GRADE assessments were conducted.
RESULTS: Thirty-five RCTs involving 3,036 participants, all conducted in China, were included. Adjunctive HBOT was associated with higher MoCA scores (MD = 2.90, 95% CI: 2.47-3.33; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 84%) and MMSE scores (MD = 2.68, 95% CI: 2.20-3.16; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 83%). Improvements were also observed in NIHSS (MD = -2.61, 95% CI: -3.34 to -1.89; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 93%), MBI (MD = 6.64, 95% CI: 3.76-9.52; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 82%), and BI (MD = 8.77, 95% CI: 4.72-12.82;p < 0.00001; I 2 = 82%). No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed for MoCA (p = 0.10) or MMSE (p = 0.43). Higher baseline MoCA scores tended to be associated with smaller treatment effects in meta-regression (β = -0.1411, p = 0.0637; R 2 = 15.42%). Substantial heterogeneity remained largely unexplained. Evidence certainty was low for MoCA, MMSE, and MBI and very low for NIHSS and BI.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive HBOT may provide cognitive and functional benefits in patients with PSCI. However, substantial unexplained heterogeneity, low-to-very-low certainty of evidence, and the exclusively Chinese evidence base warrant cautious interpretation and limit generalizability. Further well-designed RCTs involving diverse populations are needed.

Title: Exploratory predictive value of novel inflammatory biomarkers for microvascular obstruction after emergency revascularization in STEMI patients.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory markers with the formation of microvascular obstruction (MVO) and their exploratory predictive performance in STEMI patients after PCI.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted based on a prospective cohort, which included the patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. All patients underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging within 7 days post-surgery, and were classified into MVO and non-MVO groups based on the examination results. Emergency and first post-PCI routine blood test and other clinical data were collected from patients, and various cell ratios were calculated, including the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI). The risk factors for MVO were evaluated by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 311 patients with STEMI were included. Among them, 198 developed MVO and the other 113 were MVO free. After adjustment for clinical covariates, higher post-PCI WBC, NEU, SIRI and NLR and greater peri-PCI eosinophil decline were associated with MVO. In the correlation-reduced joint analysis, post-PCI SIRI retained the most robust association.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative WBC, NEU, SIRI, NLR, ΔEOS, ΔEOS% showed exploratory predictive performance for the formation of MVO after PCI in STEMI patients, and post-PCI SIRI showed the most robust association after accounting for biomarker intercorrelation.

Title: Functional changes during inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation in Poland: an ICF-based analysis of functioning relevant to healthy aging and public health.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) provides a comprehensive framework for assessing rehabilitation outcomes beyond traditional physiological measures.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study used a longitudinal pre-post design and involved a secondary analysis of anonymized data collected during a national pilot implementation of an ICF-based functional assessment system in routine Polish rehabilitation services It aimed to characterize within-patient changes in functioning observed between admission and discharge among 100 adults undergoing inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation, with a mean age of 68.7 ± 10.8 years (with 75% in the ≥65 years group), at baseline and 2-3 weeks post-rehabilitation. Changes in ICF qualifiers for Body Functions (B), Activities and Participation (D), and Environmental Factors (E) were evaluated using paired comparisons.
RESULTS: At baseline, the greatest impairments were observed in energy and drive functions (b130), sleep functions (b134), pain (b280), exercise tolerance functions (b455), joint mobility (b710), muscle power (b730), muscle endurance (b740), changing basic body position (d410), maintaining a body position (d415), and walking (d450). Between admission and discharge, significant reductions in impairment severity were observed in several body function categories, including muscle power (median qualifier 3 → 1), muscle endurance (3 → 2), joint mobility (3 → 1), pain (b280), exercise tolerance (1 → 0), and sensations associated with cardiovascular and respiratory functions (2 → 1) (all adjusted p < 0.01). Significant reductions in activity limitations were also observed for changing basic body position (3 → 2), maintaining a body position (3 → 2), walking (2 → 1), transfers (severe/complete limitation: 17% → 4%), daily routines (severe/complete limitation: 36% → 19%), and multiple self-care activities multiple self-care activities, including washing (1 → 0), caring for body parts (1 → 0), toileting (severe/complete limitation: 2% → 0%), and dressing (1 → 0) (all adjusted p < 0.01). Environmental factors remained stable, with medications, assistive products and technologies and family support consistently identified as facilitators of functioning.
CONCLUSION: These findings describe differences across several dimensions of ICF-rated functioning between admission and discharge during inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation. They suggest that routine ICF-based assessments may provide a useful multidimensional description of functioning. Future controlled studies could examine the extent to which these differences are attributable to rehabilitation, while dedicated validation studies could assess the responsiveness of the ICF-based assessment system and the clinical meaning of changes in qualifier scores.

Title: Development and validation of a simple clinical prediction model for post-stroke seizures in critically ill patients: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke seizures (PSS) are common in critically ill stroke patients, but ICU-specific risk prediction tools are lacking, and the independent impact of PSS on mortality remains controversial.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort included 6,586 adult stroke patients from 208 US ICUs in the Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Patients were randomly divided 7:3 into training and internal validation sets. The primary endpoint was coded in-hospital post-stroke seizures identified via diagnosis codes during the index hospitalization. Candidate predictors were screened using logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were, respectively, evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration slopes and calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to evaluate the association between PSS and in-hospital mortality and length of stay.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of coded in-hospital PSS was 7.5%. Head-to-head comparison identified SOFA as the best-performing routine ICU severity score for coded PSS prediction, outperforming GCS, OASIS and APACHE II. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified five independent clinical predictors for coded in-hospital PSS: younger age, elevated admission body temperature, pre-existing hypertension, lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, and lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score. The model achieved AUCs of 0.702 in the training set and 0.713 in the validation set, with stable performance across age, gender, and stroke subtype subgroups. A three-tier bedside risk stratification was derived, with observed coded PSS rates of 3.4, 6.8, and 16.2% for low-risk, intermediate-risk, and high-risk groups. After PSM, coded PSS was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR = 0.84, p = 0.295) or prolonged hospital stay (mean difference = -0.30 days, p = 0.167).
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a simple prediction model for coded in-hospital PSS in critically ill stroke patients. Coded PSS itself was not independently associated with increased mortality. This model remains a research tool that has not undergone external validation and cannot yet guide real-world clinical monitoring or pharmacological intervention. These findings are applicable to clinically evident, coded convulsive seizures and may not generalize to non-convulsive seizure phenotypes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Predictors and prescribing patterns of definite anticholinergic medication use among community-dwelling older adults in Saudi Arabia: a retrospective multicenter cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Anticholinergic medications are associated with cognitive impairment and falls in older adults, yet multicenter evidence from Saudi Arabia remains limited. This study characterized prescribing patterns and factors associated with definite anticholinergic burden among older adults receiving outpatient care.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cross-sectional study used outpatient records and dispensing data from two tertiary hospitals located in Al Khobar and Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia, between 2019 and 2024. Adults aged 60 years or older receiving at least one medication scoring 2 or 3 on the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale were included. Robust linear, negative binomial, and logistic regression models examined definite ACB score, additional qualifying medications, and multiple medication use.
RESULTS: The study included 1,664 older adults with 2016 patient-medication instances. Polypharmacy was present in 84.3%, and 17.5% received multiple qualifying medications. Bladder antimuscarinics, antipsychotics, and tricyclic antidepressants accounted for 78.1% of medication instances, while urology, psychiatry, and neurology accounted for 72.0%. A corresponding coded diagnosis was identified for 20.0% of evaluable instances. Polypharmacy, hypertension, depression, Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder were independently associated with all three outcomes. Schizophrenia showed the strongest associations with definite ACB score (B = 2.206; 95% CI, 0.429-3.982), additional medications (incidence rate ratio = 4.395; 95% CI, 2.499-7.732), and multiple medication use (adjusted odds ratio = 8.303; 95% CI, 3.275-21.055).
CONCLUSIONS: Definite anticholinergic use was concentrated within a limited number of medication classes and prescribing specialties. Psychiatric disorders and polypharmacy were consistently associated with higher burden, supporting targeted medication review in these patients and specialties.

Title: Comparison of cardiopulmonary function in patients with scoliosis at rest and during exercise: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative cardiopulmonary assessment in scoliosis is typically dominated by resting spirometry and the Cobb angle, yet resting tests may understate functional impairment and curve magnitude predicts it only weakly. This study integrated resting echocardiography, static pulmonary function testing, CT lung volume, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in the same preoperative patients to characterize cardiopulmonary impairment and to separate the structural determinants of lung volume from those of exercise reserve.
METHODS: In this single-center case-control study, 33 consecutive preoperative patients with scoliosis [21 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), 12 congenital scoliosis (CS); aged 10-20 years] were compared with 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Predicted spirometric values were derived from arm span with the GLI Global equations. Analyses used effect sizes with false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction, body-size-adjusted hierarchical regression, and cross-validated ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Resting cardiac function was preserved (left ventricular ejection fraction, cardiac output and cardiac index all non-significant after FDR), whereas restrictive ventilation and exercise reserve were reduced: FVC 72.0% vs. 92.8% predicted (q < 0.001), peak oxygen uptake 21.8 vs. 29.6 mL/min/kg (q < 0.001), O₂ pulse 5.9 vs. 9.7 mL/beat (q < 0.001), and VE/VCO₂ slope 32.4 vs. 27.5 (q < 0.001). Among 13 patients normal at rest, 10 (77%) were abnormal on CPET. Thoracic height independently predicted restrictive impairment beyond the Cobb angle, kyphosis, and body size (FVC %predicted B = 3.65 per cm, 95% CI   1.64-5.65; AUC 0.90, cross-validated 0.84; threshold 19.6 cm), whereas no deformity parameter independently predicted exercise capacity. At matched thoracic height, congenital scoliosis had lower CT lung volume than idiopathic scoliosis (1,881 vs. 2,356 cm3; p = 0.030).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative scoliosis is characterized by preserved resting indices but a frequently occult reduction in exercise reserve, including an exercise cardiac limitation revealed by O₂ pulse that resting echocardiography does not show. Thoracic height is a body-size-independent predictor of restrictive lung volume with a clinically usable threshold, while exercise reserve is multifactorial and requires direct CPET assessment. The two dimensions of preoperative cardiopulmonary risk should therefore be measured separately.

Title: Nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression in stroke patients: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression in stroke patients.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 300 patients with stroke completed a general information questionnaire, the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF), the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), and the Modified Barthel Index (MBI). Independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, hierarchical linear regression, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis were used.
RESULTS: The mean FoP score was 30.34 ± 8.56. In the hierarchical regression model, higher PSS was associated with lower FoP (B = -0.223, P < 0.001). Compared with employed participants, unemployed participants had lower FoP scores (B = -3.188, P = 0.008), and severe ADL dependence was associated with higher FoP compared with independence (B = 4.921, P = 0.035). The restricted cubic spline analysis indicated evidence of nonlinearity (P foroverall < 0.001; P for nonlinear = 0.023). Exploratory piecewise linear regression identified an estimated change point at a PSS score of 67 (P = 0.011). Below 67, each one-point increase in PSS was associated with a 0.319-point lower FoP score (B = -0.319, 95% CI -0.396 to -0.241; P < 0.001). At PSS scores ≥ 67, the slope was not statistically significant and was imprecisely estimated (B = 0.304, 95% CI -0.142 to 0.751; P = 0.182).
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggested a nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression, with a change point at a perceived social support score of 67. However, this change point requires validation in larger multicenter and prospective studies. In addition, unemployed and severely dependent were independently associated with fear of disease progression. These findings may help guide more comprehensive psychosocial assessment for stroke patients at risk of fear of disease progression.

Title: The predictive model of intra-arrest blood markers for the sustained return of spontaneous circulation in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of intra-arrest blood markers, including blood routine, blood biochemistry, and coagulation profile, during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for the return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of patients who experienced OHCA and admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China, between January 2021 and December 2025 was assembled. Their clinical and demographic data were collected, and missing values were addressed using multiple imputation. Physiologic laboratory markers obtained during resuscitation were compared between the sustained ROSC and non-ROSC groups. Candidate predictors were selected based on clinical relevance, previous literature, availability at the intended prediction time point, and univariable screening, with age and gender retained as prespecified demographic covariates. Model discrimination for the prediction of sustained ROSC was evaluated using a receiver operating characteristic analysis and the area under the curve (AUC). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling to assess model stability and quantify potential overfitting.
RESULTS: A total of 283 patients were included, and among them, 94 (33.22%) achieved sustained ROSC. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation (m = 20). In univariable analyses, the sustained ROSC group had higher PCO2, platelet count, white blood cell count, and absolute lymphocyte count; higher admission glucose, fibrinogen, and serum calcium levels; shorter chest compression duration and prothrombin time; and lower epinephrine dose, serum potassium level, and international normalized ratio than the non-sustained ROSC group (all P < 0.05). A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating age; gender; white blood cell count; platelet count; blood PCO2 measured during CPR; capillary blood glucose level on admission; and fibrinogen, serum potassium, and serum calcium levels yielded a mean apparent AUC of 0.832 across the imputed datasets. After internal validation with 500 bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.807 and the bootstrap-derived calibration slope was 0.853. The final model is given as follows: logit[P(ROSC=1)] = -2.65-0.002 × age-0.790 × gender + 0.076 × white blood cell count + 0.001 × platelet count + 0.010 × PCO2-0.011 × admission glucose + 0.145 × fibrinogen-0.247 × serum potassium+0.633 × serum calcium.
CONCLUSION: In patients who experienced OHCA, higher white blood cell count and lower serum potassium levels were associated with a higher incidence of sustained ROSC. Female patients were more likely to achieve sustained ROSC than male patients. Although the model showed certain predictive value for sustained ROSC, further multicenter, large-scale studies are needed in the future.

Title: High-sensitivity troponin T as a predictor of cardiovascular events in colorectal cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: results of the COLOVASC prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy is associated with cardiovascular events in patients with colorectal cancer, yet validated tools for pre-treatment cardiovascular risk stratification are lacking. Cardiac biomarkers are not routinely incorporated into baseline assessment and prospective evidence supporting their use remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to determine whether baseline high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) provides prognostic information for major adverse cardiovascular events during chemotherapy in patients with colorectal cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Within a prospective single-center observational cohort study at the Department of Internal Medicine and Hematology, Semmelweis University, consecutive patients with histologically confirmed newly diagnosed or recurrent colorectal cancer scheduled to receive 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-based chemotherapy were enrolled between September 1, 2020, and June 2, 2024. Baseline hs-TnT concentrations were measured before treatment initiation, and patients were followed for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Independent predictors of MACE were identified using penalized multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the discriminatory performance of baseline hs-TnT and determined the optimal cut-off value using the Youden index. Adequacy index analysis assessed the relative prognostic contribution of hs-TnT to the multivariable model.
RESULTS: 180 patients were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 185 days, 44 patients (24.4%) experienced MACE, more than half of them occurred within the first two cycles of chemotherapy. Baseline hs-TnT demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting MACE (AUC 0.628, 95% CI 0.513-0.742). The optimal hs-TnT cut-off was 14 ng/L. In a multivariable analysis, elevated baseline hs-TnT (OR 2.35 per +10 ng/L, 95% CI 1.37-4.05) and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF)-inhibitor therapy (OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.23-4.60) were associated with MACEs. In a sensitivity analysis, excluding treatment-related hypertension from the composite endpoints, elevated baseline hs-TnT remained the only independent predictor. According to the adequacy index analysis, hs-TnT contributed 38.3% of the total prognostic information provided by the multivariable model.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline hs-TnT was independently associated with MACEs in patients with colorectal cancer receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. Although its discriminatory performance as a standalone biomarker was modest, hs-TnT provided incremental prognostic information for baseline cardiovascular risk assessment and may help identify patients who warrant closer cardiovascular surveillance.

Title: Exercise capacity and handgrip strength following dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training in patients with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective single-arm study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) is a severe complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) and is associated with impaired exercise capacity. Feasible rehabilitation strategies for this population remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate changes in functional exercise capacity and handgrip strength following a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program in patients with BOS after allo-HSCT and to explore associations of these changes with selected baseline characteristics.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm pre-post interventional study included 31 patients with BOS after allo-HSCT. Participants completed a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program. Six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and bilateral handgrip strength were assessed at baseline and week 12. Within-participant changes were evaluated using paired tests according to the distribution of change scores. Associations with selected baseline characteristics were examined in exploratory analyses.
RESULTS: Following the 12-week intervention, mean 6MWD increased from 406.3 m at baseline to 425.9 m at week 12, corresponding to a mean within-participant increase of 19.6 m (95% CI: 9.3-29.9 m; p < 0.001). Mean bilateral handgrip strength increased from 23.2 kg to 25.0 kg, corresponding to a mean increase of 1.8 kg (95% CI: 1.3-2.3 kg; p < 0.001). The change in 6MWD did not differ significantly between women and men (p = 0.282), whereas the increase in handgrip strength was greater in women than in men (p = 0.021). Baseline heart-rate response during the 6MWT and supplemental oxygen requirement were not clearly associated with the magnitude of functional change. No serious training-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Twelve weeks of dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training was associated with improvements in 6MWD and handgrip strength in patients with BOS after allo-HSCT. However, the single-arm design precludes causal attribution of these improvements to the intervention, and the exploratory subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger controlled studies are needed to establish efficacy and characterize potential differences in response.

Title: Effects of exercise-based interventions on balance and functional mobility in adults with chronic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate, using the GRADE framework, the effects of exercise-based interventions on Berg Balance Scale, Timed Up and Go, and Functional Reach Test outcomes in adults with chronic stroke.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database from inception to 29 June 2025 for randomized controlled trials investigating structured exercise-based interventions in adults with chronic stroke. Eligible studies enrolled adults at least 6 months after stroke onset and reported at least one validated balance or functional mobility outcome. Methodological quality was assessed using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models and expressed as mean differences (MDs) or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); exploratory univariable random-effects meta-regression was used to examine intervention duration and training frequency.
RESULTS: Sixty-nine randomized controlled trials involving 2,314 adults with chronic stroke were included. Exercise-based interventions improved Berg Balance Scale scores [MD = 2.54, 95% CI (1.83-3.26)], reduced Timed Up and Go test completion time [MD = -2.68 s, 95% CI (-3.72 to -1.65)], and improved Functional Reach Test performance [SMD = 0.65, 95% CI (0.25-1.05)]. The certainty of evidence was moderate for BBS, high for TUG, and moderate for FRT, with the degree of heterogeneity differing across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Exercise-based interventions were associated with improvements in BBS scores, TUG performance, and FRT outcomes in adults with chronic stroke, although the certainty and consistency of evidence varied across these measures. These findings support the potential role of exercise-based interventions in improving these selected outcomes. Larger pragmatic trials with standardized intervention reporting and longer follow-up are needed to clarify optimal training components, dose, delivery, and durability of effects.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42020156992, identifier CRD42020156992.

Title: Factors associated with short- and long-term maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful elective electrical cardioversion.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electrical cardioversion (ECV) effectively restores sinus rhythm in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), although arrhythmia recurrence is common. We aimed to identify factors associated with a higher probability of maintaining sinus rhythm one month after successful ECV, and after one year in those who were arrhythmia-free after the first month.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent elective ECV for persistent AF or AFL between January 2011 and June 2023. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic characteristics were analyzed to identify parameters associated with the maintenance of sinus rhythm.
RESULTS: We included 297 ECV procedures. ECV was successful in 91.9% of patients and sinus rhythm was maintained in 89.7% of them at one month and in 40.3% at one year follow-up. Shorter arrhythmia duration (OR = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.76-0.98, p = 0.026) and ventricular pacing on the pre-procedural ECG (OR = 5.212, 95% CI: 1.16-23.48, p = 0.032) were associated with one-month success. Factors associated with one-year sinus rhythm maintenance in patients who were in sinus rhythm during monthly follow-up were smaller left atrial dimensions (OR = 0.817, 95%CI: 0.77-0.98, p = 0.022), the first-ever arrhythmia episode (OR = 3.320, 95%CI: 1.10-10.05, p = 0.034), lower CHA2DS2-VASc score (OR = 0.132, 95%CI: 0.03-0.54, p = 0.005), non-smoking status (OR = 0.120, 95%CI: 0.04-0.37, p < 0.001), no previous ECV (OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.01-0.47, p = 0.005), and antiarrhythmic therapy (OR = 2.486, 95%CI: 1.01-8.65, p = 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: ECV is a reasonable rhythm-control strategy in AF/AFL particularly when performed early after arrhythmia onset, in non-smokers and patients with fewer comorbidities, antiarrhythmic treatment, smaller left atrium and no prior ECV.

Title: Real-world safety of vericiguat as a fifth-line agent in heart failure: a pharmacovigilance study of quintuple therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vericiguat, a novel soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator, is indicated for high-risk worsening heart failure (HF). However, its real-world reporting profile when added to contemporary quadruple guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT)-effectively creating a "quintuple" regimen-remains largely unexplored, particularly regarding cardiorenal and hematologic adverse-event reporting patterns.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (2021 Q1-2025 Q4). HF reports were strictly stratified into an expanded quadruple GDMT cohort [renin-angiotensin system inhibitor + beta-blocker + mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist [MRA] + sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor [SGLT2i]] and a quintuple cohort (GDMT + vericiguat). Disproportionality analysis utilized a dual-algorithm approach: the frequentist Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) and the Bayesian Information Component (IC) derived from the Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network (BCPNN). SGLT2i-stratified analyses and formal interaction testing were also performed.
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 5,524 reports (5,459 quadruple; 65 quintuple). No ROR signals were identified for hypotension (ROR = 1.66, 95% CI: 0.90-3.06), syncope (ROR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.21-3.49), or acute kidney injury (ROR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.26-1.41). Anemia met the frequentist ROR signal criterion (ROR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.03-6.58), but not the BCPNN criterion (IC = 0.96, IC-2SD = -0.29). The anemia ROR was 2.61 (95% CI: 1.03-6.58) with an SGLT2i background and 1.82 (95% CI: 0.42-7.88) without an SGLT2i background; formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification (P for interaction = 0.683). No statistically significant differences were detected in reported serious outcomes between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this FAERS analysis, no robust reporting signals were identified for hypotension, syncope, or acute kidney injury after vericiguat was added to contemporary quadruple GDMT. Although anemia met the frequentist ROR criterion, the finding was not supported by Bayesian signal detection, and formal analyses did not demonstrate significant effect modification by background SGLT2i use. Given the small vericiguat-exposed cohort, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies.

Title: Annual variation and clinical characteristics of postoperative lower extremity venous thrombosis after urological surgery: a single-center real-world study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the annual variation and clinical characteristics of clinically detected postoperative lower extremity venous thrombosis (LEVT) during hospitalization in patients undergoing urological surgery at our institution from 2022 to 2025, providing reference for perioperative thrombosis risk assessment and preventive management.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective real-world study was conducted using the hospital electronic medical record system. Patients who developed LEVT for the first time during hospitalization following urological surgery between January 2022 and December 2025 were included. Lower-extremity ultrasonography was performed based on clinical indications rather than routine systematic screening. Detailed information was extracted for patients with thrombosis, including demographic characteristics, admission-related scores and laboratory tests, surgical details, and thrombosis-related outcomes. Descriptive statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software.
RESULTS: Between 2022 and 2025, a total of 12,313 urological surgical procedures were performed at our center, among which 57 patients were newly diagnosed with postoperative LEVT during hospitalization, corresponding to an overall procedure-based clinically detected LEVT rate of 0.46% (57/12,313). The corresponding annual procedure-based clinically detected LEVT rates were 0.63% (17/2,711) in 2022, 0.43% (13/3,005) in 2023, 0.25% (8/3,256) in 2024, and 0.57% (19/3,341) in 2025, showing annual variation over the four-year study period. One patient was excluded due to archived medical records, and two patients were excluded due to incomplete data, leaving 54 patients for detailed analysis. Among these, 45 were male (83.33%) with a median age of 69.0 years (interquartile range, 61.0-74.75). Benign prostatic hyperplasia constituted the largest subgroup by primary condition (29/54, 53.70%), and transurethral resection of the prostate was the most common surgical procedure among the identified LEVT cases (28/54, 51.85%). Thrombosis predominantly involved the intermuscular veins (62.96%), followed by deep veins (35.19%). The median time to LEVT detection was 7 days after admission (IQR, 6-8) and 4 days after surgery (IQR, 3-5). Clinical manifestations were mainly local symptoms such as limb swelling or pain (79.63%). Anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin was the primary treatment (70.37%), and most patients experienced no significant complications (92.59%).
CONCLUSION: The overall procedure-based clinically detected postoperative LEVT rate during hospitalization in urological surgery was low, with annual variation observed over the four-year study period. Among the identified LEVT cases, benign prostatic hyperplasia was the most common primary condition, with intermuscular vein thrombosis being the most common type, and most cases were detected in the early postoperative period. Clinical attention should focus on continued perioperative VTE risk assessment and early recognition of clinically suspected LEVT.

Title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation paired with a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis for ankle-foot dysfunction among older adults following subacute stroke: clinical findings and exploratory neurophysiological analyses.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This work evaluated clinical effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) plus custom-made 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) for older adults living with post-stroke ankle-foot impairment. Neurophysiological assessments were also carried out for exploratory purposes, drawing exclusively on indirect physiological readouts.
