Title: Coronary artery anomalies in computed tomography of coronary arteries for symptomatic patients: Types, prevalence and association with atheromatous disease.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anomalous coronary arteries are rare but potentially dangerous. Early diagnosis and recognition can prevent serious outcomes. Our study aimed to determine the prevalence of coronary artery anomalies amongst symptomatic individuals who presented for computer tomography of coronary arteries (CTCA) and their trends with age and concurrent atherosclerotic disease.
METHODS: Retrospective study of all CTCAs for symptomatic patients was conducted over a 5-year period in a large healthcare network, including a dedicated heart hospital, to identify the types and prevalence of anomalous coronary arteries. Patients' age, symptomology and associated atherosclerotic burden represented by CAD-RADS and calcium scores were compared between the identified individuals with coronary artery anomalies.
RESULTS: A total of 13,596 patients were recruited. 296 (2.18%) patients had significant coronary anomalies. Mean age was 53.85 years. 211/296 (71.28%) patients had anomalous coronary artery origins. 180/296 (60.81%) patients had anomalous coronary artery courses in which 85/180 (47.22%) were potentially malignant (inter-arterial course). There were 25/296 (8.45%) patients with coronary artery fistulae and 12/296 (4.05%) patients with more complex coronary vascular malformations. There was statistical significance between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age and trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score.
CONCLUSION: Broad variability of incidence of coronary anomalies on imaging has been reported in the literature. To our knowledge, this study is amongst the first to demonstrate a statistically significant association between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age on CTCA, with a trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score also observed.

Title: Mid-pregnancy plasma environmental chemical exposures and maternal blood pressure in a pilot study of Black women.
Journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
Abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests Black women experience disproportionate exposure to environmental chemicals and diagnoses of hypertension during pregnancy. We characterized environmental chemicals and determined their associations with blood pressure in a cross-sectional analysis of Black women in Philadelphia. We measured 32 plasma chemicals using non-targeted analysis in samples collected between the 16th and 24th weeks of gestation in the MOMENTUM cohort (n = 68). We assessed the association between log2-transformed chemical abundance and blood pressure, as well as preterm hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), using regression analysis. We categorized chemical abundances into tertiles and modelled them as ordinal variables; blood pressure as a continuous variable; and preterm HDP as a binary variable. We assessed the mixture effect with a Weight Quantile Sum regression constraint in the positive direction. Each increase in one tertile of 4-methylbenzophenone (β = 4.48 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.84, 7.12), 4-tert-Butylcatechol (β = 3.83 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.53, 6.14), benzophenone (β = 4.05 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.49, 6.61), carvone (β = 3.50 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.19, 5.81), and tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (β = 3.98 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.23, 6.74) was cross-sectionally associated with a statistically significant increase in diastolic blood pressure. A mixture of flavoring and fragrance agents also showed a positive association with diastolic blood pressure (β = 3.05 mmHg; 95%CI: 0.60, 4.67). Exposures were not significantly associated with systolic blood pressure and preterm HDP. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in large-scale cohort studies.

Title: Explainable artificial intelligence in clinical decision support systems: a systematic review of techniques, clinical applications, evaluation, and future directions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as an important approach for improving the transparency and interpretability of artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support systems (CDSSs). However, evidence regarding the models and explainability techniques used in healthcare, their clinical evaluation, methodological quality, and progression toward real-world implementation remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the current evidence on XAI-enabled CDSSs, with particular emphasis on AI and XAI methods, clinical applications, validation, explainability evaluation, implementation, and methodological limitations.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261449460). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception through 30 June 2026 (searches run on 15 July 2026). Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles that applied artificial intelligence within healthcare clinical decision support systems, incorporated at least one explainability or interpretability technique, and demonstrated a direct role in clinical decision-making or decision support. Studies limited to prediction, classification, diagnosis, or prognostic modeling without a decision-support component were excluded. Two reviewers jointly screened titles and abstracts, independently assessed full texts, and independently extracted data using a standardized form informed by the CHARMS checklist. Risk of bias and applicability of prediction model studies were assessed using PROBAST, and reporting completeness was evaluated against relevant TRIPOD + AI recommendations where applicable. Due to substantial clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with SWiM guidance.
RESULTS: Of 2008 identified records, 68 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Publications increased substantially in 2025-2026, accounting for 47 of the 68 included studies. China and India contributed the largest number of studies (11 each), followed by the United States (10). Critical care/intensive care medicine and cardiology were the most frequently represented clinical specialties (13 studies each). Numeric patient-level sample size was reported in 35 studies. Among these, the median sample size was 973 (IQR 303-10,015; range 57-106,449), while the mean was 11,944, indicating a markedly right-skewed distribution. Internal validation was reported in 51 studies (75.0 %), whereas external validation was reported in 17 studies (25.0 %). Most systems remained at the research-prototype stage (n = 63, 92.6 %). One study (1.5 %) reported pilot testing in a clinical workflow, while only two studies (2.9 %) reported real-world or routine clinical deployment. Implementation status was unclear or not reported in two studies (2.9 %). Of the 63 studies for which PROBAST was applicable, 3 (4.8 %) were judged at low overall risk of bias and 3 (4.8 %) at high risk; the remainder were rated Unclear mainly because of incomplete reporting. Five studies describing non-prediction CDSS designs were classified as PROBAST not applicable. Clinician involvement was reported in 53 studies. Formal user studies with structured evaluation protocols were reported in 39 studies (57.4 %), but rigorous assessment of effects on decision quality or patient outcomes remained rare.
CONCLUSIONS: XAI-enabled CDSS research has expanded rapidly, yet remains largely confined to model development and technical explainability rather than rigorous clinical translation. Although SHAP and gradient-boosting methods currently predominate, external validation, real-world deployment, standardized evaluation of explanation quality, and meaningful human-centered assessment are still limited. Future work must prioritize multicenter external validation, transparent reporting, rigorous assessment of explanation fidelity and stability, active clinician and patient involvement, and prospective evaluation of effects on decision-making and patient outcomes. Closing the gap between algorithmic performance and clinically meaningful utility is essential for the safe, trustworthy, and responsible adoption of these systems.

Title: Radiofrequency ablation for tongue lymphatic malformations in children: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of radiofrequency ablation for tongue lymphatic malformations in a paediatric population and to explore predictors of symptom control.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all paediatric patients who underwent transoral radiofrequency ablation to a tongue lymphatic malformation between 2018 and 2025. The primary outcome of interest was successful control of symptoms with radiofrequency ablation alone. Secondary outcomes of interest included the degree of symptom control, complications following surgery and additional treatment types required. Non-parametric data was analysed using Mann-Whitney U test. Statistical significance was defined as p value < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 44 children were included. Lesions were classified using the Wiegand system. Stage I in 12 patients (27.3%), IIa in 5 (11.4%), IIb in 4 (9.1%), III in 12 (27.3%), IV in 11 (25.0%). Mixed disease predominated at higher stages, with 10 of the 11 stage IV lesions being mixed. Twenty-five (56.8%) patients had mixed microcystic and macrocystic disease whereas 19 patients (43.2%) had isolated microcystic disease. Symptom control with radiofrequency ablation alone was achieved in 73.8% patients (n = 31/42), with 100% Wiegand I patients, 4/5 (80%) Wiegand IIa patients, 4/4 (75%) Wiegand IIb, 7/12 (58.3%) Wiegand III, and 6/10 (60%) Wiegand IV patients achieving symptom control. Older age of first treatment was predictive of symptom control with radiofrequency ablation alone (p = 0.005). No statistically clear associations were observed for sex, prior therapies, or individual pre-operative symptom categories. Symptom improvement was recorded in 93.2% of patients (41/44). No patients reported worsening of symptoms. Nine patients required alternative therapies mainly to treat residual tongue swelling.
CONCLUSIONS: Radiofrequency ablation appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for managing symptomatic microcystic and mixed tongue lymphatic malformations and is useful as part of a multimodal treatment strategy. It was favoured particularly for controlling bleeding and improving surface related symptoms.

Title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy.
STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

Title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework.
Abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

Title: Second consensus statement on abdominal aortic aneurysms in Mexico.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive and life-threatening disease, with rupture-related mortality reaching up to 80% in Mexico. Limited national epidemiological data and the need to standardize diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up strategies prompted the development of the Second National Consensus on AAA in Mexico, coordinated by the Mexican Society of Angiology, Vascular and Endovascular Surgery (SMACVE), based on the Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines and adapted to local practice.
METHODS: The consensus was developed using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and a modified Delphi process. A panel of national and international experts evaluated 116 statements derived from Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines. Statements were discussed, reformulated when necessary, and subjected to structured voting. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement among participants.
RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for the majority of the evaluated statements, including recommendations on screening, diagnosis, preoperative assessment, medical management, indications for endovascular and open repair, rupture management, perioperative care, follow-up, and organizational aspects. Recommendations were adapted to the clinical practice environment and healthcare resources available within the Mexican healthcare system.
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides standardized definitions, diagnostic criteria, and management recommendations for AAA care in Mexico, aiming to promote evidence-based, uniform clinical practice adapted to local healthcare conditions.

Title: Estimating Functional Independence Measure Scores From Japanese Rehabilitation Notes Using a Large Language Model: Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) is a standard functional assessment tool in rehabilitation medicine; however, formal assessments are often conducted only at limited intervals. Free-text clinical notes contain more frequent observations of patients' functional status and may complement these assessments.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate item-level FIM scores from Japanese free-text rehabilitation notes using a locally deployed large language model (LLM) and to evaluate estimation performance; item-level estimability; and differences across diseases, therapy types, and admission FIM severity groups.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed free-text notes from physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) for patients hospitalized with cerebral infarction (CeI), hip fracture (HF), or vertebral fracture (VBF) at Saiseikai Moriyama Municipal Hospital between October 2019 and September 2024. Using zero-shot prompting, an LLM estimated all FIM items from each note. Estimated scores were matched to reference FIM scores recorded for the same patient on the same calendar date. Performance was evaluated using the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error, and quadratic weighted kappa. Estimation rates and comparisons with modal-score and last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) baselines were also examined.
RESULTS: Among 2,952,702 eligible note-item pairs from 164,039 retained rehabilitation-note-level outputs, the model produced 980,000 valid estimates, corresponding to an overall estimation rate of 33.2%. Among 170,744 note-item opportunities with an available same-day reference score, 57,246 (33.5%) were estimable, of which 77.7% (44,481/57,246) were within 1 point of the reference score. Estimates derived from OT notes had a lower MAE than those derived from PT notes in CeI and HF, whereas the difference was not significant in VBF. The LLM outperformed the modal-score baseline but had a higher MAE than the LOCF overall (0.825 vs 0.648).
CONCLUSIONS: The locally deployed LLM shows the potential to derive item-level FIM estimates from Japanese rehabilitation notes. Among estimable note-item pairs with a same-day reference FIM score, 77.7% were within 1 point of the reference score. These findings support the potential use of LLM-based estimation to structure functional information contained in routine rehabilitation notes and complement periodic FIM assessments. Further integration of multidisciplinary clinical records and external validation are needed to improve estimability and evaluate its value for longitudinal functional monitoring.

Title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD.
METHODS: A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO2), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO2 (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO2 improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory.
CONCLUSIONS: Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Anti-Müllerian Hormone Trajectories Across the Menopause Transition.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the trajectory of anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) decline leading to the final menstrual period, identify distinct AMH patterns, and assess their association with unique participant characteristics.
METHODS: SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation), a multisite, multiethnic perimenopausal cohort, was analyzed. Included participants had an observed final menstrual period and three or more measurements of AMH levels taken during perimenopause. Statistical modeling was used to identify AMH trajectory classes; participants were placed into predicted class based on best fit. Differences in baseline demographic and health characteristics were assessed by analysis of variance or χ2. Generalized estimating equation models were used to estimate the association between AMH trajectory class and outcomes, accounting for repeated measures.
RESULTS: A total of 1,131 women had at least three AMH measurements and an observed final menstrual period. Two AMH trajectory classes were observed: 448 participants (39.6%) with lower initial AMH and slower decline (low/slow [LS] group) and 683 participants (60.4%) with higher AMH and steeper decline (high/fast [HF] group). Participants in the LS group had a median AMH decline of 1.2 pg/mL/month; those in the HF group had a decline of 6.7 pg/mL/month. The LS classification was associated with baseline older age, higher body mass index (BMI), and non-White race and ethnicity. Trajectory classes did not differ by history of oligomenorrhea, presumptive polycystic ovarian syndrome, or smoking status. Participants in the LS group had worse postmenopausal cardiovascular risk profiles and were less likely to report frequent vasomotor symptoms after the final menstrual period.
CONCLUSION: Two different AMH trajectories to the final menstrual period were observed in a subsample of SWAN participants. Independent of a participant's premenopausal cardiovascular risk factors, lower starting AMH and slower decline were associated with higher postmenopausal cardiovascular risk.

Title: Posterior Inter-Antral Linear Ablation Using Pulsed Field Energy: Electrophysiological Validation and Early Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Durable conduction block across the left atrial roof remains challenging because of complex anatomy and limitations of thermal energy delivery. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) may enable a short posterior inter-antral line as an adjunctive strategy beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), providing linear conduction block at a more inferior posterior LA location than a conventional roofline. However, its electrophysiological characteristics and clinical relevance remain uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center, nonrandomized comparative cohort study, a prospectively enrolled cohort undergoing PVI plus posterior inter-antral linear ablation was compared with contemporaneous patients undergoing PVI without additional left atrial ablation. The primary clinical endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Propensity score matching was the primary comparative analysis; inverse probability of treatment weighting and multivariable Cox regression were sensitivity analyses. Among 306 patients, 65 underwent posterior inter-antral linear ablation and 241 underwent PVI alone. Posterior-line ablation produced characteristic reciprocal pacing responses and a caudal-to-cranial posterior wall activation pattern consistent with conduction block. During a median follow-up of 198 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 4 of 65 (6.2%) versus 38 of 241 (15.8%) patients. In the primary PSM analysis, posterior inter-antral linear ablation was associated with lower recurrence (HR 0.23; 95% CI 0.07-0.78), with consistent results in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Posterior inter-antral linear ablation using PFA provides a reproducible electrophysiological pattern of conduction block and was associated with lower short-term atrial arrhythmia recurrence than PVI alone in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. These findings warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

Title: KCNH1 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit prominent gain of function.
Abstract: Pathogenic variants in KCNH1, encoding the human ether-á-go-go voltage-gated potassium channel (EAG1, KV10.1), are associated with the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser syndrome (TBS), Zimmermann-Laband syndrome (ZLS), epileptic encephalopathy, and other undefined neurodevelopmental disorders. Investigating the functional consequences of KCNH1 variants can provide information about molecular and cellular pathophysiological mechanisms and help guide therapeutic directions. In this study, we determined the functional properties of 26 disease-associated KCNH1 variants including three recurrent and six that were previously unpublished. Findings were compared to the wildtype (WT) channel along with six rare population variants. Our approach used automated patch clamp recording of heterologously expressed KCNH1 variants in both the homozygous state (variant alone) and the clinically-relevant heterozygous state (variant co-expressed with WT channels). We also examined the impact of alternative splice isoforms on functional consequences of specific variants. We demonstrated that the majority of disease-associated KCNH1 variants exhibit features consistent with gain-of-function including hyperpolarized voltage-dependence of activation, accelerated activation kinetics, or both that promote hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential. By contrast, one unique variant discovered previously in an autism cohort had a depolarized voltage-dependence of activation and was associated with a depolarized resting potential in cells. Pharmacological testing of KCNH1 variants demonstrated differences in potency for channel block by imipramine and an investigational non-selective potassium channel blocker (LY97241) for specific variants. Collectively, our findings support gain-of-function as the most common, albeit not exclusive, molecular mechanism underlying KCNH1-related disorders and suggest opportunities for potential therapeutic drug repurposing strategies for these conditions.

Title: Heart failure beyond cardiology: a primary care perspective on the 2026 ESC guideline.
Home CHF feasibility trial protocol: Impact of at-home Subcutaneous furosemide in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Hospital admissions are common in patients with heart failure (HF), particularly in those with concomitant chronic kidney disease (HF-CKD). Hospitalisation is often driven by fluid overload, requiring intravenous furosemide. Subcutaneous furosemide is emerging as an alternative which may facilitate at-home treatment. This study will assess the feasibility of conducting a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people with HF-CKD.
METHODS: Stage one - Recruitment and monitoring of at-risk patients: We aim to recruit 200 people with HF-CKD with at least one hospital admission within the preceding year. These participants will be monitored for signs of fluid accumulation. Stage two - Treatment: The second stage will run contemporaneously to the first stage. The first 80 participants to develop fluid accumulation will be randomised to usual care (attend hospital and receive standard treatment) or at-home furosemide. The participants allocated to home treatment will administer SQIN-furosemide via a patch infusor device, 80 mg daily for five days, then be reviewed in a final clinic appointment. These participants will monitor their weight and observations daily, as well as receive a check-in call from the research team. Potassium levels will be checked twice over five days. The primary outcome of this feasibility study will be recruitment and retention of participants, as well as adherence to the intervention.
DISCUSSION: Findings from this feasibility trial will inform the planning of a definitive RCT to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people living with HF-CKD.

Title: Adverse Events Associated With Treatment for Anal High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions: A Systematic Review.
Journal: Journal of lower genital tract disease
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES/PURPOSES OF THE STUDY: To systematically review the type, severity, frequency, and reporting quality of adverse events (AEs) associated with treatment of anal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) to inform guideline development, clinical decision-making, and future research priorities, and improve patient-centered outcome assessment.
METHODS: We searched Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL databases for publications to October 11, 2024. Studies were included if reporting data on AEs relating to anal HSIL treatment. Study quality was assessed using an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Data were extracted on study characteristics, treatment protocols, and AEs.
RESULTS: Forty-two studies were included, of which 8 were high quality, 24 moderate quality, and 10 low quality. Most studies were conducted in men living with HIV and evaluated single-treatment modalities. There was considerable heterogeneity in AE definitions and data collection, precluding meta-analysis. Pain and bleeding were the most commonly reported AEs across all modalities. Ablative treatments were most frequently associated with pain (reported in 80% of studies), with radiofrequency ablation showing particularly high reported rates of bleeding (>80%). Topical treatments universally caused anal discomfort, with marked variation in terminology. Only 14 studies used a structured AE collection tool, and only 2 used validated instruments. The ANCHOR study reported fewer AEs than other studies.
CONCLUSIONS: AE reporting in anal HSIL treatment studies is inconsistent and poorly standardized. Validated definitions, structured reporting tools, and core outcome sets are urgently needed. Future studies should standardize treatment protocols, improve AE monitoring, and prioritize large comparative randomized controlled trials to guide clinical practice and shared decision-making.

Title: MACULAR STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION IN RETINAL DETACHMENT COMPLICATED BY PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY.
Journal: Ophthalmologica. Journal international d'ophtalmologie. International journal of ophthalmology. Zeitschrift fur Augenheilkunde
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Macular structural changes after surgery for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) complicated by proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) remain poorly characterised. The aim of this study was to evaluate longitudinal macular structural changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) and their relationship to visual function over 12 months in eyes undergoing pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with silicone oil tamponade for PVR-related RRD.
METHODS: Post-hoc analysis from a phase IIIb, single-centre, participant-masked, prospective, randomised controlled trial of slow-release dexamethasone in PVR-related RRD conducted at Moorfields Eye Hospital. One hundred and thirty-nine (139) eyes of 139 patients undergoing PPV with silicone oil tamponade for RRD with confirmed PVR-C were included. Spectral-domain OCT imaging and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, LogMAR) were obtained preoperatively and at 10 days, 6 months, and 12 months postoperatively. Retinal-layer thicknesses were obtained by manual segmentation and 13 qualitative biomarkers were graded. Univariable regression and Firth penalised multivariable logistic regression were used to identify early structural predictors of 12-month BCVA.
RESULTS: Central retinal thickness (CRT) increased significantly from 314.9 µm at 10 days to 370.9 µm at 12 months (p < 0.0001). The outer plexiform layer and outer nuclear layer showed dynamic changes over time. The proportion of eyes with epiretinal membrane (ERM) rose from 22.1% at 10 days to 41.2% at 6 months (p=0.001) and 49.6% at 12 months (p=0.011 versus 6 months), and cystoid macular oedema (CMO) increased from 20.7% to 52.2% (p<0.0001) and 62.6% (p = 0.029). Mean BCVA improved from 1.68 LogMAR preoperatively to 1.06 LogMAR at 10 days (p < 0.0001), with no significant further change to 0.92 LogMAR at 12 months. In univariable analysis, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) thickness, outer retinal layer thickness, gross full-thickness retinal disruption, disrupted ellipsoid and external limiting membrane, absence of a foveal bulge, subretinal PVR and persistent subretinal macular fluid at 10 days were associated with poorer 12-month BCVA (all p < 0.05). In the multivariable model, 10-day BCVA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.52, 95% CI 1.31-11.2) and gross full-thickness retinal disruption (aOR 10.51, 95% CI 1.16-1391) remained independently associated with moderate visual impairment at 12 months (BCVA worse than 6/38; LogMAR > 0.80), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.71.
CONCLUSIONS: Macular structural changes after surgery for PVR-related RRD reflect extensive cellular remodelling with progressive development of ERM and CMO. Early (10-day) postoperative OCT findings are associated with 12-month visual outcome and may help inform prognosis in PVR-related RRD.

Title: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Stroke: A Narrative Review of Pathophysiological Links, Clinical Evidence, and Diagnostic Implications.
Abstract: Background Sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) has long been hypothesized as a potential early warning sign of posterior circulation stroke, yet the causal association and clinical implications remain highly controversial. Summary This narrative review synthesizes current peer-reviewed evidence on the pathophysiological links, epidemiological associations, diagnostic strategies, and integrated management of SSNHL and stroke. Current findings demonstrate that anatomical and pathophysiological overlaps support the biological plausibility of this association, which is predominantly mediated by the vertebrobasilar circulatory system. Shared vascular and prothrombotic factors, including dyslipidemia, hyperhomocysteinemia, and MTHFR gene polymorphisms, may further contribute to the observed association. Clinically, SSNHL may present as an initial manifestation of posterior circulation infarction in a small subset of patients, particularly those with accompanying neurological symptoms or multiple vascular risk factors; however, existing epidemiological data are inconsistent, and there is insufficient evidence to define SSNHL as an independent predictor of stroke in the general population. Key Messages This review concludes that risk stratification and interdisciplinary collaboration between otolaryngologists and neurologists are critical in clinical practice: for high-risk SSNHL patients, timely neurovascular evaluation is warranted to enable early detection of cerebrovascular disease, and future large-scale prospective cohort studies and combined audiological-neurological assessment models are needed to clarify the causal relationship and optimize clinical pathways.

Title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
Abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

Title: Projected obstetric risks in an aging maternal population in Taiwan: a Bayesian age-period-cohort analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed childbearing may alter maternal and neonatal risk profiles and potentially challenge current healthcare strategies. Therefore, we aimed to provide comprehensive Bayesian projections of pregnancy outcomes through 2050 to inform urgent healthcare system adaptation.
METHODS: We analysed all singleton pregnancies in Taiwan using linked data from National Health Insurance and Birth Certificate Application databases from 2004 to 2021. Temporal trends and age-stratified prevalence were assessed for maternal (gestational hypertension [GHTN], gestational diabetes mellitus [GDM], mortality, sepsis, and postpartum hemorrhage) and neonatal (stillbirth, preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age, and large for gestational age) outcomes. Bayesian age-period-cohort models were applied to project prevalence and absolute burden through 2050.
RESULTS: From 2004 to 2021, total pregnancies declined by 25.3%, while the proportion of pregnancies among women aged ≥35 years nearly tripled (11.8%-34.6%). GHTN prevalence rose from 0.4% to 2.1% and GDM from 2.0% to 9.3%. By 2050, GHTN and GDM are projected to reach 26.4% (95% credible interval [CrI], 5.2%-67.4%) and 60.9% (95% CrI, 28.9%-85.0%), respectively, while the GDM estimate should be interpreted in light of one-step screening adoption after 2010. Preterm birth and low birth weight are projected to increase modestly to 11.2% and 11.9%. BAPC modeling indicates these trends are associated with advancing maternal age and cohort patterns, reflecting evolving risk profiles shaped by shifting healthcare and behavioral practices.
CONCLUSIONS: Obstetric risk is shifting due to demographic and generational transitions, requiring prenatal care systems to adopt more proactive and routine management approaches.

Title: Dexmedetomidine effects on metabolic rate over 5 days in humans.
Abstract: The alpha-2-adrenergic agonist drug dexmedetomidine induces sleep-like sedation and reduces global metabolic rate. Drug-induced metabolic suppression sustained over days in humans could be a strategy for reducing energy expenditure (EE), oxygen consumption (VO2), and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) during prolonged rescue or austere conditions with limited life-support. We tested the feasibility of reducing EE, VO2 and VCO2 measured with intermittent indirect calorimetry using subcutaneous infusion of dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg/hour for 18 hours per day over five days in healthy adults. Five participants received multiple days of dexmedetomidine in a laboratory setting, and five separate participants received placebo for one or five days. Relative to resting metabolic rate, dexmedetomidine infusion reduced VO2 (effects, 95%CI, at 6-hour time epoch: -0.084 L/min, -0.145 to -0.023), VCO2 (-0.067 L/min, -0.130 to -0.005) and EE (-577 kcal/day, -1016 to -137). Relative to placebo, dexmedetomidine produced light sedation (Richmond Agitation Sedation Score: -1.25; 95%CI -1.70 to -0.80 relative to placebo), with lower heart rate (-15 beats/minute; 95%CI -23 to -7) and core body temperature (-1.3ºC; 95%CI -1.7 to -0.8). Dexmedetomidine effects on all physiological variables decreased over time and were absent after day 2. Maximum and minimum plasma drug levels did not change over days. Participants reported rebound anxiety and insomnia after the study. Administering a sedating level of dexmedetomidine that reduces VO2, VCO2, and EE for 2 days was feasible in healthy adults. However, tolerance to drug effects develops by 3 days, which is a critical limitation for long-term use of this drug regimen.

Title: The effect of dual task-oriented circuit training on neuroplasticity and walking adaptability in subacute stroke patients: A pilot and feasibility study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with a substantial proportion of survivors experiencing persistent limitations in functional mobility. Although many individuals regain the ability to walk in structured clinical environments, only a minority achieve independent community ambulation due to cognitive-motor interference (CMI). The subacute phase is characterized by heightened neuroplastic potential and responsiveness to rehabilitation. Dual Task-Oriented Circuit Training (DTOCT) integrates task-oriented circuit training with concurrent cognitive challenges and may provide a functionally relevant approach to addressing cognitive-motor interference. However, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects in subacute stroke remain unclear.
METHODS: This three-arm, participant-blinded, randomized pilot and feasibility trial will recruit 36 individuals with subacute stroke and allocate them equally to DTOCT, Task-Oriented Circuit Training (TOCT), or Dual Task Training (DTT). Participants will receive three supervised sessions per week for 4 weeks (12 sessions). Primary outcomes will assess feasibility and safety, including adherence, retention, adverse events, heart rate, blood pressure, and perceived exertion. Secondary exploratory outcomes will include walking endurance assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test, gait speed using the 10-Meter Walk Test, walking adaptability using the Standardized Walking Obstacle Course, and serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor as an exploratory peripheral biomarker associated with neuroplasticity.
DISCUSSION: This pilot study is designed to determine the feasibility and safety of DTOCT and to generate preliminary effect estimates for clinical and neurobiological outcomes. The findings will inform primary outcome selection, intervention refinement, and sample-size estimation for a subsequent adequately powered randomized controlled trial rather than establish definitive efficacy or superiority.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07494357 (registered prospectively). Protocol ID: IKFR-202603.01).

Title: Cross-platform comparison of diabetic foot ulcer transcriptomes identifies partially concordant disease-associated signals.
Abstract: The extent to which diabetic foot ulcer transcriptomic findings agree across cohorts remains uncertain. We compared an RNA sequencing cohort of 13 ulcer and eight diabetic foot skin samples with a microarray cohort of six ulcer and three diabetic foot skin samples. Single-cell data from 26 participants were analyzed after aggregating gene counts within each patient and cell type. A further cohort of 10 ulcer and 11 healthy foot-skin samples provided a descriptive directional comparison. Healing-status comparisons were exploratory. The primary analysis selected 4,704 differentially expressed gene identifiers; 2,943 were represented among the 17,502 gene symbols shared with the microarray cohort. Of these, 1,254 had concordant directions and nominal microarray P < 0.05, including 1,028 with microarray false discovery rate < 0.05. Direction agreement was 70.2%, and overall effect-rank correlation was modest (Spearman ρ = 0.29). Five Hallmark gene sets met the cross-cohort enrichment criteria. More specific functional analysis of the stricter supported set highlighted cornified-envelope formation, keratinization and inflammatory-cell migration. In the additional cohort, 611 of 823 represented genes from this set agreed in direction, although its comparator differed. Twelve keratinocyte genes met the cell-type differential-expression threshold; this finding does not establish cell-type exclusivity. Healing-status results were sensitive to covariate adjustment. These data support partial concordance in ulcer-associated epithelial, inflammatory and metabolic expression patterns. Limited cohort coverage, comparator differences and unresolved confounding preclude a universal disease signature, healing predictor or causal interpretation.

Title: Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with impaired myocardial perfusion.
Abstract: A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017-2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0-5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4-2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4-3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

Title: A Physiology-Informed Deep Learning Approach for Sleep-EEG Brain Age Estimation.
Journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
Abstract: Sleep electroencephalography (EEG) contains rich signatures of biological aging, but deep-learning brain-age models often provide limited physiologic readouts. This study presents a physiology-informed deep learning framework that estimates brain age from whole-night polysomnography (PSG) and provides spectral-band-level and sleep-stage-level readouts of the features associated with age predictions. Trained and evaluated on approximately 10,000 PSG recordings across four cohorts (SHHS, MrOS, STAGES, and CFS), the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.89 $\pm$ 5.01 years. External validation in an independent cohort (HomePAP) yielded an MAE of 5.41 $\pm$ 4.57 years. The brain age gap (BAG; predicted minus chronological age) was associated with mortality risk. Specifically, each 10-year increase in BAG was associated with a 19% increase in all-cause mortality risk (hazard ratio (HR)=1.19 [95% CI: 1.11-1.28]; p<0.001) and a 25% increase in cardiovascular mortality risk (HR=1.25 [1.07-1.46]; p=0.006) after adjustment for covariates. A trainable Gabor filter bank provides explicit center-frequency and bandwidth parameters for the learned spectral representation. Spectral features extracted using the learned filter bank explained additional variance in age beyond features computed from canonical EEG bands (incremental $\triangle \rm{R}^{2}$=4.7%; p<0.001). Attribution analysis with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) revealed age-dependent shifts in spectral importance, including decreased delta and increased beta contributions with age. The model also reflected known age-related changes in sleep stages (increased wake, reduced N3/REM). Collectively, these findings provide brain-age estimates with explicit spectral-band-level and sleep-stage-level readouts that align with established sleep neurophysiology.

Title: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: feasibility, practical benefits, and surgical pitfalls from a single-center experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe surgical outcomes, technical considerations, and feasibility of redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery using initial cases as a reference cohort.
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective review of minimally invasive mitral valve surgery performed between January 2014 and January 2024 was conducted. Perioperative data, mid-term survival, and cardiac-related events were assessed in both initial and redo groups.
RESULTS: A total of 647 patients were included: 30 in the redo group and 617 in the initial group. The redo group had higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II scores (p < 0.001). In the redo group, 26 (86.7%) had undergone previous cardiac surgery via sternotomy, and 18 (60.0%) had previous mitral valve surgery. The operative time was longer in the redo group (p = 0.041), while the cross-clamping time was longer in the initial group (p = 0.019), and cardiopulmonary bypass time was comparable between groups (p = 0.95). Intubation time (p = 0.049), intensive care unit stay (p = 0.020), and in-hospital stay (p = 0.003) were longer in the redo group. However, there were no significant differences in postoperative chest tube output for 24 h (p = 0.32) or blood transfusion requirements (p = 0.087). The overall survival rates at 5 years were 70.7% (95% CI: 41.0%-87.0%) vs. 92.0% (95% CI: 88.0%-94.0%) for the redo and initial groups, respectively. Freedom from cardiac-related events did not significantly differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was feasible despite higher surgical risk and longer operative times. Early and mid-term cardiac-related outcomes appeared acceptable, although overall survival was lower in redo cases.

Title: Dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether dual antiplatelet therapy improves survival and major ischemic outcomes, and whether it increases major bleeding, compared with aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin plus a platelet adenosine diphosphate receptor inhibitor with aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding. Risk ratios were pooled with random-effects models.
RESULTS: Nine randomized trials involving 3,516 patients were included. Eight trials involving 3,496 patients reported all-cause mortality. Dual antiplatelet therapy was not associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (risk ratio 0.77, 95% confidence interval 0.34-1.75), myocardial infarction (risk ratio 0.92, 95% confidence interval 0.56-1.50), stroke (risk ratio 0.68, 95% confidence interval 0.33-1.43), or major adverse cardiovascular events (four trials, 3,054 patients; risk ratio 0.69, 95% confidence interval 0.41-1.16). Major bleeding was increased in the primary analysis (risk ratio 2.28, 95% confidence interval 1.48-3.52), but this association was attenuated after exclusion of the largest contemporary trial.
CONCLUSIONS: In randomized evidence, dual antiplatelet therapy did not clearly reduce mortality or major ischemic events after coronary artery bypass grafting compared with aspirin alone. Routine, unselected use is not supported, and individualized postoperative antiplatelet decisions remain warranted.

Title: Periodontitis Beyond ASCVD: Emerging Cardiovascular Phenotypes in Perio-Medicine.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis is increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory disease with systemic implications beyond the oral cavity. Within perio-medicine, its association with cardiovascular disease has been extensively investigated, particularly in relation to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). However, the field is now expanding toward a broader and more phenotype-specific cardiovascular framework.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review critically examines how the periodontitis-cardiovascular field has evolved from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a broader spectrum of cardiovascular phenotypes, with particular emphasis on differences in evidence maturity, contemporary mechanistic concepts, and unresolved translational questions.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Evidence from mechanistic, observational, and interventional studies was qualitatively synthesized according to its contribution to established clinical associations, supportive mechanistic evidence, emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, and unresolved questions regarding causality and clinical translation.
RESULTS: The association between periodontitis and coronary atherosclerotic disease represents the most mature component of the literature, with substantial observational and meta-analytic support, while ischemic cerebrovascular disease is also supported by consistent but more heterogeneous evidence. Beyond ASCVD, atrial fibrillation and heart failure currently represent the most developed emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, whereas evidence concerning abdominal aortic aneurysm and venous thromboembolism remains more preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Contemporary mechanistic models extend beyond bacteremia and systemic inflammation to include endothelial dysfunction, thrombo-inflammatory signaling, trained immunity, immune-cell trafficking, functional dysregulation of the oral microbiome, and shared biological vulnerabilities. However, these pathways differ markedly in cardiovascular-specific evidentiary maturity and should not be interpreted as equivalent evidence of human causality. Periodontal therapy can improve inflammatory biomarkers, endothelial function, selected metabolic parameters, and blood pressure in specific populations, but a persistent translational gap remains between surrogate-marker improvement and demonstrated reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Periodontitis may also contribute to chronic systemic inflammatory burden in susceptible individuals, although its role within cardiovascular residual inflammatory risk remains an emerging hypothesis.
CONCLUSIONS: The periodontal-cardiovascular field is evolving from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a phenotype-specific continuum of evidence maturity. Periodontitis is best interpreted as a potential modifier of cardiovascular vulnerability rather than as an established causal determinant. Future research should prioritize adequately powered cardiovascular-outcome trials, standardized periodontal phenotyping, and prospective validation of emerging phenotypes and mechanistic frameworks before periodontal information can be considered clinically actionable for cardiovascular prevention.

Title: Three-Year Follow-Up of Delandistrogene Moxeparvovec in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: Long-Term Phase 3 EMBARK Trial Results.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delandistrogene moxeparvovec, an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy, delivers an optimized micro-dystrophin transgene to address dystrophin deficiency in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). EMBARK was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-part crossover study evaluating the safety and effectiveness of delandistrogene moxeparvovec in patients with DMD who are ambulatory aged ≥ 4 to < 8 years. After completion of the EMBARK study at 2 years, patients had the option to enroll into the long-term follow-up open-label EXPEDITION study.
METHODS: Three-year functional outcomes from patients treated with delandistrogene moxeparvovec in EMBARK part 1 (single intravenous dose 1.33 × 1014 vg/kg; n = 64) were compared with a matched propensity score weighted external control (EC) cohort (n = 143) derived from randomized controlled clinical trials (patients treated with placebo only) and natural history datasets. Mixed-effects models for repeated measures accounted for missing data and estimated changes from baseline and between-cohort differences. All P values are nominal.
RESULTS: At 3 years post-infusion, patients treated in part 1 of EMBARK (aged 7-10 years at 3 years) suggested sustained and statistically significant differences versus the matched EC cohort in change from baseline in North Star Ambulatory Assessment total score (between-cohort least-squares mean difference, 4.39 points; P = 0.0002), Time to Rise (- 6.05 s; P < 0.0001), and 10-m Walk/Run (- 2.70 s; P = 0.0039), suggesting durable slowing of disease progression. No new safety signals were identified through year 3, with no emerging cardiac safety concerns as the left ventricular ejection fraction remained above the normal threshold of 55% in this population over 3 years. There were no treatment-related deaths or discontinuations due to adverse events during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: The 3-year follow-up of patients with DMD who are ambulatory treated in EMBARK part 1 compared with external comparators suggests durable functional benefit and a consistent safety profile following treatment with delandistrogene moxeparvovec, which may indicate long-term disease trajectory modification and increasing divergence from natural history over time. Graphical abstract available for this article.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBERS: EMBARK: NCT05096221; EXPEDITION: NCT05967351.

Title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group.
CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

Title: An immediate reperfusion sign might increase the likelihood of favourable outcomes in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease-related stroke who received stent-retriever-based thrombectomy.
Abstract:
OBJECTS: To investigate the relationship between the presence of an "immediate reperfusion sign (IRS)" during retrievable stent-based thrombectomy and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel-occluded acute ischaemic stroke related to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) treated with stent retrievers.
METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated. Univariate analysis and partial correlation analysis were also performed.
RESULTS: Eighty-two ICAD-LVO patients were identified from 421 endovascularly treated AIS patients from 2015 to 2024. Fifty-four of them were ultimately included in the analysis, and an IRS was observed in 41 of these patients (75.9%). Favourable outcomes were significantly more frequent in the IRS (+) group (51.2% versus 7.7%, p=0.005). The sensitivity of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes was 95.5% (21/22), the specificity was 37.5% (12/32), the positive predictive value was 51.2% (21/41), and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.3% (12/13). Additionally, the presence of an IRS, as well as age, baseline NIHSS score and successful final reperfusion, was significantly different between the favourable and unfavourable groups. Partial correlation analysis revealed a moderate correlation (r=0.412; p=0.002) between the comprehensive reperfusion score (in which the presence of an IRS and successful final reperfusion was counted as 1 point) and favourable outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In our respective cohort of patients, the presence of an IRS during stent-retriever-based thrombectomy appeared to indicate a higher rate of first-pass-effect and a 3-month favourable outcome in acute LVO stroke patients with ICAD.

Title: Outcomes of Handmade Tri-leaflet ePTFE Valved Conduits for RVOT Reconstruction: A Propensity-Matched Analysis Compared with PVR.
Abstract: We aimed to evaluate the long-term durability and valve function of handmade expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) valved conduits of different calibers and compare their outcomes with those of bioprosthetic pulmonary valve replacement (PVR). We retrospectively reviewed 100 patients undergoing RVOT reconstruction between 2007 and 2025: 66 with ePTFE conduits and 34 with bioprosthetic valves. Patients were categorized into small-conduit, large-conduit, and PVR groups. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Mean age was 1.6 ± 1.8, 11.2 ± 6.5, and 26.3 ± 16.9 years in the small-conduit, large-conduit, and PVR groups, respectively (p < 0.0001). Ten-year survival was similar among groups (100%, 100%, and 97%; p = 0.19). In contrast, the small-conduit group showed significantly lower freedom from RVOT reoperation than the large-conduit and PVR groups (53%, 85%, and 93%; p < 0.001), driven by progressive pulmonary stenosis (10-year freedom from moderate pulmonary stenosis: 9%, 55%, and 58%; p = 0.01). Freedom from moderate pulmonary regurgitation remained comparable (80%, 94%, and 85%; p = 0.37). In the matched cohort, conduit and PVR groups demonstrated similar freedom from reoperation (94% vs. 89%; p = 0.34), with numerically better valve function in the conduit group. In conclusion, large-caliber handmade ePTFE valved conduits demonstrated favorable long-term durability, with outcomes comparable to PVR in adolescent- and adult-sized patients. They may be a reasonable option for selected younger patients requiring redo RVOT reconstruction.

Title: Comparative Effectiveness of Individual Angiotensin Receptor Blockers on Osteoporosis and Osteoporotic Fracture Risk: A Nationwide Active-Comparator New-User Cohort Study.
Abstract: Osteoporosis is a major cause of morbidity and fragility fractures in older adults, and increasing evidence suggests that antihypertensive therapies may influence skeletal health beyond blood pressure control. Although angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have been associated with favorable skeletal outcomes, whether clinically relevant heterogeneity exists among individual ARBs remains unclear. Telmisartan possesses distinctive pharmacological properties, including partial peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) agonistic activity, which may confer additional effects on bone metabolism. This study evaluated whether skeletal outcomes differ between telmisartan and other ARBs using an active-comparator new-user design. To evaluate whether clinically relevant differences in osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture risk exist between telmisartan and other ARBs using Taiwan's Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC) Database. Using Longitudinal Generation Tracking Database (LGTD) housed within the Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC), we conducted a nationwide active-comparator new-user cohort study. Hypertensive patients aged 51-80 years who newly initiated telmisartan or another ARB between 2002 and 2021 were identified. Propensity score matching (1:4) was performed to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was a composite of incident osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture and time to first osteoporotic fracture was additionally evaluated as a secondary outcome. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. During a mean follow-up of 4.35 ± 4.12 years, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture compared with other ARBs (adjusted HR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.53-0.79). In analyses of individual outcomes, telmisartan use was associated with lower risks of osteoporosis (adjusted HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.84) and hip fracture (adjusted HR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.70). In the secondary fracture-only analysis, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of first osteoporotic fracture (adjusted HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90). Compared with other ARBs, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fractures in this nationwide cohort. These findings suggest that clinically relevant heterogeneity may exist within the ARB class and that antihypertensive drug selection may influence skeletal outcomes beyond blood pressure control. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

Title: Symptom burden profiles and applied medication strategies in the days before and after initiation of palliative sedation in advanced cancer patients: an international prospective multicentre observational study (PALSED).
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced cancer patients may experience refractory suffering at the end of life despite optimal symptom management. When symptoms can no longer be controlled, or not within an acceptable timeframe, palliative sedation may be indicated. However, evidence on symptom severity and pharmacological strategies before sedation remains limited. This study aimed to characterize symptom burden and medication use in the 24 h before and after initiation of palliative sedation.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, data were collected from adult cancer patients receiving palliative sedation at seven European care settings (hospital wards, hospices, and PCUs). Healthcare professionals documented symptoms, pharmacological management, and sedation characteristics. Symptom prevalence and severity was assessed by patients or proxies using the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System (ESAS).
RESULTS: Among 80 patients with palliative sedation, multiple refractory symptoms were common at initiation; 81% had two or more symptoms. Dyspnoea (23%), delirium (18%), and exhaustion (16%) were the primary symptoms prompting sedation. ESAS data (n = 66) showed high prevalence of drowsiness, appetite loss, tiredness, and reduced wellbeing (73-91%), with severe burden scores (≥ 7) in 63-78%. Prior palliative sedation, patients with fewer symptoms (1-2) received a wider range of medications, including corticosteroids, cardiovascular agents, and anti-infectives, while those with ≥ 3 symptoms more often received anxiolytics, hypnotics, and sedatives. After initiation, most medications were discontinued; opioids were continued, and midazolam was the predominant continuously administered sedative.
CONCLUSION: Refractory suffering often reflected overall clinical decline rather than isolated symptoms. While pre-sedation medication use varied, post-initiation strategies were consistent across patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Association of Blood Heavy Metal Concentrations with Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in a Consecutive Single-Center Cardiac Catheterization Cohort.
Abstract: Environmental heavy metal exposure is increasingly recognized as a potentially important but underappreciated contributor to cardiovascular disease, yet its relationship to directly observed coronary artery disease (CAD) remains poorly defined. In this single-center cohort of 52 consecutive adults undergoing cardiac catheterization at an urban Chicago tertiary care center, we paired elemental exposure profiles with direct angiographic assessment in a racially diverse, socioeconomically vulnerable population. While no individual metal independently explained obstructive CAD, circulating metal exposure patterns were more revealing: Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression demonstrated that increasing overall metal burden was associated with worse coronary phenotypes, suggesting that environmental exposures may act collectively rather than in isolation. Lead and mercury emerged as the strongest contributors and were enriched relative to National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) reference populations. Taken together, these findings offer early but meaningful evidence that environmental toxicant burden may represent an underrecognized layer of cardiovascular risk, particularly in urban communities where industrial history, aging infrastructure, and socioeconomic disadvantage intersect. This work highlights the importance of viewing cardiovascular disease not only through the lens of traditional risk factors, but also through the environments in which patients live.

Title: Baseline neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio is associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A new index, the neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol ratio (NHR), has been reported to predict atherosclerosis and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This study aimed to investigate the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (MPA/GPA).
METHODS: Clinical data of 150 patients with MPA/GPA were analysed retrospectively. Baseline demographic data, the Birmingham vasculitis activity score (BVAS), the five-factor score (FFS), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. All-cause mortality, relapse, end-stage kidney disease, cerebrovascular accident (CVA), and ACS were evaluated as subsequent complications. NHR was calculated using the following formula: neutrophil count (× 1000/mm3) / HDL-cholesterol levels (mg/dL). NHR was analysed both as a continuous variable and using exploratory categorical cut-offs. Death before CVA was treated as a competing event in the cumulative incidence analysis.
RESULTS: The median age was 63.5 years (64.0% female). Baseline NHR was significantly correlated with baseline BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. Of the five subsequent complications, only subsequent CVA demonstrated a significant area under the curve in a receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of baseline NHR. Continuous NHR was not significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP. In complementary exploratory analyses using the cohort-derived cut-off, patients with baseline NHR ≥ 0.17 had a higher frequency of subsequent CVA and a lower CVA-free survival rate than those with baseline NHR < 0.17. The former group also had a higher cumulative incidence of CVA when death before CVA was treated as a competing event. NHR ≥ 0.17 remained significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent CVA in patients with MPA/GPA. Key Points • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio was significantly correlated with baseline Birmingham vasculitis activity score, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein levels in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis. • Patients with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 had a significantly higher risk of subsequent cerebrovascular accident and a lower cerebrovascular accident-free survival rate than those with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio <0.17. • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 remained independently associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident after adjustment for age and C-reactive protein.

Title: Primary, atrial secondary, and ventricular secondary mitral regurgitation in the general population.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While primary mitral valve regurgitation (PMR) results from structural abnormalities of the mitral valve leaflets, secondary mitral valve regurgitation (SMR) arises from either mitral annular dilatation (atrial type, aSMR) or left ventricle remodelling (ventricular type, vSMR) in the absence of intrinsic leaflet disease. Although SMR is considered the most common cause of clinically relevant mitral regurgitation (MR), population-based data on its prevalence, subtype distribution, and clinical profiles are lacking. We aimed to determine the prevalence of PMR and SMR and to characterize PMR, aSMR, and vSMR in the general population.
METHODS: We analyzed the first 10,000 participants of the population-based Hamburg City Health Study enrolled 2016-2019; 8543 echocardiographic examinations were available. Mitral valve morphology and function were independently assessed by two investigators. PMR was defined by the presence of intrinsic leaflet pathology, whereas SMR was classified as ventricular when left ventricular ejection fraction was less than 50% or less than 55% in the presence of geometric distortion (tenting area ≥ 150 mm2 or coaptation depth ≥ 10 mm) and cases with left ventricular ejection fraction equal to or above 50% were classified as aSMR.
RESULTS: A total of 216 participants had moderate or severe MR (2.53% of the total cohort, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.20%-2.89%, see Fig. 3). Of these, 148 were classified as SMR (68.5%, 95% CI: 61.8%-74.7%), the remaining were mainly of primary etiology (31.5%, 95% CI: 25.3%-38.2%). Among SMR cases, aSMR was predominant (84.5%, 95% CI: 77.5%-89.9%), whereas vSMR accounted for 15.5% (95% CI: 10.1%-22.4%). Compared with aSMR, individuals with vSMR were older, more symptomatic, and more frequently had atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Echocardiographic parameters indicated more advanced cardiac remodelling and dysfunction in vSMR. Compared with SMR, participants with PMR had greater MR severity, while age and the proportion of women were numerically higher without reaching statistical significance. During a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 10 participants had died, with all-cause mortality being significantly higher among participants with PMR than among those with aSMR.
CONCLUSION: In this population-based cohort, SMR accounted for two-thirds of relevant MR, with aSMR being the predominant subtype. MR severity was higher in PMR as compared to SMR.
