Distinct echocardiographic and clinical profiles suggest more advanced disease in vSMR. Multivariate analysis revealed that atrial fibrillation was significantly more present in the vSMR cohort. These findings highlight the need for refined SMR subclassification and longitudinal studies to define prognostic implications and clinically meaningful definitions. All-cause mortality was highest in participants with PMR than in those with aSMR.

Title: GLP-1 RA Prescribing in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Cancer.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used to treat type 2 diabetes, yet little is known about its utilization patterns in patients with cancer history, given limited oncology-specific guidance.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate trends and factors associated with GLP-1 RA use among Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, comparing those with and without cancer history.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare linked data to identify patients diagnosed with 7 common cancers in 2010 to 2021 and preexisting type 2 diabetes before cancer diagnosis. A noncancer cohort with type 2 diabetes was identified from a 5% random sample of Medicare beneficiaries and matched 1:1 to patients with cancer based on sociodemographic characteristics; controls were assigned a pseudo-index date corresponding to their matched patient's cancer diagnosis date. Beneficiaries were followed up annually until death or December 31, 2022, for TM or December 31, 2021, for MA. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to July 2026.
EXPOSURES: Diagnosis of 1 of 7 common cancers.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Any GLP-1 RA use. Proportions of beneficiaries with any GLP-1 RA use annually were stratified by traditional Medicare (TM) and Medicare Advantage (MA). Multivariable logistic regression examined (1) differences in GLP-1RA use between cancer and noncancer cohorts with and without adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities and diabetes-related complications; (2) cancer-specific factors associated with GLP-1RA use among the cancer cohort after 2018.
RESULTS: A total of 373 278 Medicare beneficiaries (mean [SD] age, 76.1 [6.6] years; 188 746 [50.6%] female) with cancer and diabetes and 373 278 noncancer controls (153 358 unique beneficiaries) were included. GLP-1 RA use increased from 85 beneficiaries (0.5%) to 9083 beneficiaries (8.2%) and from 138 beneficiaries (0.9%) to 9300 beneficiaries (6.2%) in the cancer and noncancer cohorts, respectively, from 2010 to 2022 under TM; a similar increase was observed under MA. Despite higher unadjusted GLP-1 RA use among the cancer cohort than the noncancer cohort (probability difference, TM: 1.19 [95% CI, 0.94 to 1.44] percentage points [pp]; P < .001; MA: 0.45 [95% CI, 0.21 to 0.68] pp, P < .001), adjusted analysis showed no significant differences in GLP-1 RA use under TM (adjusted probability difference, 0.16 [95% CI, -0.10 to 0.41,] pp; P = .22) and lower use among cancer cohort under MA (-0.52 [95% CI, -0.76 to -0.28] pp; P < .001). Complications or comorbidities, including obesity (adjusted probability difference, TM: 3.35 [95% CI, 3.10 to 3.61] pp; P < .001; MA: 2.42 [95% CI, 2.19 to 2.64] pp; P < .001), dyslipidemia (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.26 [95% CI, 2.03 to 2.50] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.80 [95% CI, 1.57 to 2.03] pp; P < .001), neuropathy (adjusted probability difference: TM: 3.91 [95% CI, 3.64 to 4.19] pp; P < .001; MA: 3.17 [95% CI, 2.94 to 3.41] pp; P < .001), retinopathy (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.02 [95% CI, 1.78 to 2.27] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.84 [95% CI, 1.63 to 2.06] pp; P < .001), and chronic kidney disease (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.01 [95% CI, 1.76 to 2.26] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.63 [95% CI, 1.40 to 1.85] pp; P < .001) were associated with greater likelihood of GLP-1RA use. Within the cancer cohort, breast (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.05 [95% CI, 0.43 to 1.66] pp; P = .001; MA: 0.89 [95% CI, 0.37 to 1.41] pp; P = .001), gynecologic (adjusted probability difference, MA: 1.13 [95% CI, 0.45 to 1.81] pp; P = .001), and prostate (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.30 [95% CI, 0.72 to 1.88] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.07 [95% CI, 0.56 to 1.58] pp; P < .001) cancers were associated with higher GLP-1 RA use than colorectal cancer, while pancreatic cancer was associated with lower GLP-1 RA use (adjusted probability difference, TM: -2.55 [95% CI, -3.17 to -1.93] pp; P < .001; MA: -1.64 [95% CI, -2.23 to -1.05] pp; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this retrospective study of Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, GLP-1 RA use increased substantially and primarily was associated with metabolic risk profile, with limited associations with cancer status. Variation across cancer types and stages suggests oncologic context may influence prescribing.

Title: Prescribing SGLTis and GLP-1 RAs for Patients With Type 2 Diabetes, Guideline Updates, and Longitudinal Knowledge Assessment Scores.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduce cardiovascular and kidney events in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who have established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease, yet prescribing to these patients remains low.
OBJECTIVES: To describe temporal patterns in SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA prescribing before and after the 2019 American Diabetes Association (ADA) guideline update and to assess whether these patterns differed across physicians with subsequently measured different first-year American Board of Internal Medicine Longitudinal Knowledge Assessment (LKA) scores.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This serial cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2025 through January 2026, using 2017 to 2022 traditional Medicare claims. Endocrinologists first participating in the 2022 to 2023 LKA and the Medicare beneficiaries with T2D they treated were included.
EXPOSURE: Time relative to the 2019 ADA guideline update.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The annual patient-year SGLT2i and GLP-1RA guideline-targeted and nontargeted patient fill rates were the main outcome. Linear physician, year, and target subgroup fixed-effects regression models were estimated, with patient demographic and health risk controls to evaluate within-physician associations between guideline-targeted vs nontargeted patient-year fill rates each year relative to 2018 (the year before the guideline update). The variation in these associations across first-year LKA score quartiles was also evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 1061 endocrinologists caring for 177 284 Medicare beneficiaries with T2D (mean [SD] age, 74.5 [6.1] years; mean [SD] 54.4% [49.8] female; mean [SD] 9.3% [29.1] Black, 6.6% [24.9] Hispanic, and 76.2% [42.6] White non-Hispanic) were included. Adjusted guideline-targeted SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA fill rates increased monotonically from 2018 to 2022 by 11.4 percentage points (pp) (95% CI, 10.5 to 12.3 pp; P < .001) and 2.4 (95% CI, 1.4 to 3.3 pp; P < .001) for SGLT2is and GLP-1 RAs targeted vs nontargeted subgroups, respectively. The associated SGLT2i increase was 3.9 pp (95% CI, 1.4 to 6.5 pp) larger for patients of endocrinologists with top vs bottom LKA quartile scores (P = .003), but for GLP-1 RAs, this association was not statistically significant with wide confidence intervals.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study, 2019 ADA guideline update timing was associated with substantially increased SGLT2i and moderately increased GLP-1 RA guideline-concordant prescribing among guideline-targeted, compared with nontargeted, patient subgroups by 2020. These increases in SGLT2i guideline congruent prescribing were associated with higher subsequently measured first-year LKA scores.

Title: A clinical-radiological model for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbation of COPD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) has emerged as a promising tool for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) phenotyping. However, its prognostic value in acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) remains insufficiently explored, and existing risk stratification models have limited integration of imaging-derived metrics. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic model that integrates multidimensional clinical variables with QCT-derived metrics, and to compare its predictive performance with traditional clinical scores for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥40 years hospitalized with severe AECOPD were enrolled from September 2010 to October 2024, with collection of demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory indices, and chest CT imaging data. The cohort was randomly split into training and testing sets (7:3). Candidate predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Four classification models were developed and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Discriminative performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and compared with conventional clinical scores.
RESULTS: A total of 465 patients with AECOPD were included, of whom 47 (10.1%) died during hospitalization. Five independent predictors were identified: confusion, lymphocyte count <0.8 × 109/L, chronic heart failure, white blood cell count ≥10 × 109/L, and reduced pulmonary vascular fractal dimension. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI, 0.738-0.965) in the testing set, significantly outperforming other models and established clinical scores.
CONCLUSIONS: A predictive model integrating QCT-derived metrics with clinical features improved AECOPD in-hospital mortality prediction over traditional scores, supporting its utility for individualized risk stratification and management.

Title: Chronic Impact of Cavo-Tricuspid Isthmus Ablation on the Adjacent Right Coronary Artery: The IMPACT-CTI Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relative to radiofrequency ablation (RFA), pulsed field ablation (PFA) raises concerns regarding chronic coronary narrowing when energy is delivered adjacent to coronary arteries. Because PFA can provoke acute coronary vasospasm, many operators employ RFA near coronary vessels, although the comparative long-term coronary effects of PFA vs RFA are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to compare the chronic impact of cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI) ablation with PFA vs RFA vs no CTI ablation on the adjacent right coronary artery (RCA) and to explore factors associated with progressive RCA narrowing.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective registry included consecutive patients undergoing atrial fibrillation ablation who received CTI ablation with PFA or RFA or received no CTI ablation (control) and who had baseline and follow-up coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography, with blinded assessment of the RCA segment adjacent to the CTI. The primary endpoint was a ≥10% reduction in RCA caliber from baseline to the last available follow-up CT, analyzed as an event rate; ≥20% reduction and progression to clinically significant stenosis were secondary assessments. Continuous change in RCA dimension over follow-up was analyzed secondarily.
RESULTS: In total, 155 patients were included: 39 PFA, 59 RFA, and 57 control. The mean age was 69.7 ± 9.6 years, 45% were women, and 55% had coronary artery disease (CAD). CTI block was achieved in all ablation patients. For the primary endpoint, assessed from baseline to the last available follow-up CT, RCA narrowing ≥10% occurred in 12.8%, 15.3%, and 3.5% for PFA, RFA, and control patients, respectively (PFA vs RFA risk difference -2.4%; 95% CI: -15.8% to +13.1%); ≥20% narrowing occurred in 7.7%, 13.6%, and 3.5%, respectively. Mean change in RCA dimension at last CT was -4.7 ± 8.4%, -5.9 ± 11.1%, and -2.9 ± 7.0% for PFA, RFA, and control patients, respectively (secondary continuous analysis PFA vs RFA P = 0.29); median changes were -2.4% (Q1-Q3: -2.9% to 0.0%), -2.5% (Q1-Q3: -2.9% to 0.0%), and -2.4% (Q1-Q3: -2.7% to 0.0%), respectively. No patient progressed to clinically significant (≥70%) stenosis or experienced ischemic events. RCA narrowing occurred exclusively among patients with baseline CAD. In the CTI ablation cohort, ≥10% narrowing occurred in 21.9% with CAD vs 0% without CAD (P = 0.002). Sensitivity analyses stratified by CAD and restricted to first-time AF ablation did not materially change the observed PFA-vs-RFA comparison.
CONCLUSIONS: PFA (with prophylactic intravenous nitroglycerin) and RFA of the CTI produced modest, subclinical changes in the adjacent RCA, with no clinically significant stenosis; rates of RCA narrowing did not differ significantly between energy sources, but the study was not powered to establish equivalence. Progressive RCA narrowing occurred only in patients with baseline coronary disease. Larger studies are needed to establish comparative coronary safety.

Title: Transcriptomics Identifies a Small Set of Circulating Biomarkers and Signaling Pathways Dysregulated in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is sometimes challenging to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) from other cardiomyopathies with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). At present, no circulating biomarkers to distinguish HCM have been established.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to identify plasma microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers unique to HCM.
METHODS: In this multicenter case-control study, the authors performed comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling in cases with HCM and controls with hypertensive LVH, transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), and aortic stenosis (AS). For each disease group, they chronologically split the patients into training and test sets. The authors identified miRNAs that were significantly (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05) upregulated or downregulated in HCM compared with hypertensive LVH. They made the same comparisons between HCM and ATTR-CM and between HCM and AS. They determined miRNAs that were consistently upregulated or downregulated in HCM throughout all 3 comparisons. Then, they selected miRNAs independently associated with HCM after adjusting for potential confounders. Using the selected miRNAs, the authors developed a logistic regression model to distinguish HCM in the training set. They calculated the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve in the test set.
RESULTS: The authors analyzed 2,656 miRNAs in patients with HCM (n = 294), hypertensive LVH (n = 321), ATTR-CM (n = 167), and AS (n = 38). They identified 3 miRNAs (miR-454-3p, miR-98-5p, and miR-5581-3p). The logistic regression model using the 3 miRNAs had an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97) with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.90 in the test set.
CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling identified a small set of circulating miRNAs to distinguish HCM from other cardiomyopathies with LVH.

Title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort.
METHODS: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management.
RESULTS: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model.
CONCLUSIONS: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

Title: Impact of Elevated Blood Pressure Targets on Splanchnic Ischemia and Mortality in Septic Resuscitation: Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis causes deaths worldwide each day, with hemodynamic resuscitation being central to management. Guidelines recommend a 65-mm Hg mean arterial pressure (MAP) target, yet the evidence for elevated targets remains fragmented across mortality, renal, and splanchnic outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This review aims to comprehensively appraise the impact of elevated MAP targets on splanchnic ischemia, mortality, and organ-specific outcomes in septic resuscitation.
METHODS: Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar for studies comparing MAP targets in septic shock. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; randomized controlled trials [RCTs]) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (nonrandomized studies). The findings were synthesized narratively according to the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guidelines, with random-effects meta-analysis for mortality outcomes. Evidence certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: From 3254 records, 11 studies (2895 patients; 4 RCTs, 7 nonrandomized) met the inclusion criteria. Pooled 90-day mortality across 3 trials showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality with elevated MAP targets (320/720, 44.4% vs 280/722, 38.8%; OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.97-1.77). Pooled 28- or 30-day mortality showed a similar nonsignificant trend (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.98-1.61), which was robust to sensitivity analysis. Narratively, mortality findings across nonpooled observational studies were inconsistent; some linked low MAP to higher death risk, and others found no significant association. Renal outcomes were inconsistent, with some studies showing reduced renal replacement therapy or improved acute kidney injury recovery at higher targets, particularly in hypertensive or cirrhotic subgroups. Elevated MAP targets consistently increased vasopressor exposure and were associated with more arrhythmias and fewer organ support-free days. No study reported splanchnic ischemia as a discrete outcome; mesenteric ischemia rates were low and similar between arms. Overall certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher MAP targets show no clear mortality or splanchnic perfusion benefit and may increase overall harm, though select subgroups, chronic hypertension, and cirrhosis, may benefit, supporting individualized, risk-stratified MAP targeting over uniformly elevated-target strategies.

Title: International expert consensus on perioperative management of carcinoid crisis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carcinoid crisis is a critical concern for patients with neuroendocrine tumours undergoing invasive procedures. Guidance is needed to standardize and optimize perioperative care for patients at risk of carcinoid crisis. Consensus-based expert recommendations were developed for the perioperative management of carcinoid crisis among patients with midgut and bronchopulmonary neuroendocrine tumours undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A modified Delphi approach was used with four rounds of voting to reach expert consensus on statements about perioperative management of carcinoid crisis. A multidisciplinary international panel of 44 experts was formed, and 3 patient partners were engaged. Statements addressing preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative considerations were created. Panellists rated statements on a Likert scale (from 1 to 7). Three additional rounds of iterative rating and feedback were completed anonymously. Consensus was defined with median score between 5 and 7, and ≤ 13 panellists rating outside the score category containing the median.
RESULTS: Final consensus was reached on 41 statements. Of these, 12 focused on preoperative work-up and optimization, 27 on intraoperative management including monitoring, prophylaxis, and treatment of crisis, and 2 on postoperative management. The principal practice-shifting recommendations were that somatostatin analogues are not necessary for prophylaxis before surgery or on the day of operation, and treatment in the event of carcinoid crisis should start with vasopressors, with short-acting somatostatin analogues used as an adjunct.
CONCLUSION: Using modified Delphi methodology, recommendations to guide the perioperative management of carcinoid crisis were developed. Considering the importance of carcinoid crisis on the management and outcomes of patients undergoing surgical resection for neuroendocrine tumours, this guidance can help standardize care and optimize outcomes.

Title: Is retinal vein occlusion an underrecognized paraneoplastic sentinel of lymphoma? A systematic review and meta-analysis of ocular-haematological interactions.
Abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between retinal vein occlusion (RVO) and lymphoma across two complementary evidence components: a qualitative clinical synthesis of RVO occurring in patients with lymphoma and a quantitative synthesis of subsequent cancer outcomes in patients with RVO. For the qualitative synthesis, the population comprised patients with lymphoma and RVO and no comparator was required. For the quantitative synthesis, RVO was the exposure, individuals without RVO formed the comparator, and the prespecified outcomes were overall cancer and lymphoma incidence. Secondary outcomes were ocular, haematological, biochemical, immunological and protein-related clinical findings.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: RVO is a common cause of visual morbidity typically linked to vascular risk factors. Its role as a sentinel manifestation of haematological malignancy remains underrecognized. Early recognition of lymphoma-associated RVO supports timely systemic diagnosis and coordinated ophthalmic-haematological evaluation, particularly in atypical or bilateral presentations lacking conventional vascular risk factors.
METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant review (PROSPERO CRD420251134925) searched PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library and Google Scholar from inception to 21 July 2026. Eligible original human studies comprised case-based reports for qualitative synthesis and observational cohort or registry-based studies for quantitative synthesis. Case reports were appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) criteria and non-randomized studies with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool. Hazard ratios (HRs), odds ratios (ORs) and standardized incidence ratios (SIRs) were analysed as log-transformed relative-effect estimates using fixed-effects and random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran Q.
RESULTS: Twenty-six studies were included: 19 case-based publications describing 24 RVO cases with lymphoma and 7 observational studies contributing to quantitative synthesis. Central RVO (CRVO) predominated, often with bilateral severe visual impairment, optic disc swelling, diffuse haemorrhages and macular oedema. Recurrent systemic findings included anaemia, hyperviscosity, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and immunoglobulin M (IgM) paraproteinaemia. Meta-analysis demonstrated increased overall cancer risk (pooled log effect size 0.198; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.141-0.255; p < 0.001; I2 = 21.6%; ≈22% increase) and lymphoma risk (OR 1.50; 95% CI 1.08-2.09; p = 0.015; I2 = 58.9%). Age was not a significant study-level moderator (p = 0.93).
CONCLUSION: RVO, particularly atypical or bilateral CRVO, represents a clinically informative ocular presentation associated with lymphoma in the reviewed evidence. The combined ocular, haematological and quantitative findings support mechanistic links involving hyperviscosity, thrombosis, leucostasis and infiltration. Targeted systemic evaluation is warranted in high-risk presentations.

Title: Marshall Vein Ethanol Infusion and Mitral Isthmus Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation With Durable Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical significance of adding vein of Marshall ethanol infusion (VoM-EI) and mitral isthmus (MI) ablation to left atrial posterior wall isolation (LAPWI) during repeat ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) despite durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains unclear. We assessed whether this combined strategy improves sinus rhythm maintenance.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 80 consecutive patients with AF who underwent repeat ablation despite durable PVI after prior PVI-only procedures and received either LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation or LAPWI alone.
RESULTS: Of the 80 patients, 27 underwent LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation (VoM-EI group) and 53 underwent LAPWI alone (control group). During a median follow-up of 591.5 days, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence did not differ significantly in the overall cohort on unadjusted analysis but was higher in the VoM-EI group among patients with persistent AF (log-rank p = 0.041). After multivariable adjustment, the combined strategy was associated with a lower risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence in patients with persistent AF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.38; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.92; p = 0.03) and in the overall cohort (HR 0.37; 95% CI 0.14-0.86; p = 0.02), mainly driven by persistent AF. Propensity score matching showed a similar association (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.11-0.75; p = 0.01). Major complication rates did not differ between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with persistent AF despite durable PVI, adding VoM-EI and MI ablation to LAPWI was associated with lower atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence than LAPWI alone. Because the two components were applied together, this finding is hypothesis-generating.

Title: Remote Monitoring of Algorithm-Detected Compensation Cues During Long-Term Home-Based Upper-Limb Training After Stroke: A Case Series.
Abstract: This retrospective case series examined whether a webcam application can monitor algorithm-detected compensation cues during long-term home upper-limb training after stroke. Rules on MediaPipe landmarks, not validated in patients, trigger real-time cues for elbow flexion, shoulder elevation, lateral trunk lean, and head tilt. In a technical check on 621 clinician-labelled repetitions by healthy adults, the 90° abduction rules were specific but missed most simulated compensations. Six patients with post-stroke hemiparesis, selected for long, regular records, trained at home on 33-96% of days over 3.8-9.9 months. The primary outcome, the cue rate (share of repetitions with the cue), was modelled per patient across 2277 control sessions (first daily executions of 180° and 90° abduction and a hand-to-mouth task). The elbow cue was most frequent in 180° abduction and the shoulder cue in the hand-to-mouth task. Only four of 1s6 categorised leading-cue trajectories (all elbow cue) held in every applicable sensitivity analysis; their directions differed. Long-term markerless home monitoring of the cues was feasible in these selected patients. Cue rates reflect pace, cue priority, and programme adjustment, and clinical assessment was not repeated, so their changes are not evidence of clinical improvement or deterioration; validation in patients and controlled studies should follow.

Title: Threshold-Aware Link-Graph Compression with Per-Sensor Observed-Packet Coverage Constraints and Temporal Robustness in Urban LoRaWAN Networks.
Abstract: In multi-gateway LoRaWAN deployments, a single uplink packet may be received through several sensor-gateway links, creating link-graph redundancy. We formulate compression as minimum-cardinality selection under aggregate and per-sensor observed-packet coverage constraints. The sensor-separable structure enables an exact dynamic program to certify optima and benchmark a reusable fairness-aware greedy ordering, a threshold-dependent multi-cover greedy, and a coverage-only ablation. Evaluation uses 1,232,813 uplinks observed by at least 1 gateway over 17 calendar months. On this deployment, proposed and multi-cover methods matched the minimum across 1000 threshold pairs. Coverage-only was optimal for 4%, with mean and maximum gaps of 5.84 and 8 links. These methods returned different equal-cardinality subsets for 506 pairs. The proposed subset improved worst-month coverage slack in 437 cases and met both requirements in more months in 53 cases, never in fewer. Retrospective monthly optimization required 9.24-11.59 links on average, versus 19 for an all-month-feasible subset. In a 14-month prospective evaluation, the expanding-window policy achieved pass rates of 78.6%, 57.1%, and 50.0% with three or four reconfigurations of at most two links each, and an unseen sensor caused a common cold-start failure. These results quantify trade-offs among link budget, future-month compliance, and subset stability.

Title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
Abstract: Arousal, the activation dimension of the valence-arousal circumplex, indexes alertness and engagement independently of pleasantness. We evaluated whether MediaPipe FaceLandmarker iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate electroencephalography (EEG)- and photoplethysmography (PPG)-derived arousal markers during naturalistic reading. Recordings from 48 participants yielded 43,923 thirty-second windows. Raw iris distances correlated with EEG alpha (r=+0.118) and theta (r=+0.076), but face scale explained 93% of their variance. After face-width normalisation, alpha remained associated (r=+0.076), whereas theta was not statistically significant. Further adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose rendered alpha nonsignificant (r=+0.021, p=0.33). Circular-shift testing identified alpha coupling in 11/48 participants under full control, versus 28/48 using uncorrected Pearson tests. Within-subject Ridge regression, with no raw sample shared between the training and test windows, yielded a nonsignificant group mean correlation (r=+0.078, p=0.07); 13/48 participants had individually significant prediction-reference associations (11 positive), fewer when the PPG term was restricted to filter-consistent beats. Both counts are exploratory, nominal and uncorrected across participants, and come from different analyses. Neither establishes prospective monitoring performance, and the study does not validate the landmark distance as a pupil measure.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiac Ischemia Detection: A Review of Biosensor, Biomarker, and Imaging Applications.
Abstract: Ischemic heart disease is the leading cause of global mortality, yet accurate and timely detection remains constrained by incomplete signal capture, noise, operator dependence, and imperfect reference standards. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance cardiovascular sensing by extracting latent diagnostic information from routinely acquired signals. This narrative review examines AI-enabled approaches to ischemia detection across three sensing modalities: the electrocardiogram as a bioelectric sensor, cardiac troponin as a biochemical marker, and cardiac imaging technologies (echocardiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, and nuclear imaging) as structural and functional sensors. For each modality, we evaluate the sensing pipeline, the reference standards, the endpoint actually measured (from acute coronary occlusion to functional ischemia), and reported performance metrics, separating diagnostic accuracy from effects on clinical workflow, patient outcomes, and cost. We also discuss emerging directions, including foundation models and multimodal fusion, together with translational challenges such as limited prospective validation, regulatory hurdles, and uncertain cost-effectiveness. Most evidence comes from retrospective, frequently single-center studies of diagnostic performance; few studies have measured effects on workflow, and fewer still on patient outcomes or cost. Routine clinical adoption will require prospective multicenter trials, standardized performance benchmarks, and evidence of clinical and economic benefit.

Title: Cardiac Complications of Infections Due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus: A Systematic Review and Pooled Analysis of Clinical Features.
Abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) are major causes of respiratory tract infections across different age groups. Although primarily regarded as respiratory pathogens, both viruses have been associated with cardiac complications, whose clinical spectrum remains incompletely characterized. We systematically reviewed published cases of RSV- and hMPV-associated cardiac involvement and compared their clinical characteristics and outcomes. PubMed, Scopus, and EMBASE were systematically searched for reports describing cardiac complications associated with laboratory-confirmed RSV or hMPV infection. Individual patient data were pooled and analyzed using descriptive and univariate analyses. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with hMPV versus RSV diagnosis, while multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) was performed to explore multivariate patterns of clinical presentation. Age-stratified sensitivity analyses were additionally performed. Overall, 102 cases were included, comprising 71 RSV (69.6%) and 31 hMPV (30.4%). hMPV cases were significantly older than RSV cases (41.5 years, interquartile range 3.5-63.0 vs. 1.5 years, interquartile range 0.2-31.0; p < 0.001) and had a higher burden of comorbidities. Myocarditis was the most frequently reported cardiac complication in both groups (87.1% hMPV vs. 74.6% RSV), followed by heart failure and pericarditis. ICU admission was more frequent among hMPV cases (96.8% vs. 77.5%; p = 0.034), whereas overall clinical outcomes did not significantly differ between groups. In exploratory multivariable analyses, dyspnea (aOR 16.280, 95% CI 1.370-193.475) and cough (aOR 6.059, 95% CI 1.062-34.552) were associated with hMPV diagnosis, whereas rhinorrhea (aOR 0.031, 95% CI 0.003-0.286) and lethargy/altered mental status (aOR 0.103, 95% CI 0.015-0.712) were associated with RSV diagnosis. ICU admission was also associated with hMPV diagnosis (aOR 11.033, 95% CI 1.125-108.173). These estimates were characterized by wide confidence intervals and should be interpreted cautiously. MCA showed substantial overlap between RSV and hMPV cases, without clear separation of their overall clinical presentation, while most between-group differences were attenuated in age-stratified analyses. In conclusion, both RSV and hMPV can be associated with a broad spectrum of potentially severe cardiac complications, with myocarditis representing the predominant reported manifestation. Despite some differences in demographic and clinical characteristics, their overall cardiac and clinical phenotypes substantially overlap. These findings support greater awareness of potential cardiac involvement during severe RSV and hMPV infections, while highlighting the need for prospective, systematically investigated cohorts to establish the incidence, mechanisms, and long-term outcomes of these complications.

Title: A Multielement Ionomic Dysregulation Pattern Is Associated with NT-proBNP and Cardiorenal Burden in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular hemodynamic stress may be associated with alterations in the circulating ionome. We investigated whether a hypothesis-driven multielement composite, the congestion-associated ionomic dysregulation score (CIDS; higher copper and strontium and lower rubidium and iron), was associated with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and cardiorenal-hematologic burden.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study included 192 patients undergoing cardiovascular evaluation or treatment. Serum trace elements were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, and CIDS was calculated from standardized element concentrations.
RESULTS: Higher CIDS was associated with higher NT-proBNP (ρ = 0.416, FDR-adjusted p < 0.001), worse New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional status (ρ = 0.370, p < 0.001), lower hemoglobin (ρ = -0.287, p < 0.001), lower eGFR (ρ = -0.191, p = 0.012), and higher uric acid (ρ = 0.241, p = 0.002). In the common complete-case sample, each 1-SD increase in CIDS was associated with higher log-transformed NT-proBNP after multivariable adjustment (β = 0.276, 95% CI 0.077-0.475; HC3-robust p = 0.007), and model R2 increased from 0.368 to 0.407. The observed ΔR2 exceeded the median from randomly weighted composites but did not clearly exceed the permutation null distribution (empirical p = 0.063). The referral-stratified estimates differed in magnitude (β = 0.179 versus 0.569), without a significant interaction (p = 0.171).
CONCLUSIONS: CIDS was associated with myocardial stress and cardiorenal-hematologic burden in this cohort, but the single-center, cross-sectional findings do not establish causality, unique superiority over alternative composites, or external biomarker validity. Because CIDS was standardized internally within this cohort, no externally applicable reference values or clinical cutoffs can currently be defined.

Title: Dysglycemia, Dyslipidemia, and Pulmonary Tuberculosis Outcomes: Clinical Associations and Proposed Mechanisms.
Abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading global infectious disease burden. The rising global burden of dysglycemia and dyslipidemia-which geographically converges with TB in many low- and middle-income countries-poses substantial challenges to clinical management. Dysglycemia, encompassing prediabetes and diabetes mellitus, is a well-established risk factor for pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) and adverse treatment outcomes; dyslipidemia frequently co-occurs with dysglycemia, yet its relationship with PTB outcomes is complex and varies by lipid phenotype, timing of measurement, and disease stage. Clinical evidence indicates that in the context of TB-DM, comorbid dyslipidemia is associated with more severe pulmonary pathology, heightened systemic inflammation, and increased risks of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and mortality, although the overall evidence base remains associative. At the mechanistic level, chronic hyperglycemia and altered lipid metabolism may impair anti-tuberculosis immunity through complementary pathways-including macrophage effector dysfunction, T-cell exhaustion involving the advanced glycation end products (AGEs)-receptor for AGEs (RAGE) axis, and lipid-mediated modulation of inflammatory signaling-although translational evidence from preclinical models to human populations remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes current clinical and mechanistic evidence on the associations between dysglycemia, dyslipidemia, and PTB outcomes, identifies key methodological limitations in the existing literature, and outlines priorities for future research, including prospective longitudinal studies and integrated metabolic profiling, to advance evidence-based management of PTB patients with comorbid metabolic disorders.

Title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Versus Influenza in Hospitalized Adults During the Post-Pandemic Era: Clinical Characteristics, Similarities and Discrepancies.
Abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has emerged as a major cause of hospitalization among adults in the post-pandemic era. We studied the epidemiological findings and the outcomes of patients hospitalized with influenza or RSV during the first post-pandemic respiratory virus season in Northern Greece. This multicenter retrospective study included adults hospitalized with RSV or influenza between November 2023 and May 2024 at two hospitals in Thessaloniki, Greece. Epidemiological data, clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings, vaccination status, and clinical outcomes were retrieved and compared. Twenty-seven patients with RSV and forty-eight with influenza were included. RSV patients were older (77.7 vs. 67.2 years, p < 0.01) with a higher prevalence of cardiovascular disease, chronic pulmonary disease, and malignancy, and had tachypnea more frequently at presentation (p = 0.024). No significant differences in the laboratory, radiological findings, and outcomes between the two groups were recorded. No patient was vaccinated against RSV, while 20.8% of the influenza patients had been previously vaccinated. RSV patients had a greater burden of comorbidities, whereas overall clinical outcomes did not significantly differ from those with influenza.

Title: Trimetazidine in Heart Failure: From Metabolic Modulation to Clinical Outcomes-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Heart Failure (HF) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in guideline-directed medical therapy. Metabolic remodeling with impaired myocardial energy utilization has emerged as an important therapeutic target in HF. Trimetazidine, a metabolic modulator that partially inhibits fatty acid beta-oxidation and favours glucose oxidation, enhances myocardial energy efficiency without changing systemic hemodynamics. This narrative review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the cardioprotective effects of trimetazidine and critically evaluates the available clinical evidence supporting its use in HF. Experimental studies have shown that trimetazidine increases ATP production, maintains mitochondrial function, decreases oxidative stress, inhibits apoptosis of cardiomyocytes, regulates autophagy, and reduces myocardial inflammation and fibrosis. Clinical studies and meta-analyses have shown that adjunctive therapy with trimetazidine has been associated with improved left ventricular ejection fraction, ventricular remodeling, exercise capacity, New York Heart Association functional class, biomarkers of myocardial injury, and quality of life in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The available evidence also indicates reductions in cardiovascular hospitalization and possibly all-cause mortality, but these findings are based primarily on relatively small randomized trials and pooled analyses, and need confirmation in adequately powered multicenter studies. The potential role of trimetazidine alongside contemporary therapies, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and other guideline-directed treatments, is also discussed. Overall, trimetazidine appears to be a promising adjunctive metabolic therapy that may complement existing pharmacological strategies in selected patients with heart failure (Central Illustration). Further large-scale clinical trials are needed to better define its place in contemporary HF management.

Title: The MASLD-Heart Axis: Biological Mechanisms, Cardiac Remodeling, and Clinical Implications.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the hepatic manifestation of cardiometabolic dysfunction, is closely linked to atherosclerosis, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This review summarizes current evidence on the biological basis of the MASLD-heart axis, with particular emphasis on vascular injury and adverse cardiac remodeling. Methods: A narrative review of contemporary literature was conducted, including experimental studies, observational cohorts, meta-analyses, randomized clinical trials, and current guideline recommendations addressing the cardiohepatic axis. Results: The interaction between the liver and the heart involves interconnected mechanisms, including insulin resistance, lipotoxicity, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and neurohormonal activation. Experimental and translational evidence supports biologically plausible links between MASLD-related metabolic and inflammatory pathways and vascular or myocardial injury, while clinical studies consistently associate MASLD with arterial stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, atherosclerotic disease, adverse cardiac remodeling, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and cardiovascular events. Several of these associations persist after adjustment for conventional cardiometabolic risk factors, although residual confounding and shared risk determinants limit causal inference. Non-invasive tools, including the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score and transient elastography, may help identify patients at higher risk of advanced fibrosis and cardiometabolic complications. Lifestyle interventions remain the cornerstone of management, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and fibroblast growth factor-21 analogs may provide combined hepatic and cardiovascular benefits. Conclusions: The cardiohepatic axis is an important component of cardiometabolic disease, linking hepatic dysfunction with vascular and myocardial injury through shared biological pathways. Incorporating hepatic assessment into cardiovascular risk evaluation may support earlier identification of high-risk patients.

Title: Comparative Effects of IL-17 and IL-23 Inhibitors on Lipid Profiles and Lipid-Derived Atherogenic Indices in Patients with Psoriasis.
Abstract: Background: Psoriasis is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and altered lipid metabolism. The comparative effects of IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors on lipid-derived atherogenic indices remain unclear. Objective: To compare the effects of IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors on lipid parameters and lipid-derived atherogenic indices in patients with psoriasis. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, 152 patients were assessed for eligibility, and 108 were included: 51 receiving IL-23 inhibitors and 57 receiving IL-17 inhibitors. Lipid parameters, lipid-derived indices, and PASI were evaluated at baseline and after 12 months. Results: Both groups achieved marked PASI improvement. IL-23 inhibitors were associated with significant reductions in total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, triglycerides, VLDL-C, remnant cholesterol, AIP, TG/HDL-C ratio, CRI-I, CRI-II, and AC, whereas only the TG/HDL-C ratio decreased significantly in the IL-17 group. Between-group comparisons showed greater reductions with IL-23 inhibitors in these parameters and indices (all p < 0.05), while changes in PASI, LDL-C, and HDL-C were comparable. Conclusion: IL-23 inhibitors were associated with greater improvements in several lipid parameters and lipid-derived atherogenic indices than IL-17 inhibitors despite comparable clinical efficacy. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of differential cardiovascular protection.

Title: SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study Comparing Adherence and Persistence with Specific Reference to Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Poor adherence and persistence to sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are a critical issue in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), especially in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD). We aimed to compare adherence and persistence to these drugs in routine care. Methods: A retrospective propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort study was conducted using pharmacy claims data. Patients aged 40 years or older with T2DM initiating SGLT-2is or GLP-1 RAs from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2024 were included. Adherence was measured using the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR), and persistence was defined as the time to discontinuation (gap ≥ 60 days between refills). Results: At the 1-year follow-up, the SGLT-2i cohort showed significantly higher adherence compared to the GLP-1 RA cohort (86.66% vs. 76.53%; OR = 2.02) and higher persistence (71.48% vs. 66.52% at 12 months; HR = 0.83). The main factors associated with lack of persistency were newly diagnosed T2DM (HR = 1.25) and insulin use (HR = 1.32). In the CVD subgroup, the differences in favor of the SGLT-2i cohort were more pronounced for adherence (89.57% vs. 78.12%; OR = 2.44) and persistence (73.9% vs. 63.59%; HR = 0.66). Conclusions: In real-world clinical practice, adherence and persistence rates were higher in patients on SGLT-2is compared to those on GLP-1 RAs, particularly in the CVD subgroup. Our findings suggest that the new strategies are necessary to improve adherence and persistence to these medications, particularly in patients with CVD.

Title: Combination Therapy Potential of HTD1801 (Berberine Ursodeoxycholate) in MASLD/MASH and Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Disease: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum is characterized by the close interrelatedness of metabolic, hepatic, cardiovascular, and renal disease, making multidomain therapies particularly relevant to MASLD/MASH. HTD1801, an investigational ionic therapeutic, combines berberine's metabolic effects with the hepatoprotective effects of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), making it a potential multidomain therapy within this setting. This review had two related goals: first, to synthesize the mechanistic and clinical evidence for HTD1801 itself; and second, to evaluate the rationale and available evidence for extending this complementary-action approach through combination with other therapies relevant to MASLD/MASH and CKM disease. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, conference abstracts, and selected regulatory or sponsor sources were reviewed through 9 August 2026. Six CKM-relevant therapeutic classes were selected for their human evidence of multidomain benefit: metformin, GLP-1 receptor agonists, statins, SGLT2 inhibitors, PPAR agonists, and resmetirom. Studies of both HTD1801 and its individual components, berberine and UDCA, were included. A systematic review or meta-analysis was not feasible due to the limited and heterogeneous evidence base, instead necessitatinganarrative review. Results: Across seven completed HTD1801 clinical studies with publicly reported results, treatment showed multidomain metabolic and hepatic benefits across the CKM spectrum, including improvements in HbA1c, LDL-C, MRI-PDFF hepatic fat, ALT, AST, and GGT. Direct human evidence: HTD1801 + metformin, supported by a Phase 3 randomized add-on trial. Indirect human evidence: HTD1801 + SGLT2 inhibitors. Preclinical evidence: HTD1801 + GLP-1 receptor agonists; berberine + statins. Theoretical mechanistic rationale only: HTD1801 + PPAR agonists; HTD1801 + resmetirom. Overall, mechanistic and preclinical rationale has advanced further than direct human validation, and evidence remains centered largely on surrogate rather than definitive clinical outcomes. Conclusions: HTD1801 has demonstrated multidomain metabolic and hepatic activity, but direct human evidence supporting its use with other CKM therapies remains limited and is currently established only for metformin. The principal next step is to test HTD1801 in dedicated combination RCTs for clinically meaningful benefit. Further studies should characterize combination-specific safety and tolerability and compare HTD1801 with separate berberine and UDCA administration.

Title: Drug Utilization Patterns and Potential Drug-Drug Interaction Burden in Respiratory Prescriptions: A Real-World Community Pharmacy Study.
Abstract: Background: Respiratory disorders are frequently managed in community pharmacies and may involve complex multidrug regimens, particularly in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We aimed to characterize respiratory pharmacotherapy and moderate or major potential drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk using one index respiratory prescription per patient. Methods: We performed a retrospective observational secondary analysis of anonymized electronic prescription data from two Romanian community pharmacies (November 2022-October 2023). From a combined source dataset comprising prescriptions with at least two active substances, we selected records containing at least one eligible respiratory diagnosis. Demographics, diagnostic groups, active substances, therapeutic classes, medication burden, and potential DDIs were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with at least one moderate or major potential DDI. Results: The final cohort included 643 patients. Median age was 52 years [interquartile range 23.5-66.0], and 50.7% were female. Asthma was the most frequent diagnostic group (41.1%), followed by acute upper respiratory tract infections (19.8%) and COPD (15.4%). The most frequent therapeutic classes were inhaled and intranasal corticosteroids (54.0%), long-acting beta-2 agonists (46.7%), and anti-infectives (35.0%). At least one moderate or major potential DDI was identified in 28.0% of index prescriptions. In the fully adjusted multivariable model, each additional active substance was associated with higher potential DDI odds (odds ratio [OR] 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96-3.00), while cardiovascular or metabolic co-medication showed the strongest positive class-level association (OR 14.16, 95% CI 5.25-38.21). Conclusions: Respiratory prescriptions showed distinct diagnostic and therapeutic profiles. The highest prevalence of moderate or major potential DDIs among the major diagnostic groups was observed in COPD. Potential DDI risk was strongly associated with medication burden and cardiovascular/metabolic co-medication, supporting targeted community pharmacy medication review that considers both respiratory therapy and the broader pharmacotherapeutic regimen.

Title: Estrogen Receptor-Mediated Effects of a Phytoestrogen-Rich Soy-Based Diet on Metabolic Health Following Ovariectomy in Aged Mice.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Loss of ovarian hormones leads to obesity and insulin resistance (IR), increasing the risk of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. We previously showed that aged female ERa knockout (αKO) and ERb knockout (βKO) mice differentially respond to ovariectomy, with a greater adverse metabolic response in βKO mice. We later showed that young ovariectomized (OVX) βKO mice were somewhat resistant to exercise-mediated metabolic benefits including adipose tissue browning.
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: We tested the hypothesis that feeding a high phytoestrogen soy-based diet (SOY) would improve metabolic health in older OVX female mice and that αKO and βKO mice would differentially respond to the diet. Since phytoestrogens weakly bind ERs, and it is known that activation of ERa mediates insulin sensitizing and weight loss benefits, and ERb is known to improve adipocyte mitochondrial responses, we hypothesized that αKO mice would be less responsive to the systemic metabolic benefits of SOY, whereas βKO mice would be less responsive to adipocyte-specific benefits.
METHODS: We examined OVX and ovary-intact aged (~1 yr) wildtype (WT), αKO, and βKO female mice (n = 7-12/group). One week following OVX, mice were randomized to receive either SOY (585 mg phytoestrogens/kg) or a phytoestrogen-free diet (<15 mg/kg, CON) and were followed for 11 weeks. Mice were assessed for body composition (EchoMRI), energy expenditure (EE via Promethion metabolic cage system), glucose tolerance (i.p. glucose tolerance test), insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR, Adipo-IR), adipose tissue gene and protein expression for insulin signaling markers, and fasting blood lipids. To provide additional mechanistic insight, primary adipocytes were treated with phytoestrogens and assessed for insulin-mediated phosphorylation of Akt.
RESULTS: Era mediated important metabolic benefits of SOY in aged OVX mice. OVX αKO mice were unresponsive to SOY-mediated improvements in body composition and glucose tolerance, whereas SOY improved those metrics, as well as increased spontaneous physical activity in OVX WT and βKO mice (all p < 0.05). Primary adipocyte cell culture experiments revealed that insulin-mediated phosphorylation of Akt occurred even with ERα-antagonization, with no effects of estrogen or phytoestrogen treatment, at least in the small set of experiments performed.
CONCLUSIONS: SOY improved body composition and glucose tolerance in old OVX mice, effects that were absent in ERα-null mice. Soy-based diets may improve metabolic health in settings of ovarian hormone suppression via mechanisms requiring estrogen signaling pathway activation.

Title: Effects of Two Rg3-Enriched Korean Ginseng Preparations on Blood Pressure in Adults with Early-Stage Hypertension: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Ginsenoside Rg3, a bioactive component of processed Korean ginseng, has demonstrated vasodilatory and blood pressure-lowering effects; however, clinical evidence on the long-term effects of Rg3-enriched ginseng preparations remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of two differently processed Rg3-enriched Korean ginseng preparations on blood pressure in adults with early-stage hypertension. Methods: In this 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 90 adults were randomly assigned to vitamin C-treated white ginseng (VTWG), enzyme-treated red ginseng (ETRG), or placebo (n = 30 per group). Both interventions provided approximately 40 mg/day of Rg3. Changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were primary outcomes. Results: From baseline to week 12, SBP decreased by 7.27 ± 6.15 mmHg in the VTWG group and 9.86 ± 6.47 mmHg in the ETRG group, whereas it increased by 5.03 ± 6.52 mmHg in the placebo group (both adjusted p < 0.0001 vs. placebo). DBP decreased by 5.27 ± 5.58 and 6.32 ± 5.55 mmHg in the VTWG and ETRG groups, respectively, compared with a decrease of 0.90 ± 6.31 mmHg in the placebo group (adjusted p = 0.006, 0.0006, respectively). MAP also decreased significantly in both intervention groups compared with placebo (both adjusted p < 0.0001), whereas NO changes differed significantly only between ETRG and placebo (adjusted p = 0.017). No clinically meaningful safety concerns were identified. Conclusions: Twelve-week supplementation with either Rg3-enriched Korean ginseng preparation significantly reduced blood pressure compared with placebo, suggesting potential benefits for blood pressure management in adults with early-stage hypertension.

Title: Changes in Nutrition and Physical Activity up to 4 Years Following a Hypertensive Pregnancy: A Blood Pressure Postpartum Longitudinal Sub-Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Postpartum lifestyle interventions may mitigate increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risks following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). The study aimed to examine longitudinal changes in post-HDP lifestyle behaviors and women's perceptions towards healthy living.
METHODS: This study was a longitudinal sub-study of the 3-armed, multicenter Blood Pressure Postpartum (BP2) randomized controlled trial in post-HDP women, comprising different postpartum care/lifestyle intervention strategies 6-12 months postpartum and post-intervention observational follow-up to 3-4 years postpartum. The NSW Health Population Survey captured lifestyle variables 6-12 months postpartum. At 3-4 years post-HDP, the Australian Eating Survey and the International Physical Activity Questionnaire were alternatively used for diet and physical activity, respectively. Linear mixed-effects models analyzed daily consumption of vegetables/fruit, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and perception scores of healthy living for motivators, barriers, and satisfaction.
RESULTS: In 180 participants, reported mean (SD) vegetable/fruit daily intake increased (vegetable servings/day: 2.6 (1.3), 6 months vs. 2.7 (1.4), 12 months vs. 4.2 (2.0), 3-4 years, p < 0.001; fruit servings/day: 1.7 (1.0), 6 months vs. 1.7 (1.0), 12 months vs. 2.2 (1.3), 3-4 years, p < 0.001), while accompanied by other unfavorable dietary changes. Reported median [IQR] MVPA increased (minutes/week, 330 [280], 6 months vs. 313 [331], 12 months vs. 515 [690], 3-4 years, p < 0.001). Motivators to engage in healthy behaviors decreased (p < 0.001), perceived barriers increased (p < 0.001), and satisfaction with diet and body appearance worsened over time (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, women reported higher intake of both health-promoting and less health-promoting foods and higher MVPA; however, different tools were used for lifestyle measurement. Worsening perceptions were observed using the same instrument.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Effects of Combined Music and Caffeine on Psychophysiological Responses During Exercise: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Background: This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated the effects of combined music and caffeine on psychophysiological responses during exercise. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to 10 June 2026. Randomized crossover studies comparing caffeine plus music with placebo plus no music, caffeine alone, or music alone were eligible. Outcomes included rating of perceived exertion (RPE), Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale (PACES), Feeling Scale (FS), and heart rate (HR). Findings were synthesized descriptively by outcome and comparator, considering study-specific effect estimates, confidence intervals, and experimental conditions. Random-effects meta-analyses were retained as secondary exploratory summaries. Because fewer than 10 independent studies were available, meta-regression and formal assessment of small-study effects were not undertaken. Results: Five crossover studies involving 88 participants were included. Study-specific RPE estimates varied from large reductions to estimates close to the null or in the opposite direction. PACES point estimates favoured the combined intervention, but their magnitudes differed substantially in comparisons with placebo plus no music and caffeine alone. Feeling Scale and heart-rate findings also varied across studies. All four primary meta-analyses showed I2 values exceeding 90%, and the certainty of evidence was very low for all primary outcomes. Conclusions: The available evidence comprises five small crossover studies conducted in different populations and experimental settings. Study-specific findings suggest possible improvements in exercise enjoyment, while perceived exertion, affective valence, and heart-rate responses vary across studies. Neither the descriptive findings nor the secondary exploratory pooled estimates establish a stable, broadly applicable magnitude of intervention benefit. Given the very low certainty of evidence, no firm recommendations can be made regarding the use of caffeine combined with music across exercise populations and settings. Further adequately powered studies using clearly specified interventions and comparable outcome assessments are needed to determine which responses are reproducible and practically meaningful.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Effects of Caffeine-Taurine Co-Supplementation on Exercise Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Background: Caffeine-taurine combinations are widely used in commercial sports products. Whether this combination improves exercise performance is still unclear. This study aimed to estimate the effect of caffeine-taurine co-supplementation versus placebo on exercise performance. Methods: Randomized controlled trials comparing caffeine plus taurine versus placebo were searched in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and related databases up to June 1, 2026. Outcomes included heart rate (HR), reaction time (RT), time to exhaustion (TTE), rating of perceived exertion (RPE), and peak/maximal anaerobic power (PP). A random-effects model was applied. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2.0. Results: A total of 11 randomized controlled trials involving 234 participants were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with placebo, caffeine-taurine co-supplementation was associated with improvements in time to exhaustion (SMD = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.03 to 1.05) and PP (SMD = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.21 to 0.89); an expanded secondary product-level analysis that additionally included one commercial multi-ingredient energy drink yielded a smaller estimate (SMD = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.19 to 0.78) that cannot be attributed specifically to caffeine and taurine. The pooled estimate for reaction time favored supplementation (SMD = -1.49, 95% CI: -2.78 to -0.20), but very high heterogeneity and a prediction interval crossing the null indicated that the effect was not consistent across settings, whereas no meaningful effect was observed for heart rate (WMD = -0.11, 95% CI: -5.76 to 5.53). Rating of perceived exertion was significantly reduced (SMD = -0.44, 95% CI: -0.83 to -0.04). Conclusions: Caffeine-taurine-only formulations were associated with possible benefits for selected performance outcomes, including PP. However, the evidence was derived from few, generally small studies and did not establish the independent contribution of caffeine, taurine, or their interaction. Results from commercial multi-ingredient products should be interpreted at the product level rather than as evidence of an isolated caffeine-taurine effect.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Effects of Acute Ecklonia cava Supplementation on Submaximal Cycling and Repeated-Sprint Performance in Trained Cyclists: A Randomised Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This study examined whether acute Ecklonia cava (EC) ingestion altered physiological responses during submaximal cycling or power output during subsequent repeated maximal sprints in experienced male cyclists.
METHODS: Twelve cyclists completed a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants ingested 263 mg of EC extract or placebo 30 min before 60 min of cycling at 55% of the maximum work rate, followed by three 20 s maximal sprints. Blood glucose, blood lactate, heart rate, oxygen uptake and respiratory exchange ratio (RER) were measured during submaximal cycling; peak power, mean power, blood glucose and blood lactate were assessed during the repeated-sprint test. Outcomes were analysed using linear mixed-effects models incorporating treatment, time, treatment × time, experimental period and allocated sequence.
RESULTS: Blood glucose was higher overall following EC than placebo (4.23 ± 0.23 vs. 4.02 ± 0.33 mmol·L-1; mean difference, 0.213 mmol·L-1; 95% CI, 0.046 to 0.379; p = 0.023), but the treatment × time interaction was not significant (p = 0.939). EC did not affect submaximal blood lactate, heart rate, oxygen uptake or RER (all p ≥ 0.096). EC did not alter peak power (mean difference, -2.58 W; 95% CI, -29.51 to 24.35; p = 0.832), mean power (5.93 W; 95% CI, -2.47 to 14.33; p = 0.167), post-sprint glucose (p = 0.481) or post-sprint lactate (p = 0.060). No treatment × time interaction was identified for any repeated-sprint outcome (all p ≥ 0.267).
CONCLUSIONS: Acute ingestion of 263 mg of EC extract produced a modest overall elevation in blood glucose during submaximal cycling, but did not improve repeated-sprint performance or materially alter the other measured physiological responses. These findings do not support an acute ergogenic effect of EC in experienced male cyclists under the conditions tested.

Title: Gut Microbiome in Sporadic Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: MRI-Defined Phenotypes, Mechanistic Evidence, and Nutritional Implications for Brain Aging.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major vascular component of brain aging, yet potentially modifiable systemic contributors remain incompletely understood. Growing evidence links the gut microbiome to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined CSVD, but interpretation is complicated by heterogeneity in microbiome profiling, clinical populations, analytical methods, and neuroimaging phenotypes. This review critically integrates the available human evidence with complementary multi-omics, ex vivo, and experimental findings.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through 4 August 2026; 12 eligible reports representing eight cohort families were included and evaluated using a structured study-level methodological appraisal.
RESULTS: Across the available literature, ecological and host-related biological processes show greater qualitative convergence than individual taxa, although this pattern has not been formally quantified across independent cohorts. Among reported alpha diversity measures, Chao/Chao1 showed the same numerical disease-versus-control direction across four cohort families, with statistical significance in two, suggesting a recurrent but still preliminary richness-related signal; Shannon and Simpson indices were less consistent. No single genus or species has been consistently replicated across the available, largely cross-sectional cohorts. Complementary studies implicate intestinal barrier, immune-metabolic, neurovascular, and perivascular clearance pathways but do not establish a unified causal pathway in human sporadic CSVD.
CONCLUSIONS: These observations support a hypothesis-generating ecosystem-level framework. Because diet is an important modifiable determinant of the gut microbial ecosystem, these findings may have relevance for nutrition-based strategies targeting vascular brain aging. However, no CSVD-specific dietary or microbiome-directed intervention has yet been shown to modify disease progression or related MRI outcomes.

Title: Diet Quality and Co-Occurrence of Arteriosclerosis and Knee Osteoarthritis: A Cross-Sectional Survey Among Chinese Iron Workers from Shougang Group.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arteriosclerosis (AS) and knee osteoarthritis (KOA) pose a major public health challenge, yet evidence linking diet quality to the risk of comorbidity among Chinese occupational groups remains limited. This cross-sectional occupational study examined the association between diet quality indicators and the co-occurrence of AS and KOA among 1538 iron workers from Shougang Group.
METHODS: Dietary data were collected using the Diet Quality Questionnaire (DQQ) for China. Multivariable logistic regression models were performed with adjustment for relevant covariates.
RESULTS: Overall, 627 workers had co-occurrence of AS and KOA, including 579 men and 48 women. Among women, a higher continuous Global Dietary Recommendations (GDR) score was inversely associated with the odds of co-occurrence (OR = 0.75; 95% CI = 0.62-0.91). Compared with a GDR score ≤ -3, a GDR score ≥ 1 was also inversely associated with co-occurrence among women (OR = 0.13; 95% CI = 0.02-0.77); however, no statistically significant associations were observed among men or in the age- and BMI-stratified analyses.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide preliminary evidence of an inverse association between diet quality and AS-KOA co-occurrence among female workers but should be considered exploratory, requiring confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Safety and Efficacy of a Single Injection of Liposomal Latanoprost in Open-Angle and Angle-Closure Eyes.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible global vision loss, with intraocular pressure (IOP) as the sole modifiable risk factor to stall progression. First-line treatment in the form of eye drops suffers from poor bioavailability and low patient adherence, necessitating sustained-release alternatives. This study evaluates the safety and sustained efficacy of a liposomal latanoprost (LipoLat) injection in both open-angle and angle-closure eyes. Methods: This was a 3-month open-label, non-comparative pilot study that included patients aged 40 to 90 with ocular hypertension, primary open- and closed-angle glaucoma. After a 1-month washout from daily topical prostaglandin analogues, participants received a single sub-Tenon's injection of LipoLat 2 mg/mL. Primary and secondary outcome measures included safety (the incidence of serious adverse events) and IOP-lowering efficacy. Results: Nine of 12 enrolled subjects completed the 3-month follow-up. LipoLat 2 mg/mL was safe, with no serious adverse events reported. There was a significant IOP reduction from a baseline of 23.1 ± 1.76 mmHg to 18.0 ± 1.42 mmHg at month 3 (p < 0.001), representing a maximum 22.6% decrease. Adjusted mixed models confirmed a 5.11 mmHg mean IOP reduction at 3 months, with five subjects showing sustained IOP reduction beyond 3 months, and two subjects remaining medication-free for up to 9 months. Conclusions: In this study, LipoLat is shown to be a safe, well-tolerated treatment for the first time in angle-closure eyes. Its sustained efficacy may also extend beyond 3 months. Larger randomised trials are warranted to further confirm the clinical application in angle-closure eyes.

Title: Determinants of Futile Recanalization and the Influence of Age After Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Functional independence is not always achieved after successful recanalization with endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, a phenomenon termed futile recanalization (FR). We investigated factors independently associated with FR and explored whether these associations differed by age. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 231 consecutive patients treated with EVT between January 2021 and December 2024 were analyzed. FR was defined as a modified Rankin Scale score > 2 at 90 days despite a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) grade of 2b-3. Model 1 included all patients with successful recanalization. Model 2 was restricted to patients with anterior circulation infarction and assessable imaging and additionally included the Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) and collateral status. Age interactions were tested. Results: Recanalization was successful in 191 patients (82.7%), of whom 114 (59.7%) had FR. In Model 1 (n = 191), admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score (odds ratio [OR], 1.29 per point; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.18-1.42), admission glucose (OR, 1.01; 1.00-1.02), and puncture-to-recanalization time (OR, 1.02; 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with FR. In Model 2 (n = 146), sufficient collateral status (OR, 0.19; 0.08-0.47), ASPECTS (OR, 0.60; 0.39-0.91), NIHSS score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), dyslipidemia, and procedural duration were independently associated with FR, whereas glucose was not retained; Model 2 had an area under the curve of 0.88. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR; the only significant interaction was with glucose in Model 1. Conclusions: Stroke severity and procedural duration were independently associated with FR in both models. Imaging variables contributed to prognostic assessment in anterior circulation infarction. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR. The NLR association and age-stratified findings remain exploratory.

Title: Long-Term Effects of Paced Heart Rate on Central Blood Pressure in Patients with Sinus Node Dysfunction and Hypertension: A Randomised Crossover Study.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Prior cardiac pacemaker studies examining the relationship between heart rate and central (aortic) blood pressure (BP) have predominantly used acute designs, limiting generalisability to long-term settings. The aim of this study was to assess the long-term effects of two clinically realistic pacing rate strategies on the central BP profile in permanently paced sinus node dysfunction (SND) patients in sinus rhythm and on antihypertensive medication. Materials and Methods: In this prospective, single-centre, randomised, single-blind, exploratory crossover clinical trial, the study participants completed two eight-week intervention periods (DDD 55 and 75 bpm) separated by a two-week washout. Office peripheral and central haemodynamics were measured at baseline and at the end of each period non-invasively with an oscillometric cuff-based device (SphygmoCor XCEL). Results: The study included 22 subjects (median age 76 (IQR 73-78) years, 16 women). At DDD 55 bpm, central systolic BP (primary outcome) was higher than at DDD 75 bpm (mean 127.8 ± 13.4 and 121.3 ± 10.6 mmHg, respectively, p = 0.04), whereas systolic BP amplification (peripheral systolic BP-central systolic BP) and pulse pressure (PP) amplification (peripheral PP/central PP) were lower (systolic BP amplification: mean 8.5 ± 3.2 and 10.1 ± 2.9 mmHg, respectively, p = 0.02; PP amplification: mean 1.2 ± 0.1 and 1.3 ± 0.1, respectively, p < 0.01). Conclusions: Long-term pacing at a moderately accelerated physiological rate may be associated with lower central systolic BP compared with pacing at a slightly bradycardic rate, in older permanently paced SND patients with hypertension.

Title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA. Materials and Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE).
