Materials and Methods: Retrospective analysis of patients diagnosed with epigastric pain in the ED at Rambam Health Care Campus in 2014. Ultra-short heart rate variability (usHRV) indices were calculated from a 10 s ED electrocardiogram and correlated with mortality, disease severity, and disease origin. Results: 300 patients were included in this study. Due to a very low short-term mortality rate, usHRV could not be reliably assessed for this outcome. The mortality rate throughout the follow-up period of the study was 17.4%, with a median of 8.4 years. No significant association was found between long-term mortality and standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN) or root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD). In multivariate logistic analysis, high RMSSD significantly increased the risk for acute abdomen (RMSSD-adjusted odds ratio (AOR): 1.021, p-value: 0.022, Area under the curve (AUC): 73%), while high RMSSD decreased the risk for acute MI (RMSSD AOR: 0.807, p-value: 0.026, AUC: 83.6%). Conclusions: Ultra-short HRV did not predict long-term mortality in patients presenting with epigastric pain. However, RMSSD was independently associated with both acute abdomen and acute MI. These findings suggest that usHRV parameters may serve as a supportive tool in the ED to aid differentiation between abdominal and cardiac causes of epigastric pain, particularly in high-risk clinical scenarios.

Title: Occlusive Myocardial Infarction: A Practical Review of STEMI-Negative Coronary Occlusion in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
Abstract: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) remain the dominant operational categories for acute coronary syndrome triage because they are simple, widely implemented, and closely linked to reperfusion pathways. However, diagnostic ST-segment elevation and acute coronary occlusion are not synonymous. A clinically important subgroup of patients classified as NSTEMI have total or near-total culprit-artery occlusion and may experience delayed angiography despite ongoing myocardial ischemia. This structured narrative review examines the rationale, evidence, electrocardiographic patterns, quantitative bedside criteria, and emerging technologies relevant to occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI), with particular emphasis on STEMI-negative coronary occlusion. Conventional STEMI criteria are highly specific but incompletely sensitive for acute coronary occlusion, particularly in posterior or circumflex infarction, early anterior occlusion, left bundle branch block, ventricular paced rhythm, and transient reperfusion. Recognition of OMI therefore requires integration of ECG morphology, reciprocal changes, serial ECG evolution, clinical presentation, troponin kinetics, and adjunctive imaging rather than reliance on ST-segment thresholds alone. Practical patterns include hyperacute T waves, the de Winter pattern, posterior OMI, modified Sgarbossa-positive conduction abnormalities, subtle anterior OMI, and selected high-risk ischemic patterns. Artificial intelligence may improve scalable detection of subtle occlusion patterns, although external validation, workflow integration, explainability, and prospective outcome studies remain necessary. Current evidence supports OMI as a promising complementary diagnostic framework rather than an established replacement for guideline-based STEMI/NSTEMI classification. Prospective implementation studies are required to determine whether OMI-guided pathways improve clinical outcomes without unacceptable false-positive catheterization-laboratory activation.

Title: Documented Valvular Regurgitation and Explicit Heart Failure in an Internal Medicine Registry: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Routine records may conflate valvular heart disease (VHD), functional classification, and shared diagnostic assessment. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a registry VHD label and explicitly documented heart failure (HF), while recognizing that every observed valve lesion was regurgitant. Materials and Methods: The analytic sample comprised all 224 eligible adults admitted to the Internal Medicine II Department of a railway-affiliated hospital between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026: 38 with documented VHD and 186 without documented VHD. The primary outcome was an explicit HF diagnosis; a combined HF/NYHA-positive field was examined as an over-inclusive sensitivity outcome. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and total cholesterol. Results: Explicit HF was documented in 24/38 patients with VHD (63.2%) and 72/186 without VHD (38.7%; adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.38-5.99). The combined outcome was present in 28/38 (73.7%) and 101/186 (54.3%), respectively (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.09-5.21). All 38 exposed patients had documented mitral, aortic, and/or tricuspid regurgitation; no stenosis, prolapse, or prior valve intervention was recorded. Conclusions: Documented valvular regurgitation was associated with explicit HF documentation. Because regurgitation may be secondary to ventricular or atrial disease, reverse causation, shared ascertainment, non-adjudicated diagnoses, and residual confounding preclude causal, temporal, prognostic, or lesion-specific inference.

Title: Traumatic Intracranial Vascular Lesions in Adults Undergoing Vascular Imaging After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Traumatic intracranial vascular lesions are rare but severe complications of traumatic brain injury (TBI) and include arterial and venous injuries such as arterial dissections, pseudoaneurysms, arterial occlusions, venous sinus thrombosis, arteriovenous fistulas, and carotid-cavernous fistulas. Despite their clinical significance, the available literature remains limited and heterogeneous. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic yield of vascular imaging, spectrum, and imaging modalities of traumatic intracranial vascular lesions in adults with TBI. Materials and Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted from database inception to 31 August 2026 in PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library (CENTRAL) according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Cohorts of patients who underwent vascular imaging after TBI were eligible. When the full text was available, the denominator was the number of patients imaged with a modality able to detect the lesion in question and the numerator was reported at patient level for intracranial lesions. The primary analyses were restricted to cohorts with an explicit adult age criterion or a separately reported adult subgroup; cohorts with a pediatric fraction that could not be separated entered a sensitivity analysis only. Data extraction and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for prevalence studies were performed independently by two reviewers. Proportions were pooled with a logit-transformed random-effects model with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and prediction intervals, with Freeman-Tukey and generalized linear mixed models as sensitivity analyses. Results: Nineteen studies with 3542 imaged patients were included, eight of them adult cohorts with 2021 patients. In adult cohorts, the pooled diagnostic yield was 11.0% (95% CI, 2.3-39.8%; four cohorts) for dural venous sinus thrombosis, 4.8% (95% CI, 1.1-18.4%; three cohorts) for pseudoaneurysm, 1.1% (95% CI, 0.0-20.8%; two cohorts) for arteriovenous fistula, and 0.7% (95% CI, 0.2-3.1%; three cohorts) for carotid-cavernous fistula, with I2 between 74.7% and 96.2% and prediction intervals spanning most of the possible range; arterial dissection (7.0%) and arterial occlusion (5.8%) were reported by a single adult cohort and were not pooled. The proportion of patients with any lesion was not pooled, because the seven cohorts that imaged every patient differed in whether and how the venous compartment was assessed; it ranged from 1.5% to 56.9% by cohort. Adding the eleven adult-dominant cohorts gave 17.5% for sinus thrombosis and 4.5% for pseudoaneurysm. In exploratory univariable meta-regressions for sinus thrombosis, trauma mechanism, imaging modality, and study design were each associated with part of the heterogeneity and were confounded with one another in these cohorts. Conclusions: Every estimate describes the yield of vascular imaging in adults selected for it, rests on two-to-four small cohorts, and carries very low certainty; the prediction intervals show that a new cohort may fall far from the pooled value, and none of the estimates can be read as the frequency of these lesions in TBI in general.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound of Upper Airway Changes During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Elevated endotracheal tube (ETT) cuff pressure impairs tracheal mucosal perfusion and may contribute to upper airway soft-tissue changes. During cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), the cuff usually remains inflated although ventilation is suspended, yet the relevance of cuff pressure management during CPB is unclear. We compared two ETT cuff pressure strategies during CPB (0 vs. 20-30 cmH2O) on point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) measurements of upper airway soft tissue in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Materials and Methods: In this single-center, prospective, randomized, observer-blinded trial, 76 patients (ASA III-IV, aged 18-80 years) undergoing elective CABG were randomized 1:1 to a 0 cmH2O or 20-30 cmH2O ETT cuff pressure strategy throughout CPB (n = 38 per group). Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) was not used in any patient. POCUS measurements of lateral pharyngeal wall (LPW) thickness, tongue thickness, parapharyngeal distance, midsagittal tongue area, and tongue width were obtained at four time points (T0-T3). The primary analysis was the omnibus group × time interaction for LPW thickness in a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model; the between-group difference in change from T0 to T2 was a planned supporting contrast. Results: All 76 randomized patients completed the study and were analyzed. The group × time interaction for LPW thickness was significant (p < 0.001); the between-group difference in the increase in LPW thickness from T0 to T2 was 1.50 mm (95% CI 1.27 to 1.73), and 1.00 mm (95% CI 0.82 to 1.18) at postoperative hour 2. Parapharyngeal distance and tongue thickness showed the same pattern. No multiplicity-adjusted between-group difference in LPW thickness was detected at T0 or T1, and a sensitivity analysis using the pre-intervention time point (T1) as baseline gave consistent results (T2 vs. T1: 1.43 mm, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.57). In an exploratory, unadjusted secondary analysis, difficult extubation occurred in 0/38 vs. 7/38 patients (absolute risk difference 18.4 percentage points, 95% CI 5.4 to 33.4; p = 0.012). Conclusions: Complete cuff deflation during CPB was associated with smaller ultrasonographic upper airway soft-tissue changes after CPB. The trial was not powered for clinical outcomes; the lower frequency of difficult extubation is hypothesis-generating, and these data do not support a change in routine practice before confirmation in trials with patient-centered endpoints.

Title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation with Different Single-Shot Ablation Devices in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Observational Single-Center Clinical Evaluation.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: The conventional technique for atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation has gradually been supplemented by 'single-shot' devices. Comparisons of devices using three different energy sources are rare. We aimed to evaluate the outcomes of patients with AF who underwent pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using three various single-shot ablation techniques. We also examined factors associated with arrhythmia recurrence during the 12-month follow-up. Materials and Methods: We prospectively analyzed single-center data from consecutive adult patients undergoing PVI with different single-shot devices between January and December 2024. For cryoablation, a second-generation cryoballoon (AFA, Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) was used; for radiofrequency balloon ablation, the RFB catheter (Heliostar, Biosense Webster, California, CA, USA) was applied; and for the PFA-guided procedure, the Farawave (Boston Scientific, Massachusetts, MA, USA) ablation catheter was used. The procedural endpoint was to achieve intraoperative PVI. Arrhythmia recurrence was defined as any episode lasting >30 s documented by electrocardiographic recordings. Results: Ultimately, the analysis included 115 patients. Of these, 41 underwent PVI by cryoablation, 22 underwent RFB therapy, and 52 underwent PFA. The total skin-to-skin procedure time was the shortest among PFA-patients, primarily due to shorter left atrial dwell time. After 12 months of follow-up, 30 patients experienced recurrence of atrial arrhythmia. A larger left atrium diameter increased the risk of arrhythmia recurrence, whereas propafenone therapy at discharge was associated with a lower risk of recurrence during the 12-month follow-up. Conclusions: In this single-center observational study, PVI performed with PFA was associated with the shortest procedure time compared with procedures using CBA or RFB, with no difference in the risk of arrhythmia recurrence among the single-shot ablation modalities during the 12-month follow-up.

Title: Associations of TNF-α, Uric Acid, and the Leptin/Adiponectin Ratio with HOMA-IR in Hospitalized Adults: A Cross-Sectional Secondary Analysis of 147 Patients.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Anthropometric measures incompletely capture the inflammatory and adipokine heterogeneity underlying insulin resistance. We examined associations of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), serum uric acid, and the leptin/adiponectin ratio with HOMA-IR after adjustment. Materials and Methods: This single-center cross-sectional secondary analysis included 147 of 239 hospitalized adults with HOMA-IR and predefined core data; fasting glucose, insulin, and biomarker testing was elective and patient-funded. Continuous ln(HOMA-IR) was the primary outcome. A secondary upper-quartile phenotype (HOMA-IR ≥ 4.78; n = 37) was cohort-specific and non-diagnostic. Robust linear regression used HC3 standard errors. Sensitivity analyses excluded T2DM and replaced BMI with waist circumference or visceral fat area. Binary and AUC analyses were exploratory (expanded complete-case model, n = 112). Results: Each doubling of (TNF-α + 1) was associated with a 10.2% higher HOMA-IR in the expanded model (p = 0.021). The association persisted after excluding T2DM (12.1% higher HOMA-IR per doubling; n = 81; p = 0.012) and when BMI was replaced by waist circumference (p = 0.022) or visceral fat area (p = 0.018). Uric acid and the leptin/adiponectin ratio did not reach statistical significance in the adjusted continuous-outcome model. The 112 complete cases and 35 incomplete cases were broadly similar in measured baseline characteristics, although uric acid was higher among complete cases (p = 0.020). Conclusions: In this selected hospitalized cohort, TNF-α showed the most consistent adjusted association with the observed fasting glucose-insulin phenotype. The binary and discrimination analyses remain preliminary and do not establish diagnostic or clinical prediction utility. Prospective external validation is required.

Title: Structural Fetal Anomalies Identified During First-Trimester Screening: A Single-Centre Experience in Romania.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: The 11-13+6-week scan has evolved from a nuchal translucency (NT) measurement into an early anatomical survey, and the anomalies it identifies increasingly shape prenatal counselling and management. Data from Central and Eastern European screening populations are scarce. Materials and Methods: Retrospective cohort of all pregnancies undergoing first-trimester combined screening in a single fetal medicine centre in Romania between August 2009 and April 2026, with a crown-rump length of 45-84 mm. The centre provides routine screening but also receives women referred after an abnormal finding elsewhere; the cohort is therefore described as a screening population with referral enrichment. Structural anomalies recorded prospectively in the ultrasound database at the first-trimester scan were classified by organ system and by first-trimester detectability category. NT, combined risk, karyotype and pregnancy outcome were extracted from the same database. Associations were quantified with odds ratios (OR) from logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors by woman. Results: 11,229 pregnancies (10,015 women; 408 multiple pregnancies) were included. A structural anomaly was identified at 11-13+6 weeks in 197 (17.5 per 1000; 95% CI 15.3-20.1); 16.1 per 1000 (13.8-18.7) after exclusion of the years 2009-2012 and 16.9 per 1000 (14.6-19.5) in singleton pregnancies. A further 44 pregnancies had isolated cystic hygroma/hydrops or soft markers only. Cardiac defects (81; 7.2 per 1000) and abdominal-wall defects (74; 6.6 per 1000, of which 67 exomphalos) were present in 145 pregnancies (74%), followed by central nervous system (27), facial (23), skeletal (23), thoracic (10) and urogenital (10) anomalies; 37 pregnancies (19%) had anomalies in two or more systems. NT ≥ 3.5 mm was present in 59/197 (30%) anomalous versus 203/11,032 (1.8%) non-anomalous pregnancies (OR 22.8, 95% CI 16.3-31.9), and in 51% of cardiac defects. Among 37 karyotyped fetuses, 15 (41%) had a chromosomal abnormality. Pregnancy outcome was known for 87 anomalous pregnancies: 46 terminations, 33 live births and 8 fetal or neonatal deaths; 17 of 30 exomphalos cases with known outcome were live-born. Conclusions: In a screening population with referral enrichment, about 1 in 57 pregnancies had a structural anomaly identified at the 11-13+6-week scan, dominated by cardiac and abdominal-wall defects; the figure describes prenatally identified anomalies in this setting and is not a population-based prevalence. One third of these fetuses had increased NT and a high proportion of those tested had an abnormal karyotype, supporting the integration of systematic anatomical assessment and genetic evaluation into first-trimester screening.

Title: Circulating Lipids, Statins, and Metformin in Thoracic and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAA and AAA) progress silently, and no drug has been shown to slow their growth. Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA. Aneurysm growth was standardized to mm/year and pooled with random-effects models when at least three comparable studies were available. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE. Thirty-three studies were included, 32 observational and one randomized; fewer than 20% of participants were women. Circulating lipid fractions showed no consistent association with aneurysm growth. Statin use was associated with slower growth (mean difference -0.78 mm/year; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.43; I2 = 92.4%; 95% prediction interval -2.02 to 0.46 mm/year), lower all-cause mortality, and fewer aortic complications. In AAA, metformin use was associated with slower growth in observational studies (-0.34 mm/year; 95% CI -0.48 to -0.20; I2 = 46.3%), while the single randomized trial found no difference. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. In these largely observational data, aneurysm progression was more closely related to statin and metformin use than to circulating lipid levels, a pattern that is hypothesis-generating and from which causality cannot be inferred.

Title: The Impact of Environmental Humidity and Seasonal Changes on Blood Pressure and Major Health Complications: Myocardial Infarction, Stroke, Pulmonary Embolism, Syncope, and Mortality in Hypertensive Elderly Patients in the Eastern Mediterranean Region.
Abstract: Background: Relative humidity is an important meteorological factor that has received considerably less attention than temperature and atmospheric pressure regarding its effects on human health. This study investigated the association between environmental humidity, blood pressure, and major cardiovascular complications in well-controlled hypertensive patients. Methods: In this prospective study (which was analyzed retrospectively), 128 hypertensive patients aged 65-92 years were followed for five years in a primary care clinic. Clinical evaluations were performed every season, resulting in 20 seasonal observation periods. Relative humidity (RH) was measured during each patient visit. Poisson regression was used to evaluate the associations between humidity, season, age, and the occurrence of major clinical events, including myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, syncope, and death. A negative Binomial model was used to check for overdispersion; no evidence of overdispersion was detected. Repeated-measures multiple linear regression analysis was performed to assess the effect of humidity on systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Results: Relative humidity ranged from 49% to 89% during the study period. The highest number of major clinical events occurred in winter when RH was the highest (23 events), followed by summer (10), autumn (7) and spring (3). In the unadjusted analysis, higher humidity was significantly associated with an increased number of major complications. However, this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for age and season. Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure values were significantly lower in men than in women (systolic: 145.1 vs. 148.7 mmHg, p < 0.001; diastolic: 75.0 vs. 79.5 mmHg, p < 0.001). After adjustment for season, age, and body mass index, increasing humidity was associated with a significant increase in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure in men (p < 0.001), whereas no significant effect on systolic blood pressure was observed in women. In contrast, diastolic blood pressure decreased significantly with increasing humidity in women (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher relative humidity was associated with a greater number of major clinical events in the unadjusted analysis; however, this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for season and other relevant covariates. Seasonal variation was more strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes than RH considered as an isolated environmental factor. Closer monitoring of blood pressure during periods of high humidity, particularly in winter, may help reduce cardiovascular risk in elderly patients with hypertension.

Title: Optimizing Drug-Coated Balloon Outcomes: The Evolving Role of Vessel Preparation in Coronary and Peripheral Artery Interventions.
Abstract: Drug-coated balloon (DCB) therapy differs fundamentally from stent-based revascularization since the vessel itself becomes the treatment substrate. Consequently, vascular preparation is an important component of DCB therapy. This review therefore examines contemporary vessel preparation before DCB therapy across coronary and peripheral interventions, integrating lesion morphology, procedural outcomes, intravascular imaging, and clinical follow-up. Across vascular beds, the objective is not maximal plaque disruption, but sufficient modification of the dominant mechanical limitation to achieve predictable expansion, controlled vessel injury, and effective balloon-vessel wall contact. Subsequent failure after coronary DCB therapy has been associated with residual plaque burden and calcium morphology. Specialty balloons, atherectomy and intravascular lithotripsy have been associated with improved procedural success, lumen expansion, and calcium modification, with lower rates of flow-limiting dissection or bailout stenting in selected settings. Randomized evidence has generally demonstrated more consistent procedural than long-term clinical benefits. Moreover, much of the evidence supporting advanced calcium-modification strategies derives from stent-based interventions and cannot be directly extrapolated to DCB-only therapy. These findings favor a lesion-specific, preparation-dependent approach rather than routine escalation to increasingly aggressive technologies. Conventional balloons may be sufficient for mechanically responsive lesions, whereas scoring or cutting balloons, atherectomy, or intravascular lithotripsy should be selected according to lesion morphology and the specific mechanical limitation that persists after initial preparation. Intravascular imaging may facilitate objective assessment of a "DCB-ready" vessel, although validated preparation thresholds remain undefined. The question is thus not which preparation device is preferable but whether the vessel has been adequately prepared to receive the drug. Future studies should go beyond device-to-device comparisons and assess whether predefined, imaging-based preparation targets improve drug delivery, vessel healing, and durable clinical outcomes. The next step toward precision DCB therapy across coronary and peripheral disease may be to shift the focus from device selection to treatment-substrate optimization.

Title: Clinical Pregnancy Outcomes Following Blastocyst Transfer Using Media with Different Hyaluronan Concentrations:A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Hyaluronan-enriched embryo transfer media have been proposed to improve implantation and reproductive outcomes; however, their clinical benefit remains uncertain, particularly in frozen embryo transfer cycles. This study aimed to compare clinical pregnancy outcomes following blastocyst transfer using two commercially available media with different hyaluronan concentrations. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 421 blastocyst transfer cycles performed at a single IVF center between November 2024 and April 2026. Seventy-two cycles used a hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (EmbryoGlue), and 349 used a medium with a lower hyaluronan concentration (SAGE 1-Step). The primary outcome was clinical pregnancy, defined as an intrauterine pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed adjusting for maternal age and transfer type. Results: Clinical pregnancy occurred in 21/72 cycles (29.2%) in the hyaluronan-enriched medium group and 127/349 cycles (36.4%) in the lower-hyaluronan medium group (p = 0.30). The use of the hyaluronan-enriched medium was not significantly associated with clinical pregnancy after adjustment for maternal age and transfer type (aOR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.44-1.34, p = 0.352). Increasing maternal age was associated with lower odds of clinical pregnancy (aOR = 0.95 per year, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98, p = 0.002), whereas transfer type was not (aOR = 1.14, 95% CI: 0.59-2.21, p = 0.688). No significant differences were observed in either maternal age subgroup. Conclusions: In this predominantly frozen blastocyst-transfer cohort, no statistically significant difference in clinical pregnancy rates was observed between the hyaluronan-enriched and lower-hyaluronan transfer medium groups. Given the retrospective, non-randomized design, differences in medium composition beyond hyaluronan concentration, and potential residual confounding, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or as demonstrating the absence of a clinically relevant effect. Prospective randomized studies evaluating live birth are warranted.

Title: Peripheral Arterial Disease: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate and Interleukin-6 as Markers of Disease Severity and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
Abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis in which chronic inflammation contributes to disease severity. This retrospective study included patients who underwent arteriography for PAD at a single center in 2019. Of 238 arteriographies performed, inflammatory and hematologic biomarker panels were available for a subset of 71 patients with angiographically confirmed PAD. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid were compared across sex, age, diabetes, and obesity subgroups, correlated with disease severity by the Leriche-Fontaine classification, and analyzed for their association with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI; Fontaine stages III-IV vs. IIA-IIB). ESR (r = 0.408, p = 0.001) and IL-6 (r = 0.310, p = 0.009) correlated significantly with disease severity, whereas TNF-α, white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid did not. Both markers showed modest but significant discriminative performance for CLTI (IL-6: area under the curve = 0.674, p = 0.012; ESR: area under the curve = 0.673, p = 0.021). ESR and IL-6 were both associated with PAD severity suggesting a more pronounced systemic inflammatory phenotype in CLTI; their prognostic value after revascularization warrants evaluation in larger, prospective cohorts.

Title: Vascular Rings as a Cause of Respiratory Difficulties.
Abstract: Background: Vascular rings are rare congenital developmental anomalies of the cardiovascular system that present with variable respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms often refractory to what is considered a standard treatment. The aim of our study was to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway, and management of children referred to a tertiary pediatric department for unexplained respiratory symptoms in whom a vascular ring was confirmed, with particular attention to the role of echocardiography in raising the initial suspicion, and to compare our findings with published cohorts. Methods: We performed a retrospective descriptive case series of patients (n = 7) diagnosed at the Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Jessenius Faculty of Medicine in Martin, Comenius University in Bratislava, University Hospital Martin, between 2021 and 2025. Results: The median age at onset of clinical symptoms was 30 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1-120 days). The median age at definitive diagnosis was 14.5 months (IQR 4.3-94.0 months). A genetic abnormality was observed in 3 patients (42.9%), and a positive family history of congenital heart defects was present in 4 (57.1%). All patients (n = 7) were symptomatic at the time of definitive diagnosis. We observed double aortic arch (DAA) in 2 patients (28.6%), right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery (RAA + ALSA) in 4 (57.1%), and aberrant right subclavian artery (ARSA) in 1 (14.3%). One patient with RAA + ALSA had a concurrent pulmonary artery sling (PAS). In 6 patients (85.7%), the initial suspicion was raised by transthoracic or prenatal echocardiography. Six patients (85.7%) underwent surgical repair at a median age of 10.5 months (IQR 4.1-20.1 months), while in one case the risk-benefit ratio of surgery is being evaluated. Conclusions: In this series, echocardiography was a useful non-invasive modality for raising the initial suspicion, whereas CT angiography was required to define the vascular anatomy; the majority of patients were definitively diagnosed and treated within the first two years of life. In our cohort, we also identified a rare combination of a vascular ring (RAA + ALSA) and a pulmonary artery sling (PAS) in a single patient.

Title: Explainable Ensemble Boosting Framework for Chronic Disease Risk Prediction Using Lifestyle and Clinical Data: A Multi-Dataset Study.
Abstract: Chronic diseases represent a substantial public health burden, motivating the development of transparent and reproducible approaches for disease-specific risk prediction using routinely available lifestyle and clinical variables. This study presents a common explainable ensemble boosting framework for comparative prediction across three independent disease-specific datasets: heart disease, lung cancer, and diabetes. Five boosting algorithms, including XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting, were evaluated under a consistent leakage-free protocol. Each dataset was first split into stratified 80% training and 20% held-out test sets, with preprocessing, random oversampling, hyperparameter optimization, probability calibration, and threshold selection performed only on the training data. Performance was assessed using accuracy, balanced accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Brier score, and bootstrap confidence intervals. On the held-out test sets, AdaBoost achieved the highest balanced accuracy (68.07%) and ROC-AUC (71.71%) for heart disease; CatBoost achieved the highest balanced accuracy (92.59%) and ROC-AUC (96.30%) for lung cancer, although these estimates require caution because the lung-cancer test set contained only eight negative observations; and XGBoost achieved the highest balanced accuracy (77.02%), whereas Gradient Boosting achieved the highest ROC-AUC (82.43%) for diabetes. Repeated stratified cross-validation showed significant differences among the five algorithms for balanced accuracy (Friedman χ2=26.293, p<0.001), ROC-AUC (χ2=21.173, p<0.001), and F1-score (χ2=15.093, p=0.0045). Across these endpoints, Gradient Boosting achieved the best mean rank (1.98), followed by CatBoost (2.47), although no model was uniformly the highest-performing across all datasets and evaluation measures. SHAP and LIME analyses were additionally used to characterize global and local feature contributions to model predictions. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of a common explainable boosting workflow across heterogeneous disease-specific benchmark datasets while emphasizing that these results constitute internal benchmark evidence and require independent external and prospective validation before clinical application.

Title: Machine Learning Approach for Cardiovascular Disease Risk Stratification Using Ensemble Classifiers and Dimensionality Reduction.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, motivating data-driven tools that complement established clinical risk criteria. We present a two-pathway machine learning framework for CVD risk assessment. Pathway I is a brief rule-learnability verification, a four-level risk label is generated by a deterministic MEWS/Framingham-inspired scoring rule, and because the label is a deterministic function of the inputs, its near-perfect recovery by the classifiers is only a consistency check, not predictive evidence. Pathway II, the focus of the study and the main contribution of this work, is a hybrid pipeline that combines unsupervised preprocessing (K-Nearest Neighbors imputation, PCA/UMAP dimensionality reduction, K-Means phenotyping) with supervised ensemble classifiers (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), trained on an ≈70,000-record Kaggle cohort and externally validated on an independent 219-patient cohort using the same prevalent-CVD definition. On the external cohort the six pipelines performed comparably (accuracy 70-74%, external-cohort AUC 0.82-0.85); paired McNemar tests showed no significant difference between UMAP- and PCA-based pipelines (all p>0.5), and a power analysis indicates the cohort is too small to distinguish them, so no configuration is claimed to be superior. An unsupervised phenotype analysis is included as a descriptive, hypothesis-generating step; its association with the outcome is statistically significant but of negligible effect size. The framework offers a reproducible, clinically interpretable methodology for CVD risk categorization.

Title: Bridging the Allergy-Radiology Gap in Radiocontrast Media Hypersensitivity: A Patient-Level Linkage Study on Diagnostic Stewardship and Re-Exposure Outcomes.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined how allergy findings related to candidate-agent identification, subsequent real-world imaging and clinical outcomes. Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included 29 adults evaluated between January 2019 and May 2025 for contrast media hypersensitivity. Imaging and outcomes between allergy evaluation and a structured telephone interview in July 2026 were assessed retrospectively and verified in national electronic health records, without prospective follow-up. Primary outcomes were skin test positivity and new hypersensitivity reactions during subsequent contrast administration. Results: The culprit contrast agent was not documented by name in 18 patients (62.1%); median evaluation delay was 60 months. Skin tests were positive in 1/20 patients (5.0%); skin-test-negative candidate agents were identified in 19/20 (95.0%). New reactions occurred in 3/14 contrast recipients (21.4%), all with immediate Brown Grade III index reactions to iohexol. Subsequent reactions included one cardiac arrest after iohexol and two Grade II reactions after iodixanol. Of seven patients imaged without contrast, four had candidate agents but reported continuing patient and physician concerns. No Holm-adjusted comparison was significant. Conclusions: Skin testing identified a candidate agent in most tested patients, but candidate identification did not establish clinical tolerance or independent protection. A shared, individualised imaging plan should communicate agent selection, premedication decisions, test limitations and precautions to patients and radiologists while preserving access to necessary imaging.

Title: Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea Is Associated with Cholesterol Target Non-Attainment in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Secondary Analysis of a Prospective Observational Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles, but its relationship with cholesterol target attainment in patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy remains incompletely characterized. We investigated the association between severe OSA and non-attainment of predefined cholesterol thresholds in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This secondary analysis included 142 adults from a prospectively assembled observational cohort. Participants underwent in-hospital preoperative Type III cardiorespiratory polygraphy, fasting lipid assessment, and documentation of lipid-lowering therapy. Severe OSA was defined as an apnea-hypopnea index ≥30 events/h. The primary outcome was non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C) ≥ 100 mg/dL. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, high-intensity statin therapy, and non-statin lipid-lowering therapy.
RESULTS: Severe OSA was associated with higher odds of non-HDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.49, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.56-7.78; p = 0.002), LDL-C ≥ 55 mg/dL (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.18-7.29; p = 0.021), and LDL-C ≥ 70 mg/dL (OR 2.30, 95% CI 1.03-5.12; p = 0.041). In contrast, associations with continuous LDL-C (p = 0.113) and non-HDL-C (p = 0.100) concentrations were not statistically significant. No significant associations were observed for triglyceride-related or lipid-derived outcomes. The primary association with non-HDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL remained significant in the analysis restricted to statin-treated patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe OSA was associated with non-attainment of predefined cholesterol thresholds in this cardiac surgical cohort, with the strongest and most consistent association observed for non-HDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL. These findings identify an association with categorical cholesterol target non-attainment but do not establish treatment failure, causality, or a generalized increase in cholesterol concentrations.

Title: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 Is Associated with Severe Coronary Artery Calcification in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease.
Abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have a high burden of coronary artery calcification (CAC) and cardiovascular risk. GDF-15 is a stress-responsive biomarker linked to kidney dysfunction and adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but its relationship with CAC across CKD stages is incompletely characterized. We evaluated associations of GDF-15 with severe CAC and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). In this prospective observational study, 128 patients with CKD and no previous cardiovascular disease had baseline GDF-15, dp-ucMGP, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I, and NT-proBNP measured; CAC was quantified by computed tomography in 127. Severe CAC was defined as Agatston score ≥ 400. Mean serum GDF-15 was 4.5 ± 3.4 ng/mL. GDF-15 discriminated severe CAC (AUC 0.728; 95% CI 0.642-0.804; p < 0.001). Each doubling of GDF-15 was associated with higher odds of severe CAC after adjustment for eGFR, diabetes, LDL cholesterol, and phosphate (OR 2.105; 95% CI 1.045-4.240; p = 0.037), but this association was attenuated after adding high-sensitivity troponin I (p = 0.086). During 19 months, nine MACE occurred; each doubling of GDF-15 was associated with higher MACE risk (HR 2.679; 95% CI 1.278-5.625; p = 0.009). Higher GDF-15 was associated with severe CAC and cardiovascular events, supporting further evaluation in CKD.

Title: Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Findings After Lesion-Preparation Incorporating the ShockFast™ Intravascular Lithotripsy: A Prospective Single-Center Imaging Sub-Study.
Abstract: Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an established calcium modification strategy for severely calcified coronary lesions. The Shunmei ShockFast™ IVL system is a novel device that appeared safe and feasible in an initial clinical experience. However, its calcium fracture typology, depth distribution, and quantitative stent optimization characteristics have not been characterized by serial optical coherence tomography (OCT). Objectives: To provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification patterns and stent optimization metrics achieved with the ShockFast™ IVL system in a cohort of patients with severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. Methods: This is a prospective, single-center OCT imaging sub-study nested within the Cardio-FR registry (NCT04185285). We included 14 patients with OCT assessment performed at three mandatory time points-baseline (before any device delivery), post-IVL, and post-stenting-who underwent PCI with the ShockFast™ IVL system between June 2025 and April 2026. The primary endpoint was OCT-confirmed calcium fracture rate following IVL treatment. Secondary endpoints included calcium fractures ≥2 and type, post-lesion-preparation lumen gain, minimum stent area (MSA), stent expansion (SE), malapposition, and edge dissection rates. Exploratory correlative analyses between baseline calcium morphology and post-IVL stent optimization outcomes were performed. Results: Median baseline OCT MLA was 2.22 mm2 (IQR 1.4-3.61). Calcium fractures were identified in 10 of 14 lesions (71%, 95% CI 45-88%) following a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, with ≥2 fractures in 43%. Fractures were classified as partial-thickness (non-transmural) in 30% and full-thickness (transmural) in 70% of cases. Median post-lesion-preparation lumen gain was 0.53 mm2 (IQR 0.3-0.84). Median final MSA was 4.77 mm2 (IQR 3.59-5.34) and median SE was 89.5% (IQR 85-94), with SE >80% achieved in 100% of lesions. No major malapposition or medial edge dissections were recorded. Conclusions: Applied as the central calcium-modification component of a comprehensive lesion-preparation strategy, the ShockFast™ IVL system was associated with OCT-confirmed calcium fractures in the majority of the lesions, with favorable stent expansion and optimization metrics in the absence of major malapposition or edge dissections. These findings provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification mediated by a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, consistent with feasibility as a novel IVL platform suitable for further investigation in adequately powered comparative studies.

Title: A Decade of Durable Mechanical Circulatory Support with HeartMate 3 Across Age Groups in a Single-Center Experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term real-world data after HeartMate 3 implantation remain limited, particularly regarding age-specific outcomes. We evaluated on-device survival and major adverse events across nearly a decade of experience.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 215 patients undergoing primary HeartMate 3 implantation between January 2016 and October 2025. On-device mortality was analyzed using Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence estimates with heart transplantation as a competing event; age-group differences were assessed using Fine-Gray regression. Transplant-censored Kaplan-Meier survival was examined secondarily, and mortality predictors were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: Median age was 53 years and median support was 603 days. At data cutoff, 149 patients remained alive on support, eight underwent transplantation, and 58 died on support. At 5 years, the cumulative incidences of on-device death and heart transplantation were 35.3% and 4.1%, respectively, with no significant age-group difference (Fine-Gray global p = 0.088). In the secondary transplant-censored Kaplan-Meier analysis, estimated survival was 87.4% at 30 days, 81.1% at 1 year, and 63.8% at 5 years. Higher preoperative creatinine was associated with mortality (HR, 1.93 per 1-mg/dL increase; 95% CI, 1.07-3.50; p = 0.029). No intrinsic pump thrombosis occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: HeartMate 3 provided durable support with favorable long-term survival, although non-pump adverse events remained clinically relevant.

Title: Feasibility and Clinical Outcomes of a 6-Month Home-Based Telerehabilitation Program in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Prospective Single-Arm Study.
Abstract: (1) Background: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and functional impairment. This study evaluated the feasibility and adherence of a 6-month home-based telerehabilitation (TR) program and longitudinal changes in functional capacity, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and selected cardiometabolic parameters. (2) Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled 42 patients with PAD. Daily ambulation was monitored using a Xiaomi Smart Band 8, and participants received weekly telephone counseling. Assessments were performed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. (3) Results: Median daily step count increased from 5868 to 6905 steps/day (p < 0.001), whereas attainment of progressively increasing weekly targets decreased from 58.33% to 16.66% (p < 0.001). Median 6 min walk test (6MWT) distance increased from 390 m to 445 m at 6 months, a 55 m increase (p = 0.001). HRQoL, systolic blood pressure, body mass index, and total cholesterol showed significant longitudinal changes, while resting ankle-brachial index and selected cardiopulmonary exercise testing parameters remained relatively stable (p > 0.05). (4) Conclusions: The TR program was feasible and accompanied by increased activity and improved walking capacity. The divergence between absolute activity and target attainment supports multidimensional adherence assessment. Causal effects cannot be established given the single-arm design.

Title: Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement with the Perceval Plus® Versus TAVI: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Postoperative Outcomes, Hematological Dynamics, and Inflammatory Response.
Abstract: Perceval Plus and TAVI are increasingly used for severe aortic stenosis, both relying on a self-expanding nitinol stent design, yet evidence specific to Perceval Plus remains limited regarding postoperative clinical outcomes and hematological and inflammatory dynamics. We compared postoperative clinical outcomes and longitudinal platelet/CRP dynamics between Perceval Plus and TAVI in a retrospective single-center cohort, in which 26 propensity score-matched pairs were obtained (1:1 matching) from patients undergoing Su-AVR (Perceval Plus, n = 53) or TAVI (self-expanding Medtronic devices, n = 101). Mortality, echocardiographic outcomes, and rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances showed no statistically significant differences between groups, while TAVI was associated with shorter ICU and hospital stay and Su-AVR required higher FFP transfusion (p = 0.016). Platelet count declined in both groups, with a deeper nadir in Su-AVR (postoperative day 3: 66% decline) versus TAVI (day 4: 27% decline), with a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.013); CRP rose in both groups but more rapidly and to a greater magnitude in Su-AVR (time and group × time interaction, both p < 0.001). Su-AVR and TAVI showed no statistically significant differences in the clinical safety outcomes assessed but differed in postoperative hematological and inflammatory magnitude, likely reflecting multifactorial procedure- and device-related mechanisms, warranting confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies.

Title: Diaphragmatic Reconstruction with StratticeTM Biologic Mesh After Thoracic Oncologic Resection: A 10-Year Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: (1) Background: Large diaphragmatic defects following thoracic oncologic resection often require mesh reconstruction. Data regarding biologic mesh for this application remain limited. We evaluated clinical outcomes and durability of Strattice™, a non-cross-linked porcine acellular dermal matrix, for diaphragmatic reconstruction. (2) Methods: In this single-center, retrospective cohort study without a synthetic mesh comparator, we reviewed health records of 65 adults who underwent diaphragmatic reconstruction with Strattice™ mesh at a high-volume thoracic surgery center between 2014 and 2024. (3) Results: Mean hospital length of stay was 13.2 days. Atrial fibrillation was the most common post-operative complication, occurring in 44.6% of the patients. No diaphragmatic reconstruction recurrence or mesh replacement was observed during the available follow-up. (4) Conclusions: No reconstruction recurrence or mesh replacement was identified during the available follow-up, and wound infection was rare, supporting the feasibility of Strattice™ mesh for diaphragmatic reconstruction in this single-center cohort study. Strattice™ provided durable diaphragmatic reconstruction with a low observed wound infection rate and no identified reconstruction failure, supporting its feasibility for complex thoracic oncologic reconstruction.

Title: Coronary and Peripheral Venous Inflammatory Biomarkers in Acute Myocardial Infarction: Associations with Myocardial Injury, Cardiac Function, and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract: (1) Background: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) links innate immune activation to myocardial injury and adverse outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), yet the relationship between local intracoronary and systemic peripheral IL-6, and their prognostic value, remains unclear. (2) Methods: This prospective single-center study aimed to compare intracoronary and peripheral venous IL-6 and other inflammatory biomarkers in AMI, included 83 consecutive STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) or NSTEMI (non ST-elevation myocardial infarction) patients undergoing coronary angiography. Paired intracoronary and peripheral venous samples were obtained before revascularization and analyzed for IL-6, CRP, and ferritin, and correlated with LVEF (left ventricle ejection fraction), NT-proBNP, and a 30-day composite endpoint (death or heart failure hospitalization). (3) Results: Peripheral IL-6 exceeded intracoronary levels in 86.7% of patients (p < 0.001), with both peripheral IL-6 and the venous-to-coronary difference higher in STEMI than NSTEMI. IL-6 in both compartments correlated inversely with LVEF and positively with NT-proBNP and troponin I. Patients reaching the composite endpoint (10.8%) had markedly higher IL-6 and CRP. ROC analysis showed discriminatory ability for the endpoint by intracoronary and peripheral IL-6. (4) Conclusions: Intracoronary and peripheral IL-6 are associated with infarction phenotype, ventricular dysfunction, and short-term outcomes in AMI, supporting its role as an early prognostic biomarker.

Title: Cross-Disease Transcriptomic Signatures Shared by NAFLD and MI: Multicohort Machine-Learning Analysis and Exploratory IDI1 Expression Assessment.
Abstract: The molecular features shared by non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and myocardial infarction (MI) remain incompletely understood. We analyzed six microarray cohorts from the GEO database to identify shared disease-associated transcriptomic features across independent NAFLD and MI populations. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis, differential expression analysis, and fuzzy c-means clustering across ordered cross-sectional NAFLD groups were used to define candidate genes. LASSO regression, random forest, and SVM-RFE identified consensus computational candidates, which were examined using exploratory classification, receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations. IDI1 was selected for exploratory expression assessment by qPCR in patients with established MI and in a mouse model of acute ischemic myocardial injury. Fifty-three shared candidate genes were identified, and five genes were retained by all three feature-selection methods. Single-gene ROC analyses showed SULF2, GADD45A, LIN7A, and IDI1 within the analyzed case-control datasets. IDI1 expression was higher in patients with MI than in healthy controls (p = 0.004), as well as in mice blood (p = 0.034) and infarcted myocardium (p = 0.0072) following LAD ligation. These findings indicate shared transcriptomic links between NAFLD and MI, supporting an association between IDI1 and myocardial injury.

Title: Peripheral Effects of the Gut-Derived Metabolite TMAO in Two MPTP-Challenged Disease Animal Models.
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) remains incompletely understood despite its high social and economic burden, with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction recognized as central pathogenic mechanisms. 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP), a complex I inhibitor, is widely used as a model of dopaminergic neurodegeneration, while growing evidence highlights the gut-liver-brain and kidney-brain axes as important contributors to PD progression. Within this framework, trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) has emerged as a molecule of interest, linked to dementia risk and proinflammatory effects. Our study aimed to evaluate the peripheral oxidative and inflammatory consequences of acute and semi-acute MPTP exposure, alone and in combination with TMAO. In total, 96 male CD-1 mice were equally divided across two experimental settings: a semi-acute protocol (30 mg/kg i.p., MPTP once daily for five consecutive days) and an acute protocol (20 mg/kg i.p., four administrations of MPTP at two-hour intervals), with TMAO administration remaining identical across both experimental settings. The animals were randomized into four groups (control group, a TMAO-only group (40 mg/kg/day, gavage, days 0-42), an MPTP-only group, and a combined TMAO + MPTP group), with MPTP showing consistently depleted liver SOD activity across both models. In the liver, MPTP showed consistently depleted SOD activity in both models, whereas glutathione disruption and lipid peroxidation were most evident in the combined TMAO + MPTP group. These effects were explained mainly by the additive main effects of MPTP and TMAO, as no significant MPTP × TMAO interaction was found for any oxidative stress marker. Nonetheless, a significant MPTP × TMAO interaction was confirmed for liver and kidney IL-1β in the acute model. IL-1β and IL-6 were significantly elevated in the liver and kidney by both MPTP alone and its combination with TMAO, with the combined groups consistently showing the largest increases (TMAO + MPTP semi-acute vs. control and vs. TMAO, p < 0.001-0.01; TMAO + MPTP acute vs. all groups, p < 0.0001-0.01). In the kidney, the contribution of MPTP and TMAO to oxidative stress was model-dependent: in the semi-acute protocol, both MPTP and TMAO contributed to increased MDA and glutathione ratio disruption, while in the acute protocol, TMAO alone was the dominant driver of SOD depletion and MDA elevation, with their combination further amplifying IL-6 secretion. TMAO also independently drove lipid peroxidation in the heart and intestine. The acute MPTP model produced more extensive redox imbalance independently of TMAO, whereas in the semi-acute model, a comparable degree of redox disruption was only achieved through combined TMAO + MPTP exposure.

Title: Antioxidative and Anti-Inflammatory Mechanisms of Quercetin in the Prevention of Secondary Diabetes Complications.
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder linked with several microvascular and macrovascular complications and is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Uncontrolled hyperglycemia is well known to increase oxidative and inflammatory responses. Further, activation of the polyol pathway and protein kinase C (PKC), and formation of advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) and their interaction with AGE receptors (RAGEs) can cause tissue dysfunction and damage, leading to secondary diabetes complications such as diabetic retinopathy, neuropathy, nephropathy, cardiovascular complications, and cataractogenesis. Several plant products have been shown to exert potential glucose-lowering effects due to their strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Quercetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid abundant in fruits and vegetables, has attracted considerable interest because of its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties. Recent studies indicate the therapeutic potential of quercetin for controlling secondary diabetes complications. Various preclinical studies suggest that quercetin prevents the production of reactive oxygen species, suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling, activates Nrf-2-mediated antioxidant enzymes, and inhibits AGE-RAGE interactions. These actions of quercetin have been shown to prevent the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, enhance endogenous antioxidant defenses, and attenuate the pathological consequences of diabetes complications. Although preclinical findings convincingly support the protective effects of quercetin across multiple diabetic complications, clinical findings remain limited and heterogeneous. Further, randomized clinical trials, long-term safety studies, and bioavailability studies are needed to determine its therapeutic effectiveness in clinical practice. In this review, we discuss recent findings on how quercetin prevents various secondary complications of diabetes. We further discuss how quercetin could serve as a promising multi-target adjunctive therapy by addressing the oxidative and inflammatory mechanisms underlying diabetic complications.

Title: A Conceptual Translational Bench-to-Bedside Cardiac Safety Framework for Predicting Drug-Induced QT Interval Prolongation from Molecular Structure to Clinical Data.
Abstract: QT interval prolongation is associated with an increased risk of torsades de pointes (TdP), a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia, making assessment of cardiac repolarization a critical component of drug development. This work demonstrates how integrated in silico methodologies can be used to predict and quantitatively characterize QT liability across the drug discovery and development continuum. A proof-of concept translational workflow combining molecular structure analysis, in vitro pharmacology, animal data, and clinical exposure-response modeling was evaluated using the retrospective case examples verapamil and dofetilide. Molecular structure- and pharmacology-based assessments predicted hERG channel interaction and potential QT risk for both compounds. While initial in silico analyses suggested a high QT liability for verapamil and dofetilide, mechanistic electrophysiological modeling differentiated their effects. For verapamil, concurrent calcium channel inhibition offset hERG-mediated effects, resulting in predicted reductions in action potential duration and no clinically relevant QT prolongation. In contrast, dofetilide produced concentration-dependent increases in action potential duration, consistent with its known proarrhythmic potential. Translation of nonclinical findings to humans accurately predicted the absence of clinically meaningful QT effects for verapamil and identified QT prolongation exceeding the regulatory 10 ms threshold for dofetilide at therapeutic concentrations. Drug exposure and pharmacokinetic properties could be anticipated based solely on molecular structure. This conceptual workflow demonstrates how integrated quantitative in silico approaches can support earlier identification, characterization, and communication of QT risk, enabling informed decision-making and improved development efficiency from bench to bedside.

Title: TNF-α and IL-8 Are Helpful in the Prediction of Late Post-COVID-19 Venous Thromboembolic Disease-Single-Center Prospective Study.
Abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is associated with persistent inflammation and an elevated risk of late venous thromboembolism (VTE). The role of proinflammatory cytokines has been well documented in the acute phase of the disease, but their potential role in late post-COVID-19 VTE remains unknown. What is the prevalence of VTE among symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients, and which laboratory parameters could enhance the diagnostic accuracy for VTE in these patients? Consecutive patients with objectively confirmed previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, admitted to a single department of lung diseases in a tertiary hospital due to sustained symptoms of dyspnea and/or exercise intolerance, were included. Clinical assessment and laboratory testing, including cytokine profiling (Il-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α), PAI-1, and ferritin, were performed. VTE events (pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis) were confirmed by standard imaging. Clinical and laboratory parameters were compared between participants with and without VTE. 108 patients: 69 (63.9%) males and 39 (36.1%) females, entered the study. VTE episodes were diagnosed in 39.8% (16.7% in the course of COVID-19 and 23.1% after the acute phase of the disease). Patients who entered the study ≤6 months and >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection were compared. Median D-dimer concentration was higher in patients with VTE that occurred within 6 months from the COVID-19 diagnosis compared to the non-VTE group (607 ng/mL vs. 428 ng/mL, borderline significance, p = 0.0595). Median_IL-8 concentration was significantly higher in those who developed VTE more than 6 months after COVID-19 compared to non-VTE patients: 10.19 pg/mL vs. 6.61 pg/mL, respectively, p = 0.048. The same was noted for TNF-α (39.02 pg/mL vs. 24 pg/mL, respectively, p = 0.011). The best diagnostic utility for VTE prediction was obtained for TNF-α concentration in symptomatic patients diagnosed >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection (ROC AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.57-0.91). TNF-α was an independent risk factor of VTE episodes in the whole study group. Detection of elevated IL-8 and TNF-α levels later than 6 months from acute COVID-19 disease may help to identify patients at increased risk of late venous thromboembolism; nevertheless, further studies are needed to validate this observation.

Title: Maternal Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Preeclampsia from Healthy Pregnancy but Not Early-Onset from Late-Onset Subtypes: A Leakage-Free Machine-Learning and Explainability Study.
Abstract: Early-onset (EOPE) and late-onset (LOPE) preeclampsia are clinically distinct, but their molecular differences are incompletely defined. Using a strictly leakage-free pipeline, we re-examined maternal plasma proteomes of EOPE, LOPE, and healthy pregnancy (HP) and asked whether the subtypes are separable at the proteome level. Label-free LC-MS/MS proteomes comprising 370 proteins from 46 women (HP, n = 18; EOPE, n = 17; LOPE, n = 11) were analysed using limma and fully nested cross-validation, in which feature selection, class balancing, and tuning were confined to the outer training folds; model explanations used SHAP and feature-selection stability. Observed selection frequencies far exceeded a random-selection null (for example, complement factor D was selected in all 15 outer folds, Wilson 95% confidence interval 0.80 to 1.00, against an expected frequency of 0.07), indicating that the stability was not a chance artefact. Discrimination is summarised as the mean ± standard deviation across the 5-fold × 3-repeat (15) outer test folds; because the single best-performing classifier was chosen on outer-fold performance, the reported area under the curve is modestly optimistic (on average by 0.04, and by up to 0.10 relative to the median of the three classifiers), even though the leakage-free procedure was applied identically to each classifier. Disease-versus-healthy contrasts were strong and concordant, with 10 and eight differentially abundant proteins identified for EOPE and LOPE, respectively, and AUROCs ranging from 0.88 to 0.90. EOPE showed a complement/acute-phase/coagulation signature, whereas LOPE showed an apolipoprotein/lipid signature, with limma, stability analysis, and SHAP yielding convergent findings. By contrast, the EOPE-versus-LOPE comparison identified no differentially abundant proteins and showed no reliable multivariate separation. A post hoc sensitivity analysis (two-sample t-test, two-sided, α = 0.05) indicated that the discovery cohort (early-onset n = 17, late-onset n = 11) had 80% power only for very large per-protein standardised differences (Cohen's d ≥ 1.13, or d ≥ 2.10 after Bonferroni correction across the 370 proteins), and only 24% and 51% power to detect medium (d = 0.5) and large (d = 0.8) effects; the absence of a detectable early-versus-late difference is therefore consistent with limited power for small-to-moderate effects rather than proven biological equivalence. In an independent ELISA cohort (n = 87), EOPE differed from HP for seven of nine analytes, with AUCs of up to 0.82, led by sFlt-1 (fold-changes paralleled these areas under the curve: the largest early-onset median disease-to-control ratios were fibronectin 2.9, soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 2.8 and α1-antitrypsin 2.5, whereas placental growth factor decreased to 0.6 and apolipoprotein E was unchanged at 1.0); however, the subtypes again did not separate. On adjustment for maternal age, body mass index and smoking, the leading early-onset markers remained significant (soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, serum amyloid A and fibronectin robust; complement factor D and alpha-1-antitrypsin borderline), whereas maternal chronic hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disease were not recorded and could not be modelled. Benchmarked against soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (DeLong test), no novel candidate exceeded its discrimination and several were significantly lower; only glycoprotein hormones alpha chain added cross-validated incremental value in early-onset disease (cross-validated area under the curve 0.71 to 0.76), and none improved on soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 in late-onset disease; apolipoprotein E did not validate, and placental growth factor decreased as expected. Plasma proteomics distinguishes preeclampsia from healthy pregnancy and recovers coherent subtype-leaning signatures but provides little evidence of a sharp EOPE-LOPE boundary; the prioritised panel warrants validation in larger cohorts.

Title: Two Faces of the Same Thrombus: Molecular Phenotypes of Thromboinflammation in Acute Pulmonary Embolism and the Path to Phenotype-Guided Risk Stratification.
Abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially fatal cardiovascular emergency where early risk assessment determines treatment escalation. Clinical scores like PESI and sPESI are useful but capture only a single moment and cannot track evolving biological processes: coagulation on inflamed endothelium, nitric oxide signaling loss, and right ventricular pressure overload. Circulating biomarkers provide direct readouts of these events. This review proposes that acute PE molecular pathophysiology organizes into two overlapping phenotypes-two faces of the same thrombus. The first is a predominantly thromboinflammatory phenotype, driven by neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), complement activation, and endothelial injury; the second is a predominantly myocardial phenotype, driven by right ventricular pressure overload and subendocardial ischemia. We examine each phenotype's molecular basis and appraise how far corresponding biomarkers-D-dimer, cardiac troponins, natriuretic peptides, GDF-15, H-FABP, sST2, complement activation products, and inflammatory indices-have moved into clinical practice. Two issues deserve attention: biomarker kinetics during the first 72 h after symptom onset, and whether intermediate-risk patients can be separated into meaningful molecular phenotypes. We address implementation barriers: lack of harmonized assays, undefined decision thresholds, and absence of prospective multicenter validation. This narrative review connects disease mechanisms to which patients are most likely to deteriorate and outlines a research agenda for phenotype-guided risk stratification.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Patients with Cancer: A Review of Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the management of obesity and type 2 diabetes, including among patients with cancer. Although previous research has mainly focused on cancer incidence, their associations with clinical outcomes after cancer diagnosis remain less well characterized. Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate the oncologic and survival outcomes associated with GLP-1 RA use in adults with an established malignancy. We performed a systematic review of comparative studies evaluating GLP-1 RA use in patients with a confirmed cancer diagnosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications from 1 January 2016 to 8 August 2026. Twenty-six retrospective cohort studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Thirteen studies included selective GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide within the same exposure group. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Twenty-five studies evaluated overall survival and/or all-cause mortality, while nine assessed cancer recurrence, progression, or related outcomes. Survival and mortality outcomes more often favored the exposed group (especially compared with nonuse) than not, but findings were less consistent in active-comparator analyses. Evidence for recurrence and progression was sparse and heterogeneous, and no clear signal of increased risk was observed. Because all of these were observational studies with substantial differences in populations, comparators, exposure definitions, and duration of follow-up, the survival associations do not imply causality or direct antitumor effects of GLP-1 RAs. Clinically, the preponderance of evidence does not support the use of GLP-1 RAs as cancer-directed therapy, and their use in patients with cancer should be guided by established indications such as obesity and type 2 diabetes. Potential explanations include effects on glycemic and cardiovascular risk factors, treatment selection, residual confounding, or combinations thereof. Prospective studies and randomized controlled trials with cancer-specific outcomes and longer follow-up are needed to further evaluate these associations.

Title: Association Between Plasma microRNA Levels and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Participants from an Epidemiological Cohort.
Abstract: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE): CVD death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and non-fatal stroke. The associations between plasma miRNA levels and 3P-MACE in a prospective cohort from an epidemiological study were evaluated. This nested case-control study included 479 participants: 166 cases with 3P-MACE and 313 controls matched individually for sex, exact baseline age, and region of residence. Median follow-up was 10.4 years [7.0; 11.7]. Total RNA was isolated from EDTA plasma using the miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Advanced Kit. Libraries were prepared with the QIAseq miRNA UDI Library Kit and sequenced on a NextSeq 550 (1 × 75 bp). After adjustment for six and twelve preanalytical and clinical covariates, eleven and five differentially expressed (DE) miRNAs retained significant associations with 3P-MACE or CVD death, respectively. Although these findings support plasma miRNA profiles as potential MACE biomarkers, all DE miRNAs remain exploratory. Further studies in larger independent populations with cross-validation are required before integration with traditional risk markers to predict future MACE.

Title: Proteomic Remodeling in the Female Heart During Spaceflight and Recovery.
Abstract: Spaceflight profoundly impacts cardiovascular physiology. To gain insight into the underlying molecular adaptations, we examined the female cardiac proteome during spaceflight and recovery. We hypothesized that spaceflight remodels the cardiac proteome, including mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis pathways, during both flight and recovery, altering cardiovascular health risk. Proteomic analysis was performed on hearts from female C57BL/6J mice flown aboard the International Space Station (ISS) for 55 to 60 days as part of the NASA Rodent Research-20 (RR-20) study and a recovery cohort returned to Earth after 42 days, with sampling occurring five days after landing, and corresponding ground controls. Consistent with our hypothesis, spaceflight enriched mitochondrial bioenergetic pathways relative to ground controls, including cellular respiration, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation. These changes occurred alongside the remodeling of antioxidant pathways, suggesting altered redox regulation during flight and increased susceptibility to reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in the heart versus controls. Postflight recovery was characterized by distinct metabolic, redox, and structural remodeling signatures, including pathways associated with sarcomere organization, contractile function, and extracellular matrix regulation. These findings reveal cardiac proteomic remodeling during and after spaceflight and provide molecular insights relevant to cardiovascular risk assessment and countermeasure development for exploration missions.

Title: HDL Functionality, Cholesterol-Related Biomarkers and Incidence of Dementia: A Case-Cohort Study in Older Adults at High Cardiovascular Risk.
Abstract: Associations of lipid profiles, including qualitative and functional high-density lipoprotein (HDL) traits, and cholesterol-related biomarkers with incident dementia and Alzheimer's disease (AD), remain unclear. In this regard, older adults at high cardiovascular risk are at particularly high risk of developing dementia. The aim is to evaluate whether these biomarkers are associated with the incidence of dementia and AD in older adults at high cardiovascular (CV) risk. In a case-cohort study, we selected 106 incident dementia cases (82 AD) and a random subcohort of 201 non-cases. We quantified (baseline and at one-year), lipid profile; HDL-mediate cholesterol efflux capacity in a model of human neurons; HDL-mediated anti-inflammatory protection in a model of brain endothelial cells; 24S-hydroxycholesterol and apolipoprotein E. Multivariable-adjusted Cox models were addressed. HDL cholesterol was inversely associated, whereas triglycerides directly associated, with dementia and AD incidence. Higher HDL-mediated cholesterol efflux was inversely associated with dementia (HR 0.64, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.45-0.91) and AD (HR 0.52, 0.35-0.76). Greater HDL-mediated endothelial protection was associated with lower dementia and AD incidence (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.99 and HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.91, respectively). A one-year increase in 24S-hydroxycholesterol was associated with a higher incidence of any dementia (HR 2.38, 1.33-4.27) and AD (HR 2.24, 1.11-4.53). Enhanced HDL functional properties ex vivo, in preclinical models using human brain cells, together with lower levels of 24S-hydroxycholesterol, are inversely associated with the incidence of dementia and AD, highlighting these factors as promising prognostic targets in older adults at high CV risk.

Title: Circulating suPAR in Relation to Renal and Cardiovascular Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Pilot Study.
Abstract: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) is an inflammatory biomarker associated with immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence suggests that suPAR may be involved in renal and cardiovascular injury and may reflect cumulative organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Serum suPAR levels were measured in patients with SLE and healthy controls. Within the SLE cohort, suPAR levels were further evaluated according to the presence or absence of organ involvement. In this pilot study, serum suPAR levels were significantly higher in patients with SLE than in healthy controls. Within the SLE cohort, patients with renal involvement and those with reduced renal function had higher suPAR levels than their respective comparison groups. Similarly, patients with cardiovascular involvement showed significantly higher suPAR levels than SLE patients without cardiovascular involvement and healthy controls. However, serum suPAR levels were not significantly correlated with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Circulating suPAR levels are elevated in SLE and may be particularly associated with renal and cardiovascular involvement. These findings support the potential role of suPAR as a biomarker of cardiorenal involvement in SLE, although its relationship with renal function and clinical outcomes requires validation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: Tenascin X and Tenascin C Serum Levels in Relation to Age and Cardiometabolic Risk Parameters.
Abstract: Tenascin C (TNC) and tenascin X (TNX) are extracellular matrix glycoproteins in the same family but with reportedly distinct functions: TNC is acutely up-regulated during tissue damage, whereas TNX maintains structural connective tissue stability. Recently, recurring pathogenic variants in the TNX gene (TNXB) were linked to Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia, yet the regulation and clinical function of TNX remain poorly understood.
