Title: Primary Pyogenic Ventriculitis in Adults: A Retrospective Case Series of Clinical Characteristics, Cerebrospinal Fluid Parameters, and Surgical Drain Managements.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary pyogenic ventriculitis in adults is a rare, life-threatening central nervous system infection occurring in the absence of prior neurosurgical interventions or indwelling medical devices. Due to its scarcity, individual clinical trajectories, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytochemical variations, and external ventricular drain (EVD) management timing remain poorly defined. Methods: We conducted a retrospective case series of N = 8 with confirmed primary pyogenic ventriculitis admitted to a tertiary referral center in eastern Taiwan between 2019 and 2023. Individual-level clinical, neuroimaging, CSF, and surgical timing data were analyzed descriptively. Results: The cohort was 62.5% male (n = 5/8) with a median age of 60.5 years [IQR: 51.5-66.5]. All patients presented with severe initial neurological impairment (median initial Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS] = 7.5 [IQR: 4.0-9.75]). Overall 1-year mortality was 25.0% (n = 2/8, both male). Survivors (n = 6) exhibited marked initial CSF pleocytosis (median WBC = 1005.0 cells/µL [IQR: 508.0-1977.5]) and elevated protein (median = 1030.0 mg/dL [IQR: 847.5-1225.0]). Conversely, non-survivors (n = 2) demonstrated blunted initial CSF inflammatory markers (median WBC = 82.5 cells/µL; median protein = 212.1 mg/dL) alongside severe initial coma (median GCS = 3.5) and systemic shock requiring vasopressors. EVD placement occurred at a median of 2.5 days post-onset in non-survivors compared to 10.5 days in survivors, reflecting urgent, reactive surgical intervention in rapidly deteriorating cases (confounding by indication). At 1 year, surviving patients achieved a median modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 2.5 [IQR: 2.0-3.0]. Conclusions: In this rare adult primary pyogenic ventriculitis series, fatal cases were characterized by severe initial coma, vasopressor-dependent shock, and blunted CSF cellularity. Urgent EVD placement in non-survivors represented reactive rescue therapy. Future prospective multicenter registries are required to evaluate whether standardized, early intraventricular source control improves functional outcomes.

Title: Cardiovascular Manifestations of Cystic Fibrosis.
Abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) has undergone a remarkable transformation from a fatal childhood disease to a chronic adult condition, with a median predicted survival now exceeding 50 years following the introduction of highly effective CFTR modulator therapy (HEMT). This demographic shift has unmasked cardiovascular complications that were previously unrecognized due to premature mortality. In a multinational propensity-matched cohort, CF conferred a 65% higher risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACEs), including myocardial infarction, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation, versus matched controls (Frost et al., HR 1.65). In a separate Canadian population-based cohort, cardiovascular disease occurred at 2.9 times the rate of the general population and at least 20 years earlier (Arya et al., RR 2.9). Cardiac involvement extends beyond the traditional paradigm of cor pulmonale. CFTR is expressed in cardiomyocytes, vascular endothelium, and smooth muscle, where its dysfunction disrupts ion homeostasis, impairs nitric oxide-dependent vasodilation, and promotes oxidative stress. Clinically, these mechanisms manifest as biventricular dysfunction detectable by strain echocardiography and cardiac MRI even when ejection fraction is preserved, diffuse myocardial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction and accelerated arterial stiffness from childhood, increased arrhythmia susceptibility, and, in a single-center cohort, an unexpectedly high prevalence of pericardial calcification (18%) on chest CT that awaits independent replication. Paradoxically, while HEMT has dramatically improved pulmonary outcomes, it introduces new cardiovascular considerations including hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity, and cross-sectional data in modulator-treated cohorts show persistent cardiac abnormalities, though whether these predate treatment or would differ without it is unknown. This review synthesizes the genetic, molecular, and clinical dimensions of cardiovascular disease in CF; distinguishes direct CFTR-mediated cardiac effects from indirect consequences of chronic lung disease; examines vascular, electrophysiological, valvular, and pericardial manifestations; and discusses management implications including CFTR modulator therapy, exercise, nutritional paradigm shifts, and transplantation considerations.

Title: Association Between Chronic Tamsulosin Therapy and Intraoperative Hemodynamics During Spinal Anesthesia: A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract: Background: This prospective observational study investigated the association between chronic tamsulosin therapy and intraoperative hemodynamic changes in patients undergoing elective transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P) under spinal anesthesia. Methods: Adult patients scheduled for elective TUR-P under spinal anesthesia were prospectively enrolled. Patients receiving long-term tamsulosin therapy comprised the tamsulosin group, whereas those with no history of α1-adrenergic blocker use served as the control group. Hemodynamic variables, including mean arterial pressure (MAP) and heart rate, were recorded before spinal anesthesia and at predefined time points during the first 60 min after spinal anesthesia. Results: A total of 115 patients were analyzed (tamsulosin, n = 56; control, n = 59). Baseline MAP was comparable between groups. The adjusted linear mixed-effects model demonstrated a significant group × time interaction for MAP (F(5, 565.10) = 8.34, p < 0.001). Adjusted between-group MAP differences were -4.9 mmHg (95% CI, -8.8 to -1.0; p = 0.015) at 5 min, -17.0 mmHg (95% CI, -20.2 to -13.8; p < 0.001) at 30 min, and -16.4 mmHg (95% CI, -19.5 to -13.3; p < 0.001) at 60 min. Criteria-defined hypotension occurred in 21/56 (37.5%) patients in the tamsulosin group and 17/59 (28.8%) in the control group (p = 0.32). Conclusions: Chronic tamsulosin therapy was associated with lower intraoperative MAP values during spinal anesthesia, without a statistically significant increase in the incidence of clinically defined hypotension. These findings suggest that chronic tamsulosin use may be associated with a different intraoperative blood pressure response following spinal anesthesia.

Title: Organ Malperfusion and Mortality in Acute Type 1 Aortic Dissection with Iliac Extension: A Retrospective Single-Center Study Focused on Mesenteric Malperfusion and the Source-Clearance Hypothesis.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Mesenteric malperfusion is the most lethal and least recognizable complication of acute type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to examine organ-specific malperfusion patterns and 30-day mortality in acute type 1 aortic dissection with iliac extension, and to evaluate whether the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and superior mesenteric artery (SMA) origin pattern add predictive value for mesenteric malperfusion syndrome within a "source-clearance" framework. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 80 consecutive patients with acute type 1 aortic dissection extending to the iliac arteries who underwent surgical repair between January 2020 and March 2026 were reviewed. Malperfusion (preoperative finding) and malperfusion syndrome (end-organ injury persisting despite central repair) were defined for six organ systems; visceral branch origin and planimetric true lumen ratio were assessed on computed tomography angiography (CTA). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Results: Thirty-day mortality was 33.8%; 60% of patients had malperfusion, and mortality rose with the number of organs involved (0/1/≥2: 12.5%/32.1%/70.0%). Mesenteric malperfusion (n = 21) carried the highest mortality (71.4%); all nine patients who developed mesenteric syndrome died. Cerebral malperfusion was most frequent (n = 27); all nine who improved postoperatively survived, whereas mortality was 81.8% in the 22 who developed the syndrome. Preoperative shock or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) (odds ratio [OR] = 7.02), mesenteric malperfusion (OR = 6.24), LAR (OR = 1.07 per 0.01 unit) and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS; OR = 0.75 per point) were independent predictors. LAR and SMA origin pattern were uncorrelated (r = -0.04) and together raised the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for mesenteric syndrome from 0.861 to 0.955; mortality was 75% with mixed SMA origin (n = 8). Conclusions: Malperfusion is a dose-dependent risk spectrum; mesenteric involvement is its most lethal component, increasing mortality six-fold independently of hemodynamic and metabolic status. Joint interpretation of LAR and SMA origin pattern offers a practical, validation-pending framework for perioperative management of the mesenteric circulation in centers without a hybrid operating room.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Eye Disease: A Systematic Review of Screening, Diagnosis, Prognosis, Treatment-Response Prediction, and Clinical Decision Support.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding eye care beyond image-based detection toward prognosis, treatment-response prediction, monitoring, triage, and clinician-facing decision support. We evaluated AI across eye-disease screening, diagnosis, prognosis, treatment response, and decision support, emphasizing validation, explainability, and clinical readiness. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Six databases plus supplementary routes identified English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 through 10 August 2026. Included studies underwent design-mapped Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI)/adapted-JBI item-level appraisal; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results: The evidence base comprised 270 studies. Diabetic retinopathy/diabetic macular oedema was the largest clinical area (82), followed by retinal/multi-disease AI (52), glaucoma (46), and age-related macular degeneration (AMD)/macular disease (29); convolutional neural network (CNN)/convolutional deep learning was the largest primary method group (136). External validation was confirmed in 130 studies, including 95 with a clinical/geographic/prospective/real-world external-validation component (86 clinical-only and nine mixed clinical + technical); 49 had a strict direct clinical comparator and 90 used explainability. Pediatric/pediatric-relevant evidence accounted for 30 studies, while explicit optometry/optometrist involvement appeared in only three. Conclusions: Ophthalmic AI spans diagnosis through clinical management, but translation remains limited by heterogeneous outcomes, incomplete independent validation, few direct comparators, and sparse evaluation of safety, workflow effects, and patient outcomes.

Title: Pain, Low Muscle Mass, and Exercise Participation After Myocardial Infarction: Determinants of Initial Exercise Testing at a Tertiary Center Serving a Rural Region.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Musculoskeletal pain and balance impairments are common in patients referred for cardiac rehabilitation (CR), but their influence on early exercise participation and aerobic capacity remains unclear. This study examined whether pain and muscle mass are associated with initial exercise tolerance test (ETT) participation and VO2 peak. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort included 162 of 189 patients referred to CR after percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction; 105 who completed a symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise test were analyzed for VO2 peak. Pain intensity was assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS 0-10), and the skeletal muscle index (SMI) was measured using a bioelectrical impedance analysis. Determinants of ETT participation and VO2 peak were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regressions, respectively, with pain analyzed as a binary, three-category, and continuous variable. Results: More than half the patients reported musculoskeletal pain during physical activity, and 24.7% had balance problems. Patients with pain (VAS 1-10) had lower appendicular skeletal muscle mass and poorer functional status than pain-free patients. Among the 105 who completed the ETT, the pain group showed significantly lower workload-estimated metabolic equivalents [METs (Q)], respiratory exchange ratios, and peak minute ventilation and a shorter exercise time, but VO2 peak did not differ between the groups. ETT participation rates were similar across pain categories (63.4%, 67.2%, and 63.0% for VAS 0, 1-5, and 6-10, respectively). In the multivariable logistic regression, older age, hypertension, and low SMI scores were independently associated with reduced ETT participation. In the linear regression, age was the only significant predictor of VO2 peak; the SMI score showed a borderline association (p = 0.065), but pain intensity was not independently associated with VO2 peak. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal pain is prevalent among patients entering CR after myocardial infarction, and it is accompanied by low muscle mass and functional limitations. However, after adjustment, pain itself was not an independent determinant of ETT participation or VO2 peak. Low SMI scores were independently associated with reduced test participation and showed only a borderline association with aerobic capacity. These cross-sectional findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

Title: Factors Associated with Major Versus Minor Lower Extremity Amputation in Hospitalized Patients with Diabetes in Saudi Arabia.
Abstract: Background: Major lower extremity amputation (LEA) is a severe complication of diabetes with substantial disability and mortality. Evidence from Saudi Arabia with distinguishing factors linked to major versus minor amputation is limited. We examined demographic, clinical, vascular, and wound-related factors associated with amputation level among hospitalized patients with diabetes who had already undergone LEA. Methods: We conducted a retrospective comparative observational study of 230 adults with diabetes who underwent non-traumatic LEA at Al Noor Specialist Hospital, Makkah. Because the cohort comprised exclusively patients who had already undergone amputation, the analysis was explanatory in purpose and characterized factors associated with the level of amputation (major versus minor) rather than predictors of amputation occurrence in the broader population of patients with diabetic foot disease. Independent associations were examined using multivariable binary logistic regression with Firth's penalization; adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals were the principal results, and exploratory model diagnostics. Results: Major amputation occurred in 92 patients (40.0%); 138 (60.0%) underwent minor amputation. Mean age was 58.4 ± 12.6 years; 77.0% were male. After adjustment, ischemic heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 5.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.63-16.55), multiple foot ulcers (aOR 4.65, 95% CI 1.53-14.17), ulcer duration >1 month (aOR 3.15, 95% CI 1.09-9.10), and documented peripheral neuropathy (aOR 7.46, 95% CI 1.13-49.35) were independently associated with major amputation. The neuropathy estimate was imprecise, reflecting the small number of documented cases, and should therefore be regarded as highly uncertain. These exploratory associations describe the conditional comparison of amputation level within this operated cohort and should not be interpreted as individual probabilities of amputation or amputation level. Conclusions: Ischemic heart disease, multiple ulcers, prolonged ulcer duration, and documented peripheral neuropathy were associated with major amputation. These associations should be interpreted within the limits of a retrospective, single-center design with possible underascertainment of neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease. These exploratory findings require replication in independent, prospectively designed cohorts before they can be generalized to other settings or applied clinically.

Title: Coffee Consumption, Serum Copeptin, and Selected Echocardiographic Parameters in Patients with ADPKD: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Coffee consumption has been suggested to influence arginine vasopressin-related pathways and cardiovascular function. However, its relationships with serum copeptin and cardiac parameters in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between habitual coffee consumption and serum copeptin concentrations and selected echocardiographic parameters in patients with ADPKD. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 73 patients with ADPKD were classified as coffee consumers (n = 35) or non-consumers (n = 38). Serum copeptin measurements were available for 62 patients. Coffee consumption was assessed using a standardized questionnaire and expressed as grams of dry coffee per month. Multivariable models were used to assess associations with log-transformed copeptin, mitral annular e' velocity, and E/e' ratio. Results: Serum copeptin levels were lower among coffee consumers than non-consumers (median, 263.51 vs. 332.77 ng/L; p = 0.013). After adjustment, coffee consumption was associated with lower log-transformed copeptin levels (B = -0.263; p = 0.047), although this association was not statistically significant when using heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) robust standard errors (p = 0.074). Coffee consumers had higher mitral annular e' velocity (8.61 vs. 5.86 cm/s; p < 0.001), which remained significant after adjustment (B = 2.531; p < 0.001), and a lower E/e' ratio (B = -4.548; p = 0.007). Conclusions: In this ADPKD cohort, coffee consumption was associated with lower serum copeptin levels, higher mitral annular e' velocity, and lower E/e' ratio. These findings raise the hypothesis that habitual coffee consumption may be associated with vasopressin-copeptin system activity and diastolic myocardial relaxation in patients with ADPKD. However, the copeptin association was not robust to HC3 analysis, and the echocardiographic findings should be considered exploratory.

Title: Routine Pringle Maneuver During Recipient Hepatectomy Is Associated with Improved Perioperative and Early Graft Outcomes After Adult Liver Transplantation.
Abstract: Background: Recipient hepatectomy during orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is frequently complicated by severe bleeding due to portal hypertension and collateral circulation. The Pringle maneuver's benefit in this setting remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed data from 141 adults who underwent primary deceased-donor OLT at a single center between January 2020 and June 2026. A routine intermittent Pringle maneuver was introduced in 2023; 79 subsequent recipients comprised the Pringle group, while 62 earlier recipients served as historical controls. Multivariable regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to address confounding, and temporal trends within each period were examined. Results: Indication for transplantation, markers of hepatic decompensation, and extended-criteria donor status did not differ between groups. Compared with controls, the Pringle group required fewer packed red blood cell units (median 2 {IQR 0-4} vs. 3 {1-5}; p = 0.046), fresh frozen plasma units (4 {0-6} vs. 4 {3-8}; mean 4.1 vs. 6.9; no plasma transfused in 30.8% vs. 13.6%; p = 0.005), and total blood products (5 {0-9} vs. 8 {4-14}; p = 0.009). Recipient hepatectomy was shorter (129 {105-165} vs. 177 {146-208} minutes; p < 0.001), and postoperative bleeding (2.5% vs. 22.6%; p < 0.001), biliary leak (2.5% vs. 11.3%; p = 0.043), and early allograft dysfunction (EAD; 6.3% vs. 29.0%; p < 0.001) were less frequent. After adjustment, the Pringle maneuver remained associated with shorter hepatectomy (time ratio 0.76; 95% CI 0.67-0.87), reduced fresh frozen plasma (IRR 0.60; 0.40-0.91) and total blood product use (IRR 0.61; 0.40-0.92), and lower odds of postoperative bleeding (OR 0.04; 0.01-0.25), biliary leak (OR 0.13; 0.02-0.63), and EAD (OR 0.14; 0.04-0.58). Packed red blood cell transfusion was nonsignificant after adjustment (IRR 0.70; 0.43-1.12). IPTW yielded consistent findings. Overall survival did not differ (p = 0.885). Conclusions: In this historical-control study, routine intermittent Pringle maneuver was associated with improved operative efficiency, lower transfusion requirements, and fewer early complications without affecting survival; given the retrospective design and the modest absolute differences in transfusion, these findings require prospective confirmation.

Title: Cardiac-Specific AI Reconstruction Versus Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction for Emergency Coronary CT Angiography: A Paired Single-Center Study Including Triple-Rule-Out CT.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Optimizing coronary image quality is important in emergency computed tomography (CT), including coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and triple-rule-out CT angiography (TRO-CTA). We compared objective and subjective image quality between cardiac-specific artificial intelligence (AI) reconstruction and hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) using paired images from the same acquisition. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 66 of 75 consecutively assessed emergency examinations: 28 standard CCTA and 38 TRO-CTA examinations acquired without pharmacologic heart-rate control. Both protocols used identical cardiac acquisition settings. AI and HIR images were reconstructed from the same acquisition with matched cardiac phases and motion-correction settings. Objective measurements were obtained at nine coronary locations, and two readers independently assessed overall image quality and perceived vessel-edge sharpness in unmasked paired comparisons. Results: AI reduced coronary noise from 45.8 ± 8.5 to 24.2 ± 7.5 Hounsfield units (HU; -47.3%), increased signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from 9.0 ± 2.4 to 20.6 ± 5.6 (+129.6%), and increased contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) from 14.8 ± 4.2 to 45.8 ± 16.4 (+209.7%; all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Readers 1 and 2 preferred AI for overall quality in 65/66 and 63/66 examinations and for sharpness in 64/66 and 63/66, respectively. Conclusions: Cardiac-specific AI reconstruction reduced image noise and increased SNR and CNR in emergency CCTA, including TRO-CTA, with readers generally favoring AI images for perceived quality and sharpness. Further studies should evaluate whether these image-quality improvements translate into better diagnostic performance.

Title: The Influence of Deep Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest on the Incidence of Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury After Pulmonary Endarterectomy.
Abstract: Background: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is performed using phases of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA). DHCA has been discussed as a risk factor for cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (AKI). The study analyzes the influence of the duration of DHCA on the incidence of postoperative AKI in patients undergoing PEA. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adult CTEPH patients who underwent PEA. The main exposure was DHCA at 18-20 °C core temperature. Primary endpoint was postoperative AKI defined by the KDIGO serum creatinine criteria. Secondary endpoints included severe postoperative AKI, major adverse cardiovascular events and mortality. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression models were performed for risk factor analysis. Results: Four hundred and eighty-three patients were included (mean age 61 ± 13 years). The incidence of postoperative AKI was 50%. Multivariate analysis showed no association between DHCA and AKI. Postoperative AKI was independently associated with chronic kidney disease (OR = 1.76, 95% CI = 1.05-2.95), age (OR = 1.02, 95% CI = 1.00-1.03), cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.01-1.02) and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (OR = 1.05, 95% CI = 1.01-1.10). Patients with preoperative diuretics had a lower risk for postoperative AKI (OR = 0.44, 95% CI = 0.29-0.66). MACE were more frequent in patients with postoperative AKI (28.4% vs. 14.2%, p < 0.001), whereas 30-day and 1-year mortality did not differ. Conclusions: Results from this study indicate no influence of DHCA duration on occurrence of postoperative AKI. Risk factors identified for postoperative AKI were chronic kidney disease, age, CPB duration and VIS.

Title: Bilateral Internal Thoracic Artery Grafting in Coronary Surgery: A Three-Tier Decision Framework.
Abstract: The left internal mammary artery grafted to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) is the main determinant of survival in coronary artery bypass grafting, but the choice of the second graft remains controversial. The use of both mammary arteries offers a greater long-term survival benefit compared with a single mammary artery graft; however, this advantage is delayed and diminished when compared with a single mammary artery graft plus a radial artery graft. Furthermore, this approach is associated with a higher risk of sternal complications and, via mechanisms of competitive flow and steal phenomenon, of perioperative coronary malperfusion. This article proposes organising the clinical decision-making process according to three hierarchical levels: (1) absolute contraindications based on the patient's medical history that preclude the use of a particular graft (thoracic irradiation, subclavian artery disease, acute aortic dissection); (2) the haemodynamic adequacy of the graft for the target coronary territory; (3) the assessment of the risk of delayed sternal healing in the individual patient, where skeletonization has reduced the historical significance of diabetes. Overlaying these is a transversal variable represented by the harvesting technique (pedicled mammary artery vs. skeletonized mammary artery, together with the surgeon's learning curve), which re-interprets apparently unfavourable results and distinguishes the risk associated with the graft itself from that of the surgical procedure. The model aims to rationalise patient selection and reduce the persistent underutilisation of bilateral mammary artery grafting. It should be noted at the outset that this survival advantage rests largely on observational and propensity-matched evidence and has not been confirmed on an intention-to-treat basis by the only adequately powered randomised trial, so that the model proposed here is offered as a framework for selection rather than as a claim of established superiority.

Title: Exploratory Risk Assessment of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Antiphospholipid Antibody-Related Scores in Patients with ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.
Abstract: Background: Antiphospholipid antibodies have been found in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of the global antiphospholipid syndrome score (GAPSS) derivatives in predicting cardiovascular diseases in Korean patients with AAV, and to derive a simple candidate index for cardiovascular diseases. Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study including 170 patients with AAV. The adjusted GAPSS (aGAPSS), aGAPSS specific for cardiovascular diseases (aGAPSScvd), and aGAPSS for Korean patients with APS (aGAPSS [KAPS]) were calculated in each patient. The cardiovascular diseases were defined as cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The accuracy of each index was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC). An exploratory multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with a backward elimination method was performed to derive a candidate index. Covariates consisting the aGAPSScvd were included in the model. Results: The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for CVA were 0.507 (p = 0.926), 0.531 (p = 0.676), and 0.493 (p = 0.923), respectively. The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for ACS were 0.613 (p = 0.441), 0.752 (p = 0.086), and 0.796 (p = 0.043), respectively. The exploratory multivariable model revealed a candidate index, aGAPSScvd for ACS in Korean patients with AAV (aGAPSScvd [KAAV]) = 2 × lupus anticoagulant (LA) + 2 × obesity. The AUC of the aGAPSScvd (KAAV) in predicting ACS was 0.843 (p = 0.019). Conclusions: The two-item candidate index aGAPSScvd (KAAV), consisting of LA and obesity, showed discriminatory ability for ACS, which warrants further validation in larger studies.

Title: High-Volume Online Hemodiafiltration: Does Patient Phenotype Matter?
Abstract: Online hemodiafiltration (OL-HDF) has been associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with conventional hemodialysis in randomized trials, particularly in studies achieving high convection volumes. Whether specific patient phenotypes derive greater benefit from OL-HDF remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the available evidence regarding potential clinical phenotypes associated with enhanced benefit from high-volume OL-HDF, including older adults, anuric patients, individuals with heart failure, patients with poor intradialytic hemodynamic tolerance, frail patients, those with increased inflammatory burden, and incident dialysis patients. Current randomized evidence has not detected convincing treatment-effect modification across the clinical subgroups examined; however, most subgroup analyses were not designed or powered to establish equivalence of treatment effects. Higher achieved convection volumes have been associated with improved outcomes, although these observational or post-randomization associations should not be interpreted as proof of a causal dose-response relationship. Nevertheless, several high-risk clinical scenarios may be associated with greater absolute clinical benefit because of an elevated baseline risk of adverse outcomes. Available data suggest that personalization of OL-HDF should focus less on selecting eligible phenotypes and more on optimizing treatment delivery according to patient characteristics, treatment goals, and technical feasibility. Future research should explore patient-centred outcomes and identify strategies to maximize the benefits of high-volume OL-HDF within a precision medicine framework.

Title: Acute Kidney Injury After Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Incidence, Risk Factors, Clinical Impact, and Contrast-Sparing Strategies-A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinically relevant complication following percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). This systematic review evaluated its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact while separately examining the procedural feasibility and renal outcomes of contrast-sparing and zero-contrast LAAO strategies. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception through 6 October 2026. Eighteen studies met the eligibility criteria. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively, with AKI-focused evidence considered separately from contrast-sparing procedural studies. Results: Four studies primarily evaluated AKI following conventional LAAO. Three creatinine-based cohorts reported AKI incidences ranging from 5.3% to 13.7%, whereas one large administrative database study reported coded AKI in 5.3% of index hospitalizations; these estimates were not considered directly comparable. Pre-existing renal dysfunction was the most consistent marker of AKI susceptibility, and AKI was associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Fourteen studies evaluated contrast-sparing or zero-contrast approaches and generally demonstrated high procedural success. However, renal outcomes were inconsistently assessed; several studies did not systematically report AKI, and AKI occurred even after zero-contrast implantation. Conclusions: Available evidence supports the procedural feasibility of contrast-sparing and zero-contrast LAAO but does not establish that contrast avoidance prevents AKI or provides a proven nephroprotective benefit. A renal-tailored framework remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective comparative validation using standardized renal endpoints.

Title: Association of Anti-TNF Therapy with Ventricular Repolarization Indices in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Longitudinal Electrocardiographic Study.
Abstract: Background: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity that cannot be fully explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors alone. Chronic systemic inflammation has been implicated in myocardial electrical remodeling, yet the effect of anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) therapy on ventricular repolarization remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated longitudinal changes in electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarization following anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 115 patients with RA who initiated anti-TNF therapy and had clinical, laboratory, and 12-lead electrocardiographic assessments at baseline and after approximately 24 weeks. Ventricular repolarization was evaluated using QT, corrected QT (QTc), Tpeak-Tend (Tp-e), corrected Tp-e (cTp-e), and Tp-e/QT. Cross-sectional associations between repolarization indices and inflammatory/disease-related variables were assessed at 24 weeks, together with longitudinal correlations between changes in these variables and changes in repolarization indices. Results: The mean age was 54.4 ± 12.2 years, and 81.7% of participants were women. After 24 weeks of treatment, significant reductions were observed in CRP, ESR, DAS28-CRP, and HAQ scores (all p < 0.001). The Tp-e interval decreased from 85.1 ± 13.6 to 75.3 ± 13.5 ms, and the Tp-e/QT ratio decreased from 0.20 ± 0.04 to 0.18 ± 0.03 (both p < 0.001), with moderate within-subject effect sizes for both changes (Cohen's dz = 0.46). At 24 weeks, Tp-e and Tp-e/QT were positively correlated with inflammatory markers, disease activity, functional impairment, and disease duration. However, longitudinal change-to-change analyses showed no consistent associations between changes in inflammatory/disease activity measures and changes in repolarization indices, except for a weak correlation between ΔDAS28-CRP and ΔTp-e (r = 0.201, p = 0.031). Despite a significant reduction in mean QTc, the proportion of patients with prolonged QTc remained unchanged (18.3% at both assessments; McNemar p = 1.00). Conclusions: Anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA was associated with significant improvements in several ECG-derived ventricular repolarization indices alongside reductions in inflammatory and disease activity. However, the lack of consistent longitudinal correlations and the unchanged prevalence of prolonged QTc indicate that these findings should be interpreted as treatment-associated changes rather than evidence of a direct electrophysiological or antiarrhythmic effect of TNF inhibition. Prospective controlled studies incorporating clinical cardiovascular outcomes are warranted.

Title: Association Between Post-Cardiopulmonary Bypass Hemodynamics and 30-Day Mortality After Aortic Surgery: A Single-Center, Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Background: We evaluated phase-specific associations between perioperative hemodynamic variables and 30-day mortality following aortic surgery requiring cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and to assess the utility of post-CPB variables in risk stratification. Methods: We analyzed 691 patients who underwent aortic surgery requiring CPB. Hemodynamic variables were assessed during the preoperative, pre-incision, pre-CPB, and post-CPB phases and included heart rate (HR), systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean blood pressure (MBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), shock index (SI; HR/SBP), and modified shock index (MSI; HR/MBP). The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Holm correction was applied to the between-group comparisons of hemodynamic variables. Adjusted Cox models used ridge penalization and included surgery group, CPB time, and mean post-CPB vasoactive-inotropic score. Results: Thirty patients (4.3%) died within 30 days. After Holm correction, significant differences between survivors and non-survivors remained only for post-CPB SBP, MBP, SI, and MSI. In adjusted Cox models, 30-day mortality was associated with higher post-CPB SI (hazard ratio [95% CI], 1.38 [1.17 to 1.64] per 0.1-unit increase; p < 0.001) and MSI (1.29 [1.12 to 1.47] per 0.1-unit increase; p < 0.001), as well as lower SBP (1.60 [1.24 to 2.05] per 10-mmHg decrease; p < 0.001) and MBP (2.00 [1.32 to 3.03] per 10-mmHg decrease; p = 0.001); in contrast, HR and DBP did not show a significant association with 30-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier analyses confirmed poorer survival across ROC-derived post-CPB thresholds for HR, SBP, MBP, SI, and MSI (all log-rank p ≤ 0.013). Conclusions: Post-CPB SBP, MBP, SI, and MSI showed significant adjusted associations with 30-day mortality and may assist in early postoperative risk stratification. These exploratory findings require external validation, and the identified thresholds should not be interpreted as treatment targets.

Title: Experiences in the Management of Type A Aortic Dissection Following Cardiovascular Interventions: A Case Series Report.
Abstract: Background: Cardiovascular interventions such as transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) have become standard options for high-risk patients with valvular heart disease. However, iatrogenic type A aortic dissection (AAD) remains a rare but life-threatening complication, and its optimal management is controversial. Case presentation: We present four patients who developed AAD following cardiovascular interventions at our institution between 2020 and 2024, including three after TAVR and one after TEER. Three patients underwent the Bentall procedure (each requiring removal of the pre-existing transcatheter valve, and one with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting), and one underwent aortic sinus repair with ascending aorta and total arch replacement using a frozen elephant trunk, together with removal of the previously implanted TEER clip and mitral valve replacement. One patient recovered and was discharged home, another was transferred back to the cardiology department and was discharged home with no sequelae, and two left the hospital against medical advice while still in critical condition, both of whom subsequently died-one 2 days after discharge and the other immediately upon arriving home. Conclusions: Our experience indicates that patients with cardiovascular intervention-related AAD are at particularly high risk owing to pre-existing cardiac dysfunction and deterioration of other organ functions. In such patients, emergency surgical rescue can be life-saving, and the Bentall procedure proved feasible in this selected cohort; however, surgery in this setting is more complex than in routine cases. Careful evaluation, individualized surgical planning, and meticulous perioperative management are essential to improve outcomes.

Title: Outcomes in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Results from a Single Center in Romania.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Real-world data on pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) in Romania are scarce. This study evaluated the clinical characteristics, long-term survival patterns and the prognostic utility of baseline variables in a Romanian PAH cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult patients treated for PAH at a single expert center between 2007 and 2026. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and univariable Cox proportional-hazard regression models. Univariable and multivariable linear regressions were used to identify drivers of baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Results: The primary analysis cohort included 75 patients (mean age 53 ± 15 years, 71% female). Overall transplant-free survival was unexpectedly high at 97.2%, 80.8%, and 66.7% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The European Society of Cardiology (ESC)/European Respiratory Society (ERS) 3-strata risk score did not stratify survival (log-rank p = 0.9). Significant predictors of adverse outcomes in univariable analysis included six-minute walking distance (6MWD), PAH etiology and baseline coronary artery disease. In univariable analysis, lower baseline eGFR was associated with age, hypertension and diabetes mellitus, but not with pulmonary hemodynamics or transplant-free survival. Conclusions: In this regional PAH cohort, survival rates were high, likely reflecting survivor bias stemming from delayed access to care. Adverse outcomes were associated with PAH etiology and 6MWD, but the limited number of events precluded multivariable analysis.

Title: Decreased Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor, Increased FK506 Binding Protein 5 and Female Sex Are Associated with Multiscale-Assessed Depressive Symptoms During Heart Failure Decompensation: A Polish Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) may be accompanied by depressive symptoms. Risk factors for a screening diagnosis of depression (SDD) in ADHF are poorly understood. Methods: We enrolled 51 patients with a median age 67 years hospitalized due to ADHF. SDD was determined by the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) with >12 points or by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) with >11 points. Severe depressive symptoms were diagnosed based on a Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) score of >17 points. Baseline neurotrophic potential and stress response were assessed by plasma brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and FK506 binding protein 5 (FKBP5), respectively. Results: SDD was identified in 20 (39.2%) patients based on the BDI, in 13 (25.5%) based on the PHQ-9, while severe depressive symptoms according to the HDRS were found in 15 (29.4%) patients. Women had higher BDI (p = 0.044), PHQ-9 (p = 0.022) and HDRS (p = 0.006) scores than men. The BDI score correlated with plasma FKBP5 (r = 0.317, p = 0.025) and inversely with BDNF (r = -0.380, p = 0.006). In multivariable analysis, a higher BDI score was associated with female sex (β = 0.294, p = 0.033) and lower plasma BDNF (β = -0.330, p = 0.015), while a higher HDRS score was associated with female sex (β = 0.312, p = 0.010) and higher plasma FKBP5 (β = 0.388, p = 0.007). Conclusions: In a multi-scale assessment, SDD or severe depressive symptoms were identified in 25-40% of ADHF patients. A higher BDI score was independently associated with lower BDNF, whereas a higher HDRS score was associated with female sex and higher FKBP5.

Title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Pulmonary Embolism: Prevalence, Severity and the Association of Sleep-Disordered Breathing with Thromboembolic Disease.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and pulmonary embolism (PE) share several risk factors, while emerging evidence suggests a potential pathophysiological link beyond these common determinants. We aimed to characterize the prevalence and severity of OSA in patients with acute PE and to investigate whether the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) is independently associated with PE and its clinical course. Methods: In this prospective, single-center, case-control study, 128 consecutive patients with acute PE and 252 outpatient controls with other respiratory diseases underwent home respiratory polygraphy. In patients with PE, the sleep study was performed at least three months after the acute event. OSA was diagnosed and graded according to international consensus criteria. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between AHI and PE, acute PE severity, chronic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) recurrence. Results: OSA was present in 55.5% of patients with PE, with severe OSA in 28.9%, compared with 42.1% and 13.9%, respectively, among controls (p = 0.013 and p = 0.001). Patients with PE had a higher AHI (21.21 ± 19.29 vs. 14.81 ± 14.26 events/h; p = 0.007) and oxygen desaturation index (19.86 ± 18.77 vs. 13.30 ± 13.79; p = 0.003). Each 10-events/h increase in AHI was independently associated with PE after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and established VTE risk factors (OR 1.205, 95% CI 1.019-1.426; p = 0.029). AHI was not independently associated with intermediate-high/high-risk PE or chronic DVT. Among patients who discontinued anticoagulation, VTE recurrence was higher in those with OSA (36.0% vs. 13.3%; p = 0.049). Conclusions: OSA is highly prevalent and frequently severe in patients with acute PE. Increasing AHI is independently associated with the presence of PE, supporting a clinically relevant association between sleep-disordered breathing and thromboembolic disease. Because OSA was not systematically reassessed after documented resolution of PE, persistence of OSA independently of residual thromboembolic disease cannot be definitively established. Whether the observed association between OSA and recurrent VTE after anticoagulation withdrawal is confirmed in larger prospective studies remains to be determined.

Title: Early Cardiac Biomarkers for the Detection of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity is a serious complication in breast cancer treatment, particularly with anthracyclines and HER2-targeted therapy. To evaluate the association between early elevations of cardiac markers (troponin and NT-proBNP) and the development of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in adult patients with breast cancer. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261301170). A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted. Studies evaluating cardiac markers in breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy were included in the review. Results: Fourteen studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Five studies were included in the meta-analysis. Elevated troponin levels were associated with higher odds of subsequent cardiac dysfunction; however, the pooled association was not statistically significant [OR = 3.40, 95% CI 0.69-16.67, p = 0.13] and showed substantial heterogeneity [I2 = 86.97%]. A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis was used to identify a study that exerted a substantial influence; its exclusion eliminated between-group heterogeneity and attenuated the pooled effect estimate. Conclusions: Early troponin elevation may provide a biological signal of myocardial injury during cancer therapy. However, the association between elevated troponin level and cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction did not reach the threshold of statistical significance and showed substantial heterogeneity. Troponin and NT-proBNP may provide complementary information to cardiac imaging, but their predictive performance and clinical utility require further prospective validation.

Title: Diverging Trends in Treated In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Intensive Care Units and General Wards Using Location-Specific Patient-Days.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Hospital-level incidence estimates may obscure differences between intensive care units (ICUs) and general wards. We compared temporal trends in treated adult in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) using location-specific patient-days. Methods: This retrospective study covered January 2016 to June 2026 at a South Korean teaching hospital. Monthly treated IHCA counts were modeled using negative binomial regression with patient-days as an offset, a setting × time interaction, and adjustment for the COVID-19 period and seasonality. Calendar-month score-based HAC analyses assessed robustness to serial correlation. January-March 2022 was excluded because arrest location was unavailable. Results: The incidence cohort comprised 1712 events: 1373 in ICUs and 339 in general wards. The combined rate was 1.06 per 1000 patient-days. The setting × time interaction was significant (monthly IRR 0.9843, model-based 95% CI 0.9768-0.9918), corresponding to a 17.3% annual decrease in the ICU-to-ward rate ratio. Calendar-month score-based HAC confidence intervals also excluded 1. ICU incidence declined (monthly IRR 0.9875, 95% CI 0.9825-0.9925), whereas the general-ward model showed no statistically significant temporal trend (IRR 1.0033, 95% CI 0.9975-1.0090; p = 0.263). Conclusions: Location-specific patient-day denominators identified different temporal trajectories in treated IHCA. These findings describe observed treated events and do not establish changes in underlying arrest risk or resuscitation performance.

Title: Rapidly Reversible Monitored Anesthesia Care with Remimazolam and Flumazenil Reversal for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) is increasingly used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), where rapid recovery of consciousness may facilitate early postoperative neurological assessment. Remimazolam provides sedation that can be pharmacologically reversed with flumazenil. We compared emergence from sedation between a remimazolam-flumazenil-based MAC strategy and a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy in patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR. Methods: In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 84 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR were randomized 1:1 to remimazolam-remifentanil (R group) or dexmedetomidine-propofol-remifentanil (D group) MAC. Flumazenil was administered at the initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt in the R group. The primary outcome was arousal time, assessed using two prespecified measures: time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal and time from initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt to arousal. Arousal was defined as a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score of 5. Results: Eighty-three patients were included in the analysis (R group, n = 42; D group, n = 41). The time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal was shorter in the R group than in the D group (19.05 [15.77-23.59] vs. 24.09 [19.25-34.78] min; p = 0.0045). The time from initiation of the awakening attempt to arousal was also shorter (0.60 [0.33-1.00] vs. 1.00 [0-4.72] min; p = 0.0117). No patient in the R group required rescue propofol. No significant between-group differences were observed in major procedural or postoperative outcomes. Conclusions: A remimazolam-based MAC strategy with flumazenil reversal provided faster and more reliable emergence from sedation than a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy during transfemoral TAVR. These findings suggest that a reversible sedation strategy may facilitate rapid recovery of consciousness when early postoperative assessment is desired, although its impact on neurological or other clinical outcomes remains to be established.

Title: In-Hospital Outcomes According to Treatment Strategy in NSTEMI Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: No Index Revascularization, PCI, or CABG?
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Real-world data comparing treatment strategies and in-hospital outcomes across no index revascularization, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in NSTEMI patients remain limited. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 1906 NSTEMI patients undergoing coronary angiography were categorized into no index revascularization (n = 946), PCI (n = 709), or CABG (n = 251) groups. The primary endpoint was in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, cardiac arrest requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation, sustained ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation, dialysis-requiring acute kidney injury, or stroke. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with chained equations (MICE), and propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used as a sensitivity analysis. Results: In-hospital MACE was higher in the no index revascularization group than in the PCI and CABG groups (9.8% vs. 3.5% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001). Patients managed with no index revascularization were older and had a greater comorbidity burden, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, and more frequent Killip class ≥ 2. In the primary multivariable model, chronic kidney disease, Killip class ≥ 2, lower LVEF, CRP, and male sex were associated with in-hospital MACE, whereas neither PCI nor CABG strategy was independently associated with MACE. IPTW sensitivity analyses yielded similar directions of association; however, the PCI estimate crossed the conventional significance threshold after 1st-99th percentile weight truncation. Conclusions: Patients managed with no index revascularization had a higher baseline risk profile and higher unadjusted in-hospital MACE and mortality. The observed between-group differences should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects of treatment strategy because of substantial confounding by indication.

Title: Association of Platelet-Albumin-Bilirubin and Albumin-Bilirubin Scores with Angiographic No-Reflow in Patients with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary PCI.
Abstract: Background: The platelet-albumin-bilirubin (PALBI) and albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) scores integrate routinely available laboratory parameters with potential relevance to microvascular injury. We investigated their associations with angiographic no-reflow and incremental predictive value in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 1539 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. No-reflow was defined by final TIMI flow < 3 and/or myocardial blush grade 0-1 in the absence of a mechanical cause. Associations of PALBI and ALBI with no-reflow were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration, reclassification, internal bootstrap validation, and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed. Results: No-reflow occurred in 146 patients (9.5%). Both PALBI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] per 0.1-point increase, 1.315; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.228-1.408; p < 0.001) and ALBI (aOR, 1.165; 95% CI, 1.115-1.218; p < 0.001) were independently associated with no-reflow. PALBI showed greater discrimination than ALBI (AUC, 0.722 vs. 0.681; DeLong p = 0.018). Adding PALBI to the clinical model increased the AUC from 0.688 to 0.785 (ΔAUC = 0.098; p = 0.001), with significant NRI (0.777) and IDI (0.102), and improved the Brier score from 0.083 to 0.073. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.762. PALBI demonstrated a non-linear association with no-reflow (p for non-linearity <0.001), whereas ALBI showed a predominantly linear association. Conclusions: Higher PALBI and ALBI scores were independently associated with angiographic no-reflow after primary PCI in STEMI. PALBI demonstrated stronger discrimination and incremental predictive performance; however, external validation and prospective evaluation are required to determine its potential clinical utility.

Title: CT-Derived Adipose Tissue Biomarkers in Coronary and Carotid Atherosclerosis: A Systematic Review of Dual-Energy, Spectral, and Photon-Counting CT.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Advanced Computed Tomography (CT) enables multiparametric characterization of local perivascular and regional or systemic adipose tissue, potentially providing markers of vascular inflammation and cardiometabolic remodeling beyond conventional assessment of the vessel lumen and plaque. However, evidence remains fragmented across CT technologies, adipose depots and vascular territories. This systematic review evaluated human studies of adipose-tissue biomarkers derived from dual-layer spectral-detector CT (DLSCT), dual-source dual-energy CT (DS-DECT), rapid kVp-switching dual-energy CT (rsDECT), and photon-counting CT (PCCT) in coronary and carotid atherosclerosis. Methods: PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched for English-language human studies published from 1 January 2020, to 13 September 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching of eligible studies and reference-list screening of relevant reviews. Two reviewers independently performed study selection and risk-of-bias assessment. Because of clinical, technical, and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis. Results: Nineteen reports representing 15 likely independent study clusters met the inclusion criteria. DLSCT-derived pericoronary adipose-tissue attenuation; DECT-derived carotid perivascular adipose-tissue parameters; PCCT-derived adipose attenuation, volume, and radiomic features; and spectral measures of hepatic or visceral adiposity were associated with coronary artery disease, stenosis severity, high-risk plaque features, coronary calcification, or symptomatic carotid disease. Reported discrimination estimates were heterogeneous across populations, endpoints, and model structures and were predominantly derived from unvalidated development samples. Conclusions: Advanced CT-derived adipose-tissue biomarkers may complement conventional assessment of the vessel lumen and plaque by characterizing local vessel-adipose interactions and systemic cardiometabolic phenotype. However, current measurements are protocol- and platform-dependent, and clinical utility has not been established. Standardized measurement pipelines, biological validation, and prospective multicenter studies are required before routine clinical implementation.

Title: Early Changes in Spleen Stiffness After Endoscopic Treatment Are Associated with Esophageal Variceal Recurrence: A Pilot Study.
Abstract: Background: Spleen stiffness (SS) is a noninvasive marker of portal hypertension; however, the clinical significance of early changes in SS after endoscopic treatment for esophageal varices remains unclear. We evaluated whether SS and its early post-treatment changes are associated with variceal recurrence. Methods: This retrospective pilot study included 20 patients who underwent endoscopic treatment for esophageal varices. Liver stiffness (LS) and spleen stiffness (SS) were measured before treatment, approximately 1 week after the final treatment session (1W), and at 1 month and 1 year after treatment. The clinical outcome of interest was variceal recurrence within 1 year. Early changes in stiffness were calculated from 1W to 1M (Δ1M - 1W). Results: Eleven patients (55.0%) developed variceal recurrence. LS did not differ significantly between the non-recurrence and recurrence groups at any time point during follow-up. SS was comparable between the groups before treatment and at 1W but was significantly higher in the recurrence group at 1M (median [IQR], 2.75 [2.70-2.86] vs. 3.40 [3.06-3.81] m/s in the non-recurrence and recurrence groups, respectively; p = 0.003). ΔSS-VTQ (1M - 1W) was significantly greater in the recurrence group than in the non-recurrence group (-0.13 [-0.62--0.04] vs. 0.25 [-0.05-0.40] m/s, respectively; p = 0.013), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed in changes in LS. Conclusions: SS at 1 month after endoscopic treatment and its early post-treatment change were associated with variceal recurrence. Serial assessment of SS may provide useful information for early post-treatment risk assessment, although validation in larger prospective studies is needed.

Title: Comparison of Treatment Zone Decentration Between VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800 Keratorefractive Lenticule Extraction Using Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: To compare treatment-zone decentration after small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) performed with VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800 using corneal thickness difference maps derived from anterior segment optical coherence tomography. Methods: This retrospective comparative study included 44 eyes of 22 participants who underwent SMILE with VISUMAX 500 or VISUMAX 800 by a single surgeon and had preoperative and 3-month postoperative CASIA2 examinations. Treatment-zone centers were primarily identified manually relative to the corneal vertex. Between-platform differences were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE) accounting for inter-eye correlation, with additional adjustment for preoperative cylinder. Participant-level analyses and semi-automated radial color-symmetry localization were performed as sensitivity analyses. Results: Twenty-two eyes of 11 participants were included in each group. Mean radial decentration was 0.219 ± 0.134 mm with VISUMAX 500 and 0.225 ± 0.171 mm with VISUMAX 800. The mean between-group difference was 0.006 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.074 to 0.085; p = 0.890), and remained similar after adjustment for preoperative cylinder (0.006 mm; 95% CI, -0.082 to 0.094; p = 0.888). Participant-level analysis likewise showed no evidence of a between-group difference (mean difference, 0.0056 mm; 95% CI, -0.083 to 0.094; exact permutation p = 0.907). Reanalysis using semi-automated localization yielded a similarly small between-platform difference (0.0114 mm; 95% CI, -0.063 to 0.086; p = 0.763). Conclusions: In this small single-surgeon cohort, treatment-zone decentration did not differ significantly between VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800. The findings were consistent across participant-level and semi-automated sensitivity analyses. Because the study was not designed as an equivalence or noninferiority trial, these results should be interpreted as an absence of evidence for a between-platform difference rather than evidence of equivalent centration performance.

Title: Distinct Cross-Vascular Association Patterns of Carotid Plaque Burden and Vulnerability Features with Coronary Atherosclerotic Burden in Patients Undergoing Carotid Revascularization.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the associations between preoperative carotid high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (HR-MRI) plaque features and coronary atherosclerotic burden, and to compare the cross-vascular association patterns of plaque burden-related measures and individual vulnerable plaque features. Methods: This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent carotid revascularization and had both preoperative carotid HR-MRI and coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) between April 2017 and December 2024. Carotid plaque characteristics included calcification, lipid-rich necrotic core (LRNC), intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH), loose matrix (LM), ulceration, maximum wall thickness (MWT), maximum wall area (MWA), and normalized wall index (NWI). Coronary atherosclerotic burden was characterized using coronary artery calcium score (CACS), maximum luminal stenosis, and the number of diseased coronary arteries; the number of coronary arteries with ≥50% stenosis was additionally recorded. Associations between carotid plaque characteristics and coronary atherosclerotic burden were evaluated using correlation analyses and multivariable logistic regression. Results: A total of 162 patients were included (mean age, 66.11 ± 7.54 years; 138 [85.2%] men). CACS ≥ 400 was present in 76 patients (46.9%), obstructive coronary disease (≥50% stenosis in at least one coronary artery) in 96 patients (59.3%), and involvement of ≥3 diseased coronary arteries in 128 patients (79.0%). Greater coronary atherosclerotic burden was consistently associated with higher carotid calcification volume and MWT and NWI (all p < 0.05). After adjustment for clinical risk factors and correction for multiple testing, calcification volume, MWT and NWI remained associated with CACS ≥ 400, obstructive coronary disease, and involvement of ≥3 diseased coronary arteries. In contrast, individual vulnerable plaque features, including LRNC, IPH, LM, and ulceration, showed weaker and less consistent associations. Conclusions: In patients undergoing carotid revascularization, preoperative carotid HR-MRI-derived plaque burden-related features showed more consistent associations with coronary atherosclerotic burden than individual vulnerable plaque features. These findings suggest that plaque burden-related and vulnerable plaque features may reflect different aspects of atherosclerosis, with plaque burden-related measures more closely reflecting cumulative systemic atherosclerotic involvement and vulnerable plaque features primarily characterizing local plaque composition and instability.

Title: Prioritizing Emergency Medical Conditions for Health Policy Using a Stepwise Treatable-Death Framework: A Nationwide Analysis in Korea, 2018-2022.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Limited emergency-care resources require priorities based not only on mortality rates or death counts but also on the potential mortality reduction under explicit targets. We applied the age- and sex-standardized domestic short- and mid-term components of a stepwise treatable-death framework across severe emergency conditions in Korea. Methods: This retrospective nationwide study used NEDIS aggregate data from 16 regions during 2018-2022. The 20 conditions with the highest numbers of in-hospital deaths were represented as 17 groups by replacing sepsis (A41), bacterial pneumonia (J15), pneumonia of unspecified organism (J18), and pneumonitis due to solids and liquids (J69) with an extended-sepsis composite. Treatable deaths were the positive difference between observed and target-based expected deaths. National rates in 10-year age-group and sex strata were applied to regional distributions. The short-term target assumed that regions with an age- and sex-standardized mortality ratio (SMR) above 1.0 achieved the national reference level (SMR = 1.0), whereas the mid-term target assumed that all regions achieved the lowest regional SMR for the corresponding condition and year. Five-year cumulative estimates were the primary outcome measure. Results: Across the 17 groups, summed condition-level patient counts totaled 3,384,529 and in-hospital deaths totaled 357,404 (ratio of summed death counts to summed patient counts, 10.56%). Five-year cumulative short-term estimates were highest for extended sepsis (2387), bronchus and lung cancer (1984), and cardiac arrest (1662). Mid-term estimates were highest for cardiac arrest (21,547), extended sepsis (19,340), and severe trauma (7010). Conclusions: After accounting for regional differences in age and sex distributions, extended sepsis remained the condition with the largest short-term and the second-largest mid-term treatable-death burden, supporting its consideration for further policy-priority evaluation. Each treatable-death estimate is an operational policy-scenario estimate rather than an estimate of causally preventable mortality.

Title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

Title: Anterior Scleral Thickness in Young Saudi Adults Measured Using Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography: Sex- and Quadrant-Specific Variations.
Abstract: Purpose: To report baseline anterior scleral thickness (AST) values and evaluate regional and sex-related variation in healthy young Saudi adults using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT). Methods: A prospective, cross-sectional study included 55 healthy Saudi adults aged 18-40 years. Participants underwent comprehensive ocular examinations to exclude pathology or significant refractive errors. AST was measured using IMAGEnet 6 software in superior, inferior, nasal, and temporal quadrants at 0 mm, 1 mm, and 2 mm from the scleral spur using the anterior segment module of swept-source OCT. Regional and sex-related differences were evaluated using a linear mixed-effects model adjusted for age and spherical equivalent. Short-term within-session intra-observer test-retest repeatability across repeated B-scan acquisitions was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients, within-subject coefficients of variation, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results: The mean age of participants was 23.56 ± 4.61 years (34 males, 21 females). AST varied significantly according to distance and anatomical quadrant (both p < 0.001), with significant distance-by-quadrant (p < 0.001) and sex-by-distance-by-quadrant interactions (p = 0.010). The inferior quadrant generally showed greater thickness, while the superior quadrant showed lower values. Bonferroni-adjusted location-specific comparisons showed greater AST in males in the superior and temporal quadrants at both 1 mm and 2 mm from the scleral spur, whereas the remaining sex comparisons were not statistically significant. Neither age nor spherical equivalent showed a significant independent association with AST. Intra-observer ICC values ranged from 0.872 to 0.939. Conclusions: AST in young Saudi adults varies according to anatomical quadrant and distance from the scleral spur, with sex-related differences showing location-dependent patterns. These findings provide descriptive baseline data for anterior scleral morphology in this population.

Title: Association Between Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography and Carotid Artery Stenosis on CT Angiography: A Retrospective Study in a Selected Cohort of Women Aged 60-65 Years.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is an incidental mammographic finding that may be associated with systemic vascular disease. We investigated the association between mammographic BAC and carotid artery stenosis on cervical computed tomography angiography (CTA) in a clinically selected cohort of postmenopausal women aged 60-65 years. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study screened 3421 women aged 60-65 years who underwent both mammography and cervical CTA between November 2021 and May 2025. CTA examinations requested from the emergency department or cardiology clinics, examinations not performed within the same calendar year, and prespecified clinical exclusions were removed, leaving 180 women who underwent outpatient CTA for nonspecific symptoms. The median interval between examinations was 131 days. BAC was graded on a 0-3 scale, and carotid stenosis was assessed according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) criteria, using the greater degree of stenosis on either side as the patient-level value. BAC was analyzed as an ordinal variable, as a categorical variable, and using binary definitions of presence and severity. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and smoking. Results: Clinically significant stenosis (≥50%) was present in 44 women (24.4%). Its prevalence increased from 5.4% in BAC grade 0 to 75.0% in grade 3 (p for trend < 0.001). Each one-grade increase in BAC was associated with clinically significant stenosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-8.03; p < 0.001). The corresponding aORs were 16.70 (95% CI, 4.99-73.27) for any BAC and 18.49 (95% CI, 5.93-70.46) for BAC grade ≥2. Adding BAC to the clinical model increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.90 to 0.96 (DeLong p = 0.005); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.95. Inter-reader agreement for BAC grading was substantial (weighted κ = 0.79). Conclusions: In this selected cohort of women aged 60-65 years who underwent clinically indicated CTA, BAC was associated with carotid artery stenosis independently of conventional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not establish BAC as a screening or prediction tool and require prospective, population-based validation.

Title: A Simplified Physiology-Laboratory Score (PLS4) for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Cholangitis.
Abstract: Objectives: Acute cholangitis is a common biliary infection in the emergency department (ED) that can progress rapidly to septic shock and multiorgan dysfunction. The Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG2018) is the current reference standard for severity assessment but may be cumbersome during the initial ED encounter. We aimed to develop a simplified physiology-laboratory score (PLS4) computable from four routine bedside variables and to compare its early risk-stratification performance with TG2018. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included 482 adult patients with acute cholangitis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code K83.0) presenting to a tertiary university hospital ED between January 2016 and December 2021. Primary outcomes were ICU admission, vasopressor use, and prolonged hospital stay (length of stay ≥ 14 days); intubation was analyzed as an exploratory outcome. PLS4 assigned 1 point each for albumin < 3.5 g/dL, systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mmHg, heart rate ≥ 100/min, and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio ≥ 1.2 (range 0-4). Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curves, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and bootstrap optimism-corrected internal validation. Results: ICU admission occurred in 81 patients (16.8%), vasopressor use in 53 (11.0%), and prolonged stay in 111 (23.0%). The areas under the curve (AUCs) for ICU admission were 0.850 for TG2018 and 0.800 for PLS4 (p = 0.116), and the optimism-corrected AUC of PLS4 was 0.779. For vasopressor use, which is part of the TG2018 grade III definition, the AUCs were 0.936 and 0.843. When PLS4 was added to TG2018, the AUC for ICU admission increased to 0.886. At PLS4 ≥ 3, specificity reached 0.978 for ICU admission and 0.970 for vasopressor use, with event rates rising stepwise from 5.96% to 100% and 2.55% to 90.0%, respectively. Conclusions: In this single-center derivation study, PLS4 showed high specificity and added prognostic information to TG2018. It should be validated in other centers before clinical use.

Title: MicraAV Versus Dual-Chamber Transvenous Pacemakers in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A 12-Month Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Background: Data directly comparing the atrioventricular (AV)-synchronous leadless pacemaker (MicraAV) with a dual-chamber transvenous pacemaker (DDD) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remain limited. Methods: We retrospectively studied patients undergoing pacemaker implantation for advanced or complete AV block within one month after TAVR at a single Japanese center between 2016 and 2025. After exclusions, the primary cohort comprised 74 patients (MicraAV, n = 29; DDD, n = 45). Clinical outcomes were assessed through 12 months, with death treated as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes. Device and echocardiographic parameters were evaluated longitudinally. Results: MicraAV recipients were less frequently female than DDD recipients (48.3% vs. 75.6%, p = 0.025). In the MicraAV and DDD groups, respectively, all-cause mortality was 6.9% and 6.7% (unadjusted HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.19-6.68; p = 0.904), heart failure rehospitalization occurred in 17.2% and 4.4% (subdistribution HR, 4.44; 95% CI, 0.86-22.92; p = 0.075), and device-related complications occurred in 6.9% and 4.4% (subdistribution HR, 1.60; 95% CI, 0.23-11.40; p = 0.636). The median MicraAV tracking index was 88.4% [IQR, 66.4-95.1]. No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for device electrical performance or echocardiographic left ventricular parameters. Tricuspid regurgitation worsened over time in the MicraAV group. Conclusions: All-cause mortality and device-related complications were infrequent in both groups, whereas heart failure rehospitalization occurred more frequently in the MicraAV group. Given the small number of events and wide confidence intervals, these findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in larger contemporary cohorts.

Title: Prognostic Implication of a CT-FFR-Based Functional SYNTAX Score in Coronary Artery Disease Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Abstract: Background: This study aims to investigate the value of a SYNTAX score (SS) based on coronary computed tomographic angiography (cCTA)-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), termed "Functional SYNTAX score" (FSSCTA), to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This cohort study included 876 patients who underwent cCTA and underwent PCI within 30 days during 2016-2020. CT-FFR was calculated by a machine learning algorithm. All 876 patients were divided into a low-risk group (≤22) and an intermediate-to-high-risk group (>22) with cCTA-based SS (SSCTA) as the control.
