As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (P for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2300075711 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

Title: Baroreceptor Dysregulation Mediated via Neurohormonal Mechanisms in Heart Failure and its Influence on Renal Function: Potential Role of Baroreflex Activation Therapy.
Abstract: Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT), which electrically stimulates carotid sinus baroreceptors to modulate autonomic tone, has emerged as a novel adjunct to guideline-directed medical therapy for resistant hypertension and heart failure. Beyond its established cardiovascular benefits, emerging preclinical and early-phase clinical data suggest that BAT may favorably influence renal function and cardiorenal interactions. By suppressing sympathetic nervous system activity and downregulating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, BAT improves renal hemodynamics and may counteract key mechanisms leading to diuretic resistance. The latter represents a common and clinically significant challenge in patients with advanced heart failure, in whom impaired renal perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and tubular remodeling all contribute to reduced diuretic responsiveness and worsening kidney function. Early evidence indicates that BAT may preserve glomerular filtration rate, reduce proteinuria and improve urinary sodium excretion, suggesting potential renoprotective effects and a therapeutic role in mitigating diuretic resistance. However, these findings remain limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and heterogenous study populations across diverse clinical settings. This review synthesizes key physiologic mechanisms linking baroreflex signal modulation to renal outcomes and evaluates available clinical data. While BAT offers established cardiovascular benefits in heart failure, its renoprotective and diuretic-sparing potential remains investigational and lacks validation from randomized clinical trials. Dedicated prospective large-scale randomized studies are essential to establish long-term renal efficacy across the cardiorenal disease spectrum.

Title: Aortic Arch Morphology Influences Procedural Complexity During Diagnostic Coronary Angiography: Development of a CTA-Informed Procedural Complexity Index.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Procedural complexity during diagnostic coronary angiography varies considerably and may result in prolonged fluoroscopy exposure and increased contrast utilization. Although vascular access route and operator experience are recognized contributors, the influence of proximal vascular anatomy remains less clearly defined. This study evaluated the association between aortic arch branching morphology and procedural complexity and explored the development of a CTA-informed procedural complexity index.
AIM: To assess the procedural impact of aortic arch branching morphology during diagnostic coronary angiography.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 250 consecutive adult patients undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography who had preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the thoracic aorta available for evaluation. Aortic arch branching patterns were classified into four configurations (Types A-D) using axial images, multiplanar reconstructions, and three-dimensional CTA analysis. Procedural measures included fluoroscopy time, contrast volume, procedure duration, vascular access route, and access-site crossover. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess predictors of fluoroscopy time, while a separate multivariable logistic regression model for prolonged fluoroscopy was used to derive a weighted CTA-informed procedural complexity index. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, with internal validation by 10-fold cross-validation.
RESULTS: Variant aortic arch morphology was identified in 55 patients (22.0%). Patients with variant configurations had longer fluoroscopy times than those with classical Type A anatomy (7.4 ± 2.6 vs 5.9 ± 2.1 minutes; P = 0.002), greater contrast utilization (88 ± 25 vs 78 ± 21 mL; P = 0.01), and longer procedure duration (26 ± 10 vs 22 ± 8 minutes; P = 0.02). Variant arch morphology remained independently associated with longer fluoroscopy time (β = +1.3 minutes; P = 0.003). The derived procedural complexity index demonstrated an apparent area under the curve of 0.72 (95% CI, 0.64-0.80), with a 10-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.68.
CONCLUSION: CTA-defined aortic arch morphology was associated with procedural complexity during diagnostic coronary angiography. The proposed CTA-informed procedural complexity index demonstrated modest discriminatory performance and may provide additional information regarding anticipated procedural difficulty. The index should be considered exploratory and requires prospective external validation before clinical implementation.

Title: Predictive Performance of POSPOM and EuroSCORE-II for Perioperative Mortality in Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simpler generalized scores such as POSPOM (PreOperative Score to Predict Post-Operative Mortality) may appear attractive because they can be derived from routinely available variables and applied across surgical specialties, although their reliability in cardiac surgery remains uncertain.
AIM: To compare the performance of POSPOM and EuroSCORE-II scores for predicting in-hospital mortality among patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary university cardiac surgery center. A total of 320 adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, valve surgery, or combined procedures between 2021 and 2024 were included. Discrimination was assessed using ROC and precision-recall curves with DeLong's test. Calibration was evaluated using calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow testing, and GiViTI calibration belts. Agreement was analyzed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC), Bland- Altman plots, and Passing-Bablok and Deming regression.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 7.5% (24/320). POSPOM showed poorer discrimination than EuroSCORE-II (AUC 0.611 vs. 0.745; P = 0.012) and lower PR-AUC (0.115 vs. 0.287). Both models showed imperfect calibration, and agreement between scores was weak (ICC 0.283), with systematic differences observed between predicted mortality estimates. Exploratory segmented regression suggested that inter-model divergence increased with age, with an estimated breakpoint near 59 years. POSPOM did not improve reclassification (continuous NRI -0.31), and decision curve analysis favored EuroSCORE-II.
CONCLUSION: POSPOM showed poorer predictive performance than EuroSCORE-II for in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously in light of the limited number of mortality events, retrospective reconstruction of POSPOM, and the need for external validation.

Title: Efficacy of Oral Chinese Medicine in Regulating the Intestinal Flora of Patients with Chronic Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and routine therapy can improve the clinical efficacy of treating chronic heart failure, reduce side effects, and improve cardiac function.
AIM: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of oral Chinese medicine containing danshen and rhubarb components in combination with conventional western drugs in the treatment of chronic heart failure.
METHODS: This meta-analysis was registered with registration number: INPLASY202610010. PubMed, Embase, The Cochrane Library, Web of Science, China Biomedical Literature Database (CBM), China Journal Full Text Database (CNKI), Wanfang Database, and Wipu Database were searched by computer, while domestic and international orthopedic journals were searched manually. Clinical randomized controlled trials related to oral TCM containing danshen and rhubarb in combination with conventional Western medicines for the treatment of chronic heart failure that have been published in the public domain up to July 2024 were collected. The quality of the included literature was evaluated with reference to the evaluation criteria in the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Meta-analysis of the extracted data was performed using Review manager 5.4 software.
RESULTS: A total of 18 clinical randomized controlled trial studies were included, with a total of 1,455 patients with chronic heart failure, including 731 in the trial group and 724 in the control group. The combination of oral Chinese medicine and conventional treatment had a better effective rate of cardiac function improvement than conventional Western medicine treatment alone. There was better improvement in terms of 6-minute walk test distance.
CONCLUSION: Oral preparations containing danshen and rhubarb components of TCM combined with conventional methods for the treatment of chronic heart failure can regulate the intestinal flora of patients.

Title: Investigational Peptides in Orthopaedic Practice: Evidence, Safety, and Patient Counseling for BPC-157, Thymosin Beta-4, and TB-500.
Journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
Abstract: Peptide-based products, particularly Body Protection Compound-157 (BPC-157), and thymosin beta-4 (TB-4), and products marketed as TB-500, are increasingly promoted for musculoskeletal recovery despite limited clinical validation. This narrative review evaluated their molecular rationale, direct musculoskeletal evidence, human safety and efficacy data, product quality concerns, regulatory status, antidoping implications, and relevance to orthopaedic counseling. PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus were searched from inception through June 2026, with additional review of primary regulatory and antidoping sources. BPC-157 has the largest bod of direct musculoskeletal preclinical evidence, including predominantly small-animal studies involving tendon, ligament, muscle, inflammatory joint disease, and bone. However, human musculoskeletal evidence is limited to one small retrospective uncontrolled case series without validated outcome measures. Validated dosing, pharmacokinetic, and long-term safety data are lacking. TB-4 has broader experimental and human experience in ophthalmic, dermatologic, and cardiovascular applications, but direct musculoskeletal evidence remains limited to in vitro and rodent studies. These nonorthopaedic findings cannot establish musculoskeletal efficacy or safety. TB-500 is a distinct seven amino-acid fragment of TB-4 that is frequently conflated with full-length TB-4 despite the absence of validated biologic or clinical equivalence. Commercial products marketed also raise concerns regarding identity, purity, concentration, sterility, and manufacturing consistency. None of these agents has an FDA-approved musculoskeletal indication, validated orthopaedic treatment protocol, or controlled human orthopaedic efficacy evidence. Orthopaedic clinicians should specifically ask about peptide use, distinguish preclinical plausibility from clinical validation, address product quality and safety uncertainties, and counsel athletes regarding antidoping restrictions. Routine clinical use cannot be currently recommended.

Title: Quality of life in elderly patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery: The role of inflammation, nutrition and functional status.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective descriptive correlational study aimed to examine inflammation, changes in functional status, nutritional status, and quality of life in older adults undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The study sample consisted of 120 conscious and voluntary patients aged 65 years and older who underwent on-pump CABG surgery between February 2017 and January 2018 at the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery of a Ege University Medical Faculty Hospital. Data were collected at hospital admission and at the eighth postoperative week through face-to-face interviews. Data collection included sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers, functional status, nutritional status, and quality of life. Data were analyzed using SPSS for Windows, version 23.0.
RESULTS: At the eighth postoperative week, significant declines were observed in functional status, nutritional status, and physical quality of life compared with the preoperative period (p<0.05). Significant differences were also found in mental status scores, inflammatory markers, five times sit-to-stand test results, timed up and go test scores, handgrip strength, Katz index of activities of daily living scores, Lawton-Brody instrumental activities of daily living scores, anthropometric measurements, and mini nutritional assessment scores (p<0.05). Age was not significantly associated with functional status, nutritional status, or quality of life. Exploratory, unadjusted correlation analyses identified several low associations among inflammatory markers, functional status, nutritional status, and the physical and mental components of quality of life; none met the relevant Bonferroni-adjusted thresholds.
CONCLUSION: During the first eight weeks after CABG, older individuals in this cohort showed multidimensional postoperative changes, particularly in functional capacity, nutritional status, inflammatory profile, and quality of life. Because the study did not include a comparator group, these temporal changes should not be interpreted as effects attributable specifically to CABG. The findings indicate a need for multidisciplinary assessment and support for functional recovery, nutritional status, and overall well-being.

Title: Living alone and risk of mortality from all-cause and 15 specific causes-a nationally representative cohort study of US adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Living alone has been associated with higher mortality, but evidence for specific causes of death and potential drivers of these associations is limited. We examined associations between living alone and cause-specific mortality, and the extent to which sociodemographic and health-related characteristics explained these associations.
METHODS: This study included 598 023 US adults aged ≥18 years from the 1998-2018 National Health Interview Survey-National Death Index (follow-up through 2019). Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition quantified contributions of measured characteristics.
RESULTS: Adults living alone aged 18-64 and ≥65 years were at higher risk of mortality from all causes combined [HR18-64 = 1.22 (95% CI: 1.18-1.26); HR≥65 = 1.06 (1.03-1.08)], heart disease [HR18-64 = 1.41 (1.32-1.50); HR≥65 = 1.11 (1.06-1.15)], suicide [HR18-64 = 1.58 (1.30-1.92); HR≥65 = 2.03 (1.47-2.81)], and all injuries [HR18-64 = 1.27 (1.16-1.40); HR≥65 = 1.16 (1.02-1.32)], respectively, compared to adults living with others. Adults living alone were also at higher risk of mortality from cerebrovascular disease [HR18-64 = 1.23 (1.04-1.46)], colorectal cancer [HR18-64 = 1.27 (1.06-1.53)], diabetes [HR18-64 = 1.34 (1.15-1.57)], and accidents [HR18-64 = 1.17 (1.04-1.31)] in ages 18-64 and from hypertension [HR≥65 = 1.28 (1.07-1.53)] in ages ≥65 years. Sociodemographic and health-related characteristics explained 57.1% and 85.4% of the all-cause mortality difference by living arrangement in ages 18-64 and ≥65 years, respectively, with some variations in contributing characteristics across causes of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Individuals living alone had an increased risk of death from multiple causes, particularly in ages 18-64 years, with the highest risk for suicide in all ages. Mortality differences were largely explained by sociodemographic and health-related characteristics, highlighting targeted interventions to reduce mortality risks among those living alone.

Title: [Cold ischemia time in kidney transplantation: From reduction to personalization].
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cold ischemia time is a modifiable determinant of kidney transplant outcomes. Minimizing its duration remains a major goal, although allocation, transportation, and organizational constraints make some of this time unavoidable.
METHODS: We reviewed the literature published in PubMed over the past five years, supplemented by relevant landmark studies and institutional recommendations.
RESULTS: Prolonged cold ischemia is primarily associated with delayed graft function and, to a lesser extent, impaired long-term graft survival. Its impact varies according to donor and recipient characteristics. Prediction models can now estimate graft failure risk across different cold ischemia times for a given donor-recipient pair. Recent data on hypothermic machine perfusion further suggest that preservation strategies may mitigate the consequences of prolonged cold ischemia.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Personalizing cold ischemia could help identify situations in which its reduction should be prioritized and provide additional information for organ allocation and clinical decision-making. However, the moderate performance of currently available models and the lack of prospective validation preclude their use as standalone decision-making tools. Cold ischemia should therefore remain as short as possible, while its expected consequences could increasingly be assessed based on the characteristics of the donor-recipient pair and the graft preservation strategy used.

Title: Early Post-Operative Quantitative EEG Central Beta Power Predicts Futile Recanalization After Endovascular Treatment in AIS-LVO.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Despite successful endovascular recanalization in acute ischemic stroke, approximately 50%-55% of patients experience 90-day futile recanalization (FR). We evaluated the prognostic value of central relative beta power derived from early postoperative quantitative electroencephalography (QEEG) and explored QEEG associations with brain edema and parenchymal hemorrhage.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center subgroup analysis of the prospective multicenter DETECT2-China registry included 56 patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion. Patients underwent 20-30-min EEG recordings approximately 24 h after successful endovascular treatment. Multivariable logistic regression adjusting for seven clinical covariates, Firth and reduced-model sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) with the DeLong test were performed. An additional sensitivity analysis repeated QEEG feature selection within each training set. Feature reliability was evaluated using split-half intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs).
RESULTS: Of 56 patients, 31 (55.4%) developed 90-day FR. Higher central relative beta power was independently associated with lower odds of FR (adjusted OR: 0.28 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI: 0.11-0.74, p = 0.010). Integrating central beta power into the clinical model increased the fixed-feature LOOCV area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.557 to 0.719 (DeLong p = 0.007). In exploratory analyses, delta-band Brain Symmetry Index specifically tracked parenchymal hemorrhage (PH vs. no intracranial hemorrhage [No ICH], p = 0.006). Exploratory graph analysis also showed macro-scale network disintegration in FR patients. All QEEG features demonstrated high split-half reliability (ICC ≥ 0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: Central relative beta power recorded approximately 24 h after endovascular treatment was independently associated with 90-day FR and showed potential incremental prognostic value. Exploratory associations with postoperative complications suggest that QEEG may provide a non-invasive bedside "brain window" for neurocritical care.

Title: [Regional network for advanced heart failure in Tuscany: analysis of referrals and patient pathways for heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation (2020-2025)].
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced heart failure requires regional care pathways capable of identifying patients before clinical deterioration prevents access to heart transplantation (HTx) or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. The available data mainly describe patients who have already been selected for, or treated with, advanced therapies, whereas analyses of the entire referral are less frequent. The aim of this study was to describe referral volume, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of patients referred to the Tuscany regional center for evaluation for HTx and/or LVAD implantation in the period 2020-2025, with specific attention to temporal referral trends and distribution of INTERMACS profiles.
METHODS: Prospective observational registry including 468 consecutive adult patients referred to the regional reference center between January 2020 and December 2025. INTERMACS profile was assigned during the initial assessment. Candidacy for advanced therapies, pathway status of eligible patients, and temporal trend in INTERMACS groups 1-3, 4-5, and 6-7 were analyzed.
RESULTS: During the observation period, a significant increase in referral volume between 2020-2022 and 2023-2025 was observed (incidence rate ratio 1.46; 95% confidence interval 1.22-1.76; p<0.001). The distribution of aggregated INTERMACS profiles changed over time, with an increase in profiles 6-7 from 3.3% to 20.9% and a reduction in profiles 4-5. Overall, 340 patients (72.6%) were potentially eligible for advanced therapies. Of these, 144 patients, corresponding to 30.8% of the entire cohort, were considered candidates for HTx and/or LVAD. Of these, 123 (36.2%) were listed for HTx, including 5 patients with LVAD support as bridge to transplant. Among listed patients, 75 (61.0%) underwent transplantation, 46 (37.4%) remained on the active waiting list, and 2 (1.6%) died while on the waiting list. Twenty patients underwent LVAD implantation as destination therapy and 1 patient as bridge to candidacy (21 patients in total, corresponding to 6.2% of eligible patients) and 130 eligible patients (38.2%) remained under follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In this regional experience, the number of referrals to the reference center increased over time. The increasing representation of INTERMACS profiles 6-7, along with the reduction in profiles 4-5, is consistent with earlier patient management. These results demonstrate the consolidation of the regional network for advanced heart failure, but multicenter studies with systematic follow-up are needed to evaluate its impact on clinical outcomes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; English Abstract

Title: Quantification of Aortic Cusp Parameters Using Computed Tomography in Valve-Sparing Aortic Root Replacement Surgery: A Prospective Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Determining the feasibility of valve-sparing aortic root replacement (VSRR) requires accurate preoperative assessment of aortic valve cusp geometry. However, the reliability of computed tomography (CT) for measuring cusp parameters remains unclear. This study evaluated the agreement between CT-derived cusp measurements and intraoperative measurements and explored the potential of CT-based cusp asymmetry to predict intraoperative cusp plication.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 32 consecutive patients undergoing VSRR with the reimplantation technique were enrolled. Preoperative CT was used to measure cusp free margin length and geometric height. Agreement between CT-derived and intraoperative measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). An exploratory analysis evaluated whether CT-derived cusp asymmetry predicted the need for intraoperative cusp plication.
RESULTS: CT measurements demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length (ICC 0.80-0.87). In contrast, geometric height showed only moderate agreement (ICC 0.44-0.69). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminative ability of CT-derived cusp asymmetry for predicting intraoperative cusp plication (area under the curve, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.49-0.91), although the association did not reach statistical significance (p=0.06). Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated none-to-mild aortic insufficiency in 96.9% of patients.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative CT demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length in tricuspid valves, although the absolute limits of agreement were wide. CT-based quantification of cusp asymmetry may provide additional information for preoperative surgical planning; however, its association with intraoperative cusp plication remains exploratory and requires validation in larger studies.
CLINICAL RESEARCH INFORMATION SERVICE (CRIS) REGISTRATION NUMBER: KCT0006180.

Title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Typical Flutter Ablation: Risk-Stratified Monitoring Using Implantable Loop Recorders.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation (AF) arise from a common arrhythmogenic atrial substrate and frequently coexist in the same patient over the course of their lifetime. We aimed to examine the true incidence and risk factors associated with new-onset AF after successful typical atrial flutter ablation in a real-world population.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults who underwent atrial flutter ablation and received an implantable loop recorder (ILR) between 2019 and 2024 as part of a systematic post-ablation monitoring practice. Demographic and clinical variables were collected from the electronic medical record system. Cox proportional-hazards models and multivariable logistic regression were employed to identify independent predictors of AF, while the cumulative incidence of AF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and clinically relevant risk thresholds were subsequently derived.
RESULTS: Among 95 patients (mean age 69.5 ± 7.9 years; 77.9% male; mean CHA2DS2-VASc 3.3) followed for a median of 44.7 months (IQR 34.5-49.0), AF was detected in 61 (64.2%). By Kaplan-Meier estimation the cumulative incidence of AF was 30% at 3 months, 46% at 1 year, and 58% at 2 years; the median time to detection among affected patients was 124 days (IQR 13-385). Patients with detected AF had a larger left atrial volume index (LAVI; 35.2 vs. 28.2 mL/m2, p<0.001) and lower LVEF (53.1% vs. 59.6%, p<0.001) as well as higher incidence of heart failure (p = 0.032). LAVI (adjusted OR 1.10 per mL/m2, 95% CI 1.03-1.17; p = 0.006) and a reduced LVEF (≤50%; adjusted OR 9.2, 95% CI 1.9-44.5; p = 0.006) were independent predictors (AUC 0.79), and both remained independent in a Cox model (LAVI adjusted HR 1.04 per mL/m2; LVEF ≤50% adjusted HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3-3.9). A LAVI threshold of ≥26 mL/m2 functioned as a rule-out (sensitivity 92%), whereas LVEF ≤50% functioned as a rule-in (specificity 94%, PPV 92%); no single threshold or combination achieved both high sensitivity and high specificity. On stratified analysis the 2-year cumulative incidence of AF was 70% versus 20% above and below the LAVI threshold (log-rank p<0.001) and 73% versus 53% by the LVEF threshold (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Continuous post-ablation monitoring revealed AF in roughly two-thirds of patients after flutter ablation, often emerging several months following the procedure. More advanced atrial remodeling and impaired ventricular function were independent predictors of higher risk, providing practical and accessible thresholds to guide clinical decisions about which patients warrant prolonged rhythm surveillance and anticoagulation reinitiation after flutter ablation.

Title: Long-term outcomes of congenital subaortic stenosis surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate recurrence, reoperation, and aortic insufficiency progression after pediatric surgery for subaortic stenosis and explore associated study-level factors.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible studies published from 1 January 2012 to 3 July 2025. We included observational studies of patients <18 years undergoing surgical resection for SAS with a study-level mean or median postoperative follow-up of ≥ 3 years, which was the prespecified operational definition of long-term follow-up. Proportions were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was quantified using I²; meta-regression assessed study-level associations with reoperation and AI progression; and risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.
RESULTS: Seventeen retrospective studies included 1,536 patients; 1,493 contributed to the recurrence analysis. Follow-up ranged from 3.0 to 12.7 years. Overall recurrence was 21% (95% confidence interval, 16-28%; I²=88.1%). Reoperation across 16 studies was 17% (95% confidence interval, 14-20%; I²=41.6%); a prespecified definition-harmonized sensitivity analysis yielded the same estimate (17%; 95% confidence interval, 15-20%; I²=19.1%). In isolated discrete subaortic stenosis, reoperation was 8% and 12% after definition harmonization. Progression to moderate or severe aortic insufficiency was 10% (95% confidence interval, 8-13%). Older study-level age at surgery was inversely associated with reoperation (β = -0.2230; P = 0.0138), whereas higher preoperative peak left ventricular outflow tract gradient was associated with aortic insufficiency progression (odds ratio per 10-mmHg increase, 1.25; P = 0.0072).
CONCLUSIONS: Reoperation and clinically important aortic insufficiency remain substantial during follow-up after pediatric subaortic stenosis surgery. Meta-regression findings are exploratory, aggregate associations and should not guide individual operative timing or risk prediction.

Title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment.
RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N = 10, sham: N = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication (N = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN.
CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

Title: History of hypertension is associated with improved survival in patients with nonischemic etiology of heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a common comorbidity in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet its prognostic significance remains complex.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between HTN and all-cause mortality in patients with HFrEF, stratified by ischemic and nonischemic etiologies.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 11 242 patients with HFrEF treated between January 2009 and October 2025 at a national tertiary referral center. Patients were categorized according to ischemic vs. nonischemic etiology. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with multivariable adjustment for baseline characteristics.
RESULTS: HTN was present in 6992 patients (62%), and 6963 (63%) had ischemic heart disease (IHD). During a median follow-up of 5.0 years, 4952 patients (44%) died. Crude mortality was higher among hypertensive patients (46% vs. 41%, P < 0.001). In univariate analysis, HTN was associated with increased mortality risk (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.30, P < 0.001). However, after multivariable adjustment, HTN was associated with a reduction in mortality (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.97, P = 0.004). Stratified analysis demonstrated that this protective association was confined to patients without IHD (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.92, P < 0.001), while no significant association was observed in those with IHD (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.92-1.06).
CONCLUSION: In patients with HFrEF, HTN is associated with reduced mortality only in those with nonischemic etiology.

Title: Insulin resistance in the adipose tissue is associated with cardiac mortality: the Hiroshima study on glucose metabolism and cardiovascular diseases.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insulin resistance is a fundamental pathophysiology of cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to investigate the association of adipose tissue insulin resistance with cardiac and cerebrovascular mortality in comparison with hepatic and skeletal muscle insulin resistance.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 12 306 participants (mean age, 64.5 years; female, 49.9%) who underwent a general health checkup in Hiroshima City between January 1982 and March 2003. Based on the median values of adipose insulin resistance index (Adipo-IR), homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), and Matsuda index, participants were divided into high and low insulin resistance groups in adipose tissue, liver, and skeletal muscle, respectively.
RESULTS: Over a median 15.6-year follow-up period, 1001 cardiac and 629 cerebrovascular deaths occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis revealed that the hazard ratio (HR) for cardiac mortality was higher in the high Adipo-IR group than in the low Adipo-IR group (1.20 [95% confidence interval, 1.05-1.38]), whereas the HR for cerebrovascular mortality did not differ. In the stratified analyses, a significantly increased HR for cardiac mortality was observed in participants without antihypertensive or antihyperlipidemic medications in the high Adipo-IR group. HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index were also associated with cardiac mortality; however, these associations were not significant after adjusting for glycemic status.
CONCLUSION: The association between insulin resistance in various tissues and cardiac mortality has been clarified. An increased risk of cardiac mortality was associated with insulin resistance in adipose tissue, independent of glycemic status.

Title: Cytomegalovirus Donor and Recipient Serostatus and 5-Year Mortality After Heart Transplantation: Evidence of Racial Differences.
Journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) donor/recipient (D/R) serostatus is an established determinant of post-transplant outcomes in heart transplantation (HT); however, the extent to which demographic and socioeconomic (SE) factors modify CMV-related mortality risk remains unclear.
METHODS: Using the scientific registry of transplant recipients, we evaluated whether demographic and SE factors alter the association between CMV D/R serostatus and 5-year all-cause mortality among first-time, adult HT recipients (2010-2024). Multivariable competing risk models estimated sub-distribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for CMV D/R serostatus interacted with age, sex, race/ethnicity, and Distressed Community Index (DCI) categories.
RESULTS: CMV D+/R- and CMV D+/R+ serostatus were associated with increased 5-year mortality. Effect modification varied by subgroup. Age, sex, and DCI did not significantly modify CMV-associated mortality, suggesting consistent relative risk across these strata. In contrast, race/ethnicity significantly modified the association with attenuated mortality among Black HT recipients compared with White HT recipients (reference). The sHR for mortality comparing Black CMV D-/R- and CMV D+/R+ HT recipients was 0.69 lower (95% CI: 0.57-0.84; p-value < 0.001) than the corresponding estimate in White HT recipients. Similarly, the sHR comparing Black CMV D-/R- and CMV D-/R+ HT recipients was 0.78 lower (95% CI: 0.63-0.97; p-value = 0.024) than the White HT recipients. No significant differences were observed between White and Hispanic/Other racial/ethnic groups.
CONCLUSIONS: CMV-related mortality risk was evident among White recipients, however, the effect of CMV on post-transplant outcomes is attenuated in Black recipients. These findings highlight heterogeneity in CMV-associated risk and support more individualized CMV prevention and monitoring strategies incorporating demographic context.

Title: Making Brain Health Actionable for Older Persons in Primary Care: The Proposed SHAPES Framework.
Journal: Journal of primary care & community health
Abstract: Brain health is increasingly recognised as a life-course priority, but its translation into routine primary care for older persons remains uncertain. Vascular risk, sensory function, mobility, nutrition, sleep, mood, environmental exposure, and social participation are often addressed separately, leaving people with multiple recommendations but no coherent plan. We propose SHAPES-Sensory access; Heart, vessels, and movement; Appetite, food, and nutrition; Pollution, tobacco, and alcohol; Emotional health and sleep; and Social connection, purpose, and learning-as a conceptual implementation framework for co-design and feasibility testing. The workflow begins with a brief scan of all six domains. Findings are classified as Protect, Notice, or Investigate using explicit safety criteria. Notice is reserved for a mild, uncertain, non-progressive concern; any persistent, recurrent, progressive, function-limiting, or red-flag change requires clinical assessment. Safety signals take priority; otherwise, one person-valued priority is selected according to importance, likely benefit, modifiability, feasibility, and structural context. The next step may be behavioural, clinical, social/supportive, or service/system. Behavioural actions may be converted into small cue-linked actions, and meaningful success is agreed before follow-up. SHAPES is not a diagnostic test, decision rule, or validated risk score. SHAPES has not yet demonstrated content or face validity, feasibility in routine consultations, or acceptability to older persons or clinicians; its safety, equity and effectiveness also require prospective evaluation.

Title: Emerging advances in vascular Behçet syndrome.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Vascular involvement is one of the main contributors to morbidity and mortality in Behçet syndrome. This review summarizes recent advances in the pathophysiology, imaging, and management of vascular Behçet syndrome.
RECENT FINDINGS: Single-cell and translational studies support a central role for vessel-wall inflammation, neutrophil extracellular traps, and endothelial dysfunction. Common femoral vein wall ultrasonography, pulmonary artery wall assessment, and other vessel-wall imaging modalities suggest that vascular involvement may be more widespread than previously recognized. However, their diagnostic utility requires standardization and prospective validation across different cohorts and assessors. The updated 2025 EULAR recommendations position monoclonal anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα) antibodies as first-line treatment options for both remission induction and maintenance across vascular manifestations. Anticoagulation is no longer restricted to refractory thrombosis, provided that bleeding-risk is assessed and pulmonary artery aneurysms are excluded.
SUMMARY: Prompt immunosuppressive treatment with monoclonal anti-TNFα antibodies is now recommended as a first-line option for vascular involvement. Longitudinal cohorts and controlled trials are needed to validate vessel-wall imaging modalities.

Title: Accuracy Evaluation of the Omron HEM-7120 Automated Oscillometric Upper-arm Home Blood Pressure Monitor in Children and Adolescents Using the AAMI/ESH/ISO 81060-2:2018 Numerical Criteria.
Abstract: This study evaluated the Omron HEM-7120 automated oscillometric upper-arm home blood pressure monitor in children and adolescents against the numerical accuracy criteria of the AAMI/ESH/ISO Universal Standard. Test readings were compared with mercury auscultatory readings from two physicians using the same-arm sequential method. Three cuffs covered arm circumferences of 12-18, 17-22, and 22-32 cm. Of 90 participants, 85 were analyzed, yielding 255 comparisons. Mean differences were -4.0 ± 5.94 mmHg for systolic and -1.8 ± 7.20 mmHg for diastolic blood pressure, meeting Criterion 1. Participant standard deviations were 5.07 and 6.48 mmHg, below Criterion 2 limits. However, the requirements regarding age, reference-blood-pressure and cuff distributions, reference-measurement variability, and observer qualification were not fully met. The device met numerical criteria in this cohort, but it is not fully validated under the Universal Standard.

Title: Current management of Behçet syndrome.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize the most clinically relevant recent advances in the treatment of Behçet syndrome (BS), with emphasis on the updated 2025 EULAR recommendations and emerging evidence across different organ manifestations.
RECENT FINDINGS: The updated EULAR recommendations support earlier use of monoclonal TNF inhibitors (TNFi), particularly in severe ocular, vascular, and neurologic involvement, and favor their continued use for maintenance in selected major-organ disease. Recent randomized and comparative studies provide further support for TNFi in Behçet uveitis and vascular involvement. Newer agents, including PDE-4 inhibitors and JAK inhibitors (JAKi), have shown promising efficacy in mucocutaneous, gastrointestinal, ocular, vascular, and neurologic disease, although most evidence for JAKi remains derived from small uncontrolled studies. Ustekinumab has also shown encouraging results in refractory intestinal BS. The role of anticoagulation in vascular BS remains uncertain.
SUMMARY: Management of BS is increasingly organ- and risk-adapted, with earlier use of effective targeted therapies in patients at risk of irreversible damage. Despite encouraging results with several newer agents, comparative and high-quality evidence remains limited, highlighting the need for adequately powered studies with organ-specific outcomes.

Title: Interpretability of the Quantra viscoelastic test in patients with haematological malignancies presenting severe thrombocytopenia.
Journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
Abstract: Viscoelastic tests have been scarcely evaluated in patients with haematological malignancies and severe thrombocytopenia. The VISCOTHEM-1 study investigated the interpretability of Quantra results in these patients, with platelet count less than 50 × 109/l. The objective was to evaluate the correlation between clot stiffness and platelet contribution to clot stiffness (PCS) measured by Quantra and conventional laboratory platelet counts. In this exploratory, single-centre, nonrandomized prospective cohort (June-December 2024), adults with haematological malignancies, platelet count less than 50 × 109/l and no antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy or platelet-function disorders were enrolled. Patients underwent a blood count, coagulation assays, Quantra and ROTEM assessments. For patients who received transfusion, a second draw was performed one hour posttransfusion. Forty-six patients were included: 16 with platelet counts less than 10 × 109/l, 15 between 10 and 19 × 109/l, and 15 between 20 and 49 × 109/l. Fourteen patients (31%) experienced bleeding. The median PCS measured by Quantra was 2 hPa [interquartile range (IQR) 2-3.38] and correlated strongly with platelet count using conventional assay (r = 0.84, P < 0.05) and with MCE platelets measured by ROTEM (r = 0.78, P < 0.05). Clot stiffness was moderately correlated with platelet count (r = 0.48, P < 0.05) and strongly with MCF-EXTEM (r = 0.79, P < 0.05). The range of PCS values differentiated most patients except in the less than 10 × 109/l subgroup. The distributions of clot stiffness, clotting time and fibrinogen contribution to clot stiffness measured by Quantra reliably discriminated between all patients regardless of platelet count. After transfusion, PCS and clot stiffness increased significantly. Quantra results were interpretable in patients with haematological malignancies and platelet counts below 50 × 109/l and correlated both with ROTEM parameters and with conventional haemostasis assays.

Title: Diabetic retinopathy in pregnancy.
Journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of development and progression of diabetic retinopathy. This review examines the mechanisms underlying diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy, established and emerging risk factors for diabetic retinopathy progression, current screening strategies, and management options for sight-threatening disease.
RECENT FINDINGS: The severity of retinopathy at conception, glycaemic control, duration of diabetes and hypertension are established predictors of diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy. Recent data suggest that patients with no retinopathy on initial screening have a very low risk of diabetic retinopathy progression, and further screening may not be indicated during pregnancy in this cohort. Pan retinal photocoagulation remains the mainstay of treatment for sight-threatening proliferative disease, while the use of intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy remains challenging because of limited safety data. Evidence regarding the postpartum course of diabetic retinopathy remains limited.
SUMMARY: Pregnancy represents a period of increased retinal risk in women with preexisting diabetes, although this risk is not uniform. Baseline retinopathy status, duration of diabetes, extent of glycaemic control and hypertensive disease may provide a framework for future risk-stratified screening. Further prospective studies are required to determine whether surveillance can safely be individualised, and to clarify the role of anti-VEGF therapy and postpartum monitoring.

Title: System Delay and Mortality in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicentre, Retrospective, Observational Study in Seoul.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt recognition and early management of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are crucial for improving outcomes. This study investigates the association between system delay and in-hospital mortality in patients with STEMI.
METHODS: Using data from the Seoul GOLDEN-time emergency medical system registry, a multicentre retrospective registry in Seoul, this study analysed patients with STEMI who were transported to an emergency department via emergency medical service for cardiac complaints between July 2020 and December 2022. System delay included the response time (first medical contact to an ambulance on the scene), scene time (ambulance on the scene to departure), scene-to-door time (departure to hospital arrival), and door-to-balloon time.
RESULTS: Among 654 patients with STEMI who received percutaneous coronary intervention, survivors had shorter overall system delay, prehospital time, scene time, scene-to-door time, and door-to-balloon time than non-survivors. A system delay > 127.5 minutes was associated with high mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.07; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-4.13). Prolonged prehospital time (aOR, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.16-4.95), scene time (aOR, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.24-5.75), and door-to-balloon time (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.09-4.39) were each independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSION: Prolonged system delays were associated with increased in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the need for a comprehensive, system-level approach to reducing system delay across the entire STEMI care pathway.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Early Right Heart Failure After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation: A Narrative Review of Definitions, Risk Prediction, and Management.
Abstract: Early right heart failure (RHF) remains common after left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Definition and time window determine reported incidence and complicate risk-model comparison. Established risk models perform differently across cohorts and device eras, and temporary support should be matched to the dominant physiology. LV unloading alters venous return, septal geometry, and right ventricular (RV) loading, whereas perioperative stress exposes limited RV reserve. No single clinical, imaging, or hemodynamic measure reliably predicts early RHF, and existing scores perform variably on external validation. Dynamic hemodynamic assessment adds information about RV reserve and warrants prospective threshold validation. Management begins by addressing reversible causes and optimizing LVAD support. When temporary mechanical support is required, RV-specific bypass restores pulmonary forward flow, an oxygenated right atrial-to-pulmonary arterial RVAD adds gas exchange, and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation provides broader rescue for combined circulatory and respiratory failure. Comparative evidence on timing and configuration remains observational.

Title: Validation of hs-cTnI-Alinity in the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: It is unknown whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) measured on the Alinity platform (hs-cTnI-Alinity), can be used with the same clinical decision values as the Architect platform (hs-cTnI-Architect).
METHODS: In an international prospective study, hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect were measured from the same blood samples obtained at 0 h, 1 h, and 2 h from patients presenting to the emergency department with acute chest discomfort. The final diagnosis was centrally adjudicated by two cardiologists. We tested four hypotheses: hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect have (1) excellent analytical agreement, (2) high concordance at common analytical benchmarks (limit-of-detection and upper-reference-limit); (3) high diagnostic accuracy for AMI; and (4) comparable clinical performance for early rule-out and rule-in of AMI.
RESULTS: Among 1,573 eligible patients (median age 60 years, 34.7 % women) 7,438 measurements of hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect from the same samples were performed. The prevalence of AMI was 17.7 % (279/1,573). Analytical agreement between hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect was excellent (mean bias -3.6 ng/L [95 % CI -17.3 to 10.1]). Using limit-of-detection and upper-reference-limit as benchmarks, agreement was high. However, major disagreement occurred in 2.5 %, including only one AMI. Diagnostic accuracy for AMI was very high and comparable between hs-cTnI-Alinity and hs-cTnI-Architect (area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve 0.95 [95 % CI 0.95-0.96] and 0.96 [95 % CI 0.95-0.96]). Sensitivity for ruling-out AMI were >99 % and specificity >93 % and comparable between both assays when applying the ESC 0/1h and ESC 0/2h algorithm derived for hs-cTnI-Architect.
CONCLUSIONS: Analytic benchmarks and ESC 0/1h and 0/2h algorithm cut-offs originally derived for hs-cTnI-Architect might be safely applied when using hs-cTnI-Alinity.

Title: Early sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation is associated with improved cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.
Journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
Abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, but the optimal timing of initiation in those with acute coronary syndrome is not known. This study aims to assess if early therapy at discharge is superior to delayed or no therapy in reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational cohort study included individuals with type 2 diabetes admitted with an acute coronary syndrome at a single regional heart centre between July 2018 and December 2023. Individuals were stratified into three groups based on the timing of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation: (1) discharge group (initiated at hospital discharge), (2) post-discharge group (initiated after discharge during follow-up) and (3) no therapy group. The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event.
RESULTS: Among 970 eligible patients (median age, 70.2 years [IQR, 61.0-78.5 years]; 73.9% male), the median follow-up duration was 29.9 months (IQR, 20.1, 43.0 months). Compared with the discharge group, the risk of primary outcome was significantly higher in both the post-discharge group (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.50; 95% CI [1.13, 1.99], p = 0.005) and the no therapy group (aHR, 1.65; 95% CI [1.24, 2.20]; p < 0.001). Analyses were adjusted using clone-censor-weight methods and multivariable Cox-proportional hazards models.
CONCLUSIONS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor therapy at hospital discharge was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.

Title: Transfusion Management in Pregnancies Complicated by Hemoglobinopathies: Evidence, Guidelines, and Clinical Challenges.
Abstract: This review examined the evidence and guidelines on transfusion strategies, targets, and complications in pregnant women with hemoglobinopathies through a narrative review of literature published from 2010 to 2025, including randomized trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and guidance from the American Society of Hematology, the British Society for Haematology (BSH), and International Society of Blood Transfusion, as well as regional recommendations and consensus statements from thalassemia-endemic areas such as China and Southeast Asia. The findings show that pregnancy substantially alters transfusion requirements and risks in this population. In sickle cell disease, prophylactic transfusion strategies targeting hemoglobin levels of 10-11 g/dL and sickle hemoglobin fractions below 30% are associated with reduced vaso-occlusive complications and improved maternal and fetal outcomes (Grade B evidence, supported by BSH, the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, and observational meta-analyses). In β-thalassemia major, transfusion support during pregnancy typically requires intensification to maintain hemoglobin levels between 9.5-10.5 g/dL (Grade B, BSH guideline), particularly because interruption of iron chelation therapy during gestation increases the risk of iron overload and cardiac complications. Chinese and Southeast Asian expert recommendations similarly support maintaining hemoglobin at or above 10 g/dL to promote fetal growth and reduce maternal cardiac stress (Grade C, expert consensus). At the same time, transfusion-related complications, including alloimmunization, delayed hemolytic reactions, circulatory overload, acute lung injury, and iron toxicity, remain important clinical concerns. Overall, transfusion management in pregnancies complicated by hemoglobinopathies requires individualized, evidence-based strategies, careful surveillance for complications, and close multidisciplinary collaboration to optimize maternal and fetal outcomes, while incorporation of global and regional evidence enhances the relevance and applicability of current recommendations.

Title: STA-MCA Bypass for Moyamoya Vasculopathy: Early Experience and Outcomes from a National Referral Centre.
Journal: The Malaysian journal of medical sciences : MJMS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya vasculopathy is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder requiring surgical revascularisation. In Malaysia, experience with cerebral bypass has been limited. This study evaluated early outcomes of superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery (STA-MCA) bypass at a national referral centre.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on patients undergoing STA-MCA bypass between January 2017 and December 2025. Functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), while cerebral perfusion and bypass patency were evaluated using computed tomography (CT) perfusion and CT angiography or digital subtraction angiography. Statistical analyses included Fisher's exact test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman correlation.
RESULTS: A total of 74 cerebral bypass procedures were performed, including 50 for moyamoya vasculopathy, with 37 cases analysed. Median age was 43 years with female predominance (54%). Single-barrel bypass was performed in 84% of cases, with 100% final intraoperative patency. Perfusion improved in 85% of patients and graft patency in 94%. At three months, 95% achieved good functional outcome (mRS 0 to 2). Greater surgeon experience was associated with shorter operative duration (ρ = -0.463, P = 0.0039). Preoperative antiplatelet withholding was also associated with reduced operative duration (P = 0.0109) without adverse impact on clinical or radiological outcomes. No variables were significantly associated with adverse outcomes (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: STA-MCA bypass achieves excellent clinical and radiological outcomes in a maturing neurovascular programme. These findings support the development of structured revascularisation services and inform perioperative management strategies in a national referral setting.

Title: Association between Plasma Short-Chain Fatty Acids and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Nested Case-Control Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between plasma short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: A nested case-control study was conducted comprising 387 pairs of HDP cases and non-HDP controls. The HDP group included 291 cases of gestational hypertension (GH) and 96 of preeclampsia (PE) or chronic hypertension (CH) with superimposed PE (PE/CH-PE). Seven plasma SCFA levels were assayed at gestational weeks 16-20, before HDP onset. The individual effects of the seven SCFAs on HDP risk were analyzed using logistic regression, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied to calculate adjusted P-values in multivariate analysis. The joint effects of the seven SCFAs were evaluated using weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression.
RESULTS: HDP cases exhibited significantly lower median (interquartile range) valerate levels than controls (9 (5-14) vs. 10 (6-18) ng/mL, P = 0.001). Among the seven analyzed SCFAs, isobutyrate and isovalerate demonstrated the highest correlation coefficient at 0.85 (P < 0.001). Each interquartile range increase in valerate content was associated with a low risk of HDP, yielding an adjusted odds ratio (aOR) of 0.699 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.516-0.946, FDR-corrected P = 0.047). Isobutyrate and hexanoate were also inversely associated with HDP after multivariate adjustment and FDR correction (both P = 0.047), with aORs of 0.899 (95% CI: 0.826-0.980) and 0.686 (95% CI: 0.508-0.927), respectively. WQS regression revealed that joint SCFA exposure was associated with a decreased risk of HDP (aOR: 0.230, 95% CI: 0.105-0.506) and GH (aOR: 0.740, 95% CI: 0.571-0.933).
CONCLUSION: Plasma levels of valerate, isobutyrate, and hexanoate are inversely associated with HDP risk. Furthermore, the combined effect of these SCFAs is linked to a lower incidence of both HDP and GH. These findings suggest that circulating SCFAs may serve as potential early biomarkers for HDP.

Title: Age as a significant prognostic factor in patients meeting the global ARDS definition but not the Berlin definition.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: ARDS (Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome) poses significant challenges in critical care, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. The new global definition of ARDS includes some patients who are not previously considered to have ARDS. This study aims to look at the prognostic characteristics of these patients and develop a prediction model.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 5,214 patients from the Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital between December 2022 and February 2023. Patients were categorized into four groups based on the 2023 Global Definition and 2012 Berlin Definition: Global-definition-only ARDS + COVID-19, Global-definition-only ARDS-COVID-19, Berlin ARDS + COVID-19, and Berlin ARDS-COVID-19. Patient characteristics were analyzed using LASSO regression and Cox proportional hazards models to identify factors associated with 28-day mortality. A prognostic model was developed using key variables.
RESULTS: Among ARDS patients, the Berlin ARDS + COVID-19 group had the highest mortality, while the observed 28-day mortality in the Global-definition-only ARDS + COVID-19 group was of a similar magnitude to that in the Berlin ARDS without COVID-19 group. LASSO selected seven candidate predictors: heart rate, lactate dehydrogenase, platelet count, total bilirubin, D-dimer, age, and antiviral therapy. In the multivariable Cox model, lactate dehydrogenase, age, and antiviral therapy were independently associated with 28-day mortality. Compared with patients aged <75 years, the HRs for 28-day mortality were 2.09 (95% CI 1.07-4.10) for those aged 75 to <85 years and 3.78 (95% CI 2.08-6.86) for those aged ≥85 years. Antiviral therapy was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.40-0.84).The model's AUC for predicting 28-day mortality was 0.732 in the training set and 0.726 in the validation set.
CONCLUSIONS: The 2023 Global ARDS definition holds significant value in identifying COVID-19 patients receiving high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO), the Global definition may facilitate earlier identification of ARDS patients. Age is a critical risk factor, highlighting the need for heightened clinical attention in elderly patients. Antiviral therapy was associated with a lower hazard of 28-day mortality. Seven candidate predictors were selected by LASSO and evaluated in a Cox prognostic model for 28-day mortality.

Title: Salvage Yttrium-90 Transarterial Radioembolization Combined with Second-Line Molecular Targeted Agents and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progressing After TACE-Based Combination Therapy: A Single-Center Real-World Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that progresses after first-line transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with molecular targeted agents (MTAs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have limited therapeutic options. This single-center, retrospective, single-arm real-world study evaluated the efficacy and safety of salvage yttrium-90 transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 TARE) plus second-line systemic therapy in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified HCC patients receiving Y-90 TARE combined with second-line systemic therapy between July 2022 and December 2024. Tumor response was assessed per mRECIST. Objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were analyzed. Albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) scores were obtained at baseline and 1 month post-TARE to evaluate hepatotoxicity, with baseline scores used for prognostic stratification.
RESULTS: Nineteen patients with intermediate-to-advanced HCC were identified. Median predicted tumor-absorbed dose was 130.00 Gy (Q1, Q3: 120.00, 250.00). Apatinib (31.58%) and tislelizumab (36.84%) were the most common MTA and ICI. Over a median follow-up of 10.00 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 7.10-12.90), ORR was 47.37% and DCR 78.95%. Median PFS and OS were 4.53 (95% CI: 2.80-6.25) and 8.70 months (95% CI: 6.97-10.43), with 6-, 12-, and 24-month OS rates of 72.2%, 43.6%, and 29.2%. Any-grade TRAEs occurred in 78.95% and Grade 3 in 26.32%, with no Grade 4-5 events. The most frequent TRAEs were hypertension (36.84%), thrombocytopenia (31.58%), and hand-foot syndrome (31.58%). Median ALBI scores were comparable between baseline (-2.07; Q1, Q3: -2.49, -1.87) and 1-month post-TARE (-2.06; Q1, Q3: -2.23, -1.88) (Z = 1.55, P = 0.12). Further exploratory univariate Cox regression analysis showed that ALBI was the only baseline variable reaching nominal statistical significance (HR = 7.94; 95% CI: 1.61-39.05; P = 0.01); patients with ALBI ≤ -2.07 had longer OS (median: 15.70 months; 95% CI: not estimable-not estimable).
CONCLUSIONS: In this small single-center retrospective cohort, salvage Y-90 TARE combined with second-line MTAs and ICIs showed promising antitumor activity with manageable toxicity in HCC progressing after TACE-based combination therapy. Baseline ALBI was associated with OS and warrants prospective validation as a potential prognostic marker.

Title: Modified Frailty Index and Postoperative Outcomes of Zygomaticomaxillary Complex Fracture Repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The modified 5-item frailty index (mFI-5) is a comorbidity-based risk stratification tool previously validated in patients undergoing facial plastic and reconstructive surgery. This retrospective US hospital database study investigates the association between mFI-5 score and postoperative complications following zygomaticomaxillary complex (ZMC) fracture repair.
METHODS: The National Surgical Quality Improvement Program was queried for patients undergoing ZMC fracture repair between 2005 and 2020. The mFI-5 score was calculated by assigning one point for each of the following comorbidities: diabetes mellitus, hypertension, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and dependent functional status. Patients were stratified by mFI-5 score. Univariate and multivariable analyses were performed to assess associations between frailty and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: A total of 2260 patients were included and stratified by mFI-5 scores of 0 (n = 1890), 1 (n = 285), and 2 or greater (n = 85). Higher mFI-5 scores were associated with male sex, older age, higher American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, inpatient status, obesity, weight loss, bleeding disorders, and dependent functional status. Higher mFI-5 was associated with increased rates of surgical complications, urinary tract infections, prolonged ventilation over 48 h, pneumonia, cumulative morbidity, and cumulative medical complications. On multivariable analysis, mFI-5 scores of 1 (p = 0.027) and 2 or greater (p = 0.049) were independently associated with cumulative morbidity, and a score of 1 was associated with surgical complications (p = 0.022).
CONCLUSION: The mFI-5 is associated with cumulative morbidity and surgical complications following ZMC fracture repair. Assessment of frailty may improve perioperative risk stratification in this population.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

Title: Isolated Metachronous Splenic Metastasis Following Discontinuation of PD-1 Inhibitor Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Rare Pattern of Late Recurrence - A Case Report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated splenic metastasis from hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncommon, with only a small number of well-characterised solitary cases reported in the English-language literature. Moreover, late extrahepatic recurrence after immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) discontinuation in patients achieving complete response remains poorly characterized, posing significant challenges for surveillance and management.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old woman with a 6-year history of HBV-related HCC underwent sequential treatments including hepatectomy, microwave ablation, repeat hepatectomy, and PD-1 inhibitor therapy (sintilimab), achieving a sustained complete radiological response. Approximately 18 months after ICI cessation, surveillance imaging revealed an isolated 3.0 × 2.6 cm splenic lesion with markedly elevated PIVKA-II (257.81 mAU/mL; reference <40 mAU/mL) despite normal AFP. Following multidisciplinary evaluation and preoperative splenic artery embolization, open splenectomy was performed. Histopathology confirmed metastatic HCC (Glypican-3+, Arginase-1+, CK19 focal+, Ki-67 ~30%), and PIVKA-II normalized postoperatively. Maintenance lenvatinib (8 mg daily) was initiated 5 months postoperatively as a risk-adapted strategy based on high-risk pathological features. At 12-month follow-up, the patient remained without evidence of radiological or biochemical recurrence, with excellent performance status; longer follow-up is required to confirm durability of response.
CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates: (1) that the spleen may occasionally be a site of late oligometastatic recurrence in HCC sustained radiological complete response by mRECIST criteria; (2) the complementary value of PIVKA-II in detecting AFP-negative extrahepatic disease; and (3) that, in carefully selected patients, splenectomy combined with tailored systemic therapy may be a technically feasible option, though whether this approach constitutes a curative strategy remains unproven in the absence of prospective or large-cohort validation. The temporal association between ICI discontinuation and late relapse highlights critical knowledge gaps regarding immune-mediated tumor dormancy and optimal duration of immunotherapy, warranting prospective investigation.

Title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted PERT-workflow and its association with care processes and budget impact: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. In intermediate-high and high-risk PE, timely escalation beyond anticoagulation is critical, yet real-world pathways are often delayed. Pulmonary embolism response teams (PERTs) improve decision-making, but activation remains inconsistent. Whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled triage strengthens PERT and improves acute PE care has not been elucidated so far.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively screened 2500 patients presenting to our university hospital with a symptomatic central or segmental PE between 08/2022 and 07/2024. Clinical and economic outcomes were compared during a 1-year timeframe before and after implementation of an AI algorithm that analyses CT scans, flags suspected PE, and supports PERT triage. 424 patients met inclusion criteria. AI-supported triage increased PERT activation from 9.2% to 84.5% (P < 0.001). Time from CT completion to PE diagnosis decreased from 2.1 to 1.3 h (P < 0.01). Time from PE diagnosis to interventional therapy was reduced by 50% (P < 0.05). Hospital/ICU length-of-stay and 30-day mortality showed non-significant reductions. Model-based economic analysis showed lower 1-year per-patient costs and annual savings associated with AI-supported PERT.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of an AI-supported PERT workflow was associated with significant improvements in PE care processes, including higher PERT activation rates and shorter diagnostic and treatment intervals. Numerical reductions in mortality, hospital/ICU length-of-stay did not reach statistical significance. The exploratory budget impact model suggested potential cost savings, mainly driven by trends in reduced resource utilization; however, these findings require prospective validation using adequately powered clinical endpoints.

Title: Left bundle branch area pacing outcomes from an African registry: Short-term findings from the MACOP study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) provides physiological ventricular activation and has emerged as an alternative to conventional cardiac resynchronization therapy. Data on LBBAP outcomes in African populations remain scarce.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe procedural outcomes of LBBAP in an African cohort.
METHODS: A descriptive registry study included 311 patients from Kenya and South Africa who underwent LBBAP between 2021 and 2024. Data on pacing thresholds, QRS duration (QRSd), fluoroscopy time, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were collected and analyzed. Patients were stratified by baseline QRSd categories, conduction patterns, pacing indication, and LVEF.
RESULTS: The mean age was 65 ± 14 years, with 54% male. Median follow-up was 5 months. Mean pacing threshold at implant was 0.67 ± 0.52 V at 1.0 ms, remaining stable at follow-up (0.64 ± 0.48 V, P = .3). Mean QRSd decreased significantly from 136.7 ± 33.6 ms at baseline to 118.4 ± 12.0 ms post-LBBAP (P < .001), with greatest reduction in patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB: 38.9 ± 16.9 ms vs non-LBBB: 6.9 ± 30.2 ms, P < .001). Mean fluoroscopy time was 9.7 ± 7.8 minutes. Among patients with baseline LVEF <50%, mean LVEF improved from 29 ± 9% to 39 ± 12% (P < .001), with greater improvement in patients with LBBB. Procedural success rate was 95.8%. During follow-up, 12 patients (3.86%) died, all from heart failure-related causes without documented ventricular arrhythmias on device interrogation.
CONCLUSION: The Multicenter African Cardiac Outcomes in Pacing study provides the first African registry data on LBBAP, demonstrating feasibility with stable pacing thresholds, significant QRS narrowing, and LVEF improvement, particularly in patients with LBBB. These findings support LBBAP as a viable pacing strategy in resource-limited settings.

Title: A multicenter randomized controlled study to evaluate the efficacy of an artificial intelligence-based electrocardiography for the detection of atrial fibrillation in patients with suspected symptoms (DEEP-AF).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is frequently paroxysmal and asymptomatic, leading to delayed diagnosis and missed opportunities for stroke prevention. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) obtained during sinus rhythm may enable risk stratification and more efficient allocation of rhythm-monitoring resources.
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to determine whether an AI-ECG-guided strategy improves detection of newly diagnosed AF compared with usual care in patients with symptoms suggestive of AF and no prior AF diagnosis.
METHODS: DEEP-AF (A Prospective, Multi-center, Randomized Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Detection of Atrial Fibrillation Using Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography (SmartECG-AFrisk) Compared With Usual Care in Patients with Suspected Atrial Fibrillation) is a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled superiority trial conducted at 13 tertiary hospitals in South Korea. A total of 1230 adults 30 years or older with symptoms suggestive of AF and no AF on screening 12-lead ECG will be randomized 1:1 to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. In the AI-ECG group, the SmartECG-AFrisk algorithm will generate a risk score (high risk: AI score ≥50; low risk: AI score <50) to support clinician-directed rhythm monitoring within guideline-concordant practice. Usual care will follow standard clinical evaluation without access to the AI score.
RESULTS: The primary outcome is the incidence of newly diagnosed AF within 6 months, confirmed on standard ECG modalities. Secondary outcomes include time to AF diagnosis, AF detection according to AI risk strata, health care resource utilization and diagnostic efficiency, initiation and timing of anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy, AF burden, detection of other clinically relevant arrhythmias, arrhythmia-related procedures, clinical events, and patient satisfaction.
CONCLUSION: DEEP-AF will provide pragmatic randomized evidence on whether AI-ECG-guided risk stratification can improve AF detection and diagnostic efficiency in routine care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07173673.

Title: Utilization of Preventive Single-Inflow Cannula Left Atrial Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular/left ventricle (LV) overload remains a major limitation of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with cardiogenic shock. Left atrial veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (LAVA-ECMO) has been proposed to facilitate LV unloading; however, data regarding its optimal timing and clinical role remain limited.
