METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a preventive single-inflow cannula LAVA-ECMO strategy, defined as an a priori LV unloading approach implemented at extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation, either through primary LAVA-ECMO implantation or planned early conversion from VA-ECMO within 60 minutes. Between January 2020 and July 2025, eligible patients supported with VA-ECMO or LAVA-ECMO were screened. After predefined exclusions, 42 patients managed with preventive LAVA-ECMO were compared with 64 contemporaneous patients receiving conventional VA-ECMO.
RESULTS: Thirty-day all-cause mortality was lower in the LAVA-ECMO group than in the VA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 76.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.31-0.95). Failure to wean from ECMO tended to occur less frequently with LAVA-ECMO (31.0% vs 56.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.18-1.01). Signs of LV overload during ECMO support were significantly reduced in the LAVA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 82.8%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.19, 95% CI, 0.08-0.49). Overall complication rates were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, preventive LAVA-ECMO was associated with lower short-term mortality and a reduced incidence of LV overload without an apparent increase in complications. Preventive LAVA-ECMO may represent a feasible mechanical circulatory support strategy in carefully selected patients with cardiogenic shock.

Title: Accelerated pacing rates to improve exercise tolerance, quality of life, and arrhythmia burden in patients with evidence of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: The PACE-UP rationale and design.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with permanent pacemakers often present with early or established heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Increasing the lower pacing rate has demonstrated improvements in quality of life and patient physical activity, while lowering the burden of atrial arrhythmias. However, the impact on objective measures of exercise tolerance and cardiac function is not well established.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to assess the impact of an accelerated lower rate setting on peak oxygen consumption in patients with stage B/C HFpEF.
METHODS: The Accelerated Pacing Rates to Improve Exercise Tolerance, Quality of Life, and Arrhythmia Burden in Patients with Evidence of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction study is a multicenter, prospective, 2-arm randomized controlled trial recruiting 160 participants. Participants will be randomized to accelerated pacing rate (75 beats per minute) or usual care (60 beats per minute), with follow-up assessments at 4 and 52 weeks after randomization.
RESULTS: The primary endpoint is peak oxygen consumption obtained during cardiopulmonary exercise testing at 52 weeks after randomization. Secondary endpoints include change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire, device-detected atrial arrhythmias and physical activity, resting and exercise transthoracic echocardiography, and Montreal Cognitive Assessment.
CONCLUSION: This trial will be the first randomized trial to assess the impact of a high lower rate pacing on objective exercise tolerance and cardiac function in patients with stage B/C HFpEF. We anticipate the findings to improve our knowledge and guide pacemaker programming for patients with HFpEF.

Title: Vascular closure strategies in pulmonary vein isolation to reduce vascular complications and facilitate same-day discharge.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor access-site bleeding is common after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for atrial fibrillation. Vascular closure devices (VCDs) may reduce bleeding, facilitating shorter bed rest and same-day discharge (SDD).
OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the impact of closure strategies (Perclose™ ProStyle™ [VCD] and figure-of-8 [FO8]-suture) and mobilization protocols on access-site bleeding complications and length of hospital stay.
METHODS: This single-center observational study included patients undergoing a primary PVI for atrial fibrillation between January 15 and December 31, 2025, at St. Antonius Hospital, the Netherlands. 4 protocols were evaluated sequentially: cohort 1: FO8-suture + 4 hours bed rest; cohort 2: VCD + 4 hours bed rest; cohort 3: VCD + 2 hours bed rest + 2 hours seated; cohort 4: VCD + FO8-suture + 2 hours bed rest + 1 hour seated. Primary outcome was in-hospital access-site bleeding, categorized by intervention. Secondary outcomes included SDD, time to discharge, unplanned overnight stay, and emergency room visits due to groin complications.
RESULTS: A total of 738 patients were included (cohorts 1-4: n = 170, 161, 210, and 197, respectively). Baseline characteristics were comparable. 2 major bleeding complications occurred in cohort 1. Minor bleeding complications decreased across the 4 cohorts from 19.4% to 9.6% (P = .027). Female sex (odds ratio [OR], 1.52), protamine use (OR, 0.50), and cohort 4 protocol (OR, 0.38) predicted bleeding. SDD increased from 56.5% (cohort 1) to 67.0% (cohort 4, P = .168), without more unplanned overnight stays or bleeding-related emergency room visits.
CONCLUSION: The use of a VCD in combination with an FO8 suture and protamine was significantly associated with lower observed access-site bleeding complications and optimized the workflow of PVI.

Title: Timely Reperfusion in STEMI: A Closed-Loop Audit of Guideline Compliance and Practice Improvements.
Abstract:
AIM: Timely reperfusion is vital in STEMI care to reduce mortality. An initial audit showed patients transferred from emergency departments outside Dublin often exceeded the 120-minute reperfusion target. In response, Dublin Mid Leinster protocols were updated to recommend pre-transfer thrombolysis. This study evaluates the impact of these changes on reperfusion times and outcomes.
METHODS: This observational study included STEMI patients admitted to St. James's Hospital from 2021-2023, compared to a prior cohort (2017-2020). The primary outcome was time from first ECG to reperfusion. Secondary outcomes included thrombolysis rates, success (TIMI 2/3 flow on angiography) and safety.
RESULTS: Among 1,301 patients, the median ECG-to-reperfusion time among patients transferred from outside Dublin fell from 124 minutes (IQR 96-166) to 113 minutes (IQR 78-151) (p<0.0001), while the proportion achieving reperfusion within 120 minutes increased from 235/507 (46.4%) to 308/530 (58.1%). Overall thrombolysis use increased from 27/1161 (2.3%) to 131/1301 (10.1%). Among thrombolysed patients, 85/131 (64.9%) achieved successful reperfusion and severe bleeding occurred in 2/131 (1.5%). Mapping demonstrated markedly lower rates of timely reperfusion at the periphery of the DML region.
DISCUSSION: A regional protocol promoting thrombolysis substantially increased thrombolysis utilisation and improved overall timely reperfusion among STEMI patients transferred from outside Dublin. Persistent geographical disparities support further optimisation of regional pathways and consideration of prehospital thrombolysis strategies.

Title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Algorithm to Enhance Angiographic Coronary Visibility in Morbid Obesity: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

Title: Relationship between site procedural volumes and outcomes of left bundle branch area pacing using stylet-driven leads from the INSIGHT-LBBA Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch (LBB) area pacing (LBBAP) is increasingly used for patients with a ventricular pacing indication. Multi-center studies analyzing predominantly lumenless leads have suggested a learning curve for LBBAP; however, analogous data on stylet-driven leads (SDLs) are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the relationship between site volume and procedural outcomes and complications using the INGEVITY+ SDL for LBBAP.
METHODS: A secondary analysis of the INSIGHT-LBBA multi-site registry was performed, with retrospective data collected across 8 United States sites performing LBBAP with INGEVITY+ SDLs between 2020 and 2023. Outcomes included LBBAP and LBB capture success rates, pacing parameters, fluoroscopy time, number of leads used, and lead-related complications. Outcomes were assessed using a generalized estimated equation based on consecutive implants. A sensitivity analysis was performed restricted to only single- and dual-chamber LBBAP implants.
RESULTS: A total of 1374 patients were enrolled in the primary INSIGHT-LBBA registry. Overall LBBAP success and LBB capture success rates were 94.5% and 78.1%, respectively. LBBAP success rate improved with experience (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.14, per every 10 successive LBBAP implants; P = .001), with similar results in the sensitivity analysis. Fluoroscopy times and complication rates remained low (10.0 ± 9.2 minutes and 2.7%, respectively).
CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of INSIGHT-LBBA using INGEVITY+ SDLs, LBBAP and LBB capture success rates were high and improved with consecutive implants, indicative of a learning curve for implantation. Fluoroscopy times and complication rates remained low without significant change during consecutive implants. These data add to the growing literature supporting safe and effective use of SDLs for LBBAP.

Title: Routine Versus Deferred Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of concomitant coronary artery disease in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains controversial. Whether routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR provides clinical benefit compared to a strategy of deferral is unclear.
METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing routine PCI before TAVR with a strategy of PCI deferral. The primary end points were a composite of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary end points included myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization, and major bleeding. We applied a random-effects model to calculate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% CI. We also performed a pooled time-to-event analysis using reconstructed individual patient data.
RESULTS: We included 3 RCT (ACTIVATION, NOTION-3, and PRO-TAVI) comprising a total of 1156 patients. The pooled cohort had a median age exceeding 81 years and exhibited low anatomic coronary complexity (median SYNTAX score ≤10). Routine PCI did not significantly reduce the risk of MACCE (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.13; P = .25) or all-cause mortality (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.67-1.17; P = .38). Pooled Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed no difference in all-cause mortality over 48 months (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.68-1.17; P = .41). Although routine PCI was associated with a significant reduction in any revascularization (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.06-0.89; P = .03) and urgent revascularization (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87; P = .02), it was associated with increased bleeding events (HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.28-3.00; P < .01). No significant differences were observed regarding myocardial infarction or stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine PCI before TAVR did not reduce mortality or MACCE compared to a deferral strategy. Although routine PCI lowered the risk of subsequent urgent revascularization, it significantly increased the risk of major bleeding.

Title: Alcohol consumption and mortality in COPD: a population-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: COPD is characterised by multimorbidity and high mortality. Although alcohol consumption is associated with comorbidities common in COPD, its impact on COPD outcomes is uncertain. We investigated associations between baseline alcohol consumption and 10-year mortality, stratified by COPD status and examined whether comorbidity prevalence differed across alcohol categories.
METHODS: COPD was defined by post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 s/forced vital capacity <0.7; alcohol as ≤10 versus >10 units·week-1. Comorbidities were ascertained from national registries. Cox models estimated mortality hazard ratios (HRs) adjusting for age, sex, smoking, education, body mass index and comorbidities. Inverse probability weighting addressed confounding. Logistic regression examined alcohol-comorbidity associations with false discovery rate correction.
RESULTS: In 2004-2006, 4528 Danish adults aged 45-84 years were recruited. Among 3468 participants with complete alcohol and COPD data (mean age 64 years; 65% male; 12% COPD), 593 deaths occurred over 10 years. Alcohol >10 units·week-1 was not associated with mortality in unadjusted (HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.80-1.18)) or fully adjusted (HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.71-1.07)) models. COPD was strongly associated with mortality (adjusted HR 2.00 (95% CI 1.64-2.43)). No alcohol×COPD interaction was detected. Cardiovascular comorbidities were generally more prevalent among participants with COPD, although patterns varied. No associations between alcohol and individual comorbidities survived multiple testing correction.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort with predominantly moderate consumption, alcohol intake >10 units·week-1 was not associated with 10-year mortality in adults with or without COPD, whereas COPD conferred excess risk independent of comorbidity and lifestyle factors. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence that alcohol consumption is safe.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes in COPD, obstructive sleep apnoea and the overlap syndrome.
Abstract:
RATIONALE: COPD and obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) are both independently associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. It is not clear whether this risk is further increased in COPD-OSA overlap. We aimed to determine whether COPD-OSA overlap has a higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone.
METHODS: This was a matched cohort study using electronic health records from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum database (England). Exposures of interest were a diagnosis of COPD, OSA or both based on validated code lists. Our primary outcome of interest was cardiovascular mortality defined using ICD-10 codes. Our secondary outcomes of interest included: all-cause mortality, incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS), incident stroke and incident heart failure.
RESULTS: The initial study cohort consisted of 365 667 people with COPD (mean±sd) age 68±11 years, 59 526 with OSA age 57±11 years and 11 040 with COPD-OSA age 65±10 years. Cardiovascular mortality was significantly higher in patients with COPD-OSA overlap compared with OSA alone (adjusted hazard ratio 1.72 (1.58-1.88); p<0.001) but not compared with COPD alone. People with COPD-OSA overlap had 27% and 58% increased risk of developing ACS compared with COPD and OSA alone respectively, and 69% and 101% increased risk of developing heart failure compared with COPD and OSA respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: We have demonstrated that people with COPD-OSA overlap have a significantly higher cardiovascular burden compared with COPD or OSA alone with real-world implications. Earlier and targeted treatment with cardiovascular optimisation can potentially reduce downstream sequelae.

Title: Intraprocedural Angiographic Lung Perfusion: A Novel Application for Real-Time Integration Into a Fluoroscopic Platform.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment of differential lung perfusion is currently limited to periprocedural lung perfusion scans (LPS) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which do not enable for real-time decision making. This study demonstrates the development and evaluation of a novel angiographic lung perfusion (ALP) technique in patients with congenital heart disease.
METHODS: The ALP technique was used to analyze differential branch pulmonary artery (PA) flow in retrospectively identified PA angiograms with corresponding LPS or MRI. Intraclass correlation coefficient and agreement were assessed. Two mathematical models were tested (area under curve and slope) at 2 time points (second peak and average).
RESULTS: Twenty-five angiograms were analyzed. The most common cardiac anatomy was tetralogy of Fallot, and most common indication for catheterization was unilateral branch PA stenosis. The slope-based methods demonstrated high intraclass correlation coefficients with LPS/MRI (ICC, 0.84-0.86), indicating good reliability (ranging moderate-to-excellent), whereas Bland-Altman analysis showed low overall bias.
CONCLUSIONS: This ALP quantification application enables accurate lung perfusion assessment with potential for real-time integration into a fluoroscopic platform. This method provides a potential method for quantifying clinically meaningful intraprocedural information, particularly in assessing relative changes in differential perfusion before and after PA interventions. Further prospective studies are needed to confirm accuracy and clinical utility in broader populations.

Title: P-wave characteristics in Bayés syndrome predict feasibility of anterior mitral line ablation: The Left Anterior Bayés-Derived Mitral Linear Ablation Outcome and Conduction score.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bayés syndrome is characterized by a P-wave showing interatrial block (IAB) from impaired Bachmann bundle conduction. In patients without overt IAB, persistent epicardial conduction via the Bachmann bundle can hinder a successful completion of an anterior mitral line (AML) ablation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether preprocedural P-wave duration and inferior-lead P-wave morphology predict the feasibility of AML and to derive a preprocedural score.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed data of 69 consecutive patients who underwent AML radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation or tachycardia (May 2022-February 2026), of whom 57 met inclusion criteria. Preprocedural electrocardiograms in sinus rhythm were assessed for P wave. AML feasibility was classified as feasible or difficult. Firth penalized logistic regression and a random forest classifier identified predictors. The Left Anterior Bayés-Derived Mitral Linear ablation Outcome and Conduction (LA-BLOC) score was derived in the discovery cohort (n = 35) and evaluated in the temporal validation cohort (n = 22).
RESULTS: AML block was feasible in 24 patients and difficult in 11 of the discovery cohort. The feasible AML had longer P-wave duration (169 ± 28 ms vs 139 ± 31 ms; P = .012) and more frequent biphasic P waves in inferior leads. P-wave duration (continuous; area under the curve, 0.80), with a 130 ms receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, and P-wave morphology in II (odds ratio, 8.49; P = .008) were key predictors. The LA-BLOC score (P-wave duration, ≥130 ms = 1; biphasic P in II = 2 and in III = 1) with a threshold of ≥3 predicted AML feasibility (area under the curve, 0.94; sensitivity, 0.88; specificity, 1.00).
CONCLUSION: Preprocedural Bayés syndrome P-wave characteristics are associated with successful AML completion. The LA-BLOC score may facilitate preprocedural planning.

Title: Ultrasound-guided peripheral regional anesthesia vs local infiltration anesthesia for cardiac device implantation: A propensity score-matched prospective observational cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional local infiltration anesthesia (LIA) may not consistently provide adequate analgesia during cardiac device implantation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the analgesic efficacy of ultrasound-guided peripheral regional anesthesia (PRA) with LIA during cardiac device implantation.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center prospective observational cohort study including patients undergoing first-time cardiac device implantation. Data were collected in real time during routine clinical care. Patients received PRA or LIA according to routine clinical practice, as determined by the treating clinicians. Propensity score matching was performed to reduce selection bias, resulting in 48 matched patients per group. Pain intensity was assessed using a Numerical Rating Scale at predefined intraoperative procedural steps and postoperative time points, as part of standardized periprocedural care. Additional anesthetic supplementation, pain-related movement, and adverse events were recorded.
RESULTS: Among the matched patients (n = 96), pain scores at all 7 procedural steps were significantly lower in the PRA group than in the LIA group (all P < .01). In the LIA group, pain intensity peaked during pocket creation (all P < .05), whereas pain scores remained relatively consistent across procedural steps in the PRA group. Postoperative Numerical Rating Scale scores at 2-24 hours were significantly lower in the PRA group (all P < .05). Pain-related movement and additional anesthetic supplementation were less frequent in the PRA group. Adverse events were infrequent and comparable between groups.
CONCLUSION: In this propensity score-matched prospective observational cohort study, ultrasound-guided PRA was associated with improved periprocedural analgesia without an observed increase in adverse events.

Title: Cost-Effectiveness of Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for the treatment of intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE).
METHODS: A combined decision tree and Markov model was developed to estimate lifetime health care costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALY), and net monetary benefit from the perspective of the United States health care system. Event probabilities during PE management were derived from the PEERLESS randomized controlled trial. Resource utilization, costs, and long-term event probabilities were established from published literature. Scenario analyses and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed to characterize uncertainty.
RESULTS: In the base case analysis, LBMT was cost-saving to CDT (ie, lower costs and higher QALY), with a net monetary benefit of $5850 for the willingness-to-pay threshold of $120,000/QALY for LBMT when compared to CDT. In the PE management phase, LBMT yielded a net $4755 cost-saving and 0.009 QALY gained per patient vs CDT, driven in large part by reduced intensive care unit utilization (-$6454), shorter hospital stay (-$2217), avoided thrombolytic costs (-$4068), and fewer 30-day readmissions (-$1134). The long-term care phase yielded a total of $32,012 additional costs per patient over the lifetime with no incremental difference in costs or QALY between groups. These additional costs were driven by venous thromboembolism-related death ($12,377), chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension diagnosis and treatment ($8080), postacute anticoagulation management ($4512), and recurrent venous thromboembolism ($3289). LBMT remained cost-saving across scenarios evaluating CDT cost assumptions and device-specific chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension rates. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings across multiple parameter ranges.
CONCLUSIONS: Intervention with LBMT in intermediate-risk PE patients in the United States is economically attractive when compared with CDT, resulting in reduced costs and marginally improved patient benefit.

Title: Association Between β1-Selective Beta-Blocker Use and P-Wave Terminal Force in Lead V1 in Hypertensive Patients With Left Ventricular Hypertrophy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: P-wave terminal force in lead V1 (PTFV1) is an electrocardiographic marker of atrial electrical abnormality. We investigated whether β1-selective beta-blocker use was associated with PTFV1 in hypertensive patients with echocardiographically confirmed left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 182 eligible patients with essential hypertension and LVH selected from 1372 screened patients. Patients were classified as β1-selective beta-blocker users (n = 82) or nonusers (n = 100). Abnormal PTFV1 was defined as ≥ 0.04 mm s. Multivariable regression and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: PTFV1 was lower in beta-blocker users than in nonusers (0.024 [0.015-0.036] vs. 0.030 [0.020-0.048] mm s, p = 0.005). In the primary adjusted model, beta-blocker use was associated with lower PTFV1 (B = -0.008, standardized β = -0.202, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.002, p = 0.009), although model explanatory capacity was limited (R 2 = 0.064; adjusted R 2 = 0.021; overall p = 0.168). In an extended sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for diabetes, renal function, and concomitant antihypertensive therapies, beta-blocker group status remained associated with lnPTFV1 (standardized β = 0.294, p < 0.001; R 2 = 0.147; adjusted R 2 = 0.081; overall p = 0.011). Beta-blocker use was also associated with lower odds of abnormal PTFV1 (OR = 0.43, 95% CI 0.22-0.84, p = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: β1-Selective beta-blocker use was associated with lower PTFV1 and a lower likelihood of abnormal PTFV1. These findings suggest a more favorable atrial electrical profile but should be considered hypothesis-generating given the retrospective design and modest model explanatory capacity.

Title: Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Meta-analysis.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conflicting randomized trial results have generated uncertainty regarding percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) vs oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF). Thus, the objective of this study is to estimate the posterior probability that LAAO confers clinically meaningful excess ischemic stroke risk relative to OAC.
METHODS: A Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis was performed of RCT comparing LAAO with OAC in nonvalvular AF. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke, analyzed using Bayesian random-effects Poisson regression under a vague (primary), skeptical, and enthusiastic prior specification.
RESULTS: Six RCT (7004 patients, +18,000 patient-years) were included. Ischemic stroke incidence rate ratio (IRR) was 1.34 (95% credible interval [CrI], 0.91-1.97; P [IRR > 1.0] = 94%). The probability of exceeding 0.5 and 1.0 excess events/100 patient-years was 12% and 0.5%, respectively. The effect on any-stroke was smaller (IRR, 1.09; 95% CrI, 0.76-1.56; P [IRR > 1.0] = 70%; P [absolute rate difference >0.5%/y] = 4.7%), because of a reduction in hemorrhagic stroke (IRR, 0.55; 95% CrI, 0.23-1.18; P [IRR < 1.0] = 94.5%). The decrease in hemorrhagic stroke was attenuated among trials using direct oral anticoagulants for medical management (IRR, 0.80; 95% CrI, 0.33-1.75).
CONCLUSIONS: In AF, there is a high posterior probability that LAAO is associated with a higher rate of any-stroke, driven by an increase in ischemic stroke relative to OAC. However, the 95% CrI for ischemic stroke crossed unity, and the estimated absolute excess is small. This possible excess must be weighed against a substantial reduction in the risk of hemorrhagic stroke.

Title: Heart failure-related pleural effusion: determinants of pleural drainage and predictors of mortality in a cohort of 1372 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is one of the most common causes of pleural effusion, yet data on its management and prognosis in patients undergoing diagnostic thoracentesis are limited. The significance of invasive pleural interventions remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained pleural database, including consecutive patients with HF-related pleural effusion who underwent diagnostic thoracentesis. Clinical characteristics, pleural findings, need for invasive pleural management (therapeutic thoracentesis or indwelling pleural catheter (IPC)), and mortality were assessed. Fine-Gray competing-risk models and Cox regression were applied.
RESULTS: A total of 1372 patients were included (median age 85 years). During follow-up, 726 (53%) patients required at least one therapeutic thoracentesis and 81 (6%) received an IPC. In the competing-risk analysis, effusion size equal to or more than half hemithorax (sudistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 2.33), bilateral effusion (sHR 1.37), pleural fluid albumin >1.2 g·dL-1 (sHR 1.23), and male sex (sHR 1.20) were independently associated with invasive pleural management. Median survival was 14 months, with mortality rates of 50% at 1 year and 70% at 2 years. Mortality was independently associated with advanced age, elevated serum N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, renal dysfunction, and hypoalbuminemia, whereas pleural characteristics and invasive pleural management were not.
CONCLUSION: In patients with HF-related pleural effusion undergoing diagnostic thoracentesis, mortality is high and primarily driven by systemic markers of advanced HF. Invasive pleural interventions are frequently required in patients with large or bilateral effusions. In descriptive comparisons, survival was similar regardless of pleural intervention status, although causal inference is precluded by the observational design and time-dependent nature of intervention.

Title: Uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio and incident vascular calcification in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) is a composite marker that has been associated with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in individuals with diabetes mellitus (DM). However, evidence on the association between UHR and vascular calcification (VC) remains limited and is derived primarily from cross-sectional studies of abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) in the general population. Whether UHR is associated with incident VC in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unclear, and longitudinal evidence in this population is lacking.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 767 hospitalized adults with T2DM who showed no evidence of VC on their initial chest computed tomography (CT). UHR was calculated using serum uric acid (SUA) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) concentrations measured during the first hospitalization. Incident coronary and/or aortic calcification was identified on follow-up chest CT examinations. The association between UHR and incident VC was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests, multivariable Cox regression models, restricted cubic spline analysis, exploratory piecewise Cox regression, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses incorporating log-transformed UHR.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 25 months (IQR, 11-53), 351 participants (45.8%) developed incident VC. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-standard deviation (SD) increase in UHR was associated with a 24.5% higher hazard of incident VC (hazard ratio, 1.245; 95% confidence interval, 1.117-1.387; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, the adjusted HRs for Q2, Q3, and Q4 were 1.636, 1.921, and 1.876, respectively (P for trend < 0.001), although the quartile-specific estimates did not follow a strictly monotonic pattern. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall association between UHR and incident VC (P for overall < 0.001), whereas the test for nonlinearity was not statistically significant (P for nonlinearity = 0.058). No significant interactions were observed in prespecified subgroup analyses, and the findings remained robust across sensitivity analyses, including analysis using log-transformed UHR.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher UHR was associated with a greater hazard of incident coronary and/or aortic calcification in patients with T2DM. These findings extend previous cross-sectional evidence by providing longitudinal data and warrant further evaluation of UHR as a potential marker of VC risk.

Title: Olipudase alfa for acid sphingomyelinase deficiency: Evidence of efficacy from a compassionate use program.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the SMPD1 gene, leading to systemic accumulation of sphingomyelin, primarily affecting the liver, spleen, lungs, and central nervous system (CNS). Olipudase alfa represents the first approved enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) targeting the non-neurological manifestations of ASMD. This study evaluates real-world safety and efficacy data of olipudase alfa in a cohort of Italian patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical, radiological, and laboratory data from 8 Italian patients (5 pediatric, 3 adult) with chronic visceral or chronic neurovisceral ASMD. All patients received olipudase alfa through a compassionate use program between December 2021 and November 2023. Data was collected at baseline, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 months of treatment.
RESULTS: At baseline, the cohort exhibited hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial lung disease, dyslipidemia, cytopenias, and hypertransaminasemia. Treatment led to significant improvements in hematological parameters, lipid profiles, and liver enzymes. A marked reduction in lyso-sphingomyelin levels was observed, alongside a decrease in spleen and liver volumes. Pulmonary function either improved or remained stable in most patients. While seven patients showed a robust response, one individual exhibited a suboptimal clinical and biochemical clinical outcome. Overall, the therapy was well-tolerated, with a favorable safety profile and few adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, olipudase alfa was safe and effective in improving clinical and biochemical markers of ASMD, consistent with results from pivotal clinical trials. However, the observed variability in individual responses emphasizes the importance of personalized monitoring and tailored management strategies.

Title: Prenatal and Postnatal Screening for Congenital Heart Disease: Prevalence and Detection Patterns From a Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the prevalence and detection patterns of prenatal and postnatal screening for congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University between 2018 and 2020. Pregnant women with complete prenatal and postnatal follow-up data were recruited for final analysis. Prenatal and postnatal screening for CHD included mid-trimester fetal cardiac ultrasound at 20-24 gestational weeks, neonatal pulse oximetry and cardiac auscultation 6-72 hours after birth, and at a 42-day postnatal visit.
RESULTS: Of 21,920 fetuses or neonates (including 548 twin pregnancies), 318 CHD cases were identified. The annual prevalence of CHD was 14.5 per 1000 births. CHD was associated with a higher proportion of male gender in infants, preterm birth, low birth weight, and multiple pregnancy (P < 0.001). Of the 318 CHD cases, 270 (84.9%) were simple CHD and 48 (15.1%) were complex CHD (most common was tetralogy of Fallot, coarctation of the aorta). Overall, 40.6% (129/318) of CHD cases were diagnosed prenatally, and 59.4% (189/318) were diagnosed postnatally. The prenatal diagnosis rate for complex CHD was 89.6% (43/48), whereas 68.1% (184/270) of simple CHD cases were diagnosed postnatally. The annual pattern was consistent between 2018 and 2020 (χ 2 = 0.2245, P = 0.894).
CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate the application of a combined prenatal and postnatal screening strategy for comprehensive CHD detection. Prenatal screening for CHD achieved high levels of efficacy for complex CHD with a detection rate of 89.6%. Sequential newborn screening was crucial for identifying simple CHD with a postnatal detection rate of 68.1%. Our findings indicate that prenatal and postnatal detection pattern vary by CHD complexity.

Title: Incidence of traumatic injuries sustained following cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest compressions form the basis of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in out of hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Recently, mechanical CPR (MCPR) devices have been introduced, particularly in the prehospital environment, avoiding the need for clinicians to perform conventional manual CPR (CCPR). At our institution, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is available for select OHCA patients in refractory arrest (ECPR). Given ECPR patients typically undergo prolonged chest compressions, there may be a higher likelihood of injury; however, evidence directly comparing ECPR and CCPR injury rates is lacking. This study aimed to investigate incidence and type of traumatic injuries following CPR and whether a difference between ECPR and CCPR patients exists.
RESULTS: 313 OHCA were identified between 2021-2024, with 136 meeting criteria. Mean CPR duration was 24 ± 16 min, and 37 patients (27%) received MCPR. Thirteen patients had ECPR with mean time from cardiac arrest to establishment of ECMO blood flow being 63 ± 18 min, of which 11 (85%) received MCPR. Injuries occurred in 58 patients (43%), with 23 (16.9%) sustaining clinically significant injuries. Rates of mortality were higher for the injured patients compared to the non-injured patients (41 [70%] vs 33 [43%] respectively, p = ≤0.05). On multiple variable logistic regression analysis CPR > 20 min, not ECPR or MCPR, was significantly associated with traumatic injury (OR 2.45, CI 1.15, 5.23, p = ≤0.05).
CONCLUSION: CPR-related injuries are common. CPR >20 min, not ECPR or MCPR, is associated with higher rate of injury. CT imaging in this cohort could be considered to identify these injuries.

Title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a recognized comorbidity in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF); however, its true prevalence remains uncertain, and its prognostic implications have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of and risk factors for OSA in patients with IPF and to evaluate its impact on disease progression.
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 50 patients with IPF followed at a tertiary care center. All patients underwent polysomnography (PSG), and OSA was classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The Berlin Questionnaire and the Epworth Sleepiness Scale were administered prior to PSG. Forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) were measured at baseline and at 1 year. Disease progression was defined as a ≥10% decline in FVC and/or a ≥15% decline in DLCO.
RESULTS: The mean age was 67.8 ± 6.7 years, and 80% were male. OSA prevalence was 90.0% (95% confidence interval: 78.2-96.7), with mild, moderate, and severe disease each present in 30% of patients. Moderate-to-severe OSA was associated with significantly greater pulmonary function decline (P = 0.030). Hypertension and high-risk status on the Berlin Questionnaire were significantly associated with the presence of OSA.
CONCLUSIONS: OSA prevalence in IPF is remarkably high, with the majority having moderate-to-severe disease. The Berlin Questionnaire may serve as a reliable screening tool for PSG candidacy in this population. These findings suggest that OSA may contribute to functional disease progression in patients with IPF.

Title: Associated Factors of In-hospital Mortality in Adult Burn Patients: A Five-Year Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although comorbidities are recognized as important prognostic factors in burn patients, the impact of individual comorbidities and associated trauma on treatment outcomes has not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between individual comorbidities, the presence of comorbidities, associated trauma, and treatment outcomes in adult burn patients.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among all eligible adult burn patients (aged ≥18 years) admitted to Le Huu Trac National Burn Hospital, Vietnam, between January 2021 and December 2025. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Demographic characteristics, burn characteristics, comorbidities, and associated trauma were extracted from the electronic medical records. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with the study outcomes.
RESULTS: The study included 6653 adult burn patients with median age of 40 (interquartile range (IQR): 31 - 52) years (73.94% male). Among adult burn patients, hypertension and diabetes mellitus were the most common comorbidities (3.01% and 2.80%, respectively). The presence of comorbidities was an independent predictor of both complications and mortality (odds ratio (OR) = 1.926, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.180-3.144, p = 0.009; and OR = 1.785, 95% CI: 1.057-3.014, p = 0.030, respectively), along with age, total burn size, full-thickness burn size, and inhalation injury (all p < 0.001). Chronic pulmonary disease (OR = 11.371, 95% CI: 2.972-43.498, p < 0.001) and paralysis (OR = 3.451, 95% CI: 1.085-10.976, p = 0.036) remained independent predictors of mortality. Associated trauma was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: Comorbidities were independently associated with both complications and mortality in adult burn patients. Chronic pulmonary disease and paralysis were identified as independent prognostic factors for mortality. Although associated trauma was not independently associated with mortality, it was independently associated with a prolonged hospital stay.

Title: Transition readiness in adolescents with congenital heart disease during transfer to adult care: A secondary analysis of the STEPSTONES randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk of discontinuity of care during transfer from pediatric to adult services. Transition readiness is considered essential for a safe transfer. This study evaluated the effect of the STEPSTONES person-centered transition program on adolescents' self-reported transition readiness compared with usual care.
DESIGN AND METHODS: This secondary analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial conducted at two Swedish CHD centers. A total of 139 adolescents (age 16 years) were randomized to intervention (n = 70) or usual care (n = 69). The intervention group received the STEPSTONES program in addition to usual care over two years. Transition readiness was assessed at ages 16 (T0), 17 (T1), and 18.5 (T2) using the Readiness for Transition Questionnaire. Between-group differences were analyzed with Mann-Whitney U tests, and longitudinal changes were examined using mixed-design ANOVA.
RESULTS: At T2, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher overall transition readiness compared with controls (p = .011-.015), with a small effect size (r ≈ .23-.24). A significant main effect of time was found (p < .001), indicating increased readiness across adolescence in both groups. No significant group-by-time interaction was detected (p = .177), and no differences were identified at the level of individual questionnaire items.
CONCLUSIONS: The STEPSTONES program was associated with higher overall transition readiness at the time of transfer, although effect sizes were small. Structured, person-centered transition programs may enhance preparedness for adult care.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Pediatric nurses are key in supporting transition readiness. Structured transition programs may strengthen adolescents' overall preparedness for adult-oriented healthcare.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02675361.

Title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Salt and Amiloride on Vascular Stiffness in ADPKD.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) often develop early vascular stiffening and hypertension. Dietary sodium may worsen vascular stiffness via epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) activation, and ENaC inhibition might mitigate this, but this remains untested in ADPKD. We hypothesized that dietary sodium loading increases vascular stiffness in ADPKD and that the ENaC inhibitor amiloride attenuates this effect.
METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, adults with ADPKD and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥60 ml/min per 1.73 m2 completed a 2-week low-salt run-in (≤ 3.5 g/d), then were randomized 1:1 to oral sodium chloride capsules (6 g/d) or placebo for 2 weeks, followed by a 2-week open-label amiloride (20 mg/d) add-on phase in both arms. The primary outcome was pulse wave velocity (PWV). Secondary outcomes included 24-hour blood pressure (BP) and biochemical parameters.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven participants (mean age 39 ± 11 years, eGFR 89 ± 19 ml/min per 1.73 m2) were randomized to salt (n = 19) or placebo (n = 18). Salt supplementation increased PWV (6.5 ± 0.9 m/s to 6.8 ± 1.1 m/s, P = 0.02) and 24-hour systolic BP (133 ± 13 mm Hg to 138 ± 15 mm Hg, P = 0.02). Amiloride did not reduce PWV in either group, but decreased systolic BP only in the low-salt group (135 ± 11 to 130 ± 13 mm Hg, P = 0.03). Plasma potassium increased modestly in both groups following amiloride, without hyperkalemia.
CONCLUSION: In this small, short-term trial, dietary sodium significantly increased vascular stiffness and BP in early ADPKD, and amiloride significantly lowered BP only under low-salt conditions. These findings support dietary sodium restriction as a practical strategy for BP and vascular protection in early ADPKD.

Title: Circulating Soluble EGFR Correlates with Tumor Burden and Hepatic Reserve but Lacks Independent Prognostic Value in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Prospective Turkish Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Serum soluble epidermal growth factor receptor (sEGFR) is a circulating extracellular-domain EGFR fragment that is biologically distinct from membrane-bound tissue EGFR, and its clinical meaning in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has not been defined. We evaluated whether baseline serum sEGFR is related to tumor burden and hepatic reserve, and whether it carries prognostic information independent of established clinical variables.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center cohort included 84 patients with HCC evaluated between November 2014 and May 2017. Baseline serum sEGFR was measured by ELISA. Overall survival (OS) was defined from baseline serum sample collection to death from any cause or last follow-up and was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, lg-rank testing, and Cox proportional hazards models with bootstrap internal validation. The incremental value of sEGFR over alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and MELD-Na was tested in a combined model.
RESULTS: Lower serum sEGFR was associated with larger tumor size, higher AFP, higher aspartate aminotransferase and bilirubin levels, worse MELD-Na and Child-Turcotte-Pugh scores, lower insulin-like growth factor-1, and distant metastasis. Patients with sEGFR ≤13 ng/mL had shorter median OS than those with sEGFR >13 ng/mL (5.4 vs 12.1 months; log-rank p=0.0027; univariable HR 2.06, 95% CI 1.27-3.34). After adjustment for tumor size, log-transformed AFP, MELD-Na, portal vein thrombosis, and age, sEGFR was not associated with OS (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.03, p=0.69), and the estimate remained close to the null across 1000 bootstrap resamples. Adding continuous sEGFR to a model containing AFP and MELD-Na did not improve discrimination (C-index 0.657 vs 0.656).
CONCLUSION: Low serum sEGFR identifies an adverse tumor-liver phenotype and shorter unadjusted survival, but it is not an independent prognostic factor and adds no discriminative information beyond AFP and MELD-Na. Serum sEGFR is best regarded as a marker of disease phenotype; it does not perform as a stand-alone prognostic test.

Title: Short-term effects of an SGLT2 inhibitor on divalent ions in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease therapy, reducing disease progression, cardiovascular events, and mortality. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) patients were excluded from major trials, and data on electrolyte handling with SGLT2 inhibitors, in combination with tolvaptan, are lacking.
METHODS: SIDIA was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial in 15 adults with ADPKD (mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 68 ml/min/1.73 m²; median age 43 years). Participants received empagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for 14 days, separated by a 2-week washout. The primary endpoint was 24 h urinary and fractional excretion of phosphate, calcium, and magnesium. Exploratory secondary endpoints included markers of kidney stone propensity, inflammation, vitamin D metabolism, and tolerability. Treatment effects were estimated using generalized linear mixed models. Given the small sample size, analyses were exploratory and focused on effect estimation.
RESULTS: For the primary endpoint, neither 24 h urinary nor fractional excretion of phosphate, calcium, or magnesium differed between empagliflozin and placebo. Empagliflozin lowered serum uric acid (-26%), increased serum magnesium (+5.7%) and urinary citrate (+78.6%), and reduced blood pressure (-4/-7 mmHg). An expected decline in eGFR (-7.1%) was observed, with no major short-term safety signals observed. Copeptin levels increased with empagliflozin (+26%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory mechanistic trial, no substantial short-term difference in urinary or fractional excretion of divalent ions were detected with empagliflozin. The observed changes in serum magnesium, urinary citrate, uric acid, and copeptin are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, longer-term studies.

Title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559).
CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

Title: Predicting spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery: what is being predicted, and when.
Abstract: Spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery has generated a large prediction literature, but the term "prediction" is applied to signals obtained at very different points in the peri-spinal course. Most reviews group predictors by physiology or device. Here we organize them by when the signal becomes available and which clinical decision remains open. This changes how reported performance should be interpreted. A preoperative low-frequency/high-frequency heart rate variability threshold of 2.5, for example, showed only 35% sensitivity and discrimination around 0.60 in an independent cohort, whereas small development studies of other preoperative tools have reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve approaching 0.9. Pre-spinal provocation may improve discrimination while preserving time to adjust prophylaxis. Measurements obtained after intrathecal injection, and real-time algorithms operating minutes before hypotension, answer a different question because sympathetic blockade is already evolving and the decision window is narrower. Variation in hypotension definitions, treatment background, case mix, and small development samples further limits direct comparison. Routine vasopressor prophylaxis also changes what a useful predictor should do: rather than decide who receives prevention, it should help identify who needs earlier, stronger, or differently titrated treatment. Two randomized cesarean trials now support Hypotension Prediction Index-guided management, while treatment-impact evidence for true preoperative prediction remains limited.

Title: Multi-omics insights into immune dysregulation and candidate biological programs in kawasaki disease: toward precision immunomodulation.
Abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an immune-mediated pediatric vasculitis characterized by dynamic interactions among genetic susceptibility, innate and adaptive immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular remodeling. Although intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy substantially reduces coronary complications, 10%-20% of patients show persistent or recurrent fever after initial IVIG treatment, and reliable clinically validated molecular approaches for diagnosis, treatment-response prediction, and coronary-risk stratification remain unavailable. Recent advances in multi-omics technologies, including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome profiling, have expanded our understanding of KD-associated immune dysregulation. However, the clinical interpretation of these molecular findings remains challenging because of limited cohort sizes, heterogeneous control populations, treatment-related confounding, and insufficient external validation. In this review, we integrate evidence across multiple molecular layers and propose a framework in which current KD multi-omics findings converge into candidate biological programs rather than fixed molecular subtypes. These programs may represent temporally dynamic biological states along a shared inflammatory trajectory, influenced by disease phase, cellular composition, genetic background, and treatment exposure. Synthesized from convergent multi-omics evidence rather than derived from formal molecular classification, these candidate biological programs include myeloid inflammatory activation characterized by S100A8/A9 and IL-1/NF-κB signaling, interferon-associated immune responses, and vascular injury/remodeling responses involving endothelial activation and extracellular matrix regulation. Current evidence supports biologically meaningful molecular programs that may contribute to clinical heterogeneity, but prospective validation is required before molecular signatures can be applied as clinical classifiers or treatment-selection tools. Integrating multi-omics approaches with functional validation, longitudinal sampling, and multicenter studies may facilitate the development of precision immunomodulation strategies for Kawasaki disease.

Title: Botulinum toxin type a within function-oriented management of post-stroke spasticity: a narrative review.
Abstract: Post-stroke spasticity (PSS) is a heterogeneous complication of stroke that affects motor recovery, care needs, pain, positioning, and participation in daily life. Current management frameworks commonly stratify patients by time since stroke, but disease duration alone does not capture differences in neural mechanisms, residual voluntary control, functional priorities, or response to intervention. This narrative review searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Wanfang databases from inception to May 2026, prioritizing randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, systematic reviews, real-world studies, Goal Attainment Scaling research, the Upper Limb International Spasticity cohort series, best-practice guidance, and clinical trials including BEST and InTENSE. We synthesize evidence that PSS heterogeneity can be understood across central and peripheral mechanisms, temporal trajectories, and active versus passive functional consequences. Available studies suggest that active and passive functional goals differ in baseline functional profiles, outcome assessment, treatment response, and intervention requirements. However, patients sharing a functional goal type may still differ in residual voluntary control, neural and non-neural contributors to movement restriction, pain, mobility, and care dependency. Botulinum toxin type A is well aligned with focal tone reduction and passive goals, including pain relief, hygiene, and limb positioning. It may also support contracture-prevention strategies when modifiable neural muscle overactivity remains, whereas active functional gains usually require preserved motor potential and integration with task-oriented training, rehabilitation, and adjunctive modalities. We propose that functional goal type should complement time-based staging as a decision dimension rather than serve as a complete clinical phenotype. This combined framework may better align patient selection, intervention matching, outcome assessment, and longitudinal treatment planning. Prospective goal-stratified studies and standardized assessment tools are needed to test its clinical utility.

Title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional.
PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728).
EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3).
OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis.
METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated.
RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women.
CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

Title: Beyond the skin surface: untangling sensitive skin syndrome and peripheral neuropathy through an exploratory real-world data analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sensitive skin syndrome (SSS) is commonly reported despite its nonspecific definition, whereas peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains underrecognized in the general population. Because localized paresthesia and numbness-particularly in the hands and feet-may be perceived as skin problems, some patients reporting sensitive skin could have unrecognized neuropathy. This exploratory real-world evidence study investigated the potential overlap between SSS and PN.
METHODS: Patient-level real-world data from health records of individuals reporting sensitive skin were analyzed to characterize associated diagnoses, symptoms, comorbidities, and risk factors potentially related to PN.
RESULTS: Diagnoses among patients reporting sensitive skin included dermatitis (44%), altered skin sensation (33%), dry skin or urticaria (15%), and acne (13%). Within the group diagnosed with altered skin sensation, 18% reported paresthesia or tingling, 11% reported anesthesia or numbness, and 4% reported other symptoms. Documented comorbidities and risk factors included established contributors to PN, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and smoking.
DISCUSSION: The findings suggest a potential diagnostic overlap between SSS and PN and raise the hypothesis that some patients with altered skin sensation may have unrecognized PN. They also demonstrate how real-world data can reveal symptom patterns that may be overlooked during routine clinical assessment. Because the hypothesis arose from the same dataset used to explore it, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation. Nevertheless, timely differentiation between SSS and PN could facilitate appropriate clinical evaluation and improve patient health and well-being.

Title: P2Y12 inhibition, adenosine signaling, and bone remodeling: differential skeletal pharmacology of antiplatelet agents.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, and fragility fractures frequently coexist in older adults, creating an important overlap between antiplatelet therapy and orthopedic care. This narrative review examines mechanistic, preclinical, observational, and perioperative evidence concerning the skeletal effects of aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors, and other clinically relevant antiplatelet agents. Purinergic signaling provides biological plausibility for interactions between platelet inhibition and bone remodeling because P2Y12, P2Y1, P2X7, adenosine receptors, and equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 (ENT1) regulate osteoblast differentiation, osteoclast activity, inflammatory responses, and tissue repair. Aspirin shows dose- and context-dependent skeletal effects, whereas clopidogrel has been associated with impaired osteoblast mineralization in preclinical studies and conflicting fracture-risk estimates in observational cohorts. Direct skeletal evidence for prasugrel and other agents remains limited. Selected preclinical studies suggest that ticagrelor-associated ENT1 inhibition can enhance adenosine-dependent osteogenic signaling; however, clinical evidence is limited to one retrospective cohort in which ticagrelor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was associated with lower fracture risk than clopidogrel-based DAPT, while prospective skeletal outcome data are lacking. Perioperative antiplatelet management in orthopedic surgery should remain guided by cardiovascular indications, thrombotic risk, and bleeding risk. A conceptual framework may help define priorities for evaluating skeletal outcomes during antiplatelet therapy. However, current evidence is insufficient to support antiplatelet selection or switching on the basis of presumed skeletal effects.

Title: Ostial vs Left Main Crossover Stenting in Isolated Ostial Left Anterior Descending Stenosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on the optimal stenting strategy for isolated ostial left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) lesions. The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes in patients who had a significant isolated ostial LAD stenosis treated with either left main crossover stenting (LMCS) or focal ostial LAD stenting (FO-LAD).
METHODS: The primary end point of the study was target lesion failure (TLF), a composite of target lesion revascularization, target vessel myocardial infarction, and cardiac death at 2 years. Secondary end points included the individual components of the primary outcome. Additional secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events, which are a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, and any unplanned revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 522 patients were included in this study, of whom 382 underwent FO-LAD stenting and 140 underwent LMCS. The primary outcome occurred in 32 patients (22.9%) in the LMCS and in 44 patients (11.5%) in the FO-LAD group at a median follow-up of 730 days (IQR, 451-730). LMCS was associated with a higher risk of TLF compared with FO-LAD stenting (adjusted HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.16-2.98; P = .01).With regard to secondary outcomes, LMCS was associated with more major adverse cardiovascular events (31.4% vs 15.5%; adjusted HR, 2.11 [1.41-3.17]; P < .001) and cardiac death (17.1% vs 7.9%; adjusted HR, 2.05 [1.19-3.55]; P = .01]. No significant differences were observed for target lesion revascularization and target vessel myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSIONS: Left main crossover stenting was associated with a higher rate of TLF at a median follow-up of 2 years when compared with FO-LAD stenting in the treatment of patients with significant isolated ostial LAD disease.

Title: Outcomes of Surgical Versus Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair or Replacement in Patients With Myocardial Infarction and Concomitant Mitral Regurgitation: A Retrospective Analysis of Real-World Data.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

Title: Impact of a Continuous Quality Improvement Committee on Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) programs aim to enhance procedural safety and efficiency in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This analysis evaluates changes in PCI practice patterns and outcomes after implementation of a multidisciplinary catheterization laboratory CQI committee at a large academic center.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted regarding PCI procedures from January 2018 to June 2024 using National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI data. Outcomes and practice patterns were compared before (pre-CQI: 2018-October 2022) versus after CQI implementation (post-CQI: November 2022-2024). Prespecified primary end points were post-PCI acute kidney injury, periprocedural hemoglobin change, and same-day discharge.
RESULTS: Among 2759 PCI cases (1783 pre-CQI; 976 post-CQI), monthly PCI volume increased (30.7-48.2 cases/mo, P < .001). Post-CQI, radial access use increased (33.4%-58.9%, P < .001) and mean contrast volume decreased (188-153 mL, P < .001). Primary outcomes improved post-CQI: acute kidney injury decreased (14.3%-9.7%, P = .01), mean periprocedural hemoglobin change decreased (0.65-0.54 g/dL, P = .004), and same-day discharge increased (13.0%-24.7%, P < .001). Overall complication rates and in-hospital mortality remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a catheterization laboratory CQI committee was temporally associated with improved PCI safety and discharge efficiency alongside increased procedural volume and evolving case mix. These findings support CQI-driven approaches to optimize PCI care delivery.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Concurrent Impella-Assisted High-Risk PCI and TAVR in Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Aortic Stenosis.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous management of high risk, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) needing mechanical support for complex coronary artery disease in patients needing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis remains incompletely defined. We report on the feasibility and safety of a single-session strategy using Impella-assisted complex high-risk PCI (IA-CHIP) followed by transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing simultaneous IA-CHIP and TAVR at 3 tertiary centers between January 2015 and March 2026. All patients received mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous microaxial flow pump Impella CP (Abiomed) during PCI, followed by transfemoral TAVR in the same session. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was in-hospital complications, including death, stroke, major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 2, 3, or 5), acute kidney injury, permanent pacemaker implantation, and vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 12 patients were included (median age, 79.5 years [IQR, 77.0-81.2]; 91.7% male; median Charlson Comorbidity Index of 7 [IQR, 5.8-9]). Coronary lesions mainly involved left main disease in 66% of cases. Advanced calcium modification was required in 50% of cases. The median aortic valve area was 0.86 cm2, and median mean gradient was 38 mm Hg. Procedural success for IA-CHIP and TAVR was 100%. There were no in-hospital deaths, strokes, or major vascular complications. Conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 25%. An acute kidney injury occurred in 16.7% of cases, with no requirement for dialysis. The majority of patients (91.7%) were discharged home.
CONCLUSIONS: A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.

Title: Clinical Efficacy of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Diabetes: A Global Retrospective Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), a standard therapy for aortic stenosis, is preferred for older or high-risk patients. Various complications, including heart failure (HF), resulting in increased mortality, have been reported in the literature. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are recommended in HF, irrespective of ejection fraction; however, their role in reducing post-TAVR cardiovascular complications remains underexplored. We conducted a retrospective study to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes associated with the use of SGLT2i in post-TAVR patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort was based on a global database of electronic health records of more than 160 million patients. After propensity-score matching, the study population included 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients divided into 2 cohorts based on their exposure to SGLT2i. Exposure to SGLT2i was defined as exposure after 1 day of TAVR.
RESULTS: In this study of 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients, the primary outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events and secondary outcomes, ie, cardiovascular mortality, ischemic stroke, and HF exacerbation, were significantly reduced in SGLT2i-exposed post-TAVR patients at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up. Hemorrhagic stroke was comparable at the 1-month follow-up; however, it was significantly lower in SGLT2i-exposed cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. The risk of new-onset myocardial infarction was significantly reduced at 1 month; however, it was comparable between the 2 cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. Our study also demonstrated a significant reduction in the risk of end-stage renal disease in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort at the 1-year follow-up. The periprocedural risk of acute kidney injury (within 7 days of TAVR) as well as at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up was significantly lower in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, post-TAVR SGLT2i use in diabetic patients was associated with reduced cardiovascular morbidity and mortality for up to 1 year.

Title: Health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Health literacy is a key social determinant of health. Adequate health literacy has been associated with better obstetric and general adult health outcomes. However, its relationship with cardiovascular health during and after pregnancy is not well known. We aimed to estimate associations between health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-be (nuMoM2b) study and its prospective follow-up phase, the nuMoM2b Heart Health Study. Participants who completed the Rapid Estimate of Adult Literacy in Medicine-Short Form (REALM-SF) in the second trimester (16-21 weeks of gestation) and a 2-7 year postpartum study visit were included. Health literacy was classified as inadequate (REALM-SF score <7) or adequate (≥7) using standard scoring procedures. The primary outcomes were cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and 2-7 years after the first birth, assessed using a modified Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score, which includes health behaviors (diet, physical activity, sleep health, and nicotine exposure) and health factors (body mass index, blood pressure, blood glucose, and lipid levels). Secondary outcomes included LE8 subcomponents. Multivariable linear regression models, which adjusted for maternal age, insurance type, and family income, were used to evaluate associations of health literacy with LE8 overall scores and its subcomponents.
RESULTS: Among 4424 participants eligible for analysis, 3599 (81.4%) had adequate health literacy. Those with adequate health literacy were older, more likely to identify as non-Hispanic White, and more likely to have higher income, higher education, and private insurance coverage. Participants with adequate health literacy had higher early pregnancy LE8 scores (79.9 ± 13.3 vs. 73.0 ± 14.2, p < 0.001), a relationship that persisted after adjustment (aβ 3.6, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8-5.4). This association was driven by body mass index, diet, physical activity, and sleep subcomponents. Similarly, LE8 scores 2-7 years after birth were higher among those with adequate health literacy (80.1 ± 13.8 vs. 72.9 ± 14.6, p < 0.001; aβ 3.2, 95%, CI, 0.8-5.6), primarily due to healthier measures of body mass index, diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, and sleep.
CONCLUSION: Among nulliparous women, adequate health literacy scores in early pregnancy were associated with better cardiovascular health during pregnancy and several years after first birth.

Title: Associations of cardiac autonomic modulation and urinary adrenal hormones with marathon finishing time in middle-aged male athletes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The autonomic nervous and endocrine systems are involved in the physiological adaptation to exercise, and in experimental settings both the sympathovagal balance and the adrenal function are associated with athletic performance. In this real-life field study, the association between non-invasive markers of cardiac autonomic modulation, urinary adrenal hormone levels, and marathon finishing time in middle-aged Caucasian male athletes was investigated.
METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in male marathon runners aged ≥30 years. Continuous single-lead electrocardiographic (ECG) recordings were obtained using a wearable chest device from the day before the marathon until after its completion. Urinary adrenal hormone levels were measured before and after the race. Univariate linear regression analyses were performed to correlate general characteristics, nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV) parameters, and hormonal parameters with marathon finishing time. A multivariable model was then applied including age, body mass index (BMI), and training hours.
RESULTS: 104 athletes were enrolled in the study and 73 (median age 48 years, interquartile range = 16) had adequate data quality for the final analysis. Several HRV parameters correlated with better performance at univariate analysis; lower minimum nocturnal heart rate and vagal predominance, expressed as higher 2 Like Variations (2LV) values remained independently associated with shorter finishing time. Among hormonal variables, the post-/pre-race ratio of urinary normetanephrine hourly output and cortisol/cortisone ratio remained significant at multivariable analysis. Only BMI, but not age and training history, remained significant in a model integrating HRV and hormones.
CONCLUSIONS: Under real-world marathon conditions, specific HRV indices and endocrine markers showed promising value as indicators of physiological readiness with endurance exercise in male master athletes.

Title: Sex differences in electrocardiographic patterns among patients with acute coronary syndromes.
Abstract: Sex-based differences in ACS presentation and outcomes have been observed, but limited information is available on sex-specific electrocardiogram (ECG) features and their prevalence in this context. The aim of this study was to compare the prevalence of different ECG patterns between sexes and their prognostic roles for in-hospital mortality in ACS patients. This prospective single-center study (NCT02438085)° was conducted from June 2018 to December 2019, including 841 consecutive patients. Data on baseline characteristics, ECG findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected. Statistical analyses were performed to determine differences in the prevalence of various ECG patterns and identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. Males more frequently presented with ST-segment elevation (51% vs. 43%, p = 0.031) and hyperacute T waves (13% vs. 7%, p = 0.006) than females. Moreover, females more often had a normal ECG at admission (15% vs. 9%, p = 0.01). In female STEMI negative T waves (50% vs. 38%, p = 0.025) were more common than in males. Hyperacute T waves were linked to a higher risk of in-hospital death in female STEMI cases (OR=6.25, 95% CI: 1.0 -39.7, p = 0.048). Additionally the development of left bundle branch block during hospitalization (OR=14.4, 95% CI: 1.48-14 p = 0.02) was a significant predictor of in-hospital mortality in the female NSTEMI subgroup. No ECG features were found to predict in-hospital mortality in male patients. Compared to males, females with ACS often showed less frequent and less extensive ST-segment abnormalities and were more likely to have a normal initial ECG at admission. These differences could impact clinical evaluation and prognosis. Recognizing these sex-related ECG differences may help optimize the management of ACS patients. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02438085.
