We examined temporal dynamics linking sleep and circadian rhythms to persistent postsurgical pain, using longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record (EHR) data from the NIH All of Us Research Program to track sleep and circadian changes preceding EHR documentation of pain beyond expected surgical recovery. Patients later documented with persistent pain showed systematic shifts in wake timing and in heart rate circadian rhythms (elevated amplitude and mesor), with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing. These changes were absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain documentation, indicating specificity to persistent postsurgical pain rather than a postoperative or clinical-encounter effect. Findings align with evidence linking altered sleep to pain outcomes and identify cardiac circadian disruption as a distinct marker, suggesting wearable-derived features could capture physiological changes before documentation and inform intervention.

Title: Oral Health-Related Adverse Events of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As the clinical use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) continues to grow for the management of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal protection, noncirrhotic fatty liver disease, and weight management, their potential implications for oral health need to be considered.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined oral health-related adverse events (AEs) associated with GLP-1 RAs using postmarketing data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
METHODS: FAERS reports for available GLP-1 RAs, exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide, were screened from their initial market introduction through December 2025, identifying 364,274 total AE reports, of which 31,195 (8.6%) involved oral, craniofacial, or dental manifestations.
RESULTS: Tirzepatide, despite being one of the most recently approved GLP-1 RAs, accounted for the highest overall AE volume, and semaglutide demonstrated the largest proportion of oral health-related AEs. A disproportionality analysis revealed a significant drug-specific signal for dry mouth of semaglutide, while vomiting, regurgitation, and reflux-related events produced a significant signal across all 5 drugs. Sensory disorders, including dysgeusia and taste disturbances, also demonstrated significant proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) and reporting odds ratios (RORs) for several GLP-1 RAs. Association analysis of AEs showed significant associations between vomiting and taste disturbances, as well as between dry mouth and dysgeusia, particularly with semaglutide and dulaglutide.
CONCLUSION: This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

Title: Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.
METHODS: A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

Title: [Total coronary revascularization in elderly and senile patients. Rationale for the surgical approach.].
Abstract: With increasing life expectancy and the rising prevalence of coronary artery disease among elderly and senile patients, the need to optimize surgical methods of myocardial revascularization is growing. Traditional coronary artery bypass grafting via median sternotomy remains the standard of care for multivessel coronary artery disease; however, in elderly and senile patients, it is often associated with an elevated risk of perioperative complications, including infectious complications, respiratory failure, stroke, cognitive dysfunction, and prolonged recovery time. In this context, minimally invasive myocardial revascularization techniques through a left anterolateral minithoracotomy are attracting increasing interest. This analytical review compares outcomes following minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting and sternotomy-based coronary artery bypass grafting with complete myocardial revascularization in elderly and senile patients. The technical features of the approach are discussed, and an analytical review of its efficacy, safety, advantages, and prospects for use in this patient cohort is provided.

Title: [Markers of metabolic and mitochondrial stress in atherosclerosis in elderly and senile individuals.].
Abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the association between markers of metabolic stress (FGF21, GDF15, and lactate) and mitochondrial stress (p-AMPK, PGC-1α, and PINK1) and clinically significant atherosclerosis in elderly and senile individuals. This pilot comparative cross-sectional study included 310 patients aged 60-89 years. There were 162 patients with clinically verified atherosclerosis and 148 controls without clinically manifested or hemodynamically significant atherosclerotic lesions according to the available clinical and instrumental assessment. Serum levels of FGF21, GDF15, and lactate were measured using enzyme immunoassay and biochemical methods. The expression of p-AMPK, PGC-1α, and PINK1 was assessed by immunocytochemistry of buccal epithelial cells as a non-invasive model of the systemic cellular stress response. In patients with atherosclerosis, there were higher serum levels of FGF21, GDF15, and lactate, lower expression of p-AMPK and PGC-1α, and higher expression of PINK1 compared with age-matched control subgroups (p<0,001). There were the most pronounced changes in patients aged 75-89 years with atherosclerosis. In this subgroup, there were the strongest correlations between FGF21 and PINK1 (r=0,67), GDF15 and p-AMPK (r=-0,61), and FGF21 and PGC-1α (r=-0.63; p<0,001). In multivariable models, there was an independent association between reduced PGC-1α expression and increased FGF21 and GDF15 levels, older age, lower eGFR, type 2 diabetes, and higher BMI. There was also an independent association between increased PINK1 expression and GDF15, lactate, older age, lower eGFR, type 2 diabetes, and higher BMI. In elderly and senile individuals, clinically significant atherosclerosis is associated with a more pronounced profile of metabolic and mitochondrial stress. There are potential research indicators of vascular-metabolic aging among the studied markers; however, their clinical application requires further validation in prospective studies accounting for comorbidity, kidney function, inflammation, and pharmacotherapy.

Title: Long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes in type 2 diabetes: final results of the prospective DM-FibroScan Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: International guidelines recommend routine liver assessment in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the long-term clinical implications remain unclear. We aimed to characterise the long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes across the vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) spectrum in T2D.
METHODS: The prospective DM-FibroScan Study consecutively enrolled adults with T2D in Hong Kong during 2013-2014. Baseline controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) were assessed.
RESULTS: 1,862 patients were followed for a median of 11.9 years (interquartile range 11.5-12.1). The 10-year cumulative incidence of liver-related events (LREs) was 1.1% (95% CI 0.7-1.7), lower than those of all cause mortality (21.1% [19.2-22.9]), cardiovascular events (12.5% [11.0-14.2]), malignancies (9.7% [8.3-11.1]), and end-stage kidney disease (9.0% [7.7-10.3]). Most participants (84.2%) had baseline LSM <10 kPa and a low LRE incidence (0.4 [0.1-0.8] per 1,000 person-years), with cardiovascular events predominated (14.1 [12.2-16.2] per 1,000 person-years). Patients with LSM >15 kPa (5.3%) exhibited a markedly higher LRE incidence (12.2 [6.1-21.8] per 1,000 person years), approaching the incidences of malignancies and ESKD. LRE incidence per 1,000 person-years was 1.9 in patients with LSM regression (≥10 to <10 kPa) and 28.0 in those with persistently elevated LSM. Patients with elevated baseline LSM also showed higher incidences of extrahepatic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: LREs were relatively uncommon in the overall T2D population but increased substantially with advanced fibrosis. This study provides natural history data across the VCTE spectrum in a relatively unselected T2D cohort and supports integrating fibrosis assessment into routine T2D care.

Title: Catheter-related complications in children with burns: A retrospective clinical study on 103 central venous access devices.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Central venous access devices (CVADs) are often indispensable for treating burns in children. Early and late complications related to CVAD placement may result in prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity and mortality, and increased cost of care.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study describes catheter-related outcomes in children with burns who underwent CVAD insertion and were managed with standardized insertion and maintenance practices. The primary outcome was the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI), expressed per 1000 catheter days.
RESULTS: A total of 103 CVADs in 81 patients admitted to our pediatric burn unit (mean age 5.1 years, mean TBSA 22.3%) were analyzed: 39 centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs), 47 femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs), and 17 peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs). All CVADs were non-valved, non-cuffed, power-injectable polyurethane catheters; 84.5% were tunneled. The median dwell time was 18.3 days, for a total of 1883 catheter days. The incidence of CRBSI was 1.1 episodes per 1000 catheter days. Unscheduled removal due to catheter-related complications occurred in 11.7% of CVADs. No symptomatic catheter-related thrombosis was reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In children undergoing CVAD placement as a part of burn care, catheter-related complications were infrequent in this cohort managed with a standardized insertion and maintenance approach. These descriptive findings could serve as a basis for future prospective studies.

Title: Association between migraine and angiogenic biomarkers in women with suspected or confirmed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
Journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
Abstract: AimMigraine is associated with increased odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Elevated soluble Fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), decreased placental growth factor (PlGF), and upregulated sFlt-1/PlGF ratios are biomarkers of preeclampsia-related complications. Our primary objective was to examine the effect of migraine on sFlt-1, PlGF, and their ratio within subgroups of women with different HDP diagnoses. Our secondary objective was to evaluate the interrelationship between migraine and these biomarkers in the overall cohort with suspected or confirmed HDP.MethodsWe evaluated pregnant women with suspected or confirmed HDP in whom sFlt-1, PlGF and their ratio were measured during index pregnancy. Migraine diagnoses before/during index pregnancy were retrospectively assessed according to ICHD-3 criteria. Both, descriptive and adjusted analyses were performed, comparing women with and without migraine. For the latter analyses, linear regression analyses were conducted for the log-transformed sFlt-1 levels, PlGF levels and their ratio, while adjusting for gestational age, maternal age, and smoking status.ResultsAmong 234 women (mean age 32 years, SD = 5), 91 had (a history of) migraine. No significant association between migraine and the log-transformed biomarkers was observed in women with and without migraine across HDP groups, also when adjusting for confounding factors (adjusted estimates of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio: β = -0.2 [95% CI: -1.0-0.6] for women with preeclampsia or hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, and low platelet levels syndrome, β = -0.8 [95% CI: -2.0-0.4] for gestational hypertension, and β = -0.1 [95% CI: -0.7-0.4] for those without HDP). Secondary analyses showed that, when pooling the overall study population, women with migraine had lower sFlt-1 levels and sFlt-1/PlGF ratios compared to women without migraine. Adjusted analyses in the overall study population instead showed that migraine was not associated with significant changes in log sFlt-1 levels (β = -0.2 [95% CI: -0.5-0.04]), but rather with higher log PlGFs levels (β = 0.3 [95% CI: 0.03-0.6]) and lower log sFlt-1/PlGF ratios (β = -0.5 [95% CI: -1.0 - -0.08]).ConclusionsResults of this study do not support enhanced angiogenic imbalance by migraine status within HDP groups. As a consequence, interpretation of sFlt-1 and PlGF might not require modification according to migraine status within different HDP diagnoses. The findings observed in the overall cohort require cautious interpretation; whether migraine influences magnitude of angiogenic dysregulation warrants prospective investigation.

Title: Management strategies for right-to-left intraatrial shunt with thrombus in transit: a systematic review of 297 patients and associated mortality outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombus in transit (TIT) through a patent foramen ovale (PFO) or atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition associated with paradoxical embolism. Despite advances in imaging and interventional techniques, optimal management strategies remain poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes of adult patients with TIT across right-to-left intra-atrial shunts.
DESIGN: Systematic review of published cases.
DATA SOURCES AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through March 2025 for case reports, case series, and letters describing adult patients with TIT visualized by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography. After screening 1736 records, 278 studies reporting 297 patients were included. Two independent reviewers extracted demographic, clinical, imaging, treatment, and outcome data. Descriptive statistics were summarized, and treatment groups were compared using chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests. Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank testing assessed 120-day survival, and multivariable Cox regression was used to evaluate potential predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 297 patients from 278 studies were included. The mean age was 58.5 ± 15.8 years, and 50.2% were male. Respiratory symptoms predominated (77.7%), followed by cardiac (29.7%) and neurological (23.0%) manifestations. Provoked events accounted for 70.3% of cases, most commonly in the postoperative setting. Thrombi were detected by transthoracic echocardiography in 92.1% of cases and by transesophageal echocardiography in 100%. Management strategies included surgical embolectomy (57.8%), anticoagulation (36.5%), thrombolysis (13.5%), and percutaneous aspiration (2.7%); 61.1% underwent PFO/ASD closure. Overall mortality was 8.3%. Surgical management was associated with the lowest mortality (3.0%) and the highest short-term clinical improvement (90.5%; p < 0.001). Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality (16.6% and 25.0%, respectively). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated superior 120-day survival with surgical management compared with other treatment strategies (log-rank p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox models, no independent predictors of mortality were identified.
CONCLUSION: In this largest synthesis of TIT cases to date, surgical management and PFO/ASD closure were associated with favorable short-term outcomes. Surgical intervention demonstrated the lowest observed mortality, while anticoagulation provided acceptable outcomes in selected patients. Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality. These findings support the role of definitive management and shunt closure in selected patients, although prospective studies are needed to establish standardized treatment strategies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY) (Registration number: INPLASY202630021).

Title: Background Histological Lesions in Aged African Green Monkeys (Chlorocebus sabaeus) From St. Kitts.
Abstract: The Caribbean African Green Monkey (Chlorocebus sabaeus) (AGM) represents a valuable nonhuman primate model for the study of age-related pathology, with an average lifespan of over 20 years. We describe histological background and common lesions in 44 aged AGMs, >15 years, 20 males and 24 females, 26 colony-born and 18 wild-caught from a primate research facility. The most frequent cardiovascular lesion was myocardial fibrosis (54.5%), characterized by multifocal myocardial fibrosis, cardiomyocyte degeneration/necrosis, lipofuscin accumulation, and frequent concurrent vascular hyalinization affecting small to medium-sized arteries across multiple organs. Chronic kidney disease was highly prevalent, marked by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, interstitial and glomerular fibrosis, tubular degeneration, mineralization, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition; unique renal findings included intratubular iron concretions with foreign body reactions. Hepatic lesions were dominated by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and widespread hemosiderosis, indicating systemic iron overload. In the respiratory system, silica-laden macrophages (SLM) were the most common finding, alongside diverse forms of pneumonia and occasional cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Additional aging-related changes included adrenal nodular hyperplasia, uterine pregnancy-associated vascular remodeling (PAVR) (uterine hyaline deposits), and Sarcocystis infection in skeletal muscle. This retrospective, descriptive study provides initial data on age-related background histopathology in the aged AGM.

Title: Risk Factors and Predictive Model for In-Stent Restenosis After PCI in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Retrospective Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in true bifurcation coronary lesions can lead to repeat revascularization and adverse outcomes.
AIMS: To identify independent risk factors for ISR in patients with coronary bifurcation lesions undergoing PCI and to develop a predictive model for ISR-free survival.
METHODS: Patients with coronary artery disease and Medina coronary bifurcation lesions was analyzed. Baseline characteristics, laboratory values, bifurcation anatomy, and PCI details were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of ISR and its performance was evaluated Model interpretability was explored with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and a nomogram was constructed for clinical use.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed lesion/procedural factors were strongly predictive. Multivariable Cox analysis identified use of a drug-coated balloon in the side branch and side-branch stenting with a drug-eluting stent as the top independent predictors of ISR. Lesion location in the left circumflex was associated with higher ISR risk The Cox model Calibration plots showed close agreement between predicted and observed ISR probabilities. A SHAP analysis confirmed the direction and relative importance of each predictor, enhancing the model's interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: In true bifurcation PCI, Side-branch interventions are associated with higher ISR risk, whereas a simple single-stent approach confers lower risk. The developed Cox-based nomogram demonstrated robust ability to predict ISR, which can aid clinicians in risk stratification and personalized management. Early identification of high-risk patients may enable closer surveillance or preventive measures to improve long-term outcomes after bifurcation PCI.

Title: PCSK9 and Atrial Fibrillation: A New Perspective on an Old Problem.
Abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) has emerged as a novel contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF) pathophysiology. Recent studies suggest that elevated PCSK9 levels may promote AF through multiple mechanisms, including platelet activation, oxidative stress, vascular calcification, and structural atrial remodeling. PCSK9 inhibitors such as alirocumab, evolocumab, and newer agents like inclisiran have shown potential in reducing AF incidence and cardiovascular events, particularly in high-risk populations. However, evidence from randomized controlled trials with AF as a primary clinical endpoint is limited. Further mechanistic and interventional research is warranted to establish optimized therapeutic strategies targeting PCSK9 in AF prevention and management.

Title: Profiling Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Specific Signatures of Homocysteine Metabolism and Mineral Homeostasis in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The application of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) has revolutionized the management of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), rendering it a controllable disease. However, long-term administration is associated with adverse metabolic effects, particularly disruptions in homocysteine metabolism and mineral balance. A comprehensive comparison across TKI types remains absent.
OBJECTIVE: This study systematically characterized and compared the metabolic signatures elicited by first- and second-generation TKIs Imatinib, Nilotinib, and Dasatinib on homocysteine and mineral parameters in chronic myeloid leukemia.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study involved 90 stable CML patients treated with TKI therapy for at least six months at Baghdad Oncology Teaching Hospital between March 2024 and April 2025. Patients were divided into three equal groups based on their medication: Imatinib, Nilotinib, or Dasatinib. Fasting blood samples were collected and analyzed for homocysteine, PTH, calcium, potassium, creatinine, vitamin B12, and ALP. Statistical methods, including ANOVA and correlation analyses, were used to compare groups and explore drug-specific effects.
RESULTS: The three TKI groups demonstrated distinct metabolic disturbance patterns. Nilotinib was associated with the highest homocysteine levels and showed strong positive correlations with PTH and ALP. Dasatinib caused a moderate elevation in homocysteine and uniquely correlated positively with potassium. Imatinib showed the most favorable homocysteine profile, which was primarily inversely correlated with calcium. Multivariate analysis confirmed that these metabolic profiles effectively distinguished the three TKI groups.
CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrates that Imatinib, Nilotinib, and Dasatinib elicit distinct and discernible metabolic signatures. These results support the adoption of personalized, TKI-specific monitoring approaches in the management of CML, aiming to proactively reduce long-term cardiovascular and skeletal adverse effects and thereby improve alignment between the quality and duration of survival.

Title: Association of Abdominal Aortic Calcification with Pathological Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Exploratory Study.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy is an important prognostic determinant in patients with locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). However, reliable pretreatment biomarkers for predicting treatment response remain limited. Abdominal aortic calcification (AAC), an imaging marker of systemic atherosclerosis, can be readily assessed on routine computed tomography (CT). This study investigated the association between baseline AAC and pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with LAGC.
METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study included patients with histologically confirmed LAGC who received neoadjuvant FLOT chemotherapy followed by curative-intent gastrectomy between January 2024 and January 2025. Pretreatment CT images were reviewed to quantify AAC using the abdominal aortic calcification index (ACI). Pathological response was evaluated according to the Mandard tumor regression grade (TRG) system. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ACI and pathological response.
RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a median age of 64 years, and 70.2% were male. Patients with higher ACI values were significantly older than those with lower values. ROC analysis demonstrated limited discriminatory performance of ACI for predicting pathological response. Using an optimal cutoff value of 3.28, the sensitivity and specificity of ACI were 60.0% and 60.4%, respectively. Older age, hyperlipidemia, and clinical T stage were significantly associated with poorer pathological response in univariate analyses. However, ACI was not independently associated with pathological response in multivariable logistic regression analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline AAC was not independently associated with pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with LAGC. AAC may reflect host-related vascular aging rather than tumor-specific treatment sensitivity and may contribute to future exploratory risk-stratification models.

Title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy.
METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min).
CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

Title: Multidomain Polysomnographic Abnormalities in Cervical Dystonia: REM Suppression, Respiratory Instability, and Sensorimotor Dysregulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical dystonia (CD) is considered a basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and brainstem network disorder rather than an isolated focal motor disease.
OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to analyze sleep architecture, REM physiology, respiratory patterns, and sensorimotor activity in CD using full-night PSG.
METHODS: We conducted a full-night PSG case-control analysis involving 33 CD patients and 20 matched controls. Clinical scales used were Toronto Western Spasmodic Torticollis Rating Scale (TWSTRS), Craniocervical Dystonia Questionnaire (CDQ-24), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), and Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS).
RESULTS: CD patients showed greater sleep disruption than controls with significantly decreased total sleep time (TST) and reduced sleep efficiency (SE). Wake after sleep onset (WASO) was considerably higher. >70% met criteria for a study-defined severe insomnia pattern (<25% of controls). REM was absent in 42% of patients and overall REM percentage was reduced by ~70%. CD showed nearly three-fold higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), a significantly higher obstructive apnea index, and prolonged respiratory event duration. Periodic limb movements (PLMS) index was ~14 times higher. Spontaneous arousal rates were significantly increased. Greater motor disability (TWSTRS) correlated with decreased N3 sleep. Higher Tsui severity correlated with increased N2 sleep, linking clinical severity to altered sleep architecture. BDI correlated with higher AHI, greater respiratory event burden and obstructive apnea index. PLMS index showed strong internal coupling with PLMS arousal index and correlated with cardiac parameters.
CONCLUSION: Sleep measures may offer a useful non-invasive perspective on distributed network features associated with CD. These findings are associative and require replication in larger cohorts.

Title: Focused Ultrasound for Essential Tremor in Denmark: Results After 1 Year of Follow-Up.
Journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Essential tremor (ET) is the most common hyperkinetic movement disorder. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy (MRgFUSTh) has become an established therapy in drug-refractory tremor as one treatment option. Here, we present the results of a large cohort of MRgFUSTh-treated ET patients followed-up 1 year post-ablation.
OBJECTIVE: The primary endpoint durability of tremor reduction at 12 months at this timepoint.
METHODS: This was a single-hospital cohort study. Prior to, and 12 months after, treatment, patients were rated according to the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) scale, Quality of Life in Essential Tremor (QUEST) scale, Patient Global Assessment of Change (PGIC), as well as general health, well-being, and factors relating to social and everyday activities. Finally, side effects and adverse event data were collected at 12 months.
RESULTS: The current cohort comprised 111 patients. Patients showed good response to MRgFUSTh with a mean decrease of 29.5 points in the total FTM-score from pretreatment (95% CI: 26.3; 32.8, P < 0.0001) corresponding to 62.4% (95% CI: 56.4%; 68.5%). This meant a reduction in the FTM-score of 13.8 points (± 5.2 points, 95% CI: 12.79; 14.73, P < 0.00001) or 85.2% (±24.2%, 95% CI: 80.70%; 89.78%) in the treated limb. For QUEST, symptoms improved by 20.9 points (95% CI: 12.1; 29.6, P < 0.0001) corresponding to a relative improvement of 54% (95% CI: 33.2%; 75.5%).
CONCLUSION: Results showed clear and persistent tremor improvements as assessed by both clinicians and patients. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

Title: Increasing use of SGLT-2 inhibitors among patients with heart failure.
Journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this quality improvement project was to identify and address barriers contributing to the underutilization of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors in eligible patients with heart failure across the health system.
METHODS: The heart failure registry was used to identify the prescription percentage of SGLT-2 inhibitors pre- and postintervention. Interventions to increase prescribing included pharmacist education to primary care providers and use of a cost information handout.
RESULTS: Following the intervention, SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription for eligible patients improved from 7.1% (n = 630) to 9.0% (n = 814), representing a relative increase of 26.8% from baseline.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal approach involving pharmacy and primary care effectively increased SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing in patients with heart failure. Physician associates, a key part of the primary care workforce, play an important role initiating guideline-directed medical therapy.

Title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive reperfusion strategy, residual disease burden and plaque vulnerability both influence clinical recovery. The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). This pilot study explored the descriptive characteristics and short-term outcomes associated with combining rSS and OCT-derived TCFA in a highly selected STEMI cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective observational pilot study included 30 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI and culprit lesion OCT evaluation at a tertiary care center. Patients were stratified into four groups according to the presence of culprit TCFA and the post-PCI rSS threshold ( ≤ 4 vs. > 4): group 0 (TCFA absent, rSS > 4), group 1 (TCFA absent, rSS ≤ 4), group 2 (TCFA present, rSS > 4), and group 3 (TCFA present, rSS ≤ 4). The primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE)-a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, heart failure hospitalisation, and ischemic stroke-assessed over 3 months.
RESULTS: The cohort (mean age, 54.5 ± 10.1 years; 83.3% male, 40% with diabetes mellitus) had a 53.3% prevalence (16 of 30) of culprit lesion TCFA. Complete or reasonable revascularization (rSS ≤ 4) was achieved in 12 patients (40.0%). The overall cumulative 3-month MACE rate was 30.0% (9 of 30). MACE occurred in 1 of 7 patients (14.3%) in group 0, 1 of 7 (14.3%) in group 1, 4 of 11 (36.4%) in group 2, and 3 of 5 (60.0%) in group 3 (Fisher exact test, P = 0.23; log-rank P = 0.38). Patients with TCFA accounted for 7 of 9 clinical events (77.8%). Given the small subgroup sizes (n < 12), multivariable predictive risk modeling was not performed.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot cohort of STEMI patients undergoing PCI, the presence of OCT-derived TCFA was descriptively associated with higher short-term adverse event rates across both complete and incomplete revascularization strata. Given the small sample size and clear indication bias, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and support the need for adequately powered prospective registries to evaluate dual anatomical-biological risk stratification.

Title: Concurrent acute pancreatitis and splanchnic vein thrombosis in a heavy smoker: a dynamic D-dimer-based diagnostic algorithm and mechanistic insights-a case report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Splanchnic vein thrombosis (SVT) concurrent with acute pancreatitis (AP) at initial diagnosis is rare and its pathophysiology remains unclear. We describe a heavy smoker who presented with AP with occult non-occlusive SVT, which paradoxically progressed to complete thrombotic occlusion.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old male heavy smoker (40-60 cigarettes/day for 30 years) presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with AP after excluding common etiologies. On admission, D-dimer was markedly elevated at 9.15 mg/L (18 times the upper limit of normal). By day 12, despite radiological resolution of pancreatic inflammation and a significant c-reactive protein (CRP) reduction (139.16 to 45.35 mg/L), he developed mesenteric ischemia. Laboratory findings revealed a paradoxical "dynamic decoupling": D-dimer further escalated to 9.52 mg/L, fibrinogen (FIB) was consumed to 2.72 g/L, and antithrombin III (AT-III) was critically depleted to 45%. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed complete thrombotic occlusion of the superior mesenteric, splenic, and portal veins; retrospective review verified non-occlusive SVT at onset. Standard systemic anticoagulation failed to halt thrombotic progression, reaching a "pharmacological ceiling" due to profound AT-III depletion. Transjugular endovascular intervention (thrombus aspiration and catheter-directed thrombolysis) successfully reversed the intestinal ischemia.
CONCLUSIONS: In heavy smokers with AP, an initial D-dimer exceeding 18 times the upper limit of normal should prompt early contrast-enhanced CT to exclude occult SVT. When standard systemic anticoagulation fails due to a "pharmacological ceiling" of depleted antithrombin, timely endovascular escalation is a key salvage strategy.

Title: Estimation of 24-hour urinary sodium excretion using spot urine sample in the adult population in shandong, china.
Abstract: This study assessed the reliability of equations for estimating 24-hour urinary sodium excretion using first-time morning urine samples. In this study, a total of 2078 residents of Shandong Province in 2019 and 2024 were randomised, and three equations for estimating 24-HUNa were fitted using morning urine samples and 24-hour urine samples from 1454 participants (46.6 ± 13.4 years old), and the three equations as well as equations developed by other researchers were validated. In the validation group, estimated 24-HUNa was significantly correlated with measured 24-HUNa values. There was no significant difference between the estimated 24-HUNa and the measured 24-HUNa for the three equations fitted in this study, whereas there was a significant difference between the estimated 24-HUNa and the measured 24-HUNa values using Kawasaki and Tanaka. In the Bland-Altman analyses, the agreement between measured and estimated 24-HUNa values for the six equations was more than 2500 mg / 24 h. All equations showed a tendency to underestimate or overestimate 24-HUNa between different levels of actual 24-HUNa values, hypertension status, and age groups. None of the equations tested in this study could estimate an individual's 24-HUNa from a single SU. The SMASH equation fitted in this study was superior to those of other researchers in assessing population-level 24-HUNa excretion in Shandong Province.

Title: Early mediastinal shift-related complications after pneumonectomy: a comparison of three pleural cavity management strategies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Control of pleural cavity pressure after pneumonectomy is essential to prevent early hemodynamic and respiratory complications related to mediastinal shift. This study aimed to assess early postoperative adverse events according to the residual pleural cavity management strategy used.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study including patients who underwent pneumonectomies for malignant disease via thoracotomy between 2004 and 2024 in three centers. Each center historically used a single pleural cavity management strategy: no drainage (NO DRAIN group), clamped pleural drainage (CLAMPED group), or drainage connected to a pressure-balancing system (BALANCED group).
RESULTS: Overall, 304 patients were included: 106 in the NO DRAIN group, 106 in the CLAMPED group, and 92 in the BALANCED group. Four cases (1.3%) of hemodynamic or respiratory failure related to mediastinal shift occured: in the NO DRAIN group, one cardiopulmonary arrest immediately after air aspiration from the residual pleural cavity on postoperative day-one; in the CLAMPED group, two tamponades on postoperative day-2; in the BALANCED group, one acute respiratory distress with extensive subcutaneous emphysema on postoperative day-two. None of these events were fatal. Rates of atrial fibrillation (27% vs. 14% and 11%, p<0.01) and reoperation (20% vs 7% and 13%, p=0.017), as well as length of hospital stay (11.3 days vs 9.8 and 8.4, p<0.001), were higher in the CLAMPED group. One-month survival did not differ significantly between groups (94%, 95%, and 99%, p = 0.19).
CONCLUSION: Early mediastinal shift- related complications after pneumonectomy are uncommon and may occur regardless of pleural cavity management strategy. The clamped-drain strategy may be associated with increased postoperative arrhythmia.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Multicenter Study

Title: Impact of red blood cell transfusion on clinical outcomes after cardiovascular surgery: a reconstructed time-to-event meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of perioperative red blood cell transfusion on long-term outcomes after cardiovascular surgery remains controversial. This meta-analysis of reconstructed time-to-event data aimed to evaluate the association between red blood cell transfusion and clinical outcomes in adult patients undergoing cardiovascular surgery.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing perioperative red blood cell transfusion versus no transfusion in adults undergoing cardiovascular surgery. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at short- and long-term follow-up. A pairwise random-effects meta-analysis was done for 30-day mortality and other secondary outcomes, pooling risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves to perform landmark analysis and estimate restricted mean survival time (RMST) differences between red blood cell transfused and non-transfused groups. Cox frailty regression analysis was used to obtain hazard ratios (HR). Meta-regression analyses were performed to explore sources of heterogeneity, and the certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: This systematic review and meta-analysis included 15 observational studies (13 retrospective and 2 prospective) comparing the impact of red blood transfusion on cardiovascular outcomes in adult patients after cardiovascular surgery. Red blood cell transfusion was associated with a higher incidence of 30-day mortality (RR = 2.57, 95% CI [1.96, 3.38], I² = 0.0%, p < 0.001), long-term all-cause mortality (HR 1.79 (95% CI [1.75, 1.83]; p < 0.001)*, atrial fibrillation (RR 1.57 95% CI [1.21, 2.04]; p < 0.001), acute kidney injury (RR 4.52 95% CI [2.32, 8.80]; p < 0.001), myocardial infarction (RR 2.32 95% CI [1.60, 3.37]; p < 0.001), pneumonia (RR 5.10 95% CI [3.04, 8.57]; p < 0.001), reoperation for bleeding (RR 12.61 95% CI [7.99, 19.90]; p < 0.001), sepsis (RR 7.49 95% CI [2.64, 21.26]; p < 0.001), and stroke (RR 2.54 95% CI [2.04, 3.16]; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that perioperative red blood cell transfusion was associated with higher rates of mortality and adverse outcomes; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of residual confounding, baseline differences between groups, and the observational nature of the included studies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Meta-Analysis; Systematic Review; Review

Title: Risk factors of radial artery occlusion following via transradial coronary catheterization.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify the independent risk factors associated with radial artery occlusion (RAO) after right transradial coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and construct a visualized nomogram for individualized RAO risk prediction.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 561 patients with suspected angina pectoris undergoing right transradial CAG/PCI from December 2023 to June 2024; all patients received a uniform 6F radial sheath. Radial artery patency was evaluated 24 h post-procedure via modified reverse Barbeau test (MRBT). Patients were divided into RAO group (n=49) and non-RAO group (n=512). Univariate logistic regression screened candidate variables (screen threshold p<0.1), and backward stepwise multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors. A nomogram was established based on regression coefficients of independent predictors. Model performance was assessed by ROC curve (AUC), calibration curve combined with Hosmer-Lemeshow (HL) test, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: The overall incidence of RAO was 8.7%. Multivariable logistic regression identified four independent risk factors for RAO: prior coronary artery disease, multiple puncture attempts, puncture duration >15 min and radial arterial spasm. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.754 (95%CI 0.671-0.837). The calibration curve showed favorable consistency between predicted and actual RAO incidence, with HL test p=0.536. DCA verified reliable clinical net benefit of the nomogram for risk stratification.
CONCLUSIONS: Four independent predictors of post-transradial RAO were confirmed:prior coronary artery disease, multiple puncture attempts, puncture duration>15min and radial arterial spasm. The nomogram built on these four factors exhibited satisfactory discrimination, calibration and clinical utility. This tool can help clinicians screen high-risk patients and deliver targeted preventive interventions, while avoiding unnecessary prophylaxis for low-risk individuals. Further prospective external validation of this model is required.

Title: Heterogeneous cardiovascular responses to acute mean arterial pressure augmentation in septic shock: the role of ventriculo-arterial coupling and venous return.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with septic shock, vasopressor-induced mean arterial pressure (MAP) augmentation is commonly used to restore tissue perfusion; however, patients may exhibit divergent cardiovascular responses despite achieving similar arterial pressure targets. We hypothesized that this heterogeneity reflects the differences in ventricular adaptation to increases in arterial load and venous return determinants.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective physiological observational study in mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock who underwent transient MAP augmentation from approximately 65 to 85 mmHg after the initial hemodynamic resuscitation. MAP was increased by norepinephrine dose escalation or by adding vasopressin according to clinical judgment. Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography was performed immediately before and after MAP augmentation. Patients were classified a priori according to the relative changes in cardiac output (CO): flow recruitment (> 15% increase), stable flow (- 15% to + 15%), or flow deterioration (> 15% decrease). Changes in effective arterial elastance (Ea), end-systolic elastance (Ees), VA coupling (Ea/Ees), stroke volume, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), analogue mean systemic filling pressure (Pmsa), and derived venous return variables were analyzed.
RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were included. Despite comparable increases in MAP, the cardiovascular responses were heterogeneous: 10 patients (31%) exhibited flow recruitment, 17 (53%) maintained a stable flow, and 5 (16%) developed flow deterioration. Patients with flow deterioration showed a greater increase in Ea without a proportional increase in Ees, resulting in worsening VA coupling (ΔEa/Ees + 0.22 IQR [0.01-0.81]), whereas VA coupling remained stable or improved in patients with preserved or increased flow (p = 0.035). Flow deterioration was also associated with reduced LVEF and changes in the derived venous return indices, which may have contributed to the observed reduction in forward flow. Changes in VA coupling correlated with changes in IVCT (ρ = 0.788, p < 0.0001), MPI (ρ = 0.599, p < 0.0003), stroke volume (ρ =-0.418, p = 0.017), and LVEF (ρ=-0.431, p = 0.0139).
CONCLUSIONS: Acute MAP augmentation elicits heterogeneous cardiovascular responses in patients with septic shock despite similar increases in arterial pressure. Flow deterioration is characterized by worsening VA coupling, reduced stroke volume, and impaired systolic adaptation, potentially modulated by changes in the derived venous return indices.

Title: Decision dilemmas and insights in secondary prevention of ischemic stroke: a case report of an elderly patient with hereditary thrombophilia and high-risk patent foramen ovale.
Abstract: This study reports the case of a 74-year-old female patient (aged 70 at the initial 2021 event) with hereditary thrombophilia and a patent foramen ovale (PFO) possessing high-risk anatomical features. The patient presented in December 2021 with pulmonary embolism and acute multiple cerebral infarctions due to PFO-associated paradoxical embolism. Genetic testing confirmed hereditary thrombophilia (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, 4G/4G genotype). Despite standard anticoagulation, she developed recurrent thrombosis. Subsequent transesophageal echocardiography (May 2025) delineated the high-risk PFO anatomy. The Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) score was 3, corresponding to a PFO‑attributable fraction of approximately 23%. This case illustrates a dual-risk mechanism for stroke: a persistent prothrombotic state coexisting with a definitive structural embolic pathway. The patient subsequently underwent percutaneous PFO closure. This case highlights the conflict between the need for individualized intervention based on dual high-risk mechanisms and the age-based recommendations of current guidelines (ESC 2023, AHA/ASA 2021). Anatomical assessment of the PFO enables a more precise estimation of stroke recurrence risk and the potential value of closure. As a causative therapy aimed at eliminating the structural embolic pathway, PFO closure may represent a reasonable interventional strategy in such carefully selected high-risk patients; however, its definitive net clinical benefit requires validation through prospective, large-scale trials.

Title: Epicardial adipose tissue volume and nephropathy in people living with type 2 diabetes: the Kidn-EAT study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), a visceral adipose tissue located between the pericardium and the myocardium, has been linked to cardiac issues. The present study aimed to evaluate the association between EAT volume and the presence of nephropathy and its components, i.e. albuminuria/creatininuria ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classes, in patients living with type 2 diabetes (PwT2D).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present study is a cross-sectional analysis of a retrospective cohort of 700 PwT2D who had a computed tomography scan to measure both their coronary artery calcium score and EAT volume (proprietary prototype, GE HealthCare), and available data for both eGFR and ACR.
RESULTS: A total of 700 PwT2D (332 women) were included, of whom 295 patients had nephropathy (42.1%), including 87 (12.4%) with eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73m2 and 258 (36.9%) with ACR ≥ 3 mg/mmol. Mean age (± standard deviation) was 60.3 ± 10.4 years old and 44.8% had obesity. EAT volume was higher in patients with nephropathy compared to those without (respectively, 103.6 ± 39.8 versus 93.8 ± 36.8 cm3, p = 0.001). EAT volume differed across eGFR classes (≥ 60 versus < 60 mL/min/1.73m2): respectively 96.6 ± 38.1 and 107.7 ± 39.2 (p = 0.012) and ACR classes (< 3; between 3 and 29.9; ≥ 30 mg/mmol): respectively 94.7 ± 36.9, 106.0 ± 40.2, and 95.7 ± 39.8 cm3 (p = 0.004). EAT volume was weakly correlated to eGFR (r = -0.146; p < 0.001) and to ACR (r = 0.124; p = 0.001). After adjustment for major confounding factors, each 10 cm3 increase of EAT volume was associated with a 5.8% increase in the odds of nephropathy (OR = 1.058 [95% CI 1.007-1.112], p = 0.026) and a 5.9% increase in the odds of ACR ≥ 3 mg/mmol (OR = 1.059 [95% CI 1.008-1.114], p = 0.024), but not with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2 (OR = 1.047 [95% CI 0.975-1.123], p = 0.204).
CONCLUSION: EAT volume was associated with nephropathy and especially with increased ACR in PwT2D. This association may be partly explained by metabolic and inflammatory mechanisms, potentially driven by EAT and/or other associated ectopic fat depots in PwT2D.

Title: Optimal strategy for treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of clopidogrel-based antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose rivaroxaban therapy (OACART study): a study protocol for a multicenter, open-label, randomized, non-inferiority trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies have demonstrated the superior benefits of clopidogrel compared to aspirin in reducing mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and hospitalization in chronic stable patients with coronary stenting. Furthermore, dual pathway inhibition by combining low-dose rivaroxaban with aspirin (DPI) has shown superior effects in preventing cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke in stable atherosclerotic patients. However, no studies have directly compared these treatment strategies in the same population. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare clopidogrel-based antiplatelet therapy with or without aspirin (CAPT) to DPI in a 1:1 ratio in patients with high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) or in patients with both CAD and peripheral artery disease (PAD).
METHODS: Optimal strategy for treatment of Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of Clopidogrel-based Antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose Rivaroxaban Therapy (OACART) trial is a randomized multi-center study comparing the performance of the maintaining CAPT or DPI in a 1:1 ratio. The trial is powered for the non-inferiority of the CAPT in patients with chronic stable high-risk CAD or CAD+PAD to DPI with respect to the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints at 36 months.
RESULTS: Between November 2023 and April 2026, we will recruit 2758 participants from multi-center in Korea, and we will examine the net clinical outcome, including all-cause death, any myocardial infarction, any stroke, any ischemia-driven revascularization (CAD or PAD), acute limb ischemia, any major or minor amputations, any acute thromboembolism, and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis major bleeding at 36 months after study enrollment.
CONCLUSIONS: OACART trial will provide the optimal antithrombotic treatment strategy for patients with stable high-risk atherosclerosis.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS) of Republic of Korea, KCT0008458, registered on May 22, 2023. https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=28968&search_page=L.

Title: Application of multi-omics analysis in atherosclerosis.
Abstract: Atherosclerosis is a leading global cause of disability and mortality, with a rising trend of early onset across populations. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, encompassing multiple interconnected pathways including dyslipidemia, inflammation, and immune dysregulation. Current therapeutic strategies targeting lipoproteins are insufficient to address disease progression, and there remains an urgent unmet clinical need to further elucidate its pathogenic mechanisms, refine diagnostic approaches, and identify novel therapeutic targets. In recent years, the vigorous development of omics technology has provided help for in-depth investigation of the pathogenesis of diseases and search for new diagnosis and treatment targets. The application of multi-omics analysis has elevated atherosclerotic research to a new tier, yielding high-quality findings that further unravel atherogenic molecular mechanisms. These findings provide critical theoretical and translational groundwork for developing novel diagnostics, targeted therapies, and robust early risk stratification tools. In this review, we summarize integrated multi-omics applications in atherosclerosis, and outline novel perspectives for prospective therapeutic strategies.

Title: Mortality risk model for acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: development, external validation, and exploratory application in a VA-ECMO cohort.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) carries a high risk of in-hospital death. Randomized evidence does not support routine VA-ECMO use in unselected AMI-CS populations. Objective and interpretable risk stratification is clinically important when advanced mechanical circulatory support is considered.
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multi-database model development and validation study with exploratory application in a local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort. An in-hospital mortality prediction model was developed in AMI-CS patients who did not receive ECMO treatment using the MIMIC-IV database. Candidate measurements were summarized using the worst values accumulated during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Variable shrinkage was performed using LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation, and the model was established using multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation included the original fixed-structure bootstrap and an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. The latter repeated preprocessing, LASSO selection, post-LASSO handling, and model refitting within each resample. External validation was performed in the eICU cohort. The model was then applied exploratorily to the local VA-ECMO-treated AMI-CS cohort to describe model transportability and the relationship between observed and predicted outcomes.
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 355 patients, of whom 127 died in hospital (35.77%). LASSO selected 8 clinical predictors. The apparent AUC was 0.829 (95% CI 0.785-0.874). After the final model was refitted in 200 fixed-structure bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.814. In 500 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples, all repetitions were valid, the mean optimism was 0.0436, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.786 (empirical 2.5th to 97.5th percentile range: 0.745-0.832). The AUCs from the MIMIC-IV complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses were 0.820 and 0.840, respectively. In the eICU complete-case cohort, the AUC was 0.806 (95% CI 0.691-0.921), O/E was 0.733, the calibration intercept was - 0.986, and the calibration slope was 0.671. After multiple imputation in all 224 eligible eICU patients, the AUC was 0.771, O/E was 0.754, the calibration intercept was - 0.756, and the calibration slope was 0.528. The local cohort included 40 VA-ECMO-treated patients. Overall observed mortality was 42.5% (95% CI 27.0-59.1), mean predicted mortality was 59.2% (95% CI 50.6-67.2), and O/E was 0.717 (95% CI 0.418-1.149).
CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and externally validated a mortality risk model for patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock. The model may provide a research reference for early risk stratification and individualized assessment. Uncertainty in variable selection and cross-population calibration drift limit its direct clinical application. Prospective multicenter studies are required for further validation and to evaluate its role in VA-ECMO patient selection.

Title: Interpretable machine learning prediction model for postoperative pneumonia after cardiac surgery based on real-world data: a retrospective single-center study.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) is a common and clinically important complication following cardiac surgery. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an interpretable machine learning prediction model for 30-day POP after cardiac surgery using routinely collected real-world clinical data, and to describe a prototype decision-support application for potential perioperative risk stratification.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study using electronic medical record data from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery between January 2012 and December 2023 were screened; patients with massive missing clinical data, definite preoperative infection, or age < 18 years were excluded. The outcome was POP within 30 days after surgery. The final cohort was partitioned into training and held-out test sets using stratified random sampling at a 7:3 ratio before feature selection, augmentation, model fitting, and model evaluation. To reduce information leakage, preprocessing steps were fitted within the training workflow and the test set was reserved for final internal evaluation. Missing data were handled using MICE, class imbalance was addressed with Borderline-SMOTE and class weighting, predictors were selected using Boruta with recall impact over 50 iterations, and Bayesian optimization was used for hyperparameter tuning. Six machine learning algorithms (RF, SVM, XGBoost, LR, DT, and CatBoost) were compared. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, and overall classification metrics, including AUC, AP, recall, precision, accuracy, F1-score, calibration curves, and Brier score. SHAP was used for model interpretation.
RESULTS: Among 10,109 eligible patients, 1,018 (10.07%) developed POP and 9,091 did not. Seven predictors were retained in the final model: ejection fraction (EF), cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time, serum creatinine (SCr), intraoperative blood loss, gender, total bilirubin (TBIL), and platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR). CatBoost showed the best overall internal performance, with validation-set AUC of 0.9873 (95% CI: 0.9820-0.9926), AP of 0.9519 (95% CI: 0.9315-0.9722), accuracy of 0.9528 (95% CI: 0.9422-0.9635), recall of 0.9324 (95% CI: 0.9011-0.9636), and F1-score of 0.8996 (95% CI: 0.8754-0.9234). In the held-out test set, CatBoost achieved AUC of 0.9810, AP of 0.8600, accuracy of 0.9555, recall of 0.9258, precision of 0.7007, and F1-score of 0.7977. SHAP analysis showed that EF, CPB duration, SCr, and intraoperative blood loss were major contributors to predicted POP risk. A prototype web application was developed to illustrate potential perioperative use.
CONCLUSION: This study develops and internally evaluates an interpretable machine learning model for perioperative prediction of 30-day POP after cardiac surgery. The model demonstrated high internal discrimination and precision-recall performance, but the retrospective single-center design, absence of external validation, and inclusion of intraoperative predictors mean that it should be considered a perioperative risk-stratification model requiring external and prospective evaluation before routine clinical use.
REGISTRATION: This retrospective prediction-model study was not registered.

Title: Evaluating the impact of upper limb training on respiratory function in long-term tracheostomy patients: a preliminary single-center, randomized crossover study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The quality and quantity of respiratory muscles directly affect respiratory function, but it's unclear how much improved muscle function enhances cough capacity. Our preliminary studies show that active/passive lower limb training can improve cough capacity, but the impact of upper limb training is uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of passive upper limb training on cough capacity in long-term tracheostomy patients.
METHODS: In this single-center, single-blind, randomized crossover trial, a total of 27 tracheostomized patients with traumatic brain injury or stroke were enrolled. Participants were randomly allocated into three groups: the CA group (active-passive cycling (APC)/ additional physical therapy (PT) training (APTT) sequence) (n = 11); the AC group (APTT/APC sequence) (n = 10); and the control group (n = 6) (after adjusting for baseline differences using propensity score matching, the control group was reduced from 11 to 6 participants). The APC and APTT interventions were administered for 40 min per session, six times per week, over a period of two weeks, in conjunction with standard rehabilitation (SD). The control group received SD for the 14 days. Assessment metrics included the Barthel Index (BI), ultrasound evaluation of respiratory muscle thickness, and Cough Peak Flow (CPF), measured at baseline, after 7 days, and upon completion of the intervention. Comparative analyses were conducted to evaluate the effects during and following the intervention period.
RESULTS: After adjusting for baseline data, no significant differences were found between groups. While overall APC and APTT periods were similar across groups, the CA group showed significant improvements in the 5th intercostal muscle (ICM), diaphragm, and rectus femoris (RF) during the later intervention phase, with the most notable improvements in the left-sided 2nd and 5th ICM. Overall CPF remained consistent between and within groups, but its increase in the later phase was positively linked to earlier and concurrent increases in the thickness of the 5th and 2nd ICM and the diaphragm.
CONCLUSION: This study found no significant improvement in cough capacity from active-passive upper limb training compared to controls. However, it did show increased thickness in respiratory muscles like the intercostals and diaphragm in the intervention groups. This suggests that while APC training aids respiratory muscle adaptation, it doesn't directly enhance cough capacity. APC training performed similarly to APTT, indicating its potential as a supportive strategy for respiratory conditioning, but it is less effective than lower limb training for improving cough capacity. Future research with longer interventions, resistance, or greater motion range may be needed for meaningful cough function improvements.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ICTRP member): ChiCTR2500104415. Date of Registration on June 17, 2025.

Title: Design and protocol of a randomized assessor-blinded controlled trial evaluating an educational escape room for individual and team cardiopulmonary resuscitation skills among nursing students.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) depends not only on technical competence but also on effective communication, role clarity, leadership, and coordinated team performance under pressure. However, conventional CPR instruction may not adequately reproduce the collaborative and time-sensitive demands of real resuscitation. Educational escape rooms (EERs), as simulation-based gamified learning strategies, may provide a more immersive and learner-centered approach to strengthening both cognitive and teamwork-related aspects of CPR training. This study protocol was developed to evaluate the effect of a team-based CPR educational escape room (CPR-EER) integrated into advanced life support (ALS) training for undergraduate nursing students.
METHODS: This study was designed as a two-arm, parallel-group, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio. Participants were seventh-semester undergraduate nursing students at Shahid Sadoughi University of Medical Sciences, Yazd, Iran. All participants first received a standardized 8-hour CPR refresher workshop to establish a common educational baseline. The intervention group then participated in a structured CPR-EER delivered in fixed six-member teams in a simulated in-hospital cardiac arrest environment, whereas the control group continued with the routine curriculum during the primary comparison phase and received the intervention after post-test assessment. The primary outcome was team coordination during CPR, assessed using a Team Objective Structured Clinical Examination (TOSCE). Secondary outcomes included role-specific performance, CPR knowledge, and learner satisfaction. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and one month after the intervention. Data analysis was prespecified using a per-protocol framework and distribution-appropriate statistical tests.
DISCUSSION: This protocol provides a methodologically explicit and pedagogically grounded model for evaluating a gamified, team-based CPR-EER training strategy in undergraduate nursing education. By aligning intervention design, educational objectives, and outcome assessment, it may contribute to the development of more immersive, competency-oriented, and reproducible approaches to resuscitation training.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), registered on 16 October 2024, IRCT20240815062770N1. Available at: https://irct.behdasht.gov.ir/ .

Title: Urinary NT-proBNP as a noninvasive biomarker for pediatric septic shock: a comparative study with serum levels.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2024 Phoenix Sepsis Score (PSS) may not fully capture subclinical cardiovascular stress in pediatric sepsis. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), released under haemodynamic strain, is measurable in urine and serum and has been associated with cardiovascular dysfunction. This study aimed to compare urinary and serum NT-proBNP levels in pediatric sepsis and septic shock, evaluate their ability to differentiate these conditions, and examine their correlations with PSS.
METHODS: Participants aged 1 month-18 years with sepsis or septic shock according to PSS were included in this prospective cross-sectional analytical study at a tertiary hospital in Bandung, Indonesia. Urinary and serum NT-proBNP concentrations were measured within 48 h of diagnosis. Patients with preexisting heart, kidney, or urological problems were excluded. Main analyses included Mann-Whitney U, ROC curves, and Spearman correlations. To evaluate statistical stability, 1,000 bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap iterations, fragility index (FI) analysis, and time-adjusted sensitivity analyses were added.
RESULTS: Final analyses comprised 52 children (26 sepsis, 26 septic shock). Median urinary NT-proBNP levels were higher in septic shock than in sepsis (8,065 vs. 210 pg/mL; p = 0.003), as were serum NT-proBNP levels (1,655 vs. 200 pg/mL; p = 0.005). Urinary NT-proBNP had an AUC of 0.743 (95% BCa CI 0.584-0.867) for septic shock (cut-off > 9,550 pg/mL, specificity 100%, sensitivity 42.3%, FI = 4), whereas serum NT-proBNP showed an AUC of 0.726 (95% BCa CI 0.573-0.852; cut-off > 1,640 pg/mL, specificity 92.3%, sensitivity 50.0%, FI = 3). Sensitivity analyses confirmed performance stability when restricting collection to ≤ 6 h. Urinary NT-proBNP correlated weakly with PSS (r = 0.261; p = 0.031), while serum NT-proBNP did not (r = 0.221; p = 0.058).
CONCLUSIONS: Urinary NT-proBNP demonstrated moderate discriminatory ability and high specificity for pediatric septic shock, comparable to serum NT-proBNP, although its correlation with PSS was modest. It may have potential value as an adjunctive rule-in biomarker for cardiovascular stress in pediatric sepsis, but not as a screening tool or replacement for clinical assessment. Further studies are needed to determine its broader clinical utility in pediatric sepsis.

Title: Short-term outcomes associated with oral prednisolone versus posterior sub-Tenon triamcinolone acetonide in acute ocular Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe short-term clinical and anatomical outcomes associated with oral prednisolone and posterior sub-Tenon triamcinolone acetonide as initial corticosteroid-based treatment strategies in acute ocular Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease (VKH).
METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 30 treatment-naïve patients (60 eyes) with acute ocular VKH treated at a tertiary referral center between January 2021 and December 2025. Patients were classified using a study-specific two-tier designation (definite or probable VKH) derived from the 2001 Revised Diagnostic Criteria. Treatment assignment (oral prednisolone, n = 15, 1.0 mg/kg/day tapered over 3-6 weeks; or PST/STA, n = 15) was guided by clinical severity and systemic involvement. The primary outcome was complete clinical and anatomical ocular control at 3 months, defined as absence of clinically active intraocular inflammation, resolution of subretinal fluid on OCT, and stable or improved BCVA. Secondary outcomes included BCVA over 6 months, OCT-based anatomical recovery, recurrence rates, rescue therapy requirement, and adverse events. Resolution of subretinal fluid was assessed qualitatively on OCT as complete disappearance of the subretinal fluid pocket, with central macular thickness (CMT) recorded in parallel as a supportive structural measure. Statistical analyses included the independent and paired t-tests, two-sided Fisher's exact test, and Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test.
RESULTS: At 3 months, complete clinical and anatomical ocular control was achieved in 12/15 (80.0%) patients receiving prednisolone and 11/15 (73.3%) receiving PST/STA (p = 1.00, Fisher's exact test). Resolution of subretinal fluid occurred in 86.7% (13/15) and 80.0% (12/15) of patients, respectively (p = 1.00, Fisher's exact test). Mean BCVA improved in both groups over 6 months, with no statistically significant between-group difference. OCT analysis demonstrated no statistically significant between-group differences in the assessed anatomical outcomes. Recurrence occurred in 20.0% of the prednisolone group and 26.7% of the PST/STA group (log-rank p = 0.68). Systemic corticosteroid-related metabolic complications were observed only in the prednisolone group, while PST/STA was associated with transient local discomfort and mild intraocular pressure elevation. No serious ocular complications occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective, non-randomized cohort, no statistically significant differences were detected between oral prednisolone and PST/STA in the short-term clinical and anatomical outcomes assessed. Because treatment allocation was influenced by disease severity and systemic involvement, the sample size was small, no a priori sample-size calculation was performed, and the systemic corticosteroid regimen was abbreviated, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence or as establishing PST/STA as an alternative to systemic corticosteroid therapy. Prospective, adequately powered studies with standardized assessment of ocular and systemic disease severity are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07405489. Registered 30 January 2026 (retrospectively registered), https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07405489 .

Title: Myocardial injury patterns on cardiac magnetic resonance: diffuse myocardial damage with prominent septal involvement in adults with severe myocarditis requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with myocarditis suffering from cardiogenic shock may benefit from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). However, the characteristics of myocardial injury in these patients are unclear. Using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), we aimed to investigate cardiac changes in survivors with severe myocarditis treated with ECMO.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University in Nanjing, China, from July 2018 to July 2022. Patients with severe myocarditis who underwent CMR within 30 days after discontinuing ECMO were included in this study.
RESULTS: In total, 22 patients (median age: 33 years) were included. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was detected within the interventricular septum (IVS) in all patients. The mean T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) values showed similar distribution patterns to LGE. In an exploratory post-hoc age stratification based on the cohort median age of 33 years, we observed that several quantitative CMR parameters (mean ECV, minimum ECV, maximum ECV, mean T1, maximum T1, and minimum T2) were numerically higher in the older subgroup (p < 0.05). Myocardial injury was widespread in patients with severe myocarditis receiving ECMO.
CONCLUSIONS: Survivors of severe myocarditis who required ECMO support presented diffuse myocardial injury as the dominant pattern on early post-weaning CMR examination, with the interventricular septum showing notably prominent lesions among all myocardial segments.

Title: DSA radiomics and clinical features for hemorrhagic risk assessment in bAVM embolization.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic complications (HCs) remain a major cause of morbidity in endovascular treatment (EVT) for brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM), while reliable EVT-specific risk assessment remains challenging.
