This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an exploratory model integrating digital subtraction angiography (DSA) radiomics and clinical features to assess the risk of EVT-related HCs.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 620 consecutive bAVM patients who underwent first-time EVT between 2011 and 2024. Radiomics features were extracted from anteroposterior and lateral DSA images of the nidus. Clinical-only, radiomics-only, and combined models were developed using four algorithms with stratified five-fold cross-validation on the training set and evaluated on the test set. Model interpretability was performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
RESULTS: HCs occurred in 100 patients (16.1%). On the test set, the XGBoost-based fusion model achieved the best overall performance (AUC 0.81), showing a modest improvement over the radiomics-only XGBoost model while outperforming all clinical-only models. Radiomics features contributed substantially to model performance, with clinical variables providing complementary information.
CONCLUSIONS: A model integrating DSA radiomics and clinical features provides an exploratory approach to assessing the risk of EVT-related HCs in patients with bAVM. These findings suggest the potential value of DSA-derived radiomics for individualized peri-procedural risk assessment, although external validation is required before clinical application.

Title: Anterior vault as a risk stratification marker for trabecular-iris angle reduction after implantable collamer lens implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical utility of the anterior vault (AV), as measured by anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), as a risk stratification marker for a postoperative trabecular-iris angle (TIA) ≤ 20° following Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) implantation. Additionally, this study investigated postoperative alterations in iridocorneal angle dynamics after ICL placement.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational study was conducted at a single private hospital and included 185 eyes from 185 patients who underwent ICL implantation between January 2018 and December 2023. The primary endpoint was to evaluate the discriminative performance of AV for identifying eyes with postoperative TIA500 ≤20°. Secondary outcomes included preoperative and postoperative parameters associated with eyes at risk of developing postoperative TIA ≤ 20°.
RESULTS: Postoperative nasal and temporal TIA500≤20º occurred in 29(15.7%) and 38(20.5%) eyes, respectively. In the nasal quadrant, multivariate analysis identified the white-to-white/anterior-chamber depth (WTW/ACD) ratio (OR: 35.66; 95%CI: 6.14-93.86; p = 0.0031), nasal AOD500 (OR: 0.09; 95%CI: 0.02-0.27; p = 0.0077), nasal TIA500 (OR:0.85; 95%CI: 0.78-0.93; p = 0.0002), and AV (OR:0.06; 95%CI: 0.01-0.31; p = 0.0007) as independent factors associated with postoperative TIA500≤20°. In the temporal quadrant, AV (OR: 0.10; 95%CI: 0.02-0.39; p = 0.0010) and preoperative temporal TIA500 (OR: 0.84; 95%CI: 0.78-0.91; p < 0.0001) were significantly associated with post-ICL angle narrowing. The negative predictive values (NPVs) for excluding a postoperative TIA ≤ 20° were high within this cohort's prevalence parameters. In the nasal quadrant, NPVs ranged from 93.5% (AV) to 95.6% (preoperative-nasal TIA), while in the temporal quadrant, preoperative-temporal TIA showed the highest NPV at 97.8%, compared to 87.2% for AV.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identified AV, WTW/ACD ratio, and preoperative angle metrics as key markers associated with postoperative TIA500 ≤20° after ICL implantation. AV proved to be a simple, clinically valuable marker to enhance risk stratification.

Title: Beyond angina: Ranolazine is associated with increased forced-swimming endurance and altered echocardiographic parameters in healthy rats: a comparative study with Trimetazidine.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-anginal agents that modulate myocardial substrate metabolism, such as ranolazine and trimetazidine, are pharmacologically capable of altering exercise performance independently of their licensed indication in ischemic heart disease. Trimetazidine has been included on the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) Prohibited List since 2014 on the basis of comparable evidence. Whether ranolazine, a mechanistically distinct late sodium current inhibitor, produces analogous performance-modifying effects in the absence of myocardial ischemia has not been systematically examined. This exploratory, hypothesis-generating study characterized the functional exercise and structural echocardiographic correlates of chronic ranolazine and trimetazidine administration in healthy rats.
METHODS: Twenty-four male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized in a blinded, parallel-group design to ranolazine (50 mg/kg/day), trimetazidine (10 mg/kg/day), or saline control (n = 8 per group) for 30 days. Two control-group rats died under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia during baseline (day 0) echocardiography, before any study data were collected, and were excluded from all subsequent analyses, yielding a final analytic sample of 22 rats (control, n = 6; trimetazidine, n = 8; ranolazine, n = 8). Forced swimming, rotarod testing, and transthoracic echocardiography were performed at baseline, day 15, and day 30. Because Shapiro-Wilk testing indicated non-normal distributions, non-parametric statistics (Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank with Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc thresholds) were applied a priori, and exact p-values are reported throughout.
RESULTS: Total swimming time differed significantly between groups (ranolazine 39,668 s [33,794-43,838]; trimetazidine 35,694 s [30,776-39,516]; control 32,426 s [29,389-34,453]; p = 0.006), with ranolazine exceeding trimetazidine in sessions 16-18 (p < 0.001). Rotarod performance was unchanged across groups and time (p > 0.05 for all comparisons). Echocardiography showed small but statistically significant increases in interventricular septal thickness and calculated left ventricular mass in all three groups, including controls, with ejection fraction and fractional shortening preserved throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: Chronic ranolazine administration was associated with exercise-performance changes that paralleled, and in later sessions exceeded, those produced by trimetazidine, together with modest echocardiographic changes that are compatible with, but not proof of, physiological cardiac remodeling. Because the present design did not include biochemical, histological, electrocardiographic, or direct oxygen-consumption confirmation, and because the structural changes occurred in controls as well as treated animals, these observations should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than mechanistically conclusive. They identify ranolazine as a candidate worthy of further, more deeply mechanistic investigation rather than establishing, on their own, a basis for anti-doping action.

Title: The diagnostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited studies compare the clinical applications and diagnostic values of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) versus echocardiography in individuals with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).
OBJECTIVE: This study was performed to evaluate the diagnostic value of CMR in patients with HCM.
METHODS: A retrospective study without prospective follow-up was performed on the data from 100 patients diagnosed with HCM from July 2018 to December 2021. All patients underwent echocardiography, CMR scans, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Various parameters of CMR were measured and compared to those of echocardiography to evaluate the diagnostic value of CMR in the diagnosis of HCM.
RESULTS: CMR classified the patients into 6 major types based on the location of myocardial hypertrophy involvement: ventricular septal HCM (n = 43); apical HCM (n = 30); basal septal HCM (n = 4); mid-ventricular HCM (n = 13); mass‑like HCM (n = 1), and diffuse HCM (n = 9). There were 4 patients with symmetric HCM, 96 with asymmetric HCM, 41 with obstructive HCM, and 59 with non-obstructive HCM. The diagnostic accuracy rate of CMR and echocardiography for HCM was 100% and 61%, respectively, with a missed diagnosis rate of 39% (39/100). LGE showed delayed enhancement, which manifested as patchy or focal enhancement within the hypertrophied myocardium. The delayed enhancement area was limited to the hypertrophied myocardial region. CMR + LGE showed myocardial fibrosis at the apex in 62 patients. Echocardiography alone detected 17 patients apical HCM.
CONCLUSION: The combination of CMR with clinical symptoms may aid in the diagnosis and classification of HCM, as well as in the characterization of myocardial fibrosis. CMR appears to be superior to echocardiography in detecting missed CMR diagnoses. Further study is required to validate these findings.

Title: Transport mechanical ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: an exploratory prehospital pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding the use of mechanical ventilation (MV) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains limited, particularly in prehospital settings.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and generate preliminary physiologic data regarding transport MV compared with bag-valve ventilation (BV) during CPR in OHCA.
METHODS: This prospective, time-sequenced, exploratory pilot study, conducted between September 2024 and October 2025, included adult OHCA patients aged ≥ 18 years managed by the Ramathibodi Emergency Medical Operation team. Patients received BV during the first 6 months, followed by MV thereafter, delivered using a HAMILTON-T1 transport mechanical ventilator in volume-controlled mode (tidal volume: 6-8 mL/kg; respiratory rate: 10 breaths/min; PEEP: 0 cmH₂O; I:E ratio: 1:5; FiO₂: 1.0; flow trigger: off). Ventilation was assessed using arterial or venous PCO₂ obtained after ≥ 3 min following intubation or upon return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). As a pilot study, this investigation was not powered to detect differences in clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Forty-one patients were analysed (29 BV, 12 MV). The mean age was 67 ± 15 years in the BV group and 66 ± 20 years in the MV group, with 55.2% and 66.7% male patients, respectively. No statistically significant differences were detected in PCO₂, pH, or pO₂ between groups. Clinical outcomes, including sustained ROSC and 28-day survival, were also similar between groups. Mechanical ventilation was operationally feasible in the prehospital setting despite several implementation challenges.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory prehospital pilot study, MV during CPR was feasible and produced preliminary physiologic measures comparable to BV. These findings are hypothesis-generating and may inform the design of future adequately powered studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was registered with the Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20241008007; 08 October 2024).

Title: Clinical characteristics of acute poisoning-related in-hospital cardiac arrest: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute poisoning is a recognized special circumstance in cardiac arrest, yet data on acute poisoning-related in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remain limited. This study aimed to describe the toxicant spectrum, presentation-to-IHCA interval, pre-arrest physiological status, resuscitation characteristics, and hospital outcomes among patients with acute poisoning-related IHCA.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective descriptive study of consecutive emergency department presentations for acute poisoning between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Eligible presentations included patients who developed IHCA after hospital arrival and were treated with chest compressions, defibrillation, or both. We extracted toxicant categories, presentation-to-IHCA interval, the most recent documented pre-arrest assessment within 1 h before IHCA, resuscitation characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 2,016 consecutive presentations for acute poisoning, 16 index IHCA events occurred in 16 patients (0.79%). Pesticide exposure was identified in 12 cases, including bipyridyl herbicides in 6, organophosphate pesticides in 3, and other pesticides in 3. Non-pesticide toxicants included aconitine in 2 patients, a cardiac glycoside-containing plant in 1, and mixed antipsychotic drugs in 1. Twelve of 16 IHCA events occurred within 24 h of presentation. The median interval between the last documented pre-arrest assessment and IHCA onset was 11.0 min (IQR, 7.3-30.8; range, 2-53). Documented pre-arrest assessments showed abnormalities in consciousness and hemodynamic status. The median Glasgow Coma Scale score was 8 (IQR, 3-13.5), 9 patients had a score ≤ 8, and 6 required vasoactive support before arrest, of whom 4 remained hypotensive at the most recent assessment. Initial arrest rhythm was shockable in 2 patients, non-shockable in 9, and unknown in 5. Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) was achieved in 13 patients; 3 patients survived to discharge, and all survivors had favorable neurological status at discharge.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute poisoning-related IHCA was uncommon but associated with substantial mortality in this single-center descriptive cohort. Pesticide exposure predominated, most IHCA events occurred within 24 h of presentation, documented pre-arrest abnormalities were observed, and hospital survival remained poor despite frequent ROSC. These findings provide descriptive in-hospital data on a rare toxicological cardiac arrest subgroup and should not be interpreted as identifying predictors of IHCA.

Title: Effect of dapagliflozin on left ventricular longitudinal strain and atrioventricular coupling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), including dapagliflozin, were initially developed for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite the established benefits of SGLT2i in heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), their effects on myocardial deformation (assessed by global longitudinal strain, GLS) and left atrioventricular coupling (quantified by the left atrioventricular coupling index, LACI) in HFpEF patients with concomitant chronic kidney disease (CKD)-hereafter referred to as HFpEF-CKD-remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of dapagliflozin on GLS and LACI in this high-risk comorbid population.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 259 patients with HFpEF-CKD from September 2023 to October 2024. Participants were assigned to two groups: the dapagliflozin group (dapagliflozin 10 mg/day added to conventional HF and CKD therapy without SGLT2i, n = 138) and the control group (conventional HF and CKD therapy without SGLT2i, n = 121). Conventional and speckle-tracking echocardiography were performed at baseline and 6-month follow-up to assess GLS, LACI, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and left atrial volume (LAV) parameters, including minimal LAV (LAVmin) and LAV index (LAVI).
RESULTS: Compared with controls, dapagliflozin decreased GLS (between-group Δ: -1.34%, 95% CI: -1.72 to -0.97; Cohen's d = 0.875) and reduced LACI (Δ: -0.07, 95% CI: -0.09 to -0.05; Cohen's d = 0.855), both p < 0.001. The dapagliflozin group showed greater reductions in LAV parameters (ΔLAVmin: -6.38 ± 9.06 mL vs. -1.25 ± 3.78 mL, p < 0.001; ΔLAVI: -0.82 ± 1.79 mL/m² vs. -0.43 ± 1.57 mL/m², p = 0.075). LVEF remained stable in both groups (p = 0.264). Multivariable regression analysis confirmed dapagliflozin as an independent predictor for both GLS reduction (B = -1.335, 95% CI: -1.686 to -1.006, p < 0.001) and LACI reduction (B = -0.057, 95% CI: -0.074 to -0.040, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HFpEF-CKD, dapagliflozin improves left ventricular longitudinal function and atrioventricular coupling. The superior sensitivity of novel echocardiographic parameters-GLS, LACI, and LAVmin-supports their clinical utility for monitoring early cardiac functional recovery during treatment.

Title: Menopausal status modifies the association between migraine and cardiovascular disease risk: a nationwide cohort study.
Journal: The journal of headache and pain
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether menopausal status modifies the association between migraine and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in women, using both relative and absolute risk measures.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service data. Women aged ≥ 40 years who underwent the 2009 health screening and had no prior CVD (myocardial infarction or stroke) were included. Migraine was defined by using ICD-10 diagnostic codes. Menopausal status was determined from questionnaire-based reproductive history and prespecified as an effect modifier. Incident CVD and cardiovascular death were ascertained. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Among 2,156,733 women, 923,517 were premenopausal and 1,233,216 postmenopausal. In premenopausal women, CVD incidence was higher in those with migraine than in those without migraine (2.22 vs. 1.38 per 1,000 person-years), with a higher risk after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.42-1.66). In postmenopausal women, CVD incidence was also higher among those with migraine (9.53 vs. 7.50 per 1,000 person-years), although the relative association was attenuated but remained significant (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.17-1.23). Accordingly, the crude incidence rate difference associated with migraine was larger after menopause (2.03 vs. 0.84 per 1,000 person-years). The relative associations between migraine and cardiovascular outcomes were stronger in premenopausal women, whereas larger absolute risk differences were observed in postmenopausal women. This pattern was observed for CVD, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke, but not for cardiovascular death.
CONCLUSION: Migraine was associated with increased CVD risk in women. Relative associations were stronger before menopause, whereas absolute excess incidence was greater after menopause. These findings highlight the importance of considering migraine in cardiovascular risk assessment across the female life course, including after menopause.

Title: Cumulative estimated glucose disposal rate, atherogenic index of plasma, and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance and atherogenic dyslipidemia are key interrelated processes in the development of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). Although estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) have been linked to CMM, whether they provide complementary information when evaluated simultaneously remains unclear.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 4,215 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Cumulative eGDR and cumulative AIP were calculated using repeated measurements from Wave 1 and Wave 3. Participants were followed from Wave 3 to Wave 5 for incident CMM. Cox regression models, restricted cubic splines, interaction analyses, and prognostic performance analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 5.0 years, 452 participants developed incident CMM. In the mutually adjusted model, each 1-SD increase in cumulative eGDR was associated with a lower risk of incident CMM (HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.52-0.63), whereas each 1-SD increase in cumulative AIP was associated with a higher risk (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.28). Joint analysis further differentiated risk. Compared with participants with high cumulative eGDR and low cumulative AIP, the fully adjusted HRs were 1.50 (95% CI, 1.05-2.14), 2.19 (95% CI, 1.58-3.02), and 3.83 (95% CI, 2.89-5.06) for those with high eGDR and high AIP, low eGDR and low AIP, and low eGDR and high AIP, respectively. Positive additive interaction was observed, whereas multiplicative interaction was not statistically significant. The prognostic contributions of the two indices were unequal. Adding cumulative AIP to a model containing cumulative eGDR resulted in statistically significant but modest improvements in reclassification, whereas adding cumulative eGDR to cumulative AIP produced larger improvements. The model incorporating cumulative eGDR and cumulative AIP also showed better prognostic performance than the corresponding cumulative triglyceride-glucose index (TyG)-AIP model, as reflected by improvements in continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement. Findings were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative eGDR and cumulative AIP were both associated with incident CMM after mutual adjustment and provided complementary risk information. Participants with low cumulative eGDR and high cumulative AIP had the highest CMM risk, with evidence of positive additive interaction.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Feasibility of adapted basic life support training in adults with intellectual disabilities in Italy: a prospective pilot study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge, with survival depending on rapid bystander intervention. Individuals with intellectual disabilities are frequently excluded from adult Basic Life Support (BLS) training, despite their potential role as lay rescuers. The main objective was to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary educational impact of adapted BLS training in adults with mild to moderate intellectual disabilities.
METHODS: A prospective pilot feasibility study was conducted with 18 adults recruited through a community disability organization. Participants were classified using the extended Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR). Training followed the Italian Resuscitation Council methodology and was adapted to participants' cognitive needs through simplified language, repeated demonstrations, visual reinforcement, and small-group hands-on practice. Knowledge was assessed before (T0) and after training (T1) using multiple-choice tests, while practical skills were evaluated through repeated in-session assessments conducted during the course. Practical skills included cardiac arrest recognition, chest compressions, defibrillation, and airway obstruction management, each scored on a standardized 0-2 scale.
RESULTS: Participants (mean age 44.7 years; 56% women) were classified as CDR 0 (39%), CDR 0.5 (28%), and CDR 1 (33%). Knowledge improved across all CDR groups, with the proportion of correct answers increasing substantially after training; in CDR 0 participants, correct answers rose from 31% to 71% (p < 0.001). Early-session practical assessments showed high recognition of cardiac arrest (75%) and airway obstruction (100%), although execution of chest compressions and defibrillation was initially limited (12.5%). Repeated in-session practical assessments showed progressive improvement in chest compressions, defibrillation, and airway obstruction management, with final-session performance reaching 82-92% of participants achieving sufficient or higher skill levels. Satisfaction was high, with all participants reporting positive feedback.
CONCLUSION: Adapted BLS training is feasible and potentially effective in individuals with intellectual disabilities, supporting the feasibility of their inclusion in resuscitation education programs and suggesting a potential contribution to community preparedness.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Protocol no. 14/2018, approval date 15 January 2018.

Title: Age matters? Investigating VARC-3 outcomes in surgical aortic valve reoperations: a multicenter study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Redo surgical aortic valve replacement (rSAVR) is known to carry higher operative risk compared with first-time aortic valve surgery. Evidence on how age influences outcomes following rSAVR remains scarce. This study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes after rSAVR, with a focus on the role of age.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all adult patients who underwent rSAVR in four centers between January 2015 and December 2022. The primary endpoint was Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 (VARC-3) periprocedural mortality. The impact of age on survival was assessed using univariable Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 215 patients were included (63% male; median age 69 years, IQR 59-75). Previous biological prostheses were present in 165 cases (77%). The median EuroSCORE II was 4.8% (IQR 3.0-8.1). Indications for reoperation included structural valve deterioration in 100 patients (46%), endocarditis in 87 (40%), and paravalvular leak in 14 (7%). Concomitant procedures were performed in 96 patients (45%), and 39 (18%) underwent urgent surgery. A biological valve was implanted in 159 patients (74%). Periprocedural VARC-3 mortality occurred in 22 cases (10%). Age showed no significant effect on periprocedural mortality (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.53-1.42, p = 0.42). During follow-up (median 4 years, IQR 2-5), overall survival was 86% (95% CI 81-91) at 1 year and 78% (95% CI 72-85) at 5 years. Age showed a significant non-linear association with late death at follow-up (p = 0.012), with a change-point at 70 years above which the risk increased progressively (HR 2.64, 95% CI 1.04-6.71 for an 85- vs. 70-year-old patient).
CONCLUSIONS: In our multicenter experience, rSAVR remains associated with relevant periprocedural risk. Age does not influence early VARC-3 mortality, but patients aged 70 years or older, as expected, show increased long-term mortality.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Clinical risk factors associated with coronary slow flow: a meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate factors associated with coronary slow flow (CSF) using a meta-analysis and to provide evidence-based support for the prevention and management of coronary artery disease.
METHODS: Relevant studies published between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from CNKI, CBM, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, and Embase using the search terms "coronary slow flow," "coronary slow flow phenomenon," "coronary slow flow syndrome," "related factors," "influencing factors," and "risk factors." Case-control studies that met the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria were included. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), with studies scoring ≥ 7 considered high quality. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan version 5.3. This study was registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261334323).
RESULTS: A total of 41 studies were included in the systematic review. Quantitative meta-analysis was performed only for risk factors reported in a sufficient number of studies with comparable definitions and extractable data. The meta-analysis suggested that smoking (OR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.13-1.29), higher body mass index (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.06-1.36), male sex (OR = 1.51, 95% CI: 1.26-1.81), hypertension (OR = 2.32, 95% CI: 1.27-4.26), elevated homocysteine (OR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.13-2.13), elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.36-1.94), and higher uric acid levels (OR = 1.90, 95% CI: 1.47-2.46) were associated with higher odds of CSF. In contrast, higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels were associated with lower odds of CSF (OR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.38-0.55).
CONCLUSION: Coronary slow flow (CSF) may be associated with multiple clinical and biochemical factors. Smoking, increased body mass index, male sex, hypertension, and elevated levels of homocysteine, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and uric acid were associated with higher odds of CSF, whereas higher HDL-C levels were associated with lower odds of CSF. These findings suggest that unhealthy lifestyle behaviors, metabolic abnormalities, and inflammatory responses may contribute to the development of CSF. Although many CSF-associated factors are potentially modifiable, early interventions-particularly smoking cessation, blood pressure and weight control, and improvement of metabolic and inflammatory status-may help reduce the likelihood of CSF. However, these associations should be interpreted cautiously because moderate-to-high heterogeneity remained in several pooled analyses. Future high-quality prospective studies are needed to clarify the relative importance of these factors, examine potential causal relationships, and evaluate targeted interventions.

Title: How well do dementia risk scores predict dementia? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: In our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to assess the predictive accuracy and clinical applicability of ten dementia risk assessment scores for incident dementia in cohort studies. Three of 10 risk scores had sufficient, comparable data for a meta-analysis. We analyzed the Cardiovascular Risk Factors Ageing and Dementia (CAIDE), Lifestyle for brain health (LIBRA), and Alzheimer's Disease Risk Index (ANU-ADRI) in middle- and older-aged baseline populations with short, medium, and long follow-up durations, starting free from dementia, with or without other health conditions. A total of 29 studies met our inclusion criteria; 13 were included in the meta-analyses. CAIDE performed best, particularly among middle-aged participants at baseline, with longer follow-up periods, yielding pooled areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.74-0.76. ANU-ADRI showed stable, moderate predictive accuracy with AUCs of approximately 0.65-0.71. The original LIBRA showed the lowest discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.51 to 0.60, whereas the modified LIBRA performed better, with AUCs of 0.65-0.67 at short follow-up and a pooled AUC of 0.70 (95% CI 0.66-0.74) at medium follow-up. Dementia risk assessment scales show variable predictive performance across scores, baseline age, and follow-up duration, and may be useful for dementia risk stratification in clinical practice. As a substantial proportion of dementia risk is linked to potentially modifiable factors, identifying high-risk individuals may help guide timely risk-reduction strategies. Further prospective validation is needed across different populations and clinical settings.

Title: Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis following ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion: a single-centre experience of thromboembolic and bleeding outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a risk in neurosurgery, but data for adults undergoing ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt insertion are limited. The safety of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis in this population remains unclear due to concerns about bleeding. This study evaluated the safety of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after VP shunt insertion in adults in relation to VTE and haematoma risk.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 246 adult patients who underwent primary VP shunt insertion at a tertiary centre between 2017 and 2021. Data on demographics, aetiology, surgery, radiological imaging, pharmacological thromboprophylaxis, and outcomes (VTE, post-operative haematomas) were collected and reviewed. Univariate analysis and propensity-matching were used to compare outcomes.
RESULTS: Median age was 63 years (range 17-90 years); common hydrocephalus aetiologies were tumour (32.9%) and normal pressure hydrocephalus (30.5%). Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis (median post-operative day 1) was given to 76.0% (n = 187), alongside universal mechanical prophylaxis. One VTE (pulmonary embolism, 0.4%) event occurred. Routine post-operative imaging detected 12 haematomas (4.9%); 2 (0.8%) were clinically significant: 1 intracerebral haemorrhage requiring surgical evacuation and 1 managed conservatively. Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis did not significantly increase the risk of post-operative haematoma formation overall (p > 0.99) and in a propensity score matched subgroup analysis that controlled for confounders (p = 0.36).
CONCLUSION: In this study, we demonstrate that early pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after primary VP shunt insertion appears to have an acceptable safety profile without significantly increasing haematoma risk. Our findings require validation in future multicentre cohorts.

Title: Ultrasound-guided versus conventional sinus tract laser closure for adolescent sacrococcygeal pilonidal disease: a retrospective comparative study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sacrococcygeal pilonidal disease (SPD) is common in adolescents and often recurs after surgery. Sinus tract laser closure (SiLaC) helps with healing, reduces recurrence, and improves appearance but may miss sinus branches. Using ultrasound guidance during SiLaC ensures precise treatment and protects healthy tissue. This study compared the short- and medium-term efficacy of ultrasound (US)-guided SiLaC with conventional SiLaC in treating adolescent patients with SPD.
METHODS: This retrospective study gathered and analyzed clinical data from 64 adolescent (18 years or younger) patients with SPD who underwent either SiLaC or US-guided SiLaC at a single center from March 2021 to January 2025. The study included 38 patients who received conventional SiLaC and 26 patients who received US-guided SiLaC, and recorded demographics, surgical history, lifestyle factors, laser parameters, short-term complications, healing and recurrence rates, wound closure time, and recovery time.
RESULTS: Among the 64 patients, 89.1% were male and 10.9% female, with a median age of 17 years. The US-guided group had a median follow-up of 18.0 (8.0, 37.8) months, while the conventional group had 20.5 (9.5, 35.8) months, both groups with similar demographic characteristics. The US-guided group showed significantly lower intraoperative laser duration and energy use (p < 0.05), and faster wound closure (p = 0.017). Recurrence was 4% in the US group vs. 25% in the conventional group (p = 0.037). No significant difference was found in the time to resume normal activities (p = 0.091).
CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary results suggest that US-guided SiLaC enhances the precision of sinus tract ablation by providing real-time intraoperative visualization in adolescents with SPD. In this cohort, its application was associated with reduced recurrence rates and expedited wound healing. However, these findings necessitate validation through larger-scale studies.

Title: Cardiovascular Risk Prediction in Postmenopausal Women With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: An Observational Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important risk factor for cardiovascular events, yet performance of cardiovascular prediction models are understudied in the CKD population, including women with CKD.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the performance of multiple cardiovascular prediction models, the Framingham, Adult Treatment Panel (ATP) III, ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), QRISK3, and PREVENT models, in women with and without CKD.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study (Women's Health Initiative Biomarker Studies).
PARTICIPANTS: 21,548 postmenopausal women ages 50-79 without cardiovascular disease, including 1,095 with CKD defined by eGFR < 60 mL/min per 1.73 m2.
MAIN MEASURES: Model discrimination by C-statistic. Calibration by clinically relevant decision-making thresholds. Included events varied by model: Framingham model outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), angina, or coronary heart disease (CHD) death; ATP III model outcomes included fatal and nonfatal CHD; PCE and PREVENT model outcomes included CHD or ischemic stroke; QRISK3 model outcomes included CHD, stroke, or transient ischemic attack.
KEY RESULTS: Number of cardiovascular events varied based on outcome definition. For the non-CKD group, events ranged from 846 (4.1%) for ATP III to 1,435 (7.0%) for QRISK3; for the CKD group, events ranged from 93 (8.5%) for ATP III to 145 (13.2%) for QRISK3. Discrimination by C-statistic ranged from 0.57 for the Framingham model to 0.67 for PREVENT in the CKD group; in the non-CKD group, C-statistics ranged from 0.61 for the Framingham model to 0.71 for QRISK3 and PREVENT. Calibration was generally poor in both CKD and non-CKD groups, with underprediction for women with CKD across most models, as well as underprediction for women without CKD for the PREVENT model.
CONCLUSION: Common cardiovascular risk prediction models have poor discrimination and calibration in women with CKD; the PREVENT model generally underpredicted risk for women with and without CKD.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Robot-assisted versus open partial nephrectomy in patients with a solitary kidney: a systematic review and meta-analysis of perioperative and functional outcomes.
Abstract: A patient whose renal tumor develops in a solitary kidney has no contralateral organ able to compensate, and therefore offers the clearest setting in which operative injury to the kidney can be studied. Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) has become routine practice among the wider surgical population, yet no systematic appraisal has established whether it is both safe and effective when the tumor is confined to a solitary kidney. To address this gap we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing perioperative and functional endpoints between RAPN and open partial nephrectomy (OPN) in these patients. Searches of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science covered each database from its first indexed record to August 13, 2026. Studies were eligible if they were retrospective cohorts in which RAPN and OPN were compared head-to-head in patients with a tumor of a solitary kidney. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was applied to grade the methodological quality of every report that qualified. Four retrospective studies contributed 333 patients with a solitary kidney (153 assigned to RAPN and 180 to OPN). None of the primary comparisons separated the two arms: the 12-month postoperative eGFR preservation rate (MD = - 3.77%, 95% CI - 10.71 to 3.18, p = 0.287), the need for temporary postoperative dialysis (OR = 1.80, 95% CI 0.47 to 6.90, p = 0.391) and CKD stage progression (OR = 1.42, 95% CI 0.67 to 3.00, p = 0.356). Three secondary endpoints did favor the robotic arm: warm ischemia was shorter by a significant margin (WMD = - 2.15 min, 95% CI - 4.20 to - 0.09, p = 0.041), discharge occurred earlier (WMD = - 2.39 days, 95% CI -4.44 to -0.34, p = 0.012 < 0.05), and blood loss was lower (WMD = - 141.88 mL, 95% CI - 277.40 to - 6.37, p < 0.05). No significant difference emerged for operative duration, transfusion requirement, overall, intraoperative or major complications, or the positive surgical margin rate. For tumors arising in a solitary kidney, renal function at 12 months, dialysis requirement, and CKD progression did not differ significantly between the robotic and open approaches. The robotic route nevertheless delivered a shorter hospital stay, briefer warm ischemia and less blood loss, and did so without increasing complications or positive margins. These retrospective, small-sample findings suggest that RAPN may be a reasonable alternative to OPN in carefully selected patients treated at experienced centers, but they do not establish equivalence or confirm safety and effectiveness. These conclusions are limited by the small number of eligible studies and by their retrospective design; prospective, higher-quality evidence is needed before they can be confirmed.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study; Review

Title: Temporal trends and clinical factors associated with ketamine infusion in hospitalized infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
Journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize temporal trends in ketamine infusion use in extremely preterm infants with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (sBPD) and identify associated clinical factors.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a 15-year (2010-2024) retrospective cohort study of extremely preterm infants with sBPD. Time was analyzed as a categorical variable in three 5-year epochs. Ketamine exposures were described, and multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between time periods and use, adjusting for clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 8888 infants with sBPD, 112 (1.3%) received ketamine infusion, with use increasing over time and rising most sharply between 2020 and 2024. Pulmonary hypertension (adjusted odds ratio, aOR 5.47, 95% CI 1.65-18.09), stage II/III necrotizing enterocolitis (aOR 2.06, 1.24-3.43), and tracheostomy (aOR 8.32, 3.50-19.77) were independently associated with use.
CONCLUSIONS: Ketamine infusions in sBPD are uncommon but have increased over time, particularly since 2020. Use is associated with markers of greater illness severity.

Title: Association of winter indoor-temperature variability with 5-year changes in home blood pressure: the Smart Wellness Housing Cohort Survey in Japan.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: Cold indoor temperatures acutely raise blood pressure, but their long-term effects remain uncertain. We investigated whether winter indoor-temperature levels and temporal variability were associated with 5-year changes in home blood pressure. This nationwide cohort included 700 adults from 483 households with complete data. Living-room temperature was measured at 10-min intervals, and home blood pressure was measured twice each morning and evening for 2 weeks in winter at baseline and at the 5-year follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models with household random intercepts were adjusted for baseline blood pressure, individual covariates, and mean indoor temperature in analyses of variability. Mean and minimum indoor temperatures were not associated with 5-year changes in systolic or diastolic home blood pressure. In contrast, a 10 °C/day higher cumulative indoor-temperature variation was associated with 0.42 mmHg (95% confidence interval, 0.04-0.80) and 0.27 mmHg (0.01-0.54) greater increases in systolic and diastolic home blood pressure, respectively. Each additional daily indoor-temperature swing ≥3 °C and ≥5 °C was associated with 0.32 mmHg (0.004-0.636) and 0.49 mmHg (0.04-0.93) greater increases in systolic blood pressure, respectively. A model-based comparison of cumulative indoor-temperature variation values 1 standard deviation above versus below the mean yielded an estimated difference of 1.47 mmHg (0.13-2.81) in the 5-year change in home systolic blood pressure. The sensitivity analysis yielded broadly consistent results. Greater winter indoor-temperature variability was associated with larger 5-year increases in home blood pressure independently of mean indoor temperature. Clinical Trial Registration URL: http://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm . UMIN Clinical Trials Registry, Trial No. UMIN000042196.

Title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk.
METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum.
RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS (P=0.784).
CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

Title: Urgent, Emergency, and Salvage Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis may preclude waiting for elective treatment, and evidence for non-elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is limited. We assessed 12-month mortality, 30-day safety, and recovery after urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients undergoing urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI at one centre in 2022-2025. The primary endpoint was 12-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included device success, 30-day safety, and functional and echocardiographic recovery.
RESULTS: Among 53 patients, 36 underwent urgent, 14 emergency, and 3 salvage TAVI. Device success was 52/53 (98.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 1/36, 0/14, and 0/3; 12-month mortality was 2/36, 1/14, and 0/3 (3/53). Kaplan-Meier 12-month survival was 94.3% (95% confidence interval 83.5-98.1%). New atrioventricular block was detected in 2/53 on postoperative day 2; by 30 days, haemofiltration or renal replacement therapy occurred in 1/53 and permanent pacemaker implantation in 0/53. At 12 months, cardiovascular mortality was 2/53, heart-failure readmission 4/53, stroke 1/53, a separate Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2 bleeding event 1/53, and permanent pacemaker implantation 0/53. Paired analyses showed improved New York Heart Association class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12, left ventricular ejection fraction, and transvalvular gradients at 30 days and 12 months (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.

Title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequent after heart transplantation (HT) and is exacerbated by immunosuppressive therapy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve metabolic control, but data in HT recipients are limited.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, multicenter study including HT recipients with T2DM from 14 Spanish centers. In patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, we assessed antidiabetic and immunosuppressive therapies, adverse events, and changes in metabolic parameters, insulin dose, and immunosuppressant trough levels during the first year after GLP-1 RA initiation.
RESULTS: Among 734 HT recipients with T2DM (2011-2021), 108 (14.7%) received GLP-1 RAs (mean age 55.4 ± 9.0 y; 79.6% male), initiated 4.0 ± 3.1 y post-HT. At baseline, 64.8% had obesity. Semaglutide was used in 59%, dulaglutide in 27%, liraglutide in 13%, and tirzepatide in 1%; 41.7% achieved the maximum therapeutic dose. After 1 y, significant reductions were observed in body weight (-6.2 kg; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.7 to -4.5 kg), fasting glucose (-27 mg/dL; 95% CI, -41 to -7 mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (-0.74%; 95% CI, -1.12% to -0.35%), total cholesterol (-12 mg/dL; 95% CI, -19 to -6 mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-8 mg/dL; 95% CI, -14 to -2 mg/dL), triglycerides (-29 mg/dL; 95% CI, -53 to -5 mg/dL), and systolic blood pressure (-3.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, -6.4 to -0.9 mm Hg). Tacrolimus trough levels decreased modestly (-0.7 ng/mL; 95% CI, -1.4 to -0.1 ng/mL; P = 0.025), without episodes of acute rejection. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 12.0%, leading to discontinuation in 3.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

Title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Prognosis and Treatment Benefit After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) can achieve substantial mitral regurgitation (MR) reduction in appropriately selected patients, yet outcomes after technically successful intervention remain heterogeneous. This variability has prompted interest in echocardiographic markers of limited treatment benefit. However, adverse prognosis after TEER and absence of benefit attributable to TEER are fundamentally different concepts, and most available imaging studies evaluate the former rather than the latter.
METHODS: This state-of-the-art review summarizes evidence on echocardiographic assessment of prognosis and treatment response across the mitral TEER pathway, integrating baseline multichamber phenotyping, procedural and immediate hemodynamic assessment, longitudinal imaging, and evidence from randomized trials of TEER in secondary MR.
RESULTS: Baseline left ventricular remodeling and myocardial dysfunction, left atrial disease, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial uncoupling, and tricuspid regurgitation identify greater cardiovascular disease burden and residual risk after TEER. Procedural assessment extends beyond residual MR to include transmitral pressure gradient, forward flow, and left atrial hemodynamics, whereas serial imaging characterizes subsequent ventricular, atrial, pulmonary, and right-heart trajectories. Persistent structural or hemodynamic abnormalities and absence of reverse remodeling should not be equated with irreversible disease or therapeutic futility. Randomized subgroup analyses in secondary MR have not consistently demonstrated significant treatment-effect modification by several adverse echocardiographic phenotypes; however, these analyses were not adequately powered to exclude clinically meaningful interactions. Moreover, COAPT excluded patients with extreme ventricular remodeling, markedly elevated pulmonary pressures, or advanced RV dysfunction, limiting generalizability to these populations. Differences among COAPT, MITRA-FR, and RESHAPE-HF2 further caution against defining a universal echocardiographic treatment-response phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiography is essential for defining MR mechanism and severity, characterizing multichamber cardiovascular disease, evaluating procedural results, and refining longitudinal risk assessment. However, current evidence does not establish a validated echocardiographic threshold or phenotype that reliably predicts absence of treatment benefit. Randomized subgroup findings require cautious interpretation because of limited statistical power and the exclusion of patients with the most advanced ventricular and pulmonary vascular disease. Future adequately powered comparative studies should evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect across MR etiologies using standardized multichamber imaging and patient-centered outcomes.

Title: [Myocardium global longitudinal strain and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for predicting MACE risks following percutaneous coronary intervention for first-time acute myocardial infarction: a prospective cohort study].
Journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the combined predictive value of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)‑derived global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with first-time acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 134 patients with first-time AMI (99 male and 35 female patients aged 33-83 years, mean 60.19±11.7 years) were enrolled between June, 2022 and July, 2025. All the patients underwent PCI and were followed up via outpatient visits or telephone for a median of 538 days post-discharge. The patients were divided into non-MACEs (n=103) and MACEs groups (n=31) for comparison of baseline clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Baseline comparisons revealed that the MACEs group had a significantly older age, higher white blood cell count, neutrophil count, NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and NT-proBNP, and lower monocyte counts (all P<0.05) with had higher Gensini scores and incidences of anterior wall infarction, more frequent left anterior descending artery culprit lesions, but fewer right coronary artery lesions and lower rates of TIMI low-risk chest pain (P<0.05). In patients with MACEs, CMR findings revealed significantly higher frequencies of late gadolinium enhancement, end-systolic volume index, paradoxical motion, and aneurysmal wall formation, decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, and reduced infarct-segment and global radial, circumferential, and longitudinal strains (P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified NLR and GLS as independent predictors for MACEs. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that both GLS (AUC=0.825) and NLR (AUC=0.820) alone had predictive ability for MACEs, but their combination significantly increased the AUC to 0.921 (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: CMR-derived GLS and peripheral blood NLR are both strongly associated with post-PCI prognosis in first-time AMI patients, and their combination allows more accurate prediction of MACEs to facilitate effective early risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

Title: [Association between depressive symptoms and renal hyperfiltration in middle-aged and older adults].
Journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations of depressive symptoms and depressive episodes with renal hyperfiltration (RHF) in middle-aged and older adults.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 9469 middle-aged and older participants from Lanzhou site of the REACTION study. After excluding individuals with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL·min-1·1.73 m-2, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g, malignant tumors, incomplete depression questionnaire data, or antidepressant use, the participants were assessed for depressive symptoms using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and categorized in <5, 5-9, and ≥10 groups. Depressive episode status was also evaluated. RHF was defined as residuals above the 95th percentile from a regression model of log-transformed eGFR adjusted for age, sex, height, weight, hypertension, and diabetes. The associations of depressive status with RHF and the dose-response relationship between PHQ-9 total score and RHF risk were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analysis, respectively. Random forest, SHAP, and Boruta were used for exploratory analyses.
RESULTS: Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant nonlinear association between PHQ-9 total score and RHF risk. After multivariable adjustment, a significantly increased RHF risk was found in the PHQ-9 ≥10 group (OR=1.854, 95% CI: 1.074-3.201; P=0.027) but not in the PHQ-9 5-9 and PHQ-9 0-4 groups. When PHQ-9 was dichotomized as <10 and ≥10, a PHQ-9 score ≥10 was associated with a higher risk of RHF (OR=1.864, 95% CI: 1.080-3.210; P=0.025). Mild depressive episodes were not associated with RHF, whereas major depressive episodes were independently associated with increased RHF risks (OR=1.547, 95% CI: 1.082-2.212; P=0.017). Exploratory machine learning analyses showed that depressive episodes and clinically relevant depressive symptoms were stable features for RHF risk identification but with weaker contributions than age, fasting blood glucose, and systolic blood pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: In middle-aged and older adults, depressive symptoms are nonlinearly associated with RHF risks, which increased significantly when PHQ-9 score reached a clinically meaningful threshold. Major depressive episodes are also associated with increased RHF risks, and their temporal relationship and underlying mechanisms require further investigation in prospective studies.

Title: Downstream invasive testing, revascularization, and major adverse cardiovascular events following coronary CT angiography with and without fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography: A propensity-matched real-world cohort study.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography (FFR-CT) enables combined anatomical and physiological assessment of coronary artery disease using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) data. Real-world evidence comparing downstream utilization and clinical outcomes following CCTA with versus without FFR-CT remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To compare invasive coronary angiography (ICA), coronary revascularization, additional cardiac testing, and one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients undergoing CCTA with versus without FFR-CT.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Research Network, in which 118 healthcare organizations were queried. Adults undergoing CCTA between January 1, 2020, and July 20, 2024, were categorized according to receipt of FFR-CT. The initial cohorts included 17,754 patients receiving FFR-CT and 198,220 undergoing CCTA alone. After 1:1 propensity-score matching on demographic and clinical characteristics, 15,375 patients were retained in each cohort. Outcomes were assessed from days 8 through 365 after the index event. MACE was defined as death, acute myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.
RESULTS: Compared with CCTA alone, CCTA with FFR-CT was associated with higher rates of ICA (24.0% vs 12.5%; risk ratio [RR], 1.920; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.826-2.020), percutaneous coronary intervention (7.6% vs 3.7%; RR, 2.076; 95% CI, 1.883-2.290), and coronary artery bypass grafting (3.3% vs 1.8%; RR, 1.770; 95% CI, 1.533-2.045). Additional noninvasive functional cardiac testing was also more frequent following FFR-CT (7.0% vs 5.1%; RR, 1.370; 95% CI, 1.253-1.497). Conversely, FFR-CT was associated with lower one-year MACE (8.8% vs 10.5%; RR, 0.835; 95% CI, 0.779-0.894), acute myocardial infarction (3.9% vs 4.7%; RR, 0.822; 95% CI, 0.740-0.915), and all-cause mortality (2.0% vs 2.9%; RR, 0.676; 95% CI, 0.585-0.782). All comparisons were significant at p < 0.001.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large propensity-matched cohort, CCTA with FFR-CT was associated with greater downstream invasive and noninvasive testing and higher rates of PCI and CABG, but lower one-year MACE, myocardial infarction, and mortality. These findings may reflect more effective identification of actionable coronary disease; however, differences in underlying anatomical disease severity, site-level practice patterns, and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation.

Title: Artifacts, Anesthesiologists, and the Art of Seeing: Perspective on the 2026 ASE Guideline for Cardiac Ultrasound Artifact Identification and Mitigation.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

Title: Cardiac and natriuretic peptide profiles by subtype and sex in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) encompasses heterogeneous metabolic phenotypes. We examined associations of MASLD subtypes with epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) thickness, left atrial volume index (LAVI), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and whether these associations differed by sex.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In a cross-sectional analysis of 6181 adults undergoing concurrent abdominal ultrasonography and transthoracic echocardiography, participants were classified as No MASLD, Lean MASLD, Obese MASLD without diabetes, or Obese MASLD with diabetes (2023 Delphi criteria). Multivariable linear regression and sex-stratified analyses were used. Obese subtypes had greater EAT thickness, with the largest contrast in those with diabetes (β = 0.030 cm; p < 0.001). EAT associations were two- to three-fold stronger in women. Lean MASLD was associated with lower LAVI (β = -2.06 mL/m2; p < 0.001), predominantly in men. NT-proBNP was 25-39% lower across MASLD subtypes (all p < 0.001), including lean disease, and inversely associated with metabolic burden. Sex interactions were significant for all outcomes. Partial R2 was 3.0% for log NT-proBNP and 0.6-1.0% for structural outcomes. Estimates in women were similar after menopause adjustment.
CONCLUSION: MASLD subtypes were associated with different EAT, LAVI, and NT-proBNP profiles, with differences by sex. Structural contrasts were modest, whereas the association with NT-proBNP was larger. The clinical significance of these findings requires prospective evaluation.

Title: [LDL-c and residual cardiovascular risk in patients with coronary artery disease].
Abstract: In secondary prevention, current therapeutic management of dyslipidemia primarily aims to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) levels, as LDL-c is a major driver of atherosclerosis. Elevated LDL-c levels are also one of the main modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. LDL-c lowering is directly, proportionally, and linearly associated with a reduction in cardiovascular events, with no apparent threshold effect. However, patients with chronic coronary syndrome or those who have recently experienced an acute coronary event are still generally undertreated and achieve guideline-recommended targets in only one out of four cases. This article aims to explore the underlying causes of and potential solutions to this therapeutic gap, which is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Treatment adherence varies considerably across studies (randomized controlled trials or real-life studies), as well as across geographical settings, and appears to be approximately 60%. However, non-adherence to treatment alone does not explain the low proportion of patients achieving LDL-c treatment targets, which remains at approximately 25%. The underlying reasons are complex and multifactorial. Paradoxically, although the expanding therapeutic armamentarium allows for increased substantial LDL-c reductions, this has not translated into a corresponding improvement in target attainment. Therapeutic inertia may arise at the patient, physician, and healthcare system levels. Furthermore, patient education and the therapeutic alliance should remain central to patient management and should be regularly reinforced and individualized.

Title: [Translated article] Complications associated with parenteral nutrition in hospitalized patients.
Journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malnutrition is common in hospitalized patients. Parenteral nutrition is a therapeutic alternative to meet the nutritional requirements of patients in whom the gastrointestinal tract is unavailable or non-functional. This therapy has been associated with a wide range of infectious, mechanical and metabolic complications. The aim of the study was to assess the incidence of these complications.
METHOD: A prospective multicenter observational study in hospitalized adult patients receiving parenteral nutrition ≥72 h was conducted. Follow-up was performed until one week after the discontinuation of parenteral nutrition. Data were collected from electronic medical records and parenteral nutrition validation programs (Kabisoft and Clinus). Risk of malnutrition was determined according to MUST or CONUT criteria. The main variables were: incidence of catheter-related bacteriemia, catheter-tip colonization, phlebitis, thrombosis, catheter obstruction, catheter malposition, pneumothorax, hyperglycemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, hepatobiliary disorders and refeeding syndrome. A descriptive analysis was performed using SPSS v23 software.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were included, with a median age of 68 (28-90) years, 48.3% men and a body mass index of 26.2 ± 6.6 kg/m2. Of these, 61.7% were surgical patients and 46.7% were at low risk of malnutrition. Parenteral nutrition was administered for a median of 10 (3-40) days, 90.0% through central access. Patients received a mean of 18.4 ± 5.0 kcal/kg/day (74.7% of requirements), 1.1 ± 0.4 g/kg/day of protein, 2.4 ± 0.7 g/kg/day of glucose, and 0.5 ± 0.2 g/kg/day of lipids. Of them, 35% received concomitant enteral nutrition. Overall, 80.0% experienced at least one complication: metabolic (71.7%), mechanical (18.3%), and infectious (10.0%). Incidences were: hepatobiliary alteration (61.7%), hyperglycemia (48.3%), phlebitis (13.3%), catheter occlusion (8.3%), catheter-related bacteriemia (8.3%), hypertriglyceridemia (1.7%), hypercholesterolemia (1.7%), and colonization (1.7%). Gram-positive microorganisms were the most frequently isolated.
CONCLUSIONS: Although complications associated with parenteral nutrition occur, the rate of serious complications, such as infections, is low. While most patients experienced at least one complication, metabolic events were the most common, and they are generally easy to detect and manage. The incidence of mechanical complications, mainly phlebitis and catheter occlusions, was moderate.

Title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' interventions on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vascular surgeons are treating more older, frail and multimorbid patients. Integrated care models including both surgeons and geriatricians have improved peri-operative outcomes in orthopaedics. This meta-analysis investigated the impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' services on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase and recent conference abstracts were searched for studies of all methodologies comparing outcomes before and after the introduction of 'Vascular Geriatrics' service. Risk of bias was assessed using Methodological Index for Non-Randomised Studies criteria for non-randomised studies and Risk of Bias Tool (Version Two) tool for randomised. Certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations analysis. Meta-analyses compared the relative risks of inpatient mortality, complications, discharge to home and 30-day readmission using a random-effects model. Length of stay (LOS) in days was compared using mean difference.
RESULTS: Eight studies with 2441 patients were included. Models included outpatient pre-operative comprehensive geriatric assessment, inpatient geriatric liaison service and geriatrician-surgeon co-management. 'Vascular Geriatrics' was associated with a lower risk of inpatient mortality (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.9, P = .010), cardiac complications (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.19-0.62, P < .001) and infective complications (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38-0.63, P < .001). Delirium risk was reduced but not significantly (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.25-1.34, P = .20). There was no association in LOS (P = .37), discharge to home (P = .55) or 30-day readmission risk (P = .64).
CONCLUSIONS: Though study quality was poor, formalised geriatric involvement was associated with a decreased risk of adverse peri-operative outcomes in vascular patients compared to traditional care models. Further studies are needed to investigate the most effective design of geriatrician-surgeon partnership.

Title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization.
OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11).
CONCLUSIONS: recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

Title: Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
METHODS: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
RESULTS: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH.
CONCLUSIONS: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]).
CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation.
REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial

Title: Association of exercise with phenotype and arrhythmic outcomes in gene-elusive arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death in young adults and athletes. It is mostly genetically determined, with causal variants predominantly affecting desmosomal genes. Approximately one-third of patients remain gene-elusive despite extensive testing. Gene-elusive patients often report significantly higher lifetime exercise exposure than those with desmosomal ACM, suggesting a disproportionate role of exercise in this subgroup, also termed ‘exercise-induced ACM’. Yet, the effect of exercise history on the clinical characteristics and prognosis of this phenotype remains scarce.
METHODS: In this retrospective, single-centre cohort study, we included patients with definite or borderline ACM and negative genetic testing for ACM-associated genes. Exercise exposure was quantified with a standardised sports activity survey or from medical records. Competitive athletes were defined by an exercise exposure ≥24 metabolic equivalent of task-hour/week for ≥6 consecutive years and regular participation in competitive events.
