ISR was diagnosed in 40 stents (13.6%). Aalen-Johansen cumulative ISR incidence was 4.8% (95% CI 2.9-7.9), 10.2% (95% CI 7.1-14.5), and 12.9% (95% CI 9.3-18.0) at 3, 5, and 8 years, respectively. Atrial fibrillation (HR 3.71, 95% CI 1.74-7.91, p < 0.001) and in-stent CTO (HR 3.51, 95% CI 1.53-8.04, p = 0.003) were independently associated with ISR.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term ISR after CTO PCI was infrequent in this high-risk cohort, although estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected imaging follow-up among survivors. ISR was independently associated with atrial fibrillation and in-stent CTO at the index procedure.

Title: Short- and Mid-Term Clinical, Functional, and Radiographic Outcomes of the 5C® MEDic Knee System Following Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medial pivot total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has been developed to better reproduce native knee kinematics and improve patient satisfaction compared with conventional implant designs. This study evaluated the short- and mid-term clinical, functional, radiographic, and survivorship outcomes of the 5C® MEDic medial pivot knee system following primary TKA.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study included 419 primary TKAs performed in 372 patients between 2022 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS-12), Oxford Knee Score (OKS), Forgotten Joint Score (FJS-12), visual analogue scale (VAS) satisfaction, and range of motion. Radiographic evaluation included hip-knee-ankle angle, arithmetic HKA, joint line obliquity, lateral distal femoral angle, medial proximal tibial angle, and Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) classification. Implant survivorship was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed in all patient-reported outcome measures at 1 year . Mean OKS improved from 20.8 preoperatively to 41.2, while KOOS subscales demonstrated substantial gains in pain, symptoms, function, sports, and quality of life. Knee flexion increased from 111.1° to 123.2°, and extension improved from -5.6° to -0.7°. Kaplan-Meier survivorship was 99.8% at 1 year. One acute periprosthetic joint infection was successfully treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention, and one patient developed deep venous thrombosis. No cases of aseptic loosening, instability, mechanical failure, or periprosthetic fracture were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: The 5C® MEDic medial pivot knee system demonstrated excellent early clinical, functional, and radiographic outcomes, high patient satisfaction, a low complication rate, and excellent short- and mid- term survivorship following primary TKA.

Title: Contribution of genetic markers to cerebral venous thrombosis risk among Tunisian patients: A case-control study.
Abstract: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is a rare multifactorial disease which has been associated with inherited thrombophilic factors. The present study was performed to assess the association of genetic markers such as factor V of Leiden (FVL), methylenotetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) and thrombin activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor (TAFI) polymorphisms and underlying conditions as risk factors for CVT in Tunisian patients. Fifty-two patients with radiologically confirmed CVT and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled in the study. The DNAs of both groups were tested. We found that the frequency of 4G/4G of PAI-1 gene was higher among CVT group in comparison to controls (p < 0.001) and significantly associated with CVT of undetermined origin (p < 0.001). Heterozygous and homozygous models of C1040T -TAFI genotypes were associated with an increased risk of CVT compared to controls (p = 0.01; OR 6.6 and 9.15 respectively) as well as homozygous mutation of the PAI gene (p < 0.001; OR = 12.32). The risk of CVT was relevant in the presence of combined mutant genotypes of MTHFR (CT)/ PAI-1 (4G4G) and PAI-1 (4G4G)/ TAFI (CT) mutations (P = 0.035; OR: 10.68 and 13.19 respectively). This is the first case-control study from Tunisia establishing PAI-1 4G/4G and C1040T-TAFI variants as a strong risk factor for CVT in comparison to healthy controls as well as combined mutant genotypes of MTHFR, PAI-1and TAFI, so they should be included in laboratory testing panel of thrombophilia. Knowing the subset of patients carrying these genetic thrombophilia markers enables physicians to take appropriate measures to prevent future CVT recurrence.

Title: Factors Associated with Predischarge Morbidity and Mortality in Small for Gestational Age Infants: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with predischarge morbidity and mortality among small for gestational age infants.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of small for gestational age infants admitted to a level IV neonatal intensive care unit. We determined the association of clinical characteristics, congenital anomalies, and genetic disorders with the primary outcome of predischarge morbidity or mortality and characterized morbidity and mortality across congenital anomaly subgroups.
RESULTS: Among 293 small for gestational age infants, 18 (6.1%) had a genetic disorder and 103 (35.2%) had a major congenital anomaly, with congenital heart disease (CHD) representing the largest subgroup. The primary outcome of morbidity or mortality occurred in 93 infants (31.7%); 74 infants (25.3%) experienced morbidity and 19 (6.5%) died. CHD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 16.5, 95% CI 6.44-45.7) and multiple congenital anomalies (aOR: 17.8, 95% CI 4.64-71.1) were found to be strongly associated with morbidity or mortality, after accounting for sex, maternal race, and intubation > 7 days. Statistically significant associations were also found with the presence of musculoskeletal anomalies as well as genetic disorders in infants without congenital anomalies, though in limited sample sizes. CHD was the largest contributor to morbidity, whereas multiple congenital anomalies accounted for the greatest proportion of mortality. Infants with abdominal wall defects and central nervous system anomalies experienced no morbidity or mortality.
CONCLUSION: Congenital heart disease and multiple congenital anomalies were strongly associated with morbidity and mortality among SGA infants, whereas the degree of SGA alone was not. These findings suggest that risk is not explained by the degree of SGA alone and may be more strongly associated with congenital disease and other underlying factors.
KEY POINTS: Risk is highly variable in SGA infantsCHD predicts adverse outcomesMultiple anomalies predict adverse outcomesDegree of SGA alone does not explain risk.

Title: Thrombotic Risk of Targeted Therapies in Breast Cancer: A Real-World Cohort Study.
Abstract: Purpose Targeted therapies for breast cancer, including CDK4/6, PARP, mTOR, and PI3K inhibitors, have raised concerns regarding thrombosis risk, but real-world data comparing these agents remain limited. We investigated thrombosis incidence and risk factors in a large national cohort of breast cancer patients. Methods In this retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX national database, we evaluated the thrombotic risk and associated factors among patients with breast cancer treated with these therapies. The primary outcome was any arterial or venous thrombotic event. Results Among 4,165 patients on targeted therapy, treatment with CDK4/6i was associated with increased risk of any thrombosis (HR 3.36, 95% CI 2.89-3.92) and venous thrombosis (HR 4.45, 95% CI 3.68-5.39). PARPi (HR 3.78, 95% CI 1.82-7.85; venous HR 5.79, 95% CI 2.52-13.3) and everolimus (HR 6.59, 95% CI 3.82-11.4; venous HR 9.67, 95% CI 5.29-17.7) showed similar associations. Within CDK4/6i, palbociclib carried the highest hazard for any thrombosis (HR 3.64, 95% CI 3.02-4.39) and venous thrombosis (HR 5.11, 95% CI 4.05-6.45). Nicotine dependence (HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.91-2.12), brain metastases (HR 4.20, 95% CI 2.98-5.93), and higher BMI (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.03-1.03) were independent risk factors. Conclusion This real-world analysis demonstrates that CDK4/6i and everolimus were associated with increased risk of both arterial and venous thrombosis, while PARPi was specifically associated with venous thrombosis. Similar risk was seen across CDK4/6 inhibitor agents. These results support risk stratification tools incorporating both agent and patient-level factors to better inform clinical management.

Title: Cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning models for early-stage node-negative breast cancer relapse prediction.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant therapy decision in early-stage node-negative breast cancer remains one of the most challenging problems in oncology. Although most patients in this population achieve favorable outcomes with endocrine therapy alone, a subset remains at risk of relapse and may benefit from chemotherapy. Accurate identification of high-risk and low-risk patients is therefore essential to prevent both undertreatment and overtreatment.
METHODS: In this study, machine learning models were assessed using MSK-IMPACT (n=645) and METABRIC (n=503) cohorts comprising node-negative stage I-II breast cancer patients. Three experimental settings were evaluated: training on MSK-IMPACT and testing on METABRIC, the reverse direction, and five-fold cross-validation on the combined cohort. Sensitivity analysis and data harmonization were applied to identify and mitigate cohort-specific bias. Survival analysis, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretability, and ablation analyses were performed to validate clinical relevance and characterize feature contributions.
RESULTS: The combined cohort model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.788 ± 0.028 across five-fold cross-validation, while bidirectional cross-cohort validation yielded AUC of 0.741 when testing on MSK-IMPACT and AUC of 0.714 when testing on METABRIC. Survival validation on METABRIC out-of-fold predictions from the combined cohort model showed hazard ratios of 3.01 (95% CI: 2.28-3.98) for disease-free survival and 2.35 (95% CI: 1.79-3.09) for overall survival, consistent across Luminal A, Luminal B, and Triple-Negative subtypes.
CONCLUSION: Validated across two geographically independent cohorts, the proposed model enables cost-effective, gene expression-free identification of patients at high-risk of distant relapse and may facilitate adjuvant chemotherapy decision-making in early-stage node-negative breast cancer.

Title: Functional and molecular profiles of the neuroretina and retinal pigmented epithelium-choroid in response to aging and Nrf2 deletion.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Age is the leading factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD), in which retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) atrophy is a hallmark. The nuclear factor-erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), a major anti-stress transcription factor, decreases in AMD, suggesting bioenergetic stress interacts with age during AMD pathogenesis. We profiled visual function and gene expression of the retina and RPE-choroid with Nrf2 deletion and aging.
METHODS: We tested 3mo and 14mo Nrf2 null (Nrf2 KO) and Nrf2 WT mice for optokinetic tracking (OKT) and dark-adapted electroretinography (ERG) responses. Eyes were harvested for retina outer nuclear layer (ONL) thickness analysis and retina and RPE-choroid cup RNA isolation for RNAseq profiling.
RESULTS: Visual acuity was reduced with aging with lower values in the Nrf2 KO vs Nrf2 WT comparison at 14mo. We observed aged-related reduction of a-, b-, and c-wave ERG amplitudes in both WT and KO mice. Age-related c-wave decline was exacerbated by Nrf2 loss. By RNAseq, two-way ANOVA of RPE-choroid samples revealed differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with age and genotype main effects, as well as DEGs with age and genotype interaction effects. Age DEGs were over-represented in pathways related to inflammation and phagocytosis. Genotype DEGs were associated with alterations in antioxidant and inflammatory processes. Retina RNAseq showed age and genotype DEGs.
CONCLUSIONS: Ablation of Nrf2 exacerbates age-related declines suggesting that decrease in Nrf2 with aging has functional consequences for inflammation/resiliency. We provide retina and RPE-choroid bulk-RNAseq datasets from the same cohort of mice that can be interrogated to better understand degeneration of retina/RPE-choroid.

Title: Ultrasound-guided versus open surgical central venous access in children: A systematic review.
Journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
Abstract: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are essential in pediatric care for long-term venous access. While tunneled CVCs have traditionally been placed using open surgical venotomy or cut-down (OS), ultrasound-guided (USG) percutaneous insertion is widely used. However, no systematic review has yet evaluated pediatric evidence directly comparing both approaches. We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing USG and OS placement of CVCs in patients younger than 18 years. PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched until September 2025. The primary outcome was successful catheter placement; secondary outcomes included infection, thrombosis, venous diameter after catheter removal, and procedure duration. Five RCTs with 587 children were included. Placement success was comparable between techniques (97.5% USG vs. 95.7% OS; RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.96-1.05; moderate-certainty evidence). Infection rates did not differ significantly. USG was associated with a significantly lower risk of thrombosis (RR 0.34, 95% CI 0.14-0.82), consistently shorter procedure times, and better preservation of venous diameter, although the certainty of evidence for these outcomes was very low. USG placement achieves comparable success to OS but may offer procedural and vessel-preservation benefits.

Title: Patient-reported outcomes and skeletal symptoms in multiple myeloma stratified by proteasome inhibitor-based therapy: a prospective interdisciplinary cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma (MM) frequently causes osteolytic bone disease and skeletal symptoms. Proteasome inhibitors (PIs) are central to MM treatment and in routine practice, PI-based therapy is preferentially selected for patients with more active or symptomatic disease. Hereby, PIs may also exert bone-modulating effects beyond their antimyeloma activity. Whether these biological effects are reflected in patient-reported outcomes or skeletal symptoms during routine care remains unclear.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 209 patients with MM during routine interdisciplinary follow-up and stratified them by current PI-based versus non-PI-based treatment status. Sixty-nine patients were reassessed after at least 6 months. Patient-reported outcomes and skeletal symptoms were evaluated using multivariable regression and sensitivity analyses addressing baseline imbalances and treatment selection.
RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients (37%) were currently receiving PI-based treatment. In adjusted analyses, current PI-based treatment status was not associated with Quality of Life (β = -0.08, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.29; p = 0.662), health-related status (β = -0.06, 95% CI -0.42 to 0.30; p = 0.740), bone pain (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.74; p = 0.791), or prevalent osteolytic lesions (OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.53 to 2.96; p = 0.601). QoL and health-related status remained comparable during follow-up. MM-related bone pain was numerically more frequent among patients currently receiving PI-based treatment (46% vs. 33%), although the association did not reach statistical significance after multivariable adjustment (OR 1.80, 95% CI 0.93 to 3.48; p = 0.081).
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective real-world cohort, current PI-based treatment status was not associated with measurable differences in global patient-reported outcomes, overall bone pain, or prevalent osteolytic lesions compared with non-PI-based treatment. MM-related bone pain was numerically more frequent among patients currently receiving PI-based treatment, although the association did not reach statistical significance after multivariable adjustment. These findings provide a real-world description of patient-reported and skeletal outcomes according to current treatment status but do not establish whether the biological effects of proteasome inhibitors on bone remodeling translate into clinically meaningful patient-reported or structural skeletal benefits.

Title: "Markers of benefit": the influence of physiological and physical factors on the relationship between slow-paced breathing and heart rate variability.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Slow-paced breathing (SPB) improves autonomic balance and increases heart rate variability (HRV). The influence of combat-related traumatic injury (CRTI), baseline respiratory rate (RR), and physical function/activity on the relationship between SPB and HRV has not been examined previously and was the aim of this study.
METHODS: We analysed the first follow-up data from the ongoing ArmeD serVices trAuma rehabilitatioN outComE (ADVANCE) Cohort study. Short-term HRV was measured using a single-lead electrocardiogram during five minutes of spontaneous breathing, followed by five minutes of SPB (six breaths/minute). We examined the effect modification of SPB on HRV by CRTI (yes/no), RR during spontaneous breathing (< 15/≥15 breaths/minute), weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire and physical function (6-minute-walk-distance; 6MWD). Linear models for panel data were run, adjusting for age, sampling rank, ethnicity, and cardiovascular and respiratory medication.
RESULTS: A total of 962 male participants (median age: 37.6 years; n = 487 injured, n = 495 uninjured; mean 11years post-injury/deployment) with paired spontaneous-SPB HRV data were included. All short-term HRV measures increased during SPB when compared to spontaneous breathing. CRTI, 6MWD and MVPA did not significantly moderate the effect of SPB on HRV, but baseline RR ≥ 15 breaths/minute did, with Root-Mean-Square-Of-Successive-Difference (RMSSD) increasing from 15.57ms to 21.89ms (p < 0.001) during SPB.
CONCLUSION: SPB improves HRV regardless of CRTI status. Those with higher baseline RR are more likely to obtain a significant improvement in HRV during SPB. SPB-based interventions may be introduced for the rehabilitation of military personnel following injury/deployment.

Title: Exploratory clinical predictors and internally validated models of in-hospital mortality after PCI in obese patients with acute myocardial infarction and documented cardiogenic shock: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obese patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remain at high risk of early mortality despite percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Obesity and related cardiometabolic disorders may aggravate vascular and microcirculatory dysfunction, potentially involving impaired endothelial cell function. However, prognostic evidence specifically focusing on obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI remains limited. This exploratory, single-center study investigated clinical factors associated with in-hospital mortality and compared the predictive performance of logistic regression and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using rigorous internal validation.
METHODS: The archived analytic dataset contained 268 patients. After eligibility re-audit, three patients with body mass index (BMI) < 28 kg/m² were excluded, leaving 265 patients with documented AMI-CS treated with PCI. Seven routinely available candidate variables were evaluated in multivariable association and prediction analyses. Logistic regression and regularized XGBoost were compared using 20 repetitions of stratified five-fold nested cross-validation, with all model tuning confined to the inner training folds. Supplemental data on shock severity, serial lactate levels, vasoactive therapy, mechanical circulatory support, ventilation, renal replacement therapy, and hemodynamic variables were additionally evaluated descriptively and in a post hoc sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 265 patients, 202 survived and 63 died during hospitalization. Higher heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. The seven-variable logistic regression model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.767 (95% CI, 0.696-0.831) and a Brier score of 0.152, compared with an AUC of 0.712 (95% CI, 0.641-0.779) and a Brier score of 0.169 for regularized XGBoost. Serial lactate concentrations at admission, peak, 6 h, 12 h, and 24 h were consistently higher in non-survivors, and cardiac power output was modestly lower. A post hoc severity-augmented logistic model achieved an AUC of 0.922 (95% CI, 0.888-0.951), but its calibration slope was 2.077, indicating that the model was not sufficiently calibrated for clinical deployment.
CONCLUSIONS: In obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression demonstrated more favorable internally validated predictive performance than regularized XGBoost using the same routinely available predictors. The associations of diabetes and hypertension, together with abnormalities in systemic perfusion, are biologically compatible with a potential contribution of endothelial cell dysfunction and impaired microvascular regulation; however, endothelial function was not directly measured in this study. External multicenter validation and studies incorporating endothelial biomarkers are warranted to further clarify the role of endothelial dysfunction in risk stratification for this high-risk population. These findings are exploratory and internally validated only; the modest sample size, absence of external validation, and originally outcome-informed nomination of the seven candidate predictors limit generalizability and preclude claims of clinical readiness.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Comparative Study

Title: Prospective multicenter feasibility study of omnipolar near-field peak-frequency mapping for slow-pathway localization in typical atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Slow-pathway (SP) ablation is the established therapy for atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT). While conventional anatomical and electrogram-guided approaches are effective, SP localization may be challenging in a subset of procedures. Omnipolar near-field (OTNF) peak frequency (PF) mapping has been proposed as a signal-based approach to support SP localization; however, prospective multicenter data remain limited.
METHODS: Fifty consecutive adults with inducible typical AVNRT underwent catheter ablation in three Italian hospitals. High-density right atrial mapping was performed during sinus rhythm using a 16-pole grid catheter (Advisor™ HD Grid) with OTNF on the EnSite X system. PF maps were generated (high-frequency threshold > 250 Hz), and RF applications were delivered to the region of highest PF. Voltage maps were also created to delineate low-voltage bridge (LVB) regions (typically 0.04-2 mV) for retrospective overlap/localization analyses; LVB was not used to select ablation targets.
RESULTS: Acute procedural success was achieved in all patients, with no procedural complications. The effective ablation site (junctional beats with subsequent SP modification and/or non-inducibility) corresponded to the highest PF region in 45/50 patients (90%). In a retrospective overlap/localization analysis, the effective site fell within the LVB region in 36/50 patients (72%); concordance between PF-defined and LVB-defined regions at the effective site was observed in 35/50 patients (70%). Mean PF in the SP target region was 424 ± 86 Hz versus 272 ± 57 Hz in surrounding tissue (P < 0.05 on paired testing). Exploratory ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.937 with an optimal cutoff of 357 Hz (sensitivity 0.87; specificity 0.94); these estimates should be interpreted cautiously because PF guided RF target selection (incorporation/target-selection bias).
CONCLUSION: In this prospective multicenter cohort, OTNF-derived PF mapping was feasible and reproducibly identified a discrete region used to guide SP ablation in typical AVNRT. ROC-derived thresholds and performance estimates are exploratory and require independent validation in cohorts where ablation targets are not selected using PF criteria.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Use in Kidney Transplant Recipients With Post-Transplantation Diabetes Mellitus - A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have proved beneficial effects on cardiovascular risk and preservation of renal function in patients with diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, in addition to their glucose-lowering effects. This study aims to investigate whether SGLT2i was associated with a more favorable metabolic profile in kidney transplant recipients with post-transplantation diabetes mellitus (PTDM).
METHODS: In this observational study, patients receiving a kidney transplant between 2007 and 2021 in Norway were identified from the national transplant database. Patients who developed PTDM were identified through new- onset prescription of glucose- lowering treatment after kidney transplantation registered in Norwegian Prescription Database. PTDM patients were categorized whether glucose- lowering treatment included SGLT2i or not during the first 4 years after transplantation. Metabolic parameters at 5 years after transplantation reported to the Norwegian Renal Registry was compared in the 2 patient groups.
RESULTS: This observational study included 232 kidney transplant recipients with PTDM. Metabolic parameters at 5 years post-transplantation were compared among the SGLT2i-group (n = 39) and the control group (n = 193); median BMI (27.5 vs. 26.5 kg/m2, p = .22), diastolic blood pressure (80 vs. 79 mm Hg, p = .40), systolic blood pressure (129 vs. 132 mm Hg, p = .42), proteinuria-parameters (u-ACR 4.5 vs. 3.5 mg/mmol, p = .33), (u-PCR 26 vs. 13 mg/mmol, p = .29), HbA1c (52 vs. 49 mmol/mol, p = .11) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, 61 vs. 56 mL/min/1.73m2, p = .20).
CONCLUSION: Our study could not demonstrate improved metabolic parameters in PTDM patients treated with SGLT2-inhibitors at 5 years post transplantation.

Title: Trends in metabolic risk factor control and medication use among adults with type 2 diabetes in Taiwan, 2015-2024.
Journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate 10-year trends in metabolic control and guideline-directed pharmacotherapy among adults with type 2 diabetes in Taiwan.
METHODS: Using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (2015-2024), we analyzed annual trends in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and medication use. Blood pressure (BP) was assessed via a nationwide Pay-for-Performance registry. Trends were evaluated overall and across subgroups with cardiovascular disease (CVD) or chronic kidney disease (CKD).
RESULTS: The treated population expanded from 1.58 to 2.27 million. Target achievement improved significantly: HbA1c <7.0% rose from 42.5% to 55.3%, and LDL-C <100 mg/dL from 54.3% to 69.0% (both p-trend <0.001). Among patients with all three measurements available, triple-factor control reached 18.2% by 2024. These gains coincided with rapid sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) uptake (from 3.3% in 2016 to 38.0% in 2024) and increased statin use. However, 23.5% of young adults (20-44 years) maintained poor glycemic control (HbA1c ≥ 8.5%). SGLT2i use was higher in patients with CVD (43.1%) or CKD (43.8%) than in those without the respective conditions (34.7% and 36.6%), while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use remained below 4%.
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic control in Taiwan improved substantially alongside adoption of newer therapies. Gaps among younger adults and high-risk cohorts highlight the need for targeted, risk-stratified management.

Title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
Journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
Abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

Title: Preoperative normetanephrine levels, but not doxazosin dose, predict intraoperative hemodynamic instability in pheochromocytoma surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative α-adrenergic blockade is routinely recommended before adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma to reduce intraoperative hemodynamic instability. However, the need, intensity, and duration of preoperative blockade remain uncertain.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective study included adult patients who underwent adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma at Karolinska University Hospital between 2014 and 2023. The association between preoperative doxazosin treatment, plasma metanephrine and normetanephrine concentrations, and intraoperative hemodynamic instability was evaluated. Correlation analysis and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients were included (49% female; median age 59 years). Neither preoperative doxazosin dose nor treatment duration was associated with intraoperative systolic blood pressure reduction or intraoperative adenosine requirements. In contrast, higher preoperative metanephrine and normetanephrine concentrations were significantly associated with greater intraoperative vasoactive support requirements and a greater systolic blood pressure reduction after adrenal vein ligation. Tumor size showed a significant positive correlation with normetanephrine concentrations but was not independently associated with intraoperative hemodynamic instability. In multivariate analysis, preoperative normetanephrine concentration remained the only independent predictor of intraoperative reduction in systolic blood pressure after adrenal vein ligation.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative normetanephrine concentration is associated with intraoperative hemodynamic instability in pheochromocytoma surgery, whereas doxazosin dose and treatment duration were not. These findings suggest that biochemical tumor activity may be more clinically relevant than the intensity of preoperative α-blockade when assessing perioperative cardiovascular risk.

Title: Endometrial compaction and ongoing pregnancy in modified natural cycle frozen euploid embryo transfer: a prospective multicentre cohort study with standardized transvaginal ultrasound assessment.
Abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Does endometrial compaction, assessed by transvaginal ultrasound at two measurement time points, predict ongoing pregnancy in patients undergoing single euploid blastocyst transfer in a modified natural cycle frozen embryo transfer (mNC-FET)?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Endometrial compaction of ≥5% between the day of ovulation triggering and the day of embryo transfer was not associated with ongoing pregnancy rate or any secondary reproductive outcome in this prospective multicentre cohort.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Endometrial compaction-a reduction in endometrial thickness (EMT) following progesterone-induced secretory transformation-has been proposed as a potential marker of endometrial receptivity in FET cycles. However, existing evidence is conflicting. Retrospective studies have reported positive associations between compaction and ongoing pregnancy in programmed cycles, while prospective data, including the only prior study restricted to euploid single FET, have not confirmed this relationship. Crucially, most studies have used transabdominal ultrasound for the transfer-day measurement, a recognized source of measurement error. No prospective study has examined compaction exclusively in mNC-FET using transvaginal ultrasound at both time points.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Prospective multicentre observational cohort study conducted between March 2023 and March 2025 across six assisted reproduction units of Instituto Bernabeu group (Spain). A total of 207 patients who met all inclusion criteria and completed the full protocol were analysed.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Women aged 18-50 years undergoing mNC-FET with a single euploid blastocyst (confirmed by preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy via next-generation sequencing) were included. EMT was measured transvaginally at T1 (day of hCG trigger) and T2 (day of embryo transfer). Compaction was defined as a ≥5% reduction in EMT from T1 to T2. Additional thresholds of ≥10% and ≥15% were evaluated as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was ongoing pregnancy, defined as foetal cardiac activity at 10 weeks of gestation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusting for age, previous live births, previous miscarriages, BMI, and oocyte origin.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Of 207 patients, 58 (28.0%) met the compaction criterion (≥5%). The compaction group had a significantly greater T1 EMT (9.55 ± 1.54 mm vs 8.39 ± 1.14 mm, P < 0.001) and a lower T2 EMT (7.91 ± 1.19 mm vs 9.75 ± 1.55 mm, P < 0.001). Ongoing pregnancy rates were 50.0% in the compaction group versus 53.7% in the non-compaction group (P = 0.633). This difference was not significant on multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.38-1.67, P = 0.546). The null association was consistent across all compaction thresholds (≥10%: P = 0.674; ≥15%: P = 0.928) and across all secondary outcomes, including clinical pregnancy rate (56.9% vs 59.1%, P = 0.777), biochemical pregnancy loss (10.8% vs 8.3%, P = 0.737), and early pregnancy loss rate (12.1% vs 9.1%, P = 0.734). The overall ongoing pregnancy rate was 52.7% (109/207).
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: The distribution between groups was asymmetric (28% compaction vs 72% non-compaction), deviating from the balanced allocation anticipated at protocol design, which may reduce statistical power. Although both measurements were transvaginal, a subset of T1 measurements from international patients were performed at external centres and validated remotely by Instituto Bernabeu's physicians. Live birth data were only partially available at the time of analysis; however, ongoing pregnancy at 10 weeks is a validated and widely accepted surrogate for live birth in reproductive medicine trials.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: These findings do not support the hypothesis that endometrial compaction is associated with improved reproductive outcomes in mNC-FET with euploid embryos. The consistent null result across multiple thresholds and outcomes, obtained with a fully standardized transvaginal ultrasound methodology, strengthens the current evidence base. Routine assessment of endometrial compaction with the aim of identifying patients with a favourable prognosis does not appear to be clinically justified in this setting; indeed, acting upon compaction status could lead to unnecessary cycle cancellations in patients who would otherwise achieve ongoing pregnancy.
FUNDING: This study was supported by a Doctoral Research Grant awarded by Miguel Hernandez Public University, Spain (Rectoral Resolution No. 04588/2021). The funding body had no role in the study design, data collection, analysis or interpretation of the data, preparation of the manuscript, or decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
DISCLOSURES: The authors declare no competing interests related to the present study. No personal payments, financial incentives, or commercial benefits were received by any author in relation to this work.

Title: Earlier Versus Later Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Sequential Landmark Target Trial Emulation.
Journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) may improve outcomes in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the optimal timing of initiation remains uncertain, partly because prior comparisons did not restrict controls to patients still in refractory arrest at the same decision point.
METHODS: We employed target trial emulation with a sequential landmark design in the Korean nationwide OHCA registry (2016-2023). Among patients with presumed cardiac aetiology who were still receiving emergency department (ED) CPR 15 minutes after ED arrival, landmarks were set at 15, 30, and 60 minutes, each comparing ECPR initiation within the subsequent window with no ECPR during that window among patients still in refractory arrest. Treatment effects were adjusted risk differences estimated by propensity score overlap weighting with 22 covariates.
RESULTS: Of 58,668 patients with refractory OHCA, 909 received ECPR. Weighted 30-day survival (ECPR vs. control) was 31.0% vs. 16.0%, 21.6% vs. 7.2%, and 10.9% vs. 3.2% at the 15-, 30-, and 60-minute landmarks; adjusted risk differences were +15.0 percentage points (95% CI 8.0 to 22.0), +14.4 (10.4 to 18.4), and +7.7 (3.7 to 11.7) (all P<.001). Favourable neurological outcomes showed a similar pattern, and in the exploratory timing-gradient analysis, the adjusted risk difference decreased with longer door-to-ECMO times but remained statistically significant through 120 minutes.
CONCLUSIONS: ECPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcomes at every landmark, including initiation beyond 60 minutes, where weighted 30-day survival with continued conventional CPR was 3.2%. Benefit was largest with early initiation but did not disappear at the commonly applied 60-minute benchmark, which may be overly restrictive for selected patients in capable systems.

Title: Prognostic value of early post-admission pan-immune-inflammation value in Takotsubo syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation has been associated with adverse outcomes in Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), but the prognostic value of pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) has not been evaluated in this condition. We assessed whether PIV measured at days 3-5 provides prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 768 patients with TTS from two tertiary centers. PIV was calculated at admission and at days 3-5. A prespecified day-5 landmark analysis evaluated one-year major adverse clinical events (MACE), defined as all-cause death, heart failure events, arrhythmia requiring hospitalization, stroke, or acute myocardial infarction, and the incremental prognostic value of PIV at days 3-5.
RESULTS: The landmark cohort included 722 patients with 218 MACE events. In the primary complete-case analysis (n = 692; 206 events), PIV at days 3-5 was independently associated with MACE after adjustment for clinical variables and admission PIV (HR per doubling, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.16-1.42; p < 0.001), whereas admission PIV was not (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.86-1.02; p = 0.142). Adding PIV at days 3-5 to the clinical plus admission-PIV model increased the C-index from 0.659 to 0.682 (ΔC-index, 0.024; 95% CI, 0.005-0.043; bootstrap p = 0.015). The association was approximately linear on the log₂ PIV scale and robust across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: PIV measured at days 3-5 was independently associated with one-year MACE and provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV. Early post-admission PIV may represent a readily available adjunct to risk assessment, although external validation is required.

Title: Identifying the Optimal Respiratory Muscle Training Intervention for Heart Failure Patients: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory muscle training interventions have shown promising results in improving functional capacity, quality of life, and prognosis of heart failure patients. However, the optimal respiratory muscle training intervention for rehabilitation remains unclear.
METHODS: A systematic review and network meta-analysis was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library until September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effect of respiratory muscle training interventions on maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximum expiratory pressure (MEP), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), six-minute walk test (6MWT), peak oxygen uptake (VO2max), quality of life, and dyspnea. Random-effect network meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled mean differences. Interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).
RESULTS: A total of 88 RCTs (5,757 participants) were included. Medium-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) ranked highest for improving MIP (SUCRA: 89.8%). Combined aerobic and resistance exercise was optimal for MEP (SUCRA: 79.3%). Aerobic training showed the greatest benefit for FVC (SUCRA: 94.8%) and FEV₁ (SUCRA: 93.8%). Medium-intensity IMT was most effective for enhancing 6MWT performance (SUCRA: 81.6%). A combination of high-intensity IMT with aerobic training yielded the largest gains in improving VO2max (SUCRA: 74.7%), quality of life (SUCRA: 81.4%), and reducing dyspnea (SUCRA: 89.3%).
CONCLUSION: Respiratory muscle training interventions provide different benefits across key rehabilitation outcomes in heart failure. Accordingly, rehabilitation strategies may be optimized by aligning exercise modalities with patients' rehabilitation needs, preferences, and clinical profiles, rather than adopting a uniform prescription.

Title: Inferior Vena Cava Filters in Adolescents with Thromboembolic Disease: Technical Outcomes, Retrieval, and the Role of Skeletal Maturity.
Journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage. Retrieval was attempted once the initial indication had resolved and anticoagulation was feasible.
RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in every case; mean caval diameter was 17.9 ± 3.0 mm. Retrieval was attempted in 22 of 26 filters and succeeded in 19 (86% of attempts, 79% by intent to retrieve, 73% overall). One successful retrieval required a second attempt with an adjunctive loop-snare maneuver. Median indwelling time was 89 days (range 1-489). All three unsuccessful retrievals occurred at Risser stage 3 or below (3 of 7 versus 0 of 15 attempted; P = .02), not explained by caval diameter (P = .33). Seven filters (27%) remained in situ. No periprocedural adverse events occurred. Both retained filters assessed by CT showed caval wall penetration, one with strut fracture and asymptomatic migration at 16 years; chronic caval occlusion developed in one patient.
CONCLUSION: Off-label IVCF placement in adolescents achieved high technical and retrieval success. Retrieval failure was confined to skeletally immature patients and was not explained by caval diameter. Strut fracture with migration at long-term imaging reinforces the need for timely retrieval.

Title: Practical Prevention of Heart Failure Across Stages A and B: A Scientific Statement From the Japanese Heart Failure Society.
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a growing health problem in Japan, associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, recurrent hospitalization, impaired quality of life, and increasing healthcare costs. Early prevention before the onset of signs and symptoms has therefore become a major priority in cardiovascular medicine. This scientific statement from the Japanese Heart Failure Society provides practical prevention strategies for patients with HF Stage A and Stage B in Japan. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarker-guided screening using brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) to facilitate earlier detection of Stage B (pre-HF) and identification of patients at increased risk of progression to symptomatic HF. The statement summarizes evidence-based management of major cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disorders associated with HF development, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, coronary artery disease, left ventricular dysfunction, valvular heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. It also addresses disease-specific approaches for optimizing blood pressure, glycemic control, renal protection, lipid management, and weight reduction. Preventive strategies include lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, serial reassessment of natriuretic peptide levels, and appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging and timely specialist referral. Because many patients at risk for HF are managed outside specialized cardiovascular centers, practical pathways for collaboration between cardiologists and non-cardiologist physicians are essential. The importance of timely referral, shared risk recognition, and multidisciplinary care is therefore emphasized. Implementation of clinically applicable prevention strategies may help reduce progression to symptomatic HF, facilitate earlier therapeutic intervention, and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: The Role of Platelet Aggregation and Activation as Biomarkers for Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is increasingly attributed to thromboinflammation and microvascular platelet activation. Accordingly, we aimed to characterize longitudinal platelet aggregation, platelet activation, and platelet morphology in patients with aSAH and assessed their association with DCI.
METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort consisted of 206 patients with aSAH. Of the 206 patients, 144 were analyzed via platelet aggregometry, 148 via flow cytometry, and 129 had both aggregometry and flow cytometry data. An additional 52 patients had morphology data. Peripheral blood was sampled on post-bleed days 1, 2, 4, 7, and 10. Platelet aggregation was measured by Chrono-Log aggregometry; platelet activation (PAC-1, CD62P) was measured by flow cytometry; platelet morphology was measured by microscopy. Patient-level area-under-the-curve summaries were entered into binary logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) was applied across the analyte × parameter grid.
RESULTS: Sixty patients (29.1%) developed DCI. Across days 1-10, no agonist-stimulated aggregation parameter and no flow cytometric activation parameter was significantly associated with DCI after FDR correction (all q ≥ 0.42). Only morphologically activated platelets were more prevalent in DCI patients at day 2 (73.8 ± 4.9% vs. 55.6 ± 18.6%; p = 0.001), a difference that survived FDR correction (q = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral platelet function assays do not reliably stratify DCI risk after aSAH. These findings may align with the preferential consumption of the hyperactive platelets, though these findings are hypothesis-generating only and need further investigation.

Title: Evaluating the feasibility and impact of a remote, algorithm-based blood pressure titration program in postpartum women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: the postpartum algorithm for text-based hypertension management (PATH) randomized clinical trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal postpartum management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains unknown. This pilot randomized control trial explored feasibility and safety of an algorithmic, text-based intervention targeting a blood pressure (BP) < 130/80 mmHg (in accordance with American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association recommendations - ACC/AHA) on hypertension management at 6 weeks postpartum as compared with routine care.
STUDY DESIGN: 200 postpartum patients with HDP (excluding chronic hypertension) were randomized at hospital discharge for delivery or postpartum HDP admission from a tertiary care center in a 1:1 fashion to the intervention (targeting a blood pressure < 130/ 80 mmHg) or routine care. Patients and clinicians were blinded with respect to randomization.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who achieved normotension as defined by the ACC/AHA (systolic blood pressure < 130 mmHg). Secondary outcomes were frequency of medication titration, outpatient visits, and non-billable healthcare encounters.
RESULTS: The virtual intervention did not differ from routine care with respect to the primary outcome using office- ascertained BPs (72% intervention vs 74% routine care, p = 0.83). At 6 weeks postpartum, clinic systolic BP did not differ by group (121 mmHg vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.3), though home-reported SBPs during the same period were lower among those randomized to the intervention (119 mmHg vs 125 mmHg, p < 0.001). No adverse events occurred in either group.
CONCLUSIONS: As compared to routine care delivered at a tertiary care center, no differences were observed with respect to systolic BP at 6 weeks postpartum using a virtual, algorithm-based intervention. A high proportion of patients in both randomized groups achieving normotension by ACC/AHA targets without adverse events.

Title: Lipid dynamics and cardiovascular risk profiles on carbohydrate- or saturated fat-based diets: secondary analysis of the CARBFUNC trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity involves complex changes in energy metabolism and increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk independently of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Diets high or low in carbohydrates or fats can be effective for reversing obesity, but their distinct effects on metabolic health and detailed lipid profiles may differentially impact overall CVD risk, particularly with large differences in saturated fatty acid (SFA) intake.
METHODS: In a 2-year randomised controlled trial, 193 males and females with obesity were assigned to 1) an acellular carbohydrate-based diet (A-HCLF, comparator arm), 2) a cellular carbohydrate-based diet (C-HCLF), or 3) a low-carbohydrate high-fat (LCHF) diet (75 energy percent fat, thereof 30 SFAs). As secondary outcomes of the trial, plasma lipids and lipoprotein particle subfractions were quantified by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy assay, and coronary artery calcium score by CT imaging. Data were analysed by constrained linear mixed-effects modelling.
FINDINGS: Attrition was 74 (39%), 114 (59%), 128 (67%), 135 (70%), and 162 (84%) at 3, 6, 9, 12 and 24 months, respectively. Self-reported adherence ranged from 63 to 85% up to 12 months and 40-60% for the last 12 months. During the first 9-12 months, the LCHF group showed significantly greater reductions than the A-HCLF comparator and C-HCLF diets in very low-density lipoprotein particles (VLDLs), triacylglycerols (TAGs), remnant cholesterol, and the TAG/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio, alongside increases in HDL-C, total apolipoprotein A1 (apoA1), apoA1 in large HDL particles, LDL-C (attributed to large LDL particles), and the LDL-C/apolipoprotein B ratio. At 24 months, there were still greater reductions on the LCHF compared to the A-HCLF diet for TAGs, VLDL particles, remnant cholesterol, and the TAG/HDL-C ratio, as well as a greater increase in large LDL particles.
INTERPRETATION: In adults with obesity, an LCHF diet rich in SFA markedly lowered TAG-rich remnants and raised HDL-C and apoA1 compared to higher-carbohydrate diets, while shifting LDL toward larger particles without significantly increasing apoB or small LDLs-a pattern that may indicate greater lipid turnover.
FUNDING: This work was supported by the Trond Mohn Research Foundation, Bergen (Norway), the University of Bergen (Norway), Kostfonden, Stockholm (Sweden), and the Norwegian Health Association.

Title: Risk factors associated with increased mortality in patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to diabetic foot.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes is a public health problem that has been increasing in recent years. Infected diabetic foot is established by the presence of inflammatory response data associated with ulcers or tissue loss. Multiple risk factors are associated with diabetic foot and the need for amputation secondary to infection.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective observational cohort study conducted between 2019 and 2024. A total of 403 patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to soft tissue infection due to diabetic foot were included. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables were analyzed between deceased and surviving patients.
RESULTS: A total of 403 patients were included (median age: 58 years, IQR: 50-67; 72.7% male). Overall, in-hospital mortality was 13.4% (54/403), primarily driven by septic shock (44.4%) and decompensated chronic kidney disease (33.3%). Surgical reintervention was required in 11.1% of cases. In multivariable analysis, age (OR=1.06), pre-existing cardiac disease (OR=7.17), bilateral amputation (OR=4.36), Clavien-Dindo complication grade (OR=2.67), and surgical reintervention (OR=6.46) were independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality. Baseline serum albumin exerted a protective effect (OR=0.20).
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality following supracondylar amputation for diabetic foot is independently associated with acute septic burden, admission hypoalbuminemia, cardiorenal comorbidity, and surgical reintervention, rather than long-term glycemic control. Early identification of this high-risk profile at admission is critical to prioritize prompt infection control and perioperative optimization.

Title: Association between postoperative complications and recurrence-free survival in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2 negative breast cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the association between 30-day postoperative complications (POC) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) among patients with hormone receptor-positive human epidermal growth factor negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer.
METHODS: Patients aged ≥ 18 years with stage I-III HR+/HER2- breast cancer were identified from the James Cancer Registry. Recurrence was defined as local, regional, or distant disease after treatment. POC included technical, infectious, respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary complications. Multivariable regression assessed associations between time-varying postoperative complications and RFS or overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Among 3022 patients, 103 (3.4%) developed recurrent breast cancer. On univariable analysis, postoperative complications were associated with worse RFS (HR 2.20, 95% CI 1.32-3.68). After adjustment, complications were not associated with RFS (aHR 1.56, 95% CI 0.88-2.74) or OS (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.59-1.69).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with stage I-III HR+/HER2- breast cancer, 30-day postoperative complications were not associated with RFS or OS.

Title: Quantitative analysis of tissue oxygenation trajectories in DIEP flaps using near infrared spectroscopy: A retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is an adjunct for monitoring breast free flaps. However, there is a paucity of studies using large NIRS datasets to characterize how patient-, flap-, and operative-level factors and systemic hemodynamics influence postoperative tissue oxygen saturation (StO2).
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed early postoperative NIRS data from DIEP-based breast reconstructions, comprising >676,000 continuous StO₂ measurements from an exteriorized skin paddle (ViOptix). Trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with nonlinear time effects and fixed effects for patient-, flap-, and operative-level variables. Trajectory metrics (desaturation burden, variability, and overall slope) were calculated. A separate model examined the associations with matched vital signs.
RESULTS: Overall, 107 flaps in 65 patients (676,308 measurements) were analyzed. StO₂ followed a non-linear postoperative course, and most variance was between the patients (67.1%) rather than within flaps. Large skin paddles were the dominant flap-level predictor, with significantly higher mean StO₂ (adjusted +9.7% points, 95% CI 3.5-16.0; p=0.003, robust across estimators), whereas coupler diameter, arterial and venous anastomosis counts, and flap weight showed no association. Among the systemic factors, higher mean arterial pressure and peripheral oxygen saturation were robustly associated with higher StO₂, whereas temperature and heart rate did not survive autocorrelation correction. Bilaterally monitored flaps diverged among the patients (median 4.9 points). Trajectory metrics separated the two venous-failure flaps from normal variation, though negative slope alone was non-specific.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative DIEP flap StO₂ reflects flap characteristics and systemic physiology; small skin paddles may mimic venous compromise. Combining trajectory features with physiologic data may improve discrimination of true vascular compromise.

Title: Mortality after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and its clinical predictors.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) often have comorbid conditions that may adversely impact survival, but long-term mortality risk in this population remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Patients who underwent VPS placement for iNPH at a single tertiary care center between 2017 and 2025 were identified. Comorbidities, demographic characteristics, and perioperative complications were evaluated using univariable Cox regression analyses to identify factors associated with mortality at the last follow-up. Comorbidities were quantified with the modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: 452 patients were included (median age, 75.3 years; 61.9% male). Forty-four (9.7%) died during follow-up (median 39.1 months), with a median postoperative survival of 19.8 months and a median age at death of 78.4 years. Median mFI-5 was 1.0 and median CCI was 2.0. Baseline comorbidities in total cohort included prior myocardial infarction (MI) in 5.8% of patients, congestive heart failure (CHF) in 6.9%, cerebrovascular accident (CVA) in 14.4%, dementia in 27.1%, and functional dependence in 54.9%. At presentation, 96.0% had gait impairment, 84.5% had cognitive deficits, and 81.6% had urinary incontinence. Regarding perioperative outcomes, 57 patients (12.6%) were hospitalized more than one day and 30 (6.7%) required non-home discharge. Postoperative subdural fluid collections occurred in 13.6% of patients, while 6.9% underwent shunt revision. On multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher CCI (HR 1.27, p = 0.005) and hospitalization >1 day (HR 3.20, p = 0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: Nontrivial rates of mortality are seen following VPS in iNPH - approximately estimated at 10% over four years in the present study. Increased mortality appears correlated with more extensive comorbidities and poorer functional status, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection in this frail population. Notably, this mortality rate closely approximates the mortality expected on an actuarial basis for an age- and sex-matched general population and is substantially lower than mortality previously reported for patients with mild cognitive impairment, suggesting that VPS may mitigate the excess mortality otherwise anticipated in this population.

Title: Monitoring the incidence of hypotension and hypoxemia as systemic secondary insults in patients with catastrophic brain injury evolving to brain death. A prospective observational pilot study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Maintenance of systemic homeostasis and prevention of secondary injury are a cornerstone of treatment in neurocritical care to prevent organ dysfunction and adverse clinical outcome. This is a pilot descriptive and hypothesis generating study aiming to measure and characterize the incidence of systemic hypotension and hypoxemia occurring during the intensive care unit (ICU) stay in patients with catastrophic brain injury potentially evolving to brain death.
METHODS: Adult patients admitted to ICU with catastrophic brain injury and Glasgow coma scale ≤5 have been enrolled. Arterial blood pressure and SpO2 were collected minute by minute from a central station connected to patients' bedside monitors.
RESULTS: We report on 24 patients recruited prospectively from the University Hospital of Messina, Italy as a part of a larger ongoing multi-centre study. Patient monitoring data ranged from 8-3000 hours (0.3-125 days). Admission diagnoses were intracerebral haemorrhage (N= 13), TBI (N=4), SAH (N=3), ischaemic stroke (N=3) and hypoxic encephalopathy (N=1). The proportion of valid monitoring time spent with secondary insults and the pressure time index (PTI) are presented and discussed. Day 3 and 4 demonstrated the largest number of secondary insults which were mainly hypotension. Patients who progressed to brain death (n = 9) or who died in ICU from cardiac complications (n = 7) exhibited a more severe and sustained hypotensive burden compared with patients alive at discharge (n = 8). This descriptive study proved useful for identifying an optimal window for tracking insults as well as piloting several key summary measures and visualisations which will be utilized in a larger multi-centre study.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with catastrophic brain injury, the incidence of hypotension remains the highest among systemic secondary insults in patients progressing to brain death and cardiac death.

Title: Timing, dose, and Behavioral engagement in perioperative Behavioral activation: a secondary analysis of predictors of improvement in a randomized clinical trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression and anxiety are associated with poor outcomes in older adults undergoing surgery. Perioperative psychological interventions may improve symptoms, but the optimal dose, timing, and therapeutic processes remain unclear.
METHODS: This secondary analysis examined the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial. Participants were aged ≥60, scheduled for cardiac, oncologic, or orthopedic surgeries, and had clinically meaningful depression and/or anxiety symptoms on the Patient Health Questionnaire-Anxiety Depression Scale (PHQ-ADS). Analyses included participants who completed baseline and 3-month assessments. Associations between intervention components and changes in PHQ-ADS, PHQ-9 depression and GAD-7 anxiety scores were evaluated across four a priori domains: intervention dose and perioperative timing, behavioral engagement through activity plan enactment, implementation quality and target engagement through measures of activation, compassion, and surgical preparedness scores.
RESULTS: Among 138 intervention participants, greater intervention dose was associated with larger reductions in anxiety at 3 months. Pre-operative initiation was consistently associated with symptom improvement. Participants completing ≥3 pre-operative sessions had a 6.05-point greater reduction in PHQ-ADS than those completing none (p = .003). Greater mean activity-plan completion was associated with larger reductions in PHQ-ADS (b = -2.42, SE = 1.00, p = .02), PHQ-9 (b = -1.35, SE = 0.65, p = .04), and GAD-7 scores (b = -1.07, SE = 0.53, p = .05).
CONCLUSIONS: More sessions, earlier initiation, and greater behavioral engagement of patients were associated with greater reductions in depression and anxiety. Initiating behavioral activation before surgery and supporting activity-plan enactment may improve postoperative depression and anxiety symptoms for older surgical patients. Limitations include lack of random assignment to the variables studied and single-site population.

Title: Myocardial External Efficiency and Energetic Adaptation After Heart Transplantation: An Exploratory Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired myocardial energetics may contribute to graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HTX). We aimed to characterize early posttransplant myocardial external efficiency (MEE) and its relationship with mitochondrial capacity.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 22 HTX recipients underwent [11C]acetate positron emission tomography, echocardiography, biomarker testing, and high-resolution respirometry of endomyocardial biopsies once between week 1 and 3 and at 6 mo post-HTX. Temporal changes in positron emission tomography-derived MEE, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen consumption were evaluated within patients and compared with those of 20 control participants. Mitochondrial capacity was assessed only in HTX recipients.
RESULTS: MEE increased from 18 ± 5% to 21 ± 5% at 6 mo post-HTX (P = 0.003) but remained lower than in control participants (26 ± 6%, P < 0.0001). Cardiac output, myocardial oxygen consumption, and mitochondrial oxidative capacity did not change significantly over time. At 6 mo, both MEE and mitochondrial oxidative capacity correlated with left-ventricular global longitudinal strain (r = -0.49, P = 0.002; r = -0.58, P = 0.010, respectively). Furthermore, MEE was inversely associated with troponin I (r = -0.49, P = 0.030) and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (r = -0.35, P = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: MEE improved significantly from 1-3 wk to 6 mo after HTX. Both MEE and mitochondrial respiratory function were associated with left-ventricular contractile performance. Overall, these findings suggest alterations in myocardial energetics during early graft recovery and support a link between oxidative metabolism and graft performance.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).
RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

Title: Risk factors and long-term prognosis of catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombophlebitis is a possible complication of the use of indwelling catheters in hospitalized neonatal foals. Limited data are available concerning associated risk factors, and long-term prognosis regarding vein patency is currently unknown.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Identify risk factors for catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals and assess long-term prognosis in a small subset.
ANIMALS: Two hundred twenty-three foals < 31 days of age, hospitalized in Utrecht University Equine Hospital between 2019 and 2024.
METHODS: Retrospective review of medical records. Foals that received an indwelling intravenous catheter and lived for at least two subsequent days were included. Odds ratios were determined, using logistic regression, for factors potentially associated with thrombophlebitis. Owners of affected horses were contacted, and horses available for follow-up were visited for clinical evaluation.
RESULTS: Twenty-one foals (9.4%) developed catheter-associated thrombophlebitis. In a multivariable model, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU, OR 5.2, 95%CI 1.5-19.7), diarrhea (OR 4.6, 95%CI 1.4-17.3), Friesian breed (OR 4.1, 95%CI 1.1-13.9) and dwell time over four days (OR 3.9, 95%CI 1.3-14.8) were significantly associated with thrombophlebitis development. Seventeen affected foals survived to discharge. Eight horses, aged five months to five years, were available for follow-up by clinical evaluation and demonstrated appropriate blood flow.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Risk factors for developing catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in hospitalized neonatal foals were identified. This knowledge can aid in implementation of preventive measures.

Title: Aerobic physical activity is associated with lower pneumonia and COVID-19 mortality in adults with cognitive impairment.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease and pneumonia are major causes of death in dementia, but cause-specific mortality has rarely been examined in clinically confirmed cognitive-impairment cohorts. In this nationwide retrospective cohort study, 116,563 individuals with clinically confirmed mild cognitive impairment or dementia in the Korean Dementia Relief Center registry (2016-2021) were linked to health screening and death registry data. Aerobic physical activity (APA) was quantified in metabolic-equivalent minutes per week (MET·min/week). Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and subdistribution HRs (sHRs). The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate (FDR) across 18 cause-specific comparisons. During 400,500 person-years of follow-up (mean, 3.4 years), 5022 participants (4.31%) died. Compared with inactivity, low, moderate, and high APA were associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR [95% CI], 0.728 [0.652-0.813], 0.704 [0.636-0.781], and 0.636 [0.590-0.687], respectively). High APA was associated with lower pneumonia mortality (sHR, 0.554; 95% CI, 0.437-0.702) and COVID-19 mortality (sHR, 0.520; 0.368-0.735). These point estimates were numerically lower than for ischemic heart disease and cerebrovascular disease (sHRs, 0.613 and 0.630). Pneumonia mortality was lower across all APA levels after FDR control (q ≤ 0.023). The E-value for the high APA-pneumonia association was 3.01. APA was associated with lower mortality even at modest activity levels, especially for pneumonia deaths. Achievable activity goals may therefore merit prospective evaluation as part of supportive care for adults with cognitive impairment. Because APA may also indicate preserved physiological reserve, these findings do not establish causality and require confirmation using repeated, objective activity measurements.

Title: A reference-based approach using whole-brain segmentation for estimating blood activity concentration in CBV quantification.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images.
METHODS: Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling.
RESULTS: The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

Title: Changes in management of FETO-treated infants with severe CDH.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to evaluate changes in outcomes and management of infants with severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) undergoing fetoscopic endoluminal tracheal occlusion (FETO) across two eras, and to compare outcomes by side of defect over the last decade. Retrospective review of liveborn infants with severe CDH (observed to expected lung to head ratio [O/E LHR] < 0.25 left-sided; < 0.45 right-sided) who underwent FETO at King's College Hospital, London, UK, and survived to delivery. Fifty-eight infants were included across two 5-year periods (2002-2007 and 2020-2025). Survival improved from 44.1% to 70.8% (p = 0.044). Right-sided defects were more common in the second epoch (9% versus 54%, p < 0.001). All infants in the second era had echocardiography-guided inotropic and ventilatory management, which was not universally available earlier. In the second epoch surgical repair occurred later (4.0 versus 6.5 days, p = 0.018), repair by two-stage abdominal closure (laparostomy) increased from 0% to 77.8% (p < 0.001) and recurrence fell from 33 to 0% (p = 0.042). Mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy and admission were longer latterly. In thirty-one infants delivered between 2015 and 2025, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred in 67% of left-versus 92% of right-sided CDH, but at an earlier gestational age in left (p = 0.032). Left CDH infants had longer duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and hospital stay (p = 0.006) with no mortality difference (exploratory).
