Conclusions: Our cases reflect a diverse spectrum of clinical presentations of IVL indicating the heterogeneity of the disease and the importance of a multimodal, multidisciplinary approach to the optimal management of this rare entity. The absence of further disease progression in our patients following bilateral oophorectomy, i.e., iatrogenic menopause, suggests the possible hormonal dependence of IVL.

Title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).
METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.
RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

Title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle-branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit.
METHODS: Twenty-four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within-subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd.
RESULTS: LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd, compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing, 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P<0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement (ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg; all P<0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18-29 milliseconds).
CONCLUSIONS: Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic-optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical-optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.

Title: Dietary Approaches to Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Translating Mechanistic Pathways into Clinical Practice.
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent and heterogeneous sleep disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, sleep fragmentation, sympathetic activation, and increased cardiometabolic risk. Although obesity is the most recognized modifiable risk factor, growing evidence indicates that nutritional factors influence OSA through mechanisms extending beyond body weight regulation, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, gut microbiota alterations, and metabolic dysregulation. The emergence of precision medicine and incretin-based therapies has further highlighted the need to integrate personalized nutritional approaches into OSA management. A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify experimental studies, observational studies, randomized clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and international clinical guidelines addressing nutritional mechanisms, dietary patterns, gut microbiota, chrononutrition, incretin-based therapies, and precision nutrition in adults with OSA. Current evidence suggests that nutritional interventions may influence OSA through multiple biological pathways beyond weight reduction. Mediterranean and DASH dietary patterns are associated with favorable cardiometabolic effects, while dietary fiber, polyphenols, omega-3 fatty acids, and other antioxidant compounds may modulate pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial function, and metabolic regulation. However, evidence directly demonstrating improvements in objective respiratory outcomes remains limited and heterogeneous. Emerging research also suggests potential roles for gut microbiota modulation and chrononutrition in metabolic and sleep regulation, although most evidence remains mechanistic, observational, or indirect. In addition, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual incretin agonists have demonstrated clinically relevant reductions in body weight and OSA severity, providing opportunities for integration with nutritional management. Nevertheless, evidence supporting phenotype-specific and biomarker-guided nutritional interventions remains insufficient. Nutrition represents a promising adjunctive strategy in the multidisciplinary management of OSA by targeting inflammatory, metabolic, vascular, and microbiome-related mechanisms that extend beyond weight loss alone. Future research should focus on precision nutrition approaches integrating metabolic phenotyping, biomarkers, gut microbiota, and digital health technologies to optimize personalized treatment and improve long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit.
METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h).
RESULTS: The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction.
CONCLUSIONS: A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.

Title: Report from the 2026 Barth Syndrome Foundation International Scientific, Medical & Family Conference: Advances in Barth Syndrome Research, Therapy Development, and Clinical Care.
Abstract: The 2026 Barth Syndrome International Scientific, Medical & Family Conference was held at the Hyatt Regency Coconut Point, Bonita Springs, Florida, USA, from 19th to 25th July 2026 with scientific programming beginning 22nd July. This biennial event assembled researchers, clinicians, and affected community members for its first gathering since the U.S. FDA granted accelerated approval to elamipretide (Forzinity™; Mighty Therapeutics), the first therapy for Barth syndrome and first ever mitochondrially targeted therapy, in September 2025. Scientific sessions addressed: (1) emerging cardiolipin biology; (2) convergent identification of ABHD18 as a therapeutic target for correction of the cardiolipin phenotype; (3) advancing therapeutic strategies including AAV gene therapy, enzyme replacement therapy, and ABHD18 inhibition; (4) the elamipretide post-approval program, including the SPIBA-401 confirmatory trial; (5) natural history characterization covering infant outcomes, extra-cardiac manifestations, diaphragm weakness, neutropenia, and amino acid metabolism; (6) regulatory and drug development strategies in ultra-rare indications; and (7) international Centers of Expertise models and the launch of the BarthINSIGHTS registry. This report summarizes the key scientific advances, discussions, and future priorities as they relate to Barth syndrome biology, therapeutic development, and clinical care.

Title: DNA Methylation and Metabolic Syndrome in Midlife Women of the ELEMENT Cohort.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a cluster of metabolic risk factors that markedly increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Its prevalence exceeds 50% among Mexican women. A growing number of studies suggest that DNA methylation, an epigenetic mechanism, is linked to MetS. Methylation risk scores (MRS) may be able to predict future disease risk, yet prospective studies with MRS and MetS are rare, especially in Hispanic populations. We aimed to (1) replicate previously reported locus-specific DNA methylation-MetS associations, (2) identify additional loci, and (3) evaluate an MRS for predicting MetS among a sample of midlife Mexican women. Methods: We analyzed 149 women from the Early Life Exposure in Mexico to Environmental Toxicants (ELEMENT) cohort with DNA methylation measured in blood leukocytes collected around 2008 and MetS assessed approximately ten years later. Logistic regression was applied to a priori loci, and then all loci on the Infinium EPICv1 array. MRS performance was evaluated by cross-validation. Results: Four loci-probe ID cg11024682 (SREBF1), cg06500161 (ABCG1), cg22891070 (HIF3A), and cg02650017 (PHOSPHO1)-showed consistent associations with MetS. For example, each 1-percentage-point increase in methylation at cg11024682 (SREBF1) was associated with higher odds of MetS in the fully adjusted model (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 1.12-1.52). No additional loci reached Bonferroni significance, though marginal associations with MetS components were observed. The MRS derived from four replicated loci was associated with higher odds of MetS per 1-SD increase in the training set (OR = 3.55; 95% CI: 2.03-6.22). In the independent testing set, the MRS-only model improved prediction compared with the baseline covariate-only model (AUC = 0.652 vs. 0.398; ΔAUC = +0.254). Conclusions: This study provides prospective evidence that specific DNA methylation markers are associated with MetS risk in midlife Mexican women. These loci, now replicated in several cohorts, are promising biomarkers for early identification and prevention of MetS.

Title: A Combined Workplace Intervention Including Exercise and Nutrition for Health Promotion in Obese Office Workers: A Randomized Controlled Study.
Journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
Abstract: Background: During the last decades, the office workplace setting has increasingly become an inherently "obesogenic" environment, promoting unhealthy behaviors. The main objective of this study was to investigate the efficacy of a 6-month workplace combined (exercise and nutrition) intervention in obese office workers, using a randomized controlled study. An additional objective of this study was to evaluate the individual responses per participant following the program. Methods: In total, 36 obese office workers (BMI: ≥30) were randomly assigned to two equal groups: intervention (IG; age: 48.06 ± 6.60 yrs; BMI: 33.57 ± 1.58 kg/m2) and control (CG; age: 47.95 ± 5.95 yrs; BMI: 33.54 ± 1.74 kg/m2). The IG participated in a daily supervised 6-month workplace program (during working hours), including (a) exercise (flexibility, balance, strength, and aerobic) and (b) counseling and educational activities for healthy diet and hydration. The CG did not participate in any intervention. Before and after the 6-month period, the following were measured: (a) health indices (body fat, body circumferences, blood pressure, respiratory function, and lipidemic profile), (b) functional capacity indices (flexibility, balance, handgrip strength, and cardiovascular fitness), and (c) adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MedDietScore) and daily water consumption. Results: All the participants of the IG reduced body mass, body fat, and circumferences (-4.47 to -18.95%), blood pressure (-4.08 to -46.15%), lipidemic profile indicators (-2.50 to -212.67%), and heart rate recovery (-9.62 to -57.33%), while increased respiratory function (1.82-20.26%), flexibility (5.13-50%), balance (15.38-88.83%), handgrip strength (5-25%), MedDietScore (12.5-56%), and water consumption (23.08-50%). In CG, all aforementioned indices remained unchanged (p = 0.16-0.99). Conclusions: A combined workplace intervention (exercise and nutrition) constitutes an effective approach for health promotion in obese office workers.

Title: Musculoskeletal Findings Following Pre-Participation Screening in Young Athletes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
Abstract: Background: Pre-participation screening (PPS) is widely used to evaluate athletes before sport participation, traditionally focusing on cardiovascular risk prevention. However, musculoskeletal assessment performed during PPS may also allow early identification of biomechanical and structural abnormalities that can affect sport participation during growth. Objectives: This study aimed to describe the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and management pathways of musculoskeletal alterations detected during PPS in young athletes, with particular focus on referral patterns to pediatric Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) specialists. Methods: This retrospective observational study included athletes aged ≤15 years who underwent PPS between January 2022 and December 2023 at the Sports Medicine Unit of Noale (ULSS 3 Serenissima, Venice, Italy). Musculoskeletal screening was systematically performed during PPS. Athletes presenting newly detected abnormalities were either managed conservatively by the sports physician or referred for PM&R evaluation. Clinical indications for referral, imaging investigations, diagnoses, and treatment strategies were analyzed. Results: A total of 707 athletes underwent PPS during the study period. After applying exclusion criteria, 635 athletes were eligible for analysis. Musculoskeletal alterations were identified in 141 athletes (22.2%). Among them, 54 athletes were referred for PM&R evaluation and 40 completed the consultation. No statistically significant differences were observed between referred and non-referred athletes. The most frequent reasons for referral were suspected scoliosis (n = 22), foot alignment disorders n = 18), thoracic hyperkyphosis (n = 5), and lower limb length discrepancy (n = 4). Specialist evaluation resulted in conservative management in most cases, including corrective exercise programs and orthotic interventions, while one athlete required surgical treatment for congenital scoliosis. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal screening during PPS identified a broad spectrum of findings in young athletes, including clinically relevant abnormalities requiring specialist evaluation and management. These findings suggest that musculoskeletal assessment may provide an opportunity for early clinical identification within PPS; however, prospective studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy, long-term clinical benefit, injury prevention, and cost-effectiveness before routine implementation can be recommended.

Title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma and microvascular complications in patients with type 2 diabetes achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol targets: a real-world cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets, patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain at significant risk for microvascular complications. We aimed to investigate whether the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), a marker of atherogenic dyslipidaemia, is associated with these complications in a real-world cohort of patients with controlled LDL-C.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from community health centres in Shenzhen, China (2018-2024). We included 16,469 participants with T2DM and LDL-C<2.6 mmol/L at baseline, categorising them into tertiles (T1-3) based on baseline AIP. The primary outcome was a composite of incident diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, identified via ICD-10 codes. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to assess associations.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.6 years, 1,056 participants developed microvascular complications. We observed a graded association between AIP tertiles and the risk of microvascular complications. Participants in T3 had a significantly higher risk of total microvascular complications than those in T1 (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.15-1.56), while T2 showed no statistically significant increase in risk (HR = 1.10; 95% CI = 0.94-1.28). Specifically, compared to T1, T3 participants had significantly higher risks of diabetic nephropathy (HR = 1.62; 95% CI = 1.30-2.01) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (HR = 1.39; 95% CI = 1.13-1.70), while no statistically significant association was found for diabetic retinopathy risk (HR = 1.23; 95% CI = 0.93-1.63). In contrast, compared with T1 participants, those in T2 had higher risks of nephropathy (HR = 1.28; 95% CI = 1.02-1.59), but no statistically significant associations were found for diabetic peripheral neuropathy or diabetic retinopathy.
CONCLUSIONS: We found that AIP is independently associated with increased risk of microvascular complications, particularly diabetic nephropathy and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, even in T2DM patients achieving LDL-C targets. These results suggest that AIP may serve as a simple, lipid-based marker to help identify patients with residual microvascular risk beyond conventional LDL-C control.

Title: Systemic sclerosis markedly impairs health-related quality of life: a single-centre tertiary cohort study with literature-based comparison to leading causes of global disease burden.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune condition that significantly impacts the physical and mental health of affected individuals, disrupting their daily life and overall well-being. However, its impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has not been thoroughly compared to other chronic diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and stroke, the impact of which is clearly established. We explored how SSc influences HRQoL and compared its effect to that of six chronic diseases, considered the global leading causes of disease burden in high-income countries, and three common rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.
METHODS: We collected HRQoL data from SSc patients enrolled in a cross-sectional observational study at The Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust, UK. We used the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 to measure HRQoL and compared the participants' scores to published data on unipolar major depression, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, lung cancer, osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain. Mean norm-based transformed scores (NBS) were compared for all eight SF-36 health domains.
RESULTS: The 121 SSc patients (106 female; mean age = 57 years, standard deviation = 12.3), disease duration mean = 9.50 years, standard deviation = 7.4) in our study reported significantly worse perceived general health (mean (x̄) NBS = 32.82) than the other nine diseases reported in the literature. Role limitations due to physical problems (x̄ NBS = 34.77) were comparable to stroke, RA, and lung cancer. Significant impairments were noted in bodily pain (x̄ NBS = 36), similar to osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain, as well as vitality (x̄ NBS = 39.69), comparable to RA. Emotional role limitations (x̄ NBS = 41.78) were second only to major depression, similar to stroke and RA.
CONCLUSIONS: We found that SSc has a substantial impact on HRQoL, resulting in significant physical and psychological impairment comparable to that experienced by patients with RA and stroke. These findings contextualise the burden of SSc and may inform future research and clinical practice aimed at improving patient care.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Reappraising the safety of menopausal hormone therapy for women-implications for the clinic.
Journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is currently the most effective treatment for vasomotor and other estrogen deficiency-related symptoms. Despite its proven efficacy, concerns regarding long-term safety, particularly breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease, have influenced clinical practice and patterns of MHT use over the past decades. This review summarizes the evolution of evidence regarding the safety of systemic MHT, from the introduction of conjugated equine estrogens in the 1940s through landmark randomized clinical trials to contemporary evidence and international guideline recommendations. Early concerns regarding endometrial safety with estrogen-only treatment were largely resolved by the addition of progestogens for women with an intact uterus. The Women's Health Initiative trial fundamentally changed perceptions of MHT cardiovascular safety, but subsequent analyses established the "timing hypothesis," demonstrating that the benefit-risk profile depends on age and time since menopause at treatment initiation. More recent evidence has highlighted clinically relevant differences between estrogen formulations, routes of administration, and type of progestogen. Transdermal estradiol is associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism than oral estrogen, while micronized progesterone and dydrogesterone may offer a more favorable breast safety profile than some synthetic progestins, although randomized evidence is lacking. Current evidence supports an individualized approach to MHT, with treatment decisions based on symptom burden, age, time since menopause, route of estrogen administration, type of progestogen, and individual risk factors. For healthy women initiating therapy before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause, the overall benefit-risk profile is favorable. Future research should focus on optimizing formulation-specific safety, generating comparative randomized evidence, and further refining personalized treatment strategies to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

Title: The association between prolactin and myocardial function in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prolactin has been associated with cardiovascular mortality. The primary objective was to assess the association between prolactin and systolic function in patients with type 2 diabetes. Secondly, to assess the association between prolactin and diastolic function, NYHA classification, glucose, and lipid levels.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study of the Thousand&2 cohort, including 1,030 individuals with type 2 diabetes from secondary care. Echocardiography and biochemical assessment were performed at baseline. Systolic function was estimated primarily as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), secondly as global longitudinal strain (GLS), and E/e' as a marker of diastolic function. The association between echocardiography and prolactin was assessed using linear regression, presented with crude as well as adjusted estimates for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Prolactin assessments were available for 937/1030 (91%), and 14/937 (1.5%) individuals had prolactin levels above the upper reference limit. Prolactin was not associated with LVEF or GLS, whereas prolactin was associated with E/e' and NYHA classification in fully adjusted analysis in men but not in women. Prolactin was not associated with glucose or lipid levels in men or women.
CONCLUSION: Prolactin was not associated with impaired systolic function in men or women with type 2 diabetes; on the other hand, prolactin was associated with poorer diastolic function in men with type 2 diabetes. The current results point towards a gender specific effect of prolactin on the diastolic function of the heart.

Title: Effects of an EMAC Comprehensive Intervention Programme on Poststroke Depression: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
Abstract:
AIM: Evaluate the efficacy and safety of EMAC comprehensive intervention programme for poststroke depression patients.
BACKGROUND: Poststroke depression has a high incidence and significant adverse impacts. Pharmacological treatments for PSD carry certain risks. However, there is currently a lack of a comprehensive, evidence-based nonpharmacological intervention programme for PSD in China.
METHODS: Between May to October 2024, we recruited patients with first-onset stroke complicated by poststroke depression through convenience sampling from a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province. Participants were allocated to the EMAC intervention group and the conventional care control group according to their order of enrolment. This programme incorporated four key components: structured health education, mindfulness-based stress reduction training, behavioral activation techniques, and standardised cognitive training. ANCOVA was used to compare the primary outcome between groups while adjusting for baseline scores and repeated-measures analysis of variance was applied to analyze secondary outcomes across the three assessment points.
MEASURES: The primary outcome of this study was the change in depressive symptoms measured using the HAMD-17. Secondary outcomes included the five facet mindfulness questionnaire, behavioral activation for depression scale-short form, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, stroke-specific quality of life scale, and records of adverse event frequency.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, participants receiving the EMAC programme had significantly lower adjusted HAMD-17 scores at T1 (10.632 [95% CI, 10.119-11.146] vs. 12.112 [95% CI, 11.611-12.613], p < 0.001) and T2 (9.344 [95% CI, 8.663-10.025] vs. 12.053 [95% CI, 11.388-12.718], p < 0.001). Secondary outcomes showed significant improvements over time in the intervention group compared with the control group (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: This programme can effectively improve the health outcomes of patients and provides valuable evidence and reference for clinical application and dissemination of the intervention.
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PATIENT CARE: The EMAC programme provides nurses with a practical, evidence-based protocol for poststroke depression. It combines education, mindfulness, behavioral activation, and cognitive training and may provide a clear and replicable framework for supporting patients with poststroke depression. The observed improvements in depressive symptoms, cognitive function, and quality of life suggest its potential value in clinical nursing practice. Future studies may explore whether selected components of the programme can be adapted to digital platforms to improve accessibility and implementation efficiency.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Registry of Clinical Trials: ChiCTR2300070335.

Title: Genetic and functional analysis of CDH2 reveals new insights into CDH2-related disorders.
Journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Pathogenic variants in CDH2 cause agenesis of the corpus callosum, cardiac, ocular, and genital syndrome (ACOGS). We aimed to define the clinical and molecular landscape of CDH2-related developmental disorders.
METHODS: Newly identified and previously reported families were analyzed for genotype-phenotype correlations; variants were assessed using protein modeling and splicing assays.
RESULTS: Screening identified 20 new families carrying (likely) pathogenic ((L)P) alleles (n=16) or high-priority variants of uncertain significance (VUS) (n=4), including 12 novel CDH2 alleles. The combined (L)P cohort (37 individuals) showed variable ACOGS core features (mean 3; range 1-5), along with abdominal wall and/or diaphragmatic hernias and nipple, spine or gastrointestinal anomalies, each seen in ∼20% of individuals. Novel ACOGS findings included ambiguous genitalia, female genital malformations and dilated cardiomyopathy. Missense variants, principally within extracellular cadherin domains, accounted for 86% of unique (L)P alleles with clusters in EC1 and EC4-EC5; the remainder produce late protein truncations or in-frame deletions. Disruption of calcium binding was predicted by modeling. Conversely, VUS were primarily nonsense-mediated decay-sensitive or deletions (71%), linked to neurodevelopmental, kidney or other anomalies.
CONCLUSION: We expand the ACOGS spectrum and highlight its striking clinical variability. Additionally, we identify a possible milder phenotype associated with CDH2 haploinsufficiency.

Title: GDF-15 as an early marker for prognosis in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest - Experience from the HAnnover COoling REgistry.

Title: Preeclampsia Risk in Obese Pregnant Women without Diabetes Mellitus: a Meta-Analysis Comparing Metformin versus Control Group.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of metformin on reducing the risk of pre-eclampsia in obese pregnant women without diabetes.
SOURCES OF DATA: Following PRISMA guidelines, Scopus, Embase, PubMed (MEDLINE), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, LILACS, SciElo, and Web of Science were searched for articles published between 2014 and April 2024. Search terms: ("Metformin" OR "Biguanide" OR "Glucophage" OR "dimethylbiguanide") AND ("pre-eclampsia" OR "preeclampsia") AND ("obese pregnant women" OR "obesity in pregnancy" OR "maternal obesity" OR "pregnancy" OR "obesity").
STUDY SELECTION: From 2022 studies identified, three randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care in obese pregnant women without diabetes were included. Primary outcomes were pre-eclampsia incidence; secondary outcomes included gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, cesarean delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, and NICU admission.
DATA COLLECTION: Data were extracted, and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Metformin did not significantly reduce PE risk (OR: 0.42; 95% CI: 0.10-1.68; p=0.22; I2=81%). Secondary outcomes showed no significant differences. Subgroup analysis excluding a methodological outlier suggested potential benefit (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.10-0.38; p<0.00001; I2=0%). Metformin alone may not effectively prevent PE in these women, but efficacy could improve with lifestyle modifications. Study heterogeneity highlights the need for larger, rigorous trials.
CONCLUSIONS: Metformin should not be routinely recommended for pre-eclampsia prevention in obese pregnant women without diabetes until robust evidence from further research supports its efficacy.Prospero registry: CRD42024611538.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Meta-Analysis; Systematic Review

Title: Glycated hemoglobin in immediate postpartum, overweight, and pre-gestational arterial hypertension: effect on fasting glycemia one year postpartum.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the relationship between overweight, pre-gestational hypertension, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels in the immediate postpartum and fasting glycemia (FG) in low-income women one year after birth.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study assessed women who gave birth between February and August 2017 with gestational age > 35 weeks. Interviews and anthropometric evaluations were conducted within the first 24 hours after delivery. Pre-gestational anthropometric nutritional status was assessed based on maternal height measurement. Blood samples were collected after delivery and over the next year, and HbA1c ≥ 5.7% and FG > 100 mg/dL indicated a high risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). A generalized linear mixed-effects regression model was applied.
RESULTS: Among the 130 women included, 28.0% and 2.3% were overweight and had pre-pregnancy hypertension, respectively; 20.0% had altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum. As for FG, 4.6% and 14.8% were at risk of T2DM at the 6th and 12th months postpartum, respectively. The mean ± standard deviation of FG among the evaluated women was 77.9 ± 10.98 mg/dL after 6 months and 81.8 ± 15.49 mg/dL after one year of follow-up. In the model adjusted for age and schooling, the effect of overweight and pre-pregnancy hypertension was observed, as well as altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum period, on the elevation of FG, increasing the risk of T2DM.
CONCLUSION: Altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum period, pre-gestational overweight, and pre-gestational hypertension are risk factors for T2DM among low-income women, indicating the need to monitor postpartum glycemia.

Title: Comparative econometric cost analysis of inpatient versus outpatient laser treatment for twin-twin transfusion syndrome.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the costs of inpatient versus outpatient laser ablation of placental vessels treatment of severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome. To evaluate if outpatient is non-inferior to inpatient treatment with regards to feasibility and safety.
METHODS: Case-control study of 71 pregnant women who underwent laser ablation of placental vessels for treatment of severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome between 2019 and 2022. To compare the costs of outpatient versus inpatient treatments we used conditional estimation of the average costs of each procedure and the differences between them with paired data estimators: multivariate distance matching and propensity score matching. Comparisons of surgical and clinical variables were performed using the Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and Student's t-test.
RESULTS: Laser ablation of placental vessels was performed in 71 patients with severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome. Sixteen (16/71 - 23%) patients were operated on in the outpatient clinic and 55 (55/71 - 77%) were operated on as inpatients. The cost of inpatient intervention was 28% and 29% higher than the cost of the outpatient treatment, according to the multivariate distance matching and propensity score matching estimates, respectively. Apart from ex-recipient intrauterine death (greater in the outpatient group), there were no significant differences between the two groups regarding laser ablation of placental vessels, post laser treatment, perinatal variables and variables from delivery until hospital discharge.
CONCLUSION: Laser ablation of placental vessels to treat severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome in an outpatient setting is significantly cheaper than in inpatients, without any compromise in feasibility and safety, as most fetal, neonatal and maternal results were similar.

Title: Comparison of 25 µg Vaginal Misoprostol Versus Dinoprostone Gel for Induction of Labor in Term Prelabor Rupture of Membranes: A Retrospective Record-Based Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) at term occurs in 8-10% of pregnancies, and a long latency period is associated with infection in both the mother and the newborn. In women with an unfavorable cervix, cervical ripening and induction of labor are widely used with prostaglandin analogs. However, the preferred agent in women with term PROM remains unclear. This study compared the efficacy and safety of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol (prostaglandin E1) and dinoprostone (prostaglandin E2) gel in women with term PROM.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a record-based, comparative, observational study with a retrospective design conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in West India over 12 months. Records of 200 women with term PROM (≥37 weeks), singleton cephalic pregnancy, and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop's score ≤6) were reviewed. The primary outcome was the induction-to-delivery interval and the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included change in Bishop score at six hours, oxytocin dose, interval from induction to active labor, need for oxytocin augmentation, mode of delivery, and maternal and neonatal safety outcomes. An independent-samples t-test was employed for continuous variables, and chi-square or Fisher's exact test was used for categorical variables; p < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: The two groups did not differ in maternal age, parity, PROM duration, or baseline Bishop score. The mean Bishop score at six hours was significantly higher in the misoprostol group (5.68 ± 1.31 vs 4.78 ± 1.26; p < 0.001). The mean induction-to-active-labor interval (6.80 ± 1.58 vs 8.19 ± 2.06 hours; p < 0.001) and the induction-to-delivery interval (11.81 ± 3.06 vs 13.78 ± 3.99 hours; p < 0.001) were significantly shorter with misoprostol, which also required fewer doses (1.62 ± 0.63 vs 1.91 ± 0.67; p = 0.002) and less oxytocin augmentation (16 (16.0%) vs 46 (46.0%); p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours (92 (92.0%) vs 94 (94.0%); p = 0.780) or cesarean deliveries (8 (8.0%) vs 6 (6.0%); p = 0.780). The groups did not differ in uterine hyperstimulation (5% vs 2%), abnormal fetal heart rate (8% vs 6%), postpartum hemorrhage (4% vs 5%), mean birth weight, or NICU admission (4% vs 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: 25 µg vaginal misoprostol was associated with more effective cervical ripening and shorter time to delivery than dinoprostone gel, with fewer doses and a lower rate of oxytocin use, similar cesarean rates, and comparable maternal and neonatal safety. The use of low-dose vaginal misoprostol may represent a practical alternative to dinoprostone gel in term PROM.

Title: Soluble E-selectin and QRISK3-based Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Case-control Study from India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with metabolic abnormalities and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial dysfunction is considered an early event in atherogenesis, and soluble E-selectin has been proposed as a marker of endothelial activation. However, its role in cardiovascular risk assessment in PCOS remains uncertain.
AIM: The study aimed to compare circulating soluble E-selectin levels between women with PCOS and healthy controls and evaluate their association with metabolic parameters and QRISK3-based cardiovascular risk scores.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Prospective hospital-based case-control study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two hundred women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria and 50 age-matched healthy controls aged 18-40 years were enrolled. Clinical assessment, anthropometry, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, C-reactive protein and soluble E-selectin levels were evaluated. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the QRISK3 algorithm.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Group comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Mean soluble E-selectin levels were comparable between women with PCOS and controls (0.61 ± 0.33 vs. 0.61 ± 0.29 ng/mL, P = 0.935). Within the PCOS group, soluble E-selectin correlated positively with HbA1c (r = 0.326, P = 0.001) and fasting blood glucose (r = 0.271, P = 0.001), while no significant associations were observed with anthropometric measures, lipid parameters, blood pressure or QRISK3 scores. In multivariable analysis, fasting blood glucose remained independently associated with soluble E-selectin.
CONCLUSION: Soluble E-selectin levels did not differ between women with PCOS and controls and showed limited associations with cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not support a major role for soluble E-selectin in cardiovascular risk assessment among young women with PCOS.

Title: Kidney Outcomes in Structural Heart and Cardiac Surgical Trials: The Case for Longitudinal Endpoint Reporting.
Abstract: The 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/American Diabetes Association/American Society of Nephrology guideline on cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome establishes kidney function as a determinant of cardiovascular risk rather than an adjacent comorbidity. Endpoint architecture in structural heart and cardiac surgical research has not been revised accordingly. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 standardized acute kidney injury reporting with considerable rigor, staging injury on Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine criteria and requiring that new renal replacement therapy be reported discretely, but its scope is confined to the periprocedural window. No endpoint tracks filtration trajectory across follow-up, no threshold within the standard defines chronic kidney disease stage progression, and initiation of maintenance dialysis years after intervention has no reporting convention distinct from temporary replacement therapy in the immediate postoperative period. Pivotal trials consequently adjudicate cardiovascular outcomes for five years and kidney outcomes for 30 days. Registry evidence suggests the omission is consequential, with rapid filtration decline documented in more than a third of patients carrying preexisting kidney impairment within five years of cardiac surgery. This editorial argues for longitudinal reporting of estimated glomerular filtration rate, prespecification of stage progression and maintenance dialysis as adjudicated endpoints, and nephrology representation on trial steering committees with a defined role in kidney endpoint specification.

Title: Cardiac camp: An outreach program to build health literacy among underrepresented in medicine adolescents and increase diversity in medicine.
Journal: Journal of education and health promotion
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eliminating racial and ethnic disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires multilevel action, including improving health literacy and diversifying the healthcare workforce. To contribute to this goal, UCSF medical students designed an immersive summer camp to teach underrepresented minority backgrounds in medical professions (URM) high school students about CVD and encourage interest in healthcare careers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A stipend-supported, 1-week cardiology summer camp for URM Bay Area high school students was implemented by medical students. Participating students completed a preprogram and postprogram survey to assess various metrics, including knowledge of CVD, comfort discussing and teaching concepts of CVD, and interest in medical careers on a Likert scale of 1-5. The mean differences in preprogram and postprogram scores in the second cohort in 2024 (n = 25) were assessed.
RESULTS: Twenty-five students participated in the second iteration of Cardiac Camp @ UCSF (80% female) from July 24 to 28, 2024. Most identified as URM (84%), and many came from households where English was not the primary language (76%). Postcamp surveys showed increased mean scores in CVD knowledge and awareness of medical careers. Open-ended responses indicated that students enjoyed the camp activities and felt more motivated to pursue healthcare careers.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac Camp @ UCSF provides a novel framework for a pipeline program aimed at inspiring URM high school students to pursue careers in medicine. Short-term survey results showed increased CVD knowledge and confidence teaching others, aligning with Healthy People 2030 goals to reduce cardiovascular disparities and strengthen workforce diversity.

Title: A randomised controlled trial comparing a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing and a manual compression device following transradial coronary intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemostasis at radial access sites following transradial coronary intervention (TRCI) is usually achieved using manual compression devices (MCDs). Despite their widespread use, MCDs have limitations, including prolonged compression and haemostasis times as well as increased risk of radial artery occlusion (RAO), thus highlighting the need for alternative strategies to achieve faster and safer radial haemostasis.
AIMS: We sought to compare the safety and efficacy of a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing (CHD) with an MCD in achieving radial access site haemostasis following TRCI.
METHODS: A total of 258 patients were randomly assigned to receive either a CHD (n=130; Axiostat) or an MCD (n=128; TR Band) for radial haemostasis following TRCI. Time to haemostasis, post-application pain, and access site complications - including rebleeding, haematoma, RAO, and allergic reactions - were assessed.
RESULTS: Both groups had similar baseline and procedural characteristics. The CHD significantly reduced haemostasis time (5.84±2.19 min) compared with the MCD (120.2±21.88 min; p<0.001). Post-application pain scores were low and comparable between both groups. The CHD was associated with lower rates of haematoma and rebleeding. RAO occurred in 3.12% of MCD patients, while no RAO events were observed with the CHD. No serious adverse events or device-related complications were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: The CHD provided rapid haemostasis with a shorter compression time, lower RAO risk, and reduced patient-reported pain, along with minimal rebleeding, few haematomas, and no allergic events compared with MCD, without compromising safety. This clearly illustrates that the CHD is a safe and effective alternative for achieving haemostasis following TRCI, potentially enabling earlier patient ambulation and discharge.

Title: A semi-rapid deployment workflow to reduce device time in Evolut FX self-expanding transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands, improving deployment efficiency is increasingly important. We developed and implemented a semi-rapid pacing-assisted deployment workflow for the Evolut platform.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the procedural efficiency and early safety of this workflow for transfemoral (TF) Evolut FX TAVI.
METHODS: In a single-centre registry, we performed a retrospective before-and-after analysis of consecutive TF Evolut FX procedures: semi-rapid deployment (n=48) versus conventional deployment (n=53). Device time was defined as the interval from initial advancement of the delivery system to final release of the Evolut FX valve. Prolonged device time was defined as >14 minutes (>75th percentile), and determinants were assessed using Firth's penalised logistic regression.
RESULTS: The device time was shorter with semi-rapid deployment (9.0 [interquartile range [IQR] 6.0-13.0] minutes vs 14.0 [IQR 11.0-16.0] minutes; p<0.001), while operation and procedure times were similar (p=0.13 and p=0.16, respectively). The mean recapture count was higher in the semi-rapid group (0.85±1.09 vs 0.53±0.70; p=0.08), and contrast volume was higher (32.0 [IQR 25.0-42.0] mL vs 25.0 [IQR 15.0-33.0] mL; p=0.008). Paravalvular leak >=mild (31.2% vs 32.1%; p=1.0) and in-hospital pacemaker implantation (2.1% vs 7.5%; p=0.37) did not differ significantly between the groups. In multivariable analysis, recapture predicted a prolonged device time (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.75-14.19; p=0.002), whereas the semi-rapid workflow predicted a reduced device time (adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.66; p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Semi-rapid pacing-assisted Evolut FX deployment selectively reduced device time without compromising early in-hospital safety outcomes. Deployment efficiency represents a practical procedural target for workflow refinement in self-expanding TAVI.

Title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
Abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

Title: γ-Butyrobetaine, L-carnitine and acylcarnitines and their association with incident atrial fibrillation among men and women with suspected chronic coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
AIMS: Carnitine-metabolites play a key role in cell energy metabolism and have been implicated in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, any associations between L-carnitine and the precursor γ-butyrobetaine (γBB) with new-onset AF are not established. We therefore examined the relationship between serum γBB, L-carnitine and selected acylcarnitines with incident AF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 3815 patients who underwent coronary angiography due to suspected chronic coronary syndrome and followed up for incident CVD events, including new-onset AF. Risk associations between the biomarkers and incident AF were explored by logistic regression for the total population and stratified according to sex. The majority (71.6%) of the patients were men, the median age was 61 years. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years, 412 (10.8%) were reported with new-onset AF. In a multivariate model higher serum γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine [OR per 1SD (95% CI): 1.15 (1.01-1.31), P = 0.04; 1.14 (1.01-1.27), P = 0.03 and 1.15 (1.03-1.28), P = 0.01] were associated with increased risk of incident AF. These associations were particularly stronger among women (P for interaction < 0.04, all).
CONCLUSION: In this large cohort of patients with suspected chronic coronary syndrome elevated circulating levels of γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine were associated with increased risk of incident AF, with stronger associations among women. Our results motivate further studies examining the relationship between carnitine metabolites and cardiac arrhythmias and highlight the need for sex specific analyses.

Title: First Report of Real World Utilization of an Activin Signaling Inhibitor in Patients With Severe Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in the Middle East PH RISE-ME Study.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality despite advances in combination therapy. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel disease-modifying therapy targeting pulmonary vascular remodeling. Real-world data from Middle Eastern populations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study evaluating the real-world effectiveness and safety of Sotatercept in adults with PAH treated at a tertiary pulmonary hypertension expert center in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, between January 2025 and September 2026. Clinical, echocardiographic, biochemical, and risk-stratification data were extracted from electronic medical records. Primary outcomes were changes in right atrial (RA) area and NT-proBNP. Secondary outcomes included systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (SPAP), TAPSE/SPAP ratio, 6-min walk distance (6MWD), risk profile, and safety. Thirty-six patients were prescribed Sotatercept, of whom 33 received at least one dose. Most patients were female (80.6%), with a mean age of 55 years. Significant reductions occurred in RA area (- 2.67 cm2; 95% CI, -4.16 to -1.18; p < 0.001), NT-proBNP (- 46.7 pmol/L; 95% CI, -87.19 to -20.39; p < 0.001), and SPAP (- 6.00 mmHg; 95% CI, -12.00 to -0.50; p = 0.031). TAPSE increased significantly (+ 0.25 cm; 95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33; p < 0.001), and TAPSE/SPAP improved significantly (+ 0.064; 95% CI, 0.030 to 0.108; p < 0.001). Patients improved by at least one risk category. The 6MWD did not change significantly. Treatment was well tolerated, with no adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation or death; two all-cause deaths occurred during follow-up. In this real-world Middle Eastern PAH cohort, Sotatercept was associated with improved right-heart remodeling, NT-proBNP, and risk profile, with acceptable short-term safety. These findings complement trial evidence and provide early regional support for activin pathway inhibition in routine practice.

Title: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension With Cold Agglutinins Needing Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: The Use of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange.
Abstract: Cold agglutinins can be detected in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) pre-operative testing. Peri-operative management of these patients in anticipation of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest can be challenging and has not been standardized. We describe our relevant experience and suggest a potential protocolized pre-operative approach with this observational, retrospective cohort study. A chart review of all patients undergoing PTE surgery for CTEPH (1107 patients) at UC San Diego between 2019 and 2025 was performed. An Institutional Review Board approved quality improvement database on all patients undergoing PTE surgery was used. Twenty-one patients (1.9%) screened positive for cold agglutinins pre-PTE. A high co-prevalence of antiphospholipid syndrome and cold agglutinins was noted (17/21; 81%). Thermal amplitude testing (when possible) was positive for nine patients between 15°C and 18°C. Fifteen patients underwent therapeutic plasma exchange (median of two sessions) with albumin and plasma replacement fluid followed by PTE surgery with standard cooling protocol. There were no incidents of agglutination or hemolysis peri- or post-operatively. Three patients had post-operative airway hemorrhage, two of which developed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). There was one mortality in the setting of HIT with recurrent thrombosis and bleeding. Median intensive care unit and hospital length of stays were 3 and 12.5 days, respectively. We suggest a protocolized approach for the identification and management of high-risk patients with cold agglutinins, which may include therapeutic plasma exchange pre-operatively. This can successfully mitigate the potential risk of hypothermic circulatory arrest causing agglutination during surgery.

Title: Cenobamate in super-refractory status epilepticus: current evidence from a patient-level synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE) represents a challenging neurological emergency, with limited therapeutic options after conventional intravenous antiseizure medications (ASMs) and continuous anesthetic therapy have failed. Cenobamate has shown remarkable efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in SRSE is currently supported only by isolated case reports.
METHODS: We performed a patient-level synthesis of published cases of cenobamate-treated SRSE, focusing on treatment latency, titration strategy, electroclinical response, concomitant therapies, safety, and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: Three publications reporting six patients were identified. Cenobamate was introduced between 13 and 103 days after SRSE onset, following failure of multiple intravenous and oral ASMs, anesthetic agents, and, in most cases, immunomodulatory therapies. Although the timing of treatment initiation varied substantially, electroencephalographic improvement generally occurred within two weeks after cenobamate initiation and was usually accompanied by clinical recovery, successful withdrawal of anesthetic therapy, and liberation from the intensive care unit. Most patients initiated cenobamate at the recommended dose of 12.5 mg/day but underwent individualized dose-escalation schedules compared with the approved outpatient regimen. No cases of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, severe cardiac adverse events, or treatment discontinuation attributable to cenobamate were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the available evidence remains limited to a small number of observational reports, this patient-level synthesis identified consistent clinical patterns that support further investigation of cenobamate as an adjunctive therapy for SRSE. At present, no conclusions regarding treatment efficacy can be drawn. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to clarify cenobamate optimal timing, titration strategy, safety, and potential role within SRSE treatment algorithms.

Title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) in right ventricular failure and preserved LV ejection fraction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) failure with preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) is a distinct clinical entity often associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH), chronic lung diseases, or congenital heart defects, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), such as sacubitril/valsartan, have demonstrated efficacy in left-sided heart failure, but their role in isolated RV failure remains understudied.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted from 2010 to 2025 for RCTs and prospective cohorts assessing ARNI in patients with RV failure and preserved LVEF. Inclusion: Adults with RV dysfunction (e.g., TAPSE <17 mm or RV S' <9.5 cm/s) and LVEF ≥50%; ARNI vs. standard care or pre-treatment; reporting RV parameters, sPAP, NT-proBNP, 6MWD, or NYHA class.
RESULTS: Three studies (1 RCT, 2 prospective cohorts; n=120 patients) were included. ARNI improved TAPSE (WMD 1.2 mm, 95% CI 0.7-1.7; p<0.001; I²=0%), RV S' (WMD 0.5 cm/s, 95% CI 0.2-0.8; P=0.002; I²=0%), and reduced sPAP (WMD -7.5 mmHg, 95% CI -10.2 to -4.8; p<0.001; I²=15%). NT-proBNP decreased (WMD -1200 pg/mL, 95% CI -1700 to -700; p<0.001; I²=0%). 6MWD increased (WMD 30 m, 95% CI 10-50; P=0.003; I²=0%). NYHA class improved (RR 1.65 for ≥1 class improvement, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; P=0.007; I²=0%).
CONCLUSION: ARNI enhances RV function, reduces pulmonary pressures, and improves functional status in RV failure with preserved LVEF.

Title: Outcomes by Comorbidities with Tremelimumab and Durvalumab in the Randomized, Controlled Phase 3 HIMALAYA Study in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often have underlying comorbidities, which may impact prognosis and lead to safety challenges following treatment. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of the phase 3 HIMALAYA study (NCT03298451) assessed outcomes in participants with unresectable HCC and cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities at baseline.
METHODS: Participants with unresectable HCC were randomized to STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab), durvalumab monotherapy, or sorafenib. Comorbidities were based on medical history assessed at baseline and qualified using preferred terms from cardiovascular or metabolic Standardised Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Queries. Overall survival (OS) rates were evaluated in participants with or without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities within and by treatment group. The proportion of long-term survivors (alive ≥36 months post-randomization) and safety were assessed in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities. Data cutoffs: August 27, 2021 (primary analysis); January 23, 2023 (4-year updated analysis, OS, and serious treatment-related adverse events).
RESULTS: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus were the most common cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, respectively. The 48-month OS rates with STRIDE were 28.0% and 21.7% in participants with and without cardiovascular comorbidities and 20.4% and 28.5% in those with and without metabolic comorbidities, respectively. In total, 28.2% of participants with cardiovascular comorbidities and 22.6% of participants with metabolic comorbidities experienced long-term survival with STRIDE. Safety in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities was generally consistent with all participants in the safety analysis set; no new safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: OS benefits with STRIDE were similar in participants with vs. without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities, with manageable safety in participants with comorbidities. These results support the durable benefits of STRIDE in a broad population reflective of unresectable HCC globally.

Title: Blood Pressure Trajectories during Graded Exercise for the Prediction of Future Hypertension.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: An exaggerated increase in systolic blood pressure (SBP) during exercise is associated with future hypertension. While previous studies evaluated peak SBP or two-point slopes, we aimed to identify SBP response patterns from the full SBP time-series during maximal incremental exercise and assess their value for predicting future hypertension diagnosis.
METHODS: In this cohort study, we analysed SBP recordings from 3,486 normotensive adults (mean age 50.6 years; 45% women) undergoing maximal cycle ergometry. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) extracted sex-specific responses from the full SBP time-series. Associations with incident hypertension were evaluated using multivariable Cox analyses by sex and stratified by prehypertensive status (SBP 130-150 mm Hg or DBP 85-90 mm Hg).
RESULTS: In both sexes, GBTM identified three SBP response profiles, reflecting low, mid, and high responders. Over 7.9 years, 171 (8.8%) men and 169 (10.9%) women were diagnosed with hypertension. Incidence was markedly higher in high versus low responders (e.g., in women: 27.8 vs. 2.5 events per 1,000 follow-up years). The increased risk was independent of traditional risk factors, including resting SBP (hazard ratio relative to average risk (HRadj): 1.26 [95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.57] in men, 1.59 [1.22-2.07] in women). The association attenuated with increasing resting SBP in women (p interaction = 0.003). Notably, high SBP response was independently associated with future hypertension diagnosis in those without prehypertension (e.g., in women, HRadj: 2.17 [1.49-3.17]), but not in those with prehypertension. Reclassification analyses indicated incremental predictive value beyond resting and peak SBP in women without prehypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: Time-series analysis of exercise SBP revealed distinct response profiles predicting future hypertension diagnosis beyond resting blood pressure. Comprehensive interpretation of exercise SBP may improve risk stratification, particularly in women without prehypertension.

Title: Enterococcus faecalis bacteraemia and infective endocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of infective endocarditis (IE) in Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection (EF-BSI) vary more than 20-fold across published cohorts. We aimed to estimate the true IE prevalence, quantify the role of echocardiographic ascertainment in driving this variation, and assess the diagnostic performance of IE prediction scores.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science searched from inception to 16 August 2026; PROSPERO registration CRD420251240242) of observational studies reporting IE prevalence in confirmed EF-BSI episodes. Risk of bias was assessed with the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool. Pooled prevalence was estimated with a generalised linear mixed model (logit scale). Meta-regression with echocardiographic coverage as the moderator was used to derive an ascertainment-adjusted prevalence. Diagnostic performance of the NOVA, DENOVA, and MEFIER scores was summarised by random-effects pooling.
FINDINGS: Fifteen studies (11,157 EF-BSI episodes) were included. Crude pooled IE prevalence was 11.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 8.1-16.8; I2 = 97.3%). In studies with systematic echocardiography (k = 2), pooled prevalence was 24.2% (21.5-27.2; I2 = 0.0%). Meta-regression explained up to 91.5% of between-study variance; estimated plateau IE prevalence was approximately 30%. Pooled DENOVA sensitivity was 88.7% (78.9-94.3%) and specificity 84.0% (77.8-88.7%); prospective validation yielded sensitivity 79.2% (negative predictive value [NPV] 93.0%). NOVA had high sensitivity (95.6%) but low specificity (30.7%). Certainty of evidence was low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation [GRADE]).
INTERPRETATION: Once ascertainment is accounted for, approximately one quarter of EF-BSI episodes are complicated by IE. These findings support a shift from selective to routine echocardiography, with transoesophageal echocardiography (TEE) as the definitive modality. Existing scores can prioritise and sequence imaging but do not identify a subgroup in whom it may be safely omitted.
