In the fully adjusted model, each 1-standard deviation increase was not significantly associated with ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction in continuous analysis (odds ratio=1.35; 95% confidence interval: 0.42-4.40; P =  0.616 ); however, the binary comparison showed a significant association (odds ratio=1.60; 95% confidence interval: 1.11-2.31; P =  0.013 ). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant overall association ( P overall   < 0.001 ) without significant nonlinearity ( P nonlinear   = 0.194 ).
DISCUSSION: In this cohort, the triglyceride-glucose-body mass index demonstrated a significant independent association with ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction in the binary analysis, supporting its potential as a screening index for subclinical diastolic dysfunction, although external validation in independent populations is needed.

Title: Integrated hs-cTnI, global longitudinal strain, and coronary artery calcium for risk stratification of anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction in multiple myeloma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction remains a major concern in multiple myeloma, yet conventional left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) surveillance may miss early injury. We evaluated whether pre-anthracycline baseline measurements of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and coronary artery calcium (CAC), obtained before anthracycline initiation, improve risk stratification for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD).
METHODS: In this retrospective study of 312 myeloma patients receiving anthracycline-based therapy, CTRCD was defined as LVEF decline >10% to <53% or relative GLS decline >15%. Predictive performance was assessed using competing-risk models and time-dependent ROC analysis. A simplified risk score (MY-CARD) was derived and temporally validated in a separate cohort.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 91 patients (29.2%). hs-cTnI elevation and GLS worsening preceded LVEF decline, with median intervals of 8.4 and 12.6 weeks. The full model (hs-cTnI + GLS + CAC) achieved an AUC of 0.91, outperforming hs-cTnI + LVEF (0.83) and LVEF alone (0.66). The MY-CARD score stratified 12-month CTRCD risk into low (6.2%), intermediate (28.7%), and high (71.4%) categories. Patients with both hs-cTnI elevation and GLS worsening had the highest subsequent CTRCD risk (adjusted HR 5.42-7.86).
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating baseline hs-cTnI, GLS, and CAC improved CTRCD risk stratification in myeloma patients. The MY-CARD score provides a practical framework for baseline and on-treatment risk assessment, supporting closer surveillance in high-risk patients. External validation and prospective studies are warranted.

Title: The effects of aquatic exercise therapy on blood pressure in elderly people with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains one of the most common controllable risk factors for cardiovascular disease morbidity and mortality in the elderly. Aquatic exercise therapy (AET), as a safe and low-impact form of exercise, has attracted considerable attention due to its potential cardiovascular benefits; however, its impact on blood pressure control in elderly patients with hypertension remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the effects of AET on blood pressure and heart rate in elderly patients with hypertension.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and CINAHL was conducted from inception to July 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of AET compared with control interventions in older adults with hypertension were included. The primary outcomes were systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), while HR was considered a secondary outcome. Random-effects models were applied for meta-analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on the type of control intervention.
RESULTS: Four RCTs involving 123 participants were included in this meta-analysis. Compared with control conditions, aquatic exercise therapy (AET) significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) (MD -10.98 mmHg, 95% CI -17.41 to -4.56, P = 0.001; I² = 29%), diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (MD -5.97 mmHg, 95% CI -6.57 to -5.36, P = 0.001; I² = 0%), and heart rate (HR) (MD -5.91 beats/min, 95% CI -6.70 to -5.12, P = 0.001; I² = 0%). According to the GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence for the main outcomes was rated as moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: AET may be an effective non-pharmacological intervention for improving blood pressure control and reducing heart rate in older adults with hypertension. However, further well-designed RCTs with larger sample sizes are needed to confirm its long-term clinical effects.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261462262, PROSPERO: CRD420261462262.

Title: Intravenous iron supplementation in heart failure and iron deficiency: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is frequently encountered in patients with heart failure. It is related not only to anemia, but also to exercise intolerance, impaired health status, and repeated hospitalization. Intravenous iron has been evaluated in randomized trials and in many systematic reviews, but the review conclusions are not completely aligned, particularly for mortality and functional outcomes. We therefore reviewed the existing review-level evidence, with particular attention to methodological quality and repeated use of the same primary trials.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from January 2016 to 31 March 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating iron supplementation in patients with heart failure and iron deficiency. Reviews including mixed iron formulations were considered only when intravenous iron outcomes were separately reported or intravenous iron represented the predominant intervention of interest. AMSTAR2 was used to assess review quality. Trial overlap was examined using the corrected covered area (CCA), and GRADE was used to judge certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Forty-five eligible reviews were identified, and 18 representative reviews were included in the detailed synthesis. Across the available evidence, intravenous iron showed the most consistent association with reduced heart failure hospitalization, including recurrent hospitalization and composite endpoints combining heart failure hospitalization with cardiovascular death. The randomized evidence was derived predominantly from populations with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), with some trials extending eligibility into the mildly reduced ejection fraction range. Evidence for cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality remained inconsistent. Findings for functional capacity and health status were generally favorable but remained uncertain because of heterogeneity and very low certainty evidence, whereas effects on cardiac function were uncertain. No clear increase in serious adverse events was identified with intravenous iron therapy, although the certainty of safety evidence remained limited. According to AMSTAR2, methodological confidence was low in seven reviews and critically low in eleven reviews. The evidence base comprised 23 unique randomized controlled trials with 163 trial occurrences, yielding a CCA of 35.81%, indicating substantial redundancy among representative reviews included in the quantitative synthesis. GRADE certainty was moderate for overall heart failure hospitalization, low for total/recurrent hospitalization, composite hospitalization-cardiovascular death outcomes, all-cause mortality, and serious adverse events, and very low for first hospitalization, cardiovascular mortality, functional outcomes, and cardiac function.
CONCLUSIONS: Current review-level evidence, derived predominantly from populations with reduced or mildly reduced LVEF, suggests a potential reduction in heart failure hospitalization. This potential benefit should be interpreted in relation to the patient populations, clinical settings, and iron formulations studied in major randomized trials. The clinical certainty of these findings remains constrained by substantial trial overlap, prominent methodological limitations of the published reviews, and inconsistent outcome definitions. Evidence regarding mortality reduction, functional status, and structural cardiac remodeling remains uncertain and requires cautious interpretation.

Title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

Title: Soluble prebiotic fiber and glucono-δ-lactone blends integrate compatible effects to modulate microbiota composition and metabolism ex vivo.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prebiotics modulate the gut microbiome toward health-associated states. Because distinct candidate prebiotic compounds selectively stimulate microbial taxa and metabolic pathways, combining complementary ingredients may broaden or enhance beneficial outcomes. To investigate this concept, we evaluated the effects of microbiome-modulating blends of glucono-δ-lactone (GDL) and the resistant dextrin NUTRIOSE® (NUTR).
METHODS: The validated ex vivo SIFR® technology pipeline (systemic intestinal fermentation research) was used to assess how GDL, NUTR and their blends impacted the composition and metabolic activity of the gut microbiota of a small cohort of healthy adults (n = 6), while effects on gut barrier integrity (transepithelial electrical resistance, TEER) were evaluated via an in vitro co-culture of epithelial/immune (Caco-2/THP-1) cells.
RESULTS: GDL and NUTR induced distinct yet compatible shifts in microbial composition and metabolite output. GDL was rapidly fermented and specifically promoted Bifidobacterium adolescentis, while boosting butyrate-related taxa (Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Anaerobutyricum hallii) and health-associated amino acid derivatives (e.g., indole-3-propionic acid). In contrast, NUTR gradually and strongly promoted propionate through stimulating Bacteroides and Parabacteroides, as well as specific Lachnospiraceae taxa. GDL/NUTR blends displayed ratio-dependent intermediate effects of the individual ingredients. Moreover, GDL/NUTR blends enhanced gut barrier integrity under LPS-induced inflammatory stress, with increases in TEER up to +24.5%.
DISCUSSION: Overall, GDL and NUTR blends compatibly integrate divergent effects, supporting their combined use for enhancing gut health through microbiome modulation.

Title: Long-term survival after transcatheter aortic valve implantation in nonagenarian patients: a multicenter real-world study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The growing number of nonagenarian patients with severe aortic stenosis has increased interest in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in this population. However, data on long-term outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate long-term survival and procedural outcomes of TAVI in nonagenarians and to explore clinical factors associated with long-term mortality.
METHODS: We conducted an ambispective multicenter observational cohort study including patients aged ≥90 years who underwent TAVI for severe aortic stenosis between 2013 and 2021 at six centers in the Emilia-Romagna region, Italy. Baseline and procedural data were collected retrospectively, while outcome ascertainment combined prospective follow-up contacts with retrospective verification of dates of death or last confirmed vital status. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and associations with mortality were examined using an exploratory Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 60 nonagenarian patients (mean age 91 ± 1.5 years; 67% female) were included. Procedural success was achieved in 97% of cases. In-hospital mortality was 5%, and 30-day mortality was 8.3%. Over a mean observation period of 5.7 years from TAVI to death or the last confirmed vital-status assessment, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. In the exploratory multivariable analysis, male sex and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were associated with higher long-term mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients aged ≥90 years selected by the Heart Team for TAVI, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. The procedure demonstrated a high success rate and an acceptable safety profile. Male sex and COPD showed an exploratory association with worse prognosis. These findings suggest that TAVI may be a feasible option in carefully selected nonagenarians when guided by comprehensive clinical assessment and individualized decision-making.

Title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease.
CASE SUMMARY: A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability.
CONCLUSION: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Case Reports; Review; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Association between nutritional status and health perception among participants of the Academida da Saúde Program: a cross-sectional study, Belo Horizonte, 2013-2014.
Journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the association between nutritional status and health perception among participants of the Health Academy Program (Programa Academia da Saúde) in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study using baseline data from a randomized controlled community trial conducted with a representative sample of the Program. Individuals aged 20 years or older answered a questionnaire including sociodemographic variables, self-reported morbidities, and health perception, and had their nutritional status assessed. For data presentation, absolute and relative frequencies and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were used. Regression adjustments were performed to assess the association between nutritional status (underweight or normal weight, overweight, and obesity) and health perception (good or very good, and very poor, poor, or fair), and odds ratios (OR) with 95%CI were used as measures of association.
RESULTS: Of the 3,264 participants, 2,827 (88.0%) were women and 1,931 (56.6%) were adults; 1,352 (41.4%) were overweight, and 944 (28.9%) had obesity; 1,730 (53.0%) reported hypertension, 1,433 (44.3%) dyslipidemia, and 548 (16.8%) diabetes. Regarding health perception, 2,358 (72.3%) respondents rated their health as good or very good. Individuals with obesity were found to have 47.0% higher odds of reporting very poor, poor, or fair health perception compared to their counterparts.
CONCLUSION: Obesity was associated with poorer health perception among participants in the Health Academy Program.

Title: Association of NT-proBNP/LVEF with angiographic coronary disease burden in acute myocardial infarction: a retrospective study with machine learning analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) reflect complementary dimensions of ventricular stress and systolic function. Whether the NT-proBNP/LVEF ratio is consistently associated with angiographic coronary disease burden in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), and whether its predictive contribution is robust across conventional and machine-learning approaches, remains uncertain.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 375 patients with AMI who underwent coronary angiography. The continuous Gensini score was the primary outcome, while clinically anchored anatomical outcomes, including multivessel disease and high-burden coronary anatomy, served as sensitivity outcomes. Associations between log-transformed NT-proBNP/LVEF and Gensini score were assessed using multivariable median regression. Direct discrimination of NT-proBNP/LVEF versus NT-proBNP alone was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and paired DeLong testing; the incremental information provided by adding LVEF to NT-proBNP was additionally assessed using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Six multivariable models-logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and CatBoost-were internally validated using leakage-controlled repeated fivefold cross-validation with five repeats. Calibration, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-based model interpretation were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden. In the fully adjusted model, each doubling of NT-proBNP/LVEF was associated with a 12.20-point increase in median Gensini score (95% confidence interval [CI], 9.33-15.07; P < 0.001). Comparable associations were observed for high-burden anatomy (odds ratio [OR] per doubling, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.44-1.97) and multivessel disease (OR per doubling, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.36-1.84). For the secondary high-Gensini-burden outcome, NT-proBNP/LVEF and NT-proBNP showed comparable discrimination (AUC, 0.783 vs. 0.780; ΔAUC = 0.004; P = 0.362). Adding LVEF to NT-proBNP did not show clear incremental improvement by NRI or IDI. Among the six multivariable models, SVM yielded the numerically highest AUC (0.763; 95% CI, 0.715-0.811), but no pairwise AUC difference remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. XGBoost and CatBoost showed highly concordant SHAP importance rankings (Spearman ρ = 0.978), with NT-proBNP/LVEF ranked first in both models.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden across the continuous Gensini score and clinically anchored anatomical outcomes in patients with AMI. The ratio provides a parsimonious representation of ventricular stress and systolic function and showed stable predictive importance across the two boosting algorithms examined. Its discriminative performance was comparable, rather than superior, to that of NT-proBNP alone, supporting its potential role as a readily available adjunctive marker of coronary disease burden rather than a replacement for established clinical assessment.

Title: Independent association of SOT-composite with berg balance scale scores in Chinese stroke patients: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Stroke-related balance dysfunction affects 61-83% of patients, yet the quantitative relationship between sensory integration capacity and functional balance remains inadequately characterized. This study investigated the association between Sensory Organization Test (SOT) composite scores and Berg Balance Scale (BBS) performance in Chinese stroke patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed data from 339 stroke patients who received treatment at Guangdong 999 Brain Hospital between January 2021 and December 2023. Exposure variable was SOT-Composite score (0-100 points, measured via NeuroCom Smart EquiTest within 48 h). Outcome variable was Berg Balance Scale total score (0-56 points, assessed within 48 h). Two models were constructed: a Core model adjusting for age, gender, diagnosis, and disease duration, and a Sensitivity model additionally adjusting for Brunnstrom lower-extremity stage and weight symmetry index. Tertile stratification of SOT-Composite scores was performed descriptively to explore dose-response patterns.
RESULTS: In the Sensitivity model, each 1-point increase in SOT-Composite score was associated with a 0.2745-point higher Berg Balance Scale score (95% CI: 0.171-0.386, p < 0.001; Core model: β = 0.2471, 95% CI 0.137-0.357, p < 0.001). Standardized coefficient analysis in the Sensitivity model showed Brunnstrom lower-extremity stage had the strongest association (standardized β = 0.4562, p < 0.001), followed by SOT-Composite score (standardized β = 0.2527, p < 0.001). Among sensory subsystems, visual, somatosensory, and vestibular processing ratios were all significantly associated with balance performance (unstandardized β = 0.18, 0.16, and 0.15 BBS points per unit ratio change, respectively).
CONCLUSION: SOT-Composite score was independently associated with Berg Balance Scale performance in stroke patients, even after adjustment for multiple covariates. Whether targeted sensory training can improve balance outcomes warrants evaluation in future prospective intervention studies.

Title: GLP-1/GIP Uptake, Indication, and Access Pathways Among US Adults in the Understanding America Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Evidence on GLP-1/GIP therapies is largely derived from trials enrolling selected populations or medical records that miss utilization outside healthcare channels. No nationally representative cohort has characterized real-world uptake, indications, and access.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize GLP-1/GIP prevalence, indication, clinical profile, and access.
DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with three GLP-1/GIP surveillance waves (March 2024, December 2024, October 2025).
SETTING: The Understanding America Study, an address-based, nationally representative panel of approximately 15,000 US adults aged 18+ years initiated in 2014.
PARTICIPANTS: UAS participants responding to at least one surveillance wave (n=9150).
EXPOSURES: GLP-1/GIP use status (never vs any use, comprising current and former use), self-reported primary indication (diabetes, weight loss, or other), and access pathway (traditional vs non-traditional).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Survey-weighted prevalence of GLP-1/GIP use, overall and by indication and access pathway; sociodemographic, cardiometabolic, treatment, and access characteristics; and smartwatch-derived resting heart rate, heart rate variability, maximum activity heart rate, step count, and sleep duration and variability.
RESULTS: Among n=9150 adults (1274 with any use; 60.9% female; median age 53 years), weighted prevalence increased 46%, from 8.2% (March 2024) to 12.0% (October 2025) representing 32 million. Weight-loss indications grew, reaching nearly half of use (4.1% to 5.6%); diabetes-indicated use was stable (5.3% to 5.4%). Users carried high cardiometabolic burden (obesity, 68.2%; diabetes, 53.6%) but diverged by indication: diabetes-indicated users were older (median, 59 vs 49 years), whereas weight-loss-indicated users were more often female (69.9% vs 51.3%) and healthier. One in three users (~9 million) had non-traditional access, especially in weight-loss-indicated users, of whom 33% had no conventional prescription; 41% used compounding, online, or foreign pharmacies; and, 43% lacked coverage. Non-traditional users were five times as likely to report an unlisted, likely compounded formulation (19.8% vs 4.1%). All p<0.05.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Real-world GLP-1/GIP use has grown rapidly and diversified substantially in indication, access, and population profile. One in 3 users obtained treatment through nontraditional channels largely invisible to claims data, raising long-term safety, efficacy, and coverage questions. GLIMMER provides a public, nationally representative longitudinal evidence base for future payer and provider decisions.

Title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Community-Based, Family Network Heart Health Intervention - the SERVE OC Trial: Design, Rationale and Baseline Findings.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) disproportionately burdens underserved communities, where social determinants of health (SDOH) perpetuate persistent disparities. Family-based interventions leveraging social support represent a promising yet understudied approach. We describe the rationale, design, and methods of the Skills-based Educational strategies for the Reduction of Vascular Events in Orange County (SERVE OC) RCT and present baseline characteristics of enrolled families.
METHODS: SERVE OC is a 2-arm RCT of 190 Latino and Vietnamese families (486 individuals) randomized to the family-based intervention or individual self-management. The intervention was grounded in social network theory while employing community engaged strategies. Primary outcomes include achieving ideal cardiovascular health (CVH) defined by AHA Life's Essential 8 (LE8) and systolic blood pressure reduction at 12, 24, and 36 months. Baseline assessments include demographics, LE8, psychosocial factors, food security, and SDOH. Descriptive statistics and regression analyses examined cohort characteristics and associations between SDOH, food security, and LE8.
RESULTS: Over 83% of participants had suboptimal LE8 scores. Average adult total LE8 scores were 66.61 ±11.96, with physical activity as the weakest domain, compared to an average of 76.52±10.15 in children. Greater SDOH burden and food security were associated with significantly lower odds of ideal CVH and lower LE8 scores respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: SERVE OC demonstrates the feasibility of enrolling families in community-engaged RCT targeting CVD disparities in underserved population. Baseline findings confirm substantial CVD risk and SDOH burden underscoring the need for multi-level, culturally tailored interventions. Trials results will inform scalable, family-focused strategies for CVD prevention across the life course.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique Identifier: NCT05641519.

Title: Multidimensional Social Vulnerability and Hepatic and Extrahepatic Outcomes in Adults With HIV/HBV Coinfection in the United States.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HIV/HBV coinfection is associated with substantial liver-related morbidity and mortality, yet the impact of social vulnerability (SV) on clinical outcomes has not been systematically assessed. We evaluated associations of multidimensional SV with mortality, hepatic, virologic, and extrahepatic organ outcomes among adults with HIV/HBV.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data from 110 U.S. healthcare organizations (2010-2026). We propensity score matched adults with HIV/HBV with and without documented SV 1:1 (2,024 per group). SV was defined using a four-domain framework encompassing material, healthcare access and engagement, interpersonal, and psychosocial vulnerability.
RESULTS: Over 15,900 person-years, SV was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 2.06; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.72-2.47), liver composite events (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.07-1.76), hepatic decompensation (HR, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.39-2.70), hepatic failure (HR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.53-3.73), HBV viremia (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.32-2.16), and HIV viremia (HR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.71-2.46). SV was also associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.47), chronic kidney disease (HR, 1.49), and diabetes (HR, 1.25). Multidomain SV generally showed stronger associations than single-domain SV for most hepatic and virologic outcomes, with HR ranges of 1.76-2.62 versus 1.35-1.76 for single-domain SV. Healthcare access and engagement vulnerability was most consistently associated with mortality and hepatic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: SV was associated with mortality, hepatic disease, impaired HIV/HBV control, extrahepatic organ morbidity, and acute care utilization in adults with HIV/HBV. SV assessment may improve risk stratification and identify actionable intervention targets during HIV/HBV care.

Title: Imaging phenotype is more strongly associated with early neurological deterioration after acute isolated pontine infarction: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early neurological deterioration (END) is common after acute isolated pontine infarction (IPI), but the relative associations of imaging phenotype and metabolic or coagulation markers with END remain uncertain. We evaluated these domains and developed an exploratory prediction model.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 162 patients with acute IPI. END was a ≥2-point increase in total National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score or a ≥1-point increase in NIHSS motor item 5 or 6 from the admission baseline within 7 days after admission. Imaging was modeled nominally (BAD, LAA, or SAD; SAD as reference). Primary associations were estimated by Firth logistic regression. Four prespecified Firth models were compared by AUC, and the full model underwent 1,000-resample bootstrap validation.
RESULTS: END occurred in 49 patients (30.2%). In the full Firth model, BAD (OR 20.70, 95% CI 7.10-70.04; P < 0.001) and LAA (OR 5.06, 95% CI 1.84-15.41; P = 0.001), relative to SAD, were associated with END. Thrombin time (TT) was also associated with END (OR 1.34 per second, 95% CI 1.04-1.73; P = 0.020); diabetes showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.057), whereas TyG was not independently associated (P = 0.603). The apparent AUC was 0.652 (95% CI 0.562-0.742) for the base model, 0.814 (95% CI 0.745-0.883) for the base-plus-imaging model, 0.716 (95% CI 0.631-0.802) for the base-plus-metabolic/coagulation model, and 0.852 (95% CI 0.792-0.911) for the full model. Discrimination did not differ significantly between the base-plus-imaging and base-plus-metabolic/coagulation models (ΔAUC 0.098, bootstrap 95% CI -0.015-0.180; paired DeLong P = 0.066). All 1,000 bootstrap iterations succeeded; the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.818, with a calibration intercept of -0.023, calibration slope of 0.870, and Brier score of 0.162.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, BAD and LAA imaging phenotypes were independently associated with END, whereas TyG was not independently associated. However, the direct discrimination advantage of the imaging model over the metabolic/coagulation model was not statistically established. The association with TT is exploratory, and the full model and nomogram require external validation before clinical use.

Title: Limited utility of optic nerve sheath diameter for monitoring intracranial pressure in patients with intracranial hemorrhage.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Monitoring intracranial pressure (ICP) is a key component in the management of patients with intracranial hemorrhage. Transorbital ultrasound (toUS)- based measurement of the optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) - has been proposed as a non-invasive surrogate for ICP assessment. However, substantial variability in measurement techniques and cut-off values has raised concerns regarding its reliability. This study aimed to evaluate the association between repeatedly measured ONSD and invasively measured ICP in patients with intracranial hemorrhage and to assess the ability of ONSD to reflect changes in ICP over time.
METHODS: In this prospective longitudinal study ONSD was measured daily using ultrasound at 3- and 6 mm posterior to the optic disc and compared with simultaneously recorded invasive ICP measurements. A total of 55 patients with intracranial hemorrhage were included, contributing repeated measurements over a mean of 5.47 ± 2.27 days.
RESULTS: Overall, the association between ICP and ONSD was weak. In the prespecified primary analysis, ICP was not associated with bilateral mean irONSD at 3 mm (β = 0.004 mm per mmHg, 95% CI - 0.003 to 0.011; p = 0.169; marginal R2 = 0.3%). At 6 mm, a small but statistically significant relationship was detectable at bilateral ICP mean values for outer-reflection ONSD [β = 0.010, 95% CI (0.002-0.019), p = 0.016; marginal r2 = 1.3%].
CONCLUSION: ICP explains less than 2% of the variance in ONSD in this treated cohort with predominantly controlled ICP. These findings question its reliability as a stand-alone tool for serial monitoring of dynamic ICP changes in treated neurocritical care patients and therefore should not be interpreted as a direct substitute for invasive ICP or as a stand-alone measure of short-term ICP change.

Title: Barriers to intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective case report series from Honduras.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent and frequently underused in resource-limited settings. We aimed to characterize patients with AIS who did not receive IV thrombolysis at a national referral center in Honduras and to document the barriers to treatment.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, consecutive case report series of all eligible patients with AIS who were not thrombolyzed at Hospital Escuela Universitario between 1 October and 30 November 2025. We gathered demographics, socioeconomic status, admission severity, process-of-care intervals, contraindications, neuroimaging and thrombolytic availability, complications, and discharge outcomes. Contraindications were classified as absolute or relative according to the 2019 American Heart Association and American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines. A thrombolysis eligibility cascade was the principal analysis. The study was approved by the institutional review board.
RESULTS: A total of 23 patients were included (median age 70 years; 14 [60.9%] male). Extreme poverty (≥2 unsatisfied basic needs [UBN]) was present in 14 patients (60.9%). All 23 AIS presentations screened during the period were included, and no patient received thrombolysis (institutional thrombolysis rate 0%). The median onset-to-door time was 10.0 h (IQR 7.0-15.0), and only 1 of 22 patients with a recorded time (4.5%) arrived within 4.5 h. Late or unknown onset was the most frequent absolute contraindication (21 [91.3%]); neuroimaging was available in 22 (95.7%) patients, but the thrombolytic agent was unavailable in every patient (availability 0%). In the eligibility cascade, the single patient within the window had no absolute contraindication and could not be treated because no thrombolytic agent was available. The in-hospital mortality rate was 2 (8.7%), and a good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-2) occurred in 5 of 20 patients with an assessable score.
CONCLUSION: Non-administration of thrombolysis reflected late presentation and, above all, the complete unavailability of the thrombolytic agent, whereas imaging and organizational capacity were largely in place. Drug supply was the proximate, modifiable obstacle to reperfusion in this setting.

Title: Identification and characterization of a human antibody profile inversely associated with adverse cardiovascular events.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The immune response is linked to the progression of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD). We sought to characterize a predictive cardiovascular antibody biomarker using two independent cohorts.
APPROACH AND RESULTS: A human IgG profile serendipitously identified by ELISA was quantified in a well characterized cohort of 359 patients with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) who experienced a total of 71 incident adverse CVD events (death, myocardial infarction, and stroke) over a median 4.1-year follow-up. Using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis, low biomarker levels were an independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, estimated glomerular filtration rate, presence of obstructive CAD, heart failure, total cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (adjusted hazard ratio of 1.90 [95% CI: 1.03-3.49; p=0.038] between lowest and highest tertiles). Validation was then performed in a larger secondary cohort using 4356 baseline samples from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), a prospective study of cardiovascular outcomes resulting in adjusted odds ratio of 50.5 per unit decrease in log-transformed biomarker [95% CI: 2.4-2773.1; p=0.030] over one year by logistic regression analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Low levels of human IgG antibodies targeting Bovidae IgG are independently associated with increased incidence of CVD events in patients with or without a history of CAD, indicating the potential clinical predictive power of this antibody profile as an inverse biomarker for CVD.

Title: Sex Differences in the Impact of Allosensitization on Waitlist Access and Post-Transplant Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients are prone to HLA-antibody formation from multiple surgeries, transfusions, and prosthetic surgical material. Females with ACHD may accrue additional, non-surgical alloantigen exposure. Whether sex modifies the impact of allosensitization on heart transplant (HT) access and outcomes in ACHD remains unknown.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the OPTN/UNOS registry of adults with ACHD listed for first-time HT (2018-2025). Sensitization was defined by calculated panel reactive antibodies (cPRA) at listing. We tested the sex × sensitization (highly sensitized, cPRA >50%) interaction on transplant access using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, treating transplantation as the event of interest and death or removal from the waitlist as competing events, and on post-transplant survival using multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression, both adjusted for age at listing, mechanical support at listing, and the number of distinct prior cardiac surgery categories.
RESULTS: Among 856 candidates (38% female), females were more often highly sensitized than males (23% vs 14%; age-adjusted OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.26-2.61), even after adjusting for surgical burden. Sensitization reduced transplant access in females (84% to 71%; median wait 60 to 110 days, p < 0.001) but not males (79% vs 79%, median wait 88 vs 98 days). In adjusted Fine-Gray models, the subdistribution hazard for transplant was reduced in sensitized females (sHR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.72) with no effect in males (sHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.73-1.26), and the sex × sensitization interaction was significant (interaction sHR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44-0.94, p = 0.02). Post-transplant mortality was numerically higher in sensitized than non-sensitized candidates in both sexes and the sex × sensitization interaction on 1-year mortality was not significant. The sex-asymmetric effect persisted and was more pronounced in the multiorgan candidates.
CONCLUSIONS: Allosensitization is not a sex-neutral barrier to transplant in HT candidates with ACHD. Females are more sensitized and have reduced transplant access without differences in 1-year mortality. The female excess in sensitization is not accounted for by surgical burden, and the exposures responsible remain to be defined. These findings warrant a sex-aware listing strategy and further studies.

Title: Clinical Reference Percentiles for AI-derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Multicenter Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has emerged as an important cardiovascular biomarker that reflects both inflammatory and cardiometabolic risk. EAT volume and density vary significantly across populations, yet there is a lack of multicenter studies investigating the predictive value of population-specific EAT percentiles.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, we retrospectively analyzed low-dose computed tomography correction scans from 42,842 patients undergoing myocardial perfusion imaging. A derivation cohort of 15,082 patients was used to establish sex- and age-specific nomograms for EAT density and EAT volume indexed to body surface area. Percentile-based thresholds were tested for outcome prediction in a validation cohort of 27,760 patients. For clinical implementation, we developed an online EAT percentile calculator.
RESULTS: Percentile curves demonstrated increased BSA-indexed EAT volume and decreasing EAT density with age. Over a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR: 1.83 - 5.14), 4,956 patients experienced a nonfatal myocardial infarction or death. In multivariable Cox models, patients above the 95th sex- and age-specific percentile had significantly worse outcomes for BSA-indexed EAT volume [adjusted hazard ratio 1.30, 95% CI: 1.14 - 1.49, p < 0.001] and EAT density [adjusted hazard ratio 1.7, 95% CI: 1.51 - 1.92, p<0.001] when compared to patients below the 50th percentile (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Age- and sex-specific EAT percentiles provide a clinically interpretable framework for contextualizing automated EAT measurements and identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk. EAT density was a stronger prognostic marker and identified elevated risk even among patients with normal BMI, supporting its potential to provide information beyond conventional anthropometric assessment.

Title: Menstrual cycle length trajectories and their health correlates across the reproductive lifespan.
Abstract: Although the menstrual cycle is a vital sign for women's health, research investigating menstrual cycle length (MCL) trajectories across reproductive life is scarce, often categorizing just two patterns: regular and irregular. We used latent class mixed models (LCMMs) to identify MCL trajectories among 9,332 females enrolled in the Growing Up Today Study, a United States prospective cohort followed from 1996-2023. Participants who self-reported their MCL three or more times were included in the analysis. Additional demographic and health information collected from surveys were included in the descriptive statistics, stratified by trajectory classification. The best fitting LCMM identified four MCL trajectories: "always regular" (94.2% of study population), "early long transition" (2.5%), "late long transition" (3.0%), and "long to short transition" (0.2%). Those classified in the "early long transition" trajectory had a higher proportion of adulthood obesity and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS); "late long transition" individuals had higher proportions of childhood and adulthood obesity, hirsutism, severe acne in adolescence, PMOS, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and endometriosis. The identified MCL trajectories serve as a proof of concept for identifying menstrual irregularity as a signal of disease markers warranting clinical evaluation, though further validation is needed before clinical application.

Title: TRPV1-cardiac afferent ablation after completed myocardial infarction prevents arrhythmogenic remodeling.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
STRUCTURED ABSTRACT BACKGROUND: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias after completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited. Although TRPV1 afferent ablation at acute MI improves cardiac remodeling, the effect of delayed subacute targeting remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated whether ablating cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute post-MI window mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmias.
METHODS: Yorkshire pigs underwent sham surgery or anterior MI creation. Two weeks post-MI, animals were randomized to percutaneous epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX, for cardiac-selective TRPV1 afferent depletion) or vehicle administration. Four weeks later, terminal studies assessed the effects of RTX on cardiac structure and function, ventricular arrhythmogenesis, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling using in vivo electrophysiologic mapping, real-time neurotransmitter sensing, immunohistochemistry, and transcriptomic profiling.
RESULTS: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent depletion was confirmed by blunted responses to TRPV1 agonists. RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced end-diastolic diameter, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility. Endocardial electroanatomic mapping revealed improved VT/VF electrophysiologic correlates in RTX-treated animals, including fewer deceleration zones and late potentials. Epicardial multielectrode mapping demonstrated reduced electrophysiologic heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time release of adrenergic neurotransmitters (noradrenaline and neuropeptide Y) was normalized during sympathoexcitation in RTX-treated animals. Histologically, RTX treatment attenuated scar border zone myocardial fibrosis and sympathetic nerve sprouting, while suppressing T cell infiltration in cardiac sensory ganglia. Bulk RNA-sequencing of stellate ganglia revealed downregulation of adrenergic genes.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation post-completed MI alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural, functional, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling. Targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents represents a promising subacute post-MI therapeutic strategy.
UNSTRUCTURED ABSTRACT: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias following completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited, and the impact of targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute phase is unknown. We evaluated whether epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX) administration two weeks post-MI in swine mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmogenesis. Four weeks post-treatment, RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced chamber dilation, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility compared with controls. Electroanatomic and multielectrode mapping revealed fewer deceleration zones, smaller late potential areas, and reduced repolarization heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time neurotransmitter sensing demonstrated normalized adrenergic release during sympathoexcitation. Histological and transcriptomic profiling showed that RTX attenuated border-zone fibrosis, decreased sympathetic nerve sprouting, suppressed sensory ganglion T-cell infiltration, and downregulated stellate ganglion adrenergic gene expression. Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation during the subacute post-MI window alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural and autonomic remodeling, representing a promising disease-modifying therapeutic strategy.

Title: The Role of Line-Field Confocal Optical Coherence Tomography in the Diagnosis of Melanoma and Melanocytic Lesions: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT) is an emerging non-invasive imaging technique that provides real-time vertical, horizontal, and three-dimensional visualization of the skin at near-cellular resolution. We systematically reviewed the available evidence on LC-OCT in melanocytic lesions to identify diagnostic features associated with melanoma and to clarify its current clinical role. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026 in accordance with PRISMA recommendations. Thirty-two studies were included, encompassing cutaneous melanoma, lentigo maligna, and facial pigmented lesions, benign and atypical melanocytic lesions, and mucosal melanoma. Across studies, melanoma-associated findings included irregular or disorganized epidermal architecture, numerous or pleomorphic pagetoid cells, disruption or blurring of the dermoepidermal junction, atypical dermal nests, and clefting. In lentigo maligna and facial melanoma, peri-adnexal atypia and follicular involvement emerged as particularly relevant features, whereas mucosal melanoma was characterized by diffuse pagetoid spread, epithelial disarray, atypical junctional cells, and discohesive melanocytic nests. Benign lesions more often showed preserved epidermal architecture, a well-defined junction, organized nests, and a regular wave-like dermal pattern. However, substantial overlap was observed with atypical nevi, spitzoid lesions, blue nevi, melanosis, and other intermediate entities. Although selected studies reported promising diagnostic performance, the evidence remains heterogeneous and is largely based on small, descriptive cohorts. LC-OCT may therefore serve as a useful adjunct in clinically or dermoscopically equivocal melanocytic lesions, but prospective multicenter validation and assessment of reproducibility are required before widespread routine implementation.

Title: Dual Versus Mono Antiplatelet Therapy in Mild Versus Moderate Ischemic Stroke: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ATAMIS Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prespecified post hoc analysis of the ATAMIS trial (Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Mild to Moderate Ischemic Stroke) aimed to investigate whether the benefit of dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone differs in patients with mild versus moderate stroke.
METHODS: Using data from the modified intention‑to‑treat population of the ATAMIS trial, eligible patients were divided into mild (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score 4-5) and moderate (NIHSS score 6-10) groups. The primary outcome was early neurological deterioration at 7 days, defined as an increase in the NIHSS score of ≥2 points from baseline. Safety outcomes included bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage within 90 days. Binary logistic regression, Cox regression, and generalized linear models were used as appropriate. Adjusted models included age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, onset-to-treatment time, stroke cause, and other imbalanced baseline variables. Treatment-by-baseline stroke severity interaction was assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 2915 patients were included, including 1992 (68.4%) with mild stroke and 923 (31.6%) with moderate stroke. Median age was 66 years (interquartile range, 59-73); 35.0% were women. Clopidogrel plus aspirin was associated with a significantly lower risk of early neurological deterioration compared with aspirin alone in the moderate stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.17-0.59]; P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed in the mild stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.66-1.41]; P=0.841). A significant interaction was identified between treatment effect and NIHSS score subgroup (Pinteraction=0.003). The occurrence of bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage was similar between treatment groups in both severity subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute mild-to-moderate ischemic stroke, the benefit of clopidogrel plus aspirin versus aspirin alone in preventing early neurological deterioration at 7 days may be greater among patients with moderate stroke (NIHSS score 6-10) than among those with mild stroke (NIHSS score 4-5), without an increased risk of bleeding. These findings suggest that baseline stroke severity may inform antiplatelet therapy selection, and warrant confirmation in future prospective studies.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02869009.

Title: Dyspnea Reduction With L-Menthol Inhalation Improves High-Intensity Endurance Running Performance in Healthy Trained Adults.
Abstract: Dyspnea occurs during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals and may limit endurance performance. Given that L-menthol inhalation can alleviate dyspnea in other contexts, we investigated whether L-menthol inhalation reduces dyspnea and improves endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals. Nine females (mean ± standard deviation;  V ˙   O2peak = 55.8 ± 6.8 mL/kg/min) and nine males (  V ˙   O2peak = 60.3 ± 4.6 mL/kg/min) endurance runners with normal spirometry completed a randomized crossover counterbalanced trial with L-menthol inhalation or a strawberry scent (placebo). Performance was measured with a treadmill time-to-exhaustion (TTE) test at 85% of the peak velocity achieved during a preliminary cardiopulmonary exercise test. Cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and perceptual responses were measured throughout. Compared with the placebo, L-menthol inhalation reduced dyspnea across the TTE test (∼1 AU; p = 0.004) and extended the TTE test duration (406 ± 94 vs. 445 ± 106 s; p = 0.009). Pulmonary ventilation (p = 0.377), tidal volume (p = 0.298), O2 consumption (p = 0.277), CO2 production (p = 0.786), pulse O2 saturation (p = 0.766), and heart rate (p = 0.974) did not differ between conditions. Breathing frequency was lower with L-menthol inhalation than with placebo (p = 0.045). L-menthol inhalation attenuated dyspnea and enhanced high-intensity running endurance performance without substantial changes in cardiorespiratory and metabolic responses to exercise. These results suggest that dyspnea constitutes an important constraint on endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals, and identify acute L-menthol inhalation as an effective ergogenic strategy for this exercise modality and population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (U1111-1289-3438).

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Despite continuous improvements in diagnostic tools, the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is still based on electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac biomarkers supported by other non-invasive imaging techniques. However, ECG has limited sensitivity, while high-sensitivity troponin assays may show reduced specificity, particularly in older or multimorbid patients. Widely adopted clinical pathways (e.g. ESC 0/1 h algorithm) have reported high diagnostic discrimination in external cohorts (with AUC ranging from 0.93 to 0.96) which provides clinical context for interpreting our findings. These diagnostic tests have limitations that can be addressed through automated computer-based diagnostic systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Several studies in the literature have presented machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models to quickly and accurately assess the diagnosis of AMI to optimize treatment.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The aim of our analysis was to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for the diagnosis of AMI using data from all validation and test cohorts available in literature. Sensitivity and specificity for all MIs, and for STEMI and NSTEMI separately, were analysed for different types of AI approach (non-DL or DL) and for different data sources (ECG or troponin-based). Hierarchical models were used to estimate the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity and specificity.A total of 24 studies evaluating 27 AI-based diagnostic algorithms were included encompassing 166.052 patients, of which 18.850 (11.3%) had a final diagnosis of AMI. Patients were predominantly male (61.8%) with a median age of 60.7 (IQR 59.0-64.1) years. Discrimination of AI-based algorithms for the diagnosis of AMI was high with an AUC of 0.97 (sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.92). This result remained consistent when considering the ability to diagnose STEMI (AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.94) or NSTEMI (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90) separately. No significant difference was found regarding type of AI. ECG and troponin-based models were both extremely accurate, with the first ones being less sensitive and the latter less specific.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based diagnostic algorithms for AMI diagnosis were associated with particularly efficient performance. These results were consistent for both STEMI and NSTEMI considered separately. Rather than replacing conventional diagnostic pathways, AI has the potential to enhance existing tools by identifying subtle ECG features and integrating multiple data streams. While direct head-to-head comparisons with traditional statistical models are currently limited, future prospective studies evaluating AI and conventional approaches within the same clinical populations are warranted.AI did not lose accuracy depending on the data source or the type of AI applied.

Title: Corneal Aberrations and Layer-Specific Changes in Fuchs' Dystrophy: A Scheimpflug and AS-OCT-Based Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the relationship between layer-specific corneal structural changes and optical aberrations in Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy (FECD), using Scheimpflug imaging and anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT).
SETTING: Academic tertiary referral center.
DESIGN: Prospective, cross-sectional observational study.
METHODS: A total of 130 eyes (70 FECD, 60 controls) underwent high-resolution imaging using Pentacam AXL Wave and REVO HR OCT. Parameters measured included corneal thickness, Descemet's membrane thickness, epithelial thickness, keratometry, densitometry, and wavefront aberrations. Correlation and multiple regression analyses were performed. Principal component analysis (PCA) identified major structural and optical contributors to visual quality.
RESULTS: Anterior higher-order aberrations (HOAs) significantly correlated with Kmax, anterior densitometry, and Descemet's membrane thickness. Posterior HOAs correlated with central corneal thickness and posterior densitometry. Regression models identified Kmax and trefoil components as significant predictors of posterior HOAs. PCA revealed anterior HOAs, stromal haze, and optical degradation as dominant contributors to visual decline. These features varied with FECD grade and inversely correlated with best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).
CONCLUSIONS: Corneal aberrations in FECD are driven by layer-specific structural changes, notably anterior stromal haze and Descemet's membrane thickening. These precede clinical edema and contribute to early visual impairment. Combined AS-OCT and aberrometry improve disease staging and surgical planning.

Title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
Journal: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.
SETTING: 10 European study centers.
DESIGN: Prospective observational multicenter study.
METHODS: Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.
RESULTS: In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

Title: Caries experience in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, sharing several behavioral and metabolic risk factors with dental caries. While extensive research has explored links between periodontal disease and cardiovascular health, the association between dental caries experience and coronary artery disease is less understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize existing evidence regarding dental caries burden, measured by decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), among individuals with coronary artery disease.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in April 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies published from 1966 to 2025 were eligible if they assessed adult patients with CHD, ischemic heart disease (IHD), myocardial infarction (MI), or related conditions and reported dental caries experience using the DMFT index. Observational studies, including cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort designs, were included. Duplicate records were removed using specialized software. Two independent reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, resolving discrepancies by discussion. Data extraction included study characteristics, caries indices, and key findings. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: From 2339 records identified, 1677 unique studies were screened, leading to 38 full-text articles reviewed for eligibility. Ultimately, 4 studies met inclusion criteria, representing populations from Iran, Sweden, Poland, and India, with sample sizes ranging from 100 to nearly 4000 participants. All studies employed either cross-sectional or case-control designs. Findings generally indicated higher mean values of DMFT among individuals with coronary artery disease, particularly for missing teeth. Some studies showed significantly greater untreated decay and tooth loss in patients with coronary artery disease compared to controls, while restorative care levels were often similar between groups. The small number of studies and their observational nature limit definitive conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that patients with coronary artery disease may experience a higher burden of dental caries, primarily through increased missing and decayed teeth. These findings underscore the potential shared risk environment and highlight the importance of integrating oral health within cardiovascular prevention frameworks. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship and explore whether managing caries can contribute to cardiovascular risk reduction.

Title: Early detection of emergent central apnoea in patients on positive airway pressure therapy: A five-year telemonitoring cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnoea (TE-CSA) during positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy is recognised, yet its onset timing and contributing factors remain unclear. This study aimed to ascertain the onset time of TE-CSA via telemonitoring (TM) and identify associated factors.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 4,021 obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients treated with PAP and monitored via TM from 2017 to 2022 was analysed. TE-CSA was defined as a residual apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) >15 with 50% or more central events. Moreover, if the obstructive apnoea index (OAI) was > 5, patients were excluded. Patients with a central apnoea index (CAI) ≥5 at baseline were excluded. TE-CSA was categorised as transient (<12 weeks), prolonged (12-24 weeks), or persistent (>24 weeks without resolution during the follow-up period). Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed time to TE-CSA onset. A nested case-control study evaluated demographic, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, sedative use, and PAP treatment type as risk factors.
RESULTS: TE-CSA occurred in 171 (4.3%, 95% CI: 3.7-4.9) patients, predominantly prolonged (90.6%), with transient (5.9%) and persistent (3.5%) forms. TE-CSA primarily emerged within the first 60 days of PAP therapy. Multivariate analysis identified older age (Odds Ratio (OR) = 1.03, p < 0.001) and male sex (OR = 2.35, p = 0.003) as significant predictors of TE-CSA development.
CONCLUSION: Telemonitoring detected that TE-CSA onset was most commonly identified within the first 2 months of PAP therapy. Older age and male sex are key predictors. Early detection through TM could facilitate timely interventions, although therapeutic adjustments were implemented throughout the observation period and may have influenced the temporal patterns observed.

Title: Non-cancer causes of death following cervical cancer diagnosis: a SEER database study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify non-cancer mortality after cervical cancer diagnosis and examine how these risks vary over time, by disease stage, race, and registry-recorded treatment patterns.
METHODS: We analyzed 65,852 women diagnosed with cervical cancer in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-17 (2000-2021). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) compared observed deaths with age-, race-, sex-, and calendar-period-specific mortality in the U.S. general population. Fine-Gray models retained every death other than the target cause as a competing event.
RESULTS: Of 24,857 deaths, 19,975 (80.4%) were cancer-related and 4,882 (19.6%) were non-cancer-related. The overall non-cancer SMR was 1.65 (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.60-1.70). After International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage- and race-exact propensity score matching (4,506 pairs; maximum absolute standardized mean difference, 0.079), registry-inferred combined radiotherapy plus chemotherapy without surgery was not associated with overall non-cancer death (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]=1.01; 95% CI=0.88-1.16); the infectious-disease (sHR=1.72; 95% CI=0.75-3.95) and septicemia estimates (sHR=1.60; 95% CI=0.69-3.72; 23 events) were imprecise. Among 31,617 patients surviving beyond 5 years, the conditional non-cancer SMR remained elevated (1.44; 95% CI=1.38-1.49).
CONCLUSION: Non-cancer mortality remains elevated among cervical cancer survivors, including beyond the 5-year landmark. Treatment-group contrasts are strongly affected by disease stage, treatment-selection mechanisms, and unmeasured clinical factors; they should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal. Survivorship care should integrate cardiovascular, infectious, renal, respiratory, and metabolic risk management.

Title: Why early preventive check-ups matter: Unmasking subclinical abnormalities in adults aged 18-45 via systemic ultrasound phenotyping (the LUMINA score).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aim: To evaluate systemic multi-organ ultrasound phenotyping using VScan Air™ CL for detecting subclinical abnormalities in healthy adults aged 18-45 years and develop an integrated scoring system (LUMINA System) for early risk stratification.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: A prospective cohort study (2010-2025) enrolled 188 clinically healthy adults with normal biochemical markers, stratified into three age groups (18-26, 27-35, 36-45 years). Standardized ultrasound assessments of liver, kidneys, carotid arteries, heart, and thyroid were performed. The LUMINA System (score range: 0-29) integrated findings across organ systems.
RESULTS: Results: Subclinical abnormalities were detected in 79.8% of participants despite normal laboratory values. Early liver steatosis occurred in 20.7%, correlating with higher BMI, triglycerides, and HOMA-IR. Increased renal echogenicity was found in 28-35% despite preserved kidney function. Carotid intima-media thickness exceeded the 75th percentile in 22.6%, with progressive vascular stiffness. Thyroid abnormalities appeared in 47.35%, suggesting autoimmune activation. Mean LUMINA scores increased from 0.44±0.31 (18-26 years) to 12.12±3.68 (27-35 years), strongly correlating with BMI (r=0.68), waist circumference (r=0.71), and HOMA-IR (r=0.54).
CONCLUSION: Conclusions: Systemic ultrasound phenotyping enables early detection of multi-organ abnormalities in young adults with normal laboratory profiles. The LUMINA System provides unified preclinical risk stratification, revealing that metabolic, vascular, and endocrine remodeling coexist years before disease onset, enhancing preventive medicine through personalized intervention.

Title: Effectiveness of Quality Improvement Strategies in Preventing Healthcare-Associated Infections Among Neurosurgical Patients Admitted to Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a major and largely preventable cause of morbidity, excess mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and escalating healthcare costs in intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Neurosurgical patients are particularly vulnerable because of frequent exposure to invasive devices such as external ventricular drains (EVDs), central venous catheters, urinary catheters, and mechanical ventilation, combined with impaired neurological status and prolonged ICU stays. Although quality improvement (QI) strategies have been widely implemented across critical care settings, evidence specific to neurosurgical and neurocritical care populations remains fragmented.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of QI interventions in reducing HAI incidence among neurosurgical and neurological ICU patients and to assess their impact on secondary outcomes including ICU length of stay, device utilization, and bundle compliance.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from January 2010 to May 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies for the primary evidence synthesis included randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, and observational cohort studies evaluating structured QI interventions for HAI prevention in neurosurgical or neurological ICU populations, or mixed ICU settings with extractable neurocritical care data. Systematic reviews identified during screening were retained for contextual interpretation and reference screening but were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis to avoid duplication of overlapping primary data. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale according to study design.
RESULTS: Seventeen primary studies from 14 countries met eligibility criteria and were included in the primary narrative synthesis. Three systematic reviews were retained for contextual interpretation. Structured QI interventions consistently reduced device-associated infection rates across studies. The strongest evidence was observed for EVD-specific care bundles, with EVD-related infection rates decreasing from 14.35 to 3.21 per 1,000 catheter-days following bundle implementation, and one study reporting 20 consecutive infection-free months after interprofessional bundle adoption. Device-associated infection prevention bundles also demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions, including VAP rates decreasing from 68.2 to 47.4 per 1,000 ventilator-days and CAUTI rates from 24.9 to 13.4 per 1,000 catheter-days following structured educational interventions. CLABSI rates declined substantially following standardized central venous catheter bundle implementation, reaching zero in one study with sustained monitoring. Risk of bias was predominantly low to moderate across included primary studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Structured QI interventions, particularly EVD-specific care bundles, device-associated infection prevention protocols, and staff education programs with compliance monitoring, consistently reduce HAI incidence in neurosurgical and neurological ICU settings. Although the evidence base is predominantly non-randomized, findings are directionally consistent across diverse healthcare systems and institutional contexts. Universal adoption of evidence-based infection prevention frameworks in neurocritical care is strongly supported.

Title: Albuminuria as a Clinical Marker of Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction is common in diabetes and may precede clinically overt heart failure by several years. Albuminuria reflects systemic microvascular injury, but its relationship with the severity of myocardial dysfunction in patients with diabetes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether adults with diabetes and albuminuria have greater echocardiographic evidence of subclinical myocardial dysfunction than those with diabetes and normoalbuminuria.
METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with diabetes and albuminuria with those with normoalbuminuria. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences in global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', left ventricular mass index, e', and ejection fraction. Adjusted regression coefficients and odds ratios were also synthesized, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports representing 17 independent cohorts were included, with eight contributing to quantitative synthesis. Absolute GLS was significantly lower in patients with albuminuria (MD, -1.38 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.13 to -0.63; P < 0.001; I² = 82%). A greater strain deficit was observed from microalbuminuria to macroalbuminuria, although formal trend analysis was not possible. E/e' was higher in albuminuric patients (MD, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.18-2.24; P = 0.021), whereas ejection fraction did not differ. Albuminuria remained independently associated with impaired strain (pooled β = 1.06; 95% CI, 0.44-1.68) and higher odds of subclinical dysfunction (OR = 5.55; 95% CI, 3.43-8.98).
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria identifies patients with diabetes who have greater subclinical systolic and diastolic myocardial impairment despite preserved ejection fraction. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio may help identify asymptomatic patients who could benefit from deformation imaging, although prospective validation is required.
