In models fully adjusted for traditional risk factors, patients experiencing the highest SDoH burden were nearly twice as likely to experience incident diabetes compared with those with an optimal social profile (adjusted hazard ratio 1.95; 95% CI 1.81, 2.11).
CONCLUSIONS: SDoH are robust, independent predictors of T2DM. Proactive incorporation of SDoH data into patient care could optimize social interventions to prevent T2DM risk and reduce health disparities.

Title: Antinociceptive effects of subcutaneous butorphanol administration in healthy horses.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Subcutaneous (SQ) butorphanol administration maintains target plasma concentrations in horses longer than intravenous administration with fewer adverse effects. This study aimed to evaluate whether SQ butorphanol also produces clinically relevant antinociception in healthy horses.
METHODS: In a blinded, randomized, cross-over study, eight horses received 0.1 mg/kg butorphanol or equal volume (0.01 mL/kg) saline SQ in the cervical region. Thermal (TT) and pain pressure (PPT) thresholds at different body locations, along with physiological and behavioral variables, were assessed at baseline and up to 480 min post-injection. Data were analyzed using Stata/BE 17.0 and summarized as mean ± SD or median [interquartile range (IQR)], as appropriate. Mixed-effects linear regression (horse random effect) assessed treatment, time, and interaction effects (p ≤ 0.05). Adjusted marginal means (95% CI) were derived post-estimation.
RESULTS: Butorphanol produced mild, transient sedation (Wald χ 2 = 145.5, p < 0.01) with a significant treatment × time interaction (LR χ 2 = 46, p < 0.01), peaking at 45-90 min after injection. Heart rate decreased over time with both treatments, and respiratory rate was briefly reduced at 10 min with butorphanol. Mean arterial pressure was unchanged overall, and no hypotension occurred. TT and thermal excursion (TE%) showed significant treatment × time interactions (TT: LR χ 2 = 18.1, p = 0.02; TE%: LR χ 2 = 18.4, p = 0.02) at the coronary band only, decreasing 60-240 min post-butorphanol injection. PPT showed no treatment × time interaction at any site.
DISCUSSION: No clinically relevant treatment effect on TT or TE% was detected. Pressure pain threshold increased modestly for 1-2 h, but it was not statistically significant, likely due to variability and limited power. Subcutaneous butorphanol at 0.1 mg/kg produced mild, transient sedation with clinically acceptable cardiopulmonary effects, but without consistent antinociception.

Title: Prevalence and factors associated with pregnancy-induced hypertension in public general hospitals, central zone, Tigray Region Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: hypertensive disorders represent the most common medical complications in pregnancy and the leading cause of poor prenatal outcomes both in developed and developing countries. Although many studies have been done elsewhere in the globe, there is limited data on pregnancy-induced hypertension disorders and their associated factors in resource-limited Ethiopia, especially in the Tigray Region's Central Zone. Therefore, this study was designed to assess the prevalence of pregnancy-induced hypertension and its associated factors among pregnant women in General Hospitals, Central Zone, Tigray Region, Ethiopia.
METHODS: a hospital-based retrospective "cross-sectional" study design was conducted on 769 selected women who delivered at the General Hospitals of Central Zone from August 8, 2018 to July 7, 2019. A systematic sampling technique was used to select the study participants. The collected data were entered using Epi-Data 3.02; exported to and analyzed by Statistical Package for Social Science version 22. Bivariate and multivariable analysis was employed to assess the relationship between independent and dependent variables. The odds ratio along with 95% CI was estimated to identify factors associated with the outcome variable. The level of significance was declared at P-value ≤ 0.05.
RESULTS: seven hundred sixty-nine (100%) documents were included in the study. The prevalence of pregnancy-induced hypertension was found to be 5.1% (95% CI, 3.5%-6.6%). It was more likely to occur in mothers who had previous hypertension [(AOR=7.16, 95% CI: (1.65, 43.97)], substance abuse [(AOR=7.25, 95% CI: (1.43, 36.73)], family history of pregnancy-induced hypertension [(AOR=5.43, 95%: CI: (1.16, 25.45)], and multiple pregnancy [(AOR=37.09, 95% CI: (8.70, 158.06)].
CONCLUSION: pregnant women who had previous hypertension, substance abuse, family history of pregnancy-induced hypertension, and multiple pregnancies had a significant association with pregnancy-induced hypertension in this study.

Title: Phenotyping of AMI patients using machine learning: integration of clinical, metabolic, and behavioral features to identify high-risk "frailty-inflammation" phenotype.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prognosis among patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) shows substantial heterogeneity, making precise identification of high-risk phenotypes essential for improving long-term outcomes. Machine learning techniques were used to identify such phenotypes by integrating multidimensional data and to examine their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: A total of 1,139 patients with AMI were enrolled from the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University between March 2023 and June 2024. Multidimensional data, including clinical features, metabolic characteristics, and behavioral patterns, were collected. Phenotyping was performed using a hierarchical clustering algorithm. Associations between derived phenotypes and 1-year MACE were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox regression models. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) values derived from an XGBoost model were used to quantify the contributions of individual variables to cluster assignment.
RESULTS: Hierarchical clustering identified two clinical phenotypes with differing pathophysiological characteristics. Cluster 2 (n = 243, 21.3%) exhibited a high-risk "frailty-inflammation" phenotype, characterized by impaired activities of daily living, elevated risk of falls and pressure ulcers, increased high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels, and poor health behaviors. Compared with Cluster 1, patients in Cluster 2 showed a higher hazard of 1-year MACE (unadjusted HR = 4.17; 95% CI: 3.237-5.371; P < 0.001) and a markedly increased risk of all-cause mortality (HR = 12.162; 95% CI: 7.445-19.868; P < 0.001). After adjustment using the minimal sufficient confounding model (M3, incorporating 17 prespecified confounders), Cluster 2 membership remained significantly associated with an increased risk of 1-year MACE (adjusted HR = 2.726; 95% CI 1.986-3.743; P < 0.001) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR = 4.35; 95% CI 2.393-7.905; P < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, Cluster 2 membership was identified as an independent predictor for MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Integration of multidimensional data using machine learning identifies a high-risk "frailty-inflammation" phenotype in patients with AMI. This phenotype offers a comprehensive biological-functional-behavioral framework for risk stratification and may support early and precise clinical interventions to reduce long-term adverse outcomes. However, despite its potential clinical value, the current evidence is insufficient to support direct translation into routine clinical practice until independent cohort validation is performed. Future multi-center studies are warranted to confirm the robustness and generalizability of this approach, and to prospectively evaluate whether phenotype-guided intervention strategies can improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Early changes in CT-derived quantitative flow ratio after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a serial coronary physiological assessment.
Abstract:
AIMS: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic valve stenosis, but its effects on coronary physiology remain incompletely understood. CT-derived quantitative flow ratio (CT-QFR) enables non-invasive assessment of coronary physiology. This study aimed to investigate the early changes in CT-QFR following TAVR.
METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography before and within 7 days after TAVR. CT-QFR was calculated for all analyzable coronary vessels. Longitudinal changes in CT-QFR were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with patient identifier as a random effect.
RESULTS: A total of 109 patients (324 coronary vessels) were analyzed. Plaque volume, plaque burden, and minimal lumen diameter remained unchanged after TAVR, whereas transvalvular pressure gradients decreased significantly. Overall, CT-QFR increased modestly following TAVR (β=0.018, P < 0.001). Significant increases were observed in the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries, whereas no significant change was detected in the left circumflex artery. Vessels with baseline %DS ≥50% demonstrated greater CT-QFR increases than those with less severe stenosis (interaction β=0.104, P < 0.001). Likewise, vessels with baseline CT-QFR <0.80 showed significantly larger post-TAVR increases than vessels with baseline CT-QFR ≥0.80 (interaction β=0.117, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: TAVR was associated with modest early increases in CT-QFR, particularly in vessels with greater anatomical stenosis or baseline physiological impairment. These findings suggest that coronary physiological assessment in severe aortic stenosis may be influenced by valve intervention and should be interpreted cautiously during the peri-TAVR period.

Title: Association of social determinants of health and all-cause mortality among individuals across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stages 0-4: a nationwide prospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to examine the association between social determinants of health (SDOH) and all-cause mortality among middle-aged and elderly Chinese population across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0-4.
METHODS: This study included individuals across CKM stages 0-4 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study with baseline age ≥ 45 years. A cumulative SDOH score was constructed, and participants were stratified into four groups (normal group, low SDOH burden group, moderate SDOH burden group, and high SDOH burden group). Multivariate Cox regression, subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were used to examine the association between SDOH burden and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 9 years, 806 deaths (11.66%) were recorded. Multivariable Cox regression models revealed that each 1-point increase in the SDOH score was associated with a 20% elevated risk of all-cause mortality (HR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.14-1.27, p < 0.001). Compared to the normal group, the moderate SDOH burden group (HR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.19-2.10, p = 0.001) and high SDOH burden group (HR = 2.16, 95% CI: 1.65-2.82, p < 0.001) exhibited 58% and 116% increased mortality risks, respectively. Subgroup analysis demonstrated consistent associations between SDOH score and mortality across all subgroups (interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses using a weighted SDOH score yielded consistent results (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.16-1.26, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Higher SDOH burden is associated with higher all-cause mortality among population with CKM syndrome. This study underscores the necessity of incorporating SDOH screening into the CKM syndrome management framework.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02113-0.

Title: Lower lung donor PaO2/FiO2 ratio correlates with early primary graft dysfunction, but does not impact overall survival after lung transplantation: a dual center study.
Journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract: Extended criteria donor lungs falling below the arbitrarily set PaO2/FiO2 (PFR) threshold of 300 are frequently declined despite other acceptable parameters. This two-center retrospective analysis investigates whether donor PFR is a risk factor for outcomes after lung transplantation (LuTx). A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted at University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium and Motol University Hospital, Prague, Czech Republic including adult LuTx recipients from 2010 to 2022 (Leuven) and 2018-3/2023 (Prague). Primary endpoints: primary graft dysfunction (PGD) grade 3 at 24 and 72 h and 2-year overall survival. Secondary endpoints: incidence of ACR and CLAD-free survival. Donor PFR was measured from an arterial blood gas sample. Logistic and Cox regression analyses were employed to assess correlations, while survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates. A total of 984 LuTx recipients were included. Median follow-up was 4 years. Recipients were predominantly male (54%), with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease being the most common indication for transplantation. Donor characteristics included median age of 51 years, and 18% of donors were DCD. Analyses identified lower donor PFR as a risk factor for PGD grade 3 at 24 h, but not at 72 h. PFR was not associated with the incidence of ACR or with 2-year overall survival after LuTx. Donor PFR does not appear to be a risk factor for development of late PGD or for adversely impacting outcomes. However, it is associated with increased risk of early PGD.

Title: Clinical characteristics of cadonilimab-associated infusion reactions: a severity-stratified analysis of 52 cases and preliminary management framework.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical characteristics of infusion-related reactions (IRRs) associated with cadonilimab in a real-world cohort and propose preliminary management considerations based on these observations.
METHODS: A descriptive retrospective case series was conducted, involving data collection from 52 patients who received cadonilimab and subsequently experienced infusion-related reactions at a tertiary hospital between July 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified into a common IRR group (n=31) and a severe IRR group (n=21) based on the severity criteria outlined in CTCAE 6.0. We conducted a comparative analysis of baseline characteristics, IRR onset timing, clinical manifestations, management strategies, and outcomes between the two groups.
RESULTS: The median time to IRR onset was 20 minutes post-infusion, with the highest proportion of recorded IRR cases occurring during the second treatment cycle (42.3%). Severe IRR manifested as multi-organ involvement in 61.9% of cases, predominantly affecting the respiratory and cardiovascular systems. Patients with severe IRR more frequently received corticosteroids combined with antihistamines (57.1% vs. 29.0%) and had higher rates of premedication (76.2% vs. 45.2%). Twenty-four patients (46.2%) attempted same-cycle infusion resumption; among these, 15 (62.5%) successfully completed the infusion without symptom recurrence. Among the 10 severe-group patients who attempted same-cycle infusion resumption, 6 (60.0%) experienced recurrent symptoms; among all 21 severe-group patients, the recurrence rate was 28.6% (6/21). The clinically relevant same-cycle recurrence rates were 9/24 overall (37.5%), 3/14 (21.4%) in the common group, and 6/10 (60.0%) in the severe group.
CONCLUSION: Cadonilimab is associated with early-onset infusion-related reactions frequently involving multiple organ systems. Based on our institutional experience, we propose a preliminary management framework that requires prospective validation before it can be recommended for routine clinical practice.

Title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, n = 87; TAV, n = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up.
RESULTS: No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction P = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; P = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.

Title: Effects of rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel on thrombotic risk and myocardial injury indicators in patients with coronary artery ectasia.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel therapy and thrombotic risk, platelet activation, myocardial injury biomarkers, and clinical outcomes in patients with coronary artery ectasia (CAE).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 158 consecutive patients with CAE diagnosed by coronary angiography between June 2023 and June 2025. Patients receiving clopidogrel alone or rivaroxaban plus clopidogrel were compared. A 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching method was applied, generating 70 matched pairs. Thrombotic risk markers, including D-dimer (D-D), thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT), and von Willebrand factor (vWF), platelet activation parameters [ADP-induced platelet aggregation rate (ADP-PAg) and CD62P], thromboelastography parameters [maximum amplitude (MA) and reaction time (R)], and myocardial injury-related biomarkers [high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)] were evaluated at baseline and 6 months. Clinical outcomes, including thrombotic-related adverse cardiovascular events and bleeding events, were recorded during 12 months of follow-up.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. At 6 months, patients receiving rivaroxaban plus clopidogrel showed lower levels of D-D, TAT, vWF, ADP-PAg, CD62P, MA, hs-cTnT, CK-MB, H-FABP, and NT-proBNP, as well as prolonged R values, compared with those receiving clopidogrel alone (all P < 0.05). During follow-up, thrombotic-related adverse cardiovascular events occurred less frequently in the combination therapy group than in the clopidogrel group (7.14% vs. 20.00%, P = 0.027). Minor bleeding events were numerically higher in the combination therapy group (17.14% vs. 10.00%, P = 0.218), while no intracranial or fatal bleeding events occurred.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with CAE, rivaroxaban combined with clopidogrel was associated with more favorable changes in coagulation activation, platelet activity, myocardial injury biomarkers, and thrombotic-related clinical outcomes compared with clopidogrel alone. These findings suggest that combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy may represent a potential strategy for selected high-risk patients with CAE. Further multicenter prospective studies are required to confirm these observations.

Title: Neonatal respiratory distress beyond common causes: surfactant dysfunction disorders and other etiologies of childhood interstitial lung disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal interstitial lung disease (ILD) encompasses a heterogeneous group of rare disorders, among which surfactant dysfunction disorders represent a clinically distinct and severe subgroup. Diagnosis is challenging because presentation frequently overlaps with common neonatal respiratory conditions, and classification in neonates remains particularly difficult.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical characteristics, genetic spectrum, and outcomes of neonatal-onset childhood interstitial lung disease (chILD), with a focus on etiology-related differences in clinical presentation between surfactant dysfunction disorders and other chILD subtypes.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 14 patients with neonatal-onset chILD diagnosed between 2019 and 2025. Patients underwent a standardized evaluation protocol and were stratified by surfactant dysfunction mutation status to explore etiology-related differences in clinical presentation and outcome.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients were included (50% male; 42.9% consanguineous; 50% premature). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 7/14 patients (50%), most commonly in ABCA3 (21.4%) and NKX2-1 (14.3%). Patients with surfactant dysfunction mutations presented earlier (symptom onset <24 h in 100% vs. 77.8%) and required higher peak oxygen support (median FiO₂ 100% vs. 55%), whereas those with other etiologies had a longer but less fatal course. Pulmonary hypertension was present in 42.9%. Mortality was 21.4% after a median follow-up of 36 months.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small cohort, surfactant dysfunction disorders showed numerically earlier symptom onset, higher oxygen requirements, and higher mortality compared with other etiologies, although between-group differences did not reach statistical significance. Repeated surfactant requirements or failure to wean from respiratory support should prompt early systematic clinical, radiological, and genetic evaluation, particularly in preterm infants, in whom diagnostic delay may occur due to clinical overlap with respiratory distress syndrome.

Title: Clinical and radiological features of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in children: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is an uncommon but critical neurological emergency in children. Data on Chinese pediatric cohorts remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical features, imaging findings, and treatment of PRES in children to improve early diagnosis and management.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 10 children diagnosed with PRES from March 2016 to January 2025.
RESULTS: The patients included 7 males and 3 females, aged 3-13 years (mean 7.5 years). The main underlying diseases were acute lymphoblastic leukemia (3 cases) and nephrotic syndrome (3 cases). Eight children (80%) had hypertension, 6 (60%) had hypoalbuminemia, and 8 received glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. The main symptoms were headache, seizures, impaired consciousness, and visual disturbances. Cranial MRI showed symmetrical long T1 and long T2 signals in bilateral posterior cerebral white matter. After comprehensive treatment including antihypertensive, anticonvulsant, and dehydration therapy, all symptoms resolved and lesions disappeared on follow-up imaging without sequelae.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric PRES is an acute reversible disorder associated with hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Early MRI diagnosis and prompt intervention can significantly improve prognosis.

Title: Admission platelet-to-hemoglobin ratio and 1-year outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter registry cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The platelet-to-hemoglobin ratio (PHR) is a proposed prognostic marker in cardiovascular disease, but it has not been evaluated against a broad major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) endpoint in a dedicated percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) cohort, and whether it adequately summarizes its two components remains untested.
METHODS: We analyzed 1,551 patients pooled from two prospective Korean drug-eluting stent registries (2016-2022). The PHR was calculated as platelet count (×10⁹/L) divided by hemoglobin (g/L). The primary endpoint was 1-year MACE, with follow-up censored at 365 days, a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, repeat revascularization, or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox models included eight prespecified clinical covariates; the functional form was examined with restricted cubic splines, and the PHR was decomposed using nested models and a log-scale ratio-constraint test.
RESULTS: MACE occurred in 107 patients (6.9%) within 1 year. A higher PHR was independently associated with MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1-standard deviation, 1.21; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.40; P = 0.008), with no evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.700). Adding the PHR improved the clinical model (likelihood-ratio P = 0.013); the ratio constraint was not rejected (P = 0.765), and a single log-PHR term retained 98.7% of the two-component likelihood-ratio χ 2 increment over the clinical model in this cohort (bootstrap 95% CI, 21.8%-100%). The PHR was associated with all-cause and cardiovascular death (both HR, 1.28), paralleling hemoglobin. Repeat revascularization was associated with platelet count (HR, 1.39; P = 0.014), but not significantly with PHR (HR, 1.24; P = 0.081). Risk was concentrated in patients with both anemia and a platelet count at or above the median (adjusted HR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.05-3.15). The gain in discrimination was negligible (ΔAUC, +0.003; 95% CI, -0.003 to +0.012), and net benefit was virtually unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: The admission PHR was independently associated with 1-year MACE after PCI, with no evidence of nonlinearity, and its log-scale component effects were compatible with the ratio constraint in this cohort. Given the negligible gain in discrimination and net benefit, the PHR is an independent prognostic marker rather than a tool for risk reclassification.Registry registration: Clinical Research Information Service KCT0003392 and KCT0005008.

Title: Mapping the methodological framework of diabetic retinopathy interventional trials: a scoping review on trial design, execution, and reporting practices.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a prevalent and sight-threatening ocular complication of diabetes, and one of the leading causes of vision loss and blindness among the working-age population worldwide. Driven by a growing understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying DR, treatment strategies have evolved from a sole focus on glycemic control to comprehensive, multi-targeted, and multimodal therapies. This study systematically summarizes the characteristics of current clinical trials focused on DR treatment and evaluates the employed research methodologies. The aim of this review is to explore methodological trends in specific domains, with the hope that such insights may inform future efforts to optimize trial design and improve trial quality.
METHODS: This study followed the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) were retrieved. In addition, clinical trials indexed in PubMed from July 23, 2016 to July 23, 2026 were retrieved. Data from the included studies were extracted and presented in tabular form.
RESULTS: Clinical research targeting DR has expanded rapidly, reflecting a shift toward diverse interventions like anti-Vascular endothelial growth factor(anti-VEGF) drugs, laser treatments, and combined therapies. However, several methodological limitations were noted in the included studies, including the failure to specify diabetes type in over half of the cases, a predominance of small-sample trials, inconsistent reporting of intervention duration, and limited implementation of blinding due to practical constraints in ophthalmic interventions.
CONCLUSION: This review represents the first comprehensive assessment of current DR clinical research, exposing key design weaknesses in existing trials. Future meta-analyses and systematic evaluations, informed by the methodological gaps identified in this review, are urgently needed to generate robust evidence that can guide optimal treatment strategies.

Title: Prognostic value of the inflammatory burden index in predicting 1-year mortality in patients undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy for heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Heart failure (HF) is one of the leading causes of death and impairs quality of life worldwide. Systemic inflammation has been increasingly recognized as a major contributor to adverse outcomes in patients with heart failure. The Inflammatory Burden Index (IBI), a composite marker integrating C-reactive protein (CRP), neutrophils, and lymphocytes, may offer improved prognostic value over traditional inflammatory markers. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of IBI in predicting one-year mortality among patients undergoing Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy (CRT).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 525 heart failure patients who received CRT between January 2020 and January 2024. Patients were grouped based on 1-year survival status. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t-test or Mann-Whitney U test based on normality assessment, and presented as mean ± SD or median [interquartile range, IQR]. To handle right-skewness and ensure linearity in the logit, inflammatory markers were logarithmically transformed [Log(IBI) and Log(CRP)]. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed using a standardized baseline clinical model. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI), continuous Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), and DeLong's test.
RESULTS: Baseline CRP (median [IQR]: 20.90 [11.95-33.00] vs. 6.56 [3.37-13.80] mg/dL, p < 0.001) and IBI (median [IQR]: 81.15 [36.56-230.90] vs. 18.61 [7.76-44.46], p < 0.001) were significantly higher in non-survivors. In multivariable analysis, both Log(IBI) (OR: 1.983; 95% CI: 1.463-2.687; p < 0.001) and Log(CRP) (OR: 3.265; 95% CI: 2.278-4.678; p < 0.001) independently predicted 1-year mortality. Incorporating Log(IBI) or Log(CRP) significantly improved model discrimination over baseline clinical risk (AUC increased from 0.684 to 0.778 and 0.795, respectively; DeLong p < 0.001), yielding substantial IDI (0.0953 and 0.1118, p < 0.001) and continuous NRI (67.1% and 80.6%, p < 0.001) gains. Head-to-head comparison showed comparable discriminative performance between Log(IBI) and Log(CRP) models (DeLong p = 0.307).
CONCLUSIONS: Both Log(IBI) and Log(CRP) are independent predictors of 1-year mortality in HF patients undergoing CRT, offering comparable incremental prognostic utility over standard clinical risk factors. Incorporating these inflammatory biomarkers into routine risk stratification may refine the identification of high-risk candidates.

Title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited.
METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12.
DISCUSSION: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.Clinical Trial Registration: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

Title: Laboratory-derived inflammatory-nutritional exploratory phenogroups and their associations with functional limitation and 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission in patients with heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is characterized by marked clinical heterogeneity, while conventional left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-based classification may not fully capture systemic inflammatory, nutritional, hematologic, and cardiorenal abnormalities. We aimed to identify laboratory-derived inflammatory-nutritional exploratory phenogroups in hospitalized patients with HF and evaluate their associations with functional limitation and 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 1,588 hospitalized patients with HF, of whom 1,455 with complete data for 15 prespecified clustering variables were included in the primary analysis. K-means, Gaussian mixture models, and DBSCAN were compared, and K-means with K = 3 was selected based on internal separation, stability, cluster size, and clinical interpretability, with K = 2 used as a sensitivity analysis. Severe functional limitation was defined as NYHA class III-IV, and 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission was evaluated as the short-term clinical outcome. Multivariable logistic regression with HC3 robust standard errors was used to assess these associations, with multiple-imputation and median-imputation sensitivity analyses conducted in the full cohort.
RESULTS: Three phenogroups were identified: an inflammatory-cardiorenal-nutritional vulnerability phenotype, an anemia-immune dysregulation phenotype, and a relatively preserved laboratory phenotype. LVEF was similar across groups, whereas severe functional limitation and 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission differed significantly. After enhanced adjustment, compared with Cluster 3, the odds ratios for severe functional limitation were 3.814 and 5.594 for Clusters 1 and 2, respectively, and the corresponding odds ratios for 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission were 1.966 and 2.616. Higher quartiles of both ALI and PNI were associated with lower odds of severe functional limitation; higher ALI quartiles and the highest PNI quartile were associated with lower odds of 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission.
CONCLUSION: Routine admission laboratory measurements identified three exploratory HF phenogroups with distinct inflammatory, nutritional, hematologic, and cardiorenal profiles. After adjustment for continuous LVEF and NT-proBNP, the two vulnerable phenogroups remained associated with severe functional limitation and 30-day same-center all-cause unplanned readmission, with directionally consistent findings in the full-cohort and K = 2 sensitivity analyses. ALI and PNI reflect laboratory-derived inflammatory-nutritional vulnerability but cannot replace formal nutritional assessment or establish incremental predictive value. These findings remain exploratory and require validation in prospective multicenter cohorts.

Title: Associations of early-pregnancy triiodothyronine and triglycerides with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid hormones are associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), but the contribution of triiodothyronine (T3), the biologically active thyroid hormone, remains insufficiently understood. Given the established role of T3 in lipid homeostasis and the association of triglycerides (TG) with HDP, we aimed to examine the associations of early-pregnancy T3 and TG levels with HDP and evaluate the potential role of TG in the association between T3 and HDP.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 13,915 pregnant women who underwent prenatal screening between January 2020 and December 2021. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations of early-pregnancy free triiodothyronine (FT3), total triiodothyronine (TT3), and TG with HDP and its subtypes, while linear regression was used to assess the associations of FT3 and TT3 with TG. Mediation analysis assessed statistical indirect associations through TG, and multiplicative interaction analysis evaluated interactions between T3 and TG.
RESULTS: Higher early-pregnancy FT3, TT3, and TG levels were associated with higher odds of HDP (all P < 0.05), and both FT3 and TT3 were positively associated with TG (P < 0.05). Mediation analysis identified significant indirect associations through TG, representing an estimated 34.1% and 33.5% of the observed associations of FT3 and TT3 with HDP, respectively. Comparable indirect associations were observed for preeclampsia (PE), with estimated proportions of 18.6% and 28.3%, respectively. For gestational hypertension (GH), an indirect association through TG was observed for TT3 (estimated proportion, 42.0%), whereas the corresponding proportion for FT3 was not interpreted because the total association was not statistically significant. No evidence of multiplicative interaction between T3 and TG was observed in relation to HDP.
CONCLUSION: Higher early-pregnancy FT3 and TT3 levels were associated with higher odds of HDP, particularly PE. TG may represent a potential metabolic component involved in the observed associations between T3 and HDP.

Title: Physiological discordance between clinical examination, bioimpedance spectroscopy, and lung ultrasound in maintenance hemodialysis patients without heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate volume assessment in maintenance hemodialysis remains challenging because no single bedside method fully characterizes extracellular fluid overload. We evaluated discordance among clinical examination, bioimpedance spectroscopy, and abbreviated six-zone lung ultrasound, the prevalence of subclinical pulmonary congestion, and factors associated with pulmonary congestion.
METHODS: In this single-center cross-sectional study, 116 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis without clinically recognized heart failure underwent standardized clinical examination, whole-body bioimpedance spectroscopy, and predialysis six-zone lung ultrasound. Subclinical pulmonary congestion was defined as a prespecified total B-line count of ≥3 in clinically euvolemic patients. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa, and independent associations were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Among 49 clinically euvolemic patients, 27 (55.1%) had subclinical pulmonary congestion, representing 23.3% of the cohort. Clinical examination showed fair agreement with lung ultrasound for ≥3 B-lines (κ = 0.28; 95% CI, 0.11-0.45), whereas agreement between lung ultrasound and bioimpedance-defined overhydration was slight (κ = 0.16; 95% CI, -0.03 to 0.35). Bioimpedance-derived overhydration, but not interdialytic weight gain, was independently associated with subclinical pulmonary congestion.
CONCLUSION: Discordance among clinical examination, bioimpedance spectroscopy, and lung ultrasound was common and is consistent with the hypothesis that these modalities capture partially distinct aspects of volume status and pulmonary congestion. Abbreviated lung ultrasound frequently identified clinically occult pulmonary congestion despite apparent clinical euvolemia, supporting a multidimensional approach to bedside volume assessment in maintenance hemodialysis.

Title: Efficacy and safety of bone marrow mononuclear cell therapy for myocardial infarction: a dose-response meta-analysis.
Journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone marrow mononuclear cells (BMMNCs) have been investigated as a potential regenerative therapy for myocardial infarction (MI). However, whether their clinical benefits are sustained over time and what constitutes an optimal therapeutic dose remain uncertain. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and dose-response relationship of BMMNC therapy in patients with MI.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing BMMNC therapy with standard therapy or placebo in patients with MI were systematically searched in relevant databases. Statistical analyses were performed using R. Continuous outcomes were summarized as mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and dichotomous outcomes were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with 95%CIs. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, meta-regression, and restricted cubic spline models were performed to explore the effects of follow-up duration and cell dose on treatment outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 43 RCTs involving 2,213 patients receiving BMMNC therapy and 1,686 control patients were included. BMMNC therapy significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) at 6 months (MD = 2.57%, 95%CI: 0.79 to 4.35; p = 0.007), but this effect was attenuated at 12 months and did not reach statistical significance (MD = 1.59%, 95%CI: -0.06 to 3.23; p = 0.057). At the final follow-up, BMMNC therapy was still associated with a significant improvement in LVEF (MD = 2.24%, 95%CI: 0.77 to 3.71; p = 0.004). Meta-regression showed that the improvement in LVEF decreased significantly with longer follow-up duration (β = -0.296 per month, 95%CI: -0.549 to -0.043; p = 0.024). No significant linear or nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed between cell dose and LVEF improvement. Safety analysis showed that BMMNC therapy significantly reduced the risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) overall (RR = 0.62, 95%CI: 0.45 to 0.86; p = 0.0036). However, this benefit was mainly observed in low- and intermediate-dose studies (<109 cells), whereas high-dose studies (>109 cells) did not show a clear benefit (RR = 1.53, 95%CI: 0.40-5.82), suggesting a potential threshold in the dose-safety relationship. Further meta-regression indicated that increasing cell dose was significantly associated with a higher risk of MACE (β = 0.341, 95%CI: 0.104 to 0.578; p = 0.0062). Subgroup analyses suggested that a dose range of 108 to 109 cells may provide a favorable balance between LVEF improvement and safety.
CONCLUSION: BMMNC therapy may improve LVEF in the short term and reduce the risk of MACE in patients with MI; however, the LVEF benefit appears to diminish over time. Current evidence does not support a significant linear or nonlinear dose-response relationship between cell dose and LVEF improvement, although higher cell doses may be associated with increased MACE risk. Taken together, 108 to 109 cells may represent a potentially appropriate therapeutic dose range, although this finding requires confirmation in further high-quality RCTs with longer follow-up and standardized cell-processing protocols.

Title: Quality of life after cryoballoon vs. radiofrequency ablation in atrial fibrillation: a subanalysis of the FREEZE cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation for symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) is an established treatment, with cryoballoon (CBA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) showing similar success rates. However, comparative data on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes between these methods are limited. This study compares HRQoL changes following CBA vs. RFA in symptomatic AF patients.
METHODS: This sub-analysis of the FREEZE Cohort Study (NCT01360008) compared HRQoL outcomes between CBA (group A) and RFA (group B) using the EQ-5D-3L questionnaire and EHRA symptom scores at baseline and follow-up. Changes in mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, EQ-VAS, and general physical condition (GPC) were assessed.
RESULTS: Between 2011 and 2016, 4,189 patients were included, with 2,110 (50.4%) completing all HRQoL questionnaires. The mean age was 61.8 ± 10.4 years, with 39.2% female patients. Group A had a higher proportion of patients with paroxysmal AF (72.8% vs. 65.4%, p < 0.01). Overall complication rates were similar (7.6% vs. 10.1%, p = 0.07). The median follow-up was 434 (375, 517) days. Atrial arrhythmia recurrence was more frequent in group B (45.0% vs. 56.9%, p < 0.0001), as were repeat ablations (7.9% vs. 22.3%, p < 0.001) and rehospitalizations (26.0% vs. 46.7%, p < 0.0001). Both groups experienced significant improvements in HRQoL. After multivariable adjustment, group A remained associated with greater improvement in pain/discomfort (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.26-2.08), EQ-VAS (aOR 1.60, 95% CI 1.27-2.02), and the EuroQol 5D-Score (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.10-1.76).
CONCLUSION: Both CBA and RFA significantly improved HRQoL. However, CBA was associated with greater improvements in pain/discomfort, EQ-VAS, and the EuroQol 5D-Score, indicating potential differences in selected HRQoL outcomes between ablation modalities.Clinical Trial Registration: NCT01360008.

Title: Large language model-assisted CAD-RADS classification: structured report extraction, accuracy, and clinical decision-making risk of ChatGPT-4o/5 and DeepSeek-R1.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 in assigning main Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from findings-only coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) reports and to characterize management-relevant classification errors.
METHODS: This retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study included 2,100 category-balanced findings-only CCTA reports (300 per CAD-RADS category). Two experienced CCTA radiologists graded the English-translated reports; 12 disagreements were resolved by a third. ChatGPT-4o was evaluated in standard mode, ChatGPT-5 in Thinking mode, and DeepSeek-R1 in Deep Thinking mode; model generation and inference mode therefore varied together. Exact-match accuracy with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs), paired comparisons, and unweighted Gwet AC1 with 95% CIs were calculated. Management-relevant transitions and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) findings among high-risk downgrades were analyzed.
RESULTS: DeepSeek-R1 had an exact-match accuracy of 82.57% (95% CI, 80.89-84.13) and AC1 of 0.797 (95% CI, 0.778-0.816). ChatGPT-5 had an accuracy of 80.19% (95% CI, 78.43-81.84) and AC1 of 0.769 (95% CI, 0.749-0.789), whereas ChatGPT-4o had an accuracy of 53.62% (95% CI, 51.48-55.74) and AC1 of 0.460 (95% CI, 0.435-0.485). Cochran's Q test was significant (Q = 657.87; df = 2; P < 0.001); after Holm correction, DeepSeek-R1 also outperformed ChatGPT-5 in the paired comparison (P = 0.026), and both outperformed ChatGPT-4o (both P < 0.001). ChatGPT-4o downgraded 127/900 (14.11%) reference high-risk reports to CAD-RADS 3 or lower. Of these 127 cases, 65 underwent DSA within three months; DSA supported the original high-risk assessment in 56/65 (86.15%). The corresponding high-risk downgrade proportions were 37/900 (4.11%) for ChatGPT-5 and 23/900 (2.56%) for DeepSeek-R1.
CONCLUSION: The DeepSeek-R1 Deep Thinking and ChatGPT-5 Thinking configurations achieved higher accuracy than ChatGPT-4o in standard mode. Because model generation and inference mode varied together, the results do not isolate a model-family effect. LLMs merit further evaluation for secondary structuring when no documented CAD-RADS category is available, but should not overwrite a radiologist-assigned category or independently determine management.

Title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79; P = 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66; P = 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15; P = 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02; P = 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98; P = 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.64).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.

Title: Risk factors for aortic disease combined with coronary artery disease and the significance of preoperative coronary assessment in endovascular aortic repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The clinical utility of preoperative coronary assessment in patients undergoing endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains uncertain. This study aims to identify risk factors for aortic disease combined with coronary artery disease (CAD) and evaluate the impact of preoperative coronary assessment on in-hospital adverse events.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing elective EVAR at Beijing Anzhen Hospital (January 2021-June 2023). Participants were stratified by coronary assessment status within 12 months pre-surgery. Intergroup comparisons used two-independent samples t-tests and chi-square tests. In-hospital adverse events were a composite endpoint (all-cause mortality, acute myocardial infarction, acute heart failure, stroke, acute kidney injury, bleeding events, endoleak). Univariate logistic regression identified potential risk factors; variables with P < 0.10 were entered into multivariate logistic regression.
RESULTS: A total of 1,139 patients were included, of whom 385 (33.8%) underwent preoperative coronary assessment. Among assessed patients, 278 with CAD received tailored management, including revascularization or optimized medical therapy. CAD risk varied across aortic disease subtypes (P = 0.005); abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) patients had elevated risk (OR = 2.113, P = 0.027). Age (OR = 1.036, P = 0.014) and hyperlipidemia (OR = 2.652, P < 0.001) were independent CAD risk factors. The non-assessment group had higher in-hospital adverse event rates (6.0% vs. 2.6%, P = 0.012), primarily due to major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (3.4% vs. 1.3%, P = 0.035). Preoperative assessment was associated with reduced adverse event risk; non-assessed patients had a 277.9% increased risk (OR = 3.779, P = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: AAA patients have a substantially elevated risk of concurrent CAD. Comprehensive preoperative coronary evaluation before EVAR optimizes medical management and enables appropriate revascularization, enhancing procedural safety and reducing adverse cardiovascular events.

Title: Factors associated with pulmonary embolism in children with severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the clinical characteristics and factors for pulmonary embolism (PE) in children with severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP).
METHODS: This retrospective study included pediatric patients with SMPP hospitalized at the Affiliated Children's Hospital of Shandong University between October 2019 and March 2025. They were divided into the PE and control groups based on the presence/absence of PE. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with PE in children with SMPP. The area under the curve (AUC) of the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was calculated to evaluate the discriminative ability of the identified factors.
RESULTS: Among the 199 children with SMPP included in this study, 100 were diagnosed with PE and 99 served as controls. The mean age was 6.73 ± 1.79 years in the PE group and 6.57 ± 1.70 years in the control group. The mean interval from symptom onset to PE diagnosis was 17 days. The multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that duration of fever (OR = 1.122, 95%CI: 1.040-1.211, P = 0.003), extrapulmonary symptoms (OR = 3.479, 95%CI: 1.853-6.535, P<0.001), NEU (OR = 1.355, 95%CI: 1.131-1.624, P = 0.001), ESR (OR = 1.024, 95%CI: 1.003-1.047, P = 0.028), APTT (OR = 0.926, 95%CI: 0.866-0.990, P = 0.025), D-dimer level (OR = 1.210, 95%CI: 1.111-1.319, P<0.001), and cardiovascular complications (OR = 9.500, 95%CI: 1.759-51.316, P = 0.009) were independently associated with PE in children with SMPP. D-dimer showed the largest AUC (AUC = 0.806), with a sensitivity of 75% and a specificity of 74%.
CONCLUSION: Early clinical signs of pulmonary embolism (PE) in children with SMPP include nonspecific prolonged fever, elevated inflammatory markers, increased D-dimer, and cardiovascular complications.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Comprehensive coronary computed tomography angiography assessment in high-altitude diabetic populations: integrating plaque characteristics, pericoronary inflammation, and coronary function.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides complementary anatomical, inflammatory, calcific, and functional biomarkers, but their interpretation under chronic high-altitude exposure remains uncertain. We characterized CCTA phenotypes according to altitude and type 2 diabetes and explored associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective matched cohort with prospective outcome ascertainment included adults undergoing clinically indicated CCTA for suspected coronary artery disease. Participants were classified by high-altitude residence (≥2,500 m for ≥5 years) or low-altitude residence (<500 m) and by diabetes status, forming four groups. Propensity score matching was performed separately within diabetes strata using age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension, yielding 174 participants in 87 matched pairs. CCTA assessment included pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation, plaque characteristics, coronary artery calcium (CAC), coronary stenosis, and vessel-specific CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR). Primary models evaluated altitude, diabetes, and their interaction with adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension. Associations with MACE were explored using univariable Cox models among participants with follow-up.
RESULTS: In primary covariate-adjusted analyses, diabetes was associated with higher PCAT attenuation, CAC, total plaque volume, plaque burden, and maximum stenosis and with lower left anterior descending (LAD) CT-FFR (all q ≤ 0.018). Compared with the low-altitude Han group, the high-altitude Tibetan group had higher LAD and right coronary artery CT-FFR and lower CAC and plaque burden (all q ≤ 0.037). Among 13 interaction tests, only the altitude × diabetes interaction for LAD-PCAT remained significant after false discovery rate correction (-6.62 HU; 95% CI, -10.32 to -2.91; raw P < 0.001; q = 0.008). Among 119 participants with follow-up, 20 MACE occurred over a median of 28 months. Exploratory univariable analyses showed large but imprecise associations of diabetes and high-risk plaque with MACE, whereas altitude was not statistically associated with MACE (P = 0.557).
CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with a more adverse coronary CCTA phenotype, whereas the high-altitude Tibetan group showed lower CAC and plaque burden and higher vessel-specific CT-FFR than the low-altitude Han group. The association between diabetes and LAD-PCAT attenuation differed between these groups. These findings warrant validation in larger, ethnically comparable longitudinal cohorts.

Title: Association between changes in obesity- and lipid-related indices and the risk of cardiovascular disease: a prospective cohort study in Northwest China.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major global health burden. Traditional indicators inadequately capture CVD risk. This study evaluated the association between dynamic changes in novel obesity- and lipid-related indices and CVD incidence.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted with 19,315 CVD-free participants from the Jinchang Cohort in Northwest China. Changes in seven indices-WHtR, METS-VF, CVAI, BRI, TyG, TyG-WC, and TyG-BMI-from baseline to follow-up were classified via K-means clustering, and cumulative indices were calculated. Multivariable logistic and restricted cubic spline models assessed associations with incident CVD. Predictive performance was evaluated using AUC, NRI, and IDI.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 66 months, 3,200 (16.57%) participants developed CVD. The highest change classes of all indices showed significantly increased CVD risk, with the strongest associations observed for TyG-BMI (OR: 3.988, 95% CI: 3.419-4.650), TyG-WC (OR: 3.797, 95% CI: 3.215-4.484), and CVAI (OR: 3.695, 95% CI: 3.085-4.426). A significant dose-response relationship was observed for cumulative indices. Changes in CVAI (AUC: 0.642) and cumulative METS-VF (AUC: 0.659) demonstrated the highest predictive ability. Adding these indices to a model of traditional risk factors significantly improved the AUC, NRI, and IDI for CVD prediction (all p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses were consistent.
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal increases in obesity- and lipid-related indices may provide modest incremental value for CVD risk stratification when added to traditional risk factors, but their discriminative ability is moderate and further validation is required before clinical application.

Title: A machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after scalp cluster needling therapy in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive recovery varies substantially among patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSCI-MCI), whereas individualized models for predicting post-treatment cognitive improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after 1 month of scalp cluster needling therapy with prolonged needle retention (SCNT-PR) in patients with PSCI-MCI.
METHODS: This retrospective study included hospitalized patients diagnosed with PSCI-MCI between January 1, 2010, and January 1, 2023. Baseline data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke severity, imaging features, cognitive and functional assessments, emotional and sleep-related indicators, treatment-related variables, and laboratory findings. The outcome was defined as an increase of at least 2 points in the corrected Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score after treatment compared with baseline. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used to identify key predictors. Seven supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to develop pretreatment prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation.
RESULTS: A total of 750 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training set (n = 526) and a validation set (n = 224). Seven key predictors were identified from the intersection of LASSO regression and Boruta. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the acceptable performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.759. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated acceptable calibration and favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis identified baseline corrected MoCA score, years of education, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale total score, Barthel Index score for activities of daily living, age, frontal lobe lesion, and diabetes as the major contributors to model prediction. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent predictor patterns under alternative outcome definitions and predictor configurations.
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a machine learning model based on multidimensional pretreatment clinical data to predict cognitive improvement after SCNT-PR in patients with PSCI-MCI. This model may provide preliminary support for patient stratification and individualized clinical assessment, although external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Effects and safety of acupuncture on inflammatory biomarkers in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation contributes to the development and progression of coronary heart disease (CHD), and residual inflammatory risk remains an important clinical concern despite advances in standard cardiovascular therapy. Acupuncture interventions have been increasingly used as adjunctive therapies for CHD, but their effects on inflammatory biomarkers have not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the effects of acupuncture interventions on inflammatory biomarkers and to evaluate their safety in patients with CHD.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception to 12 March 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating acupuncture interventions in patients with CHD were included. The co-primary outcomes were high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and C-reactive protein (CRP). Secondary inflammatory outcomes included interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 18.0. Random-effects 95% prediction intervals were calculated for heterogeneous inflammatory outcomes with at least three studies. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical setting, and a post hoc exploratory analysis by comparator type was undertaken for CRP, with a formal test for interaction. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Thirteen randomized controlled trials involving 927 patients were included. The pooled estimates were lower for CRP standardized mean difference (SMD) = -0.87, 95% confidence interval (CI) -1.43 to -0.30; 95% prediction interval (PI) -2.15 to 0.42; low-certainty evidence] and IL-6 (SMD = -0.74, 95% CI -1.31 to -0.17; 95% PI -1.93 to 0.45; low-certainty evidence), but heterogeneity was substantial and both prediction intervals included no effect. For hs-CRP, the pooled estimate was not statistically significant (SMD = -0.79, 95% CI -1.65 to 0.07; 95% PI -2.99 to 1.42), and the evidence remained inconclusive. TNF-α also favored acupuncture, but heterogeneity and imprecision were substantial. Total cholesterol (TC) and triglycerides (TG) decreased, whereas low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) did not differ significantly. Reported adverse events did not differ significantly between groups, but safety reporting was sparse.
CONCLUSION: The pooled data yielded lower average CRP and IL-6 estimates, but low-certainty evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and prediction intervals including no effect preclude inference of a consistent anti-inflammatory benefit. Findings for hs-CRP and TNF-α were inconclusive. Current studies cannot distinguish acupuncture-specific effects from non-specific or contextual effects, and evidence on cardiovascular events and safety remains limited. Further well-designed trials are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261279145.

Title: COMPANION-002: A Randomized Phase 2/3 Trial of Tovecimig Plus Paclitaxel versus Paclitaxel Alone as a Second-line Therapy in Patients with Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with previously treated biliary tract cancer (BTC) have a short median overall survival (OS), and few treatment options. Tovecimig, a bispecific antibody to delta-like ligand-4 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A, was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in COMPANION-002, a randomized phase 2/3 study in pretreated patients with advanced BTC.
METHODS: Patients with advanced BTC with one prior systemic therapy were randomized to paclitaxel (80 mg/m2; days 1, 8 and 15) with or without tovecimig (10 mg/kg; days 1 and 15). The primary endpoint was RECIST v1.1-defined objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and OS. Crossover from the paclitaxel control arm to tovecimig plus paclitaxel was permitted following BICR-confirmed progression.
RESULTS: 168 patients were randomized 2:1 to tovecimig+paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). Tovecimig+paclitaxel significantly improved BICR-assessed ORR (18.0% vs 5.3%; P=.0228) and PFS (4.7 vs 2.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.44; P<.0001). Among 31 patients (54%) who crossed over, post-progression PFS (time from crossover to subsequent second progression) exceeded initial PFS (PFS from randomization to initial progression on paclitaxel; 3.5 vs 1.9 months; HR, 0.40; P=.0035). Overall, 142 patients (85%) received tovecimig; no difference in OS was observed (HR, 1.05; P=.779). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) with tovecimig+paclitaxel were hypertension (69.4%) and fatigue (66.7%). Grade ≥3 TEAEs occurred in 93.5% and 64.2% of patients treated with tovecimig+paclitaxel and paclitaxel alone, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Tovecimig combined with paclitaxel significantly improved ORR and PFS versus paclitaxel alone as second-line therapy for patients with BTC.

Title: Mindfulness-based perioperative care, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, and early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a prospective observational cohort study.
Abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between perioperative care by mindfulness and sleep quality, autonomic regulation, inflammatory activity, and early recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmia (AT) following radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for atrial fibrillation (AF). This was a prospective assessor-blinded observational cohort study involving 124 patients with AF who underwent their initial radiofrequency catheter ablation from April 2023 to December 2025. Conventional perioperative care was provided to one group (n=62), while the other group (n=62) received mindfulness-based perioperative care. To reduce baseline imbalance, propensity score overlap weighting was implemented. Objective sleep architecture was assessed by overnight polysomnography and autonomic function was examined by HRV analysis. hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and MCP-1 were analyzed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Health related quality of life was determined based on the SF-36 questionnaire. Compared with conventional care, mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with greater observed changes in total sleep time (389.4 ± 43.8 vs. 365.7 ± 45.2 min, P=0.012), sleep efficiency (77.4 ± 7.2% vs. 71.2 ± 7.8%, P=0.004), sleep onset latency (27.1 ± 8.8 vs. 34.8 ± 10.5 min, P=0.009), and PSQI scores (7.2 ± 2.5 vs. 9.3 ± 2.9, P=0.006). The mindfulness group also showed lower inflammatory biomarker levels and differences in short-term autonomic indices, including a lower LF/HF ratio (1.39 ± 0.41 vs. 1.66 ± 0.54, P=0.005). Early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence occurred in 6 patients (9.7%) in the mindfulness-based perioperative care group and in 11 patients (17.7%) in the conventional care group, corresponding to a crude risk ratio of 0.55 (95% CI: 0.22-1.38). Mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with improved objective and subjective sleep quality, more favorable autonomic and inflammatory biomarker profiles, better postoperative quality of life, and a lower observed rate of early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for AF.

Title: Cardioprotective mechanisms and efficacy of colchicine, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine and leflunomide in inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.
Abstract: Chronic systemic inflammation contributes to the excess risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs), raising the possibility that anti-inflammatory treatment may modify vascular risk. This review sought to critically review the mechanistic and clinical evidence for atheroprotection with colchicine and the commonly used conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine and leflunomide. We performed a targeted narrative review of key experimental studies, randomized cardiovascular outcome trials, observational RMD cohorts and systematic reviews, prioritizing evidence directly relevant to ASCVD outcomes and cardiometabolic mechanisms. Colchicine has the strongest randomized evidence for reducing recurrent ASCVD events in patients with established coronary disease, with supportive observational data in gout. Methotrexate is associated with fewer cardiovascular events in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), whereas the CIRT trial was neutral in patients without inflammatory arthritis. Hydroxychloroquine has favorable lipid, glycaemic and antithrombotic effects and observational associations with lower cardiovascular risk in RA and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but no definitive cardiovascular outcome trial. Evidence for sulfasalazine is limited and observational, and human data for leflunomide are conflicting. Cardiovascular benefit differs substantially between agents and is most convincing for colchicine in secondary prevention and for inflammation control with methotrexate in RA. Dedicated prospective trials in inflammatory RMD populations are needed before any csDMARD can be prescribed primarily for ASCVD prevention.

Title: Real-world injection burden, treatment switching, and visual outcomes in diabetic macular edema: a 563-eye cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate real-world injection burden, treatment switching patterns, and visual outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) receiving intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included 563 eyes with DME treated with anti-VEGF agents and followed for at least 12 months. All eyes received an initial loading phase of three monthly bevacizumab injections followed by a pro re nata regimen. Primary outcomes were the number of injections and outpatient visits during the first year. Secondary outcomes included change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), distribution of visual outcomes, and treatment switching patterns. Multivariable linear regression and generalized estimating equation (GEE) analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of visual outcomes.
RESULTS: Eyes received a mean of 5.4 ± 2.4 injections and attended 8.0 ± 2.2 visits during the first year. Mean BCVA improved from 0.75 ± 0.43 to 0.59 ± 0.42 logMAR (mean change - 0.16 ± 0.35; P < 0.001). Visual improvement was observed in 60.2% of eyes, stability in 21.7%, and deterioration in 18.1%. Treatment switching occurred in 29.7% of eyes, typically within the first 4-5 months. In multivariable linear regression analysis, baseline BCVA was associated with visual acuity change (β = -0.33, P < 0.001). Treatment switching was associated with visual outcomes in unadjusted analysis but was not independently associated after adjustment. In the GEE analysis accounting for inter-eye correlation, baseline BCVA remained significantly associated with visual acuity change (P < 0.001), whereas injection number (P = 0.527) and treatment switching (P = 0.976) were not associated.
CONCLUSIONS: In real-world clinical practice, anti-VEGF therapy for DME was associated with meaningful visual improvement despite a moderate injection frequency. Visual outcomes were primarily associated with baseline visual acuity rather than treatment intensity. Treatment switching was not independently associated with visual acuity change after adjustment, suggesting that it likely reflects underlying disease refractoriness rather than acting as an independent factor associated with visual outcomes; however, causal inference cannot be established due to the observational study design. These findings underscore the importance of individualized treatment strategies in DME.

Title: Association of hypothermic temperature-control duration at 33 °C with coagulation parameters after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal duration of temperature control after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains uncertain. Prolonged hypothermic temperature control may affect coagulation, but clinical data remain limited. We evaluated the association between different durations of hypothermic temperature control at 33 °C and coagulation parameters, recorded clinical safety outcomes, and 6-month neurological outcomes in patients after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 112 adult patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who achieved return of spontaneous circulation and received hypothermic temperature control at 33 °C at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital from January 2018 to June 2024. Patients were grouped by actual maintenance duration: 24 h (n = 39), 48 h (n = 30), or 72 h (n = 43). Coagulation parameters were measured serially. Recorded occult blood positivity, lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis detected by vascular ultrasonography, transfusion requirements, survival to discharge, and 6-month neurological outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Compared with the 24 h group, the 48 h and 72 h groups had longer activated partial thromboplastin time and lower platelet counts and D-dimer levels at corresponding time points. Thrombin time was prolonged in the 72 h group at 72 h. After FDR correction, statistically significant between-group differences persisted for APTT at 72 h and 96 h, TT at 72 h, D-dimer at 48 h, 72 h, and 96 h, and platelet count at 72 h and 96 h. Recorded occult blood positivity, lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis detected by vascular ultrasonography, and transfusion requirements did not differ significantly among groups. Adjusted analyses did not show significant associations between prolonged temperature control and the prespecified clinical outcomes, although several estimates had wide confidence intervals. Survival to discharge and 6-month neurological outcomes also did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort of patients after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who survived long enough to complete the assigned temperature-control protocol, hypothermic temperature control at 33 °C for 48 h or 72 h was associated with temporal changes in coagulation parameters. These changes included prolonged APTT and TT and lower platelet counts and D-dimer levels at selected time points. They were not accompanied by a statistically detectable increase in recorded occult blood positivity, lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis detected by vascular ultrasonography, or transfusion requirements. Because treatment duration was not randomly assigned, early deaths were excluded, temperature-control phase may have influenced serial laboratory comparisons, and the sample size was modest, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of safety or efficacy.
