Abstract: BackgroundRobotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) provides a minimally invasive option for advanced coronary artery disease (CAD), but evidence on its learning curve and outcomes in the Indian population remains limited.ObjectivesTo evaluate the learning curve associated with robotic CABG using BIMA and to compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between the early and late phases of surgical experience in a real-world setting.DesignRetrospective, single-center, observational chart review conducted at a high-volume quaternary cardiac care center in India.MethodsThis retrospective chart review was performed for 341 patients who underwent robotic-assisted BIMA CABG between 2020 and 2025. The learning curve was assessed using risk-adjusted cumulative summation (CUSUM), while complication trends were examined through sequential probability CUSUM failure analysis.ResultsThe cohort comprised 295 (86.51%) males with a mean age of 59.56 ± 9.93 years and a body mass index (BMI) of 25.98 ± 3.74 kg/m2. Mean console time was 101.66 ± 29.99 minutes, ICU stay 2.85 ± 0.98 days, and hospital stay 6.01 ± 2.38 days; conversion to open surgery occurred in 2.93% of cases, with in-hospital mortality of 3.52%. CUSUM analysis identified case 125 as the proficiency inflection point, after which console time significantly decreased (94.95 ± 24.32 vs. 113.38 ± 35.04 minutes; p<0.001), while ventilator duration, ICU and hospital stay, complications, and mortality remained comparable between phases. Readmission and re-exploration rates were low (2.05% each), with no deaths at 6-month follow-up. CUSUM failure analysis confirmed complication rates remained within acceptable thresholds throughout the study.ConclusionsRobotic-assisted BIMA CABG demonstrated acceptable outcomes, with operative efficiency improving after approximately 125 cases. These findings support its feasibility in experienced, high-volume centers and warrant further multicentre evaluation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Predictive factors of functional and anatomical response to dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify clinical and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) biomarkers predictive of functional and anatomical response to intravitreal dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 185 eyes of 98 diabetic patients with center-involving DME refractory to a mean of 7.1±2.8 prior aflibercept (2mg) injections. All eyes received a 0.7mg intravitreal dexamethasone implant and were followed for at least 6 months, with a mean follow-up of 12.9±2.1 months. Functional outcome was assessed by best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) and anatomical outcome by central macular thickness (CMT) on SD-OCT. Baseline OCT biomarkers included CMT, serous retinal detachment (SRD) height, integrity of the ellipsoid zone and external limiting membrane (ELM), and disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRIL).
RESULTS: Baseline BCVA was 0.72±0.31 logMAR, and CMT 432±128μm. At 6 months, BCVA improved to 0.55±0.28 logMAR, and CMT decreased to 301±96μm (both P<0.001). Functional and anatomical responses were observed in 56% and 70% of eyes, respectively. Lower baseline CMT (OR=1.42, P=0.003), smaller SRD height (OR=0.76, P=0.005), fewer prior injections (OR=1.31, P=0.010), preserved ellipsoid zone (OR=2.18, P=0.002), and intact ELM (OR=1.94, P=0.004) were independently associated with favorable functional outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Baseline SD-OCT biomarkers are significant predictors of treatment response in refractory DME and may support individualized therapeutic decision-making.

Title: Machine-learning differentiation of precordial T-wave inversion in pulmonary embolism and acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in emergency settings is a notorious diagnostic challenge due to their overlapping symptoms and shared electrocardiographic abnormalities, such as precordial T-wave inversion (TWI). This study evaluated the ability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish acute PE from ACS by analyzing the morphology of inverted T waves in precordial leads.
METHODS: This retrospective, case-control study included 200 patients (100 ACS confirmed by coronary angiography; 100 PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography) admitted to Shahid Madani Hospital, Tabriz, Iran (2023-2024), who exhibited precordial TWI. Image processing with a region-growing technique traced negative T waves in leads V1, V2, and V3. Signals were filtered using Savitzky-Golay and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) methods to extract time-frequency statistical parameters. Multiple supervised ML models were trained (80% training, 20% test with 5-fold cross-validation) over 50 random iterations.
RESULTS: The Ensemble (AdaBoost) model achieved the highest diagnostic performance, yielding an accuracy of 84.44%, sensitivity of 83.96%, specificity of 84.87%, and F1-score of 83.56%. Neural Network models performed comparably, achieving 84.00% accuracy and 85.14% sensitivity. Other evaluated algorithms (SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes) also generated acceptable discriminative accuracy (ranging from 78% to 82%).
CONCLUSION: Machine-learning algorithms can extract potentially disease-specific features from precordial T-wave morphology to differentiate PE from ACS. These findings support further investigation of AI-enhanced ECG interpretation as a rapid, low-cost, non-invasive adjunct to clinical decision-making in acute care. External validation in larger, clinically representative populations is required before clinical application.

Title: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy is an electrocardiographic pattern characterized by a regular alternation of two distinct cardiac events. It can arise from normal operation of device algorithms or indicate underlying dysfunction, such as sensing abnormalities. Accurate differentiation is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate clinical intervention.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically elucidate the mechanisms underlying pacemaker-associated bigeminy and establish a practical diagnostic framework.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of six patients exhibiting pacemaker-associated bigeminy on ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECGs). The patients were identified from the databases of the Children's Hospital of Soochow University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between March 2020 and December 2025.
RESULTS: We delineate six distinct mechanisms: 1) Non-competitive atrial pacing (NCAP) triggered by sinus tachycardia; 2) Fusion beat exclusion due to evoked response (ER) undersensing; 3) Auto capture (AC) operation with start-stop pattern constrained by maximum tracking rate (MTR); 4) Window of atrial rate acceleration detection (WARAD) activation by non-conducted atrial premature complexes; 5) A Pace on Premature Ventricular Contraction (A Pace on PVC) triggered by PVCs; and 6) Dynamic atrioventricular (AV) delay operation following atrial premature beats.
CONCLUSIONS: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy represents a spectrum of phenomena driven by specific "algorithm-rhythm interactions." Recognition of these characteristic patterns is essential for correctly distinguishing normal device function from malfunction, thereby guiding appropriate clinical management and optimizing patient outcomes.

Title: Trends in Oral Anticoagulant Prescribing for Atrial Fibrillation and Active Cancer in UK Primary Care.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation is essential in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and cancer, but recent real-world evidence on oral anticoagulant (OAC) use remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to describe recent OAC-prescribing trends and identify factors associated with OAC initiation in patients with AF and active cancer in UK primary care.
METHODS: Using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, we identified patients aged ≥50 years with incident AF (cohort entry) between 2010 and 2023 and active cancer diagnosed in the year before cohort entry. We calculated OAC initiation rates in the year following AF diagnosis among eligible patients (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2) using Poisson regression, overall and stratified by OAC type, age, sex, and cancer characteristics. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with OAC initiation.
RESULTS: Among 12,254 eligible patients, 6,940 (56.6%) initiated an OAC. OAC initiation rates rose from 89 per 100 person-years in 2010 to 385 per 100 person-years in 2023 (adjusted rate ratio: 4.32; 95% CI: 3.78-4.93), driven by increased direct oral anticoagulant prescribing. By 2023, apixaban and edoxaban predominated. OAC initiation did not differ by age and sex but was less common in patients with lung cancer (HR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.67-0.82), metastatic cancer (HR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.51-0.87), and dementia (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.64-0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: In the last decade, OAC initiation has substantially increased among eligible patients with AF and active cancer, driven by direct oral anticoagulant uptake. However, OAC initiation remained lower among patients with lung cancer, metastatic cancer, or specific comorbidities.

Title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD.
OBJECTIVES: This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety.
METHODS: Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response.
RESULTS: Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

Title: Inferior vena cava filter-related thrombosis: Mechanisms, clinical features, prevention, diagnosis, and risk-stratified management.
Abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters can provide mechanical protection from pulmonary embolism in selected patients who cannot receive anticoagulation, but filter-related thrombosis is an important complication. A uniform definition is lacking. Thrombus in the filter region may represent emboli captured by the filter, extension of pre-existing deep vein thrombosis, or local thrombus formation around the device. Filter-induced flow disturbance and vessel-wall responses may contribute to local thrombosis, although direct mechanistic evidence in humans remains limited. Reported occurrence varies substantially because study populations, imaging schedules, and outcome definitions differ. Clinically detected caval thrombosis or thrombotic occlusion is uncommon in large databases and prospective cohorts. Planned imaging before retrieval, however, often detects small intrafilter thrombi, most of which are asymptomatic. Accordingly, the clinical importance of an imaging-detected thrombus depends on whether it is accompanied by meaningful caval obstruction or symptoms. Prevention should continue throughout the filter life cycle. Filters should be used only for a time-limited, evidence-based indication. Anticoagulation should be resumed when a separate indication persists and bleeding risk permits, and retrieval should be assessed once filter-mediated pulmonary embolism protection is no longer required. Structured follow-up can help prevent loss to care. Management of established thrombosis should be guided by symptoms, impaired caval outflow, thrombus progression and chronicity, bleeding risk, and the need for filter retrieval. Anticoagulation remains foundational when indicated for active venous thromboembolism. Catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, or combined treatment may be considered for selected symptomatic, progressive, or obstructive cases, but most supporting studies are nonrandomized. Future studies require standardized minimum reporting and patient-centered outcomes.

Title: Apixaban for thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiology patients: Real-world data from a single institution.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombosis is a major complication in children with congenital or acquired heart disease, contributing to significant morbidity and mortality. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), including apixaban, are increasingly used for thromboprophylaxis in this population yet real-world paediatric data remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of apixaban as thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiac patients receiving commercially available adult tablet formulations outside a clinical trial setting.
PATIENTS/METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≤18 years with congenital or acquired heart disease who received apixaban at the University Children's Hospital Zurich from October 2022 to June 2025. Dosing was approximated to the SAXOPHONE trial using commercially available tablets that were split or crushed, without therapeutic laboratory monitoring. Outcomes included incident thrombosis (primary), major bleeding, clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB), and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were included with a median age of 4.6 years (IQR 3.3-9.8) and median apixaban exposure of 210 days (IQR 83-461), totalling 18,799 patient-days (51.5 patient-years). Single ventricle physiology was the most common underlying diagnosis (40/67, 60%) and Fontan circulation the most frequent indication (34/67, 51%). Two thrombotic events occurred (incidence rate 3.9 per 100 patient-years), both in the context of additional thrombotic risk factors. No major bleeding or CRNMB events were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban appeared safe and effective as thromboprophylaxis in this paediatric cardiology cohort, with no major or CRNMB and a low rate of thrombotic events. These findings add to the growing body of real-world evidence supporting DOAC use in children with cardiac disease.

Title: Incidence and prognostic impact of venous thromboembolism in a prospective single-center cohort of patients with cancer: The THEO study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication in oncology, representing the second leading cause of death among cancer patients after tumor progression. Isolated superficial venous thrombosis (iSVT), historically considered benign, is now emerging as a potential marker of thromboembolic risk but remains underexplored in cancer populations.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence of VTE and iSVT and evaluate the prognostic impact of VTE on all-cause mortality in a prospective cohort of patients with cancer.
METHODS: This prospective single-center cohort study included 700 cancer patients at Centre Antoine Lacassagne (Nice, France), followed for 12 months with scheduled visits at 6 and 12 months. VTE (deep vein thrombosis [DVT] or pulmonary embolism [PE]) and iSVT occurring during prospective follow-up were identified and confirmed by imaging. Incidence rates per 1000 person-years and cumulative incidence functions (accounting for death as a competing risk) were calculated. The association between VTE occurring during follow-up and all-cause mortality was assessed using a Cox proportional hazards model with VTE modeled as a time-dependent covariate. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03826043).
RESULTS: Of 700 enrolled patients, 516 were included in the analysis (median age: 65 years; 53.3% male). During 12 months of follow-up, 50 VTE events occurred (incidence: 147.5 per 1000 person-years), including DVT (110.2 per 1000) and PE (57.1 per 1000). The incidence of iSVT was 25.4 per 1000 person-years, substantially exceeding estimates reported for the general population. In multivariable time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and primary tumor site and stratified by baseline ECOG performance status, VTE was independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.36-3.15, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: VTE and iSVT incidences in this dedicated cancer center were markedly higher than those reported in general and cancer populations. These findings underscore the need for tailored thromboprophylaxis and closer surveillance in oncology settings.

Title: Ultrasound-assessed changes in abdominal fat and subcutaneous fat over the rectus femoris and gastrocnemius after a partial meal-replacement program in adults with obesity.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity is characterized not only by excess body weight, but also by abnormal regional adipose tissue distribution, which contributes to insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and metabolic syndrome (MS). Ultrasound may provide a practical method for monitoring changes in abdominal and peripheral adipose depots during nutritional treatment. The objective of the study was to evaluate changes in ultrasound-assessed abdominal and limb subcutaneous fat depots after a partial meal-replacement (pMR) program in adults with obesity METHODS: This prospective, single-arm, before-after interventional study included adults with obesity undergoing a structured pMR program. Anthropometric parameters, dietary intake, biochemical variables, and MS components were assessed at baseline and after intervention. Ultrasound was used to measure total subcutaneous fat thickness (TSFT), preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), and subcutaneous fat thickness over the rectus femoris and gastrocnemius regions (SFTRF and SFTG, respectively). Correlation and multiple regression analyses were performed to explore associations between ultrasound-derived changes and metabolic outcomes.
RESULTS: Seventy-five adults with obesity completed the study. After 12 wk, body weight decreased by 9.1 kg, with significant reductions in body mass index, waist circumference, and fat mass. Total energy intake decreased from 1663.9 ± 431.7 to 1156.5 ± 220.8 kcal/d. Fasting glucose, insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, and triglycerides improved significantly. Hypertriglyceridemia decreased from 37.6% to 20.0%, pathological high-density lipoprotein cholesterol from 45.5% to 16.9%, and MS from 52.5% to 21.5%. Ultrasound showed significant reductions in total TSFT, PFT, and SFTRF. Changes in TSFT were related to triglyceride changes, and PFT was related to body weight change. In multivariable analyses, TSFT change independently predicted changes in insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, and triglycerides, whereas PFT change independently predicted body weight change.
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-wk pMR program improved anthropometric and cardiometabolic risk markers, and produced measurable reductions in ultrasound-assessed abdominal and limb adipose depots. Ultrasound may be a useful complementary tool for monitoring adipose tissue during obesity treatment.

Title: Biological markers of grief in bereaved family members: A systematic review of cortisol, inflammatory and cardiovascular studies.
Abstract: Bereavement is among life's most stressful events, and a minority of mourners develop prolonged and disabling grief. Biological markers have been proposed as signals of this risk, but no systematic review has examined them across bereaved family members or asked how well bereaved parents (parents who have lost a child) are represented. We systematically reviewed observational studies linking a cortisol/HPA-axis, inflammatory/immune, or cardiovascular/autonomic biomarker to a validated measure of coping or grief in bereaved family members of any age or relationship to the deceased (PROSPERO CRD420261446539). Five databases were searched, with citation searching of a related review. Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria across the three domains. More severe grief was linked to blunted or flatter diurnal cortisol in three of five cortisol studies. Bereavement and greater grief were linked to raised inflammatory markers (IL-6, IL-1RA, and related cytokines), although five of seven inflammatory studies appear to come from one research programme, and one study found divergent Type I interferon gene transcription in complicated relative to uncomplicated grief. Cardiovascular and autonomic findings were mixed and depended on moderators such as coping style and childhood adversity. Some cortisol associations weakened with time since loss, so they may not be stable markers of grief severity. Only one participant across all 18 studies was an identifiable bereaved parent. Biological markers show domain-specific associations with grief, but the evidence is exploratory, and bereaved parents are largely absent from it. They should be a priority for future prospective work.

Title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnancies with cystic fibrosis after lung transplantation or during elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) therapy: a single-center descriptive cohort.
Journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in cystic fibrosis (CF) therapy, particularly CFTR modulators such as elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), are reshaping reproductive outcomes for women with advanced CF. Historically, lung transplantation (LT) was the only means to achieve sufficient respiratory stability for pregnancy. This study provides real-world clinical data describing pregnancies in women with CF after LT and during ETI therapy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of all pregnancies resulting in live births among women with CF followed at the Nantes University Hospital CF reference center between January 1, 2000 and August 31, 2024. Maternal characteristics, obstetric complications, and neonatal outcomes were collected for pregnancies after LT or under ETI treatment. Analyses were descriptive, with no statistical comparisons between groups due to small sample size and inherent clinical differences. Descriptive values from the 2021 French National Perinatal Survey are reported alongside our results for context only.
RESULTS: Among 95 pregnancies in 46 women, 56 resulted in live births, including 7 after LT and 10 during ETI therapy. In the LT cohort, pre-existing comorbidities were frequent: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) (100%), chronic hypertension (50%), and moderate renal impairment (83.3%). Preterm delivery occurred in 57.1% of pregnancies and intensive care unit admission in 42.9%. In ETI-exposed pregnancies, no gestational hypertension or preeclampsia was identified, and no woman required intensive care admission or delivered before 34 weeks. No congenital anomaly was observed in either group. Median gestational age at birth was 38 weeks + 3 days and median birth weight 3190 g in the ETI group, versus 35 weeks + 4 days and 1980 g in the LT group; these values are reported descriptively and were not compared statistically.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, ETI-exposed pregnancies were associated with reassuring maternal and neonatal outcomes, while pregnancies after LT were characterized by frequent transplant-related and vascular morbidity; the two groups were described separately and were not formally compared. These findings support the need for multidisciplinary follow-up and prospective registries to evaluate maternal and pediatric outcomes in the CFTR modulator era.

Title: Associations between vascular aging and 12 lipid composite indices: A large cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Vascular aging is an important antecedent of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet affordable, widely available biomarkers for its early detection remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive value of 12 lipid composite indices for vascular aging in a large cross-sectional sample of adults from Shenzhen, China.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of 5518 adults screened in Shenzhen (2021-2023), vascular aging (baPWV ≥ 1400 cm/s) was evaluated against 12 indices (TyG, TyG-BMI, RC, TG/HDL-C, AC, AIP, LCI, CRI-II, NHR, MHR, LHR, PHR) derived from routine laboratory and hematological data. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression across four sequentially adjusted models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) and two-piece linear models were used to evaluate dose-response relationships and thresholds. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis compared the discriminative performance of each index alone and in combination with age. Subgroup and interaction analyses examined effect modification by BMI, gender, age, hypertension, and diabetes.
RESULTS: All 12 indices remained independently associated with vascular aging after multivariable adjustment. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), each 1-unit increase in TyG was associated with an odds ratio (OR) of 2.21 (95% CI, 1.88-2.58; P < 0.001), and individuals in the highest TyG quartile (Q4) had an OR of 4.27 (95% CI, 3.16-5.77) compared with Q1; other indices showed similar effects. RCS analyses revealed significant nonlinear positive associations for several indices, with risk increasing below these thresholds. Individually, the indices had modest discrimination (AUC range, 0.562-0.726), but adding age improved all models; the TyG + age model achieved the best performance (AUC, 0.850; 95% CI, 0.838-0.862). BMI, gender, and diabetes status significantly modified several associations.
CONCLUSIONS: Among the 12 lipid composite indices evaluated, TyG-especially when combined with age-demonstrated the strongest predictive value for vascular aging in this large Chinese population, suggesting it may serve as a low-incremental-cost preliminary screening marker. However, prospective validation and intervention trials are needed to confirm the threshold and to determine whether lowering TyG attenuates vascular aging and subsequent CVD risk.

Title: Upadacitinib for the Management of Atopic Dermatitis in Patients Aged ≥60 Years: A Long-Term Multicenter Real-World Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) in the elderly is increasing worldwide and presents therapeutic challenges due to age-related comorbidities that often contraindicate systemic therapies. Although oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors show efficacy in moderate-to-severe AD, older adult patients are underrepresented in clinical trials, and regulators recommend caution in this population.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, observational study at 15 Italian university hospitals, including patients with moderate-to-severe AD aged ≥60 years treated with upadacitinib 15 or 30 mg once daily, to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of this selective JAK1 inhibitor at weeks 16, 32, 52, and 104.
RESULTS: Seventy-two patients were included (mean age 65.9 ± 6.4 years); 48/72 (66.7%) of patients showed a classical flexural phenotype; 34/72 (47.2%) presented with head-and-neck involvement. Upadacitinib led to marked and sustained improvement in both clinician-and-patient-reported outcomes, with mean Eczema Area and Severity Index decreasing from 23.9 ± 9.2 at baseline to 1.5 ± 3.0 at week 52 and 0.9 ± 2.5 at week 104. Mean itch-Numeric Rating Scales (NRS) decreased from 8.2 ± 2.0 at baseline to 1.0 ± 1.9 at week 52 and 1.0 ± 2.4 at week 104, with concomitant amelioration in sleep-NRS (6.5 ± 3.1 to 0.5 ± 1.6 and 0.3 ± 1.3) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (16.8 ± 6.9 to 1.6 ± 4.2 and 1.0 ± 3.2). Adverse events occurred in 37/72 (51,4%) patients and included dyslipidemia in 22/72 (30.6%) patients, creatine phosphokinase elevation in 15/72 (20.8%), and blood count abnormalities in 13/72 (18.1%); they were mostly mild and manageable. Overall, 16/72 patients (22.2%) discontinued treatment, including 11/72 (15.3%) due to AEs.
CONCLUSIONS: In our multicenter real-world cohort of patients aged ≥60 years, upadacitinib demonstrated rapid, sustained efficacy and an overall favorable safety profile through 104 weeks, supporting its long-term use in clinical practice with appropriate monitoring.

Title: Feasibility and acceptability of a remote blood pressure monitoring pharmacist-led telehealth programme in an emergency department transition care clinic: a pilot randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, fidelity and acceptability of a pharmacist-led remote blood pressure monitoring (RBPM) telehealth intervention in an emergency department postdischarge clinic (ED-PDC) and to assess preliminary effects on systolic blood pressure (SBP) over 12 weeks.
DESIGN: Pilot randomised controlled trial (RCT) with a parallel-group (1:1) design.
SETTING: Academically affiliated ED-PDC in Alabama, USA (July 2024–January 2025).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥18 years with SBP 130–160 mm Hg, English-speaking, smartphone owners and without an established primary care provider. The cohort was predominantly Black (71%), 38% female, with a mean age of 48.4±12.8 years. 24 were randomised (12 per arm).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomised to RBPM (Withings BPM Connect Pro) with weekly pharmacist-led telehealth visits or to usual ED-PDC care. Both arms received hypertension education and completed a 12-week in-person follow-up.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were recruitment, 12-week retention and intervention fidelity. Secondary outcomes included acceptability (acceptability of intervention measure (AIM), intervention appropriateness measure (IAM) and feasibility of intervention measure (FIM)). The exploratory clinical outcome was the change in SBP at 12 weeks.
RESULTS: Of the 27 people screened, 24 were randomised, and 16 (67%) completed the 12-week in-person visit (n=8 in each arm). RBPM participants completed a mean of 10.6±3.3 of 12 planned pharmacist visits. Acceptability was high (AIM 4.69±0.88; IAM 4.75±0.71; FIM 4.78±0.41). Mean SBP decreased from 153.5±15.8 to 128.9±21.0 mm Hg in the RBPM arm (p=0.024) and from 158.1±21.9 to 133.0±21.6 mm Hg in the usual care arm (p=0.003); the between-group difference was 0.5 mm Hg (95% CI −25.7 to 26.7). At 12 weeks, 75% (6/8) of RBPM participants achieved SBP ≤130 mm Hg versus 50% (4/8) in usual care.
CONCLUSIONS: A pharmacist-led RBPM telehealth programme integrated into an ED-PDC is feasible, highly acceptable and associated with meaningful SBP reductions and a higher rate of BP control in the RBPM arm. These promising findings support a fully powered multisite RCT.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06247111.

Title: Structured medication reviews for adults with multimorbidity and polypharmacy in primary care: a systematic review.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: Structured medication reviews (SMRs) in primary care offer a patient-centred approach to optimising medicines for adults with multimorbidity and polypharmacy, but their effect on endpoint outcomes is not yet well-established. This review summarises their impact on these outcomes and on medicines optimisation, while also highlighting common delivery methods (in-person or remote).
DESIGN: Systematic review using narrative synthesis.
DATA SOURCES: Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, Web of Science and CINAHL via OVID were searched for studies published between January 1997 and August 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Studies of adults with multimorbidity and polypharmacy receiving an SMR in primary care, compared with usual care. Randomised controlled trials, non-randomised controlled trials, cohort and cross-sectional designs were eligible.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened studies; one reviewer extracted data and a second verified them. Study quality was assessed using the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute quality assessment tools. Findings were synthesised narratively.
RESULTS: Nine studies (8213 participants) assessed SMRs in relation to physical health (n=5), functional status (n=5), safety (n=2), healthcare utilisation (n=7), cost-effectiveness (n=3) and person-centred outcomes (n=3). Most reported no changes in physical health and falls (n=5), with no improvement in functional status (n=5). Safety outcomes showed no differences in survival or mortality (n=2). Healthcare use was largely unchanged (n=7), with only one study reporting fewer medication-related admissions. Person-centred outcomes remained unchanged (n=2). Cost outcomes were favourable, with savings (n=3) and quality-adjusted life year gains (n=2). SMRs were associated with prescription changes (n=4), reduced inappropriate prescribing (n=3) and improved adherence (n=2), although several between-group comparisons showed no significant differences. SMRs were usually delivered by general practitioners, pharmacists or multidisciplinary teams to older adults, although the mode of delivery (in-person or remote) was often unclear.
CONCLUSIONS: SMRs showed little effect on endpoint outcomes, but most studies focused on prescribing rather than clinical effects, limiting this conclusion. Realising their potential requires supportive policy and collaborative practice. Unclear delivery methods hinder evaluation, and as primary care adopts digital solutions, further research on remote SMRs is needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: PROSPERO CRD42023454965.

Title: Azygos Venous Pressure and Respiratory Modulation of CSF-Venous Pressure Gradients in SIH and IIH patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The azygos system is a major drainage pathway of the thoracic spinal venous network and may participate in the regulation of spinal CSF resorption. CSF-pressure disorders such as spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) related to a CSF-venous fistula (CSFVF) and idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) could therefore be influenced by the hemodynamics and the pressure of this system. However, azygos pressure and its respiratory modulation remain poorly characterized.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 54 consecutive patients who underwent combined venous and CSF pressure measurements between September 2025 and February 2026. Forty-five patients were investigated for SIH/CSFVF and 9 for IIH. Pressures were recorded in the azygos system, intracranial venous sinuses, right atrium (CVP), and lumbar CSF compartment. Dynamic measurements were obtained during resisted inspiration, breath holding, and Valsalva. Values are reported as mean ± SD or median [IQR], as appropriate. Paired respiratory changes were assessed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: Overall, median azygos pressure was 8.0 [6.0-9.8] mm Hg and was modestly but significantly higher than CVP: 6.5 [4.0-8.0] mm Hg; median paired difference, +2.0 [1.0-3.0] mm Hg; p < .001. Azygos pressure did not differ significantly between SIH/CSFVF and IIH groups: 8.0 [6.0-9.0] versus 9.0 [8.0-10.0] mm Hg; p = .34. Level-by-level measurements in 25 patients showed only limited cranial pressure decline, with median pressure of 8.0 [6.0-9.0] mm Hg in the caudal L2-T10 segment and 7.0 [5.0-8.0] mm Hg in the cranial T9-T5 segment; p = .007. Resisted inspiration produced the largest CSF-azygos gradient, increasing from 0.0 [-3.0 to 5.0] to 12.0 [11.0-15.0] mm Hg, primarily because azygos pressure decreased from 7.0 to -6.0 mm Hg while CSF pressure remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: In the investigated population, median azygos pressure was 8mmHg, close to CVP, and stable along the spinal axis. Resisted inspiration markedly increased the CSF-azygos gradient by lowering azygos pressure, providing a hemodynamic explanation for improved CSF-venous fistula conspicuity during resisted-inspiration myelography.

Title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth.
RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

Title: Bladder Neck Versus Midurethral Placement of Retropubic Autologous Fascial Slings: A Systematic Review.
Journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare objective and subjective cure/improvement rates and surgical outcomes of female patients with stress or mixed urinary incontinence undergoing autologous retropubic pubovaginal slings between traditional bladder neck sling placement and midurethral sling placement.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of Medline, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted using standardized MeSH terms from conception to March 2025 (PROSPERO-registered). Studies underwent double screening, and a third reviewer resolved any discrepancies.
STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating outcomes of retropubic autologous slings for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) or mixed urinary incontinence (MUI). Studies published in English or French were eligible for inclusion. We included slings performed for recurrent SUI or MUI, as well as those placed concomitantly with prolapse surgery, providing a minimum postoperative follow-up of six weeks was reported. We excluded systematic reviews, meta-analyses, review articles, case reports, studies lacking details on surgical approach or sling material, and studies evaluating non-autologous slings.
STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: We evaluated study quality using RoB, the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials, and the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (NIH) Quality Assessment Tool for Observational Cohort and Cross-Sectional Studies. We present odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals to estimate the effect of sling placement location on each outcome through random-effect logistic regression.
RESULTS: We screened 5578 abstracts, assessed 233 full texts for eligibility, and retained 61 studies. 13 of these were randomized controlled trials and 48 were observational studies. Objective (74.0% vs. 81.1%, OR 1.10 [0.37-3.28]) and subjective cure (70.8% vs. 58.6 %, OR 0.46 [0.19-1.10]) were not statistically significantly different between bladder neck vs. midurethral placement of retropubic autologous fascial sling at a median of 2.4 years [0.3-6.8] postoperatively. Objective improvement (90.5% vs.84.5%, OR 0.41 [0.10-1.67]) and subjective improvement (85.9% vs. 85.1%, OR 0.77 [0.31-1.92]) rates were also similar between the groups. Most adverse events were similar between groups except midurethral placement was associated with a lower risk of de novo urgency (15.0% vs 8.3%, OR 0.50 [0.26-0.96]). Study quality assessment using the RoB tool for RCT and the NIH Quality Assessment of Observational Control and Cross-Sectional studies overall revealed a moderate to high risk of bias among included studies.
CONCLUSION: Bladder neck and midurethral placements of autologous slings have similar surgical success and adverse effects rates, with the exception of de novo urgency which favours midurethral sling placement. A randomized controlled trial is required to confirm these findings.

Title: Clinical Implementation of Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve for Revascularization Guidance: Initial Multicenter United States Experience.
Abstract: Real-world data on the adoption and clinical performance of angiography-derived physiology in the United States (U.S.) remain limited. We evaluated the implementation of FFRangio (CathWorks, Tel Aviv, Israel) and associated clinical outcomes across a multicenter U.S. healthcare system. We performed a multicenter observational cohort study across 4 centers involving consecutive adult patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography in whom FFRangio was performed in at least 1 coronary vessel based on clinical indication. The primary endpoint was target-vessel failure (TVF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction and target vessel revascularization during follow-up, stratified by FFRangio values >0.80 versus ≤0.80. A total of 675 vessels in 469 patients were assessed by FFRangio; 240 (36%) had values ≤0.80 and 435 (64%) >0.80. Among lesions with FFRangio ≤0.80, 182 (76%) underwent PCI, 27 (11%) CABG, and 32 (13%) were managed medically. Among lesions with FFRangio >0.80, revascularization was deferred in 406 (92%), with 22 (5%) undergoing PCI and 12 (3%) CABG. The LAD was the most frequently treated vessel (51%). At a median follow-up of 10.2 months, the incidence rate of TVF was 1.55% per 100 lesion-years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-3.36) in the FFRangio >0.80 group versus 6.30 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI, 3.25-11.0) in the FFRangio ≤0.80 group (hazard ratio [HR] 4.61, 95% CI: 1.61-13.2; p=0.002). Among deferred lesions with FFRangio >0.80, TVF rate was 1.73 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI: 0.64-3.77). In conclusion, FFRangio supported safe deferral of revascularization and risk-stratification, with low event rates among lesions with values >0.80.

Title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: a Report from the MARS Registry.
Abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Prior bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11.0%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs. 10.1%, p=0.17). Major bleeding (BARC ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25.0% vs. 12.5%, p=0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted OR 2.18, 95% CI 0.43-8.71, p=0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after cardiac surgery and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

Title: Efficacy of blood flow restriction combined with low-intensity aerobic training in patients with COPD: Study protocol for the BREATH randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airflow limitation, which reduces exercise capacity. Although current guidelines recommend moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise to achieve optimal physiological adaptations, many patients cannot sustain the required intensity, limiting overall therapeutic benefit. This study protocol aims to evaluate the effects of combining blood flow restriction (BFR) with aerobic training on exercise capacity, cardiopulmonary function, and health-related quality of life in patients with COPD, compared with conventional aerobic training or usual care.
METHODS: We will conduct a single-center, prospective, parallel-group randomized controlled trial. 45 clinically stable patients with COPD (GOLD stages II-IV) will be recruited. Eligible participants must have had no acute exacerbations in the past two months and be able to participate in the exercise training program. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: usual care, conventional aerobic training (60-80% VO₂ peak), or BFR-enhanced aerobic training (40-50% VO₂ peak, with 40-80% arterial occlusion pressure). All exercise sessions will be supervised, three times per week for eight weeks. The primary outcome is exercise capacity. Secondary outcomes include pulmonary function tests, respiratory muscle strength, diaphragmatic ultrasound, heart rate variability, and health-related quality-of-life questionnaires.
PLANNED OUTCOMES: BFR-enhanced aerobic training may be a safe and effective rehabilitation option for COPD patients who cannot tolerate high-intensity exercise. The BREATH trial is expected to provide essential evidence for clinical care by integrating BFR training into pulmonary rehabilitation. This approach could inform future management strategies for exercise intolerance among patients with COPD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study has been approved by the Institutional Review Board (approval number: B-ER-113-298) and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (registration number: NCT06756646).

Title: Depressive Symptoms and Incident Peripheral Arterial Disease Among Adults With CKD: Findings From the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Depression is associated with cardiovascular disease among adults with CKD, but its relationship with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) has not been thoroughly examined despite both conditions being common in this population. We evaluated the risk for incident PAD and death associated with elevated depressive symptoms among adults with CKD.
STUDY DESIGN: Observational prospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Adults with mild to moderate CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study (CRIC) Study.
EXPOSURES: Elevated depressive symptoms as defined by a Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score ≥ 11.
OUTCOMES: Incident PAD, defined as an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) < 0.9 or confirmed clinical PAD event (amputation or angioplasty). Composite outcome of incident PAD or death.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: The association between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and incident PAD, as well as a composite of incident PAD or death, was examined with Cox proportional hazard models. Mediation analysis explored the pathways between elevated depressive symptoms and these outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 2,757 individuals, 25% had elevated depressive symptoms (BDI ≥11) at baseline. During a median follow-up of 10 years, 24% of participants developed incident PAD. The rate of incident PAD was higher in those with elevated depressive symptoms (3.6 events per 100 person-years) compared with those without (2.2 events per 100 person-years). After accounting for other factors, baseline elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a higher risk of incident PAD (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.02-1.47). Smoking and physical inactivity mediated 20% and 10%, respectively, of this association. Similar associations were found between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and a composite of incident PAD or death. Findings were not different when elevated depressive symptoms were defined by BDI >14 and BDI ≥16.
LIMITATIONS: Residual bias and confounding. Absence of depression diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD in adults with CKD, which is partly mediated by smoking and physical inactivity.
INDEX WORDS: Renal failure, depression, peripheral vascular disease, mortality, health behaviors.

Title: Outcomes Following Kidney Failure From IgA Nephropathy Compared to Diabetic Kidney Disease and Other Glomerular Diseases.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a major cause of kidney disease worldwide, yet contemporary comparative outcome data following kidney failure are limited. We compared trends in access to kidney transplantation and mortality among patients with kidney failure due to IgAN, to those with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) or other glomerular diseases (GD).
STUDY DESIGN: Longitudinal cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients with kidney failure initiating maintenance dialysis (1965-2023) due to IgAN, DKD, or other GD in Australia.
EXPOSURE: Kidney failure etiology.
OUTCOMES: All-cause death, death from cardiovascular disease and cancer, and entry onto the deceased donor kidney transplant waitlist.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Age-standardized incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates and temporal trends assessed using log-linear regression-derived estimated annual percentage change (EAPC). Associations between kidney failure etiology and outcomes estimated using inverse probability treatment-weight (IPTW)- adjusted Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: 44,659 patients (4,925 with IgAN; 15,079 with other GD; 24,655 with DKD) were studied with a median follow-up of 53 months (IQR 23.3-109.8). The age-standardized incidence of IgAN remained stable over the past two decades (EAPC -0.01%, 95% CI - 0.80 to 0.78). Compared with other GD, patients with IgAN experienced lower all-cause (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.65-0.73; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.60-0.74; p < 0.001) mortality, and increased rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.39-1.73; p < 0.001). Compared with IgAN, patients with DKD had higher all-cause (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.53-1.64, p<0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.71-1.91, p<0.001), lower cancer-related mortality (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95, p=0.009), and lower rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.60-0.69, p<0.001).
LIMITATIONS: Residual confounding, diagnostic misclassification due to variation in biopsy practices.
CONCLUSION: Differences in survival and placement onto the kidney transplant waitlist exist across patients with different etiologies of kidney failure. Individuals with IgAN have longer survival and enter the transplant waitlist more often than those with DKD or other GD.

Title: Design and rationale of a multicenter randomized trial assessing strategies for catheter ablation of persistent atrial fibrillation- The STAR AF 3 trial.
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of catheter ablation procedures for the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the success rates of PVI are limited for patients with persistent AF. Yet, the optimal ablation strategy beyond PVI alone in patients with persistent AF remains to be established.
STUDY DESIGN AND OBJECTIVES: The STAR AF 3 trial is an international multicenter prospective, single-blind, blinded endpoint, clinical trial that includes patients with persistent AF of more than 3 months duration referred for a first catheter ablation procedure. Enrollment will occur at 33 centers in Europe, Canada, Australia, USA and Japan. The aim of this study is to compare the strategy of PVI alone with two strategies that add ablation to PVI: PVI+drivers ablation and PVI+posterior wall isolation. Patients will be equally randomized into one of these three ablation strategies. Patients will be followed up for 18 months. The primary endpoint will be the time to first recurrence of documented atrial tachyarrhythmia (atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia) between 91 days and 18 months after a single ablation procedure. An atrial tachyarrhythmia will qualify as a recurrence if it lasts 30 s or longer and is documented by 12-lead electrocardiogram, electrocardiographic rhythm strips, or transtelephonic monitor recordings. Although a post-ablation blanking period of 3 months will be observed, a repeat left atrial ablation procedure done at any time will also qualify as a primary endpoint event. Enrollment is completed and a total of 617 patients have been recruited into the trial. The trial is registered at the Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04428944) CONCLUSIONS: The STAR AF 3 trial is a large multicenter randomized trial assessing the optimal ablation strategy for patients with persistent AF.

Title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.
OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes.
METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

Title: CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ.
METHODS: We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL.
CONCLUSION: Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

Title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms.
METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device.
RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

Title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.
METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.
RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

Title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.
RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

Title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.
OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.
METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.
RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).
CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

Title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.
METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.
RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.
CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

Title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%.
RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

Title: Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling.
METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122).
RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004).
CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

Title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.
METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.
RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.
CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

Title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.
OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.
METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.
RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm.
