The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).
CONCLUSION: The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

Title: Evidence Suggests Linoleic Acid Exerts Health Benefits Beyond Cardiovascular Disease: A Brief Review of Clinical and Observational Studies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Questions challenging the healthfulness of diets high in linoleic acid (LA) and seed oils, which are major sources of this essential fatty acid, have recently arisen. These questions are especially relevant to adherents of plant-based diets as their LA intake is higher than the general population. Some maintain that LA increases inflammation and oxidative stress and for these reasons, despite its ability to lower circulating LDL-cholesterol levels when replacing saturated fat, does not lower cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Because most of the discussion about LA has focused on CVD, the primary focus of this manuscript is to examine the effects of LA on health outcomes aside from CVD.
RECENT FINDINGS: Interventional and observational studies indicate increasing LA intake lowers risk of CVD. Beyond CVD, possible benefits include preventing hepatic fat accumulation, increasing muscle mass, decreasing risk of skin cancer, decreasing epigenetic aging, increasing the healthspan, and improving cognitive function and decreasing risk of developing neurocognitive disorders. Support for these proposed benefits comes from observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), although more from the former. The observational evidence is especially robust in the case of cognitive function and neurological disorders, as the results of all but one of the eight recently published cohort studies show LA exposure, as assessed by dietary intake or circulating levels, is supportive of benefit, although much of the data come from analyses of one cohort. While it is premature to conclude that LA intake exerts benefits beyond CVD, evidence is sufficient to warrant that this possibility should be included in discussions about the role of LA and seed oils in the diet. Given the large contribution LA makes to energy intake, particularly among consumers of plant-based diets, research aimed at more definitively determining the range of possible benefits, especially related to cognitive function, is warranted.

Title: Pneumothorax rates following cardiac surgery with versus without continuous serratus anterior plane catheters: a secondary analysis of trial data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort.
Journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate to severe pain is common after cardiac surgery, especially in the first two postoperative days. Inadequate pain control may prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay, may increase cost, and contributes to chronic pain. Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols prioritize multimodal analgesia, including regional anesthesia techniques. In a recent randomized trial with continuous serratus anterior plane (SAP) catheters, we found unexpectedly high pneumothorax rates. To address this, we aimed to design a propensity-score-matched comparison using patients from the same institution to control for institutional practice patterns, surgical techniques, and patient demographics that could confound comparisons with published literature rates from other centres.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of RCT data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort. We compared the pneumothorax rates in patients receiving continuous SAP catheters in our previous Cardiac-Serratus Anterior Plane (Cardiac-SAP) trial with those in a retrospective institutional database cohort of patients receiving standard care undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy. The two groups were propensity score matched in a 1:20 ratio based on age, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and pre-existing respiratory disease. We analyzed univariate comparisons using Fisher's exact test or the percentile bootstrapping method.
RESULTS: We matched 50 patients from the Cardiac-SAP trial to 989 retrospective cohort patients. After matching, the SAP catheter group was associated with a significantly higher risk of pneumothorax (12% vs 3%; odds ratio, 5.3; 95% confidence interval, 2.1 to 13.6; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences for other outcomes, including ICU readmissions, length of ventilation, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Patients who developed a pneumothorax had longer ventilation time and longer hospital stays.
CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggest that SAP catheter use as a part of a randomized trial for cardiac surgery was associated with a higher rate of pneumothorax in trial participants than in a historic cohort of a similar population, though causality is unclear. Differences in monitoring within the trial and the inherent risks in this population may have contributed.

Title: Molecular-genetic mechanisms of cerebral arteriovenous malformations: A systematic review of germline, somatic and experimental evidence.
Abstract: Cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are high-flow vascular anomalies that carry a considerable burden of haemorrhagic morbidity. Work over the past decade has shown that both inherited syndromes and apparently sporadic lesions can be traced to alterations in a handful of signalling pathways, but the relevant evidence sits awkwardly between human genetic studies, animal models, and molecular profiling experiments. To bring together the current evidence on the molecular and genetic underpinnings of cerebral AVM formation, clinical course, and candidate therapeutic targets. We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from inception to 1 January 2026. Records were screened, and full texts assessed, by two reviewers working independently. Studies were eligible if they reported genetic, molecular, or epigenetic data on cerebral AVMs. Because of substantial heterogeneity in designs and outcomes, evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Of 343 records, 44 primary studies (28 clinico-genetic and 16 experimental) together with 20 reviews and meta-analyses met inclusion. Inherited AVM syndromes largely reflected germline variants in the TGF-β/BMP network (ENG, ACVRL1, SMAD4, GDF2/BMP9) or in arteriovenous-specification regulators (RASA1, EPHB4); penetrance was incomplete and there was support for local modifying "second-hit" events. Resected sporadic cerebral AVMs often carried somatic activating mutations in the RAS/MAPK cascade-mostly KRAS, less often BRAF-at low variant allele fractions that demanded high-sensitivity assays. Endothelial-specific activation of KRAS or BRAF reproduced AVM-like phenotypes in vivo and showed MEK-ERK dependence. Susceptibility variants (notably at 9p21/ANRIL), inflammatory mediators, extracellular-matrix remodelling, and epigenetic changes appear to fine-tune lesion behaviour and haemorrhagic risk. Syndromic predisposition and clonal somatic events in endothelium converge on a small set of developmental signalling axes that govern angiogenesis and vessel-wall maturation. Diagnostics anchored in this biology, together with pathway-targeted therapy, now need prospective evaluation, paired with standardised approaches for detecting low-level mosaicism.

Title: Self-Prognostic Electronic Skin for Reliability-Aware Wearable Sensing.
Abstract: Flexible wearable sensors are increasingly used for long-duration monitoring of body-state information, but they can degrade silently during operation while continuing to output physiologically plausible signals, making it difficult to determine whether an incoming measurement remains trustworthy. Here, we report a self-prognostic electronic skin platform that couples multimodal body-state sensing with autonomous sensor-health assessment. The device monolithically co-integrates piezoelectric and triboelectric transduction by origami folding into an ultrathin, six-channel wrist-mounted array (∼0.1 mm, <1 g), so that a single mechanoelectrical stream simultaneously encodes cardiovascular pulsation, wrist activity, and the device's own degradation state. A two-stage self-diagnostic framework uses an autoencoder-CUSUM pipeline to establish device-specific failure labels from degradation trajectories, followed by an LSTM-Transformer model for remaining useful lifetime prediction. Across a twenty-device cohort with a nearly sevenfold variation in lifetime, the model predicts remaining useful lifetime across the cohort's degradation trajectories with R2 = 0.95 and captures uncertainty that increases as degradation becomes more severe. In single-participant daily-use proof-of-concept testing, the system estimates physiological parameters and sensor remaining lifetime from the same stream. The predicted lifetime of a newly fabricated device remained near 100% during a representative 1.5 h segment and declined modestly to 97.2% over approximately 12 h of wear distributed across multiple days; this single-device demonstration illustrates the operation of the diagnostic channel during daily use rather than validated cross-device predictive accuracy. These results establish reliability-aware wearable sensing, in which each body-state measurement is interpreted together with the operational health of the sensor itself, with potential value for long-duration applications such as health monitoring and embodied intelligence.

Title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
Journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).
CONCLUSIONS: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

Title: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy obstruction after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy (JJ) obstruction is a rare early complication after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB). Although early small bowel obstruction after RYGB is well described, obstruction caused by hemobezoar formation remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261320591). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 2026. Eligible studies reported adults undergoing primary minimally invasive RYGB with early hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction. Data were extracted on study characteristics, presentation, diagnostic modality, operative strategy, gastric decompression, and outcomes. Given its rarity and lack of comparative cohorts, findings were summarized descriptively.
RESULTS: Six studies met inclusion criteria, including 7669 minimally invasive RYGB procedures and 29 hemobezoar-related JJ obstructions. The crude incidence was 0.38%, with per-study incidence ranging from 0.09% to 1.94%. Presentation was consistently early, most commonly within 72 postoperative hours, frequently included tachycardia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hematocrit decline, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Computed tomography with intravenous contrast was the predominant diagnostic modality, demonstrating dilation of the excluded stomach and proximal limbs with hyperdense intraluminal content at the JJ. Operative management evolved from laparotomy with JJ revision in earlier reports to laparoscopic clot evacuation with selective revision when anastomotic compromise, leak, ischemia, or ongoing bleeding was identified. Gastric remnant decompression was emphasized to reduce closed-loop distension and intraperitoneal contamination. No deaths were reported among 29 cases, although morbidity included abscess formation, anastomotic or staple-line complications, pancreatitis, respiratory complications, readmission, and repeat reoperation.
CONCLUSION: Hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction after minimally invasive RYGB is uncommon but important. It typically presents within the first postoperative days with obstructive symptoms and evidence of intraluminal bleeding. Across retrospective studies, favorable outcomes were reported following prompt CT diagnosis, early operative exploration, remnant decompression, and minimally invasive clot evacuation with selective anastomotic revision. Prospective validation of this management approach is needed.

Title: Aveir VR for Atrial Leadless Pacing in Young Patients.
Abstract: Atrial Leadless pacemaker implantspresent a new treatment for sinus node dysfunction in complex cardiac anatomies. The Aveir-VR single chamber pacemaker can be placed in the atrium to control atrial flutter, or in the ventricle to control bradycardia. In this case report, we present four cases of the implantation of the Aveir VR in the atrium of male pediatric patients to treat sinus node dysfunction. Retrospective review of patients with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and atrially placed Aveir-VRs was performed at UC Davis between April 2024 and April 2026. Femoral access was the route of implantation for all 5 patients. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was used in all cases. The patients' ages ranged between 14-17-years and follow-up appointments were held between 1-23-months. Immediately post-procedure, impedances were 380-1460 Ohms, thresholds at 0.4 ms were 2.25-3.5 V, and P-waves were between 1.7-3 mV. Follow-up impedance was between 390-720 Ohms for the patients, thresholds were 0.5-1.25 V at 0.2-0.4 ms, P-waves were between 4.5-9.1 mV, and pacing percentages were between 12-69%. This case series demonstrates the successful implant of Aveir VR leadless pacemaker in five young patients for sinus node dysfunction.

Title: Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Children and Adolescents with Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Study.
Abstract: Celiac disease (CD) is recognized as a systemic disorder extending beyond the gastrointestinal tract, with evidence of subclinical cardiovascular involvement emerging even in childhood. We aimed to evaluate myocardial function in children with CD compared to healthy controls, and to investigate whether echocardiographic parameters differ according to gluten-free diet adherence. This cross-sectional case-control study included 142 children with CD and 120 healthy controls. Conventional and advanced echocardiography were performed in all participants. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI) z-score was used for all echocardiographic outcomes. Patients were stratified by anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (anti-tTG IgA) into tTG-negative (n = 55), borderline (n = 13), and positive (n = 74) subgroups. Ejection Fraction (EF) and Fractional Shortening (FS) were modestly but significantly reduced in CD patients, while left ventricular (LV) dimensions and LV mass were not significantly different. All Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) parameters were significantly impaired in CD patients, including elevated Myocardial Performance Index (MPI) and E/e' ratios at both septal and lateral mitral annulus (p < 0.001). Myocardial function was impaired across all serological subgroups compared to controls, with no significant differences among celiac subgroups in multivariable analysis. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability of MPI between celiac patients and healthy controls, after adjustment for age, sex and z-score BMI. Children with CD demonstrate significant subclinical myocardial dysfunction, detectable by TDI, independently of serological disease activity. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to establish the long-term cardiovascular implications and the role of routine cardiac monitoring in this population.

Title: Integrating Scalability and Equity into Hypertension Remote Patient Monitoring Program Design.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) for hypertension combines home blood pressure (BP) monitoring with electronic transmission of BP readings and clinical support. RPM has the potential to improve BP control and reduce hypertension disparities, but because it depends on devices, connectivity, digital literacy, and sustained engagement, it may also worsen inequities if not intentionally designed. This review examines barriers to equitable RPM implementation and strategies to address them.
RECENT FINDINGS: RPM can improve hypertension control and extend care beyond traditional clinical settings, but its effect on health equity depends on program design. Equity should be treated as a core design principle. Future research should evaluate differential reach, engagement, effectiveness, and sustainability across populations and identify payment models that support equitable implementation at scale. Barriers to equitable RPM implementation occur at patient, clinician, health system, and policy levels. Key challenges include limited access to technology, language barriers, out-of-pocket costs, inadequate cuff sizing, unmet social needs, clinician workload, referral bias, infrastructure limitations, reimbursement variability, and the digital divide. Emerging evidence suggests that equity-focused strategies can improve reach and engagement, including provision of cellular-enabled devices, reduced patient costs, culturally and linguistically tailored support, team-based care, registry-based outreach, and routine monitoring of enrollment and outcomes across demographic groups. High-resource, low-resource, and hybrid RPM models each offer distinct advantages and tradeoffs in balancing scalability, sustainability, and equity.

Title: Early alterations in central corneal epithelial thickness after ocular chemical burns.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate central corneal epithelial thickness (CCET) during the early healing phase after ocular chemical burns using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) and to assess its relationship with clinical parameters.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 35 patients with chemical ocular burns treated between 2020 and 2024. CCET and central corneal stromal thickness were measured by AS-OCT one month after injury. Clinical data included burn severity according to the Dua classification, initial and final visual acuity (VA), epithelialization time, and treatment modality (medical therapy, autologous serum drops, or amniotic membrane transplantation [AMT]). Results were compared with healthy control group. Correlation and subgroup analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The mean age of patients was 40.2 ± 19.6 years, and 74.3% were male. Alkaline agents caused 88.6% of injuries. The mean epithelialization time was 14.0 ± 9.7 days, and mean final VA improved to 0.71 ± 0.32. Mean CCET at one month was 50.14 ± 5.33 µm, significantly thinner than in controls (59.79 ± 3.59 µm; p < 0.001). Central stromal thickness did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.181). CCET showed no significant correlation with burn grade, initial VA, or epithelialization time (all p > 0.05). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, no significant difference in CCET was observed between patients receiving standard medical therapy alone and those requiring adjunctive treatment (p = 0.510); however, treatment allocation was non-randomized and reflected disease severity.
CONCLUSIONS: CCET is significantly reduced during early recovery after chemical burns despite apparent clinical healing. AS-OCT-based CCET measurement may provide an objective structural assessment of early epithelial changes during ocular surface healing.
KEY MESSAGES: What is known: 1) Chemical ocular burns cause severe disruption of the corneal epithelium and limbal stem cell function, and clinical epithelialization can not always reflect complete microstructural recovery. 2) Anterior segment OCT allows non-invasive assessment of corneal epithelial thickness, which has been shown to be reduced in several ocular surface disorders.
WHAT IS NEW: 1) Although epithelial healing appears clinically complete in the early period after ocular chemical burns, AS-OCT demonstrated significant central corneal epithelial thinning despite a clinically stable ocular surface.

Title: Multidisciplinary perioperative management of robot-assisted renal surgery: practical considerations for partial nephrectomy and nephroureterectomy.
Abstract: Robot-assisted surgery is established across urology, but its safety depends on more than console performance. Restricted access to the patient, limited tactile feedback, external arm collisions, phase transitions, and communication failures create risks that must be managed collectively. This narrative review summarizes multidisciplinary perioperative management for robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) and robot-assisted nephroureterectomy (RANU) and introduces a proposed practice-based framework. The framework was developed by integrating multidisciplinary educational sessions and case-based discussions with a narrative synthesis of relevant literature. For RAPN, shared understanding of tumor localization, vascular-control and ischemia strategies when used, tumor excision, reconstruction when required, and hemostasis enables anticipatory preparation. For RANU, teams should anticipate transitions among renal, ureteral, and bladder-cuff phases, including possible redocking and changes in positioning or instruments. Across both procedures, recurring multidisciplinary tasks were organized into five functions: PLAN, POSITION, PREPARE, PERFORM, and PASS ON. These functions are intended to recur iteratively at critical transitions and to support shared situational awareness, closed-loop communication, emergency readiness, and structured postoperative handover. The proposed framework has not yet been validated; prospective studies should evaluate process measures, staff-reported outcomes, and patient outcomes.

Title: Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization Identifies Therapeutic Targets for Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke carries substantial residual risk despite acute revascularization and secondary prevention, and small-vessel disease (SVD) lacks specific preventive therapy. Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) identifies circulating proteins whose lifelong modulation alters stroke risk.
METHODS: We screened 589 conditionally independent cis-pQTLs from the INTERVAL study against four GIGASTROKE outcomes: any ischemic stroke (AIS), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), cardioembolic stroke (CES), and SVD. Wald ratio estimates were corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) within each outcome, with a pooled cross-outcome correction as a sensitivity analysis. FDR-significant associations underwent colocalization (approximate Bayes factor; H4 > 0.80), replication in the independent deCODE pQTL cohort, cell-type expression validation in a human brain vascular single-nucleus atlas (65,479 nuclei), and phenome-wide safety screening.
RESULTS: Ten protein-outcome associations reached FDR < 0.05; nine replicated in deCODE and eight colocalized at H4 > 0.80, with two further pairs (ABO-LAA, cyclin H-CES) in the suggestive range (H4 0.70-0.80). For SVD, higher SPATA20 raised risk (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.24-1.73, p = 5.3 × 10⁻⁶), and higher KDELC2 lowered risk (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.91, p = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴). A protective cyclin H signal for CES passed outcome-wise FDR (q = 0.046) but not the pooled correction (q = 0.059) and is reported as preliminary. ABO, MMP-12, and SWAP70 confirmed earlier reports; SCARA5 failed colocalization and replication and was excluded. Colocalization confirmed the lead liabilities for MMP-12 (atopic dermatitis, two cohorts) and SWAP70 (rheumatoid arthritis) as on-target effects; two further liability associations (allergic asthma, ER-negative breast cancer) did not meet the colocalization threshold and remain hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: Proteome-wide MR prioritizes two SVD-associated proteins: SPATA20 (risk-raising; now independently confirmed across screens) and KDELC2 (protective; newly reported). Both require replication on orthogonal proteomic platforms and functional validation before therapeutic development.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Argatroban as an Adjunct to Antiplatelet Therapy in Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a life-threatening condition. Argatroban can limit thrombus progression and improve AIS's functional outcomes. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of argatroban in combination with antiplatelet therapy compared to control.
METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched. Primary outcomes were Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2 and composite hemorrhage; secondary outcomes included mRS (0-1), early neurological deterioration (END), change in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, mortality, intracranial and organ hemorrhage. A random-effects model was used, with risk ratios (RRs) reported for binary outcomes, while mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes at 95% confidence intervals (CI) and a p-value of 0.05.
RESULTS: 17 studies were included with a total of 51,703 and 18,759 patients in the argatroban and control group, respectively. The primary outcomes, mRS (0-2), and composite hemorrhage showed no significant difference between argatroban and control (RR: 1.03, CI: 0.97-1.10, p = 0.26 and RR: 1.10, CI: 0.98-1.23, p = 0.11, respectively). However, argatroban significantly reduced END (RR: 0.48, CI: 0.30-0.75, p < 0.05) and favored mRS (0-1) with RR:1.22 (CI: 1.01-1.48, p = 0.03). The change in NIHSS score and incidence of mortality, stroke recurrence, intracranial and organ hemorrhage was comparable between the two groups. Subgroup analyses by antiplatelet drug in the intervention and comparison groups confirmed that argatroban showed the most pronounced results when combined with DAPT. While the overall pooled analysis did not demonstrate increased hemorrhagic risk, subgroup analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials revealed a significant increase in composite and intracranial hemorrhage with argatroban. GRADE assessment of RCT-derived evidence indicated very low to high certainty across all outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Argatroban as an adjunct to antiplatelet therapy did not significantly improve overall functional outcome (mRS 0-2) or reduce composite hemorrhage compared with antiplatelet therapy alone. However it appears safe and may reduce END significantly.

Title: Long-term outcomes of tracheostomy in patients with congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Data on long-term follow-up after tracheostomy in patients with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) are limited. We assessed current tracheostomy status and clinical characteristics in relation to decannulation during long-term follow-up.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, we analyzed the Japanese CDH Study Group database records from 2006 to 2023. Clinical characteristics of patients undergoing tracheostomy during hospitalization were reviewed. Using long-term follow-up data, decannulation status was assessed and decannulation rates were estimated via Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: We included 1284 patients, 38 of whom underwent tracheostomy during hospitalization. Compared with the non-tracheostomy group, the tracheostomy group had higher rates of severe cardiac anomalies (21% vs. 9%), more chromosomal abnormalities (26% vs. 7%), greater gestational age (median 37w6d vs. 37w1d), and lower birth weight (median 2468 g vs. 2704 g). Survival among the tracheostomy cohort was 74.4%, 63.7%, and 53.1% at 6, 9, and 12 years, respectively. The cumulative decannulation rate at age 6 years was 36%. Pulmonary vasodilator use at discharge was significantly more common in non-decannulated patients.
CONCLUSION: Among all CDH infants, 3.0% required tracheostomy. The cumulative decannulation rate at 6 years was 36%. Pulmonary vasodilator use at discharge was more common in non-decannulated patients.

Title: New dyslipidemia guideline makes more than half of U.S. adults eligible for statin therapy.
Effect heterogeneity of loneliness and social support on incident hypertension in older, normotensive populations.
Abstract: Although social isolation is known to impact those with cardiovascular disease, its relationship with incident hypertension is unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, we used data from the All of Us research program. Participants were enrolled between May 2017-April 2023, aged 50+ years, and had at least 60-days of EHR data pre-index date. We identified incident hypertension during follow-up. Those classified as hypertensive at or prior to the index date were excluded. We defined low social support and loneliness as binary variables. Using causal forests, we estimated treatment effects as unweighted and overlap-weighted risk differences (RD). A total of 24,720 participants with a median follow-up of 2.6 years were included. While loneliness and social support were not significantly associated with incident hypertension in the overall population, causal forests revealed meaningful effect heterogeneity, with socially isolated male (RD: 0.038, 95% CI 0.002 to 0.075; overlap-weighted RD: 0.027, 95% CI -0.005 to 0.059) and Gay or Lesbian participants (RD: 0.108, 95% CI 0.011 to 0.205; overlap-weighted RD: 0.11, 95% CI 0.008 to 0.211) experiencing a significantly elevated risk. This illustrates how machine learning, when embedded within epidemiologic frameworks, can detect subgroup vulnerability that other approaches may obscure, enabling targeting of limited resources.

Title: Pacing Related Conduction Delay as an Indicator of Intramural Site of Origin of Focal Ventricular Arrhythmias.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of intramural focal ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be challenging and is often made in retrospect after a long ineffective procedure.
OBJECTIVES: In this cohort of patients, we aim to assess the value of pace-mapping (PM), stimulus-QRS interval (S-QRS interval), and electrogram (EGM)-QRS intervals to identify the site of origin (SOO) of focal VAs.
METHODS: In a consecutive series of 46 patients with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), activation mapping and PM were performed to identify VA target sites. VA target sites were defined as sites with matching PM (≥10/12 leads) and/or sites with the earliest activation time. S-QRS interval and bipolar activation time at target sites were assessed and correlated with acute outcomes. If ablation at a target site failed, alternative sites were sought in adjacent anatomical structures. An intramural origin was defined as a VA with early activation time without a matching PM.
RESULTS: Matching PMs were identified for 32 VAs in 30 of the 46 patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed at the target site/PVC level and demonstrated that a mismatch between S-QRS and EGM-QRS of >26 milliseconds distinguished effective from ineffective ablation sites with a matching PM (area under the curve: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.94-1; sensitivity: 100%; specificity: 88.9%). A mismatch was present in 9 patients, and radiofrequency ablation failed in 8/9 of them. Alternate sites with early activation times (-48.4 ± 37.39 milliseconds) without matching PM, where radiofrequency eliminated the PVCs, were identified in 5/8 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Conduction delay with matching PMs but late activation indicates a deeper SOO. A cutoff value of >26 milliseconds between S-QRS and EGM-QRS intervals identified deeper-seated VA target sites. This required further mapping to identify alternative ablation sites. A matching PM may not always be indicative of the SOO in patients with PVCs.

Title: Safety and Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction of Advisory ePTFE-Coated Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Leads: A Multicenter Experience With RELIANCE G.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE)-coated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are associated with progressive coil calcification and rising shock impedance, prompting a recent safety advisory. However, data regarding the safety and efficacy of transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for these chronic leads remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and procedural outcomes of TLE in patients with advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study at 13 centers of patients undergoing TLE of ePTFE-coated ICD leads. Primary endpoints included procedural success, complications, and short-term mortality. Multivariable analyses identified predictors of outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 423 patients undergoing extraction of advisory RELIANCE ICD leads (Boston Scientific), mean lead dwell time was 7.5 ± 5.3 years, and impedance-defined coil calcification was present in 15.1%. Laser sheaths were used in 63.8% of procedures and multiple extraction tools in 21.7%. Complete lead removal was achieved in 95.5%, clinical success in 98.8%, and extraction failed occurred in 1.2%. Major complications occurred in 0.9% of patients, with no procedural deaths. Calcified leads were associated with longer dwell times but not higher rates of major complications. Thirty-day mortality was 2.8%, primarily among patients undergoing extraction for infection.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, TLE of advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads was associated with high procedural success and low major complication rates despite long lead dwell times. Outcomes were consistent with contemporary TLE experience and do not suggest increased procedural risk attributable to this lead model. The presence of impedance-defined coil calcification did not adversely affect procedural outcomes, supporting TLE at experienced centers when clinically indicated.

Title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.
OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.
METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.
RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

Title: Baveno VI criteria validation and development of a new non-invasive strategy for varices rule-out in patients with HCC (SAPHE-R: Stiffness, ALBI, Platelets, HEpatocellular carcinoma Rule).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Accuracy of Baveno criteria for avoiding endoscopy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncertain, and systematic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (UGE) may not be necessary. We evaluated Baveno VI criteria performance in this population and developed an alternative non-invasive rule to exclude esophagogastric varices of any grade, rather than high-risk varices (HRV).
METHODS: Patients with BCLC 0-C HCC and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) from Italian Liver Cancer (ITA.LI.CA) database, with available liver stiffness measurement (LSM), UGE, and blood tests within six months of diagnosis, were included. Independent predictors of varices identified by logistic regression were combined through grid-search to derive a rule-out strategy (SAPHE-R), validated by bootstrap-resampling and in an independent cohort (Vienna).
RESULTS: The derivation cohort comprised 598 patients (age, 69 years; male sex, 75.3%; viral etiology, 69.3%; BCLC 0/A, 77.9%; ALBI 1, 54.2%; varices, 33.4%; HRV, 11.2%). Baveno VI criteria missed 8.5% of varices and 6.0% of HRV, sparing 31.1% of UGE. Independent predictors of varices were incorporated into SAPHE-R (LSM≤16 kPa, platelet count ≥160×10⁹/L, ALBI grade 1), which missed 4.0% of varices (HRV 3.0%, spared UGE 17.6%). In the validation cohort (n=149), SAPHE-R missed 4.8% of varices (HRV 3.1%, spared UGE 14.8%). Results remained consistent in sensitivity analyses. In an exploratory analysis, no HVPG-defined CSPH was observed among SAPHE-R rule-out patients (0/22).
CONCLUSIONS: Baveno VI criteria showed suboptimal performance in patients with HCC and cACLD, whereas SAPHE-R provided a reliable non-invasive strategy to rule out varices, facilitating variceal risk assessment in patients with HCC.

Title: Clusters of modifiable dementia risk factors at mid-life and late-life and their association with incident dementia: A prospective cohort study of 246,968 adults.
Abstract: BackgroundModifiable dementia risk factors rarely occur in isolation, yet their co-occurrence and clustering remain poorly characterized, limiting identification of high-risk individuals and development of targeted strategies.ObjectiveTo identify clusters of ten modifiable risk factors in mid-life (45-65 years) and late-life (>65 years), and to examine their association with incident dementia.MethodsData were drawn from the 2012 Dutch Public Health Monitor Survey (mid-life: n = 121,120; late-life: n = 125,848), with dementia follow-up through 2023. Ten modifiable risk factors: obesity, hypertension, diabetes, hearing loss, visual loss, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol consumption, smoking, loneliness, and depression, were used to derive clusters using latent class analysis. Cox proportional hazards models examined the association between late-life clusters and incident dementia.ResultsIn mid-life (mean age, 55.7 ± 6.2 years), four risk factor clusters were identified: cardiometabolic, substance use, psychosocial, and lower risk. In late-life (mean age, 73.9 ± 6.4 years), four clusters were identified: cardiometabolic, substance use, psychosocial and physically inactive, and lower risk. After adjustment for sociodemographic factors, the psychosocial and physically inactive cluster was associated with the highest hazard of dementia (hazard ratio (HR), 1.23; 95% CI, 1.16-1.32), followed by the substance use (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.09-1.24) and the cardiometabolic cluster (HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.07-1.18).ConclusionsDistinct risk factor clusters were identified at both mid-life and late-life; the psychosocial and physically inactive cluster carried the highest risk of dementia. These findings underscore the importance of considering risk factor clustering when designing targeted interventions to reduce dementia risk across the life course.

Title: Cardiomonostack: A postoperative heart failure risk prediction model for total hip arthroplasty driven by ensemble learning.
Journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
Abstract: BackgroundAccurate perioperative risk prediction remains challenging because of class imbalance, cohort heterogeneity, unstable probability estimates and limited interpretability.ObjectiveTo develop and externally evaluate CardioMonoStack, an ensemble architecture integrating heterogeneous base learners, branch-level monotonicity priors, stacked meta-learning and feature-dependent residual logit correction.MethodsWe conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 1911 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing total hip arthroplasty across five healthcare databases. CardioMonoStack was developed using MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, validated in INSPIRE, and externally tested in eICU and MOVER. Performance was assessed using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, threshold-dependent classification measures, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Interpretability was examined using SHAP, interaction and individual conditional expectation analyses.ResultsCardioMonoStack achieved the highest AUROC point estimates among evaluated models in eICU (0.790; 95% CI 0.711-0.865) and MOVER (0.866; 95% CI 0.761-0.949), with AUPRC values of 0.569 (95% CI 0.415-0.717) and 0.571 (95% CI 0.328-0.792), respectively. Calibration and net benefit varied across cohorts and comparators. Omission of L3 increased Brier-score and log-loss point estimates in both external cohorts; paired confidence intervals supported these differences in MOVER but were inconclusive in eICU. SHAP analyses prioritised blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, age, and metabolic and demographic factors.ConclusionCardioMonoStack is a candidate framework for estimating in-hospital heart-failure risk after total hip arthroplasty. Despite promising external discrimination, prospective validation, local recalibration, and clinical impact evaluation are required before implementation.

Title: Age-stratified mortality following operative management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury.
Journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
Abstract:
CONTEXT/OBJECTIVE: Postoperative mortality following traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) remains substantial, yet the combined influence of neurologic completeness and age on survival is poorly characterized in operatively treated patients. This study evaluated age-stratified mortality after surgical management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cSCI.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using risk ratio analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards.
SETTING: Global federated electronic health record database (TriNetX).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults who underwent surgery for traumatic subaxial cSCI, identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes, with injury classified as complete or incomplete (n = 5,477).
INTERVENTIONS: Operative management of traumatic subaxial cSCI.
OUTCOME MEASURES: All-cause mortality at 3, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Independent predictors of mortality were identified via Cox regression.
RESULTS: Complete cSCI was associated with significantly higher mortality at 3 months (10.73% vs. 7.7%; RR 1.39), 6 months (12.5% vs. 9.2%; RR 1.36), and 1 year (14.7% vs. 11.2%; RR 1.31) (all P < 0.001). Mortality differences were most pronounced in patients aged 61-80 years, with approximately twofold higher risk in complete injuries. Increasing age, male sex, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality.
CONCLUSION: Complete traumatic cSCI carries significantly higher postoperative mortality than incomplete injury, particularly among patients aged 61-80 years. These findings underscore the combined prognostic impact of neurologic severity and age, and may guide perioperative counseling and risk stratification, but should not be interpreted as demonstrating formal age-dependent effect modification.

Title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.
METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial

Title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: GONet: A Molecular Interaction-Guided Graph Learning Framework for Multi-Omics Cancer Classification.
Abstract: Integrating multi-omics profiles with molecular interaction networks enables biologically informed representation learning by combining molecular measurements with prior biological knowledge. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) are well suited for modeling molecular interaction networks, existing multi-omics methods often rely on shallow representation learning or incomplete fusion strategies, which fail to fully capture complementary information and complex dependencies across heterogeneous omics layers, resulting in suboptimal performance and limited generalizability in cancer classification tasks. Here, we propose GONet, a hierarchical GNN framework that integrates omics expression profiles, including mRNA, miRNA, and protein data, with molecular interaction networks, where nodes represent omics features and edges represent molecular interactions. GONet learns global omics representations via an autoencoder, captures local structural dependencies using Deep Graph Infomax (DGI), and enhances omics-specific representations through an attention mechanism. A gated fusion module further enables adaptive integration of heterogeneous features, improving cancer subtype and stage classification. GONet was systematically evaluated on 13 publicly available benchmark datasets used in prior studies, covering 10 cancer types, ensuring fair comparison across methods. Across mRNA and miRNA datasets, GONet achieved an average AUROC of 0.9262, outperforming representative GNN- and non-GNN-based methods by 13.77% and 6.35%, respectively. On an independent CPTAC cohort spanning seven cancer types, it improved performance by 25.22% and 13.91%, respectively. Incorporating proteomics further improved cancer stage classification by 5.56%, demonstrating complementary predictive value. Ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of the DGI-based module. Overall, GONet provides a unified framework for biologically informed multi-omics graph representation learning and cancer classification.

Title: Pre-surgery statin use and outcomes in operated chronic subdural haematomas: a nationwide cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) is common in older adults, and medication exposures may influence postoperative outcomes. We assessed whether pre-surgery statin use is associated with short- and long-term outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide registry study of adults undergoing surgical evacuation of traumatic or non-traumatic cSDH (6/2004-12/2018) in Finnish university hospitals. Pre-surgery statin use was defined from national prescription records using a pill-counting approach. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were 30-day reoperation and length of hospital stay. Tertiary outcomes were 1-year mortality and reoperation. Mortality was analysed using Cox regression; reoperation with Fine-Gray models accounting for competing risk of death.
RESULTS: The cohort included 9001 patients, of whom 2450 (27.2%) used statins. Thirty-day mortality was 3.3% in statin users and 4.5% in non-users, with lower adjusted mortality among statin users (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.44-0.73). Reoperation within 30 days (n = 897) was similar between groups (sub-distribution HR 1.08; 95% CI 0.97-1.21). Hospital stay was shorter in statin users (22.1 ± 62.7 vs 26.3 ± 77.5 days; adjusted P = .002). At 1 year, mortality remained lower in statin users (13.3% vs 15.4%; HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.58-0.75), with no difference in reoperation (sub-distribution HR 1.09; 95% CI 0.96-1.22).
CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort of surgically treated cSDH patients, pre-surgery statin use was associated with lower short- and long-term mortality and shorter hospital stay, while reoperation rates were similar between statin users and non-users.

Title: Longitudinal Characterization of the Microbiological Status in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: An Italian Multicentre Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder characterized by respiratory infections leading to chronic airway colonization and progressive lung damage. The aim of this study is to evaluate prevalence and longitudinal changes of respiratory microbiological profile in children and young adults with PCD, and their association with clinical, functional, and radiological features.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, multicenter longitudinal study included PCD patients from seven Italian Pediatric Pulmonology centers within the SIMRI (Italian Pediatric Respiratory Society) "PCD and Non-CF Bronchiectasis" study group. Patients were evaluated at baseline (T0) with questionnaires, spirometry, and sputum cultures, and followed for 12 months, with quarterly assessments.
RESULTS: 82 patients were enrolled (mean age 16.1 ± 5.9 y). At T0, 21 had negative sputum, 41 were colonized, 20 had acute infection. After 12 months, 75% of colonized patients remained colonized, although the microorganism identified during follow-up was not necessarily the same as that detected at baseline, and 52% of negative patients remained negative. Among acute infection, 40% progressed to colonization and 40% became sputum-negative. No significant clinical or functional differences were observed among microbiological groups. The most common pathogens were S. aureus (acute 18%, colonization 33%), H. influenzae (acute 14%, colonization 33%), and P. aeruginosa (acute 9%, colonization 23%). Patients colonized with P. aeruginosa showed lower spirometric values and more extensive bronchiectasis.
CONCLUSIONS: In PCD patients microbiological positivity is highly prevalent, being Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa the most frequently isolated pathogens. Most patients colonized at baseline remained colonized over time and patients colonized by Pseudomonas aeruginosa tended to exhibit greater bronchiectasis extension and worse lung function.

Title: Interleukin-35 Ameliorates Obesity-Associated Impairment of Endothelium-Dependent Vasodilation via the STAT3-MAPK/ERK-eNOS Signaling Axis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity impairs endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS)-nitric oxide (NO) signaling, triggering chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and defective vasodilation, which drives cardiometabolic diseases. Existing metabolic therapies provide only indirect vascular protection and fail to resolve residual inflammatory-mediated cardiovascular risk. As an anti-inflammatory interleukin 12 (IL-12) family cytokine, interleukin 35 (IL-35) is suppressed in obesity and exerts vascular protective effects under inflammatory conditions, yet its function and underlying mechanisms in obesity‑related endothelial vasodilator dysfunction remain undefined.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese mouse model was established by 8-week high-fat diet (HFD) feeding, followed by 4-week intraperitoneal administration of recombinant mouse IL-35. Aortic-ring assays evaluated vasodilatory function. Palmitic acid (PA)-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), recapitulate lipotoxic endothelial injury, were treated with recombinant human IL-35. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, 4-amino-5-methylamino-2',7'-difluorofluorescein diacetate (DAF-FM DA) detection and immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS) were applied to detect IL-35-subunit (Epstein-Barr virus-induced gene 3 [EBI3] and interleukin-12 subunit alpha [IL-12A]) levels, eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation, phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (MAPK/ERK) signaling molecules (cellular rapidly accelerated fibrosarcoma [cRAF], mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase [MEK], and ERK) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) activation, NO production, and eNOS-binding partners. Rescue assays were performed using Raf or ERK specific inhibitors and STAT3 small interfering RNA (siRNA).
RESULTS: HFD mice displayed reduced aortic endothelial EBI3 expression, impaired endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation, decreased eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation and lowered NO production; all these phenotypes were rescued by exogenous IL-35. IP-MS and immunoblotting demonstrated that IL-35 strengthened eNOS-ERK1 interaction and restored PA-repressed phosphorylation of cRAF, MEK, ERK and eNOS Ser1177, which were abrogated by Raf or ERK blockade. Furthermore, IL-35 recovered STAT3 phosphorylation suppressed by PA, while STAT3 knockdown blunted IL-35-driven MAPK/ERK activation, eNOS phosphorylation and subsequent NO production.
CONCLUSION: IL-35 alleviates obesity-induced impairment of endothelium-dependent vasodilation via the STAT3-MAPK/ERK-eNOS axis, which elevates eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation and NO synthesis. This work supports IL-35 as a prospective therapeutic candidate for obesity-associated vascular complications.

Title: Development and validation of a prediction model for cryptogenic ischemic stroke risk in migraine patients with right-to-left shunt: A 10-year study.
Journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
Abstract: AimLong-term risk stratification for cryptogenic ischemic stroke (CIS) remains uncertain in patients with migraine and contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler ultrasound-confirmed right-to-left shunting (RLS). Therefore, we aimed to develop and externally validate a simple baseline score for identifying individuals at low risk.MethodsThis 10-year study included 978 and 237 patients in the development and external validation cohorts, respectively. Internal validation involved a five-fold cross-validation strategy. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling was used to develop the Migraine Risk Stratification Score (MRSS). Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves at 3, 5, and 7 years, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Model interpretation was based on the Cox regression coefficients, hazard ratios, and integer points assigned to each predictor. Survival divergence was assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis.ResultsAge ≥50 years (1 point), migraine with aura (2 points), and permanent and large RLS (2 points each) were identified as predictors. Patients were stratified into low- (0-4 points) and high-risk (5-7 points) groups based on total score. The high-risk group exhibited a significantly higher 10-year CIS risk (21.77% vs. 4.68%; hazard ratio: 5.06; 95% confidence interval: 3.31-7.74). The areas under the curve (AUCs) at 3, 5, and 7 years were 0.771, 0.777, and 0.751 in the development cohort; 0.753, 0.768, and 0.744 after five-fold cross-validation; and 0.917, 0.863, and 0.808 in external validation, respectively. The 3-year external AUC was based on only five events; therefore, it should be interpreted cautiously. Across evaluated horizons, the negative-predictive value was high (0.96-0.99), whereas the positive-predictive value (0.05-0.19) and F1 score (0.10-0.30) were low. Kaplan-Meier curves confirmed significant long-term stroke-free survival stratification (log-rank P < 0·001).ConclusionMRSS exhibited characteristics consistent with a rule-out-oriented baseline risk stratification tool rather than a precise individualized absolute risk assessment for treatment selection. Further prospective validation and recalibration are required.

Title: Heavy Drinking in Young Adulthood Correlates With Earlier Genetic Cardiomyopathy Diagnosis: Analyzing a Retrospective Survey.
The START-SIAPAV-PAD Registry - Rationale, study design, and baseline characteristics of an ongoing Italian multicentre registry.
Abstract: Background: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with a high burden of cardiovascular and limb events, yet guideline-directed medical therapy remains suboptimal. The START-SIAPAV-PAD registry was designed to describe characteristics, management and clinical history of patients with PAD in Italy. Baseline characteristics and treatment are reported. Patients and methods: START-SIAPAV-PAD is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry enrolling consecutive adults with PAD managed at 20 Italian Vascular centres, starting in February 2023. Standardised electronic case-report forms collect demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, haemodynamic parameters, vascular anatomy, therapies. Follow-up is planned for a minimum of 3 years. PAD severity is classified according to the Leriche-Fontaine scale, and risk-factor targets follow the 2024 ESC guidelines. Results: The present analysis includes 517 patients (72.0% male; median age 71 years) with a high prevalence of hypertension (79.2%), dyslipidaemia (85.0%), diabetes (36.9%), smoking (96.1% current or former) and chronic kidney disease (21.2%). Nearly half reported a walking distance <200 m, 77.5% had a resting ankle-brachial index ≤.80, and 17.2% presented with Leriche-Fontaine stage IV. Femoropopliteal disease was most frequent (69.8%), with multilevel involvement in 43.4%. Previous revascularisation was common, major amputation was rare. LDL cholesterol target (<55mg dL) was achieved in 27.9% of patients despite lipid-lowering therapy in 82.1%. Dual pathway inhibition, advanced lipid-lowering therapies, supervised exercise and structured smoking-cessation programmes were insufficiently adopted. Conclusions: In a population with advanced PAD and multiple risk factors we observed a substantial gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Longitudinal follow-up will assess outcomes and opportunities to improve PAD management.

Title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes.
METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified. Secondary diagnosis codes captured VTE subtypes. Primary analyses compared mortality and major complications in ANP with versus without VTE; secondary analyses compared outcomes by subtype.
RESULTS: Among 110,225 ANP hospitalizations, 12.25% had VTE. ANP with VTE had higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.89, P<0.001), longer length of stay (adjusted mean difference 10.7 d, P<0.001), and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference $151,685, P<0.001). VTE was associated with higher rates of mesenteric ischemia, gastric varices, upper GI bleeding, AKI, sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, ARDS, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion, and ICU admissions. On subtype analysis, DVT (aOR 2.39, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 1.45, P=0.001) were associated with higher mortality; SVT was not significantly associated with mortality, though the analysis was limited by few events. PVT was most strongly associated with mesenteric ischemia (aOR 8.28, P<0.001), whereas gastric varices were most associated with SVT (aOR 11.37, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 3.73, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: VTE in ANP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, systemic complications, and resource utilization, with substantial heterogeneity across subtypes. DVT-associated ANP showed higher rates of systemic complications, whereas PVT and SVT showed distinct territory-specific vascular-complication patterns. Prospective studies should evaluate phenotype-specific anticoagulation strategies.

Title: Association Between Intramuscular Injection Site and Ulcer Healing in Patients with Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Treated with Recombinant Human Hepatocyte Growth Factor Naked Plasmid: A Post Hoc Analysis of the HOPE CLTI-2 Trial.
Abstract: This study was based on the multicenter, double-blind, randomized phase III HOPE CLTI-2 trial. An exploratory post hoc analysis was performed to investigate the association between intramuscular injection site and ulcer healing outcomes in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) treated with recombinant human hepatocyte growth factor (rh-HGF), and to explore factors associated with ulcer healing. The analysis included 108 patients with CLTI treated with rh-HGF, comprising 184 ischemic lower-limb ulcers. Patients were classified according to injection site into a single-segment group, with injections limited to the calf muscles, and a multi-segment group, with injections administered to both the thigh and calf muscles. Outcomes included ulcer healing rate, time to ulcer healing, ankle-brachial index (ABI), Rutherford category, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification, and adverse clinical events. At the study endpoint, the unadjusted ulcer healing rate was significantly higher in the single-segment group than in the multi-segment group (75.0% vs. 57.1%, p = 0.014), and the observed time to ulcer healing was shorter (153.00 [91.00-184.00] days vs. 181.00 [94.00-191.00] days, p = 0.022). No significant between-group differences were observed in changes in ABI (p = 0.290) or in WIfI classification (p = 0.407). However, the distribution of Rutherford categories at study endpoint favored the single-segment group (p = 0.016). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, baseline ulcer area (odds ratio [OR]: 0.684, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.519-0.901, p = 0.007) and male sex (OR: 3.924, 95% CI: 1.164-13.232, p = 0.028) were independently associated with ulcer healing. Although the unadjusted comparisons favored the single-segment group, injection site was not independently associated with ulcer healing after multivariable adjustment (OR: 1.560, 95% CI: 0.703-3.460, p = 0.269). Therefore, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Whether a more anatomically targeted rh-HGF injection strategy under a fixed-dose regimen can improve ulcer healing requires evaluation in prospectively designed studies.

Title: Comparative lifestyle factors and outcomes of an intensive interprofessional lifestyle medicine program versus usual care in Medicare and commercially insured musculoskeletal patients with chronic disease.
Journal: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle medicine (LM) uses evidence-based interventions to reduce chronic systemic inflammation, a driver of chronic diseases and painful musculoskeletal conditions. Medicare beneficiaries represent a high-risk population for chronic systemic inflammation and may benefit from receiving care through an intensive LM program (ILMP).
OBJECTIVE: To compare baseline lifestyle factors and outcomes (1) between Medicare and commercially insured patients completing an ILMP, and (2) between Medicare patients completing an ILMP and Medicare patients receiving usual care (non-ILMP).
DESIGN: Retrospective exploratory study of repository data.
SETTING: Tertiary orthopedic center.
PATIENTS: A total of 204 Medicare and 322 commercially insured patients entered the ILMP from May 2023 to May 2025; of these, 101 Medicare and 130 commercially insured patients completed the program and were included in this study (50% vs. 40% completion rate; p = .040). A third group of 90 Medicare patients with similar conditions received usual care during this same time frame.
INTERVENTIONS: The ILMP virtually integrates individual and group visits with an interprofessional team, with patient-identified health goals.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Goal attainment; changes in weight, pain, physical/mental health, and metabolic labs from program enrollment to completion.
RESULTS: Compared to commercially insured ILMP patients, Medicare ILMP patients were older (70 ± 7 vs. 55 ± 10 years, p < .001) and had higher rates of ≥2 lifestyle-related chronic diseases (96% vs. 85%; p = .015), hypertension (72% vs. 54%; p = .010), hyperlipidemia (59% vs. 40%; p = .001), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (33% vs. 18%; p = .015) at baseline. Medicare and commercially insured ILMP patients reported similar use of program services, goal attainment, and outcomes. Compared to the Medicare usual-care group, the Medicare ILMP group had similar baseline characteristics but achieved greater weight loss (10 ± 14 lbs vs. 1 ± 4 lbs; p < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: An interprofessional ILMP delivered virtually is feasible and effective for Medicare patients with musculoskeletal conditions and lifestyle-related chronic diseases, despite having a greater baseline disease burden compared with commercially insured patients.

Title: Associations of the Baseline Level and Change in Triglyceride Glucose-Body Roundness Index With Cardiovascular Diseases: Two Large Prospective Cohorts in Europe and Asia.
Journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences
Abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the association of baseline and changes of TyG-BRI with incident CVD based on the UK Biobank and China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 418,510 and 7923 individuals from the UK Biobank and CHARLS were included in Analysis 1 (baseline TyG-BRI with CVD risk). In Analysis 2 (change in TyG-BRI with CVD risk), a total of 11,682 and 4637 participants were included in Cox proportional hazard models. We found participants with the highest baseline TyG-BRI level were associated with increased risk of incident CVD in UK Biobank (HR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.39-1.52) and CHARLS (HR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.13-1.61). Multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic spline analyses presented positive linear associations between TyG-BRI and CVD risk. Compared to persistently low levels of TyG-BRI (Class 1), those with persistently high levels (Class 3: 1.23 (1.02-1.49) and 1.42 (1.11-1.55); Class 4: 1.48 (1.17-1.87) and 1.45 (1.16-2.28); Class 5: 2.58 (1.86-3.58) and 1.63 (1.16-2.28) for UK Biobank and CHARLS) in follow-up were associated with increased risks of incident CVD. In conclusion, a high baseline TyG-BRI level and different changes in TyG-BRI level are associated with increased risks of incident CVD.

Title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and Surgical Considerations.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries.
BACKGROUND: Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations.
METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to "accessory renal artery," "multiple renal arteries," "renal artery variations," "renal vascular anatomy," "kidney transplantation," "renovascular hypertension," "computed tomography angiography," "magnetic resonance angiography," and "endovascular aortic repair" were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded.
DISCUSSION: This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases.
CONCLUSION: Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

Title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary occlusion (ACO) occurs in approximately one-quarter of patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for ACO.
METHODS: Consecutive patients admitted with NSTEMI between January 2016 and June 2023 who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Demographic, electrocardiographic, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected. Patients admitted during 2016-2020 were assigned to the training cohort (n = 670), and those admitted during 2021-2023 were assigned to the validation cohort (n = 334). Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Among 1,004 patients, 262 (26.1%) had ACO. Seven predictors, including smoking history, ST-segment depression ≥ 1 mm, regional wall motion abnormality, left ventricular ejection fraction, admission cardiac troponin I, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, were incorporated into the model. The area under the ROC curve was 0.731 (95% CI, 0.688-0.773) in the training cohort and 0.715 (95% CI, 0.654-0.776) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and validated a multidimensional prediction model for ACO in patients with NSTEMI. The model showed acceptable performance and may aid early identification before coronary angiography, although reliance on IL-6, which is not routinely available in all centers, may limit its generalizability.

Title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
Journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified.
