Choroidal volume expansion in BRVO and compositional remodeling in CRVO suggest subtype-specific choroidal involvement; together, these findings support the potential value of layer-specific retinal perfusion metrics and three-dimensional choroidal parameters for imaging-based stratification.

Title: Conventional and novel hypoxemia-related indices for obstructive sleep apnea severity and incident hypertension: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with hypertension (HTN), but the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and oxygen desaturation index (ODI) may not fully characterize nocturnal hypoxemia relevant to HTN development. We evaluated the associations of the sleep breathing impairment index (SBII) and hypoxic burden (HB) with incident HTN and compared their discriminative performance with AHI and ODI.
METHODS: This prospective study included 601 participants with OSA (AHI ≥ 15 events/h) from Sleep Heart Health Study who were free of HTN at baseline. SBII, HB, AHI and ODI were analyzed both in quartiles and as continuous variables. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to evaluate their associations with incident HTN. Discrimination performance was assessed by comparing a clinical base model with models that separately incorporating each quartile-categorized index.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of approximately 5 years, 194 (32.3%) participants developed HTN. In the primary fully adjusted model, the highest quartiles of SBII (OR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.02-2.90; p = 0.044) and HB (OR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.02-2.79; p = 0.041) were associated with higher odds of incident HTN. In the T90-adjusted sensitivity model, both associations were significant, whereas AHI and ODI quartiles remained nonsignificant. The clinical base model had a C-statistic of 0.614; adding SBII or HB, did not significantly improve discrimination.
CONCLUSION: Exploratory quartile-based analyses suggested that the highest quartiles of SBII and HB were associated with higher odds of incident HTN among participants with OSA, whereas AHI and ODI were not. These findings indicate that marked elevation in SBII and HB may provide a more comprehensive characterization of OSA-related nocturnal hypoxemia relevant to incident HTN. However, the nonsignificant continuous and overall spline analyses and the limited incremental discrimination warrant cautious interpretation and further validation.

Title: Extent of posterior wall lesion following pulmonary vein isolation with pentaspline pulsed field and cryoballoon ablation: the potential role of deployment technique.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using cryoballoon (CB) or pulsed field ablation (PFA) with a pentaspline catheter achieves similar efficacy in atrial fibrillation (AF), but lesion extension on the left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) may differ. Pentaspline-PFA (P-PFA) has been reported to create broader LAPW lesions, potentially leaving narrow viable corridors that have been hypothesized to be proarrhythmic.
OBJECTIVE: To descriptively compare the extent of chronic unintended left atrial posterior wall isolation after PVI with P-PFA and CB ablation.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center ambispective study including consecutive patients undergoing repeat left atrial mapping after index PVI with either P-PFA, using a protocol designed to ensure catheter alignment with the pulmonary veins, or CB. Patients with additional LA ablation between index procedure and remapping, unrelated LAPW scarring, or posterior pulmonary vein gaps were excluded. The primary endpoint was isolated LAPW area. Secondary endpoints included percentage of isolated LAPW and minimum residual corridor width.
RESULTS: Seventy-four patients were included in the analysis: 49 P-PFA and 25 CB. Mean age was 64.2 ± 10.0 years, 64.9% were male, and 55.4% had persistent AF. Isolated LAPW area was 8.3 ± 4.0 cm2 in the P-PFA group and 9.5 ± 3.9 cm2 in the CB group, with no statistically significant difference detected between groups (mean difference -1.26 cm2, 95% CI: -3.22 to 0.70; p = 0.203). The percentage of isolated LAPW area was 39.9 ± 17.6% vs. 38.9 ± 14.9% (p = 0.805), and minimum residual corridor width was 19.7 ± 9.9 vs. 18.6 ± 11.0 mm (p = 0.671), respectively. P-PFA was associated with shorter procedure time (44.2 ± 10.2 vs. 65.8 ± 24.6 min; p < 0.001), shorter LA dwell time (38.1 ± 9.6 vs. 60.6 ± 20.5 min; p < 0.001), lower fluoroscopy time (5.3 ± 3.9 vs. 13.0 ± 9.7 min; p < 0.001), and lower dose-area product [5.3 (2.8-9.7) vs. 19.3 (6.5-31.0) Gy·cm2; p < 0.001].
CONCLUSION: In this descriptive, hypothesis-generating study, no statistically significant difference in chronic LAPW isolation extent was detected between P-PFA and CB ablation. These findings support the hypothesis that catheter deployment technique may influence posterior wall lesion geometry, warranting confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies.

Title: Clinical phenotypes and outcomes of spinal cord stimulation in painful peripheral polyneuropathy: a cohort including diabetic, chemotherapy-induced, and idiopathic etiologies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chronic painful peripheral polyneuropathy (PPN) is a leading global cause of chronic pain and may arise from a wide range of etiologies. When pharmacological treatments fail to provide adequate pain relief, spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has demonstrated efficacy in selected subtypes. This study investigated the effectiveness of SCS in alleviating pain, neurological symptoms and signs, and other health-related outcomes in patients with diverse forms of PPN, including diabetic (DPN) and chemotherapy-induced (CIPN) peripheral neuropathies, and chronic idiopathic axonal polyneuropathy (CIAP).
METHODS: This prospective, single-center observational study included 30 patients with drug-refractory PPN (11 DPN, 8 CIPN, 9 CIAP, and 2 other etiologies: 1 amyloidosis and 1 Fabry disease). All patients were implanted with two percutaneous leads at T10-T11 targeting lower limbs; a cervical lead (C4-C7) when upper limb pain was present; and SCS system. Low-frequency (<100 Hz) sub-perception and/or supra-perception stimulation modalities were offered. Clinical outcomes were assessed at baseline and at 2, 4, 6, and 12 months post-implantation and included pain (VAS, SF-MPQ-2), neuropathic symptoms (NPSI), autonomic symptoms (SAS), neurological signs, and other health-related factors. Intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) was assessed at baseline and at 12 months.
RESULTS: Baseline evaluations demonstrated severe disease burden, with CIAP patients exhibiting more pain symptoms and DPN patients more neurologic deficits. SCS produced a significant and sustained reduction in pain intensity and symptoms (VAS from 8.6 to 2.0, SF-MPQ-2 from 115.5 to 23.0; p < 0.001) across all PPN subtypes, with greater improvements observed in DPN (p < 0.001). Additional benefits included reductions in neuropathic symptoms (NPSI from 61.1 to 11.1; p < 0.001), autonomic symptoms (SAS from 16.5 to 9.9; p = 0.02) and improvements in sleep, functioning, and quality of life (EQ-VAS from 38.8 to 77.9; p < 0.001). Neurological signs remained unchanged. Use of analgesics decreased substantially (59% complete withdrawal; 41% partial), and 96% of patients reported "much" or "very much" improvement. Twelve-month IENFD measurements showed a lower-than-expected mean decline across etiologies, with IENFD increases outnumbering decreases, although the changes were modest.
DISCUSSION: SCS was associated with substantial and durable improvements in pain, neuropathic and autonomic symptoms, and other wellbeing outcomes across multiple painful PPN etiologies. The IENFD results suggest that SCS may have some effects on small-fiber integrity.

Title: Association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term postpartum blood pressure trajectories: a community-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) increase the future risk of hypertension, but their impact on long-term postpartum blood pressure (BP) trajectories remains unclear. We aimed to characterize these trajectories and compare trajectory membership between women with and without APOs.
METHODS: This community-based cohort study included 1,346 women with documented deliveries (2004-2020) from the Kailuan Study who underwent at least three postpartum health examinations between 2006 and 2022. APOs included hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia/eclampsia), gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, and low birth weight. Generalized additive mixed models were used to characterize longitudinal changes in systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to identify distinct BP trajectory groups. Multinomial logistic regression with marginal standardization estimated adjusted risk ratio (aRR).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 9.2 years, SBP showed a nonlinear increase, with an average slope of 1.13 mmHg/year (95% CI, 0.93-1.33) during the first 6.4 years, followed by slower increases of 0.73 and 0.59 mmHg/year during 6.4-10 and 10-15 years, respectively. DBP showed a near-linear increasing pattern, whereas MAP increased linearly. Three trajectory groups were identified for each BP component. APOs were associated with higher risks of high-level SBP (aRR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.19-2.66), DBP (aRR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.24-1.87), and MAP (aRR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.16-3.64) trajectories compared with membership in the low-level BP trajectory groups. Associations varied across APOs subtypes. GDM and PTB were associated with higher risk of membership in the high-level SBP, DBP, and MAP trajectory groups compared with the corresponding low-level trajectory groups.
CONCLUSION: Different BP components exhibit distinct longitudinal patterns after delivery, APOs are associated with heterogeneous and unfavorable long-term postpartum BP trajectories.

Title: Classification of cystoid macular edema status from retinal vasculitis fluorescein angiography images using a convolutional neural network.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cystoid macular edema (CME) is a vision-threatening complication of retinal vasculitis, a rare inflammatory disease for which large imaging datasets are difficult to obtain. Detection of CME on fluorescein angiography (FA) requires expert interpretation, motivating automated image-based approaches to support clinical decision-making. Deep learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown strong performance in medical image analysis but are constrained by limited labeled data in rare diseases. Transfer learning may mitigate this limitation by adapting pretrained models to small, task-specific datasets.
METHODS: We analyzed 207 de-identified late-phase 55° FA images from 117 patients with retinal vasculitis. The primary target was concurrent patient-level CME status, established through specialist review of clinical records and optical coherence tomography obtained at the same clinical visit as FA. A patient was classified as CME-positive when CME was present in at least one eye. An ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 was evaluated using five-fold nested, patient-level cross-validation. Within each outer-development cohort, 144 candidate configurations were compared by four-fold inner cross-validation and selected according to mean inner-validation AUROC. Each selected configuration was evaluated only on its corresponding untouched outer-test fold.
RESULTS: Across 117 pooled patient-level outer-test predictions, the model-selection pipeline achieved an AUROC of 0.708 (95% CI, 0.610-0.802), an AUPRC of 0.626 (95% CI, 0.493-0.755), and an accuracy of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.641-0.803). Sensitivity was 0.694 (95% CI, 0.558-0.822), specificity was 0.750 (95% CI, 0.643-0.853), and the F1 score was 0.680 (95% CI, 0.563-0.780). Exploratory Grad-CAM analysis visualized regions associated with model predictions.
DISCUSSION: The nested model-selection pipeline showed moderate discrimination with a relatively balanced operating profile and slightly higher specificity than sensitivity. Clinically relevant false-positive and false-negative errors, together with the absence of external validation, preclude clinical deployment.

Title: Evaluation of axial length measurement and other biometric parameters using three different generations of biometers.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare biometric measurements obtained with partial coherence interferometry (IOLMaster 500, IOLM), optical low-coherence reflectometry (Lenstar 900, LS900), and swept-source optical coherence tomography (Eyestar 900, ES900).
METHODS: In this prospective, observational study, axial length (AL), anterior chamber depth (ACD), aqueous depth (AD), lens thickness (LT), and central corneal thickness (CCT) were measured with the three devices. Exclusion criteria were ocular disease, previous ocular surgery, and contact lens use within 72 h. Normality was assessed using the exact Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Comparisons were performed with paired T-tests and repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman plots, and correlation was evaluated using Pearson correlation (r), and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Subgroup analysis by eye side was conducted.
RESULTS: Two-hundred-six eyes of 103 healthy subjects (38 females) were recruited at Public hospital "San Giovanni di Dio e Ruggi d'Aragona", Salerno, Italy. All devices showed excellent correlation for AL and ACD (r ≥ 0.947, ICC≥0.939; p < 0.001). AL and ACD were comparable between LS900 and IOLM (ΔAL = +0.00 ± 0.09 mm; ΔACD = +0.01 ± 0.10 mm; p > 0.050). ES900 measured longer AL and deeper ACD than LS900 (ΔAL = +0.03 ± 0.10 mm; ΔACD = +0.04 ± 0.11 mm; p ≤ 0.031) and IOLM (ΔAL = +0.03 ± 0.08 mm; ΔACD = +0.04 ± 0.11 mm; p ≤ 0.013). Strong correlation was observed between ES900 and LS900 for CCT, AD, and LT (r ≥ 0.979, ICC≥0.961; p < 0.001). ES900 measured thicker CCT, deeper AD, and thinner LT (p < 0.017).
CONCLUSION: Despite excellent correlation, ES900 provided systematically higher AL and ACD values and different anterior segment measurements. Therefore, caution should be taken when using these devices interchangeably, especially in longitudinal studies and follow-up evaluations; device-specific interpretation is recommended to optimize refractive outcomes in cataract surgery.

Title: Interpretable model using serum biomarkers and intra-/peri-aneurysmal CTA radiomics for discriminating ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms: an external validation retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop an interpretable model that integrates diverse machine learning algorithms, fusion strategies, intra-/perianeurysmal CTA radiomics, and serum biomarkers to differentiate ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms (IAs), and to investigate the underlying biological features associated with rupture status.
METHODS: Totally, 744 IAs patients who underwent CTA were retrospectively enrolled. Data from Center 1 (N = 423) served as the training set, and data from Center 2 (N = 321) served as the external validation set. Volumes of interest were delineated in intra-aneurysmal and peri-aneurysmal 1 mm regions. The serum inflammation score (SIS) was constructed using serum biomarkers. Seven machine learning classifiers were employed to develop models, and the optimal fusion model was developed by combining all classifiers using arithmetic mean, geometric mean, weighted mean, and logistic regression (LRSLM). Model performance was assessed by the area under the curve (AUC) and decision curve analysis (DCA), while interpretability was evaluated via SHAP, correlation, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses.
RESULTS: Among the 11 models, LRSLM exhibited robust performance in the external validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.9177 with good calibration. It also demonstrated high accuracy (0.8847), recall (0.8171), and a low Brier score (0.0999), alongside greater clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities (10-85%). Correlation analyses revealed strong positive associations between intra-aneurysmal and peri-aneurysmal radiomic features (Spearman's r = 0.62, 0.72, and 0.84, respectively; all p < 0.001), as well as significant positive correlations between the intra-/perianeurysmal radiomics and SIS (Spearman's r = 0.32, 0.29, 0.32, and 0.34; all p < 0.001). RCS analysis further demonstrated a significant non-linear relationship between the intra-aneurysmal (IRSIAs) and peri-aneurysmal (PRSIAs) radiomic features and an increased incidence of IAs rupture (Non-linear p < 0.05; Overall p < 0.05). SHAP analysis highlighted key radiomics features contributors to the fusion model and supported model interpretability.
CONCLUSION: The LRSLM model achieves robust discriminative performance for differentiating ruptured from unruptured IAs. SHAP analysis enhances the interpretability of the model and may assist in identifying high-risk phenotypic features, although prospective validation is required before predictive clinical application can be considered.

Title: Estimated pulse wave velocity and dipstick proteinuria in young adults with MASLD: a cross-sectional health-check analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a non-invasive surrogate measure of arterial stiffness that has been associated with cardiovascular risk and renal abnormalities. However, studies exploring the association between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-a condition associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-are scarce. This study aimed to investigate the association between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria in patients with MASLD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1,641 MASLD patients from a cohort of individuals who underwent health check-ups at a tertiary hospital in Beijing, China. ePWV was calculated using an established equation based on age and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Participants were stratified based on ePWV tertiles. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the relationship between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria, adjusting for potential confounders such as age, sex, BMI, and comorbid conditions. Subgroup analyses were performed according to sex, diabetes, hyperuricemia, dyslipidemia, H. pylori infection, and urolithiasis.
RESULTS: Unadjusted and adjusted models consistently showed that higher ePWV was associated with higher odds of dipstick proteinuria. In the highest ePWV tertile, the odds of dipstick proteinuria were higher compared to the lowest tertile (OR: 2.44, 95% CI: 1.20-5.67, P for trend = 0.002). Subgroup analysis revealed a statistically significant interaction by dyslipidemia status, with a stronger association observed among participants without dyslipidemia (OR: 4.59, 95% CI: 2.18-9.76, P = 0.001), while no statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, hyperuricemia, H. pylori infection, diabetes mellitus, or urolithiasis.
DISCUSSION: Higher ePWV was associated with an increased likelihood of dipstick proteinuria among patients with MASLD. Further longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether ePWV is associated with subsequent urinary protein abnormalities and kidney outcomes.

Title: LASSO-based nomogram to predict early treatment failure in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with lenvatinib and tislelizumab has shown potential activity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but early treatment failure (ETF) remains common. We developed an exploratory model to estimate ETF, defined as radiologically confirmed progressive disease (PD) or all-cause death within 6 months after treatment initiation.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included advanced HCC patients treated with the triple regimen from June 2021 to June 2024. Baseline clinical, imaging, and hematological variables were analyzed. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection. Restricted cubic splines assessed linearity, and λ.1se was examined as a sensitivity analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were evaluated, with 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation repeating the modeling pipeline.
RESULTS: Among 118 patients, 33 (27.9%) experienced ETF; 28 had radiologically confirmed PD and 5 died without prior documented PD. At λ.min, LASSO selected maximum tumor diameter, Vp4 portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), ALBI score, and log10-transformed alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Under λ.1se, four predictors were retained, with SII excluded. The final model had an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.903 and an optimism-corrected ROC-AUC of 0.866. Calibration showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested net benefit over an exploratory threshold range of approximately 0.10-0.50, which should not be interpreted as a validated treatment-switching threshold.
CONCLUSION: The nomogram showed promising internal discrimination for estimating 6-month ETF risk in advanced HCC patients receiving SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab. Given the modest sample size and single-center design, the model remains exploratory and hypothesis-generating. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation or use for treatment selection.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early acute kidney injury and altered consciousness in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and altered consciousness are common and serious complications following cardiac surgery, both associated with increased morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Early prediction of these complications is essential for timely intervention. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early AKI and altered consciousness risk in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively extracted data from the MIMIC-IV database. Adult patients who underwent cardiac surgery within 24 h before ICU admission were included. The primary outcome was early AKI defined by KDIGO criteria within 48 h after ICU admission. The secondary outcome was altered consciousness within 24 h after ICU admission, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤12. A comprehensive set of candidate variables was screened using four feature selection methods (LassoCV, mRMR, mutual information, and F-test) with a voting strategy. Eight machine learning models were developed and compared. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to interpret the best-performing model. External validation was performed using data from cardiac surgery patients at Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2025.
RESULT: A total of 5,288 patients were included, with an AKI incidence of 76.2% (4,031/5,288) and an altered consciousness incidence of 22.8% (1,206/5,288). For the primary outcome of AKI, the XGBoost model achieved a training AUC of 0.787 (95% CI: 0.770-0.804) and an internal test AUC of 0.659 (95% CI: 0.629-0.688). For the secondary outcome of altered consciousness, the XGBoost model achieved an internal test AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.936-0.963). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis confirmed good calibration and clinical utility for both models. SHAP analysis identified SpO2, age, APSIII score, creatinine, and white blood cell count as the top 5 most important predictors for AKI. External validation was performed in an independent cohort of 395 cardiac surgery ICU patients from Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital, in whom the incidence of AKI and altered consciousness was 28.1% and 67.3%, respectively. The models retained acceptable discrimination in this external cohort (AKI: AUC 0.764, 95% CI: 0.711-0.818; altered consciousness: AUC 0.679, 95% CI: 0.615-0.737).
CONCLUSION: We developed interpretable XGBoost-based prediction models for both early AKI and altered consciousness risk in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU. The models exhibited excellent discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, which may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide personalized interventions.

Title: Predictors of recurrent stroke among patients with lacunar stroke receiving intensive blood pressure control: a secondary analysis of the secondary prevention of small subcortical strokes trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) lowering to <130 mm Hg is recommended in contemporary secondary stroke prevention guidelines; however, it did not significantly reduce overall recurrent ischemic stroke in the Secondary Prevention of Small Subcortical Strokes (SPS3) trial. In this post hoc secondary analysis of participant-level SPS3 trial data, we sought to identify baseline predictors of recurrent ischemic stroke among patients with lacunar stroke assigned to the lower SBP target in SPS3.
METHODS: This post hoc secondary analysis included SPS3 participants randomized to the lower SBP target (<130 mm Hg). The primary outcome was centrally adjudicated recurrent ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Candidate predictors were evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 1501 participants (41.1% aged ≥ 65 years; 60.8% were men), 120 (8.0%) experienced recurrent ischemic stroke over a median follow-up of 3.49 years (interquartile range, 1.80-5.08), corresponding to an incidence rate of 2.43 events per 100 person-years. In unadjusted comparisons, recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with diabetes mellitus (44.2% vs 34.2%; p = .036), coronary artery bypass grafting/coronary stent (9.2% vs 4.1%; p = .018), Black race (24.2% vs 14.4%; p = .007), elevated serum creatinine (14.2% vs 7.7%; p = .022), aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (44.2% vs 28.5%; p < .001), large-vessel atherosclerosis (29.3% vs 17.9%; p = .004), and lower prevalence of a subcortical qualifying stroke (21.7% vs 46.1%; p < .001). In multivariable analysis, aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.14-2.50; p = .009) and large-vessel atherosclerosis (HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.08-2.413; p = .020) were independently associated with recurrence. Randomization to aspirin plus clopidogrel was not associated with recurrent ischemic stroke (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.75-1.57; p = .661).
CONCLUSIONS: In SPS3 participants assigned to intensive SBP control, 8.0% experienced recurrent ischemic stroke. Aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke and large-vessel atherosclerosis remained independent predictors of recurrence. These findings may help identify patients who require preventive strategies beyond intensive SBP lowering.

Title: Retrospective Assessment of Pulmonary Embolism in Pregnancy and Evaluation of Pregnancy-Adapted YEARS Algorithm.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the diagnostic performance of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm applied to an Australian patient population with concurrent evaluation of its efficacy towards scan reduction.
METHODS: The pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm was applied to pregnant patients retrospectively at this single site study to determine a theoretical pathway in comparison to actual management.
RESULTS: Of 119 included patients, six (5%) had pulmonary emboli (PE). Retrospective application of the pregnancy-adapted YEARS algorithm missed no PE diagnosis. Theoretical application would have resulted in an 11.7% reduction in total CTPA and V/Q scans performed.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports the diagnostic performance benefits of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm and can potentially reduce unnecessary imaging.

Title: Effects of Brief Breathwork Under a State of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Well-Being and Diaphragm Function: A Randomized Crossover Design.
Journal: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress
Abstract: Previous investigations have identified the effectiveness of breathwork on both psychological and physical health for individuals under a resting state. However, there was no study investigating the effects of breathwork under a mentally-fatigued state. The purpose of this study was to examine the acute effects of breathwork administered after the induction of mental fatigue by a cognitive tasks on primary self-reported outcomes including positive and negative affect and self-reported stress indices, as well as on secondary physiological outcomes including diaphragm function and stress-related physiological responses. This study was employed with a randomized cross-over study design. Twenty healthy university students voluntarily participated in this study. Each of them performed a 20-min breathwork and control (quiet bed rest) condition following the Colour-Word Stroop Task (CWST) in a randomized sequence over two days separated at least by a week. Participants completed self-reported questionnaires for positive and negative affect and stress indices and underwent ultrasonographic assessments of the diaphragm function, saliva collection for cortisol and IgA, and heart rate variability assessments at baseline, pre-CWST, post-CWST, and post-intervention. The breathwork condition demonstrated significantly higher positive affect at post-intervention compared to the control condition (p = 0.021). Right hemidiaphragm excursion and left hemidiaphragm thickness at end-inspiration significantly increased from post-CWST to post-intervention in the breathwork condition. The breathwork condition appeared to improve positive affect and diaphragm function even under a mentally-fatigued state, compared to the control condition. These findings indicate that breathwork may serve as a simple, accessible, and practical strategy to enhance subjective well-being in a stressful environment and diaphragm function regardless of mental fatigue.

Title: An interval-based approach to measuring eating jet lag in female healthcare shift workers.
Abstract: Circadian rhythms regulate physiological and metabolic functions, and their disruption, particularly from shift work, is associated with adverse health outcomes such as obesity or cardiovascular disease. Meal timing variability, or eating jet lag, has emerged as a valuable marker of circadian misalignment. This study introduces a novel method to assess eating jet lag through direct comparison of food intake intervals, addressing limitations of traditional midpoint-based approaches reducing intervals to single values, potentially overlooking meaningful overlap. We conducted a cross-sectional study on 290 female healthcare professionals in Asturias, Spain, from a larger cohort of 679 participants with complete temporal data for meals across morning, afternoon, and night shifts. The proposed method calculates the degree of embedding between intake intervals during work shifts and rest days, and a global index is derived by aggregating alignment values across shifts. Results show that the interval-based method captures temporal overlap not represented by the midpoint-based approach, especially where the midpoint method underestimates alignment. Bland-Altman analysis showed systematic and proportional disagreement between the two approaches, with discrepancies greater at lower levels of alignment. This approach provides complementary information for evaluating eating-window alignment and provides a basis for future studies between eating-window alignment and health-related outcomes.

Title: Early Prediction of Cardiomyopathy in Pediatric Cancer Survivors Using Echocardiographic Video-Based Deep Learning.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiomyopathy (CM) is a leading cause of late mortality in childhood cancer survivors, but it is often identified only after irreversible cardiac remodeling has already occurred. In this proof-of-concept study, we assessed whether deep learning applied to routine echocardiographic videos can identify features predictive of future CM.
METHODS: We analyzed parasternal short-axis clips from cancer survivors ≤21 years old at cancer diagnosis. 3D deep convolutional neural networks were trained to classify CM-positive versus CM-negative studies from echocardiograms conducted up to five years prior to CM diagnosis. The performance was assessed on internal hold-out validation (Center 1) and external validation cohorts (Centers 2, 3). The model's prognostic value was evaluated by stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups for developing CM, and probability of future CM was assessed using cumulative incidence and proportional hazards regression analysis.
RESULTS: The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87±0.05 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.74±0.07 on the internal hold-out set. External validation showed near-chance single-study discrimination (AUROC 0.55±0.02 and 0.60±0.03; AUPRC 0.22±0.02 and 0.21±0.03 for Centers 2 and 3, respectively). Nevertheless, analysis of the external cohort showed significantly higher probability of CM in high- versus low-risk groups (hazard ratio 2.78, 95% CI = 1.52-5.10, p = 0.00056).
CONCLUSION: Deep learning models have the potential to identify subtle echocardiographic markers years before CM diagnosis in pediatric cancer survivors and could serve as a preliminary step toward risk-guided CM surveillance. Further refinement and validation are needed to determine the utility of deep learning for early identification of pathologic cardiac remodeling in this population.

Title: One-Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited.
AIMS: We compared 1-year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
METHODS: The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
RESULTS: From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non-ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST-segment elevation MI, 33.9% non-ST-segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post-procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow-limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non-ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non-ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06-3.17, p = 0.03). All-cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13-3.75, p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: One-year TLF and all-cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non-ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real-world clinical settings.
REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.

Title: An early risk prediction nomogram for coronary artery lesions in Kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery lesions remain a major concern in Kawasaki disease. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical nomogram for early identification of children at risk for Coronary artery lesions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 216 children with Kawasaki disease divided into a training cohort (n = 151) and a validation cohort (n = 65). Coronary artery lesions was defined as early coronary dilatation and/or coronary aneurysm. XGBoost and SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to explore age's nonlinear effect. Predictors were screened via multivariable logistic regression with elastic-net regression for supplementary assessment. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis.
RESULTS: Overall, 46 children (21.3%) developed Coronary artery lesions. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified a U-shaped age-risk pattern with cut-off points at 17 and 58 months. Male sex, age group, fever duration, systemic immune-inflammation index, C-reactive protein/albumin ratio, and intravenous immunoglobulin resistance were independent Coronary artery lesions risk factors incorporated into the nomogram. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve reached 0.835 (95% CI 0.804-0.867) in the training cohort and 0.818 (95% CI 0.767-0.869) in the validation cohort. Calibration and decision-curve analysis confirmed good consistency and favourable clinical net benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: This nomogram integrates routine clinical variables and interpretable machine learning to identify nonlinear age-related Coronary artery lesions risk and provide individualised early risk estimation. External validation in large prospective multicentre cohorts is needed before wide clinical application.

Title: Immersion in the anatomical dissection room using a virtual reality headset to reduce medical student anxiety: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract: Anatomical dissection is a fundamental component of medical education but is often associated with significant student anxiety that is hence important to consider. This randomized controlled trial aimed to assess whether immersive preparation using a 360° virtual reality (VR) video could reduce anxiety and stress in medical students prior to their first dissection experience. Second-year medical students at a single medical school in France, with no prior exposure to the dissection room, were randomized to either (1) an intervention group that received a VR-based immersive tour of the dissection environment, or (2) a control group that received a conventional introduction with photos and videos. The primary outcome was change in state anxiety, measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-State) before and after the intervention. Secondary outcomes included physiological stress measured by heart rate and overall satisfaction with the educational experience. A total of 233 students were analyzed (intervention group: n = 87; control group: n = 146), with comparable baseline demographic and psychological characteristics. Following the intervention, the intervention group showed a slight decrease in STAI-State score (from 46.7 to 46.5), whereas the control group experienced an increase (from 45.6 to 46.2), resulting in a statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.048). Changes in heart rate during dissection did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.317). Among students exposed to VR, the overall satisfaction with practical sessions was rated 7.6/10 (SD 1.2). Taken together, the present findings showed that immersive VR preparation modestly but significantly reduced pre-dissection anxiety, with high acceptability among medical students.

Title: Impact of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors Control on Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis in Chronic Hepatitis B.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) on the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) axis in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis enrolling patients with CHB who were on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs). CMRFs were defined as per established criteria; poorly-controlled CMRFs were defined with specific cut-offs measured across 5 years. Study outcomes include fibrosis progression (liver stiffness [LS] increase by ≥ 20%), liver-related events (LREs), chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 714 NUC-treated patients (median age: 61.0 [54.5-66.7] years; 69.6% male; 90.5% undetectable HBV DNA, median NUCs duration of 14.1 [11.3-16.5] years) were followed up for 9.7 (7.2-10.2) years. LREs occurred in 112 (15.7%) patients, with annual incidence rate of 1.62 events per 100 person-years. All-cause mortality was observed in 86 (12%) patients, including 47 (6.6%) liver-related mortality. The number or types of CMRFs did not display a linear positive relationship with adverse clinical outcomes. The presence of ≥ 1 poorly controlled CMRFs is independently associated with LREs (aHR: 2.001, 95% CI: 1.350-2.965), MACE (aHR: 1.042, 95% CI: 1.030-1.081), and all-cause mortality (aHR: 2.082, 95% CI: 1.006-4.310), whereas patients having ≥ 2 and ≥ 3 poorly controlled CMRFs are independently associated with CKD progression (aOR: 1.887, 95% CI: 1.115-3.221) and fibrosis progression (aOR: 1.624, 95% CI: 1.164-2.266), respectively. The results remain robust in patients without advanced fibrosis (LS ≤ 10 kPa) at baseline.
CONCLUSION: Active optimization of CMRFs should be an integral component of CHB management in addition to NUCs therapy.

Title: Accuracy of Large Language Model Chatbots in Retrieving MRI Safety Conditions for Medical Implants.
Journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrieving MRI safety conditions for implanted devices is increasingly complex and time-consuming.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the accuracy of internet-enabled large language model (LLM) chatbots in retrieving implant-specific MRI safety conditions, using manufacturer documentation as the reference standard.
STUDY TYPE: Prospective comparative evaluation in a constructed device cohort, followed by a retrospective clinical pilot.
POPULATION: Fifty purposively selected device configurations and 20 patients (10 with cardiac and 10 with noncardiac devices) referred to the MRI Safety Committee.
FIELD STRENGTH: No field-strength or sequence restrictions.
ASSESSMENT: Standardized single-shot prompts requested eight parameters from ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5: MRI safety label, field strengths, eligible regions/centering, transmit-coil restrictions, RF exposure limits, maximum spatial gradient, maximum gradient slew rate, and scan duration. Two radiologists (10 and 25 years' experience) and an MRI technologist (32 years) independently scored 1200 parameter-level outputs against manufacturer Instructions for use and technical manuals using a 5-point scale (5, fully correct; 1, substantively incorrect or fabricated); scores of 4-5 indicated accuracy. In the pilot, 160 outputs from ChatGPT-5.6, a newer version of the best-performing chatbot, were scored identically.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Intraclass correlation coefficient; Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1); Friedman test; Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; device-clustered bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs); two-sided significance threshold, p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Mean ordinal scores were 4.76 (ChatGPT), 4.20 (Gemini), and 4.17 (Claude); ChatGPT scored significantly higher. Respective pooled parameter-level accuracies were 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-0.98), 0.79 (0.71-0.86), and 0.78 (0.69-0.87). Pilot accuracy with ChatGPT-5.6 was 0.98 (95% CI, 0.94-1.00).
DATA CONCLUSION: Internet-enabled LLM chatbots correctly retrieved up to 94% of MRI safety parameters in the constructed cohort and 98% in the clinical pilot. Errors occurred even with the best-performing chatbot, requiring direct verification against current manufacturer documentation before clinical use.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: Stage 2.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

Title: Impact of chronic antiplatelet therapy on clinical outcomes of posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (PCS) is a leading cause of neurologic disability, yet the hospital course of patients receiving chronic antiplatelet therapy (cAPT) remains unclear. This study evaluates the effect of cAPT on PCS outcomes, including patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the National Inpatient Sample (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations in the United States for PCS with reported NIH Stroke Scale. Outcomes included inpatient mortality, routine discharge, complications, and receipt of reperfusion therapy. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for confounding factors, including stroke severity. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 148,740 PCS hospitalizations, 46,125 (31.0%) were receiving cAPT. These patients demonstrated reduced likelihood of undergoing intravascular thrombolysis (aOR: 0.902, 95% CI [0.835-0.975], p = 0.009) and EVT (0.868 [0.764-0.987], p = 0.031) compared to patients not on cAPT. Following IPTW, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.581 [0.496-0.680], p < 0.001) and increased routine discharge (1.14 [1.08-1.21], p < 0.001). These patients also demonstrated reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.767 [0.695-0.846], p < 0.001) and cerebral edema/herniation (0.761 [0.698-0.831], p < 0.001). Among hospitalizations undergoing EVT, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.556 [0.408-0.757], p < 0.001), increased routine discharge (1.60 [1.18-2.16], p = 0.003), and reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.778 [0.705-0.858], p < 0.001).
DISCUSSION: cAPT was associated with favorable inpatient outcomes in PCS, including lower mortality without an increased risk of serious neurological complications. Positive associations persisted among patients undergoing EVT. Prospective research is needed to confirm these results and guide therapeutic strategies.

Title: Speech- and Text-Based Emotion Recognition in Anesthesiology Residents During Critical Incident Simulation Training: Exploratory Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Communication during crisis management involves not only the exchange of clinical information but also the expression and regulation of emotional tone and sentiment, which may reflect clinician performance during a critical incident. In simulation-based medical education, these emotional dynamics are rarely measured objectively, limiting the ability to capture aspects of performance relevant to competency assessment.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether automatically extracted speech- and text-based emotion signals varied across predefined phases of critical incident simulation training and whether these signals were associated with expert-rated performance among anesthesiology residents.
METHODS: In this exploratory observational study, we analyzed 164 simulated crisis scenarios performed by 90 anesthesiology residents from 17 hospitals during a national board preparation workshop. Each high-fidelity simulation comprised 4 predefined phases: initial condition, extreme deterioration, advanced cardiovascular life support (ACLS) management, and recovery. Resident speech was isolated and analyzed using a speech-based emotion recognition (SER) model that estimated 8 emotion categories per utterance. Speech was also automatically transcribed and analyzed using text-based emotion recognition (TER), which estimated 9 emotion categories. Expert anesthesiologists rated performance on a 1-5 scale. ANOVA tested associations between emotion categories and performance, as well as variation across simulation phases. Exploratory mixed-effects sensitivity analyses accounted for repeated simulations and scenario-level clustering.
RESULTS: After 7 recordings were excluded because of technical issues, 65 of 164 (39.6%) simulations were classified as poor performance (score ≤2), 72 (43.9%) as intermediate, and 27 (16.5%) as excellent (score=5). SER categories differed across performance groups (F2,161=4.61; P=.02): poor performance showed more fear and surprise, whereas excellent performance showed more calm, happiness, and neutrality. In mixed-effects analyses, performance group remained associated with happy, angry, fearful, surprise, calm, and neutral speech-emotion proportions after false discovery rate correction. The largest excellent vs poor differences were observed for neutral (+4.24 percentage points), happy (+4.11), and surprise (-3.17) speech affect. TER showed a directionally similar but nonsignificant omnibus association (F2,161=2.57; P=.08); mixed-effects analyses identified associations with happy and sad text-emotion proportions after correction. During extreme deterioration and ACLS management, fear and surprise together accounted for 64.1% and 64.6% of classified speech emotions, respectively, among poor performances. During ACLS management, neutral and calm emotions accounted for 49.1% and 37.7%, respectively, among excellent performances.
CONCLUSIONS: Automated speech- and text-based emotion recognition captured phase-dependent affective communication patterns during critical incident simulations. Speech-derived features were more consistently associated with expert-rated performance, whereas text-derived findings were more exploratory and emotion-specific. These markers may complement simulation debriefing and formative feedback, but validation using multirater outcomes, preregistered adjusted models, and larger multicenter datasets is needed before they inform competency assessment.

Title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

Title: Factors associated with ablation zone resorption after microwave ablation in solitary T1aN0M0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: baseline lesion volume and microcalcification.
Journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify preoperative factors associated with ablation zone resorption after microwave ablation (MWA) in patients with solitary T1aN0M0 papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to explore their association with energy density.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with solitary T1aN0M0 PTC who underwent MWA in our institution between September 2013 and January 2021. Ablation zone volume was measured at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months post-ablation, and annually thereafter. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with ablation zone resorption. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared cumulative resorption rates among subgroups. Energy density was compared across subgroups.
RESULTS: A total of 296 patients were included, with an overall complete resorption rate of 73.6%. Multivariable Cox analysis identified baseline lesion volume (HR per IQR: 0.788, 95% CI: 0.678-0.917, p = 0.002) and microcalcification (HR: 0.669, 95% CI: 0.508-0.881, p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with delayed ablation zone resorption. Both factors were significantly correlated with energy density: the large-volume group (>52.1 mm³) received lower energy density than the small-volume group (≤52.1 mm³) (median 18.3 vs. 60.5 J/mm³, p < 0.001), and energy density was also lower in the microcalcification group than in those without (median 25.6 vs. 35.2 J/mm³, p = 0.030).
CONCLUSION: MWA is an effective and safe treatment for solitary T1aN0M0 PTC. Baseline lesion volume and microcalcification are independent factors associated with delayed ablation zone resorption, and their correlation with energy density provides a rationale for optimizing energy delivery strategies to facilitate resorption.

Title: Learning Curve of Robotic Atrial Septal Defect Repair: A Multidimensional CUSUM Analysis of 284 Consecutive Cases.
Journal: The international journal of medical robotics + computer assisted surgery : MRCAS
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise the learning curve of robotic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair using a multidimensional cumulative sum (CUSUM) framework.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 284 consecutive adult patients undergoing robotic ASD repair were analysed. CUSUM analysis was applied to operative time, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and hospital stay. Learning phases were identified according to inflection points of the CUSUM curves.
RESULTS: Four distinct learning phases were observed. Technical proficiency was achieved at Case 158, marked by significant reductions in operative (186.8 ± 43.3 vs. 133.7 ± 27.7 min), bypass, and cross-clamp times (p < 0.001). ICU stay and transfusion requirements progressively declined, while mortality remained low across all phases. Notably, postoperative care optimisation lagged behind technical mastery.
CONCLUSIONS: Multidimensional CUSUM analysis provides an objective, performance-based assessment of robotic ASD learning. Competency acquisition required substantial case volume, underscoring the need for structured training and longitudinal performance monitoring in robotic cardiac surgery.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Conventional Versus Lateral-Deployment RF Cannulas in Lumbar Medial Branch Radiofrequency Ablation: A Prospective Randomized Study.
Journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare conventional monopolar and lateral-deployment RF cannulas for lumbar medial branch radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in chronic facet-mediated low back pain.
DESIGN: Single-center, randomized, participant-blinded, two-arm superiority trial. Ninety participants were randomized 1:1; 84 with complete 6-month data were analyzed. The primary outcome was change in Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain intensity from baseline to 6 months. Secondary outcomes were changes in the Modified Oswestry Disability Index (MODI) and SF-12 Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Scores.
RESULTS: Mean NRS change was -2.81 points with the conventional cannula and -5.52 points with the lateral-deployment cannula. The age-adjusted between-group difference was -2.795 points (95% CI, -3.967 to -1.624; P<0.001). At 6 months, at least 50% NRS reduction was achieved by 16/42 (38.1%) and 31/42 (73.8%) participants, respectively (risk ratio, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.27-2.97; P=0.001). Age-adjusted MODI and SF-12 PCS changes favored the lateral-deployment cannula. No major procedure-related complications were observed.
CONCLUSION: The lateral-deployment cannula was associated with greater 6-month improvements in pain, disability, and physical health and with more participants achieving substantial pain relief. Larger trials with intention-to-treat analyses are needed.

Title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026.
EXPERT OPINION: The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.

Title: Pregnancy outcome after first-trimester exposure to JAK inhibitors - an evaluation of the German Embryotox cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are increasingly being used in the management of autoimmune diseases across rheumatology, gastroenterology, and dermatology, including in women of childbearing age. Consequently, pregnancies occurring during JAKi treatment are becoming more common. However, uncertainties regarding their safety during pregnancy remain, and current human data are insufficient to allow a comprehensive assessment of fetal risk.
METHODS: Observational data of pregnancies with first trimester JAKi exposure, recorded in the German Embryotox database, was analyzed. Pregnancies were prospectively enrolled between January 1, 2017, and November 15, 2025. Study endpoints included major congenital anomalies, pregnancy loss, and neonatal parameters.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised a total of 44 pregnancies exposed to baricitinib (n = 17), filgotinib (n = 3), tofacitinib (n = 8), or upadacitinib (n = 16). A total of 32 live births were recorded. Among these, two major congenital anomalies were observed, one ventricular septal defect and one hypospadias. Five spontaneous abortions occurred, including one case of fetal anencephaly, and seven elective terminations of pregnancy were reported. Additional neonatal assessments revealed two preterm births at 36 weeks' gestation, three infants born small for gestational age, and two newborns large for gestational age.
CONCLUSIONS: The current evidence is insufficient to establish or exclude an association between JAK inhibitor exposure and adverse fetal outcomes. To date, the potential for harmful effects cannot be ruled out due to the limited available data. Therefore, routine use of JAKi during pregnancy is not recommended and treatment should be approached with caution, and requires a critical risk-benefit assessment until further data is obtained.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was retrospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on March 16, 2026 (DRKS00039622).

Title: Evaluating the therapeutic benefits and safety of ecnoglutide for type 2 diabetes: evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a growing global health challenge, necessitating effective therapies that improve glycemic control and promote weight loss. Ecnoglutide, a novel cAMP-biased GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonist, has emerged as a promising therapeutic option.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted following PRISMA and AMSTAR-2 guidelines. Electronic databases were searched up to February 2026. Eligible studies included adult patients with T2DM comparing ecnoglutide with placebo or active comparators. Outcomes included glycemic parameters, anthropometric measures, metabolic indices, and safety. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Three RCTs comprising 979 participants were included. Ecnoglutide significantly reduced HbA1c (MD -0.57%, 95% CI -0.86 to -0.29) and fasting plasma glucose (MD -1.11 mmol/L, 95% CI -1.58 to -0.65), with a higher proportion achieving target HbA1c (RR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37-1.80). Significant reductions in body weight (MD -1.83 kg) and waist circumference (MD -1.53 cm) were also observed. Improvements in insulin resistance and lipid parameters were noted. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not establish a clear dose response relationship, while short-term trials showed larger glycemic reductions compared with longer follow up. Adverse events were more frequent but not statistically significant, with no increase in serious adverse events.
CONCLUSION: Ecnoglutide demonstrates significant efficacy in improving glycemic control and weight-related outcomes in T2DM, with a safety profile comparable to existing GLP-1 receptor agonists. However, larger and longer-term studies are needed to confirm its cardiovascular benefits and long-term safety.

Title: Comparison of the effects of aquatic HIIT and MICT on central hemodynamics, endothelial function, and aerobic fitness in obese school-aged children: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aquatic exercise may be a feasible strategy for improving cardiovascular health in children with obesity, but evidence comparing aquatic high-intensity interval training (aHIIT) and aquatic moderate-intensity continuous training (aMICT) remains limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial compared the effects of 8 weeks of aHIIT and aMICT on endothelial function, estimated cardiorespiratory fitness, central hemodynamic indices, arterial stiffness, and anthropometric indicators in school-aged children with obesity.
METHODS: Thirty-three children with obesity were randomized to the aHIIT group (n = 11), aMICT group (n = 11), or non-exercise control group (n = 11). The two aquatic exercise groups trained 3 days/week for 8 weeks. The aHIIT protocol consisted of 10 × 30-s high-intensity aquatic exercise (such as freestyle swimming or freestyle kicking) bouts at 80%-90% HRmax, separated by 60-s recovery intervals, whereas the aMICT protocol consisted of two 15-min continuous breaststroke bouts at 60%-70% HRmax, separated by a 5-min recovery interval. Brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) was used as the principal vascular outcome. Central hemodynamic indices were assessed using applanation tonometry, and estimated VO2max was obtained from the 20-m shuttle run test. Intervention effects were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, with the group × time interaction used as the primary test for differential intervention effects.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions were observed for estimated VO2max, FMD, AIx, and AIx@HR75. Estimated VO2max increased in both aquatic exercise groups compared with the control group. FMD improved in both exercise groups, with a greater increase observed after aHIIT. AIx and AIx@HR75 showed favorable changes after aMICT. No significant group × time interactions were observed for resting blood pressure, SEVR, ABI, cfPWV, or baPWV.
CONCLUSION: This pilot trial suggests that both aHIIT and aMICT may improve estimated cardiorespiratory fitness in school-aged children with obesity. aHIIT may be associated with greater improvement in brachial artery endothelial function, whereas aMICT may have favorable effects on selected wave-reflection-related indices. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, indirect estimated VO2max estimation, lack of maturation assessment, and unmatched exercise workload.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registration, ChiCTR2400080687.05/02/2024.

Title: Post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation and hydrocephalus in preterm infants: a five-year retrospective cohort study from a tertiary referral center.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH) is a serious complication of intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) in preterm infants and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although neonatal risk factors are well described, the contribution of maternal and perinatal factors remains inconsistent across studies.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and independent predictors of PHH among preterm neonates with IVH, and to evaluate early outcomes in a tertiary referral center.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included preterm neonates (< 34 weeks' gestation or birth weight ≤ 1500 g) with ultrasound-confirmed IVH admitted to Namazi Hospital, Shiraz, Iran, between March 2019 and March 2024. Demographic, maternal, perinatal, and neonatal variables were extracted from medical records. PHH was defined as progressive ventricular dilatation following IVH. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PHH.
RESULTS: Among 507 neonates with IVH, 154 (30.4%) developed PHH. Infants with PHH had significantly lower birth weight and gestational age and higher rates of maternal diabetes and neonatal meningitis.Each 100-g increase in birth weight was associated with a 24% reduction in the odds of developing post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (OR 0.76; 95% CI 0.7-0.83; p < 0.001).Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus/diabetes was a significant risk factor (OR 2.14; 95% CI 1.39-3.29; p = 0.001) Antenatal steroid exposure was associated with lower odds of PHH, possibly reflecting reduced hemorrhage severity(OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.35-0.80; p = 0.003).Mortality was borderline higher among infants with PHH (p = 0.05), while the need for surgical intervention was significantly higher in this group (p < 0.001).The primary clinical model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.19) and acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.75).
CONCLUSION: PHH remains a frequent and severe complication of IVH in preterm neonates. Both neonatal and selected maternal factors contribute to PHH risk, underscoring the importance of comprehensive perinatal assessment and early identification of high-risk infants.

Title: Persistent pocket-site pain after cardiac implantable electronic device implantation: a prospective observational study of prevalence, neuropathic characteristics, and quality of life.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transvenous cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation is generally considered a minor procedure, long-lasting pocket-site pain may represent an underrecognized clinical problem. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, characteristics, and clinical impact of persistent pain after CIED implantation.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients who underwent first-time CIED implantation and attended routine outpatient follow-up visits. Pain intensity was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and neuropathic pain characteristics were evaluated using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 Questions (DN-4) questionnaire. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the Short Form-12 (SF-12). Demographic and clinical data were also recorded.
RESULTS: A total of 102 patients were included in the analysis. Persistent implantation-site pain (VAS ≥ 4) was reported by 22.5% of patients. Neuropathic pain characteristics (DN-4 ≥ 4) were identified in 26.5% of patients. A moderate positive correlation was observed between VAS and DN-4 scores (ρ = 0.473, p < 0.001). However, the association between VAS ≥ 4 and DN-4 ≥ 4 was not statistically significant and had a small effect size (p = 0.118; φ = 0.15). Pain intensity was moderately negatively correlated with the SF-12 physical component score, indicating reduced physical quality of life with increasing pain severity, while mental quality of life was not significantly affected.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent pocket-site pain after CIED implantation affected a clinically meaningful proportion of patients despite generally low overall pain scores. Higher DN-4 scores were associated with poorer physical and mental quality of life and may provide additional clinical information in selected patients. However, because the categorical association between VAS-defined persistent pain and DN-4 positivity was not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger prospective studies.

Title: Triglyceride glucose index, metabolic comorbidity, and cardiovascular disease: a national cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a widely accepted surrogate biomarker of insulin resistance, strongly predicts cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. However, the mediating role of metabolic comorbidities in explaining the relationship between the TyG index and cardiovascular disease remains underexplored. Leveraging the longitudinal data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), this longitudinal study investigates how metabolic comorbidities mediate the association between the TyG index and cardiovascular risk.
METHODS: This analysis included 9,400 participants aged ≥ 45 years from CHARLS without baseline CVD. The TyG index was computed as Ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Incident cardiovascular events, which were defined as physician-confirmed heart disease or stroke, were monitored until 2020. Adjusted Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HR). The mediation analysis quantified the percentage of excess risk (PERM) attributable to metabolic comorbidities.
RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 59.0 ± 9.5 years, and 4 862 (51.7%) were females. Among eligible participants, 2,152 developed cardiovascular diseases over a 9-year follow-up, with 1,627 heart disease cases and 765 strokes. Compared with people with a lower TyG index (< 8.59 [median level]) and no comorbidity, those concurrently with a higher TyG and comorbidity had the highest risk of CVD (adjusted HR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.47-1.88), coronary heart disease (aHR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.25-1.66) and stroke (aHR, 2.94; 95% CI, 2.31-3.75). Metabolic comorbidities mediated 48.3% of the TyG-associated CVD risk, predominantly through hypertension, renal impairment, inflammation, and obesity.
CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the partial mediating role of metabolic comorbidities in the TyG index-CVD association. Future research should explore residual pathways to fully elucidate this association.

Title: ApoB/ApoA-I ratio and all-cause mortality in maintenance hemodialysis: a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional lipid markers have limited and inconsistent prognostic value in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), a phenomenon often described as the lipid paradox. We evaluated whether lipid and apolipoprotein-related markers, particularly the ApoB/ApoA-I ratio, were associated with mortality in MHD patients.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 409 MHD patients. Lipid and apolipoprotein-related markers were analyzed as standardized continuous variables. Cox regression was used for all-cause mortality, and cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray models were used for cardiovascular mortality.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 55.7 months, 148 all-cause deaths occurred, including 61 cardiovascular deaths. ApoB/ApoA-I was not associated with all-cause mortality in the unadjusted model, but was independently associated with all-cause mortality in Model 3 (hazard ratio [HR] 1.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-1.44; p = 0.012). The association was similar in sensitivity analyses. ApoB/ApoA-I was not significantly associated with cardiovascular mortality in exploratory Fine-Gray regression (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.12, 95% CI 0.89-1.43; p = 0.337) and did not improve discrimination beyond the base clinical model.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ApoB/ApoA-I may contribute to risk characterization and etiologic understanding in MHD, but do not support its use as a stand-alone clinical prediction marker.

Title: Development and external validation of a preoperative prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after hip fracture surgery in older adults: a retrospective two-center study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with hip fracture are vulnerable to postoperative major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) during hospitalization. However, early risk stratification remains difficult because existing assessments may require complex or late-available information. A simple model based on variables routinely available before surgery may support perioperative decision-making.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective two-center cohort study of patients ≥ 60 years who underwent surgery for traumatic hip fracture at 2 hospitals in China. The development cohort included 935 patients treated between January 2024 and December 2025, and the external validation cohort included 168 patients treated between January 2020 and December 2025. Candidate preoperative predictors were screened using penalized regression. Six candidate prediction models were developed and compared using the same preprocessing pipeline. The final model was calibrated using Platt scaling. Model performance was assessed in an internal test set and an external validation cohort.
RESULTS: In the development cohort, 122 of 935 patients developed postoperative in-hospital MACE. The final model was a Platt-calibrated logistic regression model including age, baseline electrocardiographic abnormality, chronic heart failure, serum potassium, albumin, and hemoglobin. In the internal test set, the model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.814, with a 95% CI of 0.748-0.876, and a Brier score of 0.102. At the prespecified threshold of 0.147, sensitivity was 0.710 and specificity was 0.754. In the external validation cohort, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.760, with a 95% CI of 0.657-0.849. The Brier score was 0.141, sensitivity was 0.788, specificity was 0.630, and negative predictive value was 0.924.
CONCLUSIONS: A simple preoperative logistic regression model based on routinely available clinical variables showed moderate discrimination in internal testing and provided preliminary external validation evidence for predicting postoperative in-hospital MACE after hip fracture surgery in older adults. The model may support early perioperative risk stratification and postoperative surveillance, although prospective multicenter validation and recalibration are needed before wider clinical use.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Development and validation of a predictive model for delayed emergence from anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed emergence from anesthesia is a common perioperative complication in elderly patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), which may lead to prolonged recovery and increased healthcare burden. However, predictive tools specifically developed for this population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a practical model to identify patients at increased risk of delayed emergence from anesthesia.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 1,400 elderly patients who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) at a tertiary hospital in Beijing between January 2020 and April 2026. An additional temporally independent cohort of 300 patients was used for temporal validation. Perioperative variables, including baseline characteristics, comorbidities, intraoperative parameters, and laboratory indicators, were collected. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the model. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and temporal validation with subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Delayed emergence occurred in 210 patients (15.00%). Six independent predictors were identified: myocardial infarction, colloid solution use, bradycardia, end-tidal CO2 < 35 mmHg, hypothermia, and APTT. The model showed excellent discrimination in the derivation cohort (AUC = 0.909, 95% CI 0.888-0.929) with good calibration and clinical utility. In the temporal validation cohort, it maintained good discrimination (AUC = 0.863) and clinical usefulness, although calibration showed some deviation from ideal agreement. Subgroup analysis suggested better performance in patients aged ≥ 80 years.
CONCLUSIONS: The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination and clinical utility for predicting delayed emergence from anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing VATS. It may facilitate perioperative risk assessment and individualized perioperative management, although further recalibration may be required before external application.

Title: Accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) for the upper limb recovery after subacute stroke (ATLAS): study protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is the second leading cause of death globally, with residual upper limb dysfunction being a major contributor to its high disability rate. Currently, there remains a lack of effective rehabilitation approaches to substantially improve upper limb dysfunction. While transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has shown potential in promoting functional reorganization in stroke patients, more effective treatment protocols are still under exploration.
