Stent geometry before and after correction was compared across four segments and with the randomized single-stent PKP arm.
RESULTS: The result was suboptimal in 22 of 30 patients (73.3%); 16 had paired OCT. After correction, minimal stent area increased in the proximal (12.5 to 14.6 mm2) and distal main vessel (7.4 to 9.1 mm2), both significant after Holm correction, and distal underexpansion fell from 13/16 (81%) to 5/16 (31%). Proximal-edge and bifurcation-core gains and the reduction in malapposition did not survive correction; eccentricity did not change significantly. No significant difference from the single-stent PKP arm was found, but the study had 80% power only for differences of 2.1 to 3.3 mm2. Of eight results judged optimal, six still showed distal underexpansion.
CONCLUSIONS: A suboptimal PSP result can be improved in the same procedure by corrective kissing-balloon inflation and final POT, mainly through larger main-vessel stent area and expansion. It did not differ significantly from an upfront PKP, but equivalence cannot be established. A PSP result judged optimal during the procedure is not necessarily optimal at offline OCT analysis.

Title: [Clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical characteristics and prognosis of atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR). Methods: This was a single-center retrospective study. Patients hospitalized at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 2020 and March 2022 and diagnosed with significant functional mitral regurgitation were enrolled. According to the type of regurgitation, patients were divided into the AFMR group and the ventricular functional mitral regurgitation (VFMR) group. Clinical and echocardiographic data were compared between the two groups. The patients were followed up until April 2024. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was the composite of cardiac death and hospitalization for heart failure. Survival was compared between the two groups using Kaplan-Meier survival curves. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Results: The study cohort consisted of 269 patients, with a median age of 66.0 (57.5, 76.0) years, among whom 172 (63.9%) were male. Patients were divided into the AFMR group (n=61, 22.7%) and the VFMR group (n=208, 77.3%). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group had a higher proportion of female patients, older age, a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, lower prevalences of coronary artery disease, fewer patients with heart failure symptoms, and a lower proportion of prior visits to cardiovascular departments (all P<0.05). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group demonstrated significantly larger anteroposterior left atrial diameter, right atrial transverse diameter, and right ventricular transverse diameter, along with a higher LVEF and a higher prevalence of moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (all P<0.05). The follow-up duration was 24.6 (5.8, 37.6) months. The AFMR group exhibited lower all-cause mortality (21.3% (13/61) vs. 38.9% (81/208), P=0.011) and a lower rate of the composite endpoint of cardiac death and heart failure hospitalization (24.6% (15/61) vs. 42.8% (89/208), P=0.010) than the VFMR group. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis also revealed that the AFMR group had a higher cumulative event-free survival rate than the VFMR group (Plog-rank=0.002). Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression analysis demonstrated that age (HR=1.038, 95%CI 1.019-1.057, P<0.001), cerebrovascular disease (HR=2.014, 95%CI 1.200-3.382, P=0.008), AFMR (HR=0.341, 95%CI 0.175-0.667, P=0.002), and moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (HR=2.297, 95%CI 1.467-3.596, P<0.001) were independent predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Conclusions: Compared with VFMR, AFMR is more common among elderly patients, female patients, and patients with atrial fibrillation and is less frequently accompanied by heart failure symptoms. The rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure are both lower in the AFMR group than those in the VFMR group.

Title: [Dual association of peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death in patients with coronary artery disease: a large-scale cohort study].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and its clinical prognostic value in patients with coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and receiving clopidogrel. Methods: This was a single-center prospective cohort study. Consecutive patients with coronary artery disease who underwent PCI at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January and December 2013 were enrolled; those receiving dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel were included. Baseline data were collected, and platelet reactivity was assessed using thromboelastography. Patients were followed up for 5 years, with cardiac death as the endpoint. Baseline eosinophil count was analyzed as a continuous variable and was also categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4). Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze the association between eosinophil count and high on-treatment platelet reactivity. Multivariable restricted cubic spline models were used to analyze the dose-response relationship. Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed according to age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to assess the predictive value of eosinophil count for cardiac death. Results: A total of 6 524 patients were included. The mean age was (58.21±10.26) years, and 5 059 (77.54%) were male. Among them, 6 050 patients completed the 5-year follow-up, and 140 cardiac deaths (2.31%) occurred. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was negatively associated with the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (OR=0.94, 95%CI: 0.90-0.98, P=0.003). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the lowest quartile group (Q1), the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity was lower in patients in the highest quartile group (Q4) (OR=0.77, 95%CI: 0.65-0.91, P=0.003). Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis showed a linear negative correlation between eosinophil count and the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (P for overall=0.012, P for nonlinearity=0.362). Further subgroup analysis showed that the above association remained consistent across clinical subgroups stratified by age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels (all P for interaction>0.05). Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was positively associated with the risk of cardiac death (HR=1.14, 95%CI: 1.07-1.21, P<0.001). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the Q1 group, the risk of cardiac death was higher in patients in the Q4 group (HR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.25-3.59, P<0.001). Conclusions: In patients with coronary artery disease undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel, baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count showed a dual association with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death. A lower count was associated with an increased risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, whereas an elevated count was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiac death.

Title: [The incidence and 1-year prognosis of heart failure following myocardial infarction during hospitalization in patients with first STEMI].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the incidence of in-hospital heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) and 1-year mortality in patients with first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to compare the 1-year mortality risk among different types of HF. Methods: Data were derived from the Henan STEMI registry, which was a multicentre, prospective, observational study in central China. After excluding patients with a history of MI or HF, patients with first STEMI were divided into the HF and non-HF groups according to the occurrence of in-hospital HF. Based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measured on the last echocardiogram during hospitalization, patients with HF were classified into HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF≥50%), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF, LVEF 41%-49%), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF≤40%), and HF with missing LVEF. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed with the log-rank test. Multivariate Cox frailty models were used to analyze the associations of HF status (present vs. absent) and different LVEF subgroups with 1-year mortality, using the non-HF group as the reference. Results: A total of 4 737 patients with first STEMI were included in the final analysis, with a median age of 62.8 (52.4, 70.8) years, of whom 1 158 (24.4%) were female. During hospitalization, 1 978 cases (41.8%) developed HF following MI, including 268 (13.5%) with HFrEF, 309 (15.6%) with HFmrEF, 707 (35.7%) with HFpEF, and 694 (35.1%) with missing LVEF. A total of 3 967 (83.7%) patients completed the 1-year follow-up. The 1-year mortality was significantly higher among STEMI patients complicated by HF than in those without (23.3% (391/1 680) vs. 5.8% (132/2 287), log-rank P<0.001). Specifically, the rates were 29.6% (67/226) for HFrEF, 20.8% (53/255) for HFmrEF, 11.7% (72/615) for HFpEF and 34.1% (199/584) for HF with missing LVEF. Multivariate Cox frailty models identified in-hospital HF following MI as a risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR=2.13, 95%CI: 1.70-2.67). Notably, HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk of 1-year mortality (HR=1.59, 95%CI: 1.16-2.17), while the HF group with missing LVEF carried the highest risk (HR=2.49, 95%CI: 1.91-3.26). Conclusions: The incidence of HF following first STEMI during hospitalization was 41.8%, with a corresponding 1-year mortality of 23.3%. In-hospital HF following MI is a risk factor for 1-year mortality in patients with STEMI. Prognosis differed notably across HF subgroups: HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk, whereas patients with missing LVEF had the worst outcome.
Publication Types: English Abstract; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: [The predictive value of left ventricular strain on cardiac magnetic resonance for adverse events in children and adolescent patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking in evaluating left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), as well as its prognostic value for adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. Patients with primary HCM aged ≤21 years who underwent standard CMR examination at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January 2010 and December 2018 were included. Baseline clinical and CMR data were collected, and follow-up was completed. The primary endpoint was composite adverse cardiovascular events, and the secondary endpoint was heart failure-related events. Patients were divided into the event group and the non-event group according to whether the primary endpoint occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Using the cohort median left ventricular GLS of -9.2% as the cut-off value, patients were stratified into the preserved GLS group (≤-9.2%) and the impaired GLS group (>-9.2%). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted, and the log-rank test was performed to compare survival differences between groups. Results: A total of 249 children and adolescents with HCM were included, aged (14.81±3.71)years, of whom 163 were males (65.5%). The follow-up duration was (66.59±33.00)months. Composite endpoint events occurred in 37 patients, including 17 heart failure-related events and 20 sudden cardiac death events; 212 patients remained event-free. After adjusting for confounders such as left ventricular ejection fraction and history of unexplained syncope, multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that the percentage of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and left ventricular GLS were independently associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.18, 95%CI 1.04-1.35, P=0.014; LGE extent: HR=1.12, 95%CI 1.06-1.18,P<0.001) and heart failure-related events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.52, 95%CI 1.18-1.96, P=0.001; LGE extent: HR=1.14, 95%CI 1.04-1.24, P=0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with impaired left ventricular GLS had lower cumulative event-free survival for both composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events compared with those with preserved GLS (log-rank all P<0.001). Conclusions: CMR feature-tracking can effectively assess left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary HCM. Left ventricular GLS and LGE percentage are independently associated with the risk of adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events in this patient population.

Title: [Expert consensus on non-invasive cardiac imaging for the evaluation of heart failure].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi

Title: [The principles of trend-in-trend design and its applications in real-world causal inference].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: The trend-in-trend (TIT) design is an emerging hybrid ecological- epidemiological research method. Based on cumulative exposure probability stratification and cross-stratum temporal trend differentiation, TIT compares differences in outcome temporal slopes across populations with distinct exposure rates. When its core assumptions are met, TIT effectively controls unmeasured confounding by indication and time-varying confounding, thereby inferring causal associations between exposure and outcomes and yielding more robust effect estimates than traditional cohort studies. This article systematically elaborates the statistical principles and core assumptions of the TIT design, compares its methodological characteristics with quasi-experimental methods including difference-in-differences and interrupted time series, and illustrates its implementation procedures through a case study evaluating the cardiovascular risk of rofecoxib. As a reliable methodological tool for real-world study, TIT is particularly applicable to post-marketing drug re-evaluation and scenarios with strong temporal trends and unmeasured confounding.

Title: [Association of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation and offspring betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase (BHMT) and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms with congenital heart disease].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: Objective: To evaluate the associations of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation, offspring BHMT and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms and their interactions with the risk for congenital heart disease (CHD) and its main subtypes. Methods: A hospital-based case control study was conducted. From January 2018 to May 2019, a total of 620 children with simple CHD and their mothers were consecutively recruited as the case group from Hunan Children's Hospital. During the same period, 620 children without any congenital anomalies and their mothers, who were diagnosed at the same hospital, were enrolled as the control group. The information about their demographic characteristics and periconceptional exposure information were collected by using structured questionnaire. In addition, peripheral venous blood samples were obtained from the children for genotyping of BHMT and BHMT2 polymorphisms. Multivariable logistic regression analysis and crossover analyses were conducted to evaluate the associations of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation, offspring BHMT and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms and their interactions with the risk for CHD and its subtypes. Results: After correction for multiple testing, multivariable logistic regression analyses showed that maternal excessive intakes of smoked food, barbecued food, fried food, pickled vegetable during early pregnancy was associated with increased risk for overall CHD in offspring [aOR>1.00, false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted P<0.05], while maternal regular intakes of fish and shrimp, fresh egg, bean, milk product as well as periconceptional folic acid supplementation were associated with reduced risk for offspring overall CHD (aOR<1.00, FDR-adjusted P<0.05). Significant associations were observed between BHMT polymorphisms and overall CHD risk, including rs3733890 (AA vs. GG, aOR=2.61, 95%CI: 1.52-4.50), rs1316753 (recessive model, aOR= 1.63, 95%CI: 1.17-2.29), and rs1915706 (CC vs. TT, aOR=2.72, 95%CI: 1.42-5.21), similar results were also found in atrial septal defect and ventricular septal defect population. Moreover, BHMT gene polymorphisms showed antagonistic interactions with the intake of fish and shrimp, as well as bean (aOR<1.00, relative excess risk of interaction <0). Conclusions: Maternal dietary patterns, folic acid supplementation, and BHMT gene polymorphisms (rs3733890, rs1316753, and rs1915706) are associated with the risk for CHD and its subtypes. In addition, interactions between BHMT polymorphisms and maternal dietary intake might contribute to the development of CHD in offspring.

Title: [Study of changing trends, risk factors and prediction of disease burden of three acquired heart diseases in China, 1990-2023].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: Objective: To analyze the characteristics of disease burden and risk factors of acquired heart diseases in China from 1990 to 2023, predict their trends from 2024 to 2050, and provide data support for the development of prevention and control policies. Methods: Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study, we collected disability-adjusted life year (DALY) data of three types of acquired heart diseases (rheumatic heart disease, hypertensive heart disease, and ischemic heart disease) in China from 1990 to 2023. Joinpoint regression model was used to estimate the average annual percentage change (AAPC) to describe temporal trends. A Bayesian age-period-cohort model was applied to predict the trends from 2024 to 2050. Results: From 1990 to 2023, the age-standardized DALY rates (ASDRs) of the three types of acquired heart diseases in China all exhibited decreasing trends, the AAPCs for rheumatic heart disease, hypertensive heart disease and ischemic heart disease were -6.6%, -3.7% and -0.8%, respectively (all P<0.001). The age group with the highest DALY rate for all the three diseases was ≥80 years, while the lowest was under 20 years. The DALY rates of rheumatic heart disease and hypertensive heart disease declined in all the age groups. For ischemic heart disease, DALY rates decreased in all the age groups except age group ≥80 years. From 2024 to 2050, the ASDRs of rheumatic heart disease and ischemic heart disease are predicted to decline in both men and women. In contrast, the ASDR of hypertensive heart disease is predicted to decline in men but rise in women. In 2023, the top three risk factors for the disease burden of hypertensive heart disease were high systolic blood pressure, high body mass index and high sodium intake. For ischemic heart disease, the top three risk factors were high systolic blood pressure, lead exposure and high LDL-C in China. Conclusions: From 1990 to 2023, the ASDRs of three acquired heart diseases in China all showed declining trends. Predictions for 2024-2050 indicate that, with the exception of hypertensive heart disease ASDR declining in men but rising in women, the ASDRs of other two diseases would continue to decline. Acquired heart disease remains a public health problem to which sustained attention needs to be paid. Targeted prevention and control efforts should focus on modifiable risk factors, with particular emphasis on high systolic blood pressure, high body mass index, and lead exposure.

Title: [Association between fine particulate matter exposure and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in urban and rural elderly population in Beijing].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: Objective: To understand the association between PM2.5 exposure and all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in elderly populations in urban and rural areas of Beijing. Methods: Based on the Beijing Elderly Comprehensive Health Cohort Study, a total of 3 472 study participants with complete baseline data were enrolled according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the information about their survival and mortality outcomes were obtained by follow up. Annual average PM2.5 exposure values were matched using remote sensing grid data and grouped by tertiles. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the associations between PM2.5 exposure and all-cause as well as CVD mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to verify the robustness of the results. Additionally, the interaction between outdoor physical activity and PM2.5 exposure was evaluated. Results: The average annual PM2.5 concentration in living area of the study participants was 79.80 μg/m³ from 2010 to 2014 , much higher than the national grade Ⅱ limit (35 μg/m³). After adjusting for confounding factors, for each 1 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 concentration, the risk for all-cause mortality increased by 5.3% (HR=1.053, 95%CI: 1.026-1.080), and the risk for CVD mortality increased by 4.6% (HR=1.046, 95%CI: 1.001-1.100). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant interaction between outdoor physical activity level and PM2.5 concentration on all-cause mortality (P=0.022). In the group without outdoor physical activity, each 1 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 concentration was associated with an 8.7% increase of risk for all-cause mortality (HR=1.087, 95%CI:1.042-1.134); whereas in the group with outdoor physical activity, the risk increased by 2.6% (HR=1.026, 95%CI: 1.001-1.062). In the group with outdoor physical activity, compared with the reference group, the study participants in the highest PM2.5 T3 group had a 52.3% increased risk for all-cause mortality (HR=1.523, 95%CI:1.171-1.979) and a 79.1% increased risk for CVD mortality (HR=1.791, 95%CI: 1.004-3.192). Conclusions: PM2.5 exposure increases the risks for all-cause mortality and CVD mortality in the elderly population in urban and rural areas in Beijing. Regular physical activity might partially offset the adverse health effects of PM2.5 exposure, but this protective effect is limited under extremely high pollution levels. It is suggested to encourage the elderly to maintain regular physical activity but have indoor physical activity in days when air PM2.5 concentrations are high.

Title: Association of Iron Deficiency Anemia with Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently have iron deficiency anemia (IDA), but the mechanism by which this condition affects clinical outcomes is not well understood. The purpose of this study was to assess whether IDA is associated with mortality in patients with AF.
METHODS: Data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) for 2021-2022 examined IDA and inpatient outcomes in a nationally representative cohort of hospitalized adults diagnosed with AF. Patients were categorized by IDA status. The factors assessed were mortality, hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications, and overall hospital expenses. Hospital, clinical, and demographic factors were included in multivariable logistic and linear regression models.
RESULTS: Of the 8.35 million AF hospitalizations, 7.1% had associated IDA. IDA was linked to multiple comorbidities along with increased risk of hypotension (OR: 1.15, 95% CI 1.12-1.17, P<0.001), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.25, 95% CI 1.23-1.27, P<0.001), and heart failure (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.29, 95% CI 1.27-1.31, P<0.001). Ironically, IDA was linked independently to decreased risks of cardiac arrest (AOR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.66-0.73, P<0.001), transient ischemic attack (AOR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63, P<0.001), stroke (OR: 0.49,95% CI 0.47-0.51, P<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.64-0.68, P<0.001). IDA was also associated with increased hospital expenses and increased LOS (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: IDA was linked to higher morbidity and healthcare use in those with AF admitted to the hospital, but there was a decrease in mortality and thromboembolic events. These results suggest the possibility of tailored iron therapy and imply a complex interaction between IDA and AF-related outcomes.

Title: Timing of Post-Stroke Seizures and Functional Outcomes: Exploring Gender-Based Disparities.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke complications significantly influence functional recovery, with seizures representing a critical determinant of poor outcomes. While acute symptomatic seizures (ASS) may reflect initial injury severity, remote symptomatic seizures (RSS) potentially exacerbate neurological damage. Emerging evidence suggests gender may modulate these relationships, though comprehensive studies remain limited.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to: (1) evaluate the impact of seizure timing (acute vs. remote), and (2) investigate gender-specific disparities in recovery patterns.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case-control study (2018-2021) of 232 patients (116 post-stroke seizure [PSS], 116 controls) matched by age, gender, and stroke type. Stroke severity was assessed using National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale/Score (NIHSS) Calculator, with functional outcomes measured via modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at discharge and 3 months. Statistical analyses included Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney tests for continuous measures, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: PSS patients demonstrated worse functional outcomes, particularly in hemorrhagic strokes (78.3% vs. 21.7% poor outcomes, P<0.001) and right-sided lesions (OR 2.7, P=0.017). Females with RSS had markedly poorer recovery than ASS cases (OR 0.1, 95% CI 0.1-0.9, P=0.015), while males showed no timing-dependent differences. Vascular comorbidities (e.g., chronic kidney disease [OR 37.5], Diabetes mellitus [OR 2.3], and smoking [OR 1.4]) compounded poor outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: RSS, especially in females, and hemorrhagic stroke are high-risk predictors of disability. Targeted seizure prophylaxis and gender-sensitive rehabilitation strategies may improve outcomes. Prospective studies should validate these associations and explore underlying mechanisms.

Title: Impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD): a study from the Australian National CHD Registry.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 1% of live births. Advances in diagnosis and treatment have markedly improved survival, resulting in a growing adult CHD population with an increasing burden of chronic disease. Here we investigate the prevalence and impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in patients with CHD.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Cohort study from the Australian National CHD Registry, linked to national administrative health data. Control patients without T2DM were selected from the Registry and matched 3:1 by age, sex, rurality, and CHD complexity.
RESULTS: Of the 58 523 individuals with CHD in the registry, 2077 (3.55%) were identified as having T2DM. Median age was 43.1 (IQR 32.0–57.9) years, and 51% were female. T2DM was associated with a hazard ratio for all-cause mortality or heart transplantation of 1.51 (95% CI 1.31 to 1.73; p<0.001). 27.6% of CHD patients with T2DM experienced any major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) versus 10.2% of controls (p<0.001). Patients with T2DM had a higher MACE rate (rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001) and had more MACE per patient (odds ratio 4.11, p<0.001) compared with controls. Individuals with T2DM also had significantly higher rates of emergency department presentations than controls (incidence rate ratio 2.35, p<0.001) and higher rates of hospital admissions (incidence rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: T2DM in patients with CHD is associated with significantly lower transplant-free survival, substantially increased MACE, and greater healthcare utilization compared to matched CHD controls.

Title: Effect of perioperative opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia on early postoperative sleep disturbance in adults undergoing elective non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery under general anaesthesia: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Early postoperative sleep disturbance is common after adult non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia and has been consistently associated with worse pain control, increased risk of postoperative delirium, impaired functional recovery and prolonged hospital stay, which imposes a significant burden on both patients and healthcare systems. Opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia is increasingly recommended within enhanced recovery after surgery pathways because it can effectively reduce opioid exposure while maintaining adequate analgesia; however, its specific effect on early postoperative sleep outcomes has not been systematically synthesised to date, leaving a critical gap in evidence-based perioperative care.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We will conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials enrolling adults aged 18 years or older undergoing elective non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery under general anaesthesia. Eligible studies must evaluate a perioperative opioid-sparing multimodal analgesic strategy, with multimodality defined at the level of the overall perioperative analgesic regimen. A single investigational adjunct may be eligible when it has a perioperative analgesic role and is incorporated into a common background analgesic regimen, such that the intervention arm as a whole constitutes multimodal analgesia. Eligible comparators will include opioid-dominant analgesia, placebo, no additional intervention or a common or otherwise comparable background analgesic regimen without the opioid-sparing component of interest. The coprimary outcomes will be subjective sleep quality during the night of surgery or, if unavailable, during the night of postoperative day 1 (POD1), and the incidence of early postoperative sleep disturbance within 3 days after surgery (including the night of surgery). Secondary outcomes will include objective sleep parameters (eg, total sleep time and sleep efficiency), postoperative opioid consumption (converted to intravenous morphine milligram equivalents where possible), pain scores, patient-reported quality of recovery assessed using validated instruments, postoperative nausea and vomiting, delirium, length of hospital stay and intervention-related adverse events. We will search MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Web of Science Core Collection from inception to 30 April 2026 as the initial search cut-off date without language restrictions. The searches will be updated before the final analysis of the systematic review. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform will also be searched for ongoing or unpublished trials, and the reference lists of included studies and relevant systematic reviews will be screened for additional eligible studies. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data and assess risk of bias (ROB) using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses will be performed where studies are clinically and methodologically comparable, and the certainty of evidence for the coprimary outcomes will be appraised using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval is not required because the review will synthesise only published aggregate data and will not involve identifiable patient information. Findings will be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, presented at relevant scientific meetings, and disseminated through academic networks to inform clinical practice. Important protocol amendments will be documented in PROSPERO and in the final review.

Title: High-intensity interval training and moderate-intensity continuous training versus usual care in adults with familial hypercholesterolaemia: protocol for the UPPA-FH three-arm randomised trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) is an inherited disorder associated with lifelong exposure to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) and substantially increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Although intensive lipid-lowering therapy is the cornerstone of management, many individuals remain at elevated residual cardiovascular risk. Exercise training may improve cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), vascular function and cardiometabolic health; however, randomised evidence comparing different exercise modalities in adults with FH is lacking. The UPPA-FH trial aims to evaluate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), compared with usual care, on CRF, subclinical atherosclerosis and cardiometabolic health in adults with FH.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The UPPA-FH is a single-centre, three-arm, parallel-group superiority randomised controlled trial. 75 adults with genetically confirmed FH will be randomly allocated (1:1:1) to 16 weeks of supervised HIIT, supervised MICT or usual care. The primary outcome is change in maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) from baseline to 16 weeks, measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Key secondary outcomes include markers of subclinical atherosclerosis (vascular inflammation, carotid intima-media thickness), arterial stiffness, biomarkers of cardiometabolic health (inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction and lipid metabolism), as well as body composition, physical function and estimated cardiovascular risk. The primary analyses will be conducted in the intention-to-treat population using a mixed model for repeated measures, adjusted for baseline outcome values and prespecified covariates. Treatment effects will be presented as adjusted between-group differences with corresponding 95% CIs. Confirmatory treatment comparisons will follow a prespecified fixed-sequence hierarchical testing procedure: (1) HIIT versus usual care; (2) MICT versus usual care and (3) HIIT versus MICT. Each comparison will be tested using a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study has been approved by the Biomedical Research Ethics Committee of Granada (reference 1417 N-23). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences and communication with healthcare professionals and patient organisations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06833944.
VERSION DATE AND IDENTIFIER: Version 2.0 (12 July 2026).

Title: Glow Up: a single-centre observational study protocol to develop digital biomarkers for prediabetes screening and digital phenotyping.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prediabetes, a key precursor to type 2 diabetes, is highly prevalent and underdiagnosed, particularly among adults aged ≥45 years with elevated body mass index (BMI). Early detection is critical because lifestyle interventions can delay or prevent progression to type 2 diabetes. The Glucose Observation and Wearable Use for Prevention (Glow Up) study aims to (1) test the feasibility of a digital biomarker for pre-diabetes screening using wearable- and smartphone-derived lifestyle factors (eg, sleep, physical activity and nutrition patterns) in daily life and to (2) characterise individual- and metabolic subgroup-level variability in lifestyle factors and glycaemic control. Specifically, we aim to examine how lifestyle factors relate to glycaemic status and identify personalised predictors of early metabolic dysregulation.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Glow Up is a prospective, single-centre, observational case-control study conducted in Switzerland. Adults (n=200) aged ≥45 years with body mass index (BMI) ≥25 kg/m² will be recruited, including n=100 individuals with pre-diabetes and n=100 age- and sex-matched normoglycaemic controls. Participants will undergo 4 weeks of continuous monitoring using a blinded continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and commercial- and medical-grade wearables; for example, capturing physical activity, sleep and physiological markers (heart rate variability, heart rate and skin temperature), in addition to completing daily image-based meal logs using smartphones. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and body anthropometrics will be collected at the enrolment visit (T0) and repeated at follow-up (T3), approximately 5 weeks apart. The primary outcome is glycaemic status at T3, classified from HbA1c and FPG using prespecified thresholds. Secondary outcomes include CGM metrics, lifestyle profiling (sleep, physical activity, stress and nutrition) and adherence to image-based meal logging.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study received ethics approval from the Ethics Committee of Eastern Switzerland on 15 May 2025 (BASEC ID: 2025–00972). Written informed consent is obtained from all participants before any study procedures are performed. Findings will be disseminated as articles in international peer-reviewed journals and as posters and oral presentations at national and international conferences. Summaries will be provided to funders and collaborators, and personalised reports to participants.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07373418.

Title: KDOQI Commentary on the 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract: Hypertension prevention, diagnosis, and management are central to modifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although the nephrology community has long recognized CKD as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, CKD has not historically been incorporated in cardiovascular risk prediction models. The new 2025 American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults addresses this gap by formally adopting the PREVENT calculator, which combines cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic health parameters to guide risk assessment and clinical decision making. The AHA/ACC guideline reinforces the broad blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg as well as makes recommendations for complex and resistant hypertension. Given the impact of these recommendations on persons living with kidney disease, the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) convened an expert work group to review and comment on the guideline. This KDOQI commentary focuses on recommendations from the AHA/ACC guideline that are pertinent to individuals at risk of CKD or with non-dialysis-dependent CKD (stages 1-5), hence excluding commentary on hypertension management in patients receiving maintenance dialysis. In areas where the AHA/ACC guideline does not offer formal recommendations (eg, medication interactions, electrolyte imbalances, and kidney injury), the work group provides expert commentary about implications for people with CKD. Overall, the work group supports the majority of the AHA/ACC recommendations and identifies areas where evidence remains limited or management in CKD warrants additional consideration.

Title: Thermal ablation in posterosuperior liver segments: Is this an indication to laparoscopic approach?
Abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: Primary liver tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and colorectal cancer liver metastases, can be treated with liver thermal ablation (LTA). Current evidence comparing percutaneous LTA (P-LTA) and laparoscopic LTA (L-LTA) is inconclusive, and data on lesions in the posterosuperior (PS) liver segments are scarce. This study aimed to compare early local recurrence rates between percutaneous and laparoscopic thermal ablation, with a focus on PS liver segments.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included all consecutive patients treated with P-LTA or L-LTA between 2010 and 2024. The primary outcome was early local recurrence (≤ 6 months); secondary outcomes were subgroup analyses of HCC nodules and microwave ablation-treated nodules.
RESULTS: The study included 101 nodules in 69 patients. Overall morbidity was higher after L-LTA, whereas chronic liver disease was more common among P-LTA patients. Early local recurrence was significantly lower after L-LTA (7% vs. 25%), and this difference was accentuated in the PS liver segments (4% vs. 33%). Multivariable analysis identified the percutaneous approach and a lesion size > 3 cm as predictors of early local recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: L-LTA appears more effective in reducing early local recurrence, particularly in the PS segments, although P-LTA remains less invasive. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to validate these findings.

Title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nomenclature change from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) better encapsulates the associated metabolic milieu. While MASLD is associated with increased heart failure (HF) risk, characteristics and outcomes of MASLD in patients with HF remain unclear. This paper aims to examine the prevalence and clinical correlates of MASLD in patients with HF from the Asian Sudden Cardiac Death in Heart Failure (ASIAN-HF) Registry.
METHODS: MASLD was defined as evidence of hepatic steatosis, with at least one of five metabolic criteria (among body mass index, glucose, blood pressure, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein thresholds). Findings were externally validated in Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS), a Hong Kong HF cohort and BIOlogy Study to TAilored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure (BIOSTAT-CHF), a HF cohort across 11 European countries.
RESULTS: Of 2698 patients with HF in ASIAN-HF, 927 (34.4%) had MASLD. They were younger, more often women and more likely to have HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) compared with those without MASLD. All-cause mortality was lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD (7.1% vs 11.7%, p=0.001), even after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR (aHR) 0.58, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.86, p=0.007). All-cause mortality was also lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD in CDARS and BIOSTAT-CHF; however, after multivariable adjustment, the association remained significant only in CDARS (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.84, p<0.001) and was attenuated in BIOSTAT-CHF (aHR 1.08, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.73, p=0.750). Using waist-to-height ratio instead of body mass index in the MASLD definition reclassified <3% of patients.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HF, MASLD is highly prevalent, especially in younger women with HFpEF and is associated with better 1-year survival than in those without MASLD.

Title: Whether to hold and what to measure: perioperative euglycemic ketoacidosis in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used for type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, including in patients without diabetes. Their ketogenic effects may be amplified perioperatively by fasting, surgical stress, and volume loss, resulting in ketoacidosis without marked hyperglycemia. Reported frequencies depend on ascertainment. Where ketones were measured against a diagnostic threshold, cohorts reported 0-1.8% in non-cardiac and mixed populations and 0-15.1% in cardiac surgery; one prospective study using a lower threshold (≥ 0.6 mmol/L) reported a far higher figure, and studies without ketone measurement reported surrogate metabolic-acidosis endpoints of 30-41%. None of these are comparable incidence estimates. Severe and fatal cases have been reported. Because plasma glucose may be normal, diagnosis requires attention to acid-base status and ketones. Quantitative blood β-hydroxybutyrate is preferred when SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i)-associated ketoacidosis is suspected; urine ketone tests may screen when blood testing is unavailable, but a negative result does not exclude it. Perioperative guidance remains inconsistent: some bodies recommend withholding SGLT2i for 3 days (4 days for ertugliflozin), whereas others support risk-stratified continuation in selected patients under specified fasting and dietary conditions. No randomized trial has compared continuation with discontinuation using perioperative ketoacidosis as an endpoint; observational evidence remains limited and conflicting, and ketone thresholds and monitoring intervals lack prospective validation. This review summarizes evidence on recognition, diagnosis, withholding, monitoring, and postoperative restart.

Title: Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).
METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF).
RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF.
CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Topical Recombinant Human Epidermal Growth Factor in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study.
Abstract: To describe recorded outcomes of diabetic foot ulcers treated with topical recombinant human epidermal growth factor as part of routine care. This retrospective, single-centre cohort study included 150 consecutive patients receiving Regen-D 150 without a control group. We added treatment when standard care did not produce adequate granulation. We defined the primary outcome as complete healing of the index ulcer without amputation. The primary outcome occurred in 101/150 patients (67.3%; 95% confidence interval 59.5-74.3). Sixteen underwent amputation (11 minor, 5 major), 27 had ongoing status at last follow-up, three died and three were lost to follow-up. Ongoing status included open wounds and closed but unconfirmed wounds. Median recorded time to healing was 13 weeks (interquartile range 10-16). Wound area analyses were exploratory because of unresolved timing inconsistencies. We could not confirm healing for all recorded healings. About two-thirds had recorded healing without amputation during variable follow-up. These uncontrolled, descriptive findings do not establish efficacy, superiority or amputation prevention.

Title: Navigating Treatment Pathways in Diabetic Foot Infection: A Practical Retrospective Analysis of Healing Predictors and the WIfI System.
Abstract: Diabetic foot infection (DFI) is a major cause of lower-extremity amputation. Evidence on optimal management remains inconsistent, and real-world data from multidisciplinary centres are limited. This study describes the characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes of patients with DFI at a tertiary referral centre. This retrospective cross-sectional study included all patients with diabetes and confirmed DFI presenting since 2022. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiologic, and wound-related data were recorded, and wounds were classified using the Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) system. Correlation and multiple linear regression analyses identified predictors of healing duration. 69 patients were included (mean age 56.4 ± 13.2 years; 58% male). Most wounds were deep (88.2%); osteomyelitis occurred in 42.2%. Conservative wound care was used in 73.9%, and 79.7% underwent bedside debridement. Minor and major amputation rates were 16.2% and 1.4%. The median healing time was 45 days (interquartile range [IQR] 54), and the mean healing time was 56.0 ± 44.9 days. Healing duration correlated with wound grade, WIfI stage, infection severity, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), white blood cell (WBC) count, international normalized ratio (INR), wound area, and delay to specialist assessment. Wound grade was the only independent predictor of healing time (β = 0.606, p = 0.001). Limb-preserving management was associated with a low major amputation rate. Wound severity was the strongest determinant of healing duration, underscoring the importance of early referral and structured risk stratification in DFI care.

Title: Preoperative respiratory muscle strength, muscle mass, and respiratory sarcopenia as predictors of postoperative pulmonary complications after thoracic and cardiac surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after thoracic and cardiac surgery and are associated with adverse outcomes. Respiratory sarcopenia (RS), characterized by coexisting reductions in respiratory muscle mass and strength, may represent a clinically relevant prognostic phenotype, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess whether low preoperative respiratory muscle mass, reduced strength, or their coexistence as RS or probable RS predicts PPCs after thoracic and cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from January 1990 to February 2026 for studies relating preoperative respiratory muscle mass, strength or flow, or RS to PPCs. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies tool. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models after harmonizing effect directions such that ORs >1 denoted higher risk.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included; all involved thoracic or cardiac surgery, and none included an upper abdominal cohort. Cutoff-based respiratory muscle strength or flow impairment was associated with increased odds of PPCs (OR 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.50-3.37; I2 = 51.2%), with the most consistent association observed for percent-predicted peak expiratory flow (PEF) (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.43-2.90; I2 = 0%). Continuous PEF was associated with PPCs, whereas ultrasound-based diaphragm indices showed smaller, non-significant associations. RS or probable RS was associated with PPCs (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.33-3.26; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative functional respiratory muscle impairment, particularly reduced PEF, and RS or probable RS were associated with PPCs. Given that the evidence was limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly derived from thoracic surgery, prospective confirmation is needed.

Title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

Title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cardio-Oncology: An Expert Consensus Statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. Endorsed by the International Cardio-Oncology Society (ICOS).
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract: This document represents a position statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) on recommendations for clinical utilization of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with cancer. The document was prepared by the SCMR Consensus Group on CMR Imaging for Cardio-Oncology and endorsed by the SCMR Publications Committee and SCMR Executive Committee. This document aims to: (1) guide the informed selection and timing of CMR; (2) inform clinical decision-making based on CMR findings; (3) educate stakeholders on the advantages and limitations of CMR in specific clinical scenarios; and (4) provide suggested protocols to tailor the CMR exam to the particular clinical question. The statements of clinical utility presented in the current document focus on the following clinical scenarios: evaluating left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction and volumes; identifying pre-clinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction with myocardial strain; and myocardial injury or edema with parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); myocarditis; vascular toxicity, with a focus on coronary artery disease (CAD); iron overload; cardiac amyloidosis; pericardial disease; valvular disease; pulmonary hypertension; and cardiac masses. Sections devoted to the special situations of radiation therapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and survivorship and pediatrics are also included. As an expert consensus statement, some recommendations are based on expert opinion and accepted best practices. This position statement emphasizes the optimal utilization of CMR in oncology patients with known or suspected cardiovascular disease; however, the authors acknowledge that CMR is not always locally available or accessible. Finally, the principal aim of this position statement is to provide specific recommendations on the use of CMR to help improve the health of cancer patients with cardiovascular disease.

Title: Reanimationless Rapid Recovery Versus Thoraco-Abdominal Normothermic Regional Perfusion for Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation Following Prolonged Asystolic Warm Ischemia.
Journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation has expanded the donor pool, yet contemporary recovery strategies remain constrained. Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultra-Oxygenated Preservation (REUP) is a non-reanimation DCD recovery strategy that eliminates the need for donor heart reperfusion prior to transplantation. As prolonged asystolic warm ischemic time (AWIT) during circulatory arrest has raised ongoing concerns, whether REUP achieves outcomes comparable to TA-NRP in DCD donors with prolonged AWIT remains unknown.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center study of DCD heart transplant recipients whose donor hearts were recovered using either TA-NRP or REUP and preserved with 10°C static cold storage. Donors with AWIT <10 minutes were excluded. The primary outcomes were severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) and 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Eighty-two DCD heart transplant recipients met inclusion criteria, including 55 TA-NRP and 27 REUP recipients. Compared with TA-NRP donors, REUP donors were older (42.0 vs 33.7 years) and experienced longer total ischemic times (285 vs 219 minutes). Severe PGD occurred in 4 TA-NRP recipients (7.3%) and no REUP recipients (0.0%). Ninety-day mortality was 12.7% versus 7.4%, respectively. In weighted bootstrap analyses, REUP was associated with a directional signal toward lower severe PGD (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-1.02; directional consistency 97.4%) and lower 90-day mortality (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.09-2.57; directional consistency 76.3%), although confidence intervals were wide.
CONCLUSIONS: Among DCD heart transplant recipients with AWIT ≥10 minutes, REUP demonstrated early graft function and short-term survival comparable to TA-NRP despite a more challenging donor profile. These findings support further prospective multicenter evaluation of REUP as a broadly deployable non-reanimation DCD heart recovery strategy.

Title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.
METHODS: The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

Title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000046847). Short tweet: Can multimodality imaging predict LV wall motion recovery after PCI for chronic total occlusion? Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.

Title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
Abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.
RESULTS: MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

Title: Clinical phenotypes, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic signatures in inflammatory myocardial disease: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory myocardial disease encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes, from subtle symptoms to fulminant heart failure. Differentiating myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis (CS), and non-confirmed cardiomyopathy (NC) remains diagnostically and prognostically challenging. We compared clinical presentation, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic profiles across these groups.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 218 adults undergoing evaluation for cardiomyopathy were classified as myocarditis (n = 81), CS (n = 84), or NC (n = 53). The primary composite outcome was all-cause mortality, mechanical circulatory support, or heart transplantation. RNA sequencing of endomyocardial biopsies was performed in 53 patients with differential expression analysis adjusted for age, RNA integrity number, and systolic blood pressure.
RESULTS: Patients with myocarditis were younger than those with CS or NC (34.7 ± 15.8 vs 57.4 ± 8.7 vs 57.6 ± 14.0 years); 70-75% were male. Myocarditis was characterized by chest pain and elevated inflammatory biomarkers, whereas CS was associated with arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction. Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested differences in event-free survival, adjusted Cox regression showed no significant between-group differences (myocarditis vs NC: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.22-4.43, p = 0.985; CS vs NC: HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.63-4.43, p = 0.307). Transcriptomic profiling revealed a more pronounced inflammatory gene expression profile in myocarditis, whereas CS showed limited differential expression and substantial overlap with NC.
CONCLUSIONS: Inflammatory myocardial disease shows distinct clinical presentations, while adjusted analyses did not demonstrate significant differences in long-term outcomes. Myocarditis showed a stronger inflammatory transcriptional signature, whereas CS exhibited limited transcriptomic differences. These findings support further investigation of RNA-based profiling as a complementary tool.

Title: Systematic Review of Clinical Utility of Multimodal Imaging in Infectious Posterior Uveitis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 12.
Abstract:
TOPIC: To systematically evaluate the clinical utility of multimodal imaging (MMI) for the diagnosis, activity assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications in the five most prevalent infectious posterior uveitides.
DESIGN: Systematic review and evidence-based quality appraisal.
PARTICIPANTS: Original research studies published between January 2018 and September 2025(primary cohort) and 2012-2017(supplemental cohort) evaluating MMI in ocular toxoplasmosis(TOXO), cytomegalovirus retinitis(CMVR), ocular tuberculosis(TB), syphilitic uveitis(SYPH), and acute retinal necrosis(ARN).
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus were systematically searched. Independent reviewers extracted reported imaging findings and clinical utility statements for: color fundus photography (CFP), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and certainty of evidence was graded using a bespoke consensus-based scheme informed by GRADE principles.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: (1)reported imaging findings for each entity and modality; and (2)statements of clinical utility for diagnosis, detection of disease activity, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications.
RESULTS: Among 122 included studies (82 primary and 40 supplemental), the primary studies contributed 5,522 individual patient examinations and 574 imaging statements, while the supplemental studies provided corroborating evidence. Overall, 366 clinical utility statements were identified across the four prespecified domains, including 30 statements supporting synergistic MMI strategies. CFP, including studies using ultra-widefield imaging, achieved high certainty for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with moderate certainty in ARN. OCT achieved high certainty across all four clinical utility domains for four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with lower certainty in ARN owing to its limited evidence base. FFA achieved high certainty for complication detection in three of five entities. FAF achieved high certainty for disease activity in four of five entities. OCTA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for two of five entities, whereas ICGA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for only one of five entities.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial evidence exists regarding the imaging findings and clinical utility of MMI in infectious posterior uveitis. Combined MMI enables integrated structural, vascular, and choroidal assessment beyond conventional clinical examination.

Title: Quantitative Analysis of Retinal Thickness and Blood Flow Changes Using SS-OCTA in Patients with Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Based on optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), we investigate the effects of Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment on retinal thickness and blood perfusion in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
METHODS: Retrospective clinical study.Forty patients (40 eyes) diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) who underwent primary 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy (25G PPV) at our hospital between January 2023 and January 2026 were enrolled. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) was performed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively to measure central macular thickness (CMT), superficial capillary plexus vessel density (SCP), deep capillary plexus vessel density (DCP), and the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and postoperative complications were also recorded, and changes in all parameters before and after treatment were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients (40 eyes) were enrolled, including 21 males (21 eyes) and 19 females (19 eyes), with a mean age of (52.65±12.91) years. The mean duration of diabetes was (10.47±6.81) years, and the baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level was (7.68%±1.34) %. At the final follow-up, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) improved significantly (P < 0.001), central macular thickness (CMT) decreased significantly, and macular edema was alleviated, showing statistically significant differences compared with preoperative values (P < 0.001). The vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus in the foveal and nasal regions was significantly improved, with a significant difference compared with the preoperative status (P < 0.05). No statistically significant differences were found in the remaining parameters ( P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The study found that in eyes with PDR following Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment, visual acuity improved and macular edema resolved. In addition to relieving vitreous traction and clearing opacified refractive media, PPV also promoted partial recovery of the superficial retinal microcirculation. However, the perfusion status of the deep capillary plexus and the architecture of the FAZ may remain relatively stable in the short term after surgery.

Title: Hemoadsorption to prevent acute kidney injury in elective cardiac surgery: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care.
METHODS: We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991).
RESULTS: A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p =  0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay.
CONCLUSION: Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).

Title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF.
STUDY DESIGN: Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019).
EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis.
OUTCOMES: Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary).
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2.
LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding.
CONCLUSIONS: Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

Title: Heart Rate-Lowering Therapies for Tachycardia in Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is defined by a sustained increase in heart rate of ≥30 beats/min within 10 minutes of standing, accompanied by symptoms of orthostatic intolerance persisting for at least 3 months. Prior research has focused on determinants of tachycardia, raising the question of whether the tachycardia represents a compensatory mechanism or the primary driver of symptoms. In this review, we summarize the available literature on heart rate-lowering interventions in POTS and examine whether reducing heart rate is associated with symptom improvement.
