AIMS: Various clinical risk factors impact the natural history of Brugada syndrome (BrS) and establish the basis of current clinical practice guidelines (CPG) indications for implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD). Due to the time-dependent expressivity of BrS, their performance in predicting the actual occurrence of arrhythmic events after ICD implantation remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the occurrence of arrhythmic events based on the CPG indications and whether the genetic substrate can add to the prediction of arrhythmic events at follow-up.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We enrolled consecutive patients who underwent ICD implant either for primary or secondary prevention. Prospective clinical data included arrhythmic history, electrocardiographic findings, therapies, SCN5A gene mutations, and genotyping of three BrS-associated single nucleotide variants. Eleven per cent of 551 patients experienced life-threatening arrhythmic events (LAE) over a median follow-up of 8.1 years. Patients with ESC class IIA indication had a similar risk profile as those implanted for secondary prevention. The recently developed BrS 5-year risk score, including clinical and genetic variables, was a determinant of outcome in the whole cohort and in patients implanted for primary prevention: 26.93 ± 3.33 vs. 4.41 ± 0.61 and 11.67 ± 1.52 vs. 5.36 ± 0.99 in patients with LAEs compared with those without events (P < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: CPG class IIa and I had a similar rate of ICD shock at follow-up. We also provide robust evidence indicating that the quantification of the BrS arrhythmic risk score at the moment of ICD implant may improve the identification of patients who will benefit from ICD at follow-up.

Title: Burden of congenital birth defects in the ten countries with the highest numbers of births from 1990 to 2023, with projections to 2040: A retrospective population-level ecological study.
Abstract: ObjectiveCongenital birth defects (CBDs) are major causes of neonatal mortality and lifelong disability worldwide. The ten countries with the highest numbers of births account for over half of global neonates, yet their CBD burden trends remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to assess the CBD burden and temporal trends in these countries from 1990 to 2023 and project trends to 2040.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective population-level ecological study using publicly available data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 on CBD burden. We analysed incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) for CBDs in India, China, Nigeria, Pakistan, Indonesia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, the United States, Bangladesh, and Brazil from 1990 to 2023. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), future trends (2024-2040) were projected using ARIMA models, and associations with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) were evaluated by Spearman correlation.ResultsIn 2023, India had the highest number of CBD cases (1,160,697), followed by Nigeria and China. Ethiopia showed the highest age-standardized incidence rate, while the United States had the lowest. From 1990 to 2023, age-standardized incidence, mortality, and DALYs generally declined, with China showing the largest reductions in mortality and DALYs. Nigeria was the only country with increasing mortality. Congenital heart anomalies were the leading cause of deaths and DALYs across all countries. Neural tube defects showed the greatest decline in incidence, whereas urogenital congenital anomalies demonstrated increasing mortality trends. SDI was negatively correlated with incidence, mortality, and DALYs (all P < 0.05). ARIMA projections suggested increasing ASIR in several countries, particularly China and Indonesia, while China and Nigeria were projected to experience increases in ASMR and ASDR through 2040, particularly among females, while Bangladesh, Ethiopia, and the United States are expected to remain stable or decline.ConclusionThe CBD burden showed marked heterogeneity across the ten countries with the highest numbers of births. Strengthening healthcare systems, prenatal care, and screening in low-SDI countries, together with targeted prevention strategies in countries with projected increases, may help reduce the global CBD burden and improve health equity.

Title: Workplace and age associated with severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies: a nationwide study in Japan.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among working-age populations globally, occupational injuries and workplace cardiovascular emergencies remain major contributors to morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between workplace settings, age groups, and the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective registry-based observational study using emergency medical services data from Japan, including 454 043 working-age individuals recorded in 2021-2023. Workplace settings (office, indoor worksite, factory, outdoor worksite, construction, agriculture, and others) and age groups were analysed in relation to event severity, categorized as non-life-threatening or life-threatening. Multivariable regression models estimated the associations, and workplace-age interactions were assessed.
RESULTS: Compared with office settings, all other workplaces were associated with higher odds of life-threatening injuries, particularly agriculture and construction. Increasing age groups were progressively associated with greater injury severity. The workplace setting was associated with the severity of stroke and ischaemic heart disease, particularly in uncontrolled outdoor environments. Stroke severity was elevated in those aged 45-59 and 60-69 years, while all older age groups were associated with severe ischaemic heart disease. Workplace-age interactions were significant only for occupational injuries.
CONCLUSIONS: Workplace and age were interactively and independently associated with the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies.

Title: Anti-annexin A5 Autoantibodies in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Related to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection (HIV-PAH): A Case-Control Study.
Abstract: Autoantibody profiles in HIV-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (HIV-PAH) remain poorly characterized. Using a validated proteomic pipeline (two-dimensional immunoblot, mass spectrometry, ELISA), we compared 20 HIV-PAH patients with 20 HIV controls without PAH. Anti-annexin A5 (AnxA5) autoantibodies were present in 55% of HIV-PAH patients versus 0% of controls (P < .001) and anti-14-3-3ε in 35% versus 5% (P = .04), despite comparable HIV duration, CD4 counts, and virological control. Both remained associated with PAH after adjustment for coinfections. These autoantibodies mirror those described in connective-tissue-disease-PAH, suggesting a possible overlap in autoimmune features and a research biomarker warranting prospective validation.

Title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.
Abstract: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

Title: Population-specific association and risk discrimination utility of the cardiometabolic index for prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity: insights from CHARLS and NHANES.
Abstract: The comorbidity of cardiometabolic diseases, such as hypertension and diabetes, is increasingly prevalent worldwide, particularly among middle-aged and elderly populations. The cardiometabolic index (CMI), a novel composite biomarker integrating features of dyslipidemia and abdominal obesity, has emerged as a potential indicator. However, its association with prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity and its risk discrimination utility across Chinese and American populations remain insufficiently investigated. This investigation utilized data from CHARLS and NHANES, encompassing 12,261 Chinese and 1,329 American participants. Multivariable logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to evaluate the association and dose-response relationship between CMI and prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity. Machine learning models were constructed to evaluate risk discrimination performance, including LightGBM, GBM, and CatBoost. Mediation analysis was further conducted to assess the potential mediating role of body mass index (BMI) in the association between CMI and the outcome. Elevated CMI was significantly associated with an increased risk of hypertension-diabetes comorbidity (CHARLS: OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 2.00-2.34; NHANES: OR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.48-2.69). RCS analysis revealed a marked nonlinear association within the Chinese cohort (threshold effect, P-nonlinear < 0.001), contrasting with a more linear relationship in the American population (P-nonlinear = 0.764). Among the machine learning models, LightGBM and GBM demonstrated superior risk discrimination performance (CHARLS AUC = 0.841; NHANES AUC = 0.948). Mediation analysis indicated that BMI exerted a significant partial mediating effect, accounting for 32.90% and 43.32% of the total association in the Chinese and American cohorts, respectively. CMI was independently associated with prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity, with notable population-specific differences in association patterns. Machine learning models incorporating CMI showed favorable risk discrimination performance. The partial mediation effect of BMI underscores the critical importance of adiposity management in mitigating cardiometabolic risk. This study provides a novel theoretical framework and methodological support for cross-population cardiometabolic health assessment.

Title: Does Ethnicity Influence the Long-Term Outcomes of Sleeve Gastrectomy? Results from a Prospectively Maintained Israeli Database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ethnic disparities often influence patient's outcomes. This study aimed to compare the weight loss and metabolic outcomes of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) in Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients.
METHODS: A prospectively maintained cohort of 892 patients (262 Arabs and 630 Jews) who underwent LSG between 2009 and 2022 at a single tertiary academic center was retrospectively analyzed. Demographic, peri-operative, and long-term outcome data were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Arabs were younger (35 vs. 44 years) and had a higher baseline BMI (45.1 vs. 42.9). Jews had more postoperative follow-ups (6.8 vs. 6.0). Despite these differences, long-term weight loss outcomes were broadly comparable between groups. %EWL outcomes did not differ significantly at 1- and 5-year follow-up. Although Arab patients demonstrated numerically higher %TWL at 1 year, this difference did not reach statistical significance and was not sustained at longer-term follow-up. Rates of comorbidity remission, including diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, were similarly high.
CONCLUSION: Despite baseline ethnic disparities, LSG was associated with comparable long-term weight loss and comorbidity resolution among Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients.

Title: Decoding the Safety Profile of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Facts, Myths, and Ongoing Controversies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) represent one of the most significant therapeutic advances in the management of type 2 diabetes and obesity. As their indications have expanded to include cardiovascular and kidney disease, safety concerns involving multiple organ systems have received increasing attention. This narrative review examines the spectrum of adverse effects linked to GLP-1RAs and provides a clinically relevant platform for assessing their safe prescription.
RECENT FINDINGS: Gastrointestinal intolerance, modest increases in heart rate, and a modest but reproducible increase in the risk of gallbladder and biliary disease represent the most consistently supported adverse effects of GLP-1RAs. A risk of pancreatitis is also considered to exist, although some studies have challenged this association. Conversely, correlations with neuropsychiatric and dermatological disorders, diabetic retinopathy, nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, perioperative aspiration, sexual and reproductive disturbances, sarcopenia, and malignancy remain controversial. Most available evidence derives from pharmacovigilance databases, retrospective observational studies, and secondary analyses of randomized trials, which are limited by reporting bias, residual confounding, and inability to establish causality. Heterogeneity in study design, statistical methodology, outcome definitions, and patient populations further complicates interpretation. Although several proposed adverse effects have biologically plausible mechanisms, prospective clinical validation remains limited. Notably, recent regulatory decisions, including the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)'s removal of the suicidality warning from GLP-1RA prescribing information, reflect the evolving nature of these safety assessments. The overall benefit-risk profile of GLP-1RAs is favorable. Most emerging safety concerns should currently be regarded as hypothesis-generating signals rather than established toxicities. Individualized risk assessment and appropriate clinical monitoring remain important as ongoing and future prospective studies further define the long-term safety of this rapidly expanding therapeutic class.

Title: [Sepsis-induced coagulopathy].
Abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) represents a frequent and prognostically highly relevant complication of sepsis, characterized by a dysregulated interaction between inflammation, endothelial activation and coagulation. Pathophysiologically, the excessive host immune response to pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMP), activation of the complement cascade, formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) and disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx collectively promote a prothrombotic and antifibrinolytic microenvironment, resulting in microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Approximately 20-25% of critically ill patients with sepsis fulfil the diagnostic criteria for SIC. Current diagnostic approaches rely on scoring systems such as the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)-SIC, ISTH overt-disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and Japanese Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (JSTH)-DIC scores; however, their clinical utility remains limited as they predominantly collate hemorrhagic parameters even though sepsis is typically characterized by a thrombotically dominated phenotype. Viscoelastic point-of-care assays enable dynamic bedside assessment of coagulation and fibrinolysis, including the frequently occurring hypofibrinolysis or fibrinolytic shutdown, which is associated with an unfavorable outcome; however, for this specific purpose, these methods have not yet been sufficiently validated or established as a diagnostic standard. Data and recommendations on specific therapeutic options are limited. A consistent pharmacological thromboprophylaxis remains the cornerstone in patients with sepsis, with low-molecular weight heparins demonstrating advantages over unfractionated heparin regarding venous thromboembolic complications. Coagulation modulating treatment, such as antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin or activated protein C, have thus far failed to demonstrate consistent survival benefits in large randomized clinical trials. Experimental approaches targeting NET formation, complement activation or fibrinolytic modulation appear mechanistically promising but require further clinical validation. Overall, SIC necessitates an individualized, pathophysiology-driven diagnostic and therapeutic approach integrating inflammatory, endothelial, thrombotic and fibrinolytic alterations.

Title: Real-World Effectiveness and Tolerability of Rimegepant as Second- or Third-Line Acute Treatment for Migraine: A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rimegepant is an oral calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist approved for both acute and preventive treatment of migraine. However, limited information is available regarding its effectiveness and tolerability when used as a second- or third-line acute treatment in patients for whom triptans and/or lasmiditan are ineffective, poorly tolerated, contraindicated, or otherwise unsuitable. This study evaluated the effectiveness and tolerability of rimegepant in this real-world clinical setting.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in 89 patients (76 female; mean age 40.6 ± 12.2 years) prescribed rimegepant 75 mg after prior use of triptans and/or lasmiditan. Participants self-recorded headache intensity using a visual analog scale (VAS) before and 2 and 4 h after taking rimegepant. Pain freedom was defined as a VAS score of 0, and treatment efficacy as a ≥ 50% reduction in VAS score. The Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) was assessed at 2 h. Continuation was defined as a request for ongoing prescription after the initial dose.
RESULTS: The study population included 35 patients (39.3%) with chronic migraine and 65 (73.0%) with prior calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibody exposure. Median VAS scores decreased from 77.0 at baseline to 18.0 at 2 h and 0.0 at 4 h (p < 0.001). Pain-free rates were 24.7% (95% CI 16.2-35.0%) at 2 h and 52.8% (95% CI 41.9-63.5%) at 4 h. Efficacy rates (≥ 50% VAS reduction) were 68.5% and 87.6% at 2 and 4 h, respectively. The continuation rate was 82.0%. Meaningful improvement on the PGIC was reported by 65.2% of patients. Adverse events occurred in 13.5% of patients. No adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were observed.
CONCLUSION: Rimegepant was associated with clinically meaningful pain relief and favorable patient-reported outcomes when used as a second- or third-line acute treatment in real-world clinical practice.

Title: The Landmark Series: Perioperative Management of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with an increasing burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-associated HCC in Western populations. In treating HCC, recurrence after curative-intent therapy remains common, creating a compelling rationale for perioperative systemic therapy.
METHODS: This Landmark Series review examines the pivotal studies that have shaped the surgical and perioperative management of HCC, tracing the evolution from principles of resectability to contemporary adjuvant and neoadjuvant immune-based strategies.
RESULTS: The development of perioperative therapy has been defined by both landmark negative trials and emerging evidence of efficacy. The STORM trial demonstrated that sorafenib's activity in advanced HCC did not translate into benefit after resection or ablation. The IMbrave050 trial subsequently demonstrated an early recurrence-free survival advantage with adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab that was not sustained with longer follow-up evaluation, whereas the KEYNOTE-937 trial failed to demonstrate benefit with adjuvant pembrolizumab. In contrast, early-phase neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor-based studies have demonstrated feasibility and meaningful pathologic responses, and the CARES-009 trial provided the first randomized phase III evidence of improved event-free survival with a perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-antiangiogenic strategy.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative management of HCC is evolving toward an integrated, multidisciplinary treatment paradigm. Although no broadly applicable adjuvant systemic therapy has been established, emerging perioperative strategies provide proof of concept that systemic therapy may improve outcomes for selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-driven patient selection, molecular residual disease assessment, standardized pathologic response criteria, and clinical trials identifying which patients require perioperative therapy and when treatment should be delivered.

Title: Effectiveness of cardiac resynchronization therapy in cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advances in cancer treatment have increased the number of survivors, making cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) an important concern. While cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is established for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and conduction disorders, its role in CTRCD remains unclear. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the benefit of CRT in patients with CTRCD.
METHODS: We performed a literature search of studies showing CRT outcomes in the specific group of CTRCD patients. The outcomes of interest were left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and LV volume improvement. A random effects meta-analysis was done to estimate 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: This analysis included four studies (one prospective and three retrospective) comprising 110 patients with CTRCD, the majority (91%, n = 100) being survivors of breast cancer or lymphoma/leukemia. Baseline LVEF ranged from 18.6% ± 7.6% to 28.5% ± 3.8% (mean 24% ± 7%). After a mean follow-up of 9 ± 5 months, LVEF increased by 9.95% (95% CI 7.79-12.11) and end-systolic volume decreased by 39.17 mL (95% CI 24.99-53.35). Three studies included a control group of patients with other forms of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy who underwent CRT implantation, showing no significant difference in LVEF improvement between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that CRT improves LVEF and LV volumes in selected patients with CTRCD, with a magnitude of reverse remodeling that appears similar to that observed in other etiologies of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. However, the evidence is limited to small observational studies, so conclusions about clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Thus, CRT may be considered in cancer patients who meet standard criteria for CRT implantation, but the decision should be individualized and guided by multidisciplinary assessment, cancer prognosis, and competing clinical risks.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer and choroidal vascularity correlate with disease activity in systemic lupus erythematosus.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) confers risk of subclinical neurovascular injury. We assessed retinal and choroidal structural alterations using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and evaluated their relationship with disease activity and immunological markers.
METHODS: In this prospective, cross-sectional study, 70 SLE patients and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examination. SD-OCT with enhanced depth imaging was used to assess peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness, macular thickness, and choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Disease activity was measured using the SLE Disease Activity Index-2 K (SLEDAI-2 K). Patients were stratified into active (SLEDAI ≥ 6, n = 18) and inactive (SLEDAI ≤ 5, n = 52) subgroups.
RESULTS: Compared to controls, SLE patients had significantly thinner global pRNFL (94.5 ± 5.0 μm vs. 100.5 ± 5.0 μm, p < 0.001) and lower CVI (65.6 ± 2.0% vs. 68.9 ± 2.0%, p < 0.001). Thinning was most pronounced in the temporal superior (TS) and temporal inferior (TI) sectors. Active SLE patients showed greater pRNFL thinning and lower CVI than inactive patients (p < 0.01). SLEDAI scores correlated negatively with temporal pRNFL thickness (TS: r=-0.58; TI: r=-0.56) and CVI (r=-0.63) (all p < 0.001). Anti-dsDNA positivity correlated with reduced pRNFL and CVI, while complement C3 levels showed positive correlations.
CONCLUSION: SD-OCT reveals significant temporal pRNFL thinning and reduced CVI in SLE patients, correlating with systemic disease activity and immunologic markers. These findings support the retina and choroid as accessible sites reflecting SLE-related neurovascular inflammation and contribute to understanding of ocular involvement in disease pathophysiology; longitudinal studies are needed to determine their utility for disease monitoring.

Title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
Journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.
RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

Title: Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® in treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
Abstract: Aim: To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® drug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database. Materials & methods: This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI. Results: A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup. Conclusion: Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

Title: Conduction System Pacing for Resynchronization Therapy in Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a promising modality for cardiac resynchronization therapy, but evidence of CSP in heart failure (HF) remains controversial.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CSP, including left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and His bundle pacing, to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in HF.
METHODS: The MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included clinical endpoints (HHF, all-cause mortality), cardiac resynchronization therapy responses (predefined and super-response), echocardiographic parameters (left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular end-systolic volume), electrophysiologic parameters (paced QRS duration and capture threshold), functional status (NYHA functional class and 6-minute walk test distance), procedural performance (procedural time, fluoroscopy time, lead implantation time), and device-related complications. (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261388077).
RESULTS: Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 1,054 patients (566 CSP and 488 BiVP) were included. CSP showed a significant reduction in primary composite endpoint (OR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.18-0.52; I2 = 0%), improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean difference: 3.06%; 95% CI: 0.82%-5.30%; I2 = 55%), and shorter paced QRS duration (mean difference:-11.49 ms; 95% CI: -20.70 to -2.28; I2 = 85%), compared with BiVP. In the LBBAP group, there were greater reductions in primary composite endpoint with higher rates of super-response (OR: 2.18; 95% CI: 1.44-3.30; I2 = 54%) compared with BiVP. No differences were observed in functional status or device-related complications.
CONCLUSIONS: CSP, and potentially LBBAP, was associated with a significantly lower composite endpoint of HHF and all-cause mortality compared with BiVP, supporting CSP as an alternative to BiVP in HF.

Title: Hemodynamic Patterns Relative to Vasopressin Initiation and Subsequent Septic Shock Progression in Children: A Retrospective Cohort, 2020-2023.
Journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the hemodynamic patterns associated with starting vasopressin in children with septic shock and to compare the early patterns based on subsequent progression of shock.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort (2020-2023) study.
SETTING: Single-center, tertiary PICU in Australia.
PATIENTS: Children younger than 18 years with septic shock.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hemodynamic variables collected at 1-minute intervals during a 1-hour observation period after starting vasopressin infusion were reviewed and collated according to whether shock subsequently progressed in the following 5 hours. In a cohort of 30 children (median age, 9 yr [interquartile range, 2-14 yr]), eight had shock progression, which was defined by echocardiography, lactate, and use of extracorporeal support. Cases with subsequent shock progression, as opposedto not, had an associated higher Phoenix score (7 [7-8] vs. 6 [5-6]; p = 0.01). The vasopressin starting dose in the shock vs. nonshock progression groups was 0.03 U/kg/hr (0.02-0.06 U/kg/hr) vs. 0.02 U/kg/hr (0.02-0.04 U/kg/hr; p = 0.72). We failed to find an association between ventricular dysfunction at baseline and the shock progression group vs. no shock progression (4/6 vs. 7/18; mean difference, 28%; 95% CI, -16% to 71%; p = 0.36). In the shock progression group, earlier pulse pressure continued on a decreasing trajectory following vasopressin initiation, despite increasing systolic and diastolic blood pressures. In those without shock progression, pulse pressure increased marginally. The difference between groups in the median pulse pressures during the observation period was 7.5 mm Hg.
CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating, retrospective study of children with septic shock treated with vasopressin, subsequent shock progression was associated with early decreasing pulse pressure. Further studies are needed to test whether early changes in pulse pressure after starting vasopressin can be used as a potential marker of subsequent shock progression.

Title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Opportunistic Screening of Left Ventricular Dysfunction Screening Using Chest Radiographs.
Abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate a deep learning model (DLLV) for identifying reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on chest radiographs (CXRs) and assess its potential as a prescreening tool for selective transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in health checkup populations. Materials and Methods Same-day CXR-TTE pairs obtained between January 2016 and September 2021 were retrospectively collected for model development. Counterfactual learning was applied to enhance model performance and interpretability. External testing included one tertiary referral center cohort and two health checkup cohorts. Discrimination was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and DLLV-based prescreening was evaluated by estimated TTE reduction and missed-case burden. Results The development dataset included 24,674 patients (32,135 CXR-TTE pairs); external cohorts included 5440, 28,034, and 6085 patients (53-62% male). DLLV achieved an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.88) for LVEF ≤ 40% in the tertiary referral cohort. In health checkup cohorts, AUCs were 0.92-0.97 for LVEF ≤ 40%, with AUPRCs of 0.04 in both cohorts, corresponding to 87-fold (95% CI: 16, 404) and 37-fold (95% CI: 3, 251) enrichment over baseline prevalence. Counterfactual reinforcement learning produced heatmaps with greater heart localization precision (P < .001 for all) and higher AUC for LVEF < 50% (P = .04). DLLV-based prescreening estimated TTE volume reductions up to 85% while identifying all 12 and 7 individuals with LVEF ≤ 40%. Conclusion DLLV identified reduced LVEF on CXRs across external test cohorts and showed potential as a prescreening tool for selective TTE in health checkup populations. ©RSNA, 2026.

Title: Validation of the "Pathobiological Determinants of Atherosclerosis in Youth Risk Score" in a Norwegian Cohort of Young Adults.
Music Therapy During Weaning From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study examined the effect of daily music therapy on weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in the ICU, with a primary focus on weaning duration. Secondary agitation, sedation, and analgesia doses, pain, delirium, and perceived stress after 90 days were assessed. Additionally, total IMV and ICU stay durations and tracheostomy rates were studied. Physiologic parameters were assessed in the music therapy group (MG). The study also aimed to promote the humanization of critical care through a biopsychosocial and creative music therapy approach.
DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally.
SETTING AND PATIENTS: Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Music therapy may serve as a nonpharmacological complementary adjunct during weaning by reducing agitation, sedation, and tracheostomy rate. It may potentially decrease perceived stress and IMV and ICU stay durations. Further research is warranted.

Title: Real-world analysis of infusion-related reactions in patients receiving subcutaneous daratumumab in Nova Scotia, Canada.
Journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
Abstract: IntroductionThis study aimed to characterize the incidence, grade, onset, duration and management of infusion-related reactions (IRRs) in patients receiving their first cycle of subcutaneous daratumumab and to evaluate the duration of the observation period.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included adult patients diagnosed with MM or AL amyloidosis who received their first cycle of subcutaneous daratumumab in Nova Scotia, Canada, between October 2021 and April 2025.ResultsSix IRRs were identified in 5 out of 140 patients (3.6%); 5 of the 6 reactions were categorized as low-grade and one patient developed grade 3 hypoxia which was managed with supplemental oxygen and diphenhydramine. The median time to IRR onset was 49.5 min (range 2-245) and the median time to resolution after intervention was 73.5 min (range 10-101). The IRR rate in patients who received 20 mg of dexamethasone or less was 5.8% versus 0% in patients who received greater than 20 mg.ConclusionsThis real-world analysis of patients receiving subcutaneous daratumumab for the first time revealed a low rate of IRRs and fewer IRRs in patients who received higher doses of dexamethasone prior to treatment. These findings suggest an important role for dexamethasone in IRR prophylaxis and support a reduction in the duration of the observation period post-subcutaneous daratumumab. Based on these results, the duration of the observation period in Nova Scotia was reduced from 4 h to 1 h, which saves chair time and has implications for cost savings, and the patient experience.

Title: Cerebral Artery Stenosis, Glymphatic Dysfunction, and Cognitive Trajectories: A Longitudinal Cohort Study of Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
Abstract:
AIMS: We aimed to investigate the role of glymphatic dysfunction in the association between stenosis and cognition.
METHODS: Older adults from a longitudinal cohort underwent magnetic resonance angiography to quantify cerebral artery stenosis burden. Glymphatic function was evaluated using diffusion tensor imaging-analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) and free water in white matter (FW-WM). Global cognitive performance was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB). Mediation analyses examined indirect effects, and longitudinal cognitive outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among 346 participants, 87 (25.1%) had at least one stenotic cerebral artery. Stenosis burden was associated with a lower DTI-ALPS index (β = -0.04, p = 0.003) and higher FW-WM (β = 0.01, p = 0.022). Both DTI-ALPS and FW-WM significantly mediated the association between stenosis burden and baseline MMSE, accounting for 13.06%-17.19% of the total effect. In longitudinal analyses, participants with stenosis and impaired glymphatic function had a higher risk of CDR-SB worsening relative to those with stenosis but preserved glymphatic function (hazard ratios 1.35-2.96) and those without stenosis (hazard ratios 3.27-4.70).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that glymphatic dysfunction may contribute to the association between cerebral artery stenosis and cognitive deterioration.

Title: Acute Perinatal Stroke Characteristics and Outcome in Southern Finland.
Abstract:
AIM: Perinatal stroke can cause lifelong morbidities. Outcome prediction is important for parental guidance and follow-up. We studied characteristics of acute perinatal stroke in a Finnish cohort.
METHODS: We performed a population-based study, identifying infants with acute neonatal cerebral ischemia or sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) in Southern Finland from 2010 to 2023. We analysed the incidence of stroke types, seizures, anti-seizure medication use, and outcomes.
RESULTS: Altogether 88 infants (1 in 3101 live births) were diagnosed with acute perinatal stroke: 67% with arterial ischemic stroke (AIS), 22% with hemorrhagic stroke (HS) and 11% with CSVT. Seizures and anti-seizure medication use occurred in 78% of infants. Cranial ultrasound infrequently recognized AIS but usually noted haemorrhage. During follow-up, 34% of infants had no adverse outcome diagnosis. The most common outcome was cerebral palsy (CP, 35%). A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types.
CONCLUSION: The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

Title: [Safety of diet therapy using ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids].
Journal: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to study the dose-dependent hypolipidemic effect of ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: An open, single-center, prospective study was conducted at the clinic of the Federal Research Center for Nutrition and Biotechnology. The tolerability, safety, and effectiveness of dietary therapy enriched with various sources of ϖ-3 PUFAs at dosages ranging from 300 to 3000 mg per day were evaluated in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
RESULTS: The study of different sources and dosages of ω-3 PUFAs demonstrated their good tolerability and safety, and revealed a dose-dependent effect on lipid profile parameters. The study demonstrated the dominant effect of different sources of ω-3 PUFAs on serum TG levels in patients with CVD.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that the inclusion of ω-3 PUFAs in the basic diet of patients with CVD and hyperlipidemia has an additional anti-atherogenic effect.

Title: Superior cervical sympathetic ganglion enlargement in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: An exploratory case-control study.
Journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
Abstract: AimIdiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) may involve bidirectional interactions between elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) and sympathetic nervous system activity along an ICP-sympathetic axis. We hypothesized that superior cervical sympathetic ganglion (SCG) volume is increased in IIH and investigated whether SCG enlargement on MRI may serve as a potential imaging covariate of disease severity associated with cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (OP).MethodsIn this retrospective case control study, we selected IIH patients with a brain MRI within six weeks prior to lumbar puncture, and control participants with normal MRIs. We measured bilateral SCG volumes on MRI, and performed group comparisons and linear regression analyses.ResultsThirty-six IIH patients and 36 controls were included. Median OP in IIH was 24.5 cmH2O. Right, but not left, SCG volume was greater in IIH than controls (281 vs. 208 mm3, P = 0.038; BMI-adjusted P = 0.032). Combined bilateral SCG volume was also increased (631 vs. 381 mm3, P = 0.030; BMI-adjusted P = 0.026). A right SCG cutoff of ≥442 mm3 discriminated elevated OP (AUC = 0.713, optimal point for OP = 37.5 cmH2O) and was associated with increased odds of elevated OP (12.11, P = 0.016).ConclusionSCG enlargement may provide a potential imaging covariate for disease severity. However, given the exploratory nature of this investigation, future validation studies will determine its value in clinical decision-making and longitudinal assessment.

Title: Age-Friendly Health System Recognition and Its Association with Improved Clinical Outcome Measures.
Journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
Abstract: The number of adults 65 years of age and older is rapidly increasing, as is health care utilization by older adults with multiple chronic conditions. The Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement, with a focus on What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility (the 4Ms), was launched in 2017 to improve management of older adults across health care settings. However, evidence of impact on outcomes remains limited. Using a national cohort of 4002 hospitals (388 with AFHS recognition from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement, as of December 31, 2024, and 3614 controls), the authors explore the associations between AFHS recognition and hospital readmission rates, mortality, and patient-reported experiences. Using difference-in-differences analyses, the authors find that level 2 AFHS recognition (i.e., hospitals with at least 3 months of data of older patients who have received 4Ms care) is associated with lower 30-day mortality rates for acute myocardial infarction (-0.41 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.75 to -0.06), pneumonia (-0.71; 95% CI, -1.29 to -0.13), and stroke (-0.56; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.07). Level 1 recognition (i.e., hospitals that have successfully developed plans to implement the 4Ms) is associated with lower readmission rates only for pneumonia (-0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.10). Furthermore, both level 1 and level 2 recognition are associated with modest reductions in Medicare spending per beneficiary. No determinative associations were identified between AFHS recognition and patient-reported experience measures. These findings provide one of the first national studies to suggest that organizations with AFHS recognition could be associated with improvement in certain outcomes and spending.

Title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T and I Discordance in Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serial troponin monitoring is used during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but guidelines do not specify whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) or T (hs-cTnT) should be measured. Unlike cardiac-specific hs-cTnI, hs-cTnT can rise from noncardiac sources.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of hs-cTnT/hs-cTnI discordance, identify clinical correlates, and evaluate prognostic implications in ambulatory ICI-treated patients.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort, patients starting ICI therapy underwent paired hs-cTnT (Roche Elecsys) and hs-cTnI (Siemens Atellica) measurements in the same banked samples at baseline and 1 month. Patients with adjudicated ICI-associated myocarditis or myositis were excluded by design.
RESULTS: Among 433 patients with paired baseline measurements, hs-cTnT was elevated in 37.9% and hs-cTnI in 1.8%; 158 (36.5%) were discordant (elevated hs-cTnT, normal hs-cTnI), and 267 (61.7%) had normal levels of both (κ = 0.036). Among 329 patients with paired data at baseline and 1 month, discordance prevalence was unchanged (38.3% vs 38.0%; McNemar P > 0.99). Independent correlates were older age, male sex, and chronic kidney disease (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 30.1 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier), elevated hs-cTnT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.00-1.81; P = 0.048); only 8 of 231 deaths (3.5%) were cardiac.
CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy, over one-third had elevated hs-cTnT with normal hs-cTnI: a stable, nonspecific pattern present before ICI exposure and consistent with noncardiac sources rather than acute cardiac injury. hs-cTnI is the more cardiac-specific assay; paired baseline measurement of both troponins may help contextualize later elevations when myocarditis is suspected.

Title: Immune Responses in Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Cardiovascular Immune-Related Adverse Events: JACC: CardioOncology State-of-the-Art Review.
Abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved cancer outcomes, their use can trigger autoimmune toxicities affecting essentially any organ system. In the cardiovascular system, these immune-related adverse events can manifest as myocarditis, pericarditis, accelerated atherosclerosis, vasculitis, arrhythmias, and other conditions. These cardiovascular toxicities are driven by the loss of peripheral tolerance, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Recent murine and human studies, particularly in immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated atherosclerosis and myocarditis, have begun to reveal the cellular and molecular mediators. Disinhibited T cell function is a central driver, but other immune and nonimmune cell types have also been implicated. Multiple inflammatory and chemokine receptor signaling pathways are activated, offering potential targets for intervention. The growing mechanistic understanding of these cardiovascular toxicities has begun to inform new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, though additional prospective trials are needed.

Title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
Abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of cortical activity and remains central to the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of iEEG data increasingly challenge conventional visual interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have accelerated quantitative analyses in electrophysiology, supporting localization, outcome prediction, and therapeutic decision-making in epilepsy. This article reviews recent advances in the application of AI to iEEG in epilepsy and in particular stereo-EEG, although the concepts discussed are broadly relevant across iEEG modalities. Although many of these approaches have shown encouraging results, the current evidence remains largely preliminary, with most studies being retrospective, single-center investigations that lack independent external validation. AI-based integration of iEEG with multimodal magnetic resonance imaging shows promise for improving surgical planning in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Concurrently, early studies suggest that AI-driven iEEG analysis may enhance epileptogenic zone identification by detecting subtle electrophysiological signatures, network interactions, and temporal dynamics. These multimodal frameworks emphasize distributed epileptic networks rather than isolated focal abnormalities. AI is also reshaping how iEEG-guided stimulation is designed and interpreted. Data-driven approaches have the potential to optimize stimulation parameters, predict network responses, and clarify mechanisms underlying diagnostic and therapeutic stimulation, laying the groundwork for adaptive, patient-specific neuromodulation. Beyond short-term epilepsy monitoring, AI applications increasingly incorporate continuous sensing, longitudinal network modeling, and integration with implantable neurotechnology platforms. Although these developments require prospective multicenter studies with external validation before widespread clinical implementation, advances in multimodal data integration, interpretable modeling, and continuous sensing position AI-enhanced iEEG as an emerging platform for precision brain network medicine for epilepsy.

Title: Oxytocin selectively enhances the recognition of infant sadness in postpartum depression.
Abstract: BackgroundLittle is known about the role of oxytocin in the processing of positive emotional infant cues in mothers with PPD.ObjectivesWe therefore examined whether intranasal oxytocin influences postpartum mothers' processing of positive infant emotional cues, both visual (facial expressions) and auditory (laughter), and intended caregiving responses.DesignThis double-blind randomized controlled crossover study included 45 mothers, with 3- to 9-month-old infants, who exhibited clinically relevant scores on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, with 35 mothers fulfilling the criteria of a major depressive episode assessed with the SCID-5.MethodsMothers participated in two randomized counterbalanced sessions, receiving oxytocin and placebo in separate sessions with a washout period in between. During both sessions they completed an infant facial emotion recognition (FER) task and listened to infant laughter while physiological and self-report measures were collected.ResultsWe found that oxytocin shifted response bias away from fear and toward sadness, while increasing accuracy for sad infant faces. This pattern suggests that oxytocin selectively reallocates attention from threat-related cues to those signaling infant need. Additionally, oxytocin elevated heart rate in response to infant laughter, indicating greater physiological engagement with positive cues, although self-reported affect and caregiving intentions were unaffected.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that oxytocin may fine-tune perceptual and physiological responsiveness to emotionally salient infant signals rather than uniformly enhancing positive emotion recognition. The adaptive implications of this shift remain mixed: enhanced sensitivity to sadness may facilitate caregiving, yet excessive focus on distress could increase negative affect in vulnerable mothers. Oxytocin's effects thus appear emotion-specific, potentially providing mechanistic insight into altered maternal perception in postpartum depression. Future work should examine real-world caregiving behaviors and individual moderators, such as depression severity and trauma history, to clarify oxytocin's potential therapeutic relevance. Registration: The study is registered at the European Clinical Trial Registry.

Title: Variability of Right Ventricular Structure and Function in Infants Across Different High-Altitude Regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO Sub-Study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Srour, MHD Osama, Darla Carvallo-Castañeda, Monica Medina, Gian Huaman, Rafael Marquez, and Katia Bravo-Jaimes.Variability of right ventricular structure and function in infants across different high-altitude regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO sub-study. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) predominance is a normal fetal state that rapidly regresses postnatally at sea level. High-altitude hypobaric hypoxic environment may alter this adaptation process. This study evaluated echocardiographic RV variations in healthy infants across different altitudes in the Peruvian Andes.
METHODS: This sub-study of the ANDES-CHD cohort included 81 healthy infants from sea level to 4,338 meters (m) in Peru. RV fractional area change (FAC) and indexed RV free wall thickness were measured. Multivariate linear regression assessed the independent effect of altitude, adjusting for relevant confounders.
RESULTS: Infants at higher altitudes exhibited a statistically significant reduction in RV FAC compared with sea level (45.5% at sea level vs. 38% at 3,259 m [p = 0.021] and 4,338 m [p = 0.006]), though all median values remained within normal physiological ranges. Sixteen percent of infants had an RV FAC < 35%, with no significant difference between high- and low-altitude groups, and no adverse outcome at 12-month follow-up. Indexed RV free wall thickness did not differ significantly across groups.
CONCLUSION: Healthy Andean infants demonstrate a physiological adaptation to high-altitude hypobaric hypoxia characterized by a statistical reduction in RV systolic function without pathological compromise, alongside normal postnatal regression of RV wall thickness.

Title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.
METHODS: The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

Title: Osteonecrosis in Antiphospholipid Syndrome: An Evidence Map and Diagnostic Attribution Framework for a Noncriteria Manifestation.
Abstract: Osteonecrosis has been reported in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) positivity, but because it also follows glucocorticoid exposure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), alcohol use, trauma, pregnancy, transplantation, and thrombophilia, its status as an APS-related manifestation is uncertain, and clinicians lack a structured way to decide whether it is APS-attributable or coincidental. We conducted a structured narrative review with evidence mapping, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus from inception to May 2026 with citation chasing; eligible reports described osteonecrosis, avascular necrosis, aseptic necrosis, or bone infarction in confirmed APS or documented aPL positivity. Twenty-two publications were charted for design, phenotype, osteonecrosis site, diagnostic modality, competing etiologies, and attribution, and synthesized narratively. Reported frequencies ranged from 3.75% and 4.5% for clinically ascertained disease to 20% for asymptomatic magnetic resonance imaging screen-detected disease in steroid-naïve primary APS-estimates that are not directly comparable. Femoral-head disease predominated, but multifocal, bilateral, and atypical-site lesions were repeatedly described. Attribution was strongest in young patients with persistent high-risk aPL, minimal traditional risk factors, and concurrent thrombotic, obstetric, or microvascular features, yet competing causes, especially glucocorticoids and SLE-frequently coexisted. We propose the APSO framework, stratifying attribution into four tiers (high-confidence, probable, uncertain/mixed, and aPL-positive osteonecrosis without classifiable APS) by APS certainty, aPL risk, osteonecrosis phenotype, and competing-cause burden. Osteonecrosis is a candidate noncriteria skeletal manifestation of APS, but aPL positivity alone is insufficient for causal attribution; prospective validation is required.

Title: Cystatin C, Neutrophil Gelatinase-associated Lipocalin, and Pro-atrial Natriuretic Peptide as Biomarkers in the Assessment of Diabetic Nephropathy Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a significant microvascular complication linked with diabetes mellitus which leads to chronic kidney disease worldwide. Conventional biomarkers, namely, serum creatinine and albuminuria often fail to detect early renal impairment.
AIM: The study aimed to compare the utility of serum cystatin C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), and pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) for assessing the severity of DN.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, observational study was conducted on 52 DN cases and 52 controls. Clinical and laboratory parameters of all were assessed at baseline. Serum creatinine, cystatin C, NGAL, and pro-ANP of cases were measured at baseline, 6 months and 12 months. Statistical analysis, including group comparison, correlation and regression analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and longitudinal analysis, was done on IBM SPSSv26.
RESULTS: At baseline, cases had significantly higher serum creatinine, cystatin C, and NGAL than controls. Pro-ANP was higher in cases but not significant. A significant Pearson's correlation appeared between cystatin C (r = -0.852), creatinine (r = -0.833), pro-ANP (r = -0.553), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (all P < 0.001). No significant correlation was observed between NGAL and eGFR. ROC analysis showed that cystatin C had the highest diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.995, P < 0.001). Time trend analysis highlighted a significant increase of cystatin C, pro-ANP, and serum creatinine (P < 0.001), but not for NGAL (P = 0.093), with increasing renal impairment over 12 months.
CONCLUSION: Cystatin C demonstrated strongest correlation with eGFR and highest diagnostic accuracy. Time trend analysis revealed significant increase in cystatin C level over 12 months, highlighting its potential role as biomarker for monitoring DN patients.

Title: A Cross-sectional Study for Estimation of Prevalence of Cognitive Impairment in Epileptic Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a frequent, but frequently overlooked, complication of epilepsy that has a negative impact on patients' quality of life and functioning. Recurrent seizures and neurological factors can have a deleterious effect on multiple cognitive domains such as memory, attention, and executive function. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scale was used to assess cognitive impairment in patients with epilepsy in this study.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to estimate the prevalence of cognitive impairment in patients with diagnosed epilepsy for more than 2 years using the MoCA scale, assess cognitive function using the MoCA score in epilepsy patients, and determine the prevalence of cognitive impairment.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted among 97 patients with epilepsy for 18 months. A MoCA scale (0-30) was used to evaluate cognitive function. Means and standard deviations were given for numerical variables, and frequencies and percentages were reported for categorical variables. The Fisher's exact test or Chi-square test was used for the analysis of categorical variables as appropriate.
RESULTS: The prevalence of cognitive impairment was significantly higher in the group with hypertension (45, 95.7%) than in the group without hypertension (40, 80.0%) (χ2 = 5.54, P = 0.02). The association between cognitive impairment and diabetes mellitus was not statistically significant. The associations with hypothyroidism, cerebrovascular accident, and ischemic heart disease were not statistically significant, as per Fisher's exact test (P = 0.99, 0.07, and 0.99, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Based on these findings, it is concluded that there is a need to consider cognitive impairment as an important and often unrecognized comorbidity with the overall disease burden of patients with epilepsy. The authors emphasize that it is crucial to include routine cognitive assessments in daily clinical practice.

Title: Diabetes, stone composition, and renal function in a large cohort of patients with nephrolithiasis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrolithiasis is linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetic patients may be at higher risk for renal decline. However, the interaction of diabetes, stone composition, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectory in patients with nephrolithiasis remains underexplored, particularly in community-based populations.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of adult stone formers with a urinary stone composition analysis on file, diabetes status and stone composition were extracted from electronic records of a large health maintenance organization. Longitudinal eGFR measurements assessed renal function decline, and the effects of stone type, diabetes, and recurrent stone events on eGFR trajectory were evaluated.
RESULTS: This study included 6,771 stone formers; 1,543 (23%) had diabetes. Diabetic patients had a significantly higher prevalence of uric-acid stones (18.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.0001). Baseline eGFR differed robustly by stone type and diabetes status. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension, the rate of eGFR decline did not differ significantly by diabetes status within either the calcium-oxalate nor uric-acid subtype. Recurrent stone formers had greater renal function loss, while socioeconomic status had limited impact on eGFR change.
CONCLUSION: Diabetic and non-diabetic stone formers show distinct baseline eGFR profiles that differ by stone composition, and diabetes was strongly associated with uric-acid stone formation; however, diabetes was not associated with an accelerated rate of eGFR decline once adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension. These findings support baseline risk stratification, rather than an accelerated-decline phenotype, as the key actionable insight for diabetic stone formers.

Title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome as an Under-Recognized Cause of Ischemic Stroke in Older Adults: A Retrospective Case Series.
Abstract: Background, objective, and methods: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is classically regarded as a cause of thrombosis and stroke in younger patients and is often considered a rare etiology beyond the sixth decade. We retrospectively describe seven older adults (ages 67-90 years; median 76; four females) with ischemic stroke in whom antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) were identified during evaluation, most after one or more cerebrovascular events. Results: Six of the seven had radiographic or clinical evidence of prior cerebrovascular disease, and several had experienced recurrent events despite antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy. Antibody profiles were heterogeneous, ranging from triple positivity with confirmed persistence to isolated lupus anticoagulant and IgM-only positivity, and competing stroke mechanisms (patent foramen ovale, large-artery atherosclerosis, and small-vessel disease) were frequently present. All patients were transitioned to a vitamin K antagonist. Conclusions: This series illustrates that aPL-associated stroke does occur in older adults and supports considering APS in the differential of cryptogenic or recurrent ischemic stroke in this population, while underscoring the need for high-specificity, persistently confirmed testing before committing a patient to lifelong anticoagulation.

Title: Metabolic, Atherogenic, and Anthropometric Markers for Discrimination of Premature Coronary Artery Disease in a Predominantly Statin-Treated Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) is increasingly recognized in younger adults and requires improved risk stratification. Conventional lipid markers may have limited discriminative value, particularly when lipid levels reflect ongoing statin therapy. This study evaluated the associations and discriminatory performance of metabolic, atherogenic, and anthropometric indices for PCAD and developed internally validated dynamic nomograms for PCAD case discrimination.
PATIENT AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective case-control study used data from the Iran Premature Coronary Artery Disease registry. A total of 3063 adults undergoing coronary angiography were included, comprising 1929 patients with PCAD and 1134 controls. Twelve metabolic, lipid-based, and anthropometric indices were calculated from fasting glucose, lipid profiles, and body measurements. Participants were randomly divided into training and validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, integrated discrimination improvement, net reclassification improvement, and decision-curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance.
RESULTS: Atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), and a body shape index (ABSI) showed consistent independent associations with PCAD. Individually, these indices showed modest discrimination. The conventional clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.677. Adding AIP and binary ABSI increased the AUC to 0.721, while the TyG plus binary ABSI model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.724, representing modest but statistically significant improvements over the conventional model. Both final models showed favorable internal calibration, and improvement in reclassification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Two dynamic web-based nomograms were developed for individualized PCAD case discrimination.
CONCLUSION: TyG, AIP, and ABSI were independently associated with PCAD and provided modest incremental discrimination beyond conventional risk factors in this predominantly statin-treated case-control cohort. The resulting dynamic nomograms provide an accessible framework for PCAD case discrimination; however, their clinical applicability and estimation of absolute risk require external validation in independent, preferably prospective, populations.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Brain edema progression rate on serial CT predicts neurological outcome after cardiac arrest: a region-specific biomarker of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the attenuation change rate on serial brain computed tomography (CT), a novel quantitative marker of temporal cerebral attenuation change, for predicting poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest (CA).
METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort. CA patients who underwent cranial CT both within 12 h and between 12 h and one week after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) were included. The attenuation change rate, calculated as the HU difference between paired scans divided by the time interval, was measured in 12 predefined brain regions. Neurological outcome was assessed using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) at discharge.
RESULTS: Of 53 patients enrolled, 17 (32.1%) had favorable neurological outcomes at discharge. Patients with poor outcomes exhibited significantly greater attenuation decline rates in all gray matter regions except for gray matter at the centrum semiovale level, including the caudate nucleus (-0.01 vs. 0.02 HU/h), putamen (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), thalamus (-0.02 vs. 0.01 HU/h), gray matter of the high convexity (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), and cerebellar gray matter (-0.02 vs. 0.03 HU/h) (all P < 0.01), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in any of the white matter regions. ROC analysis demonstrated AUCs ranging from 0.725 to 0.778, with cerebellar gray matter achieving the highest AUC (0.778; sensitivity, 75.0%; specificity, 76.5%). At the 100% specificity threshold, the caudate nucleus showed the highest sensitivity for predicting poor outcome (36.1% at a decline rate of -0.040 HU/h).
CONCLUSION: Serial CT-derived attenuation change rate may serve as an exploratory quantitative marker of cerebral edema progression after cardiac arrest. However, this single-center, small-sample study does not support its use for withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment decisions. Multicenter validation is warranted.

Title: Thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risks after mastectomy with vs without direct-to-implant reconstruction.
Abstract: Immediate direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction after mastectomy provides aesthetic and logistic advantages, including single-stage restoration and avoidance of tissue expansion. However, concerns persist that increased operative duration and procedural complexity may elevate thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risk. This study compared 90-day postoperative complication rates between mastectomy and mastectomy+DTI reconstruction. A multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult female patients with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy with or without immediate DTI between 2010 and 2025 were included; autologous and staged reconstructions were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, oncologic history, and preoperative medications. Outcomes included hematoma, acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). After matching, 11 538 patients (5769 pairs) were analyzed. Mastectomy+DTI was associated with lower hematoma rates (54 patients [0.94%] vs 81 [1.40%]; risk ratio [RR], 0.675; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.95; P = .024) and fewer DVT events (22 patients [0.38%] vs 48 [0.83%]; RR, 0.458; 95% CI, 0.28-0.76; P = .002). PE occurred in 17 patients (0.29%) vs 29 (0.50%) (RR, 0.586; 95% CI, 0.32-1.07; P = .076). Immediate DTI after mastectomy was associated with lower short-term rates of hematoma and DVT, with a nonsignificant trend toward lower PE rates. These findings suggest that immediate DTI was not associated with increased short-term thromboembolic or hemorrhagic morbidity in this matched cohort. Given the limitations of coding-based observational data and potential residual confounding, prospective multicenter studies incorporating granular perioperative variables are required to confirm these associations and refine risk-stratified decision-making in reconstructive care.

Title: Real-world thrombotic and survival outcomes with ESAs in cancer-related anemia.
Abstract: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are commonly used to treat cancer-related anemia by increasing hemoglobin levels and reducing transfusion requirements.
