OBJECTIVE: This study describes the dosing and hemodynamic effects associated with the interfacility administration of dexmedetomidine in patients with alpha-2 adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Secondarily, we describe the safety of dexmedetomidine in this patient population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case review of patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions in the interfacility setting for presumed alpha-2-adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Demographic data, dosing, and vital signs were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Over a six-month period, of 217 cases identified, 182 contained complete hemodynamic data. The average age was 39.5 years, and 67% were male. The average transport time was 15.7 minutes (range, 5-40 minutes). The mean dexmedetomidine infusion rate was 1.32 (0.31) mcg/kg/hr. The average mean arterial pressure decreased from 122.1 mm Hg (21.7) at the time of initial patient contact to 118.3 mm Hg (21.7) (mean difference, 3.80; 95% CI, 1.96-5.64) at final patient interaction. Heart rate also showed a minimal change from 104.9 (23.7) to 103.6 (21.8) beats/min (mean 1.3; 95% CI, -0.48 to 3.08). No cases of severe hypotension or clinically significant bradycardia requiring intervention were documented (one-sided 95% CI, 0-1.7%).
CONCLUSION: In this case series of patients, prehospital dexmedetomidine infusions to treat alpha-2-agonist withdrawal were associated with stable hemodynamics without significant bradycardia or hypotension. These findings support the safety of dexmedetomidine infusions for interfacility transport and provide a rationale for examining whether advanced life support clinicians can safely transport patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions for this indication.

Title: Partial Immersion Using Body Bags for Exertional Hyperthermia: A Randomized Crossover Study.
Journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recent recommendations suggest emergency medical personnel should consider rapid whole-body cooling for heat stroke patients. Cold-water immersion maximizes cooling rate and subsequent outcomes following heat stroke. Body bags filled with ice and water may provide portable, accessible partial cold-water immersion for this setting. The purpose of this study was to determine whole-body cooling rates when using body bags to facilitate partial cold-water immersion to treat exertional hyperthermia.
METHODS: A total of 9 healthy participants (8 male; mean [SD] age, 24 [4] years; height, 175 [7] cm; body mass, 83.6 [21.6] kg) completed our randomized-crossover field study. Following hydration verification, participants completed a self-paced 400 warm-up run, 1,609 m run, and 10-m sprints until rectal temperature (T-rec) reached 39.2 °C or volitional exhaustion. Following exercise, participants were cooled for a maximum of 30 minutes lying supine in the shade (control; CON) or in body bags filled with 20 gallons of ice water (5.2 [1.6] °C). Following cooling, participants sat upright for a 15-minute recovery. T-rec and heart rate (HR) were taken throughout exercise, every minute of cooling, and every 5 minutes of recovery. Participants completed both trials separated by 1 week in random order.
RESULTS: Wet bulb globe temperature between trials was not significantly different (grand mean, 28.43 [1.03] °C; P = .73). There was no difference in participant maximum T-rec (body bag, 38.98 [.23] °C; CON, 38.93 [.39] °C; P = .45); HR (body bag, 183 [14] beats per minute [bpm]; CON, 189 [13] bpm; P = .21); rating of perceived exertion (P >.99); thirst (P = .62); or thermal sensation (P = .73) during exercise. Fluid consumed (P = .40), body mass change (P = .90), 400 m run times (P = .19) and 1,609 m run times (P = .17) were no different between trials. Whole-body cooling rate for body bag was .102 (.04) °C/min, whereas CON produced a cooling rate of .040 (.04) °C/min (95% CI, .030-.095; P = .002). Total cooling time was significantly faster (13.2 (5.8) min) with BB compared to CON (27.6 (4.2) min; 95% CI, 9.2-19.5; P = .002).
CONCLUSION: In clinical settings where full-body cold-water immersion is not feasible, or during emergency transport, partial immersion via body bags offers acceptable cooling rates for hyperthermic patients. Emergency medical personnel could apply these data for support in updating heat stroke protocols to include partial immersion via body bag during transport, or immediately upon emergency department arrival.

Title: Impact of a Decision-Support Interface on Mental Workload and Stress in Prehospital Stroke Triage: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
Journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prehospital triage challenges often lead to suboptimal choices and delayed treatment for stroke patients. The objective of the study was to evaluate whether a decision-support interface to assist in stroke triage to an appropriate hospital could reduce emergency medical technicians' (EMT) mental workload.
METHODS: This randomized crossover study was conducted between February and March 2025. Each participant completed two 12-minute simulated trials in randomized order: current dispatch orders without decision support and a decision-support interface. We assessed mental workload-the mental effort required to make hospital transport decisions under time pressure during prehospital stroke triage-using heart rate variability (HRV) metrics and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). System usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale. The primary outcome was the root mean square of successive differences for each participant after completing the two trials. The secondary outcomes included the differences of NASA-TLX, System Usability Scale, and other heart rate variability parameters, including mean R-R interval (meanRR), mean heart rate, percentage of successive R-R intervals that differ by more than 50 milliseconds, low-frequency power (LF), high-frequency (HF) power, and the LF/HF ratio. Subgroup analyses examined differences by sex, education, age, and years of service.
RESULTS: A total of 35 emergency medical technician (EMT)-intermediate participants (mean age, 27.5 [5.3] years) completed the study. For the primary outcome, the root mean square of successive differences increased significantly (28.1 [13.0] vs 32.4 [13.6] milliseconds; mean difference, 4.3 milliseconds [95% CI, 1.57-6.99]; P < .01), indicating reduced mental workload when the participants used the decision-support interface. For the secondary outcomes, mean heart rate (77.5 [8.6] vs 73.8 [10.6], P < .01) decreased, mean R (784.2 [89.5] vs 808.9 [87.3], P < .01) increased, and HF power (370.1 [291.7] versus 482.6 [433.9], P = .02) increased, suggesting reduced mental workload when the participants used the decision-support interface. The mental demand scores in NASA-TLX decreased from 62.5 (14.6) to 35.5 (17.0). Emergency medical technicians with 1.0-1.5 years of service reported higher System Usability Scale scores than those with 1.5-3.0 years (84.4 versus 71.3, P = .02), and 82.9% of participants rated the system as acceptable (System Usability Scale score ≥ 70).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that integrating a web-based decision-support interface effectively reduces mental workload and psychological stress among EMTs in stroke triage.

Title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Cost Savings from Emergency Department Chest Pain Patient Evaluation: A Monte Carlo Simulation.
Journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chest pain patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) often require risk stratification through stress testing, which may necessitate hospitalization. This practice contributes to ED crowding by occupying beds with low-risk patients who may derive limited benefit from testing, thereby increasing bed occupancy, prolonging ED boarding times, amplifying crowding, and resource strain. Use of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven clinical decision support tool improves the detection of obstructive coronary artery disease and focuses diagnostic testing on those most likely to benefit.
METHODS: We created a Monte Carlo simulation informed by available published inputs and ran 1,000 trials to estimate the national impact of using an AI-driven decision-support tool to reduce avoidable downstream cardiac testing among eligible U.S. ED patients with chest pain. Model inputs included patient demographics, chest pain history, electrocardiogram (ECG) findings, medication use, and lab values (including some nonroutine tests). Our primary outcome was U.S. annual cost savings from reclassifying eligible ED patients using an AI-driven decision-support tool. Secondary outcomes included reductions in short-stay hospitalizations, cancer cases, and cancer deaths due to averted radiation exposure.
RESULTS: Universal adoption of an AI-driven decision-support tool was estimated to save a mean (standard deviation) of $675 million ($340 million) by avoiding 688,000 (147,000) downstream cardiac diagnostic tests. This resulted in annual decreases of 537,000 (115,000) hospitalizations, 8.30 million (1.96 million) bed hours, 490 (150) new cancer diagnoses, and 250 (80) cancer deaths.
CONCLUSION: Assuming similar recategorization of patients seen in a European outpatient cohort, widespread adoption of an AI-driven clinical decision-support tool to evaluate U.S. ED patients with suspected obstructive coronary disease could yield substantial benefits by reducing avoidable downstream cardiac testing. By accurately identifying patients who do not require urgent diagnostics, this approach could help mitigate crowding, relieve resource strain, and improve patient flow-supporting a more efficient emergency care system.

Title: Physiologic Stress During Walking and Cycling Early After Cardiac Surgery.
Journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize cardiac effort and heart rate (HR) responses during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) early after cardiac surgery, compare HR patterns between walking and cycle ergometry, and evaluate differences by sex, frailty, and atrial fibrillation status.
METHODS: We analyzed a publicly available PhysioNet dataset of adults ≥65 years with pre-frailty/frailty undergoing cardiac surgery who completed a 6MWT and symptom-limited cycle ergometry with continuous single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring (Polar H10). Cardiac effort was defined as total 6MWT heartbeats divided by distance walked (beats/m). Associations with cycle-ergometry performance were assessed using Spearman correlations with bootstrap CI; paired t tests compared HR responses between modalities; subgroup differences were evaluated using Welch t tests and multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled participants, 66 (83%) had analyzable 6MWT ECG recordings (mean age 73 ± 5 years; 67% male; 18 ± 8 days post-surgery). Mean 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) was 300 ± 79 m, and mean cardiac effort was 1.62 ± 0.52 beats/m. In 38 participants with paired cycle-ergometry data, HR responses were similar between walking and cycling. Greater 6MWD was associated with better cycle-ergometry performance, while higher cardiac effort was associated with lower cycle-ergometry performance. In multivariable analysis, female sex was independently associated with higher cardiac effort (β = .34 beats/m; P = .042), atrial fibrillation with lower average and end-of-test HR (P ≤ .035), and greater frailty with shorter 6MWD (P = .036).
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac effort is a feasible ECG-derived metric that complements 6MWD by integrating heart rate response with functional performance early after cardiac surgery. In this frail, predominantly beta-blocked cohort, HR responses during walking closely mirrored cycle ergometry.

Title: Recanalization After Acute Cervical Artery Dissection: A Multicenter International Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rates and factors associated with complete recanalization after cervical artery dissection (CeAD) have not been comprehensively quantified in large cohorts. We sought to determine the 6-month rate of complete recanalization in CeAD, clinical and imaging factors associated with recanalization, and risk of recurrent ischemic stroke based on recanalization status.
METHODS: This was a planned subanalysis of the Antithrombotic Treatment for Stroke Prevention in Cervical Artery Dissection study, a multicenter retrospective cohort including patients with imaging-confirmed CeAD diagnosed between January 2015 and June 2022 at 63 sites worldwide. For this analysis, we included 1,095 patients with single-vessel CeAD causing stenosis at presentation who had available follow-up vascular imaging at 6 months after CeAD. The primary outcome was complete recanalization within 6 months after CeAD. Clinical and imaging variables, as well as recurrent stroke, were compared between patients with and those without complete recanalization. Factors independently associated with complete recanalization were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Time to complete recanalization was analyzed using an accelerated failure time Weibull model.
RESULTS: Among 1,095 included patients (median age 45 years; 46.7% female), 634 (57.9%) achieved complete recanalization by 6 months. In multivariable analysis, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of complete recanalization (odds ratio [OR] 0.97 per year; 95% CI 0.96-0.98; p < 0.001). Diabetes (OR 0.46; 95% CI 0.27-0.81; p = 0.006), active smoking (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50-0.95; p = 0.025), and complete occlusion at presentation (OR 0.44; 95% CI 0.32-0.59; p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of complete recanalization. Complete occlusion at presentation was associated with both longer time to, and lower rates of, complete recanalization. We observed no effect of antithrombotic regimen (antiplatelet therapy vs anticoagulation) on complete recanalization. Incomplete recanalization was associated with a nonsignificant numerically higher proportion of recurrent stroke (5.4% vs 3.5%; p = 0.064).
DISCUSSION: Almost 60% of patients with CeAD achieved complete vessel recanalization by 6 months. Older age, diabetes, smoking, and complete occlusion at presentation were independently associated with incomplete recanalization. Further study is required to determine whether these findings may help guide tailored imaging surveillance and secondary prevention strategies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Differential Trajectories of Brain Atrophy in Multiple Sclerosis, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD: The Role of Disease Activity in MOGAD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Multiple sclerosis (MS), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4 + NMOSD) are inflammatory demyelinating disorders with distinct mechanisms of tissue injury. MS is characterized by diffuse neurodegeneration, whereas damage in antibody-mediated diseases is considered attack related. In MOGAD, the relationship between disease activity and brain atrophy remains unclear. We aimed to compare longitudinal trajectories of global and regional brain atrophy across MS, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD and investigate whether atrophy in MOGAD is associated with disease course and lesion dynamics.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis (MAGNIMS) study, patients fulfilling the following criteria were enrolled: (1) age 18 years or older, (2) MS/MOGAD/AQP4 + NMOSD diagnosis, (3) ≥2 same-scanner brain MRIs ≥6 months apart and ≥3 months postattack, (4) concurrent Expanded Disability Status Scale, and (5) disease course information. White matter lesions were segmented using the Lesion Segmentation Toolbox. Longitudinal brain volumes were quantified on lesion-filled T1-weighted images using Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG) with a within-subject template approach. In MOGAD, lesion dynamics were classified as stable/new lesions/lesion resolution. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, baseline volume, and center estimated atrophy rates.
RESULTS: Overall, 489 participants from 15 centers were included (98 MS [mean age 39.79 years, 68.37% female], 72 MOGAD [42.14 years, 66.67%], 41 AQP4 + NMOSD [51.25 years, 87.80%], and 278 healthy controls [42.94 years, 61.87%]). The mean follow-up was MS: 2.44 ± 1.55 years, MOGAD: 2.57 ± 1.85, and AQP4 + NMOSD: 3.22 ± 2.42. Compared with controls, MS showed accelerated global brain atrophy (β = -2.027 cm3 per year, 95% CI -3.430 to -0.623). MOGAD demonstrated white matter volume loss (β = -0.989, 95% CI -1.889 to -0.090) and ventricular enlargement (lateral: β = 0.219, 95% CI 0.089-0.350; third ventricle: β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.003-0.015). AQP4 + NMOSD showed pallidal volume reduction (β = -0.008, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.001). Within MOGAD, relapsing patients (62.5%) exhibited greater third ventricular expansion than MS (β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.001-0.017). MOGAD with new lesions (22.22%) had greater ventricular enlargement than controls (lateral: β = 0.359, 95% CI 0.147-0.572; third ventricle: β = 0.016, 95% CI 0.006-0.025), MS, and AQP4 + NMOSD.
DISCUSSION: Each inflammatory demyelinating disease exhibits a characteristic pattern of brain atrophy. In MOGAD, neuroaxonal loss seems associated with inflammatory activity and lesion accrual, supporting an event-driven pattern of tissue injury rather than diffuse neurodegeneration. Limitations include small NMOSD sample, heterogeneous follow-up, and potential scanner-related variability.

Title: A Recipe for Better Diabetes Management: The DASH4D Dietary Pattern.
Abstract: The 2026 American Diabetes Association "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes extensive nutrition recommendations for people with diabetes but stops short of recommending a specific dietary pattern. Instead, the guidelines recommend that all patients be referred for individualized nutrition therapy. This approach appropriately acknowledges diverse patient needs; however, it is difficult for providers to deliver any form of individualized dietary guidance without a clear starting point to guide them. In this article we examine the tension between the needs for individualization and evidence-based nutritional standards in diabetes care. We argue that the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary pattern stands out as being supported by decades of evidence from rigorous randomized clinical trials, meta-analyses, and large observational studies that have established its benefit for cardiovascular health. We summarize the recently completed DASH for Diabetes (DASH4D) trial, which demonstrated that a modified version of the original DASH eating plan, adapted for adults with diabetes, significantly reduced blood pressure and improved glycemic control in participants with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. We conclude that while individualized dietary counseling remains the standard of care, the DASH4D diet should be a recommended diet for patients with diabetes.

Title: Integrative analysis of systemic biomarkers and carotid plaque instability in patients with atherosclerosis: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract: ObjectiveCarotid plaque instability is associated with ischemic stroke; however, its relationship with systemic pathways remains incompletely understood. We explored associations between inflammatory, coagulation, metabolic, and renal biomarkers and ultrasound-defined carotid plaque instability.MethodsThis exploratory, single-center, retrospective cross-sectional association study included patients who underwent carotid ultrasonography between March 2021 and March 2025. Laboratory and imaging variables were compared between stable and unstable plaques. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed in four system-specific models adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus, followed by an integrated analysis. The incremental contribution of CRP and eGFR beyond clinical covariates was explored by comparing discrimination and calibration, with bootstrap resampling used to assess optimism.Results361 patients were included (311 stable; 50 unstable). A history of stroke was more common in the unstable-plaque group (p < 0.05). CRP levels were higher in the unstable-plaque group, whereas eGFR did not differ between groups. In multivariable analyses, no biomarker was independently associated with plaque instability. In the integrated model (n = 326; 43 events), history of stroke was associated with plaque instability (OR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.15-5.25, p = 0.020), whereas CRP (OR = 1.002 per 1 mg/L, 95% CI 0.997-1.007, p = 0.450) and eGFR (OR = 0.999 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2, 95% CI 0.988-1.011, p = 0.913) were not associated. AUCs were 0.704 for the clinical model and 0.709 for the integrated model (ΔAUC = +0.005), indicating minimal incremental discrimination.ConclusionsHistory of stroke was associated with carotid plaque instability, whereas CRP and eGFR were not independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Adding CRP and eGFR to clinical variables provided minimal incremental discrimination, suggesting limited additional value for distinguishing ultrasound-defined plaque instability. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than temporal or causal relationships.

Title: Immune-related DNA methylation signatures, age prediction, and cross-tissue assessment via biologically informed neural networks.
Abstract: Immune-related DNA methylation patterns may provide interpretable markers of biological ageing and disease relevance. This exploratory study integrated four Illumina HumanMethylation450 and MethylationEPIC datasets comprising paediatric peripheral-blood leukocytes (GSE36054; 192 retained after quality control), infant buccal cells (n = 542), neuronal nuclei (n = 58), and peripheral blood from a polybrominated-biphenyl exposure cohort (n = 659). The paediatric peripheral-blood dataset served as the primary modelling cohort, with infant buccal cells providing an independent early-life cross-tissue reference. Processing included cohort-specific quality control and normalisation, batch adjustment, empirical-Bayes differential methylation analysis, pathway enrichment, repeated 10-fold cross-validation, biologically informed neural-network modelling, feature attribution, cross-tissue assessment, gene-ablation analysis, disease mapping, and two-sample Mendelian randomisation. IL6, CXCR4, CDK11 and CREBBP showed the strongest coherent methylation signals and stable predictive contributions, whereas BCLAF1 contributed less consistently. These loci mapped to cytokine-receptor interaction, chemokine signalling, G2/M checkpoint regulation, histone acetylation, and apoptosis-related pathways. The neural network achieved a cross-validated mean absolute error of 1.87 years and R2 of 0.781; removing the polybrominated-biphenyl-associated feature filter yielded comparable performance (MAE 1.91 years; R2 = 0.772). Prioritised features also showed cross-tissue consistency in infant buccal cells. Mendelian randomisation identified genetically supported associations of IL6 methylation with preterm birth and lower mean birth weight and of CXCR4 methylation with preterm birth after multiplicity correction. These associations do not establish that methylation itself causes the outcomes. The findings prioritise immune-related methylation features across paediatric blood and infant buccal contexts within an interpretable framework for age-related methylation and outcome-oriented molecular investigation.

Title: Droplet digital PCR as a first-line detection tool in the genetic diagnosis of vascular anomalies.
Abstract: Targeted precision therapies are increasingly used in the treatment of individuals with vascular anomalies (VAs). This increases the need for rapid, accurate and inexpensive genetic diagnosis. Droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) is an alternative to next-generation sequencing (NGS), permitting rapid, highly sensitive interrogation of recurrent pathogenic mosaic variants. We examined the feasibility of ddPCR as a primary diagnostic tool in a large cohort of individuals with VAs. Lesional tissue was collected for ddPCR of up to 46 recurrent pathogenic variants across 16 genes associated with VAs. Specimens were assessed on a subset of assays for each individual based on clinical phenotype. Most individuals who had negative ddPCR results went on to high-depth gene panel or deep exome NGS, or Sanger sequencing. Here we report the phenotypic and molecular findings for 78 newly recruited and tested individuals in addition to the 60 individuals already reported from our cohort. The overall diagnostic yield for our cohort when combined with individuals previously reported was 104/138 (75%). Of 138 individuals tested, recurrent pathogenic variants were detected in 71 (51%) on ddPCR. Variants were most frequently identified in PIK3CA (n = 28), TEK (n = 18), GNAQ (n = 12), or MAP2K1 (n = 7). In a further 33 individuals, pathogenic variants were identified on NGS or Sanger sequencing. Our findings indicate that ddPCR is an efficient method achieving a high diagnostic yield in our cohort when used prior to sequencing.

Title: Age Phenotypes, Angiographic Complexity, and Inflammatory-Metabolic Profiles in First-Presentation STEMI.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Age-based comparisons in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) often use a binary young-older framework, which may obscure premature non-young disease. We evaluated age-group patterns in measured modifiable risk factors, angiographic complexity, inflammatory-metabolic indices, and in-hospital outcomes in patients presenting with first STEMI.
METHOD: This single-center retrospective study screened 421 STEMI records between January 2019 and May 2026. After exclusions, 150 patients were selected from an eligible pool of 229 using sex-stratified, equal-size quota sampling. The groups were defined as young STEMI (≤45 years), premature non-young STEMI (men 46-55 years, women 46-65 years), and older STEMI (men >55 years, women >65 years). Measured four-component standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factor (SMuRF) burden, angiographic findings, SYNTAX score, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score (HALP), C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR), mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were analyzed. Two multivariable models were used to assess age group and SYNTAX score.
RESULTS: Smoking prevalence decreased across groups, whereas diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and measured four-component SMuRF burden increased with age. Thrombus was most frequently observed in young STEMI. SYNTAX score, multivessel disease, SYNTAX ≥23, SII, and CAR increased with age, whereas HALP decreased. Non-smoking SMuRF burden distinguished premature non-young STEMI and older STEMI from young STEMI; older STEMI was independently associated with a higher SYNTAX score. No significant differences in mortality or MACE were detected.
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort, young STEMI was characterized by smoking predominance, a higher prevalence of angiographic thrombus, and lower coronary complexity, whereas older STEMI showed greater measured four-component SMuRF burden, increased coronary complexity, and less favorable inflammatory-metabolic indices. No differences were detected in in-hospital mortality or MACE.

Title: Stroke Caregiver Education and Training in an Inpatient Sub-Acute Setting: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
Journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Caregiver burden is a significant issue post-stroke. Caregivers demonstrate unmet needs throughout the rehabilitation phase, with limited literature that delves into the details of caregiver education and training (CGET) provision prior to discharge.
OBJECTIVES: To identify current practice of multidisciplinary team documentation of CGET following stroke on an inpatient subacute neurosciences ward.
METHODS: A retrospective clinical audit was conducted on 109 stroke admissions on an inpatient subacute neurosciences ward. Documented demographic information, admission and discharge Functional Independence Measure scores, and CGET from the multidisciplinary team were collected using a purpose-built audit tool. Descriptive analysis and sub-group comparison explored the findings against the Stroke Guideline recommendations.
RESULTS: Data from 109 records were included, which identified 1398 episodes of CGET. Social work (SW) (79.9%) and occupational therapy (OT) (77.1%) documented CGET more consistently than other disciplines. CGET was significantly more likely to be documented for patients with cognitive impairment, yet only three of 28 (10.7%) individuals with memory impairment had documented CGET relating to memory strategies. Nursing staff documented minimal CGET across all domains, including management of continence.
CONCLUSIONS: Inconsistent CGET was documented for stroke recovery relating to activities of daily living, mobility and cognition. Variable documentation practices highlighted challenges with interpretation. Further research is needed to determine whether functional limitations of patients are being matched with the appropriate CGET.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: multidisciplinary team caregiver education and training provision and documentation needs to be consistent, particularly relating to cognition, continence, mobility and activities of daily living.

Title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary bifurcation lesions remain one of the most challenging lesions. In particular, satisfactory clinical outcomes have not yet been achieved for side branches. The use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary arteries. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of additional DCB inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions.
METHODS: The OCVC-BIF study (Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branch of Bifurcation Lesions) was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial. Patients with bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation were enrolled in the study. The patients were randomized to receive either additional dilatation of the side branch using a DCB after DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation (DCB group) or only DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation using conventional balloons (non-DCB group). The primary end point was restenosis of the side branch, assessed using scheduled coronary angiography at 9 months or symptom-driven coronary angiography during the 1-year follow-up. Restenosis was defined as ≥50% stenosis of the side branch, determined using 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography. The key secondary end points included major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, which were defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis.
RESULTS: In total, 299 patients were randomized into the DCB (151 patients) and non-DCB (148 patients) groups between October 2019 and September 2024. Serial 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography evaluation was performed in 262 (87.6%) patients. The restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than that in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012). However, the incidence of major adverse cardiac events at 12 months was similar between them (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58).
CONCLUSIONS: Additional DCB inflation in the side branch after main-vessel DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation decreases restenosis in the side branch in the treatment of bifurcation lesions.

Title: Familial hypercholesterolaemia and thymic ageing in a Chinese cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lifelong exposure to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) patients not only increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but also affects other organs beyond the cardiovascular system. In a large FH cohort, this study investigated the effects of hypercholesterolaemia on the thymic output and explored whether lipid-lowering therapy can reverse these effects.
METHODS: According to the Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria, 562 heterozygous FH patients (236 treatment-naïve, 326 on lipid-lowering therapy) and 295 age-matched healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Thymic output was measured by circulating CD4+ recent thymic emigrants (RTEs) with flow cytometry, and T-cell receptor excision circles in sorted naïve CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Repertoire diversity and clonal expansion were evaluated by T-cell receptor beta sequencing.
RESULTS: Compared with HCs, treatment-naïve FH patients displayed a significantly reduced percentage of CD4+ RTE among naïve CD4+ T cells, particularly in those aged 18-30 years or carrying highly pathogenic LDLR variants. T-cell receptor excision circle analysis supported reduced thymic output in both CD4+ and CD8+ naïve T cells. Quantified thymic ageing further showed that FH patients reached the median CD4+ RTE percentage of HCs ∼6 years earlier (males: 19.12 vs 25.51 years; females: 19.18 vs 25.58 years). Consistent with reduced thymic output, FH patients showed skewing towards high-frequency T-cell receptor beta clones. Statin-treated FH patients, particularly females, showed higher circulating CD4+ RTE levels than statin-naïve FH patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypercholesterolaemia was associated with reduced thymic output, while statin-treated patients showed partially preserved circulating CD4+ RTE levels, supporting integrated metabolic and immunologic strategies for FH management.

Title: Antibiotic prophylaxis with vancomycin and gentamicin and the occurrence of acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: A retrospective single-centre cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vancomycin combined with gentamicin (VGA) is used as an alternative antibiotic prophylaxis in cardiac surgery when cephalosporins are contraindicated. However, the nephrotoxic potential of this combination raises concerns regarding postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between VGA prophylaxis and AKI occurrence in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), while accounting for preoperative risk factors.
DESIGN: Retrospective single-centre study. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria within 7 postoperative days.
PATIENTS: Of the 8895 eligible patients between April 2013 and December 2021, 8198 were included. Subgroup analyses were performed according to preoperative AKI risk status (high-risk: insulin-dependent diabetes, cirrhosis, acute endocarditis, preoperative critical state, emergency surgery, or cardiac transplantation).
RESULTS: In our cohort, 7469 (91%) received cephalosporins and 729 (9%) received VGA. The overall AKI incidence was 16%. AKI occurred more frequently in the VGA group (29% vs. 15%, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, VGA remained independently associated with AKI [odds ratio (OR) 1.29, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.03 to 1.62, P = 0.024], confirmed by propensity score analysis (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.09 to 1.60, P = 0.005). In subgroup analyses, VGA was significantly associated with AKI in high-risk patients (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.14 to 2.04, P = 0.004), but not in low-risk patients (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.64, P = 0.285).
CONCLUSION: In this large retrospective cohort, VGA antibiotic prophylaxis was independently associated with increased AKI risk following cardiac surgery with CPB. This association was driven primarily by patients with preoperative risk factors for AKI. Alternative prophylactic regimens should be considered in high-risk patients when possible.

Title: Plasma proteomic signatures of subclinical atherosclerosis progression for cardiovascular risk stratification: A cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing risk stratification tools inadequately identify individuals with subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) who could benefit from early intervention. This study aimed to develop protein risk scores (ProtRSs) for SA progression and assess their incremental value for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk prediction.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: In a community cohort consisting of 903 individuals undergoing repeated SA assessments (coronary artery calcium [CAC] or carotid plaque) over 6 years (2008-2009 to 2013-2014), protein biomarkers were selected from a panel of 117 proteins using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression to construct SA ProtRSs for CAC and plaque progression, respectively, and their predictive abilities for incident ASCVD risk were evaluated based on a guideline-recommended traditional risk score in a case-cohort of 1,835 individuals (2007-2008 to 2018-2021, median follow-up of 10.4 years). The ProtRSs each included 14 proteins for CAC and plaque progression, explaining 17.1% and 18.4% of respective variances. Effect sizes of these proteins on SA progression showed strong concordance with those on incident ASCVD (r  > 0.75). Each standard deviation increase in CAC and plaque ProtRSs was associated with hazard ratios of 1.36 (95% confidence interval [CI] [1.20,1.54]) and 1.38 (95% CI [1.23,1.54]) for ASCVD risk, respectively. Addition of the SA ProtRSs to the traditional risk score yielded a net reclassification improvement of 0.127 (p < 0.001). Importantly, 18.6% of traditional intermediate-risk individuals were reclassified into the high-risk category (10-year ASCVD event rate: 10.9%), indicating the need for preventive interventions, whereas 32.8% of traditional high-risk individuals were identified as having an even higher rate (13.7%), suggesting the requirement for intensified management. The main limitation is that the predictive value of ProtRSs warrants further large-scale external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: SA ProtRSs of coronary calcification and carotid plaque progression may provide additional value over traditional risk assessment, highlighting their potential in refining risk stratification and guiding targeted intervention strategies.

Title: The Pallidothalamic Tract in Functional Neurosurgery: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The pallidothalamic tract (PTT), formed by convergence of the ansa lenticularis and fasciculus lenticularis at Forel's field H1, is a major basal ganglia efferent pathway and an emerging functional neurosurgical target. No systematic review has previously synthesised outcomes across PTT-targeted interventions.
METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251248260). PubMed, OVID, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting functional neurosurgical outcomes targeting the PTT or Forel's fields. Prospective and retrospective studies, case series, and case reports were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools.
RESULTS: Forty studies encompassing 483 patients (1966-2025) were included across five modalities: MR-guided focused ultrasound (n = 143), radiofrequency ablation (n = 167), deep brain stimulation (n = 40), cryogenic lesioning (n = 82), and oil-wax injection (n = 52). Mean follow-up was 21 months. In Parkinson disease (PD; 11 studies; n = 135), mean Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale-III improvement was 39%, with reductions in dyskinesia (Unified Dyskinesia Ratings Scale 90%) and tremor (75%). In dystonia (12 studies; n = 87), Burke Fahn Marsden Dystonia Rating Scale and TWSTRS improved by 57% and 47%, respectively. Dual-target strategies, particularly PTT-VIM combinations, showed additive effects, including greater tremor reduction (77%) and improved rigidity. In drug-resistant epilepsy (6 studies; n = 157), seizure reduction occurred in 71% and seizure freedom in 33%.
CONCLUSION: PTT-targeted interventions yield meaningful motor improvements in PD and dystonia, with preliminary evidence supporting additive dual-target benefits. Seizure-reducing effects in refractory epilepsy have been reported. Evidence remains limited by small uncontrolled studies, heterogeneous outcomes, and inconsistent adverse-event reporting. Prospective trials will elucidate the efficacy, safety, and clinical role of the PTT in neurosurgery.

Title: LONGITUDINAL CLINICAL AND INTEGRATIVE MULTI-OMICS DATA REVEAL TRAJECTORY-DEFINED SUBGROUPS WITH DISTINCT KIDNEY FAILURE RISK IN DIABETIC KIDNEY DISEASE.
Abstract: Background Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of CKD globally. Despite marked heterogeneity in progression, risk stratification remains anchored to single-timepoint measures that fail to capture individual patient trajectories. We aimed to identify clinically meaningful DKD subgroups from real-world longitudinal data and characterise their molecular signatures using integrative multi-omics. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, unsupervised clustering of longitudinal creatinine and haematocrit trajectories was performed in the Salford Kidney Study (SKS; n=335 eligible for clustering, n=303 DKD) and validated in two independent cohorts: Scottish Health Research Register (SHARE; n=824) and CERCA-Diabetes (Spain; n=187). Prognostic performance was assessed by C-statistic, time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), IDI (integrated discrimination improvement), and decision curve analysis relative to the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE) and Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categorisation. Multi-omic characterisation (proteomics, metabolomics, DNA methylation) was performed in an 87-patient SKS subset using Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker Discovery using Latent Components (DIABLO). Results Two groups with markedly different progression rates were identified: high-risk (SKS-HR; n=173) and low-risk (SKS-LR; n=162). SKS-HR showed eGFR decline nearly four times faster and a higher rate of the composite kidney failure endpoint (HR 4.05 [95% CI 2.77-5.92] adjusted for age, sex, and eGFR; 2.95 [1.90-4.56] after further adjustment for haemoglobin, proteinuria, HbA1c, and cardiovascular burden; both p<0.0001). The signal was specific to renal progression (fully adjusted HR 5.98 [3.32-10.79], p<0.0001) and absent for cardiovascular or renal death (HR 1.00 [0.58-1.71], p=0.984). The subgroup-outcome association was independently replicated in SHARE (p=3.83×10⁻²⁷) and CERCA-Diabetes (p=1.72×10⁻⁴). The subgrouping added prognostic information complementary to the KFRE, raising the C-statistic from 0.689 to 0.721 when added to static KFRE and 0.711 to 0.732 when added to longitudinal KFRE. KDIGO risk categories showed limited discriminatory capacity in this predominantly G3b-G4 cohort. Hypothesis-generating multi-omic profiling showed FDR-significant enrichment for lipid transport pathways and for an independent DKD progression proteomic signature; all multi-omic findings require independent validation. Conclusions Longitudinal creatinine and haematocrit trajectories, available from routine clinical records, identify DKD patients at high risk of kidney failure with prognostic information beyond current risk tools. The high-risk subgroup warrants prospective validation and evaluation of whether subgroup assignment can improve risk stratification beyond existing clinical tools.

Title: What Are the Impacts of Immunoglobulin a Vasculitis on Choroidal Vascularity and Subfoveal Thickness in Children.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate choroidal structural and vascular changes in children with Immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV) using optical coherence tomography (OCT).
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 90 eyes of 41 children diagnosed with IgAV and 49 age-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examination and OCT imaging. Subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) were measured.
RESULTS: Subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) values were significantly lower in the patient group compared to the healthy group (p = 0.017, p = 0.018, respectively). SFCT and CVI were negatively correlated with disease activation and duration, respectively (r = -0.614 p < 0.001; r = -0.377 p < 0.05, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Children with IgAV demonstrated significantly reduced SFCT and CVI compared with healthy controls. These findings indicate the presence of choroidal structural and vascular alterations in IgAV, even in the absence of clinically apparent ocular pathology.

Title: Idiopathic Macular Hole Surgery without Intraocular Gas Tamponade: Surgical Technique, Biological Rationale, and Initial Clinical Experience.
Journal: Ceska a slovenska oftalmologie : casopis Ceske oftalmologicke spolecnosti a Slovenske oftalmologicke spolecnosti
Abstract:
AIM: The aim of the study is to describe the technique of idiopathic macular hole (IMH) surgery without the use of intraocular gas tamponade and to present the author's first clinical experience.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The operation is performed using pars plana vitrectomy, with the creation of an inverted internal limiting membrane flap (ILM flap). The flap of the patch is temporarily stabilized with decalin and then with an ocular viscoelastic device, without the subsequent use of gas tamponade (and without face-down positioning). The anatomical and functional outcome was evaluated with the aid of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and best-corrected visual acuity. Two case reports of patients with successful IMH closure using this technique are presented.
RESULTS: In all presented cases, anatomical closure of the macular hole was achieved and visual acuity improved. OCT demonstrated a relatively rapid restoration of the foveal architecture. The postoperative course was without complications and the patients were not burdened by the limitations and risks associated with gas tamponade.
CONCLUSION: IMH surgery without gas tamponade represents a  promising alternative to standard surgery. With the correct ILM flap technique, it enables us to achieve comparable anatomical and functional results while reducing the burden on the patient. However, further prospective studies are necessary to confirm the effectiveness of this method.

Title: Multiple musculoskeletal procedures over time and the risk of amyloidosis: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

Title: Longitudinal Association Between Prefrailty/Frailty and HIV-associated Neurocognitive Disorder (HAND): a Mexican Prospective Study.
Journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
Abstract: Geriatric syndromes such as frailty may be more prevalent and occur earlier in people aging with HIV, negatively impacting outcomes like cognition. Cross-sectional data show strong associations between pre-frailty/frailty and HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). However, prospective studies suggest baseline HAND increases frailty risk, while pre-frailty/frailty do not predict HAND onset. We aimed to investigate longitudinal association between baseline frailty and HAND category progression. Longitudinal analysis of 194 participants aged ≥50 years from Mexico City referral center. Two standardized geriatric assessments performed at least one year apart. HAND defined using Antinori criteria, frailty by Fried phenotype. Inverse probability weighted Cox models adjusted for confounders from directed acyclic graph (age, educational level, detectable viral load, diabetes, stroke, ischemic heart disease) determined association between frailty and HAND progression. Median age 55 (53-61) years; 167 (86%) men; median follow-up 2.3 (1.6-3.1) years. Baseline: 129 (66.4%) robust, 62 (31.9%) pre-frail, 3 (1.5%) frail. No longitudinal association between pre-frailty/frailty and HAND progression was observed in this cohort (32 progression events; adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.27-1.48; p = 0.29). No evidence of a prospective association between prefrailty/frailty and HAND category progression was observed in this cohort; most participants remained cognitively stable. To our knowledge, this is the first study describing HAND trajectories and their relationship with prefrailty/frailty in older adults with HIV in Mexico and Latin America.

Title: Sucrose induces Cardiac Hypertrophy and Renal Perivascular Fibrosis in a Novel Mouse Model of Hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excess sugar consumption increases the risk for hypertension. We previously reported pilot data demonstrating that male mice drinking 2% sucrose water develop hypertension. However, the sucrose effects on left ventricular hypertrophy, kidney fibrosis, or sex difference in hypertension remain unclear. In the present study, we characterized the cardiac and renal pathology in a larger cohort including female mice to establish a novel sucrose-induced mouse model of hypertension associated with cardiovascular remodeling.
METHODS: Eight- to nine- week-old C57BL6 mice were given drinking water containing 2% sucrose or regular water for 4 weeks. Blood pressure was monitored using a tail-cuff system. Echocardiography was performed to evaluate cardiac remodeling. Sirius red staining was performed to evaluate heart and kidney fibrosis.
RESULTS: Male mice drinking the sucrose water developed hypertension (systolic blood pressure 122.0±1.3mmHGvs 162.2±4.3 mmHG at day 28). Sucrose treatment increased left ventricular wall thickness and induced perivascular fibrosis of the heart and kidney compared to control mice. Cardiac functions were preserved. In female mice, sucrose treatment induced milder hypertension than male mice (126.9±2.4 mmHg vs 143.7±3.2 mmHg at day 28). However, sucrose treatment caused similar degree of left ventricular hypertrophy in female mice.
CONCLUSION: Sucrose water induced hypertension, cardiac hypertrophy, and fibrosis of the heart and kidney in male mice. Female mice were partially protected from hypertension but not from cardiac hypertrophy. This mouse model represents a useful tool to investigate molecular mechanisms by which hypertension and end organ damage develop with excess sugar consumption.

Title: Arterial Hypertension and Kidney Function Decline in Systemic Sclerosis and Sjögren's Disease: A Longitudinal Comparative Study.
Journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal involvement is increasingly recognized in Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Sjögren's Disease (SjD). However, the association between hypertension and renal function decline in these conditions remains poorly understood.
AIM: to compare renal function changes over time in patients with SSc and SjD; identify factors associated with clinically relevant renal function decline; and to evaluate whether the association between hypertension and renal function differs between the two diseases.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with SSc and SjD, followed for up to 3 years. Renal function was assessed using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Clinically relevant renal decline was defined as a reduction in eGFR ≥10 ml/min Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with renal function decline, including the interaction between diagnosis and hypertension.
RESULTS: A total of 238 patients were included (114 with SSc and 124 with SjD), with a median age of 55 years (IQR 45-65) in SSc and 57 years (IQR 48-66) in SjD. At baseline, SSc patients showed higher eGFR compared to SjD, but experienced a greater decline over time (median -6 vs -2.1 ml/min, p < 0.05). Overall, 33.8% of patients developed clinically significant renal decline. In multivariable analysis, hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline (OR 10.01, 95% CI 3.51-28.56, p < 0.001), whereas diagnosis was not. A significant interaction between diagnosis and hypertension was observed (OR 6.56, 95% CI 1.03-41.69, p = 0.046), indicating a stronger association between hypertension and renal function decline in SSc than in SjD. In subgroup analyses, hypertension was significantly associated with renal decline in SSc but not in SjD.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline, with a stronger association in SSc than in SjD. These findings warrant confirmation in prospective studies. Systemic Sclerosis, Sjögren's disease, Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate; arterial hypertension.

Title: Clinical characteristics and long-term follow-up of extensive macular atrophy with pseudodrusen-like appearance in Japanese patients.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the clinical characteristics and long-term follow-up findings of extensive macular atrophy with pseudodrusen-like appearance (EMAP) in a Japanese cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed Japanese patients diagnosed with EMAP who underwent genetic tests, which did not detect known pathogenic variants of inherited retinal dystrophies or age-related macular degeneration. Patients underwent comprehensive ophthalmic evaluations, including multimodal imaging (fundus autofluorescence and optical coherence tomography) and full-field electroretinography.
RESULTS: This study included eight Japanese patients with EMAP, encompassing five males and three females. The mean follow-up period was 102.5 (range, 25-180) months. The mean best-corrected visual acuity declined from 0.18 to 1.08 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (right eye) over the follow-up period. Macular atrophy and peripheral paving-stone-like degeneration were present in 75% and 87.5% of patients, respectively. Rod responses were reduced in 62.5% of patients, and delayed flicker full-field electroretinography implicit times were observed in 62.5%. Longitudinal imaging suggested phenotypic changes in a limited number of cases including progression from a predominantly central pattern to confluent involvement in one patient.
CONCLUSION: Japanese patients with EMAP exhibited structural and functional abnormalities during long-term follow-up that were consistent with broader retinal involvement extending beyond the macula.

Title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a marker of major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates.
RESULTS: The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626).
CONCLUSION: SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

Title: Insulin Resistance Markers Predict New-Onset Diabetes in Middle-Aged and Elderly Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insulin resistance (IR) is central to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, but the best IR-related marker for identifying CKM patients at high risk of diabetes remains uncertain. This study examined associations between IR-related markers and new-onset diabetes and compared their predictive performance.
METHODS: We analyzed 6,307 CKM participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and 6,388 from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess associations of triglyceride-glucose (TyG), TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), metabolic score for IR (METS-IR), and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) with diabetes. Subgroup analyses and receiver operating characteristic curves were employed to evaluate robustness and discrimination.
RESULTS: Over 7 years, diabetes developed in 736 CHARLS participants (11.67%) and 1,451 NHANES participants (22.71%). Five IR-related markers were significantly associated with the risk of diabetes and demonstrated good predictive performance. Elevated levels of TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WHtR, and METS-IR, as well as lower levels of eGDR, were associated with increased diabetes risk (all P < 0.001). Most associations remained robust across subgroup analyses. Among the five markers, eGDR demonstrated the highest predictive performance in the NHANES cohort (AUC: 0.789; 95% CI: 0.776-0.802) and showed favorable predictive ability in the CHARLS cohort.
CONCLUSION: IR-related markers are significantly associated with the risk of diabetes in individuals with CKM syndrome and serve as reliable predictors of new-onset diabetes. Among these indicators, eGDR and TyG-WHtR were relatively reliable predictors, highlighting their potential as valuable tools for early diabetes screening.

Title: Later-line Treatment Selection in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Trifluridine/Tipiracil Plus Bevacizumab, Regorafenib, and Fruquintinib.
Abstract: Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. This narrative review updates pivotal and recent evidence and proposes an evidence-informed framework that treats hematologic reserve as a clinical fitness construct rather than a fixed laboratory threshold. We additionally examine the clinical implications of low response rates, prior anti-angiogenic exposure, emerging molecular predictors including KRAS G12, evidence in older or vulnerable patients, and recent phase III developments. Current data do not support a validated molecular biomarker for choosing among these three options, and no randomized head-to-head comparison of regorafenib and fruquintinib exists. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

Title: 20-year analysis of protocol-driven quality improvement in cardiac homograft banking.
Abstract: Cardiac homografts are indispensable in complex cardiac surgery, particularly in the paediatric population. Optimising procurement and minimising discard rates are important for maintaining graft availability, especially in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated 20 years of cardiac homograft procurement at a tertiary cardiovascular centre, focusing on discard rates, causes of discard, microbiological profiles, and the impact of protocol refinements. A retrospective analysis was conducted using procurement records from the Cardiac Homograft Tissue Bank at the Institut Jantung Negara, Malaysia, between January 2004 and December 2024. The data collected included annual procurement volume, reasons for discarding, and microbiological culture results. In 2015, a revised procurement protocol was introduced, which incorporated instrument and operative field segregation, aseptic redraping, and enhanced donor screening. A total of 190 hearts were procured (mean 9.05 ± 4.18 hearts/year), with an overall discard rate of 13.7% (of 26/190). Prior to 2015, the discard rate was 17.2% (20/116), with environmental contamination accounting for the majority of the discards (75%; n=15). Fifteen microbial isolates were identified in the pre-revision period: Candida (n=6), Klebsiella (n=4), Acinetobacter (n=2), Streptococcus spp. (n=1), Streptococcus viridans (n=1), and Pseudomonas spp. (n=1). Following the 2015 protocol revision, the overall discard rate decreased to 8.1% (6/74), representing a 53% reduction, although this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.074). Environmental contamination-related discards decreased significantly from 12.9% (15/116) to 1.4% (1/74) (89% reduction; p=0.005), with only one Candida isolate identified post-revision. Protocol refinement has therefore produced a statistically significant reduction in contamination-related discards and a shift in the microbiological spectrum.

Title: Cardiomyocyte-derived IL-30 improves cardiac repair by reducing splenic germinal center activation after myocardial infarction.
Abstract: Following myocardial infarction (MI), splenic humoral immune responses contribute to cardiac injury and repair, yet the cardiac signals that govern these responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identified ischemic cardiomyocytes as a source of interleukin 30 (IL-30; the interleukin 27 p28 subunit) and investigated its role in heart-spleen communication. In mice, cardiomyocyte-specific IL-30 deficiency enhanced splenic germinal center responses and signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) phosphorylation. This deficiency increased myocardial IgG deposition, TNF-α expression in Fc gamma receptor III-positive macrophages, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis, while impairing cardiac function and aggravating ventricular remodeling. Recombinant IL-30 suppressed splenic germinal center responses and STAT1 phosphorylation and improved cardiac function. The effects of recombinant IL-30 on germinal center responses and cardiac function were abolished by B cell-specific deletion of glycoprotein 130 (gp130). Furthermore, no detectable improvement in cardiac function was observed following IL-30 treatment in splenectomized mice. In patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; n = 75), lower circulating IL-30 levels were associated with higher peripheral IgG-positive B cell frequencies. In a separate longitudinal cohort of 247 patients with STEMI, low circulating IL-30 was independently associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling at 6 months (odds ratio, 4.44; 95% confidence interval, 2.16-9.80; P< 0.001). Circulating IL-30 discriminated patients with and without adverse remodeling with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.738. These findings identify cardiomyocyte-derived IL-30 as an endogenous regulator of heart-spleen communication that restrains splenic humoral responses and limits adverse cardiac remodeling after MI.

Title: Contemporary outcomes after 100 consecutive HeartMate 3 LVAD implantations: a single-centre cohort study from a Swiss tertiary centre.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The HeartMate 3 left ventricular assist device (LVAD) is an established therapy for advanced heart failure, yet contemporary real-world data from low- or medium-volume centres remain limited. We aimed to describe the characteristics, management and clinical outcomes of patients undergoing HeartMate 3 LVAD implantation at a Swiss tertiary centre.
METHODS: We conducted an observational study including consecutive adult patients who underwent HeartMate 3 implantation at Lausanne University Hospital between November 2015 and January 2026. Baseline characteristics, INTERMACS profiles, perioperative data, survival and LVAD-related complications were assessed. The primary outcome was survival on LVAD support. Comparisons by LVAD indication were pre-specified exploratory analyses (destination therapy vs bridge-to-transplant). Survival analyses on LVAD support, with heart transplantation or LVAD explantation treated as censoring events, were reported.
RESULTS: A total of 100 patients (mean age 58 [standard deviation 12] years, 84% male, 29% destination therapy) underwent HeartMate 3 implantation. Ischaemic heart disease was the predominant aetiology (69%) and most patients (68%) were classified as INTERMACS profiles 3-4 at implantation. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 (IQR 0.5-3) years, 27 patients died on LVAD support, corresponding to a mortality incidence rate (IR) of 13.5 deaths per 100 patient-years, while 51 patients underwent heart transplantation, corresponding to an IR of transplantation of 25.4 per 100 patient-years. Five-year survival on LVAD support was 64%, with patients censored at LVAD explantation for recovery or transplantation. LVAD-related complications included bleeding (48%), infection (50%), ischaemic stroke (12%) and right ventricular failure (39%). Survival did not differ by LVAD indication (bridge-to-transplant as reference, adjusted HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.14-2.72).
CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary, real-world, medium-sized cohort, HeartMate 3 therapy provided durable long-term support across a broad spectrum of advanced heart failure patients, with outcomes consistent with those reported in large multicentre registries.

Title: Semantic distance metrics in anatomy education: Toward AI-assisted mapping of anatomy-to-clinical reasoning.
Abstract: Anatomy education traditionally emphasizes structural knowledge acquisition, with the implicit assumption that clinical reasoning capabilities will naturally follow. However, the cognitive pathway from anatomical understanding to clinical application is rarely linear or uniform. This article proposes a conceptual framework in which semantic distance-the conceptual separation between anatomical knowledge and clinical endpoints-operates at three analytically distinct levels: (1) the learner's internal cognitive network, shaped by prior experience and schema formation; (2) the structural distance within curriculum maps, ontologies, or knowledge graphs; and (3) the distributional proximity within large language model (LLM) embedding spaces, which may serve as a scalable computational proxy indicator for the first two levels. These three levels must be explicitly distinguished if semantic distance is to function as a useful construct in anatomy education. To illustrate the framework's utility, three worked examples are developed-the femoral nerve, coronary circulation, and spinal cord anatomy-accompanied by a preliminary computational illustration of embedding distances rather than an empirically validated diagnostic instrument. A practical educator workflow is proposed through which computational signals may be translated into targeted curriculum decisions. The article positions semantic distance metrics as complementary to curriculum network analytics and highlights how cross-domain transitions (from anatomy through physiology and pathology to clinical presentation) represent qualitatively different educational problems requiring different interventions. Prospective validation studies, multimodal computational approaches, and longitudinal curriculum outcome analyses are needed before this framework can be applied systematically.

Title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression.
METHODS: From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates.
RESULTS: Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).

Title: Electromechanical Window Negativity and Arrhythmic Risk in Arrhythmogenic Mitral Valve Prolapse.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is generally a benign valvular heart disease, but a subset of patients is at particular risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (AMVP).
OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the electromechanical window (EMW) as an arrhythmia-risk marker in (A)MVP (the sum of all MVP and AMVP patients).
METHODS: Healthy controls, patients with MVP without ventricular arrhythmia (MVP/-VA), and patients with AMVP with nonsustained (AMVP/nsVA) or sustained ventricular arrhythmia (AMVP/VA) (ventricular arrhythmia >30 seconds) were retrospectively included from 3 centers (derivation cohort). An independent validation (A)MVP cohort was recruited from 2 centers. EMW was calculated blinded from apical Doppler echocardiography by subtracting the QT time from the simultaneous Q-to-aortic-valve closure time (QAoC).
RESULTS: In the derivation cohort (31 controls, 31 MVP/-VA, 29 AMVP/nsVA, 14 AMVP/VA), patients with (A)MVP displayed a borderline shorter QAoCc (P = 0.06) and significantly longer QTc than controls (P < 0.0001), resulting in a more negative EMW (-18 ms [-47 to -8 ms]; P < 0.0001). EMW was most negative in patients with AMVP/VA (-71 ms [-177 to -30 ms]). These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort (n = 76 with [A]MVP), albeit at different absolute values. In a pooled receiver-operating characteristic analysis, EMW identified patients with AMVP/VA with an area under the curve of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.91), significantly outperforming QTc and QAoCc. An EMW threshold of -30 ms was the optimal cutoff (sensitivity: 0.71; specificity: 0.83). EMW was independently associated with AMVP/VA status and improved model performance in addition to established risk parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: EMW is markedly negative in patients with AMVP/VA, reflecting electromechanical discordance. Thus, EMW emerges as a promising risk-associated marker in (A)MVP.

Title: Long-Term Outcome Following Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation and Potential Emerging Etiologies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unexplained cardiac death and cardiac arrest associated with idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) are heterogeneous pathologies responsible for significant mortality in young people.
OBJECTIVES: This retrospective multicenter cohort study evaluated the natural history of a large cohort of IVF survivors including recurrence burden, emerging etiologies, and long-term management.
METHODS: This study included IVF patients from 46 tertiary centers and followed for at least 5 years. Patients over the age of 15 years who had documented ventricular fibrillation and extensive negative investigations supporting the diagnosis of IVF were included. Patients were followed in each center with their outcome being established on data collection from subsequent clinical records, new investigations, genetic results, and implanted defibrillator recordings. Recurrent arrhythmias and mortality were assessed. Diagnoses were graded as definite (direct evidence) or probable (indirect criteria).
RESULTS: A total of 825 patients (37% women; age 35.7 ± 12 years) were followed for a median duration of 120 months (Q1-Q3: 78-180 months). Death occurred in 27 patients (3.3%) from cardiac (n = 10; 1.2%), noncardiac (n = 9; 1.1%), and unknown (n = 8; 1%) causes, and few patients (4.5%) developed overt cardiomyopathy. Overall arrhythmia recurrence increased steadily over 2 decades, reaching 52.7% of patients, with a median time to first recurrence of 20 months (Q1-Q3: 5-48 months) and a similar incidence in men and women. Emergent etiologies occurred in 68.8% of the total population, and were associated with new information during recurrences, structural changes, genetic results, and mapping procedures. They included reclassified inherited arrhythmia conditions in 73 (8.8%), focal sources in 272 (33.0%), and definite or probable microstructural myocardial alterations (MiCMs) with normal imaging in 223 (27.0%), while no diagnosis was identified in 257 (31.2%). Compared with MiCM, focal IVF included more women, occurred more frequently at rest/sleep, and was associated with narrow QRS complexes (90.1 ± 12 milliseconds vs 104.8 ± 16 milliseconds; P < 0.001). Quinidine appeared effective in preventing focal IVF (68.3%) whereas beta-blockers appeared effective (49.3%) in MiCM-IVF. Catheter ablation was performed in 181 patients with no recurrence observed in 75.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter long-term cohort study of IVF survivors shows low cardiac mortality, a persistent risk of arrhythmia recurrences over time, and identifies potential emerging etiologies.

Title: Circular RNAs in Drug-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Roles, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Potential.
Journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
Abstract: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major challenge in drug development and clinical practice, often resulting in treatment interruption, drug attrition, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. DIC has been associated with a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anthracyclines, HER2-targeted therapies, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other cardiotoxic drugs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have attracted increasing attention as stable and versatile regulatory RNAs involved in cardiovascular injury. This review summarizes the biogenesis and functional mechanisms of circRNAs, their pathological roles in DIC, biomarker potential, therapeutic implications, and translational challenges. CircRNAs regulate gene expression through diverse mechanisms, including miRNA sequestration, interactions with RNA-binding proteins, transcriptional regulation, modulation of alternative splicing, and, in some cases, peptide translation. These regulatory functions have been implicated in apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, pyroptosis, and cardiac remodeling during DIC. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs may serve as candidate molecular markers and potential therapeutic targets for DIC. However, the current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, with doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity accounting for a substantial proportion of available studies. Clinical validation, particularly in well-characterized patient cohorts and across different drug classes, remains limited. Overall, further efforts are needed to establish standardized circRNA detection and quantification methods, validate their functional roles, conduct prospective clinical studies, and determine their incremental value in combination with established cardiac biomarkers before circRNA-based approaches can be translated into clinical management of DIC.

Title: No Reflow at Perfusion Imaging: Thresholds That Distinguish Functional and Tissue Outcome Groups in Acute Stroke.
Abstract: Background Poor outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may reflect microvascular dysfunction, or no-reflow phenomenon, but operational definitions are lacking. Purpose To identify the most informative candidate no-reflow definition at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging for outcome assessment. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis used data from two prospective multicenter imaging registries of patients with acute stroke who were recruited between June 2016 and July 2022, achieved modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction grade 2c or 3 recanalization after EVT, and underwent pre-EVT and 24-hour post-EVT CT or MR perfusion imaging. Candidate no-reflow definitions were evaluated across eight perfusion maps and their corresponding stepwise thresholds. Delay time (DT) quantifies the delay in contrast material arrival between arterial input and brain tissue. For primary screening, no-reflow status was defined as any residual hypoperfusion lesion for each map-threshold combination. The best-performing combination was evaluated using residual volume and reperfusion index cutoffs. The primary outcome was poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score >2); infarct growth was secondary. Associations with the outcome were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. Results The primary cohort included 67 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 56-77 years]; 41 male), and the independent cohort comprised 54 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 62-78 years]; 28 female).
