CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, the present study suggests that CPUS is feasible for identifying cardiogenic pulmonary edema in ICU patients with heart failure. Based on diagnostic agreement analysis, CPUS demonstrates promising performance for CPE detection in this critically-ill cohort.

Title: The impact of an adaptive patient-centered web application on medication optimization in patients with HFrEF: Rationale and design of the SmartHF trial.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure (HF) remains a significant public health burden, with frequent readmissions often driven by a lack of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) optimization. While clinical decision support (CDS) can improve healthcare processes, patient-centered tools that empower individuals to participate in their own care are increasingly needed. We developed SmartHF, an adaptive web application that provides patients with tailored HFrEF GDMT recommendations based on their clinical data.
METHODS: This 12-week, multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolled adults with HFrEF (LVEF </=40%). Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the SmartHF intervention or usual care. The application uses a computable algorithm to integrate electronic health record (EHR) data, including medications, laboratory results, and vitals, via patient portal authorization. The primary endpoint is the change in a GDMT medication optimization score from baseline to Week 12.
RESULTS: Enrollment concluded in August 2025 with a total of 225 participants. The study population had a mean age of 61.9 years, with 36% identifying as female and 52% as Black or African American. At baseline, 84% of participants were prescribed an ACEi/ARB/ARNI, 90% were on beta-blockers, 67% were prescribed an SGLT2i, while only 53% were on a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). The mean baseline medication optimization score was 68.5. Final trial results are expected in Winter 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: SmartHF is an innovative, low-touch digital health intervention that leverages EHR integration to facilitate patient-provider discussions on medication optimization. By providing personalized, guideline-based recommendations, the tool aims to improve GDMT prescribing in patients with HFrEF.
CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05858320.

Title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear.
METHODS: Human peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization. qPCR validation was performed in peripheral blood from 10 aSAH patients and 10 non-SAH controls; aSAH samples were collected within 24 h after rupture. Mean ages were 60.2 ± 7.7 and 63.6 ± 8.9 years, with 5 and 4 males, respectively. Brain-level validation used GSE79416 mouse cortex and OMIX006611 mouse SAH single-cell RNA-seq data. Male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks, 20-22 g) underwent cisterna magna autologous blood injection; brain tissues were collected 1 day after SAH (n = 6/group). Immune infiltration and molecular docking were also performed.
RESULTS: Among 2,645 DEGs, 35 were ferroptosis-related. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD were prioritized as ferroptosis-associated candidate genes and were upregulated in human aSAH peripheral blood, mouse SAH cortex, and the clinical qPCR cohort. Single-cell analysis showed expression of the corresponding mouse genes across annotated brain cell types, especially immune/glial populations. In mouse SAH brain tissue, MAPK3/ERK1, STAT3, PGD, and G6PD protein levels increased, p-STAT3/STAT3 ratio was elevated, MDA content increased, and GPX4 activity decreased. Immune profiling showed increased neutrophils, mast cells, and activated dendritic cells. Ganoderic acid A was prioritized as a preliminary in silico candidate.
CONCLUSION: MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD are ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aSAH, supported by human peripheral-blood, mouse cortex, single-cell, and mouse brain validation. Ganoderic acid A remains an exploratory in silico candidate requiring further functional validation.

Title: Effect of meso-and micro-level quality improvement interventions to improve intrapartum care and birth outcome in Nepal- stepped wedge cluster randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-quality intrapartum care benefits from implementation of quality improvement (QI) interventions. However, scale-up of meso- and micro-level QI interventions to improve health facility performance have shown mixed results in Nepal.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effect of such interventions to intrapartum care and intrapartum mortality (intrapartum stillbirth and first day neonatal death) in public health facilities of Nepal.
STUDY DESIGN: A stepped-wedge cluster randomized design was applied to implement the SUSTAIN package, comprising meso- and micro-level QI interventions in 8 hospitals across all provinces of Nepal over a 21-month period. Each hospital had a 2-month window to introduce QI interventions in their governance and clinical processes. Women with gestational age ≥22 weeks were included with research teams established in each hospital to monitor mortality and health workers' performance. For each outcome, hospital-specific incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by comparing event rates in the intervention period with those in the control period.
RESULTS: The study enrolled, 55,325 and 53,578 women were enrolled in the control and intervention periods, respectively. The SUSTAIN package resulted in a statistically non-significant reduction (16%) in intrapartum mortality at the hospital level (IRR 0.84 (95% CI: 0.66, 1.08)), while at the individual level there was also statistically non-significant lower odd (37%) of mortality (aOR: 0.63 (0.38, 1.04), P<.0001)). Improvement in intrapartum care were consistent in most of care indicators with adherence to hand-washing increased by 2.36 fold (IRR 2.36 (95% CI: 1.03, 5.39)), fetal heart-rate monitoring increased by 1.55 fold (IRR 1.55 (95% CI: 1.10, 2.17)), delayed cord clamping increased non-significantly by1.14 fold (IRR 1.14 (95% CI: 0.96, 1.35)), immediate skin-to-skin contact increased by 9.92 fold (IRR 9.92 (95% CI: 3.21, 30.64)), early breastfeeding increased by 4.09 fold (IRR 4.09 (95% CI: 2.07, 8.11)), and bag-and-mask within 1 minute increased by 3.30 fold (IRR 3.30 (95% CI: 2.02, 5.40).
CONCLUSION: A synergistic and multi-faceted QI package implementation can improve intrapartum care with a statistically non-significant reduction in intrapartum mortality even during the COVID-19 pandemic.
TRIAL: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN16741720.

Title: Perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes are associated with complications after Moyamoya bypass surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative hyperperfusion and insufficient perfusion augmentation are important contributors to morbidity after revascularization surgery for Moyamoya disease (MMD). Arterial spin labeling (ASL) enables noninvasive assessment of cerebral blood flow (CBF), but the relationship between perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes and specific postoperative complications after direct bypass remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes were associated with postoperative complications after direct bypass surgery in patients with MMD.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 146 patients with MMD who underwent first-time direct bypass surgery between June 2020 and October 2024. Preoperative ASL and a standardized postoperative ASL examination on postoperative day 5 were performed, and CBF values were measured in the recipient vascular territory. Subsequent intracranial hemorrhage, cerebral infarction, and postoperative seizures occurring within 90 days after surgery were analyzed. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for the hemorrhage outcome, conventional logistic regression was used for cerebral infarction, and ROC analyses included bootstrap assessment of cutoff uncertainty and 0.632 + bootstrap correction of AUC optimism.
RESULTS: Postoperative intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 8 patients (5.5%), cerebral infarction in 14 patients (9.6%), and postoperative seizures in 9 patients (6.2%); all events occurred after the day-5 ASL examination and within 90 days after surgery. ASL-derived CBF change was associated with postoperative intracranial hemorrhage in Firth penalized logistic regression (OR, 1.219; 95% profile-likelihood CI, 1.102-1.580; p < 0.001). The exploratory cutoff was >43.48 mL/100 g/min, with an apparent AUC of 0.9891 and a 0.632 + corrected AUC of 0.9890. ASL-derived CBF change was inversely associated with postoperative cerebral infarction (OR, 0.885; 95% CI, 0.839-0.933; p < 0.001). The exploratory cutoff was ≤4.48 mL/100 g/min, with an apparent AUC of 0.9150 and a 0.632 + corrected AUC of 0.9150. No significant association was observed between ASL-derived CBF change and postoperative seizures.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative ASL-derived CBF change was associated with hemorrhagic and ischemic complications after direct bypass surgery for MMD. Marked postoperative CBF elevation was observed in patients with intracranial hemorrhage, whereas insufficient perfusion augmentation was associated with cerebral infarction. The proposed thresholds are exploratory, cohort-specific estimates and require external validation before clinical application.

Title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Two-Tined Three-Site Conventional Radiofrequency Ablation of Genicular Nerves for Chronic Knee Pain.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation (GNRFA) has emerged as an effective therapy for chronic knee pain. Although some studies have evaluated its effectiveness, there is limited real-world data on the long-term patient-reported outcome (PRO) data for GNRFAs.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate PROs following conventional GNRFAs performed using two-tined electrodes and the classical three-site technique targeting the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior medial genicular nerves.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review to gather data from consecutive GNRFAs at an academic medical center from 2016 to 2023. Inclusion criteria were all adult patients who received a conventional GNRFA performed using the classical three-site technique using two-tined electrodes. All included subjects were confirmed to have a positive diagnostic response (≥50% Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) reduction) to a previous genicular nerve block. Primary outcomes were NRS pain scores, Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Global Health, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9).
RESULTS: A total of 31 patients underwent 38 GNRFAs. Relative to the pre-procedure baseline, the average NRS reduction post-procedurally was -3.17 during 0-3 months (p<0.0001), -1.31 during 3-6 months (p<0.05), and -1.92 during 6-12 months (p<0.05). Half of all patients maintained pain relief (NRS reduction greater than or equal to a minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of -2.0) for 11.17 months (95% CI: 7.29, 13.40). Although there was a positive trend for improvement in the quality-of-life measures, no statistically significant post-procedure improvement or worsening was observed during all time periods for PROMIS Physical Health, PROMIS Mental Health, and PHQ-9. Lastly, a history of depression was associated with treatment failure.
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, conventional GNRFA using the classical three-site technique demonstrated robust short-term pain reduction, and at least half of the cohort maintained clinically meaningful pain improvements for 11 months. For chronic knee pain, GNRFA is a reasonable therapeutic option in appropriately selected patients.

Title: Prospective evaluation of donor-derived cell-free DNA for noninvasive detection of acute rejection in an Asian heart transplant population.
Journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract: Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) is the gold standard for diagnosing post-heart transplant acute rejection (AR) but is invasive. Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker, yet thresholds for Asian recipients remain undefined. This prospective study enrolled 80 patients, with 299 dd-cfDNA specimens analyzed via a novel Chinese-developed next-generation sequencing assay targeting 48 Indel sites. A reference cohort (n = 42) established post-transplant dd-cfDNA kinetics, while a biopsy cohort (n = 41, 18 acute cellular rejection [ACR], 9 antibody-mediated rejection [AMR], 14 no rejection [NR]) paired with EMB evaluated diagnostic performance. dd-cfDNA peaked at week 1, with a stable trend emerging from week 4 and stable levels reached by week 8. AR patients had significantly higher dd-cfDNA levels than NR patients (0.87% vs. 0.23%, P < 0.001). The optimal composite AR threshold was 0.33% (AUC = 0.874, sensitivity 81.0%, specificity 85.7%). dd-cfDNA decreased post-therapy (P = 0.011) and showed an inverse association with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (P = 0.004). This study provides initial evidence for an assay- and cohort-specific dd-cfDNA threshold (0.33%) for AR detection in Chinese recipients. Given the modest NPV (75.0%), this threshold is better suited for a "rule-in" strategy, and low values should not be used in isolation to defer biopsy. External validation in multicenter cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

Title: Efficacy, safety, and strategy-modifying factors of pulsed field ablation for persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly applied in persistent atrial fibrillation (PerAF) and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF). Previous reviews of mixed AF populations suggested potential advantages in procedural efficiency and esophageal safety, but PerAF/LSPAF-specific evidence on long-term rhythm outcomes and on the value of posterior wall or extended substrate strategies remains limited, with substantial heterogeneity in lesion sets, endpoint definitions, and comparator types.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus through April 18, 2026, with an updated verification search performed in August 2026. Because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity, formal pairwise pooling was restricted to comparisons supported by at least two clinically homogeneous head-to-head studies; single-study comparisons were synthesized narratively, and strategy-level outcomes were explored with single-arm proportion meta-analysis of exact-count cohorts. Off-antiarrhythmic drug (off-AAD) outcomes were prioritized when available. Certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies (approximately 3,100 patients) were included. In an exploratory pooled analysis of the only two available head-to-head comparisons (380 patients, with imbalanced study weights and different lesion sets: PVI-only vs. PVI plus posterior wall isolation), PFA was associated with lower 12-month atrial arrhythmia recurrence than cryoballoon ablation [risk ratio [RR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-0.98; GRADE certainty: very low]; this is best regarded as a preliminary signal. No statistically detectable difference in major complications was observed between PFA and cryoballoon [risk difference (RD) 0.00, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.02], reflecting absence of a demonstrable difference rather than proven equivalence. Single-study comparisons against radiofrequency ablation (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.45-0.94) and hybrid-convergent ablation (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.67-1.86) yielded directionally discordant results and are presented narratively. Exploratory, non-comparative single-arm analyses yielded pooled 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia of 66.0% (95% CI 55.5%-75.2%; I²=79.0%) for PVI plus posterior wall cohorts and 82.6% (95% CI 76.3%-87.5%; I 2 = 0%) for beyond-PV/extended substrate cohorts; these estimates derive from different, non-randomized cohorts and are hypothesis-generating only.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests favorable efficacy and safety of PFA in PerAF/LSPAF, but certainty is low to very low for all key outcomes. The lower recurrence vs. cryoballoon ablation is an encouraging but preliminary signal requiring confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials with uniform lesion sets. Whether extended substrate strategies improve outcomes cannot be determined from current non-comparative data. Future studies should apply standardized off-AAD endpoints, uniform rhythm monitoring, and stratification by atrial myopathy burden and PFA platform.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: identifier INPLASY202640082; doi: 10.37766/inplasy2026.4.0082.

Title: Clinical characteristics and in-hospital prognostic factors in young patients with myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to analyze the clinical characteristics and short-term prognostic factors of young patients with acute myocardial infarction.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included young patients (aged 18 to 45 years) who visited our center for AMI from January 1, 2014, to October 31, 2023. Baseline and outcome data were collected through the medical records system, with the primary endpoint being in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Patients were divided into MACE and non-MACE groups based on the occurrence of in-hospital MACE. Coronary angiography was performed in 154/158 patients, all achieving post-procedural TIMI 3 flow. Multivariable logistic regression using Firth penalized likelihood with a priori-selected variables (LVEF, serum uric acid, age) was used to identify independent predictors of MACE.
RESULTS: Of 166 young patients initially screened, 158 were included in the final analysis after excluding 8 due to incomplete data. Among these, 27 (17.1%) experienced in-hospital MACE. Patients in the MACE group had a lower prevalence of diabetes (0.00% vs. 19.08%, P = 0.008), lower admission blood pressure and worse left ventricular dysfunction [lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), larger left ventricular end diastolic diameter (LVEDD)]. Single-vessel disease was the most common (38.96%), with 83.77% of patients having involvement of the left anterior descending artery. The proportion of left main disease was higher in the MACE group (15.38% vs. 3.91%, P = 0.045). In the Firth model, lower LVEF was the sole independent predictor of MACE (OR 0.859, 95% CI 0.794-0.917, P < 0.001), while serum uric acid and age were not significant.
CONCLUSION: The clinical characteristics and coronary artery lesion features of young AMI patients are unique. Reduced LVEF is the sole independent predictor of in-hospital MACE in our cohort, underscoring the value of ventricular function assessment for short-term risk stratification.

Title: Development of a predictive model and nomogram using CTPA parameters for the identification of group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Abstract: This study aimed to identify computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-derived predictors of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and to develop a prediction model and nomogram for non-invasive diagnosis. We retrospectively analyzed CTPA datasets from 203 patients in the training cohort and 98 patients in the validation cohort, stratified into PAH (confirmed by right heart catheterization) and non-PAH groups. Pulmonary vascular and cardiac structural metrics were measured. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression identified interventricular septal angle (IVSA), interventricular septal thickness (IVST), and right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness (RVOTW) as independent predictors. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964 and 0.969 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively, with excellent calibration and clinical utility. The CTPA-based predictive model and nomogram may serve as a useful reference tool, potentially assisting in the identification of PAH and optimizing clinical workflows.

Title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer's disease using electronic records.
Abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

Title: Abnormal lipid profiles are associated with markers of impaired fibrinolysis in patients with cirrhosis.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with liver cirrhosis exhibit abnormalities in lipid metabolism and in circulating proteins of clot breakdown. Recent studies have shown relationships between dyslipidemia and fibrinolytic abnormalities in noncirrhotic populations.
OBJECTIVES: We investigated associations between lipid profiles and fibrinolytic markers in patients with cirrhosis.
METHODS: This observational study analyzed samples from 147 patients with stable cirrhosis, decompensated cirrhosis, acute-on-chronic liver failure, and sepsis without pre-existing chronic liver disease, and from 38 healthy controls. We studied fibrinolysis by clot lysis time (CLT), plasminogen, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), and tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and lipid profiles by apolipoproteins A1 and B, common lipoproteins, triglycerides, and total cholesterol.
RESULTS: CLT was slightly enhanced in stable and decompensated cirrhosis, but prolonged in acute-on-chronic liver failure and sepsis. Plasminogen levels decreased, whereas PAI-1 and tPA increased with cirrhosis severity. All lipid parameters decreased with cirrhosis severity, besides triglyceride levels, which were preserved. In an analysis of all patients with cirrhosis combined, apolipoprotein A1 correlated inversely with CLT, levels of PAI-1 and tPA, and positively with plasminogen. Apolipoprotein B, low-density lipoprotein, and lipoprotein(a) correlated positively with plasminogen. Triglycerides correlated positively with CLT.
CONCLUSION: Cirrhosis is characterized by decreased (apo)lipoprotein levels, preserved triglyceride levels, and a shift from enhanced to impaired fibrinolysis with increasing disease severity. Lower apolipoprotein A1 levels and higher triglyceride levels are associated with impaired fibrinolysis, which may reflect biological interactions between lipid metabolism and fibrinolysis or parallel alterations secondary to hepatic dysfunction.

Title: Pre-sleep milk-derived proteins do not impair sleep or recovery in elite female athletes.
Journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep is essential for athlete recovery and performance, yet athletes frequently experience restricted or poor-quality sleep. Pre-sleep feeding (PSF) has emerged as a strategy to support recovery, but randomized, double-blinded, crossover trials comparing PSF macronutrient options on objective and subjective sleep outcomes in elite female athletes remain limited.
METHODS: Twenty-five National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I female athletes (18-25 years old) were recruited; 21 completed the trial. In a randomized, double-blinded, placebo controlled, crossover design conducted over 4-8 weeks, participants consumed four treatments for three consecutive nights each: 40 g casein protein (CAS; 160 kcal), 40 g α-lactalbumin protein (ALA; 160 kcal), 40 g carbohydrate (CHO; 160 kcal), and 40g of a placebo (PLA; 5 kcal), with a minimum three-day washout between conditions. Supplements were consumed ~2 h after the final meal and ~30 min before bedtime as the last caloric intake of the day. Objective outcomes were obtained from the WHOOP 4.0 device (total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), sleep efficiency (SE), resting heart rate (RHR), and heart rate variability (HRV)). Subjective outcomes were assessed each morning via questionnaires (subjective sleep quality (SSQ), subjective sleep onset latency (SSOL), and subjective recovery (SREC)). Nocturnal interstitial glucose was assessed via blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in a subset (n = 6). Sleep and recovery variables were analyzed using one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate treatment effects across the four supplementation conditions. For CGM data, a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate main effects of treatment and time, as well as the treatment × time interaction. Tukey's post hoc testing was used with significance set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: No significant treatment effects were observed for TST, SOL, SE, RHR, or HRV (p > 0.05). TST ranged from 7.47-7.62 h, SE from 91.5-92.0%, RHR from 53.5-54.1 bpm, and HRV from 98.2-103.9 ms across conditions. No significant treatment effects were detected for SSQ, SSOL, or SREC (p > 0.05); SSQ ranged from 69-75%, SSOL from 16-20 min, and SREC from 61-66%. In the CGM sub-analysis, a main effect of time was observed for nocturnal glucose (p = 0.008), but no differences among treatments (p = 0.187) or a time × treatment interaction (p = 0.550) were detected.
CONCLUSIONS: In NCAA Division I female athletes, three consecutive nights of pre-sleep ingestion of CAS, ALA, or CHO did not impair objective or subjective measures of sleep or recovery compared with PLA. These findings demonstrate that pre-sleep feeding, regardless of macronutrient type, can be incorporated without negatively affecting sleep quality or recovery metrics.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: STUDY00004409).

Title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma at 11-20 weeks of gestation and gestational diabetes risk: A prospective cohort study in China.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies have linked insulin resistance and the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus to the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP). This integrated lipid marker reflects cardiovascular risk and atherogenic dyslipidemia. However, its relationship with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is not completely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the association between AIP measured at 11-20 weeks of gestation and the subsequent risk of GDM and to identify the optimal AIP threshold for GDM prediction.
METHODS: A total of 2068 women with singleton pregnancies were included in this prospective cohort study from the Tongji Maternal and Child Health Cohort. AIP was calculated from fasting triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) measurements obtained at 11-20 weeks of gestation, before GDM diagnosis by 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analysis, restricted cubic spline models, and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess the relationship between GDM and AIP. The predictive performance of AIP alone and in combination with maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) was compared via receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.
RESULTS: Gestational diabetes mellitus was diagnosed in 252 participants (12.3%). Women in the highest AIP quartile demonstrated a substantially higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (adjusted odds ratio 2.56; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.63-4.01; P < 0.001), and higher AIP levels were associated with a progressively higher risk of GDM. AIP and GDM risk were found to be significantly positively correlated (P for overall association <0.001), with no statistically significant evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.700), as assessed by restricted cubic spline analysis. Based on the maximum Youden index, an AIP value equal to 0.091 was determined to be the ideal cut-off for GDM prediction. A multivariable model incorporating AIP, pre-pregnancy BMI, maternal age, and LDL-C showed improved discriminative ability compared with AIP alone (area under the curve 0.69; 95% CI 0.66-0.73).
CONCLUSION: Elevated AIP levels at 11-20 weeks of gestation were independently associated with an increased risk of GDM. Importantly, the inclusion of AIP alongside established maternal risk factors enhanced predictive accuracy. The findings of this study indicate that AIP might serve as a useful adjunctive biomarker in early antenatal screening to identify women at heightened risk for GDM.

Title: Effects of Aerobic Exercise on Autonomic and Endothelial Function and Splanchnic Hemodynamics in Compensated Cirrhosis: RCT Study.
Journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with cirrhosis often develop autonomic dysfunction (AD) and endothelial dysfunction (ED), which correlate with higher mortality. Aerobic exercise (AE) is a potential intervention, yet its effects on the autonomic nervous system (ANS) and hemodynamics remain underinvestigated in cirrhosis.
METHODS: We conducted a parallel-group randomized controlled trial including 50 sedentary patients with compensated cirrhosis. Participants were randomized to a 16-week moderate-intensity AE plus nutritional consultation (AE group; n = 25) or nutritional consultation alone (control group, CG; n = 25). Outcomes included heart rate variability (HRV), flow-mediated dilation (FMD) for peripheral circulation, mesenteric Doppler ultrasound for splanchnic hemodynamics, and sarcopenia-related outcomes (body composition, handgrip strength dynamometry, and the 6-min walk test [6MWT]). Data were analysed using intention-to-treat (ITT), modified ITT (mITT), and per-protocol approaches, as well as general linear mixed models (LMM).
RESULTS: Of the 50 participants (mean age, 62.6 ± 7.0 years; 60% female), 44 participants completed the study. Although most outcomes showed no statistically significant between-group differences, LMM analysis confirmed a significant reduction in the low-frequency to high-frequency (LF/HF) (β = -0.87, p = 0.04), indicating worsening ANS while AE remained stable. Based on mITT analysis, the AE group showed a significant with-in group increase in portal vein volume flow (median Δ = 350.66 mL/min, p = 0.003). Additionally, AE demonstrated significant improvement in 6MWT compared with CG (mean Δ = 32 m, IQR: 12.00-51.60 m, p < 0.01). No major adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: AE is safe and effectively improves functional capacity in compensated cirrhosis. However, positive signals in autonomic and hepatic parameters were not between-group significant, necessitating a cautious interpretation.

Title: Characterizing Heat Health Hazards and Receptivity of Cooling Interventions Among Indoor Lumber Mill Workers in Southern Thailand.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of two workplace cooling strategies and identify priorities for future mixed-methods research and practical solutions.
METHODS: A pilot randomized crossover field trial was conducted among 12 sawmill workers in southern Thailand under three conditions: no cooling (CON), a phase change cooling vest (VEST), and a combined cooling oasis (OASIS: hydration, fans, water dousing, cooling towels). Core temperature and heart rate were continuously monitored. Worker perceptions were explored through post-intervention focus group discussions.
RESULTS: Compared with CON, OASIS reduced core temperature (-0.24°C; 95% CI: 0.23, 0.25) and heart rate (-7 bpm; 95% CI: 6, 9), while VEST reduced core temperature (-0.17°C; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.18) and heart rate (-5 bpm; 95% CI: 4, 6). Despite greater physiological benefits from OASIS, most workers preferred VEST due to ease of use and caused minimal disruption to workflow. OASIS was perceived as effective but interruptive.
CONCLUSIONS: Combined cooling strategies can reduce heat strain in indoor industrial settings; however, the adoption of interventions is strongly influenced by practicality and economic considerations. Hybrid approaches and structural improvements are recommended. A full mixed-methods study is needed to evaluate effectiveness, productivity, and cost-effectiveness to inform scalable occupational heat policies.

Title: Early Changes in Left Atrial Mechanics During Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional echocardiographic improvements after sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy have been reported in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but data on novel composite indices of atrial mechanics, particularly the left atrial (LA) stiffness index and the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI), remain poorly characterized. The authors evaluated early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and atrial mechanics following initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center observational cohort study, patients with HFpEF in sinus rhythm who were naive to SGLT2 inhibitors received empagliflozin or dapagliflozin. Clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and comprehensive echocardiography were performed at baseline and after 3 months. Echocardiographic evaluation included LA reservoir and pump strain, the LA stiffness index (E/e'/LA reservoir strain), and LACI (minimum LA volume/LV end-diastolic volume ×100).
RESULTS: Fifty patients completed follow-up (70% women; mean age, 63.9 ± 8.1 years). New York Health Association functional class improved and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels decreased significantly (347 [134.8-524.8] vs. 257 [161.3-427.5] pg/mL; P = .007). Left atrial volume index and E/e' decreased significantly (34.6 ± 5.5 to 32.6 ± 5.7 mL/m2 and 12.1 ± 3.2 to 9.8 ± 2.8, respectively; both P < .001). Left atrial reservoir and pump strain increased, whereas the LA stiffness index and LACI decreased significantly (all P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective observational cohort of patients with HFpEF, initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and LA mechanics. Composite atrial indices, particularly the LA stiffness index and LACI, changed in parallel with established clinical and echocardiographic markers, suggesting that they may provide complementary information for monitoring early atrial remodeling during SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

Title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transfemoral access is the default approach for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC). Although ultrasound (US)-guided femoral puncture improves first-pass success and reduces vascular complications in randomized trials, real-world data in contemporary structural heart interventions, including both arterial and venous large-sheath access, remain limited. The authors aimed to compare US-guided vs. conventional transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVI and LAAC.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral structural procedures between January 2022 and December 2024 (93: TAVI; 72: LAAC). Ultrasound guidance was used in 57 procedures (34.5%). Arterial and venous cohorts were analyzed separately. Primary outcomes were absolute hemoglobin decrease (ΔHb) and access-site vascular complications (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula). In the arterial cohort, 1 : 1 propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.
RESULTS: Hemoglobin decline was significantly smaller with US guidance in both venous (0.80 ± 0.95 vs. 1.50 ± 1.11 g/dL; P = .009) and arterial procedures (0.58 ± 0.97 vs. 1.29 ± 1.00 g/dL; P = .002). In the venous cohort, complication rates were numerically lower but not statistically different (3.8% vs. 17.4%; P = .143). In contrast, arterial complications were significantly reduced with US guidance. After propensity matching (31 patients per group), complications occurred in 3.2% vs. 29.0% [Absolute Risk Reduction(ARR) = 25.8%, Number Need to Treat (NNT) = 4, P = .013].
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided transfemoral access was associated with reduced hemoglobin decline and fewer vascular complications, particularly in large-bore arterial procedures, supporting routine integration of real-time US guidance in structural interventions.

Title: Sirolimus-based immunosuppression and reported rejection or death in heart transplant recipients using the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus, although not approved for heart transplant recipients (HTRs), is frequently prescribed off-label for mitigating calcineurin inhibitor-related toxicity and promoting graft survival. However, its adverse event profile and real-world outcome associations within specific immunosuppressive combinations remain unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective pharmacovigilance study utilized data from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). To minimize confounding by concomitant medication, paired comparisons were restricted to regimens differing only by sirolimus use. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) and adjusted RORs (aRORs), controlling for demographic and geographic variables, were calculated for the composite outcome of transplant rejection or death. Each sirolimus-containing regimen was compared with its corresponding nonsirolimus reference.
RESULTS: The sirolimus plus tacrolimus regimen showed lower disproportional reporting of transplant rejection or death than the tacrolimus regimen (ROR, 0.532 [95% CI, 0.284-0.994], P=0.048; aROR, 0.419 [95% CI, 0.218-0.804], P=0.009). In other tacrolimus-based regimens (tacrolimus plus mycophenolic acid, tacrolimus plus prednisone, and tacrolimus plus mycophenolic acid plus prednisone), sirolimus addition consistently showed RORs and aRORs <1.000, indicating a similar but nonsignificant trend toward lower reporting of transplant rejection or death.
CONCLUSIONS: This FAERS-based analysis suggested an association between sirolimus-containing regimens and lower disproportional reporting of transplant rejection or death among HTRs. These findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating, as spontaneous reporting data are susceptible to confounding and cannot establish causality. Prospective studies with detailed clinical data are needed to determine whether this association persists after adequate confounding control.

Title: Cognitive Functions and Gene Polymorphism Associated with Cardiovascular Risk in Young Adults vs. Patients with Arterial Hypertension.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of the study was to examine the relationship between cognitive functions and gene polymorphism associated with cardiovascular risk in young adults and patients with arterial hypertension (AH).
METHODS: The observational study involved 152 subjects, among whom there were 2 independent groups: a group of young healthy volunteers and a group of hypertensive patients. Cognitive functions were assessed using subtests 5 and 7 of the Wechsler Scale and the Bourdon test. Genetic testing was carried out for the following polymorphisms: APOC3 -482 C>T (rs2854117), PON1 L55M A>T (rs854560), and PON1 Q192R A>G (rs662). Identification of gene polymorphisms was performed via DNA pyrosequencing.
RESULTS: In both groups (young individuals and patients with AH), the presence of the Q192R A>G polymorphism of the PON1 gene was associated with worse results on cognitive tests. In young people, lower levels of concentration of attention, as well as the degree of mastery of visual-motor skills, were also associated with the -482 C>T polymorphism of the APOC3 gene and L55M A>T of the PON1 gene.
DISCUSSION: A relationship was identified between cognitive functions and polymorphism of genes associated with cardiovascular risk. The presence of the Q192R A>G polymorphism A allele of the PON1 gene accounted for the worst results of cognitive tests, both in young adults and patients with AH.
CONCLUSION: It should be noted that polymorphic variants of genes involved in lipid metabolism and antioxidant defense-namely, the -482 C>T variant of the APOC3 gene and the L55M A>T variant of the PON1 gene-are significantly associated with lower cognitive test scores in young individuals. The genetic analysis, including the determination of the Q192R A>G polymorphism of the PON1 gene and the -482 C>T polymorphism of the APOC3 gene, may be included in the examination of patients with arterial hypertension to predict the development of cognitive dysfunction.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Selective Versus Nonselective Beta-Blockers Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Receiving Sacubitril/Valsartan.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers, selective (metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol) and nonselective (carvedilol), and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) are the first-line guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Concomitant use of carvedilol and ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) may result in additive vasodilatory effects, which may increase the risk of hypotension and limit dose titration of sacubitril/valsartan.
OBJECTIVE: This study examines differences in clinical endpoints between selective and nonselective beta-blocker therapy among patients with HFrEF receiving sacubitril/valsartan.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized TriNetX Research Collaborative real-world data. Patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan concomitantly with carvedilol were identified as the intervention cohort, while those receiving metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol served as controls. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause hospitalization during the 3-year follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced confounders. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to estimate event-free survival, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models for time-to-event outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Overall, 75 230 patients received carvedilol and 21 587 received metoprolol/bisoprolol. After PSM, 20 939 patients were included in each group. Carvedilol was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint compared with those taking metoprolol or bisoprolol (52.32% vs 46.29%; HR: 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.24; P < .0001). Carvedilol was also linked to increased hospitalization risk (HR: 1.32; 95% CI, 1.28-1.36; P < .0001) but a modest reduction in mortality (HR: 0.92; 95% CI, 0.87-0.97; P = .0011). In addition, carvedilol was associated with higher risks of hypotension, end-stage renal disease, and bradycardia. Sensitivity analysis results were consistent for the primary endpoint.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Our results suggest that carvedilol may be associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint, health care utilization, and adverse events but lower all-cause mortality compared with metoprolol or bisoprolol in patients with HFrEF taking sacubitril/valsartan.

Title: Clinical and Longitudinal Heterogeneity Within the Acute Outer Retinopathy Spectrum: A Three-Case Series.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe three distinct presentations within the acute outer retinopathy (AOR) spectrum, emphasizing differences in stage, longitudinal evolution, and structure-function relationships.
METHODS: Retrospective case series.
RESULTS: The first, a 14-year-old asymptomatic male, had bilateral sectoral and spot-like outer retinal lesions in the subacute-chronic stage. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated outer nuclear layer thinning with ellipsoid and interdigitation zone disruption and focal retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) attenuation, without the angular sign of Henle fiber layer hyperreflectivity (ASHH). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) revealed lesions with a hypoautofluorescent core and hyperautofluorescent border, while fluorescein angiography (FA) showed window-defect hyperfluorescence and focal venular wall staining. The second, a 20-year-old male, developed severe visual field loss after a viral illness. FAF showed perivenular outer retinal involvement, and OCT revealed perivenular disruption with ASHH documented at 11 months. Visual field deficits were severe and partially correlated with structural abnormalities, with incomplete recovery over 3 years. Pattern electroretinography showed borderline reduction, whereas full-field electroretinography was within the lower limits of normal. The third, a 43-year-old female, presented with acute visual symptoms and mild intraocular inflammation. FAF showed sectoral peripapillary hyperautofluorescence, with corresponding outer retinal disruption on OCT. FA demonstrated venular wall staining and optic disc hyperfluorescence without diffuse vascular leakage. Perimetry showed bilateral diffuse sensitivity loss, while electrophysiology demonstrated generalized cone-predominant photoreceptor dysfunction.
CONCLUSION: These cases illustrate clinical and longitudinal heterogeneity within established AOR patterns, including asymptomatic subacute-chronic disease, perivenular disease with structure-function dissociation and late documentation of ASHH, and symptomatic sectoral disease with diffuse photoreceptor dysfunction.

Title: Ipsilateral Versus Contralateral Femoral Access for Inferior Epigastric Artery Embolization: Impact of Patient Age on Procedural Efficiency.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Abdominal wall hematomas (AWHs) are relatively uncommon causes of acute abdominal pain but may represent potentially life-threatening vascular emergencies, particularly in elderly patients receiving anticoagulant therapy or in the setting of significant hemorrhage. Transcatheter arterial embolization of the inferior epigastric artery is the recommended first-line therapy. The contralateral femoral approach may be technically demanding in elderly patients with iliac tortuosity, calcifications, or diffuse atherosclerosis. This bicentric retrospective study compared ipsilateral versus contralateral femoral access for inferior epigastric artery embolization, evaluating procedural efficiency, radiation exposure, and clinical outcomes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A bicentric retrospective study included 48 patients treated in emergency settings for epigastric artery bleeding between June 2022 and June 2025. Patients were divided into ipsilateral (n = 23) or contralateral (n = 25) femoral access groups, with further stratification by age (< 60 vs. ≥ 60 years). Technical and clinical success, total angiographic procedure duration, fluoroscopic dose (Air Kerma, mGy), access-site complications, transfusion requirements, rebleeding, and 30-day/3-month survival were analyzed. A subgroup analysis in patients ≥ 60 years (n = 33) assessed the impact of vascular anatomy on procedural metrics.
RESULTS: Technical success was 100% in both groups, whereas clinical success was comparable between the contralateral and ipsilateral groups (96.00% vs. 95.65%, respectively). In patients ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access significantly reduced procedure time (27.90 ± 6.40 vs. 33.30 ± 8.30 min, p = 0.046) and radiation dose (254.00 [IQR 219.00-272.00] vs. 283.50 [IQR 248.80-310.80] mGy, p = 0.023). No major complications or significant between-group differences in rebleeding or survival were observed. In exploratory multivariable analysis, ipsilateral access was associated with lower Air Kerma (β = -56.43 mGy; 95% CI, -91.91 to -20.95; p = 0.002), whereas the adjusted estimate for procedure duration was less precise and did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Both femoral access routes are safe and effective. In patients aged ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access was associated with shorter procedure duration and lower radiation exposure in unadjusted analyses. Exploratory adjusted analyses suggested an association between ipsilateral access and lower radiation exposure, whereas the adjusted association with procedure duration was not statistically significant. These findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
Abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

Title: Social Isolation and Loneliness Across the Cardiovascular Disease Spectrum: A Narrative Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
Abstract: Social isolation is the objective paucity of social ties; loneliness is the subjective distress of relationships falling short of what one desires. Both are common, affecting roughly a quarter to a third of older adults, and both have cardiovascular consequences through several mechanisms, with some estimates suggesting an increase of 29% in coronary heart disease risk and 21-23% in heart failure hospitalization. We review the evidence for social isolation and loneliness' impact on cardiovascular disease separately for ischemic heart disease, heart failure, arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death, and stress- and substance-related cardiomyopathies. We also highlight plausible mechanisms by which social isolation and loneliness are linked to downstream adverse cardiovascular events, limitations with existing evidence, societal guidance, and policy frameworks currently aimed at addressing them. The evidence is densest for ischemic heart disease, though the largest cohort shows a 43% excess risk of myocardial infarction attenuating by approximately 84% to nonsignificance after full adjustment, and Mendelian randomization estimates a far smaller effect. The prognostic signal is more consistent than the etiologic one, with low functional social support carrying a pooled hazard ratio of 1.59 in established coronary disease. In heart failure, objective isolation rather than loneliness predicts post-diagnosis mortality, mainly in women, consistent with a self-care-dependent behavioral pathway.

Title: Individualized Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndrome: Current SAPT Strategies and the Potential Role of Indobufen.
Abstract: Acute coronary syndrome requires effective antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while contemporary patients often present with overlapping ischemic and bleeding risks. This clinical complexity has shifted post-PCI management from fixed-duration dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) toward individualized strategies based on DAPT duration, single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) selection, and aspirin withdrawal. Aspirin is traditionally the default maintenance agent after DAPT, although long-term aspirin use is limited by gastrointestinal intolerance, mucosal injury, and bleeding risk. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy represents an important aspirin-free strategy, with clinical application influenced by drug potency, genetic variability, tolerability, cost, and adherence. Indobufen, a reversible cyclooxygenase-targeting antiplatelet agent, has reemerged as a potential aspirin alternative by suppressing thromboxane A2 generation through a mechanism distinct from that of aspirin. Current evidence suggests that indobufen-based DAPT may provide comparable ischemic protection with fewer bleeding or gastrointestinal adverse events in selected PCI patients, particularly those with aspirin intolerance, gastrointestinal vulnerability, or high bleeding risk. These patients often present with multiple high-risk features that simultaneously elevate both ischemic and bleeding risks, underscoring the need for careful risk stratification. Most available studies have evaluated indobufen as an aspirin substitute within DAPT rather than as SAPT after DAPT discontinuation. From a pharmacoeconomic perspective, indobufen is more expensive than aspirin, although this must be weighed against potential benefits in bleeding reduction. Future randomized trials are needed to define the optimal DAPT-to-SAPT strategy and clarify the clinical position of indobufen in acute coronary syndrome-PCI.

Title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

Title: Cell-Based Inflammatory Indices for Risk Stratification in Acute Myocardial Infarction: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
Abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, despite substantial advances in reperfusion strategies and guideline-directed therapies. Increasing evidence highlights the pivotal role of inflammation. Therefore, identifying reliable and accessible inflammatory biomarkers may provide valuable prognostic information for patients with AMI. Cell-based inflammatory indices derived from routine complete blood count parameters have emerged as promising biomarkers due to their simplicity, low cost, and widespread availability. Unlike single inflammatory markers, these indices reflect the complex interactions among different immune cell populations involved in cardiovascular inflammation. Recent studies have demonstrated associations between elevated cell-based inflammatory indices and adverse outcomes following AMI. Inflammation represents a central mechanism linking coronary plaque instability, myocardial injury, and adverse outcomes after AMI. Cell-based inflammatory indices provide a practical and cost-effective approach for evaluating systemic inflammatory activity and may improve prognostic assessment in patients with AMI. Further prospective studies are required to determine their optimal clinical application, standardized cutoff values, and integration into routine cardiovascular risk models.

Title: Atrial fibrillation in stroke patients: facts, numbers and current challenges.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading, modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke, with 20-30% of stroke patients harbouring underlying AF. Management of AF, however, differs substantially depending on clinical context. In ischaemic stroke patients with pre-known AF, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the cornerstone of secondary prevention, with initiation timing guided by infarct severity following a risk-adapted approach. In patients with no history of AF, prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring after stroke or transient ischaemic attack improves AF detection rates. However, it remains uncertain whether this translates into a reduced risk of recurrent stroke, with randomised trials such as Find-AF 2 ongoing. Subclinical AF, detected via implantable devices, is associated with an increased stroke risk correlating with arrhythmia burden; recent trials (ARTESiA, NOAH-AFNET 6) suggest that anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic stroke risk in this population, but at the cost of increased bleeding, necessitating individualised decision-making. Particularly challenging are anticoagulation decisions with concomitant cerebral amyloid angiopathy or prior intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) due to competing risks of thromboembolism and haemorrhage. Recent meta-analyses indicate that resuming DOACs after ICH reduces ischaemic events but significantly raises the risk of recurrent haemorrhage, without clear improvement in net clinical benefit. New treatment options, such as left atrial appendage closure, carotid artery filter systems, factor XIa inhibitors or rhythm control, must demonstrate in adequately powered randomised controlled trials that they can optimise treatment outcomes in this complex and growing patient group. This article summarises some common interdisciplinary neurological and cardiological questions and discusses the most recent evidence on AF-related stroke prevention across various patient groups, highlighting the importance of individualised, multidisciplinary, and imaging-informed decision-making.

Title: Ultrasensitive serum levels of interleukin 13 in systemic lupus erythematosus patients: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by elevated levels of various cytokines. Interleukin (IL)-13 is a pleiotropic type 2 cytokine that plays a central role in allergic inflammation and tissue fibrosis. Until recently, serum measurement of IL-13 was not feasible because of its extremely low concentration. New highly sensitive techniques now allow its quantification at the femtogram level. In the present study, we aimed to evaluate the association between SLE-disease characteristics and ultrasensitive serum IL-13 levels.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, a comprehensive characterization of 313 patients with SLE was performed, including autoantibody profiles and indices of disease activity (SLE-DAS, SLEDAI-2 K, and LLDAS), damage (SLICC-DI), and remission (DORIS). In addition, the cohort was evaluated with complete hematological and lipid profiles, insulin resistance indices, and assessment of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis and carotid stiffness. Serum IL-13 levels were measured using the Simoa (Single Molecule Array) technique. Multivariable linear regression analyses were then conducted to examine the associations between these disease characteristics and circulating IL-13.
RESULTS: In multivariable regression analyses demographic features, disease activity indices (SLEDAI-2 K, SLE-DAS, DORIS), damage scores, overall disease duration, autoantibodies and interferon or complement levels were not associated with IL-13. However, in the adjusted models, neutrophil and platelet counts showed an inverse association with IL-13. It was also the case for metabolic factors, as higher levels of HDL-cholesterol and apolipoprotein A1 were independently associated with lower IL-13 levels, while a higher LDL: HDL ratio, a higher ApoB: ApoA1 ratio, and a higher atherogenic index were associated with superior IL-13 levels. In contrast, augmentation index was inversely and independently associated with IL-13.
CONCLUSIONS: Serum IL-13 levels are not associated with key SLE-related features such as disease activity or the autoantibodies profile. Since IL-13 was associated with an adverse lipid profile, its inverse relationship with augmentation index suggests that its cardiovascular effects may be at least partially independent of circulating lipids. These apparently divergent associations likely reflect distinct but interconnected pathways through which IL-13 influences cardiovascular risk in SLE.

Title: Performance status and outcomes in patients with cancer receiving thromboprophylaxis: a subanalysis of the AVERT trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG-PS) is central to cancer care planning and prognostication. Whether ECOG-PS also carries prognostic value in the setting of primary thromboprophylaxis for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of ECOG-PS on clinical outcomes in ambulatory patients with cancer initiating chemotherapy.
METHODS: This was a post-hoc analysis of the AVERT randomized controlled trial that evaluated apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) for thromboprophylaxis in patients at intermediate-to-high VTE risk. Multivariable survival models assessed the association between ECOG-PS (0-1 versus 2-3) and the composite primary outcome of VTE or clinically relevant bleeding (CRB), as well as its individual components and all-cause mortality, over 180 days.
RESULTS: Of 428 patients included, 368 (86.0%) and 60 (14.0%) had an ECOG-PS of 0-1 and 2-3, respectively. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.8% (n = 47) in those with ECOG 0-1 and 18.3% (n = 11) with ECOG-PS 2-3 (6-month cumulative incidence: 13.0% [95% CI: 9.8%-16.7%] versus 19.9% [95% CI: 10.5%-31.4%], respectively). Worse performance status was associated with higher risks for the composite outcome (aHR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.14-2.72; p = 0.011), CRB (aHR: 1.58; 95%CI: 1.53-1.63; p < 0.0001), and all-cause mortality (aHR: 5.77; 95% CI: 4.98-6.67; p < 0.0001). In exploratory treatment-effect analyses, apixaban reduced VTE risk across ECOG-PS strata, including among participants with ECOG-PS 2-3, without clear evidence of excess CRB in this subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: ECOG-PS predicts VTE-related outcomes in ambulatory patients with cancer and may inform individualized, value-based shared decision-making regarding anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis.

Title: Clinical spectrum and risk factors for severe arrhythmias in non-surgical pediatric patients: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical spectrum and identify risk factors for severe arrhythmias in children.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted on 428 consecutive children (0-18 years) diagnosed with arrhythmia between January 2021 and October 2025. Patients were classified as having severe arrhythmia-related clinical presentation (severe group, n = 107) or non-severe presentation (non-severe group, n = 321) according to the presence of hemodynamic instability, syncope, heart failure, or malignant arrhythmia features. Clinical spectrum characteristics were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for severe arrhythmias. Electrocardiographic (ECG), echocardiographic, and serological parameters were compared.
RESULTS: The severe group had higher proportions of infants/toddlers (0-3 years), underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and class III-IV heart function (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified these as independent risk factors (P < 0.05): infant/toddler age [2.30 (1.08-4.89)], underlying cardiac disease [12.66 (6.01-26.68)], syncope history [45.84 (12.74-164.91)], and class III-IV heart function [32.97 (13.39-81.17)]. The prediction model showed good fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.171) and discrimination (AUC = 0.925, 95% CI: 0.893-0.958). The severe group also exhibited longer QTc, wider QRS, more third-degree atrioventricular block, higher ventricular premature burden, larger cardiac dimensions (LVEDD/LAD Z-score), higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure and myocardial injury/heart failure markers (CK-MB, cTnI, BNP, NT-proBNP), but lower heart rate variability (SDNN), left ventricular ejection fraction, and serum potassium (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Infant/toddler age, underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and advanced heart failure are independent clinical risk factors for severe pediatric arrhythmias. A model incorporating these factors demonstrates strong predictive ability for early high-risk identification.

Title: COL10A1+ fibroblasts define rupture-prone abdominal aortic aneurysms and enable molecular risk stratification.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture remains the leading cause of AAA-related mortality, while current clinical management relies primarily on aneurysm diameter, which inadequately predicts rupture risk. Increasing evidence suggests that stromal cell heterogeneity critically shapes vascular remodeling; however, the specific fibroblast states associated with AAA rupture predisposition remain poorly defined.
METHODS: We integrated cross-species single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets spanning the full spectrum of AAA progression to systematically characterize fibroblast heterogeneity and state transitions. Pseudotime trajectory analysis, transcriptional regulatory network inference, and ligand-receptor interaction modeling were applied to delineate fibroblast-associated microenvironmental programs. Based on these findings, a fibroblast-derived molecular signature was constructed and validated in an independent human AAA cohort.
RESULTS: Single-cell analysis revealed a progressive transition from homeostatic IGFBP6+ fibroblasts to a disease-associated COL10A1+ fibroblast state during AAA progression. COL10A1+ fibroblasts were selectively enriched in rupture-prone lesions and exhibited transcriptional programs linked to extracellular matrix remodeling and osteogenic-like activation. Intercellular communication analysis indicated that COL10A1+ fibroblasts were predicted to engage macrophage populations through coordinated ligand-receptor signaling pathways, including MDK, CSF1, and CXCL12, collectively delineating a rupture-associated vascular microenvironment. Translationally, leveraging this fibroblast state enabled the development of a minimal two-gene risk score (COL10A1-IGFBP6), which stratified AAA patients by molecular rupture risk independently of aneurysm diameter in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a COL10A1+ fibroblast-associated transcriptional state that defines a rupture-prone vascular microenvironment in abdominal aortic aneurysm. The derived COL10A1-IGFBP6 signature establishes a biologically informed framework for molecular risk stratification, complementing anatomical size-based assessment and providing a foundation for future development of mechanism-guided strategies to refine AAA risk evaluation.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and adverse cardiovascular outcomes in dialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving maintenance dialysis experience exceptionally high cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor in the general population; however, its prognostic significance in dialysis populations remains uncertain.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort studies evaluating circulating Lp(a) levels and adverse cardiovascular outcomes in maintenance dialysis patients were conducted. MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through May 5, 2026. The outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and MACEs. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when at least two studies reported comparable adjusted hazard ratios; pooled analyses based on very few studies were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: Fifteen reports representing 14 unique cohorts and 6380 dialysis patients were included. Nine studies evaluated hemodialysis populations exclusively, three evaluated peritoneal dialysis populations, and two evaluated mixed dialysis cohorts. Exploratory meta-analyses revealed associations between elevated Lp(a) levels and all-cause mortality (HR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.24-2.02), cardiovascular mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.22-3.50), and MACE (HR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.28-1.90). Certainty was low for MACE and very low for mortality outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence suggests an association between high Lp(a) concentrations and mortality and adverse cardiovascular events in maintenance dialysis patients. However, routine clinical use for cardiovascular risk stratification cannot yet be recommended because thresholds, assay standardization, incremental predictive value, and treatment implications remain unresolved.

Title: Frailty transitions and the risk of multisystem burden of chronic disease: a prospective cohort study in China.
Journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty, defined by a decline in physiological reserve, is a key determinant of adverse health outcomes in older populations. While baseline frailty has been shown to predict the development of chronic diseases, the impact of changes in frailty status over time, particularly in rapidly ageing populations like China, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess how baseline frailty and its longitudinal transitions influence the incidence of chronic diseases across multiple organ systems.
METHODS: We analysed data from 17,708 adults (aged ≥ 40) in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) collected between 2011 and 2018. Frailty was assessed using the Rockwood Frailty Index at baseline and at two-year follow-up, categorised as stable, improved, or worsened. We applied Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the onset of 13 major chronic diseases spanning cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, neurological, psychiatric, digestive, renal, and musculoskeletal systems.
RESULTS: The study included 9,807 to 16,882 participants across 13 disease-specific subgroups, with a median follow-up period of 6.2-6.8 years for baseline frailty status and 4.4-5.0 years for frailty transitions. Frail individuals were typically older, more likely to be female, unmarried, with lower education, higher BMI, and reported fewer hours of sleep. Baseline frailty was associated with significantly higher risks for all 13 chronic diseases, with the strongest association observed for psychiatric problems (HR 5.17, 95% CI 3.24-8.24). Worsening frailty over time was linked to elevated risks, particularly for asthma (HR 3.91, 95% CI 1.28-11.91), while improvements in frailty showed reduced risks, notably for kidney diseases (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.22-0.63). The association was particularly strong in adults aged 40-65 years, indicating greater potential for risk modification in midlife.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is a dynamic and modifiable predictor of multisystem chronic disease risk. Changes in frailty status offer valuable insights into future disease development, especially among middle-aged adults. Routine frailty monitoring in clinical settings may offer a strategic opportunity to delay or prevent the onset of chronic diseases through timely interventions. These findings emphasize the need for incorporating frailty-targeted strategies into public health and clinical care policies to enhance ageing-related disease prevention.

Title: Beyond Recurrence: Impact of Surgical Technique on Testicular Microcirculation After Inguinal Hernia Repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of different inguinal hernia repair techniques on testicular perfusion remains a subject of clinical interest. While open and laparoscopic approaches demonstrate comparable outcomes in terms of recurrence and complications, their effects on testicular microcirculation are not fully elucidated.
METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 180 male patients who underwent unilateral primary inguinal hernia repair using open Lichtenstein, total extraperitoneal (TEP), or transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) techniques between January 2015 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Doppler ultrasonography parameters, including resistive index (RI), peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and testicular volume, were evaluated preoperatively, at postoperative day 7, and at 1 month. Changes over time and between groups were analyzed using multivariable regression and linear mixed-effects models. Subclinical testicular ischemia was defined based on predefined Doppler criteria.
RESULTS: Early postoperative changes in testicular perfusion parameters differed significantly between surgical techniques. At postoperative day 7, RI values were higher and EDV values were lower in the Lichtenstein group compared to TEP and TAPP (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002, respectively). These differences decreased at 1 month but remained statistically significant for RI (p = 0.003). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that surgical technique, operative time, and hernia sac size were independently associated with changes in RI. Subclinical testicular ischemia was more frequent in the Lichtenstein group, while laparoscopic approaches were associated with lower odds (TEP: OR 0.34, p = 0.002; TAPP: OR 0.41, p = 0.006). Longitudinal analysis confirmed a significant time-by-technique interaction for RI (p < 0.001), indicating partial recovery over time.
CONCLUSION: Surgical technique is associated with transient alterations in testicular perfusion following inguinal hernia repair. Open Lichtenstein repair demonstrated more pronounced early microvascular changes, whereas laparoscopic techniques exhibited a more stable perfusion profile. These findings highlight the importance of surgical technique and intraoperative handling in preserving testicular microcirculation.

Title: Association of edentulism with incident non-communicable diseases among middle-aged and older adults: a population-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Edentulism has been associated with multiple non-communicable diseases (NCDs). However, existing evidence from China is largely limited to specific high-risk regions or lacks national representativeness, and large-scale population-based prospective studies remain scarce. This study investigated the association between edentulism and the risk of developing NCDs in middle and older adults from China.
METHODS: We examined the relationship between edentulism and NCDs in the CHARLS study, a large prospective cohort of 17,708 adults in China. Follow-up started from the baseline survey in 2011 and ended at the 2018 survey, and the primary endpoint was the first diagnosis of any NCD during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) with adjustment for potential confounders.
RESULTS: A total of 6,585 participants were included, with a mean follow-up of 6.46 years. Participants with edentulism had a higher risk of NCDs (HR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.03-1.33), asthma (HR = 2.83, 95% CI: 1.38-5.79), hypertension (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.01-1.45), and cancer (HR = 2.66, 95% CI: 1.46-4.84) than those who had teeth. No statistically significant associations between edentulism and other diseases were found. Stratified analyses showed effect modification by age for asthma and by sex for dyslipidemia.
CONCLUSIONS: The study from China found that edentulism was associated with NCDs, asthma, hypertension, and cancer, and also with the other cancers category, although this finding was unstable.
