INTRODUCTION: Stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a critical juncture in clinical management. However, muscle strength training (MST) combined with blood flow restriction (BFR) has shown benefits as an adjunctive treatment, but its renal effects remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the effects of MST+BFR on markers of glomerular function in individuals with CKD-3.
METHOD: A randomized, longitudinal clinical trial with 40 participants divided into 4 groups: control (G1); low-load MST (G2); high-load MST (G3); and low-load MST combined with BFR (G4). Serum creatinine, cystatin C, microalbuminuria, and estimated eGFR were used as dependent variables. The MST protocol was conducted over 12 weeks, 3 times per week, for 30-40 minutes, with 3 exercises (single- and multi-joint) per day at progressive intensities. Data analysis (intention-to-treat) was performed using the Shapiro-Wilk test (normality), paired t-test/Wilcoxon test (within-group comparisons), ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests (between-group comparisons), Bonferroni test (post hoc corrections), and Cohen's d (effect size) with a p-value ≤ 0.05.
RESULTS: The participants were predominantly male (52.5%) with low levels of physical activity (60%), hypertension (87.5%), and some with diabetes (37.5%). Group 4 showed a significant increase in albuminuria levels (p = 0.048), as well as significant differences compared with Group 1 (creatinine, p = 0.032) and Group 2 (creatinine, p = 0.036; and eGFR-Cr, p = 0.032).
CONCLUSION: MST+BFR was not associated with severe adverse effects on serum creatinine/cystatin C levels, eGFR estimates, or urinary creatinine and microalbuminuria levels, but it may significantly increase albuminuria levels.

Title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
Abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

Title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
Abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

Title: Cardiac Effects of Combined Versus Individual Interventions of Mediterranean Diet and Exercise in Adults with the Hypertriglyceridemic Waist Phenotype: A Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype, combining abdominal obesity and elevated serum triglycerides, is associated with adverse cardiovascular prognosis. The combination of dietary and exercise programs has the potential to improve outcomes with regard to adverse cardiac remodeling and dysfunction associated with poor metabolic health. We tested the hypothesis that the combination of a Mediterranean Diet (MedDiet) and exercise interventions improves cardiac structure and function more than the sum of each individual intervention.
METHODS: We performed a randomized 2 × 2 factorial design trial that included adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype (triglycerides ≥1.50 mmol/L, waist circumference ≥80 cm in women or ≥94 cm in men). Participants were randomly assigned to one of four 16-week interventions: (1) MedDiet alone, (2) exercise alone, (3) MedDiet + exercise, or (4) control group. The MedDiet groups received education, counseling, and key food items from the MedDiet. The exercise groups participated in a structured exercise program designed to achieve 150 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week. Data were collected during the screening, baseline, and post-intervention visits. In mixed-effects models, we compared the post-intervention echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) structure and function per intervention group after adjusting for age, sex, and baseline values. We calculated an interaction ratio between MedDiet and exercise to assess their combined effect.
RESULTS: Of the 200 recruited, 185 participants (76% women) had available echocardiographic data. LV measurements were within normal range for most participants. After the intervention, the posterior wall thickness (LV structure) was higher in the MedDiet groups (0.04 [95% CI: 0.01-0.07] cm), and the septal mitral annular tissue Doppler e' velocity (diastolic function) was higher in the exercise groups (0.4 [95% CI: 0.0-0.8] cm/s). No significant interactions between interventions were identified with respect to LV measurements.
CONCLUSION: No interaction between the MedDiet and exercise interventions on LV structure and function was observed among adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype. Further research is needed to ascertain whether the combination of these interventions can prevent the development of adverse LV remodeling over the long term or in participants with more advanced cardiac alterations.

Title: Periwound Ring Enhancement on Indocyanine Green Angiography as a Prognostic Imaging Biomarker for Chronic Wound Healing.
Journal: Wound repair and regeneration : official publication of the Wound Healing Society [and] the European Tissue Repair Society
Abstract: Chronic wound healing depends on local wound-edge perfusion, which is not fully characterised by conventional vascular assessments. We evaluated whether quantitative periwound ring enhancement on indocyanine green angiography could predict 12-week wound healing. This retrospective cohort study included 71 patients with diabetic foot ulcers or pressure sores who underwent baseline indocyanine green angiography. Relative fluorescence intensity, time to peak, perfusion slope and ring continuity were quantified and integrated into an exploratory 0-8-point Perfusion Success Index. Forty-two patients achieved complete healing within 12 weeks and 29 did not. Healers showed higher relative fluorescence intensity, shorter time to peak, steeper perfusion slope, greater ring continuity and a higher Perfusion Success Index than non-healers (5.83 ± 1.45 vs. 3.24 ± 1.38, p < 0.001). The Perfusion Success Index demonstrated the highest overall discrimination for 12-week healing (area under the curve, 0.894; 95% confidence interval, 0.823-0.965); a cut-off of ≥ 5 yielded 83.3% sensitivity and 82.8% specificity. A clinical model including wound type, wound area, wound depth, infection and serum albumin had an area under the curve of 0.777, which increased to 0.908 after addition of the Perfusion Success Index (absolute increase in area under the curve, 0.131; p = 0.012). After bootstrap internal validation, the clinical-plus-index model retained favourable discrimination with an optimism-corrected area under the curve of approximately 0.87. Quantitative periwound ring enhancement on indocyanine green angiography may provide complementary prognostic information regarding wound-edge healing potential beyond conventional clinical assessment.

Title: Template-Anchored Signal Decomposition and Label Refinement for Impairment Categorization on Noisy Visual Electrophysiological Data.
Journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
Abstract: Visual electrophysiology offers an objective alternative to subjective vision assessments, providing enhanced reliability but remaining underutilized for visual impairment categorization due to imperfect datasets, noisy signals, and label inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we first construct a new dataset comprising ERG and VEP recordings from 1,970 participants with various ocular conditions and a mean age of 21.59 $\pm$ 4.47 years. A three-class categorization task is defined to reflect clinical disability grading. We then propose a template-anchored decomposition method for noise-aware signal feature extraction, using mode-specific ridge regression to isolate pathological components by removing both healthy patterns and noise artifacts. To collectively enhance feature representation from multi-channel signals, we design a joint attention encoder that combines channel attention with bilateral spatial attention across left- and right-eye channels to emphasize informative and coherent signal patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a template-anchored refinement mechanism that addresses label noise by updating soft labels during training based on the distances between each feature vector and the class templates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves consistent improvements over existing electrophysiology-based and general biosignal classification methods, supporting its feasibility for visual impairment categorization in a cohort composed primarily of young adults.

Title: Midlife physical activity trajectories are associated with reduced physical pre-frailty/frailty in older age: insights from the prospective ATTICA sub-study 2002-2024.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although physical activity in older adults has been associated with lower risk of frailty, it is unclear if midlife physical activity patterns are associated with pre-frailty/frailty status in older age.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether longitudinal midlife physical activity trajectories are associated with physical pre-frailty/frailty development in older age, independent of cardiometabolic risk and other lifestyle factors.
DESIGN: Population-based prospective cohort study.
SETTINGS: In-person assessments and telephone interviews of persons living in urban communities in Attica, Greece.
PARTICIPANTS: Surviving participants of the ATTICA cohort study (2002-2024) who were older than 33 years at baseline.
MEASUREMENTS: Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, and lifestyle parameters were recorded at baseline and throughout the study. According to binary self-reported physical activity levels (<600 vs ≥600 metabolic equivalent minutes per week) at baseline, 5-year and 10-year follow-up, 4 ordered trajectories of physical activity were defined: persistently inactive, declining activity, inclining activity, and persistently active, and their association with the odds of pre-frailty/frailty development according to the phenotypic (FRAIL scale) model were investigated by applying multivariable logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Relative to persistent inactivity, persistently active and inclining physical activity lifestyles were associated with 80% and 79% decreased odds of pre-frailty/frailty at 22-year follow-up, respectively, after adjusting for age, sex, years of education, baseline body mass index, hypertension, diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia. The population fraction of pre-frailtand frailty that could be attributed to unhealthy physical activity trajectories throughout midlife is 49.5% (95% confidence interval, 36.3 to 59.9), rising to 64.8% (95% confidence interval, 49.6 to 75.4) when also considering hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and obesity.
CONCLUSION: Steadily high or rising physical activity trajectories during midlife were associated with lower odds of physical pre-frailty/frailty in older age, independently of cardiometabolic risk factors. These findings support that achieving and maintaining higher physical activity levels across midlife may be one of the keys to healthy aging.

Title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds.
RESULTS: Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds.
DISCUSSION: Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

Title: Clinical Effectiveness of AI-Based Cardiac Arrest Prediction System for General Ward Patients (VITAL-MD): Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remains a frequent and devastating event, and conventional early warning scores (EWSs) coupled with rapid response systems (RRSs) have shown inconsistent effects on patient-centered outcomes, largely owing to limited predictive accuracy and high false-alarm burden. AI-based EWSs (AI-EWSs) have demonstrated superior discrimination retrospectively, but high-quality prospective evidence in true external validation environments remains scarce. Existing AI-EWS trials have either been confined to internal-development settings or bundled the algorithm with specific implementation infrastructure, leaving the stand-alone effect of AI-based software as a medical device (AI-SaMD) on patient outcomes uncharacterized.
OBJECTIVE: This trial will evaluate whether implementation of AI-SaMD (VUNO Med-DeepCARS) as a stand-alone clinical decision-support tool in routine general-ward care reduces IHCA compared with usual care based on conventional EWSs.
METHODS: The VITAL-MD trial (validation of an AI-based clinical deterioration prediction model on patient outcomes through a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial [SW-CRT] multicenter evaluation of DeepCARS) is a pragmatic, multicenter, SW-CRT conducted at 4 tertiary academic hospitals in the Republic of Korea. Six tertiary academic hospitals were assessed for eligibility based on inpatient capacity, RRS operating hours aligned with the national RRS pilot program, and no prior AI-SaMD use. All adult patients aged 19 years or older admitted to general wards during the 12-month trial period are included; patients younger than 19 years, or with no documented vital signs throughout hospitalization, are excluded. The 4 sites are randomized to sequentially transition from preimplementation (usual care) to postimplementation (AI-SaMD-guided care) in 4 steps separated by 7-day washout periods. DeepCARS generates real-time risk scores from 4 vital signs and integrates into the existing electronic medical record interface without altering RRS workflows. The primary outcome is the incidence of general-ward IHCA, defined per the Utstein guidelines, among the target cohort (defined as patients exceeding the alert threshold at least once). Assuming a baseline IHCA incidence of 6.70%, a 40% relative risk reduction, an intracluster correlation coefficient of 0.01, and 350 patients per cluster-period, 7002 target-cohort patients (total enrollment approximately 72,695) provide 80% power. Analyses follow the intention-to-treat principle using generalized linear mixed models adjusting for prespecified covariates, with prespecified sensitivity, subgroup, and compliance analyses.
RESULTS: The trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service (KCT0010243) on February 28, 2025. Recruitment was conducted from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. All 4 sites completed transition to the postimplementation period, and data cleaning is currently underway before the final database lock, with primary results expected in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: VITAL-MD will provide the first large-scale, multicenter randomized evidence evaluating whether an AI-EWS, deployed as a stand-alone device in external validation environments and benchmarked against real-world standard-of-care practice, improves patient-centered outcomes for general-ward patients, advancing the evaluation of AI-SaMD from retrospective diagnostic accuracy toward prospective, action-anchored clinical utility.

Title: Greenspace visitation and risk of major adverse cardiovascular events: evidence from the Houston methodist cardiovascular learning health system registry.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether mobility-derived greenspace visitation, as a behavioural measure of environmental exposure, is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) independent of individual and neighbourhood factors.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults in the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry (2016-2023). Greenspace visitation was defined at the census-tract level using mobility-derived foot-traffic data and modelled as annual visits per resident device. The primary outcome was incident MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, and all-cause mortality). The Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and Kaplan-Meier curves assessed associations with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, smoking, and neighbourhood social vulnerability. Among 1 088 866 adults without baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, median (SD) age was 49 (17.6) years, and 59.9% were female. Greenspace visitation varied across neighbourhoods and by demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Each additional 10 annual visits was associated with lower MACE risk in unadjusted models [hazard ratio (HR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.81-0.83] and after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and smoking (HR 0.89; 95% CI: 0.88-0.91). A non-linear relationship showed risk reductions at low-to-moderate visitation, plateauing at 10-15 visits annually. After adjusting for social vulnerability, associations were attenuated and no longer significant. The Kaplan-Meier curves showed higher event-free survival in high-visitation areas, consistent across MACE components.
CONCLUSION: Mobility-derived greenspace visitation is associated with lower cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight greenspace engagement as a potentially modifiable behavioural exposure and support strategies to enhance access and utilization of greenspaces for cardiovascular prevention.

Title: Timeliness of Emergency Care for Intracerebral Hemorrhage Compared With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Clinical data comparing time to presentation and stroke quality metrics for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are limited. Understanding these differences is essential to provide timely care to all stroke subtypes.
OBJECTIVE: To compare prehospital and emergency department (ED) process quality metrics between patients with ICH and AIS.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort study included patients with AIS and ICH admitted to Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)-Stroke participating hospitals from January 1, 2015, to June 30, 2024, who arrived by emergency medical services (EMS). Data were analyzed from 195 hospitals across the US.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prehospital-based and ED-based process metrics (eg, EMS prenotification, door to ED physician assessment time, door to initial brain imaging order) were assessed. Logistic and linear regression models were sequentially adjusted for patient demographics, medical history and presenting factors, and hospital characteristics. Temporal trends of prehospital care metrics were examined.
RESULTS: A total of 195 659 patients (median [IQR] age, 74.0 [63.0-83.0] years; 97 978 [50.1%] female; 31 464 with ICH and 164 195 with AIS) from 195 hospitals were included. The median (IQR) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 14 (6-23) for ICH vs 6 (2-13) for AIS (absolute standardized difference, 0.694). ICH (vs AIS) was associated with higher odds of door-to-ED physician assessment of 10 or fewer minutes after adjusting for patient demographics (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14). This association reversed after adding adjustment for medical history and presenting factors (including NIHSS) and hospital characteristics (aOR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). This pattern was observed for door to initial brain imaging order of 20 or fewer minutes (demographic-adjusted: aOR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; fully adjusted with medical history and hospital characteristics: aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97). Median last known well to arrival time increased by 32.5% for AIS (151 to 200 minutes; P < .001) and 34.3% for ICH (108 to 145 minutes; P < .001), while rates of EMS prenotification largely remained stable for both ICH and AIS.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients with acute stroke, patients with ICH arrived at the ED faster but were less likely to achieve care targets. In the context of emerging hyperacute ICH therapies and bundled care models, addressing these differences is essential to optimizing acute stroke outcomes.

Title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk.
OBJECTIVE: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios.
RESULTS: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

Title: Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) for Youth With Prolonged Concussion Recovery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Research suggests that aerobic exercise improves recovery for youth with concussion; however, prior studies primarily focused on acute concussion and required multiple in-person visits.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a virtually delivered aerobic exercise program improves recovery following concussion compared to a stretching control and examine potential moderators.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A randomized clinical trial was conducted from 2021 to 2025 comparing the Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) to a stretching control for 11- to 18-year-olds with concussion up to 1 year from injury. Participants were recruited from a variety of outpatient locations in 4 US states (Washington, Utah, Wisconsin, and Oregon). Recruitment and data collection occurred from March 2021 until October 2025, and data analysis occurred from November 2025 to April 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Youth randomized to MSTEP were provided activity trackers and an aerobic exercise program initiated at 60% of heart rate maximum. Exercise was advanced in intensity and duration over 6 weeks through weekly videoconferencing calls. Youth in the control group were given stretching exercises and similar weekly calls.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included (1) concussive symptoms and (2) health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Secondary outcomes included sleep, depression, and anxiety. Moderation by sex, age, and time since injury was examined. Patients were followed up for 6 months.
RESULTS: The sample included 210 participants, among whom 122 (58.1%) were female, mean (SD) age was 15.1 (2.2) years, and mean (SD) time since injury was 73.3 (63.3) days. Covariate-adjusted regression analysis showed significant improvement in concussive symptoms and HRQoL at all time points, with greater improvement in MSTEP compared to control at the 3-month time point for both concussive symptoms (β, -3.15; 95% CI, -6.05 to -0.25; adjusted P = .04) and HRQoL (β, 4.15; 95% CI, 0.64-7.66; adjusted P = .04). No significant differences by group were seen at 6 months. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling with exponential decay showed significantly faster symptom recovery in MSTEP compared to control (difference in rates, -0.68; 95% CI, -2.22 to -0.04; P = .002). Secondary outcomes (sleep, depression, and anxiety) improved in all participants but were not different by group. Benefit of the intervention was only significant for individuals less than 3 months from injury (concussive symptoms: β, -4.44; 95% CI, -7.99 to -0.90; unadjusted P = .01; HRQoL: β, 6.64; 95% CI, 2.55-10.72; unadjusted P = .002). No evidence was found for moderation by other factors.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Per the results of this randomized clinical trial, an aerobic exercise program improves speed of recovery following concussion for youth compared to stretching and can be delivered remotely. However, this type of program appears to be most beneficial for individuals with acute or subacute injury (<3 months since injury).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04688255.

Title: Comparing operational definitions of screening-based cognitive impairment in the Tohoku Medical Megabank cohort: Focus on digital engagement.
Abstract: BackgroundDementia prevention is a global health priority, yet most large-scale population studies come from Western settings. Japan, a rapidly aging society, provides a unique non-Western epidemiological context for characterizing cognitive decline.ObjectiveTo assess whether the Tohoku Medical Megabank (TMM) cohorts replicate established dementia-related associations, and to identify correlates that are statistically significant across three prespecified operational classifications.MethodsWe analyzed data from >81,000 participants in the TMM cohorts. Participants were classified using (i) self-reported physician-diagnosed dementia and screening-defined impairment using (ii) Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) ≤ 27 and (iii) Japanese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-J) ≤ 25. Associations with 14 established dementia-related correlates and >3,800 exploratory variables were assessed using false-discovery-rate control, semantic clustering, and sequential multivariable logistic regression.ResultsParticipants with self-reported dementia had lower MMSE and MoCA-J scores. Established correlates replicated in expected directions for at least one classification, including lower education, hypertension, depressive symptoms, and hearing difficulty. We identified 106 significant correlates across all three classifications; for self-reported dementia, digital device non-use was associated with higher odds (fully adjusted OR up to 2.97, 95% CI: 1.42-6.18), while smartphone use showed inverse associations (OR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.26-0.86); directions were consistent for screening-defined impairment.ConclusionsIn this study, leveraging existing cognitive classifications available in TMM cohorts, we found that established dementia-related associations largely replicated and identified correlates across three operational classifications. Digital disengagement emerged as a correlate that may reflect early functional change; given the cross-sectional design, causal inference requires further examination. Longitudinal validation with adjudicated diagnoses is needed.

Title: A study on the dose-response relationship between glycemic variability and in-dialysis hypotension in patients with diabetes undergoing hemodialysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the dose-response relationship between Glycemic variability (GV) and Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) in diabetic hemodialysis (MHD) patients, identify the critical Coefficient of variation (CV) threshold, and inform precision glucose management.
METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 240 diabetic MHD patients (2023-2024). Continuous glucose monitoring provided GV parameters (CV, MAGE, SD). Patients were divided into IDH (n = 98) and non-IDH (n = 142) groups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyzed dose-response; multivariate logistic regression assessed independent effects, with Subgroup analysis and interaction tests.
RESULTS: CV was significantly higher in the IDH group (42.3% vs. 26.5%, P<0.001). RCS revealed a nonlinear positive correlation (P<0.001). When CV>36%, IDH risk increased sharply (threshold effect). Each 10% CV rise increased IDH risk by 98.4% (OR 1.984). Compared to Q1, Q3 (OR 3.512) and Q4 (OR 8.637) showed significantly higher risk. Associations were stronger in patients aged ≥60 years, dialysis duration ≥36 months, or with cardiovascular disease (interaction P<0.05). CV predicted IDH with AUC=0.856; optimal cutoff 36.5% (sensitivity 78.6%, specificity 82.4%).
CONCLUSION: A significant dose-response relationship exists between GV and IDH. CV>36% is an independent risk factor. Maintaining CV below 36% may reduce IDH risk and improve outcomes.

Title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure : From Implanted Hemodynamic Monitoring Toward an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Adaptive Care Cycle.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Implanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy. We review lessons from PAP-guided remote patient management and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could support more individualized eligibility assessment and multimodal longitudinal surveillance within a patient-centered adaptive care cycle to further improve clinical outcomes.
RECENT FINDINGS: HF is increasingly recognized as a systemic disease characterized, across HF phenotypes, by multiple cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities. CHAMPION, GUIDE-HF, and MONITOR-HF did not systematically incorporate comorbidity-related risk into patient selection, while PAP-guided treatment focused predominantly on diuretic adjustment, and monitoring strategies were not adapted to individual disease trajectories. AI could help integrate multidimensional phenotyping to estimate individual risk and expected benefit pre-implant, use comprehensive longitudinal monitoring data to support personalized, actionable clinical decision-making, and enable dynamic adaptation of monitoring intensity tailored to the disease trajectory. This may improve clinical outcomes, reduce healthcare professional workload, enhance patient experience and treatment adherence, and increase cost-effectiveness.

Title: Chicken-fat clots and pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density: a retrospective autopsy study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to explore the association between chicken-fat clots (CFCs) and neutrophil-related parameters in postmortem samples. Based on previous studies suggesting a potential role of neutrophils in CFC formation, the study aimed to assess whether CFCs are associated with increased neutrophil levels or intravascular neutrophil accumulation, rather than being explained solely by the traditional concept of "slow death".
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using autopsy data from November 2020 to November 2024. A total of 152 autopsies were screened, of which 122 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final cohort. Autopsy reports were reviewed together with available clinical documentation, including information on anticoagulants, vasoactive amines, corticosteroids, ongoing infections, and laboratory tests (leukocyte count, neutrophil percentage, and absolute neutrophil count). Because premortem laboratory data were frequently unavailable, particularly in traumatic deaths, lung tissue samples from all 122 decedents were analyzed. Digital pathology techniques, including scanning and analysis using QuPath software, were employed to quantify pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density. The association between intravascular neutrophil density and CFC presence was statistically analyzed using ROC curves, χ² tests, and odds ratios.
RESULTS: CFCs were present in 34 of 122 cases (27.9%), with septic shock representing the largest cause-of-death group among CFC-positive cases (29.4%). Increased pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density was significantly associated with CFC presence (OR 21.0, p < 0.001). A threshold of 2286 neutrophils/mm² showed good discrimination for CFC presence, with an AUC of 0.840. No significant associations were identified between CFCs and anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, or the other evaluated blood parameters.
CONCLUSION: Chicken-fat clots were associated with increased pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density in this retrospective autopsy cohort, suggesting a possible relationship with systemic inflammatory or neutrophil-mediated processes. These findings do not establish pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density as a validated marker of antemortem neutrophilia and do not exclude the contribution of agonal duration or postmortem processes to CFC formation. Further studies incorporating well-defined agonal timing and closely timed premortem laboratory data are needed to clarify the biological and temporal determinants of CFC formation.

Title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach.
Abstract: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield. In this prospective cohort study, adolescents with an abnormal ECG identified through a nationwide screening program underwent comprehensive clinical/genetic evaluation. Phenotype-negative individuals were included. Relatives underwent clinical screening, with cascade genetic testing offered when probands carried a likely/definite pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy variant. Abnormal screening outcomes included relatives with (i) de novo cardiomyopathy diagnosis, (ii) early cardiomyopathic traits, or (iii) gene-positive/phenotype-negative (G + P -) status. Sixteen adolescents (0.6%) met inclusion criteria, and 3 (18.8%) were G + (MYBPC3, MYH7, ACTC1). One in five relatives (n = 13/71, 18.3%; 95% CI 11.0-28.9%) were referred, most having an abnormal ECG (12.7%). Nine relatives (12.7%; 95% CI 4.9-20.4%) exhibited early cardiomyopathy traits at baseline. One (1.4%) relative was G + /P - . Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 3 (4.2%, 95% CI 0.9-11.8%) relatives at baseline (n = 2 HCM, n = 1 DCM). One relative with early cardiomyopathy traits underwent phenoconversion (NDLVC) during follow-up at 77 months, yielding an overall diagnostic rate of 5.6% (95% CI 2.0-13.8%) in 4 unrelated families. A joint clinical-genetic approach enabled personalized surveillance in 6 relatives (8.5%), including 2 (2.8%) diagnoses that would otherwise have been missed with conventional clinical screening.Conclusion: One in five relatives of ECG‑positive phenotype‑negative adolescents received a cardiomyopathy diagnosis or had early cardiomyopathy traits. A joint clinical-genetic approach in this subgroup may aid early cardiomyopathy detection in selected families, though findings remain exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. What is Known - What is New: •Resting ECG can identify individuals harboring conditions linked to sudden cardiac death •The penetrance of cardiomyopathy is age dependent, which explains why screened adolescents may exhibit abnormal ECG patterns in the absence of a cardiomyopathy diagnosis •Our data indicate that extending screening to relatives of ECG-positive, phenotype-negative adolescents is justified, with one in five relatives receiving a new cardiomyopathy diagnosis (5.6%) or exhibiting early cardiomyopathy traits (11.3%) •A joint clinical/genetic evaluation in this context may help personalize screening strategies.

Title: Vasopressors Combination Therapy (Norepinephrine Plus Vasopressin Receptor Agonists) Improve Septic Shock Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: BackgroundStudies showed different results of vasopressors combination therapy in septic shock patients. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the outcomes of combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists in adult septic shock.MethodsCochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed databases were searched up to September 27, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists versus norepinephrine alone in septic shock patients. Two reviewers independently extracted data on mortality, ICU length of stay, renal replacement therapy (RRT) and adverse events. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess random error.ResultsTwenty-one RCTs involving 3873 septic shock patients were included. The results showed that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists was associated with lower mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.83 to 0.99, P = .02), but with an increased risk of digital ischemia (RR = 2.21, 95% CI 1.15 to 4.27, P = .02). Subgroup analysis indicated that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may provide survival benefits for more severe septic shock patients (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.00, P = .04). Moreover, compared with norepinephrine alone, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin showed a trend towards reducing the longest follow-up mortality (RR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.00, P = .05). TSA indicated lack of firm evidence for a beneficial effect.ConclusionsIn adults with septic shock, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may reduce mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (low quality of evidence), but may increase risk of digital ischemia (low quality of evidence). This benefit mainly appeared in more severe septic shock patients. Moreover, norepinephrine plus vasopressin may confer a survival advantage.

Title: Effect of a structured healthcare professional-supported kangaroo care model on clinical outcomes in preterm neonates: A retrospective quasi-experimental cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of a structured healthcare professional-supported kangaroo mother care (KMC) model on physiological stability and clinical outcomes in preterm neonates hospitalized in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
METHODS: This retrospective quasi-experimental before-after cohort study included 64 preterm neonates (intervention: n = 33; comparison: n = 31) admitted to a tertiary-level NICU. During the comparison period, conventional KMC was provided once daily by mothers. Following implementation of a structured NICU protocol on 1 March 2025, KMC was administered eight times daily at three-hour intervals by both mothers and midwives/nurses. Primary outcomes included length of hospital stay and physiological parameters measured before and after KMC sessions.
RESULTS: Neonates in the intervention group had a significantly shorter hospital stay than those in the comparison group (p < 0.001). After adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and sex, comparison-group neonates had an adjusted hospital stay 9.88 days longer than intervention-group neonates (B = 9.884, 95% CI: 5.280-14.487, p < 0.001; R2 = 0.769). Post-KMC heart and respiratory rates were significantly lower and oxygen saturation was significantly higher in the intervention group (p < 0.001). Within-group analyses also showed significant improvements in physiological parameters following KMC, with larger effect sizes in the intervention group.
CONCLUSION: A structured healthcare professional-supported KMC model was associated with improved physiological stability and shorter hospitalization, supporting the integration of midwives and nurses to sustain KMC in NICU settings.

Title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.
Abstract: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

Title: Computed tomography-derived cardiac parameters versus biochemical inflammatory indices for discriminating disease severity and identifying cardiovascular comorbidity in obstructive sleep apnoea: A cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: It is unclear whether haematological inflammatory indices or CT-derived cardiac parameters add discriminative information beyond standard clinical variables in obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome (OSAS). We compared both modalities, alone and combined, against age, sex and body mass index (BMI) for identifying severe OSAS and associated cardiovascular comorbidity.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cross-sectional study of 401 participants (240 OSAS, 161 controls). Four nested logistic regression models were fitted in the OSAS cohort: M0 (age, sex, BMI); M1 (M0 plus biochemical indices CAR, NLR, PLR, SII); M2 (M0 plus CT-derived cardiac parameters: pulmonary artery [PA] diameter, PA/aorta ratio, RV/LV ratio, ventricular wall thicknesses); and M3 (M0 plus CT plus biochemical). We compared discrimination (AUC, DeLong), reclassification (continuous NRI, IDI) and model fit (likelihood ratio tests), with internal validation by 500-iteration bootstrap optimism correction and repeated tenfold cross-validation. Missing predictor data were handled by multiple imputation (MICE, m = 20) as the primary approach. Cardiovascular outcomes were defined from echocardiography to avoid predictor-outcome overlap.
RESULTS: For severe OSAS, M2 improved on M0 (AUC 0.755 vs 0.716; LR p = 0.005; NRI + 0.60 [95% CI 0.35-0.83]; IDI + 0.055 [0.027-0.083]), whereas M1 did not (LR p = 0.62). M3 added nothing over M2 (ΔAUC = 0.007; LR p = 0.63). Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.705, 0.695, 0.721 and 0.716 for M0-M3, so the incremental gain was modest. Nocturnal hypoxaemia indices discriminated severe OSAS far better than CT (ODI AUC 0.888 vs PA diameter 0.699), and once ODI and T90 were available CT added little (ΔAUC < 0.01). CT parameters gave modest reclassification for hypertension, coronary artery disease and the composite cardiovascular outcome; biochemical indices did not.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-derived cardiac parameters, particularly PA diameter, added discrimination over age, sex and BMI for severe OSAS; haematological indices did not. When thoracic CT is already available for another indication, opportunistic measurement of PA dimensions may complement clinical risk stratification. These findings are exploratory and require prospective external validation.

Title: Treatment selection and long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years undergoing valve reintervention for failed surgical aortic bioprostheses: insights from the Netherlands Heart Registration.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe real-world treatment allocation and observed long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years with failed surgical aortic bioprostheses who underwent reintervention through valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo-SAVR) in the Netherlands.
METHODS: Patients aged 50 to < 75 years who underwent ViV-TAVI or redo-SAVR for a failing surgical bioprosthesis between 2015 and 2020 were identified from the Netherlands Heart Registration. Baseline characteristics and Dutch surgical-risk categories were compared by treatment strategy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with ViV-TAVI selection. Kaplan-Meier analysis described survival, and treatment-specific Cox models explored factors associated with all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Of 345 patients, 41% underwent ViV-TAVI and 59% redo-SAVR. Patients selected for ViV-TAVI were older (median 71 vs. 67 years, p < 0.001), had higher surgical risk (EuroSCORE II: 6.2% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.014), and had a greater comorbidity burden than redo-SAVR patients. Despite these baseline risk differences, estimated survival within the ViV-TAVI cohort was 94.2% at 30 days, 89.6% at 2 years, and 74.4% at 4 years; corresponding redo-SAVR estimates were 96.1%, 89.8%, and 88.4%. Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and chronic lung disease were associated both with ViV-TAVI selection (OR: 8.04, 95% CI: 2.16-29.92 and OR: 3.25, 95% CI: 1.53-6.92, respectively) and with all-cause mortality after redo-SAVR (HR: 15.70, 95% CI: 2.49-67.14 and HR: 4.23, 95% CI: 1.53-13.14, respectively).
CONCLUSION: In this Dutch observational registry, ViV-TAVI was predominantly selected for patients with a higher-risk clinical phenotype, while redo-SAVR was more often used in lower-risk reintervention candidates and showed higher observed long-term survival. These data describe contemporary treatment selection and prognosis but do not establish comparative superiority of either strategy.

Title: Cardio-hepatic injury phenotypes and short-term outcomes in acute decompensated heart failure.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal liver biochemistry is common in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), yet most studies evaluate individual markers rather than clinically meaningful patterns of hepatic involvement. We examined whether cardiohepatic injury phenotypes derived from routine liver tests identify distinct short-term prognostic profiles in patients hospitalized with ADHF.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included consecutive adults hospitalized with ADHF between December 2006 and 2017. Using peak in-hospital values of aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin, patients were classified into four phenotypes: no hepatic injury, hepatocellular injury, cholestatic injury, or combined injury. Associations with in-hospital mortality were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Post-discharge outcomes (30-day mortality, readmission, and their composite) were analyzed using Cox and Fine-Gray models.
RESULTS: Among 8332 ADHF admissions, 6792 (81.5%) had sufficient data for phenotype classification: 58.1% had no hepatic injury, 22.1% hepatocellular injury, 13.1% cholestatic injury, and 6.7% combined injury. In-hospital mortality differed markedly across phenotypes (3.5%, 16.3%, 9.0%, and 24.3%, respectively; p < 0.001). After adjustment, all injury phenotypes independently predicted in-hospital death compared with no injury. Among 6128 patients included in adjusted post-discharge analyses, hepatocellular and combined injury were independently associated with higher 30-day mortality and the composite outcome, whereas isolated cholestatic injury was not. Hepatocellular and combined injury independently predicted 30-day readmission.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine liver test patterns identify clinically meaningful cardiohepatic phenotypes in ADHF. While all hepatic injury phenotypes are associated with increased in-hospital mortality, only phenotypes with hepatocellular involvement predict adverse early post-discharge outcomes. Pattern-based interpretation of liver tests may improve early risk stratification in patients hospitalized with ADHF.

Title: Echocardiography-derived Left Atrial Volumetric-Mechanical Coupling Index predicts early new-onset atrial fibrillation after embolic stroke/transient ischemic attack of undetermined source.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
AIM: In patients with embolic stroke or transient ischemic attack of undetermined source (ESUS/TIA), occult atrial fibrillation (AF) is a frequent underlying mechanism with critical therapeutic implications, yet selecting patients who warrant intensified rhythm monitoring remains challenging. The Left Atrioventricular Coupling Index (LACI = LA end-diastolic volume/LV end-diastolic volume) captures atrioventricular uncoupling, whereas the Left Atrial Volumetric-Mechanical Coupling Index (LACI-VM = LAVi/a') integrates atrial size with mechanical performance; both may capture complementary domains of atrial remodelling relevant to subclinical AF. We aimed to investigate the association of LACI-VM and LACI with incident AF in ESUS/TIA.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, 285 consecutive patients with ESUS/TIA of undetermined source underwent transthoracic echocardiography at index hospitalization, including measurement of LACI-VM and LACI. The primary endpoint was new-onset AF during follow-up. Median age was 71 years and 43% were women. Over a median follow-up of 10.9 months, AF occurred in 24 patients (8.4%), with 62% of events occurring within the first year. LACI-VM was higher in patients who developed AF and remained independently associated with incident AF after multivariable adjustment (HR 6.64, CI 1.34-59.88; p = 0.041). LACI showed a non-significant association overall (HR 2.28, CI 0.74-7.01; p = 0.09), with predictive value confined to events within 12 months. A combined assessment of LACI-VM and LV filling pressures further refined risk stratification: patients with preserved LACI-VM (< 2.5) and normal filling pressures (E/e' ≤ 10) had a very low AF incidence (~ 2%), identifying a truly low-risk subgroup; conversely, when both LACI-VM (≥ 2.5) and filling pressures (E/e' > 10) were impaired, AF risk was ~ tenfold higher (~ 20%).
CONCLUSION: In ESUS/TIA, echocardiography-derived LACI-VM independently predicts incident AF and identifies patients at genuinely low risk. As a simple echocardiographic metric, its integration with LV filling pressures may support a more personalized use of rhythm monitoring.

Title: New insights into takotsubo syndrome: results from a multicenter cohort.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Takotsubo syndrome has long been deemed a benign condition following sudden emotional stress. While current mechanisms explaining the acute cardiac dysfunction are not fully understood, current evidence suggests certain takotsubo populations are at higher risk of adverse course. Acute neurologic emergencies commonly precede the takotsubo syndrome and new insights into the role of the brain-heart axis and central autonomic regions driving excess sympathetic activation have come about.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicenter analysis included 595 patients admitted between January 2013 and December 2024 with takotsubo syndrome across 13 German tertiary care centers. The aim of this study was to (I) assess whether acute brain pathology influences severity of cardiac dysfunction differently in comparison to other nonneurologic forms of physical or emotional stress, (II) investigate short-term recovery of cardiac function, and (III) improve identification of vulnerable patients susceptible to critical in-hospital course. Marginal odds ratios were estimated for cardiac complications of takotsubo syndrome across trigger groups using generalized estimating equations. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were fit to analyze the association between prespecified variables for short-term recovery of wall motion and systolic abnormalities as well as critical in-hospital course. Acute neurologic emergencies (47.5%) and common physical triggers (37.9%) were associated with higher risk of cardiac complications in takotsubo syndrome compared to emotional triggers (12.5%). Nonapical forms of takotsubo syndrome showed improved recovery of wall motion abnormalities (OR 2.70, 95% CI 1.34-5.45), while older patients had worse recovery of systolic function to discharge (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93). Conversely, younger male patients in which disease was triggered by neurologic emergencies or physical triggers presented with higher odds of critical in-hospital course.
CONCLUSION: Results of this study challenge the assumption of uniform reversibility of cardiac dysfunction and emphasize the need for early risk stratification and awareness of high-risk features as well as varying clinical presentations.

Title: Association of lipoprotein(a) with ischemia-reperfusion injury in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia adversely affects ischemia-reperfusion injury in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor beyond traditional lipid markers; however, its impact on ischemic myocardial injury remains unclear. We therefore investigated the association of Lp(a) with myocardial and microvascular damage assessed by multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), as well as clinical outcomes in STEMI patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective MARINA-STEMI (NCT04113356) cohort study, 518 STEMI patients (median age 59 years, 19% female) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were included. Lp(a) and lipid parameters, including low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, were measured at hospital admission. CMR was performed at a median of 4 days (interquartile range (IQR) 3-5) and 4 months (IQR 4-5) after PCI. The primary objective was to assess the association of Lp(a) with infarct size (IS) and severe microvascular injury, defined as intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) on baseline CMR. The clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause death, re-infarction, or new congestive heart failure). Median Lp(a) and LDL cholesterol levels were 27 nmol/l (IQR 20-90) and 141 mg/dl (IQR 117-166), respectively. LDL cholesterol correlated with IS at baseline (ρ = 0.114, p = 0.010) and was higher in patients with IMH (145 vs. 140 mg/dl, p = 0.031). In contrast, Lp(a) showed no correlation with IS (ρ = 0.051, p = 0.246) and no association with IMH (25 vs. 28 nmol/l, p = 0.632). Elevated Lp(a) (≥ 105 nmol/l) was not associated with MACE (8.7% vs. 8.8%, p = 0.966).
CONCLUSIONS: While LDL cholesterol was significantly associated with IS and IMH, Lp(a) was not related to ischemia-reperfusion injury patterns or clinical outcomes in patients with STEMI treated with primary PCI.

Title: Autonomic dysfunction in patients with Huntington's disease: Evidence from standardized cardiovascular reflex testing.
Abstract: BackgroundAutonomic dysfunction has been reported in Huntington's disease (HD), but its extent and mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate autonomic function using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CRTs) in a cohort of genetically confirmed HD patients.MethodsIn this single-center, cross-sectional study, we assessed 16 patients with manifest HD using head-up tilt test (HUTT), Valsalva maneuver (VM), deep breathing test, cold face test, and handgrip test, all performed under continuous blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) monitoring. Age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC) were included for comparison.ResultsBased on medical history, 56% of HD patients reported symptoms of orthostatic intolerance while standing. During HUTT, they showed a significant reduction in ΔBP. BP overshoot during VM was also significantly reduced. HR responses and BP changes did not differ significantly between groups across all other maneuvers. When stratified by disease stage, parasympathetic indices were lower in later-stage patients.ConclusionsHD patients exhibited subclinical adrenergic abnormalities on CRTs, with initially preserved cardiovagal control, a pattern compatible with central autonomic involvement and possible progressive impairment of both sympathetic and parasympathetic systems over time.

Title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes of pediatric thrombosis: a prospective single-center study.
Journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
Abstract: The incidence of pediatric thrombosis is increasing due to multiple causes and risk factors, including genetic and acquired factors. This study aimed to evaluate clinical characteristics, risk factors, genetic mutations, and clinical outcomes of children with thrombosis. This prospective observational study included 40 children with thrombotic events. Detailed demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging data, as well as clinical outcomes, were collected. Thrombophilia gene testing included MTHFR C677T and A1298C, Factor XIII V34L, and factor V Leiden mutations. Statistical analyses included univariate comparisons and multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of poor outcomes. Twenty percentage of the study population had genetic thrombophilia, while 80% had acquired risk factors. Acquired risk factors mainly included hematological (22.5%) and cardiac disorders (20%). Venous thrombosis was the most common site (80%), followed by arterial (10%) and cardiac (10%) thrombi. MTHFR C677T and factor XIII V34L mutations were detected with genetic thrombophilia only (P < 0.01), while factor V Leiden was present in both groups (P = 0.11). Overall, 67.5% of patients improved, 20% died, and 12.5% developed permanent disabilities. Multivariate analysis identified thrombocytopenia as an independent predictor of poor outcomes [odds ratio (OR) 18.44; 95% CI: 1.76-192.49; P = 0.02]. Positive blood cultures were associated with a fourfold increased risk of adverse outcomes (OR 4.0; 95% CI: 0.75-21.23; P = 0.1). Pediatric thrombosis was predominantly caused by acquired risk factors, though genetic mutations were significantly evident in this study. Screening and early diagnosis are essential for high-risk profiles. Identifying and managing sepsis and thrombocytopenia are critical to improving outcomes.

Title: Appropriateness of antiphospholipid antibody testing and its impact on diagnostic yield and clinical outcomes: a multicentre cohort study.
Journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
Abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an uncommon but important cause of thrombosis and pregnancy morbidity. Despite guidelines, antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) testing is frequently performed outside specialist settings, potentially reducing diagnostic yield and leading to unnecessary downstream investigations. We evaluated real-world aPL testing practices, diagnostic yield, and clinical outcomes. We conducted a retrospective cohort study across three acute hospitals, two satellite sites and 63 general practices between February and June 2024. Adults undergoing aPL testing (anticardiolipin, β2-glycoprotein-I or lupus anticoagulant) were identified from electronic pathology records. Appropriateness, completeness, results and downstream clinical outcomes were assessed against BSH/EULAR guidance and the documented clinical context. Among 691 patients tested (mean age 51.3 years; 67% women), only 34% requests were considered appropriate, and complete panels were requested in 26%. APS was confirmed in 14 patients (2%). Appropriate requests were associated with higher rates of positive results [risk ratio (RR) 2.39], APS diagnosis (RR 27.0) and management changes (RR 21.4) (all P < 0.001). Haematology, Obstetrics and Rheumatology demonstrated the highest rates of appropriate testing. aPL testing is frequently performed outside recommended clinical indications, resulting in low overall diagnostic yield. Appropriate testing is associated with improved diagnostic accuracy and clinically meaningful changes in patient management, supporting the implementation of targeted diagnostic stewardship interventions.

Title: Amlodipine and Nifedipine Associations with B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Women with Hypertension and Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) are frequently prescribed to manage hypertension in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, whether individual dihydropyridine agents exert uniform class effects on myocardial wall stress remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study analyzed 465 consecutive patients with hypertension and HFpEF (354 women and 111 men) evaluated at Kumamoto Kinoh Hospital between May 2012 and July 2018. Multivariable linear regression models assessed associations between individual dihydropyridine CCBs (amlodipine vs. nifedipine) and plasma log-transformed B-type natriuretic peptide (lnBNP) levels.
RESULTS: In multiple imputation models among women, adjusted differences in lnBNP relative to no-CCB were 0.236 (95% CI, 0.031 to 0.441) for nifedipine and -0.118 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.037) for amlodipine. Direct linear contrasts in women confirmed lower lnBNP levels with amlodipine than with nifedipine (adjusted difference, -0.355; 95% CI, -0.562 to - 0.147). In men, the corresponding amlodipine-versus-nifedipine difference was -0.051 (95% CI, -0.697 to 0.595; P=0.876). The formal sex-by-drug interaction contrast in complete-case analysis yielded an adjusted difference of - 0.424 (95% CI, -1.055 to 0.208; P = 0.188), with male precision constrained by sample size (7 male nifedipine users).
CONCLUSION: In women with hypertension and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, amlodipine use was associated with lower adjusted ln(BNP) levels than nifedipine use. These observational findings challenge the assumption of an interchangeable dihydropyridine class effect on myocardial wall stress, suggesting that individual pharmacological profiles-rather than uniform class-level equivalence-warrant attention in clinical evaluations.

Title: Systemic Vascular Contributions to Inactive Dysthyroid Optic Neuropathy: Beyond Mechanical Compression.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate systemic vascular contributions-spanning microvascular, macrovascular, and molecular levels-to inactive dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON) beyond the traditional model of mechanical compression.
METHODS: This cross-sectional comparative study enrolled 52 patients with thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), categorized into DON (n = 32) and non-DON (n = 20) groups with comparable orbital apex crowding, and 23 healthy controls. Participants underwent optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) to assess superficial macular vessel density (mVD). Systemic macrovascular status was evaluated via internal carotid artery calcification (ICAC) on computed tomography and pulse pressure (PP). Molecular assessments included blood lipids and endothelial injury markers, specifically nitric oxide (NO).
RESULTS: Patients with inactive DON exhibited significant microvascular rarefaction, with reduced mVD compared to both controls and non-DON patients (P < 0.002). DON was also associated with a higher prevalence of macrovascular pathology, including ICAC (48.3% vs. 21.7%; P = 0.017) and elevated PP (P = 0.001). At the molecular level, DON was linked to dyslipidemia (elevated triglycerides, P = 0.001; reduced high-density lipoprotein, P = 0.014) and endothelial dysfunction (lower NO; P = 0.033). Reduced mVD correlated significantly with both ICAC and PP (P < 0.033), linking systemic and ocular vascular injury.
CONCLUSIONS: Inactive DON was associated with abnormalities across retinal microvascular, systemic macrovascular, and circulating biomarker domains. These findings support further investigation of a model in which systemic vascular vulnerability may interact with local orbital compression.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: Assessment of systemic vascular risk may complement conventional orbital evaluation in patients with DON. Prospective studies are required to determine whether optimization of thyroid and vascular status can improve prevention or treatment.

Title: Prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in rural India: a cross-sectional study in the APCAPS cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia poses a growing public health challenge in India. Despite this, epidemiological data on the condition remain largely restricted to adults >60 years of age, despite the convergence of urbanisation-driven cardiometabolic risks and socioeconomic disadvantage in rural India potentially accelerating dementia onset. We investigated the prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in a transitional rural Indian cohort of adults aged ≥45 years.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we utilised data from the Andhra Pradesh Children and Parents Study cohort from 29 villages near Hyderabad, South India (2021-2023). We collected sociodemographic, occupational, and household asset data through face-to-face, questionnaire-based interviews. Cardiometabolic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and stroke) were assessed using validated methods. Dementia screening was performed using the Brief Community Screening Instrument for Dementia. We calculated prevalence estimates for dementia and used multivariable logistic regression to identify independent associations of probable dementia with sociodemographic, socioeconomic (education, occupation, household assets), and cardiometabolic factors (diabetes, hypertension, cardiac disease, and stroke).
RESULTS: The final sample included 2,163 adults aged ≥45 years. The prevalence of probable dementia (a positive screen on the BCSI-D) was 3.4% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.6-4.6) in the 45-59 age group and 7.4% (95% CI = 6.0-9.4) in the ≥60 age group. In the multivariable model, the odds of probable dementia were 2.2 times higher among unemployed or retired participants than among those working in agriculture or animal rearing (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 2.23; 95% CI = 1.26-3.95). The odds of probable dementia among literate participants were 0.5 times those among illiterate participants (aOR = 0.54; 95% CI = 0.31-0.89). The odds of probable dementia were 3.8 times higher among participants with a history of stroke than among those without (aOR = 3.77; 95% CI = 1.67-7.94).
CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that the burden of probable dementia in rural India extends into middle age, and that the condition itself is independently associated with a history of stroke and socioeconomic disadvantages. This suggests a need to extend cognitive and vascular risk assessment to adults aged ≥45 years in rural India. However, as all findings reflect positive screening results rather than confirmed diagnoses, longitudinal studies with diagnostic confirmation are needed before population-level screening recommendations can be made.

Title: Associations of cumulative exposure and dynamic trajectories of the combined atherogenic-frailty index with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) poses a growing global health burden, yet effective tools for early risk stratification remain limited. The combined impact of atherogenic dyslipidaemia and physiological frailty, captured by the atherogenic index of plasma-frailty index (AIP-FI), on CMM development is poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of cumulative exposure and longitudinal trajectories of AIP-FI with incident CMM.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 4,157 participants aged ≥45 years without baseline CMM from CHARLS. The AIP-FI was constructed as the product of AIP and a 37-deficit frailty index. Cumulative AIP-FI was calculated from repeated measurements. Longitudinal trajectories were identified using K-means clustering. Associations with incident CMM were evaluated by multivariable Cox models, RCS, K-M curves, ROC/NRI/IDI, mediation, interaction, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Over a mean 8.5-year follow-up, 612 incident CMM cases occurred. Both higher baseline and cumulative AIP-FI were significantly associated with increased CMM risk, with cumulative exposure showing a stronger effect (fully-adjusted HR per SD increment: 1.46; 95% CI = 1.38-1.54). Participants in the highest quartile of cumulative AIP-FI had a near 4-fold higher CMM risk compared to the lowest (HR = 3.95; 95% CI = 2.95-5.29). Clustering analyses revealed that groups with high-stable AIP-FI exhibited the highest CMM risks. Cumulative AIP-FI demonstrated superior predictive performance for CMM (AUC = 71.17%) and significantly improved risk reclassification over traditional markers (NRI = 0.157). Mediation analyses suggested bidirectional synergistic effects between AIP and FI.
CONCLUSIONS: In this national cohort, both the cumulative burden and adverse longitudinal trajectories of AIP-FI were independently associated with an elevated risk of CMM. Dynamic monitoring of this composite biomarker could facilitate the early identification of high-risk individuals, thereby informing targeted prevention strategies for middle-aged and older adults in China.

Title: Large-scale plasma proteomic profiling enhances prediction of heart failure among hypertensive individuals: prospective insights from the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for heart failure (HF), but current clinical models have limited ability to identify high-risk individuals before overt disease. Plasma proteomics may capture early molecular changes and improve risk prediction.
METHODS: We analysed 16,128 hypertensive UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants without baseline HF. Plasma levels of 2,911 proteins were measured using the Olink Explore platform. Participants were randomly split 1:1 into training and validation sets. HF-associated proteins were identified using Cox models in the training set, followed by LASSO regression to construct a protein risk score (PRS). Model performance was assessed in the validation set using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent ROC analysis, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI), calibration, and bootstrap validation. A parsimonious panel was derived using LightGBM and sequential forward feature selection.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.1 years, 1,074 participants developed HF. In the training set, 534 proteins were associated with HF after adjustment for demographic and clinical risk factors and were enriched in cytokine signalling, extracellular matrix organisation, and immune-cell migration pathways.
