RESULTS: Antithrombotic use increased from 74.6% to 79.4% (odds ratio [OR]/year 1.05, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.09), but plateaued after 2019, leaving 20.6% untreated in 2023. Among 4,441 patients with known atrial fibrillation (AF), oral anticoagulant use rose from 65.3% to 73.3% (OR/year 1.08; P=0.005), and 26.7% remained untreated. LDL-C <70 mg/dL improved from 32.6% to 41.9% (OR/year 1.08; P<0.001), whereas HbA1c, smoking, and weight indicators showed limited overall progress. Heterogeneity emerged: non-current smoking improved in men but not women (already near ceiling, approximately 95%); LDL-C control did not improve in adults aged 19-49 years; and BMI ≥25 kg/m² rose from 36.2% to 56.2% in this age group. Upper-bound projections estimated approximately 183, 126, and 201 potentially preventable recurrent strokes per year within the registry (not national estimates) from antithrombotic non-use, anticoagulant non-use in AF, and LDL-C gaps in large-artery atherosclerosis, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Recurrent-stroke admission revealed persistent, unevenly distributed prevention gaps. Medication reconciliation, AF detection and anticoagulation, lipid intensification, and tailored behavioral pathways should be prioritized.

Title: Precision Oxygen Modulation in the Reperfusion Era: Conditioning and Therapeutic Strategies in Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and advanced perfusion imaging have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment, yet tissue hypoxia may persist because of delayed presentation, incomplete reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow, and secondary injury. Oxygen is an essential substrate for cerebral metabolism and a modifiable therapeutic exposure; however, clinical studies of oxygen-based interventions have yielded inconsistent results because of heterogeneity in timing, dose, delivery, and patient selection. Here we propose precision oxygen modulation (POM) as a stage-, phenotype-, and tissue-informed framework for the reperfusion era-treating oxygen exposure as a dose-titrated therapy that must be matched to the right patient, time window, physiological target, and safety boundary. POM integrates oxygen conditioning strategies that may prime neurovascular resilience before or around ischemia, time-limited therapeutic oxygen strategies deployed around reperfusion to support tissue at risk, and recovery-stage strategies paired with rehabilitation. We synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence linking oxygen tension to excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and repair, while emphasizing the context-dependent risks of hyperoxia. We outline an operational decision framework and translational roadmap based on phenotype- and imaging-guided selection, biomarker validation, protocolized dosing, predefined safety boundaries, and phenotype-enriched randomized trials. POM is presented as a testable translational framework for organizing heterogeneous evidence and guiding the prospective validation of stage-specific oxygen modulation in modern stroke care.

Title: Pre-stroke functional status and prognosis following mechanical thrombectomy: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: IntroductionMechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an endovascular approach applicable to large- and medium-vessel occlusion in the context of ischemic stroke (IS), with recanalization rates superior to 80% and favorable clinical outcomes. However, its benefits in patients with pre-existing functional disability remain unclear because these individuals are typically excluded from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). This systematic review and meta-analysis therefore aimed to assess how pre-stroke functional status influences key prognostic outcomes after MT.MethodologyPubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases were searched for English studies published from inception to September 2025. Observational cohorts and RCTs were included if they evaluated patients with IS treated with MT, comparing outcomes (functional outcomes, recanalization, complications, and mortality) between patients with and without pre-stroke disability (PD and NPD, respectively). Disability was mainly defined as a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≥2 or ≥3, and analyses were stratified accordingly. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was explored with Baujat plots and leave-one-out analyses.ResultsThis review included 12 studies comprising 26,444 patients, of whom 2,837 had PD and 23,607 had NPD. Most studies defined PD as a pre-stroke mRS ≥3. Patients with PD had higher rates of diabetes (28.9% vs 18.5%), hypertension (78.9% vs 66.0%), and atrial fibrillation (46.7% vs 29.4%). In contrast, NIHSS, ASPECTS, occlusion site, and time to treatment were similar between groups. Intravenous thrombolysis was less frequently administered in the PD group (33.8% vs 46.9%). No significant difference was observed in favorable functional outcomes between patients with PD and NPD (OR = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.39-1.16). Otherwise, 90-day mortality was higher in PD patients (OR = 2.75; 95% CI: 2.38-3.18). Finally, the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and the rate of successful recanalization did not differ significantly between groups (OR = 1.19; 95% CI: 0.98-1.43, and OR = 0.89; 95% CI: 0.71-1.11, respectively).ConclusionPre-stroke disability was not significantly associated with functional outcomes or reduced recanalization rates after mechanical thrombectomy, although the substantial heterogeneity in functional outcomes warrants cautious interpretation. Pre-stroke disability was associated with higher 90-day mortality, which may be related to a greater baseline comorbidity burden and clinical vulnerability. These results support considering thrombectomy in selected patients with prior disability, while highlighting the need for individualized assessment. High-quality prospective studies are still required to confirm these findings.

Title: Associations of Traditional Chinese Medicine Therapy with Risks of Lower-Limb Amputation, Cardiovascular Mortality and All-Cause Mortality in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease-A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This is a retrospective cohort study assessing the association between the use of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and the risk of lower-limb amputation, cardiovascular (CV) mortality, and all-cause mortality among people with peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD).
METHODS: The study utilized data from the National Health Insurance Research Database of the Ministry of Health and Welfare of Taiwan. A 1:1 propensity score matching ratio based on gender, age (5-year interval), comorbidities, medications, and year of index date.The risk of outcomes among PAOD patients with and without TCM use was estimated by a Cox proportional hazards model.
RESULTS: The study findings showed that TCM treatment was associated with a significant decreased risk of lower-limb loss (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.50-0.61), CV death (aHR = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.31-0.34), and all-cause mortality (aHR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.34-0.35) among people with PAOD, especially for CV death and all-cause death.
CONCLUSION: We found that patients with PAOD treated with TCM have a decreased risk of endpoints, especially for CV death and all-cause death.

Title: Asymptomatic Portomesenteric Venous Thrombosis After Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Incidence, Natural History, and Implications for Management.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery is most often reported in symptomatic patients, leaving its frequency and natural history across the asymptomatic spectrum poorly defined. When encountered incidentally, it frequently prompts anticoagulation, hypercoagulability evaluation, or delays in oncologic treatment, despite limited evidence that intervention alters its course. Using a cohort with routine postoperative imaging, we characterized the incidence, anatomic distribution, risk factors, and clinical course of asymptomatic PMVT.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 799 consecutive patients who underwent CRC surgery between April 2019 and June 2025. All patients underwent standardized abdominal computed tomography (CT) on postoperative day (POD) 6 as part of our institutional clinical pathway for immediate postoperative follow-up. PMVT was defined radiologically, and thrombus location was classified as peripheral intrahepatic branches or main portal/superior mesenteric vein. Management followed a risk-stratified pathway of therapeutic anticoagulation or active surveillance, with radiologic resolution assessed on follow-up CT. Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was considered exploratory.
RESULTS: Asymptomatic PMVT was identified in 33 patients (4.1%), none symptomatic at detection. Thrombi were predominantly confined to the distal intrahepatic branches. In exploratory multivariable analysis, age ≤ 60 years (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.19-5.03, p = 0.015) and POD 5 WBC > 10 × 109/L (OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.16-4.93, p = 0.018) were independently associated with PMVT. Twenty-one patients received anticoagulation and 12 were managed with surveillance alone. Complete radiologic resolution occurred in all 33 patients within one year, including every patient managed without anticoagulation. Furthermore, there were no cases of thrombus extension, portal hypertension, or bowel ischemia.
CONCLUSION: When postoperative imaging is routinely performed, asymptomatic PMVT after CRC surgery is detected in approximately 4% of patients. It is typically confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and follows a uniformly benign self-limiting course, even in patients managed without anticoagulation. These findings argue against reflexive anticoagulation and extensive workup for short-segment, non-occlusive PMVT confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and support an individualized, predominantly conservative approach. We do not advocate routine postoperative CT; rather, surgeons who encounter incidental PMVT can be reassured regarding its favorable prognosis.

Title: Complex relationship between iron status and outcomes of STEMI: hypothesis-generating study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Iron deficiency (ID) is common amongst patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Its impact on outcomes remains contested. Previous studies reported favourable or adverse impacts depending on outcome measures, sampling timepoints, ID definition and follow-up duration. This study systematically characterises the prognostic impact of iron status on short-term, mid-term and long-term outcomes, and evaluates the effect of sampling timepoint and ID definition on these prognostic relationships.
METHODS & RESULTS: We performed an observational cohort study in patients with acute STEMI (n = 167) and no prior heart failure (HF). Iron markers were sampled at presentation, and successive timepoints thereafter. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance was performed at 2 days and 6 months. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), consisting of new-onset HF, recurrent MI or cardiac death were recorded over 4.5 years. Mechanisms were evaluated in a preclinical model of MI.ID was common at presentation, affecting between 44.9% and 67%, depending on ID definition. Tsat <20%, serum iron<13μM, or European Society of Cardiology's definition, but not ferritin<100μg/L, independently predicted lower risk of MACE. Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Integrating Proteomics and Mendelian Randomization to Evaluate HGF as a Potential Mediator of Stroke Risk Factors.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Stroke prediction remains suboptimal. We aimed to identify plasma proteins associated with stroke risk and evaluate their potential as clinical biomarkers and causal mediators.
EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We used a multitiered proteomic approach in the UK Biobank (UKB). In a matched nested case-control study (672 cases, 2,688 controls), 2,920 proteins were analyzed. Findings were internally validated in the UKB-PPP cohort and cross-validated using genetic instruments from seven large-scale protein GWAS meta-analyses. Mendelian randomization (MR) and mediation analyses were employed to assess causality.
RESULTS: We identified 122 proteins significantly associated with stroke risk. A 122-protein panel improved the C-index from 0.610 to 0.693. MR analysis provided genetic evidence supporting an association between higher genetically predicted Hepatocyte Growth Factor (HGF) levels and stroke risk (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.09-1.28). Mediation analysis indicated that HGF mediated 39.15% of the effect of weight and 37.28% of waist circumference on stroke risk.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Our findings support HGF as a potential mediator linking metabolic risk factors to stroke. The identified protein panel offers a robust tool for stroke risk stratification and highlights HGF as a biologically plausible candidate for therapeutic intervention.

Title: Additive Value of Acetylcholine Testing in ANOCA: A US-Based Multicenter FlowLab Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) is an underrecognized cause of angina with non-universal diagnostic techniques and patient management strategies. Among ANOCA testing, vasospasm provocation is not always performed mainly due to differences in institutional availability.
AIMS: Using the FlowLab Study, we quantified vasospasm prevalence among patients with ANOCA at US centers and compared physician decision-making, endotype distribution, and management between sites that did and did not include vasospasm testing in their workup.
METHODS: The FlowLab Study was a prospective, multicenter, US-based study of patients who were referred for coronary angiography and underwent ANOCA testing using the bolus thermodilution method. Presumed diagnosis before cardiac catheterization and final diagnosis after ANOCA testing were compared between participating sites with or without acetylcholine testing availability.
RESULTS: A total of 253 procedures at 14 US sites were included in this study. There were 155 procedures among sites performing spasm provocation testing and 98 procedures among sites not performing spasm provocation testing. Prior to cardiac catheterization, sites with spasm provocation testing were less likely to suspect epicardial coronary artery disease as the cause of angina compared to sites without (27% vs. 59.2%, p < 0.0001). A diagnosis of CMD was made more frequently at sites performing spasm testing compared to sites not performing spasm testing (68% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.0001). Similarly, among 125 patients who underwent spasm provocation testing, diagnostic yield increased from 34.4% with bolus thermodilution alone to 84.8% after the addition of spasm provocation testing (p < 0.001). In these patients, intensification involving calcium channel blockers was more frequent with epicardial (67%) and microvascular spasm (41%) than without spasm (24%, p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary US practice, adding spasm provocation testing to bolus thermodilution more than doubled diagnostic yield and was followed by medication changes directed toward the diagnosed endotype. Differences between sites with and without spasm testing also reflected variation in procedural practice.

Title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
Abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

Title: Continuous Pulse Oximetry Analysis to Predict Outcomes in Young Infants With Bronchiolitis Presenting to the Emergency Department.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictive analytics using continuously measured vital signs from bedside monitors has improved outcomes in critically ill children. We investigated whether continuous pulse oximetry data collected during emergency department (ED) evaluation can identify infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis at low risk of respiratory deterioration.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis who presented to a tertiary-care pediatric ED from November 2021 to November 2025. Infants were identified using the ICD-10 code with manual eligibility confirmation. Heart rate and oxygen saturation features were generated from continuous pulse oximetry during the first 2 hours of ED evaluation. The primary outcome was respiratory deterioration within 24 hours of ED arrival, defined as initiation of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous/bilevel positive airway pressure, or invasive mechanical ventilation. Data were split into derivation and validation cohorts (70/30, stratified by outcome). An L2-regularized logistic regression model estimated the probability of respiratory deterioration, with a classification threshold selected to prioritize sensitivity.
RESULTS: Of 290 infants meeting clinical eligibility, 117 had sufficient continuous pulse oximetry data; 57 (49%) had respiratory deterioration. The primary model included 3 features: the median and interquartile range (IQR) of heart rate, and oxygen saturation IQR. In the validation cohort, the model showed moderate sensitivity (0.78, 95% CI: 0.58-0.95) and fair discrimination (AUROC=0.78, 95% CI: 0.62-0.93).
CONCLUSION: We derived and validated a model using data from continuous pulse oximetry to identify low-risk infants with bronchiolitis. With further refinement and integration into monitor design systems, this approach may enhance clinical utility of continuous pulse oximetry.

Title: Development and Validation of a Multimodal Artificial Neural Network Model for the Diagnosis of Bladder Outlet Obstruction and Detrusor Underactivity in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: Protocol for a Diagnostic Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bladder outlet obstruction (BOO) and detrusor underactivity (DU) can produce overlapping clinical and uroflowmetric presentations in men with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). Pressure-flow studies (PFS) provide reference diagnoses, but their invasiveness and cost constrain access. Building on a single-center model that used only structured clinical, uroflowmetric, and ultrasonographic variables, this protocol adds uroflowmetry waveforms and cystoscopic images within multimodal artificial neural networks (ANNs). Whether these inputs improve diagnostic estimation beyond structured-data-only models requires evaluation in men undergoing clinically indicated cystoscopy, a selected population distinct from the broader LUTS population for whom noninvasive screening is ultimately intended.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate a multimodal ANN that estimates separate, non-mutually exclusive probabilities of BOO and DU; to compare its discrimination with structured-data-only and modality-ablation models; and to evaluate the version-locked model prospectively against PFS-based reference diagnoses.
METHODS: This two-phase study was approved by the Persahabatan General Hospital Ethics Committee (0222/KEPK-RSUPP/07/2026). Models are developed retrospectively using records of adult men with LUTS evaluated at Persahabatan General Hospital, Indonesia, in 2024-2025, and evaluated prospectively in a separate cohort enrolled from 2026 at the development site and three additional tertiary hospitals. Predictors include the International Prostate Symptom Score, comorbidities, prostate volume, free-uroflowmetry curves, and cystoscopic images. Two models are developed, one for each diagnostic target, each using parallel neural encoders with intermediate feature fusion. Reference diagnoses are assigned from PFS recordings using prespecified bladder outlet obstruction index and bladder contractility index criteria, with blinded expert review and adjudication. Internal validation uses patient-level nested stratified five-fold cross-validation, with preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning confined to training partitions. Comparators include penalized logistic regression and modality-ablation models. After internal validation, the model architecture, hyperparameters, and decision thresholds will be locked before any prospective enrollment or exposure to prospective outcome data; the lock date and version will be reported, and no prospective data, including interim performance, will be used to modify the models, which will be applied to new participants without retraining. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve net benefit will be reported separately for each diagnostic target and study phase.
RESULTS: Retrospective cohort assembly and data curation were completed in August 2026, 250 participants enrolled. Development and internal validation of the multimodal models with cystoscopy and uroflowmetry waveform are scheduled for completion in December 2026, after which the models and decision thresholds will be locked. Final external validation analyses are planned for mid-2027. No other protocol deviations have occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: The proposed multimodal ANN may support pre-PFS differentiation of BOO and DU in selected men with LUTS and facilitate mechanism-based clinical decision-making.

Title: Calibrating Machine Learning Approaches for Probability Estimation Without Calibration Data.
Abstract: Statistical prediction models for binary outcomes are becoming increasingly popular. One significant challenge is calibrating these models to suit the characteristics of a target population that is structurally different from the original population. Calibration is especially challenging when there is no training data available from the target population. To address this problem, we propose a novel calibration method, SimCal, which uses synthetic data generated from the model development data in conjunction with marginal statistics from the calibration cohort. We show that expert judgment modeling (EJM) may be used for calibration if cross-sectional data from the target population are available comprising expert judgments about the potential outcome and the covariates. We describe three alternative calibration approaches when calibration data are lacking: similarity-binning averaging (SBA), adaptive calibration of predictions (ACP), and Elkan calibration. In a simulation study, we compare SBA, ACP, Elkan calibration, and SimCal. R code for applying these methods is provided from the re-analysis of data on coronary artery disease. We illustrate all 5 calibration approaches with a real data set for predicting functional outcome after stroke and all approaches but EJM in the re-analysis of the Cleveland Clinic data. None of the approaches performed convincingly well in all situations. SimCal performed well when model parameters were correctly specified. EJM failed on the stroke data. Further research is urgently required for calibration in the absence of calibration data.

Title: Associations of Social Determinants of Health and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality: UK Biobank Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIM: Social determinants of health (SDHs) play an important role in addressing inequitable and avoidable disparities in health status within countries but lack systematic assessment in broad populations. The aim of this study was to determine the association of SDHs, individually, in combination and cumulatively, with all-cause mortality risk, cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, and cancer mortality.
METHODS: Data were obtained from 190,239 adults in the UK Biobank. Exposure variables were SDHs assessed by self-reported sociodemographic characteristics using standardized questionnaires. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate the associations of combined SDHs and cumulative number of SDHs with all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality.
RESULTS: Over a median 12-year follow-up, 9,871 deaths occurred, including 1,673 from CVD and 5,199 from cancer. Compared to favorable SDHs, medium SDHs (HR 1.143; 95% CI 1.090-1.198) and unfavorable SDHs (HR 1.642; 95% CI 1.559-1.729) were associated with higher all-cause mortality risks. Medium and unfavorable SDHs were associated with increased risks of CVD mortality (by 16.3% and 81.5%) and cancer mortality (by 7.7% and 26.1%). Having ≥8 cumulative adverse SDHs significantly heightened all-cause mortality risk. In exploratory analyses, baseline hypertension and diabetes statistically accounted for a portion of the associations between combined SDHs and mortality outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Unfavorable SDHs are substantially associated with increased risks of all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality. Exploratory findings suggest that baseline hypertension and diabetes substantially explain these associations, highlighting existing disease burden as a key driver of health inequalities.

Title: Technical Complications and Salvage of Hepatic Artery Infusion Pumps: An Institutional Experience of 2935 Consecutive Cases.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe the technical complications of hepatic artery infusion pump (HAIP) placement and characterize salvage rates.
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: HAIP chemotherapy is an effective tool used in the treatment of hepatic malignancies and has become increasingly adopted at select centers. Much of the safety data is reported from small, newer programs or older, large series.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent HAIP placement at our institution between 2000 and 2022 was conducted. Pump salvage was defined as the ability to receive HAIP chemotherapy after a pump-associated complication. Pump failure was defined as an HAIP-related complication permanently stopping ongoing HAIP chemotherapy.
RESULTS: Over the study period, 2935 patients had an HAIP placed for colorectal liver metastases (n=2582, 88%), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (n=294, 10%) or another malignancy (n=59, 2%). Of all patients, 759 (26%) had an HAIP-related complication, with 404/759 (53%) having their pump salvaged. The most common complications were abnormal perfusion (n=360 [12%], 285/360 [79%] salvaged), arterial pseudoaneurysm and/or hemorrhage (n=117 [4%], 7/117 [6%] salvaged), and pump-pocket infection (n=115 [4%], 60/115 [52%] salvaged). The complications with the highest salvage rates were pump-pocket seroma (n=15/16, 94%), pump-flipping (n=41/44, 93%), and pump-pocket hematoma (n=45/49, 92%). Unsalvaged complications were catheter dislodgement from vessel (n=0/47, 0%), catheter erosion into bowel (n=0/25, 0%), and arterial thrombosis (n=0/19, 0%). The cumulative incidence of pump failure at 1 year in patients receiving adjuvant therapy was 6.6%, and 4.5% among those receiving palliative therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: HAIP-related complications occur in about one quarter of patients, predominantly perfusion and pump-pocket complications. These are salvageable in the majority of cases with multidisciplinary interventions.

Title: The higher adherence to the DASH diet the lower incidence and mortality from cardiovascular disease and all causes: ELSA-Brasil study.
Journal: International journal of food sciences and nutrition
Abstract: To investigate the association between adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and all-cause mortality. The study included 14,621 participants from the ELSA-Brasil cohort. DASH adherence was assessed at baseline using a continuous score. Fine-Gray competing risk models were for MACE and CVD mortality, and Cox models for all-cause mortality. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors, behaviours, comorbidities, weight change, and total energy intake. Mean age was 52 years (SD 9), and mean DASH score was 23.9 (SD 4.4). Each one-point increase in the DASH score was associated with lowerrisk of MACE (sHR 0.96; 95% CI 0.92-0.99), CVD mortality (sHR 0.95; 95% CI 0.92-1.00), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Greater DASH adherence was associated with lower incidence of MACE and reduced CVD and all-cause mortality in Brazilian adults.

Title: A Pilot Randomized Study of NAT2 and YEATS4 Pharmacogenetic Return of Results in Adults with Hypertension and African Ancestry: The GUARDD-US PGx Study.
Abstract: Almost half of individuals with hypertension fail to achieve recommended blood pressure (BP) goals. Pharmacogenetic gene-drug interactions may alter the efficacy of antihypertensive agents. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled sub-study of participants (N = 1874) with hypertension and self-reported African ancestry to determine whether pharmacogenetic return of results (RoR) would improve systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 3 months. Participants were randomized to immediate pharmacogenetic RoR (intervention) or delayed RoR at trial completion (control). Clinical decision support conveyed recommendations for YEATS4-guided thiazide diuretic selection and NAT2-guided hydralazine dosing. Prespecified subgroup analyses included those with uncontrolled BP (baseline SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90 mm Hg) and actionable genotypes. Immediate RoR did not improve SBP at 3 months in a broad population of hypertensive adults with controlled and uncontrolled SBP (covariate-adjusted change in SBP between groups: -0.3 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -1.8, 1.2). In participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype (N = 867) predicting reduced thiazide efficacy, immediate RoR led to greater SBP reduction at 3 months (-2.46 mm Hg, 95% CI: -4.57 to -0.36). In participants with uncontrolled hypertension at baseline (N = 659), immediate RoR led to a greater reduction in SBP (-2.9 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -5.6, -0.3). Although no SBP reduction was observed in the whole cohort, participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype or uncontrolled BP who received immediate RoR had a significantly greater SBP improvement than those with delayed RoR. Future studies of antihypertensive pharmacogenetics should recruit individuals with uncontrolled BP and actionable genotypes.

Title: Preoperative natremia and AKI after cardiac surgery: an international multicenter prospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND GOAL OF STUDY: Whether preoperative natremia levels may play a role in the development of acute kidney injury (AKI) after cardiac surgery is uncertain. We conducted a cohort study to evaluate the influence of preoperative natremia on AKI in high-risk patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study involved 14 British and Spanish hospitals, each under local ethics committee approval. The study population comprised all consecutive patients aged 18 years or older, with a Cleveland Clinic score ≥ 4, undergoing cardiac surgery from July to December 2017. The resultant 241 consecutive patients were classified according to tertiles of preoperative natremia levels (< 139, > 139-141, and > 141 mmol/L).
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The AKIN criteria were used to define AKI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate the adjusted association between preoperative natremia and AKI. A potential link was observed between sodium levels ≤ 139 mmol/L and an increased risk of moderate-to-severe AKI relative to levels above 141 mmol/L (OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.02-3.95, p = 0.03), after multivariable adjustment for age and preoperative serum creatinine. No significant associations were observed between sodium levels and RRT or in-hospital mortality. Conclusions The results from this cohort of high-risk cardiac surgery patients lend tentative support to the hypothesis that preoperative natremia levels ≤ 139 mmol/L might be linked to a higher risk of moderate-to-severe AKI compared with levels above 141 mmol/L. These findings warrant further evaluation in a larger cohort.

Title: Effectiveness of a voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool in enhancing cardiovascular knowledge and self-management in aged patients following percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a voice-guided, tap-and-talk educational tool and assess its effectiveness in improving disease-related knowledge and self-management behaviors among older adults following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: A voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool was designed to address the specific needs of older adults post-PCI. A cluster randomized controlled trial was conducted in cardiovascular wards. The control group received conventional health education using printed manuals, whereas the intervention group received education via the tap-and-talk interactive tool. Outcomes included the level of knowledge regarding coronary heart disease and engagement in self-management behaviors. Chi-squared test and independent-sample t-test, chi-square test and paired t-test, and univariate repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) were conducted accordingly.
RESULTS: A total of 96 patients completed the study, including 49 in the experimental group and 47 in the control group.No statistically significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the groups (p > 0.05). A significant group × time interaction effect was detected for coronary heart disease (CHD)-related knowledge (F = 9.026, P < 0.001). At 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher self-management behavior scores than the control group (F = 11.607, P < 0.001). Additionally, CHD-related knowledge scores showed a mild downward trend over time in both groups (F = 124.067, P < 0.001). Consistent with the interaction effect mentioned above, the intervention group achieved significantly higher CHD-related knowledge scores than the control group at all three follow-up time points (1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention) (F = 195.188, P < 0.001). Scores in the intervention group remained consistently higher across all domains. The tool received high acceptance ratings from participants (mean score 96.04 ± 2.61).
CONCLUSION: The tap-and-talk voice-guided educational tool was effective in enhancing knowledge and promoting self-management behaviors among older adults following PCI. The tool demonstrated a high level of user acceptability within the target population.

Title: Gut Regulated Associations of Neuronal Signalling in High Blood Pressure (GRAINS-BP): a double-blinded randomised crossover placebo-controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects 1 in 3 Australian adults and is a major contributor to stroke and myocardial infarction. Despite the availability of various medications, over 50% of patients struggle to control their blood pressure (BP) due to nonadherence, difficulty finding the right treatment, or avoidance of medication. Diet plays a key role in cardiovascular health, with high-fiber intake shown to lower BP through the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites formed during fiber fermentation. A previous clinical trial found that incorporating a specific type of resistant starch - high amylose maize starch enriched with acetate and butyrate (HAMSA/B) - significantly reduced blood pressure in hypertensive patients. While the exact mechanism remains unclear, SCFAs may influence BP via the gut-brain axis by reducing muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), which has vasoconstrictor function and is elevated in hypertensive individuals.
METHODS: The GRAINS-BP clinical trial will recruit 29 adults with untreated hypertension (≥ 140/90 mmHg) for a double-blind, cross-over study using HAMSA/B administered as a shake delivered twice daily. The assessment period will span 48 days and include four visits at the Alfred Hospital, Melbourne, Australia. At visit 1, baseline measurement will be taken, including muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) and electrocardiogram (ECG). Participants will be randomised to the order in which they receive the placebo and HAMSA/B shake. Each intervention period will last 14 days, separated by a 20-day washout before participants cross over to the alternate treatment. At each visit, faecal, urine, and blood samples will be collected to investigate microbiome, cardiometabolic, renal, and immune profiles, respectively. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses will be conducted to examine treatment effects and to identify correlations among microbiome, cardiometabolic, renal, and immune outcomes.
DISCUSSION: This project's primary outcome is change in autonomic nervous system activity. Secondary outcomes include 24-h BP, gut microbiome composition, SCFA levels, immune cell profiles gastrointestinal transit time, quality of life, anxiety and depression symptoms, cognitive function, gut barrier integrity, and circulating micro- and nanoplastics. Findings from this study will reveal whether SCFAs reduce blood pressure by their influence on the autonomic nervous system.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12625000557437).

Title: Distinct hemodynamic implications of junctional rhythm versus sinus rhythm on cardiac reverse remodeling after the Maze procedure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical success after the Maze procedure is conventionally defined as "freedom from atrial fibrillation (AF)," often grouping junctional rhythm (JR) with normal sinus rhythm (NSR). However, the specific hemodynamic impact of JR remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether JR truly represents a successful outcome compared to NSR and AF.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing the Maze procedure (2012-2024). After designating the first postoperative month as a blanking period for rhythm instability, we included only patients maintaining a consistent rhythm without crossover from 1 to 12 months postoperatively: AF (n = 71), NSR (n = 213), and JR (n = 35). Outcomes included cardiac reverse remodeling-assessed by left atrial contractile strain (LASct) and chamber dimensions-and permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation.
RESULTS: In the IPTW-adjusted cohort, the NSR group achieved significant cardiac reverse remodeling, characterized by improved LVEF (58.5%), reduced LA volume index (75.1 mL/m²), and notable recovery of LASct. In stark contrast, the JR group failed to show any reverse remodeling or mechanical recovery, exhibiting hemodynamic stagnation indistinguishable from the AF group. Consequently, no significant difference in cardiac function was observed between the JR and AF groups. Furthermore, the JR group faced a drastically elevated risk of PPM implantation compared to both the NSR and AF groups (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: JR is not a benign alternative to sinus rhythm; it mimics AF in preventing cardiac reverse remodeling and carries a high risk of pacemaker dependency. Therefore, JR should be clinically differentiated from NSR and recognized as a suboptimal hemodynamic outcome similar to AF.

Title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025. Inclusion required significant right atrial remodelling, defined as a right atrial area > 25 cm2. Patients with at least moderate functional tricuspid regurgitation comprised the AFTR cohort, while patients with mild/trivial/no tricuspid regurgitation served as controls. Patients with primary valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, device-related valve disease, RV dilatation, or more than mild RV systolic dysfunction were excluded. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 152 patients were included, comprising 120 patients with AFTR and 32 controls. Compared with controls, patients with AFTR demonstrated larger atrial dimensions, higher right-sided hemodynamic-burden, impaired RV longitudinal strain, and reduced reservoir RA strain. During a median follow-up of 6.3 years, 53 deaths (45%) occurred among patients with AFTR. In univariable Cox analysis, age (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; p = 0.016), TR Vmax (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.35; p = 0.020), and lower reservoir RA strain (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p = 0.003) were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, reservoir RA strain remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: AFTR is characterized by marked biatrial remodelling and impaired right atrial function. Reduced RA reservoir strain was independently associated with mortality, supporting a potential role for RA deformation imaging in risk stratification in AFTR.

Title: Temporal synchrony promotes motor recovery and ipsilesional cortical reorganization in BCI-based stroke rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The therapeutic mechanisms of brain-computer interface (BCI) rehabilitation remain partially understood. Specifically, it is unclear whether functional gains are driven primarily by active neural engagement or strictly by the temporal contingency between motor intention and sensory feedback. This study aimed to deconstruct the BCI paradigm to isolate the specific contributions of these core components to functional recovery and cortical reorganization in subacute stroke.
METHODS: Seventy-seven subacute stroke patients were randomized into three intervention arms. Group C (synchronous) received robotic assistance strictly contingent on real-time detection of task engagement during motor imagery; Group B (asynchronous) performed identical motor imagery tasks but received temporally uncoupled robotic assistance; and Group A (sham) received sham motor imagery detection and preset passive robotic assistance. The intervention lasted for 3 weeks. The primary clinical outcome was Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) scores. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was included as an exploratory neuroimaging measure to provide preliminary information on cortical responses associated with the intervention.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight participants were included in the final analysis. After adjustment for baseline values, Group C showed significantly higher post-intervention FMA-UE scores than both Group A (adjusted mean difference = 7.47, 95% CI [1.94, 13.00], P = 0.004) and Group B (adjusted mean difference = 9.72, 95% CI [4.14, 15.30], P < 0.001). Group C also showed significantly higher post-intervention MBI scores than both Group A (adjusted mean difference = 21.15, 95% CI [12.49, 29.81], P < 0.001) and Group B (adjusted mean difference = 21.27, 95% CI [12.42, 30.12], P < 0.001). Exploratory neuroimaging analyses showed that only the change in ipsilesional sensorimotor cortex laterality index during motor imagery was significantly correlated with motor improvement (ρ = 0.404, P = 0.002, q = 0.012), whereas no resting-state or task-related fNIRS group comparisons remained significant after false discovery rate correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Synchronous BCI training was associated with superior clinical improvement compared with asynchronous and sham conditions in subacute stroke. The benefit was observed only when robotic assistance was contingent on real-time task performance, despite all three groups receiving comparable device exposure and motor imagery instruction. The neuroimaging results remain exploratory and should be confirmed in larger studies with prospectively defined imaging endpoints. Trial registration This trial was registered under the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091197) and was prospectively registered on October 21, 2024. Ethics Approval: Approved by the Ethics Committee of Xuzhou Rehabilitation Hospital (XK-LSW-20241017-009).

Title: A quasi-experimental study evaluating the effectiveness of a male-specific tuberculosis screening and diagnosis intervention in Uganda (IGNITE).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite men having a higher burden of TB, they are frequently missed by TB services due to social, behavioural, and health system factors that limit healthcare access. In Uganda, where there are no gender-specific guidelines for TB, we implemented and evaluated a gender-specific intervention to find and treat men with TB.
METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental study comparing TB notifications before (January-June 2023) and after (July-December 2023) the intervention at both intervention (Gombe and Mityana hospitals) and control (Luwero and Kiboga hospitals) sites. The intervention package aimed to enhance TB screening documentation by using checklist stamps, distribute TB educational materials, and introduce male-friendly TB clinics with evening opening hours, health education delivered by male champions, and integrated screening for TB, HIV, diabetes, and hypertension. We extracted data from TB registers and fitted a quasi-Poisson regression model, adjusting for catchment population dynamics by gender, to assess the intervention's effects on TB case notification rates.
RESULTS: Overall, 6,415 people in the participating hospitals were presumed to have TB, and 53.3% of these were females. Post-intervention, TB notifications increased by 46.3% (Female 0%, Male 88.4%) in Gombe and 36.4% (Female 26.3%, Male 45.1%) in Mityana; while they reduced by 26.7% (Female 28.8%, Male 25.5%) in Luwero and by 15.4% (Female + 23.9%, Male - 31.8%) in Kiboga. The baseline case notification rate was 246/100,000 population. Post-intervention analysis demonstrated that the intervention significantly increased TB case notification rates (RR: 1.51, 95% CI: 1.03-2.22), and males had a higher notification rate than females (RR: 1.5, 95% CI: 1.23-1.83). The treatment initiation rates pre- and post-intervention ranged between 97.4% and 100% in women, and 91.4% to 97.7% in men.
CONCLUSIONS: Gender-specific interventions for screening people with TB and linking them to care can be mutually beneficial at improving notifications among men and women.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered retrospectively on the Pan African Clinical Trial Registry (PACTR202509682831484) on 29th September 2025.

Title: Preoperative platelet-related inflammatory burden is associated with delayed early hemodynamic recovery following minimally invasive cardiac surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) is associated with reduced surgical trauma and improved postoperative recovery; however, early hemodynamic recovery remains variable and may be influenced by patient-related biological factors. This study evaluated the association between preoperative inflammatory biomarkers and delayed early postoperative recovery following MICS.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 166 consecutive patients undergoing thoracotomy-based MICS at a single tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. Preoperative inflammatory indices, including platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), were calculated from routine laboratory parameters. The primary endpoint was prolonged postoperative inotropic support (> 24 h); vasopressor-only therapy administered for vasoplegia or isolated blood pressure support was not counted. Multivariable complete-case logistic regression (n = 154), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Prolonged inotropic support was needed in 41 patients (24.7%). Patients requiring prolonged support were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration in univariable comparisons. LVEF was numerically lower but did not reach conventional statistical significance. PLR and SII were significantly higher in these patients (p = 0.003 and p = 0.010, respectively). In separate adjusted models, both PLR > = 142 and SII > = 462 were associated with prolonged support. In the combined complete-case model including both biomarkers, PLR > = 142 remained independently associated with prolonged support (OR 4.18, 95% CI 1.30-13.40, p = 0.016), whereas SII > = 462 did not (OR 1.66, 95% CI 0.52-5.31, p = 0.391). ROC analysis showed modest discrimination (PLR AUC 0.655, 95% CI 0.564-0.753, p = 0.003; SII AUC 0.634, 95% CI 0.538-0.729, p = 0.010). No significant associations were observed between inflammatory biomarkers and early mortality, acute kidney injury, or postoperative atrial fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative platelet-related inflammatory burden, as reflected by PLR, was associated with delayed early postoperative hemodynamic recovery following MICS. However, the discriminatory performance of PLR was modest, and this biomarker should be interpreted as a complementary risk indicator rather than a stand-alone decision-making tool. These findings are exploratory and require prospective validation in independent cohorts.

Title: Continuous intra-arterial versus noninvasive blood pressure monitoring for preventing hypotension during anesthesia induction in patients aged ≥ 75 years undergoing noncardiac surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypotension is common during the period after induction of general anesthesia and before surgical incision, particularly in older patients. The objective of this study was to compare the effectiveness of continuous intra-arterial pressure monitoring with that of noninvasive blood pressure monitoring in preventing hypotension during anesthesia induction in older patients (≥ 75 years) undergoing noncardiac surgery.
METHODS: In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 82 older patients who were scheduled for elective noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia were randomly assigned to the continuous intra-arterial pressure monitoring group or the noninvasive blood pressure monitoring group. The primary outcome was the area under the curve for mean arterial pressure (MAP) < 65 mmHg during the first 15 min after induction, based on invasive blood pressure measurements.
RESULTS: The area under the curve for mean arterial pressure < 65 mmHg was significantly lower in the continuous intra-arterial pressure monitoring group (median (interquartile range), 0 (0-6.09) mmHg∙min) than in the noninvasive group (3.67 (0-26.45) mmHg∙min; P = 0.008). The continuous intra-arterial pressure monitoring group also had a shorter duration of MAP < 65 mmHg (0 (0-1.42) vs. 0.87 (0-3.88) minutes; P = 0.010), received lower doses of propofol (16.67 (13.34-24.15) vs. 30 (24.17-40.83) mg; P = 0.011) and remifentanil (25.34 (16.67-40.00) vs. 34.18 (25.00-57.00) µg; P = 0.045), and received vasoactive drugs earlier (0.87 (0.67-1.00) vs. 2.33 (1.87-3.33) minutes; P < 0.001) and at higher doses in the continuous intra-arterial pressure monitoring group.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with noninvasive blood pressure monitoring, continuous intra‑arterial pressure monitoring initiated before induction was associated with reduced the incidence, severity, and duration of hypotension during anesthesia induction in older patients (≥ 75 years) undergoing noncardiac surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400088505) on August 20, 2024 ( https://www.chictr.org.cn/ ).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Extending prophylactic antimicrobial use beyond 48 h postoperatively fails to reduce surgical site infections and other healthcare-associated infections in patients undergoing colorectal resection: a Propensity Score Matching study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is controversial whether antibiotic should be used prophylactically 48 h after colorectal resection. Hence, the association of prophylactic antimicrobial (PA) use beyond 48 h postoperatively with the incidence of surgical site infections (SSI) and other healthcare-associated infections (HAI) in patients receiving colorectal resection surgery was evaluated.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 2691 patients who underwent colorectal resection between March 1, 2023, and December 31, 2025. Patients were categorized into the non-PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group (n = 1934) and the PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group (n = 757) based on whether prophylactic antibiotic use exceeded 48 h postoperatively. Propensity Score Matching (PSM) was used to balance differences in covariates between the two groups, subsequently, the relationship between prophylactic antibiotic use and infection was analyzed.
RESULTS: The incidence of surgical site infections (SSI) in patients undergoing colorectal resection was 8.51% (229/2691), while the incidence of other healthcare-associated infections (HAI) was 8.06% (217/2691). After PSM, both non-PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group and PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group were divided into 757 cases each. Multiple regression analysis showed that PA beyond 48 h postoperatively was not associated with SSI(OR = 0.85, 95% CI 0.59 -1.21, P = 0.356) and other HAI (OR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.54-1.23, P = 0.325) after adjustment for the confounding effect of age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, anemia, hypoproteinemia. Subsequent to adjustment for all confounding factors, PA beyond 48 h postoperatively was still not a influence factor for SSI (OR = 0.85, 95% CI 0.59-1.22, P = 0.372) and other HAI (OR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.18, P = 0.229). The total cost (¥57349.60 vs. ¥55039.10, P = 0.0006) were higher in the PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group than non-PA beyond 48 h postoperatively group, and no statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in postoperative hospital stay (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Extending prophylactic antimicrobial use beyond 48 h postoperatively following colorectal resection surgery was not associated with lower morbidity rate of SSI and other HAI, nor did it shorten the postoperative hospital stay; however, it resulted in elevated costs. Nonetheless, this study may contribute to the development of strategies for standardizing prophylactic medication management during the perioperative period of colorectal resection.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Preliminary construction and application of the AFSP risk stratification framework for anesthetic management in airway tumors: a case report.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To initially construct the Anatomy-Function-Surgery-Patient (AFSP) four-dimensional risk stratification framework, establish a dynamic anesthetic decision-making framework based on this framework, explore its application value in the anesthetic management of patients with airway neoplasms. This is a retrospective analysis of a single patient's multistage treatment course.
METHODS: The AFSP scoring tool was constructed based on relevant clinical guidelines and literature. A retrospective case of a 77-year-old patient with complex tracheal neoplasms was selected. The AFSP framework was applied to dynamically evaluate perioperative risks in three sequential treatment phases (tumor ablation combined with stent implantation, stent removal, and granulation tissue resection), guide the adjustment of anesthetic strategies, and observe the clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: During Stage I (tumor ablation + stent implantation), the patient's AFSP score reached 11 points, categorized as Grade IV (extremely high risk). We adopted general anesthesia supported by extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), which effectively prevented the life-threatening cannot intubate cannot oxygenate (CICO) crisis during anesthetic induction. In Stage II (stent removal), the AFSP score decreased to 8 points, falling into Grade III (high risk). The anesthetic strategy was adjusted to rapid sequence induction combined with high‑frequency jet ventilation (HFJV), which precisely targeted key risks including stent adhesion and intraoperative bleeding. For Stage III (granulation tissue resection), the AFSP score remained at 9 points (Grade III, high risk). On the basis of continuing the ventilation strategy used in Stage II, we added preoperative psychological intervention. No severe anesthesia-related complications occurred throughout the three treatment phases, and the patient completed the entire therapeutic course successfully, suggesting the application value of the AFSP framework in the anesthetic management of airway neoplasms.
CONCLUSION: The initially constructed AFSP four-dimensional risk stratification framework may facilitate the evaluation of perioperative risks in patients with airway neoplasms and help guide individualized anesthetic management strategies for those undergoing multistage treatment, potentially improving perioperative safety. This study is based on a single patient with a limited sample size; the universality of the conclusions needs to be further verified in larger cohorts, and the AFSP scoring tool requires optimization with more clinical data.

Title: The efficacy and safety of endoscopic ultrasound selective variceal devascularization for the treatment of esophagogastric varices: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroesophageal variceal bleeding is a life-threatening complication of portal hypertension. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of endoscopic ultrasound-guided selective variceal devascularization (EUS-SVD) compared with conventional endoscopic cyanoacrylate injection.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study adhered to the STROBE guidelines. Between August 2022 and June 2024, 107 patients were enrolled and allocated to conventional endoscopy (n = 52) or EUS-SVD (n = 55). Propensity score matching was performed to reduce confounding. Primary outcomes included rebleeding, ulcer formation, and resource utilization.
RESULTS: Compared with the conventional group, the EUS group required significantly lower volumes of polidocanol and cyanoacrylate (both P < 0.05). The 6‑month rebleeding rate and 3‑month ulcer formation rate were significantly lower in the EUS group (P < 0.05). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a reduced cumulative rebleeding incidence in the EUS group (HR 0.38, 95%CI 0.17-0.86, P = 0.021).
CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of a single-center retrospective design, these findings suggest that EUS-SVD may represent a promising therapeutic option for gastroesophageal varices, although it requires validation in prospective randomized trials.

Title: Analysis of myocardial work in different obesity phenotypes and its association with epicardial adipose tissue.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate subclinical cardiac dysfunction across distinct obesity phenotypes using myocardial work (MW) indices, and to investigate the moderating role of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) on MW impairment.
METHODS: One hundred ninety-two participants were categorized by BMI and metabolic status into four groups: metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). MW indices were measured using speckle-tracking echocardiography. EAT volume was quantified from ECG-gated CT scans. Associations were analyzed using ANCOVA and regression models.
RESULTS: Despite no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) among the groups, MUNW and MUO individuals exhibited significantly impaired MW, characterized by lower global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), and global work efficiency (GWE), alongside higher global waste work (GWW), compared with MHNW controls. MHO patients showed significantly better MW profiles than MUNW and MUO groups. EAT volume was increased in all obesity phenotype groups. Although no direct association was found between EAT volume and MW indices, EAT volume significantly moderated the relationship between Metabolically Unhealthy (MUH) and both GWE and GWW.
CONCLUSIONS: MW detects subclinical dysfunction earlier than LVEF across obesity phenotypes, with impairment progressively worsening from MHO to MUNW to MUO. In metabolically unhealthy individuals with increased EAT volume, more pronounced reductions in GWE and elevations in GWW were observed.
TRIAL RRGISTRATION: This study has been registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under the registration number ChiCTR2500100754 (registration date: April 15, 2025).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Immature neutrophil response is associated with cardiac complications after non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Abstract: Acute non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is complicated by systemic inflammation and cardiac dysfunction that contribute to the high rates of morbidity and mortality. To better define the mechanistic relationship between immune response and cardiac complications, we evaluated subpopulations of circulating immune cells and their associations with abnormalities of cardiac rhythm, injury biomarkers, and mechanical function after hemorrhage. In this single-site prospective observational study, we screened all adult patients presenting to our neurocritical care unit with non-traumatic SAH who required external ventricular drain (EVD) placement for treatment of hydrocephalus. Following informed consent, peripheral blood samples were obtained at post-bleed days (PBDs) 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10. Subjects were separated into groups based on evidence of cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(+))" versus "no cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(-))," and flow cytometric analysis was used to identify and quantify immune cell subpopulations. Circulating neutrophil-secreted factors, including myeloperoxidase (MPO), were measured in plasma using ELISA. We measured associations between these immune factors and cardiac abnormalities. Sixty patients were enrolled between January 2018 and August 2023. Our patient cohort was 65% female with a median age of 58 (IQR 51-68). Poor grade SAH (Hunt Hess = 4-5) occurred in 52% (n = 31) of patients. In the overall cohort 47 (78%) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (> 24-hours), and 52 (87%) underwent coil embolization/clipping of their aneurysm. The average ICU and hospital lengths of stay (LOS) were 18.5 (IQR 12.2-22) and 23 (IQR 18.2-33.8) days, respectively. In-hospital mortality for enrolled patients was 11.8% and overall mortality 6 months after discharge was 25% (n = 15). 40% (n = 24) of patients were discharged home, 37% (n = 22) to acute rehabilitation, 8% (n = 5) to SNF, and 3% (n = 2) to hospice. Cardiac abnormalities after SAH were associated with increased circulating neutrophil counts but not monocyte or lymphocyte levels. Circulating neutrophils in patients with cardiac abnormalities also had reduced cell-surface expression of maturation markers CD10, CD14, and CD16 in patients with cardiac abnormalities. Elevated levels of immature neutrophils and circulating levels of lipocalin-2, and myeloperoxidase (MPO) correlated with increased Hunt-Hess score, ICU, and hospital length of stay. Higher grade SAH was associated with increased immature neutrophil response, which was associated with cardiac abnormalities. These cardiac abnormalities tracked with increased levels of pro-inflammatory lipocalin-2 and MPO, and worse outcomes.

Title: Late cardiopulmonary morbidity in patients with Hodgkin lymphoma: a retrospective nationwide registry study.
Abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a B-cell neoplasm with a cure rate of 90%. Previous data on late morbidity in patients with HL cover the era of older treatment modalities. This real-world study consisted of 2912 patients diagnosed with HL between 2000 and 2019 in Finland and aimed to clarify the incidence of late-onset cardiopulmonary morbidity compared to matched controls. Patient data were collected from four nationwide Finnish healthcare registries. We reported a higher occurrence of coronary artery disease in patients aged < 50 years at diagnosis than in controls (RR 3.80 (2.16-6.74), p < 0001). Additionally, a higher incidence of both heart failure (RR 1.68 (1.28-2.21), p < 0.001) and valvular heart disease (RR 1.80 (1.17-2.78), p = 0.006) was detected in patients aged ≥ 50 years at diagnosis than in the controls. Remarkably, in the < 50 years age group, the incidences of pneumonia (RR 4.89 (3.58-6.71), p < 0.001) and pulmonary embolism (RR 7.78 (2.75-21.95), p < 0.001) were higher than those in the control group. In conclusion, with the current treatment modalities, late cardiopulmonary morbidity in long-term survivors remains a great challenge. A strategy for primary prevention and early detection of late toxicity remains crucial and a critical evaluation of current treatment practices is warranted.

Title: Longitudinal association between body weight change and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity in patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus: A post hoc analysis of the FMD-J study B.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: We investigated cross-sectional associations between body mass index (BMI) and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and longitudinal associations between body weight change and baPWV over 3 years in 874 patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus without coronary artery disease (475 men; mean age, 61.9 ± 9.5 years). baPWV was measured at baseline, 1.5 years, and 3 years. At baseline, BMI was inversely correlated with baPWV (r = -0.14, P < 0.001), and multivariate analysis confirmed this association (β = -12.5, P < 0.001). In generalized linear mixed-effects models adjusted for concurrent systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and other covariates, neither continuous percentage change in body weight (β = -1.2, P = 0.08) nor categorical body weight change (≥5% increase: β = -10.6, P = 0.45; ≥5% decrease: β = 18.0, P = 0.15) was associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV, with no interaction across baseline BMI categories. The modest body weight changes observed in this cohort were not significantly associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV.

Title: Biomarkers of native liver survival and portal hypertension in biliary atresia.
Journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of noninvasive markers Aspartate Aminotransferase to Platelet Ratio Index (APRi) and Infantile Biliary Atresia Liver Fibrosis score (iBALF), as well as the histological Ishak fibrosis score, as predictors of native liver survival (NLS) and portal hypertension (PH) in children with biliary atresia (BA) undergoing Kasai portoenterostomy (KPE).
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective observational study was conducted on children diagnosed with BA who underwent KPE. APRi and iBALF were calculated using laboratory data collected at hospital discharge after KPE. The degree of hepatic fibrosis was assessed and reviewed using the Ishak fibrosis score in liver biopsy specimens collected at KPE. NLS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards regression. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Higher APRi, iBALF, and Ishak fibrosis score values were associated with lower NLS (p < 0.006, p < 0.025, and p < 0.048, respectively). APRi and iBALF emerged as good PH predictors (p < 0.005 and p < 0.032, respectively).
CONCLUSION: APRi, iBALF, and the Ishak fibrosis score showed prognostic value in predicting NLS in children with BA after KPE. These findings reinforce the potential use of biomarkers in the clinical follow-up of these patients, supporting risk stratification strategies.

Title: Posterior urethral valve and chronic constipation: Association and clinical outcome following endoscopic ablation in children.
Journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Posterior urethral valves (PUV) are the most common cause of congenital urinary obstruction in male infants and may be associated with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). The association between LUTS and chronic constipation (CC) in children, known as bladder and bowel dysfunction (BBD), has been extensively investigated. However, how primary urological obstruction may influence gastrointestinal function remains poorly investigated. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of CC in children with PUV and evaluate changes in bowel symptoms following endoscopic PUV ablation.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study at "Santobono-Pausilipon Children's Hospital" in Naples, Italy, from January 2021 to March 2024. Patients aged 0-6 years with PUV were enrolled. Demographic and clinical data were collected, including age, valve type, urological signs and symptoms, comorbidities, ongoing therapies. Bowel habits were assessed at diagnosis and after PUV ablation using Rome IV criteria.
RESULTS: One hundred and one children were enrolled (mean age ± standard deviation = 32 ± 48.4 months). At baseline, 27/101 (26.7%) met Rome IV criteria for CC. After PUV ablation, constipation resolved in 19/27 patients (p < 0.01), reducing overall constipation prevalence from 26.7% to 11.9% (p < 0.01). Multivariate analysis did not identify predictors of constipation resolution.
CONCLUSIONS: Children affected by PUV exhibit a likely increased prevalence of CC. Endoscopic PUV ablation leads to significant normalization of bowel function, supporting a bidirectional interplay between urinary and gastrointestinal systems. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings in order to clarify the underlying mechanisms and optimize long-term care for affected patients.

Title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
Abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β0-thalassaemia (HbSβ0), haemoglobin S/β+-thalassaemia (HbSβ+), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

Title: Reduced Adverse Events Without Survival Benefit With HeartMate 3 vs. HeartMate II in Japan.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HeartMate 3 (Abbott Laboratories), a fully magnetically levitated left ventricular assist device (LVAD), has shown improved hemocompatibility vs. previous devices, but nationwide real-world data in Japan remain limited.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese nationwide registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed patients who underwent de novo implantation of HeartMate 3 or HeartMate II between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and device dysfunction requiring exchange or explantation within 2 years. In all, 978 patients were included in the study (HeartMate 3, n=486; HeartMate II, n=492). The 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group than in the HeartMate II group (9% vs. 23%; P<0.001). HeartMate 3 was independently associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.51; P<0.001), which remained consistent in competing-risk and several statistically matched analyses. The incidence of hemocompatibility-related adverse events, including major bleeding, stroke, and device dysfunction, was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group. In contrast, 2- and 5-year overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups (<10% for both devices).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide Japanese registry, HeartMate 3 reduced major LVAD-related complications without improving survival, supporting its clinical advantages in contemporary LVAD management.

Title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.

Title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm3/min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm3/min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm3/min) and 6.8 mm3/min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm3/min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively.
