Turmeric extract combined with other compounds (EC) and turmeric extract (E) were associated with significant reductions in FBS with WMD -10.73 (95%CI: -14.22, -7.25;SUCRA 92.2%), and -10.57 (95%CI: -14.35, -6.79;91.5%;SUCRA 91.5%), respectively. E was associated with a significant reduction in HbA1c, while EC was associated with lower HOMA-IR with MWD -0.73 (95%CI: -1.41, -0.05; SUCRA 79.8%). Whole turmeric with other compounds (WC) was associated with a significant reduction in LDL-C (WMD: -37.19, 95%CI: -56.97, -17.42; SUCRA: 97.3%). E was associated with a lower risk of incident type 2 diabetes (RR= 0.05; 95%CI:0.00,0.78), although this estimate was based on low-certainty of evidence. No significant effects were observed for inflammatory markers. Overall certainty of evidence was low due to heterogeneity and short trial durations, and variability among combination formulations. In prediabetes, formulation-specific metabolic effects were observed. However, given the low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger, longer-term trials before clinical recommendation can be made.

Title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1st, 2005, to August 6th, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency.
RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency.
CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.

Title: Plasma Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population.
AIM: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE.
METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2- and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations.
RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs. lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR 3.87, 95% CI 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR: 1.51, 95% CI: 0.82-2.80).
CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

Title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2- positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with JAK2V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin.
METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IR) per 100 person-years (PY) and incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing aspirin use versus no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n=1,760 with aspirin, n=367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in JAK2V617F-positive MPN patients receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 PY (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59 - 4.65; I2=93%) with pooled IRR receiving aspirin versus no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI 0.40 - 0.86, I2=16%). The pooled IR of major and non-major bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI 1.06 - 3.65; I2=90%) per 100 PY with pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI 1.15 - 5.11; I2=43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low.
CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence the better define the role of aspirin in JAK2V617F-positive MPNs.

Title: Ketamine Versus Magnesium Sulphate as Adjuvants to Bupivacaine in Pectoral Nerve Blocks for Mastectomy: A Randomized, Double-Blind Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pectoral nerve blocks (PECS) provide effective regional analgesia after mastectomy, but the optimal adjuvant remains unclear. This study compared ketamine and magnesium sulphate as adjuvants to bupivacaine in PECS blocks.
METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind trial, 72 patients scheduled for modified radical mastectomy were randomized into 3 equal groups (n = 24). Group A received 0.25% bupivacaine with saline (control); Groups B and C received bupivacaine with ketamine or magnesium sulphate, respectively. The primary outcome was time to first rescue analgesia; secondary outcomes included 24-hour pethidine consumption, postoperative pain (Visual Analog Scale, VAS), and hemodynamic parameters.
RESULTS: Baseline and intraoperative parameters were comparable among groups. Postoperatively, the control group had significantly higher heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and respiratory rate than both adjuvant groups during the first 12 hours. VAS scores were lower in both adjuvant groups than in the control group, and lower with ketamine than with magnesium sulphate from 1 to 8 hours. Both adjuvants significantly prolonged time to first rescue analgesia and reduced 24-hour pethidine consumption compared with control. Ketamine achieved a longer median time to first rescue analgesia (10 [IQR 8-12] vs. 8 [IQR 4-8] hours; P = .023) and lower median pethidine consumption (75 [IQR 50-100] vs. 100 [IQR 100-112.5] mg; P = .018) than magnesium sulphate.
CONCLUSION: Ketamine and magnesium sulphate both improve postoperative analgesia and reduce opioid consumption after mastectomy. Ketamine was superior to magnesium sulphate and may be the preferred adjuvant, though larger trials are needed.

Title: Factors influencing patients' health behaviors during the transitional period after heart valve replacement: a qualitative study based on the COM-B framework.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify and map perceived barriers and facilitators to health behaviors (including medication management, exercise, nutrition, psychological adjustment, and self-care) among patients during the transitional recovery phase after heart valve replacement (HVR), using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework as a guiding analytical lens, and addressing the predominantly quantitative nature of existing research.
METHODS: A descriptive qualitative design was employed. Fourteen patients at 1 week to 6 months post-HVR were purposively recruited between July and December 2024. Semi-structured interviews guided by the COM-B framework were analyzed using directed content analysis, integrating deductive coding derived from the model with inductive coding to capture emergent themes. Methodological rigor was established through interrater coding, member checking, and maintenance of an audit trail.
RESULTS: Three key themes aligned with COM-B domains (capability, motivation, opportunity) and fourteen subthemes were identified. Capability barriers included insufficient disease knowledge, negative illness perceptions, and medication management challenges. Motivational factors revealed weak baseline health awareness and low self-efficacy as barriers, alongside role recovery motivation and psychological self-adjustment as facilitators. Opportunity factors included family support, health professional guidance, and peer support as resources, alongside financial burden and environmental constraints as barriers.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identified perceived barriers and facilitators to health behaviors among patients during transitional recovery following HVR, mapped across capability, opportunity, and motivation domains using the COM-B framework. From a psychological perspective, illness perceptions, self-efficacy, role-recovery motivation, and psychological self-adjustment emerged as key psychological processes associated with behavioral engagement. Further prospective and intervention research is needed to examine these exploratory patterns and evaluate whether theory-driven strategies informed by these processes can support behavior change.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: These findings suggest the potential value of addressing psychological processes such as illness perceptions, self-efficacy, and motivational orientation alongside knowledge-based education, as a possible approach to supporting sustained engagement in health behaviors after HVR.

Title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies.
AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

Title: Clinical spectrum of heterozygous LZTR1 variation in a schwannomatosis-clinic cohort: A descriptive study of multisystem features.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: LZTR1-related disorders (LRDs) include schwannomatosis, Noonan syndrome, and variably expressed multisystem phenotypes, but the full clinical spectrum remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether adults carrying pathogenic or likely pathogenic LZTR1 variants show recurrent extracranial and central nervous system findings, while separately presenting descriptive findings from candidate VUS carriers and accounting for the limits of specialty-clinic ascertainment.
METHODS: We examined adults assessed at comprehensive schwannomatosis clinics (n = 156), including a genetically ascertained subgroup with pathogenic or likely pathogenic LZTR1 variants (n = 19) and 5 cases with candidate LZTR1 VUS. Clinical, imaging, laboratory, and genetic data were systematically reviewed and harmonized to characterize multisystem manifestations associated with LRDs.
RESULTS: Among the 19 individuals with pathogenic or likely pathogenic LZTR1 variants, recurrent manifestations included schwannomatosis (8/19), cerebral vasculopathy (7/19), congenital or peripheral vascular anomalies (8/19), neoplasia (6/19), central nervous system cystic lesions including arachnoid cysts (3/19) and perineural/Tarlov cysts (2/19), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (2/19), and vertebral endplate abnormalities/Schmorl nodes (5/19). Because phenotype counts differ when candidate VUS carriers are included, analyses are reported using clearly specified denominators: the primary analysis is restricted to pathogenic or likely pathogenic carriers (n = 19), whereas the full clinically ascertained cohort (n = 24) is presented descriptively as a sensitivity summary. Truncating, splice, and missense variants were considered separately because the small number of missense variants and limited functional evidence preclude firm genotype-phenotype conclusions. Notably, no individual fulfilled a clinical diagnosis of Noonan syndrome.
CONCLUSION: These findings support cautious recognition of possible multisystem involvement among selected individuals with pathogenic or likely pathogenic LZTR1 variants. Candidate VUS carriers are reported descriptively but are not treated as having established deleterious alleles. Larger comparator-based studies, functional validation, and standardized surveillance data are needed before broad disease-label expansion or risk-management recommendations can be made.

Title: Prospective associations between empirical dietary inflammatory pattern score and cardiovascular diseases and cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Inflammation plays an important role in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and cancer development, and dietary factors can modulate inflammation. Several studies have shown an association between Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (EDIP) and CVDs and cancer, but there are limited prospective studies in Asian populations. We aimed to prospectively investigate the association between the inflammatory potential of the diet, as measured by an EDIP score adapted to an Asian population (EDIP-A) and the risks of CVDs, cancer, and mortality from CVDs and cancer in a large multi-ethnic Asian cohort.
METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Cohort (n = 10,640), a prospective study comprising ethnic Chinese, Malay, and Indian adults aged 21-65 years, recruited between 2004 and 2010. The EDIP-A score was calculated using a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Outcomes including incidence of nonfatal stroke, nonfatal acute myocardial infarction (AMI), CVDs mortality, cancer incidence and cancer mortality were ascertained through data linkage with national registries. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between the EDIP-A score and these outcomes.
RESULTS: During 887,505 person-years of follow-up, 435 nonfatal AMI cases, 317 nonfatal strokes, and 188 CVD deaths were documented. For cancer outcomes, 653 incident cases and 176 cancer deaths were recorded. Participants in the highest quintile of EDIP-A score had a higher risk of nonfatal stroke [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.64, 95 % CI 1.06, 2.55, P-trend = 0.01] than participants in the lowest quintile. These associations remained significant after further adjustment for body mass index. These associations were modified by smoking status (P-interaction <0.05). No significant associations were observed between EDIP-A score and risk of nonfatal AMI, CVD mortality, cancer incidence and cancer mortality.
CONCLUSION: Dietary patterns with a higher proinflammatory potential were associated with higher stroke risk, particularly among smokers. These findings suggest that reducing the inflammatory potential of the diet may be a promising strategy for prevention of CVDs.

Title: Supraclavicular artery island flap for head and neck reconstruction: Our experience and exploratory analysis of risk factors.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is being increasingly used for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap. Here, we describe our experience with SCAIF for oncologic head and neck reconstruction and aim to identify patient factors associated with flap complications.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent SCAIF reconstruction at a tertiary academic center was conducted between 2015 and 2023 (n=23). Collected variables included patient characteristics, operative parameters, and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 70.2 years. Six patients had a history of prior radiation, and 6 underwent ipsilateral neck dissection. Twelve patients received adjuvant radiation following flap transfer. Minor flap-related complications included delayed wound healing (n = 3) and partial flap necrosis (n = 6). One patient experienced total flap necrosis. Systemic complications included myocardial infarction (n = 2), pulmonary embolism (n = 1), atrial fibrillation (n = 1), and deep vein thrombosis (n = 1). Advanced age was associated with recipient-site complications (p = 0.018). Elevated body mass index was associated with systemic complications, longer ICU stays, and increased total hospital length of stay (p=0.036, p = 0.008, and p = 0.001, respectively). History of vascular disease and diabetes mellitus were associated with flap necrosis and delayed wound healing, respectively (p=0.025 and p=0.004). Longer operative time was associated with flap dehiscence (p=0.002).
CONCLUSION: SCAIF is a reliable and versatile reconstructive option for oncologic head and neck defects, including in previously operated or irradiated necks. Caution is warranted particularly in patients with diabetes or vascular disease, as vascular comorbidities appear to be more clinically precise risk factors than chronological age alone. Elevated body mass index also warrants consideration.

Title: A last resort that works: Distal deep vein arterialization in no-option diabetic critical limb-threatening ischemia: A prospective interventional study.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease characterized by ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcers, and gangrene. In patients with "no-option" CLTI, distal deep vein arterialization (DDVA) offers a potential limb salvage strategy. We prospectively studied the outcomes of open DDVA in patients with diabetes with CLTI.
METHODS: This prospective interventional case series included 10 patients with diabetes with CLTI (rest pain, ulcers, or gangrene) confirmed using duplex ultrasonography and CT angiography underwent open DDVA. Vascular anastomosis was performed between the posterior tibial artery (PTA, n = 9) or anterior tibial artery (ATA, n = 1) and one of its venae comitantes in the tarsal tunnel. Demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes were analyzed. The outcomes of interest included wound healing, pain relief, limb salvage and mortality.
RESULTS: The cohort included 8 men and 2 women, with a mean age 59.6 years. All patients underwent DDVA between the posterior/anterior tibial artery and corresponding vena comitans. By 1 month, 6 patients achieved complete wound healing, whereas 4 had small residual ulcers that fully healed by 2 months, and mean VAS pain scores improved from 7.7 to 1.8. at 2 months, CT angiography confirmed patent arterio-venous anastomoses in all patients. At an average follow-up of 12.5 ± 5.9 months, all patient achieved ambulatory, ulcer free, and major amputation-free survival.
CONCLUSION: Open DDVA is a feasible and effective revascularization option in no-option diabetic CLTI, which offers encouraging early results in limb salvage, wound healing, and pain relief. Larger studies with longer follow-up and objective perfusion assessment are warranted.

Title: Impact of clozapine on the proteome: A systematic review and functional analyses.
Abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet its use is limited by potentially life-threatening adverse effects including myocarditis, agranulocytosis and pneumonia. Improved mechanistic understanding may facilitate safer prescribing. We conducted the first systematic review integrating proteomic findings associated with clozapine exposure. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase and Scopus were searched for clozapine-associated proteomic studies in animal, human and cell-based models. Differentially expressed proteins were mapped to Reactome pathways using the Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING). Using the same approach, analyses stratified all proteins by model type and replicated proteins by exposure duration and biological system. Replicated proteins were further analysed using QIAGEN Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA). Across studies, 1070 unique proteins changed following clozapine exposure (603 increased, 394 decreased, 73 discordant). Of these, 152 were identified in ≥2 studies, with 79 showing concordant directionality. Nine were replicated in ≥3 studies with consistent direction. Overall STRING analysis identified recurrent immune/inflammatory, cellular-stress and neuronal pathway enrichment, with stratified analyses providing partial support for these and related metabolic processes across model types, exposure duration and biological system. IPA highlighted necrosis-related processes and downstream disease effects involving cardiovascular, hepatic and renal systems. These findings suggest that immune, inflammatory and regulated cell-death pathways may contribute to clozapine-associated adverse effects, although their relationship to treatment response remains unknown. Limited time series data directly compare brain and peripheral blood changes. Prospective longitudinal proteomic studies during clozapine initiation are warranted to identify early biomarkers and intervention windows.

Title: Sleep-state transition instability with recurrent multisystem activation: A case-based phenotypic framework.
Abstract: The wake-to-sleep transition is a physiologically vulnerable period during which benign and pathologic motor phenomena may emerge. Current sleep nosology recognizes isolated hypnic jerks, propriospinal myoclonus at sleep onset, sleep-related rhythmic movement disorder, and other minor sleep-related motor activities, but these entities may not fully explain patients with persistent, repetitive motor activation recurring across successive attempts to fall asleep. We describe eight representative cases characterized by recurrent motor events centered on sleep onset or early sleep-state transitions, associated sensory and autonomic symptoms, clinically meaningful sleep fragmentation, and absence of a more satisfactory alternative diagnosis. On the basis of these observations, we introduce sleep-state transition instability with recurrent multisystem activation (SSTI-RMA) as a provisional, hypothesis-generating phenotypic construct rather than an established diagnostic entity. The recurring clinical pattern comprises recurrent motor activation during wake-to-sleep or early sleep transitions together with variable sensory, autonomic, cardiovascular, respiratory, or other non-motor manifestations, repetition or clustering of events, difficulty initiating or stabilizing sleep, clinically significant distress or impairment, and absence of a more satisfactory alternative explanation. We conceptualize the SSTI-RMA phenotype as a possible disorder of sleep-state instability rather than as an isolated motor phenomenon, potentially involving impaired coordination among neural, autonomic, and vascular processes during sleep entry. No validated polysomnographic signature, frequency threshold, biomarker, or prevalence estimate is currently available, and the relationship of this phenotype to severe or recurrent sleep starts remains unresolved. SSTI-RMA should therefore be regarded as a descriptive research framework intended to facilitate standardized phenotyping and prospective studies capable of determining whether it represents a distinct entity, part of a continuum of established sleep-onset phenomena, or a heterogeneous phenotype with multiple causes.

Title: From SCORE-Belgium to SCORE2: impact of successive guideline updates on cardiovascular risk categorization.
Abstract: Background: Successive European guideline updates have modified the estimation and categorisation of cardiovascular risk. The transition from the Belgian SCORE calibration to SCORE2 in 2021, followed by revision of SCORE2 thresholds in 2025, may substantially alter clinical interpretation without changes in individual patient characteristics.Methods: Adults aged 40-69 years in primary prevention were retrospectively included from two Belgian centres. Both cohorts were pooled into a single analytical population. Cardiovascular risk was assessed using the HDL-corrected SCORE-Belgium model (2019), SCORE2 (2021), and the updated SCORE2 thresholds (2025), applied to identical baseline data. Low and moderate categories were harmonised. Reclassification was analysed descriptively.Results: Among 413 individuals, 84.3% were classified as low-moderate risk with SCORE-Belgium, 11.6% as high risk, and 4.1% as very high risk. With SCORE2 (2021), 58.8% were categorised as high risk and 7.3% as very high risk. Application of the 2025 thresholds reversed this distribution: 93.5% were classified as low-moderate risk, 6.5% as high risk, and none as very high risk. These variations affected largely the same individuals and occurred despite identical underlying risk estimates.Conclusion: Guideline updates markedly influence cardiovascular risk categorisation in primary prevention. The changes observed are predominantly attributable to the definitions of thresholds, rather than to differences in the underlying risk estimates. Risk categories should, therefore, be interpreted in the context of the specific assessment framework employed. In addition, supplementary methods for refining individual risk remain necessary.

Title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI.
METHODS: This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%; p = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986; p = 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250; p = 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894; p = 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874).
CONCLUSION: Foot microcirculation differed significantly between patients with Cla and CLTI on CTP. Hb, TTP, and BF were independent predictors for CLTI. All models demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with model C yielding the highest AUC.

Title: Venous interventions reduce the risk of lymphedema in chronic venous insufficiency.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) significantly increases the risk of developing secondary lymphedema and related infections. This study tested the hypothesis that lower-extremity venous procedures can reduce the 5-year incidence of lymphedema in adults with CVI.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults (⩾ 18 years) diagnosed with CVI between Jan 1, 2005, and Jan 1, 2020, were identified and followed for at least 5 years. Patients were stratified into those undergoing venous procedures, including saphenous vein ligation, phlebectomy, sclerotherapy, and endovenous ablation, and matched controls managed without intervention. Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 on demographics, comorbidities, and infection-related variables. The primary outcome was new-onset lymphedema, assessed using Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: After matching, 17,703 patients were included in each cohort. At 5 years, new-onset lymphedema occurred in 5.1% of controls versus 4.0% of patients who underwent venous procedures (hazard ratio [HR] 1.26, 95% CI 1.14-1.40). Phlebectomy showed the strongest association with risk reduction (4.0% vs 1.5%; HR 2.60, 95% CI 1.33-5.06), followed by varicose vein sclerotherapy (5.3% vs 3.6%; HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.02-2.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Venous interventions may reduce the risk of developing lymphedema in patients with chronic venous insufficiency.

Title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.
METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.
RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.
CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

Title: Microsurgical clipping versus Woven EndoBridge embolization for intracranial aneurysms: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: To compare microsurgical clipping and Woven EndoBridge (WEB) embolization for the treatment of intracranial aneurysms, including ruptured and unruptured cases, with respect to angiographic occlusion, morbidity, mortality, and adverse events (AEs). This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 29, 2026, for comparative studies evaluating microsurgical clipping versus WEB embolization. Cohort studies and clinical trials were eligible regardless of aneurysm rupture status or morphology. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic, and predefined subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Five observational cohort studies comprising 798 patients (402 clipping, 396 WEB) were included. The most credible estimate, from the good-quality concurrent studies, showed higher occlusion with clipping (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.14 to 1.49, I2 0%). Larger pooled estimates (RR 1.71 for complete occlusion; RR 2.04 in the two-study wide-neck analysis) were strongly influenced by fair-quality studies that used external WEB comparators and by near-ceiling clipping occlusion combined with small WEB denominators, and are presented as exploratory. Adequate or complete occlusion also favored clipping (RR: 1.61, 95% CI: 1.24-2.11; P = 0.0004). There were no significant differences in morbidity (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.33-2.25) or overall mortality (RR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.37-1.28). Reported adverse-event frequencies appeared broadly comparable, although inconsistent reporting across studies precluded formal comparative analysis, and the profile of complications differed between techniques. Across wide-neck aneurysms and within the available short-term follow-up, microsurgical clipping was consistently associated with higher angiographic occlusion than WEB embolization, which was the more internally consistent estimate, although heterogeneity increased when all wide-neck-only studies were combined. No statistically significant difference was observed in morbidity or mortality. Because WEB occlusion may progress over time and long-term retreatment and recurrence data are limited, these short-term angiographic findings should not be interpreted as evidence of superior long-term durability. Because all included studies were observational, these comparisons are susceptible to selection bias, and treatment selection should remain individualized according to aneurysm characteristics, rupture status, and clinical context.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Periconceptional and early-pregnancy exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors and congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are increasingly prescribed to women of reproductive age for type 2 diabetes and cardiorenal protection, and are commonly continued through the periconceptional period until pregnancy is recognized. Human safety data on inadvertent first-trimester exposure remain scarce, creating substantial clinical uncertainty.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from inception to 15 May 2026 for observational cohort studies comparing early-pregnancy or preconception exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors with active antidiabetic comparators among women with type 2 diabetes. Adjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Three cohorts, including 669 SGLT2 inhibitor-exposed pregnancies, were eligible. In the prespecified insulin-comparator analysis, SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with major congenital malformations (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68-1.29) or cardiac malformations (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.64-1.48). The inclusion of a preconception sulfonylurea comparator cohort yielded a similar estimate for major congenital malformations (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.74-1.29). In a Korean cohort, exposure during gestational weeks 4-10 was associated with congenital heart defects (RR 2.79, 95% CI 1.16-7.06).
CONCLUSIONS: Based on the limited observational evidence available, early SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with an increased risk of overall major congenital or cardiac malformations; however, the estimates were imprecise and could not rule out clinically important increases in risk. Certainty of the evidence was low to very low because of residual confounding, live-birth selection, heterogeneous exposure definitions, and few exposed events. A possible timing-specific cardiac signal requires replication.

Title: Metabolic syndrome before 16 weeks' gestation: prevalence and haemodynamic profile in a socioeconomically disadvantaged pregnancy cohort: baseline findings from Mother's Heart Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy provides an opportunity to identify young women at risk of future cardiometabolic diseases. We aimed to determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) and its components, and to assess haemodynamic profiles in early pregnancy.
METHOD: We recruited pregnant women at Lyell McEwin Hospital before 16 weeks' gestation. Haemodynamic parameters were measured using USCOM BP+ device. Blood glucose, lipid profile, liver and renal function were assessed. We included data from 264 women aged 19-44 years in the analyses. MetS was defined using the Harmonizing the MetS criteria.
RESULTS: The prevalence of MetS was 15.1% (n = 40). Individual MetS components included high waist circumference (97.3%, n = 257), high systolic blood pressure (4.5%, n = 12), high diastolic blood pressure (1.1%, n = 3), high triglycerides (47.7%, n = 126), low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (15.2%, n = 40), and elevated fasting blood glucose (1.4%, n = 1). Compared with women without MetS, women with MetS had higher peripheral systolic blood pressure, central systolic blood pressure (cSBP), central diastolic blood pressure, central mean arterial pressure (cMAP), pulse rate (PR), and suprasystolic pulse rate, and lower suprasystolic pulse rate variability, pressure gradient, reflected wave transit time to the reflected wave peak, and pulse pressure. After adjustment for BMI and correction for multiple testing, cSBP, cMAP and PR remained independently associated with MetS (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: MetS in early pregnancy is associated with changes in cardiovascular haemodynamics, with adiposity contributing to these changes. Early screening for MetS during pregnancy may provide an opportunity to identify women at increased risk of future cardiometabolic disease.

Title: Haplotype structure and functional genotype-phenotype interactions of PON1 (L55M/Q192R) variants in Egyptian children with nephrotic syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is characterized by proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and dyslipidemia. Paraoxonase-1 (PON1), an HDL-associated antioxidant enzyme, contributes to lipid protection and redox homeostasis.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations of PON1 L55M (rs854560) and Q192R (rs662) polymorphisms with NS and their relationships with PON1 concentrations in an Egyptian pediatric cohort.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This case-control study included 84 children aged 4-12 years: 42 with NS and 42 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Serum PON1 concentration, lipid profile, albumin, blood urea, and urinary albumin excretion were assessed. PON1 polymorphisms were genotyped using tetra-primer amplification refractory mutation system polymerase chain reaction (T-ARMS-PCR).
RESULTS: Children with NS had higher total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, blood urea, and urinary albumin excretion, and lower HDL cholesterol, albumin, and PON1 concentrations than controls (all p < 0.001). The L55M MM genotype was more frequent in NS than controls (66.7% vs. 40.5%; OR = 3.77, p = 0.02) and was associated with an adverse biochemical profile. For Q192R, the R allele was associated with NS (61.9% vs. 42.9%; OR = 2.17, p = 0.01), while the RR genotype showed an association under the recessive model (OR = 2.67, p = 0.04). MM and RR carriers had the lowest PON1 concentrations. Haplotype analysis suggested associations between the LQ and MR haplotypes and NS.
CONCLUSIONS: PON1 genetic variation and reduced PON1 concentrations may contribute to the metabolic phenotype and susceptibility to NS, supporting a potential role for PON1-mediated antioxidant pathways in disease pathophysiology and variation in oxidative stress responses among children.

Title: Clinical utility and impact of myocardial viability imaging with F-18 FDG positron emission tomography to predict left ventricular function improvement following revascularization in ischemic heart disease : a single center retrospective study.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: Recent studies have questioned the benefit of myocardial viability identification and its clinical impact on revascularization decisions. We aimed to evaluate whether F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (F-18 FDG)-positron emission tomography (PET) influences real-world revascularization decisions and whether PET-defined viability helps predict improvement in ejection fraction (LVEF). We conducted a retrospective chart review of Rubidium-82 (Rb-82)/F-18 FDG PET ischemia and viability studies performed from 2020 to 2024 at our institution. Baseline characteristics including comorbidities, ejection fraction (EF) at 3 months and 1 year and PET study results were evaluated. Among patients with viability, a linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF was performed to assess temporal changes and treatment strategy interaction. One hundred and eleven patients underwent rest-stress Rb-82 PET with F-18 FDG PET imaging, of whom 99 received FDG for myocardial viability assessment. Among these patients, 65 (65.6%) demonstrated ischemic viable myocardium, while 31 (31.3%) had non-viable myocardium. Viability-positive patients were more likely to undergo revascularization (57% (n = 37) vs. 36% (n = 28) received medical therapy only). At 3-month follow-up, both revascularization and medical therapy were associated with significant improvement in LVEF among viability-positive patients. In contrast, viability-negative patients did not demonstrate significant EF improvement. Among viability-positive patients with both 3-month and 1- year EF measurements (N = 28), linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF revealed that baseline EF was a strong independent predictor of follow-up EF (p < 0.0001). From 3 months to 1 year, the revascularization group demonstrated a significant increase in EF (+ 4.28%, p = 0.014), whereas the medical therapy group showed a non-significant change (+ 1.40%, p = 0.53). However, the overall EF improvement did not differ significantly between groups after adjustment (p = 0.30). EF changes in viability-negative patients remained non-significant over time. Symptomatic improvement was documented in 55.3% of viability-positive patients. Our single-center experience shows that FDG-PET viability test continues to guide management and decision making regarding revascularization and can predict functional recovery and symptomatic improvement.

Title: Aspirin dose and coronary artery lesions in Kawasaki disease: a two-center retrospective comparative effectiveness study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Coronary artery lesions (CAL) are the most common complication of Kawasaki disease (KD). Chinese guidelines recommend aspirin at 30-50 mg/kg/day during the acute phase, yet whether the dose within this range affects coronary outcome remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 997 children with complete or incomplete KD who received IVIG plus aspirin at two tertiary hospitals in Sichuan, China, from January 2017 to December 2025. Low-dose aspirin (30 to < 40 mg/kg/day; n = 630) was compared with high-dose (40 to 50 mg/kg/day; n = 367). Confounders were selected by intersecting a directed acyclic graph (Supplementary Fig. S1) with univariate screening at P < 0.10, yielding a final multivariable model of 7 predictors (136 CAL events; events-per-variable ratio of 19.4). Linearity of the continuous covariates and the absence of multicollinearity were verified (Supplementary Tables S1-S2). The dose-response relation was examined with restricted cubic splines, and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was added as a sensitivity analysis. CAL at 4 weeks occurred in 13.5% of the low-dose group and 14.7% of the high-dose group (P = 0.658), with an adjusted OR of 0.94 (95% CI 0.64-1.38; P = 0.752). IVIG non-response was similar (4.1% vs 3.8%; P = 0.940), whereas aspirin-related adverse drug reactions were twice as frequent with high-dose aspirin (3.0% vs 6.3%; P = 0.021). The spline showed no significant linear (P = 0.253) or non-linear (P = 0.547) dose-response trend. IPTW yielded an OR of 0.95 (95% CI 0.65-1.38), and the doubly robust estimate was 0.95 (95% CI 0.65-1.40).
CONCLUSIONS: Within the guideline-recommended 30-50 mg/kg/day window, no significant differences were detected between low- and high-dose aspirin in coronary or IVIG non-response outcomes, while the lower dose halved adverse drug reactions. Although equivalence cannot be formally demonstrated in an observational study, these data suggest that 30 to < 40 mg/kg/day may be the preferable choice during the acute phase of KD in Chinese children.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Chinese guidelines recommend aspirin at 30-50 mg/kg/day during the acute phase of KD, yet comparative coronary outcome data within this dose range remain limited.
WHAT IS NEW: • In a two-center cohort of 997 children, low-dose (30 to < 40 mg/kg/day) and high-dose (40 to 50 mg/kg/day) aspirin produced similar coronary artery lesion rates and IVIG non-response rates, whereas the lower dose halved the rate of adverse drug reactions.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Comparative Study

Title: Combined use of orbital soft tissue volume and retinal microvessel density for diagnosing dysthyroid optic neuropathy.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To (i) detect changes in orbital soft tissue and retinal microstructure occurring in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), (ii) investigate the relationship between these variables and their bearing on visual impairment, and (iii) determine their combined diagnostic utility for dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON).
METHODS: Enrolled in this retrospective study were patients with TAO eyes, which included the DON group, equivocal DON (eDON) and non-DON (nDON). Patients were divided into three experimental groups: DON (n = 18 eyes), eDON (n = 24 eyes), and nDON (n = 20 eyes). At the same time, a healthy control (C) group was included (n = 30 eyes). A three-dimensional (3D) volume index, obtained by reconstructing orbital soft tissue via computed tomography (CT) and Mimics software, was used. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) was used to monitor and record retinal microstructural properties, i.e., microvessel density and thickness.
RESULTS: The DON group had significantly lower density and thickness of the retinal vasculature compared to the other groups (p < 0.05), with the exception of deep macular capillary density (MDRCP-VD), which was not statistically significant. In terms of soft-tissue volumes, the DON group had considerably higher orbital fat (OFV/BOV) and extraocular muscle indices (EOMV/BOV) than did the other groups; in contrast, the muscle cone inner volume index (MCIV/BOV) was lower (p < 0.05). A combination of the macular superficial retinal capillary plexuses (MSCRP-VD), optic nerve head vessel density-whole images (ONH-wiVD), MCIV/BOV, and EOMV/BOV yielded the highest values (AUC: 0.954, sensitivity: 95%, specificity: 88.1%) for the diagnosis of DON compared to the other groups.
CONCLUSIONS: EOMV/BOV plus MCIV/BOV, combined with MSRPC-VD plus ONH-wiVD, appears to provide the most accurate diagnostic guideline for DON. Further, 3D reconstructions of orbital soft tissue, in conjunction with OCT-A images, offer an innovative approach not only for preventing permanent loss of vision but also for enhancing the accuracy of diagnosing DON and its early stages.

Title: Immediate Hemodynamic Effects of Pulmonary Artery Flow Restrictors in Univentricular Circulation: Hypothesis-Generating Insights from High-Fidelity Physiologic Streaming Data Using Machine-Learning.
Abstract: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome has been historically palliated with the surgical Norwood or hybrid procedures. Transcatheter placement of pulmonary flow restrictors (PFR) with prostaglandin to maintain an unobstructed ductus arteriosus has emerged as an option for single-ventricle patients that are poor surgical candidates. High-fidelity physiologic data has been used to predict outcomes in interstage patients. This study aimed to characterize the acute hemodynamic effects of transcatheter flow restrictors on pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio using physiologic data. A single-center retrospective review of 10 patients who underwent transcatheter flow restrictor placement was performed. High-fidelity physiologic data (1-second resolution) from before, during, and after flow restrictor placement were utilized. Data were aggregated with the Sickbay Clinical Platform. An autoregressive integrated moving average model was used to compare variables of interest before, during, and after flow restrictor placement. A total of 10 patients were included in the study for a total of 123,509 patient seconds of monitoring. A statistically significant decrease in pulmonary-to-systemic blood flow ratio, systemic saturation, and renal oxygen extraction, and an increase in blood pressure, were observed during and after PFR placement. Flow restrictor placement is associated with an acute decrease in calculated pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio and an increase in calculated renal oxygen extraction ratio (related to an increase in systemic oxygen delivery). More importantly, this study demonstrates that high-fidelity physiologic data platforms can be used for real-time assessment of the effect of pulmonary artery flow reducers. Eventually, clinical decision algorithms may be able to guide the pulmonary artery flow reducer strategy, both intra-procedurally and afterward.

Title: Distribution patterns of postmortem intravascular gas on PMCT in natural deaths.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postmortem intravascular gas is a frequent PMCT finding, yet its forensic interpretation remains uncertain. This study investigated whether early postmortem intravascular gas distribution demonstrates reproducible systemic distribution patterns or is associated with the postmortem interval.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed 247 autopsy-confirmed natural deaths. Cases with trauma, visible putrefaction, or invasive airway management were excluded to prevent artifacts. Intravascular gas was graded (0-3) in hepatic, coronary, and cerebral vessels on pre-autopsy Postmortem Computed Tomography (PMCT). Statistical analyses evaluated associations with PMI and systemic association.
RESULTS: Gas frequently appeared in hepatic (50.6%) and coronary (51.4%) vessels, but rarely in the cerebral vasculature (9.7%). No significant linear correlation existed between gas grade and PMI across any territory. Instead, distribution demonstrated a strong systemic association between the hepatic and coronary systems (ρ = 0.765). Cerebral gas was observed only in conjunction with hepatic and coronary gas, while isolated cerebral gas was not identified.
CONCLUSION: During the early postmortem interval, intravascular gas did not demonstrate a reliable association with PMI. Instead, it follows a predictable systemic association between the hepatic, coronary, and cerebral vascular systems. Deviations from this systemic pattern, specifically isolated cerebral gas on PMCT, lead us to hypothesize that such findings may indicate antemortem etiologies such as air embolism or barotrauma, warranting future validation.

Title: Spatial corneal endothelial cell loss after preserflo microshunt implantation: association with tube insertion position.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate spatial corneal endothelial cell density (ECD) changes after PreserFlo MicroShunt™ (PFM) implantation and identify tube-related factors associated with localized endothelial cell loss.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective clinical study.
METHODS: This study included 118 eyes of 118 patients with medically refractory glaucoma who underwent PFM implantation and were followed for ≥6 months. Anterior-segment optical coherence tomography was used to evaluate tube-cornea distance, tube-cornea angle, and intracameral tube length. Gonioscopic images obtained 1 month postoperatively were used to classify tube insertion as iris-side, trabecular, or corneal-side. ECD was measured at nine corneal regions using specular microscopy. The primary outcome was the ECD reduction rate at the tube insertion site (Position 3) at 3 and 6 months. Linear mixed-effects models were used to identify factors associated with localized endothelial cell loss.
RESULTS: Tube insertion locations were iris-side in 36 eyes, trabecular in 73 eyes, and corneal-side in 9 eyes. In the primary linear mixed-effects analysis, compared with iris-side insertion, both trabecular-contact insertion (β = 12.8%, P = 0.026) and corneal-side insertion (β = 28.6%, P = 0.007) were associated with greater localized endothelial cell loss after multivariable adjustment. Central ECD reduction was mild (2.1% at 6 months).
CONCLUSIONS: Early localized endothelial cell loss after PFM implantation was associated with tube insertion position, particularly corneal-side insertion. Central ECD measurements may underestimate localized endothelial cell loss.

Title: Association between distance from the angle recess to the tube entry site and corneal endothelial cell loss after PreserFlo MicroShunt implantation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT)-derived tube parameters and corneal endothelial cell density (ECD) changes after PreserFlo MicroShunt (PMS) surgery in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and exfoliation glaucoma (XFG).
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.
METHODS: This study included pseudophakic patients with POAG or XFG who underwent PMS implantation. ECD was measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post operatively, and every 6 months thereafter. Intracameral tube parameters, including tube position and length, were assessed using AS-OCT images obtained 1 month postoperatively. Associations between OCT parameters and the monthly rate of ECD change (ECD slope) were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Mean preoperative ECD was 2384 ± 391 cells/mm2. Mean follow-up period was 15 ± 7 months, with 5.1 ± 1.3 ECD measurements per eye. Tube parameters did not differ significantly between POAG (67 eyes of 61 patients) and XFG (18 eyes of 16 patients). The mean ECD slope was -11.8 ± 2.2 cells/mm2/month in XFG and -9.8 ± 1.1 cells/mm2/month in POAG (p = 0.38). A greater distance from the angle recess to the intracameral tube entry site was significantly associated with a more negative ECD slope in both XFG and POAG groups (p = 0.02 and 0.03). Its contribution to ECD slope variance was greater in XFG than in POAG (R2 = 0.243 vs. 0.069).
CONCLUSION: A longer distance from the angle recess to the intracameral tube entry site may predict accelerated ECD loss after PMS implantation, particularly in XFG.

Title: A retrospective analysis of treatment switch from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg in nAMD.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Macular neovascularization is one of the most common causes of irreversible vision loss. Intravitreal injections with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor are the treatment of choice. In recent years, new drugs such as faricimab and aflibercept 8 mg have paved the way for longer intervals between intravitreal injections. However, there are currently very few comparative studies on these longer-acting drugs.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients with at least three consecutive intravitreal injections of faricimab due to neovascular age-related macular degeneration who were subsequently switched from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg in 2024. The primary outcome was the change in central retinal thickness as measured by optical coherence tomography. The secondary outcome was best-corrected visual acuity.
RESULTS: 41 eyes of 38 patients were included. There were no statistically significant changes in retinal thickness. Best-corrected visual acuity showed a trend towards deterioration, however not statistically significant. One patient experienced a tear of the retinal pigment epithelium after receiving the first injection of aflibercept 8 mg.
CONCLUSION: This retrospective analysis did not show statistically significant changes in central retinal thickness or best-corrected visual acuity after treatment switch from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg.

Title: Targeting health-related quality of life issues not found with functional outcome measures a year after aneurysm subarachnoid hemorrhage in a Swedish national cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Outcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is often devastating with life time issues also for independent survivors. We aimed to identify health related quality of life (HRQoL) issues in this favorable functional outcome group compared to a sex and age matched general population.
METHODS: We have analyzed data from 634 Swedish aSAH patients from a national prospective study ranging between 2014 and 2018. One year after ictus, functional outcome was analyzed using Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) and HRQoL assessed by Euro-quality of life-5 dimensions-3 levels (EQ-5D-3L). Favorable GOSE (5-8) were found in 471 patients. Age- and sex-matched populations were created by published data from a cross-sectional cohort of 32,597 people living in Stockholm County in 2006. Odds ratios (ORs) for rating a specific EQ-5D-3L level were calculated for each domain. Significance was set at α = 0.001.
RESULTS: Patients reported less mobility problems than the matched general population (9.6% vs 14.7%; OR 0.62 p = 0.002). However, with usual activities significantly more difficulties with moderate, (24.0% vs 10.9%; OR 2.58, p < .001) and any problems (27.0% vs 12.5%; OR 2.58, p < .001) were reported. More issues with extreme anxiety/depression were also reported ((5.3% vs 2.8%; OR 1.94; p = 0.002). Unfavorable GOSE patients were doing worse than the matched population in all levels and dimensions measured (Online Resource 1, 2, 3 and 4).
CONCLUSION: Although patients with favorable functional outcome report good or better mobility compared to their age and sex matched general population, they have significantly more issues with usual activities a year after aSAH more extreme issues with anxiety/depression were also reported To our knowledge, this is the first time EQ-5D-3L data is compared in a national group of aSAH patients with favorable functional outcome to a sex and age matched general population.

Title: Periodontal Disease and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Perspectives.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Periodontal disease has been increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory condition with potential systemic implications, particularly in the cardiovascular system. Heart failure (HF), a pro-inflammatory syndrome with multisystem involvement, remains a major public health burden. This state-of-the-art narrative review aims to analyze the current scientific evidence on the association between periodontal disease and heart failure, emphasizing epidemiological data, cardiac biomarkers, inflammatory mediators, and future perspectives.
RECENT FINDINGS: Current evidence indicates a high prevalence of periodontal disease among patients with HF and suggests associations between periodontal disease and elevated cardiac biomarkers, including NT-proBNP and troponin T, as well as systemic inflammatory mediators such as C-reactive protein, IL-6, and TNF-α. Interventional studies have reported reductions in some of these biomarkers following periodontal treatment, suggesting a potential biological link between periodontal inflammation and HF. However, findings remain heterogeneous, and some studies have failed to demonstrate significant associations. Current evidence supports an association between periodontal disease and heart failure, with systemic inflammation representing a potential biological link. Nevertheless, the heterogeneity of study designs, small sample sizes, and predominance of observational and cross-sectional evidence limit causal inference. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to clarify causal mechanisms and determine whether periodontal prevention and treatment can contribute to integrated strategies for patients with HF.

Title: Quality of Life in Adults With Severe Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cross-Sectional Studies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on the association between severe obesity (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 40 kg/m2) and quality of life (QoL) in adults who had not undergone bariatric surgery or other interventions specifically targeting QoL, and to identify the QoL domains in which lower scores were most consistently observed.
METHODS: Cohort and cross-sectional studies published up to March 2024 were eligible. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023374612). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, CINAHL, and LILACS were searched. Two independent reviewers selected studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute tool. Findings were synthesized narratively and through an exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of absolute SF-36 mean scores.
RESULTS: Twenty cross-sectional studies were included. The SF-36 and its variations were the most frequently used instruments. Across studies with BMI comparison groups, higher BMI categories were generally associated with lower QoL scores. The lowest scores were most consistently observed for physical functioning, role due to physical health, bodily pain, and general health. Among the mental health-related domains, vitality showed the most consistently reduced scores. Between-study heterogeneity was high for most pooled estimates.
CONCLUSION: Across the available cross-sectional evidence, adults with severe obesity generally had lower QoL, particularly in physical domains. However, substantial heterogeneity and the absence of longitudinal evidence limit certainty and preclude causal interpretation. Longitudinal studies using standardized QoL measures are needed.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Circulating Natural Killer Cells in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Neuropathy Are Altered in Their Frequency and Exhibit Impaired Functions and Angiogenic Activities.
Journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
Abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), a severe vascular complication associated with amputation and high mortality, exhibit chronic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. We previously reported an increased frequency of natural killer (NK) cells in advanced CLTI; however, whether NK cell alterations are already present in patients with peripheral neuropathy, which often precedes diabetic foot lesions with or without distal macroangiopathy, remains unclear. We conducted an observational pilot study to assess circulating NK cell frequency by flow cytometry and inflammatory plasma cytokines profiling by ELISA in 177 subjects stratified into five groups: healthy controls (HC, n = 25); T2DM without neurovascular complications (D, n = 26); non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM without foot lesions (N, n = 40); non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM with lower-limb ulcers/lesions/osteomyelitis (N1, n = 42); and macrovascular revascularized neuropathic T2DM with ulcers/lesions/osteomyelitis (NV, n = 44). NK cell subset frequencies were evaluated in an independent cohort of patients with non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM (n = 22) and healthy controls (n = 23). NKs were further characterized for degranulation capacity, secretome composition, and pro-angiogenic activity in vitro and in vivo (Hirudo verbana). NK cell frequency was significantly increased in patients with non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM compared with controls and was accompanied by elevated plasma levels of soluble mediators associated with NK cell activation and function, including TNF-α, IL-12p70, MCP-1, and IL-4. NKs from these patients exhibited impaired degranulation and reduced angiogenic capacity in vitro and in vivo. Their secretome is characterized by decreased release of pro-angiogenic factors and increased secretion of mediators involved in monocyte/macrophage recruitment, resulting in enhanced macrophage recruitment in vivo. If confirmed in larger cohorts, higher frequency and functional impairment of circulating NKs may act as novel therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers in peripheral vascular complications of T2DM.

Title: Identification of Macrophage Polarization-Related Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma Using Integrated Bioinformatics.
Abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is an incurable hematologic neoplasm with heterogeneous prognosis. Within the bone marrow microenvironment, macrophage polarization (MP) contributes to immune remodeling and may influence disease progression, yet MP-related prognostic biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic data from UCSC Xena (n = 844) and GSE4581 (n = 414) to identify differentially expressed genes between immune-hot and immune-cold MM samples stratified by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA)-derived immune scores. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and intersection with published MP-related genes yielded candidate genes, which were further refined using univariate Cox regression combined with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) machine learning algorithms to construct a prognostic model. An eight-gene signature (LGALS3, IL2RG, ADAM8, MERTK, ACSS1, ARSK, CBX6 and SOCS3) was established, demonstrating acceptable discriminatory ability for 1-, 2-, and 3-year overall survival (AUC 0.666-0.736 in training cohort). Risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration patterns, predicted drug sensitivity, and survival outcomes. A predicted competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network centered on MERTK and SOCS3 was also constructed. These findings identify eight MP-related hub genes as candidate prognostic biomarkers and provide a risk model with acceptable predictive performance, offering insights into the immune-metabolic interplay in MM and suggesting potential avenues for personalized therapeutic strategies.

Title: Taohong Siwu Decoction-Based Targeted Drug Penetration Therapy for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Hip Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Postoperative lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a common complication after hip fracture surgery, and complementary strategies targeting coagulation, inflammation, and venous circulation may provide additional preventive benefits. This retrospective cohort study included 86 patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between June 2023 and June 2024. Patients were assigned to a control group (n = 43), receiving standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis, or an observation group (n = 43), receiving additional Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy. The primary outcome was postoperative lower limb DVT within 10 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included coagulation parameters, inflammatory markers, femoral venous blood flow velocities, postoperative pain, limb swelling, and treatment-related adverse events. DVT occurred in 1/43 patients (2.33%) in the observation group and 10/43 patients (23.26%) in the control group (Fisher's exact P = 0.007). In a parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age and baseline D-dimer, adjunctive therapy remained associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative DVT (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.68, P = 0.017). After 10 days of treatment, the observation group had lower Faces Pain Scale-Revised scores and limb swelling, longer activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, lower D-dimer levels, higher common and superficial femoral vein blood flow velocities, and lower serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 levels than the control group (all P < 0.05). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in overall adverse-event occurrence, and no severe treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy combined with standard anticoagulation was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative DVT and favorable differences in coagulation, inflammatory, and venous hemodynamic parameters.

Title: Machine Learning and Post-Hoc Feature Attribution for Predicting Cardiac MRI Motion Artifacts: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Anxiety-induced motion artifacts frequently compromise image quality during non-sedated cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), leading to rescans and increased healthcare burdens. This retrospective cohort study hypothesized that combining multidimensional psychological and physiological indicators could accurately predict artifact occurrence. Baseline data from 514 adult patients, encompassing 15 clinical features, were systematically analyzed. Four machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The eXtreme Gradient Boosting model demonstrated the highest discriminative ability (AUC = 0.875). To provide clinical transparency, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was applied, revealing that state anxiety (evaluated via the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory State subscale, STAI-State), maximum breath-hold duration, and heart rate variability were primarily associated with artifact risk. The novelty of this approach lies in uncovering non-linear threshold effects-such as a sharp risk escalation when STAI-State scores exceeded 45-and complex interactions between physical capacity and claustrophobia. In conclusion, this interpretable machine learning framework offers a robust tool for patient-specific risk stratification, suggesting that preemptive and targeted nursing interventions could be optimized based on individualized algorithmic predictions.

Title: Molecular Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid in Fixed Skin Biopsies: A Simplified Sample Preparation Method.
Abstract: Hereditary transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis (ATTRv) is associated with peripheral neuropathy resulting from the accumulation of fibrillar TTR amyloid deposits in tissues including peripheral nerves and skin. Accurate diagnosis requires molecular identification of amyloid deposits in tissue specimens. Skin punch biopsy is a minimally invasive, well-established diagnostic tool used to confirm small-fiber neuropathy. Congo-red (CR) staining confirms amyloid deposition but does not determine amyloid type. Identification of TTR proteins within deposits commonly employs immunohistochemistry, which is limited by non-specific binding to blood-derived proteins and can lead to misdiagnosis. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) of laser micro-dissected amyloid fibrils precisely identifies deposited proteins but requires specialized equipment available only in dedicated medical centers. This study describes a streamlined protocol for extracting insoluble amyloid proteins from Zamboni-fixed skin biopsies for subsequent Western blotting (WB) and LC-MS/MS. The protocol includes: (a) tissue collection by cryo-sectioning of biopsy samples; (b) removal of soluble background proteins by repeated phosphate buffer rinsing; (c) extraction of insoluble proteins with formic acid; (d) removal of the volatile solvent by vacuum evaporation and lyophilization. In a proof-of-concept cohort of 24 biopsies, 15-kDa and 30-kDa immunoreactive bands consistent with TTR monomer and dimer forms were detected in 10 of 12 CR-positive, genetically confirmed ATTRv samples and in none of 12 CR-negative neurological controls. This corresponded to an estimated sensitivity of 83.3% (95% confidence interval [CI], 55.2%-97.0%) and specificity of 100% (95% CI, 75.8%-100%) within this selected cohort. An in-gel LC-MS/MS analysis of excised 15 kDa and 30 kDa bands confirmed TTR identity in WB-positive samples tested. The findings were also in concordance with an LC-MS/MS analysis of micro-dissected CR-positive fibril deposits in three tested biopsies. This protocol expands the analytical use of routinely collected skin biopsies and provides an accessible proof-of-concept approach for TTR detection.

Title: Association of Admission Serum Homocysteine with Discharge Neurocognitive Dysfunction after Acute Cerebrovascular Disease in a High-Altitude Setting.
Abstract: Discharge-phase neurocognitive abnormalities may affect rehabilitation participation, self-management, and discharge safety after acute cerebrovascular disease, but early clinically accessible correlates remain incompletely defined. We examined the association between admission serum homocysteine and clinically adjudicated discharge neurocognitive dysfunction in a high-altitude clinical setting. This single-center retrospective cohort included 227 adults admitted for acute ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or transient ischemic attack. The first available serum homocysteine measurement within 24 h of hospital arrival was analyzed continuously and by cohort-derived tertiles. The primary outcome was neurocognitive dysfunction documented within 24-48 h before discharge and adjudicated independently by two reviewers blinded to homocysteine levels; standardized cognitive instruments were not systematically available. Logistic regression was sequentially adjusted for demographic, renal, neurological, neuroimaging, and cerebrovascular phenotype-related factors. Among 227 patients, 98 (43.2%) had discharge neurocognitive dysfunction. Admission homocysteine was higher in patients with dysfunction than in those without dysfunction (18.3 ± 6.2 vs. 12.4 ± 4.7 µmol/L, P < 0.001), and dysfunction prevalence increased from 22.4% in T1 to 38.5% in T2 and 69.9% in T3 (P for trend < 0.001). In the primary fully adjusted model, each 1 µmol/L increase in homocysteine was associated with higher odds of dysfunction (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.07-1.21, P < 0.001), and T3 versus T1 remained associated with the outcome (OR 4.36, 95% CI 2.00-9.51, P < 0.001). Estimates were similar in prespecified sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of delirium or positive confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU) screening and restriction to acute ischemic stroke. Higher admission homocysteine was associated with discharge-phase neurocognitive dysfunction, supporting prospective evaluation of homocysteine as a potential marker of short-term neurocognitive vulnerability rather than a validated predictor of persistent post-stroke cognitive impairment.

Title: Sacubitril/Valsartan Improves Cardiovascular Outcomes in Elderly Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Hypertension: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Elderly patients with concurrent coronary artery disease (CAD) and hypertension face elevated risks of cardiovascular events and require therapies that balance efficacy, safety, and tolerability. Sacubitril/valsartan has demonstrated benefits in heart failure management, but evidence regarding its long-term cardiovascular outcomes in this specific population remains limited. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 150 elderly patients with CAD and hypertension to compare the effects of sacubitril/valsartan versus amlodipine, both combined with conventional therapy.
