The primary endpoint was the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 12 months. Two MACE definitions were applied in this study. Primary analysis used our predefined composite endpoint, including aggravated heart failure and arrhythmia events. A sensitivity analysis adopted the conventional MACE definition (myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, revascularization), excluding isolated ventricular premature beats. Secondary endpoints included blood pressure control, cardiac function parameters, and treatment-related adverse events. Results showed that patients treated with sacubitril/valsartan had a significantly lower incidence of MACE (10.26% vs. 27.14%, P = 0.008), superior blood pressure control, and improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) compared to the amlodipine group. Cox proportional hazards regression (Cox regression) analysis identified sacubitril/valsartan treatment as an independent protective factor against cardiovascular adverse events (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.38, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.80, P = 0.011). Both regimens were well-tolerated, with no severe adverse events reported. These findings indicate that sacubitril/valsartan is an effective and safe therapeutic option for elderly patients with CAD and hypertension, reducing long-term cardiovascular risk while improving blood pressure control and cardiac function.

Title: A Standardized Workflow for Multimodal Assessment of Right-to-Left Shunt-Related Ischemic Brain Injury.
Abstract: Right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been associated with cryptogenic stroke, migraine, and other neurological conditions in which ischemic brain injury may be clinically relevant. In routine practice, however, assessment is often fragmented. Shunt presence may be documented, but shunt burden, provoked versus non-provoked patterns, anatomical complexity, and MRI-defined brain injury are not always integrated into a reproducible workflow. Here, we describe a standardized protocol for multimodal assessment of RLS-related ischemic brain injury in a clinically selected cohort. The workflow includes patient screening, exclusion of major vascular and systemic factors that could independently contribute to brain parenchymal injury, contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler ultrasound (c-TCD) confirmation and shunt grading, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) classification, transthoracic and/or transesophageal echocardiographic anatomical assessment, structured data extraction, and dataset cleaning. To improve reproducibility, the protocol also standardizes key coding steps, including shunt-grade harmonization, classification of RLS as simple or complex, and interpretation of D-dimer values reported below the assay threshold. Using this workflow, a harmonized analytic cohort of 60 RLS-positive patients was established. MRI identified 23 MRI-negative and 37 MRI-positive patients. Representative analyses showed that MRI-positive findings were more frequent in patients with greater shunt burden and more complex anatomical phenotypes. This protocol provides an operational model for incorporating c-TCD, MRI, echocardiography, and structured clinical parameters into the evaluation of MRI-defined ischemic brain injury in RLS-positive patients. It should be interpreted as a workflow for standardized multimodal phenotyping rather than as a standalone physiologic assessment of all clinically significant or hypoxemia-related RLS.

Title: Association of Lipid Profile and Atherogenic Indices With Dietary Adherence in Paediatric Coeliac Disease.
Journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
Abstract:
AIM: The association of adherence to a gluten-free diet (GFD) on lipid metabolism and cardiovascular risk markers in paediatric coeliac disease (CD) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate lipid profile parameters and atherogenic indices according to dietary adherence in children with CD.
METHODS: Children aged 3-18 years with CD were retrospectively evaluated. GFD adherence was assessed using clinical findings, serology, and patient and/or parental reports. Lipid parameters and atherogenic indices were compared according to GFD adherence. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between GFD adherence and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI.
RESULTS: A total of 149 children included in the study; 106 (71.1%) were classified as diet-adherent and 43 (28.9%) as diet-nonadherent. HDL-C levels were significantly higher in children adhering to a GFD (55.3 vs. 46 mg/dL, p < 0.001), whereas total cholesterol, low-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol, triglyceride, and glucose levels were similar between groups. Castelli-Risk-Index-I, Castelli-Risk-Index-II, Atherogenic-Coefficient, and Atherogenic-Index-of-Plasma were significantly lower in children adhering to a GFD (all p < 0.05). Triglyceride-Glucose-Index did not differ between groups (p = 0.430). Dietary adherence remained an independent predictor of higher HDL-C levels after adjustment for age, sex, and body-mass-index (B = 8.253, 95% CI: 3.972-12.534, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: GFD adherence was associated with higher HDL-C levels and a more favourable profile of lipid-derived atherogenic indices in children with CD. These findings suggest an association between adherence to a GFD and HDL-C-related lipid parameters; however, prospective studies are needed to determine the temporal and causal relationships between dietary adherence and metabolic outcomes.

Title: Investigating Factors Associated with the Occurrence of Atrial Fibrillation after Non-cardiothoracic Surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the occurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) after cardiac and thoracic surgery is common and leads to serious complications such as patients' vital organ dysfunction, pulmonary edema, myocardial infarction, and death, evidence about the occurrence and risk factors associated with post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) as new AF immediately after non-cardiac thoracic surgery is limited. Therefore, the present study aimed at investigating the factors related to the occurrence of POAF after non-cardiothoracic surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present retrospective study was conducted on 272 patients undergoing non-cardiothoracic surgeries during 2007-2020. Patients' basic and clinical information including age, sex, BMI, addiction, comorbidities, history of non-cardiac thoracic surgery, history of cardiac surgery, history of chronic kidney disease (CKD), history of ischemic heart disease (IHD), history of heart failure (HF), valvular heart disease (VHD), and the occurrence or non-occurrence of POAF was extracted from their records and then documented.
RESULTS: In the present study, 48.1% and 51.9% of patients were with and without POAF, respectively. Risk factors associated with increasing the odds of POAF occurrence included age (OR = 1.094), anemia (OR = 3.947), IHD (OR = 4.23), CKD (OR = 4.765), VHD (OR = 4.781), pulmonary diseases (OR = 7.828), hypertension (HTN) (OR = 8.336), HF (OR = 11.790), and post-thoracic surgery (OR = 49.072) (P-value < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: According to the results of the present study, aging, comorbidities (i.e., anemia, pulmonary diseases, HTN, and CKD), heart diseases (i.e., IHD, VHD, and HF), and post-thoracic surgery were among the most significant risk factors associated with the increased occurrence of POAF.

Title: Tocilizumab in Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: This systematic review synthesizes the randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence for tocilizumab, an interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor antagonist, as an adjunctive therapy in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). IL-6 is a central mediator of the inflammatory response that follows myocardial infarction and contributes to ischemia-reperfusion injury, positioning its blockade as a plausible cardioprotective strategy. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus for RCTs of tocilizumab administered during the acute phase of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) versus placebo or standard of care; risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Given the substantial heterogeneity in population, dosing, and primary endpoints, findings were synthesized narratively rather than pooled. Four trials comprising 439 analyzed patients met the eligibility criteria, spanning NSTEMI and STEMI populations and both intravenous and subcutaneous dosing regimens, one of which was stopped early for futility. In the three intravenously dosed trials, tocilizumab more than halved the C-reactive protein area under the curve relative to placebo (all p < 0.001), with two trials also showing lower troponin release. One trial additionally demonstrated a significant improvement in myocardial salvage index and reduced microvascular obstruction on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI), without significant benefit on the final infarct size or six-month clinical outcomes; a separate, higher-risk trial found no significant benefit on infarct size, troponin, or neurohormonal activation despite comparable suppression of inflammation. Major adverse cardiac events did not differ significantly between arms in either trial assessing this endpoint, and the smallest, subcutaneously dosed trial raised an unreplicated cardiac tamponade signal. Two of the four trials were judged overall low risk of bias. Tocilizumab consistently attenuates the acute inflammatory response and, in one trial, improves imaging surrogates of myocardial salvage, but evidence for clinical benefit is absent, and the trial base remains too small and heterogeneous to support meta-analytic pooling or practice change. Larger, adequately powered trials with harmonized endpoints and blinded safety adjudication are needed.

Title: Dosimetric Impact of Simultaneous and Separate Planning with Fixed/Iris Collimators on Brain Doses in Multiple Brain Metastases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CyberKnife® stereotactic radiosurgery enables frameless, image-guided treatment of multiple brain metastases. Collimator type (Fixed vs. Iris) and planning strategy (Simultaneous vs. Separate) may influence low-dose normal brain exposure, plan quality, and treatment delivery efficiency.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare the dosimetric performance of different collimator types and planning strategies in patients with three or four brain metastases under standardized planning conditions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty patients were retrospectively replanned using four treatment configurations: Fixed Separate, Fixed Simultaneous, Iris Separate, and Iris Simultaneous. All plans were generated using identical prescription doses and planning objectives. Dosimetric evaluation included normal brain V8, V10, V12 (volumes receiving ≥8 Gy, ≥10 Gy, and ≥12 Gy), mean brain dose (Vmean), Paddick conformity index (PCI), and gradient index (GI). Comparisons were performed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Estimated treatment time was recorded for all plans.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed for V8 (P = 0.039), Vmean (P = 0.019), and PCI (P < 0.001), whereas V10 (P = 0.180), V12 (P = 0.103), and GI (P = 0.420) showed no significant differences among the planning approaches. Median dosimetric values tended to favor Iris Simultaneous planning for reducing low-dose normal brain exposure. The significant PCI difference was primarily attributable to lower conformity in the Iris Separate plans. Total planning target volume demonstrated a near-significant positive association with V12 (P = 0.057). Iris-based plans were associated with shorter estimated treatment times.
CONCLUSION: Under standardized planning conditions, Iris Simultaneous planning demonstrated favorable trends in reducing low-dose normal brain exposure while improving treatment delivery efficiency. Although conformity differed significantly among planning approaches, mainly because of lower PCI values in the Iris Separate plans, dose gradient characteristics remained comparable. These findings suggest that planning strategy may influence conformity more than dose fall-off in CyberKnife treatment of multiple brain metastases. Nevertheless, given the limited sample size, these results should be interpreted cautiously and validated in larger prospective studies.

Title: Acute deoxygenation during M-TEER: a note of caution.
Journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
Abstract:
AIMS: Right-to-left (R-L) shunting through an iatrogenic atrial septal defect (iASD) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication. We aimed to identify factors associated with clinically relevant R-L shunting requiring emergency iASD closure.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed 444 consecutive patients undergoing successful M-TEER between 2017 and 2026. Clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive haemodynamic parameters were compared between patients requiring emergency iASD closure and the remaining cohort. Six patients (1.3%) required emergency iASD closure due to R-L shunting and acute deoxygenation. All presented with severe tricuspid regurgitation, RV dilatation, and impaired RV function. Following M-TEER, right atrial pressure exceeded left atrial pressure in five patients. Compared with controls, affected patients demonstrated reduced tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (15 ± 2 vs. 19 ± 4 mm), fractional area change (FAC) (27 ± 5% vs. 43 ± 6%), and RV free wall strain (-13 ± 2% vs. -22 ± 5%). Echocardiography underestimated invasively measured systolic pulmonary artery pressure (25.8 vs. 40.3 mmHg; P = 0.035). Oxygen saturation decreased by 3-8%, with one patient developing cardiogenic shock.
CONCLUSION: Severe tricuspid regurgitation, RV dysfunction, and elevated right atrial pressure may identify patients at risk for clinically relevant R-L shunting after M-TEER. Comprehensive RV assessment, including FAC and strain, combined with invasive hemodynamic evaluation, may improve risk stratification and facilitate timely iASD closure.

Title: Potentially Clinically Relevant Drug-Drug Interactions with Direct Oral Anticoagulants: Prevalence and Contributing Factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are widely prescribed but remain susceptible to drug-drug interactions (DDIs) that increase bleeding or thrombotic risk. The real-world prevalence and factors associated with potentially clinically relevant DDIs in patients on chronic DOAC therapy require further study.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of clinically relevant DDIs involving DOACs and identify patient- and treatment-related factors associated with their occurrence.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among hospitalized adults receiving a DOAC as a home medication. Potentially clinically relevant DDIs were identified from documented home medications using the Lexicomp Online 2025 Drug Interactions database and classified as category C (monitor therapy), D (consider modification), and X (avoid combination). Clinical bleeding, thromboembolic, or other adverse outcomes were not assessed. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression analyzed patient characteristics and factors associated with DDIs.
RESULTS: Among 870 patients (mean age 71.4 ± 13.0 years), 72.8% had at least one potentially clinically relevant DDI. Among patients with at least one potentially clinically relevant DDI, 47.4% had multiple interactions. Most were Category C (97.6%), primarily involving antidepressants with antiplatelet activity (30.4%), antiplatelet agents (30.0%), amiodarone (8.5%), and NSAIDs (7.9%). Category D and X interactions (2.4%) mainly involved CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors or inducers such as dronedarone, erythromycin, and phenytoin. Independent predictors of DDI occurrence included the number of medications (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.09-1.19; p < 0.0001), coronary artery disease (OR 1.55; p = 0.039), anxiety (OR 2.02; p = 0.016), dementia (OR 2.99; p = 0.006), and depression (OR 3.27; p = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Potentially clinically relevant DDIs involving DOACs were common in this hospitalized cohort, although most identified interactions were Category C and therefore primarily warranted monitoring. Higher medication burden and several comorbidities, including coronary artery disease, depression, anxiety and dementia were associated with the presence of potentially clinically relevant DDIs. Vigilant medication review is essential to enhance safety.

Title: Nomogram for predicting post-percutaneous coronary intervention restenosis in patients with coronary artery disease and diabetes: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) combined with diabetes mellitus (DM) significantly increases the risk of vascular restenosis following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Despite advancements in stent technology, restenosis remains a concern, especially in diabetic patients. This study aims to predict restenosis risk using serum metabolites and risk factors.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 272 CAD and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients who underwent PCI between January 2020 and June 2023. Based on one-year angiographic follow-up, patients were divided into restenosis (n = 121) and non-restenosis groups (n = 151). Serum metabolites and biomarkers, including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), were evaluated, together with procedure-related characteristics (including stent type and post-procedural percentage diameter stenosis) and medication use (including calcium antagonists). Logistic regression and correlation analysis identified significant predictors, and a nomogram prediction model was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Lower HbA1c levels were associated with restenosis (rho = -0.142, P = 0.008; OR = 0.767, 95% CI [0.625-0.941]). Higher levels of IGF-I (rho = 0.328, P < 0.001; OR = 1.053, 95% CI [1.032-1.075]), LDL-C (r = 0.135, P = 0.025; OR = 1.682, 95% CI [1.107-2.555]), TNF-α (r = 0.172, P = 0.004; OR = 1.434, 95% CI [1.119-1.838]), and hsCRP (r = 0.179, P = 0.003; OR = 1.786, 95% CI [1.185-2.693]) were also significantly associated. Non-drug-eluting stents (DES) and higher percentage diameter stenosis (%DS) increased restenosis risk. Calcium antagonists use was negatively correlated with restenosis (r =  - 0.185, P = 0.002; OR = 0.449, 95% CI [0.228-0.884]). The nomogram model demonstrated good discrimination for restenosis (apparent AUC = 0.833; bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.808).
CONCLUSION: This study identified key predictive factors for post-PCI restenosis in CAD patients with DM through case-control analysis. The nomogram model showed good discrimination on internal bootstrap validation. Pending external validation, it may provide a useful exploratory tool to support risk stratification and inform management aimed at reducing the restenosis burden in high-risk cardiovascular populations.

Title: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (MICS-CABG) Versus Conventional Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (OPCAB): A Single-Center Analysis of Early Outcomes and Institutional Experience.
Abstract: Background Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG) through an anterolateral mini-thoracotomy is an alternative to conventional coronary artery bypass grafting through median sternotomy. However, evidence regarding its early clinical outcomes and institutional learning phase remains limited in developing healthcare systems. Objectives To compare the baseline clinical characteristics, intraoperative parameters, and early postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing MICS-CABG with those undergoing conventional off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB). Methods This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with multivessel coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent surgical coronary revascularization at our cardiovascular institute. Patients undergoing non-CABG cardiac procedures or those with incomplete clinical records were excluded. Data were collected on demographic characteristics, cardiovascular comorbidities, operative parameters, duration of postoperative mechanical ventilation, chest tube drainage, and early postoperative complications. Results A total of 80 patients were included, comprising 40 patients who underwent MICS-CABG and 40 who underwent conventional OPCAB. Both groups had a high prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors, including type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. The mean duration of postoperative mechanical ventilation was 8.80 ± 3.97 hours in the MICS-CABG group compared with 4.22 ± 2.64 hours in the OPCAB group. Mean postoperative chest tube drainage was 887.0 ± 611.8 mL in the MICS-CABG group and 328.9 ± 116.1 mL in the OPCAB group. No perioperative mortality occurred in either group, and no conversion from MICS-CABG to median sternotomy was observed. Conclusion MICS-CABG was technically feasible in this early institutional experience, with no perioperative mortality or conversion to sternotomy. However, patients undergoing MICS-CABG had longer postoperative mechanical ventilation and greater chest tube drainage than those undergoing conventional OPCAB. These findings support the feasibility of MICS-CABG while highlighting the need for continued evaluation of outcomes as institutional experience increases.

Title: Joint Association of Questionnaire-Defined COPD and Widened Pulse Pressure with Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Older Chinese Adults: A 7-Year CHARLS Cohort Study.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
PURPOSE: COPD and vascular aging frequently coexist in later life. Whether widened pulse pressure identifies older adults with COPD at particularly high cardiovascular risk is uncertain.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed CHARLS participants aged 60 years or older without baseline heart disease or stroke. Questionnaire-defined COPD and widened pulse pressure (≥60 mmHg) formed four phenotypes. The primary outcome was incident physician-reported heart disease or stroke; all-cause mortality was secondary, and heart disease and stroke were component outcomes. Weighted cause-specific Cox models used respondent weights and household-cluster robust standard errors. Because the joint phenotype was selected after an exploratory screen of candidate vascular indicators, this study should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.
RESULTS: Among 4183 participants, 943 developed incident cardiovascular disease and 685 died. Relative to neither exposure, COPD alone (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.84-1.57) and widened pulse pressure alone (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.70-1.25) were not associated with cardiovascular disease, whereas both exposures were (HR 1.86, 95% CI 1.26-2.76). The cardiovascular association was present for heart disease (HR 2.80, 95% CI 1.94-4.05) but not stroke (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.43-1.65). The composite cardiovascular signal should therefore not be read as a uniform effect across cardiovascular systems. For all-cause mortality, the both-exposure group had 63 deaths among 209 participants and a fully adjusted HR of 2.05 (95% CI 1.54-2.73) versus neither exposure, but mortality was not clearly higher than in the COPD-only group (HR 1.37, 95% CI 0.96-1.95).
CONCLUSION: Coexisting questionnaire-defined COPD and widened pulse pressure was associated with a higher risk of incident cardiovascular disease, primarily reported heart disease, and with higher all-cause mortality than neither exposure, although mortality was not clearly higher than among participants with COPD alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant external validation using objective pulmonary and vascular measures.

Title: Comparative Outcomes of Beta-Blockers vs Non-Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blockers in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Determining the most effective medication regimen to manage blood pressure and heart rate in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) continues to lack a clear clinical consensus. Although beta-blockers (BBs) are widely prescribed, their negative chronotropic effects may worsen exercise intolerance. Alternative agents like verapamil and diltiazem, which belong to the non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (non-DHP CCB) class, offer a physiological alternative, yet comparative data are scarce. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, comparing BBs vs non-DHP CCBs in adults with HFpEF (left ventricular ejection fraction ≥ 50%). A literature search across key databases was conducted up until May 2026. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects analytical framework incorporating the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman variance correction. Evidence certainty was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Of the 576 retrieved records, two observational cohorts (106,848 patients) met the inclusion criteria. Only one of the two eligible cohorts analyzed real patient-level data; the other was generated. The two-study pooled estimates are reported as exploratory: all-cause mortality HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.34-2.26; p = 0.336) and HF hospitalization HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.34-2.42; p = 0.446), with I² > 80% for both outcomes. At k = 2, these dispersion statistics are themselves unstable, and the pooled intervals are not clinically interpretable. Restricted to the single real-world cohort, the estimates were HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.80-0.85) and HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.91-1.05), respectively, which are the figures of one observational study and carry no meta-analytic weight. Cardiovascular mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, exercise capacity, and quality of life were prespecified but reported by neither study in poolable form. The confidence in these findings was rated as very low because the data stem from observational research and exhibit significant statistical variability alongside wide CIs. Current evidence does not demonstrate the prognostic superiority of either BBs or non-DHP CCBs in HFpEF. Given the very low certainty of the available data and high clinical heterogeneity, pharmacological selection should remain individualized. High-quality randomized controlled trials are needed to inform clinical guidelines.

Title: Minithoracotomy approach for redo mitral valve surgery: Feasibility, operative outcomes, and comparative analysis of myocardial protection techniques.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Redo mitral valve surgery (MVS) poses technical challenges and high operative risks as the result of adhesions and sternal re-entry. Right minithoracotomy has emerged as an alternative to repeat sternotomy. This study evaluated feasibility and perioperative outcomes of redo MVS through right minithoracotomy and compared 3 different myocardial protection strategies: cardioplegia, ventricular fibrillation (VF), and beating-heart.
METHODS: All patients who underwent redo MVS via right minithoracotomy between 2015 and 2023 were identified from the Mini-Mitral International Registry. The primary end point was in-hospital mortality. Secondary end points included stroke, low cardiac output, bleeding requiring revision, conversion to sternotomy, and major complications. Moreover, 3 myocardial protection strategies were analyzed: cardioplegic arrest (n = 373), VF (n = 105), and beating-heart (n = 24).
RESULTS: A total of 502 patients were included (median age 68 years). Overall in-hospital mortality was 7.6% (4.1% in elective and 24.4% in urgent cases). Conversion to sternotomy occurred in 3%. Stroke rate was 2.8% and reoperation for bleeding was 8.8%. After adjustment, VF was independently associated with a greater risk of low cardiac output (adjusted odds ratio, 3.5; P = .004). Beating-heart surgery was associated with increased in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 6.6; P = .02). No significant association was observed between myocardial protection strategy and stroke or major complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Redo MVS via right minithoracotomy is feasible and safe in experienced centers. Cardioplegic arrest was associated with more favorable early outcomes and should be considered the default myocardial protection strategy whenever feasible. No-clamp techniques remain valuable in selected high-risk scenarios but are associated with trade-offs that warrant careful patient selection.

Title: Anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with acute ischaemic stroke and cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective single-center study.
Abstract: Anxiety and depressive symptoms may coexist with cognitive dysfunction after stroke. This study characterized their frequency and severity during acute stroke hospitalization in patients with documented cognitive dysfunction. We conducted a retrospective, single-center study of 95 adults with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) and cognitive dysfunction in Romania during 2024-2025. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were derived from neuropsychological conclusions and classified as absent/minimal, mild, moderate, or severe. In the main analysis, "elements" and the depression-specific "tendency" were classified as absent/minimal, while hybrid descriptors were assigned to the adjacent higher category. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative allocations. Associations were assessed using the chi-square, Fisher's exact, or Kruskal-Wallis test. Anxiety severity was available for 94 patients and was distributed as follows: 26.6% absent/minimal, 16.0% mild, 50.0% moderate, and 7.4% severe. The severe category derived from "moderate-severe" descriptors. Overall, 73.4% had anxiety of at least mild severity. Depression severity was available for 86 patients, distributed as 74.4% absent/minimal, 17.4% mild, 7.0% moderate, and 1.2% severe; 25.6% had depression of at least mild severity. Under alternative low-level classifications, the anxiety-depression difference at the at-least-mild threshold narrowed from 47.8 to 28.1 and 9.0 percentage points. Anxiety remained more frequent. Sex was associated with both severity distributions. These proportions reflect documented severity rather than prevalence estimates derived from a uniform standardized instrument. Anxiety was more frequently documented and more often reached moderate-or-greater severity than depression. Routine neuropsychological conclusions may provide information on the affective profile during this phase of care. Longitudinal studies should examine affective, cognitive, and functional trajectories during recovery.

Title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease-Associated Heart Failure: A Systematic Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study from 1990 to 2021 with Projections up to 2050.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is strongly linked to heart failure (HF), but comprehensive global evaluations of COPD-associated HF remain limited.
METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 data, we assessed prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) of COPD-associated HF. We applied decomposition analysis, Joinpoint regression, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling to evaluate trends by sex, age, sociodemographic index (SDI), and region, and to project burden to 2050.
RESULTS: In 2021, global COPD-associated HF cases exceeded 3.61 million, a 1.4-fold increase since 1990. Age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR) and YLD rates (ASYR) increased overall. Absolute cases and YLDs rose in both sexes, but age-standardized rates declined in males and rose in females. Burden peaked at ages 70-74 and grew fastest among those aged ≥95. The Middle SDI region had the highest counts; East Asia had the highest regional burden, and China the highest national absolute burden. Only High-SDI regions showed rising ASPR and ASYR; most other regions declined, notably Eastern Europe. Projections indicate global increases in ASPR and ASYR from 2022 to 2050, with slightly higher rises in females than males.
CONCLUSION: The global burden of COPD-associated HF continues to rise with substantial heterogeneity and is projected to increase further. Coordinated international efforts and targeted prevention and management are urgently needed.

Title: Identifying a Cardio-Hepatic Phenotype by Integrating the Albumin-Bilirubin Score Into Risk Assessment in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Abstract: Risk stratification is essential in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet the prognostic utility of the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score as a marker of hepatic dysfunction remains underexplored. In this single-center study, we evaluated the clinical, neurohumoral, echocardiographic and hemodynamic correlates and prognostic value of the ALBI score, and to assess whether this score offers an incremental benefit over the Registry to EValuate Early And Long-term pulmonary arterial hypertension disease management (REVEAL) 2.0 risk score in patients with PAH. This study evaluated the prognostic value of the ALBI score and its incremental benefit in a cohort of 380 PAH patients (mean age 47.6 ± 18.3 years, 74.3% female). Patients were stratified into low (<= -2.60) and high (> -2.60) ALBI groups. High ALBI scores were significantly associated with worse functional class, reduced exercise capacity, elevated Nt-proBNP, right ventricular systolic dysfunction, and vena cava plethora (all p < 0.001). Hemodynamically, elevated ALBI correlated with increased right atrial pressure (RAP) (p = 0.005), reduced cardiac index (p = 0.002), and a narrowed trans-systemic pressure gradient (p = 0.001). Multivariable Cox regression demonstrated that ALBI was an independent predictor of mortality [Adjusted HR: 1.80 (95% CI: 1.30-2.49), p < 0.001], outperforming MELD variants and the FIB-4 index. Integrating ALBI into REVEAL 2.0 yielded higher risk discrimination (C-index: 0.756) than adding direct echocardiographic indices of right ventricular function or coupling (C-indices: 0.748-0.749). In sensitivity analyses adjusting for TAPSE/PASP, invasive cardiac index, mean RAP, and background therapy, ALBI maintained its independent prognostic value [Adjusted HR: 1.44 (95% CI: 1.01-2.05), p = 0.044], with the full model achieving a C-index of 0.801. Within the REVEAL 2.0 intermediate-risk subgroup, a high ALBI score identified patients with a three-fold higher mortality risk [HR: 3.04 (95% CI: 1.25-7.38), p = 0.014], improving discriminative performance by 26.3%. The ALBI score independently predicts mortality beyond standard pulmonary hemodynamics and echocardiographic right ventricular parameters. Incorporating ALBI into REVEAL 2.0 enhances survival prediction and aids risk refinement in intermediate-risk PAH.

Title: Mid-term results of the Lugones procedure for scimitar syndrome repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study objective was to report the mid-term outcomes of the Lugones procedure (in situ pericardial rerouting technique) and its variants for scimitar syndrome repair.
METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective descriptive study of patients undergoing scimitar syndrome repair with the Lugones procedure. Three variants were used: original, variant A with atrial septum repositioning, and variant B with an interatrial pericardial flap. Primary end points were survival, freedom from reoperation, and freedom from pulmonary venous obstruction. Follow-up was based on clinical assessment and serial echocardiography; computed tomography scan, magnetic resonance imaging/4-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging, or cardiac catheterization was obtained when echocardiographic assessment was limited, clinical or imaging findings were equivocal, or complementary anatomic/hemodynamic information was sought.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight patients from 11 institutions were included (median age, 5 years; range, 0.7-43). Preoperative scimitar vein stenosis was present in approximately 29%; aortopulmonary collaterals were embolized preoperatively in 24 patients (63%). The original procedure was performed in 28 cases, variant A in 5 cases, and variant B in 5 cases. In-hospital mortality was 0%. Early complications were uncommon (1 postoperative pulmonary venous pathway obstruction due to extrinsic compression; 1 transient diaphragmatic dysfunction). Mean follow-up was 74 months (maximum 13.5 years), with no late deaths, reoperations, recurrent obstruction, or additional late pulmonary venous pathway obstruction. Computed tomography scans consistently demonstrated wide reconstructed pathways; 4-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging showed physiological pulmonary venous flow patterns after repair.
CONCLUSIONS: The Lugones procedure yielded excellent mid-term outcomes with no deaths or reoperations and a very low incidence of postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction.

Title: Understanding the impact of socioeconomic deprivation on inpatient surgical care delivery costs in the Veterans Health Administration.
Abstract: The impact of living in high neighborhood-level socioeconomic deprivation on inpatient surgery cost is not well known. This retrospective cohort study examines the relationship between the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) and noncardiac inpatient surgery costs in the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-cardiac inpatient surgery during 2013-2019 were identified in Veterans Affairs Surgical Quality Improvement Program (VASQIP) data linked to additional VHA data sources. The cohort includes 136,631 predominantly male (97.7%) individuals with mean (SD) age of 72 (6.5) years. The 20,462 individuals with high ADI (>85) were more often Black race (27% vs 13.6%) with higher comorbidity burden (Gagne score 3.4 vs 3.1), higher frailty (29.1 vs 28.7), and more likely presenting with preoperative acute serious conditions (5.6% vs 4.5%) for more urgent (21.3% vs 18.7%) or emergent surgery (8.9% vs 8.1%, all p<0.001). After adjusting for facility and surgery year using regression, mean cost was $988 higher (95% CI: $657, $1319; p<0.001) for individuals with ADI>85. Using unconditional quantile regression, costs were even higher (>$1,600) for patients with ADI>85 at or above the 75th cost quantile. The higher costs among individuals living in high ADI areas were attenuated after controlling for comorbidity and frailty (mean cost difference of -$8; 95% CI: -$312, $296; p=0.96 after adjustment for those factors) and presentation acuity (-$57; 95% CI: -$356, $241; p=0.71). Among older patients undergoing inpatient surgery in the VHA, ADI>85 is associated with higher surgical cost, an effect which is eliminated by controlling for patient comorbidity, frailty, and presentation acuity. These results suggest potential for cost-savings by mitigating barriers to healthcare access, timely surgery access, and other downstream effects of high neighborhood-level socioeconomic deprivation before surgery becomes urgent.

Title: Absence of arrhythmogenic effects in cAMP subcellular compartments supports PDE8 as a target in atrial fibrillation.
Journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology plus
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Targeting Phosphodiesterase 8B (PDE8B) has been proposed as a strategy to restore L-type Ca2+ current (ICa,L) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the effects of total PDE8 inhibition on other Ca2+ handling or 3',5'-cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) nanodomains have not been assessed and thus the potential proarrhythmic consequences are still undetermined.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess whether PDE8 contributes to the regulation of cAMP signaling in other Ca2+ handling-related compartments and to sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release-mediated arrhythmogenic events.
RESULTS: Fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) live-cell imaging, confocal Ca2+ imaging and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) were performed in atrial myocytes and tissues allocated across experimental assays from a total cumulative cohort of 141 patients with or without AF (sinus rhythm, Ctl). cAMP levels were not significantly increased upon non-isoform-selective total PDE8 inhibition in the cytosol, in ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) or in the sarcomere nanodomains, troponin I (TpnI) and myosin binding protein C (MyBP-C). Consistently, no significant changes in the frequency of arrhythmogenic Ca2+ sparks or Ca2+ waves after total PDE8 inhibitor application were detected.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that PDE8 inhibition promotes a compartment-specific regulation of cAMP signaling that exclusively affects the L-type Ca2+ channel in human atrial myocytes. Therefore, PDE8 inhibition can be used to restore ICa,L in patients with AF, without promoting spontaneous arrhythmogenic Ca2+ releases in isolated human atrial myocytes.

Title: Correlation of blood biomarkers with microstructural brain injury in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Abstract: In-hospital mortality among resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains high. Identifying patients who will benefit from intensive care while avoiding prolonged, potentially unnecessary treatments is essential. Blood-based biomarkers provide a novel method for evaluating brain injury. The ability of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and total-tau (t-tau) to measure white and grey matter injury is unestablished in comatose OHCA survivors treated with targeted temperature management (TTM) or xenon combined with TTM. We examined correlations between the biomarkers and white and grey matter injury assessed with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). This was a randomized, single-blind, phase 2 clinical drug trial involving two multipurpose intensive care units in Finland. It was conducted between August 2009 and March 2015. One hundred and ten comatose OHCA patients aged 24 to 76 years were randomly assigned to either inhaled xenon treatment combined with 24-h TTM (33°C) (n = 55, xenon group) or TTM alone (n = 55, control group). MRI data were available from 96 patients, with a median imaging time of 53 h (interquartile range, 47-64 h) after OHCA. Biomarker data were obtained from 105 patients. In the control group of 48 patients, after adjusting for age, sex and site, a disruption of white matter microintegrity as measured by decreased fractional anisotropy (FA) of DTI, the primary endpoint of the trial, showed a significant negative correlation with NfL at 24, 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.28 to -0.37; P < 0.05), NSE at 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.30 to -0.35; P < 0.05) and t-tau only at 72 h (ρ = -0.30; P < 0.05). In the xenon group (n = 48), these correlations were absent at all timepoints. The NfL-FA partial correlations showed progressive divergence between the xenon and control groups, with a statistically significant between-group difference observed at 72 h (ρ = -0.37 versus ρ = 0.14; P = 0.016). Cortical or basal ganglia grey matter mean diffusivity did not have a consistent correlation with biomarker levels at different time points. No statistically significant differences were found between the xenon and control groups in the adjusted geometric mean levels of GFAP, NfL, NSE or t-tau at various time points following OHCA. In conclusion, NfL correlated with FA in controls but not in the xenon group. This between-group difference reached significance at 72 h, suggesting that xenon may modify the relationship between axonal injury and white matter microstructure after OHCA.

Title: Eicosanoids as Biomarkers of Hyperfiltration-Mediated Injury in CKD.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early biomarkers of hyperfiltration-induced injury are not known. We previously reported elevated urinary prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) preceding albuminuria in children with solitary kidney, and upregulated cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2)-PGE2-EP2 axis in unilaterally nephrectomized mice. To determine chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage-associated changes in urinary eicosanoids, baseline urine samples from the CKD in children (CKiD) biorepository (n = 318) and a comparator group of children with enuresis (n = 72) were analyzed.
METHODS: Liquid or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry was used to measure metabolites of arachidonic acid and linoleic acid (ng/mg creatinine, P ≤ 0.05).
RESULTS: The CKiD cohort included children with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) (71%, n = 226) and glomerular disease (29%, n = 92). Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) measurement (Iohexol) showed 27% and 73% of CAKUT subjects at CKD stages 2 and 3, respectively. Among those with glomerular disease, 42% and 58% were at CKD stages 2 and 3, respectively. Comparisons across CKD stages identified increase in urinary PGE2, thromboxane, and dihydroxy eicosatrienoic acids (DHETs), with a decrease in prostacyclin, F2-isoprostane, and 9,10-dihydroxy-octadecenoic acids (DiHOMEs) from CKD stage 2 to 3 indicating perturbed metabolism through COX and cytochrome P-450 (CYP450) pathways. In unadjusted mixed models quantifying the associations of a 2-times higher baseline eicosanoid with initial GFR found prostacyclin, PGE2/prostacyclin ratio, thromboxane/prostacyclin ratio, LTE4, 9,10-DiHOME, and F2-Isoprostane were significantly associated with higher initial GFR and remained significant after adjusting for CAKUT diagnosis, sex and baseline age, proteinuria, and hypertension. However, none of the eicosanoids were associated with change in GFR over time or time to kidney replacement therapy.
CONCLUSION: We report for the first time linoleic acid-derived metabolites in children with CKD. A longitudinal study is needed to validate selected urinary eicosanoids as early biomarkers of hyperfiltration.

Title: Neuroprotective effect of early remote ischaemic post-conditioning after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (RIPOST-CA): study protocol for a randomised, single-blinded, monocentric, controlled trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury is the leading cause of death and long-term disability after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and is driven by the ischaemia-reperfusion syndrome, for which no specific treatment exists. Remote ischaemic post-conditioning (brief, repeated cycles of limb ischaemia and reperfusion delivered with a pneumatic cuff), is protective across ischemia-reperfusion conditions. We aim to assess whether early conditioning reduces hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
METHODS: This single-centre, single-blinded, randomised (1:1) controlled trial with blinded assessment of the outcome, enrols 48 comatose adults resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Participants receive standard post-resuscitation care with three sham cuff sessions, or standard care plus three sessions of conditioning (thigh cuff, four cycles of 5-min inflation at 200 mmHg alternating with 5-min deflation), the first within 4 h of return of spontaneous circulation and repeated at the 12th and 24th hour. Randomisation is stratified by initial rhythm (shockable versus non-shockable). The primary endpoint is the change in serum neurofilament light chain between the 6th and 72nd hour after return of spontaneous circulation. Secondary endpoints include daily Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (days 1-3), serum neuron-specific enolase and protein S100-B kinetics, in-intensive care unit mortality by cause, and a favourable neurological outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at intensive care unit discharge and at 90 days.
CONCLUSION: RIPOST-CA is the first randomised trial to evaluate early remote ischemic post-conditioning on brain-injury biomarkers after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Its results could inform larger clinical trials of this simple, non-invasive intervention.Trial registration number: NCT06473207.

Title: Trigger-based adaptive proton therapy and changes in target coverage and cardiac dose in esophageal cancer.
Journal: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Inter-fractional anatomical variations during proton therapy for esophageal cancer may compromise target coverage and increase dose to surrounding organs. Adaptive replanning can mitigate these effects, but its cumulative dose-based and clinical impact remains insufficiently characterized. We evaluated offline adaptive intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) triggered by target underdose or cardiac overdose using deformable dose accumulation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 192 esophageal cancer patients treated with IMPT was analyzed. Eighty-five underwent adaptive replanning and 107 were treated non-adaptively. Dose accumulation was performed by assigning each fraction to the closest weekly repeat computed tomography (CT) scan and deformably mapping doses to the planning CT. Accumulated doses from adapted and non-adapted plans were compared for internal target volume (ITV) and gross tumor volume (GTV) coverage, target hotspots, heart and lung dose, and normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) for 2-year post-treatment mortality.
RESULTS: Compared with the non-adaptive treatment scenario, the adaptive scenario increased ITV D98% by 1.9 percentage points (pp) and GTV D98% by 0.8 pp. in the target underdose subgroup. In the cardiac overdose subgroup, mean heart dose decreased by 1.0 Gy and heart V40Gy by 1.7 pp., with no increase in mean lung dose. NTCP for 2-year post-treatment mortality decreased by 1.5 pp. in this subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: Trigger-based adaptive IMPT improved cumulative target coverage and cardiac sparing without increasing lung dose. Target underdose and cardiac overdose triggers provided complementary benefits, supporting their use in structured adaptive replanning.

Title: Effects of prenatal early food and micronutrient supplementations on body size and cardiometabolic risk factors in the 15-year-old offspring - the MINIMat randomised trial.
Journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the effects of maternal nutrition during pregnancy on offspring cardiometabolic risk is mixed. We hypothesized that 15-year-olds, whose mothers were randomised to maternal early pregnancy protein-energy supplementation, are taller and have lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol than controls. We also assessed effects of prenatal multiple micronutrient supplementation (MMS) on adolescent body size and cardiometabolic risk factors.
METHODS: In MINIMat trial (Maternal and Infant Nutrition Interventions in Matlab; ISRCTN16581394) in rural Bangladesh, pregnant women were randomised in a 2:3 factorial design to early invitation to food supplementation (around gestational week 9), vs standard programme (usual invitation); MMS was compared with folic acid and iron. Of 3267 singletons with valid birth weight, 2300 (70.4%) were measured height and weight, plasma cardiometabolic biomarkers and blood pressure at 15 years, between September 2017 and June 2019. We analysed data by linear and logistic regression, adjusting for sex, age and prenatal confounders.
FINDINGS: Adolescents whose mothers received early invitation had 0.08 units higher height z score (95% CI 0.01, 0.16) and less of them were stunted (<-2 SD; 17.4% vs 21.4%, risk difference 4.1%; 95% CI 0.8%, 7.3%; OR 0.77; 0.63, 0.95) than usual invitation group. Early invitation and MMS were unrelated to BMI, plasma cardiometabolic biomarkers or blood pressure.
INTERPRETATION: The effect of early prenatal food supplementation on height persists at 15 years. We found no effect of this intervention or MMS on cardiometabolic factors.
FUNDING: Swedish Research Council, Finnish Research Council, Finska Läkaresällskapet, Pediatric Research, Novo Nordisk, Gyllenberg and Jusélius Foundations.

Title: Tip perfusion index for monitoring perioperative stress responses in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize peri-stimulus changes in the Tip Perfusion Index (TPI) and conventional hemodynamic parameters during elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy and to compare their response dynamics among patients without major comorbidities, patients with hypertension, and patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
METHODS: Ninety patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy were prospectively enrolled and classified as Control, Hypertension, or Diabetes (n = 30 each). TPI, BP, and HR were recorded at six perioperative time points (T0-T5) under standardized general anesthesia and CO2 pneumoperitoneum. In a randomly selected subcohort (n = 5 per group), plasma E, NE, and COR were measured from T0 to T4. Data were analyzed using Chi-square tests, one-way ANOVA, mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA, and repeated-measures correlation.
RESULTS: Demographic and baseline parameters were comparable among the three groups (P > 0.05). Following endotracheal intubation and pneumoperitoneum, TPI decreased from the corresponding pre-stimulus values, whereas blood pressure and heart rate increased. Mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant Group×Time interactions for DBP (P = 0.030) and HR (P = 0.002), but not for TPI (P = 0.069) or SBP (P = 0.619). Repeated-measures correlation showed inverse associations between TPI and hemodynamic parameters and stress hormones, except for cortisol in the Diabetes group, where the association did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.057). In the separate threshold-based analysis, all participants met the predefined TPI-positive response criterion during both stimuli. During pneumoperitoneum, TPI response time differed significantly among the three groups (P < 0.001), with the longest mean response time observed in the Diabetes group, whereas no significant between-group differences in response time were observed for SBP, DBP, or HR (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: TPI showed consistent peri-stimulus changes during endotracheal intubation and pneumoperitoneum and may provide complementary information on peripheral vascular responses during surgical stress. The prolonged threshold-based TPI response time observed in patients with diabetes during pneumoperitoneum suggests a potential difference in response timing that warrants further investigation.

Title: Feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although resistance training with nutritional intervention is recommended for sarcopenia, effective programs are often difficult to implement in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation (TES) using belt electrodes with nutritional management in patients with RA.
METHODS: This pilot study was conducted as a prospective observational study with a single-arm before-after framework and enrolled outpatients with RA in remission or with low disease activity. Participants received an outpatient rehabilitation program as part of routine clinical practice once or twice weekly over 6 months, including TES applied to the lower limbs using belt electrodes (20 min per session; 20 Hz; maximum tolerable intensity) and the daily intake of an L-leucine-enriched protein-containing nutritional supplement. Feasibility and safety were evaluated based on study completion, TES session frequency, verbally confirmed adherence to nutritional supplementation, adverse events documented during the program, and maintenance of disease activity. Lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were assessed as exploratory clinical outcomes at baseline and after 6 months.
RESULTS: Of the 14 recruited outpatients with RA, 10 completed both the 6-month program and the final outcome assessment, corresponding to a study completion rate of 71.4%. Participants received a median of 34.5 TES sessions over 6 months. As exploratory clinical outcomes, the median paired changes in lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were 0.08 kg (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.00 to 0.25; P = 0.043), 1.58 kgf (95% CI, -0.35 to 7.25; P = 0.084), and 0.18 m/s (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.24; P = 0.084), respectively. Disease activity remained within the low disease activity to remission range and did not significantly change during the 6-month observation period (P = 0.214). No joint-related or cardiovascular adverse events were documented.
CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study provides preliminary information on the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining TES using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with RA. These findings may inform the design of future studies.

Title: Short-term responses across two sequential plant-based activity sessions: an exploratory fixed-order pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Structured plant-based activities combine natural materials, purposeful manual work, sensory engagement, and social interaction, but direct comparisons of practical formats in community adults remain limited. We characterized short-term responses during two sequential sessions and compared within-session changes.
METHODS: Twenty-five adults participated in a single-group, fixed-order pilot study. Session 1 involved horticultural crafting; 1 week later, Session 2 involved balm crafting followed by horticultural crafting. Twenty-three attended both sessions. DASS-21 and STAI-S were principal outcomes; horticultural wellbeing, HRV, and forehead single-channel EEG were exploratory. Within-session changes and complete-case between-session differences were estimated with 95% CIs. Post hoc TOST examined exploratory equivalence bounds.
RESULTS: Both sessions were followed by favorable short-term psychological changes. DASS-21 scores decreased by 8.57 points in Session 1 [95% CI (5.41, 11.72), n = 23] and 5.53 in Session 2 [(2.65, 8.41), n = 17]. STAI-S scores decreased by 7.30 points in Session 1 [(5.23, 9.37), n = 25] and 6.86 in Session 2 [(4.07, 9.66), n = 22]; all four Holm-adjusted p values were <0.001. Complete-case comparisons showed no statistically detectable between-session difference in DASS-21 improvement [3.12 points, 95% CI (-1.51, 7.75)] or STAI-S improvement [0.34 points, (-3.15, 3.83)]. STAI-S changes met the exploratory TOST criterion only at the broad ±0.50 standardized bound. Horticultural wellbeing improved in both sessions; SDNN and RMSSD increased, whereas EEG findings did not remain significant after multiplicity correction.
CONCLUSION: Both sessions were associated with favorable short-term psychological changes, particularly reduced distress and state anxiety. These findings support the feasibility and potential value of brief, hands-on plant-based activities in community settings and provide estimates for larger randomized, counterbalanced trials. Given the fixed order and absence of a control group, the findings are preliminary rather than definitive causal or modality-specific evidence.

Title: Comparing the Impact of Laryngoscopy on Hemodynamic Status and the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio after Induction of Anesthesia with Etomidate, Propofol, and Ketamine.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is one of the prognostic factors reflecting the balance between systemic inflammation and immunity in the body. This study aimed to compare the impact of laryngoscopy on hemodynamic status and NLR after induction of anesthesia with etomidate, propofol, and ketamine.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This triple-blind, prospective clinical trial was conducted in 2022 on 90 laryngoscopy candidates. The patients were assigned to three groups of 30. For anesthesia, 0.3 mg/kg of etomidate in the first group, 2.5 mg/kg propofol in the second group, and 2 mg/kg of ketamine in the third group were injected slowly, and the patient underwent ventilation with 100% oxygen for at least 3 minutes; then, laryngoscopy, followed by intubation, was carried out. Blood samples were collected before intubation, immediately after recovery, 20 minutes later, 1 hour later, and at the end of recovery and transmitted to the laboratory.
RESULTS: Changes in systolic blood pressure (P = 0.02), diastolic blood pressure (P < 0.01), and mean arterial pressure were significantly higher in the propofol group (P = 0.01). The heart rate (P = 0.56) and oxygen saturation level (P = 0.62) were similar between the three groups. Changes in the mean lymphocyte (P < 0.001) as well as changes in the NLR (P < 0.001) were significantly higher in the ketamine group (P < 0.001). Changes in the neutrophil mean values showed no significant differences (P = 0.24) as the incidence of complications, such as nausea, vomiting, and headache in the three groups.
CONCLUSION: The present study indicated that etomidate had hemodynamic stability and reduced changes in the mean values of lymphocyte, neutrophil, and NLR compared to ketamine and propofol.

Title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting Using Two Different Anesthetic Techniques: Postoperative Outcome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study was performed to investigate the effect of prescribing remifentanil, along with paracetamol and gabapentin in comparison of fentanyl and morphine, on pain relief and faster recovery of patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG).
MATERIALS AND METHOD: A double-blind controlled randomized clinical trial study was performed on 60 CABG candidates. In the control group, the patients underwent anesthesia drugs, analgesic drugs (fentanyl and morphine), and muscle relaxant drugs (without premedication with paracetamol, gabapentin, and remifentanil). In the intervention group, in addition to the control group medications, and bolus doses of remifentanil were used as an analgesic during the operation if analgesia was needed. Also, gabapentin 300 mg orally 1 h before surgery; gabapentin 300 mg every 8 h in the ICU; paracetamol 1 g as an intravenous infusion 30 min before the induction of anesthesia; Paracetamol 1 g every 6 h in the ICU for 3 days were prescribed.
RESULTS: The pain scores mean in the intervention group on the first, second, and third days after CABG were significantly lower than the control group (P < 0.05). Also, the percentage of delirium in the control group was significantly higher than the intervention group in the first and second days after CABG (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: According to the results, administration of remifentanil as a short-acting intraoperative opioid, and the gabapentin to treat nerve pain along with paracetamol before and after CABG surgery could effectively control pain and hemodynamic stability of patients with the least side effects besides reducing the need for additional opioids.

Title: Effects of individualized blood flow restriction during brief twice-weekly low-load cycling on mobility and muscle function in adults older than 70 years.
Journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Age-related declines in muscle strength and physical function increase the risk of mobility limitations, disability, and loss of independence. Although resistance training is effective, many older adults are unable or unwilling to perform high-load exercise, highlighting the need for time-efficient, low-load interventions that preserve physical function. Blood flow restriction (BFR) training may enhance adaptations to low-load exercise, but whether a brief, clinically feasible endurance-based BFR intervention can induce clinically meaningful improvements in mobility remains unclear.
METHODS: Twenty adults aged >70 years were randomized to six weeks of supervised low-load cycling (15 min, twice weekly) with either BFR at 60% limb occlusion pressure (INT, n = 11) or sham BFR (20mmHg, CON, n = 9). Primary outcomes were functional mobility, assessed by the DEMMI, and health-related quality of life. Secondary outcomes included Timed Up and Go (TUG), Six-Minute-Walking-Test (6MWT), lower-limb strength, handgrip strength, body composition, endurance capacity, and cardiovascular safety.
RESULTS: INT showed significantly greater improvements in functional mobility (DEMMI) compared to CON [baseline-adjusted ANCOVA: p = 0.02; Hedges' g [standardized between-group contrast, 95% CI] = 0.91 [-0.04 to 1.87]]. In secondary analyses, no significant between-group differences were observed for TUG [p = 0.14; g = -0.68 (-1.61 to 0.25)] or 6MWT distance [p = 0.08; g = 0.79 (-0.15 to 1.73)]. However, INT showed significant improvements in lower-limb strength with no relevant improvements in CON [leg press: p = 0.04, g = 0.98 [0.02 to 1.94]; leg extension: p < 0.01, g = 1.52 [0.49 to 2.56]]. Furthermore, significant improvements were also observed in muscle mass and endurance capacity (p < 0.05), as well as in health-related quality of life, including vitality [baseline-adjusted ANCOVA: p = 0.042, adjusted mean difference = 6.94 (0.29 to 13.6)] and mental health [p < 0.001, g = 1.61 (0.53 to 2.68)]. Handgrip strength was preserved in INT despite a significant decline in CON (p = 0.042). In secondary exploratory analyses, HDL cholesterol increased, and HbA1c decreased (p < 0.05). Echocardiography revealed no adverse structural or functional cardiac adaptations, and no adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: A brief, twice-weekly low-load cycling program combined with BFR elicited significant rises in lower-limb strength with associated clinically meaningful improvements in mobility despite a minimal exercise dose. Endurance-based BFR appears to be a feasible, safe, and well-tolerated strategy to improve physical function and support independent living in healthy older adults. This trial was not prospectively registered in a public trial registry. It was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (registration number: NCT07825987).

Title: Efficacy of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Urinary and Fecal Symptoms Caused by Rectocele and Cystocele.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) has received increasing interest and application as a noninvasive modality for the local treatment of solid tumors. In this study, we aim to evaluate the efficacy of HIFU in rectocele and cystocele.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial study was conducted on patients who have symptomatic grade 1 and 2 rectocele and cystocele. All patients randomized in two groups; one received HIFU therapy, and the other group underwent Kegel exercises on a daily basis. All patients were followed 2 and 6 months after intervention. The efficacy of HIFU therapy and Kegel exercises were measured based on the pelvic floor discomfort index questionnaire (PFDI-20) and Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI).
RESULTS: Both Kegel exercises and HIFU improved the scores of all sections of FSFI and PFDI questionnaires (P value < 0.05) significantly. Our data in comparison of Kegel exercises versus HIFU therapy showed no significant difference.
CONCLUSION: Our data showed good results in both sexual function and urinocolorectal symptoms after HIFU therapy.

Title: Associations between inflammatory-lipid indices and clinical outcomes in ischemic stroke patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Inflammation and dyslipidemia are critical in post-stroke prognosis. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of six common inflammatory-lipid indices to evaluate the associations between these indices and four clinical outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), and to identify generalizable consistently associated markers for all four clinical outcomes.
METHODS: In this retrospective studyassociations between inflammatory-lipid indices, namely monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR), platelet-to-HDL-C ratio (PHR), neutrophil-to-HDL-C (NHR), lymphocyte-to-HDL-C ratio (LHR), fibrinogen-to-HDL-C ratio (FHR), and C-reactive protein-to-HDL-C ratio (CRP/HDL-C), and four post-MT clinical outcomes comprised hemorrhagic transformation (HT), malignant cerebral edema (MCE) 90-day unfavorable outcome and all-cause mortality were evaluated using multivariable analyses. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple comparisons. NHR, which demonstrated consistent significance for all four clinical outcomes, was subjected to further analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 513 patients were included., demonstrated The incidences of HT, MCE, unfavorable outcome, and all-cause mortality were 30.6% (157), 22.6% (116), 54.8% (281), and 25.9% (133), respectively. The NHR was significantly associated with all four clinical outcomes (HT: odds ratio [OR] 1.079, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.023-1.142, p-FDR = 0.034; MCE: OR 1.089, 95% CI 1.031-1.154, p-FDR = 0.008; unfavorable outcome: OR 1.177, 95% CI 1.098-1.269, p-FDR < 0.001; all-cause mortality: hazard ratio [HR] 1.047, 95% CI 1.012-1.084, p-FDR = 0.022). In the subgroup analysis for all-cause mortality, an interaction between NHR and TOAST classification was observed (p for interaction = 0.023), indicating that the association with all-cause mortality was pronounced in patients with cardioembolic stroke (HR 1.109, 95% CI 1.055-1.165). Mediation analysis showed that HT (23.9%, p < 0.001) and MCE (23.8%, p < 0.001) statistically accounted for part of the associations between NHR and unfavorable outcome. The relationship between NHR and unfavorable outcome may be partially mediated by HT (23.9%, p < 0.001) and MCE (23.8%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: NHR may serve as a potentially useful complementary marker of post-MT HT, MCE, unfavorable outcome, and all-cause mortality. Its association with all-cause mortality appears stronger in patients with cardioembolic stroke. HT and MCE may act as mediators linking NHR to unfavorable outcomes. External validation is required to verify these findings.

Title: Divergent aortic root cusp-to-cusp measurement techniques on CMR: geometric implications and threshold reclassification.
Journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate discrepancies between current European guidelines (ESC vs. EACTS) regarding aortic root cusp-to-cusp measurements and assess their impact on risk stratification for prophylactic root replacement.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A retrospective analysis was performed on a relative young cohort of 50 patients (mean age 42 years) who underwent non-contrast 3D cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging. We compared the widest-to-widest cusp measurements and the middle cusp-to-cusp measurements with each other and against a traced aortic root perimeter. The widest cusp-to-cusp measurement yielded systematically higher values compared to the middle measurement, showing a significant mean difference of 3.60 mm (P < 0.001). The middle measurement demonstrated better statistical agreement with the traced aortic root perimeter, achieving a Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) of 0.98 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.96 mm. Conversely, widest cusp-to-cusp measurements exhibited substantially lower agreement (CCC 0.80) and significantly higher error rates (MAE 16.88 mm), consistently overestimating the perimeter. This led to the upward reclassification of 10.0% (5/50) and 16.0% (8/50) of patients across the 40 and 45 mm guideline thresholds, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Cusp-to-cusp measurement techniques recommended by ESC and EACTS produce systematically divergent aortic root dimensions, resulting in significant patient reclassification across clinical thresholds. Although the middle measurement aligns more closely with the traced anatomical perimeter, the principal finding of this study is that guideline choice fundamentally alters patient categorization. Standardization of aortic root measurement conventions is essential to ensure consistent international care, improve research comparability, and reconcile historical risk thresholds with modern 3D imaging.

Title: Treatment context is associated with thrombocytopenia report phenotypes in lung cancer: an active-comparator analysis of FAERS and JADER.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in lung cancer may be coded as immune, marrow suppression, coagulation, or non-specific. We tested whether coding-defined report phenotypes differed across co-reported treatment contexts.
METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2015Q1-2026Q2) and JADER through Japanese fiscal 2025Q4 (31 March 2026). Strict primary lung cancer reports were grouped as ICI without chemotherapy (C1), ICI plus chemotherapy (C2), or chemotherapy without ICI (C3). Firth models compared mutually exclusive immune-like and marrow-like anchors. Complementary analyses evaluated the broad cohort, treatment date compatibility, C3 small-cell influence, phenotype variants, onset windows, treatment-variable ablation in elastic-net report phenotype models, and a 120-report random stratified blinded review with independent ratings, third-person adjudication, inverse-selection weighting, and bootstrap uncertainty.
RESULTS: FAERS included 1,362 immune-like or marrow-like anchors. Relative to C1, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for immune-like versus marrow-like phenotype were 0.111 (95% CI, 0.069-0.173) in C2 and 0.014 (0.006-0.029) in C3; C3 was exploratory because only eight reports were immune-like. In 2,835 broad cohort reports, adjusted immune-like composition was 13.0% (95% bootstrap interval, 11.0%-15.1%) in C1 and 4.7% (3.4%-6.2%) in C2. Treatment date and stricter phenotype analyses were directionally consistent. JADER reproduced the C2 versus C1 direction but showed calibration shift; treatment-variable ablation reduced cross-database discrimination. Reviewers agreed on 111/120 reports (92.5%; 95% CI, 87.5%-96.7%; Cohen's κ, 0.897; Gwet's AC1, 0.901). In the locked 927-report frame, design-weighted final categories were 23.4% immune probable, 37.3% immune possible, 13.6% indeterminate, and 25.8% non-immune probable. Among 100 determinate reports, weighted AUROC was 0.892 (0.827-0.948), PR-AUC 0.956 (0.922-0.982), and calibration-in-the-large intercept 2.054 (1.707-2.432), indicating underprediction.
CONCLUSION: Coding-defined thrombocytopenia report composition differed across treatment contexts. Blinded review supported reproducible structured category assignment and score-based report ordering, while calibration shift and treatment-variable ablation defined important limits. Findings support pharmacovigilance case prioritization and hypothesis generation, not clinical diagnosis, incidence estimation, patient-level etiologic attribution, or causal inference.

Title: microRNA-15b modulates stress-induced premature senescence in chronic doxorubicin cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Doxorubicin (DOX) is the most widely used anthracycline in hematologic and solid tumors, whose clinical utility is constrained by dose-dependent cumulative cardiotoxicity that can progress to chronic heart failure. Although previously attributed to overt cardiomyocyte loss, emerging evidence indicates that stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS) constitutes the dominant mechanism of chronic cardiotoxicity at clinically relevant concentrations. SIPS is defined by permanent cell cycle arrest, activation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb tumor suppressor axes, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) that sustains a pro-inflammatory myocardial milieu. Nevertheless, the post-transcriptional mechanisms that govern this process remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: The post-transcriptional regulation of DOX-induced SIPS was evaluated in vitro using neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) exposed to sublethal DOX (0.1 μM) with or without prophylactic miR-15b restoration via a synthetic mimetic to assess the p53/p21, p16, SASP, lysosomal, and mitochondrial responses. In vivo, a chronic cardiotoxicity model was established in female C57BL/6 mice receiving a cumulative dose of 30 mg/kg DOX to analyze myocardial miR-15b suppression, SIPS markers, and SASP profiles across survival cohorts.
RESULTS: Sublethal DOX treatment (0.1 μM) suppressed miR-15b expression by approximately 50% in NRVMs, resulting in post-transcriptional derepression of its mitochondrial target, SIRT4. This miR-15b loss triggered a multiparametric SIPS phenotype encompassing accumulation of γH2AX foci, p53/p21 and p16 activation, SASP induction (IL-6, IL-1β, Mcp-1 and Mmp13), lysosomal dysfunction (increased SA-β-Gal staining) and mitochondrial dysfunction. Prophylactic restoration of miR-15b via a synthetic mimetic selectively attenuated the p53/p21 axis, genomic damage foci, lysosomal dysfunction, mitochondrial dysfunction and SASP (IL-6 and IL-1β), without rescuing the p16/Rb pathway. In the female C57BL/6 chronic cardiotoxicity model, the cohort spontaneously stratified into animals completing the protocol (ND; 67%) and a premature death subgroup (PD; 33%). The PD subgroup exhibited the most profound myocardial miR-15b suppression and greater accumulation of SIPS markers, including γH2AX, p16, and reduced Lamin B. Notably, the SASP displayed distinct qualitative profiles between PD and ND animals, suggesting that SASP composition, rather than magnitude alone, determines the cardiotoxic outcome.
CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings position miR-15b as a key post-transcriptional regulator of DOX-induced SIPS in the cardiomyocyte, whose sustained loss associates with cardiotoxicity severity in vivo.

Title: World Stroke Organization mechanical thrombectomy workshops combined with the Global Stroke Alliance builds regional capacity.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Access to mechanical thrombectomy (MT) remains limited in many low- and middle-income or resource-limited regions because of gaps in trained personnel, procedural experience, public awareness, and stroke-system readiness. The World Stroke Organization paired simulation-based MT workshops with the Global Stroke Alliance to combine hands-on neurointerventional education with regional advocacy, Ministry of Health engagement, public awareness activities, and stakeholder collaboration. This study evaluated the feasibility, scalability, and self-reported educational impact of MT workshops delivered within this broader WSO/GSA capacity-building framework.
METHODS: A comprehensive 22-h curriculum was developed, incorporating didactic sessions, hands-on simulations, and complex case studies in collaboration with the Global Stroke Alliance between August 2023 and July 2025. The workshops were designed for neurointerventional physicians and tailored to regional needs.
