A total of 678 patients were included. Of these, 74% were male, and the mean age was 64.69 ± 10.92 years. Wagner grade 4 ulcers accounted for 61.7% of cases, while 65.0% were classified as PEDIS grade 3. Histopathological examination identified malignancy in 4 patients (0.6%; 95% CI, 0.16-1.50); two of these patients had metastatic involvement. The treatment and care plan was modified for all patients in whom malignancy was detected. Overall, 95.6% of patients healed with wound care after surgery, without further changes to their treatment or care plan. However, 1.9% required amputation at a more proximal level, 1.3% experienced limb loss, and 1.2% died from other diabetes-related complications. Although uncommon, malignancy and metastatic involvement may occur in chronic DFUs. The possibility of malignancy should therefore be considered, particularly in nonhealing, atypical, or clinically suspicious ulcers. Ensuring appropriate histopathological evaluation of such ulcers may help healthcare professionals and wound care nurses identify primary or metastatic malignancies at an earlier stage.

Title: Acute ischemic stroke despite NOAC therapy in atrial fibrillation: Clinical factors associated with AIS in a 2-center observational case-control study.
Abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) can occur in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF) despite treatment with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs). This study evaluated clinical, treatment-related, inflammatory, and echocardiographic factors associated with AIS in NOAC-treated patients with AF. This retrospective, 2-center case-control study included 322 patients with non-valvular AF who had received NOAC therapy for at least 3 months. Of these, 112 were hospitalized with AIS and 210 were outpatient controls without AIS at the study assessment. Group differences and factors associated with AIS were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. ROC analyses were exploratory. Patients with AIS were older than controls and more often had hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, prior stroke, and prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use. In the adjusted analysis, prior stroke (OR = 32.79), coronary artery disease (OR = 3.47), prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use (OR = 2.55), female sex (OR = 2.26), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.99), and C-reactive protein (OR per mg/L = 1.10) were associated with AIS. HAS-BLED (area under the curve = 0.881, 95% CI = 0.844-0.918) and CHA2DS2-VASc (area under the curve = 0.840, 95% CI = 0.795-0.885) distinguished AIS cases from controls in exploratory ROC analyses. Among NOAC-treated patients with AF, prior stroke and cardiovascular comorbidities were strongly associated with AIS. Prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use was also associated with AIS. Inflammatory markers measured during acute stroke had limited additional value. Because this was a case-control study, the findings do not estimate stroke incidence or future stroke risk and require prospective validation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy: A comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
Abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized cardiac complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by impaired myocardial contractile reserve, diastolic dysfunction, and electrophysiological abnormalities. Despite its clinical significance, particularly in the setting of liver transplantation, CCM remains largely overlooked. We performed a narrative review of the literature on CCM published up to December 2025, covering pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, imaging modalities, biomarkers, and management strategies. Depending on the diagnostic criteria used, the prevalence of CCM ranges from 29% to 67.2%. Advanced imaging techniques, particularly global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance, enable early detection of subclinical systolic dysfunction. A "toxic triangle" comprising systemic inflammation, metabolic derangements, and neurohormonal activation represents an integrated pathophysiological model that drives myocardial fibrosis and dysfunction. Beta-blockers and aldosterone antagonists remain mainstays of pharmacological management, while liver transplantation is currently the only definitive therapy. CCM is an underrecognized condition with substantial clinical implications. Standardized diagnostic criteria, validated biomarkers, and large-scale prospective studies are urgently needed to improve patient outcomes.

Title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

Title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased sympathetic activity and an elevated cardiovascular risk. Noninvasive interventions targeting autonomic regulation may offer complementary therapeutic strategies.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the acute effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters of patients with OSA. Patients with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour) were randomly assigned to an intervention group that received a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol or a control group that rested quietly in the supine position for the corresponding period without receiving manual or tactile intervention. The intervention targeted the cervical, thoracic, and abdominal regions, under controlled conditions. The primary outcomes included heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and peripheral oxygen saturation. Measurements were obtained at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 5 and 15 minutes post-intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 95 male patients (mean age: 48.12 ± 10.21 years) completed the study. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups, except for heart rate. After adjustment for baseline heart rate using mixed analysis of covariance, no significant group × time interaction was observed for heart rate (P = .476, partial ηp2 = .008). Similarly, no significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, or peripheral oxygen saturation (all P > .05). Although significant time effects were observed for some physiological parameters, the magnitude of these effects varied across outcomes, and none was accompanied by a significant group × time interaction. Therefore, these temporal changes were not interpreted as intervention-specific effects. No adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: Heart rate changed significantly over time following the interventions; however, after adjustment for baseline heart rate, the pattern of change did not differ significantly between the fascial mobilization and control groups. Similarly, no significant between-group differences in changes over time were observed for blood pressure or oxygen saturation. These findings do not demonstrate a specific acute effect of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters assessed. Further studies using advanced measures of autonomic function and longer follow-up periods are warranted.

Title: Deaths involving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cardiac arrest in older US adults, 1999-2023: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract: National long-term trends and disparities in deaths in which both chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cardiac arrest are recorded on death certificates are not well characterized. We used CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (1999-2023) to identify US adults aged ≥ 65 years whose death certificates listed both COPD (ICD-10 J41-J44) and cardiac arrest (I46) as underlying or contributing causes. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization; the urbanization analysis was limited to 1999 to 2020 because those data were not available after 2020. Trends were analyzed using annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); P < .05 was considered statistically significant. Among 7,18,280 deaths involving concurrent coding of COPD and cardiac arrest, AAMRs declined from 86.4 in 1999 to 52.5 in 2023. A significant decrease occurred from 1999 to 2006 (APC: -2.87; P = .01), followed by a plateau and a further decline from 2021 to 2023 (APC: -4.77; P < .001). Older men exhibited higher AAMRs than older women (86.8 vs 55.2). Non-Hispanic (NH) White individuals had the highest mortality (69.7), followed by NH Black/African American (64.3) and Hispanic/Latino (60.7) populations. The West region reported the highest AAMR (98.9). During 1999 to 2020, nonmetropolitan residents had higher AAMRs than metropolitan residents (70.8 vs 67.9). Population-level mortality records involving both COPD and cardiac arrest declined overall but remained heterogeneous across demographic and geographic strata. These findings describe concurrent coding on death certificates and do not establish that COPD increases the risk of cardiac arrest or causes the observed deaths.

Title: Association of Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) with long-term mortality in type 2 diabetes patients with coronary heart disease: A prospective national cohort study.
Abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is prevalent in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with coronary heart disease (CHD), increasing cardiovascular risk. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is a novel composite biomarker, yet its prognostic value in this comorbid population remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed 909 participants with T2DM and CHD from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999 to 2010, followed until 2019. EASIX was calculated using lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and platelet count. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed associations between EASIX and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively. Time-dependent C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement evaluated the incremental prognostic value of EASIX beyond established risk factors. During a median follow-up of 111 months, 617 all-cause and 251 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Higher EASIX levels were significantly associated with increased mortality risks. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile had a hazard ratio of 1.93 (95% confidence interval = 1.48-2.50) for all-cause mortality and a subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.56 (95% confidence interval = 1.05-2.33) for cardiovascular mortality compared with the lowest quartile. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear positive relationship. Adding EASIX to a base model (age, HbA1c, and estimated glomerular filtration rate) significantly improved the C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement for both outcomes (all P < .001). Elevated EASIX levels are independently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with T2DM and CHD. In this population, its inclusion in risk assessment protocols enhances the predictive value for long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Prognostic value of systemic inflammatory markers in patients with malignancy-associated pulmonary thromboembolism: A retrospective observational study.
Abstract: Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) is a severe and potentially fatal complication in patients with malignancy. Systemic inflammation plays an important role in both cancer progression and thrombogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the association of systemic inflammatory indices with in-hospital mortality and clinical risk classification in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. This retrospective study included 75 adult patients diagnosed with both malignancy and PTE at a tertiary chest diseases center between February 2018 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, cancer types, laboratory values at diagnosis, treatment details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), lymphocyte-to-CRP ratio (LCRPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated from blood samples obtained at diagnosis. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, and the secondary outcome was the association between systemic inflammatory markers and ESC PTE clinical risk classification. The mean age was 69.5 ± 11.8 years, and 56% of patients were male. Lung (24%), colorectal (13.3%), and breast (9.3%) cancers were the most common malignancies. In-hospital mortality was 20%. Neutrophil count (P = .026), NLR (P = .032), and lactate (P = .027) were significantly higher in patients who died during hospitalization. ROC analysis identified an NLR cutoff value of 4.95, with a sensitivity of 86.7% and a specificity of 51.7%. Neutrophil count and SIRI were significantly higher in the intermediate-risk group (P = .036 and P = .049, respectively), whereas troponin was highest in the high-risk group (P < .001). Neutrophil count, NLR, and lactate levels were associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. Neutrophil count and SIRI were also associated with ESC clinical risk classification. These findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Causal effects of antihypertensive drugs on thyroid diseases: A trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization study.
Abstract: Thyroid disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular disease, including hypertension, but whether long-term modulation of antihypertensive drug targets influences thyroid disease risk remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the associations of 7 antihypertensive drug-target classes with thyroid diseases in European and East Asian populations using a trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) framework. We performed a two-sample, trans-ancestry drug-target MR analysis of 7 antihypertensive target classes. Target-proximal single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with systolic blood pressure (SBP) were used as genetic proxies. Estimates were scaled per 1-mm Hg genetically predicted increase in SBP; the putative effect of target inhibition that lowers SBP was therefore interpreted in the opposite direction. Summary statistics were obtained for 4 primary thyroid diseases, benign thyroid tumors where available, and 3 thyroid-related proteins in European and East Asian datasets. Hypertension was used as a positive-control outcome. Random-effects inverse-variance weighting was the primary method, with Wald ratio estimation for single-nucleotide polymorphism instruments and weighted-median, Cochran's Q, MR-Egger, and Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier analyses as sensitivity assessments. Within the European populace, genetic surrogates for β-blockers exhibit (odds ratio = 0.93; 95% confidence interval = 0.87-0.99) a close association with heightened susceptibility to thyroid carcinoma, whereas KCNH2 (1.15; 1.01-1.32) demonstrates an inverse correlation with thyroid cancer risk. Moreover, calcium channel blockers exhibit a conspicuous linkage with an elevated incidence of hyperthyroidism (0.97; 0.96-0.99) alongside a diminished likelihood of thyroid cancer (1.07; 1.03-1.10). CYP17A1 exerts a protective influence against hyperthyroidism (1.04; 10.1-1.07) and Graves disease (1.10; 1.05-1.16) but manifests a pathogenic effect concerning hypothyroidism (0.99; 0.97-1.00) and thyroid cancer (0.92; 0.86-0.98). Conversely, KCNJ11 demonstrates a proximate correlation between diminished hypothyroidism risk and augmented thyroid cancer susceptibility (0.83; 0.73-0.95). Analogous estimations were noted for CYP17A1 within the East Asian cohort. Genetically proxied perturbation of several antihypertensive drug targets was associated with thyroid disease risk, with CYP17A1 showing the broadest cross-ancestry pattern. These estimates reflect lifelong target-proximal genetic effects rather than the clinical effects of prescribed drugs and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending replication, pharmacoepidemiological studies, and randomized clinical trials.

Title: TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI as insulin-resistance body shape markers of mortality in middle-aged and older adults within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework: A multi-cohort observational study with external survival-model validation.
Abstract: Insulin resistance, adiposity, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease are closely interconnected in middle-aged and older adults and are central to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-related indices combine routine lipid, glucose, and anthropometric information, but their cross-population consistency and incremental prognostic value for mortality-risk assessment remain uncertain. We analyzed harmonized participant-level data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), and Health and Retirement Study (HRS), with HRS used as a sensitivity cohort. Eligible participants were aged ≥ 50 years, had follow-up beyond baseline, available mortality status, and complete data for 7 TyG-related indices. Cohort-specific Cox models estimated associations of standardized TyG, TyG-body mass index, TyG-waist circumference, TyG-waist-to-height ratio, TyG-weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), TyG-a body shape index (ABSI), and TyG-body roundness index with all-cause mortality. Nonlinearity, proportional-hazards assumptions, sensitivity analyses, NHANES heart disease mortality, incremental prediction, and survival machine learning with external validation were further assessed. The primary analytic sample included 21,044 NHANES participants, 5454 ELSA participants, and 11,157 CHARLS participants, among whom 5566, 116, and 1393 deaths occurred during follow-up, respectively. The HRS sensitivity cohort included 4103 participants and 484 deaths. In fully adjusted Cox models, all 7 TyG-related indices were associated with higher all-cause mortality in NHANES, with the strongest associations observed for TyG-ABSI (hazard ratio [HR] 1.159, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.115-1.205) and TyG-WWI (HR 1.155, 95% CI 1.113-1.199). In CHARLS, TyG-ABSI was positively associated with mortality (HR 1.088, 95% CI 1.029-1.151), whereas estimates in ELSA were imprecise. In HRS sensitivity analyses, TyG-WWI and TyG-ABSI remained positively associated with mortality. Adding TyG-related indices to a clinical Cox prediction framework produced only minimal absolute gains in discrimination. The final TyG-ABSI extreme gradient boosting survival model yielded 5-year time-dependent area under the curves of 0.808 in the NHANES internal test set and 0.760 in CHARLS. A research-use web calculator was developed for 5-year and 8-year mortality-risk estimation. TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI were the most consistent TyG-related body shape markers of all-cause mortality across international aging cohorts. Although TyG-ABSI supported externally validated survival prediction, its incremental predictive value beyond established clinical and CKM variables was limited. These findings suggest that TyG-related body shape indices may serve primarily as interpretable, low-cost CKM risk markers rather than standalone prediction tools.

Title: Impact of portal hypertension on clinical outcomes in critically Ill adult patients: A retrospective study: Outcomes in critically Ill patients with portal hypertension.
Abstract: Liver dysfunction is a common complication in critically ill patients, and portal hypertension (PHT) represents a severe hepatic pathological condition closely associated with adverse patient outcomes. This study aims to investigate the impact of PHT on clinical outcomes in critically ill adult patients. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Market for Intensive Care IV database. All critically ill patients admitted to the hospital were included in this study. Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the correlation between PHT and hospital mortality, length of stay in the intensive care unit (LOS-ICU), and length of stay in hospital in critically ill patients, and multiple collinearity checks were performed. Propensity score matching was used to minimize group differences, and subgroup analyses were conducted. A total of 46,804 adult critically ill patients were included in this study. The hospital mortality rate for critically ill patients with PHT was 19%, significantly higher than the 8.8% mortality rate for patients without PHT (P < .05). Critically ill patients with PHT also had longer LOS-ICU and length of stay in hospital and higher total bilirubin levels (P < .05). Furthermore, multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that PHT was significantly associated with hospital mortality (OR: 2.716, 95% CI: 2.330-3.158, P < .001). After propensity score matching, the baseline differences between the 2 groups were significantly reduced, and the results showed that critically ill patients with PHT had worse clinical outcomes. However, the LOS-ICU was not significantly different after matching. PHT is a significant predictor of poor prognosis in critically ill adult patients, necessitating enhanced clinical monitoring and management to improve their clinical outcomes.

Title: The Impact of Anaesthesia Method on the Use of Anaesthesia Department Resources in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.
METHODS: A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.
RESULTS: Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). However, after spinal anaesthesia, patients appeared to spend more time in the postanaesthesia care unit than after general anaesthesia (median 104 min [71-148 min] vs. 73 min [49-98 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 32 min [95% CI 23-42 min], p < 0.001). Medication for hypotension was more common in the general anaesthesia group, whereas medication for hypertension was more common in the spinal anaesthesia group. General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).
CONCLUSION: With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT (2016-002035-15).

Title: FXI and FXII in experimental stroke and FXI in clinical stroke trials.
Abstract: Targeting the contact activation system through Factor XI (FXI) or Factor XII (FXII) inhibition represents a major paradigm shift in antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke. Unlike traditional anticoagulants, contact pathway factors drive pathological thrombus propagation and thromboinflammation; crucially, while FXII plays a negligible role in physiological hemostasis, FXI contributes only secondarily, thereby substantially uncoupling antithrombotic efficacy from major bleeding risk. However, a notable disconnect exists between experimental models and clinical development. Preclinical stroke literature, primarily rodent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) models, is overwhelmingly concentrated on FXII targeting, where FXII deficiency or blockade consistently reduces cerebral infarct volumes, preserves microvascular perfusion, and attenuates thromboinflammation, whereas experimental studies of direct FXI treatment remain sparse. Conversely, human clinical translation has focused largely on oral FXIa inhibitors, maintaining a favorable bleeding profile across indications but yielding mixed efficacy, ranging from neutral Phase II studies and the early termination of OCEANIC-AF to positive secondary stroke prevention data. Following positive OCEANIC-STROKE findings, asundexian (under FDA priority review as of September 2026) emerges as a prospective add-on to antiplatelet therapy for the secondary prevention of noncardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA, particularly in nonlacunar or atherosclerotic populations. Reconciling preclinical FXII data with clinical FXIa trial outcomes provides a timely rationale to systematically review evidence across MCAO models and human stroke trials to delineate the distinct therapeutic potentials of FXI and FXII inhibition.

Title: The impact of COVID-19 on all-cause mortality and life expectancy: findings from a population-based cohort in uMkhanyakude district, northern KwaZulu-natal.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the comprehensive death reporting system in South Africa, significant gaps persist in our understanding of the pandemic's impact in rural areas.
METHODS: We computed monthly death counts stratified by demographic factors from a population-based demographic surveillance cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal. We fit seasonally adjusted negative binomial regression models to estimate excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic period (5 March 2020 to 31 December 2021) compared to the pre-pandemic period (1 January 2015 to 4 March 2020). We then assessed the relative risk of death by health and sociodemographic factors and considering apotential interaction with the COVID-19 pandemic. Finally, we calculated changes in life expectancy at the age of 15 and conducted a decomposition analysis to identify life expectancy changes by age group.
RESULTS: We observed two major periods of excess mortality during the beta and delta waves of the COVID-19 pandemic, respectively. During the pre-pandemic period, people with HIV (PWH) had slightly higher mortality rates (RR = 1.8; 95%CI 1.3 - 2.4) than their HIV-negative counterparts. This excess risk reduced during the COVID-19 period (HIV RR = 1.5; 95%CI 1.2 - 2.0). Similar patterns were noted for individuals with diabetes (pre-pandemic RR = 1.6; 95%CI 1.2 - 2.2 vs during COVID-19 RR = 1.4; 95%CI 1.1 - 1.9). In contrast, individuals with hypertension experienced a 15% relative increase death rate during the pandemic compared to pre-COVID period (p-interaction = 0.003). Similarly, hypertensive PWH had significantly elevated mortality risks during COVID-19 (RR = 2.18; 95% CI: 1.45-3.26, p < 0.001). Throughout the study, women consistently had higher life expectancy at age 15 than men. However, women contributed more to pandemic-related life expectancy reductions, along with specific age and health groups.
CONCLUSION: We found contrasting impacts of co-morbidities on mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic in rural South Africa, and that reductions in life expectancy at age 15 were greater in women than men. These findings emphasize the critical need to consider specific needs of rural populations, and tailor public health strategies that prioritize vulnerable populations and address health inequities to mitigate the effects of pandemics in low-resource settings.

Title: Online clinical readiness course enhanced knowledge and perceived confidence of trainees during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education globally. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the International Emergency Medicine Education Project's online COVID-19 Clinical Readiness Course in enhancing participants' knowledge and perceived confidence in managing COVID-19.
METHODS: This is a prospective, mixed-methods study. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-course assessments and surveys, while qualitative feedback was gathered via open-ended responses at the end of the course. Non-parametric tests were used for statistical comparisons, and thematic analysis of qualitative data was performed using customized large language model tools with human review and triangulation.
RESULTS: A total of 703 participants from 72 countries enrolled, 644 (91.6%) completed the knowledge assessments, and 510 (72.5%) completed the exit surveys. The majority (77.2%) were medical trainees, and 51.4% were from low- and lower-middle-income countries. The median score increased from 60 to 92 (p < 0.001) post-course. Perceived confidence in managing key clinical scenarios, including hypoxia, early symptoms, airway problems, sepsis, and cardiac arrest, also increased significantly (p < 0.001). Participants reported that the course met their expectations, with a median (IQR) score of 9 (8-10). Qualitative feedback revealed high satisfaction and highlighted areas for improvement.
CONCLUSION: The online Clinical Readiness Course significantly improved knowledge and perceived confidence in COVID-19 management among medical trainees worldwide. Scalable online education may help address training gaps during public health emergencies and support global medical education.

Title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality Among U.S. Women with Breast Cancer: a National NHANES Analysis.
Journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular complications are an important and increasingly recognized concern among women with breast cancer. Racial and ethnic differences in cardiovascular disease burden suggest that certain populations may be at heightened risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study examined racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality among women with breast cancer using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 669 women with self-reported breast cancer identified in NHANES and linked to the National Death Index. Participants were categorized by race and ethnicity as Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, Mexican American, Other Hispanic, or Other Race. Heart failure prevalence was evaluated as a clinically relevant cardiovascular outcome. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause and cardiovascular-specific mortality, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and forest plots were generated to visualize differences across groups.
RESULTS: Non-Hispanic Black women demonstrated the highest prevalence of cardiovascular disease, including heart failure (8.2%), compared with Non-Hispanic White (7.4%), Other Race (6.1%), Other Hispanic (2.2%), and Mexican American women (1.7%). Non-Hispanic Black women showed a trend toward poorer survival outcomes, with an elevated risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.80; 95% CI: 0.96-3.36) compared with Mexican American women. After multivariable adjustment, this association persisted (HR 1.81; 95% CI: 0.96-3.41). Cardiovascular-specific mortality was higher among Non-Hispanic Black women, reaching statistical significance in the fully adjusted model (adjusted HR 3.46; 95% CI: 1.66-7.24).
CONCLUSION: Racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality were observed among women with breast cancer, with Non-Hispanic Black women experiencing a higher burden. These findings highlight the need for targeted, evidence-based strategies to address cardiovascular risk and improve equitable outcomes in this population.

Title: Planned Antihypertensive Deprescribing in Long-Term Care Residents: A Systematic Review of Randomized Evidence.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence supporting antihypertensive treatment in older adults is derived largely from populations that differ from long-term care residents, in whom frailty, dementia, multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and competing clinical priorities may alter the balance between preventive benefit and treatment burden.
OBJECTIVES: The aim was to synthesize randomized evidence on planned antihypertensive deprescribing in institutional long-term care and determine whether clinically and methodologically comparable effects support a common treatment-effect estimate.
METHODS: Randomized or cluster-randomized studies of planned antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care were systematically reviewed. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, Web of Science Core Collection, trial registries, and PROSPERO were searched from inception and updated to 20 August 2026. Meta-analysis was reserved for outcomes with at least two clinically and methodologically compatible estimates of a common, interpretable effect; otherwise, structured study-level synthesis was used. Result-specific risk of bias was assessed with the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2), and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) tool.
RESULTS: Three randomized long-term care studies involving 1548 residents were included. Their populations, deprescribing strategies, monitoring, restart criteria, and follow-up differed substantially, and no outcome was considered sufficiently clinically and methodologically comparable for meta-analysis. RETREAT-FRAIL reported an adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause mortality of 1.02 (95% confidence interval 0.86-1.21) over a median potential follow-up of 38.4 months, whereas DANTON reported an HR of 1.65 (0.95-2.85) to 32 weeks; Gulla/COSMOS had no cluster-adjusted comparative mortality estimate. At 16 weeks in DANTON, deprescribing increased systolic blood pressure by 11.0 mmHg (5.6-16.4), increased diastolic blood pressure by 4.6 mmHg (1.1-8.1), and reduced the number of antihypertensive drugs by 1.2 (1.0-1.4). Evidence for hospitalization, falls, cardiovascular events, cognition, function, and quality of life remained sparse, outcome-specific, or at risk of bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Randomized evidence for antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care remains sparse and clinically heterogeneous. Within individual trials, supervised deprescribing reduced antihypertensive exposure and raised blood pressure, but the magnitude and clinical consequences varied by strategy and follow-up. Current evidence does not establish a common effect on mortality, hospitalization, or other resident-important outcomes, making trial-specific estimates and deprescribing protocols more informative than a single pooled treatment effect.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261370802.

Title: Impact of matched samples on domain harmonization in cross-cohort NMR metabolomics.
Journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Machine learning models trained on metabolomics data frequently show reduced performance when applied to independent cohorts because of domain shifts introduced by differences in analytical platforms, sample handling, storage conditions, and metabolite quantification procedures. Robust approaches for harmonizing metabolomics datasets across cohorts are therefore needed to improve model transferability and reproducibility.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of matched samples on domain harmonization and cross-cohort prediction performance in NMR metabolomics data, and to compare multiple harmonization strategies for improving model generalization across independently acquired datasets.
METHODS: A machine-learning framework was developed to classify ICD-10 code I50.9 (unspecified heart failure) using plasma NMR metabolomics data from the Estonian Biobank. Models were trained on a source dataset comprising 12,000 samples measured at Nightingale Health and evaluated on an independently measured destination dataset of 295 samples acquired on a different NMR platform. Harmonization approaches included within-domain normalization, Optimal Transport, Bridge mapping, and Empirical Bayes correction. The effect of matched samples was assessed using up to 108 duplicated biospecimens measured in both datasets. Additional validation was performed using independently generated human gestational diabetes and mouse diabetes metabolomics datasets from Metabolomics Workbench.
RESULTS: Domain harmonization generally improved cross-cohort prediction compared with unaligned data, particularly when matched samples were available. Predictive performance increased as the number of matched samples used for calibration increased, although gains varied across methods. Nevertheless, simple within-domain normalization consistently provided strong performance and often matched or exceeded more complex alignment approaches. External validation using fully unmatched human and mouse metabolomics datasets demonstrated that harmonization strategies improved classification performance relative to raw data, supporting the broader applicability of the framework.
CONCLUSION: Matched samples substantially enhance domain harmonization and improve the transferability of metabolomics prediction models across analytical platforms and cohorts. However, robust normalization remains a strong baseline, and the benefits of more sophisticated alignment methods depend on the availability and representativeness of matched reference samples. These findings provide practical guidance for developing reproducible cross-cohort metabolomics machine-learning models while preserving biologically relevant signals.

Title: Changes in biventricular myocardial function after six months of ixekizumab therapy in patients with psoriatic arthritis: a prospective speckle-tracking echocardiographic study.
Abstract: To evaluate longitudinal changes in conventional and speckle-tracking echocardiographic indices in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) who achieved a disease activity index for psoriatic arthritis (DAPSA)-defined clinical response during ixekizumab therapy.In this prospective single-centre observational cohort, 21 adults with PsA underwent clinical, laboratory and transthoracic echocardiographic assessment before ixekizumab initiation and after 6 months of treatment. The principal echocardiographic outcome was the within-patient change in absolute left vetricle global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) between baseline and 6 months. Secondary echocardiographic outcomes included right ventricle (RV) GLS, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (RV S') and tricuspid E to E' ratio (E/E'), while clinical secondary outcomes included DAPSA, body surface area (BSA), minimal disease activity (MDA), C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Mean age was 49.6 ± 11.6 years, 57.1% were male and 11 patients (52.4%) were biologic-naïve. MDA was achieved by 17 patients (81.0%). DAPSA decreased from 28.9 ± 4.3 to 7.7 ± 4.2, accompanied by reductions in CRP and ESR (all p < 0.001). Absolute LV GLS increased from 18.5 ± 1.3% to 20.5 ± 1.9% (mean change 2.0%, 95% CI 1.49-2.51; p < 0.001), while absolute RV GLS increased from 21.5 ± 3.3% to 25.8 ± 4.2% (mean change 4.29%, 95% CI 3.37-5.20; p < 0.001). LVEF, TAPSE, RV S' and E/E' also improved significantly. Although DAPSA reduction correlated with increased LVEF, while BSA reduction with increased LV GLS and TAPSE, these associations were exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously. Among patients with PsA who achieved clinical response to ixekizumab, 6 months of treatment was accompanied by improvements in left- and right-ventricular functional indices. Because the cohort was small, responder-enriched and lacked a comparator group, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

Title: Durable improvements in lipid profile and atherogenic indices more than a decade after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.
Abstract: Long-term effects of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) on lipid metabolism, particularly beyond 10 years, are not well defined. This study evaluated changes in standard lipid parameters and atherogenic indices more than 11 years after stand-alone LSG. This retrospective cohort study included adults who underwent primary stand-alone LSG between 2005 and 2009. Patients with revisional bariatric procedures or major gastrointestinal or appetite-related disorders were excluded. Lipid profiles were assessed preoperatively and at follow-up beyond 11 years. Primary outcomes were long-term changes in triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, and non-HDL-C. Secondary outcomes included changes in the atherogenic index of plasma, triglyceride/HDL-C ratio, Castelli risk indices I and II, atherogenic coefficient, and use of lipid-lowering medications. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent predictors of lipid change. Eighty-six patients (79.1%, female) were analyzed, with a mean follow-up of 13.4 ± 1.3 years. Mean total body weight loss (%TBWL) was 28.8 ± 12.5%. Triglyceride levels decreased from 130.7 ± 64.9 to 91.2 ± 36.8 mg/dL, HDL-C increased from 45.2 ± 9.5 to 62.6 ± 14.7 mg/dL, and non-HDL-C decreased from 151.9 ± 38.0 to 134.0 ± 27.4 mg/dL (all p < 0.001). Total cholesterol remained unchanged, while the reduction in LDL-C was no longer significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. All five atherogenic indices showed significant improvement (p < 0.001). Greater %TBWL was independently associated with higher HDL-C and lower triglyceride levels at follow-up. More than a decade after stand-alone LSG, improvements in triglycerides, HDL-C, non-HDL-C, and atherogenic indices remain robust. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously regarding cardiovascular and atherosclerotic risk.

Title: Postoperative DWI morphology and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 139 consecutive patients undergoing resection of eloquent-area supratentorial gliomas (WHO 2-4). Postoperative MRI (< 48 h) classified lesions as sector- or rim-shaped. Neurological status was assessed at discharge and 4-6 months.
RESULTS: DWI lesions occurred in 44/139 patients (31.7%; 31 sector-shaped, 13 rim-shaped); 59 (42.4%) worsened at discharge. Overall, DWI positivity alone was not associated with worsening. Sector-shaped DWI lesions were associated with neurological worsening (positive predictive value, PPV of 58.1%) and remained associated after multivariable adjustment (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.30-11.29), although the confidence interval was wide and the unadjusted association was borderline. Rim-shaped lesions carried a PPV of 38.5%, comparable to the risk in DWI-negative patients (37.9%), and the two morphologies did not differ significantly in direct comparison. Awake craniotomy was also independently associated with worsening, and frontal site with a lower risk. 61% of worsening occurred with negative DWI. A deficit was present at the 4-6 month follow-up in 9 patients (6.5%), all with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and was associated with a ≥ 50% evoked-potential decrease.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, postoperative DWI positivity was associated with neurological worsening mainly when the lesion was sector-shaped, a finding that requires confirmation in larger series. Rim-shaped lesions showed a risk of worsening similar to that of a negative scan. Most worsening occurs without DWI ischemia, suggesting non-ischemic mechanisms of function-guided surgery. A deficit at follow-up occurred only in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and was associated with intraoperative neurophysiological changes.

Title: Risk of early stroke recurrence and procedural stroke or death in carotid near occlusion patients scheduled for carotid endarterectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid near occlusion (NO) refers to distal internal carotid artery (ICA) narrowing caused by proximal carotid stenosis (CS). Stroke risk and optimal management of NO remain controversial. Our aim was to determine the prevalence of NO severities, rates of preoperative ischemic cerebrovascular events (iCVEs), 30-day procedural stroke and death, and hyperperfusion syndrome in patients with NO in a prospective CS cohort undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA).
METHODS: We reanalyzed posthoc CTAs from 443 symptomatic and asymptomatic CS patients. Subtle NO (s-NO) was defined as a 1.0-mm difference in distal luminal diameter between ipsilateral and contralateral ICA. NO with full collapse (fc-NO) was defined as ≤2.0 mm and/or an ipsilateral-to-contralateral ICA diameter ratio ≤0.42. Conventional stenosis was defined as CS >50% using NASCET criteria. Rates of preoperative iCVEs and 30-day procedural stroke and death were compared between s-NO, fc-NO, and conventional stenosis.
RESULTS: NO occurred in 143 (32%) patients: 124 (87%) s-NO and 19 (13%) fc-NO. NO was not significantly associated with increased preoperative iCVEs (7.6% vs 13%, OR 1.82, 95%Cl 0.96-3.47) or procedural stroke or death (5.6% vs 3.3%, OR 1.73, 95%Cl 0.67-4.50) compared with conventional stenosis. After CEA, hyperperfusion syndrome was frequent in NO patients (7.0% vs 2.7%, OR 2.8, 95% CI1.1-7.1). One patient developed fatal hyperperfusion-related intracranial hemorrhage.
CONCLUSION: CTA-detected NO is common, particularly in subtle forms, and important for stenosis assessment and management. Unlike earlier studies, NO was not associated with increased preoperative or procedural stroke or death, but hyperperfusion syndrome after CEA was more frequent.

Title: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage of deep neck space abscesses: outcomes and predictors of treatment failure.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical evidence supporting ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage (US-PCD) as a first-line treatment for deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs) remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of US-PCD as initial management for DNSAs and to identify factors associated with treatment efficacy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with DNSAs who underwent US-PCD as a first-line treatment at four tertiary hospitals in China between 2015 and 2022. All patients were hemodynamically stable and had a stable airway, with preprocedural contrast-enhanced CT/MRI confirming no extensive mediastinal involvement beyond the anterosuperior compartment. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify preprocedural predictors of US-PCD efficacy.
RESULTS: US-PCD was performed in 117 patients. The procedure was technically accessible in 116 (98%) patients, among whom 12 (10%) had descending mediastinitis confined to the anterosuperior mediastinum. No procedure-related major complications occurred. Drainage success was achieved in 98 patients (84%). Among the 18 patients (16%) in whom US-PCD failed, three (3%) died and the remaining 15 (13%) required open surgical drainage. Multiple septations and leukocyte count were significant in univariate but not multivariable analysis. The only independent predictor of drainage failure was the presence of serious associated events-a composite variable including descending mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and vascular thrombosis (OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 1.9-17.4, p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage represents an effective minimally invasive first-line option for selected patients with deep neck space abscesses; however, open surgery should be prioritized when serious associated events are present.
KEY POINTS: Question For deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs), ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage (US-PCD) is a common surgical alternative, but its outcomes and predictors as a first-line treatment remain unclear. Findings US-PCD was effective as a first-line treatment for selected DNSAs. Only serious associated events-mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and thrombosis-independently predicted drainage failure. Clinical relevance US-PCD may be considered a first-line minimally invasive option for hemodynamically and airway-stable DNSA patients, even with anterosuperior mediastinal extension. Surgical drainage remains prioritized for cases with serious associated events to achieve rapid infection control.

Title: Association between ambient temperature and thrombosis-related signaling lipids: Implications for early cardiovascular risk.
Journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonoptimal temperatures significantly contribute to cardiovascular mortality, a burden expected to increase with climate change. Sensitive biomarkers for early cardiovascular risks remain scarce.
OBJECTIVE: We examined how thrombosis-related signaling lipids respond to ambient temperature, analyzing dose-response and lag patterns over a 30-day period, and assessed whether lipid changes mediate the association between temperature and thrombosis biomarkers using mediation analyses.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective panel study of 112 participants (aged 42-80) in Beijing (2016-2017), each completing an average of 3.4 visits. Targeted lipidomics quantified 12 thrombosis-related signaling lipids, including thromboxane (Tx) B2, three lyso-platelet-activating factors (LysoPAFs), seven lysophosphatidic acids (LPAs), and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P). Ambient temperature data were obtained from the China National Meteorological Information Centre. Associations between cumulative temperature exposures (up to 30 days) and lipids were analyzed using generalized additive mixed models. Mediation analyses assessed whether lipid changes mediated temperature effects on soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L), a sensitive biomarker for thrombotic disease.
RESULTS: Cold exposure was associated with significant decreases in TxB2, two LysoPAFs, and most LPAs (11-88% lower, median 45%, at a 30-day cumulative temperature of -0.8 °C vs. 18.7 °C). Heat exposure significantly increased all thrombosis-related lipids except LPA 20:3 (26% to 2,484% higher, median 65%, at a 30-day cumulative temperature of 27.7 °C vs. 18.7 °C), along with sCD40L (304% higher). Lipid effects were significant from 1-30 days of cumulative exposure, whereas heat-related sCD40L increases emerged after 6 days. LPA 18:0/18:1/20:4/22:6 and S1P mediated 12-32% of the heat-sCD40L association.
SIGNIFICANCE: Higher ambient temperatures are associated with increased thrombosis-related lipids, which may act as early indicators of cardiovascular risks from heat exposure.
IMPACT: This study quantified thrombosis-related signaling lipids across major lipid classes, i.e. eicosanoids (oxylipins), sphingolipids, and lysophospholipid, in a longitudinal panel study. Heat exposure significantly increased these signaling lipids, which responded to heat earlier than soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L), a sensitive thrombotic biomarker. Mediation analysis revealed that these lipids mediate up to 32% of the heat-related thrombotic response. These findings suggest that thrombosis-related signaling lipids may serve as early indicators of heat-related cardiovascular risk, with implications for biomarker-based screening and climate change adaptation strategies.

Title: Carotid energy pulsatility index provides complementary hemodynamic information to renal function in a community-based cohort.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: Conventional hemodynamic, including Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV), characteristic impedance (Zc), and brachial pulse pressure, do not directly quantify pulsatile energy transmission through the arterial system. Carotid energy pulsatility index (PI), derived from synchronized carotid pressure-flow waveforms, may capture this complementary aspect of arterial hemodynamics. We examined whether carotid energy PI was independently associated with renal function after accounting for conventional vascular hemodynamic measures. Participants from the community-based Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors Two-Township Study (CVDFACTS) underwent synchronized carotid pressure-flow waveform assessment. Associations of carotid energy PI with eGFR were evaluated using multivariable, restricted cubic spline, and segmented regression analyses. Among 1424 participants (46.8% men; mean age 59.7 ± 11.9 years), higher carotid energy PI was independently associated with lower eGFR after adjustment for covariates (standardized β = -0.088, 95% CI -0.136 to -0.039; P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline and segmented regression analyses identified turning points at 11.395 m/s for cfPWV and 0.043 for carotid energy PI. Compared with participants with low cfPWV and low carotid energy PI, those with concurrent elevations in both parameters had lower eGFR (β = -3.58, 95% CI -6.03 to -1.12; P = 0.004). Carotid energy PI was independently associated with renal function, with the greatest renal burden observed when pulsatile energy and arterial stiffness were jointly elevated. These findings suggest that carotid energy PI provides information complementary to conventional vascular measures.

Title: Impact of Photon-Counting CT Acquisition Modes on Coronary Stenosis Assessment and Radiation Dose: A Phantom and Clinical Evaluation.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) offers high spatial resolution and dose-efficient coronary CT angiography (cCTA), but protocol selection, especially optimal acquisition mode, requires balancing spacial resolution, temporal robustness and radiation exposure. This study evaluated various PCD-CT acquisition modes in terms of image quality, blooming, stenosis grading, diagnostic accuracy, and radiation dose using phantom and clinical cCTA.
METHODS: First-generation dual-source PCD-CT was used with four acquisition modes: high-pitch spiral with prospective ECG-gating (Flash), Sequence, Spiral, and retrospective ultra-high-resolution (UHR) spiral mode. Phantom experiments used six 3D-printed coronary artery models with stenoses ranging from 21% to 73%. In a retrospective clinical study, 41 cCTA examinations were analyzed. Qualitative and quantitative image assessments used invasive coronary angiography as reference standard for diagnostic accuracy. Patient characteristics and radiation doses were recorded.
RESULTS: UHR demonstrated the highest image quality and the lowest quantitative blooming in phantom and clinical data (clinical image quality score: UHR 4.12 ± 0.99 vs. Flash 3.00 ± 0.86; p = 0.002). Diagnostic accuracy varied across protocols for detecting ≥50% and ≥70% stenoses was high across all modes (e.g., Flash: 76.5% each; Sequence: 100% and 57.1%; UHR: 64.7% and 82.4%). Radiation dose was highest in UHR (26.44 ± 9.76 mSv) compared with Sequence (13.65 ± 8.86 mSv) and Flash (1.40 ± 0.32 mSv); all p ≤ 0.011.
CONCLUSION: While UHR acquisition provides highest image quality in PCD-CT cCTA, lower-dose acquisition modes achieve comparable diagnostic accuracy for coronary stenosis detection. Protocol selection should therefore be individualized, and prospective controlled studies are required.

Title: Systemic outcomes following maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder associated with an elevated risk of systemic comorbidities. Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) surgery can reduce upper airway obstruction and improve sleep parameters, but its systemic health benefits remain less well characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis was performed to synthesize evidence on the systemic health outcomes associated with MMA in patients with OSA. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through May 20, 2026. Inclusion criteria encompassed original research studies (case series, cohort studies, trials) reporting systemic health outcomes after MMA for OSA. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using an NIH quality assessment tool. Seven studies (271 patients), with mean follow-up ranging from 5.2 months to 6.6 years, met the inclusion criteria . All studies reported significant reductions in apnea-hypopnea index postoperatively. Four studies included in a meta-analysis demonstrated statistically significant reductions in blood pressure: systolic, mean difference -8.6 mmHg (95% confidence interval -14.2 to -3.0); diastolic, mean difference -5.3 mmHg (95% confidence interval -8.5 to -2.0). MMA for OSA not only improves airway patency and sleep metrics, but is also associated with enduring systemic health benefits, including a blood pressure reduction. Limited evidence also suggests potential improvements in neurocognitive outcomes. Although the evidence suggests a positive impact, further high-quality randomized controlled trials employing rigorous outcome measures (e.g., ambulatory blood pressure monitoring) are needed to fully delineate the persistent systemic effects of maxillomandibular advancement.

Title: Prognostic impact of coronary artery ectasia after acute coronary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is associated with abnormal coronary flow, thrombus formation, and impaired reperfusion, but its prognostic significance after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate clinical outcomes among patients with versus without CAE presenting with ACS.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from inception to April 2026 for studies comparing ACS patients with versus without CAE. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Subgroup, leave-one-out, and Bayesian random-effects analyses were performed to assess robustness.
RESULTS: Twelve observational studies comprising 13,540 patients were analyzed, including 1177 with CAE and 12,363 without CAE. Follow-up ranged from in-hospital assessment to 120 months. CAE was associated with a higher risk of recurrent myocardial infarction (RR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.16-3.32; P = 0.022; I2 = 61.1%), corresponding to an estimated absolute excess of 58.6 events per 1000 patients and a descriptive number needed to harm of 17. For stroke, the prespecified Hartung-Knapp analysis yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.59-3.61), whereas conventional random-effects inference, used as the basis of interpretation, yielded an RR of 2.40 (95% CI, 1.08-5.31; P = 0.031). This estimate was based on 3 studies and was model-sensitive. CAE was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality, in-hospital mortality, cardiac death, repeat revascularization, or MACE. Stent thrombosis was not pooled because only 2 studies provided estimable stent-exposed comparisons. Bayesian analyses supported the recurrent myocardial infarction finding.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients presenting with ACS, CAE identifies a higher-risk ischemic phenotype, with the most consistent association observed for recurrent myocardial infarction. Prospective studies are needed to define CAE-specific risk stratification and treatment strategies.

Title: Efficacy of Distraction Techniques on Preschool Children's Pain and Physiological Indicators During Venipuncture: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to determine and compare the effect of listening to music and watching cartoons on pain and physiological indicators resulting from venipuncture in hospitalized children at the Hefdah-Shahrivar Educational and Medical Center in Rasht, Iran.
DESIGN & METHODS: This clinical trial enrolled 114 hospitalized children aged 3-6 years over 3 months. The participants were allocated to three groups: music, cartoon, and control using a consecutive random sampling method and block randomization. Interventions were performed from 3 minutes prior to the procedure until its completion. Pain was assessed using the Oucher pain scale, and physiological indicators (HR and SpO2) were measured using a pulse oximeter 3 minutes before, during, and after the procedure. Data analysis was performed using SPSS version 16, employing descriptive statistics and statistical tests, including ANCOVA and Bonferroni post hoc tests.
RESULTS: The children in the music and cartoon groups had a significantly lower mean pain score than the control group (p < .001), while no significant difference was observed between the two intervention groups (p > .05). Regarding mean heart rate, a significant difference was observed only at the end of venipuncture between the cartoon and control groups (p < .05), with no significant differences in other variables (p > .05). The mean percentage of blood oxygen saturation did not differ significantly between the groups (p > .05).
CONCLUSION: Listening to music and watching cartoons were effective in reducing pain associated with venipuncture in children. Therefore, nurses can utilize these low-cost and low-risk nonpharmacological methods to alleviate pain resulting from invasive procedures.

Title: Rheumatic lesions of the pulmonary valve: A systematic review of the literature.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatic pulmonary valve disease accounts for<1% of cases of rheumatic heart disease. Because of its rarity, this valvular disease is often overlooked and underdiagnosed.
AIM: To conduct a systematic review of reported cases of rheumatic pulmonary valve disease worldwide.
METHODS: Studies reporting confirmed cases of rheumatic pulmonary valve disease, and providing sufficient clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic or follow-up data were included. Duplicate checking, selection, data extraction and quality assessment of the included studies were carried out by two reviewers, independently. The Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools were used for quality assessment. The process did not result in a meta-analysis because of significant heterogeneity and a lack of data. The review protocol is registered on the Prospective Registry of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261341732).
RESULTS: We identified 909 publications across the six databases. Following deduplication and selection, we included a total of 30 studies involving 35 patients, published between 1931 and 2025. Case reports predominated, accounting for 87% of studies (n=26); case series accounted for 13% (n=4). Age ranged from 3 to 83 years (median 29 years). There was a female predominance (n=20; 57%). India accounted for 37% of cases (n=13), followed by the USA with 11% (n=4). Only 46% of patients (n=16) presented with acute rheumatic fever or pre-existing rheumatic heart disease on admission. Dyspnoea was a constant symptom in all patients. Seven patients (20%) presented with atrial fibrillation. A procedure was performed in 74% of cases (n=26): pulmonary valve replacement in 40% (n=14); balloon dilation in 11% (n=4); and intraoperative commissurotomy in 20% (n=7). The clinical outcome was favourable in 74% of the documented cases (n=26).
CONCLUSIONS: Rheumatic pulmonary valve disease is a rare condition, but is likely to be underdiagnosed and underreported; it most commonly forms part of a quadrivalent valve disease. This review highlights the need for increased clinical and paraclinical vigilance when assessing the pulmonary valve in rheumatic heart disease.

Title: Cardiovascular Toxicities of Contemporary Cancer Immunotherapies: A Narrative Review of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors, Bispecific T-Cell Engagers, and CAR-T Cell Therapies.
Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), bispecific T-cell engagers (BiTEs), and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies have produced durable responses across different hematologic malignancies, but each class carries cardiovascular liabilities that differ fundamentally in mechanism, incidence, timing, and mortality risk. A structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE from inception through March 2026 was performed, supplemented by pharmacovigilance data from FAERS and WHO VigiBase, to review and synthesize the available evidence on cardiovascular toxicity and provide a structured comparison of incidence, mechanisms, clinical presentation, outcomes, and monitoring strategies to guide clinical practice. ICI-associated myocarditis is rare (0.06%-1.14%) but carries a case fatality rate approaching 50%, a lethality amplified by combination regimens and obscured by preserved left ventricular ejection fraction in approximately half of presentations. BiTEs may occupy a mechanistically intermediate position: cardiovascular adverse events are reported in 8% to 20% of pharmacovigilance cases, and 83% of these arise without documented concurrent cytokine release syndrome (CRS), implying that their immunopathological profile lies closer to ICI than to CAR-T injury. Bispecific agents are not a homogeneous class: blinatumomab, teclistamab, talquetamab, and elranatamab differ in construct, target antigen, disease setting, CRS frequency, and reported cardiovascular phenotype, and agent-level effects cannot presently be separated from population-level ones. CAR-T cell therapy produces cardiovascular events in up to 19% to 26% of patients, predominantly through IL-6-driven, CRS-coupled hemodynamic injury, with left ventricular dysfunction resolving in the majority following CRS management. Across all 3 classes, foundational clinical trials incorporated no routine cardiac monitoring, current surveillance practices are heterogeneous, and no prospective head-to-head comparative data exist. Each immune therapy class poses a qualitatively distinct cardiac threat at a different point in the treatment course. Risk-adapted surveillance extending beyond the CRS window appears prudent for BiTEs, although this reflects extrapolation rather than validated evidence; serologic and imaging monitoring regardless of systemic symptoms remains essential for ICI recipients; and CRS-guided early intervention is the cornerstone of CAR-T cardiotoxicity management. This review aims to provide clinicians with a comprehensive overview of the cardiovascular toxicities associated with these modern therapies.

Title: Associations of body shape, visceral adiposity, and metabolic function indices with risk of major noncommunicable diseases: evidence from a nationwide population cohort.
Abstract: Comparative data evaluating the predictive performance of various obesity and metabolic indices for multiple noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) remain limited. We used the data sourced from the Health Evaluation and risk Reduction through nationwide Teamwork cohort (ChinaHEART), a national population-based study that enrolled 4,258,033 Chinese adults and followed them for more than 20 million person-years between November 2014 and December 2023. Fifteen obesity and metabolic indices were categorized into three groups: (1) body shape-related indices, including body mass index (BMI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), a body shape index (ABSI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and conicity index (CI); (2) visceral fat-related indices, including lipid accumulation product (LAP) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI); and (3) metabolic function-related indices, including triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-BMI, TyG-BRI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-ABSI, TyG-WWI, and TyG-CI. The study outcomes comprised composite events of death or first hospitalization attributable to each of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), diabetes mellitus (DM), cancers, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) individually. Composite obesity and metabolic indices reflecting visceral adiposity accumulation and insulin resistance, respectively exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy for cardiovascular and diabetic risk, whereas their performance for cancer and COPD was comparatively limited. These findings support the paradigm that weight management strategies should be guided by risk assessments rather than relying solely on body weight or body shape. Furthermore, the development of diverse definitions for obesity measurement and management tailored to different population subgroups is warranted.

Title: Extracardiovascular immune-related adverse events in patients with suspected cardiac toxicity associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but may cause immune-related adverse events (iRAEs). Cardiovascular iRAEs, especially myocarditis, carry high morbidity and mortality. Extracardiovascular iRAEs are included as diagnostic criteria for myocarditis, yet their prevalence, spectrum, and clinical impact in patients with suspected cardiovascular iRAEs are poorly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-center observational study between March 2022 and December 2023. Consecutive patients referred to cardio-oncology for suspected ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity underwent systematic cardiovascular evaluation, internal medicine assessment, pharmacovigilance review, and multidisciplinary adjudication. Data included cardiovascular and extracardiovascular iRAEs, treatment decisions, and outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 208 patients enrolled (median age 60 years; 78% female), 206 completed follow-up. Cardiovascular iRAEs were confirmed in 108 patients, predominantly myocarditis (75%). Extracardiovascular iRAEs occurred in 32% of patients (n = 67; 97 events), most frequently endocrine (57.6%, mainly thyroid), followed by muscular and cutaneous events (each 9.3%). Most extracardiovascular iRAEs were CTCAE grade 2, while severe muscular or neurological toxicities, including myositis and myasthenia gravis, occurred in 1.4%. Myocarditis was more frequent in patients with extracardiovascular iRAEs (57% vs. 34%). In 18 cases, extracardiovascular iRAEs fulfilled IC-OS minor criteria, enabling a definite myocarditis diagnosis. ICIs were discontinued in 56% of patients, with extracardiovascular iRAEs contributing in 15%, and accounted for nearly one-third of indications for immunosuppressive therapy. Mortality was mainly cancer-related.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients referred for suspected ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity, extracardiovascular iRAEs are frequent and clinically relevant. They contribute to myocarditis diagnosis and management, supporting systematic multidisciplinary cardiology-internal medicine evaluation.

Title: Prospective evaluation assessing the influence of outcome definition, cohort inclusion and DORIS remission in predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with systemic lupus erythematosus.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is associated with increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). The Predictors of Pregnancy Outcomes: Biomarkers in Antiphospholipid Syndrome and SLE (PROMISSE) study set the benchmark for APO rates in SLE but used narrow APO definitions, including only outcomes deemed most severe, and excluded high-risk patients. Therefore, PROMISSE may underestimate the true burden of APOs in SLE and how PROMISSE findings translate to real-world SLE pregnancies is unclear. Thus, we sought to evaluate APO rates and predictors, including Definition of Remission in SLE (DORIS) status, influenced by inclusion criteria and APO definitions.
METHODS: We studied 107 SLE pregnancies in 107 individuals from a prospective cohort, with multifetal pregnancies as the sole exclusion criterion. The cohort was analysed overall and in two subgroups, a PROMISSE-eligible subset meeting PROMISSE inclusion criteria (n=90) and a higher-risk PROMISSE-ineligible (based on proteinuria >1 g/g, hypertension, prednisone >20 mg/day, serum creatinine >1.2 mg/dL and/or diabetes) subset (n=17). APOs were defined using PROMISSE and selected American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) definitions.
RESULTS: Using PROMISSE-defined outcomes, APOs occurred in 30% of the total cohort, 24% of the PROMISSE-eligible subset and 59% of the higher-risk PROMISSE-ineligible subset. Applying ACOG definitions increased event rates across all groups (50%, 43% and 82%, respectively). APOs, particularly preterm birth and pre-eclampsia, were observed more frequently among patients not in DORIS remission. All three neonatal deaths and all three pregnancy losses occurred in patients in non-remission.
CONCLUSIONS: APO rates in SLE are highly impacted by the patient population studied and outcome definitions. Across disease severity, APOs were observed more frequently in the absence of DORIS remission. The high APO rate in the PROMISSE-ineligible subset reflects patients with high-risk clinical features for whom pregnancy would often be deferred until disease optimisation, emphasising the need for robust preconception counselling in SLE patients.

Title: Long-term outcomes and impact of diagnostic coding of patients with heart failure identified in primary care: insights from the OSCAR-HF cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Misclassification of heart failure (HF) in primary care electronic health records (EHRs) may affect care quality and outcomes. The OSCAR-HF (Optimising Standards of Care of Heart Failure in general practice) study implemented audit and feedback to improve HF identification in Belgian general practices. We assessed long-term outcomes in the OSCAR-HF cohort and examined differences by preaudit HF registration status.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We followed 538 patients identified with HF after an EHR audit in eight primary care practices (2017, median follow-up 7.4 years). Overall survival at 1, 2 and 5 years was 93.2%, 84.3% and 62.4%. During follow-up, 1083 hospital admissions occurred; 11.3% were HF-related and 64.3% were non-cardiovascular. We compared patients with a preaudit registered HF diagnosis (n=177) versus those without (n=361). Preaudit registered patients had more HF admissions during follow-up (23% of patients vs 13%, p=0.002), yet lower all-cause mortality in multivariable analysis (adjusted HR 0.62; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.95). Nearly half of the HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) population had no preaudit HF registration (49%, n=54/110). Unregistered patients more often had HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (61% of patients vs 49%, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this primary care HF cohort, HF admissions were infrequent and most hospitalisations were non-cardiovascular. Patients with a registered preaudit HF diagnosis had more HF admissions but lower mortality. The high proportion of unregistered HFrEF and the increased range of therapeutic options for the HFpEF spectrum underscore the need for comprehensive case-finding and accurate coding across the HF spectrum in primary care.

Title: Comparative analysis of pregnancy outcomes in women with type 1 vs type 2 diabetes mellitus: A 10-year retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the global rise in diabetes mellitus (DM), pregnancies in women with preexisting DM are becoming increasingly common and are associated with a higher risk of adverse outcomes. However, the relative impact of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) vs type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unclear.
