Coronary-ventricular coupling emerges as a promising automated CT-derived imaging marker with a biologically plausible pathophysiological basis, linking coronary arterial volume to ventricular size in mitral valve disease.

Title: The Association of Fasting Glucose and Total Cholesterol with Cognitive Performance in a Primary Care Population: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Objectives: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the associations between fundamental metabolic markers, specifically fasting glucose and total cholesterol, and cognitive performance in a primary care population, continuing previous analyses focused on subclinical vascular parameters. Methods: The study included 137 primary care patients who completed neuropsychological assessments (Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)) and a clinical interview. Fasting glucose and total cholesterol levels were extracted from their medical records. Results: Based on the MMSE, 26 participants (19.0%) had mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 8 (5.8%) had neurocognitive disorders. Univariate regression analysis revealed that fasting glucose was significantly and inversely associated with the total ACE-III score (B = 0.277; 95% CI: -0.441 to -0.113; p = 0.001) and the M-ACE subscale score (B = 0.175; 95% CI: -0.342 to -0.008; p = 0.046). Conversely, total cholesterol showed a positive association with both the overall ACE-III score (B = 0.173; 95% CI: 0.006 to 0.340; p = 0.046) and the M-ACE score (B = 0.219; 95% CI: 0.053 to 0.385; p = 0.011). A potential clinical paradox was observed, as among patients with established cardiovascular disease, lower total cholesterol (177.39 vs. 201.58 mg/dL, p = 0.047) co-occurred with poorer cognitive outcomes (mean ACE-III: 81.47 vs. 87.62, p = 0.003), possibly reflecting a confounding effect of statin therapy. Standard MMSE scores did not correlate significantly with any evaluated metabolic parameters. Conclusions: Fasting glucose and total cholesterol are cross-sectionally associated with cognitive performance in this primary care cohort, whereas standard MMSE scores did not exhibit significant metabolic correlations. Given the exploratory, cross-sectional design, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and do not establish clinical screening utility or causality. The disparate patterns of association between the ACE-III and MMSE suggest that these screening tools may capture metabolism-related cognitive variations differently, highlighting the need for prospective longitudinal research.

Title: A Distinct Circulating Biomarker Signature of Acute Thrombophlebitis: Associations Among Heparin, Midkine, Pleiotrophin, Dermcidin, and Ghrelin.
Abstract: Background: Acute superficial venous thrombosis (SVT) presenting with clinical features of thrombophlebitis is increasingly recognized as a thromboinflammatory disorder in which innate immunity and coagulation are closely interconnected. Nonetheless, the role of endogenous antimicrobial peptides and heparin-binding growth factors in its pathogenesis is still inadequately comprehended. We investigated circulating dermcidin (DCD), ghrelin (GHR), heparin (HP), midkine (MK), and pleiotrophin (PTN) to explore their potential involvement in the thromboinflammatory network underlying SVT. Methods: In this prospective case-control study, 30 individuals with SVT and 28 healthy controls matched for age and sex were recruited. DCD, GHR, HP, MK, and PTN concentrations were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Results: Patients with SVT exhibited significantly higher circulating DCD, GHR, MK, and PTN concentrations and significantly lower the measured HP concentration than healthy controls (all p < 0.05). Following LMWH treatment, the measured HP concentration increased significantly (p < 0.05), whereas DCD, GHR, MK, and PTN showed downward trends. Conclusions: Acute superficial venous thrombosis is associated with coordinated alterations in circulating the measured heparin, dermcidin, ghrelin, midkine, and pleiotrophin, reflecting a systemic thromboinflammatory biomarker profile. These findings suggest potential interactions among heparin biology, heparin-binding growth factors, and innate immune mediators but do not establish direct molecular interactions, heparin sequestration, functional depletion, or causality. This biomarker profile establishes a foundation for creating hypotheses for forthcoming investigations that include direct biochemical validation, standardized longitudinal sampling, and independent cohorts.

Title: Impaired Left Atrial Function in Patients with Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source (ESUS) refers to non-lacunar ischemic stroke without an identified cause and is presumed to be related to a cardioembolic mechanism. A potential etiological factor is atrial fibrosis leading to left atrial (LA) dysfunction, also known as atrial cardiomyopathy. This study aimed to compare advanced transthoracic echocardiographic parameters of LA function in patients with ESUS and age- and sex-matched controls. Methods: In this prospective matched observational case-control study, fifty patients with ESUS and 50 age- and sex-matched controls were analyzed. All participants underwent comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). LA parameters included four-dimensional volumetry, LA strain (LAS), and LA stiffness index calculated as the ratio of E/e' to reservoir strain. All ESUS patients additionally underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) to assess the presence of patent foramen ovale (PFO). Results: Compared with controls, ESUS patients had significantly reduced LAS in the reservoir phase (LAS-r 37.3% vs. 42.3%; p < 0.01) and conduit phase (LAS-cd 22.9% vs. 28.4%; p < 0.01), as well as a higher LA stiffness index (0.171 vs. 0.149; p < 0.01). No significant differences were found in LA size or volume. In subgroup analysis, ESUS patients with and without PFO did not differ, while both subgroups showed significant impairment compared with controls. Conclusions: ESUS is associated with impaired LA functional properties despite preserved LA size. LAS may provide complementary information on subclinical LA functional abnormalities in patients with ESUS; however, its clinical and prognostic significance requires validation in prospective studies.

Title: A Multidimensional Assessment of Cardiometabolic Risk in Asian Americans with Chronic Hepatitis B Using the All of Us Datasets.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Asian Americans (AAs) bear a disproportionate burden of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), with one in 12 living with this condition. Despite evidence that cardiometabolic conditions accelerate CHB progression and hepatocellular carcinoma risk, cardiometabolic comorbidities in this population remain critically understudied. This study provides an assessment of cardiometabolic burden and phenotypic heterogeneity among AAs with CHB. Methods: We analyzed data from the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset v8 (n = 436 AAs with CHB). We ran descriptive analyses to examine four cardiometabolic conditions (hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus [T2DM], dyslipidemia, and central obesity). Unsupervised clustering (k-prototypes and k-modes) identified cardiometabolic phenotypes in the overall sample and stratified by sex and age. Multinomial logistic regression examined sociodemographic predictors of cluster membership. Results: Cardiometabolic burden was substantial: 38.76% had hypertension, 25.46% dyslipidemia, 17.66% T2DM, and 16.74% central obesity. Nearly two-thirds (61.93%) had at least one cardiometabolic condition, and over one-quarter (28.90%) had two or more. Cluster analysis identified three phenotypes: "Young/Healthy" (54.6%), "Dyslipidemia-Dominant" (19.7%), and "Hypertension-Dominant" (25.7%). Sex- and age-stratified analyses revealed divergent metabolic profiles not apparent in the overall solution. Conclusions: AAs with CHB carry a high and heterogeneous cardiometabolic burden. Integrated metabolic screening and sex- and age-informed prevention strategies may be warranted for this high-risk population, though prospective validation is needed to establish the clinical utility of these phenotypes.

Title: Association Between Admission Neutrophil Count and Preoperative Deep Vein Thrombosis Risk in Older Patients with Hip Fracture: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Objective: This study investigated the association between admission neutrophil count and the risk of preoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in older patients with hip fractures. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged ≥65 years with hip fractures between January 2015 and September 2019. The primary outcome was the presence of preoperative DVT diagnosed by color Doppler ultrasonography. We used multivariable logistic regression models to assess the association. We examined nonlinearity using smooth curve fitting and threshold effect analysis. Results: Among the 1807 patients, 571 (31.6%) developed preoperative DVT. We identified a nonlinear relationship with a threshold effect. The inflection point for neutrophil count was 3.17 × 109/L. Below this threshold, no significant association with DVT risk was observed (OR = 1.90, 95% CI: 0.90-3.99, p = 0.092). Interestingly, above this threshold, each 1 × 109/L increase in neutrophil count was associated with 8% lower odds of preoperative DVT (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.89-0.96, p < 0.001). Conclusions: In older hip fracture patients, admission neutrophil count exhibits a curvilinear association with preoperative DVT risk with a threshold effect at 3.17 × 109/L. This data-driven threshold finding is exploratory and hypothesis-generating. It may support subsequent external validation and mechanistic research.

Title: From Mechanism to Management in Vasovagal Syncope: An Integrative Review.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Vasovagal syncope is the most common subtype of reflex syncope and a frequent cause of transient loss of consciousness. Although its prognosis is generally benign, recurrent episodes can cause injury, restrict daily activities, and impair quality of life; patients who remain symptomatic despite first-line measures present a therapeutic challenge. This review integrates current evidence on mechanisms, prediction, and treatment, examining whether arterial-pressure defence and baroreflex behaviour provide a useful physiological framework. Methods: We conducted a narrative integrative review of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to June 2026, prioritising randomised trials, meta-analyses, major observational studies, guidelines and multi-society statements. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or de novo quantitative synthesis was undertaken. Results: Current evidence supports a dynamic failure of cardiovascular compensation during orthostatic stress, with variable contributions from impaired vasoconstrictor support and cardioinhibition. Laboratory haemodynamic and autonomic markers may anticipate tilt-test outcome, but this should not be equated with prediction of spontaneous clinical recurrence. Tilt training may modify vasoconstrictor reserve and baroreflex indices, although clinical efficacy varies with protocol and adherence. Therapeutic options extend from counter-pressure manoeuvres and selected pharmacological agents to pacing in highly selected patients with documented clinically relevant asystole; cardioneuroablation remains an emerging intervention. Conclusions: The haemodynamic phenotype may inform treatment selection but should not be used as a stand-alone indication for invasive therapy. We propose an evidence-informed, mechanism-based model of care, incorporating patient-reported outcomes, shared decision-making and cautious evaluation of emerging predictive and interventional approaches.

Title: Development and Validation of a Predictive Model for 6-Month All-Cause Mortality in Pulmonary Embolism.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet existing risk stratification tools predominantly focus on short-term outcomes. In this study, we set out to develop and externally validate a predictive model for 6-month all-cause mortality in PE patients using routinely available clinical parameters. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients with PE from two independent cohorts. The MIMIC-IV database served as the training set for variable selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. External validation was performed using data from the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University. Model performance was assessed through discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results: The training cohort comprised 814 patients from the MIMIC-IV database, with a 6-month all-cause mortality rate of 21.3% (n = 174). LASSO regression initially selected 13 predictors. External validation in the local cohort (n = 217, 6-month all-cause mortality: 16.5%) refined these to four core predictors: respiratory rate, oxygen saturation (SpO2), and the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI). The parsimonious model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.74-0.88), excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.367), and positive net clinical benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. After standardizing SIRI to absolute counts, SIRI was retained as a pre-specified inflammatory predictor. Conclusions: This simplified model incorporating four readily available clinical variables accurately predicts 6-month all-cause mortality in patients with PE.

Title: Prognostic Impact of Transient Return of Spontaneous Circulation According to Low-Flow Time in Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Undergoing Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Low-flow time (LFT) is a major prognostic factor in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR), but chronological LFT may not fully reflect ischemic burden when transient return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) occurs. We investigated whether the association between transient ROSC and outcomes varies according to LFT. Methods: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 810 adults with witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge, and the secondary outcome was good neurological outcome. A prespecified subgroup analysis compared LFT ≤90 versus >90 min, followed by an exploratory analysis using <60, 60-90, and >90 min categories. Multivariable logistic regression and interaction analyses were performed. Results: Among 810 patients, 450 (55.6%) experienced transient ROSC. In the prespecified analysis, transient ROSC was associated with survival in patients with LFT ≤90 min (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 2.375; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.076-5.241; p = 0.032), but not in those with LFT >90 min (AOR, 0.884; 95% CI, 0.595-1.315; p = 0.543), with a significant interaction (p = 0.036). The exploratory three-category analysis showed a significant association in the 60-90-min subgroup (AOR, 3.399; 95% CI, 1.021-11.316; p = 0.046), although the global interaction was not significant (p = 0.126). No significant interaction was observed for good neurological outcome. The prespecified survival interaction remained significant in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: The association between transient ROSC and survival after ECPR differed according to LFT using the prespecified 90-min cutoff. Transient ROSC may provide prognostic information complementary to chronological LFT, whereas the three-category findings should be considered exploratory.

Title: The Relationship Between the Remnant Cholesterol Inflammation Index and Coronary Collateral Circulation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Although chronic total occlusion (CTO) often presents with varying degrees of coronary collateral circulation (CCC), the biological factors accompanying inadequate collateralization are not fully established. The Remnant Cholesterol Inflammation Index (RCII) is a composite metric integrating atherogenic lipid load and systemic inflammation. This study examined the association between RCII and CCC and the discriminative ability of RCII for identifying insufficient collateral networks in patients with CTO. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, single-center analysis evaluated 359 patients with at least one major epicardial CTO who underwent diagnostic coronary angiography between 15 January 2023 and 15 January 2026. Participants were stratified via the Rentrop scoring system into poor (grades 0-1; n = 168) and good (grades 2-3; n = 191) CCC cohorts. RCII was calculated as [remnant cholesterol (mg/dL) × high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP, mg/L)]/10, with remnant cholesterol derived as total cholesterol minus LDL-C and HDL-C. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models, together with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, were used to assess the association of RCII with poor CCC and its discriminative ability. Results: Patients with poor CCC exhibited significantly higher RCII values compared with the good CCC cohort (19.7 ± 4.7 vs. 6.5 ± 2.4, p < 0.001). Following multivariable adjustment, higher RCII remained independently associated with poor collateralization (OR 1.120, 95% CI 1.052-1.199; p < 0.001), alongside right coronary artery (RCA) CTO and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). RCII showed discriminative ability for poor CCC (AUC 0.792, 95% CI 0.745-0.835; p < 0.001), which was greater than that of remnant cholesterol, hs-CRP, or SII considered separately. In this cohort, an RCII threshold above 12.3 identified poor CCC with 80% sensitivity and 71% specificity. Conclusions: In this retrospective cohort, higher RCII was independently associated with inadequate coronary collateralization in the setting of CTO. RCII may represent a candidate marker of the combined residual lipid and inflammatory burden; prospective studies and external validation, together with formal assessment of clinical utility, are required before any clinical application can be considered.

Title: Distinct Determinants of Hospitalisation and In-Hospital Mortality After Acute Stroke: Insights into Stroke-Heart Syndrome (SHS-PARTICLES Study).
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) involves myocardial injury, cardiac dysfunction, and arrhythmias after acute stroke, playing a key role in prognosis. Most evidence comes from acute ischaemic stroke (IS), while cardiac involvement after haemorrhagic stroke (HS) is less understood. Additionally, the prognostic roles of cardiac biomarkers, neurological severity, and cardiac systolic function on early outcomes are not well defined. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 586 patients with stroke, assessing admission and peak high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), length of hospital stay (LOS), and in-hospital mortality. Univariable and multivariable regression analyses evaluated factors associated with mortality and LOS. Results: The cohort comprised 586 patients with acute cerebrovascular events, including 560 (95.6%) with acute ischaemic cerebrovascular disease (ischaemic ACVD) and 26 (4.4%) with HS. HS patients had higher hs-cTnI elevations and concentrations, whereas NT-proBNP did not differ between stroke subtypes. In univariable analyses, age, hs-cTnI, NT-proBNP, LVEF, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) were associated with in-hospital mortality. In multivariable analysis, peak NT-proBNP remained independently associated with mortality even after logarithmic transformation. Older age, higher NIHSS and mRS scores, and lower LVEF were associated with longer LOS only in univariable analyses. Conclusions: Cardiac and neurological abnormalities provide complementary prognostic roles after acute stroke. HS was associated with a more pronounced myocardial injury profile, whereas peak NT-proBNP was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings support integrated neurological and cardiovascular risk assessment after acute stroke.

Title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Cardiometabolic, Inflammatory, Hormonal, Body Composition, and Behavioral Health Profiles in Physically Active Young Adults: An Analytical Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background: The Mediterranean Diet (MD) is linked to better cardiometabolic and inflammatory health, but its relationships with appetite-related hormones, body composition, and behavioral health remain unclear in physically active young adults from understudied Arab settings. Objective: To examine associations between MD adherence and cardiometabolic, inflammatory, hormonal, body-composition, and behavioral-health profiles, including sleep quality, physical activity, perceived recovery, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL), among physically active young adults in Jordan. Methods: Eighty adults aged 18-35 years (44 men and 36 women) were recruited from fitness centers and campuses in Amman. MD adherence was assessed using the validated Moroccan Arabic version of the 14-item Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS; adherent ≥ 8). Fasting lipid profile, C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), leptin, and ghrelin were measured using enzymatic and ELISA methods. Anthropometric and body-composition measures were assessed using stadiometry and multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Sleep quality, physical activity, perceived recovery, and HRQoL were assessed using validated questionnaires. Results: 60% of participants were non-adherent to the MD. In exploratory analyses, non-adherence was associated with higher odds of abnormal triglycerides (adjusted OR = 9.17, 95% CI: 2.08-40.38). After additional adjustment for percent body fat, the association with abnormal CRP remained significant (adjusted OR = 5.39, 95% CI: 1.34-21.61), whereas the association with abnormal leptin was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted OR = 3.47, 95% CI: 0.75-16.07). The leptin finding was sensitive to adjustment for adiposity, while residual confounding remains possible for the CRP association. Non-adherent participants had higher BMI, body fat mass, and percent body fat, and lower physical HRQoL. No statistically significant associations were detected for ghrelin, resting blood pressure, or resting heart rate. The IL-6 findings were inconclusive because 62.5% of measurements were below the assay detection limit. Conclusions: Greater MD adherence was associated with a more favorable cardiometabolic and body-composition profile in this exploratory cross-sectional sample. These hypothesis-generating findings highlight the importance of considering dietary quality alongside physical activity and require confirmation in larger prospective studies with more comprehensive confounder adjustment.

Title: Prescribing Appropriateness and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized Adults with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic required repeated revision of national treatment protocols; evaluating prescribing against the guidance then in force is central to stewardship. Objective: To characterize clinical outcomes of adults hospitalized with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, and to assess prescribing appropriateness using the Medication Appropriateness Index (MAI) benchmarked against contemporaneous Ministry of Health (MOH) guidance. Methods: Single-center retrospective cohort study of all adults (aged 18 years or over) admitted with COVID-19 between 1 March 2020 and 28 February 2021. Two trained clinical pharmacists independently applied the MAI to 1018 prescriptions. All associations were examined in univariable, unadjusted analyses. Results: Hypertension (44.1%), diabetes (38.7%), end-stage renal disease (13.7%), and cardiac disease (12.4%) were prevalent. In-hospital mortality was 26.8% (121/451 patients with a determinate outcome). Diabetes (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.32-3.08), hypertension (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.26-2.93), and cardiac disease (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.15-3.64) were each associated with higher unadjusted odds of death; patients who died were on average 15.8 years older (p < 0.0001). Overall, 936 of 1018 prescriptions (91.9%) were appropriate; rates ranged from 99.4% (311/313) for enoxaparin to 42.9% (6/14) for hydroxychloroquine, the latter based on a small number of prescriptions. Inappropriate prescriptions were flagged mainly in the duration (82.9%) and indication (70.7%) domains, and receipt of at least one inappropriate prescription was not associated with mortality (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.31-1.12; p = 0.10). Conclusions: Anticoagulants and corticosteroids were largely prescribed in line with contemporaneous MOH guidance; several repurposed agents were not. These findings support an MAI-based audit against the guideline version in force as a tool for quality control.

Title: The Psychosocial Pathways of Expectancy-Value Beliefs, Physical Fitness, and Executive Function Among Adolescents.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Adequate physical fitness has been associated with cognitive health among adolescents, and psychosocial processes may help explain this relationship. However, evidence regarding the mechanisms linking physical fitness and cognitive health remains limited. Guided by expectancy-value theory, this study examined the direct and indirect effects of expectancy-value beliefs on executive function through physical fitness among adolescents. Methods: A prospective research design was used. Participants were 424 adolescents (58% female; Mage = 12.72 years, SD = 0.93) recruited from the southwestern United States. Physical fitness components, including cardiovascular fitness, muscular fitness, flexibility, and body mass index (BMI), were assessed using the FITNESSGRAM® test battery. Expectancy-value beliefs and executive function were measured using validated self-report instruments. Structural equation modeling was conducted to examine the proposed relationships. Results: Expectancy-value beliefs were significantly associated with all physical fitness components (rs ranged from -0.86 to 0.46, ps < 0.01) except flexibility. Cardiovascular fitness and muscular fitness were negatively associated with executive function scores (rs ranged from -0.29 to -0.21, ps < 0.01), whereas BMI was positively associated with executive function scores. The proposed model demonstrated an acceptable fit (χ2/df = 284.16/113, p < 0.001; CFI = 0.90; RMSEA = 0.06, 90% CI [0.05, 0.07]). There was a significant indirect effect of expectancy-value beliefs on executive function through physical fitness (β = -0.11). The model explained 12% of the variance in physical fitness and 9% of the variance in executive function. Conclusions: The findings provide evidence for the proposed psychosocial mediation model linking expectancy-value beliefs, physical fitness, and executive function among adolescents. It suggests strategies that strengthen perceived competence and task values may improve physical fitness and, in turn, enhance executive function.

Title: Inpatient Expenditure Composition and Factors Associated with High-Expenditure Patients with Chronic Wounds: A Retrospective Analysis.
Abstract: Background: Chronic wounds impose a substantial clinical and economic burden on patients and health systems. The purpose of this study was to characterize the composition and concentration of inpatient expenditure among patients with chronic wounds, identify clinical and treatment-related factors associated with higher inpatient expenditure, and describe the characteristics and expenditure contribution of high-expenditure patients. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 713 patients discharged after inpatient treatment for chronic wounds at a tertiary hospital in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China, between 2020 and 2024. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, infection status, wound pathogen results, treatment procedures, clinical outcomes, length of stay, and inpatient expenditure were collected. Patients in the top 10% of total inpatient expenditure were defined as high-expenditure patients. Descriptive analyses, expenditure stratification, multivariable regression, and expenditure concentration analyses were performed. Results: Medical consumables, diagnostic services, treatment procedures, and medications were the main components of inpatient expenditure. Length of stay, peripheral arterial disease, clinical infection, cardiovascular disease, comorbidity burden, wound pathogen results, and surgical interventions were associated with higher inpatient expenditure. High-expenditure patients represented a small proportion of the cohort but accounted for approximately one-third of total inpatient expenditure and had greater clinical complexity, including higher prevalence of infection and vascular disease and more intensive treatment needs. Conclusions: Inpatient chronic wound care is characterized by substantial expenditure, complex clinical management, and concentration of resource use among a small high-expenditure subgroup. Early risk identification, multidisciplinary management, standardized treatment pathways, and targeted resource-allocation strategies may help improve the efficiency of chronic wound care.

Title: Association of Combined Cardiometabolic and Muscle Impairment Index with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Progression Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Prospective Two-Cohort Study.
Abstract: Introduction: Advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome portends poor cardiovascular outcomes. The cardiometabolic index (CMI) and muscle-loss index (MLI) independently reflect metabolic and cardiovascular risk, but their combined effect on CKM syndrome remains unexplored. We aimed to evaluate the association of CMI-MLI with advanced CKM stages cross-sectionally and with incident CVD longitudinally, among adults aged 45 years and older. Methods: We analyzed data from adults aged ≥45 years in the CHARLS (2011-2020) and NHANES (1999-2004). The CMI-MLI index was calculated as the natural logarithm of CMI × MLI, where CMI = (triglycerides/HDL-cholesterol) × (waist/height) and MLI = cystatin C/creatinine. CKM syndrome was staged from 0 to 4 per metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal status, with Stage 3 defined by a high 10-year Framingham risk (≥21.6% in men, ≥21.5% in women) or advanced CKD. Logistic regression assessed the cross-sectional association of CMI-MLI with advanced CKM stages, with a sensitivity analysis defining Stage 3 solely by advanced CKD to address potential circularity; Cox regression evaluated its relationship with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). Results: Among 6921 CHARLS and 3185 NHANES participants (the latter serving as a cross-sectional replication cohort), higher CMI-MLI quartiles were significantly associated with advanced CKM stages in both cohorts (p for trend <0.0001). Over a median 9-year follow-up of 5768 CHARLS participants with baseline CKM stages 0-3, 1384 incident CVD events occurred. Participants in the highest CMI-MLI quartile had a significantly higher risk of incident CVD (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.15-1.59) than those in the lowest quartile, and each SD increase in CMI-MLI was independently associated with a higher CVD risk (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.04-1.17). Conclusions: CMI-MLI was significantly associated with advanced CKM stages and independently predicted incident CVD among individuals free of baseline disease. The cross-sectional association was attenuated when Stage 3 was defined solely by advanced CKD, suggesting partial circularity between the CMI components and the risk score, whereas the prospective association with incident CVD was unaffected. Although its discriminatory ability was modest (area under the curve 0.605) and its incremental value over CMI alone was limited, CMI-MLI may serve as a simple, parsimonious marker for identifying individuals with concurrent cardiometabolic and muscle-related risk.

Title: Community Pharmacy Involvement in Cardiovascular Patient Follow-Up: A Conceptual Framework for Integrated Ambulatory Pharmaceutical Care.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, requiring coordinated long-term management of cardiovascular risk factors, complex pharmacotherapy, and continuity of care across healthcare settings. Community pharmacists are well-placed to support ambulatory cardiovascular care; however, their contribution often remains insufficiently integrated into cardiovascular care pathways, limiting continuity, information exchange, and coordinated medication management across community, primary, and specialist care. This study aimed to establish the scientific basis for the development of an Integrated Ambulatory Pharmaceutical Follow-Up Programme in Cardiology by synthesising the available evidence on pharmacist-led cardiovascular care. Methods: An evidence-informed narrative synthesis was conducted using targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, complemented by manual screening of reference lists. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomised controlled trials, and high-quality observational studies addressing pharmacist-led interventions in cardiovascular risk management, heart failure, transitions of care, cardiac rehabilitation, and integrated pharmaceutical care. Evidence was mapped across clinical outcomes, care processes, professional roles, and implementation requirements and subsequently translated into the components of the proposed integrated ambulatory care framework. Results: The available evidence consistently indicates that pharmacist-led interventions improve cardiovascular risk factor control, medication adherence, pharmacotherapy optimisation, and patient-reported outcomes. Community pharmacies provide accessible and effective settings for cardiovascular risk screening, chronic disease monitoring, and structured follow-up. In heart failure, pharmacist involvement supports optimisation of guideline-directed medical therapy, while during care transitions it contributes to the identification and reduction in medication-related problems. In cardiac rehabilitation and secondary prevention, pharmacist-led care supports medication optimisation, adherence, and cardiovascular risk-factor management. Overall, the available evidence supports the integration of community pharmacists into multidisciplinary ambulatory cardiovascular care pathways and provides the evidence base for the proposed conceptual framework. Conclusions: The proposed Integrated Ambulatory Pharmaceutical Follow-Up Programme in Cardiology provides an evidence-informed conceptual framework to support the structured integration of community pharmacists into ambulatory cardiovascular care. Its implementation has the potential to strengthen continuity of care, optimise pharmacotherapy, and support improved cardiovascular outcomes when supported by collaborative practice models, interoperable health information systems, and appropriate organisational frameworks.

Title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
Abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

Title: Contemporary Approaches to Prehospital Acute Coronary Syndrome Risk Stratification: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Chest pain is a common high-risk complaint encountered by emergency medical services (EMS). Early identification and treatment of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) improve outcomes, yet prehospital evaluation remains constrained by limited diagnostic resources. This narrative review examines contemporary approaches to prehospital ACS risk stratification, diagnostic technologies, and decision-making. A targeted PubMed search of peer-reviewed publications and selected grey literature published between 2020 and 2025 was supplemented by targeted searches and citation review. Relevant literature published after the initial search period was incorporated during manuscript preparation and revision. Studies addressing prehospital ACS risk stratification, electrocardiogram (ECG) assessment, point-ofcare biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnostics, and systems-level cardiac triage were included and synthesized thematically. Biomarker-integrated pathways, particularly HEART-derived approaches combined with point-of-care troponin testing, demonstrated the strongest evidence for safe prehospital risk assessment and reduced healthcare utilization. Biomarker-free approaches offered broader applicability but lower diagnostic certainty. ECG acquisition and transmission remained foundational for STEMI recognition and activation, while AI-assisted ECG interpretation and decision-support tools showed promising diagnostic performance but lacked prospective outcome-based validation. Gaps remain regarding atypical presentations, sex-specific strategies, and validation across diverse EMS environments. Overall, contemporary evidence supports structured prehospital risk stratification as decision support rather than definitive diagnosis. Implementation depends on provider training, protocol standardization, resources, and integration within regional systems of care. Future research should prioritize validation across diverse EMS settings, atypical and sex-specific presentations, and prospective evaluation of emerging diagnostic technologies.

Title: Clinical Presentation, Management and Outcome of Heart Failure Patients.
Journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is a major public health issue with rising hospitalizations and high mortality. This study was conducted to assess the clinical presentation, management and outcome of heart failure patients presenting to a tertiary care hospital.
METHODS: A prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary cardiac center in Nepal over a period of six months among admitted patients aged 18 years and above with heart failure. Data on demographics, etiology, treatment, and outcomes were collected via structured interviews, chart review, clinical observation, phone calls and follow-up. Etiologies were defined per standard criteria and patients were categorized according to the clinical and echocardiographic diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 1523 patients included, the mean age of the cohort was 61.5 ± 14.9 years, and 62.0 % were male. Coronary artery disease (65.8%) was the most common etiology, followed by idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (15.0%) and rheumatic heart disease (7.2%). Acute coronary syndrome (39.9%) was the primary aggravating factor. Guideline-directed medical therapy use included Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (68.5%), Beta-blockers (66.1%), and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (61.2%); however, the use of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitors was low (15.2%). Device therapy was rare (0.26%). The overall mortality rate was 12.7%, comprising 4.7% in-hospital mortality and 7.9% 90-day mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary artery disease is the commonest etiology, with Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker as the commonest prescription, followed by Beta-blockers and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, with device therapy being rare, with an overall mortality of 12.7%.

Title: Comparative outcomes of central venous access via open jugular and ultrasound-guided subclavian approaches in low-weight pediatric patients: a study with secondary outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The necessity of this study stems from the lack of comparative evidence on the outcomes of central venous catheterization via the open internal jugular and ultrasound-guided subclavian approaches in low-weight pediatric patients. Its innovation lies in the simultaneous evaluation of both primary and secondary outcomes of these two techniques in this vulnerable population.
METHODS: This prospective randomized clinical trial at Mardani Azar Children's Hospital (winter 2022-2023) included 92 pediatric patients under five kilograms weight, randomly assigned to either open internal jugular or ultrasound-guided subclavian vein catheterization (46 per group). Procedural success and major complications-such as pneumothorax, arterial cannulation, ectopic catheter placement, infection, and thrombosis-were evaluated intraoperatively and during a two-weeks follow-up using imaging and clinical assessment.
RESULTS: The mean catheter placement time was significantly longer in the jugular group than in the subclavian group (41.19 ± 13.8 vs. 33.15 ± 12.12 min; P = 0.04). No cases of pneumothorax, hemothorax, bleeding, arrhythmia, occlusion, infection, or death occurred in either group. Hematoma developed only in the jugular group (6 vs. 0; P = 0.02), and all cases were associated with a procedure duration greater than 35 min (P = 0.041). In the subclavian group, all failures (n = 4) and upper limb edema (n = 3) occurred exclusively in patients under 2.5 kg, with both outcomes significantly linked to lower body weight (P = 0.03 and P = 0.014, respectively). Other complications showed no significant differences between groups.
CONCLUSION: Both approaches were generally safe, with no major adverse events observed in either group. Ultrasound-guided subclavian access was associated with a shorter procedure time, whereas hematoma occurred only in the jugular group and catheterization failure and upper-limb edema were seen only in low-weight infants in the subclavian group. However, because access site and technique were evaluated together, their independent effects could not be determined. In addition, the findings in infants weighing < 2.5 kg were based on few events and should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This clinical trial was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) with the code IRCT20230901059317N1(Registration date: 2024-02-16).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of deep vein thrombosis in elderly ICU patients: multicenter development and external validation.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a frequent complication in elderly intensive care unit (ICU) patients, while reliable prediction tools for this population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of DVT in critically ill elderly patients.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, ICU patients aged ≥ 75 years from two tertiary medical centers in China were enrolled. Patients with pre-existing DVT were excluded. A development cohort (Suzhou, n = 1,717) and an external validation cohort (Xi'an, n = 533) were established. Clinical variables collected within 24 h after ICU admission were used to predict incident DVT during ICU stay. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was applied for feature selection, and four machine learning models were developed and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and interpretability were evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
RESULTS: DVT occurred in 15.2% and 21.0% of patients in the development and external validation cohorts, respectively. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance, with AUCs of 0.843 in internal validation and 0.811 in external validation. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risks. Key predictors included D-dimer, C-reactive protein, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, procalcitonin, mechanical ventilation, and mechanical thromboprophylaxis. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of individual predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early DVT prediction in elderly ICU patients. The model may support risk stratification and clinical decision-making in critical care settings.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Clinical and etiological profile of patients with bitemporal optic disc pallor visiting at a tertiary eye hospital.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bitemporal optic disc pallor may result from chiasmal compression as well as bilateral toxic, nutritional, hereditary, or inflammatory optic neuropathies. Data describing its clinical and etiological profile in Nepal are limited. This study was conducted with the aim to describe the clinical and etiological profile of patients with bitemporal optic disc pallor and to evaluate the relationship between clinical, visual-field, neuroimaging, and OCT findings.
METHODS: A hospital-based prospective, cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with clinically documented bitemporal optic disc pallor presenting to Biratnagar Eye Hospital, Nepal. The minimum calculated sample size was 49, and 50 participants were included in the final analysis. Demographic and clinical findings, Humphrey visual-field patterns, neuroimaging findings, optical coherence tomography-derived retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and macular ganglion cell analysis (GCA) measurements, and relevant blood investigations were evaluated. Data were summarized using frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 38.58 ± 15.20 years, and 58.0% were male. Diminution of vision was the predominant presenting complaint (88.0%). Central scotoma was the most common visual-field defect (48.0%), followed by cecocentral scotoma (26.0%) and bitemporal hemianopia (20.0%). Nutritional optic neuropathy was the most frequent etiology (26.0%), followed by toxic optic neuropathy (20.0%); Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and inflammatory optic neuropathy each accounted for 18.0%. Pituitary macroadenoma was present in 16.0% and Rathke cleft cyst in 2.0%. Bitemporal hemianopia was predominantly associated with sellar lesions. The combined pituitary macroadenoma/Rathke cleft cyst group had the lowest mean RNFL thickness (67.4 ± 10.7 μm). Temporal RNFL thinning was more prominent in toxic optic neuropathy and Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, with mean temporal RNFL values of 39.5 and 40.8 μm, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Bitemporal optic disc pallor demonstrated a diverse etiological spectrum. Sellar lesions were predominantly associated with bitemporal hemianopia and greater overall RNFL loss, whereas non-sellar optic neuropathies were more frequently associated with central or cecocentral scotomas and temporal RNFL thinning. Combined clinical examination, visual-field assessment, neuroimaging, and optical coherence tomography may assist in differentiating the underlying causes.

Title: Log-transformed systemic inflammation response index improves prediction of 28-day ICU mortality in critically ill patients with cirrhosis and atrial fibrillation: development in MIMIC-IV and external validation in eICU-CRD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-term mortality is high among critically ill patients with cirrhosis and atrial fibrillation (AF). Existing scores such as SOFA, MELD-Na, and CHA₂DS₂-VASc do not directly reflect systemic inflammation. We investigated whether blood count-derived inflammatory indices could improve prediction of 28-day ICU mortality in this high-risk population.
METHODS: Adult ICU patients with cirrhosis and AF were identified from MIMIC-IV v3.1 (single-center development cohort) and eICU-CRD v2.0 (multicenter external validation cohort). Five inflammatory indices, including SIRI, log-SIRI, SII, log-SII, and NLR, were compared by adding each marker to a base model of age, sex, SOFA, and MELD-Na. The final model was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation used 1000-resample bootstrap, and performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, reclassification, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 454 patients from MIMIC-IV and 121 from eICU-CRD were included. The 28-day ICU mortality rates were 19.6% and 16.5%, respectively. Among the five candidate markers, SII achieved the highest AUC (0.758) and lowest AIC, but its per-unit odds ratio (1.0001) made point-based nomogram construction impractical. log-SIRI was selected for its interpretable per-unit odds ratio (1.48) and near-identical discrimination to SII (ΔAUC - 0.007), together with the biological argument that its three-lineage formulation avoids platelet count, which is unreliable in cirrhosis. Adding log-SIRI to the base model increased the AUC from 0.721 to 0.751 (ΔAUC + 0.030, DeLong P = 0.026) and improved model fit on likelihood ratio testing (χ² = 9.18, P = 0.002), with concordant improvement in continuous NRI (0.241, P = 0.037) and calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P 0.002 to 0.729). The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.734. External validation in eICU-CRD yielded an AUC of 0.818.
CONCLUSION: Log-SIRI was associated with 28-day ICU mortality after adjustment for age, sex, SOFA, and MELD-Na. The improvement in AUC over the base clinical model was modest but statistically significant, corroborated by concordant improvements in likelihood ratio, continuous NRI, and calibration. Prospective external calibration is needed before individual clinical use.

Title: Early serial changes in FIB-4 after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and short-term clinical outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index combines age, aminotransferase levels, and platelet count. Although developed for chronic liver fibrosis, its components may reflect acute hepatic and systemic injury after cardiac arrest. The primary aim of this study was to characterize early changes in FIB-4 from admission to an approximately 72-hour repeat assessment after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Secondarily, we evaluated the association of FIB-4 values with 28-day mortality and whether repeat measurement provided additional prognostic information.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to the intensive care unit after sustained return of spontaneous circulation between May 1, 2023, and May 1, 2026. After a record-level eligibility audit, 188 patients were included; 28-day vital status was available for 182. FIB-4 was calculated from the first laboratory set obtained at intensive care unit admission and from the complete laboratory set closest to 72 h after the admission laboratory sample within a 48-96-hour window. The primary analysis assessed paired change in FIB-4. Secondary analyses examined the association of admission FIB-4 with 28-day mortality and, using a 72-hour landmark approach, the association of repeat FIB-4 with subsequent mortality through day 28 and its incremental contribution beyond the admission value.
RESULTS: A valid repeat FIB-4 measurement was available in 122 patients. In paired analysis, median FIB-4 decreased from 5.21 at admission to 3.16 at approximately 72 h (p < 0.001). Of the 182 patients with known 28-day vital status, 82 died (45.1%). Admission FIB-4 was higher in patients who died than in survivors (6.84 [3.25-10.75] vs. 4.14 [2.32-8.16]; p = 0.019). Each doubling of admission FIB-4 was associated with higher odds of mortality in the unadjusted analysis (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.02-1.55; p = 0.029); however, in the OHCA-specific complete-case model, the adjusted association was not statistically significant (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.91-1.46; p = 0.227), and adding FIB-4 to the clinical model increased the AUC only from 0.647 to 0.648 (difference, 0.001). In the 72-hour landmark cohort, 56 patients had an available pre-landmark repeat measurement and known 28-day vital status; 29 died after the landmark. Repeat FIB-4 showed weak discrimination for subsequent mortality (AUC, 0.585), and the OR per doubling was 1.23 (95% CI, 0.86-1.76; p = 0.255). Adding repeat FIB-4 to the admission value increased the AUC from 0.575 to 0.581 (difference, 0.006; 95% CI, - 0.053 to 0.205; likelihood-ratio p = 0.294).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with available paired measurements, FIB-4 decreased from admission to the approximately 72-hour repeat assessment; however, the magnitude of change showed little discriminatory ability for subsequent mortality in the landmark cohort. Higher admission FIB-4 was associated with mortality in the unadjusted analysis, but this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for major OHCA-specific prognostic factors, and FIB-4 provided essentially no incremental discrimination when added to the clinical model. The incremental prognostic contribution of repeat measurement remained uncertain because of the limited landmark sample and imprecise estimates. FIB-4 should be regarded as a research marker of the acute systemic and hepatic response after cardiac arrest rather than as a stand-alone clinical prediction tool.

Title: Preoperative Naples Prognostic Score and outcomes after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory and nutritional status may refine risk assessment before coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study evaluated the association between preoperative Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) and early and follow-up outcomes after isolated CABG.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included adults who underwent isolated CABG between 2020 and 2023. Patients without a recorded preoperative NPS were excluded. The recorded NPS (0-4) was categorized as low (score 0), intermediate (scores 1-2), or high (scores 3-4). Outcomes were institutionally recorded binary event indicators. Logistic regression evaluated associations with 30-day major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), follow-up MACCE, and follow-up all-cause death.
RESULTS: The analytic cohort included 332 patients: 16 low-NPS, 193 intermediate-NPS, and 123 high-NPS patients. Follow-up all-cause death occurred in 25 patients (7.5%) and was more frequent in the high-, intermediate-, and low-NPS groups, respectively (15.4%, 3.1%, and 0.0%; exact P < 0.001). Any follow-up MACCE occurred in 45 patients (13.6%; 18.7%, 11.4%, and 0.0% across the same groups; exact P = 0.050). Thirty-day MACCE occurred in 11 patients (3.3%); its analyses were exploratory. Per 1-point increase in NPS, the adjusted odds ratio for follow-up all-cause death was 1.69 (95% CI 1.00-2.84; P = 0.048) in the clinical model and 2.06 (95% CI 1.25-3.39; P = 0.005) in the EuroSCORE II complete-case model.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative NPS was associated with greater follow-up all-cause mortality after isolated CABG. Associations with composite MACCE were less consistent after adjustment. NPS may support inflammatory-nutritional risk interpretation alongside established surgical risk assessment, but the findings require confirmation in cohorts with standardized follow-up and time-to-event data.

Title: Acetabular-only robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty is associated with lower surgeon stress index and perceived workload than conventional total hip arthroplasty: a prospective comparative cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted THA (RATHA) has been associated with greater component-positioning accuracy, but surgeon workload during RATHA remains unclear. This study compared objective physiologic stress and perceived workload during conventional THA (CTHA) and RATHA.
METHODS: This exploratory, hypothesis-generating study prospectively evaluated 60 elective primary THAs, comprising 30 CTHAs and 30 RATHAs, as repeated procedural observations from a single high-volume, fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon. All procedures were performed through a standardized posterolateral approach. RATHA used the MAKO system for acetabular preparation and cup implantation only. Intraoperative physiologic data were collected using a Hexoskin smart garment. Whole-case outcomes included heart rate, stress index, root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), respiratory rate, minute ventilation, and energy expenditure rate. Perceived workload was assessed using the Surgery Task Load Index (SURG-TLX). Phase-specific stress index and RMSSD were analyzed across exposure, acetabular preparation, femoral preparation, and wound closure.
RESULTS: Baseline patient characteristics were comparable between groups. Operative time was significantly longer during RATHA than CTHA (141.50 ± 30.76 vs 116.86 ± 21.88 min, p < 0.001). Despite this, RATHA was associated with a lower SURG-TLX composite score (adjusted mean difference, - 0.47; 95% CI - 0.85 to - 0.09; p = 0.039), with lower scores for task complexity and situational stress. Whole-case stress index was lower during RATHA (adjusted mean difference, - 2.52; 95% CI - 4.21 to - 0.83; p = 0.004), whereas the between-group difference in whole-case RMSSD was not statistically significant (geometric mean ratio, 1.35; 95% CI 0.98-1.86; p = 0.067). Heart rate, respiratory rate, minute ventilation, and energy expenditure rate did not differ significantly between groups. Phase-specific analysis showed lower stress index during RATHA in exposure, acetabular preparation, and femoral preparation, but higher stress index during wound closure. RMSSD was higher during RATHA in exposure and acetabular preparation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-surgeon cohort, the acetabular-only RATHA workflow was associated with lower perceived workload and a lower mean whole-case stress index than the CTHA workflow despite longer operative time. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant validation in multisurgeon studies.

Title: Hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices after cardiac arrest: a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoglobin targets are absent from post-cardiac arrest guidelines. New trials suggest that patients with brain and myocardial injury, injuries common post-arrest, may benefit from higher hemoglobin targets. Trends in post-arrest hemoglobin and real-world practices remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult cardiac arrests at three academic hospitals. We screened in-hospital and out-of-hospital arrests with resuscitation efforts ongoing at hospital arrival for inclusion. Patients who survived the initial resuscitation and had a hemoglobin value measured were included. All post-arrest hemoglobin values and red blood cell transfusions were collected through 30 days; descriptive statistics and graphical visualization were used to present hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices. Exploratory analyses evaluated the association between hemoglobin and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Of 2,634 cardiac arrests, 958 met inclusion criteria, with 152 (15.9%) out-of-hospital arrests and 806 (84.1%) in-hospital. The mean initial post-arrest hemoglobin was 9.75 g/dL (SD 2.60), with hemoglobin levels declining progressively over the first 20 days post-arrest. Red cell transfusions were delivered for 369 (38.5%) patients in the 30 days post-arrest, with 1,238 total transfusions. The mean pre-transfusion hemoglobin value was 6.96 g/dL (SD 1.06). Pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels were < 7 g/dL for 762 (61.6%) of transfusions, and ≥ 7 g/dL for 476 (38.4%) of transfusions. Over 30 days, the highest proportion of patients transfused was in the first 48 h. Patients with initial post-arrest hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL had lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.46-0.84, p<0.01). In time-varying analysis, post-arrest hemoglobin through 30 days demonstrated an L-shaped association with mortality, with 95% of the total reduction in mortality hazard captured below 9.20 g/dL.
CONCLUSIONS: Anemia is common after cardiac arrest, worsening in initial survivors. There is substantial variation in pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels, reflecting clinical equipoise. Clinical trials are needed to disentangle anemia as a driver versus a marker of outcomes, and test whether the risk is modifiable.

Title: Explainable machine learning and unsupervised anatomical phenotyping of mitral valve prolapse in patients with severe mitral regurgitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) is increasingly recognized in mitral valve prolapse (MVP), but its anatomical embedding within degenerative MVP remains incompletely defined. We assessed whether explainable supervised learning and unsupervised clustering could identify MAD-associated MVP phenotypes.
METHODS: We analyzed a public surgical cohort of 979 patients with MVP and clinically significant mitral regurgitation. Etiology was classified as Barlow disease (BD) or fibroelastic deficiency (FED). Logistic regression, Random Forest and XGBoost were evaluated for MAD prediction using nested cross-validation with threshold optimization, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit (decision-curve analysis). XGBoost explainability was assessed using SHAP. UMAP-based clustering using anatomical and clinical variables (excluding MAD and etiology from the input) was performed, with prespecified cluster-number and stability sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Unsupervised phenotyping identified three anatomical clusters. The smallest cluster (n = 91, 9.3%) showed the highest MAD prevalence (36.3% vs. 12.0% and 15.8%), marked BD enrichment (95.6%), universal bileaflet prolapse and ≥ 4-scallop involvement, larger MV diameters and less chordal rupture; this phenotype was reproducible across UMAP settings. Supervised models showed only moderate MAD discrimination (XGBoost AUROC 0.695 ± 0.057; PR-AUC 0.314 ± 0.066), with modest calibration (Brier 0.13-0.20; slopes < 1) and limited net benefit, and were therefore interpreted as explanatory rather than diagnostic. SHAP identified BD status as the strongest contributor, followed by number of prolapsing scallops, mitral valve diameters, LV volumes and bileaflet prolapse.
CONCLUSION: Explainable and unsupervised analyses concordantly identified a MAD-enriched, BD-dominant bileaflet/multiscallop MVP phenotype, supporting the concept that MAD is embedded within broader annular-leaflet remodeling rather than being an isolated binary abnormality. These findings require prospective, multimodality, outcome-linked external validation before clinical application.

Title: Type 4 macular neovascularization in a consecutive age-related macular degeneration cohort: detected prevalence and multimodal imaging findings.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine the detected prevalence of type 4 macular neovascularization (MNV) within a retrospectively screened age-related macular degeneration (AMD) cohort and to characterize its clinical, structural, and angiographic features.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 4658 structural OCT examinations from 962 eyes of 500 patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Eyes with structural OCT findings suggestive of type 4 MNV underwent multimodal evaluation via structural OCT and available OCT angiography (OCTA). Cases were categorized as definite, probable, or non-type 4 MNV according to predefined multimodal imaging criteria. Detected prevalence within the screened cohort was calculated at the patient and eye levels with exact 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The detected prevalence of definite type 4 MNV within the entire consecutive AMD cohort was 2.00% (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.96-3.65%) at the patient level and 1.04% (95% CI, 0.50-1.90%) at the eye level. The hyperreflective oblique band (HOB), subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM), and ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss were present in all the definite cases. Central posterior hyaloid fibrosis (CPHF) was observed in half of the definite cases, whereas the remaining eyes exhibited posterior hyaloid central hyperreflectivity (PHCH). By definition, the OCTA criterion of a continuous flow signal extending from the inner choroid to the preretinal space was fulfilled in all definite cases. During follow-up, HOB, CPHF, and PHCH remained stable, whereas exudative activity varied.
CONCLUSIONS: Within this consecutive AMD cohort, type 4 MNV was an uncommon phenotype characterized by recognizable structural and angiographic features. Structural OCT was used to identify eyes suspicious for type 4 MNV, whereas designation as definite type 4 MNV required demonstration on OCTA of the continuous flow signal specified in the predefined criteria. Our findings further characterize the clinical, structural, and angiographic features of type 4 MNV in this retrospective cohort.

Title: Body weight following a multidomain lifestyle intervention in older adults at risk of dementia - A post-hoc analysis of the AgeWell.de-trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle interventions provide a promising approach to address higher body weight as a risk factor for dementia.
OBJECTIVE: The AgeWell.de-trial was primarily designed to preserve cognitive function and reduce dementia risk. In this post-hoc analysis, we investigated body weight following the multidomain intervention among older adults with overweight or obesity, as well as the role of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss.
METHODS: Analyses used data from the cluster-randomized AgeWell.de-trial, testing a multidomain intervention (dietary counselling, enhancement of physical, social and cognitive activity, medication review, intervention for cardiovascular risk factors, depressive symptoms/grief, if applicable) over 24 months in adults aged 60 to 77 years at risk for dementia. Associations between intervention allocation and body weight at follow-up were analyzed using linear regression, controlling for covariates, based on multiply imputed data.
RESULTS: The sample included n = 678 participants with a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², mean age (SD): 68.9 (4.8), 52.1% female. Group allocation was not associated with body weight at 24-month follow-up (b (unstandardized regression coefficient) = -0.30, 95% CI: -0.51; 1.11). Older age (b = -0.14, 95% CI: -0.25; -0.03) and a high level of education (b = -1.28, 95% CI: -2.55; 0.00) were linked to lower body weight at follow-up, while higher baseline body weight predicted higher body weight at follow-up (b = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.91; 0.98). Levels of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss remained high but stable in both groups, regardless of group allocation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this post-hoc analysis, group allocation was not associated with lower body weight at follow-up. Despite high levels of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss and favorable changes in diet and physical activity in the intervention group, these changes did not translate into measurable weight loss.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: AgeWell.de was prospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on December 7th, 2017 (DRKS trial identifier DRKS00013555).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Non-Invasive Assessment Across the Continuum.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) is a key determinant of surgical candidacy, locoregional therapy safety, and systemic treatment outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet its non-invasive assessment remains challenging because the Baveno criteria were derived in HCC-free cirrhosis. This review synthesises current evidence on non-invasive tests (NITs) for CSPH across the HCC care continuum, organised around three clinical scenarios: pre-operative assessment, on-treatment monitoring, and pre-immunotherapy evaluation.
RECENT FINDINGS: Liver stiffness-based Baveno rule-out retains value in early HCC but can miss haemodynamically confirmed CSPH in up to 23% of patients with favourable criteria. Spleen stiffness and imaging surrogates offer higher specificity, and longitudinal NIT monitoring is emerging as a need during locoregional and systemic therapy, which themselves can modify portal pressure. Real-world data report variceal bleeding in about 7% of patients receiving atezolizumab-bevacizumab, supporting variceal screening before anti-angiogenic treatment. AI-based multimodal models show promise in cirrhosis but lack HCC-specific validation. A scenario-based NIT strategy integrating liver stiffness, spleen stiffness, imaging collaterals, and selective HVPG measurement can guide CSPH assessment from surgical candidacy through systemic treatment. HCC-specific thresholds, longitudinal validation, and randomised evaluation of NSBB prophylaxis during immunotherapy are the highest-priority research areas.

Title: Six-month comparative outcomes of endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty versus laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: an MBSAQIP analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: North American data regarding long-term efficacy and durability of endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) are remarkably scarce outside of clinical trial settings hampering our understanding of its optimal role in the obesity care continuum. The aims of this study are to compare safety and efficacy of elective ESG versus laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) at 6 months using accredited MBSAQIP centers.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program (MBSAQIP) database for 2023 and merged with the 6‑month follow‑up data file. The primary objectives of the study were to characterize the long-term six-month changes in weight and metabolic comorbidities of ESG patients in contrast to their LSG counterparts. Logistic regression models were to evaluate for differences in six-month serious complications and emergency department readmissions between ESG and LSG.
RESULTS: A total of 115,476 patients were included, comprising 114,967 LSG and 509 ESG procedures. Patients undergoing ESG were slightly older (44.5 ± 11.2 vs. 42.4 ± 11.9 years, p = 0.0001) and had lower baseline BMI (40.9 ± 8.6 vs. 45.0 ± 7.8 kg/m2, p < 0.0001) and mean body weight (113.2 ± 28 vs. 124.5 ± 26.3 kg). At 6 months, LSG resulted in greater weight reduction, with larger BMI loss (8.2 ± 10.8 vs. 3.9 ± 12.0 kg/m2, p < 0.0001), and total weight loss (22.6 ± 35.6 vs. 11.1 ± 37.7 kg, p < 0.0001). For patients undergoing LSG, there was a near 50% reduction in medication/insulin-dependent diabetes along with improvements in rates of dyslipidemia, hypertension, and sleep apnea. Importantly, no clinically meaningful comorbidity improvements from baseline to 6 months were seen following ESG.
CONCLUSION: When compared to ESG at 6 months, LSG provides an improvement in total body weight loss, has a reduced operative time, and is associated with dramatic metabolic comorbidity improvement including a reduction in resolution of medication and insulin-dependent diabetes. No clinically meaningful comorbidity resolution was seen in patients receiving ESG compared to LSG at 6 months although this cohort was less comorbid at baseline.

Title: Collaborative Multidisciplinary Assessment of Performance: A Development Guide for Pediatric Heart Centers.
Journal: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
Abstract: In July 2023 the Criss Heart Center at Children's Nebraska launched weekly Collaborative Multidisciplinary Assessment of Performance Rounds (CMAP) as part of a structured, prospective Safety Management System framework. CMAP are designed to facilitate transparent, timely, and multidisciplinary evaluation of patient outcomes following pediatric heart surgery. This initiative uses real-time data from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database to create plots of each surgical patient's journey of risk-versus-time, from surgery through discharge, which are presented at weekly one-hour rounds. The ultimate goal of CMAP is to improve team performance and enhance patient outcomes.

Title: Changes in modifiable dementia risk factors and subjective cognitive decline in mid and later life.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Exposure to modifiable dementia risk factors (MDRFs) contributes substantially to dementia risk across the life course. Less is known about persistence and changes in these factors during mid- and later life and how they relate to early neurophysiological changes associated with dementia. This study examined rates and changes in MDRFs over two years and their associations with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among older adults.
DESIGN: Cohort study.
SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants were 2370 adults aged 55-92 years (M = 68.54, SD = 7.15; 56.5% female) who completed the 2018 and 2020 waves of a longitudinal survey of ageing in New Zealand.
MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported hypertension, diabetes, hearing impairment, vision impairment, current smoking, hazardous alcohol use, physical inactivity, depression, and loneliness were classified into four categories across waves: stable absence, reduction, onset, and stable presence. SCD was assessed in 2020. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between MDRF categories and SCD.
RESULTS: Survey-weighted responses indicated 8.6% of older adults experienced SCD. Diabetes, hearing impairment, current vision impairment, stable presence of physical inactivity, depression, and current loneliness were associated with increased odds of SCD.
CONCLUSIONS: Both the onset and reduction of psychosocial and sensory MDRFs in mid- and later life have measurable implications for subjective cognitive outcomes in a general population sample. Prevention and reduction of diabetes, sensory loss, physical inactivity, depression, and social isolation represent meaningful targets for supporting cognitive well-being among older adults.

Title: ChatGPT Versus MediSearch: A Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Platforms for Patient Education in Cardiac Surgery and Cardiac Anesthesia.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the reliability and readability of responses generated by two artificial intelligence (AI) platforms-ChatGPT and MediSearch-to common patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and its anesthetic implications.
DESIGN: Prospective, comparative, cross-sectional evaluation.
SETTING: Single-institution academic study; no direct patient involvement. Questions were sourced from publicly available online data (Google "People Also Ask" feature).
PARTICIPANTS: One hundred unique patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and anesthesia, categorized using the Rothwell classification system (80 fact, 14 policy, 6 value).
INTERVENTIONS: Each question was submitted individually to the free versions of ChatGPT (version 4.0) and MediSearch. Responses were evaluated using three validated metrics: reliability, assessed using the modified DISCERN tool; readability, assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FK) and Coleman-Liau index (CL); and clinical accuracy, assessed by a board-certified cardiothoracic anesthesiologist and a board-certified cardiothoracic surgeon using a 3-point Likert scale.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: MediSearch demonstrated significantly higher reliability (mean DISCERN score, 4.64 v 2.47; p < 0.001). ChatGPT generated significantly more readable responses (mean FK score, 10.33 v 11.34 [p < 0.01]; mean CL score, 15.72 v 17.30 [p < 0.001]) and significantly higher clinical accuracy (mean, 0.82 v 0.71; p < 0.01). Subgroup analysis by Rothwell category confirmed MediSearch's reliability advantage across all question types, while ChatGPT's readability advantage was most pronounced for fact-based questions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a critical trade-off between evidence-based reliability and linguistic accessibility in AI-generated cardiac surgery patient education content. MediSearch offers superior reliability, while ChatGPT provides more readable and accurate responses. Neither platform achieves the sixth-grade readability level recommended for broad public accessibility. These findings underscore the need for AI platforms to balance clinical accuracy with health literacy standards before being endorsed as patient education tools in high-stakes settings.

Title: Global Longitudinal Strain as a Predictor of Challenging Separation from Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although reduced left ventricular ejection fraction is a risk factor for adverse postoperative outcomes, its ability to predict challenging cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) separation remains limited. We aimed to determine whether preoperative left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), measured with a fully automated speckle-tracking echocardiographic software (LV AutoStrain) before induction of general anesthesia, can predict challenging separation from CPB.
DESIGN: Single-center prospective observational study.
SETTING: Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB.
