OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the rule-out yield of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) algorithm for 30-day major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in emergency department (ED) patients aged ≥ 80 years, and explore whether frailty modifies performance.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included patients aged ≥ 80 undergoing 0/1-h hs-cTnI sampling for suspected acute coronary syndrome. Frailty was defined using the Clinical Frailty Scale (≥ 5). The prespecified primary outcome was the 30-day MACE miss rate in the rule-out stratum against a 1% threshold.
RESULTS: Of 1,136 screened encounters, 800 were analyzed (median age 83 years; 56.9% female); 312 (39.0%) were frail. Blinded re-abstraction of 80 records yielded kappa 0.82 (0.71-0.93) for frailty and agreement ≥ 0.71 across variables. The algorithm classified 120 patients (15.0%) as rule-out (prespecified target, 236); two had 30-day MACE (miss rate 1.7%; wide 95% Wilson CI, 0.5%-5.9%), an imprecise estimate whose upper bound exceeds the 1% threshold. A post hoc bounding analysis counting all 11 rule-out patients with incomplete nonfatal ascertainment as events raised the upper bound to 10.8% (6.4%-17.7%). Sensitivity was 99.0% and negative predictive value 98.3%. In prespecified exploratory analysis, no statistically significant independent association was observed between frailty and 30-day MACE (average marginal effect + 1.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.05 to + 7.20; p = 0.744).
CONCLUSIONS: The ESC algorithm ruled out only 15% of octogenarians, potentially reflecting baseline age- and renal-related troponin elevations. Limited rule-out sample size, wide confidence intervals, and incomplete follow-up prevent a definitive safety conclusion.

Title: Safety, Efficacy, and Pharmacokinetics of Agalsidase Alfa in Treatment-Naive Chinese Patients with Fabry Disease: 52-Week Phase 3, Open-Label, Single-Arm Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical data on the efficacy, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of agalsidase alfa in Chinese patients with Fabry disease are limited. We evaluated the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of agalsidase alfa in Chinese patients who are treatment-naive over 52 weeks.
METHODS: This was an open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, multicenter (six centers in China) phase 3 study. Patients with Fabry disease (aged 7-65 years; either sex) received agalsidase alfa 0.2 mg/kg intravenously (every other week for up to 52 weeks). The primary endpoint was the incidence of serious treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs). Secondary endpoints included the incidence of TEAEs, changes from baseline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), left ventricular mass index (LVMI), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and agalsidase alfa pharmacokinetics.
RESULTS: Overall, 20 patients were enrolled (May 2022 to January 2024) and received ≥ 1 dose of agalsidase alfa. The median number of infusions was 27; median exposure duration was 12.0 months. Agalsidase alfa was generally well tolerated. Two patients (10.0%) reported one serious TEAE each (sepsis, ectopic pregnancy). All patients reported ≥ 1 TEAE, most of which were mild or moderate (98.2%); nine patients (45.0%) had ≥ 1 TEAE assessed as related to treatment. Baseline eGFR, LVMI, and LVEF were 118.8 (21.4) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38.0 (11.2) g/m2.7, and 66.8% (4.9), respectively. Renal function and cardiac structure and function remained relatively stable over 52 weeks; mean (SD) changes in eGFR, LVMI, and LVEF from baseline were 4.1 (12.5) mL/min/1.73 m2, 0.56 (8.71) g/m2.7, and 0.8% (3.3%), respectively. Agalsidase alfa exposure (area under the concentration-time curve and maximum serum concentration) was generally similar at week 0 and at week 28.
CONCLUSIONS: Data from this 52-week study support the use of agalsidase alfa as a long-term treatment option for Chinese patients with Fabry disease. Safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic profiles were consistent with studies in other populations. Graphical Abstract available for this article.
GOV ID: NCT04974749.

Title: Association of renal resistive index with coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether renal resistive index (RRI) is independently associated with the presence of coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and to explore its unadjusted associations with continuous coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 120 patients with preserved renal function who underwent renal Doppler ultrasonography before CCTA. The primary outcome was the presence of coronary artery calcification, defined as a CACS > 0. Associations of RRI with continuous CACS and CAD-RADS categories were evaluated in exploratory, unadjusted analyses. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the independent association between RRI and CACS > 0. A clinical model and the same model supplemented with RRI were compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: RRI was higher in patients with CACS > 0 than in those with CACS = 0 (0.697 ± 0.051 vs. 0.646 ± 0.054, p < 0.001) and correlated with CACS (r = 0.474, p < 0.001). RRI also differed across CAD-RADS categories (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, smoking, and dyslipidaemia, each 0.01-unit increase in RRI was independently associated with higher odds of CACS > 0 (adjusted OR 1.137, 95%CI 1.041-1.242; p=0.005). Adding RRI improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p=0.003) but did not significantly improve discrimination (AUC 0.782 vs. 0.819; DeLong p = 0.129).
CONCLUSION: RRI was independently associated with the presence of coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function. Associations with continuous CACS and CAD-RADS categories were exploratory and unadjusted.

Title: Social jetlag in a longitudinal Chinese wearable cohort: weekly variation, solar-time mismatch, and sleep-activity associations.
Journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine how sleep-corrected social jetlag (SJLsc) varied with work-rest schedules and solar time zone and how it was associated with sleep, physical activity, and nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV).
METHODS: Wearable-device and questionnaire data from 63,752 adults contributing 2,037,507 person-weeks were analyzed. SJLsc was the difference in sleep midpoint between workdays and free days, corrected for sleep debt. High SJL was SJLsc > 1 h. Weeks were classified as normal, extended-rest (statutory holidays added), or extended-work (weekend days reassigned as workdays). Provinces were grouped as east, central, or west by solar time offset, the gap between local solar time and China Standard Time. Generalized linear mixed models tested week type and solar offset. Within-person centering was used to separate between- from within-person associations.
RESULTS: Median SJLsc was 0.70 h. High SJL was more common by week than by person (25.02% of person-weeks vs 20.25% of participants). High SJL was less likely during extended-rest (OR = 0.844, 95% CI 0.830-0.859) and extended-work weeks (OR = 0.776, 95% CI 0.758-0.794), while short-sleep odds were higher in both. Locations farther west were associated with later sleep and greater SJLsc. Adverse associations of SJL with sleep and physical activity were stronger between people than within people, whereas HRV showed no robust association.
CONCLUSION: Associations of social jetlag with sleep and physical activity were driven mainly by between-person differences. Lower social jetlag during extended-rest and extended-work weeks coexisted with higher odds of short sleep, suggesting that social jetlag should be interpreted alongside sleep duration and schedule context.
CURRENT STUDY/STUDY RATIONALE: Social jetlag has been linked to adverse sleep and health outcomes, but prior studies have relied largely on cross-sectional or questionnaire-based measures. Large longitudinal wearable data can test how social jetlag varies across real-world schedules and examine associations between social jetlag and sleep, physical activity, and HRV, with stable person-level differences or week-to-week change clearly defined.
STUDY IMPACT: In 63,752 Chinese adults, high social jetlag was more common at the week level than at the person level, and lower social jetlag during altered schedules did not necessarily indicate longer or more continuous sleep. Adverse associations with sleep and physical activity were driven mainly by between-person differences, supporting trait-state decomposition in clinical sleep research.

Title: Alteration of sublingual microcirculation in anemic patients during gastric cancer surgery under goal-directed fluid therapy: a prospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
Abstract: Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) relies primarily on macrocirculatory hemodynamic variables for optimizing fluid therapy. Patients undergoing gastric cancer surgery often present with anemia, which may impair microvascular endothelial function and tissue oxygenation. How preoperative anemia influences intraoperative sublingual microcirculation and macro- and micro-circulatory coherence under GDFT is not known. Patients undergoing open radical gastrectomy were divided into anemic and non‑anemic groups according to their hemoglobin (Hb) levels. All patients received GDFT guided by pulse pressure variation. Sublingual microcirculatory (microvascular flow index [MFI], proportion of perfused vessels [PPV], total and perfused vessel density) and macrocirculatory (cardiac index [CI] and mean arterial pressure [MAP]) variables were measured before (T0) and immediately after induction of general anesthesia (T1), after tumor resection (T2) and at the end of surgery (T3). Mixed linear models were used to compare intergroup differences in sublingual microcirculation over time, and to analyze the correlations between macro- and micro-circulatory variables. Correlations between preoperative Hb and changes in MFI from each intraoperative time point to T0 were additionally assessed. A total of 49 patients were analyzed in present study. MFI showed a significant group‑by‑time interaction between the two groups (P = 0.030). In anemic patients (n = 22), MFI was significantly lower than that in non‑anemic patients (n = 27) at T1 (P = 0.013), and between-group differences were no longer evident at T3 (P = 0.461) under GDFT, although MFI remained below baseline in both groups. PPV was lower in anemic patients at T2 (P = 0.010). Correlation analyses demonstrated that lower preoperative Hb levels were associated with greater reductions in ΔMFI from T1 to T0 (Pearson's r = 0.343, P = 0.016) and T2 to T0 (Spearman's ρ = 0.369, P = 0.009). No significant associations were found between macro- and micro-circulatory variables in either group. Under GDFT, anemic patients exhibited greater perioperative alterations in sublingual microcirculation, particularly after anesthesia induction and tumor resection. Lower preoperative Hb concentrations were associated with greater reductions in MFI. Further, the lack of detectable associations between macrocirculatory and sublingual microcirculatory variables suggests that conventional hemodynamic targets may not fully reflect sublingual microvascular perfusion in this vulnerable population.Trial registration number: NCT07583927.

Title: Clinical implications of intraoperative premature ventricular contractions for 30-day cardiovascular outcomes after liver transplantation.
Journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
Abstract: To examine the association between intraoperative premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden and 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in liver transplantation (LT) recipients, and to determine whether complex ventricular ectopy carries prognostic significance distinct from isolated PVCs. In this retrospective cohort study, continuous intraoperative ECG recordings from 2,290 consecutive LT recipients were analyzed using a validated AI-based detection pipeline. PVCs were classified as isolated or complex (couplet, NSVT, bigeminy, trigeminy), with total complex PVC burden as the primary exposure. Associations with 30-day MACE were estimated by multivariable logistic regression across burden tertiles. Sensitivity analyses used a hard MACE endpoint excluding arrhythmic components and with additional adjustment for isolated PVC burden. MACE occurred in 515 patients (22.5%). PVCs were detected in 98.2% of patients; isolated PVC prevalence did not differ between those with and without MACE (98.4% vs. 98.0%, P = 0.666), whereas complex PVC prevalence was significantly higher in the MACE group (93.2% vs. 85.8%, P < 0.001). Total complex PVC burden showed a graded association with MACE across tertiles (T1 aOR 1.71, 95% CI 1.11-2.65; T2 aOR 2.26, 95% CI 1.47-3.47; T3 aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.83-4.27), whereas isolated PVC burden was not associated with MACE in any tertile. The association persisted in both sensitivity analyses. Complex intraoperative ventricular ectopy, but not isolated PVCs, was independently associated with 30-day MACE in LT recipients. AI-enabled PVC quantification may identify an intraoperative signal associated with postoperative cardiovascular risk, although prospective and external validation is required before clinical application.

Title: A Meta-Analysis on Outcomes of Zanidatamab Plus Chemotherapy in Patients with Advanced HER2-positive Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zanidatamab is a novel HER2-targeted antibody that binds to two non-overlapping extracellular domains of the HER2 receptor. Early-phase trials have shown clinical benefit of first-line Zanidatamab in patients with advanced HER2-positive esophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA). We performed a meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of zanidatamab in this patient population.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, ASCO, and ESMO databases for studies examining zanidatamab as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive advanced GEA. Outcomes of interest included progression-free survival (PFS); objective response rate (ORR); disease control rate (DCR); duration of response (DOR); and incidence of adverse events (AEs). Analyses were presented as median or proportions in percentages with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Random-effect models were used for analysis, which were carried out using R software (v4.5.2).
RESULTS: Three clinical trials involving 685 patients with advanced HER2-positive GEA treated with zanidatamab in combination with chemotherapy and/or tislelizumab were included. Overall, the reconstructed pooled median OS was 26.05 months (95% CI: 23.60-30.04), while the pooled median PFS was 12.61 months (95% CI: 11.05-14.60). The pooled ORR was 70% (95% CI, 67-74), DCR was 96% (95% CI, 78-100), and median DOR was 17.11 months (95% CI, 13.07-22.40). Treatment-related diarrhea leading to dose reduction was observed in 16% (95% CI, 1%-75%) of patients. Treatment discontinuation due to any cause rate was 20% (95% CI, 3%-44%). Serious treatment-emergent AEs occurred in 66% (95% CI, 50%-81%) of patients. Common any-grade AEs included diarrhea (89%; 95% CI, 75%-98%), nausea (60%; 95% CI, 45%-74%), and infusion-related reactions (30%; 95% CI, 19%-43%). Grade ≥ 3 diarrhea, nausea, and treatment-related AEs rates were as follows: 26% (95% CI, 19%-34%), 5% (95% CI, 2%-13%), and 65% (95% CI, 58%-71%), respectively. Other important AEs include immune-mediated AEs (25% incidence rate), left ventricular dysfunction (6% incidence rate), and non-infectious pulmonary toxicity (4% incidence rate).
CONCLUSIONS: Our pooled analyses suggest that zanidatamab exhibits meaningful activity as first-line treatment of advanced HER2-positive GEA. Yet, concerning toxicity rates were also consistently reported across studies. Future randomized studies are needed to further explore its activity and safety profile in this population.

Title: Age-associated radiomic phenotyping in mice using multi-energy photon-counting and preclinical CT: an exploratory study.
Abstract: To investigate whether CT-derived radiomic features capture imaging patterns associated with chronological age groups in mice and to assess the influence of imaging platform and photon-counting CT reconstruction strategy on classification performance. Female C57BL/6NRj mice from three chronological age groups (28, 88, and 99 weeks; n = 11) underwent clinical photon-counting CT (PCCT) and preclinical Albira II CT. Heart, liver, and spleen were segmented and radiomic features were extracted. The individual mouse was defined as the independent biological unit. Model development and evaluation used nested leave-one-mouse-out cross-validation with all preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and, where applicable, reconstruction-energy selection restricted to the respective training folds. Organ-level class probabilities were averaged to generate one mouse-level prediction. Monoenergetic PCCT reconstructions from 40 to 180 keV were evaluated, including a fully nested energy-and-pipeline selection analysis. A grouped mouse-level permutation analysis with 200 permutations was performed for the primary monoenergetic workflow. Albira II correctly classified 5/11 mice (45.5%; 95% CI, 21.3-72.0%), whereas PCCT-SPP correctly classified 10/11 mice (90.9%; 95% CI, 62.3-98.4%). The fully nested monoenergetic PCCT workflow correctly classified 9/11 mice (81.8%; 95% CI, 52.3-94.9%; balanced accuracy, 83.3%; macro-F1, 83.3%). Energy-specific performance varied considerably: 110 keV showed the highest accuracy (81.8%) and was selected in 7/11 outer folds, whereas the highest macro one-vs-rest AUC occurred at 130 keV (0.867). None of the 200 permuted analyses reached the observed fully nested monoenergetic accuracy (plus-one corrected Monte-Carlo p = 0.005). CT-derived radiomic features showed chronological age-group-associated patterns in this exploratory murine cohort, with classification performance varying substantially across imaging platforms and reconstruction strategies. PCCT-SPP showed the numerically highest performance, while monoenergetic PCCT demonstrated pronounced energy dependence without evidence for a universally optimal reconstruction energy. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts and correlation with independent biological-aging reference measures.

Title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome: a single-center case series and systematic review.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of our study was to evaluate the clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, and prognostic features of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome (IM3OS).
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of seven patients with IM3OS treated at Hospital del Mar between 2020 and 2025, together with a systematic review and descriptive patient-level synthesis of the published literature. PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase were searched for reports published between 2015 and 2025, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included case reports, case series, letters, correspondence, and conference abstracts providing sufficient individual patient-level data.
RESULTS: In our series, all seven patients were male, with a median age of 81 years. The most frequent tumor types were non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (42.8%) and urothelial carcinoma (28.5%). Diplopia (71.4%), ptosis (71.4%), and dyspnea (71.4%) were the most common presenting manifestations. Most patients received high-dose corticosteroids (71.4%), intravenous immunoglobulins (85.7%), and additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents (85.7%). The systematic review included 71 studies and 103 patients. Median age was 71 years, and 68.9% were male. Melanoma (35.9%), renal cell carcinoma (16.5%), and NSCLC (16.5%) were the most frequent malignancies. Ptosis (71.8%) and weakness (62.1%) were the most common presenting symptoms. The most frequently reported initial regimen was methylprednisolone 1 g/day (35.9%), and 52.4% of patients received additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents.
CONCLUSION: IM3OS is a rare, early-onset, clinically severe immune-related overlap syndrome with a high mortality rate requiring prompt recognition, structured multisystem assessment, close cardiorespiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary management. Current evidence remains observational and does not allow conclusions regarding therapeutic superiority.

Title: Ambulatory blood pressure characteristics and left ventricular hypertrophy in untreated children with primary hypertension.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: To identify clinical and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)-derived factors associated with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in untreated children and adolescents with primary hypertension. This retrospective study included 306 untreated patients aged 9-17 years with newly diagnosed primary hypertension. LVH was defined as a left ventricular mass index ≥ 45 g/m^2.16. Propensity score-based overlap weighting was used to balance demographic and obesity-related characteristics between patients with and without LVH. Weighted logistic regression was performed to evaluate clinical, laboratory, and ABPM-derived factors associated with LVH. LVH was present in 89 patients (29.1%). Grade 2 office hypertension was the strongest factor associated with LVH (OR 4.22, 95% CI 2.29-7.77; P < 0.001). Selected metabolic and inflammatory markers showed exploratory associations with LVH. Among continuous ABPM parameters, nighttime mean diastolic blood pressure was associated with LVH (OR 1.54 per 10-mmHg increase, 95% CI 1.02-2.31), although this association was lost after adjustment for hypertension grade. In contrast, a systolic non-dipper pattern remained associated with LVH after adjustment for hypertension grade (OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.18-6.80; P = 0.020).
CONCLUSION: LVH was common among untreated children with primary hypertension, with office HTN severity being the predominant associated factor. Abnormal circadian BP patterns may provide complementary information for identifying children with LVH.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Left ventricular hypertrophy is a common form of cardiac target-organ damage in children with primary hypertension. • Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring provides information on nocturnal blood pressure and circadian patterns beyond office blood pressure.
WHAT IS NEW: • In untreated children, grade 2 office hypertension was the factor most strongly associated with left ventricular hypertrophy. • A systolic non-dipping pattern remained associated with left ventricular hypertrophy after adjustment for hypertension severity, suggesting additional value of circadian blood pressure assessment.

Title: Retinal layer thickness as a potential marker for future cardiovascular events - a UK Biobank cohort study using optical coherence tomography.
Abstract:
AIMS: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. For CVD prevention, effective screening is needed to identify high-risk individuals. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides a noninvasive, low-cost "quick look" into the brain and has recently shown thinning of certain retinal layers in patients with previous CVD. We explored if OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses could predict future major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: stroke/myocardial infarction/cardiovascular death).
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data of 51,293 participants from the UK Biobank were analyzed. We used cause-specific hazard models to evaluate the association of retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness with incident MACE, adjusting models for cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and performed subanalyses for association with incident stroke and myocardial infarction.
RESULTS: Median follow-up time was 14.7 years. Both RNFL thickness (aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, p < 0.001) and GCIPL thickness (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.92-1.00, p = 0.04) were statistically associated with incident MACE in cause-specific hazard models adjusted for CVRF. Interestingly, RNFL thickness was more strongly associated with incident myocardial infarction (aHR 0.94, 95% CI 0.88-0.99, p = 0.02) while GCIPL was more strongly associated with incident stroke (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: RNFL and GCIPL thicknesses are associated with future MACE, even after adjusting for CVRF. OCT-measured retinal layer thickness could contribute to the assessment of cardiovascular risk.

Title: [Clinical analysis of 369 deaths within 30 days following surgical treatment of proximal femur fracture].
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 30-day mortality rate after surgical treatment of proximal femur fractures (PF) is reported in the literature to be up to 10%. Clinical studies in German-speaking countries on the suspected causes or underlying diagnoses have not yet been available, which is the reason for this study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The retrospective single-center cohort study is based on a database that records PF. Patients who died within 30 days postoperatively between 2006 and 2025 were included. The primary study endpoint was the causes of death, as documented in the final discharge summary. The secondary study endpoint was a descriptive analysis of deaths occurring within 24 h (day 0) postoperatively, as well as an assessment of variables associated with mortality between postoperative days 1-15 and days 16-30.
RESULTS: The overall cohort comprised 5431 patients with PF. Of these, 369 patients (6.8%) died within 30 days. The mean age was 85.2 years (53-101 years). Compared with the preceding 5‑year periods, the mortality rate decreased significantly in the last period (2021-2025; p = 0.007). The causes of death were respiratory (n = 105) and cardiovascular events (n = 54), multiorgan failure (n = 44), palliative condition (n = 32), renal events (n = 23), acute gastrointestinal diseases (n = 24), cerebral events (n = 15), periprosthetic infection including sepsis (n = 2), and other causes (n = 3). In 67 individuals, the cause of death was unclear. Within 24 h (day 0), 29 patients died, of whom n = 11 died from bone cement embolism or fat embolism syndrome. Five patients died in the operating room. More patients died between days 1 and 15 compared with the second half of the observation period (n = 216 vs. n = 124; p = 0.001), particularly during the first week (n =  145). In the first half, more women (p = 0.016) and patients treated with joint arthroplasty (p = 0.002) also died. All other variables were not statistically significant. With regard to the causes of death, both groups showed a similar distribution (p = 0.056).
CONCLUSION: In our cohort of patients with PF, the first postoperative week was the most vulnerable period for death. The causes of death provide an approximation to this previously largely overlooked topic, but they are consistent with registry or autopsy data. Over the 20-year analysis, mortality most recently declined significantly.
EVIDENCE: III; retrospective cohort study.

Title: [Invasive intracoronary imaging : Role in routine cardiology].
Abstract: Intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, provides detailed insights into plaque morphology and facilitates the precise planning and guidance of percutaneous coronary interventions, especially in patients with complex coronary lesions. Based on the results of multiple randomized clinical trials, current clinical guidelines recommend the use of intracoronary imaging for the treatment of complex coronary lesions. However, the appropriate application of both imaging modalities requires a thorough understanding of their technical principles, as well as their respective strengths and limitations. This article therefore reviews the technical fundamentals of optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, illustrates their clinical application through selected case examples, and summarizes the current evidence supporting their use.

Title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
Journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed.
RESULTS: Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

Title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified.
PRIMARY ENDPOINT: modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients.
RESULTS: Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months.
CONCLUSION: In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative.
KEY POINTS: Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.

Title: Thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications in NPM1-mutated AML: Association with APL-like immunophenotype and impact on early mortality.
Abstract: NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is generally classified as favorable risk; however, early mortality remains a concern. A subset of NPM1-mutated AML exhibits a CD34-low/negative and HLA-DR-low/negative immunophenotype resembling acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), raising the possibility that these patients may also share an increased susceptibility to coagulation abnormalities. While thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications are well recognized in APL, their frequency and prognostic significance in NPM1-mutated AML remain incompletely defined. In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with newly diagnosed NPM1-mutated AML were included. Immunophenotyping was performed using multiparametric flow cytometry, and an APL-like immunophenotype was defined by low or absent CD34 and HLA-DR expression. Clinically significant thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications were recorded within the first 100 days, and early mortality (30-, 60-, and 100-day) was assessed as the primary survival outcome. A total of 70 patients were included, of whom 24 (34.3%) had an APL-like immunophenotype. Compared with the non-APL-like group, the APL-like group had lower fibrinogen levels (309.5 [211-421] vs. 410 [214-518] mg/dL; p = 0.015) and higher D-dimer levels (5.73 [2.4-9.2] vs. 2.50 [0.9-5.0] mg/L; p = 0.012) at diagnosis. Clinically significant thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications occurred in 12 patients (17.1%) and were more frequent in the APL-like group than in the non-APL-like group (33.3% vs. 8.7%; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, the APL-like immunophenotype (OR, 8.79; 95% CI, 1.46-53.05; P=0.018) and a white blood cell count > 35 × 10⁹/L (OR, 10.96 [1.48-80.92] p = 0.019) were independently associated with these complications. Compared with patients without complications, those with thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications had lower 30-day (66.7% vs. 93.0%; P = 0.006), 60-day (57.1% vs. 91.2%; p = 0.002), and 100-day OS (45.7% vs. 87.6%; p < 0.001). Thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications remained independently associated with 100-day mortality in multivariable Cox analysis (HR, 5.79 [1.85-18.06] p = 0.003). In NPM1-mutated AML, the immunophenotypically defined APL-like subset is associated with a procoagulant profile and an increased risk of clinically significant thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications; importantly, these events were independently associated with early mortality.

Title: Antithrombotic strategies and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock requiring short-term mechanical circulatory support.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock following acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) is associated with high mortality. Short-term mechanical circulatory support (ST-MCS) is frequently used after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to stabilize hemodynamics. However, balancing anticoagulation (AC) and antiplatelet therapy in this setting poses substantial bleeding risk.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate real-world antithrombotic strategies and associated ischemic and hemorrhagic complications in AMI-CS patients receiving ST-MCS.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included all consecutive AMI-CS patients who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS between January 2017 and October 2024. AC and antiplatelet regimens were recorded from ST-MCS initiation until shock resolution. Ischemic and hemorrhagic events during this period were analyzed. The primary composite clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of ischemic events and all-cause mortality occurring during the period of cardiogenic shock.
RESULTS: Among 71 patients with AMI-CS who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS (mean age 62 ± 13 years, 69% male), in-hospital mortality was 56%, and MACE occurred in 42%. At ST-MCS initiation, 79% received triple therapy, decreasing to 39% by Day 7. Ischemic events were infrequent (8%) and mainly cerebrovascular. No cases of recurrent myocardial infarction or stent thrombosis were observed. Major bleeding (BARC ≥ 3) occurred in 32% of patients, typically within the first 48 h, and was more frequent in those supported with VA-ECMO.
CONCLUSION: In AMI-CS patients requiring ST-MCS, ischemic events were uncommon, whereas major bleeding was frequent and occurred early. These findings underscore the need for individualized antithrombotic strategies in this high-risk population.

Title: Perinatal management and delivery-room stabilization in congenital complete heart block: an 11-year experience at a tertiary center.
Abstract: Congenital complete heart block (CCHB) is a rare condition associated with significant perinatal hemodynamic instability. Although advances in prenatal diagnosis and pacing have improved survival, evidence guiding delivery-room stabilization remains limited. To describe our institutional experience in the perinatal management of CCHB, focusing on delivery-room stabilization and neonatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study at a tertiary center including newborns with CCHB over an 11-year period (2009-2020). Fetal characteristics, delivery-room interventions, and neonatal outcomes were analyzed. In 2014, a structured delivery-room stabilization protocol was introduced, incorporating ECG monitoring, anticipatory preparation for respiratory support and intravenous isoproterenol, and immediate availability of transcutaneous pacing (TCP) when indicated. Fourteen newborns were diagnosed with CCHB, with prenatal diagnosis in 13/14. Major congenital heart defects (CHD) were present in 3/14 newborns, and nine cases were immune-mediated. Prematurity occurred in 9/14. Respiratory support in the delivery room was required in 10/14 infants. Two infants with severe cardiorespiratory instability required intubation, TCP, and isoproterenol in the delivery room. Following NICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation was required in 5/14 infants and inotropic support in 6/14. Invasive pacing was required in 9/14 infants, including 3/14 within the first 24 h of life. One patient required ECMO support. Survival to neonatal discharge was 13/14.Conclusion: Newborns with CCHB may require advanced stabilization at birth. A structured delivery-room strategy may incorporate anticipatory respiratory and hemodynamic support, including TCP in selected unstable newborns. Multidisciplinary coordination and CCHB-specific delivery-room planning provide a framework for anticipating potential stabilization needs. What is Known • Congenital complete heart block is associated with significant perinatal morbidity and may require early pacing. • Standard neonatal resuscitation algorithms may be insufficient in these patients. What is New • This study describes an 11-year experience with perinatal management and delivery-room stabilization of newborns with CCHB. • A CCHB-specific strategy integrating anticipatory cardiorespiratory support and transcutaneous pacing in selected unstable newborns is proposed as a pragmatic framework for delivery-room stabilization.

Title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

Title: Opportunistic Detection of Hepatic Steatosis Using Postcontrast Liver Attenuation at Coronary CT Angiography.
Abstract: Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of postcontrast liver attenuation measured with coronary CT angiography (CCTA) for opportunistic detection of hepatic steatosis and to assess the impact of tube potential variation on optimal attenuation thresholds and overall performance. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included adult patients who underwent CCTA with concomitant unenhanced coronary Agatston scoring (January to December 2025). Moderate-to-severe hepatic steatosis was defined as unenhanced liver attenuation less than 40 HU. Postcontrast liver attenuation was measured using standardized regions of interest. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with Youden index-based threshold determination. Associations between hepatic steatosis, Agatston score categories, and Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categorizations were evaluated using likelihood ratio χ2 tests. Results Among 300 included patients (mean age ± SD, 55.6 years ± 12.0; 170 males), moderate-to-severe steatosis was present in 109 patients (36.3%). Postcontrast liver attenuation demonstrated high diagnostic performance across all settings (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.88, 0.95, and 0.89 at 100, 120, and 140 kVp, respectively). Optimal thresholds decreased with increasing tube potential (54, 47, and 40 HU at 100, 120, and 140 kVp, respectively). Patients with steatosis had a lower frequency of coronary artery calcium scores of zero (43.7% vs 57.6%) and a higher frequency of coronary artery calcium scores of 101-300 (11.7% vs 4.9%; P = .042), whereas CAD-RADS distribution was similar (P = .12). Conclusion Postcontrast liver attenuation measured with CCTA demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for opportunistic identification of moderate-to-severe hepatic steatosis across different tube potential settings. Hepatic steatosis was associated with coronary calcium burden but not with CAD-RADS categorization. Keywords: CT-Coronary Angiography, Abdomen/GI, Coronary Arteries, Liver Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

Title: Clinical Presentation, Acute Clinical Response, Drug Tolerability, and Short-Term Outcome of Cats Treated for Acute Congestive Heart Failure With Pimobendan (2017-2022): 71 Cases.
Journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical effects, drug tolerability, and short-term outcomes of cats treated with pimobendan (PB) in conjunction with other therapies for acute congestive heart failure (CHF).
DESIGN: Retrospective single-center study (2017  to 2022).
SETTING: Academic teaching and referral hospital.
ANIMALS: Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days.
CONCLUSIONS: The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

Title: Safety and Outcomes of Percutaneous Vegetation Aspiration During Transvenous Lead Extraction: A Multicenter Experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for cardiac implantable electronic device infection has high procedural success, but with a 1-year mortality approaching 25%. Potential mechanisms include septic embolization and persistent infected lead casts or "ghosts." Percutaneous mechanical aspiration of lead-related vegetations during TLE is a potential strategy to reduce vegetation burden, but safety and outcomes data are limited.
OBJECTIVES: To describe a multicenter experience utilizing percutaneous vegetation aspiration during TLE, including vegetation characteristics, procedural techniques, complications, and outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter registry included patients undergoing aspiration of lead-related masses at the time of TLE between 2016 and 2024 across six institutions. Clinical, microbiologic, and procedural data were collected. Vegetation size and outcomes were assessed using transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiography.
RESULTS: Fifty-three patients (62 ± 14 years, 28% female) underwent aspiration of 63 vegetations during extraction of 114 leads (mean dwell time 9.0 ± 8.2 years). Indications included bacteremia in 44 (83%), fungemia in 4 (8%), fever of unknown origin in 1 (2%), and aseptic thrombus debulking in 4 (8%). Mean vegetation size was 2.8 ± 1.8 cm. Aspiration devices included Penumbra Indigo (34%), Inari FlowTriever (30%), and AngioVac (36%). Complete aspiration occurred in 40 patients (75%). TLE achieved complete success in 49 (92%) and clinical success in 52 (98%). Major complications related to aspiration occurred in 2 patients (4%). After a median follow-up of 139 days, 10 patients (19%) died.
CONCLUSIONS: Percutaneous vegetation aspiration during TLE appears feasible and generally safe. However, mortality following extraction for device-related infection remains substantial, and the impact of adjunctive aspiration on outcomes requires further study.

Title: Statin Prescribing and Guideline Concordance Among Adults With HIV Aged 40-75 Years in a Single Urban Outpatient HIV Clinic, 2024.
Journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with HIV (PWH) have elevated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. Following the REPRIEVE trial, 2024 HHS Adult and Adolescent Antiretroviral Guidelines recommend at least moderate-intensity statins for adults with HIV aged 40-75 years with 10-year ASCVD risk 5% to <20%. The 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline expands eligibility, supporting statins for all adults aged 40-75 years with HIV for primary prevention, regardless of LDL-C. We evaluated statin prescribing and HHS guideline concordance for primary prevention in this population.
SETTING: Single urban outpatient HIV clinic in the United States.
METHODS: Retrospective electronic health record review of adults with HIV aged 40-75 years with an outpatient HIV visit on or after February 27, 2024. Statin prescribing was an active prescription at the index visit. ASCVD risk was abstracted from clinical documentation; virologic suppression was HIV RNA <50 copies/mL. Primary-prevention eligibility followed the February 27, 2024 HHS framework: LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL plus ASCVD risk ≥5% or diabetes mellitus.
RESULTS: Of 753 patients reviewed, 414 met inclusion criteria. Statins were prescribed for 212 (51.2%). Statin-prescribed patients were older (median 62 vs. 54 years) with higher median ASCVD risk (13% vs. 7%). ASCVD risk was unavailable for 100 (24.2%). Among 242 patients eligible for primary-prevention statin therapy, 128 (52.9%) had an active statin prescription at the index visit. In multivariable modeling (n=314), higher ASCVD risk, higher CD4 count, and virologic suppression were independently associated with prescribing.
CONCLUSIONS: Only half of statin-eligible adults with HIV were prescribed statins, with the largest gap among those eligible by ASCVD risk 5% to <20% without diabetes. The 2026 ACC/AHA guideline expands eligibility to all adults aged 40-75 years with HIV. These findings highlight opportunities to improve implementation of guideline-directed cardiovascular prevention through improved cardiovascular risk assessment, clinician education, and electronic clinical decision support.

Title: Emerging non-AIDS comorbidities among adults with and without perinatally-acquired HIV.
Journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with perinatally acquired HIV (PHIV) who age into adulthood may be at risk for the early development of specific non-AIDS associated comorbidities (NAC). It is unclear whether the early initiation of ART among PHIV may decrease risk for the development of specific NAC.
METHODS: This retrospective study examined NAC outcomes among a cohort of PHIV and an age range-matched cohort of people with non-perinatally acquired HIV (NPHIV). Multivariate logistic regression models examined the association between clinical/demographic predictors and NAC and the association between early vs. late ART initiation and development of NAC among PHIV. Log rank test was used to compare Kaplan-Meier curves for NAC outcomes.
RESULTS: Compared to NPHIV (N=173), PHIV (N=171) significantly differed by age (30.1 vs 31.8 yrs), tobacco use, lower CD4 nadir, and with less HIV viral suppression. Both groups had high rates of HTN (PHIV 38.5%, NPHIV 29.5%), ≥stage 3 CKD (PHIV 5.9%, NPHIV 1.73%), hypercholesterolemia, and asthma. PHIV demonstrated higher likelihood of hypertension (OR 1.87, 95%CI 1.1-3.2), chronic kidney disease (OR 6.95, 95%CI 1.7-29.7), and a non-significant trend towards higher likelihood of death. PHIV had significantly earlier acquisition of HTN, and CKD. Rates of NAC among patients within the PHIV cohort did not differ based on early vs. late ART initiation.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared to NPHIV of similar age, PHIV adults had higher rates of HTN and CKD and were more likely to acquire these diseases at a younger age than NPHIV. These findings may have long term implications for cardiovascular risk among aging PHIV.

Title: Prothrombotic States in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Real-world Evidence on Clinical Features and Outcomes from Hospital-Based Stroke Registry Program in India.
Journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Prothrombotic states (PSs) are important but underrecognized contributors to acute ischemic stroke (AIS), particularly in resource-limited settings where thrombophilia testing is not routinely available. This study estimated the prevalence and spectrum of PSs in AIS and compared clinical characteristics and outcomes across risk categories.
METHODS: This study used multicenter registry-based observational cohort data from 77 Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of NCD Epidemiology (ICMR-NINE) Hospital-Based Stroke Registries in India (2020-2025). Adults (≥18 years) with clinically and radiologically confirmed AIS were included. Clinical characteristics were compared across hyperhomocysteinemia and inherited (H&I), acquired, and triggering PSs, conventional risk factors, and no-risk-factor categories. Binary logistic regression identified predictors of poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≥3).
RESULTS: Among 69,734 AIS patients, 3,109 (4.5%) had documented PSs. H&I (3.12%) was most common, followed by acquired (0.75%) and triggering conditions (0.72%). Patients with PSs were younger and had fewer conventional risk factors. Large artery atherosclerosis, multiple brain-area involvement, and multi-territory infarcts were more frequent. Acquired states were more frequent among patients with greater stroke severity and were observed more frequently among those who experienced higher in-hospital mortality (11.6%) and 90-day mortality (32.1%). In adjusted analyses, acquired states independently predicted poor outcomes [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.91; 95% confidence interval: 1.53-2.40], whereas H&I (aOR: 0.63) and triggering states (aOR: 0.75) were associated with lower odds of poor outcome than conventional risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: PSs account for a small but clinically important proportion of AIS in India. Acquired PSs are associated with worse prognosis, underscoring the need for targeted evaluation and context-specific guidelines in resource-limited settings.

Title: Lower circulating angiotensinogen levels across ACLD stages are associated with hepatic dysfunction and mortality.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The liver produces angiotensinogen (AGT), the key upstream precursor of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). We measured AGT levels in patients across distinct advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) stages and investigated the impact of AGT levels on clinical outcomes.
METHODS: We included clinically stable ACLD outpatients undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement between May 2018 and October 2023, as well as healthy controls (HCs) recruited in the prospective Vienna Cirrhosis Study (VICIS; NCT03267615). AGT was assessed by converting it to angiotensin I (Ang I) through incubation with excess recombinant human renin. RAS parameters were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Patients were stratified as compensated (cACLD), single decompensated (sdACLD), or further decompensated ACLD (fdACLD).
RESULTS: Overall, 60 individuals (cACLD: n=16; sdACLD: n=22; fdACLD: n=12; HC: n=10) were included. AGT levels decreased significantly compared with HC and with increasing ACLD severity (HC: 943.2 vs. cACLD: 550.4 vs. sdACLD: 476.9 vs. fdACLD: 439.8 nmol/L; p<0.001). In contrast, plasma concentrations of Ang II (cACLD: 23.1 vs. sdACLD: 156.0 vs. fdACLD: 162.4 pmol/L; p=0.002) and Ang 1-7 (cACLD: 3.0 vs. sdACLD: 3.2 vs. fdACLD: 8.5 pmol/L; p=0.022) increased significantly with ACLD severity. AGT did not correlate with Ang II (ρ=-0.23; p=0.101), but with Ang 1-7 (ρ=0.32; p=0.022) and MELD-Na (ρ=-0.29; p=0.042). Exploratory survival analyses, limited by the small sample size, showed that lower AGT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted for age and MELD-Na: asHR: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.09-2.27; p=0.012/adjusted for age and albumin: asHR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.05-2.21; p=0.026).
CONCLUSIONS: AGT levels decreased in ACLD, correlated with hepatic dysfunction, and were linked to all-cause mortality in exploratory survival analyses. Still, classical and alternative RAS parameters increased in parallel to ACLD severity.

Title: Retinal Flattening Associated With Photoreceptor Degeneration Leads to the Formation of Staphyloma-Like Morphology in Retinitis Pigmentosa.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: A staphyloma-like morphology has been reported in eyes with retinitis pigmentosa (RP). We investigated retinal curvature in RP using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography and explored the mechanisms underlying this abnormal morphology.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 74 eyes with RP and 40 control eyes, all with axial lengths of 22 to 26 mm. The curvature of Bruch's membrane was analyzed in the central and peripheral regions of all eyes. In 37 RP eyes with an ellipsoid zone (EZ) length ≥ 1.5 mm, curvature was further evaluated in EZ-preserved and EZ-defected areas and across the EZ boundary.
RESULTS: Central macular curvature was significantly steeper in RP eyes (-23.55 ± 17.56 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1) than in controls (-7.72 ± 6.46 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1), whereas the peripheral retina was significantly flatter in RP (-6.84 ± 10.18 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1, inferior) than in controls (-15.14 ± 4.76 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1). Curvature was steeper in EZ-preserved areas (-30.40 ± 24.34 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1) than in EZ-defected areas (-8.00 ± 6.40 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1). Around the EZ edge, curvature on the central side was significantly steeper than that on the peripheral side.
CONCLUSIONS: In RP, retinal curvature flattens with photoreceptor degeneration, resulting in relatively steep concavity in the central macula or EZ-preserved regions. These findings suggest that photoreceptor loss contributes to secondary alterations in global retinal and ocular configuration.

Title: Circulating SCGB3A2 Is Associated With Impaired Coronary Collateralization in Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion and Type 2 Diabetes: A Proteomic Discovery and Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with impaired coronary collateralization in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO), but circulating biomarkers reflecting defective collateral remodeling remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Olink proteomic profiling was performed in a discovery cohort of 88 CTO patients with T2DM stratified by collateral status. Candidate proteins were prioritized using nominal differential expression and partial least squares-discriminant analyses. Secretoglobin family 3A member 2 (SCGB3A2) was selected for validation by ELISA in an independent cohort of 832 CTO patients (425 with T2DM and 407 without diabetes). Associations with collateralization and incremental predictive value beyond clinical risk factors were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 265 proteins, eight showed nominal differential expression, with SCGB3A2 exhibiting the strongest signal and highest variable importance. In the T2DM cohort, serum SCGB3A2 levels were significantly higher in patients with poor collateralization and inversely correlated with Rentrop grades (both p < 0.001). SCGB3A2 remained independently associated with poor collateralization after multivariable adjustment (OR per 10 ng/mL increase, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.39-1.94; p < 0.001). Addition of SCGB3A2 to a clinical model improved discrimination with an increase in C-statistic from 0.73 to 0.78 and reclassification (NRI 0.62; IDI 0.08). Similar associations were observed in patients without diabetes.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating SCGB3A2 is independently associated with impaired coronary collateralization in CTO patients. It may reflect biological processes underlying collateral failure and improve risk stratification, particularly in patients with T2DM.

Title: Chronic Anticoagulation Increases Complications in Obliterative Prolapse Surgery.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Chronic anticoagulation has been identified as a risk factor for postoperative complications in other specialties, but there is a paucity of data on its effect on older women undergoing obliterative prolapse repair.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess whether chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased serious adverse events (SAEs) after obliterative prolapse surgery.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of women 65 years or older undergoing obliterative prolapse repair at 2 academic institutions from 2016 to 2023. Patients were identified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code and grouped by preoperative chronic anticoagulation status. The composite primary outcome was defined as SAE within 8 weeks of surgery. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, controlling for relevant variables with P <0.10 on univariate analysis.
RESULTS: Among the 777 older women who underwent obliterative surgery, 97 (12.5%) were chronically anticoagulated. The most commonly used anticoagulants were apixaban (n = 37, 38.1%) and clopidogrel (n = 31, 32%), with 21.7% reporting concomitant use of aspirin. Anticoagulated individuals were more likely to be current smokers and to have a history of venous thromboembolism, myocardial infarction, and stroke (P < 0.05). Chronically anticoagulated women had 1.72 times greater adjusted odds of experiencing SAE (95% CI, 1.02-2.91). Chronic anticoagulation was associated with an increased incidence of readmission, cardiac complications, transfusion, hematoma, and organ-space surgical site infection (P < 0.05). Rates of SAEs were highest in individuals taking rivaroxaban (35.7%) and those taking concomitant aspirin (38.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: Chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased odds of SAE in older women undergoing obliterative prolapse surgery. Physicians should consider this additional risk in surgical decision making and counseling on anticoagulant suspension and resumption perioperatively.

Title: Impact of comedication on survival and toxicity in patients treated with systemic therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
Journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
Abstract: IntroductionThis study aims to evaluate the association between concomitant medication, survival and toxicity in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) treated with systemic therapy.MethodsAll uHCC patients treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab or durvalumab plus tremelimumab in our center were included. Endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), HCC-specific survival, grade ≥4 adverse events (AE) and treatment-related discontinuation.ResultsOne hundred and five patients were included, 88 treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and 17 with durvalumab plus tremelimumab. The most common prescribed concomitant medication was cardiovascular drugs (62%). Median PFS and HCC-specific survival were 6.0 (95% CI 4.0-12.0) and 19.0 months (95% CI 14.0-25.0) for atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus 5.0 (95% CI 2.0-19.0) and 17.0 months (95% CI 7.0-21.0) for durvalumab plus tremelimumab, respectively. Five (6%) and 4 (24%) patients presented at least one grade ≥4 AE, respectively (P = 0.04). Grade ≥4 AE and treatment-related discontinuation were more frequent in patients with at least one psycholeptic or psychoanaleptic drug (17% vs 3%, P = 0.03 and 12% vs 2%, P = 0.03).ConclusionsIn this real-world cohort of patients with uHCC, baseline concomitant medication was not significantly associated with PFS or HCC-specific survival. Psycholeptic or psychoanaleptic drug intake was associated with grade ≥4 AE and treatment-related discontinuation, but these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the retrospective design, small sample size and potential confounding.

Title: Impact of diabetic foot ulcers on mortality risk: Lessons from a 35-year Brazilian cohort followed at an association of people living with diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) on mortality risk in a Brazilian cohort of individuals followed at an association of people living with diabetes mellitus.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This retrospective, population-based epidemiological study assessed the impact of DFUs on mortality risk in a cohort of Brazilian individuals with types 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus. Data were obtained from medical records covering the period from 1990 to 2024 and included sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, and therapeutic variables. Survival analyses were conducted using Cox proportional hazards models, with death as the event of interest, and were adjusted for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Among the 382 participants included in the final analysis, DFUs, amputations, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy were associated with increased mortality risk by 89%, 123%, and 37%, respectively. Peripheral artery disease showed a modest, but not statistically significant, increase in mortality risk. Patients with DFUs who were not using oral antidiabetic drugs had a 165% higher mortality risk, and those with prior amputations and poor fasting glucose levels had a 41% increased mortality risk.
CONCLUSION: Overall, DFUs were identified as critical predictors of mortality in people living with diabetes mellitus, mostly among those with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The impact of DFUs on mortality risk is multifaceted and context-dependent, highlighting the leading role of prior amputations. These findings underscore the need for targeted early interventions and the implementation of strategies aimed at reducing mortality in this high-risk population.

Title: Longitudinal Modeling of Cardiometabolic Dysfunction in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Using Item Response Theory.
Abstract: Cardiometabolic dysfunction in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) is reflected by multiple risk factors and cannot be fully characterized by any single biomarker. Item response theory (IRT) provides a framework for integrating observed risk factors into latent measures of underlying cardiometabolic dysfunction. Routinely collected measurements of systolic and diastolic blood pressure (sBP and dBP), high- and low-density lipoproteins (HDL and LDL), triglycerides (TG), HbA1c, and BMI from 33,396 adults newly diagnosed with T2D were analyzed, with biomarkers categorized into four ordered levels. A two-dimensional model described the data better than a unidimensional, identifying a blood pressure-related latent variable ( ψ  1) primarily informed by sBP and dBP, and a metabolic latent variable ( ψ  2) primarily informed by HDL, HbA1c, TG, and BMI, while LDL showed low discrimination on both dimensions. At baseline, age at T2D diagnosis was associated with both latent variables, with opposing effects of 0.02 for ψ  1 and -0.07 for ψ  2. Sex was associated with ψ  2, with women scoring 0.43 units lower than men on the latent variable scale. Longitudinally, ψ  1 and ψ  2 showed post-baseline offsets of -0.10 and -0.22, respectively, followed by separately estimated annual slopes of approximately -0.03 year-1. HbA1c exhibited a distinct trajectory with an initial post-baseline improvement followed by deterioration, requiring an item-specific slope of 0.45 year-1. The ψ  2 contributed modest additional information for all-cause mortality beyond age and sex. This framework integrated routinely collected biomarkers into continuous latent measures of multidimensional cardiometabolic dysfunction while accounting for differences in their contributions to the latent dimensions.

Title: Life's Essential 8 score and arterial stiffness in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Research examining the connection between Life's Essential 8 score (LE8) and arterial stiffness (AS) in patients with diabetes is currently insufficient. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between cardiovascular health and the development of AS in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in a cohort study.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 2,685 patients with T2D were enrolled in this study. All patients were divided into four groups based on quartiles of cumulative exposure of LE8 (cum-LE8) score. The study endpoint was increased AS (iAS), which was defined as a brachial - ankle pulse wave velocity ≥ 1800 cm/s. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to determine the cumulative incidence of iAS, while the log-rank test was utilized to evaluate the differences among groups. Cox proportional hazards regression model was applied to investigate the impact of various cum-LE8 groups on the risk of iAS.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 9.76 years, we identified 1,375 cases of iAS. The incidence rate of iAS in the quartile 1-4 were 71.02 (64.24-78.52), 67.68 (61.13-74.94), 56.05 (50.28-62.47) and 50.47 (45.05-56.53) per 1000 person-years, respectively. The cumulative incidence of iAS was highest in quartile 1 and gradually decreased from quartile 1 to quartile 4 (log-rank P < 0.01). Compared with quartile 1, the hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) of quartile 2-4 were 0.69 (0.59-0.80), 0.41 (0.35-0.49), and 0.15 (0.12-0.18), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Attaining a superior long-term cardiovascular health status is related to a reduced risk of iAS.

Title: Participant experience with the SpaceLabs 90227 ambulatory blood pressure monitor and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro device.
Abstract: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is recommended for confirming hypertension and assessing out-of-office blood pressure (BP). However, patient burden and device tolerability may limit broader implementation. We compared participant experience with a traditional oscillometric ABPM device and a compact cuff-integrated ABPM. The PRO-BP Study was a pilot randomized crossover study of 20 adults in New York City. Participants completed two 24-h ABPM periods over 7 days using the SpaceLabs 90227 and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro devices. After each period, participants rated comfort, pain, sleep interference, embarrassment, noise, skin irritation, and interference with daytime activities. Both devices achieved guideline-based recording-quality thresholds. Compared with SpaceLabs, ABPMpro was associated with greater comfort [median: 7.0 (interquartile range - IQR: 5.0-8.5) vs. 3.5 (IQR: 2.0-6.5); P = 0.026] and less pain [1.5 (0-3.5) vs. 5.0 (0.5-7.0); P = 0.022]. Other experience ratings did not differ significantly. Participant experience should be considered alongside recording quality when evaluating validated ambulatory BP monitoring technologies.

Title: Pulmonary embolism in shoulder arthroplasty: a National Joint Registry Study.
Journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In the UK, there is no specific guidance on prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism (VTE) following shoulder arthroplasty (SA). This study reviews the current incidence of pulmonary embolism (PE) and prophylaxis practices following SA in England.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Joint Registry (NJR) for all SAs from 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2022 and linked with Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). ICD-10 codes identified incidence of PE at 30 and 90 days from arthroplasty. Incidence for PE was calculated by cohort and implant type at 30 and 90 days postoperatively. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated independently with PE.
RESULTS: A total of 47,145 procedures were included in the NJR HES linked database; 26,403 reverse SAs (RSAs), 12,736 total SAs (TSAs) and 8,006 hemiarthroplasties (HAs). The cumulative incidence of PE was 0.25% at 30 days and 0.33% at 90 days. By implant type, the cumulative incidence was 0.32% following RSA, 0.15% following TSA and 0.18% following HA at 30 days, and 0.41%, 0.21% and 0.25%, respectively, at 90 days. Chemical VTE prophylaxis was received following 74.55% of procedures and mechanical prophylaxis following 96.27%. Most common chemical prophylaxis was low molecular weight heparin (91.34%). Congestive cardiac failure, peripheral vascular disease, metastatic disease and trauma indication were associated independently with PE.
CONCLUSIONS: Although uncommon, PE remains an important postoperative complication given its associated morbidity and mortality. Despite most patients receiving some form of prophylaxis no agreed guidance exists in SA and further studies are needed to inform such guidance.

Title: Prenatal Diagnosis and Postnatal Follow-Up of 19 Fetuses With 16p13.11 Microduplication in a Cohort of 12,038 Pregnancies From South Zhejiang.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal interpretation of 16p13.11 microduplication remains difficult in daily practice, mainly because the same duplication may be associated with very different clinical outcomes. In this study, we reviewed fetuses diagnosed with 16p13.11 microduplication at our center and summarized their prenatal findings, pregnancy outcomes, and postnatal development to provide data that may be useful in prenatal counseling.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 12,038 pregnant women who underwent amniocentesis at Wenzhou Central Hospital between 2014 and 2025. Chromosomal microarray analysis was performed in all cases. For fetuses carrying 16p13.11 microduplication, we reviewed the indication for amniocentesis, ultrasound findings, pregnancy outcome, and available postnatal follow-up information.
RESULTS: Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) identified 16p13.11 microduplication in 19 fetuses, with duplication sizes ranging from 0.80 to 1.60 Mb. The main indications for prenatal diagnosis were advanced maternal age (n = 7), adverse pregnancy history (n = 5), ultrasound abnormalities (n = 4), and high-risk serum screening results (n = 3). Three pregnancies were terminated. Sixteen infants were live-born, of whom two were lost to follow-up. Among the remaining 14 children, the follow-up period ranged from 10 months to 10 years. One infant was hospitalized at birth for a ventricular septal defect, and one child showed growth and developmental delay. Five children showed better growth and development than their peers, whereas seven had no apparent abnormalities during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: The follow-up results in our cohort are consistent with the incomplete penetrance and variable outcomes reported for 16p13.11 microduplication. In this cohort, most live-born children showed mild or no clinical manifestations. In prenatal counseling, this CNV should be discussed together with fetal imaging results, inheritance pattern, family history, and available follow-up data rather than interpreted as an isolated finding.

Title: Age-associated clinical patterns in paediatric myocarditis: left ventricular function as the key early risk stratifier.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In myocarditis, early identification of high-risk patients is essential, robust prognostic markers are lacking. We aimed to identify early clinical risk stratifier at index hospitalization for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: We analysed 725 paediatric patients with possible/definite myocarditis enrolled in the prospective multicentre MYKKE registry (2013-2024). MACE included mechanical circulatory support (MCS), heart transplantation, or death during initial admission. Model-based recursive partitioning (MOB) and bootstrap-based logistic regression with multiple imputation were applied for risk stratifier selection out of 20 baseline variables. The model was externally validated in the Swedish SWEDCON- cohort (n = 243). Discrimination was assessed by the area under the curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Among 725 patients (median age 14.3 years [IQR 4.0-16.4]; 33% female), 88 (12.2%) experienced MACE (MCS 10.9%, transplantation 4.3%, death 2.2%). MOB identified left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 39% as the only stable risk stratifier, delineating a "heart failure type" in younger children (1.9 years; LVEF 24%), and a "chest pain type" in adolescents with preserved LVEF (15.6 years; LVEF 59%). LVEF was confirmed as the sole robust risk stratifier (OR per 1% increase: 0.90 ; 95% CI 0.881-0.917; p < 0.01; AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.896-0.903). In SWEDCON (7.4% MACE), discrimination was maintained (AUC 0.894, 95% CI 0.80-0.991).
CONCLUSION: Reduced LVEF at presentation was the only reproducible and externally validated risk stratifier of MACE during index hospitalization. Two age-associated clinical patterns were observed: a high-risk "heart failure type" in younger children and low-risk "chest pain type" in adolescents.

Title: Preoperative transthoracic echocardiogram and delay to geriatric hip fracture surgery.
Journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delays to surgery confer increased morbidity and mortality in elderly patients who have sustained hip fractures. Preoperative investigations including transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) are often requested. The aim of this study was to determine whether there were delays to surgery when these patients underwent preoperative TTE.
METHODS: Electronic databases were searched from inception until April 2025. All relevant studies were identified with data extracted and meta-analysed.
FINDINGS: A total cohort of 2,581 patients was extracted from 5 studies; 865 (34%) patients received a preoperative TTE, and 1,716 (66%) patients did not. Baseline characteristics of age, sex, fracture pattern and treatment were similar. Patients receiving a preoperative TTE were more likely to have coronary artery disease (CAD), congestive cardiac failure (CCF) and arrythmia. The mean time to surgery was 9.4h (p = 0.09) shorter in the group not receiving a TTE.
