The mean length of hospital stay was 0.6 days (p = 0.03) shorter in those who did not receive a preoperative TTE.
CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between time to surgery and preoperative TTE. However, the data available are limited by heterogeneity, confounding and insufficient statistical power. In general, improving access to, and efficiency in TTE could help minimise delays to surgery, particularly in centres with limited resources. Strict adherence to American College of Cardiology guidelines for preoperative TTE indications is recommended.

Title: Enoxaparin dose assessment in paediatric cardiology patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enoxaparin is a commonly utilized anticoagulant, particularly in infants and children. Recent literature has highlighted the need to initiate enoxaparin at higher doses, especially at younger ages, due to differences in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. The aim of this study was to investigate the enoxaparin dose required to achieve therapeutic effect in patients ≤ 2 months, >2 to ≤ 6 months, >6 to ≤ 12 months, and >12 months old.
METHODS: This retrospective chart review includes patients aged 0-18 years admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit over a five-year period. Patients were included who achieved a therapeutic anti-Xa within goal of 0.5-1 units/mL.
RESULTS: Seventy-one patients were included in the analysis; 26 (37%) were ≤ 2 months old, 21 (30%) were >2 to ≤ 6 months old, 10 (14%) were >6 to ≤12 months old, and 14 (20%) were >12 months old. There was a significant difference in the median enoxaparin dose required among these age groups, with medians of 2.13 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.95, 2.53], 1.81 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.52, 2.40], 1.44 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.31, 1.71], and 1.16 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.00, 1.26], respectively (p < 0.001). The difference between initial and therapeutic doses was greater in infants compared to children >12 months of age, despite higher initial doses in patients ≤ 6 months old.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit required an increased median enoxaparin dose and a higher number of dosing changes and experienced longer times to achieve therapeutic anti-Xa levels compared to older children.

Title: Escherichia coli hns and methylglyoxal link gut microbial metabolism to host neuronal gene regulation in Parkinson's disease.
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra (SN). Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in PD pathogenesis, how defined bacterial genes and their metabolites influence host neuronal gene regulation remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial hns-methylglyoxal (MG) pathway linking Escherichia coli (E. coli) metabolism to host neuronal gene regulation. In the stool metagenomic cohort, hns, a bacterial gene encoding the histone-like nucleoid structuring protein and primarily derived from E. coli, was enriched particularly in body-first PD, a subtype associated with gut-originating pathology. In a separate plasma MG cohort, plasma levels of MG, a reactive metabolite whose bacterial production was hns-dependent in our model system, were higher in body-first than in brain-first PD and were nominally inversely associated with cardiac meta-iodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) uptake within the body-first group. Using Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) PD models, we found that feeding with Δhns E. coli protected dopaminergic neurons, whereas exogenous MG abolished this neuroprotection. Transcriptomic and neuronal RNAi analyses identified rig-5 as a host mediator of hns deletion-induced neuroprotection. Cross-species analyses identified LSAMP as a candidate mammalian ortholog of rig-5. MG suppressed LSAMP expression in human neuronal cells, and LSAMP expression was reduced in the post-mortem SN of patients with PD. Conversely, Lsamp expression was increased in the SN of mice colonized with Δhns E. coli. Together, these findings delineate a microbial gene-metabolite-host gene pathway through which E. coli hns and MG modulate rig-5-dependent dopaminergic vulnerability in C. elegans, with corresponding changes of LSAMP expression in mammalian systems.

Title: Long-Term Proton Pump Inhibitors in Lung Transplant Recipients: Near-Universal Use Without Clear Impact on Clinical Outcomes Over a 20-Year Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a known risk factor for chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), the main barrier to long-term survival in lung transplant recipients (LTR). While proton pump inhibitors (PPI) are effective for symptomatic treatment of GERD, data are sparse on the prevalence of long-term PPI use and association with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adult first-time LTR between 1999 to 2018 who were alive and CLAD-free at 1-year post-transplant. PPI exposure was defined as ≥8 continuous weeks in the first year, started within 6 months post-transplant.
RESULTS: 1308 LTR were included, with 1170 (89.4%) exposed to PPI. PPI use increased over time and remained above 90% from 2007 onwards. In multivariable analyses, LTR on PPI had similar time to CLAD and time to death/retransplant compared to those not on PPI. Similarly, no differences in outcomes were observed between LTR on once-daily and twice-daily dosing, or after accounting for the number of reflux episodes on 24 h pH-impedance monitoring. Positive bronchoalveolar lavage cultures and acute rejection over the first-year post-transplant was also comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term use of PPI became near-universal without observable effect on clinical outcomes. While further research is needed, these findings question the routine use of PPI in LTR.

Title: Association of Referring Specialty With Limb Loss in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
Abstract: ObjectiveChronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. While delayed referral is known to worsen outcomes, the impact of referring specialty remains unclear. This study evaluates whether different referral sources to vascular surgery impact mortality and major amputation rates.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted of patients referred to vascular surgery for CLTI at a single institution (2021-2022). The outcomes investigated were mortality, amputation and composite freedom from amputation or mortality (amputation free survival). Univariable analysis was first conducted followed by multivariable Cox regression utilizing variables which had a univariable P value of <0.1 for the outcomes.ResultsAmong 132 patients, 19.7% died and 19.7% underwent major amputation. Mean duration of follow up for included patients was 1471 days (4.03 years). Congestive heart failure (CHF) independently predicted mortality (HR 3.86, P = .0114) on multivariable analysis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD), gangrene, and non-healing wounds were associated with amputation on univariable analysis (P < .05). Referral from emergency medicine had multivariable association with higher amputation rates, while podiatry referral demonstrated a protective effect (HR 0.28, P = .0472). Referral from emergency medicine had multivariable association with reduced amputation free survival relative to all other specialties combined (HR 2.953 (1.66-5.26), P < .001) and relative to other specialties individually (P = .0023).ConclusionsOutcomes in CLTI are associated with variations in both comorbidities and referral patterns. Earlier, multidisciplinary referral pathways may improve limb salvage as patients with CLTI referred from emergency have higher amputation rates and reduced amputation free survival.

Title: Subspecialty headache clinic visit reduced healthcare utilization in patients with migraine: Single institution retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate whether care in a subspecialty headache center, compared with a general neurology clinic, was associated with lower 90-day unplanned healthcare utilization (HCU) in patients with migraine and to identify patient-level factors associated with higher unplanned HCU.
BACKGROUND: Migraine is a common, disabling condition that frequently prompts emergency department (ED) evaluation and treatment. It ranks among the leading global causes of years lived with disability and imposes a substantial financial burden. People with migraine are most often managed in general neurology clinics rather than in specialty centers. Subspecialty headache centers can offer more advanced and guideline-based care, but their impact on post-visit HCU is not well defined.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of adults with a migraine diagnosis cared for at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center from 2018 to 2023. Unplanned HCU was defined as any ED visit, urgent care encounter, or hospital admission within 90 days after the index outpatient general neurology or subspecialty headache center visit (first qualifying migraine-coded encounter in the study period). Associations between clinic type and unplanned HCU were evaluated with adjustment for age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, Area Deprivation Index, and comorbidities, and, in a subset with available data, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System 16-item Profile (PROMIS-16) domains.
RESULTS: Of 38,472 patients included, 16,209 (42.1%) were evaluated in the subspecialty headache center. Total 90-day unplanned HCU was 12.6% in the subspecialty headache center vs. 15.4% in general neurology clinics (p < 0.001). Subspecialty headache center evaluation was associated with 15% lower odds of unplanned HCU (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79-0.90, p < 0.001). The association remained after accounting for patient characteristics (aOR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92) and PROMIS-16 domains (aOR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.59-0.76). Higher unplanned HCU was also associated with younger age at diagnosis, Medicaid and Medicare insurance/coverage, non-White races, comorbidities like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, and worse pain interference and physical function scores.
CONCLUSION: Evaluation in a subspecialty headache center was associated with approximately 15% lower odds of 90-day unplanned HCU. Subspecialized migraine care may represent a high-value care model.

Title: Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Model Using Phonocardiogram and Single-Lead ECG Signals for Detecting Moderate-or-Greater Aortic Stenosis: Multicenter External Validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis (AS), often remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, making early detection challenging. Although cardiac auscultation is a traditional screening tool, its diagnostic accuracy is limited. We aimed to externally validate a deep learning-based model (eAS model) using phonocardiogram (PCG) and single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals to detect moderate-or-greater AS.
METHODS: PCG and ECG recordings were acquired using a PCG device (Cardio-EGG). Transthoracic echocardiography served as the reference standard. The external validation cohort consisted of 951 patients from 3 medical institutions, including 70 with moderate-or-greater AS. The primary outcome was sensitivity for detecting moderate-or-greater AS; secondary outcomes included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios (LR).
RESULTS: The external validation cohort (n = 951, median age 73 years, male 65%) exhibited more advanced valvular disease than the training/development cohort. The eAS model achieved an AUROC of 0.9632 (95% CI: 0.9471-0.9774). Using the pre-determined threshold, sensitivity was 92.9% and specificity 87.9%, yielding a positive LR of 7.65 and negative LR of 0.08. Model-derived probabilities showed strong associations with echocardiographic measures of AS severity (adjusted R2 = 0.5051 for peak transvalvular velocity). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed generally consistent performance, although estimates were imprecise in small subgroups.
CONCLUSION: The eAS model demonstrated high diagnostic performance for detecting moderate-or-greater AS in a multicenter external validation cohort. AI-based PCG/ECG analysis may support the decision to refer patients from auscultation to echocardiography for AS evaluation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.
Abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

Title: Distinct Etiological and Clinical Patterns of Acute Mesenteric Ischemia at High Altitude: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chen, Chen, Yang, Li, Xu, Fan, Xu, Zhijuan Liu, and Dong Wu. Distinct etiological and clinical patterns of acute mesenteric ischemia at high altitude: a retrospective comparative study. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.
BACKGROUND: Acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) is a life-threatening abdominal emergency, yet evidence regarding its etiology and clinical outcomes in high-altitude populations remains limited. This study aimed to compare the etiology, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of AMI between high- and low-altitude populations in China.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study at two tertiary referral centers in China: People's Hospital of the Xizang Autonomous Region (PHOXAR; 3,700 m) and Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH; <100 m). Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) comparisons were restricted to the overlapping period of 2020-2024.
RESULTS: Among 186 patients in the high-altitude cohort and 549 in the low-altitude cohort, MVT was more frequent at high altitude (84.9% vs. 61.2%, p < 0.001). 158 high-altitude and 120 low-altitude patients with MVT were compared. Cirrhosis-related (29.1% vs. 11.7%) and erythrocytosis-related MVT (27.2% vs. 1.7%) were more common in the high-altitude cohort, whereas autoimmune disease-related MVT (0.6% vs. 11.7%) and thrombophilia (0 vs. 16.7%) were more frequent in the low-altitude cohort. High-altitude patients had higher hemoglobin/hematocrit, bilirubin, and fibrinogen levels and a higher mean onset-to-admission time (95.4 vs. 30.2 days). They underwent surgery less frequently (29.7% vs. 80.0%, p < 0.001) and had higher in-hospital mortality (26.6% vs. 11.7%, p = 0.004). Mortality was not significantly different among patients admitted within 2 days (31.6% vs. 8.3%, p = 0.111) but remained higher among those admitted after 2 days (25.9% vs. 12.5%, p = 0.012). Male sex, older age, alcohol consumption, smoking, and higher hematocrit, bilirubin, and fibrinogen were independently associated with the high-altitude MVT phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: AMI in the high-altitude population was characterized by a marked predominance of MVT, with distinct etiological and clinical profiles and poorer outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early recognition, timely referral, and improved access to appropriate treatment for AMI in high-altitude settings.

Title: AI and Deep Learning in Cardiovascular Imaging: From Risk Stratification to Precision Phenotyping.
Abstract: Cardiovascular imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of cardiovascular disease, yet the complexity and volume of imaging data increasingly exceed the capacity of conventional interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning offer new tools to extract quantitative, prognostic, and phenotypic information from routine cardiovascular images. This review summarizes the fundamentals of AI and deep learning, including model architectures, training strategies, and their relevance to cardiovascular imaging, followed by a focused discussion of current applications across chest radiography, chest computed tomography, computed tomography angiography/cardiac computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and nuclear cardiology imaging. Studies were selected with emphasis on original investigations, large cohort analyses, and external validation studies reflecting current applications of AI in cardiovascular risk stratification and precision phenotyping. Across these modalities, AI applications in automated image processing and analysis have become relatively mature. Multiple multicenter and real-world studies have validated their value in improving efficiency and supporting cardiovascular management. Approaches that move beyond conventional human-defined imaging metrics to infer cardiovascular risk and disease phenotype remain at an earlier stage, requiring further standardization, validation, and clinical evaluation. AI is expanding the role of cardiovascular imaging from visual interpretation toward integrated assessment for risk stratification and precision phenotyping, though further work is needed to confirm generalizability and real-world performance before these tools can guide individual patient management.

Title: Concentration-QTc Analysis Supporting Thorough QT Study Waiver for Forvisirvat: Electrocardiogram Assay Sensitivity Demonstrated via Meal Effect.
Abstract: Concentration-QTc analysis from Phase 1 studies is increasingly used to evaluate QTc prolongation risk as an alternative to thorough QT (TQT) studies. According to International Conference on Harmonization E14 documents, such analyses should include exposures at twice the highest clinically relevant exposure instead of a positive control to establish electrocardiogram (ECG) assay sensitivity; however, achieving this may be challenging when the highest dose in Phase 1 studies is restricted for various reasons. This study evaluated the QTc prolongation risk of forvisirvat via concentration-QTc analysis and demonstrated ECG assay sensitivity via the well-described meal effect. A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, single ascending dose study evaluated the effect of forvisirvat on ECG parameters following single oral doses up to 80 mg in 32 healthy adults. Time-matched plasma forvisirvat concentrations and 12-lead ECG data were collected. The prespecified linear mixed-effects model assessed the impact of forvisirvat on baseline- and placebo-adjusted QT interval corrected by the Fridericia method (ΔΔQTcF). ECG assay sensitivity was established by prospectively evaluating the postprandial QTcF shortening. The two-sided 90% confidence interval (CI) for the model-predicted ΔΔQTcF was below 10 ms up to the maximum observed plasma concentration of 703 ng/mL. Meal-induced QTcF shortening was -6.38 ms (95% CI, -8.51 to -4.26) at 4 h after the standardized lunch, with the two-sided 95% CI below 0. Forvisirvat showed no QTcF prolongation, and ECG assay sensitivity was confirmed via meal-induced QTcF shortening. These results supported regulatory acceptance of a TQT study waiver by the Japanese Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency.

Title: Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years.
RESULTS: Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.

Title: Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Health literacy is a critical component of high-quality stroke care. Across the continuum from prevention through recovery, health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke-related morbidity. Despite its importance, it is often overlooked, leaving patients and caregivers overwhelmed by communication demands that exceed their capacity. These mismatches are especially pronounced among individuals with stroke-related cognitive or language impairments, limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, or limited digital literacy. This scientific statement synthesizes current evidence on the role of health literacy and communication within stroke systems of care and identifies nurse-led opportunities to advance equity and patient-centered outcomes while recognizing this as a shared interprofessional responsibility. Nurse-led interventions, including teach-back-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, have demonstrated improvements in stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness. However, the literature is marked by methodological heterogeneity. Many studies are underpowered and infrequently use validated health literacy or communication measures. Future directions include standardized assessment of health literacy; literacy-sensitive, nurse-led, and interprofessional care models; workforce training in plain-language and culturally responsive communication; and organizational health literacy principles. Emerging technologies, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, offer promise for improving communication and personalization but require rigorous evaluation to minimize bias and ensure equity and usability.

Title: Retinal vasculature changes after 0.125% atropine treatment in children with myopia measured using optical coherence tomography angiography: A pilot study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The study assessed the microvascular changes in the retina after the use of 0.125% atropine in children with myopia and the association between retinal microvascular changes and the effects of myopia treatment.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This is a prospective cohort study. Children with myopia aged 5-18 years old were included in the study. Retina microvascular parameters were measured with spectral domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography devices during the follow-up. The main outcome measurements include vessel density of the superficial vascular plexus (SVP), deep vascular plexus, and axial length (AL).
RESULTS: A total of 64 eyes of 36 patients were included. A significant decrease in parafoveal vessel density of the SVP was observed in the first 3 months (P = 0.032). The change in parafoveal vessel density of the SVP in the first 3 months correlated negatively with the change in the AL after 1 year (r = -0.430, P = 0.028).
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that 0.125% atropine might induce changes in the retina vasculature in children with myopia and that these changes might correlate with myopia progression. Nevertheless, as a pilot study, this result may need to be confirmed in larger studies.

Title: Comparing optical coherence tomography angiography biomarker for primary open-angle glaucoma and normal tension glaucoma progression in different stage.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare peripapillary and parafoveal microvasculature between primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) at different disease stages using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study classified eyes into early, moderate, or severe visual field defect based on Hodapp-Parrish-Anderson criteria. OCTA was used to assess radial peripapillary capillaries (RPCs), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), parafoveal vessel density, and ganglion cell complex thickness. Global and sectoral parameters were compared between POAG and NTG, with subgroup analysis by disease severity.
RESULTS: In early-stage glaucoma, global RNFL thickness was significantly lower in NTG eyes (87.5 ± 11.3 µm) compared to POAG eyes (92.4 ± 10.5 µm, P = 0.034), especially in the superior-nasal sector (111.7 ± 28.4 µm vs. 122.7 ± 26.8 µm, P = 0.030). In severe-stage glaucoma, POAG eyes showed lower nasal-superior RPCs (32.1% ± 9.8% vs. 39.2% ± 8.8%, P = 0.044), nasal-inferior RPCs (32.9% ± 10.6% vs. 40.0 ± 6.9%, P = 0.012), and temporal-superior RNFL thickness (53.0 ± 15.0 µm vs. 69.9 ± 21.7 µm, P = 0.019).
CONCLUSION: The microvasculature in the sectoral peripapillary and parafoveal regions shows significant differences between POAG and NTG across various stages. This suggests that the mechanisms underlying these glaucoma subtypes may differ at different stage.

Title: Prenatal Remote Blood Pressure Monitoring and Detection of Chronic Hypertension.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether universal enrollment in a prenatal remote blood pressure (BP) monitoring program initiated at the first prenatal visit is associated with higher rates of new chronic hypertension diagnosis before 20 weeks of gestation compared with usual care.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study comparing patients enrolled and those not enrolled in the remote BP monitoring intervention between September 2021 and May 2023. Two:one optimal pair propensity score matching balanced nine demographic and clinical covariates between groups. A logistic regression model with remote BP monitoring enrollment as the sole independent variable estimated the odds of chronic hypertension diagnosis within 20 weeks; cluster-robust SEs accounted for within-pair dependence. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs and average predicted probabilities were reported.
RESULTS: Of 3,294 patients initially included (508 remote BP monitoring, 2,786 usual care), 1,521 remained after 2:1 matching (507 remote BP monitoring, 1,014 usual care). Remote BP monitoring patients had 68.0% higher odds of chronic hypertension diagnosis (OR 1.68, 95% CI, 1.10-2.57, P=.017). Predicted probability of chronic hypertension diagnosis was 8.5% (95% CI, 6.1-10.9%) in the remote BP monitoring group versus 5.2% (95% CI, 3.8-6.6%) in usual care.
CONCLUSION: Universal prenatal remote BP monitoring is associated with significantly higher odds of chronic hypertension diagnosis before 20 weeks compared with propensity score-matched controls, enabling timely chronic hypertension-specific management.

Title: Pregnancy After Laparoscopic Radiofrequency Ablation: A Case Report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) has garnered popularity as a promising uterus-sparing option for the management of leiomyomas. However, data on fertility and reproductive outcomes, particularly rare complications such as uterine rupture, remain limited.
CASE: Twenty-nine-year-old G0 patient with infertility underwent uncomplicated laparoscopic RFA of a 1.18×1.33-cm anterior fundal intramural leiomyoma. She conceived spontaneously 2 years later and presented at 17 weeks of gestation with an anterior fundal uterine rupture, which was repaired successfully. Patient underwent scheduled cesarean delivery at 35 weeks and delivered a live-born 2,390-g boy with Apgar scores of 9 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging at 6 months postpartum (26 months after ablation) revealed no myometrial lesions.
CONCLUSION: Current data on reproductive outcomes after laparoscopic RFA are reassuring with regard to uterine rupture, but more prospective studies are needed. Although rare, uterine rupture should be considered a potential serious risk after laparoscopic RFA and discussed during patient counseling.

Title: Safety, Efficacy, and Effectiveness of Pulsed Field Ablation with Farapulse™ to Treat Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Single-center Study.
Journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management
Abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) using the Farapulse™ system (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) is a novel, non-thermal ablation technology developed to treat atrial fibrillation (AF) with improved safety and procedural efficiency. We present prospective single-center data on the safety, efficacy, and effectiveness of PFA in a real-world patient population. We enrolled 100 consecutive patients with symptomatic AF undergoing catheter ablation with the Farapulse™ system. Procedural characteristics, clinical outcomes, and acute safety events were evaluated. Freedom from AF recurrence was assessed at 6 months. The cohort had a mean age of 69.2 ± 10.9 years, and 47% were women. Pulmonary vein isolation was achieved in 96% of patients, with additional posterior wall ablation performed in 66%. The median procedure and fluoroscopy times were 42 and 12 min, respectively. No major adverse events occurred. At 6 months, 82% of patients were free from atrial arrhythmia recurrence off anti-arrhythmic drugs. PFA with the Farapulse™ system demonstrated high acute efficacy, excellent safety, and promising short-term effectiveness in a real-world population with AF. These findings support the broader adoption of PFA in routine clinical practice.

Title: A Discrete Hemodynamic Control System: Proof-of-Concept In-Vivo Study in Canine Heart Failure Using a Pulmonary Artery Catheter.
Journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
Abstract: Objective: Managing heart failure requires simultaneous regulation of mean arterial pressure, cardiac output, and left atrial pressure, which is challenging due to complex cardiovascular interactions and limited monitoring. This study presents a proof-of-concept in-vivo evaluation of a discrete two-degree-of-freedom hemodynamic control system designed to regulate these three hemodynamic variables through titration of cardiovascular interventions under pulmonary artery catheter monitoring. Results: Across five consecutive trials in three canine models of heart failure induced by tachycardia pacing, the cohort-averaged mean arterial pressure, cardiac output, and left atrial pressure were each within ±10% of their respective targets when evaluated using the final three intervention measurements, with absolute percentage errors decreasing from 16.8% to 9.0%, 23.4% to 3.8%, and 87.5% to 5.5%, respectively. In a more severely complicated heart failure model with coronary embolization, outcomes revealed control limitation primarily due to pharmacological resistance, highlighting the importance of choosing the appropriate target value. Conclusions: This proof-of-concept in-vivo study demonstrates the feasibility of implementing discrete two-degree-of-freedom hemodynamic control under pulmonary artery catheter-based monitoring and phlebotomy-mediated volume removal in anesthetized canine models of tachycardia-pacing-induced heart failure. Further studies are required to evaluate the effects of inter-subject variability and clinical generalizability.

Title: Development and Internal Validation of an Inflammatory-Coagulation Biomarker-Enhanced Nomogram for 90-Day Outcome After Deep Hypertension-Related Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early prognostic assessment after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) relies mainly on neurological severity and neuroimaging features. Whether routinely available inflammatory-coagulation biomarkers provide meaningful incremental information beyond these established predictors remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an admission-based nomogram incorporating inflammatory-coagulation biomarkers for predicting 90-day poor functional outcome in patients with deep hypertension-related ICH.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with deep hypertension-related ICH admitted between January 2020 and December 2025. Poor functional outcome was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 4-6. Candidate predictors available within 24 hours of admission were evaluated using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, Brier score, bootstrap internal validation, reclassification metrics, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Among 462 patients, 162 (35.1%) had poor functional outcome. The final model retained age, Glasgow Coma Scale score, hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage, admission blood glucose, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and ln(D-dimer). Adding NLR and ln(D-dimer) increased the AUC from 0.765 to 0.828 (P = 0.008), representing a statistically significant but modest absolute improvement of 0.063, and reduced the Brier score from 0.178 to 0.142. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.816. Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit than the conventional model across threshold probabilities of 15%-65%. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent biomarker associations and model performance.
CONCLUSION: Adding NLR and D-dimer to established clinical-imaging predictors provided a modest improvement in 90-day outcome prediction in deep hypertension-related ICH. These biomarkers may offer complementary prognostic information, but the clinical importance of this incremental gain remains to be established. External validation is required before broader clinical application.

Title: Risk stratification of Stage B heart failure with BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL: development of the PHASE Index from the CHART-2 Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels of 35-100 pg/mL, common in preclinical heart failure (HF), are associated with heterogeneous prognosis and are influenced by age and renal function. We aimed to characterize risk heterogeneity in preclinical HF patients with BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL and to develop a practical risk stratification model.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Data from the Chronic Heart Failure Registry and Analysis in the Tohoku District-2 (CHART-2) Study, a prospective multicentre cohort with long-term follow-up, were analysed. Among patients with Stage B HF (n = 4074; age 67.6 ± 12.0 years), the predictability of BNP for 10-year HF-related events was evaluated across strata of age and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). In patients with BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL, a composite risk score-the Pre-Heart Failure Assessment and Screening Evaluation (PHASE) Index-was developed using classification and regression tree analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards modelling. BNP discrimination varied significantly by age and eGFR (P < 0.05), indicating that a single BNP threshold is insufficient for risk stratification in preclinical HF. The PHASE Index, incorporating age, BNP, eGFR, left ventricular ejection fraction, body mass index, and hypertension, stratified patients with BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL into four categories and demonstrated superior discrimination compared with BNP alone (c-index 0.723 vs. 0.587, P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Patients with preclinical HF and BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL exhibit substantial risk heterogeneity. The PHASE Index improves identification of high-risk individuals and provides a pragmatic tool for risk stratification beyond the conventional BNP threshold.

Title: Risk of atrial fibrillation according to electrocardiographic risk factors: a nationwide cohort study of 1.5 million patients.
Abstract:
AIMS: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with an increased risk of stroke, yet no evidence exists on the collective effect of electrocardiogram (ECG) risk factors in early detection of AF. We aimed to evaluate the risk of new-onset AF and stroke according to specific ECG risk factors to identify patients at high risk of developing AF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We included patients who had an ECG performed and grouped them according to how many of the following ECG risk factors they presented with: Elevated heart rate at rest, prolonged PR-interval, biphasic P-waves, abnormal P-terminal force in V1, and prolonged P-wave duration. Among 1 434 491 included patients, 632 628 had none of the five ECG risk factors and 802 163 had at least one ECG risk factor on their ECG. The 5-year cumulative incidence of AF and stroke was lowest among patients with no ECG changes and exceeded 8% and 7%, respectively among patients with all five ECG risk factors [AF: 8.3%, 95% confidence interval (CI): 5.7-11.0%, stroke: 7.3%, 95% CI: 4.7-9.9%]. Patients with all five ECG risk factors had a two-fold increased risk of AF [hazard ratio (HR): 2.57, 95% CI: 1.85-3.57] and of stroke (HR: 2.11, 95% CI: 1.47-3.01) compared to patients with none.
CONCLUSION: The selected ECG risk factors were commonly observed. The 5-year incidence of AF and stroke was low among patients with no ECG risk factors, yet increased in a dose-response-like manner according to the number of ECG risk factors. Scoring patients according to simple ECG risk factors effectively identified patients at high risk of AF and stroke.

Title: Federated learning for privacy-preserving opportunistic screening of lumbar-spine DXA-defined osteoporotic-level bone mineral density using chest radiographs: A multi-center independent validation study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of an artificial intelligence (AI) system trained via federated learning for opportunistic screening of lumbar-spine DXA-defined osteoporotic-level bone mineral density (T-score ≤ -2.5) using routine chest X-rays (CXRs) in a multi-center independent validation setting.
METHODS: A deep learning model was developed via privacy-preserving federated learning on 5943 paired CXR and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) examinations and validated on an independent dual-center cohort of 3007 adults undergoing same-day CXR and DXA. Ground truth was a lumbar spine DXA T-score ≤ -2.5. The primary metric was AUROC, alongside sensitivity and specificity. Image-only and clinical-only ablation models were evaluated on the same cohort to disentangle imaging from demographic contributions.
RESULTS: Among 3007 validation cases, 200 (6.7%) had a T-score ≤ -2.5. The AI achieved an AUROC of 0.942 (95% CI, 0.923-0.962), with sensitivity of 91.0% and specificity of 82.7%, and performance was preserved across study sites, sexes, and the clinically relevant older stratum (≥60 years). In ablation analysis, the image-only model achieved AUROC 0.931 (95% CI 0.912-0.950) and the clinical-only baseline 0.780 (0.732-0.827); non-overlapping 95% CIs (image-only higher) support an independent imaging contribution beyond demographics.
CONCLUSIONS: This federated learning-based AI demonstrates high discrimination for identifying lumbar-spine DXA-defined osteoporotic-level bone mineral density (T-score ≤ -2.5) from standard CXRs and shows temporal transportability across two institutions without centralizing raw imaging data. Positioned as a triage adjunct to confirmatory DXA, it offers a scalable, privacy-preserving opportunistic screening solution.

Title: Recent advances in conversion therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombosis.
Abstract: Portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) is one of the most clinically consequential manifestations of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It reflects aggressive tumor biology, compromises portal venous inflow, and reduces the therapeutic window for locoregional intervention. Historically, macroscopic portal vein invasion generally placed patients within advanced-stage treatment pathways, in which systemic therapy constituted the standard treatment backbone and curative-intent approaches were applicable only to selected patients. This paradigm has now shifted. In recent years, the management of unresectable HCC has been reshaped by immune-based systemic therapy, more active tyrosine kinase inhibitor-based combinations, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), selective transarterial therapies, thrombus-directed radiotherapy, and increasingly standardized multidisciplinary conversion strategies. Consequently, a subset of patients with liver-dominant HCC and PVTT can now be downstaged to radical resection or other definitive local treatment, particularly when liver function is preserved and therapy is initiated before irreversible hepatic decompensation develops. This review summarizes recent advances in the diagnosis and classification of PVTT, the biological and technical rationale for conversion therapy, and the evolving evidence for systemic therapy, HAIC, transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), radiotherapy, triple-modality treatment, salvage surgery, and postoperative management. It also highlights key limitations, including the predominance of retrospective East Asian cohorts, heterogeneity in PVTT classification and treatment protocols, uncertainty regarding the optimal timing of surgery, and the absence of validated biomarkers for selecting patients most likely to benefit from aggressive multimodality treatment. Overall, the available evidence supports integrating response-guided multidisciplinary strategies into established evidence-based treatment frameworks for carefully selected patients. Even so, conversion therapy for HCC with PVTT remains an evidence-evolving strategy that should be applied with careful patient selection, disciplined treatment sequencing, and substantial institutional expertise rather than adopted as a universal standard of care.

Title: Patient and healthcare system factors associated with participation in municipal smoking cessation programs after hospitalization for atherosclerotic vascular disease in Norway: A prespecified analysis of two randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Persistent smoking after hospitalization for an atherosclerotic vascular event remains common, and only a small proportion attend cardiac rehabilitation or community-based lifestyle support, including smoking cessation programs. This study aimed to identify patient and healthcare system factors associated with participation in a municipal smoking cessation program among patients with atherosclerotic vascular disease included in a smoking cessation trial.
METHODS: A prespecified secondary analysis was conducted of two randomized cessation trials with patients recruited between 2021 and 2023 at three hospitals in Norway. Hospitalized patients with established atherosclerotic vascular disease who smoked at least one cigarette daily were randomized to motivational counseling with proactive referral to the municipal cessation program (intervention) or brief advice and contact information (control). Data were collected from medical records and self-report questionnaires. Associations between patient and healthcare system factors and program participation were explored using logistic regression analyses, adjusting for age, site and group allocation.
RESULTS: In all, 268 of 280 patients were eligible at 6 months (median age 65 years, 39% women). Participation in the cessation program was 42% (56/134) in the intervention and 9% (12/134) in the control group. Among participants, 57% (39/68) quit smoking, compared with 30% (59/200) among non-participants. In the total sample, older age (adjusted odds ratio, AOR=0.65 per 10 year increase; 95% CI: 0.47-0.90), living alone versus with others (AOR=0.30; 95% CI: 0.14-0.65), and lower versus higher education (AOR=0.40; 95% CI: 0.18-0.89) were negatively associated with participation. Analysis restricted to the intervention group yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Participation in a municipal smoking cessation program among hospitalized patients with atherosclerotic vascular disease remained suboptimal, despite proactive motivational counseling and proactive referral. Older patients, those living alone, and patients with lower level of education were less likely to participate, highlighting the need for targeted referral strategies and tailored support for these groups.

Title: Long-term limb salvage and functional recovery in advanced Charcot neuroarthropathy complicated by a non-healing diabetic foot ulcer: a CARE-compliant case report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced Charcot neuroarthropathy complicated by diabetic foot ulceration is a limb-threatening condition associated with progressive foot deformity, recurrent ulceration, infection, impaired wound healing, and a high risk of major amputation. Evidence describing long-term limb preservation following multimodal conservative management remains limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and diabetic peripheral neuropathy presented with advanced Charcot neuroarthropathy of the left foot, complicated by a chronic, non-healing dorsal diabetic foot ulcer (3 × 4 cm; Wagner Grade 3; University of Texas Grade 3-D) and a lateral draining sinus. During the earlier course of the disease, magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated extensive Charcot-related bony destruction with findings suggestive of secondary osteomyelitis. The diagnosis was made by the treating podiatric surgeon based on clinical and imaging findings. Microbiological and histopathological confirmation was not available. Despite prior hospitalization, incision and drainage, and approximately 15 days of intravenous antibiotic therapy, satisfactory wound healing was not achieved.
INTERVENTION: The patient underwent multimodal conservative management comprising continuation of conventional antidiabetic therapy, complete bed rest during the active wound-management period, structured local wound care using Aragvadhadi Kashayam, internal Ayurvedic medications (Pachanamritham Kashayam and Chandraprabha Vati), dietary regulation, and regular clinical follow-up. Custom-made protective footwear had previously been prescribed for the Charcot-related deformity and was used for approximately six months before discontinuation because of discomfort.
OUTCOMES: Progressive reduction in wound exudate and slough was followed by healthy granulation tissue formation, complete epithelialization of the dorsal ulcer, and healing of the lateral draining sinus. Limb preservation was achieved without major amputation over approximately four years of follow-up. The patient subsequently regained independent ambulation, resumed routine occupational and daily activities, and maintained functional mobility. The clinical course was documented through serial clinical photographs and follow-up assessments.
CONCLUSION: This case describes a favorable long-term outcome, including limb preservation and functional recovery, following multimodal conservative management in a patient with advanced Charcot neuroarthropathy complicated by chronic ulceration. Given the single-case design and the simultaneous use of multiple therapeutic interventions, the independent contribution of individual treatment components cannot be determined. Further prospective studies are warranted.

Title: Stent biomechanics in hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis: from site-specific loading to a staged device-validation framework.
Abstract: Hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis is usually managed as one local variant of central venous stenosis, yet its mechanical environment is distinctive. The vein follows a long, multi-axially curved retrosternal course through a narrow window between the manubrium and the aortic arch, bounded by two separate junctions, the lateral venous angle and the medial brachiocephalic-caval confluence. An implanted stent is therefore exposed to focal unidirectional compression, cyclic bending and torsion, short landing zones, and branch-coverage risk, conditions not reproduced by circumferential radial testing. The sternum-aortic corridor reported in affected patients, about 4.6 mm, is narrower than the nominal diameter of stents deployed there, placing the implied compression at or beyond the lowest level characterized in published bench comparisons; pulsatile durability testing covers only cardiac-frequency diametric cycling, and pooled cohorts seldom report the segment separately. This Review synthesizes published anatomical, clinical, engineering, and computational evidence and reframes the problem as a site-specific biomechanical and device-validation question with three validation priority stages (P1-P3). P1 (required) evaluates base-platform mechanics, structure, fatigue, and deployment: focal crush resistance and recovery, radial resistive versus chronic outward force, bending and torsion durability, foreshortening, deployment accuracy, branch preservation and, for covered constructs, covering fatigue. P2 (required) evaluates anatomy-specific hemodynamics of the same platform by patient-specific computational modeling and experimental flow testing, reporting shear, residence, gradient, edge-recirculation, branch-flow, and pressure-loss metrics against matched comparators. P3 (optional) covers an added drug, coating, or surface; baseline thrombogenicity, hemocompatibility, tissue compatibility, and structural integrity remain required base-platform attributes. We state two falsifiable hypotheses with the bench, computational, imaging, and clinical evidence that would support or refute them: H1 (mechanical), that resistance to focal unidirectional crush may govern stent deformation, durability, and in-stent restenosis localization more strongly than circumferential radial resistive force alone; and H2 (hemodynamic), that stent architecture and edge configuration may generate spatially reproducible disturbed-flow regions adding incremental prediction of later in-stent restenosis distribution beyond anatomical and procedural covariates. Direct prospective evidence remains sparse: the framework is a problem definition and validation roadmap, not a clinical algorithm, device ranking, or evidence of superior performance.

Title: The association of cardiovascular disease (CVD) with progression of advanced fibrosis risk in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Advanced fibrosis is the best predictor of future severe liver outcomes in patients with metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Our study aims to determine the association between cardiovascular disease (CVD) with time to a high-risk Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) in patients with low-risk MASLD.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study comes from a primary care clinic between 2012 and 2021. The cohort included patients with MASLD and a FIB-4 score at low-risk for advanced fibrosis (<1.3). Patients were followed for the outcome of having a high-risk FIB-4 (≥2.67) or until the end of the study period. The primary predictor variable was CVD, a composite of ICD-9/10 codes for coronary artery, cerebrovascular, and peripheral arterial disease. Covariates included demographic and comorbidity variables. Unadjusted and adjusted Cox regression models were developed for the outcome of time to a high-risk FIB-4 score.
RESULTS: The cohort included 859 patients with a mean age of 49.6 years (± 13.7) and mean body mass index of 34.1 (± 8.3) kg/m2. Included patients were 70% female and 41% non-white. Of the cohort, 32%, 36%, and 74% had CVD, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, respectively. During a mean follow-up of 3.8 (± 2.7) years, 9.3% (80) of the sample had a subsequent high-risk FIB-4 score. The multivariable Cox regression model demonstrated a significant association between CVD (HR 2.13; 95%CI 1.33-3.40) and chronic kidney disease (HR 2.05; 95%CI 1.23-3.42) with the time to transition to a high-risk FIB-4 score.
CONCLUSION: Our study showed that CVD is associated with an increased risk of progression of FIB-4 scores at low- to high-risk for advanced fibrosis in MASLD patients. Future research investigating how control of cardiometabolic comorbidities impact fibrosis progression in MASLD is warranted.

Title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Past, Present, and Future.
Journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management
Abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an important alternative strategy for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), particularly when long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) is contraindicated or poorly tolerated. Initially developed as a surgical technique based on ligation or excision of the left atrial appendage, LAAC has progressively shifted toward refined, minimally invasive transcatheter approaches. Randomized and observational data have established non-inferiority to warfarin, and non-inferiority compared with direct oral anticoagulants has also been suggested in selected high-risk cohorts and is currently under prospective evaluation in pivotal trials. At the same time, indications for LAAC are expanding beyond the classical high-bleeding-risk population, now encompassing patients undergoing atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and those with only moderate thromboembolic risk but intolerance to OAC. Parallel advances in device design aimed at improving anatomical conformability, sealing performance, and surface biocompatibility seek to reduce peri-device leak (PDL), device-related thrombus (DRT), and bleeding and may allow for simplified or shortened post-procedural antithrombotic regimens. This narrative review summarizes the historical evolution of LAAC from surgical to contemporary transcatheter solutions, outlines key clinical evidence versus medical therapy, and discusses emerging implant-based and implant-free technologies. As evidence accumulates from ongoing randomized controlled trials, LAAC may transition from a niche intervention to a more widely adopted, guideline-supported component of AF management. However, broader implementation will depend on robust demonstration of long-term safety and efficacy, including clarification of PDL-, DRT-, and bleeding-related trade-offs, to define when LAAC can serve not only as an alternative to OAC but also as a tailored option for selected NVAF patients.

Title: Association of the Platelet-to-Neutrophil Ratio With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Liver Fibrosis in U.S. Adults: NHANES 2017-March 2020.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a chronic liver disease that is not related to alcohol and is characterized by excessive accumulation of fat within liver cells. As one of the most common chronic liver diseases worldwide, MASLD affects about a quarter of the world's population and is expected to become a leading indication for liver transplantation by 2030. The disease not only increases the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, but also is closely associated with a variety of extra-hepatic complications such as type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Although many biomarkers such as N-terminal type III collagen propeptide (PRO-C3), enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF), and Fibrosis-4 Score (FIB-4) have been used to identify and predict MASLD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), their clinical utility remains limited. Recent studies have shown that neutrophils and platelets play a crucial role in the progression of MASLD. The platelet-to-neutrophil ratio (PNR), a novel biomarker, has shown predictive value in ovarian cancer and myocardial infarction. However, PNR has not been fully studied in MASLD. The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PNR and MASLD and to explore its relationship with hepatic steatosis and fibrosis.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic dataset. Hepatic steatosis was defined as a controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥ 274 dB/m, and MASLD was defined as hepatic steatosis plus at least one cardiometabolic criterion according to the 2023 multisociety steatotic liver disease (SLD) nomenclature. Advanced liver fibrosis was defined as a liver stiffness measurement (LSM) ≥ 8.2 kPa. PNR was calculated as the platelet count divided by the neutrophil count and log2-transformed (log2-PNR). Missing covariates were handled by multiple imputation (m = 20). Survey-weighted logistic regression, natural-spline smoothing, threshold effect analysis, and subgroup analyses were used to evaluate the association between log2-PNR and MASLD.
RESULTS: A total of 3437 adults aged 18 years and older were included (mean age 47.5 ± 17.5 years; 48.1% male). In the fully adjusted model, higher log2-PNR was inversely associated with MASLD (OR 0.75 per doubling of PNR, 95% CI 0.63-0.90), and with hepatic steatosis; participants in the highest PNR quartile had lower odds of MASLD than those in the lowest quartile. Threshold effect analysis identified a breakpoint at PNR approximately 38 for MASLD, with a significant nonlinear pattern. Higher log2-PNR was also inversely associated with advanced fibrosis (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.33-0.57), with no significant nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses showed that the inverse association was more pronounced in males and non-Hispanic White participants for MASLD (P for interaction = 0.009 and 0.037, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Higher log2-PNR was inversely associated with the cross-sectional presence of MASLD and hepatic steatosis, and with advanced liver fibrosis, in U.S. adults. Log2-PNR, an easily obtained inflammatory marker, is independently associated with MASLD. These findings require validation in prospective cohort studies.

Title: Targeting calciphylaxis: the emergence of vitamin K as a potential treatment.
Abstract: Calciphylaxis, or calcific uraemic arteriolopathy, is a rare, life-threatening vascular disorder predominantly affecting patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), especially those on dialysis. It is characterized by arteriolar calcification, thrombosis, and painful ischemic skin lesions that frequently ulcerate, contributing to high morbidity and mortality. Calciphylaxis arises from medial arterial calcification, endothelial injury, and a pro-inflammatory, pro-thrombotic milieu. Disruption of vitamin K-dependent pathways, particularly impaired γ-carboxylation of matrix Gla protein (MGP), a potent inhibitor of vascular calcification, has emerged as a key mechanistic contributor. Functional vitamin K deficiency is common in CKD and is exacerbated by vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin, which markedly increase calciphylaxis risk. Observational studies show elevated levels of inactive MGP and other undercarboxylated Gla proteins in affected patients, linking vitamin K insufficiency to disease pathogenesis. Case reports and preliminary interventional studies suggest that vitamin K supplementation could restore MGP activity, reduce vascular calcification, and support wound healing, robust randomized controlled trial data are lacking. Ongoing trials, including the BEAT-Calci adaptive platform, aim to clarify the efficacy, optimal dosing, and safety of vitamin K as a targeted therapeutic strategy. Precision medicine approaches using vitamin K biomarkers and individualized anticoagulation may further improve outcomes. In conclusion, vitamin K-dependent pathways represent a promising mechanistic and potentially modifiable target in calciphylaxis. High-quality clinical trials are urgently needed to validate supplementation strategies and develop evidence-based, individualized management protocols for this severe condition.

Title: The State of Mohs Micrographic Surgery in 2025-2026: Current Challenges, Pressures, and the Path Forward.
Journal: The Journal of clinical and aesthetic dermatology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) unites staged extirpation, comprehensive intraoperative histopathologic assessment, and immediate reconstruction to deliver durable local control with tissue conservation in anatomically critical sites. Contemporary practice, however, is shaped by intersecting forces: stewardship of indications, reimbursement trends, vertical consolidation, expanding use of intraoperative immunohistochemistry (IHC), and the emergence of complementary modalities (superficial radiation therapy; hedgehog and programmed cell death-1 [PD-1] inhibitors) alongside digital tools (teledermatology, artificial intelligence [AI], optical coherence tomography [OCT], reflectance confocal microscopy [RCM]).
OBJECTIVE: To provide a narrative synthesis that clarifies where MMS adds the greatest value, delineates the appropriate roles of competing and complementary treatments, and outlines pragmatic steps (clinical, economic, and educational) to preserve high-quality, margin-controlled cutaneous oncology.
METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of MEDLINE and Embase (January 2000-December 2025) using controlled vocabulary and keywords for MMS; basal cell and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; melanoma in situ; radiation therapy; systemic therapy (hedgehog/PD-1); IHC; teledermatology/AI; and optical imaging (OCT/RCM). Eligible studies included randomized trials, prospective cohorts, comparative observational studies, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and cost or reimbursement analyses reporting local control/recurrence, complications, episode-level cost, or implementation outcomes.
CONCLUSION: MMS provides superior or noninferior oncologic control with tissue preservation, same-day repair, and favorable safety in ambulatory settings. Appropriate use criteria should be framed as clinical stewardship, while superficial radiation and systemic therapies are best positioned as complements to MMS when surgery is infeasible or as neoadjuvant/adjuvant strategies. Sustaining the value of MMS will require explicit documentation of surgeon work and practice expense, standardized outcomes and patient-reported measures, equitable workforce strategies, and measured adoption of validated technologies such as OCT/RCM and AI. Payers and policymakers should recognize and preserve the true clinical and economic contribution of MMS.

Title: Cardiometabolic therapy for rhythm control: a case report of refractory atrial fibrillation resolving after initiation of semaglutide for obesity.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF) and has been linked to processes involved in atrial structural and electrical remodelling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists reduce cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk and are increasingly regarded as cardiometabolic therapies. Whether these agents modify the trajectory of atrial cardiomyopathy or exert direct antiarrhythmic effects beyond their metabolic actions remains an area of active investigation.
CASE SUMMARY: A 50-year-old man with obesity (body mass index 34.9 kg/m2) and persistent AF presented with persistent symptomatic episodes despite four prior pulmonary vein isolation procedures and repeated electrical cardioversions. Rhythm monitoring was performed continuously using a wearable device since 2023, documenting recurrent episodes lasting 8-30 h with a modified European Heart Rhythm Association (mEHRA) class IIb-III symptom burden. Echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function and left atrial enlargement. In January 2026, once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide was initiated for weight management (0.25 mg/week with subsequent dose escalation). While a weight reduction of 14 kg was observed within 6 months, AF episodes and symptoms ceased immediately after treatment initiation and have not recurred during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case describes cessation of recurrent AF episodes following initiation of semaglutide in a patient with obesity and prior ablation failure. Potential mechanisms may include cardiometabolic effects as well as direct myocardial effects on sodium and calcium handling that have been described experimentally. Although a causal relationship cannot be established from a single observation, this finding may serve as a hypothesis-generating signal and provide a rationale for prospective studies evaluating cardiometabolic therapies as potential adjuncts in rhythm control strategies.

Title: Right Ventricular Stroke Work Index and Its Prognostic Value in a Lung Transplant Population With Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung transplantation requires meticulous preoperative assessment. Recipients with Group 3 pulmonary hypertension can be at higher risk of mortality and primary graft dysfunction (PGD). We conducted a study to determine whether the right ventricular stroke work index (RVSWI), a right-heart catheterisation haemodynamic indicator assessing right ventricle function, could predict 1-year survival in this setting.
METHODS: Monocentric, retrospective, observational cohort study approved by our local ethics review board, between January 2013 and December 2023. We included lung transplant recipients who underwent preprocedural right-heart catheterisation assessment and presented with Group 3 pulmonary hypertension. We first determined a clinically relevant RVSWI threshold. The primary endpoint was mortality at 1 year amongst two groups of patients according to this threshold.
RESULTS: 66 patients (age 57.0 ± 11.4 years, male 56%) were included amongst a study population of 699 patients. Double-lung transplantations represented most of the procedures (91%). In univariate analysis, RVSWI was statistically associated with PGD Grade 3 at Day 3 and intraoperative veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) at a threshold of RVSWI = 13.5. Mortality at 1 year did not differ between the groups RVSWI ≤ 13.5 (6 patients, 14.6%) and RVSWI > 13.5 (6 patients, 24%) even after accounting for potential confounding factors.
CONCLUSIONS: In our lung transplant population with Group 3 pulmonary hypertension, RVSWI was not associated with mortality at 1 year. A higher RVSWI seemed associated with significant events such as intraoperative ECMO and PGD Grade 3. Further studies are needed to assess RVSWI's prognostic value in this setting.

Title: Duration of surfactant administration and its impact on stabilisation of vital parameters in very preterm neonates <28 weeks of gestational age (SurfStab): 1 min versus 5 min-study protocol for a prospective randomised-controlled phase IV trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory distress syndrome remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in extremely preterm neonates. Surfactant replacement therapy substantially improves survival. Current European Consensus Guidelines recommend the less invasive surfactant administration (LISA) technique. However, no evidence exists on whether the duration of administration affects physiological stability. Rapid surfactant administration may provoke transient hypoxia or bradycardia due to airway obstruction, whereas slower delivery could potentially reduce such fluctuations.
METHODS/DESIGN: The SurfStab Trial is a single-centre, randomised, controlled phase IV clinical trial conducted at the Division of Neonatology, Medical University of Graz, Austria. Extremely preterm neonates (< 28 weeks of gestation) requiring surfactant via LISA will be randomly allocated (1:1) to receive surfactant administration over either 1 min ("1-min group") or 5 min ("5-min group"). The primary outcome is the maximum change in cerebral oxygen saturation (crSO2), measured continuously using near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) from 5 min before LISA catheter insertion (baseline) to 15 min after completion of the procedure. Secondary outcomes include changes in arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2), heart rate (HR), arterial blood pressure (ABP), thoracic electrical impedance tomography (EIT), lung ultrasound, and the need for repeat surfactant administration, invasive ventilation, or supplemental oxygen up to three and up to 48 h after study intervention, as well as short-term outcomes at hospital discharge. The planned sample size is 76 neonates.
DISCUSSION: This trial will address a crucial gap in neonatal care by determining whether the duration of surfactant administration influences cerebral and systemic oxygen stability in extremely preterm neonates. The findings may refine evidence-based recommendations for optimal LISA procedure and may contribute to improved outcomes.
