Title: Perfusion Index as a Predictor of Hypotension Following Spinal Anesthesia in Below-Umbilical Surgeries.
Abstract: Background Hypotension following spinal anesthesia is common and may adversely affect end-organ perfusion. Perfusion index (PI), derived non-invasively from pulse oximetry, reflects peripheral vascular tone and may help identify patients at risk of post-spinal hypotension. This study aimed to determine the diagnostic threshold of baseline PI for predicting hypotension following spinal anesthesia in adults undergoing elective below-umbilical surgery and to assess its diagnostic performance. Methods This prospective observational diagnostic accuracy study included adult patients aged 18-65 years with the American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I or II undergoing elective below-umbilical surgery under spinal anesthesia. Baseline PI, heart rate, and blood pressure were recorded before spinal anesthesia, followed by serial hemodynamic and PI measurements for 30 minutes. Hypotension was defined as a decrease in mean arterial pressure of >20% from baseline. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed to determine the optimal baseline PI cut-off using Youden's index, with an estimation of sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and accuracy. Results A total of 92 patients were analyzed, of whom 21 (22.8%) developed post-spinal hypotension. Baseline PI was significantly higher among patients who developed hypotension than among those who did not (4.38±1.67 vs. 1.51±0.53, P<0.001). Baseline PI demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.999 (95% confidence interval: 0.995-1.000, P<0.001). A baseline PI of ≥2.53 yielded 100% sensitivity, 98.6% specificity, 95.2% positive predictive value, 100% negative predictive value, and 98.9% overall accuracy. Conclusion Baseline PI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for predicting post-spinal hypotension in adults undergoing elective below-umbilical surgery. A baseline PI of ≥2.53 may help identify patients at increased risk and facilitate anticipatory hemodynamic management.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence, Mechanisms, and Adverse Effects.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors were initially developed as oral hypoglycemic agents for type 2 diabetes (T2D), but mounting evidence has solidified their role as practice-changing therapies for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, which includes congestive heart failure (CHF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). This review summarizes the pivotal randomized controlled trials evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors, highlighting their clinical efficacy, key mechanisms of action, and adverse effects. As indications continue to expand and more patients are prescribed SGLT2 inhibitors, hospitalists must have a thorough understanding of this important medication class.

Title: Comparison of Mortality and Revision Rates between Cemented and Cementless Fixation in Bipolar Hemiarthroplasty: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUD: The purpose of this study was to compare the mortality and the revision rates between patients undergoing cementless hemiarthroplasty (HA) and cemented HA using national claims data in South Korea.
METHODS: We identified patients who received HA from January 2003 to December 2019 using procedural codes and categorized them into 2 groups according to the fixation method: with or without cement. Orthopedic complications including dislocations, periprosthetic fractures (PPFs), and periprosthetic joint infections were evaluated. The revision survivorship was calculated using the following endpoints: stem revision only, conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) (including stem revision), any stem revision, conversion to THA (cup only), and any revision. Short-term mortality and adverse cardiac events were also assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 175,841 patients including 64,786 (36.8%) with cement and 111,055 (63.2%) without cement received HA. The cemented group (80.5 ± 8.1 years) was older than the cementless group (77.8 ± 10.3 years) (p < 0.001) and had fewer comorbidities. The PPFs were less common in the cemented group (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.64; 95% CI, 0.58-0.70). The risk of conversion to THA was higher (aHR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.39-1.98); however, the risks of stem revision only (aHR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.53-0.70), any stem revision (aHR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.98), and any revision (aHR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.76-0.87) were lower in the cemented group. The cemented group had a 5-fold higher mortality rate (10 / 64,786) on the day of surgery compared to the cementless group (2 / 111,055). The adjusted in-hospital mortality was higher in the cemented group (aHR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.45-1.62). The cemented group had higher risks of myocardial infarction (aHR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.09-1.51), stroke (aHR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.18-1.36), and heart failure (aHR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.22-1.43) compared to the cementless group.
CONCLUSIONS: Cemented fixation had a higher risk of short-term mortality and adverse cardiac events after HA, while it had a lower risk of femoral stem revision and PPFs.

Title: Carotid atherosclerosis progression in patients with Parkinson's disease: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding the association between Parkinson's disease (PD) and cardio-cerebrovascular risk remains conflicting, and it is unclear whether the dynamic progression of carotid atherosclerosis in PD patients differs from that in non-PD individuals. This study aimed to compare the progression of carotid atherosclerosis over a 1-year follow-up between PD patients and matched controls, and to investigate whether PD influences this progression independently of traditional cardiovascular risk factors.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study ultimately included 61 PD patients and 59 age- and sex-matched non-PD controls. Carotid ultrasound was performed at baseline and at the 1-year follow-up. The primary outcome was the annual change in total plaque area (ΔTPA), with plaque progression defined as ΔTPA ≥ 0.05 cm2. Multivariable logistic regression models, adjusting for diabetes, smoking, total cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), were used to assess the independent association between PD status and plaque progression.
RESULTS: At baseline, carotid intima-media thickness and TPA were significantly lower in the PD group than in the control group (both P < 0.05). After 1 year, ΔTPA was significantly smaller in the PD group (P < 0.001), and the incidence of plaque progression was 6.56% in PD patients versus 25.42% in controls. Multivariable regression analysis showed that PD status was a protective factor against atherosclerosis progression (adjusted OR = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.074-0.984, P = 0.047). Within the PD group, no significant associations were observed between plaque progression and disease-specific factors such as disease duration, motor severity, or levodopa equivalent daily dose.
CONCLUSION: Carotid atherosclerosis progression is significantly slower in PD patients than in non-PD individuals, and this effect is independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings suggest that PD patients may exhibit a "vascular protective phenotype," and that a unique shared regulatory network may exist between neurodegenerative processes and peripheral vascular homeostasis.

Title: Clinical characteristics and surgical outcomes of neonates with congenital duodenal obstruction: a 10-year experience of trans-anastomotic tube use at a tertiary center in Oman.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the demographic and clinical characteristics of neonates with congenital duodenal obstruction (CDO) and to describe postoperative outcomes of intraoperative trans-anastomotic feeding tube (TAT) placement.
METHODS: We included a retrospective cohort of infants diagnosed (≤1 month of age) with CDO at the Royal Hospital, Oman, between January 2012 and December 2022. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize numerical and categorical data. A subgroup analysis compared outcomes between infants with TAT (Group 1) and without TAT (Group 2). Data were analyzed using independent sample t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, analysis of variance, and χ2 test as appropriate.
RESULTS: Forty-two infants were included; 24 were born ≥38 weeks, 23 were female and 24 had birth weight ≥2.5 kg. Intrinsic CDO was the most common presentation (n=21). Cardiac anomalies were present in 19 infants, and syndromes in 18 infants, mainly trisomy 21 (n=11). In subgroup analysis, Group 1 (n=13) had a longer median hospital stay than Group 2 (n=18), but this failed to reach statistical significance (22 vs. 16 days, p=0.13). Rates of central line insertion (69.2% vs. 66.7%, p=0.88), parenteral nutrition (76.9% vs. 83.3%, p=0.65), duration of total parenteral nutrition (12.5 vs. 11 days, p=0.96), time to start enteral feeds (4 vs. 4 days, p=0.93) and time to full enteral feeds (10 vs. 12 days, p=0.32) were similar between groups. Overall complication rate was 19.4% (6/31), with no TAT-related complications.
CONCLUSION: Demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable with international findings. TAT insertion was safe but did not improve postoperative outcomes.

Title: Local infiltration anesthesia (anterior field block) vs. general anesthesia for thyroidectomy: effects on operative time, complications, and cost-a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis with subgroup analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroidectomy involves the removal of part or all of the thyroid gland, commonly performed for goiters, hyperthyroidism, or carcinomas, with 450,000-500,000 procedures performed annually in the United States. General anesthesia is traditionally used, providing optimal surgical conditions but associated with risks such as cardiovascular complications and longer hospital stays. Local anesthesia is gaining interest for high-risk patients, offering potentially similar outcomes to general anesthesia, while reducing postoperative complications and costs. The choice of anesthetic technique impacts patient safety, healthcare costs, and overall experience, yet no meta-analysis has previously compared local and general anesthesia for thyroidectomy.
AIM: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare surgical and perioperative outcomes of general anesthesia vs. local anesthesia in thyroidectomy, focusing on operative time, complications, cost, and postoperative recovery, to inform clinical practice.
METHODS: This review was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus was performed from database inception to August 2025. We included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies comparing local infiltration anesthesia with general anesthesia in patients with thyroidectomy. Key outcomes included operative time, intraoperative and postoperative complications, hospital stay length, pain scores, patient satisfaction, and cost. Data were extracted independently by two authors. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias In Non-Randomized Studies of Interventions tool for non-randomized studies. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework. Statistical analysis was performed using Review Manager (RevMan), calculating mean differences and risk ratios under a random-effects model, with heterogeneity assessed using the I 2 statistic. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The systematic search identified 1,785 studies, of which 252 duplicates were removed. After screening, 1,508 studies were excluded, leading to a full-text review of 25 studies and ultimate inclusion of 5 studies comprising 508 patients undergoing thyroid surgery with either local or general anesthesia. Local anesthesia was associated with a shorter operative time than general anesthesia (mean difference -18.32 min, 95% CI: -27.31 to -9.15), but heterogeneity was high (I 2 = 95%), and the effect was significant only in cohort studies and not in randomized trials, and therefore, this finding should be interpreted with caution. No significant differences were observed between groups in nerve injury or respiratory distress, although evidence certainty for these outcomes was low. A cost analysis suggested that local anesthesia was less expensive than general anesthesia across all studies reporting cost data. Patient satisfaction appeared comparably high in both groups across the studies that assessed this factor.
CONCLUSION: Local anesthesia was associated with shorter operative times, lower costs, and shorter hospital stays compared with general anesthesia in thyroidectomy. However, these findings are drawn from a small number of studies and therefore should be interpreted cautiously. General anesthesia also likely remains necessary for more advanced procedures requiring airway control and complete patient immobility.

Title: Dynamic changes in CBC-derived inflammatory indices before and during acute coronary syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a within-patient paired study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with excess cardiovascular risk, but within-patient changes in complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices at the onset of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are not well described. We compared pre-event and acute-phase values in the same patients and contextualized pre-event values against a healthy cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, within-patient paired study reviewed hospital records from July 1, 2018, to December 30, 2025 (approximately 90 months). Among 3,960 hospitalized patients with RA, 89 had clinician-confirmed ACS and qualifying paired CBC measurements. Acute-phase CBCs were obtained within 24 hours after symptom onset, and pre-event CBCs were the most recent routine measurements obtained more than 14 days before the event. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated and natural log-transformed. Pre-event values were also compared with a healthy cohort (n = 110), with age- and sex-adjusted analyses used because residual demographic imbalance was present.
RESULTS: Pre-event log(NLR), log(SII), and log(SIRI) were higher in the RA cohort than in healthy controls and remained higher after adjustment for age and sex (all P< 0.001). Within-patient analyses showed increases during ACS, with mean Δlog values of 0.466 for NLR, 0.508 for SII, and 0.381 for SIRI (all Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q< 0.001). Neutrophilia increased from 11.2% before the event to 41.6% during ACS (McNemar P< 0.001). Exploratory subgroup estimates were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across several small strata; changes did not differ materially between remission/low and moderate/high RA activity groups.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with RA who developed ACS, CBC-derived inflammatory indices were higher than in a healthy comparison cohort before the event and increased further within the first 24 hours of ACS. The paired design quantifies change relative to each patient's own pre-event value. Without a non-RA ACS comparator, however, the study cannot establish RA-specific inflammatory priming or a causal chronic-to-acute mechanism. Prospective studies with serial sampling and clinical outcomes are needed.

Title: A peri-tumoral TREM2-high myeloid state, myeloid continuum polarization, and white matter disconnection in long-term cognitive survivorship after diffuse glioma: a neuroimmune-connectomic cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether a TREM2-high myeloid state and myeloid continuum polarization are associated with long-term cognitive survivorship in diffuse glioma has not been integrated with white matter connectomics and systemic neuroinflammation in a longitudinal framework.
METHODS: In a single-center retrospective cohort of 214 adults with WHO grade 2-4 diffuse glioma (168 IDH-mutant and 46 IDH-wildtype; median follow-up, 5.2 years), a 6-plex tyramide-amplified multiplex immunofluorescence panel was applied to 186 tumors. FlowSOM meta-clustering of 2.41 × 106 myeloid cells across the tumor core, peri-tumoral white matter, and infiltrative margin generated a patient-level Glioma-Associated Myeloid Polarization Continuum Index (GAM-PCI). Connectome-based lesion-symptom mapping, longitudinal serum biomarker profiling, and observational mediation models were integrated. The tissue-connectomic mediation model included 162 complete cases, and the serum-path model included 45 patients with complete paired serum and tissue data.
RESULTS: FlowSOM resolved six marker-defined meta-clusters (bootstrap Jaccard, 0.78-0.88). C4 was TREM2-high with all other panel markers intermediate (17.1% of myeloid cells), was enriched in peri-tumoral white matter relative to tumor core (21.0% vs. 13.8%, P < 0.001), and remained associated with arcuate fasciculus (AF) disconnection after adjustment for GAM-PCI (β = 0.21 per 10-percentage-point increase, P = 0.002). CD163+CD206+ cells showed greater spatial colocalization with myelin basic protein fragments in peri-tumoral white matter (Morisita-Horn index, 0.71 [0.58-0.82]) than at the infiltrative margin (0.42 [0.31-0.55]; P < 0.001), and their mean distance to the white matter boundary was 38 ± 14 µm versus a null median of 87 µm (P < 0.001). In 45 paired serum-tissue cases, T2 serum sTREM2 was associated with the peri-tumoral C4 proportion (Spearman ρ = 0.42, P = 0.004). Long-term cognitive decline occurred in 88 of 214 patients (41.1%), and AF disconnection independently predicted impairment (adjusted odds ratio, 1.52 per 10% increase; 95% CI, 1.25-1.88). In 162 complete tissue-connectomic cases, the model-based serial indirect association through MBP loss and AF disconnection was β = -0.19 (95% CI, -0.29 to -0.10; P < 0.001). In a separate 45-patient serum-path model, the estimated indirect association through T2 sTREM2/IL-6 was β = -0.06 (95% CI, -0.11 to -0.02; P = 0.004). The AF × IDH interaction was significant (P = 0.032), whereas a difference in C4 proportion by IDH status was not detected and equivalence was not established (TOST P = 0.078).
CONCLUSION: In this observational cohort, marker-defined peri-tumoral myeloid states, white matter disconnection, and systemic neuroimmune abnormalities were associated with long-term cognitive outcome. The mediation analysis provide model-dependent structural decompositions under stated assumptions and do not establish causal direction, cellular origin, or treatment effects.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Restrictive hypertonic saline resuscitation is associated with less intestinal injury after hemorrhagic shock in rats and with coordinated changes in MALAT1, miR-145-5p, and BNIP3 expression.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intestinal ischemia-reperfusion contributes to barrier failure and secondary organ injury after hemorrhagic shock. It is not known whether restrictive hypertonic saline resuscitation alters the resulting intestinal injury or the accompanying non-coding RNA response.
METHODS: One hundred male Sprague-Dawley rats were allocated to normal control, hemorrhagic shock, conventional 0.9% saline resuscitation (CFR), restrictive 7.5% hypertonic saline resuscitation (RFR), or superior mesenteric artery ischemia-reperfusion control groups. Hemorrhagic shock was induced by controlled blood withdrawal to maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP) at 35-40 mmHg for 60 min. CFR targeted an MAP of approximately 80 mmHg, whereas RFR targeted an MAP of approximately 60 mmHg. Three-hour survival was recorded. Coagulation, serum IL-6 and TNF-α, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, H&E staining, and TUNEL were assessed in assay-specific subsets. Public GEO datasets were analyzed for exploratory transcriptomic context.
RESULTS: Three-hour survival was 75% in RFR and 60% in CFR (two-sided Fisher exact test, P = 0.501). In the coagulation cohort, prothrombin time (PT) and thrombin time (TT) were shorter in RFR than in CFR after Dunn-Holm adjustment; no differences were observed for activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), international normalized ratio (INR), and prothrombin activity (PA). RFR had lower serum IL-6 and TNF-α, better-preserved ileal morphology, and lower TUNEL positivity in representative fields than CFR. MALAT1 was lower, while miR-145-5p and Bnip3/BNIP3 were higher in RFR. Exploratory analyses of public datasets confirmed that Malat1 and Bnip3 are expressed in the intestinal cell populations relevant to ischemia-reperfusion injury.
CONCLUSION: Under the present experimental conditions, restrictive hypertonic saline resuscitation was associated with a less severe acute intestinal injury phenotype than conventional isotonic resuscitation. The coordinated changes in MALAT1, miR-145-5p, and BNIP3 do not establish a linear regulatory axis and require functional validation.

Title: Obstructive sleep apnea and selected comorbidities - a literature review of cohort studies.
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is the most common type of sleep-related breathing disorder, characterized by repeated episodes of upper airway collapse and resulting hypoxia during sleep. Intermittent hypoxemia may exert a multisystemic impact and modulate the course of comorbidities. Pathophysiological mechanisms such as oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction contribute to adverse health outcomes including cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular complications, metabolic disorders, cancer, neurodegenerative conditions, or behavioral abnormalities. Treatment of OSA may mitigate progression of comorbidities and reduce the associated social and economic burden. This literature review aims to explore the relationships between OSA and selected comorbid diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), stroke, diabetes, cancer, and hypertension, based on cohort studies in the literature.

Title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation.
METHODS: Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding.
RESULTS: In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; p = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year.
CONCLUSION: JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

Title: Beyond detection: developing probabilistic hemodynamic phenotyping after a positive point-of-care pulmonary hypertension test.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a heterogeneous condition in which hemodynamic subtype directs management and specialist referral. PH can be identified non-invasively at the point of care by a previously developed, regulatory-cleared machine-learned diagnostic (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.95, sensitivity 82%, specificity 92%), but a positive test result raises a second clinical question: which patients have pre-capillary disease and therefore warrant referral to a specialist PH center. A probabilistic post-test phenotyping model was developed to estimate hemodynamic subtype probabilities and support rule-out of pre-capillary PH among test-positive patients.
METHODS: Subjects with right heart catheterization (RHC)-confirmed PH [mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) ≥25 mmHg] enrolled in a prospective multisite trial (NCT04031989) who tested positive on the previously validated point-of-care PH diagnostic formed the analysis cohort (n = 139). Hemodynamic subtypes were assigned per 2015 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) criteria. A one-vs.-one (OvO) Gaussian mixture model (GMM) framework, combining unsupervised clustering with post hoc supervised assignment of subtype probabilities was applied to features derived from non-invasive orthogonal voltage gradient and photoplethysmographic signals to generate subject-level subtype probability estimates. Blinded validation in a large dataset has not yet been performed; development results are reported, supported by a small blinded independent dataset.
RESULTS: At an exemplar post-hoc rule-out threshold of 16% pre-capillary probability, the GMM OvO approach yielded sensitivity 86% (95% CI: 71%-95%), specificity 51% (95% CI: 41%-61%), negative predictive value 88% (95% CI: 73%-96%) at an assumed pre-capillary prevalence of 34%, and a negative likelihood ratio (LR-) of 0.27 (95% CI: 0.07-0.70) on the development cohort. Supportive out-of-sample discrimination was observed in the blinded independent cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: A GMM OvO probabilistic model applied to non-invasive point-of-care signals can generate PH subtype probability estimates and may support rule-out of pre-capillary disease among true-positive patients. The model reuses signals already acquired for PH detection and can therefore be implemented as a software addition to an existing point-of-care workflow. Independent blinded validation is required to comprehensively characterize model performance.

Title: Spatial robustness of P100 latency compared with amplitude: a data-driven rationale for visual pathway monitoring during neuroendovascular procedures.
Abstract: Intraoperative visual evoked potential (VEP) monitoring has a reputation for being unreliable, and much of that belongs to P100 amplitude. Amplitude shifts with electrode position, anesthetic depth, and dipole geometry. Practice has nonetheless tended to lean on amplitude, and to treat latency as the weaker of the two. Neuroendovascular procedures give reason to shift that emphasis. During open surgery there can be a mixture of direct and ischemic neural injury, whereas in an endovascular procedure the brain is not dissected and the monitored pathway is threatened almost exclusively through perfusion. Oligodendrocytes are more vulnerable to ischemia than neurons, so myelinated conduction may slow before neurons are lost, and latency may prolong before amplitude falls. We first asked whether latency can be measured reliably enough. In a retrospective series of 49 eyes from 28 patients, the median spatial variability index across O1, Oz, and O2 was 2.10% for P100 latency and 40.9% for amplitude. Amplitude varied more than latency in 47 of 49 eyes and in all 28 patients. Latency behaves as a stable temporal measure of signal arrival, amplitude as a spatially sampled field measure. Some evidence for this exists in intraprocedural somatosensory monitoring. In an exploratory analysis of successfully reperfused thrombectomy patients, tree-based models separated 90-day functional outcome more consistently and efficiently by latency than by amplitude. If VEP latency behaves the same way, monitoring need not depend on the parameter that is hardest to trust, and VEP could be used actively in these procedures. We therefore propose that reproducible P100 latency prolongation may mark evolving visual pathway ischemia, and specify three studies that would test it. The first measures the temporal variability of intraoperative P100 latency and reports the smallest change it can resolve. That number sets the floor for any alarm threshold, including one below the conventional 10%. The second follows retrochiasmal perfusion-risk procedures with concurrent electroretinography, asking whether latency prolongation tracks angiographic events and precedes major amplitude loss. The third separates retinal from central contributions in ophthalmic-territory procedures. The present data establish spatial robustness only. Temporal stability and ischemia detection are the endpoints of those studies.

Title: Machine learning prediction of deep vein thrombosis before staged surgery in lower-leg and ankle fractures treated with temporary external fixation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) detected between temporary external fixation and staged definitive surgery can complicate perioperative management of lower-leg and ankle fractures. We developed machine-learning models to estimate DVT probability during this interval.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included adults admitted during 2015-2025 who underwent staged fixation and bilateral lower-extremity venous ultrasonography. A stratified 70:30 split defined development and validation sets. Development-set imputation, Boruta feature selection, and five-fold cross-validation were used to develop 12 classifiers. Algorithms were compared in the validation set. The selected Naive Bayes pipeline underwent 500 development-cohort bootstrap replications for optimism correction. Discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, and decision curves were evaluated. SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) and a bilingual research prototype web application supported interpretation.
RESULTS: Among 356 patients, 55 (15.4%) had DVT, including 40 with calf muscular vein thrombosis. The development and validation sets comprised 250 patients (39 events) and 106 patients (16 events). Boruta retained nine predictors. Naive Bayes had the highest validation receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC), 0.807 (95% confidence interval, 0.705-0.909). Precision-recall AUC was 0.343, sensitivity was 0.875, and specificity was 0.589. Beta calibration reduced the Brier score from 0.135 to 0.116 without changing discrimination. The apparent AUC was 0.858, mean bootstrap optimism was 0.084, and optimism-corrected AUC was 0.773. Injury-to-admission time, calcium, age, platelet count, fibrinogen, and hemoglobin had the largest mean absolute SHAP values.
CONCLUSION: The model may support risk stratification for an ultrasound-detected composite DVT endpoint in this staged-treatment population. Its proposed use is to inform surveillance timing and intensity while retaining routine bilateral ultrasonography. Prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Estimated glucose disposal rate shows the broadest associations with cardiometabolic multimorbidity progression in early cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stages: a longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early risk stratification may help prevent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0-3. We compared the estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR), triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) for incident CMM, disease transitions, and incremental prediction.
METHODS: This longitudinal cohort analysis included 6,407 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study participants aged 45-79 years at CKM stages 0-3 and free of CMM in 2011, with follow-up through 2020. CMM was defined as the coexistence of at least two of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) per standard deviation in the adverse direction (lower eGDR or higher TyG or AIP). Restricted cubic-spline and multistate models assessed dose-response patterns and transitions; five repetitions of stratified fivefold out-of-fold validation evaluated incremental 9-year prediction.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 9.0 years, 593 participants developed CMM. Primary-model HRs per adverse standard deviation were 1.92 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.77-2.09) for eGDR, 1.69 (95% CI, 1.57-1.82) for TyG, and 1.51 (95% CI, 1.39-1.64) for AIP. After CKM-stage adjustment, eGDR remained associated with all three disease-accumulation transitions (false-discovery-rate-adjusted P ≤ 0.009); TyG remained associated only with the earliest transition, and no AIP transition survived correction. Among single-marker additions, eGDR yielded the largest point gain in discrimination (ΔC-index, 0.041; 95% CI, 0.027-0.055). Adding TyG to eGDR further increased the C-index by 0.012 (95% CI, 0.005-0.020), whereas adding AIP to eGDR plus TyG changed the C-index by 0.001 (95% CI, -0.003 to 0.005). Calibration slopes were 0.910-0.945. Interval-aware and competing-risk analyses were consistent.
CONCLUSION: All three indices were associated with incident CMM. eGDR showed the most consistent transition associations and the numerically largest single-marker gain in internally validated prediction; TyG was complementary, whereas AIP added little beyond eGDR and TyG. Independent external validation and clinical-utility assessment are needed before use in early risk stratification.

Title: The Prognostic Value of PaCO2 on the Response to Noninvasive Ventilation in Patients with AECOPD Complicated by Type II Respiratory Failure.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) complicated by Type II respiratory failure frequently requires noninvasive ventilation (NIV). However, 10-25% of patients fail NIV and require intubation. The optimal timing and threshold of partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2) for predicting NIV failure remain unclear.
METHODS: In this two-center retrospective cohort study of 676 patients with AECOPD and Type II respiratory failure treated with NIV between 2012 and 2025, we used multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis (4 knots at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles) to assess the dose-response relationship between 24-hour post-treatment PaCO2 and NIV failure.
RESULTS: NIV failure occurred in 73 patients (10.8%). After full adjustment for age, heart rate, white blood cell count, hemoglobin, albumin, blood urea nitrogen, D-dimer, and baseline HACOR score, each 1 mmHg increase in 24h PaCO2 was associated with 3% higher odds of NIV failure (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear L-shaped association (overall P < 0.001; nonlinear P < 0.01), with a threshold at 60.2 mmHg. Below this threshold, no significant association was observed; above it, odds increased markedly; this threshold requires further external validation in independent patient populations. After adjustment for confounding variables, the fully‑adjusted multivariable model yielded an AUC of 0.805 (95% CI 0.751-0.860).
CONCLUSION: A 24-hour post-treatment PaCO2 exceeding 60.2 mmHg identifies patients at high risk for NIV failure. This readily available bedside measure may guide escalation decisions in AECOPD with Type II respiratory failure.

Title: Renal Dysfunction and Cardiorenal Syndrome in Acute Heart Failure: A Systematic Review of Residual Congestion and Decongestion Response.
Abstract: Renal dysfunction is common during hospitalization for acute heart failure and is traditionally considered a defining feature of cardiorenal syndrome type 1. However, the prognostic significance of worsening renal function may depend on the clinical context, particularly whether congestion persists or effective decongestion is achieved. This systematic review evaluated contemporary evidence regarding the relationships among renal dysfunction, residual congestion, decongestion response, and clinical outcomes in adults hospitalized with acute heart failure or cardiorenal syndrome type 1. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched for studies published between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, prespecified analyses of clinical trials, and post hoc analyses of trial-derived data that reported both renal and congestion-related outcomes. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Residual congestion was consistently associated with worse clinical outcomes, whereas worsening renal function during effective decongestion did not uniformly predict adverse renal or cardiovascular events. Studies evaluating venous excess ultrasound (VExUS)-guided and bioimpedance-guided strategies suggested that objective congestion assessment may improve decongestion phenotyping, although the available evidence remains limited. Overall, the findings support a renal-congestion framework in which kidney function is interpreted alongside congestion burden, diuretic response, perfusion status, and the trajectory of renal recovery. This approach may better distinguish high-risk persistent congestion from transient renal changes occurring during successful decongestion. Future prospective studies should determine whether combined renal-congestion phenotypes improve risk stratification beyond creatinine-based definitions of cardiorenal syndrome alone.

Title: Pentasystem embolism associated with transient antiphospholipid antibodies in severe M. pneumoniae pneumonia: a "Dual-Hit" case report and systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thromboembolism is a critical complication of severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP) in children, yet its clinical spectrum and immunothrombotic mechanisms remain poorly defined. The "dual-hit" hypothesis-synergy between infection-induced inflammation and transient antiphospholipid antibodies (aPLs)-lacks integrated clinical validation.
METHODS: We report a case of extensive multi-system thrombosis in a 6-year-old boy with SMPP. A systematic review of literature (January 2020-December 2025) identified 19 studies comprising 199 pediatric cases.
RESULTS: In the index case, thrombosis coincided with hyperinflammation and transient aPLs, which seroconverted to negative upon recovery. Pooled analysis showed multi-system involvement in 27.1% of cases (54/199). Among tested patients (n = 65; 32.7% of the cohort), aPL positivity was 69.2% (45/65). Most patients achieved favorable outcomes with anticoagulation and immunomodulation.
CONCLUSION: This study is consistent with the "dual-hit" model in SMPP, where systemic inflammation may prime the endothelium and transient aPL positivity coincides with an extensive thrombotic burden. The high prevalence of multi-system involvement supports low-threshold vascular imaging and aPLs screening, along with biomarker-guided management. Transient aPLs should be interpreted as a potential risk-amplifying biomarker rather than a proven causal driver of thrombosis.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Case Reports

Title: Vascular norepinephrine responsiveness index for early risk stratification in emergency department septic shock: a real-world cohort study from a Latin American sepsis code registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Septic shock is characterized by heterogeneous vascular responsiveness to norepinephrine. The vascular norepinephrine responsiveness index (VNERi), calculated as diastolic arterial pressure divided by the product of norepinephrine dose and heart rate, has been proposed as a bedside risk-stratification marker. Its performance in routine emergency department care remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with septic shock treated with norepinephrine in the emergency department from 2023 to 2025. The index time was the first protocolized invasive hemodynamic assessment after norepinephrine initiation. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression evaluated the association between VNERi and mortality, adjusting for age, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, Charlson comorbidity index, and serum lactate. Discrimination was compared with that of the mean arterial pressure-to-norepinephrine dose ratio (MAP/NE) using paired receiver operating characteristic curves. Non-linearity was assessed using restricted cubic splines. The previously reported value of 6.7 and a cohort-specific cutoff derived using the Youden index were explored.
RESULTS: Among 238 patients, 70 experienced 28-day in-hospital mortality. Median age was 72 years, 52.9% were female, median Charlson comorbidity index was 4, and mean Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 7.4. Each 1-unit increase in VNERi was independently associated with lower odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.79-0.91). VNERi showed modestly greater discrimination than MAP/NE (AUROC, 0.737 [95% CI, 0.675-0.799] vs. 0.667 [95% CI, 0.592-0.742]; p = 0.012). The spline model fit better than the linear specification (p = 0.014). Mortality was 48.0% with VNERi <6.7 and 8.8% with VNERi ≥6.7. The cohort-specific cutoff of 7.6 provided only a marginally higher Youden index than 6.7 (0.475 vs. 0.470).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower VNERi was independently associated with higher 28-day in-hospital mortality and showed modestly greater discrimination than MAP/NE. Prospective multicenter validation using standardized measurement timing and external validation of candidate thresholds are required before clinical implementation.

Title: Comparison of angioplasty, stents and conventional medical therapy for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerosis: a network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical treatment and endovascular therapy are widely employed in the management of symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis, however, the comparative effectiveness of these treatment modalities remains uncertain.
METHODS: We searched major Chinese and English databases to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing four different endovascular modalities against other comparable non-endovascular therapies for patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS). Eligible participants were individuals who had experienced a transient ischemic attack (TIA) or non-disabling stroke within the preceding 12 months. The literature search cutoff date was 11 January 2026.
RESULTS: For safety outcomes, the SUCRA ranking was as follows: medical treatment (MT) (SUCRA 90.1%) > drug-coated balloons (DCB) (SUCRA 52.8%) > balloon dilatation angioplasty (BDA) (SUCRA 40.7%) > bare metal stents (BMS) (SUCRA 35.4%) > drug-eluting stents (DES) (SUCRA 31.0%). MT exhibited a superior safety profile compared with BMS, with a statistically significant difference (RR = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.31 to 0.72). For long-term outcomes, exploratory SUCRA probability rankings were as follows: BDA (SUCRA 86.7%) > DES (SUCRA 77.4%) > MT (SUCRA 23.8%) > BMS (SUCRA 12.1%), and between-treatment differences were not statistically significant across all interventions.
CONCLUSION: In terms of short-term safety, BMS treatment strategies were significantly inferior to medical treatment (MT), while no statistically significant differences in safety were observed among the various endovascular treatment modalities. In terms of adverse events during long-term follow-up, between-treatment differences were not statistically significant. Despite relatively high SUCRA values for BDA and DES for long-term outcomes, these rankings should be interpreted cautiously given the lack of statistically significant inter-group differences. Further research is required to verify the performance of each endovascular treatment strategy about restenosis.

Title: Pathogenicity assessment of a bicuspid aortic valve-associated ELASTIN variant using a zebrafish model.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is one of the most common congenital heart defects but its genetic basis remains incompletely defined. Extracellular matrix components play key roles in outflow tract (OFT) and valve development, but their contribution to BAV is not fully established. Following the analysis of a cohort of BAV patients, we identified a family harbouring a rare human ELASTIN (ELN) variant (p.Gln691X). Here, we investigated the pathogenicity of this variant using an in vivo zebrafish model.
METHODS: We generated a zebrafish elna/b double knockout (KO) using an RNAless CRISPR Cas9 strategy to avoid genetic compensation. Cardiovascular morphology and function were assessed in mutant embryos. To evaluate pathogenicity of the human ELN p.Gln691X variant, mutant and control embryos were rescued by mRNA injection encoding either WT human ELN or the p.Gln691X variant.
RESULTS: elna/b double KO zebrafish exhibited cardiovascular defects including OFT anomalies, reduced stroke volume and dysmorphic aortic valves, highlighting Elastin's critical role in cardiac development. We then used this model to test the ELN variant identified in the BAV family. We found that wild-type ELN mRNA was able to restore normal cardiac function and morphology, whereas the variant ELN mRNA failed to do so.
DISCUSSION: Our study establishes a robust in vivo model to assess ELN variant pathogenicity and provides evidence linking ELASTIN to BAV, opening new avenues for uncovering the genetic mechanisms underlying BAV.

Title: 4D-Micro: a tiered, testable framework for hemodynamic-tissue perfusion mismatch in cardiac surgery.
Abstract: Organ dysfunction can develop after cardiac surgery even when mean arterial pressure, cardiac output, hemoglobin, temperature, and pump flow meet conventional targets. These variables remain the safety foundation, but they do not directly establish exchange-capable capillary flow or cellular oxygen use. We propose 4D-Micro, an unvalidated conceptual framework organized around four necessary functions: barrier and conduit integrity, perfusion driving, hemorheology, and cellular oxygen use. The framework was formalized from a recurrent clinical reasoning problem through targeted evidence mapping and explicit construction rules; it was not derived from a new patient dataset or statistical latent-variable analysis. 4D-Micro separates where recovery is discordant from the provisional mechanism that might explain it, then uses a prespecified proximal response and stopping boundary to update that explanation. It is not a substitute for established cardiac surgical monitoring or a claim that all four domains can be measured directly at the bedside. A tiered implementation distinguishes a core mode based on routine variables, an enhanced mode using regional and congestion signals, and a research mode using direct microvascular or biomarker measurements. Insufficient or conflicting data remain indeterminate rather than being forced into a phenotype. We specify a staged validation pathway: content and feasibility testing, prospective assessment of classification reliability and construct validity, and only then a pragmatic comparison with protocolized usual hemodynamic care. The framework should be narrowed or rejected if it cannot be applied reliably, its predicted responses are not observed, or it fails to improve decision processes without added harm.

Title: Upper extremity motor outcomes during paired vagus nerve stimulation in chronic ischemic stroke: a retrospective single-health-system cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent upper extremity (UE) impairment after stroke is a major cause of long-term disability, and treatment options in the chronic phase are limited. In randomized trials, vagus nerve stimulation paired with task-specific rehabilitation (Paired VNS) produced greater improvement in UE function and activity than the same rehabilitation with sham stimulation, leading to FDA approval in 2021.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of adults with chronic stroke and persistent UE deficits who underwent Vivistim implantation and participated in a Paired VNS program delivered across 5 outpatient clinics within our health system. The primary outcome was change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) from baseline (Paired VNS therapy initiation) to end of the intended Paired VNS therapy protocol (18 sessions). A ≥6-point improvement defined a clinically meaningful response. Adverse events were a secondary safety outcome, ascertained from routine clinical documentation and not systematically collected beyond early postoperative follow-up.
RESULTS: 32 patients underwent device implantation; 28 (88%) completed the intended protocol within the health system and had paired FMA-UE assessments available for the primary analysis. Ages ranged from 34 to 81 years (mean 62.1) and the median time since stroke was 3.0 years (IQR 1.7-4.2). FMA-UE scores improved for all 28 local completers. The mean increase of 9.43 points was statistically significant (95% CI 7.20-11.66; p < 0.001), the median increase was 8.0 points (IQR 5.0-13.25) and 20 patients (71.4%; 95% CI 52.9-84.7%) achieved a clinically meaningful response. Chart-derived clinical notes provided illustrative context regarding individual changes in daily activities that accompanied UE motor improvement in selected cases. Among the 32 implanted patients, one postoperative hematoma resolved without intervention and one device was explanted after 410 days due to chest tingling.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-health-system cohort, Paired VNS was associated with significant improvement in FMA-UE scores among 28 local completers. The findings are directionally consistent with prior trial evidence.

Title: Malnutrition risk factors and a pre-post evaluation of a multicomponent management program in older inpatients with chronic heart failure: a single-centre retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate nutritional impairment-related outcomes admission among hospitalized older patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and to conduct a pre-post evaluation of the clinical effect of a unified multicomponent management program delivered to all enrolled patients during their inpatient stay.
METHODS: A single-centre retrospective observational study was split into two independent analytical parts. Part 1: Retrospective risk factor and model construction analysis: We screened 200 complete medical records of elderly CHF inpatients admitted from March 2023 to March 2024, stratified participants into nutritionally impaired (n = 71) and non-impaired (n = 129) groups based on combined admission GNRI + NRS2002 assessment using a pre-defined "and" algorithm: impaired if GNRI ≤98 and NRS2002 ≥ 3; non-impaired if GNRI >98 and NRS2002 < 3, then performed univariate, multicollinearity and multivariate logistic regression analyses to screen nutritional risk-related variables and construct an internally validated nomogram prediction model, only using cross-sectional admission data without repeated follow-up assessment. Uncontrolled inpatient before-after observational sub-study: All 200 enrolled patients received a unified full-hospital multicomponent management program, which was uniformly implemented from the first day of each patient's admission throughout their entire hospital stay. Nutritional risk status, NYHA classification, Hb, CRP, and SAS scores were measured at two fixed time points: baseline (admission day, before intervention initiation) and discharge day (post full-course intervention). No parallel control group was set, no external follow-up after discharge was conducted, and all 200 patients had complete paired admission-discharge data with zero loss to follow-up; routine standard heart failure drug treatment remained consistent for all subjects during hospitalization without additional concurrent therapeutic adjustments. Collinearity diagnostics and logistic regression were applied for the risk factor section; paired t-tests and chi-square tests were adopted for within-cohort before-after comparisons. Missing clinical data were excluded prior to analysis; only fully documented cases were retained.
RESULTS: Univariate testing revealed significant intergroup differences in smoking history, NYHA cardiac function classification, hemoglobin (Hb), C-reactive protein (CRP), and SAS scores (all p < 0.05), with no severe multicollinearity detected (variance inflation factor ≤ 10, tolerance ≥ 0.1). Multivariate logistic regression identified smoking history (OR = 2.437, p = 0.003), NYHA classification (OR = 2.632, p = 0.002), Hb (OR = 0.921, p < 0.001), CRP (OR = 2.894, p < 0.001), and SAS score (OR = 1.086, p < 0.001) as factors independently associated with. The nomogram prediction model built on these five indicators yielded an AUC of 0.869 (95% CI: 0.814-0.923) on internal ROC validation, with a non-significant Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit p-value of 0.266, demonstrating satisfactory discriminative and calibration performance. The combined "and" algorithm identified 71 impaired patients, while GNRI alone flagged 89 patients and NRS2002 alone flagged 78 patients; the overlap between the two tools is illustrated in a Venn diagram. After standardized implementation of the multicomponent management program for all patients, the proportion of patients with NYHA class I-II increased, while the proportion with NYHA class III-IV and the admission-determined nutritional impairment rate declined significantly (all p < 0.05). Marked improvements in Hb, CRP, and SAS scores were also observed post-intervention relative to admission baseline (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Hospitalized older CHF patients bear a prominent admission nutritional impairment burden. Smoking history, NYHA classification, Hb, CRP, and SAS score are independently associated with admission nutritional impairment-related variables, and the established nomogram can assist clinical high-risk population screening. The uncontrolled inpatient before-after comparison demonstrated significant improvements in cardiac function, nutritional risk status, inflammatory markers, and anxiety after the multicomponent management program; due to the absence of a control group and potential confounding inpatient factors, causal effects of the intervention cannot be confirmed; only observational within-cohort changes are described. This study provides real-world retrospective evidence including a nutritional risk prediction model and preliminary observational intervention outcomes, with major limitations consisting of a single-centre design and an uncontrolled pre-post comparison lacking parallel controls.

Title: C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and diabetic vascular complications risk among patients with diabetes: a national cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) has emerged as an innovative biomarker for insulin resistance and inflammatory processes. Nevertheless, the association between CTI and diabetic vascular complications (DVCs) and its subtypes in individuals with diabetes remains unclear.
METHODS: This cohort study included 23 068 participants with diabetes from the UK Biobank at baseline (2006-2010). Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to evaluate the associations of CTI and triglyceride-glucose-related indices with the risk of DVCs and its subtypes. Separate analyses were conducted for individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D). The predictive performance of these indices was assessed using the net reclassification index (NRI) and Harrell's concordance index.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up period of 13.3 years, 4089 (26.8%) individuals developed DVCs. A significant positive linear relationship was observed between CTI and the risk of incident DVCs. For 1 SD increase in CTI, the corresponding HRs (95% CIs) were 1.05 (1.02 to 1.11) for overall DVCs, 1.21 (1.16 to 1.27) for diabetic kidney disease, 1.19 (1.13 to 1.26) for diabetic retinopathy (DR), 1.34 (1.26 to 1.43) for diabetic neuropathy (DN), 1.22 (1.14 to 1.31) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) and 1.05 (1.00 to 1.10) for cardiovascular disease. RCS revealed approximately an inverse L-shaped relationship for DR, DN and PAD. The addition of CTI to the model significantly improved NRI and Harrell's concordance index for DVCs incidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrated a significant positive association between CTI and the incidence of DVCs in individuals with T1D and T2D. Furthermore, our study revealed dose-response relationships between CTI and all subtypes of DVCs, providing more comprehensive risk stratification information for individuals with diabetes.

Title: Prognostic discrimination of SOFA-2 vs. SOFA-1 and incremental information from cardiovascular scoring and vasoactive support intensity in patients with sepsis receiving early vasoactive therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with sepsis who require vasoactive support during the first 24 h of intensive care represent a heterogeneous population. It is uncertain whether the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score improves mortality discrimination compared with the SOFA-1 score and whether observed circulatory support intensity provides complementary prognostic information.
METHODS: This multicohort observational study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) for a 24-h conditional landmark analysis. Patients alive and still in the ICU beyond 24 h were followed from ICU admission +24 h through ICU day 28 for reconstructed all-cause mortality. We compared SOFA-1 and SOFA-2, evaluated SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, analyzed first-24-h five-agent norepinephrine-equivalent peak burden (norepinephrine, epinephrine, dopamine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin), and internally evaluated an exploratory drug-composition model. Fixed strata were assessed directionally in eICU Collaborative Research Database and an independent-center high-risk stress test cohort with cohort-specific endpoints.
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV 24-h landmark cohort included 11,892 patients and 2,687 post-landmark deaths. SOFA-2 showed no observed discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.731 vs. 0.732; difference, -0.0005; 95% confidence interval, -0.0086 to 0.0076; P = 0.908). The SOFA-2 cardiovascular score had lower discrimination than the SOFA-1 cardiovascular score (0.663 vs. 0.676; P = 0.006). Mortality was 51.94% for the exploratory SOFA-2 ≥12 group and 17.09% below 12, and increased from 11.30% to 47.45% across four study-defined peak burden categories. The SOFA-2-plus-drug-composition model had an apparent AUROC of 0.768 and a bootstrap-corrected AUROC of 0.767, but it was not externally validated. Fixed strata preserved the direction of risk ranking in both external cohorts, whereas absolute risk and calibration differed.
CONCLUSION: SOFA-2 did not show an observed overall mortality discrimination advantage over SOFA-1 in this population. SOFA-2 total and cardiovascular scores, together with observed vasoactive support intensity, provided complementary prognostic description at 24 h. The ≥12 rule is exploratory, and drug-related associations do not establish causal treatment effects or clinical decision utility.

Title: Case Report: An enlarging left ventricular mass during anticoagulation in a patient receiving almonertinib after thoracic radiotherapy: diagnostic uncertainty and individualized management.
Abstract: Distinguishing a left ventricular thrombus from a cardiac tumor is challenging when a large mass arises at an atypical non-apical site, particularly in a patient with cancer. We describe a 37-year-old man with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutant non-small cell lung cancer receiving almonertinib who developed a broad-based posterior wall left ventricular mass while cancer imaging remained stable. At detection, the reported left ventricular ejection fraction estimate was 55%, and no regional wall motion abnormality was documented. Cardiac CT showed no calcification or appreciable arterial- or delayed-phase enhancement, and Doppler echocardiography showed no internal flow. Low-mechanical-index contrast-enhanced echocardiography showed no appreciable internal perfusion in the contemporaneous examination report; later archived images also showed persistent absence of perfusion, although early-phase cine loops were not retained for retrospective reassessment. These concordant avascular features supported the presence of a thrombus but were not diagnostic. Cardiac magnetic resonance was recommended but declined because of financial concerns, and histopathology was unavailable. After approximately 9 months of prescribed edoxaban 60 mg once daily with reported adherence, the maximum linear dimension increased from 39.7 to 51.0 mm. A posterior wall regional wall motion abnormality was first documented 5 months after mass detection and therefore could not explain the lesion already present at detection. Edoxaban levels and edoxaban-calibrated anti-factor Xa activity were not measured, and human interaction data for almonertinib and edoxaban were unavailable. This case highlights the need to keep the diagnosis qualified and to reassess alternative pathology and anticoagulant exposure when an imaging-supported left ventricular thrombus follows an unexpected course.

Title: Comparative safety outcomes of three venous access routes for totally implantable venous access port placement and exploratory assessment of pre-removal catheter-related thrombosis in breast cancer patients.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety outcomes of totally implantable venous access port (TIVAP) implantation through the internal jugular vein (IJV), subclavian vein (SCV), and axillary vein (AxV) in patients with breast cancer, and to explore a pre-removal thrombosis risk-stratification framework integrating D-dimer levels and vascular ultrasonography findings.
METHODS: Data from 475 breast cancer patients who underwent TIVAP implantation were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were classified according to implantation route: IJV (n = 161), SCV (n = 138), and AxV (n = 176). Baseline characteristics, procedure variables, postoperative complications, and Clavien-Dindo grades were analyzed. Among these patients, 234 underwent both pre-removal D-dimer testing and vascular ultrasonography, and 18 asymptomatic thrombotic events were identified. Firth penalized logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with thrombosis. ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory ability of D-dimer, and the optimal cutoff was determined using the Youden index. Patients were categorized into four scenarios according to D-dimer and ultrasonography findings.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable among the three groups. The complication rate was higher in the SCV group than in the IJV and AxV groups (16.67% vs. 7.45% vs. 5.68%, P = 0.002). Catheter fracture and pinch-off syndrome occurred exclusively in patients receiving SCV access. Firth penalized logistic regression showed that higher D-dimer levels and longer catheter dwell time were associated with asymptomatic catheter-related thrombosis. D-dimer showed moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.721). At the ROC-derived cutoff of 0.251 μg/mL, sensitivity was 77.78%, specificity was 76.85%, LR+ was 3.36, and LR- was 0.29. Integration of D-dimer and ultrasonography yielded four exploratory pre-removal profiles, including 166 double-negative, 4 D-dimer-negative/ultrasound-positive, 50 D-dimer-positive/ultrasound-negative, and 14 double-positive patients.
CONCLUSION: Compared with the SCV approach, the AxV approach showed a lower observed complication rate in this retrospective cohort, whereas no statistically significant difference in overall complications was observed between the AxV and IJV groups. D-dimer alone was insufficient to exclude thrombosis. The combined D-dimer/ultrasonography framework should be regarded as exploratory and requires prospective validation before its potential clinical application can be considered.

Title: Dynamic machine-learning model for early prediction of intraoperative hypotension using 5-minute perioperative time-series data: a multicenter retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is a common and potentially preventable complication strongly associated with postoperative acute kidney injury, myocardial injury, and mortality. Current approaches to IOH management remain largely reactive, and existing prediction tools have variable clinical utility. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a dynamic machine-learning model using routinely collected perioperative data to perform one-step-ahead prediction of intraoperative hypotension on a regularized 5-minute intraoperative grid.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 702 adults undergoing non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia for model development and internal validation and an independent external cohort of 248 patients. A dynamic prediction framework was constructed using routinely collected preoperative variables and intraoperative 5-minute time-series data. Individualized baseline features and temporal predictors were derived from rolling observation windows. Four machine-learning algorithms were compared using a fully nested grouped cross-validation framework with external validation. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based interpretability.
RESULTS: All four machine-learning models demonstrated good discrimination in the primary fully nested case-grouped internal validation, with AUROC values ranging from 0.842 to 0.857. Random forest achieved the highest AUROC (0.857, 95% CI 0.841-0.868), the highest AUPRC (0.413, 95% CI 0.367-0.452), and extra trees achieved the lowest Brier score (0.093, 95% CI 0.088-0.098). In the independent external validation cohort, random forest remained the best-performing model, yielding an AUROC of 0.894 (95% CI 0.875-0.907), an AUPRC of 0.540 (95% CI 0.457-0.596), and a Brier score of 0.092 (95% CI 0.083-0.102). SHAP analysis consistently identified MAP-derived features, including current MAP, recent hypotensive burden, recent MAP measurements, relative MAP reduction, and MAP variability, as the most influential predictors across all four models.
CONCLUSIONS: A dynamic machine-learning model using routinely collected perioperative time-series data accurately predicted MAP <65 mmHg at the next scheduled 5-minute intraoperative time point in an independent external cohort. These findings support further evaluation of this short-horizon risk stratification model in prospective clinical workflow studies.

Title: A lipid-related transcriptomic signature for distinguishing Kawasaki disease from febrile infections: a Mendelian randomization and machine-learning study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) diagnosis remains challenging because no pathognomonic test exists and the clinical presentation overlaps extensively with common childhood infections. Acute KD is accompanied by reproducible lipid perturbations, yet whether these changes are causally linked to the innate immune-driven vascular damage of KD vasculitis is unestablished. We aimed to derive a lipid-related transcriptomic signature for distinguishing KD from febrile infections and to characterize its relationship with innate immune remodeling.
METHODS: Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) screened 422 candidate exposures (419 lipid/metabolic traits and three immune-cell phenotypes) against two independent KD GWAS cohorts, with multiplicity correction. Differentially expressed genes from a training cohort comparing KD with rigorously classified febrile controls were intersected with a broad lipid-metabolism-related GeneCards set, yielding 459 candidates. The 459 candidates were evaluated across 130 machine-learning combinations; a full-training LASSO fit at lambda.1se yielded a 12-gene candidate panel, and the saved penalized model was applied unchanged to an independent cohort without batch correction. The immune microenvironment was estimated using CIBERSORT, acute-to-convalescent expression changes were tracked longitudinally, and selected markers were assessed in TNF-α-stimulated HUVECs.
RESULTS: No exposure survived correction for the 422 tests performed (minimum Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.979). All nine discovery-stage nominal hits were evaluated in a second KD GWAS; eight had directionally concordant point estimates, but none reached an unadjusted P < 0.05 in the second cohort. The frozen penalized model achieved an external AUC of 0.851 (95% CI 0.768-0.934) in GSE68004 without cross-cohort batch correction. CIBERSORT indicated a higher estimated neutrophil fraction in KD, concordant with a mature-neutrophil marker score from the same matrix. CETP, KREMEN1, and CCL23 were lower in convalescent samples after IVIG (all FDR < 0.0001) and were induced in TNF-α-treated HUVECs, together with VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and IL-8.
CONCLUSIONS: The frozen penalized model showed moderate discrimination between KD and febrile controls, but the selected 12-gene set represents one candidate realization of a partition-sensitive modeling pipeline. KREMEN1 warrants separate biological study on the basis of marginal, longitudinal, and immune-association findings rather than its selection stability. Recalibration and prospective validation are required before clinical use. The HUVEC findings are transcriptional and hypothesis-generating.

Title: The relationship between heart rate variability and eye movement characteristics in adolescents with internet gaming disorder: the mediating role of impulsivity.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate alterations in heart rate variability (HRV) and exploratory eye-movement characteristics in adolescents with Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), examine the associations among HRV, impulsivity, and exploratory eye-movement characteristics, and further conduct an exploratory mediation analysis based on the observed correlation pattern.
METHODS: A cross-sectional case-control study was conducted involving 75 adolescents who met the diagnostic criteria for IGD and 75 age-, sex-, and education-matched healthy controls (HCs). All participants completed psychological assessments, including the 20-item Internet Gaming Disorder Test, the Chinese Revised Version of the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale-11 (BIS-11), the Hamilton Anxiety Scale, and the Hamilton Depression Scale. HRV parameters, including heart rate (HR), standard deviation of NN intervals (SDNN), and root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), were collected. Eye movement parameters included the number of eye fixations (NEF), responsive search scores (RSS), total eye scanning length (TESL), mean eye scanning length (MESL), and discriminant analysis score. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0. Pearson correlation analyses were conducted to examine associations among variables, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied for multiple comparisons. Mediation analyses were performed using the PROCESS macro in SPSS with the bootstrap method to test the significance of indirect effects.
RESULTS: (1) Compared with the HC group, the IGD group exhibited reduced HRV, characterized by significantly decreased RMSSD and SDNN values and increased HR (all p < 0.001). (2) Compared with the HC group, the IGD group showed significant alterations in eye movement performance, including decreased NEF and RSS, as well as reduced TESL and MESL (all p < 0.001). (3) Pearson correlation analyses within the IGD group revealed that RMSSD was negatively correlated with BIS-11 total scores, BIS-11 total scores were negatively correlated with RSS, and RMSSD was positively correlated with RSS. (4) The exploratory mediation analysis showed a significant indirect association between RMSSD and RSS through BIS-11 total scores (unstandardized indirect effect = 0.0375, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0061, 0.0903]), accounting for approximately 33.0% of the total association.
CONCLUSION: This study examined the interrelationships among physiological, cognitive, and behavioral characteristics of IGD. Adolescents with IGD exhibited reduced HRV, increased impulsivity, and altered exploratory eye-movement characteristics. Impulsivity statistically accounted for part of the association between RMSSD and RSS.

Title: Effect of an artificial intelligence health education accurately linking system on self-management in young and middle-aged patients after percutaneous coronary intervention: a protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is a common heart disease worldwide, and the morbidity and mortality rates among Chinese residents continue to rise. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can improve survival rates, but long-term management is required after the procedure. Traditional interventions have shortcomings such as dependence on medical institutions and the lack of personalized treatment plans. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Artificial Intelligence-based Health Education Precision Linkage System (AI-HEALS) in improving self-health management among young and middle-aged patients after PCI.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-center, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group controlled trial. Eligible patients aged 18-59 years from Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, will be randomly allocated at a 1:1 ratio to receive either standard care plus the AI-HEALS intervention (intervention group) or standard care alone (control group). The primary outcome is the change in self-management ability from baseline to the 3-month intervention endpoint, assessed using the Coronary Heart Disease Self-Management Behavior Scale (CSMS). Secondary outcomes include medication adherence, dietary behavior, exercise frequency, and psychological indicators. Assuming an effect size of d = 0.69, 80% statistical power, and a two-sided significance level of α = 0.05, with an anticipated 20% dropout rate, the required sample size was calculated as 86 participants (43 per group). Primary analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. Generalized linear mixed models will be used for repeated measures outcomes, and multiple imputation by chained equations will handle missing data. Quantitative findings will be integrated with qualitative data from structured interviews conducted among intervention group participants.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University (Approval No.[2024] 409-002). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conferences.Clinical Trial Registration: http://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2500100519.

Title: Two-year dynamic risk stratification and adjuvant radioiodine efficacy in initial non-distant metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma harboring TERT promoter mutations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of postoperative radioiodine (131I) ablation remains unclear for patients with initially diagnosed non-distant metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) with harboring TERT promoter(TERT-p) mutations, it is unknown whether 131I therapy reduces the risk of persistent or recurrent disease. This study investigated clinicopathological features, 2-year dynamic therapeutic responses and progression-free survival (PFS) in this specific patient cohort.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled 113 eligible patients, allocated to the 131I ablation group (n=62) and non-131I group (n=51). Two-year dynamic risk stratification assessed treatment response. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models were used for survival analysis.
RESULTS: The predominant TERT-p variant was C228T (89.4%), and most patients carried concurrent BRAFV600E mutations. Only initial surgical approach remained an independent intergroup variable. Within 2 years, 46.0% achieved acceptable responses, associated with sex and primary surgery (p=0.036,p < 0.001). High baseline ATA risk was strongly correlated with structural residual lesions and unfavorable therapeutic response (p < 0.001).No significant between-group differences in response were observed across all ATA risk subgroups. The median follow-up was 4.6 years; 3- and 5-year PFS rates were 67.5% and 39.1%. Age ≥55 years, N1b stage and high baseline ATA risk were independent adverse predictors of PFS. Both 2-year therapeutic response and PFS at the end of follow-up exhibited no statistical differences between the 131I group and non-131I group.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective observational cohort, postoperative 131I ablation was not associated with improved PFS among patients with non-distant metastatic TERT-p-mutant PTC. Advanced age, N1b lymphatic metastasis and high baseline ATA risk independently predict poor outcomes. Biologically, TERT-p mutations induce tumor dedifferentiation and impaired iodine uptake, diminishing 131I efficacy. Clinically, routine 131I yields no survival benefit for this high-risk molecular subgroup, guiding individualized surveillance and avoiding redundant 131I exposure.

Title: Association between patent foramen ovale and anxiety: a prospective study with deep learning-assisted analysis of contrast echocardiography.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To prospectively investigate the association between patent foramen ovale (PFO), detected via agitated saline contrast echocardiography (ASCE), and anxiety using a deep learning approach.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study consecutively enrolled 161 participants between July 15, 2025 and October 31, 2025.
