Participants were stratified into ASCE-negative (n=58) and ASCE-positive (n=103) groups based on the examination results. All participants underwent ASCE and anxiety assessment using the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS). An artificial intelligence model was developed using a 10-fold cross-validation approach on the 103 ASCE-positive videos to predict anxiety scores. The primary endpoint was the association between PFO and anxiety, while the deep learning model was evaluated as a secondary/exploratory endpoint. Statistical analyses, including logistic regression, were performed with statistical significance set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: Compared to the ASCE-negative group, the ASCE-positive group exhibited significantly higher anxiety levels (SAS score: 45.0 vs. 38.0, p<0.001) and a higher prevalence of anxiety (32.0% vs. 5.2%, p<0.001). Logistic regression identified a strong association between ASCE-positive status and anxiety (adjusted odds ratio=8.64, p<0.001), with no clear dose-dependent relationship across shunt grades. The imaging-only deep learning model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.76 ± 0.12 and an R² of 0.46 ± 0.03 across cross-validation folds. After incorporating clinical and sociodemographic confounders, the model's performance improved to an MAE of 5.15 ± 0.10 and an R² of 0.59 ± 0.02.
CONCLUSION: This prospective study confirms a significant association between PFO and anxiety and demonstrates the feasibility of using ASCE-based deep learning models to predict anxiety risk, although clinical application requires external validation.

Title: Predictive value of the monocyte-to-albumin ratio at admission for 30-day mortality in elderly patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a retrospective analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The monocyte-to-albumin ratio (MAR) integrates systemic inflammation and nutritional status and has been proposed as a predictor of mortality after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). However, independent validation in an exclusively elderly cohort remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between admission MAR and 30-day mortality in patients aged ≥65 years with sICH.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 206 consecutive elderly patients with acute sICH. MAR was calculated as monocyte count (×109/L) divided by serum albumin (g/L). The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Optimal MAR cutoff was determined by Youden's index. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: 30-day mortality was 38.8%. MAR was significantly higher in non-survivors (0.022 vs. 0.016, p < 0.001). The optimal cutoff was 0.021 (AUC 0.648, 95% CI 0.572-0.724), providing sensitivity of 57.5% and specificity of 68.3%. MAR performance was comparable to the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (AUC 0.643) and systemic inflammatory response index (AUC 0.637). After adjustment, MAR > 0.021 was independently associated with 30-day mortality (adjusted HR 2.41, 95% CI 1.51-3.85, p < 0.001). In a sensitivity analysis using the ICH score as the primary severity covariate, MAR remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.25-3.26, p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: Admission MAR is independently associated with 30-day mortality in elderly sICH patients, although its discriminative ability is limited (AUC 0.648). As a simple, routinely available parameter, MAR may serve as a supplementary-not standalone-bedside risk stratification tool.

Title: Personalized anticoagulant therapy in venous thromboembolism: current role of direct oral anticoagulants, unmet clinical needs, and future perspectives on Factor XI inhibition.
Abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The introduction of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has transformed the management of VTE by providing effective and convenient alternatives to vitamin K antagonists. However, despite their favorable efficacy-safety profile, clinically relevant bleeding, treatment individualization, and the management of patients with competing thrombotic and hemorrhagic risks remain important unmet clinical needs. Contemporary VTE management increasingly requires a personalized approach integrating clinical characteristics, comorbidities, biomarkers, and real-world evidence to optimize anticoagulant selection, treatment intensity, and duration. Large prospective registries have expanded our understanding of VTE across heterogeneous clinical settings, including cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative VTE, incidental and subsegmental pulmonary embolism, and other high-risk populations frequently underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. In parallel, emerging prognostic tools, including D-dimer, hemoglobin, inflammatory indices, lipid-related biomarkers, and machine-learning-based prediction models, are contributing to a more refined assessment of thrombotic and bleeding risk. These emerging therapies are being evaluated as potential strategies to reduce bleeding while maintaining antithrombotic efficacy; however, recent phase III findings have demonstrated heterogeneous efficacy across clinical indications, emphasizing that their future role is likely to be indication-specific. This narrative review examines the current role of DOACs in VTE management, discusses the clinical and biological determinants of individualized anticoagulant therapy, and critically appraises the evolving and heterogeneous evidence for Factor XI inhibition as a potential future anticoagulant strategy.

Title: Explainable machine-learning model for postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after gynecologic cancer surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially fatal complication after radical surgery for gynecologic malignancies, yet population-specific risk tools remain limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 500 consecutive patients who underwent radical surgery for cervical, endometrial, or ovarian cancer (January 2022-January 2025). The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n=351, 70%) and a validation set (n=149, 30%) at a 7:3 ratio. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression, and 10 machine-learning algorithms were trained and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated, and the optimal model was interpreted using SHAP.
RESULTS: DVT occurred in 116 patients (23.2%). Five variables were independently associated with DVT: age, Caprini score, lymphocyte count, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR).Across candidate models, CatBoost achieved the optimal overall performance on the validation set, yielding an AUC of 0.816 (95% CI: 0.738-0.881), with sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI: 0.700-1.000) and specificity of 0.730 (95% CI: 0.515-0.876), and SHAP analysis ranked the predictors by mean absolute SHAP value in the following order: lymphocyte count, Caprini score, age, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR).
CONCLUSION: An interpretable CatBoost-based model enables individualized postoperative DVT risk stratification after gynecologic cancer surgery and may support targeted, evidence-based thromboprophylaxis and perioperative nursing management.

Title: Predictors of futile recanalization following endovascular therapy for acute anterior circulation large vessel occlusion stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is effective for acute anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO), yet futile recanalization remains common. Identifying its predictors is essential to optimize patient selection.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 311 patients with anterior circulation LVO who underwent successful EVT. Patients were divided into an effective recanalization group (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≤ 2, n = 150) and a futile recanalization group (mRS > 2, n = 161). Clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and a predictive model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
RESULTS: Baseline comparisons between the two groups showed significant differences in age, sex, atrial fibrillation, stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), C-reactive protein, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) infarct volume, DWI-Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (DWI-ASPECTS) score, number of procedure attempts, and procedure time. Univariate logistic regression and multivariate logistic regression identified admission NIHSS score (OR = 1.381, 95% CI: 1.113-1.713, p = 0.003), DWI infarct volume (OR = 1.057, 95% CI: 1.025-1.090, p < 0.001), DWI-ASPECT score (OR = 69.240, 95% CI: 9.819-488.254, p < 0.001), procedure time (OR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.005-1.018, p < 0.001), and SHR (OR = 3.447, 95% CI: 1.302-9.129, p = 0.013) as independent predictors of futile recanalization. A combined model incorporating these five predictors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.815 (sensitivity: 0.789, specificity: 0.787, Youden index: 0.576).
CONCLUSION: Admission NIHSS score, SHR, DWI infarct volume, DWI-ASPECT score, and procedure time are independent predictors of futile recanalization after EVT for anterior circulation LVO stroke. Higher NIHSS score, elevated SHR, larger infarct volume, lower DWI-ASPECT score, and prolonged procedure time increase the risk of poor functional outcome despite successful reperfusion.

Title: Sarcopenia and outcomes after revascularization for peripheral arterial disease: a scoping review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sarcopenia, a degenerative skeletal muscle disease associated with aging and chronic diseases, is a recognized risk factor for poor postoperative outcomes in various surgical fields. However, in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) undergoing revascularization, systematic evidence on its epidemiology, assessment practices, and prognostic impact is lacking. This scoping review aims to synthesize available evidence to clarify the prevalence, diagnostic methods, and association between sarcopenia and adverse postoperative outcomes in patients with PAD, thereby informing perioperative risk stratification and targeted interventions.
METHODS: This study was conducted following the Arksey & O'Malley scoping review framework and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) revised scoping review methodology. Relevant studies were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang Data, and VIP Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database from inception to June 30, 2025. Eligible studies were published in Chinese or English and focused on the impact of sarcopenia on the prognosis of patients with PAD. The extracted data were collated, categorized, and summarized.
RESULTS: Twelve studies were included. The prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with PAD ranged from 9.01% to 66.67%. Most existing studies diagnosed sarcopenia solely based on imaging-derived muscle parameters without comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and physical function. Despite these methodological limitations, imaging-evident muscle loss was correlated with elevated postoperative mortality, increased risk of cardiovascular events, and poor limb prognosis in patients with PAD.
CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia is prevalent among patients with PAD and serves as a potential risk factor for adverse postoperative outcomes. Inconsistent diagnostic criteria and substantial methodological heterogeneity across current studies restrict the generalizability of available evidence. Future efforts are required to establish a standardized, multidimensional assessment system for sarcopenia, and high-quality prospective studies are needed to clarify its perioperative prognostic value.

Title: Associated factors and predictive modeling of deep vein thrombosis in stroke patients undergoing rehabilitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify factors associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and to develop predictive models to facilitate individualized risk assessment in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 240 patients with stroke admitted to a rehabilitation department, including 63 patients with DVT and 177 without DVT. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were collected. Univariate analysis was performed to screen variables potentially associated with DVT, followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify variables independently associated with DVT. In parallel, six machine-learning models were developed using all baseline variables. The full cohort was evaluated across 100 stratified 8:2 train-test splits, with repeated five-fold cross-validation performed within each training subset and corresponding held-out subsets used for testing. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to enhance interpretability.
RESULTS: Multivariable analysis identified lower Barthel Index [odds ratio (OR) = 0.979, p = 0.008], diabetes (OR = 0.434, p = 0.032), and malignant tumor (OR = 2.883, p = 0.014) as variables independently associated with DVT. The final logistic regression model achieved an AUC of 0.765. Among machine learning models, the random forest model demonstrated the highest mean cross-validated AUC (0.781 ± 0.022) and the highest mean held-out AUC across 100 stratified train-test splits (0.797 ± 0.062). SHAP analysis indicated that age, D-dimer level, Barthel Index, activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), and disease course were the five most influential contributors to Random Forest predictions.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our findings support the use of integrated predictive approaches for DVT risk assessment and targeted screening in stroke rehabilitation settings.

Title: Remote ischemic conditioning plus stenting for symptomatic carotid artery stenosis (RICSICAS): rationale and design.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) has emerged as a promising non-invasive strategy to protect the brain, with evidence suggesting its benefit in patients with carotid artery stenting (CAS). However, the long-term benefit and safety of chronic RIC in this population remain unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether chronic RIC reduces the incidence of major vascular events in high-risk patients with carotid artery stenosis who received CAS.
METHODS: RICSICAS is a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded endpoint evaluation (PROBE), single-center trial. We plan to enroll 450 high-risk patients with symptomatic carotid artery stenosis (Essen score ≥ 3) scheduled for CAS. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either standard medical therapy plus RIC or standard medical therapy alone. The RIC protocol involves bilateral upper-arm cuff inflation to 200 mmHg (5-min inflation/5-min deflation, 5 cycles) performed 1-2 times daily, starting 3 days before CAS and continuing for 12 months post-procedure, thus constituting a combined peri-procedural and chronic RIC strategy. The primary efficacy endpoint is the composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, TIA, and vascular death within 12 months. Safety endpoints include any RIC-related adverse event (e.g., limb pain, petechiae, peripheral nerve injury), and any serious adverse event.
SAMPLE SIZE: Assuming a 12-month event rate of 20% in the control group and a 40% relative risk reduction with RIC, with 80% power and a two-sided α of 0.05, 355 patients are required. Accounting for a 20% dropout rate/loss-to-follow-up, as well as the consumption of the interim analysis, the total sample size is set as 450.
DISCUSSION: This trial will provide high-level evidence on the role of long-term RIC as an adjunctive therapy for high-risk patients with symptomatic carotid artery stenosis undergoing CAS.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, identifier: NCT07412249.

Title: Early clinical outcomes after switching to faricimab in previously treated diabetic macular edema.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate short-term functional, anatomical, morphologic, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived outcomes after switching to intravitreal faricimab in previously treated diabetic macular edema (DME) with persistent or recurrent center-involving retinal fluid after conventional anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy without angiopoietin-2 inhibition.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 50 eyes from 50 patients with previously treated DME and center-involving intraretinal and/or subretinal fluid at the time of switching. All eyes received four consecutive monthly intravitreal faricimab injections. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) were assessed through Month 4. OCT morphologic features were evaluated at baseline and Month 4, and OCTA-derived foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area, superficial capillary plexus vessel density (SCP-VD), and deep capillary plexus vessel density (DCP-VD) were evaluated at baseline, Month 1, and Month 4.
RESULTS: Mean CMT decreased from 526.8 ± 55.8 μm at baseline to 255.6 ± 20.5 μm at Month 4, while mean BCVA improved from 0.80 ± 0.19 to 0.28 ± 0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001), with consistent linear mixed-effects model results. SRF resolved in all 11 eyes with baseline SRF. IRF resolved in 38 of 50 eyes (76.0%) and decreased in the remaining 12 eyes. HRF resolved in 4 of 10 eyes (40.0%) and decreased in the remaining 6 eyes. FAZ area, SCP-VD, and DCP-VD showed no significant longitudinal change. Baseline FAZ area showed weak inverse correlations with CMT reduction and BCVA improvement, but these associations did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction. Baseline SCP-VD and DCP-VD were not significantly associated with treatment response. No serious ocular or systemic adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Faricimab switching followed by four consecutive monthly injections was associated with substantial short-term anatomical and visual improvement in previously treated DME with persistent or recurrent center-involving retinal fluid. Early clinical improvement occurred without parallel changes in global OCTA-derived perfusion parameters. Larger prospective controlled studies are needed to clarify the treatment-specific contribution and durability of faricimab switching.

Title: Prognostic value of platelet-to-white blood cell ratio in critically ill patients with non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage: a machine learning-driven study of the public database and the hospital information system.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment of prognosis is crucial for managing non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (NSAH) patients. The study aimed to explore the association between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) and all-cause mortality in this high-risk population and to develop machine learning models to improve prognostic accuracy.
METHODS: Using data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV). The observational endpoints were 30-day and 365-day mortality. Patients were categorized into four groups based on the quartiles of PWR. Kaplan-Meier curves, multivariate Cox regression analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and subgroup analyses were applied. We also developed machine learning models that include PWR and clinical features selected with the Boruta and LASSO algorithms to predict 30-day mortality. Model performance was evaluated by the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and the area under the curve (AUC). Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was utilized to provide model interpretability. External validations in the eICU-Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Hospital Information System (HIS) of the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University were used to assess generalizability.
RESULTS: A total of 1,176 patients with critically ill NSAH were enrolled from MIMIC-IV, predominantly male (58.8%), with a median age of 62 years. In multivariable Cox models, higher PWR quartiles were independently associated with lower risk of 30-day (HR = 0.55, 95% CI 0.35, 0.86, p = 0.009) and 365-day (HR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.37, 0.77, p = 0.001) mortality after fully adjusting. RCS suggested a linear association. No significant interaction was observed by subgroup analysis across all subgroups. The top-performing machine learning model attained an AUC of 0.868 during internal validation (MIMIC-IV). External validations yielded AUC values of 0.874 (eICU-CRD) and 0.763 (HIS). SHAP analysis revealed a correlation between decreased PWR and an elevated predicted risk of mortality.
CONCLUSION: PWR is an independent predictor of short- and long-term mortality in ICU patients with NSAH. Machine learning models incorporating PWR significantly improve risk stratification, thereby providing precious support for the early identification and personalized management of patients in the ICU.

Title: How consistent is the determination of the anaerobic threshold among members of the same cardiac rehabilitation team?
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Consistency in the anaerobic threshold (AT) determination is essential for cardiac rehabilitation teams comprising multiple professionals who conduct cardiopulmonary exercise tests (CPETs) and interpret their results. The effect of years of experience on interpreting CPET results, including the AT, has been examined. However, consistency in the AT determination among members of the same institution with experience beyond the training period has not been reported.
METHODS: We evaluated consistency in the AT determination among four members at a cardiovascular hospital (three full-time physical therapists and one part-time consultant physician) with 4 to 30 years of experience with CPETs. Another full-time physical therapist acted as the controller and did not participate in the AT reading. This retrospective study used 260 blinded and randomized CPET data files from 130 patients (130 data pairs comprising inpatient and outpatient data). All observers determined the AT twice using the modified V-slope method.
RESULTS: The mean AT values showed significant interobserver differences (p<0.001) driven by a slightly but significantly lower value determined by the consultant physician. No significant differences in the values determined by the three full-time staff members were observed. Despite interobserver differences during inpatient and outpatient phases, the longitudinal change in the AT did not differ significantly (p=0.58). The intrarater reliability of four observers was good [intraclass correlation coefficient (1,1) = 0.87-0.94], with limits of agreement of 103.6 to 185.0 mL/min. The inter-rater reliability was also good [intraclass coefficient (2,1) = 0.87], with limits of agreement of observer pairs of 139.2 to 220.5 mL/min. Reliability was not associated with years of experience.
CONCLUSIONS: Good consistency in the AT determination is achievable in a clinical setting. Adherence to a single standardized method across the team likely facilitates this consistency and provides a reliable objective measure for monitoring exercise tolerance.

Title: Interpretable machine learning models to predict venous thromboembolism in sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face a substantially elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet prediction tools tailored for this population are lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate interpretable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital VTE in septic patients with T2DM.
METHODS: A total of 648 sepsis patients with T2DM admitted to Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital between January 2020 and October 2024 were included in this retrospective cohort study, an internal validation cohort of 303 patients was retrospectively collected from Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital between November 2024 and December 2025, and an independent external validation cohort of 260 patients was retrospectively collected from Xi'an No. 3 Hospital (a separate tertiary care center) between November 2023 and December 2025. Six machine learning algorithms-Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest-were developed and compared. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm combined with forward sequential feature selection. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC), calibration (calibratin plots and Brier scores), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Model interpretability was enhanced using SHAP analysis.
RESULTS: Among the 648 internal patients, 115 (17.7%) developed VTE. The Boruta algorithm and forward sequential feature selection identified five key predictors: D-dimer, C-reactive protein (CRP), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), international normalized ratio (INR), and fibrin degradation products (FDP). Among the six algorithms, LightGBM achieved the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.9025 in the test set, 0.8048 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.8902 in the external validation cohort. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis confirmed positive net clinical benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis revealed that elevated D-dimer, CRP, INR, and FDP, together with shortened APTT, were the strongest drivers of VTE risk. Sensitivity analyses excluding D-dimer-driven cases, removing the D-dimer feature, and restricting to symptomatic VTE yielded consistent results (AUC range: 0.84-0.89).
CONCLUSIONS: The LightGBM model incorporating five readily available coagulation and inflammatory markers accurately predicts in-hospital VTE in sepsis patients with T2DM, with robust discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. SHAP-based interpretability enhances transparency and may facilitate personalized risk stratification and informed thromboprophylaxis decisions in this high-risk population.

Title: Multimodal evaluation and etiology-oriented management of chronic intracranial venous hypertension.
Abstract: Chronic intracranial venous hypertension (CIVHS) comprises a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by impaired cerebral venous outflow and symptoms related to elevated intracranial pressure. Although venous sinus stenting is increasingly used for venous sinus stenosis with elevated trans-stenotic pressure gradients, venous sinus stenosis is an imaging phenotype rather than a single diagnosis. We retrospectively reviewed 13 consecutive patients with CIVHS who underwent clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic evaluation, including conventional neuroimaging, MR or CT venography, digital subtraction angiography, venous manometry when indicated, and selective high-resolution MRI. All patients initially presented to ophthalmology and had papilledema. Patients were classified according to presumed mechanisms of venous outflow impairment, and treatment was tailored to the anatomical substrate, hemodynamic findings, and clinical context. Six etiological categories were identified: intrinsic transverse sinus stenosis, extrinsic transverse-sigmoid sinus compression, shunt dependency syndrome, jugular foramen stenosis related to chronic organized thrombus, JAK2 V617F mutation-positive essential thrombocythemia with suspected microvascular venous congestion, and dialysis catheter-related central venous stenosis. An additional chronic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis case was included as an illustrative secondary comparator but was not classified as idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Treatments included venous sinus stenting, shunt-related management, hematologic-directed therapy, anticoagulation, acetazolamide, weight control, and conservative management. Among the 13 cohort patients with available follow-up, symptoms improved or remained clinically stable; Case 14 was lost to follow-up. No stent failure was documented during short-term follow-up, but long-term surveillance data were unavailable. These findings support an etiology-oriented, multimodal approach to chronic intracranial venous hypertension.

Title: Association between lesion-specific fat attenuation index and high-risk plaque on coronary computed tomography angiography.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between lesion-specific fat attenuation index (FAI) derived from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and CCTA-defined high-risk plaque (HRP).
METHODS: A total of 560 patients undergoing CCTA for the first time who had at least one evaluable coronary atherosclerotic lesion were consecutively included. One target lesion was selected for each patient. Four CCTA-derived high-risk plaque features were assessed, including low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, spotty calcification, and the napkin-ring sign. Lesions exhibiting at least two of these features were classified as CCTA-defined HRP, and lesion-specific FAI was quantified from the pericoronary adipose tissue surrounding the target lesion and expressed in Hounsfield units (HU). Binary logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between lesion-specific FAI and CCTA-defined HRP. Restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to characterize the shape of the association, and subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Lesion-specific FAI was significantly higher in patients with CCTA-defined HRP than in those without HRP (-76.5 ± 4.8 HU vs. -81.0 ± 4.8 HU), with a mean difference of 4.47 HU [95% confidence interval (CI), 3.54-5.41 HU, P < 0.001] and a Cohen's d of 0.93. In the fully adjusted model, each 5-HU increase in lesion-specific FAI was associated with higher odds of CCTA-defined HRP [odds ratio (OR), 2.03; 95% CI, 1.52-2.69; P < 0.001]. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall association between lesion-specific FAI and CCTA-defined HRP (P for overall <0.001), with no significant evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.702). The association remained consistent across the examined subgroups, with no significant interactions, and the findings remained robust in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher lesion-specific FAI was independently associated with CCTA-defined HRP, with higher odds of HRP across increasing FAI values. The association remained consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Lesion-specific FAI may provide complementary information for characterizing CCTA-defined high-risk plaque and assessing the local perilesional environment. Further prospective studies with invasive imaging or longitudinal clinical outcomes are needed to determine its potential incremental value.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and early LDL-cholesterol target attainment after a first acute coronary syndrome: a real-world cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy, early attainment of the guideline-recommended LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) target after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains suboptimal. Baseline factors associated with early LDL-C target attainment remain incompletely characterized, particularly the role of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]. We aimed to assess early LDL-C target attainment after a first ACS and identify baseline factors associated with target attainment, with a particular focus on Lp(a).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive hospitalized adults with a first ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2025 and April 2026. The primary endpoint was attainment of the guideline-recommended LDL-C target at early follow-up, defined as LDL-C < 55 mg/dL and a ≥ 50% reduction from baseline. Associations between clinical variables and LDL-C target attainment were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Eighty-two patients were included; 70.7% were male and 37.2% had elevated Lp(a) levels. At a median follow-up of 5 weeks (IQR, 4-6), 31.7% attained the LDL-C target despite prescription of high-intensity statin therapy at discharge. In the multivariable model, low Lp(a) (OR 8.72; 95% CI 2.04-37.33), current smoking (OR 5.29; 95% CI 1.42-19.69), and ezetimibe use in addition to high-intensity statin therapy at discharge (OR 5.28; 95% CI 1.31-21.32) were associated with LDL-C target attainment.
CONCLUSIONS: Early LDL-C target attainment after a first ACS remained limited despite routine prescription of high-intensity statin therapy. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a lower likelihood of attaining the LDL-C target. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.

Title: Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair at Centers With and Without On-Site Cardiac Surgery: A Comparative Registry With a Shared Interventional Team.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence for M-TEER performed at centers with versus without on-site cardiac surgery is lacking. We compared early outcomes at two centers that shared the same interventional operator team but differed in the availability of on-site cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected registry data from 64 consecutive patients with severe (4+) MR treated at a center without on-site cardiac surgery (no-CCH, n = 21) and a center with on-site cardiac surgery (CCH, n = 43). The same interventional operator team performed every procedure. At the no-CCH center, surgical expertise was provided through a shared Heart Team and a formal emergency transfer pathway. The cohorts were treated in sequential calendar periods. Principal comparative endpoints were MVARC device and procedural success at 30 days. Exploratory non-inferiority analyses used margins of -12.5% and -10%.
RESULTS: MVARC technical success was 100% versus 97.7%. Device and procedural success were each 81.0% versus 72.1% (risk difference [RD] +8.9%, 95% CI -14.9 to +27.5; p = 0.547). Freedom from major MVARC serious adverse events was 95.2% versus 95.3%. Twelve of 16 device-success failures involved a mean transmitral gradient ≥ 5 mmHg. Surgical conversion and in-hospital death were 0% in both centers.
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary same-team comparison, 30-day MVARC device and procedural success rates were 81.0% at the no-CCH center and 72.1% at the CCH center. Confidence intervals were wide and non-inferiority was not established. These findings support prospective evaluation of network-based M-TEER programs with shared interventional expertise and formal surgical backup.

Title: Initial treatment strategies and outcomes across haemodynamic thresholds and risk stratification in incident systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a EUSTAR analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Real-world initial treatment strategies in SSc-PAH remain incompletely described. We aimed to characterise these strategies across haemodynamic thresholds and risk strata and evaluate outcome associations.
METHODS: We analysed treatment-naïve SSc-PAH patients in EUSTAR (2000-2021) fulfilling the 2022 haemodynamic definition. Initial therapy comprised treatment initiated within 4 months of RHC. As-treated (AT) analyses were primary and intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses supportive. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and 36-month PAH progression.
RESULTS: Among 301 patients, 198 (66%) initiated therapy and 170 maintained therapy for ≥3 months. Therapy was initiated in 31% with milder haemodynamic impairment (mPAP 21-24 mmHg and/or PVR 2-3 WU) versus 79% fulfilling the previous haemodynamic definition; combination therapy increased from 14% to 67% across low- to high-risk strata. Over a median 3.9 years, 125 (42%) died and 85/227 (37%) progressed. Adjusted ITT analyses showed no association with either outcome, whereas adjusted AT analyses showed lower mortality risk with sustained monotherapy and combination therapy (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.27-0.92 and HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.88, respectively) and lower PAH progression risk with sustained initial therapy (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.18-0.76). In the milder haemodynamic subgroup, the mortality estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise.
CONCLUSION: Initial treatment strategies reflected haemodynamic severity and baseline risk, while variation suggested potential implementation gaps. Sustained initial therapy was associated with lower risks of mortality and PAH progression. Contrasting ITT and AT estimates highlight challenges in observational treatment-outcome comparisons. Findings in the milder haemodynamic subgroup support dedicated prospective studies.

Title: Endovascular aortic arch repair: a review of current technologies, clinical outcomes, and future directions.
Abstract: Endovascular treatment of the aortic arch (EndoArch) has emerged as an increasingly important therapeutic option for the management of complex aortic arch disease, driven by continuous advances in device technology, imaging, procedural planning, and operator experience. Although conventional open arch replacement remains the reference treatment for many patients, endovascular approaches have considerably expanded therapeutic options for individuals considered at high surgical risk. However, the anatomical complexity of the aortic arch, the need to preserve supra-aortic trunk perfusion, and the risk of neurological complications continue to make these procedures technically demanding. This review provides an updated overview of contemporary EndoArch, with a particular focus on currently available endovascular and hybrid strategies, clinical outcomes, procedure-related complications, and future perspectives. Available evidence demonstrates encouraging technical success and acceptable early and mid-term results in carefully selected patients treated at experienced aortic centers, although most data derive from retrospective observational studies and long-term durability has yet to be established. Careful patient selection, meticulous procedural planning, and a multidisciplinary approach remain fundamental to achieving optimal outcomes. Ongoing technological developments, including improvements in endograft design, procedural standardization, advanced imaging, and the progressive extension of endovascular treatment to more proximal aortic segments, are expected to further broaden the applicability of EndoArch. Continued clinical experience and longer-term follow-up will be essential to better define the role of these techniques in contemporary management of aortic arch disease.

Title: Prognostic value of liver scoring systems in predicting early outcomes after pericardiectomy: a single-center retrospective study.
Journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
Abstract: Pericardiectomy for constrictive pericarditis remains a high-risk operation, and early outcomes are inadequately predicted by conventional cardiac risk models despite the high prevalence of chronic hepatic congestion in this population. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of 104 consecutive patients undergoing isolated pericardiectomy between 2010 and 2024 to determine whether established hepatic scoring systems [Child-Pugh, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease-Sodium (MELD-Na)] predict early mortality and major postoperative morbidity. Preoperative clinical and biochemical variables were used to derive the hepatic scores. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; the secondary endpoint was new postoperative renal-replacement therapy. Thirty-day mortality was 4.8% (5/104). Patients were classified as Child-Pugh A in 66 (63.5%), B in 35 (33.7%), and C in 3 (2.9%), with corresponding mortalities of 1.5%, 2.9%, and 100% (p<0.01 for trend). Discrimination for 30-day mortality was strong for Child-Pugh [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.00], MELD (0.85, 0.60-0.98), and MELD-Na (0.83, 0.55-0.97), whereas EuroSCORE II showed no meaningful predictive ability (AUC≈0.51). Hepatic dysfunction quantified by Child-Pugh and MELD-based scores is a strong predictor of early mortality after pericardiectomy and outperforms conventional cardiac risk models in this cohort. Incorporation of structured hepatic assessment into preoperative risk stratification may improve perioperative planning and patient counseling; however, the small number of Child-Pugh C patients and the retrospective single-center design necessitate validation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: Association of the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio with kidney stone status: cross-sectional and machine-learning analyses.
Abstract: This study investigated the association between triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (TG/HDL-C) and kidney stone status and evaluated its contribution to multivariable classification models. A total of 1,174 patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University were included, with kidney stone status confirmed by urological imaging. Multivariable analyses were used to assess the association between TG/HDL-C and kidney stone status. Supplementary population-based analyses were conducted using weighted data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Seven machine-learning models were developed and internally evaluated within the clinical cohort, and SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model outputs. In the clinical cohort, a higher TG/HDL-C ratio was associated with greater odds of kidney stone status after multivariable adjustment (OR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.73-2.70). The association was generally consistent across subgroups defined by age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, and diabetes, with no significant interactions observed. A directionally similar association was identified in the weighted NHANES analysis (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.01-1.07). Among the evaluated machine-learning models, the random forest model achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the internal validation set (AUROC, 0.818; 95% CI, 0.775-0.859). SHAP analysis identified the TG/HDL-C ratio as an important contributor to model classification. These findings indicate that the TG/HDL-C ratio is an accessible metabolic marker associated with kidney stone status. However, the observational design precludes causal inference, and prospective studies with external model validation are warranted.

Title: Ventriculostomy-associated infection rates and routine EVD replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is associated with a significant risk of ventriculostomy-associated infection (VAI), which can lead to severe complications. The relationship between catheterization duration, routine catheter exchange, and infection risk remains debated. This meta-analysis aimed to estimate the contemporary pooled VAI rate and evaluate the effect of catheter type and management strategy on infection risk.
METHODS: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42025632997) systematic review and meta-analysis. MEDLINE, Cochrane, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched through February 2024. Studies reporting EVD infection counts with catheter-days were included. Random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) meta-analysis pooled log-transformed infection rates. Subgroup analyses compared impregnated versus plain catheters and pre-/post-2010 era. Two RCTs were qualitatively synthesized. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane RoB2.
RESULTS: Nineteen cohort studies and two RCTs were included. Critically, neither RCT demonstrated benefit from routine replacement (Wong 2002: RR = 1.80, 95% CI 0.33-9.81, p = 0.50; Keong 2012: RR = 0.58, 95% CI 0.33-0.99, favouring silver-impregnated catheters over standard catheters rather than supporting exchange). All 19 observational cohort studies confirmed that routine fixed-interval EVD replacement was not practiced at any included institution, precluding direct observational comparison. Eight cohort studies contributed 167 infections across 22,839 catheter-days to quantitative synthesis. The pooled VAI rate was 7.87 per 1,000 catheter-days (95% CI 4.67-13.25; I2=91%, τ2=0.506). The 95% prediction interval was 1.78-34.85/1,000 catheter-days, reflecting wide variation across settings. Antimicrobial-impregnated catheters had a pooled rate of 4.85 versus 17.03/1,000 catheter-days for plain catheters.
CONCLUSION: Routine fixed-interval EVD replacement is not supported by current evidence, independently confirming IDSA 2017 Recommendation 78. Antimicrobial-impregnated catheters and infection prevention bundles appear more effective at reducing VAI rates than scheduled catheter exchange alone. Further adequately powered RCTs are needed and research should standardize reporting of institutional replacement practices and evaluate broader-spectrum antimicrobial catheter technologies targeting both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms.

Title: Acute kidney disease after acute kidney injury: incidence, risk factors, and association with de novo chronic kidney disease.
Abstract: Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) is defined as acute kidney injury (AKI) persisting for 7 to 90 days and represents a window for interventions to improve renal outcomes. However, data on AKD remain underexplored. This retrospective cohort study at Tongji Hospital, China, included 23,868 adult patients who survived at least one AKI episode between January 2015 and April 2024. Using electronic medical record data, we aimed to quantify the incidence of AKD among AKI survivors, identify independent risk factors, and evaluate the association between AKD and de novo chronic kidney disease (CKD). Among the cohort, 10,884 patients (45.6%) progressed to AKD. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that advanced age, preexisting hypertension, heart failure, cirrhosis, recent diuretic use, hepatorenal syndrome, higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate, higher AKI stage, and dialysis-requiring AKI were independent risk factors for AKD. Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis accounting for acute-phase mortality confirmed that higher AKI severity was independently associated with AKD progression. In a subcohort of 6597 patients without preexisting CKD who had at least one year of follow-up, 19.8% developed de novo CKD. Cox proportional hazards analysis demonstrated that patients with AKD had a significantly increased risk of de novo CKD compared to those without AKD (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.70-2.17). These findings highlight the high proportion of AKD among patients with AKI, and emphasize the importance of early detection and targeted management for high-risk groups. It is critical to strengthen post-discharge renal function monitoring and intervention strategies for AKI patients to improve long-term renal outcomes.

Title: Refractory Angina Pectoris: Medical and Interventional Treatment Options.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is among the more common cardiovascular diseases, affecting 4.7 million people in Germany alone. As many as 20% of patients with CHD still suffer from angina pectoris despite appropriate antianginal therapy and revascularization. Refractory angina pectoris reduces quality of life and increases mortality. In this review, we describe therapeutic strategies and the clinical evidence underlying them.
METHODS: This review is based on publications up to December 2025 retrieved through a selective search in Medline/PubMed for RCTs, before-and-after studies, and guidelines on the treatment of refractory angina pectoris.
RESULTS: The treatment of refractory angina pectoris begins with reducing risk factors, optimizing pharmacotherapy, and considering revascularization for functionally significant coronary stenosis. If these treatment options have been exhausted, the implantation of a sinus reducer may be considered, as recommended in the European guidelines (recommendation grade IIb). The evidence for this is derived from randomized trials and from multiple registry and observational studies. In the sham-controlled COSIRA trial, which involved 104 patients, an improvement in angina symptoms by at least two classes on the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) grading scale was observed in 35% of patients six months after implantation, compared with 15% in the control group. The multicenter ORBITA-COSMIC trial, which involved 51 patients, also yielded a reduction in daily angina pectoris compared with the control group (OR 1.40; 95% CI: [1.08; 1.83]). Potential complications include migration, embolization of the reducer, and coronary sinus perforation or dissection in 1-2% of patients. These events are only rarely clinically significant.
CONCLUSION: The sinus reducer may improve symptoms in selected patients, but the reported periprocedural complications and limited evidence to date on long-term outcomes should enter into the decision whether to provide this treatment to the individual patient.

Title: Sex-Based Differences in Chronic Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based disparities in patient enrollment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyze sex-based enrollment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time.
METHODS: RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrollment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (HR or RR) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrollment was 27.0% (95%CI: 22.0% to 32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95%CI: 21.0% to 29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, p < 0.001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89-1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95%CI 0.68-0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: p = 0.44; RR: p = 0.95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84-0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95%CI 0.90-1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95%CI 0.50-0.93).
CONCLUSION: Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

Title: Open-Irrigated Versus Non-Irrigated Catheters in SVT Ablation: Substrate-Specific Outcomes in AVRT and AVNRT.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Open-irrigated catheters (OIC) provide improved cooling, deeper lesion formation, and enhanced safety during radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). However, comparative evidence regarding substrate-specific outcomes with OIC versus non-irrigated catheters (NIC) for supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) remains limited. This study compared acute ablation success (AAS) and recurrence after first-time RFCA using OIC versus NIC, with particular emphasis on differential outcomes in atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT) and atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of consecutive patients undergoing first-time RFCA for AVNRT or AVRT between 2017 and 2023 was analyzed. Patients were categorized by catheter type (OIC vs. NIC). Primary outcomes were AAS and SVT recurrence during 24-month follow-up. Multivariate logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used for adjusted analyses. Subgroup analyses were performed for AVNRT and AVRT.
RESULTS: Among 302 procedures, OIC were used in 113 (37.4%). Overall AAS was achieved in 85.4% of cases (92.0% OIC vs. 81.5% NIC; p = 0.012). Recurrence occurred in 17.9% (7.1% OIC vs. 24.3% NIC; p < 0.001). In multivariable analyses, OIC use was independently associated with higher AAS (adjusted RR 1.12; 95% CI 1.05-1.20; p = 0.001) and lower recurrence (adjusted HR 0.24; 95% CI 0.12-0.52; p < 0.001). In the AVRT subgroup, OIC use was associated with higher AAS (89.9% vs. 76.6%; p = 0.014) and lower recurrence (adjusted HR 0.25; 95% CI 0.11-0.57; p < 0.001), whereas no significant differences were observed in AVNRT.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, OIC use was associated with higher AAS and lower recurrence, with the favorable association primarily observed in AVRT rather than AVNRT. These findings support further evaluation of substrate-specific catheter selection, particularly for accessory pathway ablation.

Title: EXPRESS: Diagnostic and prognostic value of on-site CT-derived fractional flow reserve in intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
Journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) in cerebrovascular disease remains undefined. This study validated the diagnostic and prognostic value of an on-site CT-FFR in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) patients.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled sICAS patients with 30 - 99% stenosis confirmed by CTA, divided into two substudies. The diagnostic performance study included 259 patients undergoing CTA and CT perfusion (CTP) or four-dimensional CTA (CTP as reference standard). In prognosis study, 452 patients with at least 1-year follow-up were included. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was used to measure CT-FFR. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and predictive value by Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: The diagnostic performance of CT-FFR was significantly higher than diameter stenosis (DS) on both per-patient (P = 0.009) and per-lesion (P = 0.004) basis. And the cut-off value of CT-FFR diagnosing cerebral hypoperfusion was 0.80. 15.0% (68 / 452) patients experienced recurrent ischemic events during the median 24 (17-33) months follow-up. CT-FFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond traditional cardiovascular risks plus DS (AUC = 0.797 vs 0.716, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This on-site CT-FFR can serve as a valuable tool for diagnosis and risk stratification in sICAS patients.

Title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.
AIMS: We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.
RESULTS: The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Tranexamic Acid in Endoscopic Surgery for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A TURP-Dominated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhaging continues to be a significant issue in endoscopic procedures for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Tranexamic acid (TXA) has garnered heightened scrutiny for its ability to mitigate bleeding-associated problems during transurethral prostate procedures. We performed a comprehensive meta-analysis to assess the effectiveness and safety of TXA in individuals having endoscopic procedures for BPH, acknowledging that the existing data primarily originated from transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP).
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ICTRP were examined from the beginning of their databases until April 2026. Pooled mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) together with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were computed utilizing RevMan 5.4. Sensitivity analyses and assessment of publication bias were performed using R version 4.4.2.
RESULTS: Fifteen randomized controlled studies with 1,310 people were qualified. Compared to the control group, TXA significantly reduced operational time (MD = -6.49 minutes, 95% CI: -10.79 to -2.20) and intraoperative blood loss (MD = -66.68 mL, 95% CI: -123.84 to -9.51). TXA also led to significantly less hemoglobin loss at 24 hours (MD = -0.58 g/dL, 95% CI: -0.88 to -0.29) and decreased irrigation fluid volume (MD = -0.45 L, 95% CI: -0.80 to -0.10). However, there were no significant differences between groups in duration of continuous bladder irrigation, catheterization time, length of stay, weight of resected adenoma, blood transfusion requirements, incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or quality of endoscopic.
CONCLUSIONS: TXA correlated with less intraoperative hemorrhage, decreased hemoglobin depletion after 24 hours, reduced irrigation fluid usage, and shortened surgical duration in endoscopic procedures for BPH. These results should be regarded primarily as evidence from TURP, demonstrating consistent effects across both monopolar and bipolar subgroups. Evidence outside TURP was limited to a single holmium laser enucleation of prostate RCT, which contributed data only to operative time among the statistically significant outcomes. Reported DVT were rare, and the available evidence remains underpowered to determine the thromboembolic safety profile of TXA. Additional RCTs are necessary to elucidate the function of TXA in various surgical methodologies and among patients with an elevated risk of hemorrhage. The PROSPERO Registration: The study was registered on https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ (registration number: CRD420251044211; registration link: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251044211).

Title: Ultrasound-Based Prediction of Skin-to-Renal Pelvis Distance for Percutaneous Renal Access.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies examining anatomical changes in the prone position during endourological procedures lack predictive formulas for estimating the renal pelvis-to-skin distance (KSD). Furthermore, existing equations for renal depth-an important parameter for accurate glomerular filtration rate (GFR) assessment-are based on supine measurements. This study aimed to develop predictive formulas for estimating renal depth in the prone position for patients undergoing percutaneous renal access.
METHODS: A total of 86 healthy volunteers (46 men, 40 women) were enrolled in a prospective study conducted at the 2nd Department of Urology, Papageorgiou General Hospital between June and September 2020. Participants completed a questionnaire on medical history, demographic, and somatometric characteristics. Renal KSD was measured ultrasonographically in the prone position using a convex probe placed parallel and 1 cm below the 12th rib, with the posterior axillary line as a landmark. The biopsy line targeted the midpoint of the renal pelvis. Distances were analyzed in relation to clinical and anthropometric variables, and predictive equations were generated for each kidney.
RESULTS: The following equations were derived: left kidney: distance = 1.5 + 0.272 × body mass index (BMI) - 0.452 × gender; right kidney: distance = 1.619 + 0.259 × BMI - 0.457 × gender (BMI: gender coded as 0 = male, 1 = female). Mean renal depth was 7.81 cm for the right kidney and 8.23 ± 1.47 cm for the left. Distances were significantly greater in men (p = 0.004 right; p = 0.005 left). A strong positive correlation was observed between right and left kidney depths (r = 0.859, p < 0.001), as well as with body weight and waist circumference. In men, greater right kidney depth was associated with hypertension, low high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and metabolic syndrome (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: These formulas provide a simple and reliable method for estimating renal depth in the prone position, potentially improving procedural accuracy and patient safety during percutaneous renal access.

Title: 4HER-Embedding a Post-Pregnancy Cardiometabolic Health Clinic Into Routine Care.
Journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women who experience gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) face a significantly elevated risk of developing chronic diseases, including Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease (CVD). The postpartum period of 3-6 months represents a unique opportunity for targeted risk reduction; yet engagement with follow-up care is often low due to systemic and personal barriers.
AIM: This study aimed to adapt and implement a dedicated women-focused, cardio-metabolic risk reduction clinic at an Australian tertiary maternity hospital, modelled on the successful Canadian MotHERS program. We also aimed to describe the initial implementation and baseline characteristics of the attending high-risk cohort.
METHODS: Using a Hybrid Type 2 design to test the clinical effectiveness and evaluate implementation processes, eligible women with GDM or HDP from the Mater Mothers' Hospitals (MMH) were invited for post-pregnancy visits (3 and 9 months) that focused on risk screening and stratification and systematic connection to primary care. We report on their attendance and baseline clinical and lifestyle characteristics.
RESULTS: The clinic achieved a high initial reach, with 126 of 178 eligible women (70.8%) attending. The cohort demonstrated a high-risk profile; mean BMI was 29.4 (6.3) kg/m2, mean waist circumference was 99.7 (14.8) cm, and over 50% of the cohort had a 'high' lifetime cardiovascular risk score. Lifestyle and health screen data also revealed significant modifiable risks CONCLUSION: The implementation of the 4HER clinic successfully engaged a substantial proportion of women with medically complicated pregnancies who demonstrate an elevated baseline burden of cardio-metabolic risk.

Title: Machine learning predictors of post-radiotherapy cardiotoxicity in a Latin American breast cancer cohort: Clinical risk factors outperform cardiac dosimetry.
Journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most evidence on post-radiotherapy cardiotoxicity (CDT) derives from Global North cohorts, and the relative contribution of baseline clinical risk versus cardiac dosimetry remains poorly characterized in Latin American populations.
PURPOSE: To examine, in a Chilean breast cancer cohort, whether baseline clinical risk factors or cardiac dose-volume metrics better predict post-RT cardiac events, using supervised and unsupervised learning.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 42 breast cancer patients treated with thoracic radiotherapy (RT, median heart dose 2.6 Gy; median follow-up 84.4 months). CDT was defined per CTCAE v5.0 ( ≥ Grade 1), excluding Grade 1 events coded under the non-specific term "Cardiac disorders - Other, specify", which on review were incidental imaging findings. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters from seven cardiac substructures were extracted. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for prediction, principal component analysis (PCA) and kernel PCA for exploratory clustering, and bootstrap 0.632+ for optimism correction. The 2023 American Heart Association (AHA) PREVENT score was evaluated post hoc.
RESULTS: Ten patients (23.8%) developed CDT and 16 (38.1%) experienced cardiovascular events. No DVH differences were found between CDT+ and CDT- groups across any cardiac structure (all p > 0.05  ), although the design is powered only for large effects. By contrast, IMRT delivered significantly higher cardiac doses than 3D-CRT across multiple substructures, without a differential CDT rate. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease was the strongest predictor (crude OR = 6.50, p = 0.020  ; adjusted OR = 2.08, 95% CI 1.03-4.16, p = 0.040  ). The median time to the first CTCAE-graded event was 48.4 months. The clinical-only model reached an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.783 versus 0.604 for dosimetry alone; the combined model corrected to 0.649 (95% CI 0.204-0.933). The AHA PREVENT score showed no significant risk gradient (trend p = 0.203  ) but was markedly less susceptible to overfitting than DVH-only models (optimism 0.089 vs. 0.194).
CONCLUSIONS: In this low-cardiac-dose cohort, baseline clinical variables outperformed cardiac dose-volume metrics in predicting post-RT cardiac events, although the design was not powered to exclude a dose-effect relationship at these exposures. Registry-based baseline risk assessment is therefore the more robust starting point in this setting, and IMRT breast RT planning warrants multi-substructure cardiac dosimetry monitoring.

Title: Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Ethanol Ablation for Benign Insulinoma: A Single-Centre Experience and Literature Review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Insulinoma is a predominantly benign pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour that is traditionally managed surgically. However, surgical invasiveness and anaesthesia-related risks limit its applicability in selected patients. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided ethanol ablation has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and feasibility of EUS-guided ethanol ablation for benign insulinoma.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 17 patients with insulinoma who underwent EUS-guided ethanol ablation, predominantly as a primary treatment. All procedures were performed by experienced gastroenterologists using 95% absolute ethanol.
RESULTS: The study cohort had a mean age of 58.47 ± 12.29 years and a mean disease duration of 34.43 months (range, 0.36-84.0). Clinical success was achieved in 16 patients (94.1%). One patient with an initial suboptimal response successfully underwent a repeat ablation after 8 months. Over a median follow-up period of 46.1 months (range, 6.6-97.8), one patient was lost to follow-up. Disease recurrence was observed in four patients, resulting in a recurrence rate of 25% (4/16) among those with available follow-up data. Three recurrent cases underwent repeat ablation, all achieving symptomatic resolution. A total of 22 ablation procedures were performed. Adverse events were documented in 36.4% (8/22) of procedures, with the majority being mild (31.8%, 7/22) and one severe adverse event (4.5%, 1/22).
CONCLUSIONS: EUS-guided ethanol ablation is an effective and well-tolerated treatment for benign insulinoma. It represents a viable minimally invasive alternative to surgery and remains effective for managing recurrence or initial treatment failure without compromising subsequent surgical options.

Title: Elevated serum soluble PD-L1 is associated with adverse outcomes after autologous stem cell transplantation in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma patients.
Abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a plasma-cell malignancy in which immune-evasion mechanisms may contribute to disease progression. Soluble programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) has been associated with adverse outcomes in MM, but its prognostic significance before and after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) remains incompletely defined. To evaluate serum PD-L1 concentrations before and six months after ASCT and to assess their associations with clinical outcomes, including overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), relapse, and graft failure. This prospective observational study included 40 transplant-eligible patients with MM treated at the Ain Shams University Bone Marrow Center. Serum PD-L1 was measured by ELISA before ASCT and six months after transplantation. Clinical outcomes were assessed during follow-up through 180 days, and associations with survival and adverse outcomes were evaluated using correlation analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Pre- and post-transplant PD-L1 levels were negatively correlated with OS (pre: r = -0.44, p = 0.004; post: r = -0.48, p = 0.002). Patients with relapse had higher pre- and post-transplant PD-L1 levels than those without relapse (119.2 vs. 74.6 pg/mL, p = 0.01; and 184.4 vs. 63.4 pg/mL, p = 0.01, respectively). Post-transplant PD-L1 was higher in patients with graft failure than in those without graft failure (178.7 vs. 87.5 pg/mL, p = 0.008). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed poorer OS and DFS among patients with higher PD-L1 according to the study cutoffs. In conclusion, higher serum PD-L1 levels before and after ASCT were associated with adverse clinical outcomes in this cohort. Given the small sample size, limited follow-up, single-center design, and multiple unadjusted comparisons, these findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger studies.

Title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for intensive care unit admission and mortality in rapid response team-activated ward patients: a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in South Korea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Factors driving intensive care unit (ICU) transfer decisions and mortality after rapid response team (RRT) activation remain unclear. We identified independent predictors of ICU admission, 28-day mortality, and in-hospital mortality in RRT-activated ward patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults with first RRT activation from September 2023 to August 2025 at a Korean tertiary hospital (n=549). Multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination was used.
RESULTS: Of 549 patients, 191 (34.8%) were transferred to the ICU. ICU admission was independently predicted by procalcitonin >0.5 ng/ml (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.833; P=0.021) and lower hemoglobin (aOR, 0.808 per g/dl; P=0.040), whereas solid tumor was associated with lower transfer likelihood (aOR, 0.142; P<0.001). Mortality did not differ significantly between ICU and ward groups at 28 days (27.7% vs. 27.7%, P=0.937) or during hospitalization (46.1% vs. 40.2%, P=0.162). Declining peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂)/fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO₂) ratio, rising lactate, and hyperkalemia predicted both mortality outcomes. Lower platelet count uniquely predicted 28-day mortality, whereas solid tumor, chronic kidney disease, and deep learning-based continuous cardiac arrest risk score (DeepCARS) additionally predicted in-hospital mortality. ICU admission itself was not independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: ICU transfer after RRT activation appears to reflect acute reversibility, clinical trajectory, and possible at/after-activation goals-of-care processes rather than severity alone. Mortality was more closely associated with oxygenation failure, hypoperfusion, and electrolyte instability than with disposition.

Title: A Machine Learning Model Based on Ultrasound and Serological Markers for Predicting Postoperative Stenosis of Rex Shunt Procedure in Children With Extrahepatic Portal Venous Obstruction.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the value of combining ultrasound parameters with serological markers for predicting postoperative Rex shunt stenosis in children with extrahepatic portal venous obstruction (EHPVO).
METHODS: The training cohort and temporal validation cohort consisted of 114 and 38 children with EHPVO after Rex shunt procedure, respectively. The study variables included clinical characteristics, ultrasound parameters, and serological markers. Five machine learning models were developed to predict postoperative stenosis after the Rex shunt procedure at different follow-up periods, with performance evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
RESULTS: In the temporal validation cohort, the optimal Logistic regression model integrating ultrasound parameters and serological markers achieved AUROCs of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.38-0.84) at 1 month, 0.67 (95% CI: 0.45-0.90) at 3 months, and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.67-0.98) at 6 months for predicting stenosis.
CONCLUSIONS: A model combining serological markers and ultrasound parameters serves as a promising exploratory prototype for predicting Rex shunt stenosis in children with EHPVO, pending further independent multicenter validation.

Title: Pulsed Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation: Esophageal Lesions and Suspected Gastroparesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal mucosal injury and gastroparesis are clinically important complications of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal modality that may spare these complications due to its myocardial tissue selectivity.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to compare the incidence of endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) and suspected gastroparesis between RFA and PFA as the primary endpoints. Secondary endpoints included perioperative complications, procedural parameters, and 365-day clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Between July 2023 and July 2025, patients undergoing a first-time AF ablation with RFA or PFA were enrolled. RFA was performed using either a QDOT MICRO catheter (Biosense Webster, Inc., Irvine, CA, USA) or a TactiFlex Ablation Catheter, Sensor Enabled (Abbott, Abbott Park, IL, USA), while PFA was performed using the FARAPULSE system or the PulseSelect system. All patients underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy on the day after ablation. An EDEL was defined as esophageal erythema, erosion, ulcer, or atrio-esophageal fistula. Suspected gastroparesis was defined as gastric food residue after > 12 h of overnight fasting. Clinical follow-up was performed with 12-lead or Holter electrocardiography.
RESULTS: A total of 84 patients were included (RFA: n = 43; PFA: n = 41). Esophageal erosion was observed in 2 patients in the RFA group (4.7%) and in none in the PFA group (p = 0.49). Suspected gastroparesis occurred in 15 patients treated with RFA (34.9%) and in none treated with PFA (P<0.001). All patients were asymptomatic during endoscopy. No other procedural complications were observed in either group. The total procedure time was significantly shorter with PFA (158.5 ± 40.8 vs. 193.8 ± 38.3 min, p < 0.001), while the fluoroscopy time was longer. At 365 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence rates were comparable between the two groups (p = 0.47).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center cohort, PFA was associated with a significantly lower incidence of suspected gastroparesis than RFA, and no EDELs were observed in the PFA group. PFA may reduce gastrointestinal injury associated with AF ablation. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their clinical significance.

Title: Oral Health and High-Complexity Networks: A Functional Interdependence Analysis via Health Information Systems.
Abstract:
AIM: This study analysed the integration levels and co-assistance patterns of the dentistry service within a high-complexity hospital in Paraguay, under the framework of Integrated Health Service Delivery Networks (IHSDN).
METHODS: Using a retrospective observational design, Big Data from the Hospital Information System (HIS) were processed between March and August 2025.
