Title: Identification of symptomatic carotid atherosclerotic plaques using dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography-derived perivascular adipose tissue parameters and plaque morphology.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish and validate a multidimensional model for identifying symptomatic carotid plaques based on the combination of plaque morphological characteristics and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) parameters obtained from dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography (DLCT).
METHODS: This single-center study included 256 patients with carotid atherosclerosis. Patients were divided into symptomatic and asymptomatic groups based on the presence or absence of transient ischemic attack or ipsilateral ischemic stroke within 2 weeks before DLCT. The study comprised a retrospective training cohort (n = 133), a retrospective internal validation cohort (n = 58), and a prospectively enrolled independent temporal test cohort (n = 65). Conventional plaque characteristics and multiple PVAT parameters were compared between the two groups. Imaging variables independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques were identified using multivariable logistic regression and incorporated into classification models.
RESULTS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and the effective atomic number (Zeff) of PVAT were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Model 2 incorporated all three parameters demonstrating strong discriminatory performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.907, 0.825, and 0.848 in the training, validation, and test sets, respectively. Incorporation of PVAT Zeff improved the discriminative performance and reclassification beyond conventional stenosis and plaque-burden assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and PVAT Zeff were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Adding PVAT Zeff to conventional plaque characteristics improved model discrimination and provided complementary information for the characterization of symptomatic lesions.

Title: Signs of Life and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Multicenter Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of individual signs of life (SOLs) remains unclear in patients experiencing traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (t-OHCA).
OBJECTIVES: To describe clinical outcomes among patients with t-OHCA by the presence of each SOL at the scene.
METHODS: Data from the SOS-KANTO 2017 study, a multicenter prospective registry of OHCA cases treated between 2019 and 2021, were retrospectively analyzed. Adult patients diagnosed with t-OHCA were included, excluding those with a palpable pulse upon emergency medical service (EMS) arrival. Patients were categorized into eight subgroups based on the presence of three SOLs at the scene-the pupillary light reflex, spontaneous respiration, and cardiac electrical activity - and descriptive analyses were performed. The primary outcome was survival beyond the emergency department (ED).
RESULTS: Of the 462 patients included in the analysis, two (0.4%) exhibited all three SOLs, and 18 (3.9%) exhibited two SOLs; in the latter group, two demonstrated cardiac activity and a pupillary reflex, and 16 had cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration. Among the 124 patients (26.8%) with only one SOL, 117 had cardiac activity, three showed a pupillary reflex, and four exhibited spontaneous respiration. No SOLs were observed in 318 patients (68.8%). Overall, 22 patients (4.8%) survived beyond the ED. The highest survival rate was observed in the subgroup with both cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration (4/16; 25%), followed by the subgroup with cardiac activity alone (10/117; 8.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among the t-OHCA patients, survival beyond the ED was observed more frequently in those with cardiac electrical activity at the scene.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
Abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

Title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

Title: Impact of HIV on Perioperative Organ Injury and Surgical Outcomes in 41 Million Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While antiretroviral therapy has improved surgical safety for people living with HIV, comprehensive data on perioperative organ injury and its impact on patient safety remain limited. This study aimed to compare the incidence of perioperative organ injury, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, and hospitalization costs between people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals undergoing surgery in the United States.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021. The population-based sample included adult patients (age >18 years) identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. Of 41,622,004 eligible surgical admissions, 2,088,307 (5.0%) were people living with HIV and 39,533,697 were HIV-negative. Primary outcomes were perioperative organ injury incidence and associated mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay and total hospital charges. Adjusted models accounted for baseline characteristics and surgical complexity.
RESULTS: Among the 41,622,004 surgical admissions, people living with HIV were found to be older and carried a significantly higher comorbidity burden, with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 8 compared to 1 in the HIV-negative group. Perioperative organ injury occurred in 1,348,363 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (64.6%) compared with 7,867,547 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (19.9%). Acute myocardial infarction (33.5%) and acute kidney injury (22.0%) were the most common injuries among people living with HIV. In-hospital mortality occurred in 66,935 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (3.2%) compared with 872,170 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (2.2%). Hospital length of stay and hospital charges were also significantly higher. Adjusted analyses demonstrated that HIV status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-1.78), longer hospital length of stay (β = 2.73 days; 95% CI, 2.56-2.90), a decreased likelihood of home discharge (hazard ratio [HR], 0.73; 95% CI, 0.72-0.73), and increased hospitalization costs (β = $18,423; 95% CI, 16,712-20,134). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that elevated perioperative risk persisted among patients with asymptomatic HIV infection, although the greatest risk was observed among patients with symptomatic HIV disease/AIDS.
CONCLUSIONS: People living with HIV incur a significantly higher risk of perioperative organ injury and worse surgical outcomes despite advances in antiretroviral therapy. HIV status was independently associated with adverse perioperative outcomes in adjusted models, supporting its inclusion as a risk stratification variable in surgical planning. Future research should incorporate immunologic markers, such as CD4 count and viral load, to further refine perioperative risk prediction and optimize outcomes for this population.

Title: Evaluating the Role of Lower Extremity Elastic Bandage in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower extremity compression therapy has been proposed as an adjunct to mitigate diuretic resistance during acute decompensation of heart failure (ADHF). We evaluated the effect of lower leg compression with elastic bandages on diuretic efficiency in patients with diuretic-resistant ADHF.
METHODS: Historical cohort study enrolling adult cardiac ICU admissions with ADHF who used elastic bandages (EB) at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota from 2007 to 2017. The diuretic efficiency before and after applying EB was the primary outcome.
RESULTS: A total of 176 patients with heart failure who received elastic bandages were included. The in-hospital mortality rate, the median hospital length of stay, and 30-day hospital readmission were 9.7%, 11.4 days (IQR 7.1-19.0), and 11%, respectively. When EB was applied, the average daily loop diuretic dosage was decreased by a mean difference of 1.19 mg per 40 mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: 0.22 to 2.2; p = 0.016). The average post-EB diuretic efficiency was 1,355 mL (IQR 1,119, 1,590) per 40-mg furosemide, which was significantly higher than before EB application, with a mean difference of 340 mL per 40-mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: -554, -125; p = 0.002). A higher diuretic efficiency led to lower diuretic doses. Average daily urine output before and after EB application was not different (2,642 pre-EB vs. 2,792 post-EB mL/day; 95% CI: -455 to 154; p = 0.33).
CONCLUSION: EB use enhances diuretic efficacy during ADHF. Further studies are needed to determine the potential clinical benefits and risks of applying EB compression treatment in ADHF.

Title: Association of Neutrophil-To-Lymphocyte Ratio and Atherogenic Index of Plasma With Angiographically Confirmed Coronary Artery Disease.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: BackgroundThe neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) have been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD). We investigated their associations with angiographically confirmed CAD and lesion severity.MethodsThis retrospective study included 2,933 patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD at Wuhan Third Hospital. CAD was defined as ≥50% luminal stenosis in at least one major coronary artery or branch. Lesion severity was assessed using the Gensini score. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.ResultsAmong 2,933 patients, 1,615 had CAD and 1,318 had no significant stenosis. NLR and AIP were higher in patients with CAD and increased across Gensini score categories (all P<0.05). After adjustment, AIP remained independently associated with CAD (OR=1.557, P=0.042), whereas NLR did not (OR=1.019, P=0.581). AIP alone showed limited discrimination (AUC=0.537). A multivariable model including age, blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, and AIP showed an AUC of 0.779. Adding AIP did not significantly improve AUC (DeLong P=0.153) or NRI (0.071, P=0.106), although IDI improvement was significant (0.002, P<0.05).ConclusionsIn patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD, NLR and AIP were associated with CAD and angiographic disease burden. AIP remained independently associated with CAD, whereas NLR did not. However, AIP showed limited discrimination and no clear incremental improvement beyond conventional variables. These findings do not support population screening or routine clinical implementation.

Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Significant Fibrosis in Steatotic Liver Disease: A Model Development Study.
Journal: Online journal of public health informatics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent and noninvasive identification of patients with significant fibrosis remains a clinical challenge.
OBJECTIVE: We conducted an exploratory evaluation of explainable machine-learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a U.S. population-based cohort of adults with SLD, with particular attention to sensitivity, false-negative risk, and the limitations of using AUROC alone to assess screening suitability.
METHODS: We evaluated explainable machine-learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a U.S. population-based dataset. Forty-three routinely available clinical, demographic, anthropometric, laboratory, and lifestyle variables were included. After preprocessing and imputation, data were split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) addressed class imbalance in the training set. Logistic regression, random forest, support-vector machine, XGBoost, k-nearest neighbors, naïve Bayes, artificial neural network, and a stacked ensemble were trained and evaluated. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, Cohen's kappa, and area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC). Because the intended use case was screening or triage, sensitivity was given particular interpretive importance. In addition to overall discrimination, a primary analytical objective was to examine sensitivity trade-offs, false-negative classifications, and the implications of model performance for screening suitability. Global and local model interpretability were assessed using feature importance, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, individual conditional expectation (ICE) plots, and individualized explanations.
RESULTS: Among 7,056 participants, 716 (10.1%) had significant fibrosis. XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination (AUROC, 0.79), followed by random forest (AUROC, 0.78) and logistic regression (AUROC, 0.77), but its sensitivity was low (0.17), indicating limited utility for screening at the evaluated threshold. Logistic regression and naïve Bayes demonstrated the highest sensitivity (0.65 and 0.55, respectively), suggesting that models with slightly lower discrimination may be more appropriate for triage-oriented use. Across models, waist circumference, body-mass index, cardiovascular comorbidity, sex, HbA1c, and liver enzymes were the most influential predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory model development study, moderate discrimination did not necessarily translate into clinically meaningful screening performance. The highest-AUROC model showed poor sensitivity, indicating substantial false-negative risk and limiting its usefulness for screening in its current form. Because imputation was performed before the train-test split, reported performance estimates may be optimistic and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of clinical readiness. Leakage-free preprocessing, threshold optimization, calibration assessment, decision-curve analysis, external validation, and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical application.

Title: High Thrombus Burden in Premature Type 1 Myocardial Infarction: Cross-Sectional Associations With STEMI Presentation, Coronary Flow, and Systemic Inflammation.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated whether admission complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices were associated with angiographic high thrombus burden (HTB) in premature myocardial infarction (MI).
METHOD: Consecutive patients aged <45 years with type 1 MI and an identifiable culprit lesion who underwent coronary angiography between 2020 and 2024 were included in this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional analysis. Thrombus burden was assessed using the Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) thrombus grading scale, with occluded vessels reclassified after restoration of coronary flow; HTB was defined as grades 4-5. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) were evaluated using clinically defined multivariable logistic regression models, with and without adjustment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) presentation.
RESULTS: Among 137 patients (77 with STEMI and 60 with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction [NSTEMI]), 81 had an occluded culprit vessel; after restoration of coronary flow, only two lesions remained classified as grade 5. HTB was identified in 79 patients (57.7%) and was associated with STEMI presentation (67.1% vs. 41.4%, P = 0.003) and culprit vessel occlusion (69.6% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.004). Neither NLR (P = 0.54) nor SIRI (P = 0.20) differed significantly between thrombus burden categories, and neither was associated with HTB after adjustment for pre-event characteristics (odds ratio [OR] 1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.94-1.17 and OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.95-1.35, respectively) or additional adjustment for STEMI presentation (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.92-1.14 and OR 1.08, 95% CI 0.90-1.30, respectively), whereas STEMI presentation remained significantly associated with HTB (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.33-5.68, P = 0.006). The findings were consistent across all sensitivity analyses, and discriminatory performance was negligible (areas under the curve of 0.531 and 0.564). No significant differences in in-hospital outcomes were detected; however, these comparisons were underpowered.
CONCLUSION: In young patients with angiographically confirmed type 1 MI, HTB was associated with STEMI presentation and initial coronary occlusion but not with admission inflammatory indices.

Title: Risk Factors, Ischemic Delay, and In-Hospital Outcomes by Sex in Adults Aged 18-50 Years with STEMI Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Exploratory Single-Center Cohort.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe sex differences in cardiovascular risk factors and reperfusion delays and explore in-hospital outcomes in adults aged 18-50 years with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHOD: This retrospective single-center cohort included 497 consecutive patients (71 [14.3%] women) treated during 2023-2024. Hard major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) comprised all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or stroke. A nonstandard expanded clinical deterioration composite additionally included incident cardiogenic shock and, among patients admitted in Killip class I, incident heart failure. Sex comparisons and Firth penalized logistic models were exploratory.
RESULTS: Mean age was 40.7 +- 5.3 years. Current smoking was more frequent in men (69.0% vs 39.4%; P < 0.001), whereas obesity was more frequent in women (54.9% vs 26.8%; P < 0.001). Age-adjusted median symptom-to-first-medical-contact, first-medical-contact-to-device, and total ischemic times were 46, 10, and 48 minutes longer in women, respectively (all P < 0.001). Hard MACCE occurred in 21 patients (4.2%), incident heart failure occurred in 13 of 390 eligible patients (3.3%), and the expanded composite occurred in 46 patients (9.3%). The expanded composite occurred in 12 of 71 women and 34 of 426 men (16.9% vs 8.0%; unadjusted P = 0.025), and incident cardiogenic shock occurred in 7 women and 13 men (9.9% vs 3.1%; unadjusted P = 0.015). In the parsimonious baseline model, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for female sex was 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-5.42), attenuating to 1.90 (95% CI, 0.83-4.18) after adding admission Killip class ≥II.
CONCLUSION: Women had a different risk-factor distribution and longer documented ischemic delays. The association between sex and the expanded composite was sensitive to adjustment for baseline clinical severity. Sex-specific outcome estimates are hypothesis-generating given the small female subgroup and event counts. The retrospective single-center design, absence of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable care- and referral-pathway variables limit causal interpretation.

Title: Automated Two-component Pre-CTPA ECG Risk Phenotype and 365-day Mortality among ECG-evaluated Patients with Computed Tomography-confirmed Pulmonary Embolism.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electrocardiographic abnormalities are common in acute pulmonary embolism, but their prognostic value in public waveform-linked cohorts remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether an interpretable automated two-component pre-CTPA ECG risk phenotype was associated with 365-day mortality among ECG-evaluated patients with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism.
METHOD: This secondary analysis used a retrospective cohort derived from MIMIC-IV-Ext-PE linked to MIMIC-IV-ECG. The source population included 1,534 unique PE-positive patients after patient-level indexing. A total of 650 patients had an ECG within 6 hours before CTPA, 571 were admission-linked, and 567 passed waveform signal-quality screening. The exposure assigned 1 point for tachycardia >100 beats/min and 1 point for V3 T-wave inversion. The primary Cox model was adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, PE subtype, ICU admission initiated at or before CTPA, and early physiologic derangement after excluding heart rate from the derangement definition.
RESULTS: The primary cohort included 567 patients and 126 deaths within 365 days. Crude 365-day mortality increased across score levels: 15.0% for score 0, 26.8% for score 1, and 41.7% for score 2. In the primary model, each 1-point increase in the score was associated with higher 365-day mortality (HR 1.70 [1.36-2.13], P<0.001). The exposure-level proportional hazards diagnostic did not show clear evidence of violation (P=0.060). A stabilized inverse-probability-of-selection weighted Cox model yielded a similar estimate (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28-1.99; P<0.001), although measured selection imbalance was reduced but not eliminated.
CONCLUSION: Among ECG-evaluated patients with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism, an automated two-component pre-CTPA ECG risk phenotype was associated with higher 365-day mortality. The phenotype should be interpreted as an early prognostic marker requiring further validation rather than as a validated clinical decision tool.

Title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals.
Abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual's deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span-wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

Title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer's disease.
Abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2CV), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.
Publication Types: Clinical Trial, Phase I; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Prospective evaluation of the clinical effectiveness of an innovative catalytic wound care technology.
Journal: Wounds : a compendium of clinical research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic wounds present a significant health concern due to their prolonged healing time, risk of severe complications, and the burden they place on patients, health care providers, and the health system.
OBJECTIVE: To prospectively evaluate an advanced wound care treatment that delivers catalytic technology (through polymers engineered to replicate the extracellular matrix) and facilitates copper-dependent cellular signaling pathways involved in wound healing.
METHODS: This interrupted time series was a multisite, within-patient controlled, clinical evaluation of the catalytic technology involving 25 participants each with at least 1 chronic wound (pressure injury, diabetic foot ulcer, or venous leg ulcer). Participants received standard wound care for 28 days (control phase), followed by 28 days with the catalytic technology replacing the primary dressing (intervention phase). Wound percent area reduction (PAR) was assessed weekly.
RESULTS: The average wound age prior to study inclusion was 84 weeks. In the control phase, the average PAR was -1.0%. In the intervention phase, the average PAR was 56.6%, showing that the catalytic technology accelerated wound healing (total overall change, 57.6%; P < .0001; > 95% power). The catalytic technology also demonstrated a safety profile equivalent to that of current state dressings.
CONCLUSION: When used in combination with standard of care practices to promote wound healing, the catalytic technology was shown to be an effective tool in the treatment of chronic wounds compared with other available wound dressings.

Title: Lymphedema therapy and wound healing: a retrospective analysis of pretreatment and posttreatment wound volume.
Journal: Wounds : a compendium of clinical research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous leg ulcers (VLUs) frequently exhibit prolonged healing times, particularly in the presence of lower extremity lymphedema. One approach to managing VLU is to combine traditional wound care with lymphedema therapy (LT). Despite recognition of compression as an effective agent for management of chronic wounds, use of lymphedema services remains insufficient among health care providers.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effectiveness of LT for tissue repair and examine the effect of various factors on wound healing.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Electronic medical records of patients with VLU who completed LT between June 2016 and March 2020 were reviewed. Wound volume (length × width × depth) was compared before and after LT, and medians of nonnormally distributed data were compared via the Wilcoxon signed rank test. Demographic characteristics and medical history were evaluated to determine their relationship to VLU healing. A 3-step hierarchical approach was used to investigate the effect of various factors on predicting tissue repair.
RESULTS: A total of 178 wounds in 115 patients were included in the analysis. The average wound volume before LT was 14.4 cm³. After lymphedema intervention, the mean wound volume decreased to 3.8 cm³, a significant reduction in wound size (P < .001). A hierarchical regression model revealed no statistically significant relationships between wound closure and age, sex, comorbidities, or treatment-related factors. However, body mass index emerged as a moderately significant predictor of wound healing (P = .013).
CONCLUSION: The findings support the effectiveness of LT for healing chronic VLU in patients with lymphedema treated in an outpatient clinic.

Title: Association between the hemoglobin albumin lymphocyte and platelet score and chronic kidney disease: Insights from patient data and animal models.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocytes and platelets (HALP) score, a novel nutritional and inflammatory biomarker, has been used in various chronic disease studies. However, the relationship between the HALP score and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly elucidated. This study aimed to explore the association between the HALP score and CKD.
METHODS: Our analysis encompassed 25,181 adult participants drawn from NHANES cycles spanning 2009-2018. Weighted multivariable logistic regression and generalized additive models (GAMs) were employed to evaluate the independent associations between the HALP score and three outcomes: CKD, albuminuria, and low-estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). CKD was defined as albuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥ 30 mg/g) or low-eGFR (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2). Threshold effects were examined using two-piecewise linear regression. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were applied to compare the discriminative capacity of the HALP score with the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR). A 5/6 nephrectomy rat model of CKD was established to evaluate the HALP values and their components.
RESULTS: After adjustment for multiple confounders, higher HALP scores were inversely associated with prevalent CKD (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.94-0.99) and albuminuria (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99). However, the association between the HALP score and low-eGFR was no longer statistically significant in Model 3. Non-linear analyses revealed a threshold pattern, with higher HALP scores inversely associated with prevalent CKD up to an inflection point of 52.43 (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.95-0.99), beyond which no significant association was observed. For albuminuria, the corresponding inflection point was 49.82. Subgroup and interaction analyses indicated no meaningful effect modification by age, sex, BMI, hypertension, or diabetes. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results. ROC analysis demonstrated that the HALP score had modestly higher AUCs for CKD and albuminuria compared with PNI, SII, LMR, and PLR. In the animal experiment, CKD rats exhibited significantly lower calculated HALP values, which were inversely correlated with serum creatinine (Scr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), further supporting the biological plausibility of the HALP-CKD association.
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study, lower HALP scores are independently associated with a higher prevalence of CKD and albuminuria. As an affordable and readily measurable composite index, a low HALP score may represent a complementary marker of prevalent CKD, while its clinical utility requires prospective validation.

Title: Utility of follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) occurs in approximately 20-40% of patients and has been shown to be a major predictor of mortality. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) can detect late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), which can indicate myocardial inflammation and/or fibrosis. However, the role of CMRI at diagnosis and to monitor evolution of cardiac manifestations in EGPA remains unclear. Our aim was to describe the CMRI findings in our EGPA patient cohort, including the presence and persistence of LGE, and to report on the clinical outcomes observed during follow-up.
METHODS: This monocentric retrospective descriptive cohort study included 75 patients diagnosed with EGPA, who were seen at least twice between 2015 and January 2023.
RESULTS: Among these 75 patients (male 56%, mean age at diagnosis 45 years), 30 patients underwent CMRI at diagnosis, 9 (30%) of whom had cardiac symptoms. All 30 patients (100%) were treated with glucocorticoids, with 13 (43%) also receiving cyclophosphamide. 16/30 (53%) had LGE on first CMRI; 10/11 had persistent LGE on second CMRI, 4/4 had LGE on third CMRI, and 2/2 had LGE on fourth CMRI. Of these 30 patients, 3 (10%) had cardiovascular events at follow-up, 2 of whom had atrial fibrillation (neither had LGE on their CMRIs), and 1 of whom had coronary artery disease requiring stenting (with LGE on his 4 CMRIs).
CONCLUSIONS: The role of CMRIs to study and monitor cardiac involvement in EGPA remains unclear. LGE most often persists despite treatment, with no apparent association with adverse cardiac outcomes in this cohort.

Title: Serum advanced glycation end products and glyoxalase-1 levels in Behçet's disease: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Behçet's disease (BD) is a chronic, systemic inflammatory disorder. Despite the presence of chronic inflammation in BD, a clear increase in atherosclerotic cardiovascular mortality has not been documented. However, chronic inflammation may contribute to atherogenesis through various pathways, including accelerated generation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). The objective of this study was to assess serum AGEs, Nε-carboxymethyllysine (CML), and glyoxalase-1 (GLO1) levels in a cohort of individuals with BD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study comprised 81 patients with BD (mean age: 43±11 years; 51 men/30 women) and 56 control subjects (mean age: 52±11 years; 45 women/11 men). Serum concentrations of AGEs, CML, and GLO1 were assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
RESULTS: AGE levels in patients with BD were significantly higher than those in the control group (BD: median 555 [453-864] ng/L vs. controls: median 512 [430-557] ng/L; p=0.008). CML levels in patients with BD were also higher than those in controls (median 532 [443-694] ng/mL vs. median 360 [308-442] ng/mL; p<0.001). Moreover, GLO1 levels in patients with BD were significantly lower than those in controls (median 15 [13-22] ng/mL vs. median 21 [18-27] ng/mL; p<0.001). No significant differences were observed in AGEs, CML, or GLO1 levels in individuals with BD according to smoking status, BMI, colchicine, glucocorticoids, immunosuppressive therapies, or major organ involvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated levels of advanced glycation end products and decreased glyoxalase-1 levels were observed in BD. This pattern suggests that the inflammatory process in BD may be associated with AGE accumulation and attenuation of protective antioxidant/dicarbonyl-detoxification pathways. Elevated AGEs may contribute to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis in individuals with BD.

Title: Factors associated with chronic kidney disease in patients with gout: a two-centre study incorporating ultrasonographic features.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant comorbidity in patients with gout, yet the specific phenotypes associated with its prevalence remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to evaluate the association between clinical indicators and ultrasonographic features with CKD using a transparent, interpretable machine learning approach.
METHODS: This cross-sectional bicentric study analysed a cohort of 666 patients with gout, who were partitioned into a derivation cohort (n=500) for model development and internal validation, and an independent validation cohort (n=166). Three architectures (GLM, Random Forest, SVM) modelled associations between biomarkers and CKD status. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified individual variable contributions, and a dynamic nomogram visualised cumulative relevance.
RESULTS: Six key correlates were identified, comprising two clinical indicators (age and hypertension) and four ultrasonographic findings (bone erosion, high-burden (≥3 joints) tophi, synovial hyperplasia, and double contour sign). The GLM demonstrated the strongest associative performance, with an AUC of 0.842 (internal) and 0.835 (independent cohort), indicating high discriminative power. SHAP analysis identified advanced age and ultrasound-detected tophi as the most influential contributors to the observed associations. DCA and calibration plots confirmed that the framework accurately reflected the underlying probability distribution.
CONCLUSIONS: We established an interpretable analytical framework that characterises the clinical and ultrasonographic profile associated with CKD in gout. By integrating imaging markers with clinical indicators, this approach identifies associated phenotypes, providing a transparent reference for individualised assessment and enhanced clinical vigilance regarding renal status.

Title: Clinically overt aortic aneurysm in giant cell arteritis: a nationwide hospital-based study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the incidence, time to aortic aneurysm (AA) diagnosis, and factors associated with AA development in patients admitted with giant cell arteritis (GCA).
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, registry-based study using the Spanish National Hospital Discharge Database. The study included all hospitalised patients aged ≥50 years with a diagnosis of GCA between 2016 and 2024.
RESULTS: Among 5,120 patients hospitalised because of GCA without prior AA, 54 (1.1%) were diagnosed with AA during current admission (AAo group) and 41 (0.8%) developed AA during follow-up (AAf group). Median time from first GCA admission and AA diagnosis was 2.7 years. Incidence rate was 1.8 per 100 patient-years. Established heart disease was markedly more frequent in the AAo compared with the other groups (50.0% at onset vs. 19.5% during follow-up and 32.3% in patients without aneurysm; p=0.006). After adjustment, male sex was independently associated with a higher risk of AA at baseline (RRR 2.42, 95% CI 1.40-4.20), whereas smoking at GCA diagnosis was the only factor independently associated with AA development during follow-up (RRR 3.23, 95% CI 1.47-7.08).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinically recognised AA was uncommon among hospitalised patients with GCA and was associated mainly with traditional cardiovascular risk factors, particularly male sex and smoking. Because estimates were based on hospital discharge diagnoses, they reflect clinically overt, hospital-recorded AA rather than the overall aneurysm burden in GCA. Follow-up should prioritise individualised vascular surveillance, particularly in smokers.

Title: Phenotype-based risk stratification for deep vein thrombosis in Behçet's disease: a global 10-year longitudinal study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Vascular involvement, particularly deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Behçet's disease (BD). This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for DVT and establish a robust framework for phenotype-based risk stratification.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global health research network and identified 19,739 patients with BD. Three independent propensity score-matched cohorts were established to evaluate the impact of intestinal involvement, thrombophlebitis, and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify independent predictors of DVT over a 10-year follow-up. To ensure the robustness of our findings and minimise peri-diagnostic detection bias, a 90-day landmark analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Multivariable analysis identified APS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 6.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.56-8.64) and a history of thrombophlebitis (aHR 5.92, 95% CI 4.72-7.41) as the strongest independent predictors of DVT. In the 90-day landmark analysis, these associations remained significant, with persistent risk observed for APS (aHR 5.10) and thrombophlebitis (aHR 2.50), confirming their long-term predictive value. Additional independent predictors included intestinal involvement (defined as non-infective inflammatory colitis; aHR 1.51), obesity (aHR 1.98), glucocorticoid use (aHR 1.78), and male sex (aHR 1.77).
CONCLUSIONS: APS and thrombophlebitis, markers of heightened inflammatory and thrombotic activity at diagnosis, also appear to be persistent indicators of elevated DVT risk in BD. These findings support phenotype-based risk stratification and highlight the need for intensive monitoring and individualised preventive strategies to improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Effects of cannabidiol on risky decision-making and autonomic function in alcohol use disorder.
Abstract:
AIMS: To examine the effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on psychophysiological responding and risky decision-making in individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD).
METHODS: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, 18 participants with AUD completed the Columbia Card Task (CCT) following administration of CBD and placebo. Skin conductance responses (SCR) and high-frequency heart rate variability (HF-HRV) were assessed as indices of autonomic responding during task performance. Risk-taking was indexed by the number of cards selected on the CCT.
RESULTS: CBD did not significantly affect SCR (P = .16, pBH = .326) or risky decision-making on the CCT (P > .63, pBH = 0.67). However, CBD significantly increased HF-HRV (β = 0.53, SE = 0.19, P = .005; pBH = 0.020). There was no evidence that the relationships between HF-HRV or SCR and risky decision-making differed between CBD and placebo conditions (drug × HF-HRV: P = .92; drug × SCR: P = .958; both pBH = .958).
DISCUSSION: CBD increased HF-HRV but did not significantly alter SCR, risky decision-making, or the relationship between autonomic responses and risky decision-making. These findings suggest that CBD influences autonomic responding during task performance, although the functional significance of this effect remains uncertain. The modest sample size and relatively healthy, non-treatment-seeking sample may have limited the ability to detect broader physiological and behavioural effects.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Echocardiography: A Critical Review of Models, Validation, and Clinical Impact.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To critically review artificial intelligence (AI) in echocardiography, linking model design and technical performance to validation and clinical use.
METHODS: We synthesized literature assembled through Web of Science and Scopus collections and targeted revision searches. Evidence was organized by echocardiographic task, model paradigm, data source, evaluation protocol, and level of clinical validation.
RESULTS: AI applications span acquisition guidance, image analysis, quantitative measurement, disease assessment, and outcome prediction, with emerging foundation, multimodal, and examination-level models. Most studies assess retrospective task performance; fewer evaluate cross-site transportability or clinical impact. Reproducible performance has been demonstrated for view recognition, segmentation, and selected measurements under aligned protocols, and prospective trials confirm workflow gains. However, evidence linking AI to improved clinical decisions or patient outcomes remains limited. Generalizability is further constrained by uneven dataset coverage and inconsistent evaluation protocols.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports AI assistance in selected echocardiographic tasks; however, clinical use requires external validation, failure reporting, and ongoing monitoring in intended settings.
SIGNIFICANCE: This review links model development with validation evidence to guide clinical evaluation and identify priorities for prospective studies in echocardiography.

Title: Human vs Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Coronary Occlusions in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) on the electrocardiogram (ECG) can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), non-STEMI, ST depression, or other patterns (eg, de Winter T waves and hyperacute T waves), posing a diagnostic challenge. Even experienced physicians may overlook OMI on ECG, leading to delays in catheterization laboratory activation. Recently, smartphone apps using AI have been shown to exhibit promising accuracy in ECG interpretation in large datasets.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of our study was to retrospectively compare the diagnostic performance of an AI-based application (PMCardio) with that of interventional cardiologists in interpreting nonpathognomonic ECGs that generated debates about diagnosis.
METHODS: In total, 33 ECGs that were diagnostically challenging upon patient admission to the emergency department were included. A group of 3 interventional cardiologists, blinded to the final diagnosis, independently assessed whether the ECG suggested OMI requiring immediate invasive coronary angiography. The diagnostic performance of the cardiologists was compared to that of the AI application, using the results of coronary angiography as the gold standard and considering any lesion with ≥90% stenosis as positive.
RESULTS: Of the 33 patients, 29 (88%) had a final diagnosis of cardiac origin for their chest pain, including 23 acute coronary syndromes, of which 13 (57%) were OMI. The 3 cardiologists achieved sensitivities of 62%, 85%, and 62%; negative predictive values (NPVs) of 74%, 83%, and 69%; specificities of 70%, 50%, and 55%; and positive predictive values (PPVs) of 57%, 52%, and 47%. Their overall misclassification rates were 33%, 36%, and 42%. In contrast, AI analysis demonstrated a sensitivity and NPV of 100%, a specificity of 60%, a PPV of 62%, and an overall misclassification rate of 24%.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study of challenging ECGs, an AI application demonstrated better diagnostic performance of OMI as compared to cardiologists. These findings highlight the potential of AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making.

Title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.
CONCLUSIONS: LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.

Title: Uptake and Inequalities in Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation After Decentralization.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite clinical benefits and guideline recommendations, uptake of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) following coronary artery disease remains suboptimal, with barriers including transportation issues, travel distance, and geographic location. To overcome these barriers, decentralization strategies that move health care to local settings have been developed across several countries.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether CR uptake improved following decentralization, and whether geographic and social inequalities were reduced.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This register-based cohort study used data from 2013 to 2022, with data analysis performed from April to August 2025. This population-based study was conducted within 21 Danish municipalities. All participants were patients aged 30 years or older discharged alive after acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting. Patients were identified in the Danish National Patient Register. Patients were excluded if they had a previous diagnosis or procedure or did not reside within the study area.
EXPOSURES: Travel distance from home to nearest CR facility and educational level.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Uptake (attending at least 1 training session within 180 days from discharge) was analyzed using modified Poisson regression to quantify differences in proportions before and after decentralization with adjustment for relevant covariates.
RESULTS: A total of 19 375 patients were eligible for the study, and 295 patients with missing information on exposures or covariates were excluded. Among the included 19 080 patients, 13 355 (70.0%) were male, and 10 868 (57.0%) were aged 60 to 79 years. The median (IQR) travel distance was reduced from 15.1 (5.9-25.7) km to 7.2 (2.8-14.8) km after decentralization, and uptake increased by 16% (risk ratio [RR], 1.16; 95% CI, 1.12-1.19). Among the 20% of patients with the longest travel distance, uptake increased by 45% (RR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.33-1.58), and geographic inequality was significantly reduced. Among patients with short education, uptake increased by 27% (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.20-1.35), and social inequality was significantly reduced.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 19 080 patients, there was increased uptake of CR after decentralization to primary care, accompanied by significant reductions in geographic and social inequalities. The findings support decentralized delivery of CR as a feasible and equitable model, but ongoing monitoring of quality and safety remains essential.

Title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTION: Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications.
RESULTS: The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

Title: Comment on "Association between postoperative arterial blood gas parameters and cognitive dysfunction following coronary artery bypass grafting: a prospective observational study".
Clinical validation of an intra-abdominal pressure monitoring system by comparison with pneumoperitoneum pressure.
Journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
Abstract: In critically ill patients, intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is associated with organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Acute kidney injury may occur early, since the kidney is particularly vulnerable to elevated intra-abdominal pressure (IAP). Accurate and timely measurement of IAP is essential for early detection of IAH and the initiation of appropriate therapeutic interventions. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the accuracy of an IAP monitoring system compared to a reference standard, the CO2 insufflator, during laparoscopy. The second aim was to assess the changes in renal biomarker levels during and after increases in IAP through pneumoperitoneum. A prospective cohort study in patients undergoing laparoscopy at the University Medical Center Groningen. IAP measurements were performed with a urinary catheter using an IAP monitoring system (Accuryn® Monitoring System, Accuryn Medical) and compared to the pressure set at the CO2-insufflator system. Bland-Altman analysis was performed with accounting for repeated measures. Urine samples were collected at several time-points and Kidney Injury Molecule 1 (KIM-1), Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP-2), urinary Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin (NGAL), Liver-type Fatty Acid-Binding Protein (L-FABP), and albumin-creatinine ratio were measured. Between March 2025 and January 2026, 99 measurements were performed in 29 patients. One patient (3%) underwent hemicolectomy, and 28 patients underwent endometriosis surgery (97%). Analysis showed a bias of -1.4 mmHg (95% CI (-1.96 - (-0.82)) and limits of agreement of - 5.96 mmHg and 3.2 mmHg (95% CI -6.8-3.99) between the IAP monitoring system and the CO2-insufflators. The precision was 2.3 mmHg. The levels of renal biomarkers KIM-1, TIMP-2 and albumin/Cr ratio increased during laparoscopy compared to baseline, suggesting that relatively small IAP increases during laparoscopy have a subclinical effect on the kidney. The IAP monitoring system underestimated the IAP set by the CO2-insufflator by approximately 1 mmHg. The wide limits of agreement warrant cautious interpretation. Overall, the IAP monitoring system showed reasonable accuracy and precision. The increase of several renal biomarkers during laparoscopy compared to baseline may reflect a direct effect of elevated IAP on the kidney.

Title: A real-world multicenter study of statins in compensated advanced chronic liver disease on hepatic decompensation and mortality outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Statins exert pleiotropic effects, including antiinflammatory, endothelial, and antifibrotic actions, which may slow the progression of cirrhosis. However, their use in patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) remains limited due to concerns regarding potential hepatotoxicity, and data specific to this population remains sparse.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multinational cohort study of adult cACLD (LSM >10 kPa) patients using data from the Cirrhosis Outcome and Research Endeavor (CORE) consortium, across 13 centers in 8 countries. Baseline statin use was the exposure of interest. Associations with first and second hepatic decompensation, composite liver-related events, and all-cause and cause-specific mortality were assessed using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression across two sequentially adjusted multivariable models and an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) analysis.
RESULTS: Among 2267 patients, 786 (34.7%) were statin users. Statin use was independently associated with a lower risk of first decompensation (Model 1: sHR 0.64; Model 2: sHR 0.66; IPTW: sHR 0.56) and composite liver-related events (Model 1: sHR 0.61; Model 2: sHR 0.63; IPTW: sHR 0.50), with benefit most pronounced in the moderate-risk portal hypertension strata and MASLD subgroup. No association was observed with all-cause, liver-related, or cardiovascular mortality. Associations with second decompensation were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: In this large multinational cohort of cACLD patients, statin use was associated with reduced risk of hepatic decompensation and liver-related events, but not all-cause mortality. These findings support a potential benefit for statins in this population.

Title: Ramadan Fasting in Chronic Heart Failure: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a significant global health concern, affecting over 64 million individuals worldwide. During Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, Muslims abstain from food, drink, smoking, and sexual activity between dawn and sunset. This systematic review investigates the potential impact of Ramadan observance in patients with CHF.
METHODS: In accordance with JBI and PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify clinical studies examining the effects of Ramadan fasting in patients with CHF. Review articles, case reports, animal studies, editorials, conference abstracts, and commentaries were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using the JBI critical appraisal tools.
RESULTS: The search identified 137 articles, of which seven met the inclusion criteria. The included studies were mostly conducted in MENA region. Overall, Ramadan fasting was not associated with increased hospitalization rates, deterioration in clinical status, or higher mortality among patients with heart failure.
CONCLUSION: This study suggest that fasting may be relatively safe when undertaken with appropriate medical supervision and adherence to prescribed treatment. Nonetheless, larger prospective studies are warranted to further validate these observations.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Intracranial Hypertension: From Single-Centre Development to Multicentre Validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Raised intracranial pressure is one of the most severe secondary insults after traumatic brain injury. Recognising physiological patterns before they progress to dangerous intracranial pressure elevations could enable preventive rather than reactive interventions. In our previous Uppsala single-centre study, an XGBoost machine learning model showed high discriminative performance for prediction of imminent intracranial pressure insults. The model identifies short-term physiological trajectories associated with imminent threshold crossing rather than predicting independent future clinical events. Whether these results are generalisable across centres is unknown. The aim was therefore to evaluate whether the XGBoost model trained on an Uppsala dataset maintains similar performance when applied to a multicentre TBI cohort - The CENTER-TBI High-Resolution ICU cohort.
METHODS: The XGBoost model trained on the Uppsala high frequency traumatic brain injury cohort was externally validated using data from the multicentre CENTER-TBI cohort. Minute-level averages of intracranial pressure and invasive arterial blood pressure were used to predict the onset of an intracranial pressure insult within 30 min on the basis of a 4h historical window. A bidirectional validation design was applied and performance was assessed using multiple metrics.
RESULTS: The cohorts comprised 602 patients from Uppsala and 255 patients from the CENTER-TBI database. When trained on the Uppsala cohort and tested on CENTER-TBI, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 97.4%, sensitivity of 93.8%, and specificity of 98.6%. Training on CENTER-TBI and testing on the Uppsala dataset yielded an AUROC of 96.1%, sensitivity of 81.2%, and specificity of 98.7%. Balanced accuracy exceeded 88% in both validation directions.
CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost model retained high performance under external multicentre validation, indicating that pre-insult physiological patterns preceding increased intracranial pressure are shared across cohorts. Differences in sensitivity between validation directions were observed and may reflect cohort characteristics or dataset size. These findings support the need for local evaluation before clinical implementation.

Title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A total of 176 high-risk patients with IE were enrolled from 10/2020 to 10/2024. Patients with intraoperative hemoadsorption (HA group, n = 93) were compared to patients without hemoadsorption (control, n = 83). The primary endpoint was a composite of 30-day mortality, incidence of vasoplegic syndrome within the first 24 h and 7 days postoperatively, and intensive care (ICU) stay, analyzed using an unmatched hierarchical win-ratio method.
RESULTS: There were no differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. The mean hemoadsorption time was 106 ± 61 min in the HA group. Vasoplegic syndrome was more frequent in the control group (49.4% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.001). Importantly, 30-day mortality was also significantly lower with intraoperative hemoadsorption (7.5% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.003). The mean ICU stay was shorter in the HA group (7.8 ± 4.6 vs. 11.5 ± 4.2 days, p < 0.001). The analysis met the primary endpoint in favor of patients receiving intraoperative hemoadsorption (win ratio 3.83; 95% CI 2.55, 5.74; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk cardiac surgery patients with IE, the intraoperative use of hemoadsorption was associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative vasoplegic syndrome and lower overall 30-day mortality. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the study's methodological limitations and confirmed in future randomized controlled trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB00012919) of the French Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery (CERCSFCTCV20251021).

Title: Nonlinear age-related differences in clinical profiles of obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study of 1,508 Chinese patients.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize age-related clinical profiles and nonlinear age associations in treatment-naive Chinese patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1,508 patients aged 18-88 years at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (2022-2025). Clinical and polysomnographic characteristics were compared across five age groups. Restricted cubic splines assessed continuous-age associations, with separate overall and nonlinearity tests and sex-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Sex-adjusted logistic models evaluated prevalent severity, sleepiness, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; age-quartile comparisons were supplementary.
RESULTS: Among 1,840 participants undergoing PSG, OSA detection differed across ages, with a greater increase among women (age-by-sex interaction P = 0.031). Respiratory severity was broadly comparable across age groups. In unadjusted analyses, body mass index and Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores showed nonlinear age associations (both P < 0.001), as did lowest oxygen saturation (P = 0.018) and selected Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) components. Global PSQI was associated with age overall, without clear nonlinearity (P = 0.099). Sex adjustment attenuated nonlinearity for oxygen saturation and sleep latency. Older age was associated with higher prevalence odds of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes. Excessive daytime sleepiness showed a midlife elevation.
CONCLUSION: OSA clinical profiles differ across ages, with nonlinearity in selected measures. Older patients have greater comorbidity burden and poorer reported sleep quality despite comparable respiratory severity.

Title: Minoxidil and Prostaglandin Analogs for Chemotherapy-Induced Alopecia: A Scoping Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced alopecia (CIA) is common, distressing, and markedly impairs patients' quality of life. Although scalp cooling is the only approved preventive strategy, its effectiveness and accessibility remain limited. Therefore, alternative pharmacologic approaches, such as minoxidil and prostaglandin analogs, have been explored.
METHODS: This scoping review aimed to explore the available evidence on minoxidil's efficacy and safety and the potential role of prostaglandin analogs in alopecia. PubMed, Cochrane Library, Medical Online, and Ichushi-Web were comprehensively searched from inception to February 2026. Studies evaluating minoxidil in CIA and prostaglandin analogs in any alopecia type were included. Case reports, case series, and non-human studies were excluded.
RESULTS: Seven studies were included. Five studies evaluated minoxidil in CIA, including two randomized controlled trials and three retrospective studies on prophylactic and therapeutic use, respectively. Prophylactic topical minoxidil did not markedly prevent CIA but was associated with earlier hair regrowth. In contrast, therapeutic use-particularly of oral minoxidil-improved hair density and treatment response. No serious adverse events were reported, although cardiovascular effects remain a concern with oral formulations. Two randomized controlled trials evaluated prostaglandin analogs in non-chemotherapy-related alopecia and showed markedly improved hair density and regrowth. However, no study directly assessed their efficacy in CIA.
CONCLUSIONS: Minoxidil may be beneficial for hair regrowth in CIA but shows limited preventive efficacy. Prostaglandin analogs are promising but untested in this setting. Future studies should evaluate their role, particularly in combination with minoxidil, to address the current evidence gap and improve outcomes for patients with CIA.

Title: Strain-Based Assessment of Post-TAVR Left Bundle Branch Block in Bicuspid Aortic Valve Using Patient-Specific Computational Modeling.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) left bundle branch block (LBBB) is the most common post-TAVR cardiac conduction abnormality (CCA), particularly in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Prior computational studies evaluated generalized CCA risk but did not quantify LBBB-specific mechanical injury or compare self-expanding (SE) and balloon-expandable (BE) devices in BAV. This proof-of-concept study established a patient-specific computational framework to (1) quantify mechanical stretch in the left bundle branch (LBB)-adjacent region, (2) identify a preliminary, cohort-specific strain-based separation value associated with post-TAVR LBBB, and (3) compare device-related LBBB risk trends between SE and BE devices.
METHODS: Cardiac CT scans from six type I BAV TAVR patients were analyzed (two with LBBB and four without CCA). Patient-specific finite element models incorporated anatomy and leaflet calcification. The LBB region was defined using membranous septum length and anatomical landmarks. Simulations reproduced implantation of deployed SE devices and virtual BE devices at standardized depth. Area-weighted logarithmic strain (LE), contact pressure, oversizing index, eccentricity index, and expansion metrics were computed.
RESULTS: LBB-adjacent LE showed clear separation (0.15-0.24 in LBBB vs. 0.03-0.11 without CCA), with 0.11 as a preliminary cohort-specific separation value. Mean LE was higher with SE than BE devices (0.11 vs. 0.08). Contact pressure showed no consistent association with outcome, suggesting that LE differences reflect multiple contributing factors.
CONCLUSION: In this six-patient cohort, LBB-adjacent strain clearly separated LBBB from No-LBBB cases, whereas contact pressure showed no consistent relationship with outcome. Larger cohorts and sensitivity analyses are needed to establish its clinical utility for BAV TAVR risk stratification or device selection.

Title: Comparison of efficacy and safety between Neuroform Atlas stent-assisted coiling and coiling alone for irregular intracranial aneurysms: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract: The Neuroform Atlas stent-assisted coiling (SAC) technique offers theoretical advantages for the treatment of irregular intracranial aneurysms (IIAs); however, comparative data with coiling alone remain limited. This study aimed to compare angiographic and clinical outcomes between SAC and coiling alone in patients with IIAs. This single-center retrospective study included patients with IIAs treated between January 2022 and December 2023. Patients were divided into the SAC group and the coiling alone group. The primary outcome was the complete occlusion rate at the last angiographic follow-up. A total of 210 aneurysms were included (103 SAC, 107 coiling alone). Significant baseline imbalances were present: the SAC group had wider necks (4.27 ± 1.54 vs. 3.55 ± 1.26 mm, P < 0.001), smaller dome-to-neck ratios (1.29 ± 0.48 vs. 1.77 ± 0.80, P < 0.001), and importantly, a higher proportion of unruptured aneurysms (42.7% vs. 14.0%, P < 0.001). No significant difference was observed in immediate complete occlusion (84.5% vs. 91.6%, P = 0.111). At the last angiographic follow-up (mean 6-8 months), the SAC group had a higher complete occlusion rate (93.0% vs. 74.6%, P = 0.004) and a lower recurrence rate (5.6% vs. 22.0%, P = 0.012). The incidence of favorable discharge outcomes (mRS ≤ 2) was higher in the SAC group (89.3% vs. 74.8%, P = 0.006), but this difference was not sustained at 1 year (90.3% vs. 85.0%, P = 0.249). Hospitalization costs were higher in the SAC group (20,906vs.20,906vs.18,284, P = 0.008). Asymptomatic cerebral infarction occurred more frequently in the SAC group (16.5% vs. 7.5%, P = 0.043). Neuroform Atlas SAC was associated with higher long-term complete occlusion rates and lower recurrence compared with coiling alone for IIAs, but also with higher costs and more asymptomatic cerebral infarctions.

Title: Postnatal evolution of electrocardiographic parameters in preterm infants: a prospective longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Electrocardiography (ECG), an indispensable bedside tool in neonatal intensive care, complements echocardiography by providing assessment of cardiac rhythm and conduction, and when advanced imaging is unavailable, serves as a screening tool. Preterm birth alters cardiac and autonomic maturation. Applying term-based ECG norms may misclassify physiological findings in preterm. We aimed to characterise serial ECG maturation in preterms from birth to term-equivalent age and define gestational- and postnatal-age-specific patterns relevant to clinical interpretation. In this prospective cohort, infants between 28⁰/₇ and 36⁶/₇ weeks' gestation without congenital heart disease underwent serial 11-lead ECG recording within 24 h of birth, on day 7, day 28 and at term-equivalent age. Postnatal and gestation-based differences in ECG parameters were analysed and centile charts were generated. Among 249 infants (mean gestation-334/₇ weeks), 213 completed follow-up until term-equivalent age. ECG parameters demonstrated consistent maturation across time points. The mean QRS axis shifted leftward from 117° at birth to 82° at term-equivalent age (p < 0.001). PR-interval, QRS and P-wave duration remained stable across all time points. Mean QTc showed minimal overall change. Transient QTc prolongation occurred in 8.1% of infants and resolved by term-equivalent age. Right precordial R-wave amplitudes declined over time, whereas left precordial amplitudes increased. At term-equivalent age, very preterm infants exhibited a more leftward QRS axis compared with late preterm infants. Infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia showed trends toward right ventricular dominance.
CONCLUSION: Preterm ECG findings are dynamic, gestation-dependent markers of cardiovascular transition. This study characterises longitudinal ECG maturation in preterms and provides reference values, supporting improved decision-making in preterm care.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Electrocardiographic reference nomograms used in neonatal practice are primarily based on paediatric cohorts or cross-sectional studies of term infants. These references provide limited information on longitudinal electrophysiologic maturation in preterm neonates.
WHAT IS NEW: • In a cohort of 249 preterm infants, serial ECG measurements demonstrated changes in axes, QTc, and precordial voltages from birth to term-equivalent age. • These gestation and age-specific trajectories support cautious interpretation of preterm ECGs using term-derived standards.

Title: Laser versus Mechanical Lithotripsy for Endourological Treatment of Bladder Stones: A Prospective Multicenter Analysis from the EAU-Endourology Bladder Lithiasis Assessment of Surgical Treatment (BLAST) registry.
Abstract: We aim to compare perioperative outcomes, postoperative stone-free rate, complications, and predictors of treatment success in patients undergoing endourological treatment of bladder stones using laser versus mechanical energy. We performed a prospective multicenter analysis from the Bladder Lithiasis Assessment of Surgical Treatment (BLAST) registry. Patients undergoing endourological treatment for bladder stones between May 2025 and September 2025 were included and stratified according to the energy source used for stone fragmentation: laser or mechanical energy, reflecting a pragmatic, category-level comparison of heterogeneous device platforms rather than a device-specific efficacy analysis. Postoperative stone-free rate was assessed at 4-6 weeks and graded from A to D; Grade A indicated complete clearance, while Grade A and B were considered stone-free. Secondary outcomes included operative parameters, complications, hospital stay, and reintervention.
