The phenotype was independently associated with all-cause mortality using either formula: adjusted hazard ratios were 1.54 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.07-2.21] for the published formula and 2.14 (95% CI, 1.52-3.00) for the new equation. Four-category and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining handgrip strength with creatinine- and cystatin C-derived estimated SMI identifies a sarcopenia-related high-risk phenotype and stratifies mortality risk in non-dialysis-dependent CKD. This approach may support screening when direct muscle mass assessment is unavailable but requires further validation before use as a diagnostic substitute.

Title: Restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in Africa: clinical outcomes, resource stewardship, and future directions.
Abstract: Blood transfusion continues to be a vital part of contemporary healthcare, especially in treating severe anemia, bleeding, trauma, obstetric crises, and critical conditions. In Africa, where transfusion-dependent conditions are prevalent and blood supplies often limited, establishing the best transfusion threshold is crucial for enhancing patient outcomes while maximizing the use of scarce resources. Restrictive transfusion practices that typically use lower hemoglobin thresholds (7-8 g/dL) are now widely accepted globally as they minimize unnecessary transfusions while maintaining safety across various clinical environments. In contrast, liberal approaches, defined by elevated transfusion thresholds (9-10 g/dL), might still be suitable for specific patient groups, such as individuals with acute coronary syndromes, persistent significant bleeding, or serious symptomatic anemia. This review analyzes the existing evidence regarding restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in the African context, focusing on clinical outcomes, resource management in healthcare, and prospective avenues for practice and investigation. Research from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and global guidelines consistently shows that restrictive transfusion strategies correlate with similar mortality, morbidity, hospital stay duration, and functional recovery in most stable hospitalized patients, while minimizing transfusion-related complications and preserving limited blood resources. Nevertheless, the direct relevance of evidence produced mainly in high-income countries needs thorough evaluation due to Africa's distinct epidemiological characteristics, healthcare system constraints, and blood service deficiencies. Enhancing patient blood management initiatives, increasing voluntary blood donations, improving transfusion oversight, and producing robust African clinical evidence are essential priorities.

Title: Heart failure in Somalia: a scoping review of the epidemiology, etiology, clinical characteristics, management, outcomes, and evidence gaps.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is an important cause of morbidity, hospitalisation, disability, and mortality, but evidence from Somalia remains fragmented and largely confined to individual hospital-based studies. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on the epidemiology, aetiologies, clinical and diagnostic characteristics, management, outcomes, and research gaps relating to heart failure in Somalia.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to 27 July 2026. Backward citation searching was conducted on 3 August 2026. Original studies reporting heart-failure-specific findings from Somalia, including Somaliland and Puntland, were eligible. Screening was conducted independently by two reviewers. Data were charted using a structured form and verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised descriptively without meta-analysis because of substantial heterogeneity and possible participant overlap.
RESULTS: The searches identified 111 records, of which 56 were duplicates. Fifty-five records underwent title and abstract screening, 13 reports were assessed in full text, and 12 studies published between 2011 and 2025 were included. Eleven studies were associated with a single tertiary hospital in Mogadishu, and no study provided nationally representative or multicentre evidence. Reported aetiologies and associated conditions included hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, anaemia, thyroid dysfunction, renal disease, and thiamine-deficiency wet beriberi. Echocardiography was the principal diagnostic method, but heart-failure definitions and ejection-fraction thresholds varied substantially. Management data were limited mainly to selected populations with thyroid dysfunction, left ventricular thrombus, or wet beriberi. Outcome reporting was sparse and included in-hospital mortality, first-year outcomes in a thrombus cohort, length of stay, stroke, thrombus resolution, and exploratory prognostic indices.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence on heart failure in Somalia is emerging but remains geographically concentrated, methodologically heterogeneous, and insufficient to estimate national burden, treatment coverage, or long-term outcomes. Prospective multicentre studies and a staged heart-failure registry using standardised diagnostic definitions, clear denominators, treatment indicators, and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

Title: Diabetic retinal neurovascular unit injury: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and integrated therapeutic strategies.
Abstract:
AIM: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) has long been regarded as an isolated retinal microvascular disease. Histopathological, molecular, imaging, and multi-omics evidence now supports disruption of retinal neurovascular unit (NVU) homeostasis as a central mechanism of DR, in which neuronal degeneration, reactive gliosis, and microvascular damage reinforce one another. This narrative review summarizes the anatomy and physiology of the NVU, its temporal evolution in DR, the molecular pathways of neurovascular crosstalk, quantitative imaging assessment, and integrated therapeutic strategies, and indicates where the evidence remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to July 2026 for reports on the retinal NVU in diabetes, and reference lists of retrieved articles were screened. Because this is a narrative rather than a systematic review, records were screened by the authors without a formal risk-of-bias assessment or quantitative synthesis. English-language reports addressing retinal NVU structure, diabetes-related injury mechanisms, imaging quantification, or NVU-directed interventions were eligible, and priority was given to human histopathological studies, prospective imaging cohorts, and translational intervention studies. Eighty-two references were included.
KEY FINDINGS: Neurodegeneration is the earliest readily detectable change of NVU dysfunction in most cohorts, whereas microvascular injury amplifies retinal damage. Combined optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), and electroretinography (ERG) allow stage-specific quantification, and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and deep capillary plexus vessel density (DVD) are among the most consistently reported early markers, although this evidence varies. Polyol pathway activation, AGE-RAGE and protein kinase C signaling, oxidative stress, HIF-1α/vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, microglial STING and inflammasome activation, and non-coding RNA dysregulation jointly mediate bidirectional neurovascular injury. Vascular-targeted monotherapy cannot halt inner retinal neuronal loss, whereas multi-target strategies remain largely preclinical or at an early trial stage.
CONCLUSIONS: In our interpretation, early neurodegeneration is the most readily detectable biomarker, microcirculatory damage acts as a disease amplifier, and complete NVU disintegration is the terminal common pathway. This framework is proposed to support ultra-early risk stratification and synergistic multi-target intervention, and is offered as one interpretation of a still-evolving evidence base rather than an established consensus.

Title: Serum T50 is not independently associated with coronary artery calcification in early chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The serum T50 test quantifies calcification propensity, with lower values indicating a higher propensity for calcification. Lower T50 values have been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, particularly in advanced chronic kidney disease. Whether serum T50 is associated with coronary artery calcification (CAC) in individuals with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function remains unclear. We examined this association in a population-based cross-sectional study.
METHODS: We analysed 1945 participants from the population-based Lifelines ImaLife cohort with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function (estimated glomerular filtration rate, 37.5-87.6 ml/min/1.73 m²). Serum T50 was measured using a standardized nephelometric assay. CAC was assessed by electrocardiographically triggered non-contrast computed tomography and categorized into 0, 1-99, 100-399, and ≥400 Agatston units. Associations between continuous T50 (per 10-min increase) and CAC categories were examined using multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of the 1945 participants, 56.5% had detectable CAC (CAC 1-99: 30.9%, 100-399: 14.4%, ≥400: 11.2%). In crude analyses, higher T50 values were associated with the presence of CAC [odds ratio (OR) 1.02, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.03] and with CAC categories 1-99, 100-399, and ≥400 versus 0 (ORs 1.01, 1.02, and 1.03, respectively). These associations were no longer significant after adjustment for age, body mass index, and sex. Subgroup analyses did not identify risk groups in which T50 was significantly associated with the presence or severity of CAC.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function, T50 was not independently associated with prevalent CAC after multi-variable adjustment.

Title: Clinicopathological Evolution of Pyrrolizidine Alkaloid-induced Liver Injury: Transition From SOS to PSVD?
Journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS) is characterized by hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cell injury and detachment, hepatic sinusoidal congestion, and hepatic cell necrosis. Currently, limited data exist concerning changes during the recovery period, especially histopathological changes. The purpose of this study was to investigate the evolution of pathology in patients with pyrrolizidine alkaloid (PA)-induced SOS and in a monocrotaline-induced SOS rat model.
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with PA-induced SOS who underwent liver biopsy after achieving clinical remission were consecutively enrolled in this retrospective study. To compare the clinical and pathological differences between patients with acute and convalescent SOS, a 2:1 matched analysis was performed based on age, sex, treatment regimen, and baseline Drum Tower Severity Scoring (DTSS) during the acute phase. Additionally, an animal model of PA-induced SOS was established through the administration of monocrotaline.
RESULTS: Fourteen consecutive patients with SOS who had adequate liver biopsy specimens obtained during recovery were identified. During convalescence, most laboratory and imaging findings, such as the map-like enhancement observed on computed tomography, also disappeared. However, histopathological analysis revealed a distinct shift from hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cell injury in the acute phase to portal tract abnormalities, primarily characterized by portal vein stricture, in the recovery phase. These pathological changes were corroborated in our animal model.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that both patients with PA-induced SOS and rats in the convalescent stage may exhibit porto-sinusoidal vascular disease-like changes. Regular follow-up and dynamic pathological assessment are therefore recommended to facilitate the early detection of potential signs of portal hypertension.

Title: Applications of artificial intelligence in personalized nutrition interventions.
Abstract: Unhealthy dietary patterns remain a major modifiable contributor to the global burden of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, individuals can respond markedly differently to identical foods, limiting the effectiveness of one-size-fits-all dietary guidance. This review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to personalized nutrition interventions across three interconnected layers. At the biological level, inter-individual variability can be characterized by three mechanistic dimensions: nutrigenomic variation, which influences nutrient metabolism and disease susceptibility; metabolomic biomarkers, which objectively capture dietary exposure and early metabolic alterations; and the gut microbiome, which bidirectionally mediates diet-host interactions. At the technological level, AI integrates these dimensions into multimodal digital profiles. Machine learning models predict individual postprandial glycemic and lipemic responses, with reported correlations of up to r = 0.77 in large cohorts; deep learning and computer vision automate dietary assessment; natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) support nutrition counseling; knowledge graphs enable constraint-aware food recommendations; and digital-twin and adaptive closed-loop systems incorporating continuous glucose monitoring and wearable-device data support real-time nutritional interventions. However, the strength of clinical evidence varies across disease domains. Glycemic management in T2DM and prediabetes currently has the most mature randomized controlled trial evidence: an AI-enabled personalized intervention combining algorithmic dietary personalization with CGM-linked feedback improved glycemic endpoints compared with a Mediterranean diet, while a fully automated AI-delivered diabetes prevention program achieved outcomes non-inferior to those of human coaching. In obesity, cardiovascular disease, oncology, and gastrointestinal disorders, the evidence remains mixed or preliminary. Clinical translation also faces substantial challenges, including biased and inconsistently standardized dietary and multi-omics data; the underrepresentation of non-European populations, which limits model generalizability and raises concerns about health equity; limited model explainability; privacy and data-governance challenges; immature regulatory pathways for adaptive software as a medical device; and specific risks associated with LLMs, such as hallucinated or guideline-discordant dietary advice. AI-enabled personalized nutrition is therefore progressing from proof of concept toward clinical translation. Realizing its potential equitably will require multi-ethnic nutrition-omics cohorts, privacy-preserving multicenter collaboration, dietitian-led human-AI collaboration, and lifecycle safety governance for generative models.

Title: New insights into the gut-heart axis: microbial metabolite biomarkers, multi-omics, and engineered bacterial delivery systems.
Abstract: Despite rapid growth in gut-heart axis research, clinical translation remains limited. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing recent evidence on microbiota-derived metabolites, biomarkers, multi-omics workflows, and engineered bacterial interventions in cardiovascular disease (CVD). We examine how TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine exert context-dependent cardiovascular effects, and why functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures. We then evaluate multi-omics strategies, metagenomics, metabolomics, proteomics, single-cell and spatial omics, and bioinformatics integration, for causal inference and biomarker validation. Finally, we assess engineered bacterial delivery systems, including gene circuit design, colonization control, biocontainment, and safety, and outline short-, medium-, and long-term milestones for clinical translation, cost-effectiveness, and intellectual property. The key takeaway is that precision microbiome medicine in CVD will require standardized assays, prospective validation, robust regulatory pathways, and equitable commercialization. By linking mechanistic insights with translational requirements, this review provides a framework for developing microbiome-targeted diagnostics and therapeutics in CVD.

Title: Comparison of indomethacin and nifedipine regarding ductus arteriosus Doppler findings after laser therapy for monochorionic diamniotic twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indomethacin is administered to reduce preterm labor after fetoscopic laser photocoagulation (FLP) of placental anastomoses.
OBJECTIVE: To compare ductus arteriosus (DA) Doppler findings in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies complicated by twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome following FLP between cases treated with indomethacin and those treated with nifedipine.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data of 86 pregnant women aged 17-41 yr who underwent FLP in Shariati hospital, Tehran, Iran from October 2024-November 2025 were extracted from medical records and then followed up. In the study, based on pulse rate, the cases were placed in one of 2 groups: nifedipine (pulse rate < 100) and indomethacin (pulse rate > 100) for 48 hr. In cases receiving indomethacin, 6 cases developed DA constriction. A comprehensive fetal echocardiography was performed to assess the status of the DA before and after FLP.
RESULTS: Peak systolic velocity was higher in both donor (145.7 ± 32.2, p = 0.012) and recipient twins (147.2 ± 23.6, p = 0.010) in the constricted group compared with the non-constricted groups. In recipient twins, end-diastolic velocity mean was also significantly increased (32.0 in the constricted, 19.9 in the indomethacin, and 18.7 in the nifedipine group, p = 0.012), while pulsatility index mean was significantly lower in the constricted group (1.8, 2.6, 2.5, respectively, p = 0.010).
CONCLUSION: DA constriction is associated with significant changes in blood flow indices, a higher incidence of right ventricular dysfunction, and a greater prevalence of valvular regurgitation. In this study, fetal DA constriction resolved during the short-term follow-up period.

Title: Association Between Cardiovascular Comorbidities and Clinical Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized for AECOPD.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore the association of cardiovascular disease (CVD) count and combinations with prolonged length of stay (LOS) and 1-year acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD)-related readmission among patients hospitalized for AECOPD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included 3684 admissions from 2281 patients with AECOPD between 2015 and 2024, without adjustment for baseline COPD severity. The assessed CVDs were hypertension (HTN), ischemic heart disease (IHD), arrhythmia, heart failure (HF), and peripheral arterial disease (PAD). The primary outcome was prolonged LOS, defined as a hospital stay of ≥14 days. Generalized estimating equation logistic regression models and Cox models with patient-level clustering were used to evaluate prolonged LOS and 1-year AECOPD-related readmission, respectively. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the findings for prolonged LOS.
RESULTS: At least one CVD was present in 71.7% of admissions. After full adjustment, 2 CVDs (odds ratio [OR]: 1.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.18-2.16) and ≥3 CVDs (OR: 1.95; 95% CI: 1.30-2.93) were associated with prolonged LOS (P for trend <0.001). The adjusted hazard ratios for 1-year AECOPD-related readmission were 1.38, 1.42, and 1.68 for 1, 2, and ≥3 CVDs, respectively (P for trend = 0.006). HTN + IHD + PAD showed the strongest association with prolonged LOS (OR: 2.53; 95% CI: 1.25-5.12). HTN + Arrhythmia was associated with both prolonged LOS (OR: 1.83; 95% CI: 1.15-2.92) and readmission (hazard ratio: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.04-2.45). Associations of CVD count with prolonged LOS remained generally consistent in subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Increasing CVD count was associated with progressively higher risks of prolonged LOS and 1-year AECOPD-related readmission, with the association with prolonged LOS becoming evident from two coexisting CVDs. Associations with these outcomes varied across CVD combinations, suggesting that both CVD count and combination may help identify patients at increased risk of adverse hospital and post-discharge outcomes.

Title: Multimodal investigation of the association between bevacizumab and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and severe condition that may be associated with exposure to certain drugs. Bevacizumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting vascular endothelial growth factor, has been classified as having a possible association with PAH, but data remain scarce. This study aimed to assess the potential link between bevacizumab exposure and PAH through complementary clinical, medico-administrative and pharmacovigilance databases.
METHODS: We performed a multimodal investigation combining: 1) case identification from the French Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) Registry, 2) a population-based cohort analysis using the French National Health Data System (Système National des Données de Santé (SNDS)) and 3) a disproportionality analysis in the World Health Organization pharmacovigilance database (VigiBase). Clinical, haemodynamic and exposure data were reviewed in the French PH Registry; prevalence of PAH in patients exposed to bevacizumab was computed in the SNDS; and disproportionality analyses (information component (IC) values) were calculated in VigiBase.
RESULTS: Seven cases of PAH temporally associated with bevacizumab were identified in the French PH Registry, most displaying predisposing conditions (BMPR2 mutation, portal hypertension or COPD). In the SNDS cohort of 9964 PAH patients, 30 had prior bevacizumab exposure, with no increased incidence compared to the general population. In VigiBase, 21 PAH cases were reported with bevacizumab, yielding a modest disproportionality signal only under broad definitions (IC 0.4 (95% credibility interval 0.1-0.6)).
CONCLUSIONS: Across complementary data sources, there was no evidence of a causal association between exposure to bevacizumab and the development of PAH in adults. However, the effect of bevacizumab as a secondary trigger in predisposed individuals cannot be definitely or completely excluded.

Title: Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery in acute settings: state-of-the art.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Operating in acute surgical settings is significantly different from elective surgery. One aspect is the complexity of acutely ill or injured patients with abnormal physiology, unoptimized comorbidities, and unplanned interventions. Traditional visual and tactile assessments of the surgical field anatomy and tissue viability have documented limitations. The need for integrated technology to augment such assessments is described. Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery (ICG-FGS) is a promising tool, given its history, safety, low cost, and accumulated experience in elective settings for many surgeries, to help transform precision surgery into acute settings (trauma and emergency surgery). An updated review is needed based on new evidence outlining the current landscape of ICG in acute settings.
METHODS: We performed a comprehensive review of literature update in the last two decades through June 2026, covering PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and published societal guidelines, including, but not limited to, the World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) consensus position paper and the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons (SAGES) review.
RESULTS: ICG is applicable across the full spectrum of acute surgical care, classified under two principal functions: anatomical mapping (biliary, ureteric, thoracic duct, and vascular structures) and perfusion assessment (bowel and mesenteric ischemia, anastomotic perfusion, pancreatic necrosis, burns, soft tissue, extremity trauma, and organ injury). Emerging and less commonly reported applications include necrotizing fasciitis debridement guidance, traumatic brain injury monitoring, penetrating abdominal trauma, gonadal torsion, fistula detection, damage control surgery, and AI-augmented quantitative fluorescence. The WSES consensus and SAGES meta-analysis provided strong prospective validation to date regarding anastomotic leakage reduction. Current gaps include the absence of standardized dosing protocols in acute settings, limited randomized data, and the subjectivity inherent to qualitative fluorescence interpretation.
CONCLUSIONS: ICG fluorescence-guided surgery is a safe, low-cost, and rapidly deployable adjunct for emergency surgery. Its breadth of applicability warrants wider consideration and integration into acute surgical workflows to inform surgical decision making based specific considerations including specific indications, evidence support, equipment availability, local expertise, workflow readiness and clinical judgement. Standardized protocols, prospective trials, objective and AI-powered quantification are the research priorities to further clarify its practical role.

Title: Application of AI-assisted compressed sensing cine sequence in the assessment of cardiac function in children with Kawasaki disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is an important tool for assessing the cardiac structure and function in Kawasaki disease. To perform a prospective analysis comparing the newly developed temporal artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted compressed sensing cine (ACS-cine) and conventional cine (Conv-cine) in the assessment of cardiac function in Kawasaki disease patients.
METHODS: This study included 45 patients (35 males), who were scanned using both ACS-cine and Conv-cine sequences. Left and right ventricular ejection fractions (LVEF and RVEF), left and right ventricular end-systolic volumes (LVESV and RVESV), and left and right ventricular end-diastolic volumes (LVEDV and RVEDV) were measured. The image quality and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of the two methods were also assessed.
RESULTS: The mean acquisition time of ACS-cine was significantly shorter than that of Conv-cine (17.18±2.45 vs. 251.12±38.01 seconds, P<0.05). In terms of cardiac function measurements, the median LVEF measured by Conv-cine was higher than that of ACS-cine (63.0% vs. 61.0%, P<0.05), while median LVESV was lower in Conv-cine than in ACS-cine (26.5 vs. 27.9 mL/m2, P<0.05). The image quality score of ACS-cine was slightly higher than that of Conv-cine (4.41±0.50 vs. 3.87±0.65, P<0.001). The inter-observer consistency was almost perfect for both ACS-cine (ICC: 0.882-0.978) and Conv-cine (ICC: 0.952-0.991).
CONCLUSIONS: ACS-cine technology demonstrates significant time efficiency advantages in CMR with satisfactory image quality, although there are statistically significant differences in the measurement of certain cardiac function parameters (LVEF and LVESV) compared to Conv-cine.

Title: Preoperative antiplatelet strategies and coronary artery bypass graft outcomes: bleeding and cardiovascular events in 41,696 patients with acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study wasto evaluate the clinical effects of preoperative antiplatelet therapy (APT) discontinuation timing on major bleeding and adverse cardiac events in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from Fuwai Cardiac Surgery Database (FCSD), specifically from 41,689 patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing isolated CABG (2009-2019). A comparison was conducted between 10,739 patients treated with continuation APT (AP group; discontinued ≤7 days preoperation; including aspirin alone, clopidogrel alone, or aspirin + clopidogrel) and 30,950 patients with discontinuation therapy (NAP group; >7 days preoperation). Major bleeding events were defined according to the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium-CABG criteria. Composite adverse events (30-day all-cause mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, and acute renal failure) were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was applied to estimate effects.
RESULTS: Adverse cardiac events occurred in 7.8% of patients in the AP group and 9.1% in the NAP group (P<0.001), but there was no difference in the incidence of major bleeding events. Multivariable analysis showed that continuation therapy significantly decreased the risk of adverse cardiac events [odds ratio (OR) 0.832; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.754-0.918; P<0.001] without increasing the risk of major bleeding events (OR 1.006; 95% CI: 0.926-1.093; P=0.88). Subgroup analysis identified certain strategies for reducing adverse events without bleeding.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative continued APT significantly reduces the risk of 30-day adverse cardiac events post-CABG without increasing the risk of major bleeding. Optimal strategies include clopidogrel alone (discontinued <3 days preoperatively) and dual-antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel discontinued 5-7 days preoperatively).

Title: Discrepancy Between Preoperative and Intraoperative Central Corneal Epithelial Thickness During Alcohol-Assisted PRK.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the agreement between preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT)-derived central corneal epithelial thickness (CET) and an intraoperative epithelial thickness estimate derived from optical coherence pachymetry (OCP) during alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy (PRK).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 116 eyes of 58 consecutive patients who underwent bilateral myopic alcohol-assisted PRK between June 2020 and October 2021. Preoperative CET was assessed using anterior-segment OCT. The OCP-derived intraoperative epithelial thickness estimate was calculated as the difference between total corneal pachymetry readings obtained immediately before and after epithelial removal. Demographic, preoperative clinical, and refractive data, as well as intraoperative laser parameters, were collected.
RESULTS: Mean age was 26.31 ± 7.44 years (range, 18-45), and 63.8% of patients were female. Mean sphere and spherical equivalent were -3.49 ± 1.63D and -3.16 ± 1.63D, respectively. Mean preoperative OCT-derived CET was 53.2 ± 3.5  μm (range, 42-69  μm), whereas the mean OCP-derived intraoperative CET was significantly higher at 59.8 ± 14.8  μm (range, 21-99  μm; p < 0.0001). This discrepancy was consistent in both eyes of each patient. The intraoperative estimate exceeded the preoperative OCT-derived CET in 73.3% of eyes. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated poor agreement between the two approaches, with wide limits of agreement from -15.7  μm to +34.8  μm. Preoperatively, 98.3% of eyes had CET values within the 40-60-μm range, compared with 44.8% of the OCP-derived intraoperative estimates. The difference between measurements significantly correlated with preoperative corneal thickness (r = 0.45, p < 0.001) and intraoperative CET (r = 0.97, p < 0.0001) but not refractive error or intraoperative and environmental parameters.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative OCT-derived CET and OCP-derived intraoperative CET demonstrate a systematic discrepancy and poor agreement during alcohol-assisted PRK. The intraoperative estimates were higher on average and substantially more variable than preoperative OCT measurements. These differences may have implications for surface ablation procedures, particularly transepithelial PRK, in which an assumed epithelial thickness profile is incorporated into treatment planning.

Title: Short-term clinical outcomes of nasoduodenal tube versus feeding jejunostomy after minimally invasive esophagectomy: a retrospective cohort study with exploratory microbiome analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophagectomy remains an effective treatment for esophageal cancer but is associated with severe postoperative complications, in which nutritional status plays a critical role. The optimal route for enteral feeding remains uncertain. To address this uncertainty, we compared the short-term clinical outcomes of the two approaches and exploratorily analyzed the differences in gut microbiota.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients who underwent minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) between July 2018 and June 2021. Primary outcomes were surgery-related complications (including anastomotic leakage, anastomotic stenosis, pneumonia, respiratory failure, cardiac events, chylothorax, intestinal fistula and bowel obstruction) and catheter-related outcomes (including occlusion, accidental removal, displacement and retention time). Baseline data were extracted from medical records. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to control for potential confounders. Intestinal fluid and fecal samples were collected after enteral nutrition for 16S ribosomal DNA (16S rDNA) sequencing.
RESULTS: After PSM, a total of 381 patients (nasoduodenal tube: 282; feeding jejunostomy: 153) was finally included. The feeding jejunostomy group exhibited a higher incidence of pneumonia (21.49% vs. 33.99%, P=0.007), respiratory failure (3.07% vs. 13.07%, P<0.001), anastomotic stenosis (1.32% vs. 5.23%, P=0.03) and bowel obstruction (0% vs. 2.16%, P=0.03). Nasoduodenal tube placement was associated with more accidental removal (13.16% vs. 0.65%, P<0.001) and catheter displacement (13.60% vs. 6.54%, P=0.03). The catheter retention time {37 [interquartile range (IQR): 15-40] days vs. 39 (IQR: 37-42) days, P<0.001} was also shorter in nasoduodenal tube group.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, nasoduodenal tube placement was associated with a higher incidence of catheter-related complications, whereas feeding jejunostomy was linked to more surgery-related complications. Nasoduodenal tube placement also showed potential functional advantages for the gut microbiome. However, future multi-center randomized controlled trials are still needed to minimize potential confounders and validate the differences between the two enteral nutrition routes.

Title: Associated factors for unfavorable prognosis in neonates with septic shock.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal septic shock represents a life-threatening complication of neonatal sepsis associated with substantial in-hospital mortality. Conventional diagnostic criteria only detect shock at the decompensated stage, which inevitably delays optimal treatment. This study aimed to identify independent predictors associated with adverse outcomes in neonates with septic shock and evaluate the predictive performance of combined early laboratory biomarkers and point-of-care cardiac ultrasound parameters.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was performed on 98 neonates diagnosed with septic shock admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of Chengdu Women's and Children's Central Hospital from January 2024 to December 2025. Patients were stratified into a favorable prognosis group (n=67) and an unfavorable prognosis group (n=31) based on discharge outcomes. Perinatal baseline data, initial laboratory tests and bedside critical cardiac ultrasound measurements were compared between groups. Univariate analyses followed by backward stepwise binary logistic regression were used to screen independent prognostic predictors, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to quantify predictive efficacy.
RESULTS: Compared with patients with favorable outcomes, neonates with poor prognosis exhibited lower gestational age, birth weight and Apgar scores, elevated serum interleukin-6 (IL-6), myoglobin (MYO) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I; reduced serum albumin and calcium, as well as increased serum potassium. Cardiac ultrasound revealed significantly decreased velocity-time integral (VTI), cardiac output (CO) and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) in the unfavorable prognosis group (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified gestational age, VTI and TAPSE as independent protective factors, while elevated IL-6 served as an independent predictor for adverse prognosis (P<0.05). ROC analysis demonstrated that TAPSE yielded the highest area under the curve (AUC =0.857), followed by VTI (AUC =0.785), gestational age (AUC =0.739) and IL-6 (AUC =0.716). The combined four-marker model achieved an AUC of 0.905, which outperformed all individual indicators.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower gestational age, elevated IL-6, and reduced VTI and TAPSE independently associated with poor prognosis in neonates with septic shock. Integrated assessment combining perinatal characteristics, admission inflammatory biomarkers and bedside cardiac ultrasound enables identification of high-risk infants, and may facilitate risk stratification for neonatal septic shock.

Title: Liposomal bupivacaine versus ropivacaine thoracic paravertebral block for thoracoscopic atrial septal defect repair: analgesic efficacy and cardiac biomarker outcomes in a single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracoscopic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair, although minimally invasive, can cause substantial postoperative pain. Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) provides effective chest wall analgesia, and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), a long-acting local anesthetic with sustained release, may prolong analgesic duration. We investigated whether ultrasound-guided TPVB using long-acting LB improves postoperative analgesia without compromising cardiovascular safety compared with ropivacaine (RP).
METHODS: This randomized, assessor-blinded trial enrolled 94 patients undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, who were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ultrasound-guided TPVB with either LB or RP. Eligibility criteria included age 18-55 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) II-III, New York Heart Association (NYHA) II-III, and ejection fraction (EF) >50%. Randomization was computer-generated with sealed envelopes. Safety monitoring included continuous electrocardiography (ECG) for arrhythmias, with Clavien-Dindo grading and Naranjo causality assessment. The primary endpoint was the numerical rating scale (NRS, 0-10) pain score during coughing at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included NRS scores at other time points, 72-h opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME), time to first rescue analgesia, extended analgesia outcomes [postoperative days 4-7 (POD4-POD7)], perioperative hemodynamics, postoperative recovery, cardiac/inflammatory biomarker trajectories, and adverse events (with postoperative arrhythmias analyzed separately).
RESULTS: Baseline demographic, clinical, and intraoperative variables were well-balanced between groups (all P>0.05). Compared with RP, LB was associated with lower NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing from extubation through 72 h (all P<0.05), including the primary endpoint at 24 h. LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2500112278, retrospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on November 12, 2025.

Title: Associated factors for in-hospital mortality in patients with fulminant myocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fulminant myocarditis (FM) progresses rapidly and carries high all-cause in-hospital mortality. Patients in the early phase often develop cardiogenic shock and malignant ventricular arrhythmias, with widely varying mortality rates reported across studies. Existing single-center cohorts yield conflicting prognostic findings with marked cross-cohort heterogeneity, and no standardized meta-analysis with GRADE certainty grading has been published to guide risk stratification. This meta-analysis pooled prognostic associations of all-cause in-hospital mortality in FM to inform acute risk evaluation and personalized care.
METHODS: Eleven Chinese and English electronic databases were searched from database establishment through June 2025. Eligible studies were observational cohorts reporting prognostic associations of all-cause in-hospital mortality among FM patients. Two independent reviewers completed screening, data extraction and quality assessment separately. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and AHRQ checklist were adopted to evaluate methodological quality. Pooled analyses were performed via the statsmodels package in Python, and the GRADE framework was applied to rate the certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: 26 retrospective cohort studies with 4,890 FM patients were enrolled. Ten potential factors were meta-analyzed, of which six showed statistically significant associations with in-hospital mortality (P < 0.05), including age (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.02-1.04), cardiac arrest or CPR (OR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.49-4.44), lactate (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.00-1.16), cTnI (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), LVEF (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.90-0.97), and intravenous immunoglobulin therapy (OR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.02-0.86). CK-MB, serum creatinine, total bilirubin, and VT/VF showed no statistically significant association (all P > 0.05). GRADE evidence ratings indicated low-certainty evidence for age and cTnI, and very-low-certainty evidence for the remaining significant factors. Sensitivity analyses indicated unstable pooled estimates for lactate and intravenous immunoglobulin therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Four factors showed positive associations with elevated all-cause in-hospital mortality. LVEF was inversely associated with mortality, whereas the inverse association for IVIG represents a fragile treatment-related signal. These findings may inform acute risk screening, but most associations were supported by low or very low certainty evidence and should not be interpreted as causal. All included data were derived from retrospective cohorts. Standardized multicenter prospective studies are required to verify these prognostic associations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399446, identifier CRD420261399446.

Title: Peri-interventional neutrophil extracellular traps and immune surveillance in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and recurrence after liver resection or thermal ablation.
Abstract: Recurrence remains common after curative-intent liver resection or thermal ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). These interventions transiently remodel the hepatic and treatment-bed immune microenvironment through overlapping but distinct processes, including tissue injury, vascular and coagulation activation, neutrophil recruitment, and, particularly during resection, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion. We organize the evidence using a peri-interventional two-component heuristic: chronic liver disease and tumor-associated inflammation may shape baseline susceptibility, whereas acute treatment injury may trigger intervention-specific neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) accumulation. Experimental studies across liver-intervention and cross-cancer models link NETs to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity, tumor-cell retention, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and metabolic adaptation. Patient-linked evidence remains limited and largely associative; much of the mechanistic framework therefore relies on colorectal liver metastasis and cross-cancer models. Translational studies should distinguish monitoring, pharmacodynamic, prognostic, and predictive applications and prioritize serial MPO-DNA as the best-supported circulating peri-interventional candidate, with NE-DNA or H3Cit-based measures as supportive assays and spatial validation where feasible. Candidate preclinical approaches include limiting NET formation, degrading established NET structures, and disrupting NET-target-cell signaling. NET-checkpoint combinations remain preclinical hypotheses, particularly because current phase III adjuvant ICI studies have not established postoperative HCC benefit. Because NET and neutrophil functions are context dependent, prospective studies should define intervention-specific NET kinetics, immune correlates, target engagement, recurrence phenotype, and safety.

Title: Comparative efficacy of digital health intervention delivery modalities on quality of life, anxiety, and depression in coronary heart disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonadherence to traditional cardiac rehabilitation and persistent psychological distress among patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) severely undermine desired therapeutic outcomes. Digital health interventions (DHIs) emerge as promising strategies to effectively tackle this adherence and mental health issue remotely.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to conduct a network meta-analysis (NMA) to compare and rank the comparative efficacy of various DHI delivery modalities in improving quality of life (QoL), anxiety, and depression among patients with CHD.
METHODS: A systematic search strategy was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane, CNKI, VIP, WanFang, and SinoMed databases to search for randomized controlled trials (RCTs)published from their inception to February 1,2026.We carried out a frequentist NMA using Stata 18.0to compare the efficacy of various DHIs against standard care. The quality of literature was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version2.0).The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework, and interventions were ranked utilizing the surface under the cumulative ranking (SUCRA)curve.
RESULTS: A total of 44RCTs involving 8,495 patients were enrolled. The NMA revealed that for improving QoL, telephone follow-up (standardized mean difference 2.98, 95%CI 1.75-4.20) and social media (SMD 1.13, 95%CI 0.42-1.84) were statistically superior to usual care. Notably, telephone follow-up, with a SUCRA of 99.5%, appeared to be the most effective option. Regarding psychological outcomes, web-based platforms demonstrated the highest probability of being the best intervention for reducing both anxiety (SMD -1.56,95%CI-2.34 to -0.79;SUCRA 98.6%) and depression (SMD-1.07,95%CI-1.94to-0.20;SUCRA 91.4%).Safety analyses showed interactive modalities significantly reduced adverse events, whereas one-way SMS carried a significantly higher risk than interactive telephone support(OR 3.38,95%CI 1.13-10.13).
CONCLUSIONS: The research suggests that telephone follow-up ranked highest among the included studies for improving short-term QoL, while web-based platforms showed a high probability of being effective for alleviating long-term anxiety and depression. However, these rankings should be interpreted cautiously, as intervention content, duration, and patient populations varied considerably across trials, and the small number of studies for certain modalities limits the robustness of direct comparisons. Social media interventions also emerged as a versatile option with benefits across all three outcomes, though their modest effect sizes warrant further optimization of engagement strategies. Passive SMS interventions present potential safety concerns, as their unidirectional nature may attenuate timely symptom recognition and delay appropriate care-seeking-a hypothesis supported by their significantly higher adverse event rates compared with interactive modalities. These results provide crucial evidence-based support for healthcare providers to tailor specific DHIs to individual patient needs.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261380157.

Title: Albuminuria is associated with higher turnover-related bone histomorphometric indices in chronic kidney disease stages 3-4.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biological determinants of bone turnover in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain incompletely understood. Although albuminuria is an established marker of kidney damage and predictor of renal and cardiovascular outcomes, its relationship with bone remodeling, as assessed by quantitative bone histomorphometry, has not previously been investigated.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional study of 56 adults with CKD stages 3-4 who underwent transiliac bone biopsy with quantitative histomorphometry following double tetracycline labeling. Associations between 24-h urinary albumin excretion and individual bone histomorphometric parameters were evaluated using multivariable linear regression. Models were adjusted for age, sex, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23).
RESULTS: In multivariable analyses, higher 24-h urinary albumin excretion was associated with a histomorphometric pattern consistent with increased bone turnover, reflected by greater bone formation and cell surface indices. Specifically, log₁₀-transformed urinary albumin excretion was associated with higher bone formation rate (B = 0.295, 95% CI 0.088 to 0.501; P = 0.008), osteoblast surface (B = 0.588, 95% CI 0.187 to 0.988; P = 0.005) and osteoclast surface (B = 0.464, 95% CI 0.041 to 0.887; P = 0.033). Associations with mineralization-related parameters and bone volume were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CKD stages 3-4, higher urinary albumin excretion was independently associated with quantitative histomorphometric indices of higher bone turnover. These findings suggest that albuminuria may mark a bone remodeling phenotype not fully captured by eGFR, iPTH, and FGF23. Larger prospective studies are needed to define the biological basis and clinical implications of this association.

Title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting flexible bronchoscopy utilization in children with lobar pneumonia caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The recent resurgence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) pneumonia has increased the number of children with lobar pneumonia who may receive flexible bronchoscopy (FB), yet the decision to perform FB remains subjective, and no quantitative tool exists for this specific high-risk subgroup. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a nomogram to predict FB utilization in children with MP-related lobar pneumonia using routine admission indicators to support real-time bedside decision-making.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 345 children (aged 1 month-18 years) with serology-confirmed MP-related lobar pneumonia (January 2022-March 2025); those with congenital heart disease, immunodeficiency, or plastic bronchitis were excluded. Patients were divided into FB (n=171) and non-FB (n=174) groups based on whether FB was performed. Laboratory predictors were restricted to values obtained within 72 hours of admission and before the FB decision. FB was recommended if symptoms or signs persisted after ≥72 hours of standard therapy. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors, and a nomogram was constructed and internally validated by 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Viral coinfection [odds ratio (OR) =23.271, 95% confidence interval (CI): 9.299-64.900, P<0.001] was the strongest independent risk factor for FB utilization, while bacterial coinfection (OR =0.215, 95% CI: 0.088-0.507, P<0.001) and male sex (OR =0.146, 95% CI: 0.061-0.313, P<0.001) were independent protective factors. The nomogram incorporating these six variables demonstrated moderate discrimination (apparent AUC =0.741, 95% CI: 0.689-0.792; cross-validated AUC =0.705) and good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.56). At the optimal cutoff value of 0.56, the model had a sensitivity of 51.5% and a specificity of 85.1%. DCA demonstrated net clinical benefit over a "treat-all" strategy within a threshold probability range of 0.1-0.3.
CONCLUSIONS: The nomogram showed modest ability to predict FB use in this single-center cohort, but its clinical utility for identifying children with lobar pneumonia caused by MP who truly require FB remains uncertain.

Title: Echocardiography-based multimodal models for thromboembolic risk prediction in atrial fibrillation: a narrative review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes, stroke, vascular disease, age 65-74 years, sex category (CHA2DS2-VASc) score is fundamental for assessing thromboembolic risk in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, its limitations arise from relying solely on clinical parameters, without considering individual cardiac structural and functional changes. This review aims to explore the development and implementation of multimodal risk prediction models that integrate echocardiographic parameters with clinical data and biomarkers to achieve a more precise and individualized risk assessment.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted using relevant electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, Web of Science and Embase) to identify studies focusing on echocardiographic parameters, AF, and thromboembolic risk prediction models published up to May 2026.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Echocardiographic parameters evaluating the left atrium and left atrial appendage (LAA; size, function, and morphology) have emerged as significant predictors of both prevalent thrombus formation and future thromboembolic events. This review details these key parameters and critically assesses various multimodal approaches, including those combining clinical-echocardiographic scores with artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. Importantly, these models demonstrate enhanced predictive accuracy for specific clinical endpoints over traditional clinical scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Utilizing a multimodal approach provides a promising supplementary tool for refined risk assessment, rather than replacing guideline-based anticoagulation decisions. Future directions should focus on standardizing echocardiographic measurements, expanding the use of AI for automated analysis, and conducting prospective interventional trials to confirm clinical benefit.

Title: Applying Lifestyle Medicine to Improve Health Outcomes in People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.
Abstract: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) and autism spectrum disorder experience disproportionately high rates of chronic disease, often exacerbated by systemic care barriers. Despite these concerns, interventions for this population rarely target overall health and wellness and often rely on practices that can contribute to poor health outcomes. This retrospective review includes data collected at The Center for Discovery, a residential care program for people with severe and complex disabilities. This analysis evaluates health outcomes among 295 adults with I/DD, including autism, who received a comprehensive lifestyle medicine intervention. Prevalence rates of chronic conditions among those receiving the intervention were compared to national and New York State disability benchmarks. Results suggest an association with substantially lower prevalence of key conditions, including obesity, diabetes, and hypertension, with a median risk ratio of 0.325 (range: 0.23-0.76) compared to U.S. population benchmarks. These findings suggest that participation in an integrated lifestyle medicine model, SynergE6® Healthspan Model, could be associated with lower chronic disease prevalence among adults with I/DD. Because this was a retrospective observational study using external benchmark comparisons, prospective controlled studies are needed to determine whether these associations are causal.

Title: Health outcomes of U.S. active component service members working in high risk occupations for blast overpressure exposure: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: Active component military service members are exposed to increased risk of occupational blast overpressure (BOP) exposure during deployment as well as training. This retrospective cohort study examined the incidence of first-time diagnoses of traumatic brain injury (TBI), insomnia, migraine headache, depressive or anxiety disorders, noise-induced hearing injury (NIHI), and essential hypertension among active component service members (ACSMs) in the U.S. Army, Air Force, and Marine Corps. Incidence rates (IRs) were compared between ACSMs who served in occupations at high risk for BOP exposure (n=831,050) and those who never served in such occupations (n=2,229,594). Overall incidence of TBI was 243.8 per 10,000 person-years in the high-risk occupational cohort and 140.9 per 10,000 person-years in the low-risk occupational cohort. Incidence of NIHI was 342.7 and 218.1 per 10,000 person-years in the high- and low-risk cohorts, respectively. After adjusting for demographic and military characteristics, ACSMs in occupations with high risk of BOP experienced higher IRs of TBI (adjusted IR ratio [aIRR] 1.43; 95% CI 1.42, 1.44) and NIHI (aIRR 1.39; 95% CI 1.38, 1.40). Increasing time since entering the cohort was associated with a greater increase in migraine headache incidence among ACSMs in high-risk BOP occupations compared with those in low-risk occupations. Despite these differences, the distribution of disease burden categories from 2024 health care encounters was similar among cohorts. These findings emphasize the importance of mitigating occupational blast hazards and strengthening surveillance efforts to protect the long-term health of ACSMs. Adjusted IRs of TBI and NIHI were higher among service members in occupations at high risk for BOP exposure than among those who had never worked in such occupations. Increasing time in the cohort was associated with a greater increase in migraine headache incidence among service members in high-risk BOP occupations than among those in low-risk occupations.

Title: Eculizumab in rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis: a case-series report.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical outcomes and safety profile of eculizumab as adjunctive therapy in a case series of patients with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) due to anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) disease and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV).
METHODS: We reported 7 patients with AAV and 5 patients with anti-GBM disease who presented to our center between March 2025 and January 2026. All patients received eculizumab (900 mg, 1-4 doses) in addition to standard immunosuppressive therapy. Serum creatinine (Scr), urinary red blood cell (uRBC) count, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR), and dialysis dependence were assessed at baseline and at 3 months. Adverse events were monitored throughout follow-up.
RESULTS: In AAV patients, mean Scr decreased from 407.38 μmol/L to 231.27 μmol/L (p = 0.025), mean uRBC from 384.27/μL to 68.75/μL (p = 0.033), and mean UPCR from 2.20 g/g to 1.64 g/g (p = 0.179) at the 3rd month. In anti-GBM patients, mean Scr declined from 575.07 μmol/L to 263.80 μmol/L (p = 0.024), mean uRBC from 1648.60/μL to 461.92/μL (p = 0.132), and mean UPCR from 10.88 g/g to 3.75 g/g (p = 0.126). At baseline, 6 patients required renal replacement therapy, and after treatment, 4 became dialysis-independent. One AAV patient progressed to hemodialysis, and one anti-GBM patient remained dialysis-dependent. All anti-GBM antibodies and MPO-ANCA (except one patient) seroconverted to negative at month 3. During follow-up, only one case of COVID-19 infection and one oral ulcer were recorded; no severe infections occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this descriptive case series, we observed trends toward improved renal function and hematuria at 3 months in patients with severe RPGN who received eculizumab in addition to standard immunosuppression, with earlier initiation and milder baseline renal impairment appearing to correlate with more favorable outcomes. Nevertheless, the lack of a control group and the marked interpatient variability in baseline characteristics and concomitant therapies preclude any conclusion regarding a causal effect of eculizumab. Instead, these data serve as real-world observations that can generate hypotheses for future studies. Definitive evidence on the efficacy and safety of eculizumab in RPGN must await larger, prospective, controlled investigations.
Publication Types: Case Reports; Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Plasma p-tau181 moderates the association between ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk and mild cognitive impairment - HABS-HD.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study examined cross-sectional associations between ten-year American Heart Association (AHA) atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk and plasma Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarkers in relation to cognitive outcomes and to determine whether ASCVD risk modifies biomarker-cognition relationships.
METHODS: Baseline data were analyzed from cognitively unimpaired and mild cognitive impaired (MCI) participants enrolled in the Health and Aging Brain Study-Health Disparities (HABS-HD), a large, community-based cohort enriched for racial and ethnic diversity. Plasma biomarkers included amyloid-β42/40 (Aβ42/Aβ40), phosphorylated tau (p-tau181 and p-tau217), and neurofilament light (NfL). Ten-year ASCVD risk was calculated using pooled cohort equations. Multivariable logistic regression models examined associations of ten-year ASCVD risk and plasma biomarkers with MCI, while multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) Sum of Boxes scores. Separate models were constructed for Aβ42/40, p-tau217, p-tau181, NfL, and apolipoprotein (APOE) ε4 carrier status, and analyses were stratified by race and ethnicity. ASCVD × biomarker interaction terms were tested to evaluate effect modification.
RESULTS: Increased ten-year ASCVD risk was consistently associated with increased odds of MCI, ranging from OR = 2.62 (95% CI: 1.31-5.17) to OR = 4.22 (95% CI: 2.04-8.64), lower MMSE scores, ranging from β = -1.90 (95% CI: -2.62 to -1.18) to β = -2.56 (95% CI: -3.30 to -1.82), and increased CDR Sum of Boxes scores, ranging from β = 0.28 (95% CI: 0.09-0.46) to β = 0.39 (95% CI: 0.20-0.58). The ASCVD × p-tau181 interaction was significant for MCI (OR = 1.91; 95% CI: 1.26-2.95) and CDR Sum of Boxes (β = 0.27; 95% CI: 0.16-0.39). ASCVD associations with CDR Sum of Boxes ranged from β = 0.11 (95% CI: -0.08 to 0.30) to β = 0.24 (95% CI: 0.04-0.43) among non-Hispanic White participants, β = 0.80 (95% CI: 0.10-1.51) to β = 1.17 (95% CI: 0.49-1.86) among non-Hispanic Black participants, and β = 0.36 (95% CI: 0.08-0.65) to β = 0.52 (95% CI: 0.25-0.80) among Hispanic participants.
CONCLUSION: Greater ten-year ASCVD risk was consistently associated with cognitive impairment independent of plasma AD biomarkers, with evidence that p-tau181 modifies these associations and that their magnitude varies across racial and ethnic groups.

Title: Nonlinear and Vessel-Specific Association Between Coronary Artery Calcium Burden and Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography Underestimation of Coronary Stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) introduces substantial artifacts in coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Although calcification is classically associated with overestimation of stenosis severity, underestimation may be even more clinically hazardous because underestimation can lead to inappropriate deferral of revascularization. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the association between CAC burden and CCTA underestimation, with emphasis on vessel-specific anatomical heterogeneity.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 673 patients without known coronary artery disease who underwent both CCTA and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) within 90 days, yielding 2692 vessel observations. Underestimation was defined strictly at the vessel level as a CCTA stenosis grade lower than the corresponding ICA grade. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to characterize the nonlinear association between CAC burden and the risk of underestimation. Within-patient clustering across the left main (LM), left anterior descending (LAD), left circumflex (LCX), and right coronary artery (RCA) was accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEEs).
RESULTS: Any-vessel underestimation occurred in 389 patients (57.8%). Vessel-specific susceptibility varied markedly: LM, 3.0%; LAD, 27.9%; LCX, 29.3%; and RCA, 22.4%. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between total CAC score and patient-level underestimation in the fully adjusted model (p-overall = 0.014; p-nonlinear = 0.004), with an upward risk trajectory observed as calcification increased relative to the median reference of 301. GEE modeling confirmed that patient-level CAC burden independently predicted vessel-level underestimation (CAC ≥400 vs. 0: odds ratio, 2.01; 95% confidence interval, 1.20-3.36; p = 0.008), with a significant interaction between CAC and vessel territory (p < 0.001). A sensitivity analysis restricted to patients without any CCTA overestimation (n = 155) confirmed a robust nonlinear association between total CAC score and pure underestimation risk (p-overall = 0.012; p-nonlinear = 0.005), suggesting that concurrent overestimation noise partially obscures this dynamic risk trajectory in the full cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: The association between calcification burden and CCTA underestimation is nonlinear and strongly dependent on coronary territory. Since the RCS-derived odds ratio (OR) = 1, crossings depend on the median reference value (CAC = 301) and should be interpreted as markers of risk trajectory rather than absolute diagnostic cutoffs. Integrating total calcium burden with vessel-specific susceptibility may help mitigate the risk of missed severe stenosis on CCTA.

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for preoperative prediction of intraoperative hypothermia in gynecological laparoscopic surgery: a two-center cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypothermia (IOH, temperature <36.0 °C) is a common complication in gynecological laparoscopic surgery that leads to significant adverse outcomes that would benefit from preoperative risk prediction.
METHODS: We developed and compared two predictive models-a conventional multivariable logistic regression (LR) model and a gradient boosting machine (XGBoost) model-to preoperatively predict IOH based on 20 objectively measurable preoperative clinical variables that could be directly extracted from electronic health records (EHRs). The derivation cohort consisted of 460 cases from a tertiary care center in 2024, which were randomly divided into a training set (n = 322) and a test set (n = 138) at a 7:3 ratio. For external validation, we used an independent cohort of 183 cases from a second medical institution during the same period. Model performance was evaluated using metrics including the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method applied for feature importance analysis.
RESULTS: We initially analyzed 20 preoperative variables. The final model incorporated eight key indicators: body mass index (BMI), ASA physical status, fasting period, basal body temperature, estimated surgical duration, hypertension status, serum albumin level, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). The derivation cohort consisted of 460 patients, split into a training set (n = 322) and a test set (n = 138). An independent external validation cohort included 183 patients. By AUROC comparison, the XGBoost model outperformed the LR model in both the training set (0.933 vs. 0.891) and the external validation set (0.870 vs. 0.838), while performing slightly lower in the test set (0.821 vs. 0.865).
CONCLUSIONS: We developed and validated an interpretable XGBoost model using eight readily available preoperative clinical indicators. The model demonstrated good performance for the preoperative prediction of IOH in gynecological laparoscopic surgery, which may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and timely intervention.

Title: Achieved systolic blood pressure and cardiovascular outcomes in advanced chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) evidence for lower systolic blood pressure (SBP) targets is limited and guideline recommendations are conflicting. We investigated the association between achieved SBP and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in nephrology-referred patients with CKD.
METHODS: In this nationwide, observational cohort from the Swedish Renal Register-chronic kidney disease (SRR-CKD), we included adults with CKD stages 3-5 referred to nephrology outpatient clinics between 2006 and 2017. Mean office SBP during the first year was categorized in incrementally higher SBP groups with 130-<140 mmHg as reference. The primary outcome was MACE; secondary outcomes were its components and all-cause death, analyzed using cause-specific multivariable-adjusted flexible parametric survival models.
RESULTS: Among 23 317 patients (median age 72 years; 64% men; median estimated glomerular filteration rate (eGFR) 24 ml/min/1.73 m²), over a median follow-up of 2.5 years, 8556 (37%) experienced MACE and 7686 (33%) died. Compared with SBP 130-<140 mmHg, SBP 120-<130 mmHg was associated with lower risks of MACE [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 0.93, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.87-0.99] and all-cause mortality (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-0.99), whereas SBP ≥160 mmHg was associated with higher risks of MACE (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.28-1.49) and death (HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.20-1.38). MACE risk was nonproportional and declined over time in patients with SBP 100-<120 mmHg, demonstrating lower MACE risk compared to 130-<140 after 3 years. In continuous analyses, MACE risk was lowest around 125 mmHg and increased at higher SBP levels.
CONCLUSIONS: In nephrology-referred patients with advanced CKD, achieved SBP around 120-<130 mmHg (near 125 mmHg) was associated with the lowest cardiovascular and mortality risk, while SBP ≥140 mmHg, especially ≥160 mmHg, was consistently associated with higher MACE risk.

Title: Vascular access options for complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary interventions: contemporary strategies, trade-offs, and practical algorithms.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular access is an important component of CHIP planning that influences procedural feasibility, safety, and completeness. It affects bleeding and vascular complications, guide-catheter support, compatibility with intravascular imaging and calcium-modification devices, chronic total occlusion techniques, closure and bailout options, and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) planning. Contemporary CHIP populations are increasingly older or frail and more often have chronic kidney disease, peripheral artery disease, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, prior bypass surgery, calcification, or CTO; access choice should extend beyond radial vs. femoral.
SUMMARY: This review appraises proximal and distal radial, femoral, ulnar, and brachial access; sheathless, slender, and RailTracking strategies; large-bore femoral workflows; and access planning when MCS is considered. We discuss preprocedural arterial assessment, ultrasound and micropuncture, prior access footprint, closure feasibility, hostile femoral anatomy, alternative access, and complication prevention and rescue. The available literature supports a non-dogmatic approach in which access architecture is matched to patient vulnerability, arterial anatomy, lesion complexity, guide and device requirements, support needs, haemostasis feasibility, and bailout planning. Recent randomised evidence further reinforces selective rather than routine prophylactic MCS in nonemergent high-risk PCI.
CONCLUSIONS: Forearm access should remain central whenever it permits procedural success without compromising device delivery, imaging, guide support, or bailout flexibility. Femoral access remains indispensable when large-bore support, maximal guide stability, complex device delivery, or rapid escalation are anticipated. Within a comprehensive CHIP plan, the preferred access architecture is the smallest one that enables the intended revascularisation, safe haemostasis, and timely rescue.

Title: Residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk in statin-treated patients: mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and future directions-a scoping review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statins remain the cornerstone of pharmacological prevention for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) because of their proven ability to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). However, many patients continue to experience ASCVD events despite achieving guideline-recommended LDL-C targets with maximally tolerated statin therapy, highlighting the persistence of residual ASCVD risk. This scoping review synthesized current evidence on residual ASCVD risk in statin-treated patients, focusing on its epidemiology, underlying mechanisms, clinical evidence, therapeutic strategies beyond statins, and barriers to optimal risk reduction.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Electronic databases were systematically searched, yielding 1,240 records. After duplicate removal and screening, 195 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and 35 studies were included in the final qualitative synthesis. The included evidence comprised randomized controlled trials, observational cohort studies, registry-based investigations, and systematic and narrative reviews.
RESULTS: The included studies were synthesized into five major themes: epidemiology of residual ASCVD risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical evidence from landmark trials and real-world studies, therapeutic strategies beyond statins, and challenges limiting effective risk reduction. Evidence consistently demonstrated that residual ASCVD risk persists despite substantial LDL-C reduction because of multiple interacting factors, including elevated triglyceride-rich remnant lipoproteins, lipoprotein(a), persistent inflammation, metabolic comorbidities, vascular aging, treatment-implementation barriers, and behavioral factors. Landmark clinical trials, including IMPROVE-IT, FOURIER, ODYSSEY OUTCOMES, REDUCE-IT, CANTOS, LoDoCo2, and CLEAR Outcomes, demonstrated incremental cardiovascular benefit from combination lipid-lowering and selected anti-inflammatory therapies, while emerging therapies targeting lipoprotein(a), IL-6 signaling, and RNA-based pathways offer promising strategies for further reducing residual ASCVD risk.
CONCLUSION: Residual ASCVD risk remains a major challenge despite guideline-directed statin therapy. Effective risk reduction requires a comprehensive approach that extends beyond LDL-C lowering to include combination lipid-lowering therapy, inflammation-targeted interventions, lifestyle optimization, improved treatment adherence, and individualized risk assessment. Continued evaluation of emerging therapies and precision medicine approaches is essential to further reduce the global burden of ASCVD.

Title: Predictive value of combined estimated plasma volume status and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for cardiovascular mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction with heart failure.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are novel biomarkers reflecting hemodynamic load and systemic inflammatory immune status, respectively. This study aimed to explore the prognostic value of combined ePVS and NLR for cardiovascular mortality in patients with heart failure (HF) complicating acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study consecutively enrolled patients diagnosed with AMI complicated by HF at Putian University Affiliated Hospital from January 2020 to June 2024. Admission hemoglobin and hematocrit levels were used to calculate ePVS, while routine blood test parameters were applied to determine NLR. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular mortality within two years after AMI. Cox proportional hazards regression models were constructed to analyze the associations of ePVS and NLR with clinical endpoints. The predictive efficacy of single and combined ePVS and NLR was comprehensively evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: A total of 2046 patients were ultimately included. During a mean follow-up of 819 days, endpoint events occurred in 14.90% of the study population. Univariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS served as a strong risk factor for cardiovascular mortality (HR = 1.571, 95% CI: 1.502-1.642, P < 0.001). After adjusting for age, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and NLR, both ePVS (HR = 1.436, 95% CI: 1.370-1.505, P < 0.001) and NLR (HR = 1.330, 95% CI: 1.258-1.406, P < 0.001) remained independent predictors of cardiovascular mortality. The combined predictive model integrating ePVS and NLR exhibited significantly superior predictive performance compared with either biomarker alone (AUC: 0.794 for ePVS vs. 0.891 for ePVS + NLR, P < 0.001). Both NRI and IDI analyses further verified the significant improvement in predictive accuracy of the combined model (all P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: ePVS and NLR represent valuable prognostic biomarkers for cardiovascular mortality in AMI patients. The combination of ePVS and NLR significantly improves predictive performance and facilitates precise risk stratification.
