Title: Comparative efficacy of Traditional Chinese Medicine classical prescriptions for angina pectoris: a network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of classical prescriptions from Shang han Lun (Treatise on Febrile Diseases) and Jin gui Yao lue (Synopsis of the Golden Chamber) combined with conventional biomedicine in the treatment of angina pectoris of coronary heart disease.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eight commonly used Chinese and English databases were searched for relevant clinical studies published before 25 December 2024. Revman 5.4 and Stata14.0 software were used for data analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 131 studies involving 11,292 participants (5,660 in intervention groups and 5,632 in control groups) were included. Most classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed favorable associations with improvements in angina pectoris efficiency, electrocardiogram (ECG) efficiency, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome outcomes compared with conventional treatment alone. Subgroup analyses showed partially different patterns of relative efficacy among prescriptions, with LGZG demonstrating more consistent performance in stable angina pectoris, while other prescriptions showed variable rankings in unstable angina pectoris. For lipid-related and inflammatory outcomes, results were inconsistent across studies, and current evidence remains insufficient to support robust comparative conclusions among classical prescriptions. Regarding safety outcomes, GZFL combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed a relatively favorable safety profile, while other classical prescriptions demonstrated comparable rates of adverse events to conventional therapy.
CONCLUSION: Classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy may be associated with improvements in clinical outcomes of angina pectoris, with an overall acceptable safety profile observed across most intervention. However, due to limitations in study quality, heterogeneity, and indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further high-quality, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these observations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251029216.

Title: Association and discriminative value of insulin resistance surrogate markers for aortic stiffness in asymptomatic adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance surrogate markers, including the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, TyG-BMI, and TG/HDL-C ratio, have been associated with aortic stiffness in high-risk populations. Their comparative associations and incremental discrimination in asymptomatic adults remain unclear. We therefore compared these markers and evaluated a simplified model for cfPWV-defined aortic stiffness.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 654 asymptomatic adults aged ≥18 years who underwent routine health examinations at two tertiary medical centers. After exclusions, 457 participants formed the modeling cohort and 101 formed the external validation cohort. Aortic stiffness was defined as cfPWV ≥10 m/s. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate associations between the three surrogate markers and aortic stiffness. Restricted cubic spline regression assessed potential nonlinear associations. Incremental discrimination was evaluated using ΔAUC, NRI, and IDI. Six machine-learning models were compared, and the most interpretable model was evaluated in an independent institutional validation cohort.
RESULTS: Aortic stiffness was present in 32.8% (150/457) of the modeling cohort. After full adjustment, the TyG index was independently associated with aortic stiffness (per-SD OR = 3.44, P = 0.002), as were TG/HDL-C (OR = 3.11, P = 0.039) and, more weakly, TyG-BMI (OR = 1.52, P = 0.043). The model including TyG showed higher discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.014, DeLong P = 0.025) and reclassification (continuous NRI = 0.692 and IDI = 0.041; both P < 0.001) than the base model. A data-derived TyG cutoff of 8.68 was identified as a potential marker for exploratory risk stratification. The five-variable model, comprising age, MAP, diabetes mellitus, smoking, and TyG, yielded AUCs of 0.931 in the modeling cohort and 0.909 in the external validation cohort. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses showed similar patterns.
CONCLUSION: Among the three surrogate markers, the TyG index showed the strongest adjusted association with aortic stiffness and the greatest incremental discrimination beyond conventional clinical variables. The five-variable model showed good discrimination in an independent institutional validation cohort. However, these cross-sectional findings support only potential risk-stratification value and do not establish temporal sequence, causality, or clinical utility; prospective studies are required to assess broader generalizability.

Title: Development of a nomogram for predicting wall irregular pulsation and risk stratification in intracranial aneurysms.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurate rupture risk stratification for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs) presents clinical challenges. Aneurysm wall irregular pulsation is an imaging biomarker of aneurysm vulnerability. This study aims to develop a nomogram for predicting wall irregular pulsation and risk stratification in intracranial aneurysms.
METHODS: This was a consecutive cross-sectional observational study with prospective data collection for UIAs between 2017 and 2020. The irregular pulsation was defined as sequential morphological alterations observed in three or more consecutive phases by on four-dimensional CT angiography (4D-CTA). A generalized estimating equation (GEE) method identified independent predictors of the presence of wall irregular pulsation. A logistic regression-based predictive model was developed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: We included 202 patients with 262 unruptured aneurysms. Multivariable analysis revealed four independent predictors of the presence of wall irregular pulsation: aneurysm location at ACA/PCom/Posterior (OR: 2.17, 95% CI 1.21-3.88; p = 0.0099), presence of daughter sac (OR: 5.15, 95% CI 1.91-13.86; p = 0.001), aspect ratio (OR: 1.80, 95% CI 1.09-2.99; p = 0.022), and neck size (OR: 1.23, 95% CI 1.02-1.48; p = 0.030). The developed model demonstrated good discrimination, achieving a sensitivity of 88.5%, specificity of 71.2%, overall accuracy of 76.9%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.808 (95% CI, 0.704-0.913). Further validation using an independent cohort yielded comparable performance, with a sensitivity of 76.9%, specificity of 88.9%, overall accuracy of 81.8%, and an AUC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.694-1.000). A nomogram was constructed to visualize the model.
CONCLUSION: This study presents a logistic regression-based model for predicting aneurysm wall irregular pulsation. The nomogram visually assesses individualized risks, demonstrating potential for future clinical implementation in bedside decision-making.

Title: Parental obesity and offspring cardiometabolic trajectories from childhood to adulthood.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Parental obesity is a strong risk factor for childhood adiposity. However, evidence regarding its association with longitudinal cardiometabolic disease progression in offspring remains limited. We aimed to examine whether parental obesity is associated with adverse cardiometabolic trajectories in offspring from childhood to adulthood.
METHODS: We analyzed prospective data from the China Health and Nutrition Survey (1989-2015). Offspring aged ≥2 years were categorized according to parental overweight/obesity status: neither parent affected (Group 1, reference), only father affected (Group 2), only mother affected (Group 3), and both parents affected (Group 4). We used linear mixed-effects models with polynomial age terms to estimate longitudinal trajectories and annual changes in body mass index, waist circumference, and blood pressure. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess hazard ratios for incident overweight/obesity, central obesity, and hypertension.
RESULTS: Among 4,982 offspring, those with both parents affected (group 4) had the highest baseline levels; however, annual rates of increase were not consistently higher. Male offspring in group 4 had the highest risks for incident overweight/obesity (HR = 3.72; 95% CI, 1.73-7.99) and central obesity (HR = 2.46; 95% CI, 1.31-4.62); the association with hypertension was elevated but did not reach statistical significance (HR = 1.55; 95% CI, 0.86-2.77). Female offspring in group 4 had the highest risk for incident overweight/obesity (HR = 4.60; 95% CI, 1.93-10.94). Formal interaction tests for sex × parental obesity were not significant for any outcome (all P interaction > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Parental obesity, particularly when both parents are affected, is associated with higher baseline cardiometabolic risk levels and substantially higher disease risk in offspring, though the annual rates of increase do not consistently differ across groups. These findings underscore the family unit as a critical target for early preventive strategies.

Title: Perioperative temporary microaxial left ventricular assist device support in patients with low ejection fraction undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite advances in mechanical circulatory support (MCS), outcomes in high-risk coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with low ejection fraction (EF) remain unclear. We evaluate short-term outcomes associated with temporary microaxial flow pump (TMFP) support in high-risk patients undergoing CABG during the same hospitalization.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed 111 patients who underwent CABG with Impella 5.5 or LD TMFP support during the same hospitalization between April 2018 and January 2025. Patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were excluded. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and postoperative outcomes were collected. Statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.4.0 with significance defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The cohort (n = 111) had a mean age of 69 years and was 75% male (83/111). Comorbidities documented prior to index hospitalization included hypertension (85%, 94/111), diabetes mellitus (57%, 63/111), coronary artery disease (CAD) (47%, 52/111), and at least one prior cardiac surgery or intervention (31%, 34/111). Support was planned in 30% (33/111) of cases and unplanned in 70% (78/111). 30-day survival was 89.2% (99/111) and 1-year survival of 74.8% (83/111). No statistically significant differences in mortality were observed according to performance of concomitant procedures or operative time periods (2018-2020 vs. 2021-2025).
CONCLUSION: In high-risk low-EF patients undergoing CABG, TMFP support during the same hospitalization was associated with acceptable 30-day and 1-year survival outcomes among patients considered unsuitable for PCI and/or advanced therapies at the time of surgery. Mortality was not significantly different among patients undergoing concomitant procedures or between planned vs. unplanned TMFP placement. These findings support TMFP's growing role in complex coronary surgeries and warrant further studies to define optimal application and surgical candidacy.

Title: Residual risk persists in severely calcified lesions despite optimal stent expansion: a paradoxical finding from an IVUS-guided PCI cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary artery calcification (CAC) is associated with adverse events after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), traditionally attributed to inadequate stent expansion. Whether severe CAC confers residual risk despite optimal acute mechanical results remains unknown.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 709 patients who underwent pre-procedural intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) before PCI. Patients were classified as no calcification (n = 417), mild CAC (arc ≤180° or length ≤5 mm, n = 168), or severe CAC (arc >180° and length >5 mm, n = 124). The primary endpoint was clinically driven target vessel revascularization (TVR); the secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Post-PCI minimum stent area (MSA) and expansion index were compared across groups. Multivariable Cox regression using three prespecified adjustment models was performed.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 18.6 months, 57 patients (8.0%) experienced TVR and 122 (17.2%) experienced MACE. Post-PCI MSA (5.9 vs. 5.6 vs. 5.8 mm2; P = 0.286) and expansion index (0.89 vs. 0.88 vs. 0.88; P = 0.485) were comparable across groups, indicating acceptable acute stent expansion in severely calcified lesions. Nevertheless, severe CAC remained independently associated with increased TVR risk in the primary analysis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.51, 95% CI 1.33-4.74, P = 0.005), persisting after extended adjustment (aHR 2.61, P = 0.007) and after excluding rotational atherectomy (RA) cases (aHR 2.29, P = 0.018). The association between severe CAC and MACE was more modest (aHR 1.77, P = 0.014) and attenuated after extended adjustment (aHR 1.49, P = 0.119). Calcified nodules, present in 64.5% of severe CAC lesions, independently predicted TVR (aHR 3.04, P < 0.001). Mild CAC showed no significant risk elevation.
CONCLUSION: Severe CAC identifies a subgroup at persistently elevated risk for repeat revascularization despite achieving stent expansion comparable to non-calcified lesions, challenging the conventional paradigm linking calcification to adverse events solely through underexpansion.

Title: Three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction as a guideline-anchored framework for choosing between lung-sparing resection and image-guided ablation in deep subsolid pulmonary nodules: a thoracic surgeon's perspective.
Abstract: Low-dose computed tomography screening has markedly increased the detection of small, deeply located subsolid pulmonary nodules, and local therapy for these lesions now encompasses anatomical segmentectomy, tailored sublobar resection, lobectomy, and image-guided thermal ablation. Although multidisciplinary pathways already inform modality selection, three-dimensional (3D) anatomical reconstruction - despite its established role in segmentectomy planning - is rarely used as a shared patient-specific dataset to guide both resection and ablation decisions. In this perspective, a thoracic surgeon argues that, for a deep or cross-segment subsolid nodule with an established indication for local therapy, a single patient-specific 3D dataset can inform both branches of the decision. The same volumetric anatomy - including nodule size and consolidation-to-tumor ratio, segmental boundaries, bronchovascular relationships, pleura, and the chest wall - is first used to determine whether adequate-margin lung-sparing resection is achievable and, if it is not, to assess whether ablation is anatomically feasible through three sequential filters: trajectory safety, perilesional structural risk, and predicted ablative coverage. The approach is illustrated with a representative case and discussed in the contexts of multifocal disease, the post-resection lung, and perivascular lesions, together with the trade-offs associated with forgoing nodal staging and tissue diagnosis. The framework does not expand indications beyond those already supported by guidelines. Rather, it operationalizes these recommendations through patient-specific anatomy, with the aim of making modality selection more transparent, reproducible, and auditable. It remains an unvalidated, single-center proposal that requires prospective evaluation.

Title: Machine-learning phenotyping and exploratory medication-outcome associations in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a multicohort retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The marked clinical and pathophysiological heterogeneity of HFpEF has repeatedly undermined uniform treatment strategies. Consequently, identifying distinct phenotypes and medication-associated patterns across phenotypes may inform future precision-medicine research.
METHODS: In this multicohort retrospective study, patients with HFpEF were included from MIMIC-IV (derivation cohort, n = 2,511), the MIMIC-III CareVue subset (internal validation cohort, n = 1,524), and the Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University (external application cohort, n = 340). Unsupervised K-prototypes clustering was used to derive phenotypic groups, with K = 2 evaluated as a lower-resolution sensitivity solution. All phenotype-stratified medication analyses were exploratory. In the derivation and internal validation cohorts, overlap weighting was the primary weighted analysis and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was a sensitivity analysis; external medication estimates were reported descriptively because adequate within-group covariate balance was not achieved. A TabPFN phenotype-assignment classifier was developed after recursive feature elimination, evaluated in internal validation against independently reclustered labels aligned by prespecified one-to-one Hungarian assignment on cluster-profile distances, and applied without refitting in the external cohort.
RESULTS: The primary three-cluster solution identified clinically interpretable but partially overlapping cardiorenal-metabolic, hypertensive-pulmonary, and low-blood-pressure/arrhythmia profiles. K = 2 had a higher mean silhouette width than K = 3 (0.083 versus 0.060), whereas both solutions showed high median resampling stability (ARI, 0.940 versus 0.924). A graded 365-day mortality difference was observed across the three clusters in the derivation cohort, but between-cluster survival differences were not statistically significant in the internal validation or external application cohorts. In the derivation and internal validation cohorts, no weighted cluster-specific medication association remained statistically significant after FDR correction, and all medication-by-cluster interaction tests were nonsignificant. External medication estimates were descriptive and were not used for confirmatory inference. The fixed TabPFN classifier achieved one-versus-rest AUCs of 0.951-0.969 in internal validation (10-bin multiclass ECE = 0.028).
CONCLUSION: Routinely collected ICU data supported an exploratory framework for describing overlapping HFpEF phenotypes and reproducibly assigning machine-derived labels. The analyses did not establish phenotype-specific medication effects, and the classifier should be regarded as a research tool pending prospective multicenter validation.

Title: Association between the stress hyperglycemia ratio and neovascular glaucoma in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neovascular glaucoma (NVG) is a sight-threatening complication of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). The stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), which quantifies the discrepancy between acute admission glucose and chronic glycemic background, has been associated with adverse outcomes in diabetic populations, but its relationship with NVG remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between the SHR and prevalent NVG among patients with PDR.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, patients with PDR presenting to Shaoxing People's Hospital between 2023 and 2025 were categorized according to NVG status (49 with NVG; 215 without). The SHR was calculated as admission blood glucose (mmol/L) ÷ (1.59 × HbA1c - 2.59). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs), with the per-0.1-unit SHR increment as the primary effect measure; Firth penalized regression and a model excluding HbA1c were fitted as sensitivity analyses. Non-normally distributed variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test, with a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.0063 for the eight baseline comparisons. Discrimination was internally validated by bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Patients with NVG were younger (median 57.0 vs. 62.0 years; p < 0.001) and had higher SHR values (median 0.96 vs. 0.82; p < 0.001). The SHR was independently associated with prevalent NVG (aOR per 0.1-unit increment 1.31, 95% CI 1.12-1.53; p < 0.001); the Firth-penalized estimate was nearly identical (aOR 1.29, 95% CI 1.11-1.50). The events-per-variable ratio was 6.1; subgroup estimates were statistically unstable and are reported as exploratory only. The optimism-corrected C-statistic was 0.724.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional analysis, an elevated SHR was associated with a higher prevalence of NVG among patients with PDR. Because established NVG may itself increase admission glucose through acute stress, reverse causation cannot be excluded. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, externally validated cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

Title: Real-world anatomical and functional outcomes following Faricimab therapy in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a one-year observational study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study evaluated 12-month anatomical and functional outcomes of Faricimab in Italian patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).
METHODS: 30 eyes from 30 participants who completed the 12-month follow-up were retrospectively analyzed at "Luigi Vanvitelli" University Eye Clinic (Naples) and "Rummo" Hospital Ophthalmology Unit (Benevento). All underwent best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Patients were stratified by anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) treatment [naïve (N = 22); non-naïve (N = 8)], baseline macular neovascularization (MNV) type and fluid distribution. BCVA and central retinal thickness (CRT) were assessed at 6 and 12 months. The association between baseline subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM) status and longitudinal BCVA and CRT was also investigated.
RESULTS: The intravitreal injection number was similar between naïve and non-naïve eyes (median, 6 vs. 7; p = 0.093). One adverse event (vitreitis with ocular hypertension) occurred. Mixed-effects modelling showed significant longitudinal improvements in BCVA from baseline to months 6 and 12, with no significant time-by-treatment-history interaction. Baseline retinal fluid distribution was not significantly associated with differences in BCVA changes, while baseline SHRM status showed a significant time-by-SHRM interaction for BCVA, although multiplicity-adjusted between-group comparisons were not significant at any time point. CRT decreased significantly from baseline to months 6 and 12, whereas the change between months 6 and 12 was not statistically significant. SHRM thickness also decreased significantly from baseline to months 6 and 12. Exploratory analyses by MNV subtype did not identify significant differences in 12-month BCVA or CRT. In exploratory multivariable analysis, baseline BCVA was the only factor significantly associated with 12-month BCVA, whereas age, previous anti-VEGF treatment, and baseline SHRM were not.
DISCUSSION: This retrospective two-center study showed significant improvements in BCVA and CRT after 12 months of Faricimab, with no statistically detectable difference in longitudinal BCVA according to previous anti-VEGF exposure. Although baseline SHRM was associated with a significant time-by-SHRM interaction for BCVA, the absence of significant multiplicity-adjusted between-group differences limits interpretation of a differential response according to SHRM status. Given the small sample size and retrospective design, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

Title: Evaluation of cardiovascular risk using smartwatch-measured pulse wave velocity in China: a nationwide cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, driven by arteriosclerosis, are China's leading causes of death. Smartwatch-measured pulse wave velocity (SW-PWV) is an algorithm-derived estimate of carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) generated using a built-in machine-learning algorithm. A previous validation study showed good agreement between smartwatch-estimated cfPWV and Complior Analyse measurements, with a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.9045 and a mean absolute error of 0.66 m/s.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the distribution of smartwatch-measured pulse wave velocity (SW-PWV) according to age, sex, and body mass index (BMI), and to investigate its cross-sectional associations with cardiovascular risk factors and established cardiovascular disease (CVD).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed 165,549 users who completed at least one valid SW-PWV measurement using compatible Huawei smartwatches between December 2020 and August 2022. Analyses of cardiovascular risk factors and CVD were restricted to 35,402 users who completed the "Vascular Health" app questionnaire, in which physician-diagnosed conditions were self-reported according to predefined criteria. A threshold of 10 m/s, adapted from guideline recommendations for cfPWV, was explored for SW-PWV. Spearman's correlation, Kruskal-Wallis test, multiple regression, and Mann-Whitney U-test were used for analysis. Data were reported as median (interquartile range) or mean ± standard deviation.
RESULTS: SW-PWV correlated positively with age, male sex, and BMI. After age- and BMI-stratification, SW-PWV increased progressively across all cohorts. Average SW-PWV was significantly higher in males than in females. SW-PWV was significantly elevated in participants with hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, coronary heart disease, stroke, and carotid plaque, with hypertension and carotid plaque exhibiting the strongest correlations. SW-PWV demonstrated moderate discrimination for prevalent CVD (area under the curve = 0.71). When applying the guideline-recommended cfPWV threshold of 10 m/s to SW-PWV, sensitivity was 13.6% and specificity was 96.7%.
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study, SW-PWV was associated with age, sex, and BMI, with SW-PWV ≥10 m/s linked to a higher prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors and CVD. These findings suggest that the guideline-derived 10 m/s threshold of cfPWV might serve as a preliminary or exploratory threshold reference for SW-PWV, though direct validation against conventional cfPWV and prospective longitudinal studies are required before clinical implementation.

Title: A prospective study evaluating clopidogrel resistance among patients with ischemic cerebrovascular events across different ethnic groups in Israel.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clopidogrel is commonly used for secondary prevention after ischemic cerebrovascular events, but substantial interindividual variability in pharmacodynamics response has been reported. Individuals demonstrating resistance to clopidogrel face a higher likelihood of recurrent ischemic events. This study evaluated clopidogrel responsiveness among Jewish and Arab patients treated within the same regional healthcare setting.
METHODS: This prospective cohort included 102 patients with ischemic cerebrovascular events (acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack) receiving clopidogrel for secondary prevention. Patients received either a loading dose (300 in 62 patients, 600 mg in 1 patient) followed by maintenance therapy or at least 7 days of 75 mg daily maintenance dosing (n = 39) prior to blood sampling. Platelet responsiveness was measured using the vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP) phosphorylation assay (PLT VASP/P2Y12, BioCytex, France). Patients were categorized according to VASP platelet reactivity index (PRI) as adequate responders (PRI <50%), intermediate responders (PRI 50%-69%), or patients with high residual platelet reactivity, operationally defined in this study as PRI ≥70%.
RESULTS: The study included 102 enrolled patients, of whom 57 (55.9%) were Jewish and 45 (44.1%) were Arab. A valid VASP-PRI measurement was available for 101 patients (57 Jewish and 44 Arab); one Arab patient had no evaluable PRI measurement. Therefore, analyses of platelet reactivity were based on 101 patients The median PRI for all patients was 65.5 (49.1-80.3), with no statistically significant differences between Jewish and Arab (p = 0.251). Overall, 42.6% were classified as non-responders, 29.7% as partial responders, and only 27.7% demonstrated adequate platelet inhibition. Jewish patients were significantly older than Arab patients (p = 0.008), whereas Arab patients had a significantly higher BMI (p = 0.019). Other demographic and clinical features were similar across groups.
CONCLUSIONS: A high proportion of patients demonstrated elevated residual platelet reactivity according to the operational PRI threshold used in this study. No statistically significant ethnic difference in PRI was detected; however, the ethnic comparison was exploratory and the study was not powered to exclude modest between-group differences. Larger prospective studies incorporating CYP2C19 genotyping and longitudinal clinical outcomes are warranted.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Reduce Heart Failure Hospitalization, Cardiovascular Death and Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease are the principal drivers of morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in landmark trials, yet cross-trial inconsistencies in cardiovascular mortality, renal endpoints and drug-specific effects leave the class-level estimates incompletely synthesized.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 15 May 2026. Large placebo-controlled RCTs (≥ 1000 participants) and prespecified subgroup analyses in adults with T2DM were eligible. The primary outcome was the composite of first hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) or cardiovascular death (CV death). Secondary outcomes were 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), CV DEATH, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, first HHF and composite kidney outcomes. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects inverse-variance models.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies (76 969 patients; 41 761 SGLT2i, 35 208 placebo) were included. SGLT2i reduced the primary composite by 23% (HR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.73-0.81, p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%), with no effect modification by baseline HF (p-interaction = 0.82) or established ASCVD (p-interaction = 0.46). MACE was reduced by 14% (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92), driven by significant reductions in CV DEATH (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93) and MI (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.96), with no significant effect on stroke (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.81-1.08). First, HHF was reduced by 29% (HR: 0.71, 95% CI: 0.66-0.77) and composite kidney outcomes by 31% (HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.60-0.79).
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i confer consistent and clinically meaningful cardiorenal protection in T2DM across the full spectrum of cardiovascular and renal risk. The ertugliflozin estimate and the moderate heterogeneity in kidney outcomes should be interpreted in the context of trial-level clinical differences and nonstandardized kidney endpoint definitions. These findings support proactive, guideline-concordant initiation of evidence-based SGLT2i agents by endocrinologists, cardiologists and primary care providers as foundational therapy in T2DM.

Title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Immune-Related Adverse Event of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study and Literature Review.
Journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize clinical and laboratory characteristics of peripheral neurological immune-related adverse event (irAEs-PN) patients, to improve understanding and provide reference for early diagnosis of irAEs-PN caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors.
METHODS: We screened 61 patients with irAEs in our center from September 2020 to June 2025. In addition, studies with detailed clinical data related to irAEs-PN were collected in PubMed database from January 2015 to June 2025. A total of 50 patients with irAEs-PN were included, including 8 cases from our center and 42 cases reported in literature. The patients' demographic information, clinical characteristics, electrophysiological examination, therapy and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and summarized.
RESULTS: Among the eight patients in our center, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in two cases, and limb weakness, occurring in six cases. Electrophysiology identified two axonal neuropathies, three demyelinating, and three mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies. Among the 42 patients reported in literature, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in 39 cases, and limb weakness, occurring in 41 cases. Electromyography identified 13 axonal neuropathies, 25 demyelinating neuropathies, and 4 mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies.
CONCLUSIONS: In most patients, irAEs-PN is characterized by demyelinating sensorimotor involvement of both the upper and lower limbs. In individuals receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, prompt electromyography after the onset of neuropathic symptoms can aid in detecting neurological involvement and facilitate earlier treatment.

Title: Clinical Markers of Vulnerability for Bleeding in Men With Prostate Cancer and Antithrombotic Treatment.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Men with prostate cancer have a high risk for bleeding when treated with antithrombotics. The aim of this study was to investigate clinical markers for vulnerability for bleeding in these men the last year of life.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study on deceased patients with advanced prostate cancer admitted to specialized palliative care and treated with antithrombotics the last year of life. Relative risk (RR) was calculated with log-binomial models.
RESULTS: Of 100 men with end-stage prostate cancer, 64 men were treated with antithrombotics. Twenty-four of these (37.5%) suffered from bleeding during the last year of life. Clinical markers associated with an increased vulnerability for bleeding were need of blood transfusion, RR 3.15 (95% CI: 1.34-7.39); low thrombocyte count, RR 2.41 (95% CI: 1.39-4.16); and deep venous thrombosis treatment, RR 2.44 (95% CI: 1.21-4.94). Age, type of antithrombotic, use of steroids, or NSAID were not risk factors. In 50%, antithrombotic treatment continued during the last week in life.
CONCLUSIONS: Antithrombotic treatment the last year of life is associated with a high risk of bleeding in men with prostate cancer. Clinical markers associated with increased vulnerability for bleeding are low thrombocyte count and need of transfusions.

Title: Relationship between extent of jeopardized myocardium derived from myocardial viability study to post-myocardial infarction outcome.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the relationship between the extent of jeopardized myocardium, quantified using cardiac viability imaging, and clinical outcomes in patients after myocardial infarction. By utilizing rest myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and cardiac 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) analyzed with Emory Cardiac Toolbox software (ECTb), the study aimed to determine how quantitative viability parameters correlate with left ventricular functional recovery and post-myocardial infarction outcomes, and to assess their utility in guiding clinical decision-making.
METHODS: This prospective study included 85 patients who underwent 2-day rest MPI followed by cardiac FDG-PET/CT imaging. Quantitative parameters, including the percentage of jeopardized myocardium, comprising viable, scarred, and total jeopardized myocardial segments, along with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were obtained using the ECTb platform (version 4.2). The relationship between these quantitative PET parameters and functional myocardial recovery, defined as improvement in ≥5% LVEF as assessed by two-dimensional echocardiography, was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Follow-up was conducted over a period of 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year to assess the association between baseline quantitative imaging parameters and the occurrence of adverse cardiac events.
RESULTS: The analysis demonstrated that the extent of viable myocardium was a strong predictor of functional recovery (area under the curve, 0.762; P < 0.001), with a cutoff of approximately 17% yielding 76.7% sensitivity, 68.8% specificity, and 71.8% accuracy. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) occurred in 16% of patients. There was no significant association with imaging parameters, except a nonsignificant trend for scar burden in medically managed patients. Patients undergoing surgical intervention had a significantly greater extent of jeopardized myocardium, underscoring the role of viability imaging in therapeutic decision-making.
CONCLUSION: The extent of viable myocardium identified through imaging was strongly correlated with functional recovery, as reflected by improvements in cardiac function on follow-up echocardiography. Although no significant relationship with MACE was seen in the overall cohort, the higher burden of jeopardized myocardium in surgically treated patients underscores the value of viability imaging in guiding revascularization decisions, supporting FDG-PET/CT as a useful tool for post-myocardial infarction risk stratification and management.

Title: Soluble Indicators of Endothelial Injury and Activation Emerge During Acute HIV Infection and Persist Despite Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy Initiation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular activation occurs during human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study investigates whether vascular endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during acute HIV infection (AHI) and persist despite immediate antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation.
METHODS: Thirteen plasma biomarkers indicative of endothelial and hemostatic perturbations were measured in 83 RV254 AHI cohort participants during pre-ART AHI and at week 288 post-ART, compared with cross-sectional measures from 32 people without HIV (PWoH). Hierarchical clustering was applied to week 288 biomarker profiles of RV254 participants and PWoH to identify distinct biomarker phenotypes.
RESULTS: During pre-ART AHI, RV254 participants exhibited higher intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), tissue factor, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase than PWoH (P < .05), independent of age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). These markers correlated with plasma HIV RNA or the CD4/CD8 ratio (P < .05). At week 288, significant reductions in ICAM-1, VCAM-1, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-C, VEGF-D, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase and a significant increase in tissue plasminogen activator were observed in RV254 (P < .05). However, VCAM-1 and thrombomodulin remained higher, and VEGF-A remained lower in RV254 participants compared to PWoH (P < .05). Hierarchical clustering identified 2 distinct clusters. Despite comparable 10-year CVD risk, 1 cluster exhibited concomitant elevation of ICAM-1, ICAM-2, VCAM-1, and E-selectin. Notably, 45% of RV254 participants vs 13% of PWoH were classified into this phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during AHI and correlate with HIV-related parameters. Despite suppressive ART, RV254 participants remained approximately 3.5 times more likely than PWoH to exhibit an endothelial activation biomarker phenotype.

Title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced left ventricular (LV) dysfunction complicates fluid resuscitation, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema and worsening outcomes. Echocardiographic assessment is often delayed, and natriuretic peptides such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) have limited diagnostic accuracy in this setting. We evaluated a smartphone-based electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis application for screening LV dysfunction in patients with sepsis.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, we included 425 adult sepsis patients from three university hospitals who underwent both a 12-lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiography within 72 hours of emergency department admission. ECG images displayed on a monitor were photographed and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based smartphone application (ECG Buddy™), which generated a quantitative digital biomarker for LV dysfunction (quantitative electrocardiogram scores for LV dysfunction [QCG-LVDys]). LV dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%. The diagnostic performance of QCG-LVDys for detecting LV dysfunction was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). A predefined comparison with NT-proBNP was performed in the single center where NT-proBNP was routinely measured.
RESULTS: In the overall multicenter cohort, QCG-LVDys showed high diagnostic performance for LV dysfunction, with an ROC-AUC of 0.901. Using an optimized threshold (37.35), QCG-LVDys achieved a sensitivity of 89.6%, specificity of 75.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97.5%. In the NT-proBNP subset, QCG-LVDys outperformed NT-proBNP (ROC-AUC 0.911 vs. 0.637, P < 0.001). Higher QCG-LVDys values were associated with increased lactate levels (P = 0.002) and 28-day in-hospital mortality (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Evaluating Perfusion Quantification for Phase-Resolved Functional Lung MRI Using Gaussian Filtering.
Abstract: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI enables contrast-free lung perfusion quantification (QQuant). Current quantification uses a single median value per slice of maximal blood exchange fraction (ΔS), which limits regional assessment, whereas regional ΔS causes artifacts. This retrospective study aims to optimize QQuant by applying Gaussian filtering to ΔS to improve intrascan/interscan repeatability in healthy volunteers, while evaluating whether the optimized QQuant retains agreement with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) patients and exhibits a physiologically plausible gravity-dependent perfusion gradient. Analysis was performed on 29 healthy subjects (11 female, age: 19-33 years), 20 COPD patients (three female, age: 46-76 years) and 15 CTEPH patients (six female, age: 44-82 years), scanned at 1.5 T. Healthy subjects underwent four PREFUL scans in two sessions. Patients just underwent one PREFUL and DCE scan. QQuant maps were calculated while applying different Gaussian filter options to ΔS. In patients, PREFUL-derived QQuant maps were coregistered to DCE-derived pulmonary blood flow (PBF) maps for global and voxel-wise correlations. In healthy subjects, the gravity-dependent perfusion gradient was quantified by linear regression of slice-wise QQuant across five coronal slices. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved intrascan and interscan repeatability in healthy subjects (mean bias: ≤ 2.94 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.2) compared with the current slice median setting (mean bias: ≥ 3.75 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.68). Correlations with PBF remained stable after filtering (σ = 1.5) in COPD (filtered vs. default ΔS: global r = 0.57 vs. r = 0.59, voxel-wise r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.32) and CTEPH (global r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.28, voxel-wise r = 0.40 vs. r = 0.41), all significant except global CTEPH. The filtered QQuant maps showed a significant gravity-dependent perfusion gradient (ΔS filtered σ = 1.5) of 1.47 mL/min/100 mL/cm. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved QQuant repeatability while preserving DCE-MRI agreement and is therefore recommended. The observed gravity-dependent perfusion gradient confirms physiological plausibility, supporting potential in clinical use.

Title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease increases the risk of cardiovascular disease occurrence in nonsmokers: A nationwide cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, and patients experience a high prevalence of concomitant cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In this study, we aimed to determine whether never smokers with COPD exhibit an increased risk of CVD compared with those without COPD and whether this risk parallels that observed in smokers with COPD.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank (CKB). Spirometry was performed on all the participants, and COPD was defined as the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) <0.7. Eligible participants in our study were free of diagnosed CVDs, including ischemic heart disease, heart failure, hypertension, or atrial fibrillation at baseline. The clinical outcomes were the incidences of these 4 CVDs and their overall incidence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate the associations of COPD and smoking status with incident CVD outcomes.
RESULTS: Among all eligible participants (n = 366,161, 20,887 with COPD), 40,861 incident cases of CVD events were observed during a median follow-up time of 10 years. Compared with never smokers without COPD, those with COPD exhibited a significantly higher risk of overall CVD, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.23 (95% CI: 1.09-1.39) for men and 1.24 (95% CI: 1.17-1.31) for women. Among male COPD participants, the incidence rates of overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, and hypertension, but not that of heart failure, were similar between never smokers and smokers. In contrast, female COPD participants who never smoked exhibited lower risks across all cardiovascular endpoints compared with their smoking counterparts. These results remained unchanged after propensity score matching.
CONCLUSION: In never smokers, COPD per se serves as an independent risk factor for CVD. Among men with COPD, smoking exposure confers no added hazard, whereas women with COPD who smoke remain at higher risk for CVD than their never-smoking counterparts.

Title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
Abstract: Background: Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes. Patients and methods: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex. Results: Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing. Conclusions: Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

Title: Diagnostic Yield of a Systematic IWT Score-Guided Echocardiographic Pathway for Cardiac Amyloidosis in Patients with Increased Left Ventricular Wall Thickness: A Prospective Multicentre Study.
Beyond Patency: Patient-Centered Outcomes and the Proposed Accountability Gap in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
Abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries 1-year mortality of 20% to 25%, comparable with many solid-organ malignancies. Technically successful revascularization, defined by anatomical patency, does not reliably deliver pain relief, restored function, or sustained quality of life. This narrative review synthesizes landmark randomized trials (BEST-CLI, BASIL-1, BASIL-2) and current European and United States guidelines, grading every claim with a scheme in which population indirectness downgrades design strength. We examine 4 domains of morbidity persisting after anatomically successful revascularization: mechanistically heterogeneous pain; functional and quality-of-life decline; psychological burden; and sustained health care use, including chronic opioid use (approximately 35%), unhealed wounds at 1 year (10%-32%), and unplanned 30-day readmission (approximately 25%). No patient-reported outcome measure has been validated specifically for CLTI or used as a co-primary trial endpoint. We propose an accountability gap: the under-measured transfer of unresolved morbidity from vascular services to primary care. We state it as a falsifiable prediction about the discrimination of patency rather than prevalence, with a pre-specified effect size, explicit treatment of death as a competing risk, and a core outcome battery justified against COSMIN criteria. Patient co-production is the indispensable next step.

Title: Outcomes and Predictors of Inpatient Mortality for Infective Endocarditis in Patients with Malignancy: Contemporary Nationwide Study from the United States.
Abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) in patients with malignancy represents a high-risk clinical cohort, yet nationwide data on outcomes and predictors of mortality remain limited. Using the United States National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), we identified hospitalizations involving IE and a malignancy diagnosis. Inpatient mortality, complications, and temporal trends were analyzed overall and across malignancy subtypes, causative organisms, and prosthetic valve status. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was performed across the full IE cohort. Of 635 715 IE hospitalizations, 44 060 (6.9%) involved a malignancy diagnosis. Inpatient mortality was higher in this group than among IE hospitalizations without malignancy (13.5% vs 9.8%; P < .001), and malignancy remained associated with mortality after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 1.29; 95% CI 1.19-1.39; P < .001). The proportion of IE hospitalizations involving malignancy increased from 6.7% in 2016 to 7.7% in 2022. Fungal infection, shock, acute kidney injury, and stroke were associated with mortality. Prosthetic-valve IE had lower mortality than non-prosthetic-valve IE (7.7% vs 13.9%; P < .001). These findings identify a high-risk, heterogeneous phenotype and support earlier diagnostic evaluation and coordinated oncology, cardiology, and infectious diseases management.

Title: Early Ulnar Artery Occlusion and Recanalization After Coronary Angiography via Distal Ulnar Access: A Doppler-Followed Case Series.
Abstract: This single-center retrospective case series assessed early ulnar artery patency by Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) after coronary angiography via distal ulnar access (DUA), described flow evolution in patients with follow-up, and reported access-related complications. Thirty-eight consecutive patients with a day-3 DUS after coronary angiography via DUA between September 2023 and March 2024 were included. All procedures were performed by 1 operator using a short 6F sheath and 5000 IU intra-arterial heparin. Flow was categorized as thrombosis/no flow, monophasic, or triphasic; the primary endpoint was day-3 non-triphasic flow, and month-1 and month-3 DUS were selective. Mean age was 58.8 ± 10.1 years and 47.4% were male; 21.1% underwent same-session percutaneous coronary intervention. On day 3, thrombosis/no flow occurred in 18.4% (7/38), monophasic flow in 5.3% (2/38), and triphasic flow in 76.3% (29/38); non-triphasic flow was 23.7% (9/38). Month-1 DUS (n = 35) showed no thrombosis/no flow and 94.3% triphasic flow; month-3 DUS (n = 4) was triphasic in all. No clinically relevant hematoma, neuropathy, hand ischemia, or functional impairment was documented. After coronary angiography via DUA, day-3 non-triphasic flow occurred in 23.7%; selective follow-up suggested recanalization without major clinical complications, but limits generalizability.

Title: Underserved communities at risk of heart failure: effectiveness of community-based recruitment strategies and burden of unrecognised cardiovascular disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients from socioeconomically deprived and ethnically diverse backgrounds are under-represented in cardiovascular research. EARLY-HF is a community-based pilot study designed to predict incident HF in primary care. We aimed to assess effectiveness of recruitment strategies for engaging underserved populations and quantify the burden of unrecognised CVD.
METHODS: Prospective cohort study enrolling 550 adults aged ≥50 years with two or more cardiometabolic risk factors and no prior diagnosis of HF. Participants were recruited via: (i) targeted identification using electronic health records in eight primary care centres; (ii) digital advertising and targeted social media campaign; (iii) ten community outreach events; (iv) direct referral from family or friends. The baseline study visit included ECG, blood sampling, and imaging.
RESULTS: 185 (34%) participants were from the most deprived Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintile and 97 (18%) were of non-White ethnicity. Primary care and digital advertising were the most effective recruitment strategies, enrolling 444 (81%) and 68 (12%) participants respectively, while maintaining diverse representation. The social media campaign generated 15,207 advertisement clicks and 1,012 expressions of interest at a cost of £5.93 per sign-up. Community outreach events enrolled 5 (1%) participants and were resource intensive. A substantial burden of previously unrecognised CVD was identified: 125 (23%) participants had clinically actionable cardiac abnormalities, including 46 (9%) with previously unrecognised myocardial infarction, 331 (60%) had uncontrolled blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg), and 162 (30%) had elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/ml).
CONCLUSIONS: Primary care-embedded and digital recruitment strategies can effectively engage underserved communities at risk of HF, at scale and at low cost. This population has a very high burden of unrecognised CVD.

Title: Genetic landscape of paediatric channelopathies and cardiomyopathies in Hong Kong.
Journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies are important causes of sudden cardiac death. The genetic background of these conditions in Asian paediatric populations has rarely been reported. This study aimed to report the genetic underpinnings of these conditions in patients treated at a single tertiary paediatric cardiac centre in Hong Kong.
METHODS: All patients diagnosed with cardiac channelopathy or cardiomyopathy who underwent genetic testing in our cardiology centre between 2007 and 2022 were included in this cohort study. Phenotype classification, genetic testing methodologies, and results were reviewed. Genetic yields were assessed.
RESULTS: In total, 165 probands were identified. Ninety-four probands carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant (57.0%), whereas 27 probands (16.4%) had only variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 58 patients with channelopathy (63.7%) and 36 patients with cardiomyopathy (48.6%), including 22 novel variants (16 P/LP variants and 6 VUS). The yield of P/LP variants was highest in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (81.8%). The clinical features of selected probands with significant mortality or morbidity were described in relation to variant details. The yield of subsequent cascade genetic screening among first-degree relatives was 27.3%.
CONCLUSION: This study describes the genetic landscape of paediatric cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies at a single tertiary paediatric cardiology centre in Hong Kong. The findings facilitated genotype-guided management and enabled identification of at-risk family members for the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

Title: Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers Presenting to a Pediatric Emergency Department.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical presentation and management of anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 0 to 24 months presenting to a pediatric emergency department between June 2019 and June 2022 with concern for anaphylaxis. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and 10th Revision codes associated with anaphylaxis and confirmed to meet 2006 National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/Food Allergy and Anaphylaxis Network clinical criteria by chart review. Demographic and clinical information-including presenting symptoms, administered treatment, and patient disposition-were abstracted from the electronic medical record. Treatments of interest included epinephrine, antihistamines, corticosteroids, albuterol, and intravenous fluids. Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 225 potentially eligible encounters, we identified 155 patients who met inclusion criteria. Median age was 10.8 months (interquartile range: 8.4 to 15.6). Food triggered 96.1% of episodes. Skin and mucosal symptoms occurred in 99.4% of patients, gastrointestinal symptoms in 74.2%, respiratory symptoms in 57.4%, and cardiovascular symptoms in 5.8%. Intramuscular epinephrine was administered to 87.1% of patients, 90.4% of whom received a single dose. Most patients (88.4%) were discharged home, and none of those admitted required additional epinephrine.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, reactions were most often food-triggered and characterized by mucocutaneous symptoms with gastrointestinal and/or mild-to-moderate respiratory symptoms. Severe respiratory or cardiovascular involvement was uncommon. Symptoms tended to resolve after a single dose of epinephrine, and most patients were discharged home.

Title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification.
METHODS: Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite.
RESULTS: Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

Title: Impact of beetroot juice ingestion on upper- and lower-body muscular endurance in resistance-trained females: A randomized, double-blind, crossover study.
Abstract: BackgroundNitrate-rich beetroot juice offers potential ergogenic effects in resistance training. However, existing literature overwhelmingly focuses on males, leaving a significant gap regarding female responses.AimThis study evaluated acute effects of inorganic nitrate (NO3-) supplementation on resistance exercise performance to failure in recreationally trained females.MethodsIn a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, sixteen females (27 ± 4.7 years; one repetition maximum [1RM] bench press: 31.4 ± 6.5 kg; 1RM leg press: 198.6 ± 44.0 kg) performed four sets of bench press and 45° leg press to concentric failure at 60% of 1RM (2-min rest intervals) following the ingestion of nitrate-rich beetroot juice (BEET It Sport®: 12.8 mmol NO3-), a placebo drink (0.92 mmol NO3-), or nothing (control) 2.5 h before exercise.ResultsNitrate-rich beetroot juice ingestion had no effect on performance in either the upper-body (bench press total repetitions: Control: 55.6 ± 9.7 reps; Placebo: 58.9 ± 13.0 reps; Nitrate: 56.0 ± 14.0 reps, p = 0.785, ηp2 = 0.003) or lower-body (leg press total repetitions: Control: 82.6 ± 36.0 reps; Placebo: 80.4 ± 37.0 reps; Nitrate: 79.3 ± 30.0 reps, p = 0.945, ηp2 = 0.001) exercises in resistance-trained females. There were also no effects of nitrate on rating of perceived exertion, heart rate, blood pressure, or lactate compared to placebo (p > 0.05).SummaryAcute NO3- supplementation did not alter performance or modulate the physiological response to resistance exercise in recreationally trained females. These results suggest that the ergogenic potential of NO3- may be limited in this population.

Title: Intelligent thermoregulation strategy versus routine thermal management on myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery during gastrointestinal tumor resection in elderly patients (SAGE): a multicenter, parallel-group, superiority trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but adequately powered trials using high-sensitivity troponin endpoints is lacking. The SAGE trial evaluates whether an intelligent, closed-loop thermoregulation strategy reduces myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) in high-risk elderly patients.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial conducted at seven tertiary hospitals in China. Participants aged ≥65 years scheduled for elective gastrointestinal tumor resection under general anesthesia are randomly assigned (1:1) to intelligent closed-loop warming (target 36.8 °C, upper limit 37.0 °C) or routine thermal management (active warming only if core temperature ≤35.5 °C). The primary outcome is the incidence of MINS within the first 2 postoperative days , adjudicated using high-sensitivity troponin thresholds per AHA criteria. Secondary outcomes include surgical site infection, transfusion requirement, hypothermia burden, emergence delirium, delayed emergence, and postoperative shivering. With 695 participants per group (total 1,390, accounting for 10% dropout), the trial has 80% power at a one-sided significance level of 0.05 to detect a 6 absolute percentage point reduction in MINS (12% to 6%) with a superiority margin of -2 percentage points.
DISCUSSION: The SAGE trial is designed to generate new evidence on the relationship between intraoperative hypothermia exposure and postoperative cardiovascular complications. It will evaluate whether closed-loop targeted normothermia reduces myocardial injury and will explore hypothermia exposure thresholds that may inform individualized perioperative management for geriatric surgical patients.
TRIAL ACRONYM: Intelligent Thermoregulation Strategy for Advanced-Age Elders undergoing gastrointestinal tumor resection (SAGE).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), identifier: ChiCTR2600117264. Registered on January 21, 2026 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).

Title: Medication-induced Micronutrient Deficiencies in Early-stage Chronic Kidney Disease.
Journal: Recent advances in food, nutrition & agriculture
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a growing global health burden, with early-stage patients often managed through long-term pharmacotherapy. However, prolonged use of common medications may unintentionally disrupt micronutrient balance, compounding the metabolic and cardiovascular risks already present in CKD.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review aims to explore the associations between frequently prescribed medications and the development of micronutrient deficiencies in early-stage, non-dialysis CKD patients, highlighting underlying mechanisms, clinical implications, and potential management strategies.
METHODS: Relevant literature published between 2020 and 2025 was identified through structured searches of PubMed, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational cohorts, and prior reviews evaluating the effects of medications on micronutrient status in CKD stages 1-3. Evidence was narratively synthesized according to medication class, nutrient affected, and reported clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Approximately 30-35 key studies were included. Phosphate binders, diuretics, antihypertensives, proton pump inhibitors, and immunosuppressants were most commonly associated with disruptions in vitamin D, iron, vitamin B12, calcium, and magnesium metabolism. These imbalances may contribute to anemia, mineral bone disorder, cardiovascular complications, and immune dysfunction in early CKD.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that medication-induced micronutrient disturbances may act as modifiable contributors to anemia, mineral-bone disorder, cardiovascular risk, and immune dysfunction in early-stage CKD. Routine nutritional monitoring alongside pharmacotherapy may therefore represent an important preventive strategy.
CONCLUSION: Medication-induced micronutrient deficiencies represent a clinically relevant yet underrecognized challenge in CKD management. The findings of this review are hypothesisgenerating and underscore the need for systematic, longitudinal research to establish causal pathways and inform evidence-based supplementation guidelines. Integrating nutritional monitoring into pharmacologic care may improve outcomes in early-stage CKD.

Title: The Role of Decompressive Craniectomy for Severe Refractory Head Injury.
Abstract: Decompressive craniectomy is a potential therapeutic option for patients with severe traumatic brain injury and refractory intracranial hypertension, although its indications and clinical benefits remain controversial. A total of 4060 articles were identified, with 94.6% published after 2010. Several major randomized clinical trials have shaped current understanding of decompressive craniectomy, including the RESCUE-ASDH for primary intracranial hypertension, and the DECRA and RESCUEicp for secondary intracranial hypertension. RESCUE-ASDH and DECRA showed no overall benefit and suggested potential harm associated with decompressive craniectomy. RESCUEicp trial showed reduced mortality and sustained long-term improvement in a subset of patients, although many survivors remained in a dependent state. Critical appraisal of the inclusion and exclusion criteria of these trials, together with supporting evidence from animal studies, suggest that decompressive craniectomy should not be treated as primary intervention for traumatic brain injury. Instead, it may be more appropriately used as an adjunct procedure to prevent worsening cerebral edema following other neurosurgical interventions - such as evaluation of contusions or hematomas - when the operative hemisphere is tight and swollen. Decompressive craniectomy performed solely to control refractory intracranial hypertension in traumatic brain injury is unlikely to provide meaningful patient-centered benefit. Its role as an adjunct procedure after evacuation of contusions or hematomas remains uncertain, particularly in patients with a low predicted risk of unfavorable outcome. Decision regarding decompressive craniectomy should incorporate shared decision making and reflect careful consideration of the functional outcomes acceptable to patients and their families.

Title: Abdominal Normothermic Regional Perfusion Versus Normothermic Machine Perfusion of DCD Kidneys Aged 50 Years or Older: A Propensity Score Matched Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The use of donor kidneys from older donation after circulatory death (DCD) donors is limited due to increased susceptibility to ischemia-reperfusion injury, resulting in delayed graft function (DGF) and graft loss. While hypothermic machine perfusion (HMP) with oxygen (HMPO2) offers some benefit, clinical outcomes remain suboptimal. Emerging normothermic preservation techniques, such as abdominal normothermic regional perfusion (aNRP) and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP), may enhance graft viability in high-risk transplants. This study compares post-transplant outcomes of aNRP versus NMP in DCD donors over 50 years of age.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were collected from two clinical trials (NMP group) and a national registry (aNRP group). The primary outcome was the incidence of DGF. Secondary outcomes included primary non-function (PNF), acute rejection, death-censored graft and patient survival, and longitudinal kidney function (eGFR) until three years after transplantation.
RESULTS: The outcomes of 85 kidneys that underwent aNRP were compared to 29 kidneys that underwent NMP. No significant difference was observed in the incidence of DGF (aNRP: 46% vs. NMP: 52%, p = 0.82), PNF (aNRP: 8% vs. NMP: 7%, p = 0.87) or acute rejection (25% vs. 31%, p = 0.67). Death-censored graft and patient survival was similar in the aNRP and NMP group. At three years post-transplant, median eGFR was 38 (±2.1) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the aNRP group and 33 (±3.8) mL/min/1.73 m2 in the NMP group.
CONCLUSION: The findings of this study demonstrate that both aNRP and NMP provide similar graft outcomes in older DCD kidney transplantation, potentially increasing the acceptance of high-risk donor kidneys by transplant centers. The interpretation of the results of this study is limited by its non-randomized design and small sample size.

Title: Venlafaxine modulates white matter integrity in dorsal and ventral language pathways after subcortical stroke: a longitudinal TBSS study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subcortical aphasia results from disrupted cortico-subcortical language networks after left-hemispheric infarction. Venlafaxine, an SNRI, may accelerate language recovery, but its effects on white matter plasticity remain unclear. We used diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) to assess early venlafaxine effects on dorsal and ventral language pathways in subacute stroke.
METHODS: Thirty-two patients with first-ever left subcortical infarction and mild-to-moderate aphasia were randomized to venlafaxine (n=16; 75 mg/day, day 7-week 4) or control (n=16). DTI was acquired at 30±7 and 90±7 days post-stroke. TBSS compared fractional anisotropy (FA) in language-related tracts using permutation testing with TFCE (corrected p<0.05).    .
RESULTS: At Visit 2, venlafaxine recipients had higher FA in right superior longitudinal fasciculus/arcuate fasciculus (SLF/AF), bilateral inferior fronto-occipital fasciculi (IFOF), and left inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), but lower FA in left SLF and uncinate fasciculus (UF). At Visit 3, FA increases extended to SLF/AF and UF, yielding bilateral dorsal and ventral enhancement; only right ILF FA decreased. FA changes positively correlated with aphasia quotient, spontaneous language fluency, and picture-naming improvements.  .
CONCLUSION: Early venlafaxine induces biphasic white matter remodeling: initial contralesional and bilateral ventral enhancement, followed by bilateral integration, suggesting optimized language network reorganization.

Title: Intraoperative Anesthetic Parameters Predict Early Allograft Dysfunction in Pediatric Living Donor Liver Transplantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early allograft dysfunction (EAD) is a major complication of pediatric liver transplantation associated with prolonged ICU stay, increased mortality, and graft loss. Existing risk models focus on donor and surgical variables; the contribution of intraoperative anesthetic management remains poorly characterized in pediatric living donor liver transplantation (LDLT).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 124 consecutive pediatric LDLT recipients. Three intraoperative anesthetic parameters were evaluated as predictors of EAD (Olthoff criteria): relative mean arterial pressure (MAP) drop (%), norepinephrine (NE) infusion duration (min), and peak intraoperative lactate (mmol/L). Discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression addressed near-complete separation. Internal validation used bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations).
RESULTS: The cohort (median age 18.5 months, IQR 8.0-96.0; biliary atresia the most common indication) included 50 patients (40.3%) with EAD. All three parameters showed excellent univariable discrimination: NE duration (AUC = 0.993), peak lactate (AUC = 0.936), and MAP drop (AUC = 0.894); all p < 0.001. Three preoperative variables (hemoglobin, bilirubin, albumin) reached univariable significance (all p < 0.05) but with modest discrimination (AUC 0.384-0.617), markedly inferior to all intraoperative parameters (AUC 0.894-0.996). In the multivariable model, MAP drop (OR 22.27; 95% CI 1.80-275.4; p = 0.016) and NE duration (OR 3066657; p = 0.018) independently predicted EAD. The combined model achieved AUC = 0.999 (bootstrap 95% CI: 0.994-1.000; Brier score = 0.013). NE duration ≥ 70 min yielded sensitivity 1.000 and NPV 1.000. EAD-positive patients had significantly longer ICU stay (5 vs. 3 days; p = 0.004) and mechanical ventilation duration (24 vs. 0 h; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative anesthetic parameters-particularly NE duration and MAP drop-are powerful independent predictors of EAD in pediatric LDLT, substantially outperforming preoperative variables, three of which reached statistical significance but with markedly lower discriminative power. Intraoperative hemodynamic management may represent a modifiable determinant of early graft outcomes. External validation is warranted.

Title: Cannabinoids for Acute Pain Management: A Contemporary Scoping Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global opioid crisis has intensified interest in non-opioid and opioid-sparing analgesic strategies, including cannabinoids. Despite the expanding legal landscape for cannabis and a rapidly growing cannabinoid market, the clinical evidence for cannabinoid use in acute pain management remains inconsistent and largely of low quality.
METHODS: This contemporary scoping review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of six electronic databases (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalKey, EMBASE, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and BIOSIS) was performed for literature published between 1 January 2016 and 5 April 2026, with the final database search executed on 5 April 2026, addressing the pharmacology, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and perioperative implications of cannabinoids in acute and postoperative pain. Two blinded reviewers independently screened records and charted data against predefined eligibility criteria; discrepancies were resolved by a third author. Findings are summarized narratively and in tabular format, and the study selection process is depicted in a PRISMA flow diagram.
RESULTS: Preclinical evidence supports robust antinociceptive effects of cannabinoids through multiple receptor pathways; however, these findings have not translated reliably into human acute pain models. Metaanalytic data demonstrate either no significant reduction in acute pain scores with cannabinoids versus placebo, or only small, clinically uncertain improvements. The opioid-sparing effect, while promising in preclinical and some chronic pain studies, has not been demonstrated for acute postoperative pain. A notable exception is a 2024 randomized trial showing a 40% reduction in opioid requirements with perioperative dronabinol after cardiac surgery. Safety data indicate that non-serious adverse events (dizziness, nausea, sedation) are consistently more frequent with cannabinoids than placebo. The 2023 American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (ASRA) consensus guidelines now formalize 21 recommendations for perioperative cannabinoid management.
CONCLUSION: While the biological rationale for cannabinoid analgesia is compelling, the clinical evidence base for acute pain remains insufficient to support routine use. Cannabinoids may serve as adjuncts in specific populations, but require careful patient selection, dose titration, and safety monitoring. Well-designed, large randomized controlled trials targeting defined acute pain populations are urgently needed.

Title: Association Between Baseline Cognitive Impairment and Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is common among patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), yet its prognostic significance in the context of catheter ablation remains unclear.
