AIMS: We aimed to investigate whether baseline cognitive impairment, assessed by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), was associated with post-ablation AF recurrence.
METHODS: Based on the China-AF Registry, we identified 2692 patients with nonvalvular AF who underwent index catheter ablation and had baseline MoCA assessments from 2022 to 2024. Patients were stratified into mild cognitive impairment (MCI, MoCA ≤ 26) and normal cognition (MoCA > 26) groups. The primary outcome was AF recurrence beyond the blanking period. The secondary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, ischemic stroke, and major bleeding. To adjust for confounding factors, we applied inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) methodology. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs).
RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, all baseline covariates were well balanced (all standardized mean differences < 0.03). Over a median follow-up of 218 days (IQR, 192-376), the MCI group had a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence (aHR 1.48; 95% CI, 1.27-1.73; p  <  0.001). The composite secondary endpoint did not demonstrate a statistically significant between-group difference (aHR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.25-4.52; p = 0.945). The association between baseline MCI and AF recurrence was consistent across all prespecified subgroups (all p for interaction > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In this large prospective registry study, an independent association was observed between baseline cognitive impairment and an elevated risk of post-ablation AF recurrence. Cognitive assessment may be useful for risk stratification but requires external validation.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT06987825.

Title: Timing of Catheter Ablation After Heart Failure Diagnosis for Atrial Fibrillation: A Propensity-Score-Matched Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF). However, most of the evidence on the importance of ablation timing has been anchored to AF rather than HF onset, leaving the optimal interval between HF diagnosis and ablation incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the timing of catheter ablation following the first diagnosis of HF and subsequent clinical outcomes in patients with established AF.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective propensity-score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults (≥18 years) with AF who subsequently developed HF and underwent catheter ablation were included. The primary analysis compared ablation from day 1 through 3 months after HF diagnosis with ablation at least 91 days after HF diagnosis. Propensity-score matching yielded 2,570 patients in each group. Outcomes were assessed for 2 years after ablation and included all-cause mortality, electrical cardioversion, emergency department or inpatient encounters, and HF exacerbation. A 1-year timing threshold and analyses stratified by recorded left ventricular ejection fraction were examined as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Mean follow-up was 549.3±253.2 days after early ablation and 534.1±255.3 days after later ablation. Mortality was similar between groups (11.0% vs 10.0%; hazard ratio [HR] 1.078, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.910-1.276; p = 0.384), as were emergency department or inpatient encounters (66.2% vs 65.6%; HR 1.006, 95% CI 0.940-1.076; p = 0.865). Early ablation was associated with fewer cardioversions (15.0% vs 18.6%; HR 0.788, 95% CI 0.689-0.901; p < 0.001) and fewer HF exacerbation events (39.5% vs 46.0%; HR 0.824, 95% CI 0.758-0.896; p < 0.001). The 1-year timing analysis showed a similar pattern for cardioversion and the HF exacerbation.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AF and HF who ultimately underwent ablation, ablation within 3 months of HF diagnosis was associated with fewer subsequent cardioversions and HF exacerbations than ablation performed from day 91 onward. However, there was no significant difference in mortality between the two cohorts. These findings identify the first months after HF diagnosis as a clinically relevant period for reassessing rhythm-control strategy and warrant prospective evaluation of ablation timing after HF recognition.

Title: Nurse Practitioner-Led Integration of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients With Obesity-Related Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Prospective Clinical Effectiveness Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is characterized by systemic inflammation and reduced functional capacity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve symptoms and weight in randomized trials, but uptake in routine cardiovascular practice is inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate a structured nurse practitioner-led program for GLP-1 RA initiation in obesity-related HFpEF.
METHODS: Prospective 12-month, single-center pre-post effectiveness study at a U.S. urban academic outpatient cardiology clinic. Adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%, body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, New York Heart Association class II-III symptoms, and at least 1 cardiometabolic comorbidity were enrolled. The intervention included registry-based identification, baseline assessment, patient education, protocolized titration, and longitudinal follow-up. Each participant's 12-month preenrollment period served as a comparator. The primary outcome was GLP-1 RA initiation and 12-month persistence.
RESULTS: Of 156 enrolled, 128 (82.1%) completed follow-up. Mean age 67.4 ± 11.2 years; 61.7% female; 43.8% Black. GLP-1 RA use rose from 7.8% to 92.2% (87.5% at target dose). Mean weight decreased 6.2 ± 3.8 kg, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improved 16.6 ± 11.3 points, and 6-minute walk distance rose 48.3 ± 36.2 m (all P < .001). Systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c (diabetic subgroup), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide all decreased significantly. Heart failure hospitalization fell from 18.2% to 4.7% (P = .002). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common; 4.7% discontinued for intolerance.
CONCLUSIONS: A structured nurse practitioner-led cardiometabolic program was associated with high GLP-1 RA initiation and persistence and with clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and hospitalization in obesity-related HFpEF.

Title: Ambulatory and Unattended, Automated Office Blood Pressure in People With and Without HIV in Tanzania: A Cohort Study of Repeatability and Regression to the Mean.
Abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (sSA) bears a high burden of hypertension and HIV, yet blood pressure measurement often relies on single-day, conventional office readings, prone to measurement error. We assessed the short-term repeatability of unattended, automated office BP (uAOBP) and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM), and whether reproducibility differs by HIV status in Tanzania. We analyzed data from the Mwanza HIV&CVD cohort study, using measurements from enrollment and 1-month later. Bland-Altman plots visualized mean differences and limits of agreement. Reproducibility of hypertension classification was calculated using Cohen's kappa, with differences by HIV status evaluated using large-sample variance. Of 999 participants enrolled, 750 (384 people with HIV (PWH) and 366 people without HIV (PWoH)) had valid ABPM measurements at both timepoints. The mean difference in systolic blood pressure was significant for uAOBP (-1.02 mmHg; 95% CI -1.76, -0.27) but not 24 h ABPM (-0.46; -1.02, 0.10), with similar results for diastolic blood pressure. Bland-Altman plots showed narrower limits of agreement for ABPM. Kappa statistics were 0.45 (0.33, 0.56) for uAOBP and 0.56 (0.50, 0.62) for 24 h ABPM. Regression dilution ratios were 0.77 and 0.82 for systolic and diastolic uAOBP and 0.73 and 0.77 for ABPM. Reproducibility did not differ by HIV status. ABPM and uAOBP demonstrated high short-term reproducibility, with ABPM showing greater stability for hypertension classification. Reproducibility did not differ by HIV status, supporting the use of both approaches in sub-Saharan Africa.

Title: Early experience of a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at Peking Union Medical College Hospital: a retrospective descriptive study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart-brain comorbidities present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because neurological and cardiac conditions often share pathophysiological mechanisms yet create conflicting treatment demands. Multidisciplinary wards integrating neurosurgery, cardiac surgery, cardiology, and neurology have been proposed, but real-world experience remains limited. We report the initial experience of a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at a Chinese tertiary referral center.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of all consecutive patients admitted to the Heart-Brain Integrated Ward at Peking Union Medical College Hospital between July 1 and August 21, 2026. Clinical data were entered prospectively into the electronic medical record during routine care and analyzed retrospectively. Variables included demographics, neurological and cardiac diagnoses, a six-category comorbidity classification, MDT decisions, treatment strategies, and discharge outcomes. Treatment categories were predefined as: (i) diagnostic procedures, (ii) therapeutic single-system interventions, (iii) staged dual-system treatment within the same admission, and (iv) synchronous dual-system treatment in a single session.
RESULTS: Fifty-six patients (42 males, 75.0%; mean age 62.4 ± 12.2 years, range 19-80) were enrolled. The most common category was I.1 (shared atherosclerotic vascular disease; 29/56, 51.8%), predominantly ischemic cerebrovascular disease with coronary artery disease (18/56, 32.1%). Category IV (psychocardiological disorders) accounted for 12 patients (21.4%), and Category V (therapeutically interactive) for 3 (5.4%). All patients underwent at least one MDT discussion (100%), and 55 (98.2%) required a second. Of 56 patients, 41 (73.2%) underwent surgical or endovascular intervention and 15 (26.8%) received medical management or remained under evaluation. Among treated patients, 4 (7.1%) received synchronous dual-system procedures, 13 (23.2%) completed staged procedures within the same admission, and 24 (42.9%) underwent single-system intervention. Fourteen patients (25.0%) required intervention for both organ systems. No in-hospital mortality or major procedure-related complications were observed among 38 discharged patients (67.9%); 18 patients (32.1%) remained hospitalized at data cutoff.
CONCLUSIONS: Establishing a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at a tertiary referral center appears operationally feasible and enables structured MDT-based care for complex neuro-cardiac patients. The early disease spectrum is dominated by atherosclerotic pan-vascular disease. Synchronous dual-system procedures were performed in a small selected subset without observed major early events among discharged patients, but this cannot establish safety or generalizability. Larger prospective studies with controlled comparisons and longer follow-up are needed.

Title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis of 39,918 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (RA-CABG) is an evolving minimally invasive alternative to conventional CABG (C-CABG), but comparative evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis to compare outcomes between RA-CABG and C-CABG.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science through January 2026. Studies comparing RA-CABG to C-CABG reporting at least one outcome of interest were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses using DerSimonian-Laird estimators were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Trial sequential analysis evaluated the conclusiveness of cumulative evidence.
RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 39,918 patients (13,638 RA-CABG; 26,280 C-CABG) were included. All included studies were observational in design, and long-term outcome data were sparse. RA-CABG was associated with significantly lower mortality (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.43-0.69; P < 0.001; I²=0%), atrial fibrillation (OR 0.53; P < 0.001), respiratory failure (OR 0.31; P < 0.001), blood transfusion (OR 0.28; P < 0.001), hospital length of stay (MD - 1.95 days; P < 0.001), and ICU stay (MD - 22.7 h; P < 0.001). Stroke showed a non-significant trend favoring RA-CABG (OR 0.76; P = 0.071). Trial sequential analysis confirmed conclusive evidence for mortality, atrial fibrillation, respiratory failure, and blood transfusion. Results were robust across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: In this meta-analysis of observational studies, RA-CABG was associated with significantly improved short-term outcomes compared to C-CABG across multiple endpoints, with conclusive statistical evidence for four of seven binary outcomes. However, all included studies were observational, and these associations should be interpreted with caution given potential residual confounding and case-selection bias. Multicenter randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Preoperative levels of biomarkers of coagulation to predict massive bleeding after surgical repair for acute type A aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly emergent condition with a high mortality rate. The condition poses an imminent risk of serious complications such as coagulopathy with massive bleeding. This increases the risk of mortality even after surgical repair. Procoagulant drugs are routinely administered but some patients still suffer postoperative massive bleeding that can be fatal. The study aimed to investigate whether massive bleeding after surgical treatment for type A aortic dissection can be predicted preoperatively through routine coagulation tests such as APTT, PT (INR), fibrinogen, D-dimer, and platelets.
METHODS: The study was a retrospective, single-center, cohort study performed at a tertiary cardiac surgery unit. A total of 474 patients who underwent surgery for type A aortic dissection at our department between January 2005 and May 2023 were included in the study. Of these, 87 patients had massive postoperative bleeding after surgery for type A aortic dissection and were compared to 387 patients who did not have massive postoperative bleeding. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed using logistic regression. The multivariable model included predictors of massive bleeding. Bleeding-related routine lab variables were then forced into the model.
RESULTS: Patients with massive bleeding (18%) had higher preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) (33 s vs 29 s, p<0.01), and creatinine (97 µmol/L vs 87 µmol/L, p<0.01), as well as lower preoperative platelet counts (172 × 109/L vs 187 × 109/L, p=0.03) compared to patients without massive bleeding. Patients with massive bleeding also had longer duration of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) (221 min vs 170 min, p<0.01) and suffered more postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative APTT per mmol increment (OR 1.04 (95% CI 1.01-1.07, p=0.01), preoperative APTT > 34.5 s (OR 2.95 (95% CI 1.60-5.47), p<0.01), preoperative creatinine > 82.5 µmol/L (OR 2.16 (95% CI 1.15-4.06), p=0.02), hypertension (OR 1.83 (95% CI 1.01-3.32), p<0.05) and CPB time per 10 min increment (OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13, p<0.01)) as independent predictors of massive bleeding.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

Title: Plerixafor and G-CSF Versus Placebo and G-CSF in Moderately Mobilizing Patients With Multiple Myeloma to Optimize Hematopoietic Stem Cell Collection Results (OPTIMIZE).
Abstract: Efficient collection of hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) is essential for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in multiple myeloma (MM). Although plerixafor is routinely used in poor mobilizers, its role in patients with intermediate mobilization capacity remains unclear. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IV trial, MM patients with peripheral blood (PB) CD34+ counts of 15-40 cells/μL after steady-state G-CSF mobilization were randomized to receive plerixafor or placebo. The primary endpoint was successful collection of ≥ 6.0 × 106 CD34+ cells/kg, sufficient for two ASCTs, during a single apheresis session. Secondary endpoints included CD34+ kinetics, graft composition, colony-forming capacity, engraftment, immune reconstitution, and safety. Twenty-one patients were enrolled before premature study termination due to changes in first-line MM therapy and the COVID-19 pandemic. Plerixafor significantly increased PB CD34+ cell counts compared with placebo (p < 0.001). All patients receiving plerixafor achieved the primary endpoint, whereas none in the placebo group achieved it (p < 0.001). Mean CD34+ yield was significantly higher with plerixafor (10.4 ± 1.9 × 106/kg vs. 2.9 ± 1.3 × 106/kg; p < 0.001). Plerixafor-mobilized grafts contained significantly higher numbers of primitive hematopoietic progenitor subsets and demonstrated increased CFU-GM formation, indicating enhanced clonogenic potential. Despite marked differences in graft quantity and quality, engraftment kinetics, graft sustainability, and immune reconstitution were comparable between groups. In MM patients with intermediate mobilization capacity, the addition of plerixafor markedly improved stem cell mobilization efficiency and enriched grafts with functionally robust progenitor cells. These findings suggest that selected patients beyond conventional poor mobilizers may benefit from plerixafor-assisted mobilization. Trial Registration: EudraCT nr.: 2016-004122-41.

Title: Systemic inflammation in optic neuropathies: comparative insights from hematological and composite indices.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices among patients with multiple sclerosis-associated optic neuritis (MS-ON), non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), idiopathic intracranial hypertension-related optic neuropathy (IIH-ON), and healthy controls, while accounting for demographic confounding.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 135 participants: 36 patients with MS-ON, 29 with NAION, 34 with IIH-ON, and 36 healthy controls. Six composite inflammatory indices, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score, were calculated from routine laboratory measurements obtained at diagnosis before treatment. Log-transformed indices were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for age and sex. False discovery rate correction was applied across the six indices. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed for indices showing significant adjusted group effects.
RESULTS: Significant differences in age and sex distribution were observed among the groups. After adjustment for age and sex, overall group effects remained for NLR (p = 0.008) and SIRI (p = 0.033), although only NLR remained significant after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.047). Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons demonstrated higher NLR in MS-ON than in healthy controls (adjusted geometric means 2.83 vs. 1.80, p = 0.005). NLR discriminated MS-ON from controls with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.681 (95% CI, 0.554-0.807), while SIRI showed a comparable AUC of 0.661 (95% CI, 0.535-0.787). Among conventional hematological parameters, red cell distribution width remained elevated in IIH-ON, whereas serum albumin remained lower in MS-ON and IIH-ON after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In the primary analysis, NLR was the only index that retained significance after adjustment for age, sex, and multiple testing, with higher values in MS-ON than in healthy controls. The sensitivity of several other indices to robust inference and the modest ROC performance warrant cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of dietary supplements in dilated cardiomyopathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure and cardiovascular mortality, partly due to impaired myocardial energy metabolism. Dietary supplements may offer benefits through improved mitochondrial function and antioxidant effects, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) suggest they can enhance cardiac function in DCM. However, direct comparisons among supplements are lacking, and the optimal strategy and dose-response relationship remain undetermined.
METHODS: Eight databases were searched for RCTs evaluating dietary supplements in DCM. Continuous outcomes were analysed by frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA; Stata/MP 18.0); N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class were synthesised by pairwise meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs (1,259 participants) were included. For left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) 150 mg/d produced the largest improvement versus conventional treatment (CT) (mean difference [MD] = 11.26, 95% confidence interval [CI] 8.55 ~ 13.98; surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] 93.4%), followed by taurine and CoQ10 90 mg/d. CoQ10 150 mg/d also ranked first for reducing left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD; -5.40, - 8.14 ~ - 2.66) and end-systolic diameter (LVESD; -6.31, - 8.60 ~ - 4.01). For heart rate, n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) gave the most robust reduction (- 3.94 bpm, - 5.11 ~ - 2.77). In pairwise meta-analysis, CoQ10 lowered NT-proBNP and improved NYHA status (risk ratio [RR] for ≥ 1-class improvement 1.23, 1.10 ~ 1.38). Network inconsistency was significant for LVESD (P = 0.008). Certainty of evidence (GRADE) was low to very low, and moderate only for n-3 PUFAs; all supplements were well tolerated.
CONCLUSIONS: In this network, higher-dose CoQ10 (150 mg/d) showed the most favourable overall profile for systolic function and ventricular dimensions, while n-3 PUFAs offered the most reliable benefit for heart rate. Given small samples, predominantly Chinese open-label trials, a heterogeneous and time-varying CT comparator, local inconsistency, and poor safety reporting, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, well-designed international RCTs with longer follow-up.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: Long-Term Quantitative MRI and Quality-of-Life After Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke - A MR CLEAN-NO IV Substudy.
Abstract: This study aims to explore the long-term evolution of endovascular treatment after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) using quantitative MRI, and its relationship with quality of life (QoL). In this long-term substudy of patients from the MR CLEAN-NO IV trial, patients were included who received 24-hour post-stroke MRI and were functionally independent 90 days after stroke onset. Patients underwent a quantitative MRI exam three years after stroke onset to measure focal volume loss, myelin damage, iron deposition, and atrophy within and around the ischemic lesion seen on 24-hour-MRI, in addition to a QoL assessment. Bayesian statistical analyses were used to assess MRI measures lateralized to the ipsilateral hemisphere and to evaluate the relationship of these measures with baseline and treatment characteristics along with QoL. The Bayes Factor (BF) reflected moderate, strong or very strong evidence (BF = 3.0;20;1.5⋅102 respectively). In the 24 included patients, prominent focal volume loss, iron deposition, ventricular enlargement and myelin damage (BF:2.0⋅102) were observed peripheral to the initial 24-hour DWI lesion at long-term FU MRI. In the basal ganglia nuclei, very strong evidence of focal volume loss (BF > 8.1⋅102) and moderate to very strong evidence of iron deposition (BF: 5.0 to 2.7⋅102) were observed at long-term assessment. Higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced long-term ventricular atrophy (BF:5.8). Long-term differences in ipsilateral versus contralateral hippocampal volume difference (BF:8.0) and iron deposition (BF:4.1) were moderately associated with QoL. Long-term subtle yet widespread demyelination and iron deposition were observed, and these changes correlated with long-term recovery.

Title: Advanced Age is Not Associated With An Increased Risk of Postoperative Complications in Breast Reduction Surgery: A Comparative Study on 1716 Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age is frequently cited as a surgical risk factor; yet, its influence on outcomes following breast reduction remains unclear. With increasing numbers of elderly patients presenting with macromastia, determining whether advanced age independently affects complication rates is clinically important.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether age ≥ 65 years is an independent risk factor for postoperative complications following bilateral reduction mammaplasty and to identify associated patient- and procedure-related variables.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1716 female patients who underwent bilateral breast reduction at a single tertiary center (2005-2024), stratified into older (≥ 65 years, n = 174), and non-older (< 65 years, n = 1542) groups. Primary outcome was Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications requiring surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Older patients had significantly higher comorbidity prevalence (69.0% vs. 46.1%; p < 0.001), including diabetes and hypertension, and greater bilateral resection weights. Despite this, overall complication rates were significantly lower in the older group (8.6% vs. 16.1%; OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.009). Hematoma and deep wound infection rates were also lower, while fat necrosis occurred more frequently and was managed conservatively in most cases. On multivariable analysis, higher BMI (OR 1.10; p = 0.004) and active smoking (OR 1.80; p = 0.004) were independent predictors of complications; age ≥ 65 was not significantly associated with complications (OR 0.55; p = 0.062).
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced age alone was not independently associated with increased complications. BMI and smoking were the main modifiable factors associated with postoperative risk. Age-based exclusion criteria are not supported by these findings in this cohort of selected surgical patients; individualized risk assessment should be applied to all candidates.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

Title: Effects of immersive virtual reality and non-immersive video distraction on preoperative anxiety in patients undergoing elective abdominal surgery: a three-arm randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative anxiety negatively impacts surgical outcomes. This study evaluated the effects of immersive virtual reality (VR) vs non-immersive video distraction on preoperative anxiety, physiological stress, and heart rate in elective abdominal surgery.
METHODS: In this three-arm randomized controlled trial (NCT05718661), 96 elective abdominal surgery patients were allocated to immersive VR, non-immersive video, or a control group ( n = 32  per group). Both intervention groups viewed identical relaxing audiovisual content for 15 min via a VR headset or a smartphone screen; controls received standard care. Preoperative anxiety was measured with the Visual Analogue Scale-Anxiety (VAS-A). Physiological stress scores and heart rate were tracked using a wearable smart band before and after the intervention.
RESULTS: VAS-A scores worsened in controls (p < 0.001) but decreased significantly in both the VR (p < 0.001) and video (p = 0.002) groups, with no significant difference between the two active interventions (p > 0.05). Device-derived stress scores increased in controls (p = 0.018) and decreased in the video group (p = 0.017), with no change in the VR group (p = 0.568). Heart rate changes did not differ significantly among groups (p < 0.206).
CONCLUSIONS: Both immersive VR and non-immersive video distraction significantly reduce preoperative anxiety compared with standard care; however, VR is not superior to conventional video viewing. Given its equivalent efficacy, lower cost, and simpler implementation, non-immersive video represents a practical, scalable non-pharmacological strategy for perioperative anxiety management.

Title: Oral eplerenone in first-episode acute central serous chorioretinopathy: results of a double-masked randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is a pachychoroid disorder characterized by serous retinal detachment driven by choroidal vascular dysfunction and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) overactivation. Eplerenone, a selective MR antagonist, has been proposed as a therapeutic option, although clinical evidence remains inconsistent.
METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 44 patients with first-episode acute CSCR received either oral eplerenone (25 mg twice daily) or placebo for three months. Outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), subretinal fluid (SRF) height, subfoveal choroidal thickness (CT), and OCT-angiography parameters of retinal and choroidal microvasculature.
RESULTS: Both groups demonstrated significant reductions in CMT and SRF over time, but SRF absorption was significantly greater in the eplerenone group at 3 months (P < 0.05). Choriocapillaris vessel density and flow index improved significantly with eplerenone (P < 0.001), while superficial, deep, and radial peripapillary plexus densities did not differ between groups. BCVA improved similarly in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Eplerenone accelerates SRF resolution and enhances choriocapillaris perfusion in acute CSCR, although visual outcomes remain comparable to placebo. Early MR antagonism may offer anatomical and microvascular benefits in CSCR management.

Title: Autonomic function and signal complexity reflect level and severity of traumatic spinal cord injury.
Abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Observational single-centre cohort study.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and signal complexity (SC) and their relationships with neurological injury level and severity, as well as their prognostic value for six-month mortality and functional recovery in patients with traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI).
SETTING: Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden.
METHODS: This study included 164 adult patients with TSCI treated in neurointensive care (NIC) (2008-2022). Continuous high-frequency physiological data from the first 7 post-injury days were analysed to derive HRV, BRS, and SC for heart rate (HR), mean arterial pressure, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Associations with neurological injury level, injury severity, NIC physiology, neurological improvement, and six-month mortality were assessed.
RESULTS: Patients with cervical injuries had higher HRV, BRS (both p < 0.01), and SC for DBP (p < 0.05) than those with thoracic injuries. Complete cervical injuries had higher HRV (p < 0.05), but lower HR SC (p < 0.01) compared with incomplete cervical injuries. Higher HR SC was associated with neurological improvement at discharge (odds ratio 1.08 [95% confidence interval 1.01-1.16]; p < 0.05), whereas higher HRV was associated with increased six-month mortality (odds ratio 1.01 [95% confidence interval 1.00-1.02]; p < 0.05). Other autonomic and complexity measures showed limited prognostic value.
CONCLUSION: Systemic autonomic indices after TSCI vary with injury level and severity and may capture distinct aspects of autonomic dysfunction beyond clinical grading. However, their limited prognostic value for neurological recovery and mortality suggest that outcome prediction after TSCI may depend more on other clinical factors and, possibly, more direct intraspinal physiological markers.
SPONSORSHIP: NA.

Title: Impact on mortality of inhaled nitric oxide in newborns ≤34 weeks with early hypoxemic respiratory failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is approved for hypoxemic respiratory failure (HRF) associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH) in term and near-term neonates; however, its use in preterm infants ≤34 weeks' gestation remains controversial, with limited and inconsistent evidence of survival benefit.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between iNO use and mortality in preterm neonates ≤34 weeks' gestation.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Major databases were searched up to October 11, 2025. Observational studies and clinical trials reporting mortality in preterm infants with early HRF treated with iNO were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and six (n = 556 infants) in the meta-analysis. Study quality ranged from poor to good, with limitations related to confounding and heterogeneity. No significant reduction in mortality was observed with iNO compared with standard care (RR 0.65; 95% CI 0.29-1.48; I² = 55.7%). Infants receiving iNO were more severely ill at baseline. A positive oxygenation response was associated with improved outcomes and varied by gestational age (GA), timing of PH onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and hypoxemia severity.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence regarding the survival benefit of iNO in preterm infants ≤34 weeks remains inconclusive.
IMPACT: This systematic review and meta-analysis show that inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is not associated with a consistent reduction in mortality in preterm infants ≤34 weeks at the population level. It adds evidence that outcomes are strongly influenced by clinical context, particularly, illness severity, gestational age, timing of pulmonary hypertension onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and response to therapy. These findings support a selective, phenotype-driven approach rather than routine iNO use in all preterm infants with hypoxemic respiratory failure. The results may inform clinical decision-making and highlight the need for well-designed randomized trials in this high-risk population.

Title: Testing neurobiological models of reward/incentive sensitization in the continuation of alcohol use disorder (AUD) symptoms in young adults with AUD: A four-year longitudinal study.
Journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains an urgent public health problem. Alcohol response phenotype may be an important factor underlying vulnerability to and progression of AUD. This study examined the prospective association between acute alcohol responses and continued or remitted AUD over time in young adults with AUD. This sample was N = 101 AUD participants (Mage=27.1 ± 4.0 SD yrs) comprising the third cohort of the Chicago Social Drinking Project. They completed two beverage challenge  laboratory sessions (0.8 g/kg fixed-dose alcohol vs. placebo) and four years of follow-up to ascertain future AUD symptoms, drinking behaviors, and consequences. Retention was high with an overall 99.2% follow-up rate. Analyses identified three AUD trajectory subgroups over follow-up including a high AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 37), a medium AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 48), and a low AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 16). Generalized estimating equations showed that greater sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, including stimulation and hedonic and motivational reward (liking and wanting, respectively) predicted more AUD symptoms over follow-up (ps<0.001) and were positively associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. However,  sedation, heart rate, and cortisol response to alcohol were not  significantly associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. In sum, greater alcohol stimulation, liking, and wanting prospectively predicted the continuation and increasing severity of AUD over a four-year period. The findings challenge theoretical models emphasizing reward deficit and global tolerance in addiction and support the role of positive reinforcement, indexed by sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, as an important factor in AUD  persistence. CLINICAL TRIAL: Name: Chicago Social Drinking Project Registration #: NCT00961792 URL: http://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT00961792.

Title: Angiotensin peptide and aldosterone concentrations in response to four classes of blood-pressure-lowering drugs in hypertensive patients: A randomized trial.
Abstract: The renin angiotensin aldosterone system (RAS) regulates blood pressure and fluid balance by a cascade of angiotensin (Ang) peptides. Antihypertensive drug classes differentially modulate this cascade. This study examined how four mechanistically distinct antihypertensive drugs affect plasma concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone in untreated hypertensive patients. In this randomized, open-label, parallel-group study, 88 patients received 4 weeks of monotherapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi), angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB), calcium channel blocker (CCB), or hydrochlorothiazide (HCT). Equilibrium concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone were quantified by LC-MS at baseline and after 4 weeks, both pre- and 4 h post-dose; drug exposure was confirmed by measured drug concentrations. Seventy-two participants completed the 4-week treatment (ACEi n = 18, ARB n = 17, CCB n = 20, HCT n = 17). The most prominent effects were seen for Ang I, Ang II, and aldosterone and were reflected in biomarkers for plasma renin activity (PRA-Q; Ang I+Ang II), ACE activity (ACE-Q; Ang II/Ang I), and the aldosterone/Ang II ratio (AA2-R). Downstream peptides showed minimal or no changes. Relative to baseline, ACEi increased Ang I and reduced ACE-Q. ARB increased Ang I and Ang II and lowered AA2-R without altering ACE-Q. CCB and HCT produced only minor changes. ACE-Q < 1.05 pM/pM identified ACEi use, and AA2-R < 0.85 pM/pM as well as Ang II > 175 pM identified ARB use. RAS-targeted monotherapy produces distinct peptide-level signatures that can be captured by Ang-derived biomarkers, supporting their potential utility for monitoring drug intake in personalized hypertension management.

Title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on serum vitamin D levels and health outcomes in pediatric population with obesity/overweight: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Because 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol is lipophilic, children with obesity/overweight are at increased risk of its deficiency, potentially leading to health issues such as compromising bone mineralization and cardiometabolic health.
OBJECTIVES: Our goal was to assess the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol supplementation on serum Vitamin D levels and various health parameters such as BMI and cardiovascular risk markers.
METHODOLOGY: Data were extracted from PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar. Following search string was used in each database: (Vitamin D OR 25(OH)D OR cholecalciferol) AND (Obese OR Overweight) AND (randomized trial OR RCT OR intervention) AND (children OR adolescent OR pediatric). Clinical trials assessing the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol D supplementation in pediatric populations with overweight or obesity, regardless of formulation, dosage, or duration, were included. A total of 24 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 11 randomized controlled trials were eligible for meta-analysis. The included studies' quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB-2) tool. Primary outcome was serum Vitamin D levels while secondary outcomes include cardiovascular risk markers, lipid profile, insulin sensitivity, and change in BMI. Follow-up done at 8 weeks, 12 weeks, 24 weeks, 26 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.
RESULTS: Supplementing with 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol significantly raised the levels of serum vitamin D in children with obesity/overweight. No adverse events occurred following supplementation. Decrease in BMI, serum triglycerides and inflammatory markers were observed but its effects on metabolism and cardiovascular health remained insignificant. According to meta-analysis, vitamin D supplementation (interventional) arm group differed from the placebo by a standardized mean difference of 3.12 ng/ml (95% CI:1.72-4.52).
CONCLUSION: Vitamin D supplementation in children with overweight /obesity correct the deficiency and significantly raise Vitamin D levels with no adverse events. To assess effective therapies to enhance metabolic and cardiovascular outcomes in the pediatric population with overweight/obesity, new trials should be conducted.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Thromboembolic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter and Type 2 Diabetes: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
Comparative Cardiorenal Efficacy and Safety of SGLT2 Inhibitors and Finerenone in Chronic Kidney Disease With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: No randomized trial has compared SGLT2 inhibitors with finerenone in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with Type 2 diabetes. We estimated their comparative cardiorenal efficacy and safety.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and trial registries were searched from inception to August 2026 for placebo-controlled outcome trials. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled in a frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, and the between-class contrast was derived indirectly through placebo. Risk of bias followed RoB 2 and certainty followed CINeMA.
RESULTS: Ten trial datasets formed a star network without closed loops. Versus placebo, both classes reduced kidney function progression (SGLT2 inhibitors HR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.56-0.73; finerenone 0.84, 0.77-0.92) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.61, 0.53-0.69; 0.78, 0.66-0.92). Indirectly, SGLT2 inhibitors were favoured for kidney function progression (0.76, 0.64-0.90) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.77, 0.63-0.95), with no significant difference for atherothrombotic events or mortality. The kidney contrast remained significant after excluding high-risk-of-bias datasets, restricting to dedicated CKD trials and applying a uniform endpoint; the heart-failure contrast did not persist in dedicated CKD trials. Finerenone increased hyperkalemia without increasing acute kidney injury. Certainty was low or very low for every between-class comparison.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors and finerenone both provide cardiorenal protection and appear complementary rather than interchangeable. Indirect differences favouring SGLT2 inhibitors derive from a loop-free network with unverifiable transitivity and low certainty; they are hypothesis-generating and should not be used to rank the agents. Safety domains are not reported comparably across classes.
