Exploratory adjusted analyses incorporating measured kidney-related variables were consistent with substantial confounding and should be interpreted cautiously because key measures of illness severity were unavailable. Ninety-day readmission occurred in 40% of hospitalizations and did not differ by consultation status.
CONCLUSIONS: Nephrology consultation occurred in fewer than half of hospitalizations and was more common in patients with advanced kidney dysfunction; however, a significant proportion of patients with acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease did not receive consultation. These findings highlight variability in nephrology consultation practices and referral patterns in hospitalized patients with heart failure and kidney dysfunction.

Title: Real-World Diagnostic Coding and Biomarker Testing for CKD Across Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cancer: A Multisite OMOP Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing prevalence of CKD necessitates standardized assessment of kidney function across various healthcare sites.1 Patients at risk, particularly those with diabetes, hypertension, or cancer, frequently do not receive recommended laboratory monitoring.2,3 This study assesses guideline recommended testing among various medical centers using the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) common data model (CDM). The objectives are to report methodologies for extracting relevant measurements within OMOP and assess the frequency of specific biomarker evaluations and diagnosis codes in select cohorts.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of adult patients at 6 medical centers throughout the U.S. with a healthcare encounter to determine the frequency of diagnosis codes and biomarker measurements [eGFR, urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR), cystatin C, and aldosterone levels] among patients with relevant risk factors and probable CKD (sustained eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73m2).
RESULTS: Among 9,212,799 patients with medical visits in 2024, 3% had a documented diagnosis of CKD, while 8% and 17% had a diagnosis of diabetes or hypertension, respectively. Also in 2024, only 47% of patients with probable CKD had a diagnosis code for CKD. Of the patients with diagnosed and probable CKD by eGFR, 25% had an UACR in 2024. Only 30% of patients with a diagnosis of diabetes, and 14% of patients with a diagnosis of hypertension had an UACR and eGFR in 2024. From 2021-2024, Cystatin C values were more common in patients with cancer compared to patients without cancer (1% vs 0.5%). The highest frequency of aldosterone testing (7%) was observed in patients with a diagnosis code for hypertension, serum potassium level <3 meq/L, eGFR> 60 ml/min/1.73m2, and albuminuria.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates low frequency of guideline-recommended kidney health assessments and CKD diagnosis across multiple U.S. medical centers, including albuminuria, cystatin C, and aldosterone testing.

Title: [Correlation between albuminuria and glycated haemoglobin in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²].
Abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage chronic kidney disease worldwide. Albuminuria, assessed by the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), is an independent marker of both renal prognosis and cardiovascular risk. To assess the correlation between HbA1c and ACR in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and to determine the prevalence of pathological albuminuria in this population. A retrospective case-control study conducted from June 2023 to June 2026. Cases were diabetic patients (HbA1c ≥ 6.5%) and controls were non-diabetic subjects (HbA1c < 5.7%), all with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (KDIGO stages G1: ≥ 90 and G2: 60-89) and an available ACR measurement. Albuminuria was classified according to KDIGO as A1 (< 30 mg/g), A2 (30-300 mg/g) and A3 (> 300 mg/g). eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI 2021 equation. Statistical analysis used Spearman, Mann-Whitney and Chi² tests. Four hundred and twenty subjects were included: 232 diabetic patients and 188 non-diabetic controls. The prevalence of pathological albuminuria was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in controls (44.0% vs. 21.3%; p < 0.0001), as was the median ACR (23.5 vs. 9.0 mg/g; p < 0.0001). Within the diabetic group, no significant correlation was found between HbA1c and ACR (Spearman r = 0.016; p = 0.814). In contrast, ACR was significantly higher in stage G2 than in stage G1: 33.5 vs. 15,0 mg/g (p = 0.003), and increased with age (r = 0.169; p = 0.010). This study reveals a high prevalence of pathological albuminuria in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Point HbA1c does not predict the degree of albuminuria, whereas eGFR stage and age are its main biological determinants. These findings support an integrated biological approach combining ACR and eGFR with HbA1c monitoring.

Title: Association of BMAL1, CLOCK, and CRY1 gene polymorphisms with metabolic syndrome and glycemic phenotypes: a case-control study in a Turkish population.
Abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) comprises cardiometabolic abnormalities that elevate the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Growing evidence links circadian rhythm disruption to obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and MetS. This study investigated functional polymorphisms in circadian rhythm-related genes and their associations with MetS and key clinical parameters. A total of 200 patients with MetS and 104 healthy controls were enrolled. Genotyping was performed using PCR-RFLP. Univariate and age-adjusted multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate independent genetic risk factors. The GC genotype of the CRY1 rs2287161 polymorphism was found to be significantly more frequent in the MetS group compared with healthy controls (p = 0.009). After adjusting for age in multivariable logistic regression, the CRY1 rs2287161 GC genotype remained a significant, independent factor for MetS (adjusted OR=0.381, 95%  CI: 0.175-0.831, p=0.015). No significant differences were observed between the MetS and control groups in terms of genotype distributions of BMAL1 rs7950226 and CLOCK rs1801260 (p > 0.05). Among MetS patients, individuals carrying the BMAL1 rs7950226 AA genotype exhibited significantly higher fasting plasma glucose levels compared with those carrying the GA and GG genotypes (p = 0.039). An altered distribution of the CRY1 rs2287161 polymorphism was observed in this Turkish cohort, with the GC genotype showing an age-independent statistical association with MetS risk. Additionally, BMAL1 rs7950226 variation modulates glycemic parameters within MetS patients, reinforcing the role of core circadian genes in metabolic regulation.

Title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system.
RESULTS: Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

Title: Home-Based Programs and Cardiac Rehabilitation Participation Among Veterans With Ischemic Heart Disease.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a guideline-recommended secondary prevention program that reduces morbidity and mortality among patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) yet remains underutilized. Over the past decade, the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has implemented strategies to increase CR participation, including expansion of virtual home-based CR (HBCR) programs as alternatives to traditional center-based CR (CBCR).
OBJECTIVE: To examine temporal trends and factors associated with CR participation among veterans with IHD.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used national VHA electronic health record data to evaluate CR participation among veterans hospitalized for IHD, identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9), ICD-10, or Current Procedural Terminology codes from 2012 to 2022. Data were analyzed from October 25, 2025, to July 25, 2026.
EXPOSURES: Availability of CR delivery models at Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities, including referral to community care programs only, VA CBCR, or VA HBCR.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of eligible veterans with acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft surgery who participated in any type of CR within 12 months of the index event, identified using Current Procedural Terminology codes and VA stop codes from VA-provided, VA-purchased, or Medicare-claimed services. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with CR participation.
RESULTS: Among 405 907 veterans with IHD (mean [SD] age, 68.5 [11.1] years; 391 998 men [96.6%]), 63 185 (15.6%) participated in CR. Participation increased from 9.6% in 2012 to 17.1% in 2022, with a peak of 19.7% in 2018. In 2022, participation was higher at facilities offering HBCR (20.0%) compared with those offering CBCR without HBCR (14.8%) or referral to community care programs only (14.3%). The adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of participation among veterans treated at facilities offering HBCR was 1.80 (95% CI, 1.75-1.84), whereas the AOR of participation at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.26-1.32) compared with referral to community care programs only.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of veterans with IHD, participation in CR nearly doubled between 2012 and 2022. Patients who had index events at facilities offering HBCR had higher CR participation than those at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR, or at facilities offering only referral to community care. Broader availability of HBCR programs may help improve participation within large health systems.

Title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Facility Access and Clinical Outcomes Among Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The proliferation of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) facilities across the US has raised questions about whether expanding capacity improves outcomes in areas already served vs those without prior access.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between the opening of PCI-capable facilities and outcomes following acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in communities with and without baseline PCI access.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used California data from inpatient, emergency department, and ambulatory surgery encounters from January 1, 2011, to December 31, 2022, including all adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of AMI. Zip code communities were categorized by baseline (2011) access to PCI-capable facilities within a 30-minute drive.
EXPOSURE: Opening of a PCI-capable facility within 30 minutes of a community's zip code during the study period.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were (1) admission to a PCI-capable facility, (2) receipt of PCI during the index hospitalization, (3) unscheduled acute care visit within 30 days, and (4) all-cause mortality at 30 days and 1 year. Linear probability models with community and time-fixed effects estimated changes in outcomes following PCI facility openings separately for communities with and without baseline access.
RESULTS: Among 590 282 patients with AMI (157 435 younger than age 60 years [27%]; 222 773 female [38%]; 63 460 Asian [11%], 129 137 Hispanic [22%], 315 326 White [53%]), 500 778 (85%) lived in communities with baseline PCI access, and 89 504 (15%) lived in communities without; 18 805 patients (21%) without baseline access experienced a PCI opening. Openings in communities without baseline access were associated with a 30.0 percentage point (pp) increase (95% CI, 28.2 to 31.8 pp) in admission to PCI-capable hospitals and a 5.1 pp increase (95% CI, 3.3 to 7.0 pp) in PCI receipt, along with reductions in 30-day (-1.8 pp; 95% CI, -3.2 to -0.5 pp) and 1-year (-2.8 pp; 95% CI, -4.7 to -1.0 pp) mortality. In contrast, openings in communities with baseline access were associated with smaller gains in admission (1.5 pp; 95% CI, 1.1 to 1.9 pp), modest increases in PCI use (1.0 pp; 95% CI, 0.5 to 1.6 pp), decreases in unscheduled visits within 30 days (-0.7 pp; 95% CI, -1.2 to -0.2 pp), and no mortality change. Sensitivity analyses restricted to higher-volume PCI centers (50 annual cases or more) yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 590 282 patients with AMI in California, opening new PCI facilities was associated with substantial improvements in communities without prior PCI availability, including a 53% relative increase in access to admission, 16% increase in PCI use, and 20% and 15% reductions in 30-day and 1-year mortality, respectively. In contrast, already served areas showed smaller benefits and no mortality improvement. PCI expansion should prioritize underserved regions to maximize population-level benefits and avoid inefficient duplication of services.

Title: Culture results of heart valves resected from patients with active Enterococcus faecalis infective endocarditis undergoing heart valve surgery: insights into duration of antibiotic treatment required to achieve valve sterilisation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Heart valve culture results from patients with infective endocarditis (IE) provide insights into the antibiotic treatment duration required to achieve valve sterilisation. We aimed to assess the valve culture positivity rates of valves resected from patients with Enterococcus faecalis IE (EFIE).
METHODS: This was a national retrospective observational cohort study assessing adults with EFIE receiving valve surgery from 2004 to 2023 in Aotearoa New Zealand. We compared the valve culture result with the antibiotic treatment regimen and duration received before surgery.
RESULTS: One hundred and nine patients with EFIE met inclusion criteria. The valve culture positivity rate was 95% and 39% for valve samples obtained within 14 days or after 14 days of antibiotic treatment respectively. In addition to amoxicillin and/or benzylpenicillin, 40 patients received ceftriaxone and 38 received gentamicin as the sole pre-surgery synergistic antibiotic. There was no difference in valve culture positivity rates comparing the ceftriaxone and gentamicin synergistic antibiotic groups (P = 0.49).
CONCLUSION: Patients with EFIE who received valve surgery within 14 days of commencing antibiotic treatment had a very high valve culture positivity rate and this rate continued at moderate levels for those who received surgery after 14 days. We observed no difference in valve culture positivity rates when ceftriaxone or gentamicin was used as the sole pre-surgery synergistic antibiotic. The valve samples that remained culture positive after prolonged antibiotic treatment may help explain the higher relapse rate of patients with EFIE who do not receive valve surgery when compared with patients with other causes of IE.

Title: Partial Splenectomy as a Definitive or Interim Solution for Young Children with Transfusion-dependent Hemolytic Anemia: Long-term Results from a 15-Year Cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of partial splenectomy (PS) as a definitive or interim spleen-preserving strategy in young children with transfusion-dependent congenital hemolytic anemia (HA).
METHODS: Patients with congenital HA who required frequent blood transfusions and underwent PS at the present center between 2010 and 2025 were included. The hemoglobin (Hb) level, reticulocyte count, and the need for transfusions (if any) during the follow-up period were noted. Ultrasonography of the splenic remnant was obtained at baseline, 1 mo, and 18 mo following the PS.
RESULTS: Fourteen children (median age: 23 mo; range: 7-40) underwent PS by laparotomy (n = 12) or laparoscopy (n = 2). Median follow-up after PS was 9 y (IQR: 4.8-10.5). Following PS, 8/14 (57%) patients became transfusion-free, with a median Hb of 10.3 g/dL at last follow-up. Five (36%) patients continued to require occasional transfusions and subsequently underwent total splenectomy after a median of 3 y; All of them became transfusion-free thereafter. No episode of mortality, sepsis, or thrombosis occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: PS may serve as a definitive procedure in selected young children with congenital hemolytic anemia and as a bridge to later total splenectomy in others. This approach may be particularly relevant in resource-limited settings, where blood availability, transfusion safety, and the risk of transfusion-transmitted infections are concerning.

Title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Change in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR).
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments. Carotid Doppler spectrograms from a wireless, wearable critical care Doppler ultrasound system are analyzed for ccFTΔ during a PC (either infusion of 300 mL of crystalloid over 3 min or a Trendelenburg maneuver). The primary objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of PR patients by previously described ccFTΔ thresholds (i.e., both 4 and 7 ms ccFTΔ ), describe time-to-peak (TTP) ccFTΔ, and evaluate the ability of baseline ccFT to detect ccFTΔ during PC, using both the equations of Wodey and Bazett. Comparisons of related outcomes were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure, baseline ccFT discrimination was quantified using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and TTP was estimated using patient-level bootstrap resampling. Threshold-agnostic ccFTΔ trajectories were additionally explored using unsupervised k-means clustering of patient-level temporal responses for both correction equations.
RESULTS: A PC was attempted in 4367 patients and an adequate ccFTΔ was collected from 4,128 patients (95%). In total, 982,937 Doppler cardiac cycles are included. The median ccFTΔ was 7.3 milliseconds (ms). 51.9% of patients had a ccFTΔ ≥ 7 ms, while 68.6% had a ccFTΔ ≥ 4 ms by the equation of Wodey. For Bazett, these fractions were 61.2% and 73.5%, respectively. For patients identified as PR based upon either a 4 ms or 7 ms ccFTΔ threshold, the time-to-peak ccFTΔ was 27.5 s for both equations. Baseline absolute ccFT did not discriminate PR from PUR patients under both correction formulae (AUROC 0.56-0.57).
CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge this is the largest reported dataset of ED patients with suspected sepsis receiving PR assessments by Doppler ultrasound, comprising nearly 1 million Doppler cardiac cycles obtained from over 4100 ED patients. Both 7 ms and 4 ms ccFTΔ thresholds described clinically-accepted rates of PR. The TTP was roughly 30 s into PC and baseline ccFT did not accurately detect ccFTΔ during PC. Finally, a hypothesis-generating analysis identified four distinct ccFTΔ trajectories during PC which may represent unique preload response patterns during PR testing.

Title: Association of pericoronary and epicardial adipose tissue thickness with coronary artery calcium score using cardiac computed tomography.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the associations of pericoronary (PCAT) and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) thickness with coronary artery calcium score (CACS) using cardiac computed tomography.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 1,032 patients (516 women, 516 men; median age, 54 years) who underwent coronary CT angiography. CACS was quantified using the Agatston method. Mean PCAT thickness was measured at predefined anatomical landmarks along the major coronary arteries, while mean EAT thickness was assessed at the right ventricular free wall. Associations with CACS were evaluated using correlation, multivariable linear and logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: Detectable coronary artery calcification was observed in 432 patients (41.9%). Although both PCAT (r = 0.461, p < 0.001) and EAT thickness (r = 0.375, p < 0.001) correlated with CACS, PCAT thickness remained significantly associated with higher CACS after adjustment for age, sex, and EAT thickness. In logistic regression, each 1-mm increase in PCAT thickness was associated with 43% higher odds of coronary calcification (OR, 1.436; 95% CI: 1.298-1.588; p < 0.001). PCAT showed greater discriminatory performance than EAT (AUC, 0.736 vs. 0.695; DeLong p = 0.010), and adding PCAT to an age-and-sex model increased the AUC from 0.744 to 0.795 (DeLong p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: PCAT thickness was associated with CACS after adjustment for age, sex, and EAT thickness and showed greater discriminatory performance than EAT thickness for the presence of coronary calcification. PCAT thickness may provide additional imaging information from CCTA, although its incremental clinical value requires prospective validation.

Title: Cardiorenal Protective Glucose-Lowering Treatment Patterns in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Based on a Real-World Study: A Clinical Phenotype Cluster Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiorenal protective glucose-lowering treatments (CPT), consisting of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), are widely applied in clinical management of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes linked to CPT prescribing patterns and construct a multilevel correlation framework for standardized CPT clinical application.
METHODS: Data were extracted from the baseline dataset of an observational registry cohort study across 61 medical centers between 2023 and 2024. Based on multiple factors, clinical phenotypes of patients were identified via the Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) clustering algorithm, CPT utilization was compared across different phenotypes.
RESULTS: A total of 9000 patients with T2DM were enrolled [median age 55 (46, 63) years, 60.8% male and 39.2% female, median diabetes duration 5.37 (0.85, 11.44) years]. Three clinically distinct phenotypes were identified: Cluster 1 [older patients with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk], Cluster 2 (metabolically stable patients without cardiorenal risk), and Cluster 3 (younger patients with obesity, high metabolic risk and short diabetes duration). The CPT utilization rates of the three clusters were 49.0%, 44.1% and 51.1%, respectively (P < 0.001), with Cluster 3 having the highest rate. Cluster 2 was dominated by SGLT2is monotherapy (73.1%). Cluster 3 showed a marked preference for GLP-1RAs-based regimens (43.6% in total), whereas Cluster 1 had an intermediate proportion of GLP-1RAs-related regimens (31.5%).
CONCLUSION: Three clinical phenotypes were identified via cluster analysis. The younger obese group with high metabolic risk had the highest CPT utilization rate and preferred GLP-1RAs, while the older group with high ASCVD risk was predominantly treated with SGLT2is alone.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with https://www.chictr.org.cn/ under registration number ChiCTR230007376 on 20 July 2023.

Title: Oxidized mitochondrial DNA as a potential biomarker and mechanistic driver of autophagy-mitophagy dysregulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension: a narrative review.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is recognized as a mitochondria-centered disease characterized by early bioenergetic and redox abnormalities that influence pulmonary vascular remodeling. Oxidized mitochondrial DNA (Ox-mtDNA), which combines mitochondrial stress with innate immune activation and dysregulated Ca2+ signaling to sustain hyperproliferation and apoptosis resistance in pulmonary arterial endothelial and smooth muscle cells, is a persistent danger signal rather than just a result of mitochondrial injury. Vasodilator therapy targeting the prostacyclin, nitric oxide, and endothelin pathways has made great strides, yet many patients still make progress. These treatments primarily enhance hemodynamics and vasomotor tone, but they do not directly reverse the cellular and molecular mechanisms that sustain pulmonary vascular remodeling. In this model, inflammatory signaling and mitochondrial redox imbalance are mutually reinforcing rather than strictly sequential: oxidative stress produces Ox-mtDNA, which mediates inflammatory activation, and cytokine and interferon signaling from the inflammatory process further weakens antioxidant defenses and mitochondrial respiration, increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) output. Because Ox-mtDNA's synthesis, escape, sensing, and clearance all influence inflammatory tone and Ca2+ homeostasis, convergent experimental and clinical observations support Ox-mtDNA as an upstream, therapeutically actionable node. This review describes how mtDNA oxidation, reactive oxygen species amplification, and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload are all facilitated by the convergence of chronic hypoxia, inflammatory cytokines, altered shear stress, and genetic vulnerability. According to the literature, oxidative lesions increase mtDNA bioactivity and persistence when nuclease and autophagy-lysosome clearance systems are overloaded. Pathways of cytosolic and extracellular mtDNA escape, such as vesicular export, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) or voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC)-dependent leakage, and sublethal membrane permeabilization, are summarized in this review. It is also explained how Ox-mtDNA rewires the autophagy-mitophagy axis through reduced flux and skewed signaling, allowing injured mitochondria to continue acting as signal emitters. ER Ca2+ handling and stress-induced remodeling of ER-mitochondria contact sites (MAMs) as upstream amplifiers of mitochondrial damage are also covered. Instead of using prospective, longitudinal cohorts, the majority of these mechanistic data and the correlation between circulating Ox-mtDNA and PAH severity are now based on cross-sectional human sampling and non-PAH disease models. Therefore, until such validation is completed, the biomarker potential of Ox-mtDNA should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Title: Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided transumbilical three-port laparoscopic suprainguinal varicocelectomy with testicular artery and lymphatic preservation for pediatric varicocele: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the technical feasibility and short-term perioperative and cosmetic outcomes of indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence-guided transumbilical three-port laparoscopic suprainguinal varicocelectomy with testicular artery and lymphatic preservation in pediatric patients, and to describe changes in testicular volume and testicular volume discrepancy (TVD) at 6 months after surgery.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on pediatric patients with varicocele who underwent surgical treatment at our institution between January 2023 and December 2024. All patients underwent ICG fluorescence-guided transumbilical three-port laparoscopic suprainguinal varicocelectomy with testicular artery and lymphatic preservation. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, cosmetic outcomes, and ultrasonographic testicular-volume measurements were analyzed. Paired preoperative and 6-month postoperative testicular-volume measurements were compared.
RESULTS: All 42 procedures were completed laparoscopically without conversion or intraoperative complications. The median operative time was 26 min, median estimated blood loss was 2 mL, and postoperative hospital stay was 1 day. Lymphatic vessels were visualized and preserved in all patients. During a median follow-up of 11 months, no hydrocele, recurrent varicocele, testicular atrophy, or Doppler-detected venous reflux was observed. At 3 months, the median Vancouver Scar Scale score was 1; 31 patients (73.8%) were very satisfied and 11 (26.2%) were satisfied with the cosmetic outcome. At 6 months, mean ipsilateral testicular volume increased from 9.45 to 10.84 mL, while mean TVD decreased from 14.92% to 7.65%.
CONCLUSION: ICG fluorescence-guided transumbilical three-port laparoscopic suprainguinal varicocelectomy with testicular artery and lymphatic preservation was technically feasible in this retrospective cohort and was associated with favorable short-term perioperative and cosmetic outcomes.

Title: Phenotypic spectrum of 1q21.1 copy number variants in 42 children: genotype-phenotype correlations and clinical implications.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chromosome 1q21.1 copy number variants (CNVs) are associated with a broad and variable clinical spectrum encompassing neurodevelopmental, anthropometric, and systemic anomalies. The incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity of these rearrangements pose significant challenges for clinical interpretation and genotype-phenotype correlation. We retrospectively analyzed 42 pediatric patients with 1q21.1 CNVs, identified by chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), evaluated at a single tertiary center between 2019 and 2025. Patients were classified according to CNV type and localization: distal deletions (n = 30), distal duplications (n = 7), proximal deletions (n = 3), and proximal duplications (n = 2). Clinical findings were compared according to CNV type, sex, inheritance pattern, parental origin, and deletion size. The median age at presentation was 27 months. Among distal deletion carriers, microcephaly (60.0%), short stature (40.0%), and developmental delay (39.3%) were the most frequently observed findings. Cardiac anomalies were present in 34.5% of deletion patients, with two patients dying due to severe cardiac complications during follow-up. Macrocephaly was identified exclusively in duplication carriers (28.6%), corroborating the mirror phenotype of reciprocal 1q21.1 rearrangements. Developmental delay was significantly more frequent in duplication compared with deletion carriers (85.7% vs. 39.3%; p = 0.041). Cardiac anomalies were significantly more common in female patients (p < 0.05). No significant differences were identified according to inheritance status, parental origin, or deletion size, reflecting the variable expressivity of this locus. One proximal deletion patient was diagnosed with TAR syndrome through combined microarray and exome sequencing, confirming the two-hit molecular mechanism involving a 1q21.1 deletion and a pathogenic RBM8A variant.
CONCLUSION: This study delineates the broad phenotypic spectrum of 1q21.1 CNVs in a pediatric cohort, highlighting microcephaly and cardiac anomalies as clinically significant findings and reinforcing the mirror phenotype of reciprocal rearrangements. The absence of consistent genotype-phenotype correlations underscores the contribution of modifier factors beyond the CNV itself. Routine cardiac evaluation and multidisciplinary follow-up are recommended for all carriers.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Distal 1q21.1 CNVs cause microcephaly, developmental delay, and cardiac anomalies with incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. • Reciprocal rearrangements show a mirror phenotype: microcephaly in deletion and macrocephaly in duplication carriers.
WHAT IS NEW: • This is among the few single-center cohorts characterizing all four 1q21.1 CNV subtypes in a pediatric series. • Cardiac anomalies were more frequent in female carriers, a sex-specific observation warranting further investigation. • Inheritance status, parental origin, and deletion size did not appear to significantly influence clinical phenotype.

Title: Correction to: Sacubitril/valsartan compared to equivalent/sub-equivalent dose angiotensin receptor blocker or angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Risk factors for cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes in populations with overweight and obesity: an umbrella review and cohort analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Individuals with overweight and obesity are at high risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We aimed to identify the risk factors for CVD, CKD, and T2DM among individuals with overweight and obesity, and to validate the associations of these risk factors with the three outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review and a cohort analysis. Seven databases were searched from inception to December 31, 2025. Systematic reviews reporting the risk factors in populations with overweight and obesity, and CVD, CKD, or T2DM were included. The ROBIS and GRADE tools were used to assess the methodological quality and certainty of evidence. A cohort study dataset from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) was used for validation. Associations with the composite outcome and its individual components (CVD, CKD, and T2DM) were examined.
RESULTS: Nine systematic reviews were included in the umbrella review, and three key factors were identified. Anthropometric measures were associated with CVD (HRs 1.10-1.29) and T2DM (RRs 1.31-1.88). Compared with metabolically healthy individuals, those with metabolically unhealthy phenotypes had HRs ranging from 1.46 to 2.68. Metabolically unhealthy individuals had higher risks (RRs 2.42-5.90). Unhealthy dietary patterns increased CVD, CKD and T2DM risk (HRs 1.11-2.05), whereas healthy dietary patterns reduced risk. In this cohort study, 1,305 participants were included, and 538 developed CVD, CKD or T2DM. Transitioning from a metabolically healthy to a metabolically unhealthy phenotype (OR 1.66 [1.19, 2.30]), transitioning from a metabolically unhealthy to a metabolically healthy phenotype (OR 1.56 [1.08, 2.24]), and maintaining a stable metabolically unhealthy status (OR 1.88 [1.39, 2.54]) were significantly associated with an increased risk of incident CVD, CKD and T2DM composite; disease-specific analyses indicated that this association was driven primarily by T2DM.
CONCLUSIONS: Our analyses revealed that anthropometric measures, metabolic phenotypes, and dietary patterns are associated with CVD, CKD, and T2DM among individuals with overweight and obesity, especially T2DM. Integrated prevention strategies targeting these modifiable risk factors should be prioritized to optimize clinical management.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261350841.

Title: Diagnostic Testing Is Not Associated with Patient Experience in Common Pediatric Cardiology Referrals.
Abstract: To describe patient and family experience (PFE) scores for common new pediatric cardiology referrals and to evaluate whether the intensity of cardiac testing is associated with patient experience. We performed a retrospective study of PFE surveys completed following new outpatient pediatric cardiology visits at a single tertiary center from 2022 to 2023. Patients ≤ 18 years old referred for chest pain, palpitations, murmur, or dizziness/syncope were included. Survey domains included overall experience, provider respect, communication, and time spent with the provider. Responses were dichotomized, with top-box approach scores designated as 9-10 on a 0-10 Likert scale or a response of "yes, definitely." Additional variables included patient demographics, clinic location, referral-to-visit interval, cardiac testing performed and follow-up recommendations. Univariable and multivariable statistical analysis were used to identify factors associated with top-box scores. A total of 1293 surveys were analyzed. The performance of cardiac testing-including echocardiography, exercise stress testing, or ambulatory monitoring-was not associated with higher PFE scores. PFE scores also did not differ significantly by referral reason, clinic location, referral-to-visit interval, or follow-up recommendation. Overall PFE scores were high (91% in top-box category). Among common pediatric cardiology referrals, greater testing intensity was not associated with improved patient and family experience. These findings suggest that reducing non-essential testing may represent an opportunity to optimize resource utilization without negatively affecting perceived quality of care.

Title: Predictive value of left ventricular 18F-FDG PET/CT derived parameters and uptake patterns for chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in patients with lymphoma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity significantly impacts the survival and quality of life of lymphoma patients. Since traditional echocardiographic markers often detect injury only after irreversible damage, there is an urgent need for early biomarkers. We aimed to evaluate the predictive value of myocardial FDG uptake patterns and quantitative parameters from routine oncologic PET/CT for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included lymphoma patients treated with anthracycline-based regimens at a single hospital between 2015 and 2024. Patients underwent FDG PET/CT at baseline and after chemotherapy. CTRCD was operationally defined using the LVEF-based component of the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guidelines on follow-up echocardiography. Metabolic parameters including maximal standard uptake value (SUVmax), cardiac metabolic volume (CMV), cardiac metabolic activity (CMA), and visual uptake patterns were analyzed on pre and post-treatment PET scans.
RESULTS: Post-treatment SUVmax, CMV, and CMA were significantly higher in patients who developed cardiotoxicity (p = 0.04, 0.017, and 0.03, respectively). In univariable logistic regression, focal/diffuse myocardial uptake was significantly associated with CTRCD, whereas SUVmax ≥8.49 and CMV ≥66.9 showed borderline associations. In multivariable analysis including SUVmax, CMV, and focal/diffuse uptake pattern, only the focal/diffuse uptake pattern remained independently associated with CTRCD (OR = 10.71, 95% CI: 2.10-54.69, p = 0.004). Notably, absent myocardial FDG uptake after treatment was observed only in patients without CTRCD in this cohort. Baseline PET parameters showed no significant predictive value (p = n.s.).
CONCLUSION: Routine post-treatment oncologic FDG PET/CT may provide exploratory information on myocardial metabolic changes associated with CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Although quantitative PET parameters differed between patients with and without CTRCD, the focal/diffuse myocardial uptake pattern was the only imaging variable that remained independently associated with CTRCD after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation using standardized myocardial metabolic preparation and predefined imaging timepoints.

Title: Structural and Microvascular Alterations in Macular Telangiectasia Type 2: The Diagnostic Value of Vessel Tortuosity.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate structural and microvascular changes in macular telangiectasia (MacTel) type 2 using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT-angiography (OCTA) derived vascular parameters, and to examine their relationship in the macula.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study included 27 MacTel type 2 patients and 54 age-and-gender-matched healthy controls. Participants underwent OCT, and OCTA imaging. Images from the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP) analyzed with OCTA Vascular Analyzer (OCTAVA) software to obtain different vascular parameters. Statistical analysis involved Mann-Whitney U tests, Spearman's correlations, and multivariate logistic regression; p <0.05 was considered significant after adjusting using the false discovery rate.
RESULTS: MacTel type 2 patients exhibited significant reduction in macular thickness in all inner ETDRS subfields (p < 0.05). Mean vessel tortuosity (mTort) in the DCP was significantly decreased in MacTel type 2 (p = 0.025). Macular thickness showed significant negative correlations with SCP-VD in the inner nasal region (r = -0.426, p = 0.034), and DCP-VD in the inner temporal region (r = -0.572, p = 0.003). Logistic regression identified central, inner nasal, and outer superior macular thickness, along with reduced mTort, as independent predictors of MacTel type 2 (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study highlights significant structural and microvascular changes in MacTel type 2, including macular thinning and reduced mean tortuosity. Additionally, the normal structural-vascular correlations were disrupted in MacTel Type 2, and different microvascular correlation patterns were observed in these patients. The identification of new vascular parameters may contribute to a better understanding of MacTel type 2.

Title: Anterior Corneal Higher-Order Aberrations and Quantitative Macular OCT Angiography Metrics in Healthy Eyes: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether anterior corneal higher‑order aberrations (HOA) influence the measurement of macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) features, including foveal avascular zone (FAZ) parameters and macular vessel density (VD) across different retinal layers.
METHODS: We conducted a single‑center, retrospective, cross-sectional study of 110 healthy eyes of 110 patients. Anterior corneal HOA were measured over a fixed 6-mm zone by Scheimpflug-Placido corneal topography. Macular OCTA (6 × 6 mm) provided VD in the superficial (SCP) and deep (DCP) capillary plexuses, and FAZ area, perimeter, and circularity on the full inner retinal slab. Signal strength index (SSI), axial length, tear‑break‑up time, scotopic pupil diameter, age, and sex were also recorded. Each OCTA parameter was then regressed on total HOA by multivariable linear regression with adjustment for these covariates, and an exploratory mediation analysis partitioned the association into signal‑strength‑mediated and non‑mediated components.
RESULTS: Corneal total HOA was inversely associated with SCP whole‑image VD (standardized β = ‑0.41, partial r = ‑0.56) and, more strongly, with DCP whole‑image VD (β = ‑0.50, partial r = ‑0.62; both p < .001). Only 35% of the association was mediated by SSI. Absolute VD differences between the lowest and highest HOA tertiles were 3.60% for SCP and 3.94% for DCP. FAZ area, perimeter, and circularity showed no association with corneal HOA (all |β| <0.07; p > .50).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher anterior corneal HOA were associated with lower measured macular VD, and the device SSI explained only part of this. FAZ metrics were unaffected. No independent reference measurement of retinal perfusion was available, so whether this reflects a measurement effect or a true perfusion difference remains undetermined.

Title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
Abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Effect of Postoperative Arrhythmia in Children Less Than 18 Years of Age Following Congenital Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Study.
Journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
Abstract: BackgroundPostoperative arrhythmias are common among children after congenital cardiac surgery, potentially compromising hemodynamic stability and postoperative recovery. This study aimed to assess the impact of arrhythmias on hemodynamics and clinical outcomes.Material and MethodsThree hundred and twenty-nine children under 18 years of age undergoing congenital cardiac surgery were studied prospectively. In addition to standard postoperative hemodynamic monitoring, electrical cardiometry (ICON®) was used to assess hemodynamic parameters across time points (prearrhythmia, during arrhythmia, and postarrhythmia). Repeated measures were analyzed using Friedman test followed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons. Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify independent predictors and calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR).ResultsPostoperative arrhythmias occurred in 53/329 patients (16.1%). Junctional ectopic tachycardia (34%, [18/53]) and supraventricular tachycardia (30.2%, [16/53]) were the most common. Arrhythmias were associated with low cardiac output (IRR 3.43; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.27-5.17; P < .001), ventricular dysfunction (IRR 2.55; P < .001), acute kidney injury (IRR 2.01; P = .006), and liver dysfunction (IRR 4.56; P = .002) on unadjusted analysis. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables like central venous pressure (CVP) and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) on multivariable analysis. Elevated CVP, VIS, and hypokalemia were predictors of arrhythmia.ConclusionsArrhythmias occurred in approximately one-sixth of children following congenital cardiac surgery and were associated with adverse hemodynamic changes, organ function, and recovery. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables (CVP and VIS), suggesting that arrhythmia may reflect underlying instability rather than a primary causal factor.

Title: A retrospective review of health profiles and functional capacity of elderly crane operators in Singapore.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of crane operators aged 70 years and above is increasing in Singapore, requiring annual relicensing assessments to ensure medical and functional fitness for work.
AIMS: To examine the health status, functional capacity and employment outcomes of elderly crane operators and evaluate relicensing effectiveness.
METHODS: A serial cross-sectional study was conducted using relicensing assessment data from a tertiary healthcare institution in Singapore from 2016 to 2022. Medical history, laboratory test results, functional assessments and employment status were analysed. Chi-square and ANOVA tests were used to compare outcomes across years and between employed and retired operators. Logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with employment status in 2022.
RESULTS: A total of 456 relicensing assessments were conducted for 195 unique crane operators. Hypertension (61%), diabetes mellitus (29%) and cataracts (25%) were the most common medical conditions. Annual blood tests showed increasing trends in the proportion of operators with abnormal fasting plasma glucose over time (p-trend < 0.05). A longer completion time for the 3D construction test (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02, P < 0.05) was positively associated with retirement but presence of any cardiovascular diseases (aOR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.99, P < 0.05) showed an inverse association. Two operators failed the Colour Trails Test-2 and were deemed unfit for relicensing.
CONCLUSIONS: The relicensing assessment process identifies crane operators unfit to work due to functional or medical impairments. Cognitive and visuospatial assessments play a key role in determining workability. Findings highlight the need for workplace health programs targeting chronic disease management and cognitive health.

Title: The Impact of Statin Therapy on Postoperative Short- and Long-term Mortality and Morbidity After Non-Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract:
AIMS: Statins' anti-inflammatory and endothelial-stabilising effects suggest perioperative value, but trials of de novo initiation were discredited following research misconduct. Whether established preoperative statin therapy lowers postoperative mortality dose-dependently remains unclear.
METHODS: We studied 56,362 patients aged ≥45 years undergoing non-cardiac surgery at two university hospitals (2016-2023). Preoperative statin exposure was assessed as status (any vs none), intensity (high vs low/intermediate), and regimen (high vs low/intermediate vs none). Primary outcomes were 30- and 365-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, using random forest-estimated propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect in the treated, was applied to balance measured confounders. Associations were estimated with weighted Cox regression.
RESULTS: Overall, 372 patients (0.6%) died within 30 days and 3,735 (6.6%) within 365 days. After weighting, all covariates were balanced. Statin therapy showed a directionally consistent but non-significant association with lower 30-day mortality (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57-1.07), and was associated with lower 365-day mortality (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.73-0.90; ARD -1.2 percentage points; number needed to treat 83). A dose-response relationship was evident: versus no statin, high-intensity therapy showed a 29% lower hazard (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.60-0.83; ARD -2.3 points) and low/intermediate-intensity a 16% lower hazard (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.74-0.96). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults undergoing non-cardiac surgery, established preoperative statin therapy was associated with dose-dependent lower 365-day mortality. These findings suggest perioperative statin continuation as a preventive strategy and warrant confirmation in a randomised trial.

Title: Imaging Pars Plana in Acute Anterior Uveitis: Association with Inflammatory Activity.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the association between pars plana thickness and disease activity in acute anterior uveitis.
METHODS: Participants underwent anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) of the ciliary body using Topcon DRI-OCT Triton plus with an anterior segment adapter. Pars plana thickness was measured 3 mm posterior to the scleral spur in the nasal and temporal side. Patients received standard topical therapy and were followed longitudinally with repeat examination and AS-OCT imaging.
RESULTS: Forty nine eyes of 49 patients with anterior uveitis and 49 eyes of 49 healthy control were included in the analysis. The mean pars plana thickness was significantly greater in eyes with anterior uveitis compared to controls in both nasal (323.16 ± 81.14 µm vs 227.43 ± 56.68 µm; p < 0.001) and temporal side (354.48 ± 75.56 µm vs 235.31 ± 48.99 µm; p < 0.001). Supraciliary fluid (SCF) was detected in 59.2% of cases at baseline. Two or more than two step reduction in anterior chamber cell grade was documented in 24 eyes. It was associated with a significant decrease in nasal (313.18 ± 61.92 µm to 266.09 ± 64.95 µm; p < 0.001) and temporal pars plana thickness (362.39 ± 80.05 µm to 288.52 ± 74.03 µm; p < 0.001). Resolution of clinical activity was documented in 19 eyes. In this cohort, SCF was detected in 47.4% of eyes at baseline, declining to 10.50% at resolution.
CONCLUSIONS: Pars plana thickness may serve as a novel, non-invasive imaging marker that parallels longitudinal resolution in anterior uveitis.

Title: Anticoagulation after transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement: A narrative review.
Abstract: BackgroundBioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, specifically surgical (SAVR) and transcatheter (TAVR), is among the most frequently performed cardiac interventions globally, yet anticoagulation strategies after implantation remain incompletely defined. Atrial fibrillation, notably prevalent pre- and post-operatively in these patients, substantially amplifies thromboembolic risk and complicates decision-making in an already elderly, frail, and comorbid population.ObjectivesTo critically evaluate current anticoagulation strategies after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement across sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation in both SAVR and TAVR, and to identify evidence gaps and guideline inconsistencies.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review of major international guidelines (ESC/EACTS 2025, ACC/AHA 2020, and NICE 2021) and key clinical trials on antithrombotic therapy in valve replacement populations. Focus was placed on bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, with mechanical and non-aortic valves excluded.ResultsAspirin monotherapy is the most consistently supported strategy after bioprosthetic TAVR in sinus rhythm, though guidelines diverge on duration and recommendation strength. In atrial fibrillation, all three guidelines apply uniform CHA2DS2-VASc-based frameworks irrespective of AF phenotype, procedural context, or detection modality, reflecting lacking evidence rather than deliberate clinical judgement. No trial has enrolled patients specifically with new-onset post-procedural AF or stratified by AF subtype, and subclinical AF after bioprosthetic AVR remains entirely uncharacterised.ConclusionsGuideline divergence reflects a structurally inadequate evidence base rather than genuine clinical equipoise. Individualised decisions informed by procedure type, AF phenotype, frailty, and bleeding risk are required to guide clinical practice, alongside an adequately powered stratified randomised trial incorporating mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring.

Title: [Autumn vaccinations for older adults: Influenza, Covid-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)].
Abstract: Today, the Federal Commission on Vaccination (EKIF) recommends two vaccinations for people aged 65 and over in the autumn: one against flu and one against Covid-19. The new RSV vaccines are recommended for people aged 75 and over and for people aged 60-74 with relevant underlying conditions, but basic health insurance does not yet cover the costs. These vaccines each reduce the risk of illness and hospitalisation to varying degrees, and the risk of serious side effects is very low. The flu vaccine reduces the risk of heart attack, at least in terms of secondary prevention. However, the high Number Needed to Vaccinate (NNV) to prevent respiratory infection- or pneumonia-related hospitalisation (over 1000 for covid vaccines and well over 3000 for flu vaccines) may lead doctors to question the effectiveness of vaccination. For the new RSV vaccines, the NNV is lower at approximately 250 for individuals aged over 75. Additionally, the protective effect lasts for at least two seasons. Although the EKIF strongly recommends the high-dose flu vaccine, it is 50 % more expensive and, in a randomised head-to-head comparison involving 466 000 participants, only slightly more effective than standard-dose vaccines (NNV = approx. 1832).

Title: Peptides in urology and sexual medicine: clinical effectiveness, dosing, indications, and safety: a narrative review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peptide-based therapies are increasingly used in urology and sexual medicine, although adoption is often influenced by off-label prescribing, direct-to-consumer promotion, and limited long-term safety data. We review mechanisms, clinical evidence, dosing, safety, and regulatory status of these agents.
METHODS: A structured search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar identified studies of peptide-based therapies in sexual medicine. Search terms included Bremelanotide, Melanotan II, Kisspeptin, Oxytocin, PnPP-19, Gonadorelin and growth hormone secretagogues, including GHRP-2, GHRP-6, Ibutamoren, Ipamorelin, Tesamorelin, Sermorelin, and CJC-1295. Of 725 records, 76 studies met inclusion criteria. Findings were synthesized narratively given heterogeneity across studies.
RESULTS: Peptides reviewed act through diverse mechanisms, including central modulation of desire and arousal, stimulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal and growth hormone axes, and nitric oxide-mediated effects on erectile physiology. Bremelanotide and Tesamorelin are the most clinically established agents, with defined dosing and regulatory approval for selected indications. Kisspeptin shows early promise but remains investigational. Growth hormone secretagogues reliably increase growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1 concentrations; however, evidence for improved sexual function, physical performance, or quality of life remains limited. Melanotan II, Ibutamoren, CJC-1295, and related agents remain accessible through unregulated markets, raising concerns about product quality, dosing variability, and incompletely characterized adverse effects. Oxytocin has biologic plausibility but limited efficacy data, whereas PnPP-19 remains preclinical. Gonadorelin was Food and Drug Administration approved but is no longer manufactured. Across peptide classes, safety data are limited by short follow-up, small samples, and incomplete assessment of cardiovascular, metabolic, and oncologic outcomes.
DISCUSSION: Peptide-based therapies in urology and sexual medicine show selective therapeutic potential, but most remain insufficiently validated for clinical use. Clinicians should distinguish approved therapies from investigational and nonregulated compounds and counsel patients regarding uncertain benefit, potential harm, and risks of unsupervised use. Randomized trials with standardized dosing and long-term safety assessment are needed before broader adoption.

Title: Rethinking Obstructive Sleep Apnea Care in Obesity: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure, Incretin-Based Therapy, or Both?
Journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
Abstract: Obesity is a primary driver of obstructive sleep apnea and contributes substantially to its associated cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Although continuous positive airway pressure remains the standard treatment, its efficacy is often limited by suboptimal patient adherence and its impact on cardiovascular outcomes has yet to be consistently established in major clinical trials. Treatments aimed at the underlying problem, excess adiposity, are therefore needed. Weight loss, whether achieved through lifestyle interventions or bariatric surgery is well-known to improve obstructive sleep apnea. The recent introduction of highly effective weight loss medications, most notably incretin-based agents, now offers a pharmacological approach to accomplish the same result. Recent randomized controlled trials in patients with obesity demonstrated that these medications significantly decrease the apnea-hypopnea index and enhance oxygen saturation, with a significant proportion of disease remission. In light of these findings, we propose a therapeutic algorithm stratifying treatment according to symptoms and body mass index. For asymptomatic patients with obesity and obstructive sleep apnea, we suggest incretin-based therapy as a first-line option to concurrently address excessive weight and obstructive sleep apnea. Conversely, in individuals with impaired sleep-related quality of life combining continuous positive airway pressure and incretin therapy may be more appropriate, pairing immediate symptom control with longer-term weight loss. This integrated strategy, prioritizing weight management alongside symptom relief, may offer a comprehensive approach to treat obesity-related obstructive sleep apnea and decrease its associated cardiovascular risks.

Title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1.
CONCLUSION: CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

Title: Sex- and Time-Resolved Physiological and Gut Ecosystem Responses to a Food-Grade Microbiome-Targeted Intervention in Collegiate Endurance Athletes.
Abstract: Endurance athletes experience sustained physiological demands during high-volume training, yet evidence for microbiome-targeted interventions in real-world settings remains limited. We conducted a two-stage, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 150 athletes allocated 2:1 to combined probiotics-yeast extract (CPYE) or placebo for 6 weeks; 44 completers confirmed for the 12th Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region University Games entered an exploratory 6-week extension with intensified training. Integrating wearable-derived phenotyping, field-based cardiorespiratory indices, clinical assessments, fecal metagenomics, and metabolomics, we found that during the randomized short-term phase, CPYE was associated with changes in device-estimated maximal oxygen uptake, exercise heart-rate indices, lactate, and redox biomarkers versus placebo. Exploratory sex-stratified analyses suggested heterogeneous response patterns, while the selected long-term extension indicated time-dependent changes requiring confirmation. Multi-omics identified sex- and phase-associated differences in microbial taxa, functions, metabolites, and network topology. Indirect-effect models nominated candidate features (rmlD, PISD-linked phosphatidylethanolamine pathways, Bacteroides ovatus, and folate-related functions) as potential indirect correlates of host outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of CPYE-associated responses in collegiate endurance athletes; subgroup, long-term, network, and indirect-effect results are hypothesis-generating.

Title: Childhood onset, indolent progression, and risk of hepatic rupture: the natural history of hereditary lysozyme amyloidosis.
Journal: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lysozyme amyloidosis (ALys) is a rare systemic amyloidosis caused by pathogenic variants in LYZ. We describe the natural history and outcomes for this disease in the largest cohort yet published.
METHODS: All patients diagnosed with ALys at the National Amyloidosis Centre between 1988 and 2025 were included. Diagnosis was established by immunohistochemistry or proteomics with the identification of a variant in LYZ. Trends in data were analysed longitudinally.
RESULTS: Thirty-five patients were included (median age: 45 years). Twenty-five (71%) carried the Asp67His (p.Asp85His) variant. Median age at symptom onset was 23.7 years, and 43% reported childhood symptoms. Sicca syndrome was the commonest presenting manifestation (46%), followed by gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms (23%). Renal involvement occurred in 57%. Eight developed kidney failure requiring renal replacement therapy. Six kidney transplants were performed with no amyloid recurrence. Liver involvement was present in 80%. Spontaneous hepatic rupture or haemorrhage occurred in five patients, necessitating emergency liver transplantation in four. GI bleeding occurred in 31%. Reproductive outcomes were successful in many patients.
CONCLUSIONS: ALys is characterised by early symptom onset, indolent systemic progression, and risk of catastrophic hepatic or splenic rupture. These findings provide a framework for surveillance, transplantation planning, and future therapeutic studies.

Title: Ventriculolumbar Irrigation Effects on Delayed Cerebral Infarction and Outcome After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Prospective Registry Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) remains associated with high morbidity and mortality, largely determined by delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI). Active blood clearance and vasodilation (ABCD) therapy targets key pathophysiological mechanisms of DCI by enhancing the clearance of blood from cerebrospinal fluid and counteracts vasospasm through continuous intrathecal fibrinolytic and spasmolytic irrigation. Although ABCD therapy has previously been implemented using technically demanding treatment approaches, this study introduces ventriculolumbar irrigation (VLI) as a simplified, bedside-applicable method. This study evaluates whether VLI-based ABCD therapy is associated with an improvement in DCI and morbidity.
METHODS: In this prospective registry study, consecutive aSAH patients treated with the novel VLI-based ABCD therapy (pressure-controlled VLI with urokinase and on-demand nimodipine) between 2019 and 2025 were compared with matched controls receiving standard care. The primary outcome was the incidence of DCI and the secondary outcome was modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 180 days.
RESULTS: Seventy-two patients treated with VLI-based ABCD therapy were compared with 144 matched controls. VLI treatment was associated with significantly lower rates of DCI (9.7% vs 29.9%, P < .001), morbidity (mean mRS 2.33 vs 3.37, P < .001), and shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (9.7% vs 31.9%, P < .001). Compared with isolated, passive cerebrospinal fluid drainage, VLI was associated with lower DCI rates (9.7% vs 30.7%, P < .001) and reduced morbidity (mean mRS 2.33 vs 3.39, P < .001).
CONCLUSION: The novel and simplified VLI therapy was associated with considerably improved outcomes: lower DCI rates and shunt-dependent hydrocephalus. VLI offers a bedside technique to actively remove intrathecal blood and deliver intrathecal spasmolysis for the prevention of DCI. Randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Establishing reference values for aortic pulse wave velocity in healthy Chinese adults: a national multicenter prospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The use of carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV), a reliable indicator of aortic stiffness and a powerful predictor of cardiovascular disease, has remained limited in routine clinical practice in China, due to the lack of standardized reference values. This national multicenter study aimed to establish the reference values for cfPWV in healthy Chinese adult population.
METHODS: Participants were prospectively recruited across 29 participating centers in China and were categorized by age decade and blood pressure (BP) categories. A consistent ultrasound semi-automatic technique along with standardized measuring protocols was applied across all centers and participants to measure cfPWV. The carotid-femoral transit distance was determined using 0.8× direct carotid-femoral tape measure distance, and the cfPWV was calculated as transit distance/transit time.
RESULTS: The study included 3328 adult participants (1431 men, 43%), age 45.7 ± 14.4 years. The distribution of cfPWV values with age and BP categories were described, and reference values were established. The 5th and 95th percentile values for cfPWV were: 18-29 years: 4.27, 7.57 m/s; 30-39 years: 4.65, 8.45 m/s; 40-49 years: 5.14, 9.49 m/s; 50-59 years: 5.34, 10.82 m/s; 60-69 years: 5.52, 12.04 m/s; and at least 70 years: 6.05, 14.69 m/s, respectively. Age, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, sex, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level and family history of cardiovascular disease were independently correlated with cfPWV (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Based on a large cohort of Chinese population, this study has established the reference values for cfPWV. Given the profound cardiovascular implications and powerful predictive value of cfPWV, the findings of this study represent a critical step forward in facilitating the wider integration of aortic stiffness assessment into routine clinical practice in China.

Title: Survival and mortality in adults with cancer and pre-existing mental illness across multimorbidity types: a decade of population-based data from Alberta, Canada.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults living with cancer and pre-existing mental illness (PMI) represent a particularly vulnerable population. This study examined whether multimorbidity protects against or increases mortality among adults with cancer and PMI.
METHODS: We used Alberta Health Services administrative data (n = 15,144), to identify adults with both PMI and cancer diagnosed between 2013-2022, including demographic, comorbidity, and cancer information. The analysis used Cox proportional hazard models (HR) to evaluate the impact among different multimorbidity categories on all-cause mortality. The multimorbidity categories were classified as cardiometabolic (e.g. cardiovascular disease), musculoskeletal (e.g. rheumatic disease), chronic airway (e.g. chronic pulmonary disease), and general multimorbidity (e.g. including liver and renal disease). Multimorbidity combinations were defined as the presence of conditions across two or more categories.
RESULTS: In a cohort of 15,144 adults with cancer, 39.1% died during follow-up. In the overall cohort, compared with those without multimorbidity, adjusted models showed that multimorbidity increased mortality for cardiometabolic conditions (HR = 1.25, 95%CI 1.13-1.37), chronic airway disease (HR = 1.88, 95%CI 1.69-2.08), general multimorbidity (HR = 1.90, 95%CI 1.59-2.27), and multimorbidity combinations (HR = 2.29, 95%CI 2.08-2.51). Musculoskeletal conditions were not significant. By PMI subtype, multimorbidity combinations were consistently associated with increased mortality across mood, anxiety, substance use, and multiple psychiatric disorders (HRs = 1.67-1.91). General multimorbidity was associated with increased mortality in anxiety, substance use, and multiple psychiatric disorders (HRs = 1.72-2.74), whereas chronic airway disease was significant only in mood disorders. Cardiometabolic and musculoskeletal conditions were not associated with mortality after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Different multimorbidity categories are associated with increased mortality among adults with cancer and PMI. These findings underscore the importance of jointly considering psychiatric and physical health comorbidities in cancer care.

Title: Air Pollution and Neurovascular Health in Pakistan: An Emerging Public Health Crisis in South Asia - A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Air pollution is an increasingly important public health concern in Pakistan, especially in rapidly urbanizing cities where concentrations of PM2.5, PM10, and other airborne toxicants frequently exceed recommended safety limits. Although the respiratory and cardiovascular consequences of air pollution are widely recognized, its contribution to neurovascular injury remains comparatively underrepresented in public health planning. This review synthesizes national and international evidence on the relationship between air pollution exposure and neurovascular outcomes, with particular emphasis on stroke-related mechanisms, cerebrovascular injury, and evidence gaps relevant to Pakistan and South Asia. Current evidence suggests that fine and ultrafine particulate matter may contribute to neurovascular damage through systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier disruption, microglial activation, vascular inflammation, atherosclerosis, and pro-thrombotic changes. These pathways provide biologically plausible links between chronic pollutant exposure and increased susceptibility to ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, cerebral small vessel disease, and impaired neurological recovery. However, Pakistan-specific longitudinal studies, biomarker-based investigations, and exposure-linked stroke surveillance data remain limited, restricting the integration of environmental exposure into neurovascular risk assessment and policy development. Given Pakistan's high pollution burden, dense urban populations, and increasing stroke-related morbidity, air pollution should be considered a potentially modifiable neurovascular risk factor. Strengthening air-quality monitoring, developing local epidemiological cohorts, integrating pollution exposure with hospital and stroke-registry data, and implementing targeted prevention strategies for high-risk populations may help reduce the future burden of pollution-associated neurovascular disease in Pakistan.

Title: C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index and all-cause mortality in postmenopausal women: A dual-cohort study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation each predict cardiovascular mortality, but they are usually studied separately. The C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI) combines both, yet its prognostic value in postmenopausal women, who experience concurrent rises in insulin resistance and inflammation, remains unknown.
METHODS: We identified postmenopausal women from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) (1999-2018; n = 7007) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) (2011; n = 4235). CTI = 0.412 × ln [hs-CRP (mg/L)] + ln[(fasting triglycerides × fasting glucose)/2]. The endpoint was all-cause mortality. We fitted Cox models, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and piecewise regression with likelihood ratio tests for threshold detection.
RESULTS: Over a median 9.0 years (CHARLS) and 11.9 years (NHANES), 2940 deaths occurred (26.2%). Each 1-unit CTI increase carried a 28% higher mortality hazard after full adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.20-1.35; P < 0.001). The dose-response was nonlinear in NHANES (P < 0.001) but linear in CHARLS (P = 0.14). In NHANES, a threshold emerged at CTI = 5.43: above it, per-unit HR = 1.85 (95% CI 1.62-2.11); below, HR = 0.99 (95% CI 0.89-1.10; P = 0.87). The highest versus lowest tertile HRs were 1.51 (1.16-1.97) in CHARLS and 1.35 (1.22-1.49) in NHANES. Excluding baseline cancer cases did not change the results.
CONCLUSION: Higher CTI predicts greater all-cause mortality in postmenopausal women. In the US cohort, risk rose sharply, above CTI = 5.43. The same trend in the Chinese cohort, although linear, suggests that CTI might be a useful risk marker across populations.
