Title: Blood pressure and homocysteine-lowering effects of the amlodipine/folic acid combination in patients with hypertension and serum homocysteine concentration ≥10 μmol/l (H-type hypertension): a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled clinical trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated plasma homocysteine (Hcy ≥10 μmol/l) and hypertension, defined as H-type hypertension, can synergistically increase the risk of cardiovascular diseases, especially for stroke. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of amlodipine-folic acid in lowering both blood pressure (BP) and plasma Hcy, compared with amlodipine alone.
METHODS: Eligible participants (299 males and 241 females) were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to 5 mg amlodipine (control, group A), 5 mg amlodipine plus 0.4 mg folic acid (group B), or 5 mg amlodipine plus 0.8 mg folic acid (group C). All participants were followed at 2, 4, 6, and 8 weeks. The primary outcome was the efficacy of lowering both BP and Hcy.
RESULTS: Among the 540 participants who were randomized, the efficacy of lowering both BP and Hcy was significantly better in groups B and C compared with group A at the end of 4 weeks, and sustained at the end of 8 weeks (group B vs. group A: 31.7% vs. 6.1%, P < 0.001; group C vs. group A: 32.8% vs. 6.1%, P < 0.001). Both groups B and C were more efficacious in lowering Hcy and raising folate levels than amlodipine alone at 8 weeks. There was no significant difference in BP lowering and adverse events among the three treatment groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In H-type hypertension patients, amlodipine-folic acid (5 mg/0.4 mg or 5 mg/0.8 mg) had a significantly higher efficacy of lowering both BP and plasma Hcy compared with amlodipine alone. The efficacy of BP lowering and safety profile were comparable among the three treatment groups. This trial was registered in clinicaltrials.gov, identifier: NCT01848873.

Title: Cardiovascular risk stratification using chest CT in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of incidentally detected coronary artery calcification (CAC) on routine chest computed tomography (CT) for cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM).
METHODS: In this single-centre cross-sectional study, adult patients with IIM who underwent non-cardiac, non-gated high-resolution chest CT (HRCT) were included. CAC was visually categorized as absent, mild, moderate or severe. Diagnostic performance for established coronary artery disease (CAD) and established cardiovascular (CV) events was assessed. Kaplan-Meier analyses evaluated CV death-free survival, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with CAC. A matched systemic sclerosis (SSc) cohort served as validation cohort.
RESULTS: Among 234 patients with IIM (mean age 57.1 [15.9] years; 70.1% female), CAC was present in 43.2%. Higher CAC thresholds showed greater specificity for established CAD and prior CV events, whereas lower thresholds were more sensitive. CAC was associated with reduced CV death-free survival (log-rank P = 0.0095), with a stepwise decline across CAC severity categories. Findings were similar in the matched SSc cohort. Increasing CAC burden was associated with older age, smoking, higher CV risk burden, interstitial lung disease and higher disease activity. In adjusted analyses, high disease activity was independently associated with moderate CAC (odds ratio [OR] 4.01; 95% CI: 1.29, 12.50), while a higher number of concomitant DMARDs was associated with severe CAC (OR 2.55; 95% CI: 1.27, 5.11).
CONCLUSION: Incidentally detected CAC on routine chest CT provides diagnostic and prognostic information in IIM and may represent a pragmatic approach to improve cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

Title: Cardiopulmonary Fitness and Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation in Patients With Myocarditis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is a powerful predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. The cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) is considered a gold standard in assessing CRF. Patients with myocarditis are recommended to abstain from exercise because of the risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Therefore, the clinical benefit of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has not been previously established in this population.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to assess the CRF of myocarditis and the safety and effectiveness of an exercise-based CR program in these populations.
METHOD: A total of 70 consecutive patients with a diagnosis of myocarditis admitted to Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology between October 2021 and December 2024 were enrolled in the current study. CPET was performed within 3-6 months of hospital discharge. The exercise-based CR program was performed for 3 months. The protocol included biomarker analysis, CPET, and standard-of-care echocardiography (including resting left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain [GLS]). Data were collected at admission and 3 months after discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 70 patients with myocarditis were enrolled. Among them, 47 patients completed the rehabilitation program and had complete follow-up assessments, including cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and were included in the final analysis. In comparison with NFM, patients with FM were more often female, and had higher levels of creatine kinase (CK), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), urea nitrogen (UN), N-terminus probrain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), fasting blood glucose (FBG), and white blood cell (WBC). For FM, echocardiography revealed more frequently signs of left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in the form of a reduced ejection fraction (p < 0.01), and lower GLS (p < 0.01) in contrast to NFM. CPET results showed that FM patients had markedly lower exercise capacity, impaired ventilatory efficiency, and pulmonary function (p < 0.05). After the 3-month exercise-based CR program, both groups demonstrated significant improvements in peak VO2, peak workload, and MVV. However, no significant between-group differences were observed in the magnitude of improvement in CRF.
CONCLUSION: CRF was substantially impaired in patients recovering from myocarditis, particularly among those with fulminant presentations. Participation in a structured 3-month exercise-based CR program was feasible and was associated with favorable changes in exercise capacity and cardiopulmonary performance.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400088436.

Title: Oral Anticoagulant Monotherapy vs. Combination Therapy in Chronic Coronary Syndrome Requiring Long-Term Anticoagulation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: IntroductionEvidence surrounding the optimal antithrombotic regimen for patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) requiring oral anticoagulation remains scarce. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of oral anticoagulant (OAC) monotherapy compared to OAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) in this population.MethodsWe systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) till February 2026 comparing OAC monotherapy versus OAC plus SAPT in patients with CCS. Primary outcomes included major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, net adverse clinical events (NACE), all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular (CV) deaths. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated.ResultsOAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.38-0.65; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%). Similarly, OAC monotherapy significantly reduced the incidence of NACE (RR: 0.64; 95% CI: 0.50-0.81; p < 0.001; I2 = 64%). There was no significant difference between the two strategies in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.79; 95% CI: 0.55-1.13; p = 0.20; I2 = 52%). However, OAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of CV mortality (RR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97; p = 0.03; I2 = 3%).ConclusionIn patients with CCS requiring long-term oral anticoagulation, OAC monotherapy significantly reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, CV mortality, and NACE compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT). Rates of major ischemic events, Myocardial Infarction, stroke, and all-cause mortality were comparable between the two strategies.

Title: Effects of adenosine on oxidative stress and inflammation in patients with coronary heart disease underlying percutaneous coronary intervention.
Journal: The Journal of international medical research
Abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether rapid intracoronary adenosine administration attenuates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-induced systemic inflammation and oxidative stress in patients with coronary artery disease.MethodsThis prospective, randomized controlled trial enrolled patients undergoing coronary angiography (coronary angiography group) or PCI. Patients undergoing PCI were assigned to receive intracoronary adenosine (PCI + adenosine group) or placebo (PCI group). Blood levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. cytokines), anti-inflammatory mediators, and oxidative stress indicators (superoxide dismutase and malondialdehyde) were measured before and 24 h after the procedure.ResultsCompared to the coronary angiography group, patients undergoing PCI who received placebo exhibited concurrent elevations in inflammatory and anti-inflammatory markers at 24 h. Intracoronary adenosine significantly suppressed the rise in the levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. interleukin-6 reduced by 35% vs. placebo) and enhanced anti-inflammatory responses (e.g. interleukin-10 increased by 40% vs. placebo). Following PCI, oxidative stress was evident in placebo-treated patients, as reflected by decreased superoxide dismutase activity (15% reduction) and increased malondialdehyde levels (30% elevation). Adenosine restored superoxide dismutase activity to near-baseline levels and reduced malondialdehyde elevation by 85% compared to placebo.ConclusionsIntracoronary adenosine mitigates PCI-associated systemic inflammation and oxidative stress by rebalancing inflammatory pathways and preserving redox homeostasis. These findings highlight its potential as a therapeutic adjunct for improving clinical outcomes following PCI and warrant further validation in large-scale trials.Clinical Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR); identifier: ChiCTR1800019349.

Title: Transforming value-based deep vein thrombosis care through a pharmacist-led clinic.
Journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To address gaps in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) care, our health system implemented a pharmacist-led DVT clinic to standardize treatment, provide immediate access to pharmacy and vascular surgery services, and reduce emergency department (ED) and inpatient utilization for DVT management.
METHODS: This was a retrospective, pre-post cohort study of a DVT clinic that centralized imaging, diagnosis, anticoagulant initiation, and pharmacy services into a single outpatient location. Patients diagnosed with a DVT between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, were included. The co-primary outcomes were the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the acute care setting compared before and after the DVT clinic opened (2023 vs 2024) and compared between patients seen in the clinic or not (2024 only). A χ2 test was used to analyze the co-primary outcomes, with significance defined as a P value of less than 0.05.
RESULTS: The pharmacist saw 205 patients across 363 visits in 2024. Compared to 2023 baseline data, the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the ED in 2024 decreased from 88.6% to 53.3% (P < 0.001), while the rate of inpatient admission for DVT decreased from 25.5% to 13.9% (P < 0.001). Stratified analysis of the 2024 data demonstrated significantly lower acute care utilization for DVT among patients managed in the DVT clinic compared to those not seen, including for ED encounters (15.2% vs 91.5%; P < 0.001) and inpatient admissions (1.8% vs 26%; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The pharmacist-led DVT clinic represents a transformative advancement in pharmacy practice, redefining the role of pharmacists in ambulatory care and establishing a replicable model to optimize value-based care that shifts treatment for appropriate populations from acute to outpatient management.

Title: [Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung diseases: current state of the art].
Abstract: Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung diseases (PH-ILD) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung diseases. Diagnosis is challenging and relies on a combination of clinical, functional, biological, radiological and echocardiographic findings. Definitive diagnosis is established by right heart catheterisation, which confirms the presence of pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Until 2021, and the INCREASE study, all randomised controlled trials evaluating therapies approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension in patients with PH-ILD yielded disappointing results. However, recent advances exploring the potential of novel therapeutic strategies have renewed interest in PH-ILD, with a progressive paradigm shift opening new perspectives for a condition that was until recently associated with a poor prognosis.

Title: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Effects on Pulmonary Hemodynamics and Left Ventricular Function in Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) are strongly linked to pulmonary hypertension and left ventricular abnormalities, driving cardiovascular issues. OHS, with daytime hypercapnia, affects 10%-20% of OSA patients. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the first-line therapy, but its cardiac effects are inconsistent.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis adhering to the PRISMA 2020 statement. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 (RCTs) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS; cohort studies). Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs using random-effects models (restricted maximum likelihood) with Hartung-Knapp adjustment.
RESULTS: Eight studies (574 participants; 2 RCTs, 6 cohorts) were included, showing that CPAP significantly reduced pulmonary arterial pressure (MD = -2.32 mmHg, 95% CI: -3.88 to -0.76, p = 0.004) versus controls. Secondary analyses indicated improved left ventricular diastolic function (early-to-late diastolic mitral inflow velocity [E/A] ratio: MD = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.09 to 0.48, p = 0.004). No significant effects on left ventricular mass index (LVMi) (MD = -2.31 percentage points, 95% CI: -6.38 to 1.77, p = 0.27) or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (MD = 0.53 percentage points, 95% CI: -1.49 to 2.55, p = 0.61) were found. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness. Funnel plot analysis suggested potential publication bias for pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP)/mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), E/A ratio, and LVEF, while LVMi showed low bias.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with OSA or OHS, CPAP reduces pulmonary arterial pressure and improves LV diastolic function, but it does not significantly alter LVMi or ejection fraction. These findings support CPAP as a key intervention to mitigate pulmonary hemodynamic burden and diastolic dysfunction in this high-risk population, while its potential to reverse structural cardiac remodeling requires further study.

Title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known.
METHODS: Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio.
RESULTS: Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59).
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.

Title: Development and Validation of a Coronary Artery Calcium Volume and Density Score.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a useful tool for coronary heart disease (CHD) risk prediction. The current standard method, the Agatston score, weights plaque area upward by density. However, higher density is inversely associated with CHD. We aimed to develop and validate a CAC score accounting for the inverse association of density with CHD, and the nonlinear association between CAC volume and density in a prospective cohort study.
METHODS: A CAC volume and density score was developed, which adjusts CAC volume for density based on whether the volume level was <130 mm3. We used data from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) to develop and assess the score, including all participants with CAC>0 and follow-up for CHD events. Score performance for CHD risk prediction was compared with the pooled cohort equations and the Agatston score using Cox proportional hazards models and Harrell C-index and continuous and categorical net reclassification improvement. Analyses were also stratified by Agatston score, age, sex, race/ethnicity, and statin use. Finally, performance was evaluated in 4 longitudinal cohorts for external validation.
RESULTS: The MESA cohort included 3360 individuals. CAC volume and density score improved the C-index for CHD to a greater degree over the pooled cohort equation (0.699 [95% CI, 0.675-0.723]) compared with the Agatston score (0.687 [95% CI, 0.663-0.711]) and resulted in greater continuous net reclassification improvement (0.54 [95% CI, 0.43-0.64]) compared with the Agatston score (0.45 [95% CI, 0.34-0.56]) when added to the pooled cohort equation. The greatest improvement in risk prediction was in those with lower burden of CAC (Agatston <300). Consistent results were seen in stratified analyses and external validation cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: The CAC volume and density score, which adjusts CAC volume downward for higher density, and can be calculated from existing CAC reports, significantly improves risk discrimination and reclassification compared with the Agatston score.

Title: Executive Summary of the Clinical Practice Guideline on Tinnitus Update.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tinnitus is the perception of sound without an external source. More than 50 million people in the United States have reported experiencing tinnitus, resulting in an estimated prevalence of 10% to 15% in adults. The focus of this guideline is on tinnitus that is both bothersome and persistent (lasting 6 months or longer), which often negatively affects the patient's quality of life. The target audience for the guideline is any clinician, including allied health professionals, involved in managing patients with tinnitus. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome.
PURPOSE: The purpose of this guideline is to provide and update evidence-based recommendations for clinicians managing patients with tinnitus. The target audience for this guideline is any clinician involved in managing patients with tinnitus. People with tinnitus may be evaluated by a variety of health care providers, including primary care clinicians, specialty clinicians, and allied health professionals including audiologists and clinical psychologists. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome. Most people with tinnitus have associated hearing loss, such as sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) secondary to aging (presbycusis), noise exposure (noise-induced hearing loss), or acoustic trauma. Tinnitus can also be a symptom of numerous auditory and non-auditory system disorders, ranging from middle ear diseases, such as otosclerosis and eustachian tube dysfunction, to inner ear and auditory nerve pathologies such as Ménière's disease and vestibular schwannoma. Nonauditory system disorders that can cause tinnitus include vascular anomalies, myoclonus, and intracranial hypertension. The Guideline Update Group (GUG) placed emphasis on the need for thorough clinical evaluation to identify these potentially treatable and sometimes serious disorders. However, patients with identifiable causative diagnoses other than sensorineural hearing loss are excluded from this guideline as they are excluded from nearly all randomized controlled trials of tinnitus management, making it impossible to generalize trial results to these patients. Nevertheless, clinicians should decide whether to apply the recommendations of this guideline to patients with these conditions on an individualized basis. The guideline also underscores the need to distinguish between subjective, objective, and pulsatile tinnitus to further direct patient evaluation and management. Comprehensive management of objective tinnitus and pulsatile tinnitus is not within the scope of this guideline. Pulsatile tinnitus is the perception of a rhythmic sound in the absence of an external source that may be pulse-synchronous, which is often but not always related to vascular causes, or pulse-asynchronous, which is typically associated with mechanical causes such as palatal or middle ear myoclonus.1 Further, the guideline does not apply to transient ear noise, which is the sudden perception of a tonal or ringing sound in 1 ear, lasting fewer than 5 minutes, that may be accompanied by a sense of hearing loss or aural fullness, as it does not typically require clinical management.2 The guideline also excludes patients with tinnitus related to complex auditory hallucinations or hallucinations related to psychotic or seizure disorders. This is an update to an evidence-based clinical guideline developed for the evaluation and management of tinnitus. This updated guideline provides clinicians with a logical framework to improve patient care and mitigate the personal and social effects of persistent, bothersome tinnitus. The first part of the guideline is focused on the clinical evaluation of patients with tinnitus, including the history, physical exam, and selection and timing of diagnostic testing and specialty referral to identify potential underlying treatable pathology and reduce the risk of self-harm. The remainder of the guideline is focused on the evaluation and treatment of patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus, with recommendations to evaluate and measure its effects as well as to determine the most appropriate interventions to improve symptoms and quality of life.
ACTION STATEMENTS: The Guideline Update Group made strong recommendations for the following Key Action Statements (KAS): Clinicians should distinguish patients with bothersome tinnitus from patients with nonbothersome tinnitus (KAS 2). Clinicians should inquire about risks for self-harm in a patient with bothersome tinnitus (KAS 3). Clinicians should not obtain neuroradiologic imaging in patients with tinnitus specifically to evaluate the tinnitus unless specific concerning features are present (KAS 6). The Guideline Update Group made recommendations for the following KASs: Clinicians should perform a targeted history and physical examination at the initial evaluation of a patient with tinnitus (KAS 1). Clinicians should obtain a comprehensive audiological evaluation in patients with tinnitus (KAS 5). Clinicians should educate patients with tinnitus about the natural history and effects of, and management strategies for tinnitus (KAS 7). Clinicians should recommend a hearing aid evaluation for patients with hearing difficulties and persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 8). Clinicians should refer patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus for cochlear implant evaluation when they meet audiologic criteria for referral (KAS 9). Clinicians should recommend Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 11). Clinicians or their designee should assess and document outcomes of interventions in patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 15). The Guideline Update Group made recommendations against for the following KASs: Clinicians should not routinely recommend antidepressants, anticonvulsants, anxiolytics, or intratympanic medications for a primary indication of treating persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 12). Clinicians should not recommend dietary supplements for the primary indication of persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 13). Clinicians should not recommend repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for the treatment of patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 14A). The Guideline Update Group offered options for the following KASs: Clinicians may inquire about somatosensory features in patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 4). Clinicians may recommend sound enrichment to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 10). Clinicians may offer bimodal neuromodulation to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 14B).

Title: Understanding the Mortality Trends in Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiomyopathy: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis From 1999-2024.
Journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) associated with Cardiomyopathy (CM) continues to be the major cause of death. However, a national longitudinal study examining mortality trends from these conditions is still lacking. This study assessed mortality trends due to these conditions among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2024.
METHODS: An observational analysis of U.S. mortalities due to VA in patients with CM (ICD-10 I47.2, I49.0 and I25.5, I42 respectively), was conducted using CDC WONDER. Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMR) per 100,000 calculated and trends were assessed by calculating Average and Annual Percent Change (AAPC, APC), using joinpoint regression stratified by year, sex, race, and region.
RESULTS: From 1999 to 2024, 81,204 VA with CM-related deaths occurred with the overall AAMR declined from 2.54 in 1999 to 1.01 in 2024 (AAPC: -3.55%; p < 0.000001). AAMRs decreased from 1999 to 2007 (APC: -7.93), remained stable till 2022 (APC: -0.66), and dropped by 2024 (APC: -6.87). Men exhibited greater AAMRs (2.42) than women (0.68). Racially, the AAMRs were most pronounced in Non-Hispanic (NH) Blacks (1.97), followed by NH Whites (1.42), whereas Hispanics and NH Others experienced similar AAMRs of 0.97. Geographically, Delaware and the Western regions experienced the highest rates of mortality (2.2 and 1.53, respectively). Urban areas had higher AAMRs than rural settings (1.45 vs. 1.4) CONCLUSION: Although VA-CM mortality has declined over the past two decades, differences by race, sex, and geography remain, underscoring the need for targeted healthcare strategies.

Title: Effects of Antimicrobial Mouthwashes on Oral Health and Blood Pressure: A Preliminary Parallel Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although antimicrobial mouthwashes vary in efficacy and safety for managing biofilm-induced gingivitis, concerns remain regarding their potential to reduce nitric oxide bioavailability and increase hypertension risk. Therefore, we investigated whether octenidine is more effective and causes fewer adverse events than chlorhexidine, and whether antimicrobial mouthwash use increases hypertension risk.
METHODS: In this parallel randomized controlled trial, 90 participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to rinse with 10 mL of 2% saline (Group I), 0.2% chlorhexidine (Group II), or 0.1% octenidine (Group III) for 21 days. Co-primary outcomes (clinical parameters and blood pressure) and secondary outcomes (salivary bacterial count, adverse events, and pulse pressure) were assessed over 42 days.
RESULTS: At day 22, antimicrobial mouthwashes significantly reduced clinical (29%-52%) and microbial (> 92%) measures (p < 0.001), whereas saline produced minimal changes (p > 0.05). Salivary nitrate levels showed the opposite trend. Groups II and III showed comparable efficacy, but octenidine was associated with fewer adverse events. Although systolic blood pressure increased slightly in all groups, the changes were clinically insignificant. Elevated pulse pressure in antimicrobial groups returned to baseline by Day 42.
CONCLUSIONS: Octenidine (0.1%) was safer and comparably effective to chlorhexidine. Short-term antimicrobial mouthwash had no clinically significant effect on blood pressure.

Title: Epidemiology, clinical profile, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending at Spanish emergency departments (EDEN-56 study).
Journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with active cancer are increasing, clinically complex emergency department (ED) population, but large multicenter European data are limited.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the epidemiology, baseline characteristics, diagnoses, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending Spanish EDs, and assess whether associations between active cancer and short-term outcomes varied with age and sex.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Secondary analysis of the Emergency Department and Elder Needs retrospective multicenter registry, including all patients aged greater than or equal to 65 years attending 52 Spanish EDs during 1-7 April 2019. Patients with and without active cancer were compared. Annualized incidence was extrapolated overall, by sex, and by age. Age-related patterns were modeled using restricted cubic splines.
OUTCOME AND ANALYSIS: ED length of stay, hospitalization, length of hospitalization, and index-episode death. Age-by-cancer and age-by-sex interactions were assessed in unadjusted and multivariable models.
MAIN RESULTS: Among 25 557 older ED patients, 4701 (18.4%) had active cancer. The estimated annualized incidence of ED presentations was 10 885 per 100 000 inhabitants aged greater than or equal to 65 years [95% confidence interval (CI): 10 576-11 200], higher in men (annualized rate ratio: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.70-1.91) and in the mid-to-late 80s. Patients with cancer had more severe comorbidity (58.9 vs. 12.9%), polypharmacy (26.6 vs. 21.3%), and walking handicaps (31.5 vs. 28.2%). Malignancy accounted for only 7.7% of ED diagnoses in the cancer group; infections, heart failure, and respiratory conditions were frequent. Active cancer was associated with longer median ED stay (4.0 vs. 3.3 h; adjusted difference: 0.3, 95% CI: 0.1-0.4), higher hospitalization [32.5 vs. 24.0%; adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.34, 95% CI: 1.25-1.44], longer median hospitalization (7.5 vs. 6.9 days; adjusted difference: 0.5, 0.1-0.9), and higher index-episode mortality (5.5 vs. 2.5%; adjusted OR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.81-2.50). Age significantly modified ED length of stay, hospitalization, and mortality, with significantly different age-related changes between patients with and without cancer. Among patients with cancer, age-related trajectories did not significantly differ by sex.
CONCLUSION: Active cancer is common among older ED patients and associated with substantial resource use and worse short-term outcomes. These associations vary with age, supporting multidimensional assessment beyond chronological age or cancer status alone.

Title: An urgent call for quality measures for cardiac implantable electronic device infections in the United States.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract: Infection is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). Over 400,000 CIEDs are placed annually in the United States with an infection rate of approximately 1-2% in the first 12 months after implantation. In 2010, the American Heart Association provided a class I recommendation for complete system removal in all cases of endovascular CIED-I or pocket infection. Retrospective studies have shown that CIED removal is associated with improved outcomes, and prompt CIED removal within 7 days of confirmed infection is associated with lower mortality at 1-year compared to extraction after 7 days. Despite these strong recommendations and existing evidence, data demonstrates that ∼80% of patients with CIED-I do not undergo device extraction. To address this gap, we advocate for creation of an electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) that would create incentives for hospitals to provide efficient, guideline-concordant care, analogous to existing eCQMs for other conditions, such as ST elevation myocardial infarctions. At present, patients with CIED-Is are dying unnecessarily due to non-adherence with evidence-based, guideline recommended care. Healthcare providers and professional societies, working alongside government agencies, have an opportunity to significantly improve outcomes by developing a sustainable, accountable care model for CIED-Is.

Title: Cardiovascular and comorbid risk factors for thrombosis in primary immune thrombocytopenia: a single-center retrospective study.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence that patients with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) are at increased risk of thrombosis. The associations of clinical and comorbid factors with thrombosis in ITP remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the incidence rate and risk factors of arterial and venous thrombosis among patients with primary ITP.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted, enrolling adult patients diagnosed with ITP at Qilu Hospital between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2025. Thrombosis incidence was calculated using person-years of follow-up, and multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Sensitivity analyses were also conducted using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model regression, with death as a competing event.
RESULTS: Among 764 patients with ITP with 3540.8 person-years of follow-up, the incidence was 5.7 (95% CI, 4.9-6.5) per 100 person-years for arterial thrombosis and 2.1 (95% CI, 2.1 1.6-2.6) for venous thrombosis. The median age at thrombosis onset and the interval from ITP diagnosis to the index thrombotic event were 67.5 years and 2.4 years for arterial thrombosis and 62.0 years and 1.2 years for venous thrombosis, respectively. Recent 3-month exposure to all 3 ITP-targeted therapies increased the risk of both arterial and venous thrombosis.
CONCLUSION: Advanced age, prior thromboembolism, comorbidities, recent exposure to ITP-targeted therapies, and cardiovascular risk factors were independent risk factors for thrombosis in ITP. Thromboembolism in ITP mostly occurred in the presence of multiple thrombotic risk factors. Continuous risk assessment and optimized management are essential throughout the clinical course of ITP.

Title: Contribution of short-term changes in a composite health score on pathways linking social disadvantage and health: evidence from the UK biobank prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic and repeated exposure to external stresses may be embodied and generate an adverse biological response, in-turn affecting health. We investigated the role of 4-year change in a Biological Health Score (BHS) in the pathway linking social exposures to all-cause mortality, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (AS-CVD), and cancer incidence.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed 20,048 participants (10,266 women and 9782 men, aged 37-73 years at baseline) from the UK Biobank prospective cohort with repeated biomarker assessments. The BHS was derived from 15 biomarkers covering cardiovascular, metabolic, inflammatory, liver, and renal systems. We examined associations between BHS change and six social exposures using sex-stratified linear models. Associations between BHS change and subsequent all-cause mortality, AS-CVD incidence, and cancer incidence (ascertained through registry linkage until December 2022) were estimated using sex-specific Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline BHS and time between assessments, with sequential adjustment for additional exposures. Finally, we assessed whether BHS change mediated associations between social exposures and health outcomes using counterfactual mediation analysis.
FINDINGS: Total BHS increased over a mean interval of 4.3 years in both men and women, as did all sub-scores except the cardiovascular one. Lower education, low qualification, and financial difficulties were associated with greater increases in BHS. A 1-unit increase in BHS change was associated with: higher all-cause mortality in both men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.46, 95% CI 1.25-1.71) and women (1.26, 1.02-1.56); higher AS-CVD incidence in men (1.33, 1.13-1.57) and women (1.24, 1.03-1.48) and higher cancer incidence in men (1.16, 1.01-1.41) and women (1.29, 1.06-1.58). While no clear mediation by BHS change was observed for women, AS-CVD, or cancer, BHS change explained a small but statistically significant proportion of the association between low income and financial difficulties and mortality, in men.
INTERPRETATION: Whilst acknowledging the limitations of our dataset, we show that changes in a composite biological score over a few years, independent of age and baseline score, are socially-patterned and associated with subsequent mortality and cardiovascular disease, suggesting that repeated biological measurements may provide complementary information beyond single time-point assessments. Future research should extend these analyses to multiple repeated measurements, enabling the exploration of the dynamics of the embodiment of time-resolved external stresses and their effects on health.
FUNDING: Research Council of Norway, European Commission.

Title: Pacemaker Dependency in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Dual-chamber Devices After Alcohol Septum Ablation: A Retrospective Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA) are at risk for high-degree atrioventricular (AV) block, often requiring permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation. However, long-term pacemaker dependency in this population remains unclear.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed HOCM patients who underwent ASA and subsequent implantation of a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) due to procedure-related AV block between 2016 and 2023. CIED interrogation at ≥ 6 weeks postimplantation was used to assess ventricular pacing (VP). Pacemaker dependency was defined as > 1% VP. Associations with baseline characteristics were examined using logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 464 patients undergoing ASA, 95 (20.5%) received a CIED, and 67 were available for follow-up. Only 30 patients (44.8%) showed > 1% VP; 9 (13.4%) were completely dependent (100% VP). In contrast, 31 patients (46.3%) had ≤ 0.1% VP. Persistent AV block was more common in patients with preinterventional left bundle branch block. Intraprocedural AV block showed a trend toward persistent pacemaker dependency.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, long-term pacemaker dependency after ASA was unexpectedly low. These findings suggest that AV conduction may recover in a significant proportion of patients, raising the question of whether some may safely avoid PPM implantation. Larger prospective studies are needed to guide device therapy decisions in this population. Our findings challenge the assumption of permanent AV block after ASA and suggest reconsidering routine early device implantation in selected patients.

Title: Invasive Non-typhoidal Salmonella Infections in Adults: Clinical Features, Focal Disease, and Antimicrobial Resistance in a Turkish Tertiary-Care Center.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) infection may cause severe systemic and focal disease, particularly in patients with comorbidities or immunosuppression. Data on the clinical features and antimicrobial resistance patterns of iNTS infections in Türkiye remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and microbiological characteristics of adult patients with microbiologically confirmed iNTS infection at a tertiary-care center in Türkiye.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center case series included adult patients diagnosed with iNTS infection at a tertiary-care hospital in Türkiye between December 2015 and December 2025. Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella infection was defined as isolation of non-typhoidal Salmonella from blood or normally sterile body sites. Clinical, microbiological, antimicrobial susceptibility, and outcome data were analyzed.
RESULTS: Nine patients with iNTS infection were identified. The median age was 54 years (IQR, 45-68), and 5 patients (55.6%) were male. Underlying comorbidities were present in 8 patients (88.9%), most commonly hypertension, diabetes mellitus, autoimmune diseases, and HIV infection. Gastrointestinal symptoms were observed in only 2 patients (22.2%), whereas 7 patients (77.8%) presented without typical enteric manifestations. Bacteremia was detected in 7 patients (77.8%), and focal invasive infections were identified in 5 patients (55.6%), including spondylodiscitis, septic arthritis, thyroid abscess, and liver abscess. Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis was the predominant serovar, identified in 6 isolates (66.7%), while 3 isolates (33.3%) were classified as Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica without further serovar determination. All isolates remained susceptible to third-generation cephalosporins, whereas resistance to ampicillin and ciprofloxacin was detected in 4 (44.4%) and 3 isolates (33.3%), respectively. The median length of hospitalization was 16 days, and 2 patients (22.2%) died during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella infection may present with heterogeneous and frequently non-enteric manifestations, particularly in adults with significant comorbidities or immunosuppression. The high frequency of focal invasive disease and the relatively high rate of ciprofloxacin resistance in this series highlight the importance of early microbiological diagnosis, evaluation for metastatic infectious foci, and appropriate empirical antimicrobial therapy.
GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Graphical Abstract.

Title: The association between albuminuria and coronary atherosclerotic burden in the general population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Albuminuria predicts cardiovascular events, but its association with prevalent subclinical coronary atherosclerosis is less well defined. We examined the cross-sectional relationship between urinary albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) and coronary atherosclerotic burden in middle-aged adults from Sweden nationwide.
METHODS: UACR was measured in fasting spot urine in 9424 SCAPIS participants from Uppsala and Malmö. Coronary atherosclerosis was quantified by coronary artery calcium score (CACS; n = 9277) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA; n = 9187) for stenosis. Linear regression related log(UACR) to log(CACS) with sequential adjustment: Model 1 (age, sex, ethnicity, site), Model 2 (+blood pressure, antihypertensive treatment, diabetes and antidiabetic treatment), and Model 3 (+LDL cholesterol, lipid-lowering treatment, smoking status, and eGFR). Logistic regression examined prevalent calcification (CACS>0) and stenosis; subgroup analyses excluded CKD, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and diabetes stepwise.
RESULTS: Higher UACR was associated with higher CACS in the full cohort: β = 0.21 (95% CI 0.14-0.27), 0.08 (0.01-0.15), and 0.07 (0.00-0.14) in Models 1-3, respectively. Associations persisted after excluding CKD and cardiovascular disease (n = 8448): β = 0.20 (0.13-0.27), 0.19 (0.12-0.26), and 0.07 (0.00-0.15). With further exclusions, Model 3 estimates attenuated and were non-significant (no CKD/cardiovascular disease/hypertension: β = 0.06 [-0.02 to 0.14]; additionally no diabetes: β = 0.05 [-0.03 to 0.14]). In Model 1, each log-increase in UACR was associated with higher odds of CACS>0 (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.05-1.12) and stenosis (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.08), but associations attenuated and were non-significant in Models 2-3.
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria is associated with greater coronary calcification burden, including in broadly healthy individuals, supporting the concept that albuminuria may reflect vascular disease early in the cardiovascular disease continuum.

Title: Prevalence, Health Care Burden, and Longitudinal Outcomes of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Among People With Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are common comorbidities. We aimed to assess health care resource use and outcomes associated with COPD in patients hospitalized for HF.
METHODS: This was an exploratory cohort analysis of patients hospitalized for HF and enrolled in the Patient-Centered Care Transitions in HF cluster-randomized trial. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included all-cause and HF hospitalization, health care resource use, and direct health care costs. Survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline variables.
RESULTS: Among 4441 patients discharged alive, 1136 (25.6%) had COPD at baseline. All-cause mortality was higher at 5 years among patients with vs without COPD (75.2% vs 60.9%, adjusted hazard ratio 1.29, 95% confidence interval 1.19-1.40). Patients with COPD had more frequent all-cause rehospitalizations (mean [standard deviation] 3.4 [6.6] vs 2.7 [8.6] per patient, P = 0.01), but no significant difference in HF rehospitalizations (0.9 [2.3] vs 0.9 [4.5] per patient, P = 0.74). Patients with COPD had more annual physician visits, multidisciplinary clinic visits, and supportive care (all P < 0.01), as well as greater annual direct health care costs in Canadian dollars (at 5 years: $91,888 [$109,319] vs $76,823 [$116,218]) than those without COPD, primarily driven by rehospitalizations.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients discharged alive after hospitalization for HF, COPD is common and is associated with higher all-cause mortality and all-cause rehospitalizations, greater health care use, and higher direct health care costs. Interventions to reduce the health care burden in HF should include broad approaches that address important comorbidities.

Title: Effect of statins on the mortality of long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a population-based study in endemic area.
Journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) are at risk of excessive mortality. This territory-wide cohort study aims to investigate the relationship between statin use and mortality among 5-year survivors of NPC.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study conducted with data from a territory-wide registry. Patients who survived five years after being diagnosed with non-metastatic NPC in Hong Kong between 1 January 1997 and 30 December 2015 were included. Patients were divided into statin users and statin non-users. We performed the inverse propensity of treatment weighting (IPTW) method to balance confounding factors. The primary outcome of overall survival (OS) was compared between the two groups and stratified by the cause of death, statin types and duration of statin usage.
FINDINGS: 7872 subjects (2439 statin users and 5433 statin non-users) were included in the final analysis. The 10-year, 15-year, and 20-year survival probabilities of statin users compared to non-users were 89.1 vs. 71.8%, 77.2 vs. 55.1%, and 59.2 vs. 42.4% respectively (HR 0.46, p < 0.001). After adjusting for immortal time bias, the hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.71 (p < 0.001). Statin use was associated with reduced risk of death due to secondary malignancy (HR 0.51; p = 0.002), cardiovascular disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.002), and pulmonary disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.011). Mortality was significantly lower in long-term statin usage of >6 years (HR 0.31; p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, patients who received second- or third-generation statins were associated with a lower risk of mortality (HR 0.66 and HR 0.41, respectively), although this finding requires further validation.
INTERPRETATION: Our study suggests that statin usage is associated with reduced mortality in long-term NPC survivors. Further prospective study is warranted.
FUNDING: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

Title: Atorvastatin Prevents Early Lipotoxic Remodelling in Right Ventricular Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) pacing can induce metabolic and structural alterations in left ventricular (LV) myocardium, including lipid accumulation, glycogen depletion, and increased endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. This study evaluated protective effects of atorvastatin on RV pacing-induced metabolic dysfunction.
METHODS: Fifteen male Lanyu miniature pigs were randomized into sham control (n = 5), RV pacing (n = 5), and RV pacing with atorvastatin treatment (n = 5) groups. RV pacing was achieved via ventricular lead implantation at the RV outflow tract, followed by complete atrioventricular block, with ventricular pacing maintained for at least 80 beats/min in dual-chamber, dual-sensing, dual-response, rate-responsive mode to provide atrial-synchronous ventricular pacing while allowing atrial sensing or pacing. The RV pacing with atorvastatin treatment group received atorvastatin (40 mg/d) starting 2 weeks before surgery until euthanasia at 6 months. Metabolic, histologic, and molecular parameters were assessed in LV myocardial tissue.
RESULTS: Compared with sham controls, RV pacing significantly increased myocardial lipid accumulation, with higher triglyceride (2.43 ± 0.17 vs 1.74 ± 0.14 μg/mg, P < 0.01) and diacylglycerol (2902 ± 567.7 vs 977.5 ± 182.5 μg/mg, P < 0.01) levels, and significantly reduced glycogen content (0.09 ± 0.03 vs 0.21 ± 0.03 μg/mg, P < 0.05). ER stress markers binding immunoglobulin protein and cleaved caspase-9 were markedly increased in the RV pacing group (P < 0.0001). Atorvastatin significantly reduced lipid accumulation (triglycerides: 1.83 ± 0.08 μg/mg; P < 0.05), ER stress, and apoptosis, but did not significantly restore glycogen levels.
CONCLUSIONS: RV pacing induces lipid accumulation, glycogen loss, and increased ER stress in the LV myocardium. Atorvastatin partially mitigated these effects by normalizing fatty acid metabolism and reducing ER stress and apoptosis, suggesting a potential role in attenuating early/subclinical RV pacing-induced metabolic remodelling.

Title: Validation of the discriminatory performance of the iPREFACE score for clinically significant fetal acidemia: an outcome-enriched nested case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiotocography is widely used for monitoring fetal well-being during labor; however, its clinical utility remains limited due to a high false-positive rate, particularly in predicting adverse neonatal outcomes such as cerebral palsy. Despite its implementation, the incidence of cerebral palsy has not decreased, whereas cesarean section rates have increased. Severe fetal acidemia has been shown to be associated with neonatal brain injury. The iPREFACE score was developed to address this limitation by evaluating the accumulation of fetal stress due to uterine contractions based on the five-tier classification of fetal heart rate (FHR) patterns defined by the Japanese Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology. Previous studies have demonstrated that the iPREFACE score significantly correlates with umbilical artery (UmA) blood gas parameters, including pH, base excess (BE), and lactate, and has a high predictive ability for fetal acidemia.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to validate the discriminatory performance of the iPREFACE score for clinically significant fetal acidemia, defined as UmA pH<7.1, using an outcome-enriched artificially balanced cohort. Secondary analyses evaluated performance at UmA pH<7.2 and <7.0, and an exploratory analysis assessed UmA pH<7.3 to examine stepwise fetal deterioration during labor.
STUDY DESIGN: A nested case-control study was conducted involving women who had full-term vaginal deliveries at a single center between January 2017 and July 2023. To construct an outcome-enriched cohort, cases with UmA pH<7.2 were matched 1:1 with randomly selected controls with UmA pH≥7.2. The iPREFACE score was calculated by summing the levels of FHR waveform patterns in the 30 minutes before delivery. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate discriminatory performance at different thresholds of UmA pH (<7.1, <7.2, <7.0, and <7.3). Correlations between the iPREFACE score and UmA blood gas parameters (pH, pCO₂, pO₂, HCO₃⁻, BE, and lactate) were assessed using linear and quadratic regression models. Bland-Altman analysis was performed to assess agreement between predicted and measured UmA pH values.
RESULTS: Of the 272 patients, 15 (5.5%) had UmA pH<7.1 and 6 (2.2%) had UmA pH<7.0. The ROC-AUC for the iPREFACE score was 0.851 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.771-0.931) for the primary outcome of UmA pH<7.1. The AUC was 0.912 (95% CI: 0.879-0.945) for UmA pH<7.2 and 0.823 (95% CI: 0.656-0.989) for UmA pH<7.0. In the exploratory analysis, the AUC for UmA pH<7.3 was 0.833. Quadratic regression analysis revealed that the iPREFACE score had the highest coefficient of determination (R²) with pH (0.415), followed by BE (0.357), pCO₂ (0.230), lactate (0.165), and HCO₃⁻ (0.106), whereas pO₂ showed a notably lower correlation (R²=0.02). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean difference of -0.16 between predicted and measured UmA pH values, with limits of agreement from -0.41 to 0.09.
CONCLUSION: In an outcome-enriched cohort, the iPREFACE score demonstrated discriminatory performance for clinically significant fetal acidemia (UmA pH<7.1) and significant correlations with key UmA blood gas parameters, particularly pH and BE. Consistent discriminatory performance across multiple pH thresholds supports further evaluation of the iPREFACE score for stepwise assessment of progressive fetal deterioration during labor.

Title: Blood lead exposure, renal hyperfiltration, and accelerated kidney function decline among people living with HIV in northern Tanzania: A longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People living with HIV (PLWH) face a high burden of kidney disease from HIV-related injury, antiretroviral toxicity, and environmental lead exposure. Renal hyperfiltration, an early compensatory state, may precede accelerated kidney function decline, yet its relationship with lead exposure remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa.
METHODS: We analyzed prospective longitudinal data from the Mwanza HIV and Cardiovascular Disease cohort in northern Tanzania (baseline analytic sample N = 943; 467 PLWH and 476 HIV-uninfected partners). Linear mixed-effects models used all available repeated eGFR measurements over four years; parent-cohort retention was 93.9% at 36 months. Blood lead levels were measured from dried blood spots using ICP-MS. eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI 2021 equation at baseline and over four years. Hyperfiltration was defined using sex-specific thresholds (>130 mL/min/1.73 m² for males, >125 mL/min/1.73 m² for females). Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear regression and linear mixed-effects models, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, smoking, and HIV status.
RESULTS: Baseline eGFR: Higher log₁₀ blood lead levels were independently associated with lower baseline eGFR (fully adjusted β = -1.3; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.17; p = 0.025), indicating an inverse cross-sectional association between lead exposure and kidney function at baseline. Longitudinal eGFR decline: Baseline hyperfiltration was strongly associated with subsequent eGFR decline over the four-year follow-up. Compared with participants with normal baseline filtration, those with hyperfiltration experienced an additional annual reduction of -9.5 to -9.9 mL/min/1.73 m² compared with normal filtration (p < 0.001) over four years follow-up. Consequently, participants with baseline hyperfiltration experienced the steepest declines over four years (approximately -25 to -26 mL/min/1.73 m²). Higher lead exposure was also associated with progressively worsening eGFR trajectories, with the greatest deterioration observed among participants with baseline hyperfiltration. Sensitivity analyses using an age-adjusted hyperfiltration definition and excluding extreme blood-lead values produced results consistent with the primary models.
CONCLUSION: Baseline renal hyperfiltration was strongly associated with subsequent kidney decline among people living with HIV, with greater declines observed among those with higher blood lead levels. These findings highlight the potential importance of lead exposure and kidney function monitoring in PLWH, particularly in resource-limited settings, while recognizing that the observed associations do not establish causality.

Title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

Title: Prognostic Impact of a Simple GDMT Score on Clinical Outcomes and Cardiac Reverse Remodelling in Patients with ADHF: Insights from the JROADHF-Next Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reported results indicate that implementation rates of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) are associated with improved prognosis and cardiac function in heart failure (HF) patients. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between what we term a "simple GDMT score" calculated at discharge and subsequent cardiac reverse remodelling and long-term outcomes in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF, using data from the Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (JROADHF-NEXT) prospective registry.
METHODS: We analyzed 2313 hospitalized patients with HFrEF or HFmrEF, stratifying them into high-score (≥ 5 points) and low-score (< 5 points) groups based on their discharge GDMT score.
RESULTS: The high-score group demonstrated a significantly lower risk of the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization (hazard ratio = 0.64, 95% confidence interval: 0.55-0.76), an association that remained significant following multivariable adjustment (adjusted model: hazard ratio = 0.70, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-0.88). Furthermore, the high-score group exhibited significantly greater improvements in echocardiographic indices, including absolute changes in left ventricular ejection fraction (P < 0.001), left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (P < 0.001), and left ventricular end-systolic volume index (P < 0.001), and showed significant reductions in brain natriuretic peptide (P = 0.005) and N-terminal pro brain natriuretic peptide levels (P < 0.001) at 1-year follow-up assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher simple GDMT score at discharge is independently associated with better 2-year clinical outcomes and favourable cardiac reverse remodelling in this cohort of HFrEF/HFmrEF patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF. These findings suggest that a simple assessment of GDMT at discharge may serve as a practical benchmark of discharge medical optimization in routine clinical care.

Title: Frailty and Bleeding Events in Heart Failure: Insights from the JROADHF-NEXT.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frail patients are considered to be at higher risk of bleeding than non-frail patients; however, the association between frailty and bleeding risk in patients with heart failure (HF) remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the prevalence of bleeding events, examine the relationship between frailty severity and bleeding risk, and assess the association between bleeding events and subsequent mortality in patients with HF receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from the Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure-Next, a prospective, multicentre, nationwide registry. Frailty was evaluated using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Bleeding events were defined as major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, based on the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis Bleeding Scale.
RESULTS: Among 4016 patients, 3029 (75.4%) were discharged on antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication. After excluding 89 with missing CFS data, 2940 patients were analyzed (mean age: 75 ± 12 years; 64.0% male). Patients were grouped by CFS scores: 1-3 (n = 1033); 4-5 (n = 1364); and 6-9 (n = 543). At 2 years, 149 (5.0%) experienced bleeding. Higher CFS scores were associated with increased bleeding risk (CFS score 4-5: hazard ratio [HR]: 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-2.34; CFS score 6-9: HR: 1.75; 95% CI: 1.04-2.93). In addition, bleeding events were associated with a higher risk of mortality (HR: 2.80; 95% CI: 1.88-4.17, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is associated with bleeding risk in patients with HF receiving antithrombotic therapy. Bleeding events were associated with a higher risk of subsequent death.

Title: Single-view echocardiography-based deep learning for pulmonary hypertension detection: a multi-level supervised and explainable approach.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of pulmonary hypertension (PH), particularly mild disease, remains challenging. We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model for noninvasive PH screening using single-view transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), without reliance on Doppler measurements.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, apical four-chamber (A4C) TTE cine loops were collected between January 2023 and June 2025. A total of 144 patients with PH confirmed by right heart catheterization (RHC), 17 RHC-confirmed non-PH patients, and 95 non-PH controls defined by TTE under strict inclusion criteria were included. An additional temporally independent validation cohort of 40 RHC-confirmed subjects was enrolled between December 2025 and May 2026. Multiple DL architectures were evaluated for detecting PH. Model performance was assessed at both sample and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity.
RESULTS: A total of 256 patients with 318 TTE examinations were included for model development and independent validation, and an additional 40 RHC-confirmed subjects with 40 TTE examinations were included for temporal validation. The multi-level supervised model achieved the best performance among the evaluated architectures, with a patient-level AUROC of 1.000 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.998-1.000], sensitivity of 0.954, and specificity of 1.000 in the independent validation cohort. In the temporal validation cohort, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.843-0.992), with sensitivity of 0.875, specificity of 0.813, and accuracy of 0.850. In an analysis of 50 RHC-confirmed subjects, the DL model achieved an AUROC of 0.937 (95% CI: 0.865-0.987) for distinguishing mild PH from non-PH, with sensitivity of 0.857 and specificity of 0.864, compared with AUROCs of 0.607-0.825 for conventional echocardiographic parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable DL framework based on single-view A4C echocardiography for noninvasive PH assessment. The model showed promising performance, including preserved sensitivity for mild PH. Further multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Impact of hypertriglyceridemia on right ventricular deformation in patients with left ventricular myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a significant risk factor for myocardial infarction (MI), adversely affecting left ventricular (LV) structure and function and worsening clinical outcomes. Given the interaction between ventricles, the right heart may also be affected by MI. This study investigated the additional effects of HTG on right ventricular (RV) deformation in patients with acute MI.
METHODS: The study included 101 patients with MI [58 without HTG (HTG-) and 43 with HTG (HTG+)] and 83 control participants, all of whom underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The patients with MI were categorized into HTG+ and HTG- subgroups. RV and LV function and strain were assessed, and multivariate linear regression was performed to identify determinants of RV peak strain (PS).
RESULTS: Compared with the HTG- group, the HTG+ group exhibited higher total cholesterol and troponin levels (P=0.002 and P=0.043, respectively), as well as significantly lower RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05 after Bonferroni correction). RV radial PS was inversely correlated with LV mass (r=-0.349, P=0.021), total cholesterol (r=-0.402, P=0.007), troponin (r=-0.584, P<0.001), and infarct size (r=-0.410, P=0.006). RV circumferential PS was correlated with multiple LV parameters, lipids, and infarct extent (r=0.323 to 0.574; all P<0.05). After adjusting for age, sex, and blood pressure, HTG remained independently associated with impaired RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: HTG is associated with greater RV strain impairment in patients with MI. Our findings suggest that triglyceride levels and LV infarct extent may be associated with RV strain impairment, warranting further investigation in prospective studies.

Title: Association between microwave ablation and remission in patients with Graves' hyperthyroidism receiving continuous antithyroid drug treatment: a single-arm prospective study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Graves' disease (GD) is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism. Nearly half of patients develop persistent/recurrent GD (prGD) after antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy. Microwave ablation (MWA) is a precise minimally invasive therapeutic modality; however, evidence regarding its efficacy for prGD remains limited. This study therefore evaluated the efficacy of MWA in treating prGD and investigated factors predictive of post-MWA remission.
METHODS: This single-arm prospective study enrolled 45 patients with prGD who underwent bilateral thyroid MWA under ultrasound guidance at the Affiliated Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine between January 2023 and April 2024. The primary outcome was the remission rate during follow-up, defined as maintenance of normal thyroid function for at least 6 months after ATD discontinuation. Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test was used to analyze remission, and logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to identify factors associated with remission.
RESULTS: The cohort included 34 females and 11 males, with a median follow-up of 31.00 (28.00, 33.00) months. Notable findings included a significant reduction in the median thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor antibody level at the last follow-up (P<0.001). Both thyroid volume and the average methimazole (MMI) dose were significantly reduced (both P<0.001). At the last follow-up, remission was achieved in 29 patients, yielding a total remission rate of 64.44%. Patients in the remission group had smaller baseline thyroid volumes than those in the non-remission group. Preoperative thyroid volume was independently associated with remission [odds ratio (OR) =0.829; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.707-0.971; P=0.020], with an optimal cutoff of 29.35 mL [area under the curve (AUC) =74.4%; 95% CI: 0.596-0.892; sensitivity =72.4%; specificity =68.7%]. All nine patients with thyroid volumes less than 20 mL achieved remission. No severe complications were reported during the follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: MWA was associated with decreased thyroid volume and reduced MMI dosage in patients with prGD, and clinical remission was observed in a subset of these patients. A preoperative thyroid volume of less than 29.35 mL is associated with a higher likelihood of remission.

Title: Allostatic Load and Severe Clinical Phenotypes in Major Depressive Disorder: A Cross-Sectional Statistical Mediation Analysis of Perceived Stress, Cognitive Impairment, and Suicidal Ideation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perceived stress is associated with adverse clinical features of major depressive disorder (MDD), but the role of multisystem physiological dysregulation remains uncertain. We examined whether allostatic load (AL) was statistically associated with the relationship between perceived stress and cognitive impairment or severe suicidal ideation.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional electronic medical record study included 385 adults with DSM-5 MDD assessed within a single three-day index window. Perceived stress was measured with the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), and chronic exposure context was characterized from documented negative life events. AL was calculated from 15 cardiovascular, metabolic, immune-inflammatory, and neuroendocrine indicators. Cognitive impairment was defined as Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) <26 and severe suicidal ideation as Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) ideation severity ≥4. Sequential logistic regression and bootstrap product-of-coefficients statistical mediation analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Compared with Low AL, High AL was associated with cognitive impairment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.17, 95% CI 2.89-13.15) and severe suicidal ideation (aOR 6.43, 95% CI 2.98-13.88; both P<0.001). Continuous AL showed consistent associations with both outcomes. The indirect effect through AL was supported for cognitive impairment (0.39, 95% bootstrap CI 0.16-0.69), but not for severe suicidal ideation (0.14, 95% bootstrap CI -0.12 to 0.41).
CONCLUSION: Higher AL was independently associated with both adverse clinical phenotypes. Statistical mediation was supported for the perceived stress-cognitive impairment association but not for suicidal ideation. Because exposure, mediator, and outcomes were assessed within the same index window, temporal and causal mediation cannot be inferred.

Title: Preprocedural Q-wave Depth Does Not Predict Mortality After Primary Coronary Intervention for ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathologic Q waves on the admission electrocardiogram (ECG) have historically been markers of myocardial necrosis and adverse outcomes after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Although quantitative markers such as Q-wave width may add prognostic value, they can be difficult to apply clinically. We hypothesised that maximal and average pre-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) Q-wave depth could predict short- and medium-term mortality.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI (N = 625). Pre-PCI ECGs were analysed using European Society of Cardiology/American Heart Association definitions to identify pathologic Q waves. Maximal and average Q-wave depth (mm) and infarct territory were recorded. Posterior patterns, bundle branch block confounding interpretation, and Q waves outside the culprit territory were excluded. Outcomes were all-cause mortality at 3 and 12 months.
RESULTS: Of the 625 patients studied, 203 with pathologic Q waves in the infarct territory had complete depth measurements for analysis. Twelve-month mortality was 7.4% (15 of 203). Neither maximal nor average Q-wave depth was associated with mortality at 3 or 12 months in any infarct territory. Pain-to-balloon time demonstrated a weak positive correlation with maximal (Spearman rho = 0.204, P = 0.004) and average (rho = 0.152, P = 0.033) Q-wave depth.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, observational cohort of STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, preprocedural Q-wave depth was not associated with all-cause mortality at 3 or 12 months. These findings do not support Q-wave depth as a standalone pre-PCI prognostic marker; larger studies and alternative ECG measures may be more informative. Q-wave depth was weakly associated with total ischemic time, warranting further evaluation in larger multicentre cohorts.

Title: Inflammation Mediates the Relationship Between Serum Uric Acid and New-Onset Diabetes Risk in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease: Results from a Multicenter Cohort Study [Letter].
